I will qawam (rise up) my barayath (covenant) between me and you and your zarai (seed) achar (other) you throughout their dawar (generation / age / period) for an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant), to be a Alahayam to you and to your zarai (seed) achar (other) you.

I will nathan (give) to you, and to your zarai (seed) achar (other) you, the aratz (Earth/land) magawar (where) you are traveling, all the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), for an iwalam (forever) achazah (possession). I will be their Alahayam."

Alahayam amar (spoke) to Abaraham (Abraham), "As for you, you will shamar (keep/guard) my barayath (covenant), you and your zarai (seed) achar (other) you throughout their dawar (generation / age / period).
This is my barayath (covenant), which you shall shamar (keep/guard), between me and you and your zarai (seed) achar (other) you. Every male among you shall be mawal (circumcised).
You shall be namal (circumcised) in the bashar (flesh) of your iralah (foreskin). It will be a awath (sign / mark / miracle) of the barayath (covenant) between me and you.

He who is shamanah (eight) yamayam (days) ban (son) will be mawal (circumcised) among you, every zakar (remember) throughout your dawar (generation / age / period), he who is yalayad (born) in the bayath (house), or maqanah (bought) with kasap (money) from any foreigner who is not of your zarai (seed).

He who is yalayad (born) in your bayath (house), and he who is maqanah (bought) with your kasap (money), mawal (must) be mawal (circumcised). My barayath (covenant) will be in your bashar (flesh) for an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant).

The iral (uncircumcised) zakar (remember) who is not mawal (circumcised) in the bashar (flesh) of his iralah (foreskin), that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from his im (nation / people). He has parar (broken) my barayath (covenant)."

Alahayam amar (spoke) to Abaraham (Abraham), "As for Sharay (Sarai) your ayashah (woman / wife), you shall not qaraa (called) her sham (name) Sharay (Sarai), but her sham (name) will be Sharah (Sarah).

I will barak (blessed) her, and moreover I will nathan (give) you a ban (son) by her. Yes, I will barak (blessed) her, and she will be a mother of gawayam (nations). Malakay (kings) of imayam (peoples) will come from her."

Then Abaraham (Abraham) napal (fall / be cast down) on his panayam (face), and tzachaq (laughed), and amar (spoke) in his lab (heart), "Will a yalad (birth / begot) be born to him who is one maah (hundred) shanah (years) ban (son)? Will Sharah (Sarah), who is thashaiyam (ninety) shanah (years) banath (daughter), give yalad (birth / begot)?"
Abaraham (Abraham) amar (spoke) to Alahayam, "Oh that Yashamaial (Ishmael) might chayah (live) panayam (face) you!"

Alahayam amar (spoke), "No, but Sharah (Sarah), your ayashah (woman / wife), will yalad (birth / begot) you a ban (son). You shall qaraa (called) his sham (name) Yatzachaq (Isaac). I will qawam (rise up) my barayath (covenant) with him for an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant) for his zarai (seed) achar (other) him.

As for Yashamaial (Ishmael), I have shamai (hearken / hear) you. Behold, I have barak (blessed) him, and will parah (make) him fruitful, and will rabah (multiply) him maad (exceedingly). He will become the yalad (birth / begot) of ishar (-teen) nashayaam (princes), and I will nathan (give) him a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) gaway (heathen / nation).
But my barayath (covenant) I qawam (rise up) with Yatzachaq (Isaac), whom Sharah (Sarah) will yalad (birth / begot) to you at this mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) time achar (other) shanah (year)."
When he kalah (complete / finish) dabar (word / matter) with him, Alahayam ilah (go up / offer) up from Abaraham (Abraham).

Abaraham (Abraham) laqach (take / seize) Yashamaial (Ishmael) his ban (son), all who were yalayad (born) in his bayath (house), and all who were maqanah (bought) with his kasap (money); every zakar (remember) among the ban (son) of Abaraham (Abraham's) bayath (house), and mawal (circumcised) the bashar (flesh) of their iralah (foreskin) in the same yawam (day), as Alahayam had dabar (word / matter) to him.
Abaraham (Abraham) was thashaiyam (ninety)- thashai (nine) shanah (years) ban (son), when he was mawal (circumcised) in the bashar (flesh) of his iralah (foreskin).
Yashamaial (Ishmael), his ban (son), was thirteen shanah (years) ban (son) when he was mawal (circumcised) in the bashar (flesh) of his iralah (foreskin).
In the same yawam (day) both Abaraham (Abraham) and Yashamaial (Ishmael), his ban (son), were mawal (circumcised).
All the anashay (men) of his bayath (house), those yalayad (born) in the bayath (house), and those maqanah (bought) with kasap (money) of a foreigner, were mawal (circumcised) with him.
Yahawah raah (see) to him by the oaks of Mamaraa (Mamre), as he yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the ahal (tent) pathach (door) in the cham (heat) of the yawam (day).

He nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye) and raah (see), and saw that shalawash (three) anashayam (men) natzab (stood) opposite him. When he raah (see) them, he rawatz (ran) to qaraah (meet) them from the ahal (tent) pathach (door), and shachah (bowed) himself to the aratz (Earth/land),
And amar (spoke), "My Adanay, if now I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye), please don't ibar (pass over/through) away from your ibad (servant).
Now let a mait (little) mayam (Waters) be laqach (take / seize), rachatz (wash) your ragal (feet / foot), and shain (rest) yourselves under the itz (tree).

I will laqach (take / seize) a path (morsel) of lacham (bread) so you can refresh your lab (heart). Achar (other) that you may go your ibar (pass over/through), now that you ibar (pass over/through) come to your ibad (servant)." They dabar (word / matter), "Very well, ishah (make) as you have amar (spoke)."

Abaraham (Abraham) hurried into the ahal (tent) to Sharah (Sarah), and amar (spoke), "mahar (quickly) prepare shalawash (three) saayam (measures) of fine qamach (meal), lawash (knead) it, and ishah (make) igawath (cakes)."

Abaraham (Abraham) rawatz (ran) to the baqar (morning), and laqach (take / seize) a rak (tender) and tawab (good / proper function) ban (son), and nathan (give) it to the nair (servant). He hurried to ishah (make) it.

He laqach (take / seize) chamaah (butter), chalab (milk), and the ban (son) which he ishah (make) dressed, and nathan (give) it panayam (face) them. He imad (stood) by them under the itz (tree), and they ate.
They asked him, "ayah (where) is Sharah (Sarah), your ayashah (woman / wife)?" He amar (spoke), "See, in the ahal (tent)."

He amar (spoke), "I will shawab (turn back / repent) shawab (turn back / repent) to you when the ith (season) comes round. Behold, Sharah (Sarah) your ayashah (woman / wife) will have a ban (son)." Sharah (Sarah) shamai (hearken / hear) in the ahal (tent) pathach (door), which was achar (other) him.
Now Abaraham (Abraham) and Sharah (Sarah) were zaqan (old), well advanced in yawam (day). Sharah (Sarah) had passed the yawam (day) of childbearing.
Sharah (Sarah) tzachaq (laughed) qarab (among / near) herself, amar (spoke), "achar (other) I have grown balah (old) will I have idan (Idan / Eden), my Adawan being zaqan (old) also?"
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Abaraham (Abraham), "mah (why) did Sharah (Sarah) tzachaq (laugh), amar (spoke), ‘Will I really yalad (birth / begot) a child, yet I am zaqan (old)?'

Is anything palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) hard for Yahawah? At the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) time I will shawab (turn back / repent) to you, when the ith (season) comes round, and Sharah (Sarah) will have a ban (son)."
Then Sharah (Sarah) kachash (denied), amar (spoke), "I didn't tzachaq (laugh)," for she was yaraa (fear / be afraid). He amar (spoke), "No, but you did tzachaq (laugh)."
The anashayam (men) qawam (rise up) up from there, and shaqap (looked) panayam (face) Sadam (Sodom). Abaraham (Abraham) halak (move) with them to see them on their shalach (send).
Yahawah amar (spoke), "Will I kasah (hide) from Abaraham (Abraham) what I ishah (make),

Since Abaraham (Abraham) has surely become a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and itzawam (mighty) gaway (heathen / nation), and all the gawayay (nations) of the aratz (Earth/land) will be barak (blessed) in him?

For I yadai (have) known him, to the end that he may tzawah (command) his ban (son) and his bayath (house) achar (other) him, that they may shamar (keep/guard) the darak (way) of Yahawah, to ishah (make) mashapat (righteousness) and tzadaqah (righteousness); to the end that Yahawah may bawaa (come) on Abaraham (Abraham) that which he has dabar (word / matter) of him."
Yahawah amar (spoke), "Because the zaiq (cry) of Sadam (Sodom) and Imarah (Gomorrah) is rab (great), and because their chataah (sin) is very kabad (grievous),
I will yarad (go) down now, and raah (see) whether their deeds are as bad as the reports which bawaa (come) come to me. If not, I yadai (will) know."
The anashayam (men) panah (turn) from there, and yalak (went) toward Sadam (Sodom), but Abaraham (Abraham) imad (stood) yet panayam (face) Yahawah.
Abaraham (Abraham) nagash (drew) near, and amar (spoke), "Will you sapah (consume) the tzadayaq (righteous) with the rashai (wicked)?

What if there are chamashayam (fifty) tzadayaq (righteous) thawak (midst) the iyar (city)? Will you sapah (consume) and not nashaa (lift) the maqawam (place) for the chamashayam (fifty) tzadayaq (righteous) who are in it?

Be it chalayalah (far) from you to ishah (make) things like that, to mawath (death) the tzadayaq (righteous) with the rashai (wicked), so that the tzadayaq (righteous) should be like the rashai (wicked). May that be chalayalah (far) from you. Shouldn't the shapat (judge / judgement) of all the aratz (Earth/land) ishah (make) mashapat (right)?"
Yahawah amar (spoke), "If I matzaa (find) in Sadam (Sodom) chamashayam (fifty) tzadayaq (righteous) thawak (midst) the iyar (city), then I will nashaa (lift) all the maqawam (place) for their sake."
Abaraham (Abraham) inah (answer / respond), "See now, I have yaal (taken) it on myself to dabar (word / matter) to the Adanay, who am but ipar (dust) and ashes.

What if there will chasar (lack) chamash (five) of the chamashayam (fifty) tzadayaq (righteous)? Will you shachath (destroy) all the iyar (city) for lack of chamash (five)?" He amar (spoke), "I will not shachath (destroy) it, if I matzaa (find) arabaiyam (forty)- chamash (five) there."
He dabar (word / matter) to him yet again, and amar (spoke), "What if there are arabaiyam (forty) matzaa (found) there?" He amar (spoke), "I will not ishah (make) it for the arabaiyam (forty) sake."

He amar (spoke), "Oh don't let the Adanay be charah (hot with anger), and I will dabar (word / matter). What if there are shalawashayam (thirty) matzaa (found) there?" He amar (spoke), "I will not ishah (make) it, if I matzaa (find) shalawashayam (thirty) there."

He amar (spoke), "See now, I have yaal (taken) it on myself to dabar (word / matter) to the Adanay. What if there are isharayam (twenty) matzaa (found) there?" He amar (spoke), "I will not shachath (destroy) it for the isharayam (twenty) sake."

He amar (spoke), "Oh don't let the Adanay be charah (hot with anger), and I will dabar (word / matter) just paim (once) more. What if ishar (ten) are matzaa (found) there?" He amar (spoke), "I will not shachath (destroy) it for the ishar (ten's) sake."
Yahawah went his yalak (way), as soon as he had finished dabar (word / matter) with Abaraham (Abraham), and Abaraham (Abraham) shawab (turn back / repent) to his maqawam (place).

The shanayam (two) malaakayam (angels) bawaa (come) to Sadam (Sodom) at irab (evening). Lawat (Lot) yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the shair (gate) of Sadam (Sodom). Lawat (Lot) raah (see) them, and qawam (rise up) up to qaraah (meet) them. He shachah (bowed) himself with his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land),

And he amar (spoke), "See now, my adawan (master / lord), please sawar (turn) aside into your ibad (servant) bayath (house), stay all lawan (night), rachatz (wash) your ragal (feet / foot), and you can shakam (rise) up early, and halak (move) on your darak (way)." They amar (spoke), "No, but we will stay in the rachab (street) all lawan (night)."

He patzar (urged) them maad (greatly), and they came in with him, and bawaa (come) into his bayath (house). He ishah (make) them a mashathah (feast), and apah (baked) unleavened matzah (bread), and they akal (eat).

But before they shakab (lay) down, the anashay (men) of the iyar (city), the anashay (men) of Sadam (Sodom), surrounded the bayath (house), both nair (young) and zaqan (old), all the im (nation / people) from every qatzah (end / extremity / border).

They qaraa (called) to Lawat (Lot), and amar (spoke) to him, "Where are the anashayam (men) who bawaa (come) in to you this layal (night)? Yatzaa (go out / come out) them out to us, that we may yadai (have) sex with them."
Lawat (Lot) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to them to the dalath (door), and sagar (shut) the dalath (door) achar (other) him.
He amar (spoke), "Please, my ach (brother/kinsman), don't act so wickedly.

See now, I yadai (have) shanayam (two) virgin banawath (daughters). Please yatzaa (go out / come out) me bring them out to you, and you may ishah (make) to them what seems tawab (good / proper function) to you. Only don't ishah (make) anything to these yadaiw (men), because they bawaa (come) come under the tzal (shadow) of my qawarah (roof)."

They amar (spoke), "nagash (stand) halaah (back)!" Then they amar (spoke), "This achad (one) fellow bawaa (come) in to live as a foreigner, and he appoints himself a shapat (judge / judgement). Now will we raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) worse with you, than with them!" They patzar (pressed) hard on the ayash (man / husband) Lawat (Lot), and nagash (drew) near to shabar (break) the dalath (door).
But the anashayam (men) shalach (send) out their yad (hand), and bawaa (come) Lawat (Lot) into the bayath (house) to them, and sagar (shut) the dalath (door).

They nakah (struck) the anashayam (men) who were at the pathach (door) of the bayath (house) with sanawar (blindness), both qatan (small / young / least) and gadawal (very great/important/mighty), so that they laah (wearied) themselves to matzaa (find) the pathach (door).

The anashayam (men) amar (spoke) to Lawat (Lot), "Do you have anybody else here? Sons-in-law, your ban (son), your banath (daughter), and whoever you have in the iyar (city), yatzaa (go out / come out) them out of the maqawam (place):
For we will shachath (destroy) this maqawam (place), because the outcry against them has gadal (grown) great panayam (face) Yahawah that Yahawah has shalach (send) us to shachath (destroy) it."

Lawat (Lot) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and dabar (word / matter) to his sons-in-law, who were pledged to marry his banath (daughter), and amar (spoke), "qawam (rise up) up! Yatzaa (go out / come out) out of this maqawam (place), for Yahawah will shachath (destroy) the iyar (city)." But he seemed to his sons-in-law to be joking.

When the shachar (morning) ilah (go up / offer), then the malaakayam (angels) hurried Lawat (Lot), amar (spoke), "qawam (rise up) up! Laqach (take / seize) your ayashah (woman / wife), and your shanayam (two) banath (daughter) who are here, lest you be sapah (consumed) in the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the iyar (city)."

But he mahah (lingered); and the yachazaqaw (men) grabbed his yad (hand), his ayashah (woman / wife) yad (hand), and his shanayam (two) banath (daughter)' yad (hand), Yahawah being chamalah (merciful) to him; and they yatzaa (go out / come out) him out, and yanach (set) him outside of the iyar (city).

It yatzaa (go out / come out) to pass, when they had taken them out, that he amar (spoke), "malat (escape) for your napash (soul)! Don't nabat (look) achar (other) you, and don't imad (stay) anywhere in the kakar (plain). Malat (escape) to the har (mountain), lest you be sapah (consumed)!"
Lawat (Lot) amar (spoke) to them, "Oh, not so, my Adawan.

See now, your ibad (servant) matzaa (has) found favor in your iyan (eye), and you have gadal (magnified) your loving chasad (grace), which you have shown to me in chayah (saving) my napash (soul). I can't malat (escape) to the har (mountain), lest rai (evil) dabaq (overtake) me, and I mawath (death).

See now, this iyar (city) is qarawab (near) to nawas (flee) to, and it is a matzair (little) one. Oh malat (let) me escape there (isn't it a matzair (little) one?), and my napash (soul) will chayah (live)."

He amar (spoke) to him, "hanah (Behold), I have granted your dabar (word / matter) concerning this thing also, that I will not hapak (overthrow) the iyar (city) of which you have dabar (word / matter).
Hurry, malat (escape) there, for I can't ishah (make) anything until you bawaa (come) there." Therefore the sham (name) of the iyar (city) was qaraa (called) Tzair (Zoar).
The shamash (sun) yatzaa (go out / come out) risen on the aratz (Earth/land) when Lawat (Lot) bawaa (come) to Tzair (Zoar).
Then Yahawah matar (rained) on Sadam (Sodom) and on Imarah (Gomorrah) sulfur and ash (fire) from Yahawah out of the sky.
He overthrew al (toward) irayam (cities), all the kakar (plain), all the yashabay (inhabitants) of the irayam (cities), and that which tzamach (grew) on the adamah (ground).
But his ayashah (woman / wife) nabat (looked) back from achar (other) him, and she became a natzayab (pillar) of malach (salt).
Abaraham (Abraham) shakam (got) up early in the baqar (morning) to the maqawam (place) where he had imad (stood) panayam (face) Yahawah.

He shaqap (looked) panayam (face) Sadam (Sodom) and Imarah (Gomorrah), and panayam (face) all the aratz (Earth/land) of the kakar (plain), and raah (see), and saw that the qayatawar (smoke) of the aratz (Earth/land) ilah (go up / offer) up as the qayatawar (smoke) of a kabashan (furnace).

It happened, when Alahayam shachath (destroyed) the iray (cities) of the kakar (plain), that Alahayam zakar (remember) Abaraham (Abraham), and shalach (send) Lawat (Lot) out of the thawak (midst) of the hapakah (overthrow), when he overthrew the iray (cities) in which Lawat (Lot) lived.

Lawat (Lot) ilah (go up / offer) up out of Tzair (Zoar), and lived in the har (mountain), and his shanayam (two) banath (daughter) with him; for he was yaraa (fear / be afraid) to live in Tzair (Zoar). He lived in a mairah (cave) with his shanayam (two) banath (daughter).

The bakayarah (firstborn) amar (spoke) to the younger, "Our ab (father) is zaqan (old), and there is not a ayash (man / husband) in the aratz (Earth/land) to bawaa (come) in to us in the darak (way) of all the aratz (Earth/land).
Yalak (come), nashaqah (lets) make our ab (father) shaqah (drink) yayan (wine), and we will shakab (lie) with him, that we may chayah (preserve) our ab (father) zarai (seed)."

They shaqah (made) their ab (father) shaqah (drink) yayan (wine) that layal (night): and the bakayarah (firstborn) bawaa (come) in, and shakab (lay) with her ab (father). He didn't yadai (know) when she shakab (lay) down, nor when she qawam (rise up).

It came to pass on the next macharath (day), that the bakayarah (firstborn) amar (spoke) to the younger, "Behold, I shakab (lay) last amash (night) with my ab (father). Shaqah (let) us make him drink yayan (wine) again, tonight. You bawaa (come) in, and shakab (lie) with him, that we may chayah (preserve) our ab (father) zarai (seed)."

They shaqah (made) their ab (father) shaqah (drink) yayan (wine) that layal (night) also. The younger went and shakab (lay) with him. He didn't yadai (know) when she shakab (lay) down, nor when she qawam (rise up) up.
Thus shanayam (two) of Lawat (Lot's) banawath (daughters) were with harah (child) by their ab (father).
The bakayarah (firstborn) yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son), and sham (name) him Mawaab (Moab). He is the ab (father) of the Mawaab (Moabites) to this yawam (day).
The younger also yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son), and qaraa (called) his sham (name) Banaimay (Ben Ammi). He is the ab (father) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) to this yawam (day).
Abaraham (Abraham) traveled from there toward the aratz (Earth/land) of the nagab (south), and lived between Qadash (Kadesh) and Shawar (Shur). He lived as a foreigner in Garar (Gerar).

Abaraham (Abraham) amar (spoke) al (toward) Sharah (Sarah) his ayashah (woman / wife), "She is my achawath (sister)." Abayamalak (Abimelech) malak (king) of Garar (Gerar) shalach (send), and laqach (take / seize) Sharah (Sarah).

But Alahayam bawaa (come) to Abayamalak (Abimelech) in a chalawam (dream) of the layal (night), and amar (spoke) to him, "Behold, you are a mawath (death) man, because of the ayashah (woman / wife) whom you have laqach (take / seize). For she is a bail (man's) wife."
Now Abayamalak (Abimelech) had not qarab (come close) near her. He amar (spoke), "Adanay, will you harag (kill) even a tzadayaq (righteous) gaway (heathen / nation)?

Didn't he amar (spoke) me, ‘She is my achawath (sister)?' She, even she herself, amar (spoke), ‘He is my ach (brother/kinsman).' In the tham (integrity) of my labab (heart) and the innocence of my kap (hands) ishah (make) I done this."

Alahayam amar (spoke) to him in the chalawam (dream), "Yes, I yadai (know) that in the tham (integrity) of your labab (heart) you ishah (make) done this, and I also withheld you from chataa (sinning) against me. Therefore I didn't allow you to nagai (touch) her.

Now therefore, shawab (turn back / repent) the ayash (man / husband) ayashah (woman / wife). For he is a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and he will palal (pray) for you, and you will chayah (live). If you don't shawab (turn back / repent) her, yadai (know) for sure that you will mawath (death), you, and all who are yours."

Abayamalak (Abimelech) shakam (rose) early in the baqar (morning), and qaraa (called) all his ibad (servant), and dabar (word / matter) all these things in their azan (ear). The anashayam (men) were very scared.

Then Abayamalak (Abimelech) qaraa (called) Abaraham (Abraham), and amar (spoke) to him, "What ishah (make) you done to us? How have I chataa (sinned) against you, that you bawaa (come) brought on me and on my mamalakah (kingdom) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chataah (sin)? You ishah (make) done maishayam (deeds) to me that ought not to be ishah (make)!"
Abayamalak (Abimelech) amar (spoke) to Abaraham (Abraham), "mah (what) did you see, that you ishah (make) done this thing?"

Abaraham (Abraham) amar (spoke), "Because I amar (spoke), ‘raq (concept: what comes out / spittle) the yaraah (fear) of Alahayam is not in this maqawam (place). They will harag (kill) me for my ayashah (woman / wife) dabar (word / matter).'
Besides, she is amanah (indeed) my achawath (sister), the banath (daughter) of my ab (father), but not the banath (daughter) of my am (mother); and she became my ayashah (woman / wife).

It happened, when Alahayam thaih (caused) me to wander from my ab (father) bayath (house), that I amar (spoke) to her, ‘This is your chasad (grace) which you shall show to me. Everywhere that we bawaa (come), amar (spoke) of me, "He is my ach (brother/kinsman)."'"

Abayamalak (Abimelech) laqach (take / seize) tzaan (sheep) and cattle, male ibadayam (servants) and female shapachath (servants), and nathan (give) them to Abaraham (Abraham), and shawab (turn back / repent) Sharah (Sarah), his ayashah (woman / wife), to him.
Abayamalak (Abimelech) amar (spoke), "Behold, my aratz (Earth/land) is panayam (face) you. Yashab (inhabit/dwell) where it pleases you."

To Sharah (Sarah) he amar (spoke), "Behold, I nathan (give) given your ach (brother/kinsman) a alap (thousand) pieces of kasap (silver). Behold, it is for you a kasawath (covering) of the iyanayam (eyes) to all that are with you. In front of all you are vindicated."
Abaraham (Abraham) palal (prayed) to Alahayam. Alahayam rapaa (healed) Abayamalak (Abimelech), and his ayashah (woman / wife), and his female amah (servants), and they yalad (birth / begot) children.
For Yahawah had itzar (closed) up tight all the racham (womb) of the bayath (house) of Abayamalak (Abimelech), dabar (word / matter) of Sharah (Sarah), Abaraham (Abraham's) ayashah (woman / wife).
Yahawah paqad (visit) Sharah (Sarah) as he had amar (spoke), and Yahawah ishah (make) to Sharah (Sarah) as he had dabar (word / matter).

Sharah (Sarah) harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) Abaraham (Abraham) a ban (son) in his zaqan (old) age, at the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) time of which Alahayam had dabar (word / matter) to him.
Abaraham (Abraham) qaraa (called) his ban (son) who was yalad (birth / begot) to him, whom Sharah (Sarah) yalad (birth / begot) to him, Yatzachaq (Isaac).
Abaraham (Abraham) mawal (circumcised) his ban (son), Yatzachaq (Isaac), when he was shamanah (eight) yamayam (days) ban (son), as Alahayam had tzawah (commanded) him.
Abaraham (Abraham) was one maah (hundred) shanah (years) ban (son) when his ban (son), Yatzachaq (Isaac), was yalad (birth / begot) to him.
Sharah (Sarah) amar (spoke), "Alahayam ishah (make) made me tzachaq (laugh). Everyone who shamai (hearken / hear) will tzachaq (laugh) with me."

She malal (said), "Who would have malal (said) to Abaraham (Abraham), that Sharah (Sarah) would yanaq (nurse) banayam (children)? For I have yalad (birth / begot) him a ban (son) in his zaqan (old) age."
The yalad (birth / begot) gadal (grew), and was weaned. Abaraham (Abraham) ishah (make) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) mashathah (feast) on the yawam (day) that Yatzachaq (Isaac) was weaned.
Sharah (Sarah) raah (see) the ban (son) of Hagar (Hagar) the Matzaray (Egyptian), whom she had yalad (birth / begot) to Abaraham (Abraham), tzachaq (mocking).
Therefore she amar (spoke) to Abaraham (Abraham), "garash (cast) out this handmaid and her ban (son)! For the ban (son) of this handmaid will not be heir with my ban (son), Yatzachaq (Isaac)."
The thing was very grievous in Abaraham (Abraham's) iyan (eye) on account of his ban (son).

Alahayam amar (spoke) to Abaraham (Abraham), "Don't let it be grievous in your iyan (eye) because of the nair (boy), and because of your handmaid. In all that Sharah (Sarah) amar (spoke) to you, shamai (hearken / hear) to her qawal (sound / voice). For from Yatzachaq (Isaac) will your zarai (seed) be qaraa (called).
I will also shawam (place / establish / appoint) a gaway (heathen / nation) of the ban (son) of the handmaid, because he is your zarai (seed)."

Abaraham (Abraham) shakam (rose) up early in the baqar (morning), and laqach (take / seize) lacham (bread) and a chamath (bottle) of mayam (Waters), and nathan (give) it to Hagar (Hagar), shawam (place / establish / appoint) it on her shakam (shoulder); and gave her the yalad (birth / begot), and shalach (send) her away. She departed, and thaih (wandered) in the madabar (wilderness) of Baar-Shabai (Beersheba).
The mayam (Waters) in the chamath (bottle) was kalah (complete / finish), and she shalak (cast) the yalad (birth / begot) under achad (one) of the shayacham (shrubs).

She yalak (went) and yashab (inhabit/dwell) down opposite him, a rachaq (good) way off, about a bow tachah (shot) away. For she amar (spoke), "Don't raah (see) me see the mawath (death) of the yalad (birth / begot)." She yashab (inhabit/dwell) over against him, and nashaa (lift) up her qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept).

Alahayam shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the nair (boy). The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Alahayam qaraa (called) to Hagar (Hagar) out of the sky, and amar (spoke) to her, "What ails you, Hagar (Hagar)? Hagar (Don't) be afraid. For Alahayam has shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the nair (boy) where he is.

Get up, nashaa (lift) up the nair (boy), and chazaq (hold) him in your yad (hand). For I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) him a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) gaway (heathen / nation)."

Alahayam paqach (opened) her iyan (eye), and she raah (see) a baar (well) of mayam (Waters). She yalak (went), malaa (filled) the chamath (bottle) with mayam (Waters), and shaqah (gave) the nair (boy) shaqah (drink).
Alahayam was with the nair (boy), and he gadal (grew). He lived in the madabar (wilderness), and became, as he rabah (grew) up, an archer.
He lived in the madabar (wilderness) of Paaran (Paran). His am (mother) laqach (take / seize) a ayashah (woman / wife) for him out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

It happened at that ith (time), that Abayamalak (Abimelech) and Payakal (Phicol) the shar (prince / ruler) of his tzabaa (troop) amar (spoke) to Abaraham (Abraham), amar (spoke), "Alahayam is with you in all that you ishah (make).

Now, therefore, shabai (swear / take oath) to me here by Alahayam that you will not shaqar (deal) falsely with me, nor with my nayan (son), nor with my nakad (son's) son. But according to the chasad (grace) that I ishah (make) done to you, you shall ishah (make) to me, and to the aratz (Earth/land) in which you have lived as a foreigner."
Abaraham (Abraham) amar (spoke), "I will shabai (swear / take oath)."
Abaraham (Abraham) complained to Abayamalak (Abimelech) awadawath (because) of a mayam (Waters) baar (well), which Abayamalak (Abimelech's) ibaday (servants) had violently gazal (taken) away.
Abayamalak (Abimelech) amar (spoke), "I don't yadai (know) who ishah (make) done this thing. You didn't nagad (tell) me, laa (NOT) did I shamai (hearken / hear) of it, until today."
Abaraham (Abraham) laqach (take / seize) tzaan (sheep) and cattle, and nathan (give) them to Abayamalak (Abimelech). Those two karath (cut) a barayath (covenant).
Abaraham (Abraham) natzab (set) shabai (seven) ewe kabashath (lambs) of the tzaan (flock) by themselves.
Abayamalak (Abimelech) amar (spoke) to Abaraham (Abraham), "What do these shabai (seven) ewe kabashath (lambs) which you have natzab (set) by themselves mean?"
He amar (spoke), "You shall laqach (take / seize) these shabai (seven) ewe kabashath (lambs) from my yad (hand), that it may be a idah (witness) to me, that I have chapar (dug) this baar (well)."
Therefore he qaraa (called) that maqawam (place) Baar-Shabai (Beersheba), because they both shabai (swear / take oath) there.

So they karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) at Baar-Shabai (Beersheba). Abayamalak (Abimelech) qawam (rise up) up with Payakal (Phicol), the shar (prince / ruler) of his tzabaa (troop), and they shawab (turn back / repent) into the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines).
Abraham natai (planted) a tamarisk ashal (tree) in Baar-Shabai (Beersheba), and qaraa (called) there on the sham (name) of Yahawah, the iwalam (forever) Al.
Abaraham (Abraham) lived as a foreigner in the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines) many yamayam (days).
It happened achar (other) these things, that Alahayam tested Abaraham (Abraham), and amar (spoke) to him, "Abaraham (Abraham)!" He amar (spoke), "Here I am."

He amar (spoke), "Now take your ban (son), your only ban (son), whom you ahab (love), even Yatzachaq (Isaac), and go into the aratz (Earth/land) of Mawarayah (Moriah). Ilah (go up / offer) him there for a burnt ilah (offering) on achad (one) of the harayam (mountains) which I will amar (spoke) you of."

Abaraham (Abraham) shakam (rose) early in the baqar (morning), and chabash (saddled) his donkey, and laqach (take / seize) shanayam (two) of his nair (young) men with him, and Yatzachaq (Isaac) his ban (son). He split the itz (wood) for the burnt ilah (offering), and qawam (rise up) up, and yalak (went) to the maqawam (place) of which Alahayam had amar (spoke) him.
On the shalayashay (third) yawam (day) Abaraham (Abraham) nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye), and raah (see) the maqawam (place) rachawaq (far) off.

Abaraham (Abraham) amar (spoke) to his nair (young) men, "Stay here with the donkey. The nair (boy) and I will yalak (go) kah (yonder). We will shachah (worship), and shawab (turn back / repent) back to you."

Abaraham (Abraham) laqach (take / seize) the itz (wood) of the burnt ilah (offering) and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it on Yatzachaq (Isaac) his ban (son). He laqach (take / seize) in his yad (hand) the ash (fire) and the maakalath (knife). They shanayam (two) yalak (went) yachad (together).

Yatzachaq (Isaac) amar (spoke) to Abaraham (Abraham) his ab (father), and amar (spoke), "My ab (father)?" He amar (spoke), "Here I am, my ban (son)." He amar (spoke), "Here is the ash (fire) and the itz (wood), but where is the shah (lamb) for a burnt ilah (offering)?"
Abaraham (Abraham) amar (spoke), "Alahayam will raah (see) himself the shah (lamb) for a burnt ilah (offering), my ban (son)." So they shanayam (two) yalak (went) yachad (together).

They bawaa (come) to the maqawam (place) which Alahayam had amar (spoke) him of. Abaraham (Abraham) banah (build) the mazabach (altar) there, and irak (laid) the itz (wood) in irak (order), iqad (bound) Yatzachaq (Isaac) his ban (son), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) him on the mazabach (altar), on the itz (wood).
Abaraham (Abraham) shalach (send) out his yad (hand), and laqach (take / seize) the maakalath (knife) to shachat (kill) his ban (son).
The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah qaraa (called) to him out of the sky, and amar (spoke), "Abaraham (Abraham), Abaraham (Abraham)!" He amar (spoke), "Here I am."

He amar (spoke), "Don't shalach (send) your yad (hand) on the nair (boy), neither ishah (make) anything to him. For ithah (now / present moment) I yadai (know) that you yaraa (fear) Alahayam, since you have not withheld your yachayad (son), your only ban (son), from me."

Abaraham (Abraham) nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye), and raah (see), and saw that achar (other) him was a ayal (ram) achaz (caught) in the sabak (thicket) by his qaran (horn). Abaraham (Abraham) yalak (went) and laqach (take / seize) the ayal (ram), and ilah (go up / offer) him up for a burnt ilah (offering) thachath (under) of his ban (son).
Abaraham (Abraham) qaraa (called) the sham (name) of that maqawam (place) Yahawah Will Provide. As it is amar (spoke) to this yawam (day), "On Yahawah har (mountain), it will be raah (see)."
The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah qaraa (called) to Abaraham (Abraham) a shanay (second) time out of the sky,

And amar (spoke), "I have shabai (swear / take oath) by myself, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, yain (because) you ishah (make) done this thing, and have not withheld your ban (son), your only yachayad (son),

That I will barak (blessed) you barak (blessed), and I will rabah (multiply) your zarai (seed) greatly like the kawakabay (stars) of the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and like the chawal (sand) which is on the shapah (seashore). Your zarai (seed) will yarash (possess) the shair (gate) of his ayab (enemy).
In your zarai (seed) will all the gawayay (nations) of the aratz (Earth/land) be barak (blessed), ashar (who/that) you have shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice)."

So Abaraham (Abraham) shawab (turn back / repent) to his nair (young) men, and they qawam (rise up) up and yalak (went) yachad (together) to Baar-Shabai (Beersheba). Abaraham (Abraham) lived at Beersheba.

It happened achar (other) these things, that it was nagad (told) Abaraham (Abraham), amar (spoke), "Behold, Malakah (Milcah), she also has yalad (birth / begot) banayam (children) to your ach (brother/kinsman) Nachawar (Nahor):
Iwatz (Uz) his bakawar (firstborn), Bawaz (Buz) his ach (brother/kinsman), Qamawaal (Kemuel) the ab (father) of Aram (Aram),
Kashad (Chesed), Chazaw (Hazo), Paladash (Pildash), Yadalap (Jidlaph), and Bathawaal (Bethuel)."

Bathawaal (Bethuel) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Rabaqah (Rebekah). These shamanah (eight) Malakah (Milcah) yalad (birth / begot) to Nachawar (Nahor), Abaraham (Abraham's) ach (brother/kinsman).
His payalagash (concubine), whose sham (name) was Raawamah (Reumah), also yalad (birth / begot) Tabach (Tebah), Gacham (Gaham), Thachash (Tahash), and Maikah (Maacah).
Sharah (Sarah) chay (life) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) twenty-seven shanayam (years). This was the length of Sharah (Sarah's) chay (life).

Sharah (Sarah) mawath (death) in Qarayathaarabai (Kiriath) Arba (the same is Chabarawan (Hebron)), in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan). Abaraham (Abraham) bawaa (come) to sapad (mourn) for Sharah (Sarah), and to bakah (weep) for her.
Abaraham (Abraham) qawam (rise up) up from panayam (face) his mawath (death), and dabar (word / matter) to the banay (children) of Chath (Heth), amar (spoke),

"I am a gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) and a thawashab (foreigner) living with you. Nathan (give) me a achazah (possession) of a burying-place with you, that I may qabar (bury) my mawath (death) out of my panayam (face)."
The banay (children) of Chath (Heth) inah (answer / respond) Abaraham (Abraham), amar (spoke) to him,

"Shamai (hearken / hear) us, my Adawan. You are a nashayaa (prince) of Alahayam thawak (midst) us. Qabar (bury) your mawath (death) in the best of our tombs. Laa (NOT) of us will kalaa (withhold) from you his tomb. Qabar (bury) your mawath (death)."
Abaraham (Abraham) qawam (rise up) up, and shachah (bowed) himself to the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land), even to the banay (children) of Chath (Heth).

He dabar (word / matter) with them, amar (spoke), "If it be your napash (soul) that I should qabar (bury) my mawath (death) out of my panayam (face), shamai (hearken / hear) me, and pagai (entreat) for me to Iparawan (Ephron) the ban (son) of Tzachar (Zohar),

That he may nathan (give) me the mairah (cave) of Makapalah (Machpelah), which he has, which is in the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of his shadah (field). For the malaa (full) kasap (price) nathan (give) him give it to me thawak (midst) you for a achazah (possession) of a burying-place."

Now Iparawan (Ephron) was sitting in the thawak (midst) of the banay (children) of Chath (Heth). Iparawan (Ephron) the Chathay (Hittite) inah (answer / respond) Abaraham (Abraham) in the azan (ear) of the banay (children) of Chath (Heth), even of all who bawaa (come) in at the shair (gate) of his iyar (city), amar (spoke),

"No, my Adawan, shamai (hearken / hear) me. I give you the shadah (field), and I give you the mairah (cave) that is in it. In the iyan (eye) of the banay (children) of my im (nation / people) I nathan (give) it to you. Qabar (bury) your mawath (death)."
Abaraham (Abraham) shachah (bowed) himself down panayam (face) the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land).

He dabar (word / matter) to Iparawan (Ephron) in the azan (ear) of the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land), amar (spoke), "But if you will, please shamai (hearken / hear) me. I will nathan (give) the kasap (price) of the shadah (field). Laqach (take / seize) it from me, and I will qabar (bury) my mawath (death) there."
Iparawan (Ephron) inah (answer / respond) Abaraham (Abraham), amar (spoke) to him,

"My Adawan, shamai (hearken / hear) to me. What is a piece of aratz (Earth/land) worth arabai (four) maah (hundred) shaqal (shekels) of kasap (silver) bayan (between) me and you? Therefore qabar (bury) your mawath (death)."

Abaraham (Abraham) shamai (hearken / hear) to Iparawan (Ephron). Abaraham (Abraham) shaqal (weighed) to Iparawan (Ephron) the kasap (silver) which he had dabar (word / matter) in the azan (ear) of the banay (children) of Chath (Heth), arabai (four) maah (hundred) shaqal (shekels) of kasap (silver), according to the ibar (pass over/through) sachar (merchants)' standard.

So the shadah (field) of Iparawan (Ephron), which was in Makapalah (Machpelah), which panayam (face) before Mamaraa (Mamre), the shadah (field), the mairah (cave) which was in it, and all the itz (trees) that were in the shadah (field), that were in all of its gabawal (border/boundary), were deeded
To Abaraham (Abraham) for a maqanah (possession) in the iyan (eye) of the banay (children) of Chath (Heth), before all who bawaa (come) in at the shair (gate) of his iyar (city).

Achar (other) kan (for sure), Abaraham (Abraham) qabar (bury) Sharah (Sarah) his ayashah (woman / wife) in the mairah (cave) of the shadah (field) of Makapalah (Machpelah) panayam (face) Mamaraa (Mamre) (that is, Chabarawan (Hebron)), in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan).

The shadah (field), and the mairah (cave) that is in it, were deeded to Abaraham (Abraham) for a achazah (possession) of a qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) place by the banay (children) of Chath (Heth).
Abaraham (Abraham) was zaqan (old), and well bawaa (come) in yawam (day). Yahawah had barak (blessed) Abaraham (Abraham) in all things.

Abaraham (Abraham) amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), the zaqan (elder) of his bayath (house), who mashal (rule/have dominion) over all that he had, "Please shawam (place / establish / appoint) your yad (hand) under my yarak (thigh).

I will make you shabai (swear / take oath) by Yahawah, the Alahayam of shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) and the Alahayam of the aratz (Earth/land), that you shall not laqach (take / seize) a ayashah (woman / wife) for my ban (son) of the banawath (daughters) of the Kanainay (Canaanites), qarab (among / near) whom I live.
But you shall yalak (go) to my aratz (Earth/land), and to my relatives, and laqach (take / seize) a ayashah (woman / wife) for my ban (son) Yatzachaq (Isaac)."

The ibad (servant) amar (spoke) to him, "What if the ayashah (woman / wife) isn't abah (be willing / desire) to yalak (follow) me to this aratz (Earth/land)? Must I shawab (turn back / repent) your ban (son) again to the aratz (Earth/land) you yatzaa (go out / come out) from?"
Abaraham (Abraham) amar (spoke) to him, "Beware that you don't shawab (turn back / repent) my ban (son) there again.

Yahawah, the Alahayam of shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), who laqach (take / seize) me from my ab (father) bayath (house), and from the aratz (Earth/land) of my birth, who dabar (word / matter) to me, and who shabai (swear / take oath) to me, amar (spoke), ‘I will nathan (give) this aratz (Earth/land) to your zarai (seed).' He will shalach (send) his malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) panayam (face) you, and you shall laqach (take / seize) a ayashah (woman / wife) for my ban (son) from there.

If the ayashah (woman / wife) isn't abah (be willing / desire) to yalak (follow) you, then you shall be naqah (clean/innocent) from this my shabawaih (oath). Only you shall not shawab (turn back / repent) my ban (son) there again."

The ibad (servant) shawam (place / establish / appoint) his yad (hand) under the yarak (thigh) of Abaraham (Abraham) his adawan (master / lord), and shabai (swear / take oath) to him il (over) zah (this / that / these) dabar (word / matter).

The ibad (servant) laqach (take / seize) ishar (ten) gamalayam (camels), of his adawan (master / lord) gamalayam (camels), and departed, having a variety of tawab (good / proper function) things of his adawan (master / lord) with him. He qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) to Aramanaharayam (Mesopotamia), to the iyar (city) of Nachawar (Nahor).

He made the gamalayam (camels) barak (blessed) down outside the iyar (city) by the baar (well) of mayam (Waters) at the ith (time) of irab (evening), the ith (time) that women yatzaa (go out / come out) out to draw shaab (water).

He amar (spoke), "Yahawah, the Alahayam of my adawan (master / lord) Abaraham (Abraham), panayam (face) give me success this yawam (day), and show chasad (grace) to my adawan (master / lord) Abaraham (Abraham).
Behold, I am natzab (standing) by the spring of mayam (Waters). The banawath (daughters) of the anashay (men) of the iyar (city) are yatzaa (go out / come out) out to shaab (draw) mayam (Waters).

Let it happen, that the nairah (young) lady to whom I will amar (spoke), ‘Please natah (let) down your kad (pitcher), that I may shathah (drinks),' and she will amar (spoke), ‘shathah (drinks), and I will also shaqah (give) your gamal (camels) a drink,'—let her be the one you have yakach (appointed) for your ibad (servant) Yatzachaq (Isaac). By this I yadai (will) know that you ishah (make) shown chasad (grace) to my adawan (master / lord)."

It happened, before he kalah (complete / finish) finished dabar (word / matter), that behold, Rabaqah (Rebekah) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, who was yalad (birth / begot) to Bathawaal (Bethuel) the ban (son) of Malakah (Milcah), the ayashah (woman / wife) of Nachawar (Nahor), Abaraham (Abraham's) ach (brother/kinsman), with her kad (pitcher) on her shakam (shoulder).

The nairah (young) lady was very tawab (good / proper function) to maraah (look) at, a bathawalah (virgin), neither had any ayash (man / husband) yadai (known) her. She yarad (went) down to the spring, malaa (filled) her kad (pitcher), and ilah (go up / offer) up.
The ibad (servant) rawatz (ran) to qaraah (meet) her, and amar (spoke), "Please give me a gamaa (drink), a mait (little) mayam (Waters) from your kad (pitcher)."
She amar (spoke), "shathah (drinks), my Adawan." She hurried, and yarad (let) down her kad (pitcher) on her yad (hand), and shaqah (gave) him drink.
When she kalah (complete / finish) done shaqah (giving) him drink, she amar (spoke), "I will also shaab (draw) for your gamal (camels), until they kalah (complete / finish) done shathah (drinks)."
She hurried, and irah (emptied) her kad (pitcher) into the shaqath (trough), and rawatz (ran) again to the baar (well) to shaab (draw), and shaab (drew) for all his gamal (camels).
The ayash (man / husband) looked steadfastly at her, remaining charash (silent), to yadai (know) whether Yahawah had tzalach (made) his darak (journey) prosperous or not.

It happened, as the gamalayam (camels) kalah (complete / finish) done shathah (drinks), that the ayash (man / husband) laqach (take / seize) a zahab (gold) ring of baqai (half) a shekel mashaqal (weight), and shanayam (two) tzamayadayam (bracelets) for her yad (hand) of ishar (ten) shekels mashaqal (weight) of zahab (gold),
And amar (spoke), "Whose banath (daughter) are you? Please nagad (tell) me. Is there maqawam (place) in your ab (father) bayath (house) for us to lawan (lodge) in?"
She amar (spoke) to him, "I am the banath (daughter) of Bathawaal (Bethuel) the ban (son) of Malakah (Milcah), whom she yalad (birth / begot) to Nachawar (Nahor)."
She amar (spoke) moreover to him, "We have gam (indeed / moreover) thaban (straw) and masapawaa (provender) rab (enough), and maqawam (place) to lawan (lodge) in."
The ayash (man / husband) bowed his qadad (head), and shachah (worshiped) Yahawah.

He amar (spoke), "barak (blessed) be Yahawah, the Alahayam of my adawan (master / lord) Abaraham (Abraham), who has not forsaken his loving chasad (grace) and his amath (truth) toward my adawan (master / lord). As for me, Yahawah has nachah (led) me in the darak (way) to the bayath (house) of my adawan (master / lord) relatives."
The nairah (young) lady rawatz (ran), and nagad (told) her am (mother) bayath (house) about these dabarayam (words).
Rabaqah (Rebekah) had a ach (brother/kinsman), and his sham (name) was Laban (Laban). Laban (Laban) rawatz (ran) out to the ayash (man / husband), to the spring.

It happened, when he raah (see) the ring, and the tzamadayam (bracelets) on his achawath (sister's) yaday (hands), and when he shamai (hearken / hear) the dabaray (words) of Rabaqah (Rebekah) his achawath (sister), amar (spoke), "kah (this) is what the ayash (man / husband) dabar (word / matter) to me," that he bawaa (come) to the ayash (man / husband). Behold, he was imad (standing) by the gamalayam (camels) at the spring.
He amar (spoke), "bawaa (come) in, you barak (blessed) of Yahawah. Why do you imad (stand) outside? For I have panah (turn) the bayath (house), and maqawam (place) for the gamalayam (camels)."

The ayash (man / husband) bawaa (come) into the bayath (house), and he unloaded the gamalayam (camels). He nathan (give) thaban (straw) and masapawaa (provender) for the gamalayam (camels), and mayam (Waters) to rachatz (wash) his ragalay (feet) and the ragalay (feet) of the anashayam (men) who were with him.
Food was set panayam (face) him to akal (eat), but he amar (spoke), "I will not akal (eat) until I have dabar (word / matter) my dabar (word / matter)." He amar (spoke), "dabar (word / matter) on."
He amar (spoke), "I am Abaraham (Abraham's) ibad (servant).

Yahawah has barak (blessed) my adawan (master / lord) maad (greatly). He has become gadal (great). He nathan (give) given him tzaan (flocks) and baqar (morning), kasap (silver) and zahab (gold), male ibadam (servants) and female shapachath (servants), and gamalayam (camels) and donkeys.

Sharah (Sarah), my adawan (master / lord) ayashah (woman / wife), yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son) to my adawan (master / lord) when she was zaqanah (old). He nathan (give) given all that he has to him.

My adawan (master / lord) made me shabai (swear / take oath), amar (spoke), ‘You shall not laqach (take / seize) a ayashah (woman / wife) for my ban (son) of the banawath (daughters) of the Kanainay (Canaanites), in whose aratz (Earth/land) I live,
But you shall yalak (go) to my ab (father) bayath (house), and to my relatives, and laqach (take / seize) a ayashah (woman / wife) for my ban (son).'
I asked my adawan (master / lord), ‘What if the ayashah (woman / wife) will not yalak (follow) me?'

He amar (spoke) to me, ‘Yahawah, panayam (face) whom I halak (move), will shalach (send) his malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) with you, and tzalach (prosper) your darak (way). You shall laqach (take / seize) a ayashah (woman / wife) for my ban (son) of my relatives, and of my ab (father) bayath (house).

Then will you be naqah (clean/innocent) from my alah (curse / oath), when you bawaa (come) to my relatives. If they don't nathan (give) her to you, you shall be naqay (clear) from my alah (curse / oath).'

I bawaa (come) this yawam (day) to the spring, and amar (spoke), ‘Yahawah, the Alahayam of my adawan (master / lord) Abaraham (Abraham), if now you yash (do) tzalach (prosper) my darak (way) which I halak (move)—

Behold, I am natzab (standing) by this spring of mayam (Waters). Let it happen, that the maiden who yatzaa (go out / come out) out to shaab (draw), to whom I will amar (spoke), "Please shaqah (give) me a mait (little) mayam (Waters) from your kad (pitcher) to shaqah (drink),"
And she will tell me, "shathah (drinks), and I will also shaab (draw) for your camels,"—let her be the ayashah (woman / wife) whom Yahawah has appointed for my adawan (master / lord) ban (son).'

Before I kalah (complete / finish) finished dabar (word / matter) in my lab (heart), behold, Rabaqah (Rebekah) yatzaa (go out / come out) out with her kad (pitcher) on her shakam (shoulder). She yarad (went) down to the spring, and shaab (drew). I amar (spoke) to her, ‘Please shaqah (let) me drink.'

She hurried and yarad (let) down her kad (pitcher) from her shoulder, and amar (spoke), ‘shathah (drinks), and I will also shaqah (give) your gamalayam (camels) a shaqah (drink).' So I shathah (drinks), and she also shaqah (gave) the gamalayam (camels) a shaqah (drink).

I shaal (asked) her, and amar (spoke), ‘Whose banath (daughter) are you?' She amar (spoke), ‘The banath (daughter) of Bathawaal (Bethuel), Nachawar (Nahor's) ban (son), whom Malakah (Milcah) yalad (birth / begot) to him.' I shawam (place / establish / appoint) the ring on her ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and the tzamayadayam (bracelets) on her yad (hand).

I bowed my qadad (head), and shachah (worshiped) Yahawah, and barak (blessed) Yahawah, the Alahayam of my adawan (master / lord) Abaraham (Abraham), who had nachah (led) me in the amath (truth) darak (way) to laqach (take / seize) my adawan (master / lord) ach (brother/kinsman) banath (daughter) for his ban (son).

Now if you yash (will) ishah (make) chasad (grace) and truly with my adawan (master / lord), nagad (tell) me. If not, nagad (tell) me, that I may panah (turn) to the right yamayan (right hand), or to the shamaawal (left hand)."

Then Laban (Laban) and Bathawaal (Bethuel) inah (answer / respond), "The thing yatzaa (go out / come out) from Yahawah. We can't dabar (word / matter) to you rai (bad) or tawab (good / proper function).

Behold, Rabaqah (Rebekah) is panayam (face) you. Laqach (take / seize) her, and yalak (go), and let her be your adawan (master / lord) ban (son) ayashah (woman / wife), as Yahawah has dabar (word / matter)."
It happened that when Abaraham (Abraham's) ibad (servant) shamai (hearken / hear) their dabar (word / matter), he shachah (bowed) himself down to the aratz (Earth/land) to Yahawah.

The ibad (servant) yatzaa (go out / come out) out kalay (jewels) of kasap (silver), and kalay (jewels) of zahab (gold), and bagad (clothing), and nathan (give) them to Rabaqah (Rebekah). He also nathan (give) magadanah (precious) things to her ach (brother/kinsman) and her am (mother).

They akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), he and the anashayam (men) who were with him, and stayed all lawan (night). They qawam (rise up) up in the baqar (morning), and he amar (spoke), "shalach (send) me away to my adawan (master / lord)."
Her ach (brother/kinsman) and her am (mother) amar (spoke), "Let the nairah (young) lady stay with us a few yamayam (days), at aw (or) ishawar (ten). Achar (other) that she will yalak (go)."
He amar (spoke) to them, "Don't achar (other) me, since Yahawah has tzalach (prospered) my darak (way). Shalach (send) me away that I may yalak (go) to my adawan (master / lord)."
They amar (spoke), "We will qaraa (called) the nairah (young) lady, and shaal (ask) her."
They qaraa (called) Rabaqah (Rebekah), and amar (spoke) to her, "Will you yalak (go) with this ayash (man / husband)?" She amar (spoke), "I will yalak (go)."
They shalach (send) away Rabaqah (Rebekah), their achawath (sister), with her yanaq (nurse), Abaraham (Abraham's) ibad (servant), and his ayash (man / husband).

They barak (blessed) Rabaqah (Rebekah), and amar (spoke) to her, "Our achawath (sister), may you be the mother of alapay (thousands) of rababah (ten) thousands, and let your zarai (seed) yarash (possess) the shair (gate) of those who shanaa (hate) them."

Rabaqah (Rebekah) qawam (rise up) with her ladies. They rakab (rode) on the gamalayam (camels), and yalak (followed) the ayash (man / husband). The ibad (servant) laqach (take / seize) Rabaqah (Rebekah), and went his yalak (way).
Yatzachaq (Isaac) bawaa (come) from the bawaa (come) of Baaralachayaraay (Beer Lahai) Roi, for he lived in the aratz (Earth/land) of the nagab (south).

Yatzachaq (Isaac) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to shawach (meditate) in the shadah (field) at the irab (evening). He nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye), and raah (see), and, behold, there were gamalayam (camels) bawaa (come).
Rabaqah (Rebekah) nashaa (lift) up her iyan (eye), and when she raah (see) Yatzachaq (Isaac), she dismounted from the gamal (camel).

She amar (spoke) to the ibad (servant), "Who is the ayash (man / husband) who is halak (move) in the shadah (field) to qaraah (meet) us?" The ibad (servant) amar (spoke), "It is my adawan (master / lord)." She laqach (take / seize) her tzaiyap (veil), and kasah (covered) herself.
The ibad (servant) sapar (book) Yatzachaq (Isaac) all the things that he ishah (make) done.

Yatzachaq (Isaac) bawaa (come) her into his am (mother) Sharah (Sarah's) ahal (tent), and laqach (take / seize) Rabaqah (Rebekah), and she became his ayashah (woman / wife). He ahab (love) her. Yatzachaq (Isaac) was nacham (turn away / repent) achar (other) his am (mother) death.
Abaraham (Abraham) laqach (take / seize) another ayashah (woman / wife), and her sham (name) was Qatawarah (Keturah).
She yalad (birth / begot) him Zamaran (Zimran), Yaqashan (Jokshan), Madan (Medan), Madayan (Midian), Yashabaq (Ishbak), and Shawach (Shuah).
Yaqashan (Jokshan) became the father of Shabaa (Sheba), and Dadan (Dedan). The banay (sons) of Dadan (Dedan) were ashawaray (asshurim), Latawasham (Letushim), and Laamayam (Leummim).
The banay (sons) of Madayan (Midian): Iyapah (Ephah), Ipar (Epher), Chanawak (Hanoch), Abayadai (Abida), and Aladaih (Eldaah). All these were the banay (children) of Qatawarah (Keturah).
Abaraham (Abraham) nathan (give) all that he had to Yatzachaq (Isaac),

But to the banay (sons) of Abaraham (Abraham's) payalagashayam (concubines), Abaraham (Abraham) nathan (give) mathanath (gifts). He shalach (send) them away from Yatzachaq (Isaac) his ban (son), while he yet chay (life), eastward, to the qadam (east) aratz (Earth/land).
These are the yamay (days) of the shanay (years) of Abaraham (Abraham's) chay (life) which he chayay (life): one maah (hundred) seventy-five shanay (years).

Abaraham (Abraham) gawai (gave) up the spirit, and mawath (death) in a tawab (good / proper function) shayabah (old age / white hair - due to age) age, an old zaqan (man), and shabai (full) of years, and was asap (gathered) to his im (nation / people).

Yatzachaq (Isaac) and Yashamaial (Ishmael), his ban (son), qabar (bury) him in the mairah (cave) of Makapalah (Machpelah), in the shadah (field) of Iparawan (Ephron), the ban (son) of Tzachar (Zohar) the Chathay (Hittite), which is panayam (face) Mamaraa (Mamre),
The shadah (field) which Abaraham (Abraham) qanah (purchased) of the banay (children) of Chath (Heth). Abaraham (Abraham) was qabar (bury) there with Sharah (Sarah), his ayashah (woman / wife).
It happened achar (other) the mawath (death) of Abaraham (Abraham) that Alahayam barak (blessed) Yatzachaq (Isaac), his ban (son). Yatzachaq (Isaac) lived by Baaralachayaraay (Beer Lahai Roi).

Now this is the history of the thaladath (generations) of Yashamaial (Ishmael), Abaraham (Abraham's) ban (son), whom Hagar (Hagar) the Matzaray (Egyptian), Sharah (Sarah's) handmaid, bore to Abaraham (Abraham).

These are the shamawath (names) of the banay (sons) of Yashamaial (Ishmael), by their shamawath (names), according to the order of their birth: the bakawar (firstborn) of Yashamaial (Ishmael), Nabayawath (Nebaioth), then Qadar (Kedar), Adabaal (Adbeel), Mabasham (Mibsam),
Mashamai (Mishma), Dawamah (Dumah), Mashaa (Massa),
Hadad, Thayamaa (Tema), Yatawar (Jetur), Napayash (Naphish), and Qadamah (Kedemah).

These are the banay (sons) of Yashamaial (Ishmael), and these are their sham (name), by their chatzar (villages), and by their encampments: shanayam (two) nashayaam (princes), according to their amah (nations).

These are the shanay (years) of the chay (life) of Yashamaial (Ishmael): maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) thirty-seven shanay (years). He gawai (gave) up the spirit and mawath (death), and was asap (gathered) to his im (nation / people).
They lived from Chawayalah (Havilah) to Shawar (Shur) that is panayam (face) Matzarayam (Egypt), as you bawaa (come) toward Ashawar (Assyria). He lived opposite all his relatives.
This is the history of the thawaladath (generations) of Yatzachaq (Isaac), Abaraham (Abraham's) ban (son). Abraham became the yalad (birth / begot) of Yatzachaq (Isaac).

Yatzachaq (Isaac) was arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years) ban (son) when he laqach (take / seize) Rabaqah (Rebekah), the banath (daughter) of Bathawaal (Bethuel) the Aramay (Syrian) of Padan (Paddan) Aram, the achawath (sister) of Laban (Laban) the Aramay (Syrian), to be his ayashah (woman / wife).
Yatzachaq (Isaac) entreated Yahawah for his ayashah (woman / wife), because she was iqar (barren). Yahawah was entreated by him, and Rabaqah (Rebekah) his ayashah (woman / wife) harah (conceived).
The banayam (children) ratzatz (struggled) together qarab (among / near) her. She amar (spoke), "If it be so, why do I live?" She yalak (went) to darash (inquire) of Yahawah.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to her, "shanayam (two) gayayam (nations) are in your batan (womb). Shanayam (two) laamayam (peoples) will be parad (separated) from your body. The one laamayam (people) will be amatz (stronger) than the other laamayam (people). The rab (elder) will ibad (servant) the younger."
When her yawam (day) to be yalad (birth / begot) were malaa (fulfilled), behold, there were thawamam (twins) in her batan (womb).
The raashawan (first) yatzaa (go out / come out) out adamanay (red) all over, like a shair (hair) adarath (garment). They sham (name) him Ishaw (Esau).

Achar (other) that, his ach (brother/kinsman) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and his yad (hand) achaz (had) hold on Ishaw (Esau's) iqab (heel). He was sham (name) Yaiqab (Jacob). Yatzachaq (Isaac) was shashayam (sixty) shanah (years) ban (son) when she yalad (birth / begot) them.

The nairayam (boys) gadal (grew). Ishaw (Esau) was a skillful tzayad (hunter), a ayash (man / husband) of the shadah (field). Yaiqab (Jacob) was a quiet ayash (man / husband), living in ahalayam (tents).
Now Yatzachaq (Isaac) ahab (love) Ishaw (Esau), because he pah (ate) his tzayad (venison). Rabaqah (Rebekah) ahab (love) Yaiqab (Jacob).
Yaiqab (Jacob) boiled stew. Ishaw (Esau) bawaa (come) in from the shadah (field), and he was famished.
Ishaw (Esau) amar (spoke) to Yaiqab (Jacob), "Please lait (feed) me with that same adam (red) stew, for I am famished." Therefore his sham (name) was qaraa (called) Adawam (Edom).
Yaiqab (Jacob) amar (spoke), "First, makar (sell) me your bakawarah (birthright)."
Ishaw (Esau) amar (spoke), "Behold, I am halak (move) to mawath (death). What good is the bakawarah (birthright) to me?"
Yaiqab (Jacob) amar (spoke), "shabai (swear / take oath) to me yawam (day)." He shabai (swear / take oath) to him. He makar (sold) his bakawarah (birthright) to Yaiqab (Jacob).

Yaiqab (Jacob) nathan (give) Ishaw (Esau) lacham (bread) and stew of lentils. He akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), qawam (rise up) up, and went his yalak (way). So Ishaw (Esau) bazah (despised) his bakawarah (birthright).

There was a raib (famine) in the aratz (Earth/land), bad (besides) the raashawan (first) raib (famine) that was in the yamay (days) of Abaraham (Abraham). Yatzachaq (Isaac) yalak (went) to Abayamalak (Abimelech) malak (king) of the Palashathay (Philistines), to Garar (Gerar).
Yahawah raah (see) to him, and amar (spoke), "Don't yarad (go) down into Matzarayam (Egypt). Live in the aratz (Earth/land) I will amar (spoke) you about.

Live in this aratz (Earth/land), and I will be with you, and will barak (blessed) you. For to you, and to your zarai (seed), I will nathan (give) all these aratzath (lands), and I will qawam (rise up) the shabawaih (oath) which I shabai (swear / take oath) to Abaraham (Abraham) your ab (father).

I will rabah (multiply) your zarai (seed) as the kawakabay (stars) of the sky, and will nathan (give) to your zarai (seed) all these aratzath (lands). In your zarai (seed) will all the gawayay (nations) of the aratz (Earth/land) be barak (blessed),

Iqab (award / effect after the cause) Abaraham (Abraham) shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice), and shamar (keep/guard) my requirements, my matzawah (commandments), my chaqah (statutes), and my thawarah (instruction)."
Yatzachaq (Isaac) lived in Garar (Gerar).

The anashay (men) of the maqawam (place) shaal (asked) him about his ayashah (woman / wife). He amar (spoke), "She is my achawath (sister)," for he was yaraa (fear / be afraid) to amar (spoke), "My ayashah (woman / wife)," lest, he thought, "the anashay (men) of the maqawam (place) might harag (kill) me for Rabaqah (Rebekah), because she is tawab (good / proper function) to maraah (look) at."

It happened, when he had been there a arak (long) yawam (day), that Abayamalak (Abimelech) malak (king) of the Palashathay (Philistines) shaqap (looked) out at a chalawan (window), and raah (see), and, behold, Yatzachaq (Isaac) was caressing Rabaqah (Rebekah), his ayashah (woman / wife).

Abayamalak (Abimelech) qaraa (called) Yatzachaq (Isaac), and amar (spoke), "Behold, ak (surely) she is your ayashah (woman / wife). Why did you amar (spoke), ‘She is my achawath (sister)?'" Yatzachaq (Isaac) amar (spoke) to him, "Because I amar (spoke), ‘Lest I mawath (death) because of her.'"

Abayamalak (Abimelech) amar (spoke), "What is this you ishah (make) done to us? Achad (one) of the im (nation / people) might easily have shakab (lain) with your ayashah (woman / wife), and you would bawaa (come) brought asham (guilt) on us!"

Abayamalak (Abimelech) tzawah (commanded) all the im (nation / people), amar (spoke), "He who touches this ayash (man / husband) or his ayashah (woman / wife) will mawath (death) be put to mawath (death)."
Yatzachaq (Isaac) zarai (sowed) in that aratz (Earth/land), and reaped in the same shanah (year) one maah (hundred) times what he planted. Yahawah barak (blessed) him.
The ayash (man / husband) gadal (grew) great, and gadal (grew) more and more until he became very gadal (great).
He had maqanah (possessions) of tzaan (flocks), maqanah (possessions) of baqar (morning), and a rab (great) ibadah (household). The Palashathay (Philistines) qanaa (jealous) him.

Now all the baarath (wells) which his ab (father) ibaday (servants) had chapar (dug) in the yamay (days) of Abaraham (Abraham) his ab (father), the Palashathay (Philistines) had satham (stopped), and malaa (filled) with ipar (earth).
Abayamalak (Abimelech) amar (spoke) to Yatzachaq (Isaac), "yalak (go) from us, for you are much itzam (mightier) than we."
Yatzachaq (Isaac) departed from there, chanah (encamped) in the nachal (stream / river) of Garar (Gerar), and lived there.

Yatzachaq (Isaac) chapar (dug) again the baarath (wells) of mayam (Waters), which they had chapar (dug) in the yamay (days) of Abaraham (Abraham) his ab (father). For the Palashathay (Philistines) had satham (stopped) them achar (other) the mawath (death) of Abaraham (Abraham). He qaraa (called) their shamawath (names) after the shamawath (names) by which his ab (father) had qaraa (called) them.
Yatzachaq (Isaac's) ibaday (servants) chapar (dug) in the nachal (stream / river), and matzaa (found) there a baar (well) of chay (life) mayam (Waters).

The herdsmen of Garar (Gerar) argued with Yatzachaq (Isaac's) herdsmen, amar (spoke), "The mayam (Waters) is ours." He qaraa (called) the sham (name) of the baar (well) Ishaq (Esek), because they contended with him.
They chapar (dug) achar (other) baar (well), and they argued over that, also. He qaraa (called) its name Shatanah (Sitnah).

He ithaq (left) that place, and chapar (dug) achar (other) baar (well). They didn't argue over that one. He qaraa (called) it Rachabawath (Rehoboth). He amar (spoke), "For ithah (now / present moment) Yahawah has rachab (made) room for us, and we will be parah (fruitful) in the aratz (Earth/land)."
He ilah (go up / offer) up from there to Baar-Shabai (Beersheba).

Yahawah raah (see) to him the same layal (night), and amar (spoke), "I am the Alahayam of Abaraham (Abraham) your ab (father). Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), for I am with you, and will barak (blessed) you, and rabah (multiply) your zarai (seed) for my ibad (servant) Abaraham (Abraham's) sake."

He banah (build) an mazabach (altar) there, and qaraa (called) on the sham (name) of Yahawah, and natah (pitched) his ahal (tent) there. There Yatzachaq (Isaac's) ibaday (servants) karah (dug) a baar (well).
Then Abayamalak (Abimelech) halak (move) to him from Garar (Gerar), and Achazath (Ahuzzath) his marai (friend), and Payakal (Phicol) the shar (prince / ruler) of his tzabaa (troop).
Yatzachaq (Isaac) amar (spoke) to them, "madawai (for what reason?) Bawaa (come) you come to me, since you shanaa (hate) me, and have shalach (send) me away from you?"

They amar (spoke), "We raah (see) plainly that Yahawah was with you. We amar (spoke), ‘Let there now be an alah (curse / oath) bayan (between) us, even bayan (between) us and you, and let us karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with you,

That you will ishah (make) us no rai (harm), as we have not nagai (touched) you, and as we ishah (make) done to you raq (concept: what comes out / spittle) but tawab (good / proper function), and have shalach (send) you away in shalawam (peace / safety).' You are ithah (now / present moment) the barak (blessed) of Yahawah."
He ishah (make) them a mashathah (feast), and they akal (eat) and shathah (drinks).

They shakam (rose) up some time in the baqar (morning), and shabai (swear / take oath) ayash (man / husband) to ach (brother/kinsman). Yatzachaq (Isaac) shalach (send) them away, and they departed from him in shalawam (peace / safety).

It happened the same yawam (day), that Yatzachaq (Isaac's) ibaday (servants) bawaa (come), and nagad (told) him awadawath (concerning) the baar (well) which they had chapar (dug), and amar (spoke) to him, "We matzaa (have) found mayam (Waters)."
He qaraa (called) it Shibah. Therefore the sham (name) of the iyar (city) is Baar-Shabai (Beersheba) to this yawam (day).

When Ishaw (Esau) was arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years) ban (son), he laqach (take / seize) as ayashah (woman / wife) Yahawadayath (Judith), the banath (daughter) of Baaray (Beeri) the Chathay (Hittite), and Bashamath (Basemath), the banath (daughter) of Ayalawan (Elon) the Chathay (Hittite).
They grieved Yatzachaq (Isaac's) and Rabaqah (Rebekah's) rawach (spirit / wind).

It hayah (came to pass), that when Yatzachaq (Isaac) was zaqan (old), and his iyan (eye) were kahah (dim), so that he could not raah (see), he qaraa (called) Ishaw (Esau) his gadawal (very great/important/mighty) ban (son), and amar (spoke) to him, "My ban (son)?" He amar (spoke) to him, "Here I am."
He amar (spoke), "See now, I am zaqan (old). I don't yadai (know) the yawam (day) of my mawath (death).

Now therefore, please nashaa (lift) your kalay (weapons), your thalay (quiver) and your qashath (bow), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out to the shadah (field), and tzawad (take) me tzayadah (venison).
Ishah (make) me savory food, such as I ahab (love), and bawaa (come) it to me, that I may akal (eat), and that my napash (soul) may barak (blessed) you taram (before) I mawath (death)."

Rabaqah (Rebekah) shamai (hearken / hear) when Yatzachaq (Isaac) dabar (word / matter) to Ishaw (Esau) his ban (son). Ishaw (Esau) yalak (went) to the shadah (field) to tzawad (hunt) for tzayad (venison), and to bawaa (come) it.

Rabaqah (Rebekah) amar (spoke) to Yaiqab (Jacob) her ban (son), amar (spoke), "Behold, I shamai (hearken / hear) your ab (father) dabar (word / matter) to Ishaw (Esau) your ach (brother/kinsman), amar (spoke),
‘Bawaa (come) me tzayad (venison), and ishah (make) me savory food, that I may akal (eat), and barak (blessed) you panayam (face) Yahawah panayam (face) my mawath (death).'
Now therefore, my ban (son), shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice) according to that which I tzawah (command) you.

Yalak (go) now to the tzaan (flock), and laqach (take / seize) me from there shanayam (two) tawab (good / proper function) young izayam (goats). I will ishah (make) them savory food for your ab (father), such as he ahab (love).
You shall bawaa (come) it to your ab (father), that he may akal (eat), so that he may barak (blessed) you panayam (face) his mawath (death)."

Yaiqab (Jacob) amar (spoke) to Rabaqah (Rebekah) his am (mother), "Behold, Ishaw (Esau) my ach (brother/kinsman) is a shaiyar (hairy) ayash (man / husband), and I am a chalaq (smooth) ayash (man / husband).
What if my ab (father) touches me? I will seem to him as a deceiver, and I would bawaa (come) a qalalah (curse) on myself, and not a barakah (blessing)."
His am (mother) amar (spoke) to him, "Let your qalalah (curse) be on me, my ban (son). Only shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice), and yalak (go) laqach (take / seize) them for me."
He yalak (went), and laqach (take / seize) them, and bawaa (come) them to his am (mother). His am (mother) ishah (make) savory food, such as his ab (father) ahab (love).

Rabaqah (Rebekah) laqach (take / seize) the chamadah (good) clothes of Ishaw (Esau), her gadawal (very great/important/mighty) ban (son), which were with her in the bayath (house), and labash (put) them on Yaiqab (Jacob), her younger ban (son).
She labash (put) the irath (skins) of the young izayam (goats) on his yad (hand), and on the chalaqah (smooth) of his tzawaar (neck).
She nathan (give) the savory food and the lacham (bread), which she ishah (make) prepared, into the yad (hand) of her ban (son) Yaiqab (Jacob).
He bawaa (come) to his ab (father), and amar (spoke), "My ab (father)?" He amar (spoke), "Here I am. Who are you, my ban (son)?"

Yaiqab (Jacob) amar (spoke) to his ab (father), "I am Ishaw (Esau) your bakawar (firstborn). I ishah (make) done what you asked me to do. Please qawam (rise up), yashab (inhabit/dwell) and akal (eat) of my tzayad (venison), that your napash (soul) may barak (blessed) me."
Yatzachaq (Isaac) amar (spoke) to his ban (son), "How is it that you matzaa (have) found it so mahar (quickly), my ban (son)?" He amar (spoke), "Because Yahawah your Alahayam gave me success."
Yatzachaq (Isaac) amar (spoke) to Yaiqab (Jacob), "Please nagash (come) near, that I may mawash (feel) you, my ban (son), whether you are really my ban (son) Ishaw (Esau) or not."

Yaiqab (Jacob) nagash (went) near to Yatzachaq (Isaac) his ab (father). He mashash (felt) him, and amar (spoke), "The qawal (sound / voice) is Yaiqab (Jacob's) qawal (sound / voice), but the yadayam (hands) are the yadayam (hands) of Ishaw (Esau)."
He didn't recognize him, because his yaday (hands) were shaiyar (hairy), like his ach (brother/kinsman), Ishaw (Esau's) yaday (hands). So he barak (blessed) him.
He amar (spoke), "Are you really my ban (son) Ishaw (Esau)?" He amar (spoke), "I am."

He amar (spoke), "nagash (bring) it near to me, and I will akal (eat) of my ban (son) tzayad (venison), that my napash (soul) may barak (blessed) you." He nagash (brought) it near to him, and he akal (eat). He bawaa (come) him yayan (wine), and he shathah (drinks).
His ab (father) Yatzachaq (Isaac) amar (spoke) to him, "nagash (come) near now, and nashaq (kiss) me, my ban (son)."

He nagash (came) near, and nashaq (kissed) him. He rawach (spirit / wind) the rayach (smell) of his bagad (clothing), and barak (blessed) him, and amar (spoke), "raah (see), the rayach (smell) of my ban (son) is as the rayach (smell) of a shadah (field) which Yahawah has barak (blessed).
Alahayam nathan (give) you of the tal (dew) of the sky, of the fatness of the aratz (Earth/land), and rab (plenty) of grain and new thayarawash (wine).

Let imayam (peoples) ibad (servant) you, and laamayam (nations) shachah (bow) down to you. Be Adawan over your ach (brother/kinsman). Let your am (mother) banay (sons) shachah (bow) down to you. Arar (cursed) be everyone who arar (curses) you. Barak (blessed) be everyone who blesses you."

It happened, as soon as Yatzachaq (Isaac) kalah (complete / finish) made an end of barak (blessed) Yaiqab (Jacob), and Yaiqab (Jacob) had just yatzaa (go out / come out) out from the panayam (face) of Yatzachaq (Isaac) his ab (father), that Ishaw (Esau) his ach (brother/kinsman) bawaa (come) in from his tzayad (hunting).

He also ishah (make) savory food, and bawaa (come) it to his ab (father). He amar (spoke) to his ab (father), "Let my ab (father) qawam (rise up), and akal (eat) of his ban (son) tzayad (venison), that your napash (soul) may barak (blessed) me."
Yatzachaq (Isaac) his ab (father) amar (spoke) to him, "Who are you?" He amar (spoke), "I am your ban (son), your bakawar (firstborn), Ishaw (Esau)."

Yatzachaq (Isaac) charad (trembled) violently, and amar (spoke), "Who, then, is he who has tzawad (taken) tzayad (venison), and bawaa (come) it me, and I have akal (eat) of all before you bawaa (come), and have barak (blessed) him? Yes, he will be barak (blessed)."

When Ishaw (Esau) shamai (hearken / hear) the dabaray (words) of his ab (father), he tzaiq (cried) with an maad (exceeding) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and mar (bitter) tzaiqah (cry), and amar (spoke) to his ab (father), "barak (blessed) me, even me also, my ab (father)."
He amar (spoke), "Your ach (brother/kinsman) bawaa (come) with maramah (deceit), and has laqach (take / seize) away your barakah (blessing)."

He amar (spoke), "Isn't he kay (surely) qaraa (called) Yaiqab (Jacob)? For he has iqab (supplanted) me these paim (two) times. He laqach (take / seize) away my bakawarah (birthright). See, now he has laqach (take / seize) away my barakah (blessing)." He amar (spoke), "Haven't you atzal (reserved) a barakah (blessing) for me?"

Yatzachaq (Isaac) inah (answer / respond) Ishaw (Esau), "Behold, I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) him your Adawan, and all his ach (brother/kinsman) nathan (give) I given to him for ibadayam (servants). With grain and new thayarawash (wine) have I samak (sustained) him. What then will I ishah (make) for you, my ban (son)?"

Ishaw (Esau) amar (spoke) to his ab (father), "Have you but achad (one) barakah (blessing), my ab (father)? Barak (blessed) me, even me also, my ab (father)." Ishaw (Esau) nashaa (lift) up his qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept).
Yatzachaq (Isaac) his ab (father) inah (answer / respond) him, "Behold, of the fatness of the aratz (Earth/land) will be your mawashab (dwelling), and of the tal (dew) of the sky from il (over).

By your charab (sword) will you chayah (live), and you will ibad (servant) your ach (brother/kinsman). It will happen, when you will paraq (break) loose, that you shall shake his il (over) from off your tzawaar (neck)."

Ishaw (Esau) shatam (hated) Yaiqab (Jacob) il (over) of the barakah (blessing) with which his ab (father) barak (blessed) him. Ishaw (Esau) amar (spoke) in his lab (heart), "The yamay (days) of abal (mourning) for my ab (father) are at qarab (come close). Then I will harag (kill) my ach (brother/kinsman) Yaiqab (Jacob)."

The dabaray (words) of Ishaw (Esau), her gadawal (very great/important/mighty) ban (son), were nagad (told) to Rabaqah (Rebekah). She shalach (send) and qaraa (called) Yaiqab (Jacob), her younger ban (son), and amar (spoke) to him, "Behold, your ach (brother/kinsman) Ishaw (Esau) nacham (turn away / repent) himself about you by planning to harag (kill) you.
Now therefore, my ban (son), shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice). Qawam (rise up), barach (flee) to Laban (Laban), my ach (brother/kinsman), in Charan (Haran).
Stay with him a achad (one) yamayam (days), ashar (who/that) your ach (brother/kinsman) fury shawab (turn back / repent) away;

Until your ach (brother/kinsman) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) shawab (turn back / repent) away from you, and he shakach (forgets) what you ishah (make) done to him. Then I will shalach (send), and laqach (take / seize) you from there. Mah (why) should I be shakal (bereaved) of you shanayam (two) in achad (one) yawam (day)?"

Rabaqah (Rebekah) amar (spoke) to Yatzachaq (Isaac), "I am qawatz (weary) of my chay (life) panayam (face) of the banawath (daughters) of Chath (Heth). If Yaiqab (Jacob) laqach (take / seize) a ayashah (woman / wife) of the banawath (daughters) of Chath (Heth), such as these, of the banawath (daughters) of the aratz (Earth/land), what mah (good) will my chay (life) do me?"

Yatzachaq (Isaac) qaraa (called) Yaiqab (Jacob), barak (blessed) him, and tzawah (commanded) him, "You shall not laqach (take / seize) a ayashah (woman / wife) of the banawath (daughters) of Kanain (Canaan).

Qawam (rise up), yalak (go) to Padan (Paddan) Aram, to the bayath (house) of Bathawaal (Bethuel) your am (mother) ab (father). Laqach (take / seize) a ayashah (woman / wife) from there from the banawath (daughters) of Laban (Laban), your am (mother) ach (brother/kinsman).
