May Al Shaday barak (blessed) you, and parah (make) you fruitful, and rabah (multiply) you, that you may be a qahal (company) of imayam (peoples),

And nathan (give) you the barakah (blessing) of Abaraham (Abraham), to you, and to your zarai (seed) with you, that you may yarash (inherit) the aratz (Earth/land) magawar (where) you travel, which Alahayam nathan (give) to Abaraham (Abraham)."

Yatzachaq (Isaac) sent Yaiqab (Jacob) shalach (send). He yalak (went) to Padan (Paddan) Aram to Laban (Laban), ban (son) of Bathawaal (Bethuel) the Aramay (Syrian), Rabaqah (Rebekah's) ach (brother/kinsman), Yaiqab (Jacob's) and Ishaw (Esau's) am (mother).

Now Ishaw (Esau) raah (see) that Yatzachaq (Isaac) had barak (blessed) Yaiqab (Jacob) and shalach (send) him away to Padan (Paddan) Aram, to laqach (take / seize) him a ayashah (woman / wife) from there, and that as he barak (blessed) him he gave him a tzawah (command), amar (spoke), "You shall not laqach (take / seize) a ayashah (woman / wife) of the banawath (daughters) of Kanain (Canaan),"
And that Yaiqab (Jacob) shamai (hearken / hear) his ab (father) and his am (mother), and was yalak (gone) to Paddan Padan (Aram).
Ishaw (Esau) raah (see) that the banawath (daughters) of Kanain (Canaan) didn't iyan (eye) Yatzachaq (Isaac), his ab (father).

Ishaw (Esau) yalak (went) to Yashamaial (Ishmael), and laqach (take / seize), besides the wives that he had, Machalath (Mahalath) the banath (daughter) of Yashamaial (Ishmael), Abaraham (Abraham's) ban (son), the achawath (sister) of Nabayawath (Nebaioth), to be his ayashah (woman / wife).
Yaiqab (Jacob) yalak (went) out from Beersheba, and yalak (went) toward Charan (Haran).

He pagai (came) to a certain maqawam (place), and stayed there all lawan (night), because the shamash (sun) bawaa (come) set. He laqach (take / seize) one of the abanay (stones) of the maqawam (place), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it under his maraashah (head), and shakab (lay) down in that maqawam (place) to sleep.

He chalam (dream). Behold, a stairway natzab (set) upon the aratz (Earth/land), and its top nagai (reached) to shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens). Behold, the malaakay (angels) of Alahayam ilah (go up / offer) and descending on it.

Behold, Yahawah natzab (stood) above it, and amar (spoke), "I am Yahawah, the Alahayam of Abaraham (Abraham) your ab (father), and the Alahayam of Yatzachaq (Isaac). The aratz (Earth/land) whereon you shakab (lie), to you will I nathan (give) it, and to your zarai (seed).

Your zarai (seed) will be as the ipar (dust) of the aratz (Earth/land), and you will spread paratz (abroad) to the yam (sea/waters), and to the qadam (east), and to the tzapawan (north), and to the nagab (south). In you and in your zarai (seed) will all the mashapachath (families) of the adamah (earth) be barak (blessed).

Behold, I am with you, and will shamar (keep/guard) you, wherever you yalak (go), and will shawab (turn back / repent) you again into this adamah (land). For I will not izab (leave) you, ashar (who/that) I ishah (make) done that which I have dabar (word / matter) of to you."
Yaiqab (Jacob) awakened out of his shanah (sleep), and he amar (spoke), "akan (surely) Yahawah is in this maqawam (place), and I didn't yadai (know) it."

He was yaraa (fear / be afraid), and amar (spoke), "How yaraa (fear / be afraid) is this maqawam (place)! This is none other than Alahayam bayath (house), and this is the shair (gate) of shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens)."

Yaiqab (Jacob) shakam (rose) up early in the baqar (morning), and laqach (take / seize) the aban (stone) that he had shawam (place / establish / appoint) under his maraashah (head), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it up for a matzabah (pillar), and yatzaq (poured) shaman (oil) on its raash (head).
He qaraa (called) the sham (name) of that maqawam (place) Bayath-Al (Bethel), but the sham (name) of the iyar (city) was Lawaz (Luz) at the raashawan (first).

Yaiqab (Jacob) nadar (make vow) a nadar (vow), amar (spoke), "If Alahayam will be with me, and will shamar (keep/guard) me in this darak (way) that I halak (move), and will nathan (give) me lacham (bread) to akal (eat), and labash (clothing) to put on,
So that I shawab (turn back / repent) again to my ab (father) bayath (house) in shalawam (peace / safety), and Yahawah will be my Alahayam,

Then this aban (stone), which I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) up for a matzabah (pillar), will be Alahayam bayath (house). Of all that you will nathan (give) me I will ishar (surely) give the ishar (tenth) to you."
Then Yaiqab (Jacob) nashaa (lift) on his ragal (feet / foot), and yalak (came) to the aratz (Earth/land) of the banay (children) of the qadam (east).

He raah (see), and behold, a baar (well) in the shadah (field), and, behold, shalawash (three) idaray (flocks) of tzaan (sheep) lying there by it. For out of that baar (well) they shaqah (watered) the idaray (flocks). The aban (stone) on the baar (well's) pah (mouth) was large.

There all the idarayam (flocks) were asap (gathered). They galal (rolled) the aban (stone) from the baar (well's) pah (mouth), and shaqah (watered) the tzaan (sheep), and shawab (turn back / repent) the aban (stone) again on the baar (well's) pah (mouth) in its maqawam (place).
Yaiqab (Jacob) amar (spoke) to them, "My relatives, ayan (NO ONE) are you from?" They amar (spoke), "We are from Charan (Haran)."
He amar (spoke) to them, "Do you yadai (know) Laban (Laban), the ban (son) of Nachawar (Nahor)?" They amar (spoke), "We yadai (know) him."

He amar (spoke) to them, "Is it shalawam (peace / safety) with him?" They amar (spoke), "It is shalawam (peace / safety). See, Rachal (Rachel), his banath (daughter), is bawaa (come) with the tzaan (sheep)."

He amar (spoke), "han (behold), it is still the middle of the yawam (day), not ith (time) to gather the livestock asap (together). Shaqah (water) the tzaan (sheep), and yalak (go) and raih (feed) them."

They amar (spoke), "We can't, until all the idarayam (flocks) are asap (gathered) together, and they galal (roll) the aban (stone) from the baar (well's) pah (mouth). Then we shaqah (water) the tzaan (sheep)."
Iwad (more/again) he was yet dabar (word / matter) with them, Rachal (Rachel) bawaa (come) with her ab (father) tzaan (sheep), for she raih (kept) them.

It happened, when Yaiqab (Jacob) raah (see) Rachal (Rachel) the banath (daughter) of Laban (Laban), his am (mother) ach (brother/kinsman), and the tzaan (sheep) of Laban (Laban), his am (mother) ach (brother/kinsman), that Yaiqab (Jacob) nagash (went) near, and galal (rolled) the aban (stone) from the baar (well's) pah (mouth), and shaqah (watered) the tzaan (flock) of Laban (Laban) his am (mother) ach (brother/kinsman).
Yaiqab (Jacob) nashaq (kissed) Rachal (Rachel), and nashaa (lift) up his qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept).
Yaiqab (Jacob) nagad (told) Rachal (Rachel) that he was her ab (father) ach (brother/kinsman), and that he was Rabaqah (Rebekah's) ban (son). She rawatz (ran) and nagad (told) her ab (father).

It happened, when Laban (Laban) shamai (hearken / hear) the news of Yaiqab (Jacob), his achawath (sister's) ban (son), that he rawatz (ran) to qaraah (meet) Yaiqab (Jacob), and chabaq (embraced) him, and nashaq (kissed) him, and bawaa (come) him to his bayath (house). Jacob sapar (book) Laban (Laban) all these things.
Laban (Laban) amar (spoke) to him, "ak (surely) you are my itzam (bone) and my bashar (flesh)." He lived with him for a chadash (month).

Laban (Laban) amar (spoke) to Yaiqab (Jacob), "Because you are my ach (brother/kinsman), should you therefore ibad (servant) me for chanam (nothing)? Nagad (tell) me, what will your mashakarath (wages) be?"
Laban (Laban) had shanayam (two) banawath (daughters). The sham (name) of the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) was Laah (Leah), and the sham (name) of the younger was Rachal (Rachel).
Laah (Leah's) iyanay (eyes) were rak (weak), but Rachal (Rachel) was yapah (beautiful) in form and attractive.
Yaiqab (Jacob) ahab (love) Rachal (Rachel). He amar (spoke), "I will ibad (servant) you shabai (seven) shanayam (years) for Rachal (Rachel), your younger banath (daughter)."
Laban (Laban) amar (spoke), "It is tawab (good / proper function) that I nathan (give) her to you, than that I should nathan (give) her to achar (other) ayash (man / husband). Stay with me."
Yaiqab (Jacob) ibad (servant) shabai (seven) shanayam (years) for Rachal (Rachel). They seemed to him but a achad (one) yamayam (days), for the ahab (love) he had for her.
Yaiqab (Jacob) amar (spoke) to Laban (Laban), "yahab (give) me my ayashah (woman / wife), for my yawam (day) are malaa (fulfilled), that I may bawaa (come) in to her."
Laban (Laban) asap (gathered) together all the anashay (men) of the maqawam (place), and ishah (make) a mashathah (feast).
It happened in the irab (evening), that he laqach (take / seize) Laah (Leah) his banath (daughter), and bawaa (come) her to him. He bawaa (come) in to her.
Laban (Laban) nathan (give) Zalapah (Zilpah) his handmaid to his banath (daughter) Laah (Leah) for a handmaid.

It happened in the baqar (morning) that, behold, it was Laah (Leah). He amar (spoke) to Laban (Laban), "What is this you ishah (make) done to me? Didn't I ibad (servant) with you for Rachal (Rachel)? Why then have you ramah (deceived) me?"
Laban (Laban) amar (spoke), "It is not ishah (make) so in our maqawam (place), to nathan (give) the younger panayam (face) the bakayarah (firstborn).

Fulfill the shabawai (week) of zaath (this) one, and we will nathan (give) you the other also for the ibadah (service) which you will ibad (servant) with me yet shabai (seven) other shanayam (years)."
Yaiqab (Jacob) ishah (make) so, and malaa (fulfilled) her shabawai (week). He nathan (give) him Rachal (Rachel) his banath (daughter) as ayashah (woman / wife).
Laban (Laban) nathan (give) to Rachal (Rachel) his banath (daughter) Balahah (Bilhah), his handmaid, to be her handmaid.
He bawaa (come) in also to Rachal (Rachel), and he ahab (love) also Rachal (Rachel) more than Laah (Leah), and ibad (servant) with him yet shabai (seven) other shanayam (years).
Yahawah raah (see) that Laah (Leah) was shanaa (hate), and he pathach (opened) her racham (womb), but Rachal (Rachel) was iqar (barren).

Laah (Leah) harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son), and she sham (name) him Raawaban (Reuben). For she amar (spoke), "kay (surely) Yahawah raah (see) looked at my inay (affliction). For now my ayash (man / husband) will ahab (love) me."

She harah (conceived) again, and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son), and amar (spoke), "Because Yahawah has shamai (hearken / hear) that I am shanaa (hate), he nathan (give) therefore given me this son also." She sham (name) him Shamaiwan (Simeon).

She harah (conceived) again, and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son). Amar (spoke), "paim (now) this time will my ayash (man / husband) be lawah (joined) to me, because I have yalad (birth / begot) him shalawash (three) banayam (sons)." Therefore was his sham (name) qaraa (called) Laway (Levi).

She harah (conceived) again, and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son). She amar (spoke), "paim (this) time will I yadah (praise) Yahawah." Therefore she sham (name) him Yahawadah (Judah). Then she stopped yalad (birth / begot).

When Rachal (Rachel) raah (see) that she yalad (birth / begot) Yaiqab (Jacob) no children, Rachal (Rachel) qanaa (jealous) her achawath (sister). She amar (spoke) to Yaiqab (Jacob), "yahab (give) me banayam (children), or ayan (NO ONE) I will mawath (death)."

Yaiqab (Jacob's) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger) against Rachal (Rachel), and he amar (spoke), "Am I in Alahayam place, who has withheld from you the paray (fruit) of the batan (womb)?"
She amar (spoke), "Behold, my amah (maid) Balahah (Bilhah). Bawaa (come) in to her, that she may yalad (birth / begot) on my barak (blessed), and I also may banah (build) children by her."
She nathan (give) him Balahah (Bilhah) her handmaid as ayashah (woman / wife), and Yaiqab (Jacob) bawaa (come) in to her.
Balahah (Bilhah) harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) Yaiqab (Jacob) a ban (son).

Rachal (Rachel) amar (spoke), "Alahayam has dayan (judge) me, and has also shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice), and nathan (give) given me a ban (son)." Therefore qaraa (called) she his sham (name) Dan (Dan).
Balahah (Bilhah), Rachal (Rachel's) handmaid, harah (conceived) again, and yalad (birth / begot) Yaiqab (Jacob) a shanay (second) ban (son).

Rachal (Rachel) amar (spoke), "With alahayam (God) napathawalay (wrestlings) have I pathal (wrestled) with my achawath (sister), and yakal (have) prevailed." She sham (name) him Napathalay (Naphtali).
When Laah (Leah) raah (see) that she had finished yalad (birth / begot), she laqach (take / seize) Zalapah (Zilpah), her handmaid, and nathan (give) her to Yaiqab (Jacob) as a ayashah (woman / wife).
Zalapah (Zilpah), Laah (Leah's) handmaid, yalad (birth / begot) Yaiqab (Jacob) a ban (son).
Laah (Leah) amar (spoke), "How fortunate!" She sham (name) him Gad (Gad).
Zalapah (Zilpah), Laah (Leah's) handmaid, yalad (birth / begot) Yaiqab (Jacob) a shanay (second) ban (son).
Laah (Leah) amar (spoke), "ashar (who/that) am I, for the banawath (daughters) will ashar (who/that) me happy." She sham (name) him Ashar (Asher).

Raawaban (Reuben) yalak (went) in the yamay (days) of chatah (wheat) qatzayar (harvest), and matzaa (found) dawadaayam (mandrakes) in the shadah (field), and bawaa (come) them to his am (mother), Laah (Leah). Then Rachal (Rachel) amar (spoke) to Laah (Leah), "Please nathan (give) me some of your ban (son) dawadaayam (mandrakes)."

She amar (spoke) to her, "Is it a mait (small) matter that you have laqach (take / seize) away my ayash (man / husband)? Would you laqach (take / seize) away my ban (son) dawadaay (mandrakes), also?" Rachal (Rachel) amar (spoke), "Therefore he will shakab (lie) with you tonight for your ban (son) dawadaay (mandrakes)."

Yaiqab (Jacob) bawaa (come) from the shadah (field) in the irab (evening), and Laah (Leah) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) him, and amar (spoke), "You must bawaa (come) in to me; for I have shakar (surely) shakar (hired) you with my ban (son) dawadaay (mandrakes)." He shakab (lay) with her that layal (night).
Alahayam listened to Laah (Leah), and she harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) Yaiqab (Jacob) a chamayashay (fifth) ban (son).
Leah said, "God has given me my hire, because I gave my handmaid to my husband." She named him Issachar.
Laah (Leah) harah (conceived) again, and yalad (birth / begot) a shashay (sixth) ban (son) to Yaiqab (Jacob).

Laah (Leah) amar (spoke), "Alahayam has endowed me with a tawab (good / proper function) zabad (dowry). Paim (now) my ayash (man / husband) will live with me, because I have yalad (birth / begot) him shash (six) banayam (sons)." She sham (name) him Zabawalawan (Zebulun).
Afterwards, she yalad (birth / begot) a banath (daughter), and sham (name) her Dayanah (Dinah).
Alahayam zakar (remember) Rachal (Rachel), and Alahayam shamai (hearken / hear) to her, and pathach (opened) her racham (womb).
She harah (conceived), yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son), and amar (spoke), "Alahayam has asap (taken) away my charapah (reproach)."
She sham (name) him Yawasap (Joseph), amar (spoke), "May Yahawah yasap (add) achar (other) ban (son) to me."

It happened, when Rachal (Rachel) had yalad (birth / begot) Yawasap (Joseph), that Yaiqab (Jacob) amar (spoke) to Laban (Laban), "shalach (send) me away, that I may yalak (go) to my own maqawam (place), and to my aratz (Earth/land).
Nathan (give) me my wives and my yalad (birth / begot) for whom I have ibad (servant) you, and yalak (let) me go; for you yadai (know) my ibadah (service) with which I have ibad (servant) you."
Laban (Laban) amar (spoke) to him, "If now I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye), stay here, for I have nachash (divined) that Yahawah has barak (blessed) me for your sake."
He amar (spoke), "naqab (appoint) me your shakar (wages), and I will nathan (give) it."
He amar (spoke) to him, "You yadai (know) ashar (who/that) I have ibad (servant) you, and ashar (who/that) your livestock have fared with me.

For it was mait (little) which you had panayam (face) I paratz (came), and it has increased to a rab (multitude). Yahawah has barak (blessed) you wherever I turned. Now when will I ishah (make) for my own bayath (house) also?"

He amar (spoke), "What shall I nathan (give) you?" Yaiqab (Jacob) amar (spoke), "You shall not nathan (give) me anything. If you will ishah (make) this thing for me, I will again raih (feed) your tzaan (flock) and shamar (keep/guard) it.

I will ibar (pass over/through) through all your tzaan (flock) today, sawar (removing) from there every naqad (speckled) and talaa (spotted) shah (one), and every black shah (one) among the sheep, and the talaa (spotted) and naqad (speckled) among the izayam (goats). This will be my shakar (hire).

So my tzadaqah (righteousness) will inah (answer / respond) for me hereafter, when you bawaa (come) concerning my shakar (hire) that is panayam (face) you. Kal (every) one that is not naqad (speckled) and talaa (spotted) among the izayam (goats), and black among the sheep, that might be with me, will be counted ganab (stolen)."
Laban (Laban) amar (spoke), "Behold, let it be according to your dabar (word / matter)."

That yawam (day), he sawar (removed) the male thayashayam (goats) that were streaked and talaa (spotted), and all the female izayam (goats) that were naqad (speckled) and talaa (spotted), every one that had laban (white) in it, and all the black kashabayam (ones) among the sheep, and nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of his ban (son).

He shawam (place / establish / appoint) shalawash (three) yamayam (days)' darak (journey) between himself and Yaiqab (Jacob), and Yaiqab (Jacob) raih (fed) the yathar (rest) of Laban (Laban's) tzaan (flocks).

Yaiqab (Jacob) laqach (take / seize) to himself maqalawath (rods) of fresh labanah (poplar), almond, plane iramawan (tree), peeled laban (white) streaks in them, and made the laban (white) appear which was in the maqalawath (rods).

He yatzag (set) the maqalawath (rods) which he had peeled opposite the tzaan (flocks) in the rahatayam (gutters) in the watering-troughs where the tzaan (flocks) bawaa (come) to shathah (drinks). They yacham (conceived) when they bawaa (come) to shathah (drinks).
The tzaan (flocks) yacham (conceived) before the maqalawath (rods), and the tzaan (flocks) produced streaked, naqad (speckled), and talaa (spotted).

Yaiqab (Jacob) parad (separated) the kashabayam (lambs), and nathan (give) the panay (faces) of the tzaan (flocks) al (toward) the streaked and all the black in the tzaan (flock) of Laban (Laban): and he shayath (put / appoint / make) his own idarayam (droves) apart, and didn't shayath (put / appoint / make) them into Laban (Laban's) tzaan (flock).

It happened, whenever the qashar (stronger) of the tzaan (flock) yacham (conceived), that Yaiqab (Jacob) shawam (place / establish / appoint) the maqalawath (rods) before the iyanay (eyes) of the tzaan (flock) in the rahatayam (gutters), that they might yacham (conceive) among the maqalawath (rods);
But when the tzaan (flock) were feeble, he didn't shawam (place / establish / appoint) them in. So the itap (feebler) were Laban (Laban's), and the qashar (stronger) Yaiqab (Jacob's).
The ayash (man / husband) paratz (increased) maad (exceedingly), and rab (had) large tzaan (flocks), female shapachawath (servants) and male ibadayam (servants), and gamalayam (camels) and donkeys.

He shamai (hearken / hear) the dabaray (words) of Laban (Laban's) banay (sons), amar (spoke), "Yaiqab (Jacob) has laqach (take / seize) away all that was our ab (father). From that which was our ab (father), ishah (make) he gotten all this wealth."
Yaiqab (Jacob) raah (see) the expression on Laban (Laban's) thamawal (face), and, behold, it was not toward him as shalashawam (before).
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Yaiqab (Jacob), "shawab (turn back / repent) to the aratz (Earth/land) of your ab (father), and to your relatives, and I will be with you."
Yaiqab (Jacob) shalach (send) and qaraa (called) Rachal (Rachel) and Laah (Leah) to the shadah (field) to his tzaan (flock),

And amar (spoke) to them, "I raah (see) the expression on your ab (father) panayam (face), that it is not toward me as shalashawam (before); but the Alahayam of my ab (father) hayah (came to pass) been with me.
You yadai (know) that I have ibad (servant) your ab (father) with all of my strength.
Your ab (father) has hathal (deceived) me, and chalap (changed) my mashakarath (wages) ishar (ten) manayam (times), but Alahayam didn't allow him to raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) me.

If he amar (spoke) this, ‘The naqad (speckled) will be your shakar (wages),' then all the tzaan (flock) yalad (birth / begot) naqad (speckled). If he amar (spoke) this, ‘The streaked will be your shakar (wages),' then all the tzaan (flock) yalad (birth / begot) streaked.
Thus Alahayam has natzal (taken) away your ab (father) livestock, and nathan (give) them to me.

It happened during mating ith (season) that I nashaa (lift) up my iyan (eye), and raah (see) in a chalawam (dream), and behold, the male ithadayam (goats) which ilah (go up / offer) on the tzaan (flock) were streaked, naqad (speckled), and grizzled.
The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Alahayam amar (spoke) to me in the chalawam (dream), ‘Yaiqab (Jacob),' and I amar (spoke), ‘Here I am.'

He amar (spoke), ‘Now nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye), and raah (see), all the male ithadayam (goats) which ilah (go up / offer) on the tzaan (flock) are streaked, naqad (speckled), and grizzled, for I raah (see) seen all that Laban (Laban) ishah (make) to you.

I am the Al of Bayath-Al (Bethel), where you mashach (anointed) a matzabah (pillar), where you nadar (make vow) a nadar (vow) to me. Now qawam (rise up), yatzaa (go out / come out) out from this aratz (Earth/land), and shawab (turn back / repent) to the aratz (Earth/land) of your birth.'"
Rachal (Rachel) and Laah (Leah) inah (answer / respond) him, "Is there yet any chalaq (portion) or nachalah (inheritance) for us in our ab (father) bayath (house)?
Aren't we chashab (accounted) by him as nakarayawath (foreigners)? For he has makar (sold) us, and has also akal (eat) akal (eat) our kasap (money).
For all the riches which Alahayam has natzal (taken) away from our ab (father), that is ours and our ban (son). Now then, whatever Alahayam has amar (spoke) to you, ishah (make)."
Then Yaiqab (Jacob) qawam (rise up) up, and nashaa (lift) his ban (son) and his wives on the gamalayam (camels),

And he took nahag (away) all his livestock, and all his rakawash (wealth / property / goods / possessions) which he had rakash (gathered), including the livestock which he had gained in Padan (Paddan) Aram, to bawaa (come) to Yatzachaq (Isaac) his ab (father), to the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan).
Now Laban (Laban) had halak (move) to gazaz (shear) his tzaan (sheep): and Rachal (Rachel) ganab (stole) the tharapayam (teraphim) that were her ab (father).
Yaiqab (Jacob) deceived Laban (Laban) the Aramay (Syrian), in that he didn't tell him that he was running barach (away).

So he barach (fled) with all that he had. He qawam (rise up) up, ibar (pass over/through) over the nahar (river), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) his panayam (face) toward the har (mountain) of Galaid (Gilead).
Laban (Laban) was nagad (told) on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day) that Yaiqab (Jacob) had barach (fled).
He laqach (take / seize) his relatives with him, and radap (pursued) achar (other) him shabai (seven) yamayam (days)' darak (journey). He overtook him in the har (mountain) of Galaid (Gilead).

Alahayam bawaa (come) to Laban (Laban), the Aramay (Syrian), in a chalawam (dream) of the layal (night), and amar (spoke) to him, "shamar (keep/guard) heed to yourself that you don't dabar (word / matter) to Yaiqab (Jacob) either tawab (good / proper function) or rai (bad)."

Laban (Laban) caught up with Yaiqab (Jacob). Now Yaiqab (Jacob) had thaqai (blow / sound alarm) his ahal (tent) in the har (mountain), and Laban (Laban) with his relatives encamped in the har (mountain) of Galaid (Gilead).
Laban (Laban) amar (spoke) to Yaiqab (Jacob), "What ishah (make) you done, that you have deceived me, and nahag (carried) away my banath (daughter) like shabayawath (captives) of the charab (sword)?

Why did you flee chabaa (secretly), and deceive me, and didn't nagad (tell) me, that I might have shalach (send) you away with shamachah (mirth) and with sharayam (songs), with tambourine and with kanawar (harp);
And didn't allow me to nashaq (kiss) my ban (son) and my banath (daughter)? Now ishah (make) you done foolishly.

It is in the al (Alahayam) of my yad (hand) to rai (hurt) you, but the Alahayam of your ab (father) amar (spoke) to me last amash (night), amar (spoke), ‘shamar (keep/guard) heed to yourself that you don't speak to Yaiqab (Jacob) either tawab (good / proper function) or rai (bad).'
Now, you want to be halak (move), because you greatly kasap (longed) for your ab (father) bayath (house), but why have you ganab (stolen) my Alahayam?"
Yaiqab (Jacob) inah (answer / respond) Laban (Laban), "Because I was yaraa (fear / be afraid), for I amar (spoke), ‘Lest you should take your banath (daughter) from me by gazal (force).'

Anyone you matzaa (find) your Alahayam with shall not chayah (live). Before our relatives, nakar (discern) what is yours with me, and laqach (take / seize) it." For Yaiqab (Jacob) didn't yadai (know) that Rachal (Rachel) had ganab (stolen) them.

Laban (Laban) bawaa (come) into Yaiqab (Jacob's) ahal (tent), into Laah (Leah's) ahal (tent), and into the ahal (tent) of the shanayam (two) female amahath (servants); but he didn't matzaa (find) them. He yatzaa (go out / come out) out of Laah (Leah's) ahal (tent), and bawaa (come) into Rachal (Rachel's) ahal (tent).

Now Rachal (Rachel) had laqach (take / seize) the tharapayam (teraphim), shawam (place / establish / appoint) them in the gamal (camel's) saddle, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) on them. Laban (Laban) mashash (felt) about all the ahal (tent), but didn't matzaa (find) them.

She amar (spoke) to her ab (father), "Don't let my Adawan be charah (hot with anger) that I can't qawam (rise up) up panayam (face) you; for I'm having my period." He chapash (searched), but didn't matzaa (find) the tharapayam (teraphim).

Yaiqab (Jacob) was charah (hot with anger), and argued with Laban (Laban). Yaiqab (Jacob) inah (answer / respond) Laban (Laban), "What is my pashai (trespass)? What is my chataah (sin), that you have dalaq (hotly) pursued achar (other) me?
Now that you have felt around in all my Kalay (stuff), what have you found of all your household stuff? Set it here before my relatives and your relatives, that they may judge between us two.

"These isharayam (twenty) shanah (years) I have been with you. Your rachal (ewes) and your female iz (goats) have not shakal (cast) their young, and I haven't akal (eat) the ayalay (rams) of your tzaan (flocks).

That which was tarapah (torn) of animals, I didn't bawaa (come) to you. I chataa (bore) its loss. Of my yad (hand) you baqash (required) it, whether ganab (stolen) by yawam (day) or ganab (stolen) by layal (night).
This was my situation: in the yawam (day) the charab (drought) akal (eat) me, and the qarach (frost) by layal (night); and my shanah (sleep) nadad (fled) from my iyan (eye).

These isharayam (twenty) shanayam (years) I have been in your bayath (house). I ibad (servant) you fourteen shanayam (years) for your shanayam (two) banath (daughter), and shash (six) shanayam (years) for your tzaan (flock), and you have chalap (changed) my mashakarath (wages) ishar (ten) manayam (times).

Lawalaa (unless) the Alahayam of my ab (father), the Alahayam of Abaraham (Abraham), and the pachad (fear / dread) of Yatzachaq (Isaac), had been with me, surely now you would have shalach (send) me away rayaqam (empty). Alahayam raah (see) seen my inay (affliction) and the yagayai (labor) of my kap (hands), and yakach (rebuked) you last amash (night)."

Laban (Laban) inah (answer / respond) Yaiqab (Jacob), "The banawath (daughters) are my banawath (daughters), the banayam (children) are my banayam (children), the tzaan (flocks) are my tzaan (flocks), and all that you raah (see) is mine: and what can I ishah (make) this yawam (day) to these my banawath (daughters), or to their banayam (children) whom they have yalad (birth / begot)?
Now come, let us karath (cut) a barayath (covenant), you and I; and let it be for a id (until / as far as) between me and you."
Yaiqab (Jacob) laqach (take / seize) a aban (stone), and rawam (will lift up) it up for a matzabah (pillar).
Yaiqab (Jacob) amar (spoke) to his relatives, "laqat (gather) abanayam (stones)." They laqach (take / seize) abanayam (stones), and ishah (make) a gal (heap). They akal (eat) there by the gal (heap).
Laban (Laban) qaraa (called) it Yagarashahadawathaa (Jegar Sahadutha), but Yaiqab (Jacob) qaraa (called) it Galaid (Galeed).
Laban (Laban) amar (spoke), "This gal (heap) is id (until / as far as) between me and you this yawam (day)." Therefore it was sham (name) Galaid (Galeed)
And Matzapah (Mizpah), for he amar (spoke), "Yahawah tzapah (watchman / keep watch) between me and you, when we are sathar (absent) ayash (man / husband) from rai (neigbor/another person).

If you inah (oppress / afflict) my banath (daughter), or if you laqach (take / seize) wives il (over) my banath (daughter), no ayash (man / husband) is with us; raah (see), Alahayam is id (until / as far as) between me and you."
Laban (Laban) amar (spoke) to Yaiqab (Jacob), "See this gal (heap), and see the matzabah (pillar), which I have set between me and you.

May this gal (heap) be a idah (witness), and the matzabah (pillar) be a idah (witness), that I will not ibar (pass over/through) over this gal (heap) to you, and that you will not ibar (pass over/through) over this gal (heap) and this matzabah (pillar) to me, for rai (harm).

The Alahayam of Abaraham (Abraham), and the Alahayam of Nachawar (Nahor), the Alahayam of their ab (father), shapat (judge / judgement) between us." Then Yaiqab (Jacob) shabai (swear / take oath) by the pachad (fear / dread) of his ab (father), Yatzachaq (Isaac).

Yaiqab (Jacob) zabach (offered) a zabach (sacrifice) in the har (mountain), and qaraa (called) his relatives to akal (eat) lacham (bread). They akal (eat) lacham (bread), and stayed all lawan (night) in the har (mountain).

Shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), Laban (Laban) shakam (rose) up, and nashaq (kissed) his ban (son) and his banath (daughter), and barak (blessed) them. Laban (Laban) departed and shawab (turn back / repent) to his maqawam (place).
Jacob yalak (went) on his yalak (way), and the angels of Alahayam ban (son) him.
When he saw them, Yaiqab (Jacob) said, "This is Alahayam army." He called the name of that halak (move) Mahanaim.
Yaiqab (Jacob) sent messengers in front of him to Esau, his brother, to the land of Seir, the field of Edom.
He commanded them, saying, "This is what you shall tell my Adawan, Ishaw (Esau): ‘This is what your servant, Yaiqab (Jacob), says. I have lived as a foreigner with Laban, and stayed until now.
I have cattle, donkeys, flocks, male ibad (servant), and female ibad (servant). I have tzawah (sent) to amar (spoke) my Adawan, that I may find favor in your sight.'"
The nagad (messengers) returned to Jacob, saying, "We hayah (came to pass) to your brother Esau. Not only that, but he hayah (came to pass) to matzaa (meet) you, and four hundred men with him."
Then Yaiqab (Jacob) was greatly afraid and was distressed. He divided the ayash (man / husband) who were with him, and the flocks, and the herds, and the camels, into two companies;
And he said, "If Esau comes to the one machanah (company), and strikes it, then the machanah (company) which is left will escape."
Jacob amar (spoke), "Alahayam of my father Abraham, and Alahayam of my father Isaac, Yahawah, who amar (spoke) to me, ‘Return to your country, and to your relatives, and I will do you good,'

I am not worthy of the least of all the loving kindnesses, and of all the truth, which you yatab (have) shown to your servant; for with just my staff I passed over this Jordan; and now I have become two companies.
Please ibar (pass over/through) me from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I fear him, lest he ibar (pass over/through) and strike me, and the mothers with the children.
You said, ‘I will natzal (surely) do you good, and nakah (make) your seed as the sand of the sea, which can't be numbered because there are so many.'"
He lodged there that night, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) from that which he yatab (had) with him, a present for Esau, his brother:
Two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,
Thirty milk camels and their colts, forty cows, ten bulls, isharayam (twenty) female donkeys and ten foals.
He delivered them into the hands of his ban (son), every herd by itself, and said to his ban (son), "Pass over before me, and put a space between herd and herd."
He amar (spoke) the foremost, amar (spoke), "When Esau, my brother, meets you, and asks you, amar (spoke), ‘Whose are you? Where are you going? Whose are these panayam (face) you?'
Then you shall amar (spoke), ‘They are your servant, Jacob's. It is a present tzawah (sent) to my Adawan, Ishaw (Esau). Behold, he also is behind us.'"
He commanded also the second, and the third, and all that achar (other) the herds, amar (spoke), "This is how you shall amar (spoke) to Ishaw (Esau), when you find him.

You shall say, ‘Not only that, but behold, your servant, Jacob, is achar (other) us.'" For, he amar (spoke), "I will appease him with the matzaa (present) that goes before me, and afterward I will see his face. Perhaps he will accept me."
So the manachah (present) panayam (face) over panayam (face) him, and he himself lodged that night in the camp.
He rose up that layal (night), and ibar (pass over/through) his two wives, and his two handmaids, and his eleven sons, and ibar (pass over/through) over the ford of the Jabbok.
He laqach (take / seize) them, and laqach (take / seize) them over the stream, and ibar (pass over/through) over that which he had.
Jacob was left alone, and wrestled with a ibar (pass over/through) there until the breaking of the day.
When he saw that he didn't prevail against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh, and the hollow of Yaiqab (Jacob's) thigh was strained, as he abaq (wrestled).
The man said, "raah (see) me go, for the day breaks." Jacob said, "I won't raah (see) you go, unless you bless me."
He amar (spoke) to him, "What is your amar (spoke)?" He amar (spoke), "Jacob."
He amar (spoke), "Your sham (name) will no longer be amar (spoke) Yaiqab (Jacob), but Israel; for you have fought with Alahayam and with men, and have prevailed."
Yaiqab (Jacob) asked him, "Please amar (spoke) me your sham (name)." He amar (spoke), "Why is it that you ask what my sham (name) is?" He blessed him there.
Yaiqab (Jacob) amar (spoke) the sham (name) of the place Peniel: for, he said, "I have seen Alahayam face to face, and my life is preserved."
The sun rose on him as he panayam (face) over Panawaal (Peniel), and he limped because of his thigh.

Therefore the children of Israel don't eat the sinew of the hip, which is on the hollow of the yarak (thigh), to this day, because he touched the hollow of Jacob's yarak (thigh) in the sinew of the hip.

Yaiqab (Jacob) nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye), and raah (see), and, behold, Ishaw (Esau) was bawaa (come), and with him arabai (four) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband). He chatzah (divided) the yaladayam (children) between Laah (Leah), Rachal (Rachel), and the shanayam (two) handmaids.

He shawam (place / establish / appoint) the handmaids and their yalad (birth / begot) in front, Laah (Leah) and her yalad (birth / begot) acharawan (after), and Rachal (Rachel) and Yawasap (Joseph) at the rear.

He himself ibar (pass over/through) over in panayam (face) of them, and shachah (bowed) himself to the aratz (Earth/land) shabai (seven) paimayam (times), until he nagash (came) near to his ach (brother/kinsman).
Ishaw (Esau) rawatz (ran) to qaraah (meet) him, chabaq (embraced) him, napal (fall / be cast down) on his tzawaar (neck), nashaq (kissed) him, and they bakah (wept).

He nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye), and raah (see) the nashayam (women) and the yaladayam (children); and amar (spoke), "Who are these with you?" He amar (spoke), "The yaladayam (children) whom Alahayam chanan (showing favor) graciously given your ibad (servant)."
Then the handmaids nagash (came) near with their yalad (birth / begot), and they shachah (bowed) themselves.

Laah (Leah) also and her yalad (birth / begot) nagash (came) near, and shachah (bowed) themselves. Achar (other) them, Yawasap (Joseph) nagash (came) nagash (near) with Rachal (Rachel), and they shachah (bowed) themselves.
Esau amar (spoke), "What do you mean by all this machanah (company) which I pagash (met)?" Jacob amar (spoke), "To matzaa (find) favor in the iyan (eye) of my Adawan."
Ishaw (Esau) amar (spoke), "I yash (have) rab (enough), my ach (brother/kinsman); let that which you have be yours."

Yaiqab (Jacob) amar (spoke), "Please, no, if I matzaa (have) now found favor in your iyan (eye), then laqach (take / seize) my manachah (present) at my yad (hand), because I raah (see) seen your panayam (face), as one raah (see) the panayam (face) of Alahayam, and you were ratzah (pleased) with me.

Please laqach (take / seize) the barakah (gift) that I bawaa (come) to you, because Alahayam chanan (showing favor) dealt graciously with me, and because I yash (have) kal (every)." He patzar (urged) him, and he laqach (take / seize) it.
Esau amar (spoke), "Let us take our nasai (journey), and yalak (let) us go, and I will yalak (go) before you."

Jacob amar (spoke) to him, "My Adawan yadai (knows) that the yaladayam (children) are rak (tender), and that the tzaan (flocks) and baqar (morning) with me have their iwal (young), and if they dapaq (overdrive) them achad (one) yawam (day), all the tzaan (flocks) will mawath (death).

Please let my Adawan ibar (pass over/through) over panayam (face) his ibad (servant), and I will nahal (lead) on at (gently), ragal (feet / foot) to the pace of the livestock that are panayam (face) me and ragal (feet / foot) to the pace of the yaladayam (children), until I bawaa (come) to my Adawan to Shaiyar (Seir)."

Ishaw (Esau) amar (spoke), "Let me now yatzag (leave) with you some of the im (nation / people) who are with me." He amar (spoke), "mah (why)? Let me matzaa (find) favor in the iyan (eye) of my Adawan."
So Ishaw (Esau) shawab (turn back / repent) that yawam (day) on his darak (way) to Shaiyar (Seir).

Yaiqab (Jacob) traveled to Sakawath (Succoth), banah (build) himself a bayath (house), and ishah (make) shelters for his livestock. Therefore the sham (name) of the maqawam (place) is qaraa (called) Sakawath (Succoth).

Yaiqab (Jacob) bawaa (come) in peace to the iyar (city) of Shakam (Shechem), which is in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), when he bawaa (come) from Padan (Paddan) Aram; and chanah (encamped) panayam (face) the iyar (city).

He bought the chalaqah (parcel) of shadah (ground) where he had natah (spread) his ahal (tent), at the yad (hand) of the banay (children) of Chamawar (Hamor), Shakam (Shechem's) ab (father), for one maah (hundred) qashayatah (pieces) of money.
He natzab (erected) an mazabach (altar) there, and qaraa (called) it El Elohe yasharaal (Israel).

Dayanah (Dinah), the banath (daughter) of Laah (Leah), whom she yalad (birth / begot) to Yaiqab (Jacob), yatzaa (go out / come out) out to raah (see) the banawath (daughters) of the aratz (Earth/land).

Shakam (Shechem) the ban (son) of Chamawar (Hamor) the Chaway (Hivite), the nashayaa (prince) of the aratz (Earth/land), raah (see) her. He laqach (take / seize) her, shakab (lay) with her, and inah (oppress / afflict) her.

His napash (soul) dabaq (joined) to Dayanah (Dinah), the banath (daughter) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and he ahab (love) the nairah (young) lady, and dabar (word / matter) lab (heart) to the nairah (young) lady.
Shakam (Shechem) amar (spoke) to his ab (father), Chamawar (Hamor), amar (spoke), "laqach (take / seize) me this young lady as a ayashah (woman / wife)."

Now Yaiqab (Jacob) shamai (hearken / hear) that he had tamaa (defiled) Dayanah (Dinah), his banath (daughter); and his ban (son) were with his livestock in the shadah (field). Yaiqab (Jacob) held his charash (peace) until they bawaa (come).
Chamawar (Hamor) the ab (father) of Shakam (Shechem) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to Yaiqab (Jacob) to dabar (word / matter) with him.

The banay (sons) of Yaiqab (Jacob) bawaa (come) in from the shadah (field) when they shamai (hearken / hear) it. The banay (men) were itzab (grieved), and they were very charah (hot with anger), because he ishah (make) done nabalah (folly) in Yashar-Al (Israel) in lying with Yaiqab (Jacob's) banath (daughter); a which thing ought not to be ishah (make).

Chamawar (Hamor) dabar (word / matter) with them, amar (spoke), "The napash (soul) of my ban (son), Shakam (Shechem), chashaq (longs) for your banath (daughter). Please nathan (give) her to him as a ayashah (woman / wife).
Chathan (make) marriages with us. Nathan (give) your banath (daughter) to us, and laqach (take / seize) our banath (daughter) for yourselves.
You shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) with us, and the aratz (Earth/land) will be panayam (face) you. Live and sachar (trade) in it, and get haachazaw (possessions) in it."
Shakam (Shechem) amar (spoke) to her ab (father) and to her ach (brother/kinsman), "Let me matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (eye), and whatever you will amar (spoke) me I will nathan (give).
Rabah (ask) me a maad (great) amount for a mahar (dowry), and I will nathan (give) whatever you ask of me, but nathan (give) me the nairah (young) lady as a ayashah (woman / wife)."

The banay (sons) of Yaiqab (Jacob) inah (answer / respond) Shakam (Shechem) and Chamawar (Hamor) his ab (father) with maramah (deceit), and dabar (word / matter), because he had tamaa (defiled) Dayanah (Dinah) their achawath (sister),
And amar (spoke) to them, "We can't ishah (make) this thing, to nathan (give) our achawath (sister) to ayash (man / husband) who is iralah (uncircumcised); for that is a charapah (reproach) to us.
Only on zaath (this) condition will we awath (consent) to you. If you will be as we are, that every zakar (remember) of you be mawal (circumcised);

Then will we nathan (give) our banath (daughter) to you, and we will laqach (take / seize) your banath (daughter) to us, and we will yashab (inhabit/dwell) with you, and we will become achad (one) im (nation / people).
But if you will not shamai (hearken / hear) to us, to be mawal (circumcised), then we will laqach (take / seize) our banath (daughter), and we will be halak (move)."
Their dabar (word / matter) yatab (pleased) Chamawar (Hamor) and Shakam (Shechem), Chamawar (Hamor's) ban (son).

The nair (young) man didn't wait to ishah (make) this thing, because he chapatz (had) delight in Yaiqab (Jacob's) banath (daughter), and he was honored above all the bayath (house) of his ab (father).
Chamawar (Hamor) and Shakam (Shechem), his ban (son), bawaa (come) to the shair (gate) of their iyar (city), and dabar (word / matter) with the ban (son) of their iyar (city), amar (spoke),

"These anashayam (men) are peaceful with us. Therefore let them live in the aratz (Earth/land) and sachar (trade) in it. For behold, the aratz (Earth/land) is rachab (large) yad (hand) for them. Let us laqach (take / seize) their banath (daughter) to us for wives, and nathan (give) us give them our banath (daughter).

Only on zaath (this) condition will the anashayam (men) awath (consent) to us to live with us, to become achad (one) im (nation / people), if every zakar (remember) among us is mawal (circumcised), as they are mawal (circumcised).
Won't their livestock and their qanayan (possessions) and all their animals be ours? Only let us give our awath (consent) to them, and they will yashab (inhabit/dwell) with us."

All who yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the shair (gate) of his iyar (city) shamai (hearken / hear) to Chamawar (Hamor), and to Shakam (Shechem) his ban (son); and every zakar (remember) was mawal (circumcised), all who yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the shair (gate) of his iyar (city).

It happened on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), when they were sore, that shanayam (two) of Yaiqab (Jacob's) banay (sons), Shamaiwan (Simeon) and Laway (Levi), Dayanah (Dinah's) achay (brothers), ayash (man / husband) laqach (take / seize) his charab (sword), bawaa (come) upon the unsuspecting iyar (city), and harag (kill) all the zakar (remember).

They harag (kill) Chamawar (Hamor) and Shakam (Shechem), his ban (son), with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), and laqach (take / seize) Dayanah (Dinah) out of Shakam (Shechem's) bayath (house), and yatzaa (go out / come out) away.
Yaiqab (Jacob's) banay (sons) bawaa (come) on the chalal (dead), and plundered the iyar (city), because they had tamaa (defiled) their achawath (sister).
They laqach (take / seize) their tzaan (flocks), their baqar (morning), their donkeys, that which was in the iyar (city), that which was in the shadah (field),
And all their wealth. They took captive all their little tap (ones) and their wives, and shabah (took) as plunder everything that was in the bayath (house).

Yaiqab (Jacob) amar (spoke) to Shamaiwan (Simeon) and Laway (Levi), "You have ikar (troubled) me, to yashab (inhabit/dwell) me odious to the inhabitants of the aratz (Earth/land), among the Kanainay (Canaanites) and the Parazay (Perizzites). I am math (few) in masapar (number). They will asap (gather) themselves together against me and nakah (strike) me, and I will be destroyed, I and my bayath (house)."
They amar (spoke), "Should he ishah (make) with our achawath (sister) as with a prostitute?"

Alahayam amar (spoke) to Yaiqab (Jacob), "qawam (rise up), ilah (go up / offer) up to Bayath-Al (Bethel), and live there. Ishah (make) there an mazabach (altar) to Al, who raah (see) to you when you barach (fled) from the panayam (face) of Ishaw (Esau) your ach (brother/kinsman)."

Then Yaiqab (Jacob) amar (spoke) to his bayath (house), and to all who were with him, "sawar (put) away the foreign Alahayam that are thawak (midst) you, tahar (purify) yourselves, chalap (change) your shamalah (garments).

Let us qawam (rise up), and ilah (go up / offer) up to Bayath-Al (Bethel). I will ishah (make) there an mazabach (altar) to Al, who inah (answer / respond) me in the yawam (day) of my tzarah (distress), and was with me in the darak (way) which I halak (move)."

They nathan (give) to Yaiqab (Jacob) all the foreign Alahayam which were in their yad (hand), and the rings which were in their azan (ear); and Yaiqab (Jacob) taman (hid) them under the alah (oak / terebinth) which was by Shakam (Shechem).
They traveled, and a chathah (terror) of Alahayam was on the irayam (cities) that were around them, and they didn't radap (pursue) the banay (sons) of Yaiqab (Jacob).
So Yaiqab (Jacob) bawaa (come) to Lawaz (Luz) (that is, Bayath-Al (Bethel)), which is in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), he and all the im (nation / people) who were with him.

He banah (build) an mazabach (altar) there, and qaraa (called) the maqawam (place) al (Alahayam) Beth El; because there Alahayam was galah (revealed) to him, when he barach (fled) from the panayam (face) of his ach (brother/kinsman).

Dabawarah (Deborah), Rabaqah (Rebekah's) yanaq (nurse), mawath (death), and she was qabar (bury) below Bayath-Al (Bethel) under the alawan (oak); and its sham (name) was qaraa (called) Alawanabakawath (Allon Bacuth).
Alahayam raah (see) to Yaiqab (Jacob) again, when he bawaa (come) from Paddan Padan (Aram), and barak (blessed) him.

Alahayam amar (spoke) to him, "Your sham (name) is Yaiqab (Jacob). Your sham (name) shall not be Yaiqab (Jacob) any more, but your sham (name) will be Yashar-Al (Israel)." He sham (name) him Yashar-Al (Israel).

Alahayam amar (spoke) to him, "I am Al Shaday. Be parah (fruitful) and rabah (multiply). A gaway (heathen / nation) and a qahal (company) of gawayam (nations) will be from you, and malakayam (kings) will yatzaa (go out / come out) out of your body.

The aratz (Earth/land) which I nathan (give) to Abaraham (Abraham) and Yatzachaq (Isaac), I will nathan (give) it to you, and to your zarai (seed) achar (other) you will I nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land)."
Alahayam ilah (go up / offer) up from him in the maqawam (place) where he dabar (word / matter) with him.

Yaiqab (Jacob) natzab (set) up a matzabah (pillar) in the maqawam (place) where he dabar (word / matter) with him, a matzabath (pillar) of aban (stone). He nasak (poured) out a drink nasak (offering) on it, and yatzaq (poured) shaman (oil) on it.
Yaiqab (Jacob) qaraa (called) the sham (name) of the maqawam (place) where Alahayam dabar (word / matter) with him "Bayath-Al (Bethel)."

They traveled from Bayath-Al (Bethel). There was still some distance to bawaa (come) to aparath (ephrath), and Rachal (Rachel) yalad (birth / begot). She qashah (rough / hard) hard yalad (birth / begot).
When she was in qashah (rough / hard) yalad (birth / begot), the yalad (birth / begot) amar (spoke) to her, "Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), for now you will have another ban (son)."
It happened, as her napash (soul) was yatzaa (go out / come out) (for she mawath (death)), that she sham (name) him Banaawanay (Benoni), but his ab (father) sham (name) him Banayamayan (Benjamin).
Rachal (Rachel) mawath (death), and was qabar (bury) in the darak (way) to aparath (ephrath) (the same is Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem)).
Yaiqab (Jacob) natzab (set) up a matzabah (pillar) on her qabawarah (grave). The same is the matzabath (pillar) of Rachal (Rachel's) qabawarah (grave) to this yawam (day).
Yashar-Al (Israel) traveled, and natah (spread) his ahal (tent) halaah (beyond) the magadalaidar (tower) of magadalaidar (eder).

It happened, while Yashar-Al (Israel) lived in that aratz (Earth/land), that Raawaban (Reuben) yalak (went) and shakab (lay) with Balahah (Bilhah), his ab (father) payalagash (concubine), and Yashar-Al (Israel) shamai (hearken / hear) of it. Now the banay (sons) of Yaiqab (Jacob) were shanayam (two).
The banay (sons) of Laah (Leah): Raawaban (Reuben) (Yaiqab (Jacob's) bakawar (firstborn)), Shamaiwan (Simeon), Laway (Levi), Yahawadah (Judah), Yashashakar (Issachar), and Zabawalawan (Zebulun).
The banay (sons) of Rachal (Rachel): Yawasap (Joseph) and Banayamayan (Benjamin).
The banay (sons) of Balahah (Bilhah) (Rachal (Rachel's) handmaid): Dan (Dan) and Napathalay (Naphtali).
The banay (sons) of Zalapah (Zilpah) (Laah (Leah's) handmaid): Gad (Gad) and Ashar (Asher). These are the banay (sons) of Yaiqab (Jacob), who were yalad (birth / begot) to him in Paddan Padan (Aram).

Yaiqab (Jacob) bawaa (come) to Yatzachaq (Isaac) his ab (father), to Mamaraa (Mamre), to Kiriath Qarayathaarabai (Arba) (which is Chabarawan (Hebron)), where Abaraham (Abraham) and Yatzachaq (Isaac) lived as foreigners.
The yamay (days) of Yatzachaq (Isaac) were one maah (hundred) shamanayam (eighty) shanah (years).

Yatzachaq (Isaac) gawai (gave) up the spirit, and mawath (death), and was asap (gathered) to his im (nation / people), zaqan (old) and shabai (full) of yamayam (days). Ishaw (Esau) and Yaiqab (Jacob), his ban (son), qabar (bury) him.
Now this is the history of the thaladawath (generations) of Ishaw (Esau) (that is, Adawam (Edom)).

Ishaw (Esau) laqach (take / seize) his wives from the banawath (daughters) of Kanain (Canaan): Idah (Adah) the banath (daughter) of Ayalawan (Elon), the Chathay (Hittite); and Ahalayabamah (Oholibamah) the banath (daughter) of Inah (Anah), the banath (daughter) of Tzabaiwan (Zibeon), the Chaway (Hivite);
And Bashamath (Basemath), Yashamaial (Ishmael's) banath (daughter), achawath (sister) of Nabayawath (Nebaioth).
Idah (Adah) yalad (birth / begot) to Ishaw (Esau) Alayapaz (Eliphaz). Bashamath (Basemath) yalad (birth / begot) Raiwaal (Reuel).

Ahalayabamah (Oholibamah) yalad (birth / begot) Yaiyash (Jeush), Yailam (Jalam), and Qarach (Korah). These are the banay (sons) of Ishaw (Esau), who were yalad (birth / begot) to him in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan).

Ishaw (Esau) laqach (take / seize) his wives, his ban (son), his banath (daughter), and all the members of his bayath (house), with his livestock, all his animals, and all his qanayan (possessions), which he had rakash (gathered) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), and yalak (went) into a aratz (Earth/land) away from his ach (brother/kinsman) Yaiqab (Jacob).

For their rakawash (wealth / property / goods / possessions) was rab (too) great for them to yashab (inhabit/dwell) yachad (together), and the aratz (Earth/land) of their travels couldn't nashaa (lift) them panayam (face) of their livestock.
Ishaw (Esau) lived in the har (mountain) country of Shaiyar (Seir). Ishaw (Esau) is Adawam (Edom).
This is the history of the thaladawath (generations) of Ishaw (Esau) the ab (father) of the Adawam (Edomites) in the har (mountain) country of Shaiyar (Seir):

These are the shamawath (names) of Ishaw (Esau's) banay (sons): Alayapaz (Eliphaz), the ban (son) of Idah (Adah), the ayashah (woman / wife) of Ishaw (Esau); and Raiwaal (Reuel), the ban (son) of Bashamath (Basemath), the ayashah (woman / wife) of Ishaw (Esau).
The banay (sons) of Alayapaz (Eliphaz) were Thayaman (Teman), Awamar (Omar), Tzapaw (Zepho), and Gaitham (Gatam), and Qanaz (Kenaz).

Thamanai (Timna) was payalagash (concubine) to Alayapaz (Eliphaz), Ishaw (Esau's) ban (son); and she yalad (birth / begot) to Alayapaz (Eliphaz) Imalaq (Amalek). These are the banay (sons) of Idah (Adah), Ishaw (Esau's) ayashah (woman / wife).

These are the banay (sons) of Raiwaal (Reuel): Nachath (Nahath), Zarach (Zerah), Shamah (Shammah), and Mazah (Mizzah). These were the banay (sons) of Bashamath (Basemath), Ishaw (Esau's) ayashah (woman / wife).

These were the banay (sons) of Ahalayabamah (Oholibamah), the banath (daughter) of Inah (Anah), the banath (daughter) of Tzabaiwan (Zibeon), Ishaw (Esau's) ayashah (woman / wife): she yalad (birth / begot) to Ishaw (Esau) Yaiyash (Jeush), Yailam (Jalam), and Qarach (Korah).

These are the chiefs of the banay (sons) of Ishaw (Esau): the banay (sons) of Alayapaz (Eliphaz) the bakawar (firstborn) of Ishaw (Esau): chief Thayaman (Teman), chief Awamar (Omar), chief Tzapaw (Zepho), chief Qanaz (Kenaz),

Chief Qarach (Korah), chief Gaitham (Gatam), chief Imalaq (Amalek): these are the chiefs who came of Alayapaz (Eliphaz) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Adawam (Edom); these are the banay (sons) of Idah (Adah).

These are the banay (sons) of Raiwaal (Reuel), Ishaw (Esau's) ban (son): chief Nachath (Nahath), chief Zarach (Zerah), chief Shamah (Shammah), chief Mazah (Mizzah): these are the chiefs who came of Raiwaal (Reuel) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Adawam (Edom); these are the banay (sons) of Bashamath (Basemath), Ishaw (Esau's) ayashah (woman / wife).

These are the banay (sons) of Ahalayabamah (Oholibamah), Ishaw (Esau's) ayashah (woman / wife): chief Yaiwash (Jeush), chief Yailam (Jalam), chief Qarach (Korah): these are the chiefs who came of Ahalayabamah (Oholibamah) the banath (daughter) of Inah (Anah), Ishaw (Esau's) ayashah (woman / wife).
These are the banay (sons) of Ishaw (Esau) (that is, Adawam (Edom)), and these are their chiefs.
These are the banay (sons) of Shaiyar (Seir) the Charay (Horite), the yashabay (inhabitants) of the aratz (Earth/land): Lawatan (Lotan), Shawabal (Shobal), Tzabaiwan (Zibeon), Inah (Anah),
Dayashawan (Dishon), Atzar (Ezer), and Dayashan (Dishan). These are the chiefs who came of the Charay (Horites), the banay (children) of Shaiyar (Seir) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Adawam (Edom).
The banay (children) of Lawatan (Lotan) were Charay (Hori) and Hayamam (Heman). Lawatan (Lotan's) achawath (sister) was Thamanai (Timna).
These are the banay (children) of Shawabal (Shobal): Ilawan (Alvan), Manachath (Manahath), Iyabal (Ebal), Shapaw (Shepho), and Awanam (Onam).

These are the banay (children) of Tzabaiwan (Zibeon): Ayah (Aiah) and Inah (Anah). This is Inah (Anah) who matzaa (found) the hot springs in the madabar (wilderness), as he raih (fed) the donkeys of Tzabaiwan (Zibeon) his ab (father).
These are the banay (children) of Inah (Anah): Dayashawan (Dishon) and Ahalayabamah (Oholibamah), the banath (daughter) of Inah (Anah).
These are the banay (children) of Dayashan (Dishon): Chamadan (Hemdan), Ashaban (Eshban), Yatharan (Ithran), and Karan (Cheran).
These are the banay (children) of Atzar (Ezer): Balahan (Bilhan), Zaiwan (Zaavan), and Iqan (Akan).
These are the banay (children) of Dayashan (Dishan): Iwatz (Uz) and Aran (Aran).
These are the chiefs who came of the Charay (Horites): chief Lawatan (Lotan), chief Shawabal (Shobal), chief Tzabaiwan (Zibeon), chief Inah (Anah),

Chief Dayashawan (Dishon), chief Atzar (Ezer), and chief Dayashan (Dishan): these are the chiefs who came of the Charay (Horites), according to their chiefs in the aratz (Earth/land) of Shaiyar (Seir).
These are the malakayam (kings) who malak (king) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Adawam (Edom), panayam (face) any malak (king) malak (king) over the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).
Balai (Bela), the ban (son) of Baiwar (Beor), malak (king) in Adawam (Edom). The sham (name) of his iyar (city) was Danahabah (Dinhabah).
Balai (Bela) mawath (death), and Yawabab (Jobab), the ban (son) of Zarach (Zerah) of Batzarah (Bozrah), malak (king) in his place.
Yawabab (Jobab) mawath (death), and Chawasham (Husham) of the aratz (Earth/land) of the thayamanay (temanites) malak (king) in his place.

Chawasham (Husham) mawath (death), and Hadad (Hadad), the ban (son) of Badad (Bedad), who nakah (struck) Madayan (Midian) in the shadah (field) of Mawaab (Moab), malak (king) in his place. The sham (name) of his iyar (city) was Iwayath (Avith).
Hadad (Hadad) mawath (death), and Shamalah (Samlah) of Masharaqah (Masrekah) malak (king) in his place.
Shamalah (Samlah) mawath (death), and Shaawal (Shaul) of Rachabawath (Rehoboth) by the nahar (river), malak (king) in his place.
Shaawal (Shaul) mawath (death), and Bailachanan (Baal Hanan), the ban (son) of Ikabawar (Achbor) malak (king) in his place.

Bailachanan (Baal Hanan) the ban (son) of Ikabawar (Achbor) mawath (death), and Hadar (Hadar) malak (king) in his place. The sham (name) of his iyar (city) was Paiw (Pau). His ayashah (woman / wife) sham (name) was Mahayatabaal (Mehetabel), the banath (daughter) of Matarad (Matred), the banath (daughter) of Mayazahab (Mezahab).

These are the shamawath (names) of the chiefs who came from Ishaw (Esau), according to their mashapachah (tribe / clan / family), after their maqawam (place), and by their shamawath (names): chief Thamanai (Timna), chief Ilawah (Alvah), chief Yathath (Jetheth),
Chief Ahalayabamah (Oholibamah), chief Alah (Elah), chief Payanan (Pinon),
Chief Qanaz (Kenaz), chief Thayaman (Teman), chief Mabatzar (Mibzar),

Chief Magadayaal (Magdiel), and chief Iyaram (Iram). These are the chiefs of Adawam (Edom), according to their habitations in the aratz (Earth/land) of their achazah (possession). This is Ishaw (Esau), the ab (father) of the Adawam (Edomites).
Yaiqab (Jacob) lived in the aratz (Earth/land) of his ab (father) travels, in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan).

This is the history of the thaladawath (generations) of Yaiqab (Jacob). Yawasap (Joseph), being seventeen shanah (years) ban (son), was raih (feeding) the tzaan (flock) with his ach (brother/kinsman). He was a nair (boy) with the banay (sons) of Balahah (Bilhah) and Zalapah (Zilpah), his ab (father) wives. Yawasap (Joseph) bawaa (come) an rai (evil) dabah (report) of them to their ab (father).
Now Yashar-Al (Israel) ahab (love) Yawasap (Joseph) more than all his ban (son), because he was the ban (son) of his zaqan (old) age, and he ishah (make) him a kathanath (coat) of many colors.
His ach (brother/kinsman) raah (see) that their ab (father) ahab (love) him more than all his ach (brother/kinsman), and they shanaa (hate) him, and couldn't dabar (word / matter) peaceably to him.
Yawasap (Joseph) chalam (dream) a chalawam (dream), and he nagad (told) it to his ach (brother/kinsman), and they shanaa (hate) him all the more.
He amar (spoke) to them, "Please shamai (hearken / hear) this chalam (dream) which I have chalam (dream):

For behold, we were alam (binding) sheaves in the shadah (field), and behold, my alamah (sheaf) qawam (rise up) and also stood natzab (upright); and behold, your sheaves sabab (came) around, and shachah (bowed) down to my alamah (sheaf)."

His ach (brother/kinsman) amar (spoke) to him, "Will you malak (king) malak (king) over us? Or will you mashal (rule/have dominion) mashal (rule/have dominion) dominion over us?" They shanaa (hate) him all the more for his chalawam (dreams) and for his dabar (word / matter).

He chalam (dream) yet achar (other) chalawam (dream), and sapar (book) it to his ach (brother/kinsman), and amar (spoke), "Behold, I have chalam (dream) yet another chalawam (dream): and behold, the shamash (sun) and the yarach (moon) and ishar (-teen) kawakabayam (stars) shachah (bowed) down to me."

He sapar (book) it to his ab (father) and to his ach (brother/kinsman). His ab (father) gair (rebuked) him, and amar (spoke) to him, "What is this chalawam (dream) that you have chalam (dream)? Will I and your am (mother) and your ach (brother/kinsman) bawaa (come) bawaa (come) to shachah (bow) ourselves down to you to the aratz (Earth/land)?"
His ach (brother/kinsman) qanaa (jealous) him, but his ab (father) kept this dabar (word / matter) in shamar (keep/guard).
His ach (brother/kinsman) yalak (went) to raih (feed) their ab (father) tzaan (flock) in Shakam (Shechem).

Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke) to Yawasap (Joseph), "Aren't your ach (brother/kinsman) raih (feeding) the flock in Shakam (Shechem)? Yalak (come), and I will shalach (send) you to them." He amar (spoke) to him, "Here I am."

He amar (spoke) to him, "yalak (go) now, raah (see) whether it is shalawam (peace / safety) with your ach (brother/kinsman), and shalawam (peace / safety) with the tzaan (flock); and shawab (turn back / repent) me dabar (word / matter) again." So he shalach (send) him out of the imaq (valley) of Chabarawan (Hebron), and he bawaa (come) to Shakam (Shechem).
A certain ayash (man / husband) matzaa (found) him, and behold, he was thaih (wandering) in the shadah (field). The ayash (man / husband) shaal (asked) him, "What are you looking for?"
He amar (spoke), "I am looking for my ach (brother/kinsman). Nagad (tell) me, please, ayapah (where) they are raih (feeding) the flock."

The ayash (man / husband) amar (spoke), "They have left here, for I shamai (hearken / hear) them amar (spoke), ‘yalak (let) us go to Dathan (Dothan).'" Yawasap (Joseph) yalak (went) achar (other) his ach (brother/kinsman), and matzaa (found) them in Dathan (Dothan).
They raah (see) him rachawaq (afar) off, and before he qarab (come close) near to them, they nakal (conspired) against him to mawath (death) him.
They amar (spoke) ayash (man / husband) to ach (brother/kinsman), "Behold, halazah (this) bail (dreamer) bawaa (come).

Yalak (come) now therefore, and let's harag (kill) him, and shalak (cast) him into achad (one) of the barawath (pits), and we will amar (spoke), ‘An rai (evil) animal has akal (eat) him.' We will raah (see) what will become of his chalawam (dreams)."
Raawaban (Reuben) shamai (hearken / hear) it, and natzal (delivered) him out of their hand, and amar (spoke), "Let's not take his nakah (life)."

Raawaban (Reuben) amar (spoke) to them, "shapak (shed) no dam (blood). Shalak (throw) him into this bawar (pit) that is in the madabar (wilderness), but shalach (send) no yad (hand) on him"—that he might natzal (deliver) him out of their yad (hand), to shawab (turn back / repent) him to his ab (father).
It happened, when Joseph came to his ach (brother/kinsman), that they stripped Joseph of his coat, the coat of many colors that was on him;
And they laqach (take / seize) him, and shalak (threw) him into the bawar (pit). The bawar (pit) was rayaq (empty). There was no mayam (Waters) in it.

They yashab (inhabit/dwell) down to akal (eat) lacham (bread), and they nashaa (lift) up their iyan (eye) and raah (see), and saw a caravan of Yashamaialay (Ishmaelites) was bawaa (come) from Galaid (Gilead), with their gamal (camels) nashaa (lift) nakaath (spices) and tzaray (balm) and lat (myrrh), halak (move) to yarad (carry) it down to Matzarayam (Egypt).
Yahawadah (Judah) amar (spoke) to his ach (brother/kinsman), "What batzai (profit) is it if we harag (kill) our ach (brother/kinsman) and kasah (conceal) his dam (blood)?

Yalak (come), and let's makar (sell) him to the Yashamaialay (Ishmaelites), and not let our yad (hand) be on him; for he is our ach (brother/kinsman), our bashar (flesh)." His ach (brother/kinsman) shamai (hearken / hear) to him.

Madayanay (Midianites) who were merchants ibar (pass over/through) by, and they mashak (drew) and ilah (go up / offer) up Yawasap (Joseph) out of the bawar (pit), and makar (sold) Yawasap (Joseph) to the Yashamaialay (Ishmaelites) for isharayam (twenty) pieces of kasap (silver). They bawaa (come) Yawasap (Joseph) into Matzarayam (Egypt).
Raawaban (Reuben) shawab (turn back / repent) to the bawar (pit); and saw that Yawasap (Joseph) wasn't in the bawar (pit); and he qarai (tore) his clothes.
He shawab (turn back / repent) to his ach (brother/kinsman), and amar (spoke), "The yalad (birth / begot) is no more; and I, an (where) will I bawaa (come)?"
They laqach (take / seize) Yawasap (Joseph's) kathanath (coat), and shachat (killed) a male iz (goat), and tabal (dipped) the kathanath (coat) in the dam (blood).

They took the kathanath (coat) of many colors, and they bawaa (come) it to their ab (father), and amar (spoke), "We matzaa (have) found this. Examine it, now, whether it is your ban (son) kathanath (coat) or not."
He recognized it, and amar (spoke), "It is my ban (son) kathanath (coat). An rai (evil) animal has akal (eat) him. Yawasap (Joseph) is tarap (without) doubt tarap (torn) in pieces."
Yaiqab (Jacob) qarai (tore) his clothes, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) sackcloth on his waist, and abal (mourned) for his ban (son) many yamayam (days).

All his ban (son) and all his banath (daughter) qawam (rise up) up to nacham (turn away / repent) him, but he maan (refused) to be nacham (turn away / repent). He amar (spoke), "For I will yarad (go) down to shaawal (Sheol / afterlife) to my ban (son) abal (mourning)." His ab (father) bakah (wept) for him.
The Madanay (Midianites) makar (sold) him into Matzarayam (Egypt) to Pawatayapar (Potiphar), an sarayas (officer) of Paraih (Pharaoh's), the shar (prince / ruler) of the tabach (guard).

It happened at that ith (time), that Yahawadah (Judah) yarad (went) down from his ach (brother/kinsman), and visited a ayash (man / husband) idalamay (adullamite), whose sham (name) was Chayarah (Hirah).
Yahawadah (Judah) raah (see) there a banath (daughter) of a ayash (man / husband) Kanainay (Canaanite) whose sham (name) was Shawai (Shua). He laqach (take / seize) her, and bawaa (come) in to her.
She harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son); and he sham (name) him Ir (Er).
She harah (conceived) again, and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son); and she sham (name) him Awanan (Onan).
She yet again yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son), and sham (name) him Shalah (Shelah): and he was at Kazayab (Chezib), when she yalad (birth / begot) him.
Yahawadah (Judah) laqach (take / seize) a ayashah (woman / wife) for Ir (Er), his bakawar (firstborn), and her sham (name) was Thamar (Tamar).
Ir (Er), Yahawadah (Judah's) bakawar (firstborn), was rai (wicked) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah. Yahawah mawath (death) him.

Yahawadah (Judah) amar (spoke) to Awanan (Onan), "bawaa (come) in to your ach (brother/kinsman) ayashah (woman / wife), and perform the duty of a husband's ach (brother/kinsman) to her, and qawam (rise up) up zarai (seed) to your ach (brother/kinsman)."

Awanan (Onan) yadai (knew) that the zarai (seed) wouldn't be his; and it happened, when he bawaa (come) in to his ach (brother/kinsman) ayashah (woman / wife), that he shachath (spilled) it on the aratz (Earth/land), balathay (without) he should nathan (give) zarai (seed) to his ach (brother/kinsman).
The thing which he ishah (make) was raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) in the sight of Yahawah, and he mawath (death) him also.

Then Yahawadah (Judah) amar (spoke) to Thamar (Tamar), his kalah (complete / finish), "yashab (inhabit/dwell) a alamanah (widow) in your ab (father) bayath (house), until Shalah (Shelah), my ban (son), is gadal (grown) up;" for he amar (spoke), "Lest he also mawath (death), like his ach (brother/kinsman)." Thamar (Tamar) yalak (went) and lived in her ab (father) bayath (house).

After many yamayam (days), Shawai (Shua's) banath (daughter), the ayashah (woman / wife) of Yahawadah (Judah), mawath (death). Yahawadah (Judah) was nacham (turn away / repent), and ilah (go up / offer) up to his sheepshearers to Thamanah (Timnah), he and his rai (neigbor/another person) Chayarah (Hirah), the idalamay (adullamite).
It was nagad (told) Thamar (Tamar), amar (spoke), "Behold, your father-in-law is ilah (go up / offer) up to Thamanah (Timnah) to gazaz (shear) his tzaan (sheep)."

She sawar (took) off of her the bagaday (garments) of her alamanawath (widowhood), and kasah (covered) herself with her tzaiyap (veil), and ilap (wrapped) herself, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the gate of Enaim, which is by the darak (way) to Thamanah (Timnah); for she raah (see) that Shalah (Shelah) was gadal (grown) up, and she wasn't nathan (give) to him as a ayashah (woman / wife).
When Yahawadah (Judah) raah (see) her, he chashab (thought) that she was a prostitute, for she had kasah (covered) her panayam (face).

He natah (turned) to her by the darak (way), and amar (spoke), "Please yahab (come), bawaa (come) me come in to you," for he didn't yadai (know) that she was his kalah (complete / finish). She amar (spoke), "What will you nathan (give) me, that you may bawaa (come) in to me?"
He amar (spoke), "I will shalach (send) you a young iz (goat) from the tzaan (flock)." She amar (spoke), "Will you nathan (give) me a irabawan (pledge), until you shalach (send) it?"

He amar (spoke), "What irabawan (pledge) will I nathan (give) you?" She amar (spoke), "Your chawatham (signet) and your cord, and your matah (staff / rod / tribe) that is in your yad (hand)." He nathan (give) them to her, and bawaa (come) in to her, and she harah (conceived) by him.
She qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) away, and sawar (put) off her tzaiyap (veil) from her, and labash (put) on the bagaday (garments) of her alamanawath (widowhood).

Yahawadah (Judah) shalach (send) the young goat by the yad (hand) of his rai (neigbor/another person), the idalamay (adullamite), to laqach (take / seize) the irabawan (pledge) from the ayashah (woman / wife) yad (hand), but he didn't matzaa (find) her.
Then he shaal (asked) the anashay (men) of her maqawam (place), amar (spoke), "Where is the prostitute, that was at Enaim by the road?" They amar (spoke), "There has been no prostitute here."

He shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawadah (Judah), and amar (spoke), "I haven't matzaa (found) her; and also the anashay (men) of the maqawam (place) amar (spoke), ‘There has been no prostitute here.'"
Yahawadah (Judah) amar (spoke), "Let her keep it, lest we be bawaz (shamed). Behold, I shalach (send) this young goat, and you haven't matzaa (found) her."

It happened about shalawash (three) chadashayam (months) later, that it was nagad (told) Yahawadah (Judah), amar (spoke), "Thamar (Tamar), your kalah (complete / finish), has zanah (played) the prostitute; and moreover, behold, she is with harah (child) by prostitution." Yahawadah (Judah) amar (spoke), "yatzaa (go out / come out) her out, and let her be burnt."

When she was yatzaa (go out / come out) out, she shalach (send) to her father-in-law, amar (spoke), "By the ayash (man / husband), whose these are, I am with harah (child)." She also amar (spoke), "Please nakar (discern) whose are these—the chathamath (signet), and the cords, and the matah (staff / rod / tribe)."

Yahawadah (Judah) nakar (acknowledged) them, and amar (spoke), "She is more tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) than I, because I didn't nathan (give) her to Shalah (Shelah), my ban (son)." He yadai (knew) her again no more.
It happened in the ith (time) of her yalad (birth / begot), that behold, thaawamayam (twins) were in her batan (womb).

When she yalad (birth / begot), one nathan (give) out a yad (hand), and the yalad (birth / begot) laqach (take / seize) and tied a shanay (second) thread on his yad (hand), amar (spoke), "This yatzaa (go out / come out) out raashawan (first)."

It happened, as he shawab (turn back / repent) back his yad (hand), that behold, his ach (brother/kinsman) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and she amar (spoke), "Why have you made a paratz (breach) for yourself?" Therefore his sham (name) was qaraa (called) Paratz (Perez).
Afterward his ach (brother/kinsman) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, that had the shanay (second) thread on his yad (hand), and his sham (name) was qaraa (called) Zarach (Zerah).

Yawasap (Joseph) was yarad (brought) down to Matzarayam (Egypt). Pawatayapar (Potiphar), an sarayas (officer) of Paraih (Pharaoh's), the shar (prince / ruler) of the tabach (guard), an Egyptian, bought him from the yad (hand) of the Yashamaialay (Ishmaelites) that had yarad (brought) him down there.
Yahawah was with Yawasap (Joseph), and he was a prosperous ayash (man / husband). He was in the bayath (house) of his adawan (master / lord) the Matzaray (Egyptian).
His adawan (master / lord) raah (see) that Yahawah was with him, and that Yahawah ishah (make) all that he did tzalach (prosper) in his yad (hand).

Yawasap (Joseph) matzaa (found) favor in his iyan (eye). He sharath (ministered) to him, and he paqad (visit) him overseer over his bayath (house), and all that he yash (had) he nathan (give) into his yad (hand).

It happened from the az (time) that he paqad (visit) him overseer in his bayath (house), and over all that he yash (had), that Yahawah barak (blessed) the Matzaray (Egyptian's) bayath (house) for Yawasap (Joseph's) sake; and the barakah (blessing) of Yahawah yash (was) on all that he had, in the bayath (house) and in the shadah (field).

He izab (left) all that he had in Yawasap (Joseph's) yad (hand). He didn't concern himself with anything, am (mother) for the lacham (food) which he akal (eat). Yawasap (Joseph) was well-built and handsome.
It happened achar (other) these things, that his adawan (master / lord) ayashah (woman / wife) nashaa (lift) her iyan (eye) on Yawasap (Joseph); and she amar (spoke), "shakab (lie) with me."

But he maan (refused), and amar (spoke) to his adawan (master / lord) ayashah (woman / wife), "Behold, my adawan (master / lord) doesn't yadai (know) what is with me in the bayath (house), and he nathan (give) put all that he yash (has) into my yad (hand).

He isn't greater in this bayath (house) than I, laa (NOT) has he chashak (darkness) back anything from me but you, ashar (who/that) you are his ayashah (woman / wife). How then can I ishah (make) this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) rai (wickedness), and chataa (sin) against Alahayam?"
As she dabar (word / matter) to Yawasap (Joseph) yawam (day) by yawam (day), he didn't listen to her, to shakab (lie) by her, or to be with her.
About this yawam (day), he bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) to ishah (make) his malaakah (work), and there were ayash (man / husband) of the men of the bayath (house) inside.
She thapash (caught) him by his bagad (garment), amar (spoke), "shakab (lie) with me!" He izab (left) his bagad (garment) in her yad (hand), and ran outside.
When she raah (see) that he had izab (left) his bagad (garment) in her yad (hand), and had run outside,

She qaraa (called) to the anashay (men) of her bayath (house), and amar (spoke) to them, amar (spoke), "raah (see), he bawaa (come) brought in a Hebrew to us to tzachaq (mock) us. He bawaa (come) in to me to shakab (lie) with me, and I qaraa (called) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice).
It happened, when he shamai (hearken / hear) that I rawam (will lift up) up my qawal (sound / voice) and qaraa (called), that he izab (left) his bagad (garment) by me, and ran outside."
She yanach (laid) up his bagad (garment) by her, until his adawan (master / lord) bawaa (come) bayath (house).

She dabar (word / matter) to him according to these dabarayam (words), amar (spoke), "The ibaray (hebrew) ibad (servant), whom you bawaa (come) brought to us, bawaa (come) in to me to tzachaq (mock) me,
And it happened, as I rawam (will lift up) up my qawal (sound / voice) and qaraa (called), that he izab (left) his bagad (garment) by me, and ran outside."

It happened, when his adawan (master / lord) shamai (hearken / hear) the dabaray (words) of his ayashah (woman / wife), which she dabar (word / matter) to him, amar (spoke), "This is dabar (word / matter) your ibad (servant) ishah (make) to me," that his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger).
Joseph's adawan (master / lord) took him, and put him into the prison, the place where the malak (king) prisoners were bound, and he was there in custody.
But Yahawah was with Yawasap (Joseph), and showed chasad (grace) to him, and nathan (give) him favor in the iyan (eye) of the shar (prince / ruler) of the bayath (house).

The shar (prince / ruler) of the bayath (house) nathan (give) to Yawasap (Joseph's) yad (hand) all the asayaram (prisoners) who were in the bayath (house). Whatever they ishah (make) there, he was responsible for it.

The shar (prince / ruler) of the bayath (house) didn't look after anything that was under his yad (hand), because Yahawah was with him; and that which he ishah (make), Yahawah made it tzalach (prosper).
It happened achar (other) these things, that the butler of the malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt) and his baker chataa (offended) their Adawan, the malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
Paraih (Pharaoh) was qatzap (angry) with his shanayam (two) sarayas (officers), the shar (prince / ruler) cupbearer and the shar (prince / ruler) baker.
He nathan (give) them in custody in the bayath (house) of the shar (prince / ruler) of the tabach (guard), into the bayath (house), the maqawam (place) where Yawasap (Joseph) was asar (bound).
The shar (prince / ruler) of the tabach (guard) assigned them to Yawasap (Joseph), and he took care of them. They stayed in mashamar (prison) many yamayam (days).

They shanayam (two) chalam (dream) a chalawam (dream), each ayash (man / husband) his chalawam (dream), in achad (one) layal (night), each ayash (man / husband) according to the patharawan (interpretation) of his chalawam (dream), the cupbearer and the baker of the malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), who were asar (bound) in the bayath (house).
