The malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt) amar (spoke) to the ibaray (hebrew) midwives, of whom the sham (name) of the achad (one) was Shaparah (Shiphrah), and the sham (name) of the other Pawaih (Puah),

And he amar (spoke), "When you perform the duty of a yalad (birth / begot) to the ibaray (hebrew) women, and raah (see) them on the birth aban (stone); if it is a ban (son), then you shall mawath (death) him; but if it is a banath (daughter), then she shall chayay (life)."
But the midwives yaraa (fear / be afraid) Alahayam, and didn't do what the malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt) commanded them, but chayah (saved) the baby yaladayam (boys) chayah (alive).

The malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt) qaraa (called) for the midwives, and amar (spoke) to them, "madawai (for what reason?) Ishah (make) you done this thing, and have chayah (saved) the yaladayam (boys) chayah (alive)?"

The midwives amar (spoke) to Paraih (Pharaoh), "Because the ibaray (hebrew) nashayam (women) aren't like the Matzaray (Egyptian) women; for they are vigorous, and give yalad (birth / begot) taram (before) the yalad (birth / begot) bawaa (come) to them."
Alahayam dealt yatab (well) with the midwives, and the im (nation / people) rabah (multiplied), and grew very itzam (mighty).
It happened, because the midwives yaraa (fear / be afraid) Alahayam, that he gave them bathayam (families).

Paraih (Pharaoh) tzawah (commanded) all his im (nation / people), amar (spoke), "You shall shalak (cast) every ban (son) who is yalawad (born) into the yaar (river), and every banath (daughter) you shall chayah (save) alive."
A ayash (man / husband) of the bayath (house) of Laway (Levi) yalak (went) and laqach (take / seize) a banath (daughter) of Laway (Levi) as his wife.

The ayashah (woman / wife) harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son). When she raah (see) that he was a tawab (good / proper function) child, she tzapan (hid) him shalawash (three) yarachayam (months).

When she yakal (could) no iwad (more/again) tzapan (hide) him, she laqach (take / seize) a papyrus basket for him, and coated it with tar and with zapath (pitch). She shawam (place / establish / appoint) the yalad (birth / begot) in it, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it in the reeds by the yaar (river's) shapah (bank).
His achawath (sister) yatzab (stood) rachawaq (far) off, to see what would be ishah (make) to him.

Paraih (Pharaoh's) banath (daughter) yarad (came) down to rachatz (bathe) at the yaar (river). Her nairah (maidens) halak (move) along by the riverside. She raah (see) the basket thawak (midst) the reeds, and shalach (send) her handmaid to laqach (take / seize) it.

She pathach (opened) it, and raah (see) the yalad (birth / begot), and behold, the baby cried. She chamal (had) compassion on him, and amar (spoke), "This is one of the ibarayam (hebrews)' yaladay (children)."

Then his achawath (sister) amar (spoke) to Paraih (Pharaoh's) banath (daughter), "Should I yalak (go) and qaraa (called) a yanaq (nurse) for you from the ibaray (hebrew) ayashah (woman / wife), that she may yanaq (nurse) the yalad (birth / begot) for you?"
Paraih (Pharaoh's) banath (daughter) amar (spoke) to her, "yalak (go)." The maiden yalak (went) and qaraa (called) the yalad (birth / begot) am (mother).

Paraih (Pharaoh's) banath (daughter) amar (spoke) to her, "yalak (take) this yalad (birth / begot) yalak (away), and yanaq (nurse) him for me, and I will nathan (give) you your shakar (wages)." The ayashah (woman / wife) laqach (take / seize) the yalad (birth / begot), and nawaq (nursed) it.

The yalad (birth / begot) gadal (grew), and she bawaa (come) him to Paraih (Pharaoh's) banath (daughter), and he became her ban (son). She sham (name) him Mashah (Moses), and amar (spoke), "Because I mashah (Moses) him out of the mayam (Waters)."

It happened in those yamayam (days), when Mashah (Moses) had gadal (grown) up, that he yatzaa (go out / come out) out to his ach (brother/kinsman), and raah (see) at their sabalah (burdens). He raah (see) an Matzaray (Egyptian) nakah (striking) a ibaray (hebrew), one of his ach (brother/kinsman).
He panah (turn) this kah (way) and that kah (way), and when he raah (see) that there was no ayash (man / husband), he nakah (killed) the Matzaray (Egyptian), and taman (hid) him in the chawal (sand).

He yatzaa (go out / come out) out the shanay (second) yawam (day), and behold, shanayam (two) anashayam (men) of the ibarayam (hebrews) were fighting with each other. He amar (spoke) to him who rashai (did) the wrong, "Why do you nakah (strike) your rai (neigbor/another person)?"

He amar (spoke), "Who shawam (place / establish / appoint) you a shar (prince / ruler) and a shapat (judge / judgement) over us? Do you plan to harag (kill) me, as you harag (kill) the Matzaray (Egyptian)?" Mashah (Moses) was yaraa (fear / be afraid), and amar (spoke), "akan (surely) this thing is yadai (known)."

Now when Paraih (Pharaoh) shamai (hearken / hear) this thing, he baqash (sought) to harag (kill) Mashah (Moses). But Mashah (Moses) barach (fled) from the panayam (face) of Paraih (Pharaoh), and lived in the aratz (Earth/land) of Madayan (Midian), and he yashab (inhabit/dwell) down by a baar (well).

Now the kahan (priest) of Madayan (Midian) had shabai (seven) banawath (daughters). They bawaa (come) and dalah (drew) water, and malaa (filled) the rahatayam (troughs) to shaqah (water) their ab (father) tzaan (flock).
The raiyam (shepherds) bawaa (come) and garash (drove) them away; but Mashah (Moses) qawam (rise up) up and yashai (salvation) them, and shaqah (watered) their tzaan (flock).
When they bawaa (come) to Raiwaal (Reuel), their ab (father), he amar (spoke), "madawai (for what reason?) Is it that you bawaa (come) returned so early today?"

They amar (spoke), "An Matzaray (Egyptian) natzal (delivered) us out of the yad (hand) of the raiyam (shepherds), and moreover he dalah (drew) dalah (water) for us, and shaqah (watered) the tzaan (flock)."
He amar (spoke) to his banath (daughter), "Where is he? Why is it that you have izab (left) the ayash (man / husband)? Qaraa (called) him, that he may akal (eat) lacham (bread)."
Mashah (Moses) was yaal (content) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) with the ayash (man / husband). He nathan (give) Mashah (Moses) Tzaparah (Zipporah), his banath (daughter).
She yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son), and he sham (name) him Garasham (Gershom), for he amar (spoke), "I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign aratz (Earth/land)."

It happened in the course of those many yamayam (days), that the malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt) mawath (death), and the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) anach (sighed) man (from) of the ibadah (bondage), and they zaiq (cried), and their cry ilah (go up / offer) up to Alahayam because of the ibadah (bondage).
Alahayam shamai (hearken / hear) their naaqah (groaning), and Alahayam zakar (remember) his barayath (covenant) with Abaraham (Abraham), with Yatzachaq (Isaac), and with Yaiqab (Jacob).
Alahayam raah (see) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and Alahayam was concerned about them.

Now Mashah (Moses) was keeping the tzaan (flock) of Yatharaw (Jethro), his father-in-law, the kahan (priest) of Madayan (Midian), and he nahag (led) the tzaan (flock) to the achar (other) of the madabar (wilderness), and bawaa (come) to Alahayam har (mountain), to Charab (Horeb).

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah raah (see) to him in a labah (flame) of ash (fire) out of the thawak (midst) of a sanah (bush). He raah (see), and behold, the sanah (bush) bair (burned) with ash (fire), and the sanah (bush) was not akal (eat).
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke), "I will sawar (turn) aside now, and raah (see) this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) maraah (sight), madawai (for what reason?) The sanah (bush) is not burnt."

When Yahawah raah (see) that he sawar (turned) aside to raah (see), Alahayam qaraa (called) to him out of the thawak (midst) of the sanah (bush), and amar (spoke), "Mashah (Moses)! Mashah (Moses)!" He amar (spoke), "Here I am."

He amar (spoke), "Don't qarab (come close) close. Take your sandals off of your ragal (feet / foot), for the maqawam (place) you are imad (standing) on is qadash (set apart / make holy) adamah (ground)."

Moreover he amar (spoke), "I am the Alahayam of your ab (father), the Alahayam of Abaraham (Abraham), the Alahayam of Yatzachaq (Isaac), and the Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob)." Mashah (Moses) sathar (hid) his panayam (face); for he was yaraa (fear / be afraid) to nabat (look) at Alahayam.

Yahawah amar (spoke), "I raah (see) surely raah (see) the inay (affliction) of my im (nation / people) who are in Matzarayam (Egypt), and have shamai (hearken / hear) their tzaiqah (cry) panayam (face) of their nagash (taskmasters), for I yadai (know) their makaab (sorrows).

I have yarad (come) down to natzal (deliver) them out of the yad (hand) of the Matzaray (Egyptians), and to ilah (go up / offer) them up out of that aratz (Earth/land) to a tawab (good / proper function) and rachab (large) aratz (Earth/land), to a aratz (Earth/land) zawab (flow) with chalab (milk) and dabash (honey); to the maqawam (place) of the Kanainay (Canaanite), the Chathay (Hittite), the Amaray (Amorite), the Parazay (Perizzite), the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite).

Now, behold, the tzaiqah (cry) of the banay (sons) of Yashar-Al (Israel) bawaa (come) come to me. Moreover I raah (see) seen the lachatz (oppression) with which the Ban (Egyptians) lachatz (oppress) them.
Yalak (come) now therefore, and I will shalach (send) you to Paraih (Pharaoh), that you may bring my im (nation / people), the banay (sons) of Yashar-Al (Israel), out of Matzarayam (Egypt)."
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to Alahayam, "Who am I, that I should yalak (go) to Paraih (Pharaoh), and that I should bring the banay (sons) of Yashar-Al (Israel) out of Matzarayam (Egypt)?"

He amar (spoke), "Certainly I will be with you. This will be the awath (sign / mark / miracle) to you, that I have shalach (send) you: when you have brought the im (nation / people) out of Matzarayam (Egypt), you shall ibad (servant) Alahayam on this har (mountain)."

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to Alahayam, "Behold, when I bawaa (come) to the banay (sons) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and amar (spoke) them, 'The Alahayam of your ab (father) has shalach (send) me to you;' and they ask me, 'What is his sham (name)?' What should I amar (spoke) them?"
Alahayam amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "I AM WHO I AM," and he amar (spoke), "You shall amar (spoke) the banay (sons) of Yashar-Al (Israel) this: 'I AM has shalach (send) me to you.'"

Alahayam amar (spoke) moreover to Mashah (Moses), "You shall amar (spoke) the banay (sons) of Yashar-Al (Israel) this, 'Yahawah, the Alahayam of your ab (father), the Alahayam of Abaraham (Abraham), the Alahayam of Yatzachaq (Isaac), and the Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob), has shalach (send) me to you.' This is my sham (name) iwalam (forever), and this is my zakar (remember) to all dawar (generation / age / period).

Yalak (go), and asap (gather) the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel) asap (together), and amar (spoke) them, 'Yahawah, the Alahayam of your ab (father), the Alahayam of Abaraham (Abraham), of Yatzachaq (Isaac), and of Yaiqab (Jacob), has raah (see) to me, amar (spoke), "I paqad (visit) surely paqad (visit) you, and seen that which is ishah (make) to you in Matzarayam (Egypt);

And I have amar (spoke), I will ilah (go up / offer) you up out of the inay (affliction) of Matzarayam (Egypt) to the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kanainay (Canaanite), the Chathay (Hittite), the Amaray (Amorite), the Parazay (Perizzite), the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite), to a aratz (Earth/land) zawab (flow) with chalab (milk) and dabash (honey)."'

They will shamai (hearken / hear) to your qawal (sound / voice), and you shall bawaa (come), you and the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel), to the malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and you shall amar (spoke) him, 'Yahawah, the Alahayam of the ibarayayam (hebrews), has qarah (met) with us. Now please yalak (let) us go shalawash (three) yamayam (days)' darak (journey) into the madabar (wilderness), that we may zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah, our Alahayam.'
I yadai (know) that the malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt) won't nathan (give) you permission to halak (move), no, not by a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand).

I will shalach (send) out my yad (hand) and nakah (strike) Matzaray (Egypt) with all my palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) which I will ishah (make) in its middle and achar (other) that he will shalach (send) you go.
I will nathan (give) this im (nation / people) favor in the iyan (eye) of the Matzaray (Egyptians), and it will happen that when you yalak (go), you shall not yalak (go) empty-handed.

But every ayashah (woman / wife) shall shaal (ask) of her neighbor, and of her who visits her bayath (house), kalay (jewels) of kasap (silver), kalay (jewels) of zahab (gold), and shamalah (clothing); and you shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) them on your ban (son), and on your banath (daughter). You shall plunder the Ban (Egyptians)."

Mashah (Moses) inah (answer / respond), "But, behold, they will not aman (believe / have faith) me, nor shamai (hearken / hear) to my qawal (sound / voice); for they will amar (spoke), ‘Yahawah has not raah (see) to you.'"
Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, "What is that in your yad (hand)?" He amar (spoke), "A matah (staff / rod / tribe)."
He amar (spoke), "shalak (throw) it on the aratz (Earth/land)." He shalak (threw) it on the aratz (Earth/land), and it became a snake; and Mashah (Moses) ran nawas (away) from it.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "shalach (send) out your yad (hand), and achaz (take) it by the zanab (tail)." He shalach (send) out his yad (hand), and chazaq (took) hold of it, and it became a matah (staff / rod / tribe) in his kap (hand).

"That they may aman (believe / have faith) that Yahawah, the Alahayam of their ab (father), the Alahayam of Abaraham (Abraham), the Alahayam of Yatzachaq (Isaac), and the Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob), has raah (see) to you."

Yahawah amar (spoke) iwad (more/again) to him, "Now bawaa (come) your yad (hand) inside your cloak." He bawaa (come) his yad (hand) inside his cloak, and when he yatzaa (go out / come out) it out, behold, his yad (hand) was tzarai (leprous), as white as shalag (snow).

He amar (spoke), "shawab (turn back / repent) your yad (hand) inside your cloak again." He shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand) inside his cloak again, and when he yatzaa (go out / come out) it out of his cloak, behold, it had shawab (turn back / repent) again as his other bashar (flesh).

"It will happen, if they will neither aman (believe / have faith) you nor shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of the raashawan (first) awath (sign / mark / miracle), that they will aman (believe / have faith) the qawal (sound / voice) of the acharawan (latter) awath (sign / mark / miracle).

It will happen, if they will not aman (believe / have faith) even these shanayam (two) athawath (signs), neither shamai (hearken / hear) to your qawal (sound / voice), that you shall laqach (take / seize) of the mayam (Waters) of the yaar (river), and shapak (pour) it on the yabashah (dry land) land. The mayam (Waters) which you laqach (take / seize) out of the yaar (river) will become dam (blood) on the dry yabashath (land)."

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to Yahawah, "O Adanay, I am not dabar (word / matter), neither shalashawam (before) az (now), nor since you have dabar (word / matter) to your ibad (servant); for I am kabad (slow) of pah (speech), and of a kabad (slow) lashawan (tongue / language)."

Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, "Who shawam (place / establish / appoint) adam (man's) pah (mouth)? Or who shawam (place / establish / appoint) alam (one) mute, or charash (deaf), or paqach (seeing), or iwar (blind)? Isn't it I, Yahawah?
Now therefore yalak (go), and I will be with your pah (mouth), and yarah (teach) you what you shall dabar (word / matter)."
He amar (spoke), "Oh, Adanay, please shalach (send) someone else."

The ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah was charah (hot with anger) against Mashah (Moses), and he amar (spoke), "What about Aharawan (Aaron), your ach (brother/kinsman), the Lawayay (Levite)? I yadai (know) that he can dabar (word / matter) dabar (word / matter). Also, behold, he yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) you. When he raah (see) you, he will be shamach (glad) in his lab (heart).

You shall dabar (word / matter) to him, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the dabarayam (words) in his pah (mouth). I will be with your pah (mouth), and with his pah (mouth), and will yarah (teach) you what you shall ishah (make).
He will be your dabar (word / matter) to the im (nation / people); and it will happen, that he will be to you a pah (mouth), and you will be to him as Alahayam.
You shall laqach (take / seize) this matah (staff / rod / tribe) in your yad (hand), with which you shall ishah (make) the athath (signs)."

Mashah (Moses) yalak (went) and shawab (turn back / repent) to Yathar (Jethro) his father-in-law, and amar (spoke) to him, "Please yalak (let) me go and shawab (turn back / repent) to my ach (brother/kinsman) who are in Matzarayam (Egypt), and raah (see) iwad (more/again) they are still chay (life)." Yatharaw (Jethro) amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "yalak (go) in shalawam (peace / safety)."

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses) in Madayan (Midian), "yalak (go), shawab (turn back / repent) into Matzarayam (Egypt); for all the mathaw (men) who baqash (sought) your napash (soul) are mawath (death)."

Mashah (Moses) laqach (take / seize) his ayashah (woman / wife) and his ban (son), and rakab (set) them on a donkey, and he shawab (turn back / repent) to the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt). Mashah (Moses) laqach (take / seize) Alahayam matah (staff / rod / tribe) in his yad (hand).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "When you yalak (go) shawab (turn back / repent) into Matzarayam (Egypt), raah (see) that you ishah (make) panayam (face) Paraih (Pharaoh) all the mapathayam (wonders) which I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) in your yad (hand), but I will chazaq (harden) his lab (heart) and he will not let the im (nation / people) shalach (send).
You shall amar (spoke) Paraih (Pharaoh), ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, Yashar-Al (Israel) is my ban (son), my bakawar (firstborn),

And I have amar (spoke) to you, "Let my ban (son) shalach (send), that he may ibad (servant) me;" and you have maan (refused) to shalach (send) him go. Behold, I will harag (kill) your ban (son), your bakawar (firstborn).'"
It happened on the darak (way) at a malawan (lodging) place, that Yahawah pagash (met) Moses and wanted to mawath (death) him.

Then Tzaparah (Zipporah) laqach (take / seize) a tzar (flint), and karath (cut) off the iralah (foreskin) of her ban (son), and nagai (cast) it at his ragal (feet / foot); and she amar (spoke), "Surely you are a chathan (bridegroom) of dam (blood) to me."
So he let him rapah (alone). Then she amar (spoke), "You are a chathan (bridegroom) of dam (blood)," because of the mawalah (circumcision).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Aharawan (Aaron), "yalak (go) into the madabar (wilderness) to qaraah (meet) Mashah (Moses)." He yalak (went), and pagash (met) him on Alahayam har (mountain), and nashaq (kissed) him.
Mashah (Moses) nagad (told) Aharawan (Aaron) all the dabaray (words) of Yahawah with which he had shalach (send) him, and all the athath (signs) with which he had instructed him.
Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) yalak (went) and asap (gathered) together all the zaqanay (elders) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Aharawan (Aaron) dabar (word / matter) all the dabarayam (words) which Yahawah had dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), and ishah (make) the athath (signs) in the iyan (eye) of the im (nation / people).

The im (nation / people) aman (believe / have faith), and when they shamai (hearken / hear) that Yahawah paqad (visit) visited the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and that he raah (see) seen their inay (affliction), then they bowed their yaqadaw (heads) and shachah (worshiped).

Afterward Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) came, and amar (spoke) to Paraih (Pharaoh), "This is what Yahawah, the Alahayam of Israel, yaamaraw (says), ‘Let my im (nation / people) shalach (send), that they may hold a feast to me in the madabar (wilderness).'"

Paraih (Pharaoh) amar (spoke), "Who is Yahawah, that I should shamai (hearken / hear) to his qawal (sound / voice) to let Yashar-Al (Israel) shalach (send)? I don't yadai (know) Yahawah, and moreover I will not let Yashar-Al (Israel) shalach (send)."

They amar (spoke), "The Alahayam of the ibarayam (hebrews) has qaraa (called) with us. Please yalak (let) us go shalawash (three) yamayam (days)' darak (journey) into the madabar (wilderness), and zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah, our Alahayam, lest he pagai (fall) on us with dabar (word / matter), or with the charab (sword)."

The malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt) amar (spoke) to them, "Why do you, Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron), take the im (nation / people) from their maishah (work)? Yalak (get) back to your sabalah (burdens)!"
Paraih (Pharaoh) amar (spoke), "Behold, the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land) are now many, and you make them shabath (shabath / rest) from their sabalah (burdens)."
The same yawam (day) Paraih (Pharaoh) tzawah (commanded) the nagashayam (taskmasters) of the im (nation / people), and their shatar (officers), amar (spoke),

"You shall no longer nathan (give) the im (nation / people) thaban (straw) to laban (make) labanah (brick), as shalashawam (before). Yalak (let) them go and qashash (gather) thaban (straw) for themselves.

The number of the labanayam (bricks), which they ishah (make) shalashawam (before), you require from them. You shall not garai (diminish) anything of it, for they are rapah (idle); therefore they tzaiq (cry), amar (spoke), ‘yalak (let) us go and zabach (sacrifice) to our Alahayam.'
Let heavier ibadah (work) be kabad (laid) on the anashayam (men), that they may ishah (make) therein; and don't let them pay any attention to shaqar (lying) dabaray (words)."

The nagashay (taskmasters) of the im (nation / people) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and their shatar (officers), and they amar (spoke) to the im (nation / people), amar (spoke), "This is what Paraih (Pharaoh) yaamaraw (says): ‘I will not nathan (give) you thaban (straw).
Yalak (go) yourselves, laqach (take / seize) thaban (straw) ashar (who/that) you can matzaa (find) it, for nothing of your ibadah (work) shall be garai (diminished).'"
So the im (nation / people) were pawatz (scattered) abroad throughout all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) to qashash (gather) qash (stubble) for thaban (straw).
The nagashayam (taskmasters) were urgent amar (spoke), "Fulfill your maishah (work) quota yawam (day), as when there was thaban (straw)!"

The shataray (officers) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), whom Paraih (Pharaoh's) nagashay (taskmasters) had shawam (place / establish / appoint) over them, were nakah (beaten), and amar (spoke), "Why haven't you kalah (complete / finish) your quota both thamawal (yesterday) and today, in laban (making) brick as shalashawam (before)?"

Then the shataray (officers) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) bawaa (come) and tzaiq (cried) to Paraih (Pharaoh), amar (spoke), "Why ishah (make) you deal this way with your ibad (servant)?

No thaban (straw) is nathan (give) to your ibad (servant), and they amar (spoke) us, ‘ishah (make) labanah (brick)!' And behold, your ibad (servant) are nakah (beaten); but the chataa (fault) is in your own im (nation / people)."
But he amar (spoke), "You are rapah (idle)! You are rapah (idle)! Therefore you amar (spoke), ‘yalak (let) us go and zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah.'
Yalak (go) therefore now, and ibad (servant), for no thaban (straw) shall be nathan (give) to you, yet you shall nathan (give) the same number of labanayam (bricks)!"

The shataray (officers) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) raah (see) that they were in rai (trouble), when it was amar (spoke), "You shall not garai (diminish) anything from your yawam (day) quota of labanah (bricks)!"
They pagai (met) Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron), who natzab (stood) in the qaraah (way), as they yatzaa (go out / come out) out from Paraih (Pharaoh):

And they amar (spoke) to them, "May Yahawah raah (see) at you, and shapat (judge / judgement), because you have made us a stench to be baash (abhorred) in the iyanay (eyes) of Paraih (Pharaoh), and in the iyanay (eyes) of his ibad (servant), to nathan (give) a charab (sword) in their yad (hand) to harag (kill) us."

Mashah (Moses) shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "Adanay, why have you raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) trouble on this im (nation / people)? Why is it that you have shalach (send) me?

For since I bawaa (come) to Paraih (Pharaoh) to dabar (word / matter) in your sham (name), he has raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) trouble on this im (nation / people); neither have you natzal (delivered) your im (nation / people) at natzal (all)."

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "Now you shall raah (see) what I will ishah (make) to Paraih (Pharaoh), for by a chazaq (strong) yad (hand) he shall shalach (send) them go, and by a chazaq (strong) yad (hand) he shall garash (drive) them out of his aratz (Earth/land)."
Alahayam dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), and amar (spoke) to him, "I am Yahawah;
And I raah (see) to Abaraham (Abraham), to Yatzachaq (Isaac), and to Yaiqab (Jacob), as Al Shaday; but by my sham (name) Yahawah I was not yadai (known) to them.
I have also qawam (rise up) my barayath (covenant) with them, to nathan (give) them the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), the aratz (Earth/land) of their travels, in which they lived as aliens.

Moreover I have shamai (hearken / hear) the naaqah (groaning) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), whom the Matzarayam (Egyptians) ibad (servant) in bondage, and I have zakar (remember) my barayath (covenant).

Therefore amar (spoke) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), ‘I am Yahawah, and I will yatzaa (go out / come out) you out from under the sabalath (burdens) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and I will natzal (rid) you out of their ibadah (bondage), and I will gaal (redeem) you with an natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm), and with gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shapatayam (judgments):

And I will laqach (take / seize) you to me for a im (nation / people), and I will be to you a Alahayam; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who yatzaa (go out / come out) you out from under the sabalawath (burdens) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians).

I will bawaa (come) you into the aratz (Earth/land) which I nashaa (lift) to nathan (give) to Abaraham (Abraham), to Yatzachaq (Isaac), and to Yaiqab (Jacob); and I will nathan (give) it to you for a mawarashah (heritage): I am Yahawah.'"

Mashah (Moses) dabar (word / matter) so to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), but they didn't shamai (hearken / hear) to Mashah (Moses) for qatzar (anguish) of rawach (spirit / wind), and for qashah (rough / hard) ibadah (bondage).
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),
"Bawaa (come) in, dabar (word / matter) to Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), that he let the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shalach (send) out of his aratz (Earth/land)."

Mashah (Moses) dabar (word / matter) panayam (face) Yahawah, amar (spoke), "Behold, the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) haven't shamai (hearken / hear) to me. How then shall Paraih (Pharaoh) shamai (hearken / hear) to me, who am of iral (uncircumcised) shapathayam (lips)?"

Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses) and to Aharawan (Aaron), and gave them a tzawah (command) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and to Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), to yatzaa (go out / come out) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

These are the raashay (heads) of their ab (father)' bayath (house). The banay (sons) of Raawaban (Reuben) the bakawar (firstborn) of Yashar-Al (Israel): Chanawak (Hanoch), and Palawaa (Pallu), Chatzarawan (Hezron), and Karamay (Carmi); these are the mashapachath (families) of Raawaban (Reuben).

The banay (sons) of Shamaiwan (Simeon): Yamawaal (Jemuel), and Yamayan (Jamin), and Ahad (Ohad), and Yakayan (Jachin), and Tzachar (Zohar), and Shaawal (Shaul) the ban (son) of a Kanainay (Canaanite) woman; these are the mashapachath (families) of Shamaiwan (Simeon).

These are the shamawath (names) of the banay (sons) of Laway (Levi) according to their thawaladah (generation): Garashawan (Gershon), and Qahath (Kohath), and Mararay (Merari); and the shanay (years) of the chay (life) of Laway (Levi) were one maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - shabai (seven) shanay (years).
The banay (sons) of Garashawan (Gershon): Labanay (Libni) and Shamaiy (Shimei), according to their mashapachah (tribe / clan / family).

The banay (sons) of Qahath (Kohath): Imaram (Amram), and Yatzahar (Izhar), and Chabarawan (Hebron), and Izayaal (Uzziel); and the shanay (years) of the chay (life) of Qahath (Kohath) were one maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - shalawash (three) shanay (years).
The banay (sons) of Mararay (Merari): Machalay (Mahli) and Mawashay (Mushi). These are the mashapachath (families) of the Laway (Levites) according to their thawaladah (generation).

Imaram (Amram) laqach (take / seize) Yawakabad (Jochebed) his dawadah (father's) sister to himself as ayashah (woman / wife); and she yalad (birth / begot) him Aharawan (Aaron) and Mashah (Moses): and the shanay (years) of the chay (life) of Imaram (Amram) were a maah (hundred) and shalawashayam (thirty) - shabai (seven) shanay (years).
The banay (sons) of Yatzahar (Izhar): Qarach (Korah), and Napag (Nepheg), and Zakaray (Zichri).
The banay (sons) of Izayaal (Uzziel): Mayashaal (Mishael), and Alayatzapan (Elzaphan), and Satharay (Sithri).

Aharawan (Aaron) laqach (take / seize) Alayashabai (Elisheba), the banath (daughter) of Imayanadab (Amminadab), the achawath (sister) of Nachashawan (Nahshon), as his ayashah (woman / wife); and she yalad (birth / begot) him Nadab (Nadab) and Abayahawaa (Abihu), Alaizar (Eleazar) and Ayathamar (Ithamar).
The banay (sons) of Qarach (Korah): Asayar (Assir), and Alaqanah (Elkanah), and Abayaasap (Abiasaph); these are the mashapachath (families) of the qarachay (korahites).

Alaizar (Eleazar) Aharawan (Aaron's) ban (son) laqach (take / seize) one of the banawath (daughters) of Pawatayaal (Putiel) as his ayashah (woman / wife); and she yalad (birth / begot) him Payanachas (Phinehas). These are the raashay (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' houses of the Lawayay (Levites) according to their mashapachah (tribe / clan / family).

These are that Aharawan (Aaron) and Mashah (Moses), to whom Yahawah amar (spoke), "yatzaa (go out / come out) out the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) from the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) according to their tzabaa (troop)."

These are those who dabar (word / matter) to Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), to yatzaa (go out / come out) out the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) from Matzarayam (Egypt). These are that Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron).
It happened on the yawam (day) when Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt),

That Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke), "I am Yahawah. Dabar (word / matter) to Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt) all that I dabar (word / matter) to you."
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) panayam (face) Yahawah, "Behold, I am of iral (uncircumcised) shapathayam (lips), and how shall Paraih (Pharaoh) shamai (hearken / hear) to me?"

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "raah (see), I nathan (give) made you as Alahayam to Paraih (Pharaoh); and Aharawan (Aaron) your ach (brother/kinsman) shall be your nabayaa (prophet/prophecy).

You shall dabar (word / matter) all that I tzawah (command) you; and Aharawan (Aaron) your ach (brother/kinsman) shall dabar (word / matter) to Paraih (Pharaoh), that he shalach (send) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) go out of his aratz (Earth/land).
I will harden Paraih (Pharaoh's) lab (heart), and rabah (multiply) my awath (sign / mark / miracle) and my mawapath (wonders) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

But Paraih (Pharaoh) will not shamai (hearken / hear) to you, and I will nathan (give) my yad (hand) on Matzarayam (Egypt), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out my tzabaa (troop), my im (nation / people) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) by gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shapatayam (judgments).

The Matzarayam (Egyptians) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on Matzarayam (Egypt), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) from thawak (midst) them."
Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) ishah (make) so. As Yahawah tzawah (commanded) them, so they ishah (make).

Mashah (Moses) was shamanayam (eighty) shanah (years) ban (son), and Aharawan (Aaron) shamanayam (eighty)- shalawash (three) shanah (years) ban (son), when they dabar (word / matter) to Paraih (Pharaoh).
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses) and to Aharawan (Aaron), amar (spoke),

"When Paraih (Pharaoh) dabar (word / matter) to you, amar (spoke), ‘nathan (give) a mawapath (miracle)!' Then you shall amar (spoke) Aharawan (Aaron), ‘laqach (take / seize) your matah (staff / rod / tribe), and shalak (cast) it down panayam (face) Paraih (Pharaoh), that it become a thanayan (serpent).'"

Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) bawaa (come) in to Paraih (Pharaoh), and they ishah (make) so, as Yahawah had tzawah (commanded): and Aharawan (Aaron) shalak (cast) down his matah (staff / rod / tribe) panayam (face) Paraih (Pharaoh) and panayam (face) his ibad (servant), and it became a thanayan (serpent).

Then Paraih (Pharaoh) also qaraa (called) for the chakam (wise) men and the makashapayam (sorcerers). They also, the charatamay (magicians) of Matzarayam (Egypt), ishah (make) the same thing with their lahat (enchantments).

For they ayash (man / husband) shalak (cast) down their matah (staff / rod / tribe), and they became thanayanam (serpents): but Aharawan (Aaron's) matah (staff / rod / tribe) balai (swallowed) up their matah (staff / rod / tribe).
Paraih (Pharaoh's) lab (heart) was chazaq (hardened), and he didn't shamai (hearken / hear) to them; as Yahawah had dabar (word / matter).
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "Paraih (Pharaoh's) lab (heart) is stubborn. He maan (refuses) to let the im (nation / people) shalach (send).

Go to Paraih (Pharaoh) in the baqar (morning). Behold, he yatzaa (go out / come out) out to the mayam (Waters); and you shall natzab (stand) by the yaar (river's) shapah (bank) to qaraah (meet) him; and the matah (staff / rod / tribe) which was hapak (turned) to a nachash (serpent) you shall laqach (take / seize) in your yad (hand).

You shall amar (spoke) him, ‘Yahawah, the Alahayam of the ibarayam (hebrews), has shalach (send) me to you, amar (spoke), "Let my im (nation / people) shalach (send), that they may ibad (servant) me in the madabar (wilderness):" and behold, until now you haven't shamai (hearken / hear).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "In this you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah. Behold, I will nakah (strike) with the matah (staff / rod / tribe) that is in my yad (hand) on the mayam (Waters) which are in the yaar (river), and they shall be hapak (turned) to dam (blood).

The dagah (fish) that are in the yaar (river) shall mawath (death), and the yaar (river) shall become foul; and the Matzaray (Egyptians) shall loathe to shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters) from the yaar (river)."'"

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "Tell Aharawan (Aaron), ‘laqach (take / seize) your matah (staff / rod / tribe), and natah (stretch) out your yad (hand) over the mayamay (waters) of Matzarayam (Egypt), over their yaar (rivers), over their streams, and over their maqawah (gathering / collection), and over all their agam (ponds) of mayam (Waters), that they may become dam (blood); and there shall be dam (blood) throughout all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), both in vessels of itz (wood) and in vessels of aban (stone).'"

Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) ishah (make) so, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded); and he rawam (will lift up) up the matah (staff / rod / tribe), and nakah (struck) the mayam (Waters) that were in the yaar (river), in the iyan (eye) of Paraih (Pharaoh), and in the iyan (eye) of his ibad (servant); and all the mayam (Waters) that were in the yaar (river) were hapak (turned) to dam (blood).

The dagah (fish) that were in the yaar (river) mawath (death); and the yaar (river) became foul, and the Matzarayam (Egyptians) couldn't shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters) from the yaar (river); and the dam (blood) was throughout all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

The charatamay (magicians) of Matzarayam (Egypt) ishah (make) the same thing with their lat (enchantments); and Paraih (Pharaoh's) lab (heart) was chazaq (hardened), and he didn't shamai (hearken / hear) to them; as Yahawah had dabar (word / matter).
Paraih (Pharaoh) panah (turn) and bawaa (come) into his bayath (house), and he didn't even shayath (put / appoint / make) zaath (this) to lab (heart).
All the Matzaray (Egyptians) chapar (dug) around the yaar (river) for mayam (Waters) to shathah (drinks); for they couldn't shathah (drinks) of the mayam (Waters) of the yaar (river).
Shabai (seven) yamayam (days) were malaa (fulfilled), achar (other) Yahawah had nakah (struck) the yaar (river).
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), natah (go) in to Yahawah (Pharaoh), and amar (spoke) him, "This is what Yahawah amar (spoke), ‘Let my people natah (go), that they may serve me.
If you refuse to natah (let) them go, behold, I will plague all your yad (hand) with tzaparadai (frogs):

And the river shall swarm with tzaparadaiyam (frogs), which shall ilah (go up / offer) up and ilah (go up / offer) into your house, and into your bedroom, and on your bed, and into the house of your servants, and on your people, and into your ovens, and into your kneading troughs:
And the tzaparadaiyam (frogs) shall come up both on you, and on your im (nation / people), and on all your servants.'"

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "amar (spoke) Aaron, ‘Stretch out your hand with your rod over the yaar (rivers), over the streams, and over the pools, and cause tzaparadaiyam (frogs) to come up on the land of Egypt.'"
Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt; and the frogs machar (came) up, and covered the land of Egypt.
The magicians did the same thing with their enchantments, and sawar (brought) up tzaparadaiyam (frogs) on the land of Egypt.

Then Paraih (Pharaoh) tzaiq (called) for Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron), and dabar (word / matter), "Entreat Yahawah, that he yatzaa (go out / come out) away the tzaparadaiyam (frogs) from me, and from my people; and I will let the people yatzaa (go out / come out), that they may sacrifice to Yahawah."

Mashah (Moses) dabar (word / matter) to Yahawah (Pharaoh), "I give you the honor of setting the time that I should pray for you, and for your servants, and for your people, that the tzaparadaiyam (frogs) be mawath (death) from you and your bathayam (houses), and remain in the river only."
He said, "Tomorrow." He said, "Be it according to your word, that you may know that there is none like Yahawah our Alahayam.
The frogs shall depart from you, and from your houses, and from your servants, and from your people. They shall remain in the river only."
Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) natah (went) out from Yahawah (Pharaoh), and Mashah (Moses) cried to Yahawah al (toward) the frogs which he had brought on Yahawah (Pharaoh).
Yahawah ishah (make) according to the word of Moses, and the frogs died out of the houses, out of the courts, and out of the aratz (Earth/land).
They ishah (make) them together in heaps, and the land stank.
But when Paraih (Pharaoh) saw that there was a respite, he chazaq (hardened) his lab (heart), and didn't shamai (hearken / hear) to them, as Yahawah had dabar (word / matter).
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "amar (spoke) Aaron, ‘shalach (send) out your rod, and strike the dust of the earth, that it may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.'"

They did so; and Aaron shalach (send) out his hand with his rod, and struck the dust of the adamah (earth), and there were lice on man, and on animal; all the dust of the adamah (earth) became lice throughout all the adamah (land) of Matzaray (Egypt).
The magicians tried with their enchantments to produce lice, but they couldn't. There were lice on yadai (man), and on animal.
Then the magicians said to Pharaoh, "This is the finger of Alahayam:" and Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he didn't listen to them; as Yahawah had spoken.

Yahawah said to Moses, "Rise up early in the morning, and panayam (face) panayam (face) Paraih (Pharaoh); behold, he bawaa (come) out to the water; and tell him, ‘This is what Yahawah says, "Let my panay (people) ishah (make), that they may ishah (make) me.

Else, if you will not let my zabachaw (people) yalak (go), behold, I will send swarms of flies on you, and on your servants, and on your zabachaw (people), and into your zabachaw (houses): and the zabachaw (houses) of the Egyptians shall be full of swarms of flies, and also the aratz (Earth/land) whereon they are.

I will kawan (set) apart in that day the land of Goshen, in which my nazabach (people) dwell, that no swarms of flies shall be there; to the end you may know that I am Yahawah in the midst of the earth.
I will put a division between my zabachanaw (people) and your zabachanaw (people): by tomorrow shall this sign be."'"

Yahawah did so; and there yalak (came) grievous swarms of flies into the zabach (house) of Paraih (Pharaoh), and into his servants' zabachatham (houses): and in all the land of Egypt the land was corrupted by reason of the swarms of flies.
Paraih (Pharaoh) amar (spoke) for Mashah (Moses) and for Aaron, and amar (spoke), "yatzaa (go out / come out), zabach (sacrifice) to your Alahayam in the land!"

Mashah (Moses) said, "It isn't appropriate to do so; for we shall sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians to Yahawah our Alahayam. Behold, shall we sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, and won't they stone us?
We will ishah (make) three days' ishah (make) into the wilderness, and ishah (make) to Yahawah our Alahayam, as he shall command us."
Paraih (Pharaoh) said, "I will shalach (send) you go, that you may sacrifice to Yahawah your Alahayam in the wilderness, only you shall not shalach (send) very far away. Pray for me."

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke), "Behold, I yatzaa (go out / come out) out from you, and I will ithar (pray) to Yahawah that the irab (evening) of flies may sawar (depart) from Paraih (Pharaoh), from his ibad (servant), and from his im (nation / people), machar (tomorrow); only don't let Paraih (Pharaoh) hathal (deal) deceitfully any more in not letting the im (nation / people) shalach (send) to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah."
Mashah (Moses) yatzaa (go out / come out) out from Paraih (Pharaoh), and ithar (prayed) to Yahawah.

Yahawah ishah (make) according to the dabar (word / matter) of Mashah (Moses), and he sawar (removed) the irab (evening) of flies from Paraih (Pharaoh), from his ibad (servant), and from his im (nation / people). There shaar (remained) not achad (one).
Paraih (Pharaoh) kabad (hardened) his lab (heart) paim (this) time also, and he didn't let the im (nation / people) shalach (send).

Then Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "bawaa (come) in to Paraih (Pharaoh), and dabar (word / matter) him, ‘This is what Yahawah, the Alahayam of the ibarayam (hebrews), amar (spoke): "Let my im (nation / people) shalach (send), that they may ibad (servant) me.
For if you maan (refuse) to shalach (send) them go, and chazaq (hold) them still,

Behold, the yad (hand) of Yahawah is on your livestock which are in the shadah (field), on the sawasayam (horses), on the donkeys, on the gamalayam (camels), on the baqar (morning), and on the tzaan (flocks) with a very kabad (grievous) dabar (word / matter).

Yahawah will palah (make) a distinction between the livestock of Yashar-Al (Israel) and the livestock of Matzarayam (Egypt); and nothing shall mawath (death) of all that belongs to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel)."'"
Yahawah shawam (place / establish / appoint) a mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) time, amar (spoke), "machar (tomorrow) Yahawah shall ishah (make) this thing in the aratz (Earth/land)."

Yahawah ishah (make) that thing on the next macharath (day); and all the livestock of Matzaray (Egypt) mawath (death), but of the livestock of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), not achad (one) mawath (death).

Paraih (Pharaoh) shalach (send), and, behold, there was not so much as achad (one) of the livestock of the Yashar-Al (Israelites) mawath (death). But the lab (heart) of Paraih (Pharaoh) was stubborn, and he didn't let the im (nation / people) shalach (send).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses) and to Aharawan (Aaron), "laqach (take / seize) to you chapan (handfuls) of ashes of the kabashan (furnace), and let Mashah (Moses) zaraq (sprinkle) it toward the sky in the iyan (eye) of Paraih (Pharaoh).

It shall become small abaq (dust) over all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and shall be a shachayan (boil) parach (breaking) out with boils on adam (man) and on animal, throughout all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt)."

They laqach (take / seize) ashes of the kabashan (furnace), and imad (stood) panayam (face) Paraih (Pharaoh); and Mashah (Moses) zaraq (sprinkled) it up toward the sky; and it became a shachayan (boil) parach (breaking) out with boils on adam (man) and on animal.

The charatamayam (magicians) couldn't imad (stand) panayam (face) Mashah (Moses) panayam (face) of the shachayan (boils); for the shachayan (boils) were on the charatamayam (magicians), and on all the Matzaray (Egyptians).
Yahawah chazaq (hardened) the lab (heart) of Paraih (Pharaoh), and he didn't shamai (hearken / hear) to them, as Yahawah had dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "shakam (rise) up early in the baqar (morning), and yatzab (stand) panayam (face) Paraih (Pharaoh), and amar (spoke) him, ‘This is what Yahawah, the Alahayam of the ibarayam (hebrews), amar (spoke): "Let my im (nation / people) shalach (send), that they may ibad (servant) me.

For paim (this) time I will shalach (send) all my magapah (plagues) against your lab (heart), against your officials, and against your im (nation / people); that you may yadai (know) that there is none like me in all the aratz (Earth/land).

For now I would have shalach (send) out my yad (hand), and nakah (struck) you and your im (nation / people) with dabar (word / matter), and you would have been kachad (cut) off from the aratz (Earth/land);
But indeed for this cause I have imad (made) you stand: to show you my kach (strength / mighty / power), and that my sham (name) may be sapar (book) throughout all the aratz (Earth/land);
As you still salal (exalt) yourself against my im (nation / people), that you won't shalach (send) them go.

Behold, machar (tomorrow) about this ith (time) I will cause it to matar (rain) a very kabad (grievous) barad (hail), such as has not been in Matzarayam (Egypt) man (from) the yawam (day) it was founded even until now.

Now therefore command that all of your livestock and all that you have in the shadah (field) be brought into shelter. Every adam (man) and animal that is matzaa (found) in the shadah (field), and isn't asap (brought) bayath (house), the barad (hail) shall yarad (come) down on them, and they shall mawath (death)."'"

Those who yaraa (fear / be afraid) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah among the ibaday (servants) of Paraih (Pharaoh) made their ibaday (servants) and their livestock nawas (flee) into the bathayam (houses).
Whoever didn't respect the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah izab (left) his ibad (servant) and his livestock in the shadah (field).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "natah (stretch) out your yad (hand) toward the sky, that there may be barad (hail) in all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), on adam (man), and on animal, and on every ishab (herb) of the shadah (field), throughout the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt)."

Mashah (Moses) natah (stretched) out his matah (staff / rod / tribe) toward the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and Yahawah nathan (give) qawal (sound / voice), barad (hail), and lightning flashed down to the aratz (Earth/land). Yahawah matar (rained) barad (hail) on the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
So there was very severe barad (hail), and lightning mixed with the barad (hail), such as had not been in all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) since it became a gaway (heathen / nation).

The barad (hail) nakah (struck) throughout all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) all that was in the shadah (field), both adam (man) and animal; and the barad (hail) nakah (struck) every ishab (herb) of the shadah (field), and shabar (broke) every itz (tree) of the shadah (field).
Only in the aratz (Earth/land) of Gashan (Goshen), where the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) were, there was no barad (hail).

Paraih (Pharaoh) shalach (send), and qaraa (called) for Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron), and amar (spoke) to them, "I have chataa (sinned) paim (this) time. Yahawah is tzadayaq (righteous), and I and my im (nation / people) are rashai (wicked).
Ithar (pray) to Yahawah; for there rab (has) been enough of alahayam (God) qalath (thunderings) and barad (hail). I will shalach (send) you go, and you shall imad (stay) no yasap (longer)."

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to him, "As soon as I yatzaa (go out / come out) gone out of the iyar (city), I will parash (spread) abroad my kap (hands) to Yahawah. The qalawath (thunders) shall chadal (cease), neither shall there be any more barad (hail); that you may yadai (know) that the aratz (Earth/land) is Yahawah.
But as for you and your ibad (servant), I yadai (know) that you don't yet yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah Alahayam."
The pashathah (flax) and the shairah (barley) were nakah (struck), for the shairah (barley) was in the abayab (ear), and the pashathah (flax) was in bloom.
But the chatah (wheat) and the spelt were not nakah (struck), for they had not apayal (grown) up.

Mashah (Moses) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the iyar (city) from Paraih (Pharaoh), and parash (spread) abroad his kap (hands) to Yahawah; and the qalawath (thunders) and barad (hail) chadal (ceased), and the matar (rain) was not nathak (poured) on the aratz (Earth/land).

When Paraih (Pharaoh) raah (see) that the matar (rain) and the barad (hail) and the qalath (thunders) were chadal (ceased), he chataa (sinned) yet more, and kabad (hardened) his lab (heart), he and his ibad (servant).

The lab (heart) of Paraih (Pharaoh) was chazaq (hardened), and he didn't let the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shalach (send), just as Yahawah had dabar (word / matter) yad (hand) Mashah (Moses).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "bawaa (come) in to Paraih (Pharaoh), for I kabad (have) hardened his lab (heart), and the lab (heart) of his ibad (servant), that I may show these my awath (sign / mark / miracle) in their qarab (among / near),

And that you may sapar (book) in the azan (ear) of your ban (son), and of your ban (son) ban (son), what things I have ilal (done) to Matzarayam (Egypt), and my awath (sign / mark / miracle) which I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) among them; that you may yadai (know) that I am Yahawah."

Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) bawaa (come) in to Paraih (Pharaoh), and amar (spoke) to him, "This is what Yahawah, the Alahayam of the ibarayam (hebrews), yaamaraw (says): ‘How mathay (long) will you maan (refuse) to inah (oppress / afflict) yourself panayam (face) me? Let my im (nation / people) shalach (send), that they may ibad (servant) me.
Or kay (surely), if you maan (refuse) to let my im (nation / people) shalach (send), behold, machar (tomorrow) I will bawaa (come) arabah (locusts) into your country,

And they shall kasah (cover) the surface of the aratz (Earth/land), so that one won't be yakal (able) to raah (see) the aratz (Earth/land). They shall akal (eat) the yathar (residue) of that which has palayatah (escaped), which shaar (remains) to you from the barad (hail), and shall akal (eat) every itz (tree) which tzamach (grows) for you out of the shadah (field).

Your bathay (houses) shall be filled, and the bathay (houses) of all your ibad (servant), and the bathay (houses) of all the Matzaray (Egyptians); as neither your abawath (fathers) nor your abawath (fathers)' abawath (fathers) raah (see) seen, since the yawam (day) that they were on the adamah (earth) to this yawam (day).'" He panah (turn), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out from Paraih (Pharaoh).

Paraih (Pharaoh's) ibaday (servants) amar (spoke) to him, "How long will this man be a mawaqash (snare) to us? Let the zah (this / that / these) shalach (send), that they may ibad (servant) Yahawah, their Alahayam. Don't you yet yadai (know) that Matzarayam (Egypt) is abad (destroy / perish)?"

Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) were shawab (turn back / repent) again to Paraih (Pharaoh), and he amar (spoke) to them, "yalak (go), ibad (servant) Yahawah your Alahayam; but who are those who will halak (move)?"

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke), "We will yalak (go) with our nair (young) and with our zaqan (old); with our ban (son) and with our banath (daughter), with our tzaan (flocks) and with our baqar (morning) will we yalak (go); for we must hold a chag (feast/festival) to Yahawah."
He amar (spoke) to them, "Yahawah be with you if I will shalach (send) you go with your little tap (ones)! Raah (see), rai (evil) is clearly before your panayam (face).
Not so! Yalak (go) now you who are gabarayam (men), and ibad (servant) Yahawah; for that is what you baqash (desire)!" They were garash (driven) out from Paraih (Pharaoh's) panayam (face).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "natah (stretch) out your yad (hand) over the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) for the arabah (locusts), that they may ilah (go up / offer) up on the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and akal (eat) every ishab (herb) of the aratz (Earth/land), even all that the barad (hail) has shaar (left)."

Mashah (Moses) natah (stretched) out his matah (staff / rod / tribe) over the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and Yahawah nahag (brought) an qadayam (east) rawach (spirit / wind) on the aratz (Earth/land) all that yawam (day), and all the layal (night); and when it was baqar (morning), the qadayam (east) rawach (spirit / wind) nashaa (lift) the arabah (locusts).

The arabah (locusts) ilah (go up / offer) up over all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and nawach (rested) in all the gabawal (border/boundary) of Matzarayam (Egypt). They were very kabad (grievous). Panayam (face) them there were no such arabah (locusts) as they, neither achar (other) them shall be such.

For they kasah (covered) the surface of the whole aratz (Earth/land), so that the aratz (Earth/land) was chashak (darkness), and they akal (eat) every ishab (herb) of the aratz (Earth/land), and all the paray (fruit) of the itz (trees) which the barad (hail) had yathar (left). There yathar (remained) nothing green, either itz (tree) or ishab (herb) of the shadah (field), through all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
Then Paraih (Pharaoh) qaraa (called) for Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) in mahar (haste), and he amar (spoke), "I have chataa (sinned) against Yahawah your Alahayam, and against you.
Now therefore please nashaa (lift) my chataah (sin) again, and ithar (pray) to Yahawah your Alahayam, that he may also sawar (take) away from me this mawath (death)."
He yatzaa (go out / come out) out from Paraih (Pharaoh), and ithar (prayed) to Yahawah.

Yahawah hapak (turned) an maad (exceeding) chazaq (strong) yam (sea/waters) rawach (spirit / wind), which nashaa (lift) up the arabah (locusts), and drove them into the sawap (red) yam (sea/waters). There shaar (remained) not achad (one) arabah (locust) in all the gabawal (border/boundary) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
But Yahawah chazaq (hardened) Paraih (Pharaoh's) lab (heart), and he didn't let the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shalach (send).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "natah (stretch) out your yad (hand) toward the sky, that there may be chashak (darkness) over the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), even chashak (darkness) which may be mashash (felt)."

Mashah (Moses) natah (stretched) out his yad (hand) toward the sky, and there was a apalah (thick) chashak (darkness) in all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) shalawash (three) yamayam (days).

They didn't raah (see) ayash (man / husband) ach (brother/kinsman), neither did anyone qawam (rise up) from his place for shalawash (three) yamayam (days); but all the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) had awar (light) in their mawashab (dwellings).

Paraih (Pharaoh) qaraa (called) to Mashah (Moses), and amar (spoke), "yalak (go), ibad (servant) Yahawah. Only let your tzaan (flocks) and your baqar (morning) yatzag (stay) behind. Let your little tap (ones) also yalak (go) with you."
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke), "You must also nathan (give) into our yad (hand) ishayanaw (sacrifices) and burnt ilawath (offerings), that we may ishah (make) to Yahawah our Alahayam.

Our livestock also shall yalak (go) with us. Not a parasah (hoof) shall be shaar (left) behind, for of it we must laqach (take / seize) to ibad (servant) Yahawah our Alahayam; and we don't yadai (know) with what we must ibad (servant) Yahawah, until we bawaa (come) there."
But Yahawah chazaq (hardened) Paraih (Pharaoh's) lab (heart), and he wouldn't shalach (send) them go.
Paraih (Pharaoh) amar (spoke) to him, "yalak (get) away from me! Be careful to raah (see) my panayam (face) no more; for in the yawam (day) you raah (see) my panayam (face) you shall mawath (death)!"
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke), "You have dabar (word / matter) kan (for sure). I will raah (see) your panayam (face) again no more."

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "Yet achad (one) nagai (plague) more will I bawaa (come) on Paraih (Pharaoh), and on Matzarayam (Egypt); afterwards he will shalach (send) you go. When he shalach (send) you go, he will garash (surely) garash (thrust) you out kalah (complete / finish).

Dabar (word / matter) now in the azanay (ears) of the im (nation / people), and let them shaal (ask) every ayash (man / husband) of his neighbor, and every ayashah (woman / wife) of her neighbor, kalay (jewels) of kasap (silver), and kalay (jewels) of zahab (gold)."

Yahawah nathan (give) the im (nation / people) favor in the iyan (eye) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians). Moreover the ayash (man / husband) Mashah (Moses) was very gadawal (very great/important/mighty) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), in the iyan (eye) of Paraih (Pharaoh's) ibaday (servants), and in the iyan (eye) of the im (nation / people).
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke), "This is what Yahawah amar (spoke): ‘About layal (midnight) I will yatzaa (go out / come out) out into the thawak (midst) of Matzarayam (Egypt),

And all the bakawar (firstborn) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) shall mawath (death), from the bakawar (firstborn) of Paraih (Pharaoh) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) on his kasaa (throne), even to the bakawar (firstborn) of the female servant who is achar (other) the rachah (mill); and all the bakawar (firstborn) of livestock.
There shall be a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) tzaiqah (cry) throughout all the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), such as there has not been, nor shall be any more.

But against any of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) a kalab (dog) won't even bark or charatz (move) its lashawan (tongue / language), against ayash (man / husband) or animal; that you may yadai (know) that Yahawah palah (makes) a distinction between the Matzarayam (Egyptians) and Yashar-Al (Israel).

All these your ibad (servant) shall yarad (come) down to me, and bow down themselves to me, amar (spoke), "yatzaa (go out / come out) out, with all the im (nation / people) who ragal (feet / foot) you;" and achar (other) that I will yatzaa (go out / come out) out.'" He yatzaa (go out / come out) out from Paraih (Pharaoh) in hot ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "Paraih (Pharaoh) won't shamai (hearken / hear) to you, that my mawapath (wonders) may be rabah (multiplied) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt)."

Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) ishah (make) all these mapathayam (wonders) panayam (face) Paraih (Pharaoh), and Yahawah chazaq (hardened) Paraih (Pharaoh's) lab (heart), and he didn't let the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shalach (send) out of his aratz (Earth/land).
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), amar (spoke),
"This chadash (month) shall be to you the raash (head) of chadashayam (months). It shall be the raashawan (first) chadash (month) of the shanah (year) to you.

Dabar (word / matter) to all the idah (congregation) of Yashar-Al (Israel), amar (spoke), ‘On the ishawar (tenth) day of this chadash (month), they shall laqach (take / seize) to them every ayash (man / husband) a shah (lamb), according to their abath (fathers)' bayath (house), a shah (lamb) for a bayath (house);

And if the bayath (house) is too mait (little) for a shah (lamb), then he and his neighbor qarawab (next) to his bayath (house) shall laqach (take / seize) one according to the makasah (number) of the napashath (souls); pah (according) to ayash (man / husband) everyone can eat you shall kasas (make) your count for the shah (lamb).
Your shah (lamb) shall be thamayam (complete / whole) blemish, a zakar (remember) a shanah (year) old. You shall laqach (take / seize) it from the kabashayam (sheep), or from the izayam (goats):

And you shall mashamarath (duty / watch) it until the fourteenth yawam (day) of the same chadash (month); and the kal (every) qahal (assembly) of the idah (congregation) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall shachat (kill) it at irab (evening).

They shall laqach (take / seize) some of the dam (blood), and nathan (give) it on the shanayam (two) doorposts and on the mashaqawap (lintel), on the bathayam (houses) in which they shall akal (eat) it.
They shall akal (eat) the bashar (flesh) in that layal (night), tzalay (roasted) with ash (fire), and unleavened matzah (bread). They shall akal (eat) it with marar (bitter) herbs.
Don't akal (eat) it naa (raw), nor bashal (boiled) at all with mayam (Waters), but tzalay (roasted) with ash (fire); with its raash (head), its karai (legs) and its inner qarab (among / near).
You shall yathar (let) nothing of it remain until the baqar (morning); but that which thawathayaraw (remains) of it until the baqar (morning) you shall sharap (burn) with ash (fire).

Kakah (this) is how you shall akal (eat) it: with your belt on your waist, your nail (shoes) on your ragal (feet / foot), and your maqal (staff) in your yad (hand); and you shall akal (eat) it in chapazawan (haste): it is Yahawah pasach (passover).

For I will ibar (pass over/through) through the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) in that layal (night), and will nakah (strike) all the bakawar (firstborn) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), both adam (man) and animal. Against all the Alahayam of Matzarayam (Egypt) I will ishah (make) shapatayam (judgments): I am Yahawah.

The dam (blood) shall be to you for a awath (sign / mark / miracle) on the bathayam (houses) where you are: and when I raah (see) the dam (blood), I will pasach (pass) over you, and there shall no nagap (plague) be on you to mashachayath (destroy) you, when I nakah (strike) the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

This yawam (day) shall be to you for a zakarawan (memorial), and you shall chagag (keep) it a chag (feast/festival) to Yahawah: throughout your dawar (generation / age / period) you shall chagag (keep) it a feast by an chaqah (ordinance) iwalam (forever).

"‘shabai (seven) yamayam (days) you shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread); even the raashawan (first) yawam (day) you shall shabath (shabath / rest) away yeast out of your bayath (house), for whoever thaakalaw (eats) chamatz (leavened) bread from the raashawan (first) yawam (day) until the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from Yashar-Al (Israel).

In the raashawan (first) yawam (day) there shall be to you a qadash (set apart / make holy) maqaraa (convocation), and in the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) a qadash (set apart / make holy) maqaraa (convocation); no kind of malaakah (work) shall be ishah (make) in them, except that which every napash (soul) must akal (eat), that only may be ishah (make) by you.

You shall shamar (keep/guard) the feast of unleavened matzah (bread); for in this same yawam (day) yatzaa (go out / come out) I brought your tzabaa (troop) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt): therefore you shall shamar (keep/guard) this yawam (day) throughout your dawar (generation / age / period) by an chaqah (ordinance) iwalam (forever).

In the raashawan (first) month, on the fourteenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month) at irab (evening), you shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread), until the isharayam (twenty) achad (one) yawam (day) of the chadash (month) at irab (evening).

There shall be no yeast matzaa (found) in your bayath (house) for shabai (seven) yamayam (days), for whoever akal (eat) that which is shaar (leavened), that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from the idah (congregation) of Yashar-Al (Israel), whether he be a foreigner, or one who is azarach (born) in the aratz (Earth/land).
You shall akal (eat) nothing chamatz (leavened). In all your habitations you shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread).'"

Then Mashah (Moses) qaraa (called) for all the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and amar (spoke) to them, "mashak (draw) out, and laqach (take / seize) tzaan (lambs) according to your mashapachah (tribe / clan / family), and shachat (kill) the pasach (passover).

You shall laqach (take / seize) a agadah (bunch) of azawab (hyssop), and tabal (dip) it in the dam (blood) that is in the basin, and nagai (strike) the mashaqawap (lintel) and the shanayam (two) doorposts with the dam (blood) that is in the basin; and ayash (man / husband) of you shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the pathach (door) of his bayath (house) until the baqar (morning).

For Yahawah will ibar (pass over/through) through to nagap (strike) the Matzarayam (Egyptians); and when he raah (see) the dam (blood) on the mashaqawap (lintel), and on the shanayam (two) doorposts, Yahawah will pasach (pass) over the pathach (door), and will not allow the destroyer to bawaa (come) in to your bayath (house) to nagap (strike) you.
You shall shamar (keep/guard) this thing for an chaq (statute) to you and to your ban (son) iwalam (forever).

It shall happen when you bawaa (come) come to the aratz (Earth/land) which Yahawah will nathan (give) you, according as he has dabar (word / matter), that you shall shamar (keep/guard) this ibadah (service).
It will happen, when your ban (son) ask you, ‘What do you mean by this ibadah (service)?'

That you shall amar (spoke), ‘It is the zabach (sacrifice) of Yahawah pasach (passover), who pasach (passed) over the bathay (houses) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) in Matzarayam (Egypt), when he nagap (struck) the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and spared our bathay (houses).'" The im (nation / people) bowed their qadad (heads) and shachah (worshiped).
The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) yalak (went) and ishah (make) so; as Yahawah had tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron), so they ishah (make).

It happened at chatzay (midnight), that Yahawah nakah (struck) all the bakawar (firstborn) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), from the bakawar (firstborn) of Paraih (Pharaoh) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) on his kasaa (throne) to the bakawar (firstborn) of the shabay (captive) who was in the bayath (house); and all the bakawar (firstborn) of livestock.

Paraih (Pharaoh) qawam (rise up) up in the layal (night), he, and all his ibad (servant), and all the Matzarayam (Egyptians); and there was a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) tzaiqah (cry) in Matzarayam (Egypt), for there was not a bayath (house) where there was not one mawath (death).

He qaraa (called) for Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) by layal (night), and amar (spoke), "qawam (rise up) up, yatzaa (go out / come out) out from thawak (midst) my im (nation / people), both you and the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel); and yalak (go), ibad (servant) Yahawah, as you have dabar (word / matter)!
Laqach (take / seize) both your tzaan (flocks) and your baqar (morning), as you have dabar (word / matter), and be yalak (gone); and barak (blessed) me also!"

The Matzaray (Egyptians) were chazaq (urgent) with the im (nation / people), to shalach (send) them out of the aratz (Earth/land) in mahar (haste), for they amar (spoke), "We are all mawath (death) men."
The im (nation / people) nashaa (lift) their batzaq (dough) before it was chamatz (leavened), their mashaarath (kneading) troughs being tzarar (bound) up in their clothes on their shakam (shoulders).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ishah (make) according to the dabar (word / matter) of Mashah (Moses); and they shaal (asked) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians) kalay (jewels) of kasap (silver), and kalay (jewels) of zahab (gold), and shamalah (clothing).
Yahawah nathan (give) the im (nation / people) favor in the iyan (eye) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians), so that they let them have what they asked. They despoiled the Matzarayam (Egyptians).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) traveled from Raimasas (Rameses) to Sakawath (Succoth), about shash (six) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) on ragalay (foot) who were gabarayam (men), bad (besides) tap (children).
A irab (evening) rab (multitude) ilah (go up / offer) up also with them, with tzaan (flocks), baqar (morning), and even very much livestock.

They apah (baked) unleavened igath (cakes) of the batzaq (dough) which they yatzaa (go out / come out) out of Matzarayam (Egypt); for it wasn't chamatz (leavened), because they were garash (thrust) out of Matzarayam (Egypt), and couldn't wait, neither ishah (make) they prepared for themselves any food.
Now the time that the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) lived in Matzarayam (Egypt) was arabai (four) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) shanah (years).

It happened at the qatz (end) of arabai (four) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) shanah (years), even the same yawam (day) it happened, that all the tzabaawath (armies) of Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) out from the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

It is a layal (night) to be much shamar (keep/guard) to Yahawah for yatzaa (go out / come out) them out from the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt). This is that layal (night) of Yahawah, to be much shamar (keep/guard) of all the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) throughout their dawar (generation / age / period).
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron), "This is the chaqah (ordinance) of the pasach (passover). No foreigner shall akal (eat) of it,
But every ayash (man / husband) ibad (servant) who is maqanah (bought) for kasap (money), when you have mawal (circumcised) him, then shall he akal (eat) of it.
A thawashab (foreigner) and a hired shakayar (servant) shall not akal (eat) of it.

In achad (one) bayath (house) shall it be akal (eat); you shall not yatzaa (go out / come out) out anything of the bashar (flesh) chawatz (abroad) out of the bayath (house); neither shall you shabar (break) a itzam (bone) of it.
All the idah (congregation) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall ishah (make) it.

When a gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) shall live as a foreigner with you, and will ishah (make) the pasach (passover) to Yahawah, let all his zakar (remember) be mawal (circumcised), and then let him qarab (come close) near and ishah (make) it; and he shall be as one who is azarach (born) in the aratz (Earth/land): but no iral (uncircumcised) person shall akal (eat) of it.
Achad (one) thawarah (instruction) shall be to him who is azarach (born) at home, and to the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who lives as a foreigner thawak (midst) you."
All the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ishah (make) so. As Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron), so they ishah (make).
It happened the same yawam (day), that Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) by their tzabaa (troop).
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

"Qadash (set apart / make holy) to me all of the bakawar (firstborn), whatever patar (opens) the racham (womb) among the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), both of adam (man) and of animal. It is mine."

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to the im (nation / people), "zakar (remember) zah (this / that / these) yawam (day), in which you yatzaa (go out / come out) out from Matzarayam (Egypt), out of the bayath (house) of ibad (servant); for by chazaq (strength) of yad (hand) Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) you out from this place. No chamatz (leavened) bread shall be akal (eat).
This yawam (day) you yatzaa (go out / come out) out in the chadash (month) abayab (abib).

It shall be, when Yahawah shall bawaa (come) you into the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kanainay (Canaanite), and the Chathay (Hittite), and the Amaray (Amorite), and the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite), which he shabai (swear / take oath) to your ab (father) to nathan (give) you, a aratz (Earth/land) zawab (flow) with chalab (milk) and dabash (honey), that you shall ibad (servant) this ibadah (service) in this chadash (month).
Shabai (seven) yamayam (days) you shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread), and in the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) shall be a chag (feast/festival) to Yahawah.

Unleavened matzah (bread) shall be akal (eat) throughout the shabai (seven) yamayam (days); and no chamatz (leavened) bread shall be raah (see) with you, neither shall yeast be raah (see) with you, in all your gabawal (border/boundary).

You shall nagad (tell) your ban (son) in that yawam (day), amar (spoke), ‘It is ibawar (because) of that which Yahawah ishah (make) for me when I yatzaa (go out / come out) out of Matzarayam (Egypt).'

It shall be for a awath (sign / mark / miracle) to you on your yad (hand), and for a zakarawan (memorial) between your iyan (eye), that the thawarah (instruction) of Yahawah may be in your pah (mouth); for with a chazaq (strong) yad (hand) Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) brought you out of Matzarayam (Egypt).
You shall therefore shamar (keep/guard) this chaqah (ordinance) in its mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) from yawam (day) to yawam (day).

"It shall be, when Yahawah shall bawaa (come) you into the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kanainay (Canaanite), as he shabai (swear / take oath) to you and to your ab (father), and shall nathan (give) it you,

That you shall ibar (pass over/through) apart to Yahawah all that patar (opens) the racham (womb), and every firstborn which you have that comes from an animal. The zakarayam (males) shall be Yahawah.

Every firstborn of a donkey you shall padah (redeem) with a shah (lamb); and if you will not padah (redeem) it, then you shall irap (break) its neck; and you shall padah (redeem) all the bakawar (firstborn) of adam (man) among your ban (son).

It shall be, when your ban (son) shaal (asks) you in machar (time) to come, amar (spoke), ‘What is this?' That you shall amar (spoke) him, ‘By chazaq (strength) of yad (hand) Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) us out from Matzarayam (Egypt), from the bayath (house) of ibad (servant);

And it happened, when Paraih (Pharaoh) qashah (rough / hard) hardly shalach (send) us go, that Yahawah harag (kill) all the bakawar (firstborn) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), both the bakawar (firstborn) of adam (man), and the bakawar (firstborn) of animal. Therefore I zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah all that patar (opens) the racham (womb), being zakarayam (males); but all the bakawar (firstborn) of my ban (son) I padah (redeem).'

It shall be for a awath (sign / mark / miracle) on your yad (hand), and for symbols between your iyan (eye): for by chazaq (strength) of yad (hand) Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) us out of Matzarayam (Egypt)."

It happened, when Paraih (Pharaoh) had let the im (nation / people) shalach (send), that Alahayam didn't nachah (lead) them by the darak (way) of the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines), kay (surely) that was qarawab (near); for Alahayam amar (spoke), "Lest perhaps the im (nation / people) change their minds when they raah (see) malachamah (war), and they shawab (turn back / repent) to Matzarayam (Egypt);"

But Alahayam sabab (led) the im (nation / people) around by the darak (way) of the madabar (wilderness) by the sawap (red) yam (sea/waters); and the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up chamash (armed) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

Mashah (Moses) laqach (take / seize) the itzamawath (bones) of Yawasap (Joseph) with him, for he had shabai (swear / take oath) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shabai (swear / take oath), amar (spoke), "Alahayam will paqad (visit) paqad (visit) you, and you shall ilah (go up / offer) up my itzamawath (bones) ilah (go up / offer) from here with you."
They took their nasai (journey) from Sakawath (Succoth), and chanah (encamped) in Atham (Etham), in the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the madabar (wilderness).

Yahawah halak (move) panayam (face) them by yawamam (by day) in a imawad (pillar) of inan (cloud), to nachah (lead) them on their darak (way), and by layal (night) in a imawad (pillar) of ash (fire), to give them awar (light), that they might yalak (go) by yawamam (by day) and by layal (night):
The imawad (pillar) of inan (cloud) by yawamam (by day), and the imawad (pillar) of ash (fire) by layal (night), didn't depart from panayam (face) the im (nation / people).
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),
