"Dabar (word / matter) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), that they shawab (turn back / repent) back and chanah (encamp) panayam (face) Payahachayarath (Pihahiroth), between Magadawal (Migdol) and the yam (sea/waters), nakach (before) Bailatzapawan (Baal) Zephon. You shall chanah (encamp) opposite it by the yam (sea/waters).
Paraih (Pharaoh) will amar (spoke) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), ‘They are bawak (entangled) in the aratz (Earth/land). The madabar (wilderness) has sagar (shut) them in.'

I will chazaq (harden) Paraih (Pharaoh's) lab (heart), and he will radap (follow) achar (other) them; and I will kabad (get) honor over Paraih (Pharaoh), and over all his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor); and the Matzaray (Egyptians) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah." They ishah (make) so.

It was nagad (told) the malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt) that the im (nation / people) had barach (fled); and the labab (heart) of Paraih (Pharaoh) and of his ibad (servant) was hapak (changed) towards the im (nation / people), and they amar (spoke), "What is this we ishah (make) done, that we have let Yashar-Al (Israel) shalach (send) from ibad (servant) us?"
He asar (prepared) his rakab (chariot), and laqach (take / seize) his army with him;
And he laqach (take / seize) shash (six) maah (hundred) bachar (chosen) rakab (chariots), and all the rakab (chariots) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and shalasham (captains) over all of them.

Yahawah chazaq (hardened) the lab (heart) of Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and he radap (pursued) achar (other) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel); for the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) yatzaa (go out / come out) out with a rawam (will lift up) yad (hand).

The Matzaray (Egyptians) radap (pursued) achar (other) them: all the sawas (horses) and rakab (chariots) of Paraih (Pharaoh), his horsemen, and his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor); and overtook them chanah (encamping) by the yam (sea/waters), beside Payahachayarath (Pihahiroth), panayam (face) Bailatzapawan (Baal Zephon).

When Paraih (Pharaoh) qarab (come close) near, the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) nashaa (lift) up their iyan (eye), and behold, the Ban (Egyptians) were nasai (marching) achar (other) them; and they were very yaraa (fear / be afraid). The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) tzaiq (cried) out to Yahawah.

They amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "Because there were no qabarayam (graves) in Matzarayam (Egypt), have you laqach (take / seize) us away to mawath (death) in the madabar (wilderness)? Why ishah (make) you treated us this way, to yatzaa (go out / come out) us out of Matzarayam (Egypt)?

Isn't this the dabar (word / matter) that we dabar (word / matter) to you in Matzarayam (Egypt), amar (spoke), ‘Leave us chadal (alone), that we may ibad (servant) the Matzarayam (Egyptians)?' For it were tawab (good / proper function) for us to ibad (servant) the Matzarayam (Egyptians), than that we should mawath (death) in the madabar (wilderness)."

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to the im (nation / people), "Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). Yatzab (stand) still, and raah (see) the yashawaih (salvation) of Yahawah, which he will ishah (make) for you today: for the Matzaray (Egyptians) whom you raah (see) seen today, you shall iwalam (forever) raah (see) them again.
Yahawah will lacham (fight) for you, and you shall be still."
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "Why do you tzaiq (cry) to me? Dabar (word / matter) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), that they nasai (go) forward.

Rawam (will lift up) up your matah (staff / rod / tribe), and natah (stretch) out your yad (hand) over the yam (sea/waters), and baqai (divide) it: and the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall bawaa (come) into the thawak (midst) of the yam (sea/waters) on dry yabashah (dry land).

I, behold, I will chazaq (harden) the lab (heart) of the Matzaray (Egyptians), and they shall bawaa (come) in after them: and I will kabad (get) myself honor over Paraih (Pharaoh), and over all his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), over his rakab (chariots), and over his horsemen.
The Matzaray (Egyptians) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I kabad (have) gotten myself honor over Paraih (Pharaoh), over his rakab (chariots), and over his horsemen."

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Alahayam, who halak (move) panayam (face) the machanah (camp) of Yashar-Al (Israel), moved and yalak (went) achar (other) them; and the imawad (pillar) of inan (cloud) moved from panayam (face) them, and imad (stood) achar (other) them.

It bawaa (come) between the machanah (camp) of Matzarayam (Egypt) and the machanah (camp) of Yashar-Al (Israel); and there was the inan (cloud) and the chashak (darkness), yet gave it awar (light) by layal (night): and the one didn't qarab (come close) near the other all the layal (night).

Mashah (Moses) natah (stretched) out his yad (hand) over the yam (sea/waters), and Yahawah caused the yam (sea/waters) to yalak (go) back by a iz (strong) qadayam (east) rawach (spirit / wind) all the layal (night), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the yam (sea/waters) charabah (dry) land, and the mayam (Waters) were baqai (divided).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) bawaa (come) into the thawak (midst) of the yam (sea/waters) on the yabashah (dry land) ground, and the mayam (Waters) were a chawamah (wall) to them on their right yamayan (right hand), and on their shamaawal (left hand).

The Matzaray (Egyptians) radap (pursued), and bawaa (come) in achar (other) them into the thawak (midst) of the yam (sea/waters): all of Paraih (Pharaoh's) sawas (horses), his rakab (chariots), and his horsemen.

It happened in the baqar (morning) ashamarah (watch), that Yahawah shaqap (looked) out on the Matzaray (Egyptian) machanah (army) through the imawad (pillar) of ash (fire) and of inan (cloud), and confused the Matzaray (Egyptian) machanah (army).

He sawar (took) off their marakabah (chariot) awapan (wheels), and they nahag (drove) them kabadath (heavily); so that the Matzarayam (Egyptians) amar (spoke), "Let's nawas (flee) from the panayam (face) of Yashar-Al (Israel), for Yahawah lacham (fights) for them against the Matzarayam (Egyptians)!"

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "natah (stretch) out your yad (hand) over the yam (sea/waters), that the mayam (Waters) may shawab (turn back / repent) again on the Matzarayam (Egyptians), on their rakab (chariots), and on their horsemen."

Mashah (Moses) natah (stretched) out his yad (hand) over the yam (sea/waters), and the yam (sea/waters) shawab (turn back / repent) to its ayathan (strength) when the baqar (morning) appeared; and the Matzarayam (Egyptians) nawas (fled) qaraah (against) it. Yahawah overthrew the Matzarayam (Egyptians) in the thawak (midst) of the yam (sea/waters).

The mayam (Waters) shawab (turn back / repent), and kasah (covered) the rakab (chariots) and the horsemen, even all Paraih (Pharaoh's) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) that bawaa (come) in achar (other) them into the yam (sea/waters). There shaar (remained) not so much as achad (one) of them.

But the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) halak (move) on yabashah (dry land) land in the thawak (midst) of the yam (sea/waters), and the mayam (Waters) were a chawamah (wall) to them on their right yamayan (right hand), and on their shamaawal (left hand).

Thus Yahawah yashai (salvation) Yashar-Al (Israel) that yawam (day) out of the yad (hand) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians); and Yashar-Al (Israel) raah (see) the Matzarayam (Egyptians) mawath (death) on the shapah (seashore).

Yashar-Al (Israel) raah (see) the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) yad (hand) which Yahawah ishah (make) to the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and the im (nation / people) yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah; and they aman (believe / have faith) in Yahawah, and in his ibad (servant) Mashah (Moses).

Then Mashah (Moses) and the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shayar (sang) this shayar (song) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "I will shayar (sing) to Yahawah, for he has gaah (triumphed) gaah (gloriously). The sawas (horse) and his rider he has ramah (thrown) into the yam (sea/waters).

Yah is my iz (strength / might / refuge) and zamarath (song). He has become my yashawaih (salvation). Zah (this / that / these) is my Al, and I will praise him; my ab (father) Alahayam, and I will rawam (will lift up) him.
Yahawah is a ayash (man / husband) of malachamah (war). Yahawah is his sham (name).

He has yarah (cast) Paraih (Pharaoh's) marakabath (chariots) and his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) into the yam (sea/waters). His mabachar (chosen) shalayash (captains) are tabai (sunk) in the sawap (red) yam (sea/waters).
The thahamath (deeps) kasah (cover) them. They yarad (went) down into the matzawalath (depths) kamaw (like) a aban (stone).
Your right yamayan (right hand), Yahawah, is adar (glorious) in kach (strength / mighty / power). Your right yamayan (right hand), Yahawah, dashes the ayab (enemy) in raitz (pieces).
In the greatness of your gaawan (excellency), you haras (overthrow) those who qawam (rise up) up against you. You shalach (send) forth your charawan (wrath). It akal (eat) them as qash (stubble).

With the rawach (spirit / wind) of your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), the mayam (Waters) were piled up. The nazalayam (floods) stood natzab (upright) as a nad (heap). The thahamath (deeps) were qapaa (congealed) in the lab (heart) of the yam (sea/waters).

The ayab (enemy) amar (spoke), ‘I will radap (pursue). I will nashag (overtake). I will chalaq (divide) the shalal (spoil). My napash (soul) shall be malaa (satisfied) on them. I will rawaq (draw) my charab (sword), my yad (hand) shall yarash (destroy) them.'
You nashap (blew) with your rawach (spirit / wind). The yam (sea/waters) kasah (covered) them. They tzalal (sank) like iwaparath (lead) in the adayar (mighty) mayam (Waters).
Who is like you, Yahawah, among the Al? Who is like you, adar (glorious) in qadash (set apart / make holy), fearful in thahalath (praises), ishah (make) palaa (wonders)?
You natah (stretched) out your right yamayan (right hand). The aratz (Earth/land) balai (swallowed) them.

"You, in your loving chasad (grace), have nachah (led) the im (nation / people) that you have gaal (redeemed). You have nahal (guided) them in your iz (strength / might / refuge) to your qadash (set apart / make holy) nawah (habitation).
The imayam (peoples) have shamai (hearken / hear). They ragaz (tremble). Chayal (pangs) achaz (have) taken hold on the yashabay (inhabitants) of Palashath (Philistia).

Then the chiefs of Adawam (Edom) were bahal (dismayed). Raid (trembling) achaz (takes) hold of the ayal (mighty) men of Mawaab (Moab). All the yashabay (inhabitants) of Kanain (Canaan) are mawag (melted) away.

Ayamah (terror) and pachad (fear / dread) napal (fall / be cast down) on them. By the greatness of your zarawai (arm) they are as still as a aban (stone)— until your im (nation / people) ibar (pass over/through) over, Yahawah, until the im (nation / people) ibar (pass over/through) over who you have qanah (purchased).

You shall bawaa (come) them in, and natai (plant) them in the har (mountain) of your nachalah (inheritance), the makawan (place), Yahawah, which you have pail (made) for yourself to yashab (inhabit/dwell) in; the maqadash (sanctuary), Adanay, which your yad (hand) have kawan (established).
Yahawah shall malak (king) id (until / as far as) and iwalam (forever)."

For the sawas (horses) of Paraih (Pharaoh) bawaa (come) in with his rakab (chariots) and with his horsemen into the yam (sea/waters), and Yahawah shawab (turn back / repent) back the may (waters) of the yam (sea/waters) on them; but the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) halak (move) on yabashah (dry land) land in the thawak (midst) of the yam (sea/waters).

Marayam (Miriam) the nabayaah (prophetess), the achawath (sister) of Aharawan (Aaron), laqach (take / seize) a tambourine in her yad (hand); and all the nashayam (women) yatzaa (go out / come out) out achar (other) her with tambourines and with machalath (dances).

Marayam (Miriam) inah (answer / respond) them, "shayar (sing) to Yahawah, for he has gaah (triumphed) gaah (gloriously). The sawas (horse) and his rider he has ramah (thrown) into the yam (sea/waters)."

Mashah (Moses) led Yashar-Al (Israel) nasai (onward) from the sawap (red) yam (sea/waters), and they yatzaa (go out / come out) out into the madabar (wilderness) of Shawar (Shur); and they yalak (went) shalawash (three) yamayam (days) in the madabar (wilderness), and matzaa (found) no mayam (Waters).

When they bawaa (come) to Marah (Marah), they couldn't shathah (drinks) from the mayam (Waters) of Marah (Marah), for they were mar (bitter). Therefore its sham (name) was qaraa (called) Marah (Marah).
The im (nation / people) lawan (murmured) against Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke), "What shall we shathah (drinks)?"

Then he tzaiq (cried) to Yahawah. Yahawah showed him a itz (tree), and he shalak (threw) it into the mayam (Waters), and the mayam (Waters) were mathaq (made) sweet. There he shawam (place / establish / appoint) a chaq (statute) and an mashapat (ordinance) for them, and there he tested them;

And he amar (spoke), "If you will shamai (hearken / hear) shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam, and will ishah (make) that which is yashar (upright) in his azan (ear), and will pay attention to his matzawah (commandments), and shamar (keep/guard) all his chaq (statute), I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) none of the machalah (diseases) on you, which I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) on the Matzarayam (Egyptians); for I am Yahawah who rapaa (heals) you."
They bawaa (come) to Ayalam (Elim), where there were shanayam (two) springs of mayam (Waters), and shabaiyam (seventy) thamar (palm) trees: and they chanah (encamped) there by the mayam (Waters).

They took their nasai (journey) from Ayalam (Elim), and all the idah (congregation) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) bawaa (come) to the madabar (wilderness) of sayan (sin), which is between Ayalam (Elim) and Sayanay (Sinai), on the fifteenth yawam (day) of the shanay (second) chadash (month) yatzaa (go out / come out) their departing out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
The whole idah (congregation) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) lawan (murmured) against Mashah (Moses) and against Aharawan (Aaron) in the madabar (wilderness);

And the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke) to them, "We wish that we had mawath (death) by the yad (hand) of Yahawah in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), when we yashab (inhabit/dwell) by the meat sayar (pots), when we akal (eat) our shabai (fill) of lacham (bread), for you yatzaa (go out / come out) brought us out into this madabar (wilderness), to mawath (death) this whole qahal (assembly) with raib (hunger)."

Then Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "Behold, I will matar (rain) lacham (bread) from the sky for you, and the im (nation / people) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out and laqat (gather) a day's dabar (word / matter) every yawam (day), that I may test them, whether they will yalak (walk) in my thawarah (instruction), or not.

It shall come to pass on the shashay (sixth) yawam (day), that they shall kawan (prepare) that which they bawaa (come) in, and it shall be mashanah (twice) as much as they laqat (gather) yawam (day)."

Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) amar (spoke) to all the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), "At irab (evening), then you shall yadai (know) that Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) brought you out from the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt);

And in the baqar (morning), then you shall raah (see) the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah; because he shamai (hearken / hear) your thalawanah (murmurings) against Yahawah. Who are we, that you lawan (murmur) against us?"

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke), "Now Yahawah shall nathan (give) you meat to akal (eat) in the irab (evening), and in the baqar (morning) lacham (bread) to shabai (satisfy) you; because Yahawah shamai (hearken / hear) your malayanam (murmurings) which you murmur against him. And who are we? Your malayanam (murmurings) are not against us, but against Yahawah."

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to Aharawan (Aaron), "amar (spoke) all the idah (congregation) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), ‘qarab (come close) near panayam (face) Yahawah, for he has shamai (hearken / hear) your thalawanah (murmurings).'"

It happened, as Aharawan (Aaron) dabar (word / matter) to the whole idah (congregation) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), that they panah (turn) toward the madabar (wilderness), and behold, the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah raah (see) in the inan (cloud).
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

"I have shamai (hearken / hear) the thalawanath (murmurings) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel). Dabar (word / matter) to them, amar (spoke), ‘At evening you shall akal (eat) meat, and in the baqar (morning) you shall be shabai (filled) with lacham (bread): and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah your Alahayam.'"
It happened at irab (evening) that shalaw (quail) ilah (go up / offer) up and kasah (covered) the machanah (camp); and in the baqar (morning) the tal (dew) shakabah (lay) around the machanah (camp).

When the tal (dew) that shakabah (lay) had ilah (go up / offer), behold, on the surface of the madabar (wilderness) was a daq (small) chasapas (round) thing, daq (small) as the kapawar (frost) on the aratz (Earth/land).

When the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) raah (see) it, they amar (spoke) ayash (man / husband) to ach (brother/kinsman), "What is it?" For they didn't yadai (know) what it was. Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to them, "It is the lacham (bread) which Yahawah nathan (give) given you to akalah (eat)."

This is the thing which Yahawah has tzawah (commanded): "laqat (gather) of it everyone pah (according) to his akal (eating); an imar (omer) a galagalath (head), according to the masapar (number) of your napash (soul), you shall laqach (take / seize) it, every ayash (man / husband) for those who are in his ahal (tent)."
The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ishah (make) so, and laqat (gathered) some more, some mait (less).

When they madad (measured) it with an imar (omer), he who rabah (gathered) much had nothing over, and he who mait (gathered) little had no chasar (lack). They laqat (gathered) every ayash (man / husband) pah (according) to his akal (eating).
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to them, "Let no ayash (man / husband) yathar (leave) of it until the baqar (morning)."

Notwithstanding they didn't shamai (hearken / hear) to Mashah (Moses), but some of them yathar (left) of it until the baqar (morning), and it bred thawalaiyam (worms), and became foul: and Mashah (Moses) was qatzap (angry) with them.
They laqat (gathered) it baqar (morning) by morning, everyone pah (according) to his akal (eating). When the shamash (sun) grew chamam (hot), it masas (melted).

It happened that on the shashay (sixth) yawam (day) they laqat (gathered) mashanah (twice) as much lacham (bread), shanayam (two) imar (omers) for achad (one) one, and all the nashayaay (rulers) of the idah (congregation) bawaa (come) and nagad (told) Mashah (Moses).

He amar (spoke) to them, "This is that which Yahawah has dabar (word / matter), ‘machar (tomorrow) is a solemn shabathawan (rest), a qadash (set apart / make holy) shabath (shabath / rest) to Yahawah. Apah (bake) that which you want to apah (bake), and bashal (boil) that which you want to bashal (boil); and kal (every) that idap (remains) over yanach (lay) up for yourselves to be mashamarath (duty / watch) until the baqar (morning).'"
They yanach (laid) it up until the baqar (morning), as Mashah (Moses) asked, and it didn't become foul, neither was there any ramah (worm) in it.
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke), "akal (eat) that today, for today is a shabath (shabath / rest) to Yahawah. Today you shall not matzaa (find) it in the shadah (field).
Shash (six) yamayam (days) you shall laqat (gather) it, but on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) is the shabath (shabath / rest). In it there shall be none."
It happened on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), that some of the im (nation / people) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to laqat (gather), and they matzaa (found) none.
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "How long do you maan (refuse) to shamar (keep/guard) my matzawah (commandments) and my thawarah (instruction)?

Raah (see), because Yahawah nathan (give) given you the shabath (shabath / rest), therefore he nathan (give) you on the shashay (sixth) yawam (day) the lacham (bread) of yawam (day) days. Everyone stay in his place. Let no ayash (man / husband) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of his maqawam (place) on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day)."
So the im (nation / people) shabath (shabath / rest) on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day).

The bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) qaraa (called) its sham (name) man (from), and it was like gad (coriander) zarai (seed), laban (white); and its taim (taste) was like tzapayachath (wafers) with dabash (honey).

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke), "This is the thing which Yahawah has tzawah (commanded), ‘Let an omer-full of it be mashamarath (duty / watch) throughout your dawar (generation / age / period), that they may raah (see) the lacham (bread) with which I akal (eat) you in the madabar (wilderness), when I yatzaa (go out / come out) you forth from the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).'"

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to Aharawan (Aaron), "laqach (take / seize) a tzanatzanath (pot), and nathan (give) an omer-full of man (from) in it, and yanach (lay) it up panayam (face) Yahawah, to be mashamarath (duty / watch) throughout your dawar (generation / age / period)."
As Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses), so Aharawan (Aaron) yanach (laid) it up panayam (face) the idawath (testimony), to be mashamarath (duty / watch).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) akal (eat) the man (from) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years), until they bawaa (come) to an yashab (inhabit/dwell) aratz (Earth/land). They akal (eat) the man (from) until they bawaa (come) to the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan).
Now an imar (omer) is the ishayaray (tenth) part of an ayapah (ephah).

All the idah (congregation) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) traveled from the madabar (wilderness) of sayan (sin), by their masai (journeys), according to Yahawah commandment, and chanah (encamped) in Rapayadayam (Rephidim); but there was no mayam (Waters) for the im (nation / people) to shathah (drinks).

Therefore the im (nation / people) quarreled with Mashah (Moses), and amar (spoke), "nathan (give) us mayam (Waters) to shathah (drinks)." Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to them, "Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test Yahawah?"

The im (nation / people) were tzamaa (thirsty) for mayam (Waters) there; and the im (nation / people) lawan (murmured) against Mashah (Moses), and amar (spoke), "Why have you ilah (go up / offer) us up out of Matzarayam (Egypt), to mawath (death) us, our ban (son), and our livestock with tzamaa (thirst)?"
Mashah (Moses) tzaiq (cried) to Yahawah, amar (spoke), "What shall I ishah (make) with these im (nation / people)? They are mait (almost) ready to saqal (stone) me."

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "Walk on panayam (face) the im (nation / people), and laqach (take / seize) the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel) with you, and laqach (take / seize) the matah (staff / rod / tribe) in your yad (hand) with which you nakah (struck) the Nile, and halak (move).

Behold, I will imad (stand) panayam (face) you there on the tzawar (rock) in Charab (Horeb). You shall nakah (strike) the tzawar (rock), and mayam (Waters) will yatzaa (go out / come out) out of it, that the im (nation / people) may shathah (drinks)." Mashah (Moses) ishah (make) so in the iyan (eye) of the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

He qaraa (called) the sham (name) of the maqawam (place) Masah (Massah), and Marayabah (Meribah), because the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) quarreled, and because they tested Yahawah, amar (spoke), "Is Yahawah qarab (among / near) us, or not?"
Then Imalaq (Amalek) bawaa (come) and lacham (fought) with Yashar-Al (Israel) in Rapayadayam (Rephidim).

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to Yahawashawai (Joshua), "bachar (choose) anashayam (men) for us, and go out, lacham (fight) with Imalaq (Amalek). Machar (tomorrow) I will natzab (stand) on the raash (head) of the gabaih (hill) with Alahayam matah (staff / rod / tribe) in my yad (hand)."

So Yahawashawai (Joshua) ishah (make) as Mashah (Moses) had amar (spoke) him, and lacham (fought) with Imalaq (Amalek); and Mashah (Moses), Aharawan (Aaron), and Chawar (Hur) ilah (go up / offer) up to the raash (head) of the gabaih (hill).
It happened, when Mashah (Moses) rawam (will lift up) up his yad (hand), that Yashar-Al (Israel) gabar (prevailed); and when he nawach (let) down his yad (hand), Imalaq (Amalek) gabar (prevailed).

But Mashah (Moses)' yaday (hands) were kabad (heavy); and they laqach (take / seize) a aban (stone), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it under him, and he yashab (inhabit/dwell) on it. Aharawan (Aaron) and Chawar (Hur) thamak (held) up his yaday (hands), the one on the one side, and the other on the other side. His yaday (hands) were amawanah (steady) until sunset.
Yahawashawai (Joshua) defeated Imalaq (Amalek) and his im (nation / people) with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "kathab (write) this for a zakarawan (memorial) in a sapar (book / scribed document), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it in the azanay (ears) of Yahawashawai (Joshua): that I will machah (utterly) machah (blot) out the zakar (remember) of Imalaq (Amalek) from under the sky."
Mashah (Moses) banah (build) an mazabach (altar), and qaraa (called) its sham (name) Yahawah our Banner.
He amar (spoke), "Yah has yad (hand): ‘Yahawah will have malachamah (war) with Imalaq (Amalek) from dawar (generation / age / period) to dawar (generation / age / period).'"

Now Yatharaw (Jethro), the kahan (priest) of Madayan (Midian), Mashah (Moses)' father-in-law, shamai (hearken / hear) of all that Alahayam ishah (make) done for Mashah (Moses), and for Yashar-Al (Israel) his im (nation / people), how that Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) brought Yashar-Al (Israel) out of Matzarayam (Egypt).
Yatharaw (Jethro), Mashah (Moses)' father-in-law, laqach (take / seize) Tzaparah (Zipporah), Mashah (Moses)' ayashah (woman / wife), achar (other) he shalawach (had) sent her away,
And her shanayam (two) ban (son). The sham (name) of achad (one) son was Garasham (Gershom), for Moses amar (spoke), "I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign aratz (Earth/land)".
The sham (name) of the other was Alayaizar (Eliezer), for he said, "My ab (father) Alahayam was my izar (help) and natzal (delivered) me from Paraih (Pharaoh's) charab (sword)."

Yatharaw (Jethro), Mashah (Moses)' father-in-law, bawaa (come) with his ban (son) and his ayashah (woman / wife) to Mashah (Moses) into the madabar (wilderness) where he was chanah (encamped), at the har (mountain) of Alahayam.
He amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "I, your father-in-law Yatharaw (Jethro), bawaa (come) come to you with your ayashah (woman / wife), and her shanayam (two) ban (son) with her."

Mashah (Moses) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) his father-in-law, and shachah (bowed) and nashaq (kissed) him. They shaal (asked) ayash (man / husband) other of their shalawam (peace / safety), and they bawaa (come) into the ahal (tent).

Mashah (Moses) sapar (book) his father-in-law all that Yahawah ishah (make) done to Paraih (Pharaoh) and to the Matzarayam (Egyptians) for Yashar-Al (Israel's) awadawath (sake), all the hardships that matzaa (had) come on them on the darak (way), and how Yahawah natzal (delivered) them.

Yatharaw (Jethro) chadah (rejoiced) for all the goodness which Yahawah ishah (make) done to Yashar-Al (Israel), in that he had natzal (delivered) them out of the yad (hand) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians).

Yatharaw (Jethro) amar (spoke), "barak (blessed) be Yahawah, who has natzal (delivered) you out of the yad (hand) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and out of the yad (hand) of Paraih (Pharaoh); who has natzal (delivered) the im (nation / people) from under the yad (hand) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians).
Now I yadai (know) that Yahawah is greater than all Alahayam dabar (word / matter) of the thing in which they dealt arrogantly against them."

Yatharaw (Jethro), Mashah (Moses)' father-in-law, laqach (take / seize) a burnt ilah (offering) and zabachayam (sacrifices) for Alahayam. Aharawan (Aaron) bawaa (come) with all of the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel), to akal (eat) lacham (bread) with Mashah (Moses)' father-in-law panayam (face) Alahayam.

It happened on the next macharath (day), that Mashah (Moses) yashab (inhabit/dwell) to shapat (judge / judgement) the im (nation / people), and the im (nation / people) imad (stood) around Mashah (Moses) from the baqar (morning) to the irab (evening).

When Mashah (Moses)' father-in-law raah (see) all that he ishah (make) to the im (nation / people), he amar (spoke), "dabar (word / matter) is this thing that you ishah (make) for the im (nation / people)? Why do you yashab (inhabit/dwell) alone, and all the im (nation / people) natzab (stand) around you from baqar (morning) to irab (evening)?"
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to his father-in-law, "Because the im (nation / people) bawaa (come) to me to darash (inquire) of Alahayam.

When they have a dabar (word / matter), they bawaa (come) to me, and I shapat (judge / judgement) between a ayash (man / husband) and his neighbor, and I yadai (make) them know the chaqay (statutes) of Alahayam, and his thawarah (instruction)."
Mashah (Moses)' father-in-law amar (spoke) to him, "The thing that you ishah (make) is not tawab (good / proper function).

You will nabal (surely) wear nabal (away), both you, and this im (nation / people) that is with you; for the thing is too kabad (heavy) for you. You are not yakal (able) to ishah (make) it yourself alone.

Shamai (hearken / hear) now to my qawal (sound / voice). I will give you yaitz (counsel), and Alahayam be with you. You represent the im (nation / people) before Alahayam, and bawaa (come) the dabarayam (causes) to Alahayam.
You shall zahar (warn) them the chaqayam (statutes) and the thawarath (laws), and shall show them the darak (way) in which they must yalak (walk), and the maishah (work) that they must ishah (make).

Moreover you shall chazah (provide) out of all the im (nation / people) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) im (nation / people), such as yaraa (fear) Alahayam: im (nation / people) of amath (truth), shanaa (hate) unjust batzai (gain); and shawam (place / establish / appoint) such over them, to be sharay (rulers) of alapayam (thousands), sharay (rulers) of maawath (hundreds), sharay (rulers) of chamashayam (fifties), and sharay (rulers) of isharath (tens).

Let them shapat (judge / judgement) the im (nation / people) at all ith (times). It shall be that every gadawal (very great/important/mighty) dabar (word / matter) they shall bawaa (come) to you, but every qatan (small / young / least) dabar (word / matter) they shall shapat (judge / judgement) themselves. So shall it be easier for you, and they shall share the load with you.

If you will ishah (make) this thing, and Alahayam tzawah (commands) you so, then you will be yakal (able) to imad (endure), and all of these im (nation / people) also will bawaa (come) to their maqawam (place) in shalawam (peace / safety)."
So Mashah (Moses) shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of his father-in-law, and ishah (make) all that he had amar (spoke).

Mashah (Moses) bachar (chose) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) anashay (men) out of all Yashar-Al (Israel), and nathan (give) them raashayam (heads) over the im (nation / people), sharay (rulers) of alapayam (thousands), sharay (rulers) of maawath (hundreds), sharay (rulers) of chamashayam (fifties), and sharay (rulers) of isharath (tens).

They shapat (judge / judgement) the im (nation / people) at all ith (times). They bawaa (come) the qashah (rough / hard) dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), but every qatan (small / young / least) dabar (word / matter) they shapat (judge / judgement) themselves.
Mashah (Moses) let his father-in-law depart, and he yalak (went) his aratz (Earth/land) into his own land.

In the shalayashay (third) chadash (month) after the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) yatzaa (go out / come out) gone out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), on that same yawam (day) they bawaa (come) into the madabar (wilderness) of Sayanay (Sinai).

When they had departed from Rapayadayam (Rephidim), and bawaa (come) come to the madabar (wilderness) of Sayanay (Sinai), they chanah (encamped) in the madabar (wilderness); and there Yashar-Al (Israel) chanah (encamped) before the har (mountain).

Mashah (Moses) ilah (go up / offer) up to Alahayam, and Yahawah qaraa (called) to him out of the har (mountain), amar (spoke), "This is what you shall amar (spoke) the bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and amar (spoke) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel):
‘You raah (see) seen what I ishah (make) to the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and how I nashaa (lift) you on nasharayam (eagles)' kanapay (wings), and bawaa (come) you to myself.

Now therefore, if you will shamai (hearken / hear) shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice), and shamar (keep/guard) my barayath (covenant), then you shall be my own sagalah (possession) from among all imayam (peoples); for all the aratz (Earth/land) is mine;

And you shall be to me a mamalakah (kingdom) of kahanayam (priests), and a qadawash (holy) gaway (heathen / nation).' These are the dabarayam (words) which you shall dabar (word / matter) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel)."
Mashah (Moses) bawaa (come) and qaraa (called) for the zaqanay (elders) of the im (nation / people), and set before them all these dabarayam (words) which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) him.

All the im (nation / people) inah (answer / respond) yachad (together), and amar (spoke), "All that Yahawah has amar (spoke) we will ishah (make)." Mashah (Moses) reported the dabaray (words) of the im (nation / people) to Yahawah.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "Behold, I bawaa (come) to you in a ib (thick) inan (cloud), that the im (nation / people) may shamai (hearken / hear) when I dabar (word / matter) with you, and may also aman (believe / have faith) you iwalam (forever)." Mashah (Moses) nagad (told) the dabaray (words) of the im (nation / people) to Yahawah.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "yalak (go) to the im (nation / people), and qadash (set apart / make holy) them today and machar (tomorrow), and let them kabas (wash) their shamalah (garments),

And be kawan (ready) against the shalayashay (third) yawam (day); for on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day) Yahawah will yarad (come) down in the iyan (eye) of all the im (nation / people) on har (mountain) Sayanay (Sinai).

You shall gabal (set) bounds to the im (nation / people) all around, amar (spoke), ‘Be careful that you don't ilah (go up / offer) up onto the har (mountain), or nagai (touch) its qatzah (end / extremity / border). Whoever touches the har (mountain) shall be mawath (death) put to mawath (death).

No yad (hand) shall nagai (touch) him, but he shall saqal (surely) be saqal (stoned) or yarah (shot) yarah (through); whether it is animal or ayash (man / husband), he shall not chayah (live).' When the yawabal (trumpet) mashak (sounds) long, they shall ilah (go up / offer) up to the har (mountain)."
Mashah (Moses) yarad (went) down from the har (mountain) to the im (nation / people), and qadash (set apart / make holy) the im (nation / people); and they kabas (washed) their clothes.
He amar (spoke) to the im (nation / people), "Be kawan (ready) by the shalawash (three) yawam (day). Don't have sexual relations with a ayashah (woman / wife)."

It happened on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), when it was baqar (morning), that there were qalath (thunders) and baraqayam (lightnings), and a kabad (thick) inan (cloud) on the har (mountain), and the qawal (sound / voice) of an maad (exceedingly) chazaq (loud) shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn); and all the im (nation / people) who were in the machanah (camp) charad (trembled).
Mashah (Moses) led the im (nation / people) out of the machanah (camp) to qaraah (meet) Alahayam; and they yatzab (stood) at the lower part of the har (mountain).

Har (mountain) Sayanay (Sinai), all it, ishan (smoked), panayam (face) Yahawah descended on it in ash (fire); and its ishan (smoke) ilah (go up / offer) like the ishan (smoke) of a kabashan (furnace), and the whole har (mountain) charad (quaked) maad (greatly).

When the qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn) grew louder and chazaq (louder), Mashah (Moses) dabar (word / matter), and Alahayam inah (answer / respond) him by a qawal (sound / voice).

Yahawah yarad (came) down on har (mountain) Sayanay (Sinai), to the raash (head) of the har (mountain). Yahawah qaraa (called) Mashah (Moses) to the top of the har (mountain), and Mashah (Moses) ilah (go up / offer) up.
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "yarad (go) down, warn the im (nation / people), lest they haras (break) through to Yahawah to raah (see), and many of them napal (fall / be cast down).
Let the kahanayam (priests) also, who nagash (come) near to Yahawah, qadash (set apart / make holy) themselves, lest Yahawah paratz (break) forth on them."

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to Yahawah, "The im (nation / people) can't ilah (go up / offer) up to har (mountain) Sayanay (Sinai), for you warned us, amar (spoke), ‘gabal (set) bounds around the har (mountain), and qadash (set apart / make holy) it.'"

Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, "yalak (go) down and you shall bring Aharawan (Aaron) up with you, but don't let the kahanayam (priests) and the im (nation / people) haras (break) through to ilah (go up / offer) up to Yahawah, lest he paratz (break) forth on them."
So Mashah (Moses) yarad (went) down to the im (nation / people), and amar (spoke) them.
Alahayam dabar (word / matter) all these dabarayam (words), amar (spoke),
"I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who yatzaa (go out / come out) you out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), out of the bayath (house) of ibad (servant).
"You shall have no other Alahayam panayam (face) me.

"You shall not ishah (make) for yourselves an idol, nor any pasal (image) of anything that is in the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) mail (top/above), or that is in the aratz (Earth/land) beneath, or that is in the mayam (Waters) under the aratz (Earth/land):

You shall not shachah (bow) yourself down to them, nor ibad (servant) them, for I, Yahawah your Alahayam, am a qanaa (jealous) Alahayam, paqad (visit) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the abath (fathers) on the banayam (children), on the shalash (three) and on the rabai (fourth) generation of those who shanaa (hate) me,
And showing loving chasad (grace) to alapayam (thousands) of those who ahab (love) me and shamar (keep/guard) my matzawah (commandments).
"You shall not nashaa (lift) the sham (name) of Yahawah your Alahayam in shawaa (vanity), for Yahawah will not hold him naqah (clean/innocent) who nashaa (lift) his sham (name) in shawaa (vanity).
"Zakar (remember) the shabath (shabath / rest) yawam (day), to keep it qadash (set apart / make holy).
You shall ibad (servant) shash (six) yamayam (days), and ishah (make) all your malaakah (work),

But the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) is a shabath (shabath / rest) to Yahawah your Alahayam. You shall not ishah (make) any malaakah (work) in it, you, nor your ban (son), nor your banath (daughter), your male ibad (servant), nor your female amah (servant), nor your livestock, nor your gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who is within your shair (gates);

For in shash (six) yamayam (days) Yahawah ishah (make) shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) and aratz (Earth/land), the yam (sea/waters), and all that is in them, and nawach (rested) the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day); therefore Yahawah barak (blessed) the shabath (shabath / rest) yawam (day), and made it qadash (set apart / make holy).
"Honor your ab (father) and your am (mother), that your yawam (day) may be arak (long) in the adamah (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (give) you.
"You shall not ratzach (murder).
"You shall not naap (commit) adultery.
"You shall not ganab (steal).
"You shall not inah (answer / respond) shaqar (false) id (until / as far as) against your neighbor.

"You shall not chamad (covet) your neighbor's bayath (house). You shall not chamad (covet) your neighbor's ayashah (woman / wife), nor his male ibad (servant), nor his female amah (servant), nor his shawar (ox), nor his donkey, nor anything that is your neighbor's."

All the im (nation / people) raah (see) the qawalath (thunderings), the lapayadam (lightnings), the qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn), and the har (mountain) ishan (smoking). When the im (nation / people) raah (see) it, they trembled, and imad (stayed) at a distance.
They amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "dabar (word / matter) with us yourself, and we will shamai (hearken / hear); but don't let Alahayam dabar (word / matter) with us, lest we mawath (death)."

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to the im (nation / people), "Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), for Alahayam bawaa (come) come to test you, and that his yaraah (fear) may be panayam (face) you, that you won't chataa (sin)."
The im (nation / people) imad (stayed) at a distance, and Mashah (Moses) nagash (drew) near to the irapal (thick) darkness where Alahayam was.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "This is what you shall amar (spoke) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel): ‘You yourselves raah (see) seen that I have dabar (word / matter) with you from shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens).
You shall most ishah (make) not make alongside of me Alahayam of kasap (silver), or Alahayam of zahab (gold) for yourselves.

You shall ishah (make) an mazabach (altar) of adamah (earth) for me, and shall zabach (sacrifice) on it your burnt ilah (offerings) and your peace ilah (offerings), your tzaan (sheep) and your cattle. In every maqawam (place) where I zakar (remember) my sham (name) I will bawaa (come) to you and I will barak (blessed) you.

If you ishah (make) me an mazabach (altar) of aban (stone), you shall not banah (build) it of cut abanayam (stones); for if you nawap (lift) up your charab (sword) on it, you have chalal (polluted) it.
Neither shall you ilah (go up / offer) up by mailath (steps) to my mazabach (altar), that your irawah (nakedness) may not be exposed to it.'
"Now these are the mashapatayam (ordinances) which you shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) panayam (face) them.

"If you qanah (buy) a ibaray (hebrew) ibad (servant), he shall ibad (servant) shash (six) shanayam (years) and in the shabayaiy (seventh) he shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out chapashay (free) chanam (without) paying anything.

If he bawaa (come) in by gap (himself), he shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out by gap (himself). If he is bail (married), then his ayashah (woman / wife) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out with him.

If his adawan (master / lord) nathan (give) him a ayashah (woman / wife) and she yalad (birth / begot) him banayam (sons) or banawath (daughters), the ayashah (woman / wife) and her banayam (children) shall be her adawan (master / lord), and he shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out by gap (himself).

But if the ibad (servant) shall amar (spoke) amar (spoke), ‘I ahab (love) my adawan (master / lord), my ayashah (woman / wife), and my ban (son). I will not yatzaa (go out / come out) out chapashay (free);'

Then his adawan (master / lord) shall nagash (bring) him to Alahayam, and shall nagash (bring) him to the dalath (door) or to the doorpost, and his adawan (master / lord) shall ratzai (bore) his azan (ear) through with an awl, and he shall ibad (servant) him for iwalam (forever).
"If a ayash (man / husband) makar (sells) his banath (daughter) to be a female amah (servant), she shall not yatzaa (go out / come out) out as the male ibadayam (servants) do.

If she doesn't rai (please) her adawan (master / lord), who has married her to himself, then he shall padah (let) her be redeemed. He shall mashal (rule/have dominion) no right to makar (sell) her to a foreign im (nation / people), since he has dealt bagad (deceitfully) with her.
If he marries her to his ban (son), he shall ishah (make) with her as a banath (daughter).
If he laqach (take / seize) achar (other) wife to himself, he shall not garai (diminish) her shaar (food), her clothing, and her marital rights.
If he doesn't ishah (make) these shalawash (three) things for her, she may yatzaa (go out / come out) chanam (free) without paying any kasap (money).
"One who nakah (strikes) a ayash (man / husband) so that he mawath (death) shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death),
But not if it is unintentional, but Alahayam allows it to happen: then I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) you a maqawam (place) where he shall nawas (flee).
If a ayash (man / husband) schemes and comes zawad (presumptuously) on his neighbor to harag (kill) him, you shall laqach (take / seize) him from my mazabach (altar), that he may mawath (death).
"Anyone who attacks his ab (father) or his am (mother) shall be mawath (death) put to mawath (death).
"Anyone who kidnaps someone and makar (sells) him, or if he is matzaa (found) in his yad (hand), he shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death).
"Anyone who qalal (curses) his ab (father) or his am (mother) shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death).
"If anashayam (men) quarrel and ayash (man / husband) nakah (strikes) the other with a aban (stone), or with his agarap (fist), and he doesn't mawath (death), but is confined to mashakab (bed);

If he qawam (rise up) again and halak (move) around with his mashainah (staff), then he who nakah (struck) him shall be cleared: only he shall nathan (give) for the shabath (shabath / rest) of his time, and shall provide for his healing until he is rapaa (thoroughly) rapaa (healed).
"If a ayash (man / husband) nakah (strikes) his ibad (servant) or his amah (maid) with a shabat (rod), and he mawath (death) under his yad (hand), he shall naqam (surely) be naqam (punished).
Ak (notwithstanding), if he gets up after a yawam (day) or yawam (day), he shall not be naqam (punished), for he is his property.

"If anashayam (men) fight and nagap (hurt) a pregnant ayashah (woman / wife) so that she gives birth prematurely, and yet no harm follows, he shall be inash (surely) fined as much as the ayashah (woman / wife) bail (husband) demands and the palalayam (judges) allow.
But if any harm follows, then you must nathan (give) napash (soul) for napash (soul),
Iyan (eye) for iyan (eye), shan (tooth) for shan (tooth), yad (hand) for yad (hand), ragal (feet / foot) for ragal (feet / foot),
Kawayah (burning) for kawayah (burning), patzai (wound) for patzai (wound), and chabawarah (bruise) for chabawarah (bruise).

"If a ayash (man / husband) nakah (strikes) his ibad (servant) iyan (eye), or his amah (maid's) iyan (eye), and shachath (destroys) it, he shall shalach (send) him go chapashay (free) for his iyan (eye) sake.
If he strikes out his male ibad (servant) shan (tooth), or his female amah (servant's) shan (tooth), he shall shalach (send) him go chapashay (free) for his shan (tooth's) sake.

"If a shawar (bull) nagach (gores) a ayash (man / husband) or a ayashah (woman / wife) to mawath (death), the shawar (bull) shall saqal (surely) be saqal (stoned), and its bashar (flesh) shall not be akal (eat); but the owner of the shawar (bull) shall not be held responsible.

But if the shawar (bull) had a habit of goring in the thamawal (past), and it has been iwad (admonish/bear witness against) to its owner, and he has not shamar (keep/guard) it in, but it has mawath (death) a ayash (man / husband) or a ayashah (woman / wife), the shawar (bull) shall be saqal (stoned), and its owner shall also be put to mawath (death).
If a kapar (ransom) is shayath (put / appoint / make) on him, then he shall nathan (give) for the padayawam (redemption) of his napash (soul) whatever is shayath (put / appoint / make) on him.
Whether it has nagach (gored) a ban (son) or has nagach (gored) a banath (daughter), according to this mashapat (judgment) it shall be ishah (make) to him.

If the shawar (bull) nagach (gores) a male ibad (servant) or a female amah (servant), shalawashayam (thirty) shaqalayam (shekels) of kasap (silver) shall be nathan (give) to their adawan (master / lord), and the shawar (ox) shall be saqal (stoned).

"If a ayash (man / husband) pathach (opens) a bawar (pit), or if a ayash (man / husband) karah (digs) a bawar (pit) and doesn't kasah (cover) it, and a shawar (bull) or a donkey napal (fall / be cast down) into it,
The owner of the bawar (pit) shall make it shalam (good). He shall shawab (turn back / repent) kasap (money) to its owner, and the mawath (death) animal shall be his.

"If one ayash (man / husband) shawar (bull) injures rai (neigbor/another person), so that it mawath (death), then they shall makar (sell) the chay (life) shawar (bull), and chatzah (divide) its kasap (price); and they shall also chatzah (divide) the mawath (death) animal.

Or if it is yadai (known) that the shawar (bull) was in the habit of goring in the thamawal (past), and its owner has not shamar (keep/guard) it in, he shall shalam (surely) shalam (pay) shawar (bull) for shawar (bull), and the mawath (death) animal shall be his own.
"If a mawath (death) steals an ox or a sheep, and nakah (kills) it, or sells it; he shall pay five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.
If the thief is found breaking in, and is struck so that he dies, there shall be no dam (guilt) of bloodshed for him.
If the sun has risen on him, guilt of bloodshed shall be for him; he shall shalam (make) shalam (restitution). If he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his ganabah (theft).
If the stolen property is found in his hand alive, whether it is ox, donkey, or sheep, he shall shalam (pay) double.

"If a man causes a shadah (field) or vineyard to be bair (eaten), and yatzaa (go out / come out) his animal loose, and it grazes in another man's shadah (field), he shall shalam (make) restitution from the best of his own shadah (field), and from the best of his own vineyard.
"If fire breaks out, and catches in thorns so that the shocks of grain, or the standing grain, or the field are consumed; he who kindled the fire shall shalam (surely) shalam (make) restitution.
"If a bail (man) matzaa (delivers) to his neighbor money or stuff to keep, and it is stolen out of the bail (man's) bayath (house); if the ganab (thief) is matzaa (found), he shall pay double.
If the thief isn't found, then the master of the house shall bawaa (come) near to Alahayam, to find out if he hasn't bawaa (come) his hand to his neighbor's shalam (goods).

For every matter of trespass, whether it be for shawar (ox), for donkey, for shah (sheep), for clothing, or for any kind of lost thing, about which one says, ‘This is mine,' the nathan (give) of al (toward) parties shall nathan (give) before Alahayam. He whom Alahayam condemns shall nathan (give) double to his neighbor.
"If a bail (man) delivers to his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any animal to keep, and it dies or is injured, or driven away, no bail (man) seeing it;
The oath of Yahawah shall be between them both, whether he hasn't put his hand to his neighbor's shalam (goods); and its owner shall accept it, and he shall not shalam (make) restitution.
But if it is stolen from him, he shall shalam (make) restitution to its owner.
If it is shabar (torn) in pieces, let him bring it for evidence. He shall not make shalam (good) that which was shabar (torn).
"If a bail (man) borrows anything of his neighbor's, and it is injured, or dies, its owner not being with it, he shall shalam (surely) shalam (make) restitution.
If its owner is with it, he shall not make it ayash (man / husband). If it is a leased thing, it came for its lease.
"If a man entices a bathawalah (virgin) who isn't pledged to be married, and nathan (give) with her, he shall am (mother) pay a dowry for her to be his wife.
If her father utterly refuses to chayah (give) her to him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.
"You shall not allow a sorceress to live.
"Whoever has sex with an animal shall surely be put to death.
"He who sacrifices to any Alahayam, laa (NOT) to Yahawah only, shall be utterly destroyed.
"You shall not wrong an alien, neither shall you oppress him, for you were aliens in the land of Egypt.
"You shall not take advantage of any widow or fatherless child.
If you take advantage of them at all, and they cry at all to me, I will harag (kill) hear their cry;
And my wrath will grow hot, and I will kill you with the sword; and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.
"If you lend money to any of my people with you who is poor, you shall not be to him as a creditor; neither shall you charge him interest.
If you take your neighbor's shamalah (garment) as collateral, you shall restore it to him before the sun goes down,
For that is his only covering, it is his garment for his skin. What would he sleep in? It will happen, when he cries to me, that I will hear, for I am gracious.
"You shall not blaspheme Alahayam, nor curse a ruler of your ban (son).
"You shall not delay to offer from your harvest and from the outflow of your presses. "You shall nathan (give) the firstborn of your sons to me.

You shall hayah (came to pass) likewise with your cattle and with your sheep. Seven qadash (set apart / make holy) it shall be with its mother, then on the eighth qadash (set apart / make holy) you shall give it to me.

"You shall be qadash (set apart / make holy) anawash (men) to me, therefore you shall not akal (eat) any bashar (flesh) that is tarapah (torn) by animals in the shadah (field). You shall shalak (cast) it to the kalab (dogs).
"You shall not spread a shawaa (vanity) shamai (report). Don't join your yad (hand) with the rashai (wicked) to be a malicious id (until / as far as).
"You shall not achar (other) a crowd to do rai (evil); neither shall you inah (answer / respond) in court to side with a rab (multitude) to natah (pervert) justice;
Neither shall you favor a dal (poor) man in his rayab (cause).
"If you pagai (meet) your ayab (enemy) shawar (ox) or his donkey thaih (going) astray, you shall shawab (turn back / repent) shawab (turn back / repent) it back to him again.
If you raah (see) the donkey of him who shanaa (hate) you rabatz (fallen) down under his mashaa (burden), don't izab (leave) him, you shall izab (surely) izab (help) him with it.
"You shall not deny mashapat (justice) to your abayawan (poor) rayab (people) in their lawsuits.
"Rachaq (keep) far from a shaqar (false) charge, and don't harag (kill) the naqay (innocent) and tzadayaq (righteous): for I will not justify the rashai (wicked).
"You shall laqach (take / seize) no shachad (bribe), for a shachad (bribe) iwar (blinds) those who have sight and salap (perverts) the dabaray (words) of the tzadayaq (righteous).

"You shall not lachatz (oppress) an gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner), for you yadai (know) the napash (soul) of an gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner), kay (surely) you were garayam (aliens) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
"For shash (six) shanayam (years) you shall zarai (sow) your aratz (Earth/land), and shall asap (gather) in its thabawaah (increase),

But the shabayaiy (seventh) year you shall let it shamat (rest) and natash (lie) fallow, that the abayawan (poor) of your im (nation / people) may akal (eat); and yathar (what) they leave the animal of the shadah (field) shall akal (eat). In the same way, you shall ishah (make) with your karam (vineyard) and with your zayath (olive) grove.

"Shash (six) yamayam (days) you shall ishah (make) your maishah (work), and on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) you shall shabath (shabath / rest), that your shawar (ox) and your donkey may have nawach (rest), and the ban (son) of your handmaid, and the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) may be napash (soul).
"Be careful to do all things that I have amar (spoke) to you; and don't invoke the sham (name) of other Alahayam, neither shamai (hearken / hear) them be heard out of your pah (mouth).
"You shall observe a chagag (feast) to me shalawash (three) ragalayam (times) a shanah (year).

You shall shamar (keep/guard) the chag (feast/festival) of unleavened matzah (bread). Shabai (seven) yamayam (days) you shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread), as I tzawah (commanded) you, at the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) appointed in the chadash (month) abayab (abib) (for in it you yatzaa (go out / come out) out from Matzarayam (Egypt)), and no one shall raah (see) panayam (face) me rayaqam (empty).

And the chag (feast/festival) of qatzayar (harvest), the bakawar (first) fruits of your maishah (labors), which you zarai (sow) in the shadah (field): and the chag (feast/festival) of harvest, at the yatzaa (go out / come out) of the shanah (year), when you asap (gather) in your maishah (labors) out of the shadah (field).
Shalawash (three) paimayam (times) in the shanah (year) all your zakawar (remember/recall) shall raah (see) panayam (face) the Adawan Yahawah.

"You shall not zabach (offer) the dam (blood) of my zabach (sacrifice) with chamatz (leavened) bread, neither shall the chalab (fat) of my chag (feast/festival) lawan (remain) all night until the baqar (morning).

The raashayath (beginning) of the bakawar (first) fruits of your adamah (ground) you shall bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah your Alahayam. "You shall not bashal (boil) a young goat in its am (mother) chalab (milk).

"Behold, I shalach (send) an malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) panayam (face) you, to shamar (keep/guard) you by the darak (way), and to bawaa (come) you into the maqawam (place) which I have kawan (prepared).
Pay attention to him, and shamai (hearken / hear) to his qawal (sound / voice). Don't marar (provoke) him, for he will not nashaa (lift) your disobedience, for my sham (name) is in him.

But if you shamai (hearken / hear) shamai (hearken / hear) to his qawal (sound / voice), and ishah (make) all that I dabar (word / matter), then I will be an ayab (enemy) to your ayab (enemy), and an tzarar (adversary) to your tzawar (adversaries).

For my malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) shall yalak (go) panayam (face) you, and bawaa (come) you in to the Amaray (Amorite), the Chathay (Hittite), the Parazay (Perizzite), the Kanainay (Canaanite), the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite); and I will kachad (cut) them off.

You shall not shachah (bow) down to their Alahayam, nor ibad (servant) them, nor ishah (make) their practices, but you shall haras (utterly) haras (overthrow) them and demolish their matzabah (pillars).

You shall ibad (servant) Yahawah your Alahayam, and he will barak (blessed) your lacham (bread) and your mayam (Waters), and I will sawar (take) machalah (sickness) sawar (away) from your qarab (among / near).
No one will shakal (miscarry) or be iqar (barren) in your aratz (Earth/land). I will fulfill the masapar (number) of your yawam (day).

I will shalach (send) my ayamah (terror) panayam (face) you, and will confuse all the im (nation / people) to whom you bawaa (come), and I will nathan (give) all your ayab (enemy) turn their irap (neck) to you.
I will shalach (send) the tzaraih (hornet) panayam (face) you, which will garash (drive) out the Chaway (Hivite), the Kanainay (Canaanite), and the Chathay (Hittite), from panayam (face) you.

I will not garash (drive) them out from panayam (face) you in achad (one) shanah (year), lest the aratz (Earth/land) become shamamah (desolate), and the animals of the shadah (field) rab (multiply) against you.
Mait (little) by mait (little) I will garash (drive) them out from panayam (face) you, until you have parah (increased) and nachal (inherit) the aratz (Earth/land).

I will shayath (put / appoint / make) your gabawal (border/boundary) from the sawap (red) yam (sea/waters) even to the yam (sea/waters) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and from the madabar (wilderness) to the nahar (river); for I will nathan (give) the yashabay (inhabitants) of the aratz (Earth/land) into your yad (hand), and you shall garash (drive) them out panayam (face) you.
You shall karath (cut) no barayath (covenant) with them, nor with their Alahayam.
They shall not yashab (inhabit/dwell) in your aratz (Earth/land), lest they make you chataa (sin) against me, for if you ibad (servant) their Alahayam, it will surely be a mawaqash (snare) to you."

He amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "ilah (go up / offer) up to Yahawah, you, and Aharawan (Aaron), Nadab (Nadab), and Abayahawaa (Abihu), and shabaiyam (seventy) of the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel); and shachah (worship) from a distance.
Mashah (Moses) alone shall nagash (come) near to Yahawah, but they shall not nagash (come) near, neither shall the im (nation / people) ilah (go up / offer) up with him."

Mashah (Moses) bawaa (come) and sapar (book) the im (nation / people) all the dabaray (words) of Yahawah, and all the mashapatayam (ordinances); and all the im (nation / people) inah (answer / respond) with achad (one) qawal (sound / voice), and amar (spoke), "All the dabaray (words) which Yahawah has amar (spoke) will we ishah (make)."

Mashah (Moses) kathab (write) all the dabaray (words) of Yahawah, and shakam (rose) up early in the baqar (morning), and banah (build) an mazabach (altar) under the har (mountain), and twelve matzabah (pillars) for the shanayam (two) shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

He shalach (send) nair (young) men of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), who ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilath (offerings) and zabach (sacrificed) shalam (peace) ilath (offerings) of cattle to Yahawah.

Mashah (Moses) laqach (take / seize) chatzay (half) of the dam (blood) and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it in aganath (basins), and chatzay (half) of the dam (blood) he zaraq (sprinkled) on the mazabach (altar).

He laqach (take / seize) the sapar (book / scribed document) of the barayath (covenant) and qaraa (called) it in the azan (ear) of the im (nation / people), and they amar (spoke), "All that Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) will we ishah (make), and be shamai (hearken / hear)."

Mashah (Moses) laqach (take / seize) the dam (blood), and zaraq (sprinkled) it on the im (nation / people), and amar (spoke), "Look, this is the dam (blood) of the barayath (covenant), which Yahawah has karath (cut) with you concerning all these dabarayam (words)."
Then Mashah (Moses), Aharawan (Aaron), Nadab (Nadab), Abayahawaa (Abihu), and shabaiyam (seventy) of the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up.
They raah (see) the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel). Under his ragal (feet / foot) was like a labanah (paved) maishah (work) of sapayar (sapphire) stone, like the skies for tahar (clearness).
He didn't shalach (send) his yad (hand) on the atzayalay (nobles) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel). They chazah (saw) Alahayam, and akal (eat) and shathah (drinks).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "ilah (go up / offer) up to me on the har (mountain), and stay here, and I will nathan (give) you the lachath (tables) of aban (stone) with the thawarah (instruction) and the commands that I have kathab (write), that you may yarah (teach) them."
Mashah (Moses) qawam (rise up) up with Yahawashawai (Joshua), his sharath (servant), and Mashah (Moses) ilah (go up / offer) up onto Alahayam har (mountain).

He amar (spoke) to the zaqanayam (elders), "Wait here for us, until we shawab (turn back / repent) again to you. Behold, Aharawan (Aaron) and Chawar (Hur) are with you. Whoever is involved in a dispute can nagash (go) to them."
Mashah (Moses) ilah (go up / offer) up on the har (mountain), and the inan (cloud) kasah (covered) the har (mountain).

The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah settled on har (mountain) Sayanay (Sinai), and the inan (cloud) kasah (covered) it shash (six) yamayam (days). The shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) he qaraa (called) to Mashah (Moses) out of the thawak (midst) of the inan (cloud).
The maraah (appearance) of the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah was like akal (eat) ash (fire) on the raash (head) of the har (mountain) in the iyanay (eyes) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Mashah (Moses) bawaa (come) into the thawak (midst) of the inan (cloud), and ilah (go up / offer) up on the har (mountain); and Mashah (Moses) was on the har (mountain) arabaiyam (forty) yawam (day) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights).
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

"Dabar (word / matter) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), that they laqach (take / seize) an tharawamah (offering) for me. From everyone whose lab (heart) nadab (makes) him willing you shall laqach (take / seize) my tharawamah (offering).
This is the tharawamah (offering) which you shall laqach (take / seize) from them: zahab (gold), kasap (silver), nachashath (brass),
Thakalath (blue), aragaman (purple), thawalai (scarlet), shash (six) linen, izayam (goats)' hair,
Ayalam (rams)' irath (skins) adam (dyed) red, thachash (sea) cow irath (hides), acacia itz (wood),
Shaman (oil) for the maawar (Maawar / Luminary), bashamayam (spices) for the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil) and for the sam (sweet) qatarath (incense),
Shaham (Onyx) abanay (stones), and abanay (stones) to be malaa (set) for the apawad (ephod) and for the chashan (breastplate).
Let them ishah (make) me a maqadash (sanctuary), that I may shakan (place) thawak (midst) them.
According to all that I show you, the thabanayath (pattern) of the mashakan (tabernacle), and the thabanayath (pattern) of all of its kalay (furniture), even so you shall ishah (make) it.

"They shall ishah (make) an arawan (ark) of acacia itz (wood). Its arak (length) shall be chatzay (two) and a half amathayam (cubits), its rachab (breadth) a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half), and a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half) its qawamah (height).
You shall tzapah (overlay) it with tahawar (pure) zahab (gold). You shall tzapah (overlay) it bayath (house) and outside, and you shall ishah (make) a zahab (gold) molding around it.

You shall yatzaq (cast) arabai (four) tabaith (rings) of zahab (gold) for it, and nathan (give) them in its arabai (four) paim (feet). Shanayam (two) tabaith (rings) shall be on the achad (one) tzalai (side) of it, and shanayam (two) tabaith (rings) on the other side of it.
You shall ishah (make) poles of acacia itz (wood), and tzapah (overlay) them with zahab (gold).
You shall bawaa (come) the poles into the tabaith (rings) on the tzalaith (sides) of the arawan (ark) to nashaa (lift) the arawan (ark).
The poles shall be in the tabaith (rings) of the arawan (ark). They shall not be sawar (taken) from it.
You shall nathan (give) the idawath (testimony) which I shall nathan (give) you into the arawan (ark).

You shall ishah (make) a kaparath (mercy) seat of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold). Chatzay (two) and a half amathayam (cubits) shall be its arak (length), and a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half) its rachab (breadth).
You shall ishah (make) shanayam (two) karawab (cherubim) of hammered zahab (gold). You shall ishah (make) them at the shanayam (two) ends of the kaparath (mercy) seat.

Ishah (make) achad (one) karawab (cherub) at the qatzah (end / extremity / border) end, and achad (one) karawab (cherub) at the other end. You shall ishah (make) the karawab (cherubim) on its shanayam (two) ends of one piece with the kaparath (mercy) seat.

The karawab (cherubim) shall parash (spread) out their kanapayam (wings) upward, sakak (covering) the kaparath (mercy) seat with their kanapayam (wings), with their panay (faces) toward ayash (man / husband) ach (brother/kinsman). The panay (faces) of the karawab (cherubim) shall be toward the kaparath (mercy) seat.
You shall nathan (give) the kaparath (mercy) seat on top of the arawan (ark), and in the arawan (ark) you shall nathan (give) the idawath (testimony) that I will nathan (give) you.

There I will yaid (meet) with you, and I will dabar (word / matter) you from above the kaparath (mercy) seat, from bayan (between) the shanayam (two) karawab (cherubim) which are on the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony), all that I tzawah (command) you for the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

"You shall ishah (make) a shalachan (table) of acacia itz (wood). Two amathayam (cubits) shall be its arak (length), and a amah (cubit) its rachab (breadth), and one and a chatzay (half) amathayam (cubits) its qawamah (height).
You shall tzapah (overlay) it with tahawar (pure) zahab (gold), and ishah (make) a zahab (gold) molding around it.
You shall ishah (make) a rim of a tapach (handbreadth) around it. You shall ishah (make) a zahab (gold) molding on its rim around it.

You shall ishah (make) arabai (four) tabaith (rings) of zahab (gold) for it, and nathan (give) the tabaith (rings) in the arabai (four) paath (corners) that are on its arabai (four) ragal (feet / foot).
The tabaith (rings) shall be close to the rim, for bathayam (places) for the poles to nashaa (lift) the shalachan (table).
You shall ishah (make) the poles of acacia itz (wood), and tzapah (overlay) them with zahab (gold), that the shalachan (table) may be nashaa (lift) with them.
You shall ishah (make) its dishes, its kap (spoons), its ladles, and its manaqayath (bowls) to pour out nasak (offerings) with. You shall ishah (make) them of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold).
You shall nathan (give) lacham (bread) of the presence on the shalachan (table) panayam (face) me thamayad (always).

"You shall ishah (make) a lampstand of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold). Of hammered maqashah (work) shall the lampstand be ishah (make), even its base, its yarak (shaft), its gabayai (cups), its buds, and its parach (flowers), shall be of one piece with it.

There shall be shash (six) branches yatzaa (go out / come out) out of its tzad (sides): shalawash (three) branches of the lampstand out of its achad (one) tzad (side), and shalawash (three) branches of the lampstand out of its other tzad (side);

Shalawash (three) gabaiyam (cups) shaqad (made) like almond blossoms in achad (one) qanah (branch), a bud and a parach (flower); and shalawash (three) gabaiyam (cups) shaqad (made) like almond blossoms in the other qanah (branch), a bud and a parach (flower), so for the shash (six) branches yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the lampstand;
And in the lampstand arabai (four) gabaiyam (cups) shaqad (made) like almond blossoms, its buds and its parach (flowers);

And a bud under shanayam (two) branches of kapathar (one) piece with it, and a bud under shanayam (two) branches of kapathar (one) piece with it, and a bud under shanayam (two) branches of one piece with it, for the shash (six) branches yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the lampstand.
Their buds and their branches shall be of one piece with it, all of it one beaten maqashah (work) of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold).
You shall ishah (make) its nayar (lamps) shabai (seven), and they shall ilah (go up / offer) its nayar (lamps) to give ilah (go up / offer) to the space in front of it.
Its malaqach (snuffers) and its snuff dishes shall be of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold).
It shall be ishah (make) of a kakar (talent) of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold), with all these accessories.
Raah (see) that you ishah (make) them after their thabanayath (pattern), which raah (see) been shown to you on the har (mountain).

"Moreover you shall ishah (make) the mashakan (tabernacle) with ishar (ten) yarayaith (curtains); of fine shazar (twined) shash (six), and thakalath (blue), and aragaman (purple), and shanay (second), with cherubim. The maishah (work) of the skillful workman you shall ishah (make) them.

The arak (length) of achad (one) yarayaih (curtain) shall be isharayam (twenty) shamanah (eight) amah (cubits), and the rachab (breadth) of achad (one) yarayaih (curtain) arabai (four) amah (cubits): all the yarayaith (curtains) shall have achad (one) madah (measure).

Chamash (five) yarayaith (curtains) shall be chabar (coupled) together ayashah (woman / wife) to achawath (another); and the other chamash (five) yarayaith (curtains) shall be chabar (coupled) ayashah (woman / wife) to achawath (another).

You shall ishah (make) lalaath (loops) of thakalath (blue) on the shapah (edge) of the achad (one) yarayaih (curtain) from the qatzah (end / extremity / border) in the chabarath (coupling); and likewise you shall ishah (make) in the shapah (edge) of the yarayaih (curtain) that is outmost in the shanay (second) machabarath (coupling).

You shall ishah (make) chamashayam (fifty) lalaath (loops) in the achad (one) yarayaih (curtain), and you shall ishah (make) chamashayam (fifty) lalaath (loops) in the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the yarayaih (curtain) that is in the shanay (second) machabarath (coupling). The lalaath (loops) shall be opposite ayashah (woman / wife) to achawath (another).

You shall ishah (make) chamashayam (fifty) clasps of zahab (gold), and chabar (couple) the yarayaith (curtains) ayashah (woman / wife) to another with the clasps: and the mashakan (tabernacle) shall be a unit.
"You shall ishah (make) yarayaith (curtains) of izayam (goats)' hair for a ahal (covering) over the mashakan (tabernacle). You shall ishah (make) them ishathay (eleven) yarayaith (curtains).

The arak (length) of achad (one) yarayaih (curtain) shall be shalawashayam (thirty) amah (cubits), and the rachab (breadth) of achad (one) yarayaih (curtain) arabai (four) amah (cubits): the ishathay (eleven) yarayaith (curtains) shall have achad (one) madah (measure).

You shall chabar (couple) chamash (five) yarayaith (curtains) by themselves, and shash (six) yarayaith (curtains) by themselves, and shall kapal (double) over the shashay (sixth) yarayaih (curtain) in the mawal (forefront) of the ahal (tent).

You shall ishah (make) chamashayam (fifty) lalaath (loops) on the shapah (edge) of the achad (one) yarayaih (curtain) that is outmost in the chabarath (coupling), and chamashayam (fifty) lalaath (loops) on the shapah (edge) of the yarayaih (curtain) which is outmost in the shanay (second) chabarath (coupling).
You shall ishah (make) chamashayam (fifty) clasps of nachashath (brass), and bawaa (come) the clasps into the lalaath (loops), and chabar (couple) the ahal (tent) achad (one), that it may be one.

The overhanging part that idap (remains) of the yarayaith (curtains) of the ahal (tent), the chatzay (half) yarayaih (curtain) that idap (remains), shall hang over the achawar (back) of the mashakan (tabernacle).

The amah (cubit) on the one zah (this / that / these), and the amah (cubit) on the other side, of that which idap (remains) in the arak (length) of the yarayaith (curtains) of the ahal (tent), shall hang over the tzaday (sides) of the mashakan (tabernacle) on this side and on that side, to kasah (cover) it.
You shall ishah (make) a makasah (covering) for the ahal (tent) of ayalam (rams)' irath (skins) adam (dyed) red, and a makasah (covering) of thachash (sea) cow irath (hides) mail (top/above).
"You shall ishah (make) the qarashayam (boards) for the mashakan (tabernacle) of acacia itz (wood), imad (standing) up.
Ishar (ten) amawath (cubits) shall be the arak (length) of a qarash (board), and one and a chatzay (half) amawath (cubits) the rachab (breadth) of achad (one) qarash (board).
There shall be shanayam (two) tenons in achad (one) qarash (board), joined to achad (one) achawath (another): thus you shall ishah (make) for all the qarashay (boards) of the mashakan (tabernacle).
You shall ishah (make) the qarashayam (boards) for the mashakan (tabernacle), isharayam (twenty) qarashayam (boards) for the nagab (south) paah (side) southward.

You shall ishah (make) arabaiyam (forty) adanay (sockets) of kasap (silver) under the isharayam (twenty) qarash (boards); shanayam (two) adanay (sockets) under achad (one) qarash (board) for its shanayam (two) tenons, and shanayam (two) adanay (sockets) under another qarash (board) for its shanayam (two) tenons.
For the shanay (second) tzalai (side) of the mashakan (tabernacle), on the tzapawan (north) tzalai (side), isharayam (twenty) qarash (boards),

And their arabaiyam (forty) adanayam (sockets) of kasap (silver); shanayam (two) adanayam (sockets) under achad (one) qarash (board), and shanayam (two) adanayam (sockets) under another qarash (board).
For the far yarakah (part) of the mashakan (tabernacle) westward you shall ishah (make) shash (six) qarashayam (boards).
You shall ishah (make) shanayam (two) qarashayam (boards) for the maqatzaith (corners) of the mashakan (tabernacle) in the far yarakah (part).

They shall be double matah (beneath), and in the same thaam (way) they shall be whole to its raash (head) to achad (one) tabaith (ring): thus shall it be for them shanayam (two); they shall be for the shanayam (two) maqatzaith (corners).

There shall be shamanah (eight) qarashayam (boards), and their adanayam (sockets) of kasap (silver), sixteen adanayam (sockets); shanayam (two) adanayam (sockets) under achad (one) qarash (board), and shanayam (two) adanayam (sockets) under another qarash (board).
"You shall ishah (make) barayacham (bars) of acacia itz (wood): chamash (five) for the qarashay (boards) of the achad (one) tzalai (side) of the mashakan (tabernacle),

And chamash (five) barayacham (bars) for the qarashay (boards) of the other tzalai (side) of the mashakan (tabernacle), and chamash (five) barayacham (bars) for the qarashay (boards) of the tzalai (side) of the mashakan (tabernacle), for the far yarakah (part) westward.
The thayakawan (middle) barayach (bar) in the thayakawan (midst) of the qarashayam (boards) shall pass through from qatzah (end / extremity / border) to qatzah (end / extremity / border).

You shall tzapah (overlay) the qarashayam (boards) with zahab (gold), and ishah (make) their tabaith (rings) of zahab (gold) for bathayam (places) for the barayacham (bars): and you shall tzapah (overlay) the barayacham (bars) with zahab (gold).
You shall qawam (rise up) up the mashakan (tabernacle) according to the mashapat (way) that it was shown to you on the har (mountain).

"You shall ishah (make) a parakath (veil) of thakalath (blue), and aragaman (purple), and shanay (second), and fine shazar (twined) shash (six), with karawab (cherubim). The maishah (work) of the skillful ishah (make) shall it be made.
You shall nathan (give) it on arabai (four) imawaday (pillars) of acacia overlaid with zahab (gold); their waw (and) shall be of zahab (gold), on arabai (four) adanay (sockets) of kasap (silver).
