You shall nathan (give) up the parakath (veil) under the clasps, and shall bawaa (come) the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony) in there bayath (house) the parakath (veil): and the parakath (veil) shall badal (separated) the qadash (set apart / make holy) place from the most qadash (set apart / make holy) for you.
You shall nathan (give) the kaparath (mercy) seat on the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony) in the most qadash (set apart / make holy) place.

You shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) the shalachan (table) outside the parakath (veil), and the lampstand over nakach (against) the shalachan (table) on the tzalai (side) of the mashakan (tabernacle) toward the thayaman (south): and you shall nathan (give) the shalachan (table) on the tzapawan (north) tzalai (side).

"You shall ishah (make) a screen for the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent), of thakalath (blue), and aragaman (purple), and thawalai (scarlet), and fine shazar (twined) shash (six), the maishah (work) of the raqam (embroiderer).

You shall ishah (make) for the screen chamash (five) imawaday (pillars) of acacia, and tzapah (overlay) them with zahab (gold): their waw (and) shall be of zahab (gold): and you shall yatzaq (cast) chamash (five) adanay (sockets) of nachashath (brass) for them.

"You shall ishah (make) the mazabach (altar) of acacia itz (wood), chamash (five) amawath (cubits) arak (length), and chamash (five) amawath (cubits) rachab (broad); the mazabach (altar) shall be rabai (fourth): and its qawamah (height) shall be shalawash (three) amawath (cubits).
You shall ishah (make) its qaran (horn) on its arabai (four) panah (corner / cornerstone); its qaran (horn) shall be of one piece with it; and you shall tzapah (overlay) it with nachashath (brass).

You shall ishah (make) its sayar (pots) to dashan (take) away its ashes, its yai (shovels), its basins, its flesh hooks, and its machathah (fire) pans: all its kalay (vessels) you shall ishah (make) of nachashath (brass).

You shall ishah (make) a makabar (grating) for it of network of nachashath (brass): and on the rashath (net) you shall ishah (make) arabai (four) bronze tabaith (rings) in its arabai (four) qatzah (end / extremity / border).
You shall nathan (give) it under the ledge around the mazabach (altar) matah (beneath), that the rashath (net) may reach halfway up the mazabach (altar).
You shall ishah (make) poles for the mazabach (altar), poles of acacia itz (wood), and tzapah (overlay) them with nachashath (brass).
Its poles shall be bawaa (come) into the tabaith (rings), and the poles shall be on the shanayam (two) tzalaith (sides) of the mazabach (altar), when nashaa (lift) it.
You shall ishah (make) it with nabab (hollow) planks. They shall ishah (make) it as it raah (see) been shown you on the har (mountain).

"You shall ishah (make) the chatzar (court) of the mashakan (tabernacle): for the nagab (south) paah (side) southward there shall be qalaiyam (hangings) for the chatzar (court) of fine shazar (twined) shash (six) one maah (hundred) amah (cubits) arak (length) for achad (one) paah (side):

And its imadayam (pillars) shall be isharayam (twenty), and their adan (sockets) isharayam (twenty), of nachashath (brass); the waway (hooks) of the imadayam (pillars) and their chashaq (fillets) shall be of kasap (silver).

Likewise for the tzapawan (north) paah (side) in arak (length) there shall be qalaiyam (hangings) one maah (hundred) cubits arak (length), and its imadayam (pillars) isharayam (twenty), and their adan (sockets) isharayam (twenty), of nachashath (brass); the waway (hooks) of the imadayam (pillars), and their chashaq (fillets), of kasap (silver).

For the rachab (breadth) of the chatzar (court) on the yam (sea/waters) paah (side) shall be qalaiyam (hangings) of chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits); their imawad (pillar) ishar (ten), and their adan (sockets) ishar (ten).
The rachab (breadth) of the chatzar (court) on the qadam (east) paah (side) eastward shall be chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits).
The qalaiyam (hangings) for the one kathap (side) of the gate shall be chamash (fifteen) amah (cubits); their imawad (pillar) shalawash (three), and their adan (sockets) shalawash (three).
For the other kathap (side) shall be qalaiyam (hangings) of chamash (fifteen) cubits; their imawad (pillar) shalawash (three), and their adan (sockets) shalawash (three).

For the shair (gate) of the chatzar (court) shall be a screen of isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits), of thakalath (blue), and aragaman (purple), and shanay (second), and fine shazar (twined) shash (six), the raqam (work) of the embroiderer; their imawad (pillar) arabai (four), and their adan (sockets) arabai (four).
All the imawaday (pillars) of the chatzar (court) around shall be chashaq (filleted) with kasap (silver); their waw (and) of kasap (silver), and their adan (sockets) of nachashath (brass).

The arak (length) of the chatzar (court) shall be one maah (hundred) amawath (cubits), and the rachab (breadth) chamashayam (fifty) every where, and the qawamah (height) chamash (five) amawath (cubits), of fine shazar (twined) shash (six), and their adan (sockets) of nachashath (brass).

All the kalay (instruments) of the mashakan (tabernacle) in all its ibadah (service), and all its yathadath (pins), and all the yathadath (pins) of the chatzar (court), shall be of nachashath (brass).

"You shall tzawah (command) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), that they laqach (take / seize) to you zak (pure) zayath (olive) shaman (oil) kathayath (beaten) for the maawar (Maawar / Luminary), to cause a nayar (lamp) to ilah (go up / offer) continually.

In the ahal (tent) of Meeting, outside the parakath (veil) which is before the idawath (testimony), Aharawan (Aaron) and his banay (sons) shall keep it in irak (order) from irab (evening) to baqar (morning) panayam (face) Yahawah: it shall be a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) throughout their dawar (generation / age / period) on the behalf of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

"Qarab (come close) Aharawan (Aaron) your ach (brother/kinsman), and his banay (sons) with him, near to you from thawak (midst) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), that he may kahan (priest) to me in the priest's office, even Aharawan (Aaron), Nadab (Nadab) and Abayahawaa (Abihu), Alaizar (Eleazar) and Ayathamar (Ithamar), Aharawan (Aaron's) banay (sons).
You shall ishah (make) qadash (set apart / make holy) bagaday (garments) for Aharawan (Aaron) your ach (brother/kinsman), for kabawad (glory) and for thapaarah (beauty).

You shall dabar (word / matter) to all who are chakam (wise) lab (heart), whom I malaa (have) filled with the rawach (spirit / wind) of chakamah (wisdom), that they ishah (make) Aharawan (Aaron's) bagaday (garments) to qadash (set apart / make holy) him, that he may kahan (priest) to me in the priest's office.

These are the bagadayam (garments) which they shall ishah (make): a chashan (breastplate), and an apawad (ephod), and a maiyal (robe), and a kathanath (coat) of checker thashabatz (work), a turban, and a sash: and they shall ishah (make) qadash (set apart / make holy) bagadayam (garments) for Aharawan (Aaron) your ach (brother/kinsman), and his ban (son), that he may kahan (priest) to me in the priest's office.
They shall laqach (take / seize) the zahab (gold), and the thakalath (blue), and the aragaman (purple), and the shanay (second), and the shash (six) linen.

"They shall ishah (make) the apawad (ephod) of zahab (gold), of thakalath (blue), and aragaman (purple), shanay (second), and fine shazar (twined) shash (six), the maishah (work) of the skillful chashab (workman).
It shall have shanayam (two) kathap (shoulder) straps chabar (joined) to the shanayam (two) ends of it, that it may be chabar (joined) together.

The skillfully woven band, which is on it, that is on him, shall be like its maishah (work) and of the same piece; of zahab (gold), of thakalath (blue), and aragaman (purple), and shanay (second), and fine shazar (twined) shash (six).
You shall laqach (take / seize) shanayam (two) shaham (Onyx) abanay (stones), and pathach (engrave) on them the shamawath (names) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel):

Shash (six) of their shamawath (names) on the achad (one) aban (stone), and the shamawath (names) of the shash (six) that yathar (remain) on the other aban (stone), in the order of their thawaladah (generation).

With the maishah (work) of an charash (engraver) in aban (stone), like the engravings of a chawatham (signet), you shall pathach (engrave) the shanayam (two) abanayam (stones), according to the shamath (names) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel): you shall ishah (make) them to be enclosed in settings of zahab (gold).

You shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) the shanayam (two) abanayam (stones) on the kathap (shoulder) straps of the apawad (ephod), to be abanayam (stones) of zakarawan (memorial) for the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel): and Aharawan (Aaron) shall nashaa (lift) their sham (name) panayam (face) Yahawah on his shanayam (two) kathapath (shoulders) for a zakarawan (memorial).
You shall ishah (make) settings of zahab (gold),

And shanayam (two) sharasharath (chains) of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold); you shall ishah (make) them like cords of braided maishah (work): and you shall nathan (give) the braided sharasharath (chains) on the settings.

"You shall ishah (make) a chashan (breastplate) of mashapat (judgment), the maishah (work) of the skillful workman; like the maishah (work) of the apawad (ephod) you shall ishah (make) it; of zahab (gold), of thakalath (blue), and aragaman (purple), and shanay (second), and fine shazar (twined) shash (six), you shall ishah (make) it.
It shall be rabai (fourth) and folded double; a zarath (span) shall be its arak (length) of it, and a zarath (span) its rachab (breadth).
You shall malaa (set) in it malaah (settings) of aban (stone), arabai (four) tawarayam (rows) of aban (stone): a tawar (row) of ruby, patadah (topaz), and beryl shall be the achad (one) tawar (row);
And the shanay (second) tawar (row) a turquoise, a sapayar (sapphire), and an napak (emerald);
And the shalayashay (third) tawar (row) a jacinth, an shabaw (agate), and an achalamah (amethyst);
And the rabayaiy (fourth) tawar (row) a chrysolite, an shaham (Onyx), and a yashapah (jasper): they shall be enclosed in zahab (gold) in their malaah (settings).

The abanayam (stones) shall be according to the shamath (names) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), shanayam (two), according to their shamath (names); like the engravings of a chawatham (signet), everyone according to his sham (name), they shall be for the shanayam (two) shabat (tribes).
You shall ishah (make) on the chashan (breastplate) sharashath (chains) like cords, of braided maishah (work) of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold).

You shall ishah (make) on the chashan (breastplate) shanayam (two) tabaiwath (rings) of zahab (gold), and shall nathan (give) the shanayam (two) tabaiwath (rings) on the shanayam (two) ends of the chashan (breastplate).
You shall nathan (give) the shanayam (two) braided chains of zahab (gold) in the shanayam (two) tabaith (rings) at the ends of the chashan (breastplate).

The other shanayam (two) ends of the shanayam (two) braided chains you shall nathan (give) on the shanayam (two) settings, and nathan (give) them on the kathap (shoulder) straps of the apawad (ephod) in its forepart.

You shall ishah (make) shanayam (two) tabaiwath (rings) of zahab (gold), and you shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) them on the shanayam (two) ends of the chashan (breastplate), on its shapah (edge), which is toward the ibar (side) of the apawad (ephod) inward.

You shall ishah (make) shanayam (two) tabaiwath (rings) of zahab (gold), and shall nathan (give) them on the shanayam (two) kathap (shoulder) straps of the apawad (ephod) matah (underneath), in its forepart, close by its machabarath (coupling), mail (top/above) the skillfully woven band of the apawad (ephod).

They shall rakas (bind) the chashan (breastplate) by its tabaith (rings) to the tabaith (rings) of the apawad (ephod) with a pathayal (lace) of thakalath (blue), that it may be on the skillfully woven band of the apawad (ephod), and that the chashan (breastplate) may not swing out from the apawad (ephod).

Aharawan (Aaron) shall nashaa (lift) the shamawath (names) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) in the chashan (breastplate) of mashapat (judgment) on his lab (heart), when he bawaa (come) in to the qadash (set apart / make holy) place, for a zakarawan (memorial) panayam (face) Yahawah continually.

You shall nathan (give) in the chashan (breastplate) of mashapat (judgment) the awarayam (urim) and the thamayam (complete / whole); and they shall be on Aharawan (Aaron's) lab (heart), when he bawaa (come) in panayam (face) Yahawah: and Aharawan (Aaron) shall nashaa (lift) the mashapat (judgment) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) on his lab (heart) panayam (face) Yahawah continually.
"You shall ishah (make) the maiyal (robe) of the apawad (ephod) kalayal (all) of thakalath (blue).

It shall have a pah (hole) for the raash (head) in its thawak (midst): it shall have a shapah (binding) of woven maishah (work) around its pah (hole), as it were the pah (hole) of a coat of mail, that it not be qarai (torn).

On its shawal (hem) you shall ishah (make) ramanay (pomegranates) of thakalath (blue), and of aragaman (purple), and of shanay (second), around its shawal (hem); and paimanay (bells) of zahab (gold) thawak (midst) and around them:
A zahab (gold) paiman (bell) and a ramawan (pomegranate), a zahab (gold) paiman (bell) and a ramawan (pomegranate), around the shawal (hem) of the maiyal (robe).

It shall be on Aharawan (Aaron) to sharath (minister): and its qawal (sound / voice) shall be shamai (hearken / hear) when he bawaa (come) in to the qadash (set apart / make holy) place panayam (face) Yahawah, and when he yatzaa (go out / come out) out, that he not mawath (death).
"You shall ishah (make) a tzayatz (plate) of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold), and pathach (engrave) on it, like the engravings of a chawatham (signet), ‘qadash (set apart / make holy) TO Yahawah.'
You shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) it on a pathayal (lace) of thakalath (blue), and it shall be on the sash; on the front of the sash it shall be.

It shall be on Aharawan (Aaron's) matzach (forehead), and Aharawan (Aaron) shall nashaa (lift) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the qadash (set apart / make holy) things, which the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall make qadash (set apart / make holy) in all their qadash (set apart / make holy) mathanath (gifts); and it shall be thamayad (always) on his matzach (forehead), that they may be accepted panayam (face) Yahawah.

You shall weave the kathanath (coat) in checker work of shash (six) linen, and you shall ishah (make) a turban of shash (six) linen, and you shall ishah (make) a sash, the raqam (work) of the embroiderer.

"You shall ishah (make) kathanath (coats) for Aharawan (Aaron's) banay (sons), and you shall ishah (make) sashes for them and you shall ishah (make) headbands for them, for kabawad (glory) and for thapaarah (beauty).

You shall labash (put) them on Aharawan (Aaron) your ach (brother/kinsman), and on his ban (son) with him, and shall mashach (anoint) them, and malaa (consecrate) them, and qadash (set apart / make holy) them, that they may kahan (priest) to me in the priest's office.
You shall ishah (make) them bad (linen) breeches to kasah (cover) the bashar (flesh) of their nakedness; from the waist even to the yarakayam (thighs) they shall reach:

They shall be on Aharawan (Aaron), and on his ban (son), when they bawaa (come) in to the ahal (tent) of Meeting, or when they nagash (come) near to the mazabach (altar) to sharath (minister) in the qadash (set apart / make holy) place; that they don't nashaa (lift) iwan (guilt/iniquity), and mawath (death): it shall be a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) to him and to his descendants achar (other) him.

"This is the thing that you shall ishah (make) to them to make them qadash (set apart / make holy), to kahan (priest) to me in the priest's office: laqach (take / seize) achad (one) ban (son) par (bull) and shanayam (two) ayalam (rams) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish,

Unleavened lacham (bread), unleavened chalah (cakes) balal (mixed) with shaman (oil), and unleavened raqayaqay (wafers) mashach (anointed) with shaman (oil): you shall ishah (make) them of fine chatah (wheat) salath (flour).
You shall nathan (give) them into achad (one) sal (basket), and qarab (come close) them in the sal (basket), with the par (bull) and the shanayam (two) ayalam (rams).
You shall qarab (come close) Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son) to the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and shall rachatz (wash) them with mayam (Waters).

You shall laqach (take / seize) the bagadayam (garments), and labash (put) on Aharawan (Aaron) the kathanath (coat), the maiyal (robe) of the apawad (ephod), the apawad (ephod), and the chashan (breastplate), and clothe him with the skillfully woven band of the apawad (ephod);
And you shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) the turban on his raash (head), and nathan (give) the qadash (set apart / make holy) nazar (crown / consecrate) on the turban.
Then you shall laqach (take / seize) the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), and yatzaq (pour) it on his raash (head), and mashach (anoint) him.
You shall qarab (come close) his ban (son), and labash (put) kathanath (coats) on them.

You shall clothe them with belts, Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son), and chabash (bind) headbands on them: and they shall have the kahanah (priesthood) by a iwalam (forever) chaqah (statute): and you shall malaa (consecrate) Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son).

"You shall qarab (come close) the par (bull) panayam (face) the ahal (tent) of Meeting: and Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son) shall samak (lay) their yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the par (bull).
You shall shachat (kill) the par (bull) panayam (face) Yahawah, at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

You shall laqach (take / seize) of the dam (blood) of the par (bull), and nathan (give) it on the qaranath (horns) of the mazabach (altar) with your atzabai (finger); and you shall shapak (pour) out all the dam (blood) at the base of the mazabach (altar).

You shall laqach (take / seize) all the chalab (fat) that kasah (covers) the innards, the cover of the kabad (liver), the shanayam (two) kalayath (kidneys), and the chalab (fat) that is on them, and qatar (burn) them on the mazabach (altar).
But the bashar (flesh) of the par (bull), and its iwar (skin), and its parash (dung), you shall sharap (burn) with ash (fire) outside of the machanah (camp): it is a chataah (sin) offering.
"You shall also laqach (take / seize) the achad (one) ayal (ram); and Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son) shall samak (lay) their yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the ayal (ram).
You shall shachat (kill) the ayal (ram), and you shall laqach (take / seize) its dam (blood), and zaraq (sprinkle) it around on the mazabach (altar).
You shall nathach (cut) the ayal (ram) into its nathach (pieces), and rachatz (wash) its innards, and its karai (legs), and nathan (give) them with its nathach (pieces), and with its raash (head).
You shall qatar (burn) the whole ayal (ram) on the mazabach (altar): it is a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah; it is a pleasant aroma, an ashah (fire / offering made by fire) made by fire to Yahawah.
"You shall laqach (take / seize) the other ayal (ram); and Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son) shall samak (lay) their yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the ayal (ram).

Then you shall shachat (kill) the ayal (ram), and laqach (take / seize) some of its dam (blood), and nathan (give) it on the thanawak (tip) of the right azan (ear) of Aharawan (Aaron), and on the thanawak (tip) of the yamanay (right) azan (ear) of his ban (son), and on the bahan (thumb) of their yamanay (right) yad (hand), and on the big bahan (toe) of their yamanay (right) ragal (feet / foot), and zaraq (sprinkle) the dam (blood) around on the mazabach (altar).

You shall laqach (take / seize) of the dam (blood) that is on the mazabach (altar), and of the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), and nazah (sprinkle) it on Aharawan (Aaron), and on his bagaday (garments), and on his ban (son), and on the bagaday (garments) of his ban (son) with him: and he shall be made qadash (set apart / make holy), and his bagaday (garments), and his ban (son), and his ban (son)' bagaday (garments) with him.

Also you shall laqach (take / seize) some of the ayal (ram's) chalab (fat), the fat tail, the chalab (fat) that kasah (covers) the innards, the cover of the kabad (liver), the shanayam (two) kalayath (kidneys), the chalab (fat) that is on them, and the yamayan (right hand) shawaq (thigh) (for it is a ayal (ram) of malaa (consecration)),

And achad (one) kakar (loaf) of lacham (bread), achad (one) chalah (cake) of shaman (oiled) bread, and one raqayaq (wafer) out of the sal (basket) of unleavened matzah (bread) that is panayam (face) Yahawah.

You shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) all of this in Aharawan (Aaron's) kapay (hands), and in his ban (son)' kapay (hands), and shall nawap (wave) them for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (face) Yahawah.

You shall laqach (take / seize) them from their yad (hand), and qatar (burn) them on the mazabach (altar) on the burnt ilah (offering), for a pleasant aroma panayam (face) Yahawah: it is an ashah (fire / offering made by fire) made by fire to Yahawah.

"You shall laqach (take / seize) the chazah (breast) of Aharawan (Aaron's) ayal (ram) of malaa (consecration), and nawap (wave) it for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (face) Yahawah: and it shall be your manah (portion).

You shall qadash (set apart / make holy) the chazah (breast) of the wave thanawapah (offering), and the shawaq (thigh) of the wave thanawapah (offering), which is nawap (waved), and which is rawam (will lift up) up, of the ayal (ram) of malaa (consecration), even of that which is for Aharawan (Aaron), and of that which is for his ban (son):

And it shall be for Aharawan (Aaron) and his banay (sons) as their chaq (statute) iwalam (forever) from the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel); for it is a wave tharawamah (offering): and it shall be a wave tharawamah (offering) from the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) of the zabachay (sacrifices) of their shalam (peace) offerings, even their wave tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah.
"The qadash (set apart / make holy) bagaday (garments) of Aharawan (Aaron) shall be for his ban (son) achar (other) him, to be mashachah (anointed) in them, and to be malaa (consecrated) in them.

Shabai (seven) yamayam (days) shall the ban (son) who is kahan (priest) in his place labash (put) them on, when he bawaa (come) into the ahal (tent) of Meeting to sharath (minister) in the qadash (set apart / make holy) place.
"You shall laqach (take / seize) the ayal (ram) of malaa (consecration), and bashal (boil) its bashar (flesh) in a qadawash (holy) maqawam (place).
Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son) shall akal (eat) the bashar (flesh) of the ayal (ram), and the lacham (bread) that is in the sal (basket), at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

They shall akal (eat) those things with which kapar (atonement) was made, to malaa (consecrate) and qadash (set apart / make holy) them: but a stranger shall not akal (eat) of it, because they are qadash (set apart / make holy).

If anything of the bashar (flesh) of the malaa (consecration), or of the lacham (bread), yathar (remains) to the baqar (morning), then you shall sharap (burn) the remainder with ash (fire): it shall not be akal (eat), because it is qadash (set apart / make holy).
"You shall ishah (make) so to Aharawan (Aaron), and to his ban (son), according to all that I have tzawah (commanded) you. You shall malaa (consecrate) them shabai (seven) yamayam (days).

Every yawam (day) you shall ishah (make) the par (bull) of chataah (sin) offering for kapar (atonement): and you shall chataa (cleanse) the mazabach (altar), when you make kapar (atonement) for it; and you shall mashach (anoint) it, to qadash (set apart / make holy) it.

Shabai (seven) yamayam (days) you shall make kapar (atonement) for the mazabach (altar), and qadash (set apart / make holy) it: and the mazabach (altar) shall be most qadash (set apart / make holy); whatever touches the mazabach (altar) shall be qadash (set apart / make holy).
"Now this is that which you shall ishah (make) on the mazabach (altar): shanayam (two) kabashayam (lambs) a shanah (year) old yawam (day) by yawam (day) continually.
The achad (one) kabash (lamb) you shall ishah (make) in the baqar (morning); and the other kabash (lamb) you shall ishah (make) at irab (evening):

And with the achad (one) kabash (lamb) a isharawan (tenth) part of an ephah of fine salath (flour) mixed with the rabai (fourth) part of a hayan (hin) of kathayath (beaten) shaman (oil), and the rabai (fourth) part of a hayan (hin) of yayan (wine) for a drink nasak (offering).

The other kabash (lamb) you shall ishah (make) at irab (evening), and shall ishah (make) to it according to the meal manachah (offering) of the baqar (morning), and according to its drink nasak (offering), for a pleasant aroma, an ashah (fire / offering made by fire) made by fire to Yahawah.

It shall be a thamayad (continual) burnt ilah (offering) throughout your dawar (generation / age / period) at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting panayam (face) Yahawah, where I will yaid (meet) with you, to dabar (word / matter) there to you.
There I will yaid (meet) with the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel); and the place shall be qadash (set apart / make holy) by my kabawad (glory).

I will qadash (set apart / make holy) the ahal (tent) of Meeting and the mazabach (altar): Aharawan (Aaron) also and his ban (son) I will qadash (set apart / make holy), to kahan (priest) to me in the priest's office.
I will shakan (place) thawak (midst) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and will be their Alahayam.

They shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah their Alahayam, who yatzaa (go out / come out) them forth out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), that I might shakan (place) thawak (midst) them: I am Yahawah their Alahayam.
"You shall ishah (make) an mazabach (altar) to maqatar (burn) qatarath (incense) on. You shall ishah (make) it of acacia itz (wood).

Its arak (length) shall be a amah (cubit), and its rachab (breadth) a amah (cubit). It shall be rabai (fourth), and its qawamah (height) shall be two amathayam (cubits). Its qaran (horn) shall be of one piece with it.
You shall tzapah (overlay) it with tahawar (pure) zahab (gold), its gag (top), its qayar (sides) around it, and its qaran (horn); and you shall ishah (make) a zahab (gold) molding around it.

You shall ishah (make) shanayam (two) zahab (gold) tabaith (rings) for it under its molding; on its shanayam (two) ribs, on its shanayam (two) tzad (sides) you shall ishah (make) them; and they shall be for bathayam (places) for poles with which to nashaa (lift) it.
You shall ishah (make) the poles of acacia itz (wood), and tzapah (overlay) them with zahab (gold).

You shall nathan (give) it panayam (face) the parakath (veil) that is by the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony), panayam (face) the kaparath (mercy) seat that is over the idawath (testimony), where I will yaid (meet) with you.
Aharawan (Aaron) shall qatar (burn) qatarath (incense) of sam (sweet) spices on it every baqar (morning). When he tends the narath (lamps), he shall qatar (burn) it.

When Aharawan (Aaron) ilah (go up / offer) the narath (lamps) at irab (evening), he shall qatar (burn) it, a thamayad (perpetual) qatar (incense) panayam (face) Yahawah throughout your dawar (generation / age / period).
You shall ilah (go up / offer) no zawar (strange) qatarath (incense) on it, nor burnt ilah (offering), nor meal manachah (offering); and you shall nasak (pour) no drink nasak (offering) on it.

Aharawan (Aaron) shall make kapar (atonement) on its qaran (horn) achad (one) in the shanah (year); with the dam (blood) of the chataah (sin) offering of kapar (atonement) achad (one) in the shanah (year) he shall make kapar (atonement) for it throughout your dawar (generation / age / period). It is most qadash (set apart / make holy) to Yahawah."
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

"When you nashaa (lift) a census of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), according to those who are paqad (visit) among them, then each ayash (man / husband) shall nathan (give) a kapar (ransom) for his napash (soul) to Yahawah, when you paqad (visit) them; that there be no nagap (plague) among them when you paqad (visit) them.

They shall nathan (give) this, everyone who passes over to those who are paqad (visit), machatzayath (half) a shaqal (shekel) after the shaqal (shekel) of the qadash (set apart / make holy); (the shaqal (shekel) is isharayam (twenty) garah (gerahs);) machatzayath (half) a shaqal (shekel) for an tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah.
Everyone who passes over to those who are paqad (visit), from isharayam (twenty) shanah (years) ban (son) and upward, shall nathan (give) the tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah.

The ishayar (rich) shall not rabah (give) more, and the dal (poor) shall not mait (give) less, than the machatzayath (half) shaqal (shekel), when they nathan (give) the tharawamah (offering) of Yahawah, to make kapar (atonement) for your napash (soul).

You shall laqach (take / seize) the kapar (atonement) kasap (money) from the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and shall nathan (give) it for the ibadah (service) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting; that it may be a zakarawan (memorial) for the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) panayam (face) Yahawah, to make kapar (atonement) for your napash (soul)."
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

"You shall also ishah (make) a basin of nachashath (brass), and its kan (for sure) of nachashath (brass), in which to rachatz (wash). You shall nathan (give) it between the ahal (tent) of Meeting and the mazabach (altar), and you shall nathan (give) mayam (Waters) in it.
Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son) shall rachatz (wash) their yad (hand) and their ragal (feet / foot) in it.

When they bawaa (come) into the ahal (tent) of Meeting, they shall rachatz (wash) with mayam (Waters), that they not mawath (death); or when they nagash (come) near to the mazabach (altar) to sharath (minister), to qatar (burn) an offering made by ashah (fire / offering made by fire) to Yahawah.

So they shall rachatz (wash) their yad (hand) and their ragal (feet / foot), that they not mawath (death): and it shall be a chaq (statute) iwalam (forever) to them, even to him and to his descendants throughout their dawar (generation / age / period)."
Moreover Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

"Also laqach (take / seize) fine bashamayam (spices): of liquid mar (myrrh), chamash (five) maah (hundred) shekels; and of fragrant qanamawan (cinnamon) machatzayath (half) as much, even two maah (hundred) and chamashayam (fifty); and of fragrant qanah (cane), two maah (hundred) and chamashayam (fifty);
And of qadah (cassia) chamash (five) maah (hundred), after the shaqal (shekel) of the qadash (set apart / make holy); and a hayan (hin) of zayath (olive) shaman (oil).

You shall ishah (make) it a qadash (set apart / make holy) mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), a perfume maraqachath (compounded) after the maishah (art) of the perfumer: it shall be a qadash (set apart / make holy) mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil).
You shall use it to mashach (anoint) the ahal (tent) of Meeting, the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony),
The shalachan (table) and all its articles, the lampstand and its accessories, the mazabach (altar) of qatarath (incense),
The mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering) with all its utensils, and the basin with its kan (for sure).
You shall qadash (set apart / make holy) them, that they may be most qadash (set apart / make holy). Whatever touches them shall be qadash (set apart / make holy).
You shall mashach (anoint) Aharawan (Aaron) and his ban (son), and qadash (set apart / make holy) them, that they may kahan (priest) to me in the priest's office.

You shall dabar (word / matter) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), amar (spoke), ‘This shall be a qadash (set apart / make holy) mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil) to me throughout your dawar (generation / age / period).

It shall not be yasak (poured) on adam (man's) bashar (flesh), neither shall you ishah (make) any like it, according to its mathakanath (composition): it is qadash (set apart / make holy). It shall be qadash (set apart / make holy) to you.
Whoever compounds any like it, or whoever nathan (give) any of it on a stranger, he shall be karath (cut) off from his im (nation / people).'"

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "laqach (take / seize) to yourself sam (sweet) spices, gum resin, and shachalath (onycha), and chalabanah (galbanum); sam (sweet) spices with zak (pure) labawanah (frankincense): there shall be an equal weight of bad (each);
And you shall ishah (make) qatarath (incense) of it, a qatarath (perfume) after the maishah (art) of the perfumer, malach (seasoned) with salt, tahawar (pure) and qadash (set apart / make holy):

And you shall shachaq (beat) some of it very daqaq (small), and nathan (give) some of it panayam (face) the idawath (testimony) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting, where I will yaid (meet) with you. It shall be to you most qadash (set apart / make holy).

The qatarath (incense) which you shall ishah (make), according to its mathakanath (composition) you shall not ishah (make) for yourselves: it shall be to you qadash (set apart / make holy) for Yahawah.
Whoever shall ishah (make) any like that, to rawach (spirit / wind) of it, he shall be karath (cut) off from his im (nation / people)."
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),
"Raah (see), I have qaraa (called) by sham (name) Batzalaal (Bezalel) the ban (son) of Awaray (Uri), the ban (son) of Chawar (Hur), of the matah (staff / rod / tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah):
And I malaa (have) filled him with the rawach (spirit / wind) of Alahayam, in chakamah (wisdom), and in thabawan (understanding), and in daith (knowledge), and in all kinds of workmanship,
To chashab (devise) skillful machashabath (works), to ishah (make) in zahab (gold), and in kasap (silver), and in nachashath (brass),
And in charashath (cutting) of aban (stone) for malaa (setting), and in charashath (carving) of itz (wood), to ishah (make) in all kinds of workmanship.

I, behold, I nathan (give) appointed with him Ahalayaab (Oholiab), the ban (son) of Achayasamak (Ahisamach), of the matah (staff / rod / tribe) of Dan (Dan); and in the lab (heart) of all who are wise-hearted I nathan (give) put chakamah (wisdom), that they may ishah (make) all that I have tzawah (commanded) you:
The ahal (tent) of Meeting, the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony), the kaparath (mercy) seat that is on it, all the kalay (furniture) of the ahal (tent),
The shalachan (table) and its kalay (vessels), the tahawar (pure) lampstand with all its kalay (vessels), the mazabach (altar) of qatarath (incense),
The mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering) with all its kalay (vessels), the basin and its kan (for sure),
The finely worked garments—the qadash (set apart / make holy) bagaday (garments) for Aharawan (Aaron) the priest—the bagaday (garments) of his ban (son) to kahan (priest) in the priest's office,

The mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), and the qatarath (incense) of sam (sweet) spices for the qadash (set apart / make holy) place: according to all that I have tzawah (commanded) you they shall ishah (make)."
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

"Dabar (word / matter) also to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), amar (spoke), ‘Most ak (certainly) you shall shamar (keep/guard) my shabath (shabath / rest): for it is a awath (sign / mark / miracle) between me and you throughout your dawar (generation / age / period); that you may yadai (know) that I am Yahawah who qadash (set apart / make holy) you.

You shall shamar (keep/guard) the shabath (shabath / rest) therefore; for it is qadash (set apart / make holy) to you. Everyone who chalal (profanes) it shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death); for whoever ishah (make) any malaakah (work) therein, that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from qarab (among / near) his im (nation / people).

Shash (six) yamayam (days) shall malaakah (work) be ishah (make), but on the shabayaiy (seventh) day is a shabath (shabath / rest) of solemn shabathawan (rest), qadash (set apart / make holy) to Yahawah. Whoever ishah (make) any malaakah (work) on the shabath (shabath / rest) yawam (day) shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death).

Therefore the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall shamar (keep/guard) the shabath (shabath / rest), to ishah (make) the shabath (shabath / rest) throughout their dawar (generation / age / period), for a iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant).

It is a awath (sign / mark / miracle) between me and the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) iwalam (forever); for in shash (six) yamayam (days) Yahawah ishah (make) shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) and aratz (Earth/land), and on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) he shabath (shabath / rest), and was napash (soul).'"

He nathan (give) to Mashah (Moses), when he kalah (complete / finish) dabar (word / matter) with him on har (mountain) Sayanay (Sinai), the shanayam (two) tablets of the idawath (testimony), aban (stone) tablets, kathab (write) with Alahayam atzabai (finger).

When the im (nation / people) raah (see) that Mashah (Moses) bawash (delayed) to yarad (come) down from the har (mountain), the im (nation / people) qahal (gathered) themselves together to Aharawan (Aaron), and amar (spoke) to him, "Come, ishah (make) us Alahayam, which shall yalak (go) panayam (face) us; for as for this Mashah (Moses), the ayash (man / husband) who ilah (go up / offer) us up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), we don't yadai (know) what has become of him."
Aharawan (Aaron) amar (spoke) to them, "Take off the zahab (gold) rings, which are in the azanay (ears) of your wives, of your ban (son), and of your banath (daughter), and bawaa (come) them to me."
All the im (nation / people) took off the zahab (gold) rings which were in their azan (ear), and bawaa (come) them to Aharawan (Aaron).

He laqach (take / seize) what they yad (hand) him, and yatzar (fashioned) it with an engraving charat (tool), and ishah (make) it a masakah (molten) igal (calf); and they amar (spoke), "These are your Alahayam, Yashar-Al (Israel), which ilah (go up / offer) you up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt)."

When Aharawan (Aaron) raah (see) this, he banah (build) an mazabach (altar) panayam (face) it; and Aharawan (Aaron) made a proclamation, and amar (spoke), "machar (tomorrow) shall be a chag (feast/festival) to Yahawah."

They shakam (rose) up early on the next macharath (day), and ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilath (offerings), and nagash (brought) shalam (peace) offerings; and the im (nation / people) yashab (inhabit/dwell) down to akal (eat) and to shathah (drinks), and qawam (rise up) up to tzachaq (play).

Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), "yalak (go), yarad (get) down; for your im (nation / people), who you ilah (go up / offer) up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), have shachath (corrupted) themselves!

They have sawar (turned) aside mahar (quickly) out of the darak (way) which I tzawah (commanded) them. They ishah (make) made themselves a masakah (molten) igal (calf), and have shachah (worshiped) it, and have zabach (sacrificed) to it, and amar (spoke), ‘These are your Alahayam, Yashar-Al (Israel), which ilah (go up / offer) you up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).'"
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "I raah (see) seen these im (nation / people), and behold, they are a stiff-necked im (nation / people).

Now therefore leave me yanach (alone), that my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) may charah (hot with anger) hot against them, and that I may kalah (complete / finish) them; and I will ishah (make) of you a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) gaway (heathen / nation)."

Mashah (Moses) begged Yahawah his Alahayam, and amar (spoke), "Yahawah, why does your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) charah (hot with anger) hot against your im (nation / people), that you yatzaa (go out / come out) brought out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) with gadawal (very great/important/mighty) kach (strength / mighty / power) and with a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand)?

Why should the Matzaray (Egyptians) amar (spoke), amar (spoke), ‘He yatzaa (go out / come out) them forth for rai (evil), to harag (kill) them in the harayam (mountains), and to kalah (complete / finish) them from the surface of the adamah (earth)?' Shawab (turn back / repent) from your charawan (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and nacham (turn away / repent) of this rai (evil) against your im (nation / people).

Zakar (remember) Abaraham (Abraham), Yatzachaq (Isaac), and Yashar-Al (Israel), your ibad (servant), to whom you shabai (swear / take oath) by your own self, and dabar (word / matter) to them, ‘I will rabah (multiply) your zarai (seed) as the kawakabay (stars) of the sky, and all this aratz (Earth/land) that I have amar (spoke) of I will nathan (give) to your zarai (seed), and they shall nachal (inherit) it iwalam (forever).'"
Yahawah nacham (turn away / repent) of the rai (evil) which he dabar (word / matter) he would ishah (make) to his im (nation / people).

Mashah (Moses) panah (turn), and yarad (went) down from the har (mountain), with the shanayam (two) tablets of the idawath (testimony) in his yad (hand); tablets that were kathab (write) on shanayam (two) their ibar (sides); on the one side and on the other they were kathab (write).
The tablets were the maishah (work) of Alahayam, and the makathab (writing) was the makathab (writing) of Alahayam, engraved on the lachath (tables).

When Yahawashawai (Joshua) shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the im (nation / people) as they rai (shouted), he amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "There is the qawal (sound / voice) of malachamah (war) in the machanah (camp)."

He amar (spoke), "It isn't the qawal (sound / voice) of those who inah (answer / respond) for victory, neither is it the qawal (sound / voice) of those who inah (answer / respond) for chalawashah (being) overcome; but the qawal (sound / voice) of those who qawal (sound / voice) that I shamai (hearken / hear)."

It happened, as soon as he qarab (come close) near to the machanah (camp), that he raah (see) the igal (calf) and the machawalah (dance): and Mashah (Moses)' ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) grew charah (hot with anger), and he shalak (threw) the tablets out of his yad (hand), and shabar (broke) them thachath (under) the har (mountain).

He laqach (take / seize) the igal (calf) which they ishah (make) made, and burnt it with ash (fire), tachan (ground) it to daqaq (powder), and zarah (scattered) it on the mayam (Waters), and made the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shaqah (drink) of it.
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to Aharawan (Aaron), "What ishah (make) these im (nation / people) do to you, that you bawaa (come) brought a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chataah (sin) on them?"

Aharawan (Aaron) amar (spoke), "Don't let the ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of my Adawan grow charah (hot with anger). You yadai (know) the im (nation / people), that they are set on rai (evil).

For they amar (spoke) to me, ‘ishah (make) us Alahayam, which shall yalak (go) panayam (face) us; for as for this Mashah (Moses), the ayash (man / husband) who ilah (go up / offer) us up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), we don't yadai (know) what has become of him.'
I amar (spoke) to them, ‘Whoever has any zahab (gold), let them take it off:' so they nathan (give) it to me; and I shalak (threw) it into the ash (fire), and out came this igal (calf)."
When Mashah (Moses) raah (see) that the im (nation / people) had broken loose, (for Aharawan (Aaron) had parai (let) them loose for a derision among their qawam (rise up)),

Then Mashah (Moses) imad (stood) in the shair (gate) of the machanah (camp), and amar (spoke), "Whoever is on Yahawah side, come to me!" All the banay (sons) of Laway (Levi) asap (gathered) themselves together to him.

He amar (spoke) to them, "Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), ‘Every ayash (man / husband) shawam (place / establish / appoint) his charab (sword) on his yarak (thigh), and ibar (pass over/through) shawab (turn back / repent) and forth from shair (gate) to shair (gate) throughout the machanah (camp), and every ayash (man / husband) harag (kill) his ach (brother/kinsman), and every ayash (man / husband) his rai (neigbor/another person), and every ayash (man / husband) his neighbor.'"

The banay (sons) of Laway (Levi) ishah (make) according to the dabar (word / matter) of Mashah (Moses): and there napal (fall / be cast down) of the im (nation / people) that yawam (day) about shalawash (three) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband).

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke), "malaa (consecrate) yourselves today to Yahawah, yes, every ayash (man / husband) against his ban (son), and against his ach (brother/kinsman); that he may nathan (give) on you a barakah (blessing) this yawam (day)."

It happened on the next macharath (day), that Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to the im (nation / people), "You have chataa (sinned) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chataah (sin). Now I will ilah (go up / offer) up to Yahawah. Perhaps I shall make kapar (atonement) for your chataah (sin)."

Mashah (Moses) shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "Oh, this im (nation / people) have chataa (sinned) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chataah (sin), and ishah (make) made themselves Alahayam of zahab (gold).
Yet now, if you will, nashaa (lift) their sin—and if not, please machah (blot) me out of your sapar (book / scribed document) which you have kathab (write)."
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "Whoever has chataa (sinned) against me, him will I machah (blot) out of my sapar (book / scribed document).

Now yalak (go), nachah (lead) the im (nation / people) to the place of which I have dabar (word / matter) to you. Behold, my malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) shall yalak (go) panayam (face) you. Nevertheless in the yawam (day) when I paqad (visit), I will paqad (visit) them for their chataah (sin)."
Yahawah nagap (struck) the im (nation / people), ashar (who/that) they ishah (make) the igal (calf), which Aharawan (Aaron) ishah (make).

Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), "Depart, ilah (go up / offer) up from here, you and the im (nation / people) that you have ilah (go up / offer) up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), to the aratz (Earth/land) of which I shabai (swear / take oath) to Abaraham (Abraham), to Yatzachaq (Isaac), and to Yaiqab (Jacob), amar (spoke), ‘I will nathan (give) it to your zarai (seed).'

I will shalach (send) an malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) panayam (face) you; and I will garash (drive) out the Kanainay (Canaanite), the Amaray (Amorite), and the Chathay (Hittite), and the Parazay (Perizzite), the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite):

To a aratz (Earth/land) zawab (flow) with chalab (milk) and dabash (honey): for I will not ilah (go up / offer) up in the qarab (among / near) of you, for you are a stiff-necked im (nation / people), lest I kalah (complete / finish) you in the darak (way)."
When the im (nation / people) shamai (hearken / hear) this rai (evil) news, they abal (mourned): and no ayash (man / husband) shayath (put / appoint / make) on his jewelry.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "amar (spoke) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), ‘You are a stiff-necked im (nation / people). If I were to ilah (go up / offer) up into your qarab (among / near) for achad (one) ragai (in an instance), I would kalah (complete / finish) you. Therefore now yarad (take) off your jewelry from you, that I may yadai (know) what to ishah (make) to you.'"
The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) natzal (stripped) themselves of their jewelry from har (mountain) Charab (Horeb) onward.

Now Mashah (Moses) used to laqach (take / seize) the ahal (tent) and to natah (pitch) it outside the machanah (camp), rachaq (far) away from the machanah (camp), and he qaraa (called) it "The ahal (tent) of Meeting." It happened that everyone who baqash (sought) Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) out to the ahal (tent) of Meeting, which was outside the machanah (camp).

It happened that when Mashah (Moses) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to the ahal (tent), that all the im (nation / people) qawam (rise up) up, and natzab (stood), everyone at their ahal (tent) pathach (door), and watched Mashah (Moses), until he bawaa (come) gone into the ahal (tent).

It happened, when Mashah (Moses) bawaa (come) into the ahal (tent), that the imawad (pillar) of inan (cloud) descended, imad (stood) at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent), and dabar (word / matter) with Mashah (Moses).

All the im (nation / people) raah (see) the imawad (pillar) of inan (cloud) imad (stand) at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent), and all the im (nation / people) qawam (rise up) up and shachah (worshiped), everyone at their ahal (tent) pathach (door).

Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses) panayam (face) to panayam (face), as a ayash (man / husband) dabar (word / matter) to his rai (neigbor/another person). He shawab (turn back / repent) again into the machanah (camp), but his sharath (servant) Yahawashawai (Joshua), the ban (son) of Nawan (Nun), a nair (young) man, didn't depart out of the ahal (tent).

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to Yahawah, "raah (see), you amar (spoke) me, ‘ilah (go up / offer) up this im (nation / people):' and you haven't yadai (let) me know whom you will shalach (send) with me. Yet you have amar (spoke), ‘I yadai (know) you by sham (name), and you matzaa (have) also found favor in my iyan (eye).'

Now therefore, if I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye), please show me now your darak (ways), that I may yadai (know) you, so that I may matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (eye): and raah (see) that this gaway (heathen / nation) is your im (nation / people)."
He amar (spoke), "My panayam (face) will yalak (go) with you, and I will give you nawach (rest)."
He amar (spoke) to him, "If your panayam (face) doesn't halak (move) with me, don't ilah (go up / offer) us up from here.

For how would people yadai (know) that I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye), I and your im (nation / people)? Isn't it in that you yalak (go) with us, so that we are palah (separated), I and your im (nation / people), from all the im (nation / people) who are on the surface of the adamah (earth)?"

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "I will ishah (make) this thing also that you have dabar (word / matter); for you matzaa (have) found favor in my iyan (eye), and I yadai (know) you by sham (name)."
He amar (spoke), "Please show me your kabawad (glory)."

He amar (spoke), "I will make all my goodness ibar (pass over/through) before you, and will qaraa (called) the sham (name) of Yahawah panayam (face) you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show racham (show mercy / love) on whom I will show racham (show mercy / love)."
He amar (spoke), "You cannot raah (see) my panayam (face), for adam (man) may not raah (see) me and chayay (life)."
Yahawah also amar (spoke), "Behold, there is a maqawam (place) by me, and you shall natzab (stand) on the tzawar (rock).

It will happen, while my kabawad (glory) passes by, that I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) you in a naqarah (cleft) of the tzawar (rock), and will sakak (cover) you with my kap (hand) id (until / as far as) I ibar (pass over/through) passed by;
Then I will sawar (take) away my kap (hand), and you will raah (see) my achawar (back); but my panayam (face) shall not be raah (see)."

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "Chisel shanayam (two) aban (stone) tablets like the raashawan (first): and I will kathab (write) on the tablets the dabarayam (words) that were on the raashawan (first) tablets, which you shabar (broke).

Be kawan (ready) by the baqar (morning), and ilah (go up / offer) up in the baqar (morning) to har (mountain) Sayanay (Sinai), and natzab (present) yourself there to me on the raash (head) of the har (mountain).

No ayash (man / husband) shall ilah (go up / offer) up with you; al (not) let anyone be raah (see) throughout all the har (mountain); neither let the tzaan (flocks) nor baqar (morning) raih (feed) mawal (before) that har (mountain)."

He chiseled shanayam (two) tablets of aban (stone) like the raashawan (first); and Mashah (Moses) shakam (rose) up early in the baqar (morning), and ilah (go up / offer) up to har (mountain) Sayanay (Sinai), as Yahawah had tzawah (commanded) him, and laqach (take / seize) in his yad (hand) shanayam (two) aban (stone) tablets.
Yahawah descended in the inan (cloud), and yatzab (stood) with him there, and qaraa (called) the sham (name) of Yahawah.

Yahawah ibar (pass over/through) by panayam (face) him, and qaraa (called), "Yahawah! Yahawah, a rachawam (merciful) and chanawan (gracious) Al, arak (slow) to anger, and abundant in loving chasad (grace) and amath (truth),

Natzar (keeping) loving chasad (grace) for alapayam (thousands), nashaa (lift) iwan (guilt/iniquity) and disobedience and chataah (sin); and that will by no naqah (clean/innocent) naqah (clean/innocent) the guilty, paqad (visit) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the abawath (fathers) on the banayam (children), and on the banayam (childrens) banayam (children), on the shalash (three) and on the rabai (fourth) generation."
Mashah (Moses) hurried and bowed his qadad (head) toward the aratz (Earth/land), and shachah (worshiped).

He amar (spoke), "If now I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye), Adanay, please let the Adanay yalak (go) in the midst of us; although this is a stiff-necked im (nation / people); salach (forgive/pardon/make clean) our iwan (guilt/iniquity) and our chataah (sin), and take us for your nachal (inheritance)."

He amar (spoke), "Behold, I karath (cut) a barayath (covenant): before all your im (nation / people) I will ishah (make) marvels, such as have not been worked in all the aratz (Earth/land), nor in any gaway (heathen / nation); and all the im (nation / people) qarab (among / near) which you are shall raah (see) the maishah (work) of Yahawah; for it is an awesome thing that I ishah (make) with you.

Shamar (keep/guard) that which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day). Behold, I garash (drive) out panayam (face) you the Amaray (Amorite), the Kanainay (Canaanite), the Chathay (Hittite), the Parazay (Perizzite), the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite).

Be careful, lest you karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the aratz (Earth/land) where you are bawaa (come), lest it be for a mawaqash (snare) in the qarab (among / near) of you:
But you shall shabar (break) down their mazabach (altars), and dash in pieces their matzabah (pillars), and you shall karath (cut) down their Asharah (Asherim);
For you shall shachah (worship) no other Al: for Yahawah, whose sham (name) is qanaa (jealous), is a qanaa (jealous) Al.

"Don't karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the aratz (Earth/land), lest they zanah (play) the prostitute achar (other) their Alahayam, and zabach (sacrifice) to their Alahayam, and one qaraa (called) you and you akal (eat) of his zabach (sacrifice);

And you laqach (take / seize) of their banath (daughter) to your ban (son), and their banath (daughter) zanah (play) the prostitute achar (other) their Alahayam, and make your ban (son) zanah (play) the prostitute achar (other) their Alahayam.
"You shall ishah (make) no cast idols for yourselves.

"You shall shamar (keep/guard) the chag (feast/festival) of unleavened matzah (bread). Shabai (seven) yamayam (days) you shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread), as I tzawah (commanded) you, at the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) appointed in the chadash (month) abayab (abib); for in the chadash (month) abayab (abib) you yatzaa (go out / come out) out from Matzarayam (Egypt).
"All that patar (opens) the racham (womb) is mine; and all your livestock that is zakar (remember), the firstborn of shawar (cow) and shah (sheep).

The firstborn of a donkey you shall padah (redeem) with a shah (lamb): and if you will not padah (redeem) it, then you shall irap (break) its neck. All the bakawar (firstborn) of your ban (son) you shall padah (redeem). No one shall raah (see) panayam (face) me rayaqam (empty).

"Shash (six) yamayam (days) you shall ibad (servant), but on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) you shall shabath (shabath / rest): in plowing time and in qatzayar (harvest) you shall shabath (shabath / rest).

"You shall ishah (make) the chag (feast/festival) of shabaith (weeks) with the bakawar (first) fruits of chatah (wheat) qatzayar (harvest), and the chag (feast/festival) of harvest at the shanah (year's) thaqawapah (end).
Paim (three) times in the shanah (year) all your zakawar (remember/recall) shall raah (see) panayam (face) the Adawan Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel).

For I will yarash (drive) out gawayam (nations) panayam (face) you and enlarge your gabawal (border/boundary); neither shall any ayash (man / husband) chamad (desire) your aratz (Earth/land) when you ilah (go up / offer) up to raah (see) panayam (face) Yahawah, your Alahayam, paim (three) times in the shanah (year).

"You shall not shachat (offer) the dam (blood) of my zabach (sacrifice) with chamatz (leavened) bread; neither shall the zabach (sacrifice) of the chag (feast/festival) of the pasach (passover) be lawan (left) to the baqar (morning).

"You shall bring the raashayath (beginning) of the raashayath (beginning) bakawaray (fruits) of your adamah (ground) to the bayath (house) of Yahawah your Alahayam. "You shall not bashal (boil) a young goat in its am (mother) chalab (milk)."

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "kathab (write) you these dabarayam (words): for in accordance with these dabarayam (words) I have karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with you and with Yashar-Al (Israel)."

He was there with Yahawah arabaiyam (forty) yawam (day) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights); he neither akal (eat) lacham (bread), nor shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters). He kathab (write) on the tablets the dabaray (words) of the barayath (covenant), the ishar (ten) commandments.

It happened, when Mashah (Moses) yarad (came) down from har (mountain) Sayanay (Sinai) with the shanayam (two) tablets of the idawath (testimony) in Mashah (Moses)' yad (hand), when he yarad (came) down from the har (mountain), that Mashah (Moses) didn't yadai (know) that the iwar (skin) of his panayam (face) qaran (shone) by reason of his dabar (word / matter) with him.

When Aharawan (Aaron) and all the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) raah (see) Mashah (Moses), behold, the iwar (skin) of his panayam (face) qaran (shone); and they were yaraa (fear / be afraid) to nagash (come) near him.

Mashah (Moses) qaraa (called) to them, and Aharawan (Aaron) and all the nashaayam (rulers) of the idah (congregation) shawab (turn back / repent) to him; and Mashah (Moses) dabar (word / matter) to them.

Afterward all the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) nagash (came) near, and he tzawah (gave) them all of the commandments that Yahawah had dabar (word / matter) with him on har (mountain) Sayanay (Sinai).
When Mashah (Moses) was kalah (complete / finish) dabar (word / matter) with them, he nathan (give) a masawah (veil) on his panayam (face).

But when Mashah (Moses) bawaa (come) in panayam (face) Yahawah to dabar (word / matter) with him, he sawar (took) the masawah (veil) off, until he yatzaa (go out / come out) out; and he yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and dabar (word / matter) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) that which he was tzawah (commanded).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) raah (see) Mashah (Moses)' panayam (face), that the iwar (skin) of Mashah (Moses)' panayam (face) qaran (shone): and Mashah (Moses) shawab (turn back / repent) the masawah (veil) on his panayam (face) again, until he bawaa (come) in to dabar (word / matter) with him.

Mashah (Moses) qahal (assembled) all the idah (congregation) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and amar (spoke) to them, "These are the dabarayam (words) which Yahawah has tzawah (commanded), that you should ishah (make) them.

‘Shash (six) yamayam (days) shall malaakah (work) be ishah (make), but on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) there shall be a qadash (set apart / make holy) day for you, a shabath (shabath / rest) of solemn shabathawan (rest) to Yahawah: whoever ishah (make) any malaakah (work) in it shall be put to mawath (death).
You shall bair (kindle) no ash (fire) throughout your habitations on the shabath (shabath / rest) yawam (day).'"
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to all the idah (congregation) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), amar (spoke), "This is the thing which Yahawah tzawah (commanded), amar (spoke),

‘Laqach (take / seize) from among you an tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah. Kal (every) is of a nadayab (willing) lab (heart), bawaa (come) him bring it, Yahawah tharawamah (offering): zahab (gold), kasap (silver), nachashath (brass),
Thakalath (blue), aragaman (purple), shanay (second), shash (six) linen, izayam (goats)' hair,
Ayalam (rams)' irath (skins) adam (dyed) red, thachash (sea) cow irath (hides), acacia itz (wood),
Shaman (oil) for the maawar (Maawar / Luminary), bashamayam (spices) for the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil) and for the sam (sweet) qatarath (incense),
Shaham (Onyx) abanay (stones), and abanay (stones) to be malaa (set) for the apawad (ephod) and for the chashan (breastplate).
"‘Let every wise-hearted lab (heart) among you bawaa (come), and ishah (make) all that Yahawah has tzawah (commanded):
The mashakan (tabernacle), its outer makasah (covering), its roof, its clasps, its qarash (boards), its barayach (bars), its imawad (pillar), and its adan (sockets);
The arawan (ark), and its poles, the kaparath (mercy) seat, the parakath (veil) of the screen;
The shalachan (table) with its poles and all its kalay (vessels), and the show panayam (face);
The lampstand also for the maawar (Maawar / Luminary), with its kalay (vessels), its nayar (lamps), and the shaman (oil) for the maawar (Maawar / Luminary);

And the mazabach (altar) of qatarath (incense) with its poles, the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), the sam (sweet) qatarath (incense), the screen for the pathach (door), at the door of the mashakan (tabernacle);
The mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering), with its makabar (grating) of nachashath (brass), it poles, and all its kalay (vessels), the basin and its kan (for sure);
The qalaiy (hangings) of the chatzar (court), its imawad (pillar), their adan (sockets), and the screen for the shair (gate) of the chatzar (court);
The yathadath (pins) of the mashakan (tabernacle), the yathadath (pins) of the chatzar (court), and their mayathar (cords);

The finely worked bagaday (garments), for ministering in the qadash (set apart / make holy) place, the qadash (set apart / make holy) bagaday (garments) for Aharawan (Aaron) the kahan (priest), and the bagaday (garments) of his ban (son), to kahan (priest) in the priest's office.'"
All the idah (congregation) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) departed from the panayam (face) of Mashah (Moses).

They bawaa (come), everyone whose lab (heart) nashaa (lift) him up, and everyone whom his rawach (spirit / wind) nadab (made) willing, and bawaa (come) Yahawah tharawamah (offering), for the malaakah (work) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and for all of its ibadah (service), and for the qadash (set apart / make holy) bagaday (garments).

They bawaa (come), il (over) anashayam (men) and nashayam (women), as many as were willing-hearted, and bawaa (come) brooches, nazam (earrings), signet tabaith (rings), and armlets, all kalay (jewels) of zahab (gold); even every ayash (man / husband) who nawap (offered) an thanawapah (offering) of zahab (gold) to Yahawah.

Everyone, with whom was matzaa (found) thakalath (blue), aragaman (purple), shanay (second), shash (six) linen, izayam (goats)' hair, ayalam (rams)' irath (skins) adam (dyed) red, and thachash (sea) cow irath (hides), bawaa (come) them.

Everyone who rawam (will lift up) an tharawamah (offering) of kasap (silver) and nachashath (brass) bawaa (come) Yahawah tharawamah (offering); and everyone, with whom was matzaa (found) acacia itz (wood) for any malaakah (work) of the ibadah (service), bawaa (come) it.

All the ayashah (woman / wife) who were wise-hearted tawah (spun) with their yad (hand), and bawaa (come) that which they had matawah (spun), the thakalath (blue), the aragaman (purple), the shanay (second), and the shash (six) linen.
All the nashayam (women) whose lab (heart) nashaa (lift) them up in chakamah (wisdom) tawah (spun) the izayam (goats)' hair.
The nashaam (rulers) bawaa (come) the shaham (Onyx) abanay (stones), and the abanay (stones) to be malaa (set), for the apawad (ephod) and for the chashan (breastplate);
And the basham (spice), and the shaman (oil) for the maawar (Maawar / Luminary), for the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), and for the sam (sweet) qatarath (incense).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) bawaa (come) a freewill nadabah (voluntary / freewill offering) to Yahawah; every ayash (man / husband) and ayashah (woman / wife), whose lab (heart) nadab (made) them willing to bawaa (come) for all the malaakah (work), which Yahawah had tzawah (commanded) to be ishah (make) by Mashah (Moses).

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), "raah (see), Yahawah has qaraa (called) by sham (name) Batzalaal (Bezalel) the ban (son) of Awaray (Uri), the ban (son) of Chawar (Hur), of the matah (staff / rod / tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah).
He malaa (has) filled him with the rawach (spirit / wind) of Alahayam, in chakamah (wisdom), in thabawan (understanding), in daith (knowledge), and in all kinds of workmanship;
And to make skillful machashabath (works), to ishah (make) in zahab (gold), in kasap (silver), in nachashath (brass),
In charashath (cutting) of aban (stone) for malaa (setting), and in charashath (carving) of itz (wood), to ishah (make) in all kinds of skillful workmanship.
He nathan (give) put in his lab (heart) that he may yarah (teach), both he, and Ahalayaab (Oholiab), the ban (son) of Achayasamak (Ahisamach), of the matah (staff / rod / tribe) of Dan (Dan).

He malaa (has) filled them with chakamah (wisdom) of lab (heart), to ishah (make) all kinds of workmanship, of the charash (engraver), of the skillful chashab (workman), and of the raqam (embroiderer), in thakalath (blue), in aragaman (purple), in shanay (second), and in shash (six) linen, and of the arag (weaver), even of those who ishah (make) any workmanship, and of those who make skillful malaakah (works).

"Batzalaal (Bezalel) and Ahalayaab (Oholiab) shall ishah (make) with every wise-hearted ayash (man / husband), in whom Yahawah nathan (give) put chakamah (wisdom) and thabawan (understanding) to yadai (know) how to ishah (make) all the ishah (make) for the ibadah (service) of the qadash (set apart / make holy), according to all that Yahawah has tzawah (commanded)."

Mashah (Moses) qaraa (called) Batzalaal (Bezalel) and Ahalayaab (Oholiab), and every wise-hearted ayash (man / husband), in whose lab (heart) Yahawah nathan (give) put chakamah (wisdom), even everyone whose lab (heart) nashaa (lift) him up to qarab (come close) to the malaakah (work) to ishah (make) it:

And they laqach (take / seize) from Mashah (Moses) all the tharawamah (offering) which the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) bawaa (come) brought for the malaakah (work) of the ibadah (service) of the qadash (set apart / make holy), with which to ishah (make) it. They bawaa (come) yet to him freewill nadabah (voluntary / freewill offering) every baqar (morning).
All the chakam (wise) men, who ishah (make) all the malaakah (work) of the qadash (set apart / make holy), ayash (man / husband) bawaa (come) from his malaakah (work) which they ishah (make).

They amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke), "The im (nation / people) bawaa (come) much more than day (enough) for the ibadah (service) of the malaakah (work) which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) to ishah (make)."

Mashah (Moses) tzawah (gave) commandment, and they caused it to be qawal (sound / voice) throughout the machanah (camp), amar (spoke), "Let neither ayash (man / husband) nor ayashah (woman / wife) ishah (make) anything else for the tharawamah (offering) for the qadash (set apart / make holy)." So the im (nation / people) were kalaa (restrained) from bawaa (come).
For the stuff they had was day (sufficient) for all the malaakah (work) to ishah (make) it, and yathar (too) much.

All the wise-hearted men among those who ishah (make) the malaakah (work) ishah (make) the mashakan (tabernacle) with ishar (ten) yarayaith (curtains); of fine shazar (twined) shash (six), thakalath (blue), aragaman (purple), and shanay (second), with karawab (cherubim), the maishah (work) of the skillful ishah (make), they made them.

The arak (length) of achad (one) yarayaih (curtain) was isharayam (twenty) shamanah (eight) amah (cubits), and the rachab (breadth) of achad (one) yarayaih (curtain) arabai (four) amah (cubits). All the yarayaith (curtains) had achad (one) madah (measure).
He chabar (coupled) chamash (five) yarayaith (curtains) to achad (one) another, and the other chamash (five) yarayaith (curtains) he chabar (coupled) achad (one) to another.

He ishah (make) lalaath (loops) of thakalath (blue) on the shapah (edge) of the achad (one) yarayaih (curtain) from the qatzah (end / extremity / border) in the machabarath (coupling). Likewise he ishah (make) in the shapah (edge) of the yarayaih (curtain) that was outmost in the shanay (second) machabarath (coupling).

He ishah (make) chamashayam (fifty) lalaath (loops) in the achad (one) yarayaih (curtain), and he ishah (make) chamashayam (fifty) lalaath (loops) in the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the yarayaih (curtain) that was in the shanay (second) machabarath (coupling). The lalaath (loops) were opposite achad (one) to another.
He ishah (make) chamashayam (fifty) clasps of zahab (gold), and chabar (coupled) the yaraith (curtains) achad (one) to another with the clasps: so the mashakan (tabernacle) was a unit.
He ishah (make) yarayaith (curtains) of izayam (goats)' hair for a ahal (covering) over the mashakan (tabernacle). He ishah (make) them ishathay (eleven) yarayaith (curtains).

The arak (length) of achad (one) yarayaih (curtain) was shalawashayam (thirty) amawath (cubits), and arabai (four) amawath (cubits) the rachab (breadth) of achad (one) yarayaih (curtain). The ishathay (eleven) yarayaith (curtains) had achad (one) madah (measure).
He chabar (coupled) chamash (five) yarayaith (curtains) by themselves, and shash (six) yarayaith (curtains) by themselves.

He ishah (make) chamashayam (fifty) lalaath (loops) on the shapah (edge) of the yarayaih (curtain) that was outmost in the machabarath (coupling), and he ishah (make) chamashayam (fifty) lalaath (loops) on the shapah (edge) of the yarayaih (curtain) which was outmost in the shanay (second) chabarath (coupling).
He ishah (make) chamashayam (fifty) clasps of nachashath (brass) to chabar (couple) the ahal (tent) chabar (together), that it might be a unit.
He ishah (make) a makasah (covering) for the ahal (tent) of alayam (rams)' irath (skins) adam (dyed) red, and a makasah (covering) of thachash (sea) cow irath (hides) mail (top/above).
He ishah (make) the qarashayam (boards) for the mashakan (tabernacle) of acacia itz (wood), imad (standing) up.
Ishar (ten) amath (cubits) was the arak (length) of a qarash (board), and a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half) the rachab (breadth) of achad (one) qarash (board).
Achad (one) qarash (board) had shanayam (two) tenons, joined achad (one) to another. He ishah (make) all the qarashay (boards) of the mashakan (tabernacle) this way.
He ishah (make) the qarashayam (boards) for the mashakan (tabernacle): isharayam (twenty) qarashayam (boards) for the nagab (south) paah (side) southward.

He ishah (make) arabaiyam (forty) adanay (sockets) of kasap (silver) under the isharayam (twenty) qarashayam (boards); shanayam (two) adanay (sockets) under achad (one) qarash (board) for its shanayam (two) tenons, and shanayam (two) adanay (sockets) under another qarash (board) for its shanayam (two) tenons.
For the shanay (second) tzalai (side) of the mashakan (tabernacle), on the tzapawan (north) paah (side), he ishah (make) isharayam (twenty) qarashayam (boards),

And their arabaiyam (forty) adanayam (sockets) of kasap (silver); shanayam (two) adanayam (sockets) under achad (one) qarash (board), and shanayam (two) adanayam (sockets) under another qarash (board).
For the far yarakah (part) of the mashakan (tabernacle) westward he ishah (make) shash (six) qarashayam (boards).
He ishah (make) shanayam (two) qarashayam (boards) for the maqatzaith (corners) of the mashakan (tabernacle) in the far yarakah (part).

They were double matah (beneath), and in the same yachad (way) they were all the way to its raash (head) to achad (one) tabaith (ring). He ishah (make) this to shanayam (two) of them in the shanayam (two) maqatzaith (corners).
There were shamanah (eight) qarashayam (boards), and their adanayam (sockets) of kasap (silver), sixteen adanayam (sockets); under achad (one) qarash (board) shanayam (two) adanayam (sockets).
He ishah (make) barayachay (bars) of acacia itz (wood); chamash (five) for the qarashay (boards) of the achad (one) tzalai (side) of the mashakan (tabernacle),

And chamash (five) barayacham (bars) for the qarashay (boards) of the other tzalai (side) of the mashakan (tabernacle), and chamash (five) barayacham (bars) for the qarashay (boards) of the mashakan (tabernacle) for the hinder yarakah (part) westward.
He ishah (make) the thayakawan (middle) barayach (bar) to pass thawak (midst) in the midst of the qarashayam (boards) from the one qatzah (end / extremity / border) to the other.

He overlaid the qarashayam (boards) with zahab (gold), and ishah (make) their tabaith (rings) of zahab (gold) for bathayam (places) for the barayacham (bars), and overlaid the barayacham (bars) with zahab (gold).

He ishah (make) the parakath (veil) of thakalath (blue), aragaman (purple), shanay (second), and fine shazar (twined) shash (six): with karawab (cherubim). He ishah (make) it the maishah (work) of a skillful chashab (workman).

He ishah (make) arabai (four) imawaday (pillars) of acacia for it, and overlaid them with zahab (gold). Their waw (and) were of zahab (gold). He yatzaq (cast) arabai (four) adanay (sockets) of kasap (silver) for them.
He ishah (make) a screen for the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent), of thakalath (blue), aragaman (purple), shanay (second), and fine shazar (twined) shash (six), the raqam (work) of an embroiderer;

And the chamash (five) imawad (pillar) of it with their waw (and). He overlaid their capitals and their chashaq (fillets) with zahab (gold), and their chamash (five) adan (sockets) were of nachashath (brass).

Batzalaal (Bezalel) ishah (make) the arawan (ark) of acacia itz (wood). Its arak (length) was chatzay (two) and a half amathayam (cubits), and its rachab (breadth) a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half), and a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half) its qawamah (height).
He overlaid it with tahawar (pure) zahab (gold) bayath (house) and outside, and ishah (make) a molding of zahab (gold) for it around it.

He yatzaq (cast) arabai (four) tabaiwath (rings) of zahab (gold) for it, in its arabai (four) paim (feet); even shanayam (two) tabaiwath (rings) on its achad (one) tzalai (side), and shanayam (two) tabaiwath (rings) on its other tzalai (side).
He ishah (make) poles of acacia itz (wood), and overlaid them with zahab (gold).
He bawaa (come) the poles into the tabaith (rings) on the tzalaith (sides) of the arawan (ark), to nashaa (lift) the arawan (ark).

He ishah (make) a kaparath (mercy) seat of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold). Its arak (length) was chatzay (two) and a half amathayam (cubits), and a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half) its rachab (breadth).
He ishah (make) shanayam (two) karawab (cherubim) of zahab (gold). He ishah (make) them of beaten maqashah (work), at the shanayam (two) ends of the kaparath (mercy) seat;

Achad (one) karawab (cherub) at the qatzah (end / extremity / border) end, and achad (one) karawab (cherub) at the other end. He ishah (make) the karawab (cherubim) of one piece with the kaparath (mercy) seat at its shanayam (two) ends.

The karawab (cherubim) parash (spread) out their kanapayam (wings) on mail (top/above), sakak (covering) the kaparath (mercy) seat with their kanapayam (wings), with their panay (faces) toward ayash (man / husband) ach (brother/kinsman). The panay (faces) of the karawab (cherubim) were toward the kaparath (mercy) seat.

He ishah (make) the shalachan (table) of acacia itz (wood). Its arak (length) was two amathayam (cubits), and its rachab (breadth) was a amah (cubit), and its qawamah (height) was a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half).
He overlaid it with tahawar (pure) zahab (gold), and ishah (make) a zahab (gold) molding around it.
He ishah (make) a masagarath (border) of a tapach (handbreadth) around it, and ishah (make) a zahab (gold) molding on its masagarath (border) around it.
He yatzaq (cast) arabai (four) tabaith (rings) of zahab (gold) for it, and nathan (give) the tabaith (rings) in the arabai (four) paath (corners) that were on its arabai (four) ragal (feet / foot).
The tabaith (rings) were close by the masagarath (border), the bathayam (places) for the poles to nashaa (lift) the shalachan (table).
He ishah (make) the poles of acacia itz (wood), and overlaid them with zahab (gold), to nashaa (lift) the shalachan (table).

He ishah (make) the kalayam (vessels) which were on the shalachan (table), its dishes, its kap (spoons), its manaqayath (bowls), and its pitchers with which to nasak (pour) out, of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold).

He ishah (make) the lampstand of tahawar (pure) zahab (gold). He ishah (make) the lampstand of beaten maqashah (work). Its base, its shaft, its gabayai (cups), its buds, and its parach (flowers) were of one piece with it.

There were shash (six) branches yatzaa (go out / come out) out of its tzad (sides): shalawash (three) branches of the lampstand out of its achad (one) tzad (side), and shalawash (three) branches of the lampstand out of its other tzad (side):
