Please salach (forgive/pardon/make clean) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of this im (nation / people) according to the gadal (greatness) of your loving chasad (grace), and according as you have nashaa (lift) this im (nation / people), from Matzarayam (Egypt) even until hanah (here)."
Yahawah amar (spoke), "I have salach (forgive/pardon/make clean) according to your dabar (word / matter):
But in very awalam (deed), as I chay (life), and as all the aratz (Earth/land) shall be malaa (filled) with the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah;

Because all those men who raah (see) seen my kabawad (glory), and my awath (sign / mark / miracle), which I ishah (make) in Matzarayam (Egypt) and in the madabar (wilderness), yet have nasah (tempted) me these ishar (ten) paimayam (times), and have not shamai (hearken / hear) to my qawal (sound / voice);
Am (mother) they shall not raah (see) the aratz (Earth/land) which I shabai (swear / take oath) to their ab (father), neither shall any of those who naatz (despised) me raah (see) it:

But my ibad (servant) Kalab (Caleb), iqab (award / effect after the cause) he had achar (other) rawach (spirit / wind) with him, and has achar (other) me fully, him will I bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land) into which he bawaa (come); and his zarai (seed) shall yarash (possess) it.

Now the Imalaqay (Amalekite) and the Kanainay (Canaanite) yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the imaq (valley): machar (tomorrow) panah (turn), and nasai (go) into the madabar (wilderness) by the darak (way) to the sawap (red) yam (sea/waters)."
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses) and to Aharawan (Aaron), amar (spoke),

"How long shall I bear with this rai (evil) idah (congregation), that lawan (murmur) against me? I have shamai (hearken / hear) the thalanawath (murmurings) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), which they lawan (murmur) against me.
Amar (spoke) them, ‘As I chay (life), amar (spoke) Yahawah, laa (NOT) as you have dabar (word / matter) in my azan (ear), so will I ishah (make) to you:

Your pagar (dead) bodies shall napal (fall / be cast down) in this madabar (wilderness); and paqad (visit) who were numbered of you, according to your whole masapar (number), from isharayam (twenty) shanah (years) ban (son) and upward, who have lawan (murmured) against me,

Am (mother) you shall not bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land), concerning which I yad (hand) that I would shakan (place) you dwell therein, except Kalab (Caleb) the ban (son) of Yapanah (Jephunneh), and Yahawashawai (Joshua) the ban (son) of Nawan (Nun).
But your little tap (ones), that you amar (spoke) should be a baz (prey), them will I bawaa (come) in, and they shall yadai (know) the aratz (Earth/land) which you have maas (rejected).
But as for you, your pagar (dead) bodies shall napal (fall / be cast down) in this madabar (wilderness).

Your ban (son) shall be wanderers in the madabar (wilderness) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years), and shall nashaa (lift) your prostitution, until your pagar (dead) bodies be thamam (consumed) in the madabar (wilderness).

After the masapar (number) of the yamayam (days) in which you thawar (spied) out the aratz (Earth/land), even arabaiyam (forty) yamayam (days), for every yawam (day) a yawam (day), you will nashaa (lift) your iwan (guilt/iniquity), even arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years), and you yadai (will) know my alienation.'

I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter), am (mother) this will I ishah (make) to all this rai (evil) idah (congregation), who are yaid (gathered) together against me: in this madabar (wilderness) they shall be thamam (consumed), and there they shall mawath (death)."

The anashayam (men), whom Mashah (Moses) shalach (send) to thawar (spy) out the aratz (Earth/land), who shawab (turn back / repent), and made all the idah (congregation) to lawan (murmur) against him, by yatzaa (go out / come out) up an dabah (evil) report against the aratz (Earth/land),
Even those yamathaw (men) who yatzaa (go out / come out) up an rai (evil) dabah (report) of the aratz (Earth/land), mawath (death) by the magapah (plague) panayam (face) Yahawah.

But Yahawashawai (Joshua) the ban (son) of Nawan (Nun), and Kalab (Caleb) the ban (son) of Yapanah (Jephunneh), remained chayah (alive) of ham (they / them) men who halak (move) to thawar (spy) out the aratz (Earth/land).
Mashah (Moses) dabar (word / matter) these dabarayam (words) to all the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel): and the im (nation / people) abal (mourned) maad (greatly).

They shakam (rose) up early in the baqar (morning), and ilah (go up / offer) up to the raash (head) of the har (mountain), amar (spoke), "han (behold), we are here, and will ilah (go up / offer) up to the maqawam (place) which Yahawah has amar (spoke): for we have chataa (sinned)."
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke), "Why now ibar (pass over/through) you disobey the commandment of Yahawah, since it shall not tzalach (prosper)?
Don't ilah (go up / offer) up, for Yahawah isn't qarab (among / near) you; that you not be nagap (struck) down panayam (face) your ayab (enemy).

For there the Imalaqay (Amalekite) and the Kanainay (Canaanite) are panayam (face) you, and you shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword): because you are shawab (turn back / repent) achar (other) from following Yahawah, therefore Yahawah will not be with you."

But they ipal (presumed) to ilah (go up / offer) up to the raash (head) of the har (mountain): nevertheless the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, and Mashah (Moses), didn't depart out of the machanah (camp).
Then the Imalaqay (Amalekite) yarad (came) down, and the Kanainay (Canaanite) who lived in that har (mountain), and nakah (struck) them and kathath (beat) them down, even to Charamah (Hormah).
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),
"Dabar (word / matter) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and amar (spoke) them, ‘When you bawaa (come) come into the aratz (Earth/land) of your habitations, which I nathan (give) to you,

And will ishah (make) an ashah (fire / offering made by fire) by fire to Yahawah, a burnt ilah (offering), or a zabach (sacrifice), to palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) a nadar (vow), or as a freewill nadabah (voluntary / freewill offering), or in your mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) feasts, to ishah (make) a pleasant aroma to Yahawah, of the baqar (morning), or of the tzaan (flock);

Then he who qarab (come close) his qaraban (offering) shall qarab (come close) to Yahawah a meal manachah (offering) of a isharawan (tenth) part of an ephah of fine salath (flour) balal (mixed) with the rabayaiy (fourth) part of a hayan (hin) of shaman (oil):

And yayan (wine) for the drink nasak (offering), the rabayaiy (fourth) part of a hayan (hin), you shall ishah (make) with the burnt nasak (offering), or for the zabach (sacrifice), for achad (one) kabash (lamb).

"‘Or for a ayal (ram), you shall ishah (make) for a meal manachah (offering) shanayam (two) isharawan (tenth) parts of an ephah of fine salath (flour) balal (mixed) with the shalayashay (third) part of a hayan (hin) of shaman (oil):
And for the drink nasak (offering) you shall qarab (come close) the shalayashay (third) part of a hayan (hin) of yayan (wine), of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.
When you ishah (make) a bull for a burnt ilah (offering), or for a zabach (sacrifice), to palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) a nadar (vow), or for shalam (peace) offerings to Yahawah;

Then shall he qarab (come close) with the baqar (morning) a meal manachah (offering) of shalawash (three) isharawan (tenth) parts of an ephah of fine salath (flour) balal (mixed) with chatzay (half) a hayan (hin) of shaman (oil):
And you shall qarab (come close) for the drink nasak (offering) chatzay (half) a hayan (hin) of yayan (wine), for an ashah (fire / offering made by fire) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.
Thus shall it be ishah (make) for achad (one) shawar (bull), or for achad (one) ayal (ram), or for each of the male kabashayam (lambs), or of the young izayam (goats).
According to the masapar (number) that you shall ishah (make), so you shall ishah (make) to everyone according to their masapar (number).
"‘All who are native-born shall ishah (make) these things in this way, in qarab (come close) an ashah (fire / offering made by fire) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.

If a gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) lives as a foreigner with you, or whoever may be thawak (midst) you throughout your dawar (generation / age / period), and will ishah (make) an ashah (fire / offering made by fire) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah; as you ishah (make), so he shall ishah (make).

For the qahal (assembly), there shall be achad (one) chaqah (statute) for you, and for the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who lives as a foreigner, a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) throughout your dawar (generation / age / period): as you are, so shall the foreigner be panayam (face) Yahawah.
Achad (one) thawarah (instruction) and achad (one) mashapat (ordinance) shall be for you, and for the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who lives as a foreigner with you.'"
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),
"Dabar (word / matter) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and amar (spoke) them, ‘When you bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land) where I bawaa (come) you,
Then it shall be that when you akal (eat) of the lacham (bread) of the aratz (Earth/land), you shall rawam (will lift up) up a wave tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah.

Of the raashayath (beginning) of your irayasah (dough) you shall rawam (will lift up) up a chalah (cake) for a wave tharawamah (offering): as the wave tharawamah (offering) of the garan (threshing) floor, so you shall rawam (will lift up) it.
Of the raashayath (beginning) of your irayasah (dough) you shall nathan (give) to Yahawah a wave tharawamah (offering) throughout your dawar (generation / age / period).
"‘When you shall shagah (err), and not ishah (make) all these matzawath (commandments), which Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses),
Even all that Yahawah has tzawah (commanded) you by Mashah (Moses), from the yawam (day) that Yahawah gave commandment, and onward throughout your dawar (generation / age / period);

Then it shall be, if it be ishah (make) shagagah (unwittingly), without the iyan (eye) of the idah (congregation), that all the idah (congregation) shall ishah (make) achad (one) ban (son) par (bull) for a burnt ilah (offering), for a pleasant aroma to Yahawah, with the meal manachah (offering) of it, and the drink nasak (offering) of it, according to the mashapat (ordinance), and achad (one) male shaiyar (goat) for a chataah (sin) offering.

The kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for all the idah (congregation) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and they shall be salach (forgive/pardon/make clean); for it was an shagagah (error), and they bawaa (come) brought their qaraban (offering), an ashah (fire / offering made by fire) made by fire to Yahawah, and their chataah (sin) offering panayam (face) Yahawah, for their shagagah (error):

And all the idah (congregation) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall be salach (forgive/pardon/make clean), and the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who lives as a foreigner thawak (midst) them; for in respect of all the im (nation / people) it was done shagagah (unwittingly).
"‘If napash (soul) napash (soul) chataa (sins) shagagah (unwittingly), then he shall qarab (come close) a female iz (goat) a shanah (year) old for a chataah (sin) offering.

The kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for the napash (soul) who shagag (errs), when he chataa (sins) shagagah (unwittingly), panayam (face) Yahawah, to make kapar (atonement) for him; and he shall be salach (forgive/pardon/make clean).

You shall have achad (one) thawarah (instruction) for him who ishah (make) anything shagagah (unwittingly), for him who is native-born among the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and for the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who lives as a foreigner thawak (midst) them.

"‘But the napash (soul) who ishah (make) anything with a high hand, whether he is native-born or a foreigner, the same gadap (blasphemes) Yahawah; and that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from qarab (among / near) his im (nation / people).

Because he has bazah (despised) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, and has parar (broken) his matzawah (commandment), that napash (soul) shall karath (cut) be karath (cut) off; his iwan (guilt/iniquity) shall be on him.'"

While the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) were in the madabar (wilderness), they matzaa (found) a ayash (man / husband) qashash (gathering) itzayam (sticks) on the shabath (shabath / rest) yawam (day).
Those who matzaa (found) him qashash (gathering) itzayam (sticks) qarab (come close) him to Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron), and to all the idah (congregation).
They yanach (put) him in custody, because it had not been parash (declared) what should be ishah (make) to him.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "The ayash (man / husband) shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death): all the idah (congregation) shall ragam (stone) him with ragam (stones) outside of the machanah (camp)."

All the idah (congregation) yatzaa (go out / come out) him outside of the machanah (camp), and ragam (stoned) him to mawath (death) with abanayam (stones); as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah (Moses).
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

"Dabar (word / matter) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and amar (spoke) them that they should ishah (make) themselves tzayatzath (fringes) in the kanapay (borders) of their bagad (garments) throughout their dawar (generation / age / period), and that they nathan (give) on the tzayatzath (fringe) of each kanap (border) a cord of thakalath (blue):

And it shall be to you for a tzayatzath (fringe), that you may raah (see) on it, and zakar (remember) all the matzawath (commandments) of Yahawah, and ishah (make) them; and that you not follow achar (other) your own labab (heart) and your own iyan (eye), achar (other) which you use to zanah (play) the prostitute;
That you may zakar (remember) and ishah (make) all my matzawah (commandments), and be qadawash (holy) to your Alahayam.
I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who yatzaa (go out / come out) you out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), to be your Alahayam: I am Yahawah your Alahayam."

Now Qarach (Korah), the ban (son) of Yatzahar (Izhar), the ban (son) of Qahath (Kohath), the ban (son) of Laway (Levi), with Dathan (Dathan) and Abayaram (Abiram), the banay (sons) of Alayaab (Eliab), and On, the ban (son) of Palath (Peleth), banay (sons) of Raawaban (Reuben), laqach (take / seize) men:

And they qawam (rise up) up panayam (face) Mashah (Moses), with ayash (man / husband) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) nashayaay (princes) of the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day), called to the idah (assembly), anashayam (men) of sham (name);

And they qahal (assembled) themselves together against Mashah (Moses) and against Aharawan (Aaron), and amar (spoke) to them, "You take rab (too) much on yourself, since all the idah (congregation) are qadawash (holy), everyone of them, and Yahawah is thawak (midst) them: why then nashaa (lift) yourselves up above the qahal (assembly) of Yahawah?"
When Mashah (Moses) shamai (hearken / hear) it, he napal (fall / be cast down) on his panayam (face):

And he dabar (word / matter) to Qarach (Korah) and to all his idah (company), amar (spoke), "In the baqar (morning) Yahawah yadai (will) show who are his, and who is qadawash (holy), and will cause him to qarab (come close) near to him: even him whom he shall bachar (choose) he will cause to qarab (come close) near to him.
Ishah (make) this: laqach (take / seize) machathawath (censers), Qarach (Korah), and all his idah (company);

And nathan (give) ash (fire) in them, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) qatarath (incense) on them panayam (face) Yahawah machar (tomorrow): and it shall be that the ayash (man / husband) whom Yahawah bachar (chooses), he shall be qadawash (holy). You rab (have) gone too far, you banay (sons) of Laway (Levi)!"
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to Qarach (Korah), "shamai (hearken / hear) now, you banay (sons) of Laway (Levi)!

Is it a mait (small) thing to you, that the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel) has badal (separated) you from the idah (congregation) of Yashar-Al (Israel), to qarab (come close) you near to himself, to ibad (servant) the ibadah (service) of the mashakan (tabernacle) of Yahawah, and to imad (stand) panayam (face) the idah (congregation) to sharath (minister) to them;
And that he has qarab (come close) you near, and all your ach (brother/kinsman) the banay (sons) of Laway (Levi) with you? And do you baqash (seek) the kahanah (priesthood) also?
Therefore you and all your idah (company) are yaid (gathered) together against Yahawah: and Aharawan (Aaron), what is he that you lawan (murmur) against him?"
Mashah (Moses) shalach (send) to qaraa (called) Dathan (Dathan) and Abayaram (Abiram), the banay (sons) of Alayaab (Eliab); and they amar (spoke), "We won't ilah (go up / offer) up:

Is it a mait (small) thing that you have ilah (go up / offer) us up out of a aratz (Earth/land) zawab (flow) with chalab (milk) and dabash (honey), to mawath (death) us in the madabar (wilderness), but you must also sharar (make) yourself a sharar (prince) over us?

Moreover you haven't bawaa (come) us into a aratz (Earth/land) zawab (flow) with chalab (milk) and dabash (honey), nor nathan (give) us nachalah (inheritance) of shadah (fields) and karam (vineyards): will you naqar (put) out the iyanay (eyes) of these anashayam (men)? We won't ilah (go up / offer) up."

Mashah (Moses) was very charah (hot with anger), and amar (spoke) to Yahawah, "Don't panah (turn) their manachah (offering): I have not nashaa (lift) achad (one) donkey from them, neither have I raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) achad (one) of them."
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to Qarach (Korah), "You and all your idah (company) go panayam (face) Yahawah, you, and they, and Aharawan (Aaron), machar (tomorrow):

And each ayash (man / husband) laqach (take / seize) his machathah (censer), and nathan (give) qatarath (incense) on them, and each ayash (man / husband) qarab (come close) panayam (face) Yahawah his machathah (censer), two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) machathath (censers); you also, and Aharawan (Aaron), ayash (man / husband) his machathah (censer)."

They ayash (man / husband) laqach (take / seize) his machathah (censer), and nathan (give) ash (fire) in them, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) qatarath (incense) thereon, and imad (stood) at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting with Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron).

Qarach (Korah) qahal (assembled) all the idah (congregation) against them to the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting: and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah raah (see) to all the idah (congregation).
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses) and to Aharawan (Aaron), amar (spoke),
"Badal (separated) yourselves from thawak (midst) this idah (congregation), that I may kalah (complete / finish) them in a ragai (in an instance)!"

They napal (fall / be cast down) on their panayam (face), and amar (spoke), "Alahayam, the Al of the rawachath (spirits) of all bashar (flesh), shall achad (one) ayash (man / husband) chataa (sin), and will you be qatzap (angry) with all the idah (congregation)?"
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),
"Dabar (word / matter) to the idah (congregation), amar (spoke), ‘ilah (go up / offer) away from around the mashakan (tent) of Qarach (Korah), Dathan (Dathan), and Abayaram (Abiram)!'"
Mashah (Moses) qawam (rise up) up and yalak (went) to Dathan (Dathan) and Abayaram (Abiram); and the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel) yalak (followed) him.

He dabar (word / matter) to the idah (congregation), amar (spoke), "sawar (depart), please, from the ahalay (tents) of these rashai (wicked) anashayam (men), and nagai (touch) nothing of theirs, lest you be sapah (consumed) in all their chataah (sin)!"

So they ilah (go up / offer) away from the mashakan (tent) of Qarach (Korah), Dathan (Dathan), and Abayaram (Abiram), on sabayab (surrounding) side: and Dathan (Dathan) and Abayaram (Abiram) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and natzab (stood) at the pathach (door) of their ahal (tents), and their wives, and their ban (son), and their little tap (ones).
Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke), "Hereby you shall yadai (know) that Yahawah has shalach (send) me to ishah (make) all these maishayam (works); for they are not from my own lab (heart).
If these men mawath (death) the common mawath (death) of all adam (men), or if they be paqad (visit) after the paqadah (visitation) of all adam (men); then Yahawah hasn't shalach (send) me.

But if Yahawah baraa (created) a barayaah (new) thing, and the adamah (ground) patzah (open) its pah (mouth), and balai (swallow) them up, with all that appertain to them, and they yarad (go) down chay (life) into shaawal (Sheol / afterlife); then you shall yadai (understand) that these yadaitham (men) have naatz (despised) Yahawah."
It happened, as he kalah (complete / finish) an end of dabar (word / matter) all these dabarayam (words), that the adamah (ground) split apart that was under them;

And the aratz (Earth/land) pathach (opened) its pah (mouth), and balai (swallowed) them up, and their bayath (house), and all the adam (men) who appertained to Qarach (Korah), and all their rakawash (wealth / property / goods / possessions).

So they, and all that appertained to them, yarad (went) down chay (life) into shaawal (Sheol / afterlife): and the aratz (Earth/land) kasah (closed) on them, and they abad (destroy / perish) from thawak (midst) the qahal (assembly).
All Yashar-Al (Israel) that were around them nawas (fled) at their qawal (sound / voice); for they amar (spoke), "Lest the aratz (Earth/land) balai (swallow) us up!"
Ash (fire) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from Yahawah, and akal (eat) the two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) ayash (man / husband) who qarab (come close) the qatarath (incense).
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

"Amar (spoke) to Alaizar (Eleazar) the ban (son) of Aharawan (Aaron) the kahan (priest), that he rawam (will lift up) up the machathah (censers) out of the sharapah (burning), and zarah (scatter) the ash (fire) halaah (yonder); for they are qadash (set apart / make holy),

Even the machathah (censers) of these chataa (sinners) against their napash (soul) lives; and let them be ishah (make) beaten pach (snare / trap) for a tzapaway (covering) of the mazabach (altar): for they qarab (come close) them panayam (face) Yahawah; therefore they are qadash (set apart / make holy); and they shall be a awath (sign / mark / miracle) to the ban (son) of Yashar-Al (Israel)."

Alaizar (Eleazar) the kahan (priest) laqach (take / seize) the bronze machathah (censers), which those who were burnt had qarab (come close); and they raqai (beat) them out for a tzapaway (covering) of the mazabach (altar),

To be a zakarawan (memorial) to the ban (son) of Yashar-Al (Israel), to the end that no stranger, who isn't of the zarai (seed) of Aharawan (Aaron), qarab (come close) near to qatar (burn) qatarath (incense) panayam (face) Yahawah; that he not be as Qarach (Korah), and as his idah (company): as Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to him by Mashah (Moses).

But on the next macharath (day) all the idah (congregation) of the ban (son) of Yashar-Al (Israel) lawan (murmured) against Mashah (Moses) and against Aharawan (Aaron), amar (spoke), "You have mawath (death) Yahawah im (nation / people)!"

It happened, when the idah (congregation) was qahal (assembled) against Mashah (Moses) and against Aharawan (Aaron), that they panah (turn) toward the ahal (tent) of Meeting: and behold, the inan (cloud) kasah (covered) it, and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah raah (see).
Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) bawaa (come) to the front of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),
"Ramam (get) away from thawak (midst) this idah (congregation), that I may kalah (complete / finish) them in a ragai (in an instance)!" They napal (fall / be cast down) on their panayam (face).

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to Aharawan (Aaron), "laqach (take / seize) your machathah (censer), and nathan (give) ash (fire) from off the mazabach (altar) in it, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) qatarath (incense) on it, and yalak (carry) it maharah (quickly) to the idah (congregation), and make kapar (atonement) for them; for qatzap (wrath) yatzaa (go out / come out) gone out from Yahawah! The nagap (plague) has chalal (begun)."

Aharawan (Aaron) did as Mashah (Moses) dabar (word / matter), and rawatz (ran) into the thawak (midst) of the qahal (assembly); and behold, the nagap (plague) has chalal (begun) among the im (nation / people): and he nathan (give) on the qatarath (incense), and made kapar (atonement) for the im (nation / people).
He imad (stood) between the mawath (death) and the chay (life); and the magapah (plague) was itzar (stayed).

Now those who mawath (death) by the magapah (plague) were fourteen alap (thousand) and shabai (seven) maah (hundred), besides those who mawath (death) about the dabar (word / matter) of Qarach (Korah).
Aharawan (Aaron) shawab (turn back / repent) to Mashah (Moses) to the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting: and the magapah (plague) was itzar (stayed).
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

"Amar (spoke) to the ban (son) of Israel, and rawam (will lift up) of them rods, one for each fathers' house, of all their kahan (priest) according to their fathers' houses, twelve rods: write every ban (son) amar (spoke) on his rod.
You shall write Aaron's name on the rod of Levi; for there shall be one rod for each head of their fathers' houses.
You shall lay them up in the Tent of Meeting before the testimony, where I meet with you.

It shall happen, that the rod of the ayash (man / husband) whom I shall choose shall bud: and I will qarab (come close) to cease from me the murmurings of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), which they murmur against you."

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel); and all their princes amar (spoke) him rods, for each prince one, according to their fathers' houses, even twelve rods: and the rod of Aharawan (Aaron) was il (over) their rods.
Mashah (Moses) laid up the rods before Yahawah in the ahal (tent) of the testimony.

It happened on the next day, that Mashah (Moses) bawaa (come) into the ahal (tent) of the testimony; and behold, the rod of Aharawan (Aaron) for the house of Levi was budded, and bawaa (come) forth buds, and produced blossoms, and bore ripe almonds.
Mashah (Moses) brought out all the rods from before Yahawah to all the children of Israel: and they looked, and took every man his rod.

Yahawah said to Moses, "Put back the rod of Aaron panayam (face) the testimony, to be kept for a token against the children of rebellion; that you may kalah (complete / finish) an end of their murmurings against me, that they not napal (fall / be cast down)."
Mashah (Moses) nathan (give) so. As Yahawah amar (spoke) him, so he nathan (give).
The children of Israel dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), dabar (word / matter), "Behold, we perish! We are undone! We are all undone!
Everyone who comes near, who comes near to the tabernacle of Yahawah, mathayam (dies)! Will we mawath (death) perish?"

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Aharawan (Aaron), "You and your ban (son) and your ab (father)' bayath (house) with you shall nashaa (lift) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the maqadash (sanctuary); and you and your ban (son) with you shall nashaa (lift) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of your kahanah (priesthood).

Your ach (brother/kinsman) also, the matah (staff / rod / tribe) of Laway (Levi), the matah (staff / rod / tribe) of your ab (father), qarab (come close) near with you, that they may be lawah (joined) to you, and sharath (minister) to you: but you and your ban (son) with you shall be panayam (face) the ahal (tent) of the idawath (testimony).

They shall shamar (keep/guard) your commands, and the duty of all the ahal (tent): only they shall not qarab (come close) near to the kalay (vessels) of the qadash (set apart / make holy) and to the mazabach (altar), that they not mawath (death), neither they, nor you.

They shall be lawah (joined) to you, and shamar (keep/guard) the responsibility of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, for all the ibadah (service) of the ahal (tent): and a stranger shall not qarab (come close) near to you.
"You shall perform the duty of the qadash (set apart / make holy), and the duty of the mazabach (altar); that there be no more qatzap (wrath) on the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

I, behold, I have laqach (take / seize) your ach (brother/kinsman) the Lawayay (Levites) from thawak (midst) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel): to you they are a mathanah (gift), nathan (give) to Yahawah, to ibad (servant) the ibadah (service) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

You and your ban (son) with you shall shamar (keep/guard) your kahanah (priesthood) for everything of the mazabach (altar), and for that bayath (house) the parakath (veil); and you shall ibad (servant): I nathan (give) you the kahanah (priesthood) as a ibadah (service) of mathanah (gift): and the stranger who ban (son) near shall be put to mawath (death)."

Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Aharawan (Aaron), "I, behold, I nathan (give) given you the command of my wave tharawamah (offerings), even all the qadawash (holy) things of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel); to you nathan (give) I given them by reason of the mashachah (anointing), and to your banay (sons), as a chaq (statute) iwalam (forever).

This shall be yours of the most qadash (set apart / make holy) things from the ash (fire): every qaraban (offering) of theirs, even every meal manachah (offering) of theirs, and every chataah (sin) offering of theirs, and every asham (trespass) offering of theirs, which they shall shawab (turn back / repent) to me, shall be most qadash (set apart / make holy) for you and for your ban (son).
You shall akal (eat) of it like the most qadash (set apart / make holy) things. Every zakar (remember) shall akal (eat) of it. It shall be qadash (set apart / make holy) to you.

"This is yours, too: the wave tharawamah (offering) of their mathan (gift), even all the wave thanawapath (offerings) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel). I nathan (give) given them to you, and to your banay (sons) and to your banath (daughter) with you, as a chaq (statute) iwalam (forever). Everyone who is tahawar (clean) in your bayath (house) shall akal (eat) of it.

"All the chalab (best) of the yatzahar (fresh oil), and all the chalab (best) of the vintage, and of the grain, the raashayath (beginning) fruits of them which they nathan (give) to Yahawah, to you nathan (give) I given them.
The first-ripe fruits of all that is in their aratz (Earth/land), which they bawaa (come) to Yahawah, shall be yours; everyone who is tahawar (clean) in your bayath (house) shall akal (eat) of it.
"Everything charam (devoted) in Yashar-Al (Israel) shall be yours.

Everything that patar (opens) the racham (womb), of all bashar (flesh) which they qarab (come close) to Yahawah, both of adam (man) and animal shall be yours: nevertheless you shall padah (surely) padah (redeem) the bakawar (firstborn) of adam (man), and you shall padah (redeem) the bakawar (firstborn) of tamaa (unclean) animals.

You shall padah (redeem) those who are to be padah (redeemed) of them from a chadash (month) ban (son), according to your irak (estimation), for chamash (five) shaqalayam (shekels) of kasap (money), after the shaqal (shekel) of the qadash (set apart / make holy) (the same is isharayam (twenty) garah (gerahs)).

"But you shall not padah (redeem) the bakawar (firstborn) of a shawar (cow), or the bakawar (firstborn) of a sheep, or the bakawar (firstborn) of a iz (goat). They are qadash (set apart / make holy). You shall zaraq (sprinkle) their dam (blood) on the mazabach (altar), and shall qatar (burn) their chalab (fat) for an ashah (fire / offering made by fire) made by fire, for a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.
Their bashar (flesh) shall be yours, as the thanawapah (wave) offering chazah (breast) and as the yamayan (right hand) shawaq (thigh), it shall be yours.

All the wave tharawamath (offerings) of the qadash (set apart / make holy) things, which the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) rawam (will lift up) to Yahawah, nathan (give) I given you, and your banay (sons) and your banath (daughter) with you, as a chaq (statute) iwalam (forever): it is a barayath (covenant) of malach (salt) iwalam (forever) panayam (face) Yahawah to you and to your zarai (seed) with you."

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Aharawan (Aaron), "You shall have no nachal (inheritance) in their aratz (Earth/land), neither shall you have any chalaq (portion) thawak (midst) them. I am your chalaq (portion) and your nachalah (inheritance) thawak (midst) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

"To the banay (children) of Laway (Levi), behold, I nathan (give) given all the tithe in Yashar-Al (Israel) for an nachalah (inheritance), in chalap (return) for their ibadah (service) which they ibad (servant), even the ibadah (service) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
Iwad (more/again) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall not qarab (come close) near the ahal (tent) of Meeting, lest they nashaa (lift) chataa (sin), and mawath (death).

But the Lawayay (Levites) shall ibad (servant) the ibadah (service) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and they shall nashaa (lift) their iwan (guilt/iniquity): it shall be a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) throughout your dawar (generation / age / period); and thawak (midst) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) they shall nachal (have) no nachalah (inheritance).

For the maishar (tithe) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), which they rawam (will lift up) as a wave tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah, I nathan (give) given to the Lawayay (Levites) for an nachalah (inheritance): therefore I have amar (spoke) to them, ‘thawak (midst) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) they shall nachal (have) no nachalah (inheritance).'"
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

"Moreover you shall dabar (word / matter) to the Lawayay (Levites), and amar (spoke) them, ‘When you laqach (take / seize) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) the maishar (tithe) which I nathan (give) given you from them for your nachalah (inheritance), then you shall rawam (will lift up) up a wave tharawamah (offering) of it for Yahawah, a maishar (tithe) of the maishar (tithe).
Your wave tharawamah (offering) shall be chashab (reckoned) to you, as though it were the grain of the garan (threshing) floor, and as the fullness of the yaqab (winepress).

Thus you also shall rawam (will lift up) a wave tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah of all your maishar (tithes), which you laqach (take / seize) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel); and of it you shall nathan (give) Yahawah wave tharawamah (offering) to Aharawan (Aaron) the kahan (priest).
Out of all your mathanah (gifts) you shall rawam (will lift up) every wave tharawamah (offering) of Yahawah, of all its chalab (best), even the maqadash (holy) part of it out of it.'

"Therefore you shall amar (spoke) them, ‘When you rawam (will lift up) its chalab (best) from it, then it shall be chashab (reckoned) to the Lawayay (Levites) as the thabawaah (increase) of the garan (threshing) floor, and as the thabawaah (increase) of the yaqab (winepress).
You shall akal (eat) it in every maqawam (place), you and your bayath (house): for it is your shakar (reward) in chalap (return) for your ibadah (service) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

You shall nashaa (lift) no chataa (sin) by reason of it, when you have rawam (will lift up) from it its chalab (best): and you shall not chalal (profane) the qadawash (holy) things of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), that you not mawath (death).'"
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses) and to Aharawan (Aaron), amar (spoke),

"This is the chaqah (statute) of the thawarah (instruction) which Yahawah has tzawah (commanded): dabar (word / matter) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), that they laqach (take / seize) you a adam (red) parah (heifer) thamayam (complete / whole) spot, in which is no maawam (blemish), and which was laa (NOT) il (over).

You shall nathan (give) her to Alaizar (Eleazar) the kahan (priest), and he shall yatzaa (go out / come out) her forth outside of the machanah (camp), and one shall shachat (kill) her before his panayam (face):

And Alaizar (Eleazar) the kahan (priest) shall laqach (take / seize) of her dam (blood) with his atzabai (finger), and nazah (sprinkle) her dam (blood) toward the panayam (face) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting shabai (seven) paimayam (times).
One shall sharap (burn) the parah (heifer) in his iyan (eye); her iwar (skin), and her bashar (flesh), and her dam (blood), with her parash (dung), shall he sharap (burn):

And the kahan (priest) shall laqach (take / seize) araz (cedar) itz (wood), and azawab (hyssop), and thawalai (scarlet), and shalak (cast) it into the thawak (midst) of the sharapah (burning) of the parah (heifer).

Then the kahan (priest) shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and he shall rachatz (bathe) his bashar (flesh) in mayam (Waters), and afterward he shall bawaa (come) into the machanah (camp), and the kahan (priest) shall be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).
He who sharap (burns) her shall kabas (wash) his clothes in mayam (Waters), and bathe his bashar (flesh) in mayam (Waters), and shall be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening).

"A ayash (man / husband) who is tahawar (clean) shall asap (gather) up the ashes of the parah (heifer), and yanach (lay) them up outside of the machanah (camp) in a tahawar (clean) maqawam (place); and it shall be mashamarath (duty / watch) for the idah (congregation) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) for a mayam (Waters) for impurity: it is a chataah (sin) offering.

He who asap (gathers) the ashes of the parah (heifer) shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and be tamaa (unclean) until the irab (evening): and it shall be to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and to the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who lives as a foreigner thawak (midst) them, for a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever).
"He who touches the mawath (death) napash (soul) of any adam (man) shall be tamaa (unclean) shabai (seven) yamayam (days):

The same shall chataa (purify) himself with water on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), and on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) he shall be tahar (clean): but if he doesn't chataa (purify) himself the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), then the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) he shall not be tahar (clean).

Whoever touches a mawath (death) napash (soul), the body of a adam (man) who has mawath (death), and doesn't chataa (purify) himself, tamaa (defiles) the mashakan (tabernacle) of Yahawah; and that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from Yashar-Al (Israel): because the mayam (Waters) for impurity was not zaraq (sprinkled) on him, he shall be tamaa (unclean); his tamaah (uncleanness) is yet on him.

"This is the thawarah (instruction) when a adam (man) mawath (death) in a ahal (tent): everyone who bawaa (come) into the ahal (tent), and everyone who is in the ahal (tent), shall be tamaa (unclean) shabai (seven) yamayam (days).
Every pathach (open) kalay (vessel), which has no tzamayad (covering) pathayal (bound) on it, is tamaa (unclean).

"Whoever in the panayam (face) shadah (field) touches one who is chalal (slain) with a charab (sword), or a mawath (death) body, or a itzam (bone) of a adam (man), or a qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher), shall be tamaa (unclean) shabai (seven) yamayam (days).

"For the tamaa (unclean) they shall laqach (take / seize) of the ashes of the sharapah (burning) of the chataah (sin) offering; and chay (life) mayam (Waters) shall be nathan (give) thereto in a kalay (vessel):

And a tahawar (clean) ayash (man / husband) shall laqach (take / seize) azawab (hyssop), and tabal (dip) it in the mayam (Waters), and nazah (sprinkle) it on the ahal (tent), and on all the kalayam (vessels), and on the napashawath (persons) who were there, and on him who nagai (touched) the itzam (bone), or the chalal (slain), or the mawath (death), or the qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher):

And the tahawar (clean) person shall nazah (sprinkle) on the tamaa (unclean) on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), and on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day): and on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) he shall chataa (purify) him; and he shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (Waters), and shall be tahar (clean) at irab (evening).

But the ayash (man / husband) who shall be tamaa (unclean), and shall not chataa (purify) himself, that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from the thawak (midst) of the qahal (assembly), because he has tamaa (defiled) the maqadash (sanctuary) of Yahawah: the mayam (Waters) for impurity has not been zaraq (sprinkled) on him; he is tamaa (unclean).

It shall be a iwalam (forever) chaqah (statute) to them: and he who nazah (sprinkles) the mayam (Waters) for impurity shall kabas (wash) his clothes, and he who touches the mayam (Waters) for impurity shall be tamaa (unclean) until irab (evening).
"Whatever the tamaa (unclean) person touches shall be tamaa (unclean); and the napash (soul) that touches it shall be tamaa (unclean) until irab (evening)."

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), even the whole idah (congregation), bawaa (come) into the madabar (wilderness) of Tzan (Zin) in the raashawan (first) chadash (month): and the im (nation / people) stayed in Qadash (Kadesh); and Marayam (Miriam) mawath (death) there, and was qabar (bury) there.
There was no mayam (Waters) for the idah (congregation): and they qahal (assembled) themselves together against Mashah (Moses) and against Aharawan (Aaron).
The im (nation / people) rayab (strove) with Mashah (Moses), and amar (spoke), amar (spoke), "We wish that we had gawai (died) when our ach (brother/kinsman) gawai (died) panayam (face) Yahawah!
Why bawaa (come) you brought the qahal (assembly) of Yahawah into this madabar (wilderness), that we should mawath (death) there, we and our animals?

Why have you ilah (go up / offer) us to come up out of Matzarayam (Egypt), to bawaa (come) us in to this rai (evil) maqawam (place)? It is no maqawam (place) of zarai (seed), or of thaan (figs), or of gapan (vines), or of ramawan (pomegranates); neither is there any mayam (Waters) to shathah (drinks)."

Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) bawaa (come) from the panayam (face) of the qahal (assembly) to the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and napal (fall / be cast down) on their panay (faces): and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah raah (see) to them.
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Mashah (Moses), amar (spoke),

"Laqach (take / seize) the matah (staff / rod / tribe), and qahal (assemble) the idah (congregation), you, and Aharawan (Aaron) your ach (brother/kinsman), and dabar (word / matter) to the salai (rock) before their iyan (eye), that it nathan (give) forth its mayam (Waters); and you shall nathan (give) forth to them mayam (Waters) out of the salai (rock); so you shall shaqah (give) the idah (congregation) and their livestock shaqah (drink)."
Mashah (Moses) laqach (take / seize) the matah (staff / rod / tribe) from panayam (face) Yahawah, as he tzawah (commanded) him.

Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) qahal (gathered) the qahal (assembly) together panayam (face) the salai (rock), and he amar (spoke) to them, "shamai (hearken / hear) now, you marayam (rebels); shall we yatzaa (go out / come out) you mayam (Waters) out of this salai (rock) for you?"

Mashah (Moses) rawam (will lift up) up his yad (hand), and nakah (struck) the salai (rock) with his matah (staff / rod / tribe) paim (twice): and mayam (Waters) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth abundantly, and the idah (congregation) shathah (drinks), and their livestock.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron), "Because you didn't aman (believe / have faith) in me, to qadash (set apart / make holy) me in the iyanay (eyes) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), therefore you shall not bawaa (come) this qahal (assembly) into the aratz (Earth/land) which I nathan (give) given them."
These are the may (waters) of Marayabah (Meribah); because the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) rayab (strove) with Yahawah, and he was qadash (set apart / make holy) in them.

Mashah (Moses) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) from Qadash (Kadesh) to the malak (king) of Adawam (Edom), amar (spoke): "Thus says your ach (brother/kinsman) Yashar-Al (Israel): You yadai (know) all the thalaah (travail) that matzaa (has) happened to us:

How our ab (father) yarad (went) down into Matzarayam (Egypt), and we lived in Matzarayam (Egypt) a rab (long) yawam (day); and the Matzarayam (Egyptians) dealt raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) with us, and our ab (father):

And when we tzaiq (cried) to Yahawah, he shamai (hearken / hear) our qawal (sound / voice), and shalach (send) an malaak (angel / messenger of Yah), and yatzaa (go out / come out) us forth out of Matzarayam (Egypt): and behold, we are in Qadash (Kadesh), a iyar (city) in the uttermost of your gabawal (border/boundary).

"Please let us ibar (pass over/through) through your aratz (Earth/land): we will not ibar (pass over/through) through shadah (field) or through karam (vineyard), neither will we shathah (drinks) of the mayam (Waters) of the baar (wells): we will yalak (go) along the malak (king) darak (highway); we will not natah (turn) aside to the right yamayan (right hand) nor to the shamaawal (left hand), until we ibar (pass over/through) passed your gabawal (border/boundary)."
Adawam (Edom) amar (spoke) to him, "You shall not ibar (pass over/through) through me, lest I yatzaa (go out / come out) out with the charab (sword) qaraah (against) you."

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke) to him, "We will ilah (go up / offer) up by the masalah (highway); and if we shathah (drinks) of your mayam (Waters), I and my livestock, then will I nathan (give) its price: let me only, without doing anything else, ibar (pass over/through) through on my ragal (feet / foot)."

He amar (spoke), "You shall not ibar (pass over/through) through." Adawam (Edom) yatzaa (go out / come out) out qaraah (against) him with many im (nation / people), and with a chazaq (strong) yad (hand).
Thus Adawam (Edom) maan (refused) to nathan (give) Yashar-Al (Israel) passage through his gabawal (border/boundary), so Yashar-Al (Israel) natah (turned) away from him.
They traveled from Qadash (Kadesh): and the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), even the whole idah (congregation), bawaa (come) to har (mountain) Har (Hor).
Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) in har (mountain) Har (Hor), by the gabawal (border/boundary) of the aratz (Earth/land) of Adawam (Edom), amar (spoke),

"Aharawan (Aaron) shall be asap (gathered) to his im (nation / people); for he shall not bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land) which I nathan (give) given to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), because you marah (rebelled) against my pah (word) at the may (waters) of Marayabah (Meribah).
Laqach (take / seize) Aharawan (Aaron) and Alaizar (Eleazar) his ban (son), and ilah (go up / offer) them up to har (mountain) Har (Hor);
And pashat (strip) Aharawan (Aaron) of his bagad (garments), and labash (put) them on Alaizar (Eleazar) his ban (son): and Aharawan (Aaron) shall be asap (taken), and shall mawath (death) there."
Mashah (Moses) ishah (make) as Yahawah tzawah (commanded): and they ilah (go up / offer) up into har (mountain) Har (Hor) in the iyan (eye) of all the idah (congregation).

Mashah (Moses) pashat (stripped) Aharawan (Aaron) of his bagad (garments), and labash (put) them on Alaizar (Eleazar) his ban (son); and Aharawan (Aaron) mawath (death) there on the raash (head) of the har (mountain): and Mashah (Moses) and Alaizar (Eleazar) yarad (came) down from the har (mountain).

When all the idah (congregation) raah (see) that Aharawan (Aaron) was gawai (dead), they bakah (wept) for Aharawan (Aaron) shalawashayam (thirty) yawam (day), even all the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

The Kanainay (Canaanite), the malak (king) of Irad (Arad), who lived in the nagab (south), shamai (hearken / hear) tell that Yashar-Al (Israel) bawaa (come) by the darak (way) of Atharayam (Atharim); and he lacham (fought) against Yashar-Al (Israel), and shabah (took) some of them shabay (captive).

Yashar-Al (Israel) nadar (make vow) a nadar (vow) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "If you will nathan (give) nathan (give) this im (nation / people) into my yad (hand), then I will utterly charam (destroy) their iyar (cities)."

Yahawah shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and nathan (give) up the Kanainay (Canaanites); and they charam (utterly) destroyed them and their iyar (cities): and the sham (name) of the maqawam (place) was qaraa (called) Charamah (Hormah).

They traveled from har (mountain) Har (Hor) by the darak (way) to the sawap (red) yam (sea/waters), to sabab (compass) the aratz (Earth/land) of Adawam (Edom): and the napash (soul) of the im (nation / people) was much qatzar (discouraged) because of the darak (way).

The im (nation / people) dabar (word / matter) against Alahayam, and against Mashah (Moses), "Why have you ilah (go up / offer) us up out of Matzarayam (Egypt) to mawath (death) in the madabar (wilderness)? For there is no lacham (bread), and there is no mayam (Waters); and our napash (soul) qawatz (loathes) this qalaqal (light) lacham (bread)."
Yahawah shalach (send) sharap (fiery) nachashayam (serpents) among the im (nation / people), and they bit the im (nation / people); and many im (nation / people) of Yashar-Al (Israel) mawath (death).

The im (nation / people) bawaa (come) to Mashah (Moses), and amar (spoke), "We have chataa (sinned), because we have amar (spoke) against Yahawah, and against you. Palal (pray) to Yahawah, that he sawar (take) away the nachash (serpents) from us." Mashah (Moses) palal (prayed) for the im (nation / people).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "ishah (make) a sharap (fiery) serpent, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it on a nas (standard): and it shall happen, that everyone who is bitten, when he raah (see) it, shall live."

Mashah (Moses) ishah (make) a nachash (serpent) of nachashath (brass), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it on the nas (standard): and it happened, that if a nachash (serpent) had bitten any ayash (man / husband), when he nabat (looked) to the nachash (serpent) of nachashath (brass), he chayay (life).
The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) traveled, and chanah (encamped) in Abath (Oboth).
They traveled from Abath (Oboth), and chanah (encamped) at Iyayahaibarayam (Iyeabarim), in the madabar (wilderness) which is panayam (face) Mawaab (Moab), toward the sunrise.
From there they traveled, and chanah (encamped) in the nachal (stream / river) of Zarad (Zered).

From there they traveled, and chanah (encamped) on the other ibar (side) of the Aranawan (Arnon), which is in the madabar (wilderness), that yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the gabawal (border/boundary) of the Amaray (Amorites): for the Aranawan (Arnon) is the gabawal (border/boundary) of Mawaab (Moab), between Mawaab (Moab) and the Amaray (Amorites).
Therefore it is amar (spoke) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the malachamath (wars) of Yahawah, "Wahab (Vaheb) in Suphah, the nachalayam (valleys) of the Aranawan (Arnon),
The slope of the nachalayam (valleys) that natah (incline) toward the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Ir (Ar), shain (leans) on the gabawal (border/boundary) of Mawaab (Moab)."

From there they traveled to Baar (Beer): that is the baar (well) of which Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "asap (gather) the im (nation / people) asap (together), and I will nathan (give) them mayam (Waters)."
Then shayar (sang) Yashar-Al (Israel) this shayar (song): "ilah (go up / offer) up, baar (well); inah (answer / respond) to it:

The baar (well), which the sharayam (princes) chapar (dug), which the nadayabay (nobles) of the im (nation / people) karah (dug), with the scepter, and with their poles." From the madabar (wilderness) they traveled to Mathanah (Mattanah);
And from Mathanah (Mattanah) to Nachalayaal (Nahaliel); and from Nachalayaal (Nahaliel) to Bamawath (Bamoth);
And from Bamawath (Bamoth) to the gayaa (valley) that is in the shadah (field) of Mawaab (Moab), to the raash (head) of Pasagah (Pisgah), which shaqap (looks) down on the yashayamawan (desert).
Yashar-Al (Israel) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to Sayachawan (Sihon) malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), amar (spoke),

"Let me ibar (pass over/through) through your aratz (Earth/land): we will not natah (turn) aside into shadah (field), or into karam (vineyard); we will not shathah (drinks) of the mayam (Waters) of the baar (wells): we will yalak (go) by the malak (king) darak (highway), until we ibar (pass over/through) passed your gabawal (border/boundary)."

Sayachawan (Sihon) nathan (give) not allow Yashar-Al (Israel) to ibar (pass over/through) through his gabawal (border/boundary): but Sayachawan (Sihon) asap (gathered) all his im (nation / people) asap (together), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out qaraah (against) Yashar-Al (Israel) into the madabar (wilderness), and bawaa (come) to Yahatz (Jahaz); and he lacham (fought) against Yashar-Al (Israel).

Yashar-Al (Israel) nakah (struck) him with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), and yarash (possessed) his aratz (Earth/land) from the Aranawan (Arnon) to the Yabaq (Jabbok), even to the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon); for the gabawal (border/boundary) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) was iz (strong).

Yashar-Al (Israel) laqach (take / seize) all these irayam (cities): and Yashar-Al (Israel) lived in all the irayam (cities) of the Amaray (Amorites), in Chashabawan (Heshbon), and in all its banath (daughter).

For Chashabawan (Heshbon) was the iyar (city) of Sayachawan (Sihon) the malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), who had lacham (fought) against the raashawan (former) malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab), and laqach (take / seize) all his aratz (Earth/land) out of his yad (hand), even to the Aranawan (Arnon).

Therefore those who mashal (speak in proverb/parable) in proverbs amar (spoke), "bawaa (come) to Chashabawan (Heshbon). Let the iyar (city) of Sayachawan (Sihon) be banah (build) and kawan (established);

For a ash (fire) yatzaa (go out / come out) gone out of Chashabawan (Heshbon), a lahabah (flame) from the qarayah (city / town) of Sayachawan (Sihon). It has akal (eat) Ir (Ar) of Mawaab (Moab), The bailay (lords) of the high places of the Aranawan (Arnon).

Away (woe) to you, Mawaab (Moab)! You are abad (destroy / perish), im (nation / people) of Kamawash (Chemosh)! He nathan (give) given his ban (son) as palayatam (fugitives), and his banath (daughter) into shabay (captivity), to Sayachawan (Sihon) malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites).

We have yarah (shot) at them. Chashabawan (Heshbon) abad (destroy / perish) perished even to Dayabawan (Dibon). We have shamam (laid) waste even to Napach (Nophah), Which reaches to May-Dabaa (Medeba)."
Thus Yashar-Al (Israel) lived in the aratz (Earth/land) of the Amaray (Amorites).
Mashah (Moses) shalach (send) to ragal (spy) out Yaizayar (Jazer); and they lakad (took) its banath (daughter), and yarash (drove) out the Amaray (Amorites) who were there.

They panah (turn) and ilah (go up / offer) up by the darak (way) of Bashan (Bashan): and Iwag (Og) the malak (king) of Bashan (Bashan) yatzaa (go out / come out) out qaraah (against) them, he and all his im (nation / people), to malachamah (battle) at Adaraiy (Edrei).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "Don't yaraa (fear / be afraid) him: for I nathan (give) delivered him into your yad (hand), and all his im (nation / people), and his aratz (Earth/land); and you shall ishah (make) to him as you ishah (make) to Sayachawan (Sihon) malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), who lived at Chashabawan (Heshbon)."

So they nakah (struck) him, and his ban (son) and all his im (nation / people), until there was balathay (without) shaar (left) him sharayad (remaining): and they yarash (possessed) his aratz (Earth/land).
The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) traveled, and chanah (encamped) in the irabawath (plains) of Mawaab (Moab) ibar (beyond) the Yaradan (Jordan) at Yarayachaw (Jericho).
Balaq (Balak) the ban (son) of Tzapawar (Zippor) raah (see) all that Yashar-Al (Israel) ishah (make) done to the Amaray (Amorites).
Mawaab (Moab) was very gawar (afraid) of the im (nation / people), because they were many: and Mawaab (Moab) was qawatz (distressed) panayam (face) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Mawaab (Moab) amar (spoke) to the zaqanay (elders) of Madayan (Midian), "Now this qahal (multitude) will lachak (lick) up all that is around us, as the shawar (ox) yalachakaw (licks) up the yaraq (grass) of the shadah (field)." Balaq (Balak) the ban (son) of Tzapawar (Zippor) was malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab) at that ith (time).

He shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to Balaim (Balaam) the ban (son) of Baiwar (Beor), to Pathawar (Pethor), which is by the nahar (river), to the aratz (Earth/land) of the banay (children) of his im (nation / people), to qaraa (called) him, amar (spoke), "Behold, there is a im (nation / people) who yatzaa (go out / come out) out from Matzarayam (Egypt). Behold, they kasah (cover) the surface of the aratz (Earth/land), and they are staying opposite me.

Please yalak (come) now therefore arar (curse) me this im (nation / people); for they are too itzawam (mighty) for me: perhaps I shall yakal (prevail), that we may nakah (strike) them, and that I may garash (drive) them out of the aratz (Earth/land); for I yadai (know) that he whom you barak (blessed) is barak (blessed), and he whom you arar (curse) is arar (cursed)."

The zaqanay (elders) of Mawaab (Moab) and the zaqanay (elders) of Madayan (Midian) departed with the rewards of qasam (divination) in their yad (hand); and they bawaa (come) to Balaim (Balaam), and dabar (word / matter) to him the dabaray (words) of Balaq (Balak).

He amar (spoke) to them, "lawan (lodge) here this layal (night), and I will shawab (turn back / repent) you dabar (word / matter) again, as Yahawah shall dabar (word / matter) to me." The sharay (princes) of Mawaab (Moab) stayed with Balaim (Balaam).
Alahayam bawaa (come) to Balaim (Balaam), and amar (spoke), "Who are these anashayam (men) with you?"
Balaim (Balaam) amar (spoke) to Alahayam, "Balaq (Balak) the ban (son) of Tzapawar (Zippor), malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab), has said to me,

‘Behold, the im (nation / people) that yatzaa (go out / come out) come out of Matzarayam (Egypt), it kasah (covers) the surface of the aratz (Earth/land): now, yalak (come) qabab (curse) me them; perhaps I shall be yakal (able) to lacham (fight) against them, and shall garash (drive) them out.'"
Alahayam amar (spoke) to Balaim (Balaam), "You shall not yalak (go) with them. You shall not arar (curse) the im (nation / people); for they are barak (blessed)."

Balaim (Balaam) qawam (rise up) up in the baqar (morning), and amar (spoke) to the sharay (princes) of Balaq (Balak), "yalak (go) to your aratz (Earth/land); for Yahawah maan (refuses) to permit me to halak (move) with you."
The sharay (princes) of Mawaab (Moab) qawam (rise up) up, and they bawaa (come) to Balaq (Balak), and amar (spoke), "Balaim (Balaam) maan (refuses) to halak (move) with us."
Balaq (Balak) shalach (send) yet again sharayam (princes), more, and more honorable than they.
They bawaa (come) to Balaim (Balaam), and amar (spoke) to him, "Thus yaamaraw (says) Balaq (Balak) the ban (son) of Tzapawar (Zippor), ‘Please let nothing hinder you from halak (move) to me:

For I will kabad (promote) you to very kabad (great) honor, and whatever you amar (spoke) to me I will ishah (make). Please yalak (come) therefore, and qabab (curse) this im (nation / people) for me.'"

Balaim (Balaam) inah (answer / respond) the ibaday (servants) of Balaq (Balak), "If Balaq (Balak) nathan (give) give me his bayath (house) malaa (full) of kasap (silver) and zahab (gold), I can't ibar (pass over/through) beyond the pah (word) of Yahawah my Alahayam, to ishah (make) qatan (small / young / least) or more.
Now therefore, please wait also here this layal (night), that I may yadai (know) what Yahawah will dabar (word / matter) to me more."

Alahayam bawaa (come) to Balaim (Balaam) at layal (night), and amar (spoke) to him, "If the anashayam (men) bawaa (come) come to qaraa (called) you, qawam (rise up) up, yalak (go) with them; but only the dabar (word / matter) which I dabar (word / matter) to you, that you shall ishah (make)."
Balaim (Balaam) qawam (rise up) up in the baqar (morning), and chabash (saddled) his donkey, and yalak (went) with the sharay (princes) of Mawaab (Moab).

Alahayam ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger) because he halak (move); and the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah placed himself in the darak (way) for an shatan (adversary) against him. Now he was rakab (riding) on his donkey, and his shanayam (two) nair (servants) were with him.

The donkey raah (see) the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah natzab (standing) in the darak (way), with his charab (sword) shalap (drawn) in his yad (hand); and the donkey natah (turned) aside out of the darak (way), and yalak (went) into the shadah (field): and Balaim (Balaam) nakah (struck) the donkey, to natah (turn) her into the darak (way).
Then the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah imad (stood) in a narrow mashaiwal (path) between the karamayam (vineyards), a gadar (wall) being on this side, and a gadar (wall) on that side.

The donkey raah (see) the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah, and she lachatz (thrust) herself to the qayar (wall), and lachatz (crushed) Balaim (Balaam's) ragal (feet / foot) against the qayar (wall): and he nakah (struck) her again.

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah ibar (pass over/through) yasap (further), and imad (stood) in a tzar (oppressor / distressor) maqawam (place), where there was no darak (way) to natah (turn) either to the right yamayan (right hand) or to the shamaawal (left hand).

The donkey raah (see) the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah, and she rabatz (lay) down under Balaim (Balaam): and Balaim (Balaam's) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger), and he nakah (struck) the donkey with his maqal (staff).

Yahawah pathach (opened) the pah (mouth) of the donkey, and she amar (spoke) to Balaim (Balaam), "What ishah (make) I done to you, that you have nakah (struck) me these shalawash (three) ragalayam (times)?"
Balaim (Balaam) amar (spoke) to the donkey, "Because you have ilal (mocked) me, I wish there were a charab (sword) in my yad (hand), for now I would have harag (kill) you."

The donkey amar (spoke) to Balaim (Balaam), "Am I not your donkey, on which you have rakab (ridden) all your yawam (day) long to this day? Was I sakan (ever) in the habit of ishah (make) so to you?" He amar (spoke), "No."

Then Yahawah galah (opened) the iyanay (eyes) of Balaim (Balaam), and he raah (see) the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah natzab (standing) in the darak (way), with his charab (sword) shalap (drawn) in his yad (hand); and he qadad (bowed) his head, and shachah (fell) on his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, "Why have you nakah (struck) your donkey these shalawash (three) ragalayam (times)? Behold, I yatzaa (go out / come out) come forth as an shatan (adversary), because your darak (way) is yarat (perverse) before me:

And the donkey raah (see) me, and natah (turned) aside panayam (face) me these shalawash (three) ragalayam (times). Awalay (perhaps) she had natah (turned) aside from me, harag (kill) now I would have killed you, and chayah (saved) her alive."

Balaim (Balaam) amar (spoke) to the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah, "I have chataa (sinned); for I didn't yadai (know) that you natzab (stood) in the darak (way) qaraah (against) me. Now therefore, if it raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) you, I will shawab (turn back / repent) back again."

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah amar (spoke) to Balaim (Balaam), "yalak (go) with the anashayam (men); but only the dabar (word / matter) that I shall dabar (word / matter) to you, that you shall dabar (word / matter)." So Balaim (Balaam) yalak (went) with the sharay (princes) of Balaq (Balak).

When Balaq (Balak) shamai (hearken / hear) that Balaim (Balaam) bawaa (come) come, he yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) him to the iyar (city) of Mawaab (Moab), which is on the gabawal (border/boundary) of the Aranawan (Arnon), which is in the utmost part of the gabawal (border/boundary).

Balaq (Balak) amar (spoke) to Balaim (Balaam), "Didn't I shalach (send) shalach (send) to you to qaraa (called) you? Why didn't you halak (move) to me? Am I not yakal (able) indeed to kabad (promote) you to honor?"

Balaim (Balaam) amar (spoke) to Balaq (Balak), "Behold, I bawaa (come) come to you: have I now any yakal (power) at yakal (all) to dabar (word / matter) anything? The dabar (word / matter) that Alahayam shawam (place / establish / appoint) in my pah (mouth), that shall I dabar (word / matter)."
Balaim (Balaam) yalak (went) with Balaq (Balak), and they bawaa (come) to Kiriath Huzoth.
Balaq (Balak) zabach (sacrificed) cattle and tzaan (sheep), and shalach (send) to Balaim (Balaam), and to the sharayam (princes) who were with him.

It happened in the baqar (morning), that Balaq (Balak) laqach (take / seize) Balaim (Balaam), and ilah (go up / offer) him up into the high places of Bamawath (Baal); and he raah (see) from there the utmost part of the im (nation / people).

Balaim (Balaam) amar (spoke) to Balaq (Balak), "banah (build) me here shabai (seven) mazabachath (altars), and kawan (prepare) me here shabai (seven) parayam (bulls) and shabai (seven) ayalayam (rams)."
Balaq (Balak) ishah (make) as Balaim (Balaam) had dabar (word / matter); and Balaq (Balak) and Balaim (Balaam) ilah (go up / offer) on every mazabach (altar) a par (bull) and a ayal (ram).

Balaim (Balaam) amar (spoke) to Balaq (Balak), "yatzab (stand) by your burnt ilah (offering), and I will yalak (go): perhaps Yahawah will qarah (come) to qaraah (meet) me; and whatever he shows me I will nagad (tell) you." He yalak (went) to a bare height.

Alahayam qarah (met) Balaim (Balaam): and he amar (spoke) to him, "I have irak (prepared) the shabai (seven) mazabachath (altars), and I have ilah (go up / offer) up a par (bull) and a ayal (ram) on every mazabach (altar)."

Yahawah shawam (place / establish / appoint) a dabar (word / matter) in Balaim (Balaam's) pah (mouth), and amar (spoke), "shawab (turn back / repent) to Balaq (Balak), and thus you shall dabar (word / matter)."
He shawab (turn back / repent) to him, and behold, he was natzab (standing) by his burnt ilah (offering), he, and all the sharay (princes) of Mawaab (Moab).

He nashaa (lift) up his mashal (parable), and amar (spoke), "From Aram (Aram) has Balaq (Balak) nachah (brought) me, the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab) from the hararay (mountains) of the qadam (east). Yalak (come), arar (curse) Yaiqab (Jacob) for me. Yalak (come), zaim (defy) Yashar-Al (Israel).
Mah (how) shall I naqab (curse) whom Al has not qabab (cursed)? How shall I zaim (defy) whom Yahawah has not zaim (defied)?

For from the raash (head) of the tzarayam (rocks) I raah (see) him. From the gabaiwath (hills) I shawar (see) him. Behold, it is a im (nation / people) that shakan (place) badad (alone), and shall not be chashab (reckoned) among the gawayam (nations).

Who can manah (count) the ipar (dust) of Yaiqab (Jacob), or masapar (number) the rabai (fourth) part of Yashar-Al (Israel)? Let me mawath (death) the mawath (death) of the yashar (upright)! Let my acharayath (last) end be like his!"

Balaq (Balak) amar (spoke) to Balaim (Balaam), "What ishah (make) you done to me? I laqach (take / seize) you to qabab (curse) my ayab (enemy), and behold, you have barak (blessed) them barak (blessed)."
He inah (answer / respond) and amar (spoke), "Must I not shamar (keep/guard) heed to dabar (word / matter) that which Yahawah shawam (place / establish / appoint) in my pah (mouth)?"

Balaq (Balak) amar (spoke) to him, "Please yalak (come) with me to achar (other) maqawam (place), where you may raah (see) them; you shall raah (see) but the utmost part of them, and shall not raah (see) them all: and qabab (curse) me them from there."

He laqach (take / seize) him into the shadah (field) of tzapayam (zophim), to the raash (head) of Pasagah (Pisgah), and banah (build) shabai (seven) mazabachath (altars), and ilah (go up / offer) up a par (bull) and a ayal (ram) on every mazabach (altar).
He amar (spoke) to Balaq (Balak), "yatzab (stand) here by your burnt ilah (offering), while I qarah (meet) over there."

Yahawah qarah (met) Balaim (Balaam), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) a dabar (word / matter) in his pah (mouth), and amar (spoke), "shawab (turn back / repent) to Balaq (Balak), and amar (spoke) this."

He bawaa (come) to him, and behold, he was natzab (standing) by his burnt ilah (offering), and the sharay (princes) of Mawaab (Moab) with him. Balaq (Balak) amar (spoke) to him, "What has Yahawah dabar (word / matter)?"
He nashaa (lift) up his mashal (parable), and amar (spoke), "qawam (rise up) up, Balaq (Balak), and shamai (hearken / hear)! Listen to me, you ban (son) of Tzapawar (Zippor).

Al is not a ayash (man / husband), that he should kazab (lie), nor the ban (son) of adam (man), that he should nacham (turn away / repent). Has he amar (spoke), and will he not ishah (make) it? Or has he dabar (word / matter), and will he not make it qawam (rise up)?
Behold, I have laqach (take / seize) a command to barak (blessed). He has barak (blessed), and I can't shawab (turn back / repent) it.

He nabat (has) not seen awan (iniquity) in Yaiqab (Jacob). Neither raah (see) he seen imal (perverseness) in Yashar-Al (Israel). Yahawah his Alahayam is with him. The tharawaih (shout) of a malak (king) is among them.
Al yatzaa (go out / come out) them out of Matzarayam (Egypt). He has as it were the thawaipah (strength) of the wild ox.

Surely there is no nachash (enchantment) with Yaiqab (Jacob); Neither is there any qasam (divination) with Yashar-Al (Israel). Now it shall be amar (spoke) of Yaiqab (Jacob) and of Yashar-Al (Israel), What has Al pail (done)!

Behold, the im (nation / people) qawam (rise up) up as a labayaa (lioness), As a labayaa (lion) he nashaa (lift) himself up. He shall not shakab (lie) down until he akal (eat) of the tarap (prey), and shathah (drinks) the dam (blood) of the chalal (slain)."
Balaq (Balak) amar (spoke) to Balaim (Balaam), "Neither naqab (curse) them at qabab (all), nor barak (blessed) them at qabab (all)."
But Balaim (Balaam) inah (answer / respond) Balaq (Balak), "Didn't I dabar (word / matter) you, amar (spoke), ‘All that Yahawah dabar (word / matter), that I must ishah (make)?'"

Balaq (Balak) amar (spoke) to Balaim (Balaam), "yalak (come) now, I will laqach (take / seize) you to achar (other) maqawam (place); perhaps it will yashar (upright) Alahayam that you may qabab (curse) me them from there."
Balaq (Balak) laqach (take / seize) Balaim (Balaam) to the raash (head) of Paiwar (Peor), that shaqap (looks) down on the yashayamawan (desert).

Balaim (Balaam) amar (spoke) to Balaq (Balak), "banah (build) me here shabai (seven) mazabachath (altars), and kawan (prepare) me here shabai (seven) parayam (bulls) and shabai (seven) ayalayam (rams)."
Balaq (Balak) ishah (make) as Balaim (Balaam) had amar (spoke), and ilah (go up / offer) up a par (bull) and a ayal (ram) on every mazabach (altar).

When Balaim (Balaam) raah (see) that it iyan (eye) Yahawah to barak (blessed) Yashar-Al (Israel), he didn't halak (move), as at the other paim (times), to qaraah (meet) with nachashayam (enchantments), but he shayath (put / appoint / make) his panayam (face) toward the madabar (wilderness).
Balaim (Balaam) nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye), and he raah (see) Yashar-Al (Israel) shakan (place) according to their shabat (tribes); and the rawach (spirit / wind) of Alahayam came on him.
He nashaa (lift) up his mashal (parable), and amar (spoke), "Balaim (Balaam) the ban (son) of Baiwar (Beor) amar (spoke), the gabar (man) whose iyan (eye) was closed naam (declares prophetically);

He naam (declares prophetically), who shamai (hearken / hear) the amaray (words) of Al, who chazah (sees) the machazah (vision) of the Shaday, napal (fall / be cast down) down, and having his iyanayam (eyes) galah (open):
How tawab (good / proper function) are your ahal (tents), Yaiqab (Jacob), and your mashakan (tents), Yashar-Al (Israel)!
As nachalayam (valleys) they are natah (spread) forth, as ganath (gardens) by the riverside, as ahalayam (aloes) which Yahawah has natai (planted), as araz (cedar) trees beside the mayam (Waters).

Mayam (Waters) shall nazal (flow) from his dalay (buckets). His zarai (seed) shall be in many mayam (Waters). His malak (king) shall be higher than Agag (Agag). His malakawath (kingdom) shall be nashaa (lift).

Al yatzaa (go out / come out) him out of Matzarayam (Egypt). He has as it were the thawaipah (strength) of the wild ox. He shall akal (eat) up the gawayam (nations) his tzar (oppressor / distressor), shall garam (break) their itzam (bones) in pieces, and machatz (crush / shatter) them with his chatz (arrows).

He karai (couched), he shakab (lay) down as a aray (lion), as a labayaa (lioness); who shall qawam (rise up) him up? Everyone who blesses you is barak (blessed). Everyone who arar (curses) you is cursed."

Balaq (Balak's) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger) against Balaim (Balaam), and he sapaq (struck) his kap (hands) together; and Balaq (Balak) amar (spoke) to Balaim (Balaam), "I qaraa (called) you to qabab (curse) my ayab (enemy), and, behold, you have barak (blessed) barak (blessed) them these shalawash (three) paimayam (times).
Therefore now barach (flee) you to your maqawam (place)! I amar (spoke) to kabad (promote) you to kabad (great) honor; but, behold, Yahawah has manai (kept) you back from honor."
Balaim (Balaam) amar (spoke) to Balaq (Balak), "Didn't I also dabar (word / matter) your malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) who you shalach (send) to me, amar (spoke),

‘If Balaq (Balak) nathan (give) give me his bayath (house) malaa (full) of kasap (silver) and zahab (gold), I can't ibar (pass over/through) beyond the pah (word) of Yahawah, to ishah (make) either tawab (good / proper function) or rai (bad) of my own lab (heart). I will dabar (word / matter) what Yahawah dabar (word / matter)'?

Now, behold, I halak (move) to my im (nation / people): yalak (come), I will inform you what this im (nation / people) shall ishah (make) to your im (nation / people) in the acharayath (latter) yamayam (days)."
He nashaa (lift) up his mashal (parable), and amar (spoke), "Balaim (Balaam) the ban (son) of Baiwar (Beor) amar (spoke), the gabar (man) whose iyan (eye) was closed naam (declares prophetically);

He naam (declares prophetically), who shamai (hearken / hear) the amaray (words) of Al, yadai (knows) the daith (knowledge) of the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan), and who chazah (sees) the machazah (vision) of the Shaday, napal (fall / be cast down) down, and having his iyanayam (eyes) galah (open):

I raah (see) him, but not now. I raah (see) him, but not qarawab (near). A kawakab (star) will darak (come) out of Yaiqab (Jacob). A scepter will qawam (rise up) out of Yashar-Al (Israel), and shall machatz (crush / shatter) through the paathay (corners) of Mawaab (Moab), and qawar (break) down all the banay (sons) of Shath (Sheth).

Adawam (Edom) shall be a yarashah (possession). Shaiyar (Seir), his ayab (enemy), also shall be a yarashah (possession), while Yashar-Al (Israel) ishah (make) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor).
Out of Yaiqab (Jacob) shall one radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) dominion, and shall abad (destroy / perish) the sharayad (remnant) from the iyar (city)."

He raah (see) at Imalaq (Amalek), and nashaa (lift) up his mashal (parable), and amar (spoke), "Imalaq (Amalek) was the raashayath (beginning) of the gawayam (nations), But his acharayath (latter) id (until / as far as) shall come to destruction."

He raah (see) at the Qayanay (Kenite), and nashaa (lift) up his mashal (parable), and amar (spoke), "Your mawashab (dwelling) place is ayathan (strong). Your qan (nest) is shawam (place / establish / appoint) in the salai (rock).
Nevertheless Qayan (Kain) shall be bair (wasted), until Ashawar (Asshur) shabah (carries) you away captive."
He nashaa (lift) up his mashal (parable), and amar (spoke), "away (alas), who shall chayah (live) when Al shawam (place / establish / appoint) this?

But tzayam (ships) shall come from the yad (hand) of Kathay (Kittim). They shall inah (oppress / afflict) Ashawar (Asshur), and shall inah (oppress / afflict) Ibar (Eber). He also shall come to destruction."
Balaim (Balaam) qawam (rise up) up, and yalak (went) and shawab (turn back / repent) to his maqawam (place); and Balaq (Balak) also halak (move) his darak (way).
Yashar-Al (Israel) stayed in Shatayam (Shittim); and the im (nation / people) chalal (began) to zanah (play) the prostitute with the banawath (daughters) of Mawaab (Moab):
For they qaraa (called) the im (nation / people) to the zabachay (sacrifices) of their Alahayam; and the im (nation / people) akal (eat), and shachah (bowed) down to their Alahayam.
Yashar-Al (Israel) tzamad (joined) himself to Bailapaiwar (Baal) Peor: and the ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah was charah (hot with anger) against Yashar-Al (Israel).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Mashah (Moses), "laqach (take / seize) all the raashay (chiefs) of the im (nation / people), and yaqai (hang) them up to Yahawah before the shamash (sun), that the charawan (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah may shawab (turn back / repent) away from Yashar-Al (Israel)."

Mashah (Moses) amar (spoke) to the shapatay (judges) of Yashar-Al (Israel), "ayash (man / husband) ayash (man / husband) harag (kill) his ayash (man / husband) who have tzamad (joined) themselves to Bailapaiwar (Baal Peor)."
