So Yahawashawai (Joshua) sent the im (nation / people) shalach (send), every ayash (man / husband) to his nachalah (inheritance).

It happened achar (other) these things, that Yahawashawai (Joshua) the ban (son) of Nawan (Nun), the ibad (servant) of Yahawah, mawath (death), being one maah (hundred) and ishar (ten) shanayam (years) ban (son).

They qabar (bury) him in the gabawal (border/boundary) of his nachalah (inheritance) in Thamanathacharas (Timnathserah), which is in the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), on the tzapawan (north) of the har (mountain) of Gaish (Gaash).

Yashar-Al (Israel) ibad (servant) Yahawah all the yamay (days) of Yahawashawai (Joshua), and all the yamay (days) of the zaqanayam (elders) who yawam (day) Yahawashawai (Joshua), and yadai (had) known all the maishah (work) of Yahawah, that he ishah (make) worked for Yashar-Al (Israel).

They qabar (bury) the itzamawath (bones) of Yawasap (Joseph), which the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up out of Matzarayam (Egypt), in Shakam (Shechem), in the chalaqah (parcel) of shadah (ground) which Yaiqab (Jacob) bought of the banay (sons) of Chamawar (Hamor) the ab (father) of Shakam (Shechem) for a maah (hundred) qashayatah (pieces) of money. They became the nachalah (inheritance) of the banay (children) of Yawasap (Joseph).

Alaizar (Eleazar) the ban (son) of Aharawan (Aaron) mawath (death). They qabar (bury) him in the gabaih (hill) of Payanachas (Phinehas) his ban (son), which was nathan (give) him in the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim).

It happened achar (other) the mawath (death) of Yahawashawai (Joshua), the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shaal (asked) of Yahawah, amar (spoke), "Who should ilah (go up / offer) up for us thachalah (first) against the Kanainay (Canaanites), to lacham (fight) against them?"
Yahawah amar (spoke), "Yahawadah (Judah) shall ilah (go up / offer) up. Behold, I nathan (give) delivered the aratz (Earth/land) into his yad (hand)."

Yahawadah (Judah) amar (spoke) to Shamaiwan (Simeon) his ach (brother/kinsman), "ilah (go up / offer) up with me into my gawaral (lot), that we may lacham (fight) against the Kanainay (Canaanites); and I likewise will halak (move) with you into your gawaral (lot)." So Shamaiwan (Simeon) yalak (went) with him.

Yahawadah (Judah) ilah (go up / offer) up; and Yahawah nathan (give) the Kanainay (Canaanites) and the Parazay (Perizzites) into their yad (hand): and they nakah (struck) of them in Bazaq (Bezek) ishar (ten) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband).
They matzaa (found) Adanayabazaq (Adoni-Bezek) in Bazaq (Bezek); and they lacham (fought) against him, and they nakah (struck) the Kanainay (Canaanites) and the Parazay (Perizzites).
But Adanayabazaq (Adoni-Bezek) nawas (fled); and they radap (pursued) achar (other) him, and achaz (caught) him, and qatzatz (cut) off his bahanawath (thumbs) and his ragal (feet / foot) toes.

Adanayabazaq (Adoni-Bezek) amar (spoke), "shabaiyam (seventy) malakayam (kings), having their bahanawath (thumbs) and their ragal (feet / foot) toes qatzatz (cut) off, scavenged under my shalachan (table): as I ishah (make) done, so Alahayam has shalam (requited) me." They bawaa (come) him to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and he mawath (death) there.

The banay (children) of Yahawadah (Judah) lacham (fought) against Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and lakad (took) it, and nakah (struck) it with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), and shalach (send) the iyar (city) on ash (fire).

Afterward the banay (children) of Yahawadah (Judah) yarad (went) down to lacham (fight) against the Kanainay (Canaanites) who lived in the har (mountain) nagab (country), and in the South, and in the lowland.

Yahawadah (Judah) yalak (went) against the Kanainay (Canaanites) who lived in Chabarawan (Hebron) (now the sham (name) of Chabarawan (Hebron) panayam (face) was Kiriath Qarayathaarabai (Arba)); and they nakah (struck) Shashay (Sheshai), and Achayaman (Ahiman), and Thalamay (Talmai).
From there he yalak (went) against the yawashabay (inhabitants) of Dabayar (Debir). (Now the sham (name) of Dabayar (Debir) panayam (face) was Kiriath Qarayathasanah (Sepher).)
Kalab (Caleb) amar (spoke), "He who nakah (strikes) Kiriath Qarayathasanah (Sepher), and lakad (takes) it, to him will I nathan (give) Ikasah (Achsah) my banath (daughter) as ayashah (woman / wife)."

Ithanayaal (Othniel) the ban (son) of Qanaz (Kenaz), Kalab (Caleb's) younger ach (brother/kinsman), lakad (took) it: and he nathan (give) him Ikasah (Achsah) his banath (daughter) as ayashah (woman / wife).

It happened, when she bawaa (come), that she got him to shaal (ask) her ab (father) for a shadah (field): and she alighted from off her donkey; and Kalab (Caleb) amar (spoke) to her, "What would you like?"

She amar (spoke) to him, "yahab (give) me a barakah (blessing); for that you nathan (give) set me in the aratz (Earth/land) of the nagab (south), nathan (give) me also galath (springs) of mayam (Waters)." Then Kalab (Caleb) nathan (give) her the ilay (went up) galath (springs) and the lower galath (springs).

The banay (children) of the Qayanay (Kenite), Mashah (Moses)' brother-in-law, ilah (go up / offer) up out of the iyar (city) of thamar (palm) trees with the banay (children) of Yahawadah (Judah) into the madabar (wilderness) of Yahawadah (Judah), which is in the nagab (south) of Irad (Arad); and they yalak (went) and lived with the im (nation / people).

Yahawadah (Judah) yalak (went) with Shamaiwan (Simeon) his ach (brother/kinsman), and they nakah (struck) the Kanainay (Canaanites) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) Tzapath (Zephath), and charam (utterly) destroyed it. The sham (name) of the iyar (city) was qaraa (called) Charamah (Hormah).

Also Yahawadah (Judah) lakad (took) Izah (Gaza) with its gabawal (border/boundary), and Ashaqalawan (Ashkelon) with its gabawal (border/boundary), and Iqarawan (Ekron) with its gabawal (border/boundary).

Yahawah was with Yahawadah (Judah); and yarash (drove) out the inhabitants of the har (mountain) country; for he could not yarash (drive) out the yashabay (inhabitants) of the imaq (valley), because they had rakab (chariots) of barazal (iron).
They nathan (give) Chabarawan (Hebron) to Kalab (Caleb), as Mashah (Moses) had dabar (word / matter): and he yarash (drove) out there the shalawash (three) banay (sons) of Inaq (Anak).

The banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) did not yarash (drive) out the Yabawasay (Jebusites) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); but the Yabawasay (Jebusites) yashab (inhabit/dwell) with the banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) to this yawam (day).
The bayath (house) of Yawasap (Joseph), they also ilah (go up / offer) up against Bayath-Al (Bethel); and Yahawah was with them.
The bayath (house) of Yawasap (Joseph) thawar (sent) to spy out Bayath-Al (Bethel). (Now the sham (name) of the iyar (city) panayam (face) was Lawaz (Luz).)

The watchers raah (see) a ayash (man / husband) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the iyar (city), and they amar (spoke) to him, "Please show us the mabawaa (entrance) into the iyar (city), and we will ishah (make) chasad (grace) with you."

He showed them the mabawaa (entrance) into the iyar (city); and they nakah (struck) the iyar (city) with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword); but they let the ayash (man / husband) shalach (send) and all his mashapachah (tribe / clan / family).

The ayash (man / husband) yalak (went) into the aratz (Earth/land) of the Chathay (Hittites), and banah (build) a iyar (city), and qaraa (called) its sham (name) Lawaz (Luz), which is its sham (name) to this yawam (day).

Manashah (Manasseh) did not yarash (drive) out the inhabitants of Bayath-Shaan (Beth Shean) and its banath (daughter), nor Thainak (Taanach) and its banath (daughter), nor the yawashabay (inhabitants) of Dawar (Dor) and its banath (daughter), nor the yawashabay (inhabitants) of Yabalaim (Ibleam) and its banath (daughter), nor the yawashabay (inhabitants) of Magadawan (Megiddo) and its banath (daughter); but the Kanainay (Canaanites) yaal (would) yashab (inhabit/dwell) in that aratz (Earth/land).

It happened, when Yashar-Al (Israel) had grown chazaq (strong), that they shawam (place / establish / appoint) the Kanainay (Canaanites) to forced mas (labor), and did not yarash (utterly) yarash (drive) them out.
Aparayam (Ephraim) didn't yarash (drive) out the Kanainay (Canaanites) who lived in Gazar (Gezer); but the Kanainay (Canaanites) lived in Gazar (Gezer) qarab (among / near) them.

Zabawalawan (Zebulun) didn't yarash (drive) out the yawashabay (inhabitants) of Qatarawan (Kitron), nor the yawashabay (inhabitants) of Nahalal (Nahalol); but the Kanainay (Canaanites) lived qarab (among / near) them, and became subject to forced mas (labor).

Ashar (Asher) didn't yarash (drive) out the yashabay (inhabitants) of Ikaw (Acco), nor the yashabay (inhabitants) of Tzayadawan (Sidon), nor of Achalab (Ahlab), nor of Akazayab (Achzib), nor of Chalabah (Helbah), nor of Apaq (Aphik), nor of Rachab (Rehob);
But the Asharay (Asherites) lived qarab (among / near) the Kanainay (Canaanites), the yashabay (inhabitants) of the aratz (Earth/land); for they did not yarash (drive) them out.

Napathalay (Naphtali) didn't yarash (drive) out the yashabay (inhabitants) of Bayath-Shamash (Beth Shemesh), nor the yashabay (inhabitants) of Bayathainath (Beth Anath); but he lived qarab (among / near) the Kanainay (Canaanites), the yashabay (inhabitants) of the aratz (Earth/land): nevertheless the yashabay (inhabitants) of Bayath-Shamash (Beth Shemesh) and of Bayathainath (Beth Anath) became subject to forced mas (labor).
The Amaray (Amorites) lachatz (forced) the banay (children) of Dan (Dan) into the har (mountain) country; for they nathan (give) not allow them to yarad (come) down to the imaq (valley);

But the Amaray (Amorites) yaal (would) yashab (inhabit/dwell) in har (mountain) Charas (Heres), in Ayalawan (Aijalon), and in Shailabayam (Shaalbim): yet the yad (hand) of the bayath (house) of Yawasap (Joseph) kabad (prevailed), so that they became subject to forced mas (labor).
The gabawal (border/boundary) of the Amaray (Amorites) was from the mailahaiqarabayam (ascent) of mailahaiqarabayam (akrabbim), from the salai (rock), and upward.

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah ilah (go up / offer) up from Galagal (Gilgal) to Bakayam (Bochim). He amar (spoke), "I ilah (go up / offer) you to go up out of Matzarayam (Egypt), and bawaa (come) brought you to the aratz (Earth/land) which I shabai (swear / take oath) to your ab (father); and I amar (spoke), ‘I will iwalam (forever) parar (break) my barayath (covenant) with you:

And you shall karath (cut) no barayath (covenant) with the yawashabay (inhabitants) of this aratz (Earth/land); you shall nathatz (break) down their mazabach (altars).' But you have not shamai (hearken / hear) to my qawal (sound / voice): why ishah (make) you done this?
Therefore I also amar (spoke), I will not garash (drive) them out from panayam (face) you; but they shall be in your tzadayam (sides), and their Alahayam shall be a mawaqash (snare) to you."

It happened, when the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah dabar (word / matter) these dabarayam (words) to all the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), that the im (nation / people) nashaa (lift) up their qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept).
They qaraa (called) the sham (name) of that maqawam (place) Bakayam (Bochim): and they zabach (sacrificed) there to Yahawah.

Now when Yahawashawai (Joshua) had sent the im (nation / people) shalach (send), the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) yalak (went) every ayash (man / husband) to his nachalah (inheritance) to yarash (possess) the aratz (Earth/land).

The im (nation / people) ibad (servant) Yahawah all the yamay (days) of Yahawashawai (Joshua), and all the yamay (days) of the zaqanayam (elders) who yawam (day) Yahawashawai (Joshua), who raah (see) seen all the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) maishah (work) of Yahawah that he ishah (make) worked for Yashar-Al (Israel).
Yahawashawai (Joshua) the ban (son) of Nawan (Nun), the ibad (servant) of Yahawah, mawath (death), being one maah (hundred) ishar (ten) shanayam (years) ban (son).
They qabar (bury) him in the gabawal (border/boundary) of his nachalah (inheritance) in Timnath Heres, in the hill country of Aparayam (Ephraim), on the north of the har (mountain) of Gaish (Gaash).

Also all that dawar (generation / age / period) were asap (gathered) to their ab (father): and there qawam (rise up) achar (other) dawar (generation / age / period) achar (other) them, who didn't yadai (know) Yahawah, nor yet the maishah (work) which he ishah (make) worked for Yashar-Al (Israel).
The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, and ibad (servant) the Bail (Baals);

And they forsook Yahawah, the Alahayam of their ab (father), who yatzaa (go out / come out) them out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and yalak (followed) other Alahayam, of the Alahayam of the imayam (peoples) who were around them, and shachah (bowed) themselves down to them: and they provoked Yahawah to kais (anger).
They forsook Yahawah, and ibad (servant) Bail (Baal) and the Ishatharawath (Ashtaroth).

The ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah was charah (hot with anger) against Yashar-Al (Israel), and he nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of shasayam (spoilers) who despoiled them; and he makar (sold) them into the yad (hand) of their ayab (enemy) all around, so that they yakal (could) not any iwad (more/again) imad (stand) panayam (face) their ayab (enemy).

Wherever they yatzaa (go out / come out) out, the yad (hand) of Yahawah was against them for rai (evil), as Yahawah had dabar (word / matter), and as Yahawah had shabai (swear / take oath) to them: and they were very yatzar (distressed).
Yahawah qawam (rise up) up shapatayam (judges), who yashai (salvation) them out of the yad (hand) of those who despoiled them.

Yet they didn't shamai (hearken / hear) to their shapat (judge / judgement); for they zanah (played) the prostitute achar (other) other Alahayam, and shachah (bowed) themselves down to them: they sawar (turned) aside mahar (quickly) out of the darak (way) in which their ab (father) halak (move), shamai (hearken / hear) the matzawath (commandments) of Yahawah. They didn't ishah (make) so.

When Yahawah qawam (rise up) them up shapatayam (judges), then Yahawah was with the shapat (judge / judgement), and yashai (salvation) them out of the yad (hand) of their ayab (enemy) all the yamay (days) of the shapat (judge / judgement): for it grieved Yahawah panayam (face) of their naaqah (groaning) by reason of those who lachatz (oppressed) them and troubled them.

But it happened, when the shapat (judge / judgement) was mawath (death), that they shawab (turn back / repent) back, and dealt more corruptly than their ab (father), in yalak (following) other Alahayam to ibad (servant) them, and to shachah (bow) down to them; they didn't napal (fall / be cast down) from their mailal (doings), nor from their qashah (rough / hard) darak (way).

The ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah was charah (hot with anger) against Yashar-Al (Israel); and he amar (spoke), "Because this gaway (heathen / nation) ibar (pass over/through) transgressed my barayath (covenant) which I tzawah (commanded) their ab (father), and have not shamai (hearken / hear) to my qawal (sound / voice);
I also will not yasap (henceforth) yarash (drive) out any from panayam (face) them of the gawayam (nations) that Yahawashawai (Joshua) izab (left) when he mawath (death);
That by them I may nasah (prove) Yashar-Al (Israel), whether they will shamar (keep/guard) the darak (way) of Yahawah to yalak (walk) therein, as their ab (father) shamar (keep/guard) it, or not."
So Yahawah yanach (left) those gawayam (nations), balathay (without) yarash (driving) them out mahar (hastily); neither nathan (give) he them into the yad (hand) of Yahawashawai (Joshua).
Now these are the gawayam (nations) which Yahawah yanach (left), to nasah (prove) Yashar-Al (Israel) by them, even as many as yadai (had) not known all the malachamawath (wars) of Kanain (Canaan);

Only that the darawath (generations) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) might yadai (know), to lamad (teach / instruct) them malachamah (war), at the least such as panayam (face) yadai (knew) nothing of it:

The chamash (five) saranay (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and all the Kanainay (Canaanites), and the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), and the Chaway (Hivites) who lived on har (mountain) Labanawan (Lebanon), from har (mountain) Bailacharamawan (Baal Hermon) to the entrance of Chamath (Hamath).

They were left to test Yashar-Al (Israel) by them, to yadai (know) whether they would shamai (hearken / hear) to the matzawath (commandments) of Yahawah, which he tzawah (commanded) their ab (father) by Mashah (Moses).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) lived qarab (among / near) the Kanainay (Canaanites), the Chathay (Hittites), and the Amaray (Amorites), and the Parazay (Perizzites), and the Chaway (Hivites), and the Yabawasay (Jebusites):
And they laqach (take / seize) their banath (daughter) to be their wives, and nathan (give) their own banath (daughter) to their ban (son) and ibad (servant) their Alahayam.

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, and shakach (forgot) Yahawah their Alahayam, and ibad (servant) the Bail (Baals) and the Asharah (Asheroth).

Therefore the ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah was charah (hot with anger) against Yashar-Al (Israel), and he makar (sold) them into the yad (hand) of Kawashanarashaithayam (Cushan Rishathaim) malak (king) of Aramanaharayam (Mesopotamia): and the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ibad (servant) Kawashanarashaithayam (Cushan Rishathaim) shamanah (eight) shanayam (years).

When the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) zaiq (cried) to Yahawah, Yahawah qawam (rise up) up a savior to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), who yashai (salvation) them, even Ithanayaal (Othniel) the ban (son) of Qanaz (Kenaz), Kalab (Caleb's) younger ach (brother/kinsman).

The rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah came on him, and he shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel); and he yatzaa (go out / come out) out to malachamah (war), and Yahawah nathan (give) Kawashanarashaithayam (Cushan Rishathaim) malak (king) of Aram (Mesopotamia) into his yad (hand): and his yad (hand) izaz (prevailed) against Kawashanarashaithayam (Cushan Rishathaim).
The aratz (Earth/land) had shaqat (rest) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years). Ithanayaal (Othniel) the ban (son) of Qanaz (Kenaz) mawath (death).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) again ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah: and Yahawah chazaq (strengthened) Igalawan (Eglon) the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab) against Yashar-Al (Israel), because they ishah (make) done that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah.

He asap (gathered) to him the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) and Imalaq (Amalek); and he yalak (went) and nakah (struck) Yashar-Al (Israel), and they yarash (possessed) the iyar (city) of thamar (palm) trees.
The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ibad (servant) Igalawan (Eglon) the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab) eighteen shanah (years).

But when the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) zaiq (cried) to Yahawah, Yahawah qawam (rise up) them up a savior, Ahawad (Ehud) the ban (son) of Garaa (Gera), the Banayamayanay (Benjamite), a ayash (man / husband) atar (left-handed). The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shalach (send) tribute by him to Igalawan (Eglon) the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab).

Ahawad (Ehud) ishah (make) him a charab (sword) which had shanayam (two) payawath (edges), a gamad (cubit) in arak (length); and he wore it under his clothing on his yamayan (right hand) yarak (thigh).
He qarab (come close) the tribute to Igalawan (Eglon) malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab): now Igalawan (Eglon) was a very barayaa (fat) ayash (man / husband).
When he kalah (complete / finish) made an end of qarab (come close) the tribute, he shalach (send) away the im (nation / people) who nashaa (lift) the tribute.

But he himself shawab (turn back / repent) back from the pasayalayam (quarries) that were by Galagal (Gilgal), and amar (spoke), "I have a sathar (secret / hidden) dabar (word / matter) to you, malak (king)." The king amar (spoke), "Keep hasah (silence)!" All who imad (stood) by him yatzaa (go out / come out) out from him.

Ahawad (Ehud) bawaa (come) to him; and he was sitting by himself maqarah (alone) in the cool upper room. Ahawad (Ehud) amar (spoke), "I have a dabar (word / matter) from Alahayam to you." He qawam (rise up) out of his kasaa (seat).

Ahawad (Ehud) shalach (send) forth his shamaawal (left hand) yad (hand), and laqach (take / seize) the charab (sword) from his yamayan (right hand) yarak (thigh), and thaqai (blow / sound alarm) it into his batan (body):

And the handle also bawaa (come) in achar (other) the lahab (blade); and the chalab (fat) sagar (closed) on the lahab (blade), for he didn't shalap (draw) the charab (sword) out of his batan (body); and it yatzaa (go out / come out) out behind.
Then Ahawad (Ehud) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth into the masadarawan (porch), and sagar (shut) the dalathawath (doors) of the upper room on him, and nail (locked) them.

Now when he was yatzaa (go out / come out) out, his ibad (servant) bawaa (come); and they raah (see), and behold, the dalathawath (doors) of the upper room were nail (locked); and they amar (spoke), "Surely he is sakak (covering) his ragal (feet / foot) in the upper room."

They chawal (waited) until they were bawash (ashamed); and behold, he didn't pathach (open) the dalathawath (doors) of the upper room: therefore they laqach (take / seize) the mapathach (key), and pathach (opened) them, and behold, their Adawan was napal (fall / be cast down) down mawath (death) on the aratz (Earth/land).
Ahawad (Ehud) malat (escaped) while they waited, and ibar (pass over/through) beyond the pasayalayam (quarries), and malat (escaped) to Shaiyarah (Seirah).

It happened, when he bawaa (come) come, that he thaqai (blow / sound alarm) a shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn) in the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim); and the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) yarad (went) down with him from the har (mountain) country, and he panayam (face) them.

He amar (spoke) to them, "radap (follow) me; for Yahawah nathan (give) delivered your ayab (enemy) the Mawaab (Moabites) into your yad (hand)." They followed him, and lakad (took) the maibarawath (fords) of the Yaradan (Jordan) against the Mawaab (Moabites), and didn't allow any ayash (man / husband) to ibar (pass over/through) over.

They nakah (struck) of Mawaab (Moab) at that ith (time) about ishar (ten) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband), every shaman (lusty) ayash (man / husband), and every man of valor; and there malat (escaped) not a ayash (man / husband).
So Mawaab (Moab) was kanai (subdued) that yawam (day) under the yad (hand) of Yashar-Al (Israel). The aratz (Earth/land) had shaqat (rest) shamanayam (eighty) shanah (years).

Achar (other) him was Shamagar (Shamgar) the ban (son) of Inath (Anath), who nakah (struck) of the Palashathay (Philistines) shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) with an baqar (morning) - malamad (goad): and he also yashai (salvation) Yashar-Al (Israel).
The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) again ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, when Ahawad (Ehud) was mawath (death).

Yahawah makar (sold) them into the yad (hand) of Yabayan (Jabin) malak (king) of Kanain (Canaan), who malak (king) in Chatzawar (Hazor); the shar (prince / ruler) of whose tzabaa (troop) was Sayasaraa (Sisera), who lived in Charashath (Harosheth) of the gaway (heathen / nation).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) tzaiq (cried) to Yahawah: for he had thashai (nine) maah (hundred) rakab (chariots) of barazal (iron); and isharayam (twenty) shanah (years) he chazaqah (mightily) lachatz (oppressed) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).
Now Dabawarah (Deborah), a nabayaah (prophetess), the ayashah (woman / wife) of Lapayadawath (Lappidoth), she shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel) at that ith (time).

She lived under the thamar (palm) tree of Dabawarah (Deborah) between Ramah (Ramah) and Bayath-Al (Bethel) in the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim): and the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up to her for mashapat (judgment).

She shalach (send) and qaraa (called) Baraq (Barak) the ban (son) of Abayanaim (Abinoam) out of Qadash (Kedesh Naphtali), and amar (spoke) to him, "Hasn't Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), tzawah (commanded), ‘yalak (go) and mashak (draw) to har (mountain) Thabawar (Tabor), and laqach (take / seize) with you ishar (ten) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband) of the banay (children) of Napathalay (Naphtali) and of the banay (children) of Zabawalawan (Zebulun)?

I will mashak (draw) to you, to the nachal (stream / river) Qayashawan (Kishon), Sayasaraa (Sisera), the shar (prince / ruler) of Yabayan (Jabin's) tzabaa (troop), with his rakab (chariots) and his hamawan (multitude); and I will nathan (give) him into your yad (hand).'"
Baraq (Barak) amar (spoke) to her, "If you will yalak (go) with me, then I will yalak (go); but if you will not halak (move) with me, I will not yalak (go)."

She amar (spoke), "I will halak (move) yalak (go) with you: apas (nevertheless), the darak (journey) that you take shall not be for your honor; for Yahawah will makar (sell) Sayasaraa (Sisera) into the yad (hand) of a ayashah (woman / wife)." Dabawarah (Deborah) qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) with Baraq (Barak) to Qadash (Kedesh).

Baraq (Barak) zaiq (called) Zabawalawan (Zebulun) and Napathalay (Naphtali) together to Qadash (Kedesh); and there ilah (go up / offer) up ishar (ten) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband) at his ragal (feet / foot): and Dabawarah (Deborah) ilah (go up / offer) up with him.

Now Chabar (Heber) the Qayanay (Kenite) had parad (separated) himself from the Qayanay (Kenites), even from the banay (children) of Chabab (Hobab) the brother-in-law of Mashah (Moses), and had natah (pitched) his ahal (tent) as far as the oak in Tzainanayam (Zaanannim), which is by Qadash (Kedesh).
They nagad (told) Sayasaraa (Sisera) that Baraq (Barak) the ban (son) of Abayanaim (Abinoam) was ilah (go up / offer) up to har (mountain) Thabawar (Tabor).

Sayasaraa (Sisera) zaiq (gathered) together all his rakab (chariots), even thashai (nine) maah (hundred) rakab (chariots) of barazal (iron), and all the im (nation / people) who were with him, from Charashath (Harosheth) of the gaway (heathen / nation), to the nachal (stream / river) Qayashawan (Kishon).

Dabawarah (Deborah) amar (spoke) to Baraq (Barak), "Go; for this is the yawam (day) in which Yahawah nathan (give) delivered Sayasaraa (Sisera) into your yad (hand). Hasn't Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) out panayam (face) you?" So Baraq (Barak) yarad (went) down from har (mountain) Thabawar (Tabor), and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband) achar (other) him.

Yahawah confused Sayasaraa (Sisera), and all his rakab (chariots), and all his machanah (army), with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword) panayam (face) Baraq (Barak); and Sayasaraa (Sisera) alighted from his marakabah (chariot), and nawas (fled) away on his ragal (feet / foot).

But Baraq (Barak) radap (pursued) achar (other) the rakab (chariots), and after the machanah (army), to Charashath (Harosheth) of the gaway (heathen / nation): and all the machanah (army) of Sayasaraa (Sisera) napal (fall / be cast down) by the pah (edge) of the charab (sword); there was not a achad (one) shaar (left).

However Sayasaraa (Sisera) nawas (fled) away on his ragal (feet / foot) to the ahal (tent) of Yail (Jael) the ayashah (woman / wife) of Chabar (Heber) the Qayanay (Kenite); for there was shalawam (peace / safety) between Yabayan (Jabin) the malak (king) of Chatzawar (Hazor) and the bayath (house) of Chabar (Heber) the Qayanay (Kenite).

Yail (Jael) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) Sayasaraa (Sisera), and amar (spoke) to him, "sawar (turn) in, my Adawan, sawar (turn) in to me; don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid)." He came in to her into the ahal (tent), and she kasah (covered) him with a rug.

He amar (spoke) to her, "Please give me a mait (little) mayam (Waters) to shaqah (drink); for I am tzamaa (thirsty)." She pathach (opened) a naad (bottle) of chalab (milk), and shaqah (gave) him drink, and kasah (covered) him.

He amar (spoke) to her, "imad (stand) in the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent), and it shall be, when any ayash (man / husband) bawaa (come) and inquires of you, and amar (spoke), ‘Is there any ayash (man / husband) here?' That you shall amar (spoke), ‘No.'"

Then Yail (Jael) Chabar (Heber's) ayashah (woman / wife) laqach (take / seize) a ahal (tent) peg, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) a maqabath (hammer) in her yad (hand), and bawaa (come) laat (softly) to him, and thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the peg into his raqah (temples), and it pierced through into the aratz (Earth/land); for he was in a radam (deep) sleep; so he swooned and mawath (death).

Behold, as Baraq (Barak) radap (pursued) Sayasaraa (Sisera), Yail (Jael) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) him, and amar (spoke) to him, "yalak (come), and I will show you the ayash (man / husband) whom you baqash (seek)." He bawaa (come) to her; and behold, Sayasaraa (Sisera) napal (fall / be cast down) mawath (death), and the yathad (tent) peg was in his raqah (temples).
So Alahayam kanai (subdued) on that yawam (day) Yabayan (Jabin) the malak (king) of Kanain (Canaan) panayam (face) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

The yad (hand) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) qashah (rough / hard) more and more against Yabayan (Jabin) the malak (king) of Kanain (Canaan), until they had karath (cut) Yabayan (Jabin) malak (king) of Kanain (Canaan).
Then Dabawarah (Deborah) and Baraq (Barak) the ban (son) of Abayanaim (Abinoam) shayar (sang) on that yawam (day), amar (spoke),
"Because the leaders took the lead in Yashar-Al (Israel), because the im (nation / people) nadab (offered) themselves willingly, be barak (blessed), Yahawah!

"Shamai (hearken / hear), you malakayam (kings)! Azan (ear) ear, you razanayam (princes)! I, even I, will shayar (sing) to Yahawah. I will zamar (sing) praise to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel).

"Yahawah, when you yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of Shaiyar (Seir), when you tzaid (marched) out of the shadah (field) of Adawam (Edom), the aratz (Earth/land) raish (trembled), the sky also natap (dropped). Yes, the ibayam (clouds) natap (dropped) mayam (Waters).
The harayam (mountains) quaked at the panayam (face) of Yahawah, even Sayanay (Sinai), at the panayam (face) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel).

"In the yamay (days) of Shamagar (Shamgar) the ban (son) of Inath (Anath), in the yamay (days) of Yail (Jael), the highways were chadal (unoccupied). The halakay (travelers) yalak (walked) through iqalaqalawath (byways).
The parazawan (rulers) chadal (ceased) in Yashar-Al (Israel). They chadal (ceased) until I, Dabawarah (Deborah), qawam (rise up); Until I qawam (rise up) a am (mother) in Yashar-Al (Israel).

They bachar (chose) chadash (new) Alahayam. Then lacham (war) was in the shairayam (gates). Was there a magan (shield) or ramach (spear) raah (see) among arabaiyam (forty) alap (thousand) in Yashar-Al (Israel)?
My lab (heart) is toward the chawaqaqay (governors) of Yashar-Al (Israel), who nadab (offered) themselves willingly among the im (nation / people). Barak (blessed) Yahawah!
"Shayach (meditate), you who rakab (ride) on tzachar (bright / glisten) donkeys, you who yashab (inhabit/dwell) on rich carpets, and you who halak (move) by the darak (way).

Far from the qawal (sound / voice) of machatzatzayam (archers), in the places of drawing mashaab (water), there they will thanah (rehearse) the tzadaqah (righteousness) acts of Yahawah, the tzadaqah (righteousness) acts of his rule in Yashar-Al (Israel). "Then the im (nation / people) of Yahawah yarad (went) down to the shairayam (gates).

‘Iwar (rouse / awaken), iwar (rouse / awaken), Dabawarah (Deborah)! Iwar (rouse / awaken), iwar (rouse / awaken), dabar (word / matter) a shayar (song)! Qawam (rise up), Baraq (Barak), and lead shabay (away) your shabah (captives), you ban (son) of Abayanaim (Abinoam).'
"Then a sharayad (remnant) of the adayarayam (nobles) and the im (nation / people) came down. Yahawah radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) down for me against the gabawar (mighty).

Those whose sharash (root) is in Imalaq (Amalek) came out of Aparayam (Ephraim), achar (other) you, Banayamayan (Benjamin), among your im (nation / people). Machaqaqayam (governors) yarad (come) down out of Makayar (Machir). Those who mashak (handle) the marshal's shabat (staff) came out of Zabawalawan (Zebulun).

The shar (prince / ruler) of Yashashakar (Issachar) were with Dabawarah (Deborah). As was Yashashakar (Issachar), so was Baraq (Barak). They rushed into the imaq (valley) at his ragal (feet / foot). By the watercourses of Raawaban (Reuben), there were gadawal (very great/important/mighty) resolves of lab (heart).

Why did you yashab (inhabit/dwell) bayan (between) the mashapathayam (sheepfolds), To shamai (hearken / hear) the whistling for the idarayam (flocks)? At the watercourses of Raawaban (Reuben) There were gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chaqaray (searchings) of lab (heart).

Galaid (Gilead) lived ibar (beyond) the Yaradan (Jordan). Dan (Why) did Dan gawar (remain) in anayawath (ships)? Ashar (Asher) yashab (inhabit/dwell) still at the chawap (haven) of the yam (sea/waters), and lived by his creeks.
Zabawalawan (Zebulun) was a im (nation / people) that jeopardized their lives to the mawath (death); Napathalay (Naphtali) also, on the marawam (high) places of the shadah (field).

"The malakayam (kings) bawaa (come) and lacham (fought), then the malakayam (kings) of Kanain (Canaan) lacham (fought) at Thainak (Taanach) by the may (waters) of Magadawan (Megiddo). They laqach (take / seize) no plunder of kasap (silver).
From the sky the kawakabayam (stars) lacham (fought). From their masalah (courses), they lacham (fought) against Sayasaraa (Sisera).

The nachal (stream / river) Qayashawan (Kishon) garap (swept) them away, that qadawam (ancient) nachal (stream / river), the nachal (stream / river) Qayashawan (Kishon). My napash (soul), march on with iz (strength / might / refuge).
Then the horse iqabay (hoofs) stamped because of the prancings, the prancings of their abayar (strong) ones.

‘Arar (curse) Marawaz (Meroz),' amar (spoke) the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah. ‘Arar (curse) arar (bitterly) its yashab (inhabit/dwell), because they didn't bawaa (come) to izarah (help) Yahawah, to izarah (help) Yahawah against the gabawar (mighty).'

"Yail (Jael) shall be barak (blessed) above nashayam (women), the ayashah (woman / wife) of Chabar (Heber) the Qayanay (Kenite); barak (blessed) shall she be above nashayam (women) in the ahal (tent).
He shaal (asked) for mayam (Waters). She nathan (give) him chalab (milk). She qarab (come close) him chamaah (butter) in a adayar (lordly) sapal (dish).

She shalach (send) her yad (hand) to the yathad (tent) peg, and her right yamayan (right hand) to the workmen's halamawath (hammer). With the hammer she struck Sayasaraa (Sisera). She struck through his raash (head). Yes, she machatz (crush / shatter) and chalap (struck) through his raqah (temples).

At her ragal (feet / foot) he karai (bowed), he napal (fall / be cast down), he shakab (lay). At her ragal (feet / foot) he karai (bowed), he napal (fall / be cast down). Ashar (who/that) he karai (bowed), there he napal (fall / be cast down) down shadad (dead).

"Through the chalawan (window) she shaqap (looked) out, and yabab (cried): Sayasaraa (Sisera's) am (mother) looked through the ashanab (lattice). ‘Why is his rakab (chariot) so bawash (long) in bawaa (come)? Why do the paimay (wheels) of his marakabah (chariots) wait?'
Her chakam (wise) sharah (ladies) inah (answer / respond) her, Yes, she shawab (turn back / repent) amar (spoke) to herself,

‘Matzaa (have) they not found, chalaq (have) they not divided the shalal (spoil)? A lady, rachamah (two) ladies to raash (head) gabar (man); to Sayasaraa (Sisera) a shalal (spoil) of dyed garments, a shalal (spoil) of dyed garments embroidered, of dyed garments embroidered on both sides, on the tzawaaray (necks) of the shalal (spoil)?'

"So let all your ayab (enemy) abad (destroy / perish), Yahawah, but let those who ahab (love) him be as the shamash (sun) when it yatzaa (go out / come out) forth in its gabawarah (strength)." Then the aratz (Earth/land) had shaqat (rest) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah: and Yahawah nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of Madayan (Midian) shabai (seven) shanayam (years).

The yad (hand) of Madayan (Midian) izaz (prevailed) against Yashar-Al (Israel); and panayam (face) of Madayan (Midian) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ishah (make) them the manaharawath (dens) which are in the harayam (mountains), and the mairawath (caves), and the strongholds.

So it was, when Yashar-Al (Israel) had zarai (sown), that the Madayan (Midianites) ilah (go up / offer) up, and the Imalaq (Amalekites), and the banay (children) of the qadam (east); they ilah (go up / offer) up against them;

And they chanah (encamped) against them, and shachath (destroyed) the yabawal (increase) of the aratz (Earth/land), until you bawaa (come) to Izah (Gaza), and shaar (left) no machayah (sustenance) in Yashar-Al (Israel), neither shah (sheep), nor shawar (ox), nor donkey.

For they ilah (go up / offer) up with their livestock and their ahal (tents); they bawaa (come) in as arabah (locusts) for rab (multitude); both they and their gamal (camels) were without masapar (number): and they bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land) to shachath (destroy) it.
Yashar-Al (Israel) was brought very dalal (low) panayam (face) of Madayan (Midian); and the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) zaiq (cried) to Yahawah.
It happened, when the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) zaiq (cried) to Yahawah awadawath (because) of Madayan (Midian),

That Yahawah shalach (send) a ayash (man / husband) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel): and he amar (spoke) to them, "Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), ‘I ilah (go up / offer) you up from Matzarayam (Egypt), and yatzaa (go out / come out) you forth out of the bayath (house) of ibad (servant);

And I natzal (delivered) you out of the yad (hand) of the Matzaray (Egyptians), and out of the yad (hand) of all who lachatz (oppressed) you, and garash (drove) them out from panayam (face) you, and nathan (give) you their aratz (Earth/land);

And I amar (spoke) to you, "I am Yahawah your Alahayam; you shall not yaraa (fear / be afraid) the Alahayam of the Amaray (Amorites), in whose aratz (Earth/land) you yashab (inhabit/dwell)." But you have not shamai (hearken / hear) to my qawal (sound / voice).'"

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah bawaa (come), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) under the alah (oak / terebinth) which was in Iparah (Ophrah), that pertained to Yawaash (Joash) the abayahaizaray (abiezrite): and his ban (son) Gadaiwan (Gideon) was chabat (beating) out chatah (wheat) in the gath (winepress), to nawas (hide) it from the Madayan (Midianites).
The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah raah (see) to him, and amar (spoke) to him, "Yahawah is with you, you gabawar (mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) of valor!"

Gadaiwan (Gideon) amar (spoke) to him, "Oh, my Adawan, if Yahawah is with us, why then matzaa (has) all this happened to us? Where are all his wondrous palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) which our ab (father) sapar (book) us of, amar (spoke), ‘Didn't Yahawah ilah (go up / offer) us up from Matzarayam (Egypt)?' But now Yahawah has natash (cast) us off, and nathan (give) us into the kap (hand) of Madayan (Midian)."

Yahawah panah (turn) at him, and amar (spoke), "yalak (go) in this your kach (strength / mighty / power), and yashai (salvation) Yashar-Al (Israel) from the kap (hand) of Madayan (Midian). Haven't I shalach (send) you?"

He amar (spoke) to him, "O Adanay, mah (how) shall I yashai (salvation) Yashar-Al (Israel)? Behold, my alap (family) is the poorest in Manashah (Manasseh), and I am the tzaiyar (least) in my ab (father) bayath (house)."
Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, "nakah (surely) I will be with you, and you shall strike the Madayan (Midianites) as achad (one) ayash (man / husband)."
He amar (spoke) to him, "If now I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye), then show me a awath (sign / mark / miracle) that it is you who dabar (word / matter) with me.

Please don't mawash (go) away, until I bawaa (come) to you, and yatzaa (go out / come out) out my manachah (present), and yanach (lay) it panayam (face) you." He amar (spoke), "I will wait until you shawab (turn back / repent) back."

Gadaiwan (Gideon) bawaa (come) in, and ishah (make) a young iz (goat), and unleavened matzawath (cakes) of an ayapah (ephah) of qamach (meal). He shawam (place / establish / appoint) the meat in a sal (basket) and he shawam (place / establish / appoint) the maraq (broth) in a parawar (pot), and yatzaa (go out / come out) it out to him under the alah (oak / terebinth), and nagash (presented) it.

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Alahayam amar (spoke) to him, "laqach (take / seize) the meat and the unleavened matzawath (cakes), and yanach (lay) them on halaz (this) salai (rock), and shapak (pour) out the maraq (broth)." He ishah (make) so.

Then the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah shalach (send) out the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the mashainah (staff) that was in his yad (hand), and nagai (touched) the meat and the unleavened matzawath (cakes); and ash (fire) ilah (go up / offer) up out of the tzawar (rock), and akal (eat) the meat and the unleavened matzawath (cakes); and the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah departed out of his iyan (eye).

Gadaiwan (Gideon) raah (see) that he was the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah; and Gadaiwan (Gideon) amar (spoke), "ahah (alas), Adawan Yahawah! Because I raah (see) seen the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah panayam (face) to panayam (face)!"
Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, "shalawam (peace / safety) be to you! Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). You shall not mawath (death)."

Then Gadaiwan (Gideon) banah (build) an mazabach (altar) there to Yahawah, and qaraa (called) it "Yahawah is Peace." To this yawam (day) it is still in Iparah (Ophrah) of the abayahaizaray (abiezrites).

It happened the same layal (night), that Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, "laqach (take / seize) your ab (father) shawar (bull), even the shanay (second) shawar (bull) shabai (seven) shanayam (years) old, and haras (throw) down the mazabach (altar) of Bail (Baal) that your ab (father) has, and cut down the Asharah (Asherah) that is by it;

And banah (build) an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah your Alahayam on the raash (head) of this stronghold, in an orderly mairakah (way), and laqach (take / seize) the shanay (second) par (bull), and ilah (go up / offer) a burnt ilah (go up / offer) with the itz (wood) of the Asharah (Asherah) which you shall karath (cut) down."

Then Gadaiwan (Gideon) laqach (take / seize) ishar (ten) anashayam (men) of his ibad (servant), and ishah (make) as Yahawah had dabar (word / matter) to him: and it happened, because he yaraa (fear / be afraid) his ab (father) bayath (house) and the anashayam (men) of the iyar (city), so that he could not ishah (make) it by yawamam (by day), that he ishah (make) it by layal (night).

When the anashay (men) of the iyar (city) arose shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), behold, the mazabach (altar) of Bail (Baal) was nathatz (broken) down, and the Asharah (Asherah) was cut down that was by it, and the shanay (second) par (bull) was ilah (go up / offer) on the mazabach (altar) that was banah (build).

They amar (spoke) ayash (man / husband) to rai (neigbor/another person), "Who ishah (make) done this thing?" When they darash (inquired) and baqash (asked), they amar (spoke), "Gadaiwan (Gideon) the ban (son) of Yawaash (Joash) ishah (make) done this thing."

Then the anashay (men) of the iyar (city) amar (spoke) to Yawaash (Joash), "yatzaa (go out / come out) out your ban (son), that he may mawath (death), because he has nathatz (broken) down the mazabach (altar) of Bail (Baal), and because he has karath (cut) down the Asharah (Asherah) that was by it."

Yawaash (Joash) amar (spoke) to all who imad (stood) against him, "Will you rayab (contend) for Bail (Baal)? Or will you yashai (salvation) him? He who will rayab (contend) for him, let him be put to mawath (death) by baqar (morning). If he is a Alahayam, let him rayab (contend) for himself, because someone has nathatz (broken) down his mazabach (altar)."
Therefore on that yawam (day) he qaraa (called) him Yarabail (Jerub-Baal), amar (spoke), "Let Bail (Baal) rayab (contend) against him, because he has nathatz (broken) down his mazabach (altar)."

Then all the Madayan (Midianites) and the Imalaq (Amalekites) and the banay (children) of the qadam (east) asap (assembled) themselves yachad (together); and they ibar (pass over/through) over, and chanah (encamped) in the imaq (valley) of Yazaraial (Jezreel).

But the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah labash (came) on Gadaiwan (Gideon); and he thaqai (blow / sound alarm) a shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn); and Abayaizar (Abiezer) was zaiq (gathered) together achar (other) him.

He shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) throughout all Manashah (Manasseh); and they also were zaiq (gathered) together achar (other) him: and he shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to Ashar (Asher), and to Zabawalawan (Zebulun), and to Napathalay (Naphtali); and they ilah (go up / offer) up to qaraah (meet) them.
Gadaiwan (Gideon) amar (spoke) to Alahayam, "If you yash (will) yashai (salvation) Yashar-Al (Israel) by my yad (hand), as you have dabar (word / matter),

Behold, I will yatzag (put) a gazah (fleece) of tzamar (wool) on the garan (threshing) floor; if there is tal (dew) on the gazah (fleece) only, and it is charab (dry) on all the aratz (Earth/land), then shall I yadai (know) that you will yashai (salvation) Yashar-Al (Israel) by my yad (hand), as you have dabar (word / matter)."

It was so; for he shakam (rose) up early on the next macharath (day), and pressed the gazah (fleece) zawar (together), and wrung the tal (dew) out of the gazah (fleece), a sapal (bowl) malaa (full) of mayam (Waters).

Gadaiwan (Gideon) amar (spoke) to Alahayam, "Don't let your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) be charah (hot with anger) against me, and I will dabar (word / matter) but paim (this) once. Please let me make a trial just paim (this) once with the gazah (fleece). Let it now be charab (dry) only on the gazah (fleece), and on all the aratz (Earth/land) let there be tal (dew)."
Alahayam ishah (make) so that layal (night): for it was charab (dry) on the gazah (fleece) only, and there was tal (dew) on all the aratz (Earth/land).

Then Yarabail (Jerubbaal), who is Gadaiwan (Gideon), and all the im (nation / people) who were with him, shakam (rose) up early, and chanah (encamped) beside the spring of Iyanacharad (Harod): and the machanah (camp) of Madayan (Midian) was on the tzapawan (north) side of them, by the gabaih (hill) of Mawarah (Moreh), in the imaq (valley).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Gadaiwan (Gideon), "The im (nation / people) who are with you are rab (too) many for me to nathan (give) the Madayan (Midianites) into their yad (hand), lest Yashar-Al (Israel) paar (vaunt) themselves amar (spoke) me, saying, ‘My own yad (hand) has yashai (salvation) me.'

Naa (now) therefore qaraa (called) in the azanay (ears) of the im (nation / people), amar (spoke), 'Whoever is yaraa (fearful) and charad (trembling), let him shawab (turn back / repent) and depart from har (mountain) Galaid (Gilead).'" Isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) of the im (nation / people) shawab (turn back / repent), and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) shaar (remained).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Gadaiwan (Gideon), "The im (nation / people) are still rab (too) many. Yarad (bring) them down to the mayam (Waters), and I will test them for you there. It shall be, that of whom I amar (spoke) you, ‘This shall yalak (go) with you,' the same shall yalak (go) with you; and of whoever I amar (spoke) you, ‘This shall not yalak (go) with you,' the same shall not yalak (go)."

So he yarad (brought) down the im (nation / people) to the mayam (Waters); and Yahawah amar (spoke) to Gadaiwan (Gideon), "Everyone who laqaq (laps) of the mayam (Waters) with his lashawan (tongue / language), like a kalab (dog) laqaq (laps), you shall yatzag (set) him by himself; likewise everyone who karai (bows) down on his barak (blessed) to shathah (drinks)."

The masapar (number) of those who laqaq (lapped), putting their yad (hand) to their pah (mouth), was shalawash (three) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband); but all the yathar (rest) of the im (nation / people) karai (bowed) down on their barak (blessed) to shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Gadaiwan (Gideon), "By the shalawash (three) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) who laqaq (lapped) will I yashai (salvation) you, and nathan (give) the Madayan (Midianites) into your yad (hand). Let all the other im (nation / people) yalak (go), ayash (man / husband) to his own maqawam (place)."

So the im (nation / people) laqach (take / seize) food in their yad (hand), and their shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn); and he shalach (send) all the men of Yashar-Al (Israel) every ayash (man / husband) to his ahal (tent), but chazaq (retained) the shalawash (three) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband): and the machanah (camp) of Madayan (Midian) was beneath him in the imaq (valley).
It happened the same layal (night), that Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, "qawam (rise up), yarad (go) down into the machanah (camp); for I nathan (give) delivered it into your yad (hand).
But if you are yaraa (afraid) to yarad (go) down, yarad (go) with Parah (Purah) your nair (servant) down to the machanah (camp):

And you shall shamai (hearken / hear) what they dabar (word / matter); and afterward your yad (hand) will be chazaq (strengthened) to yarad (go) down into the machanah (camp)." Then yarad (went) he down with Parah (Purah) his nair (servant) to the outermost part of the chamash (armed) men who were in the machanah (camp).

The Madayan (Midianites) and the Imalaq (Amalekites) and all the banay (children) of the qadam (east) napal (fall / be cast down) along in the imaq (valley) like arabah (locusts) for rab (multitude); and their gamal (camels) were without masapar (number), as the chawal (sand) which is on the shapah (seashore) for rab (multitude).

When Gadaiwan (Gideon) bawaa (come) come, behold, there was a ayash (man / husband) sapar (book) a chalawam (dream) to his rai (neigbor/another person); and he said, "Behold, I chalam (dream) a chalawam (dream); and behold, a tzalawal (cake) of shairah (barley) lacham (bread) hapak (tumbled) into the machanah (camp) of Madayan (Midian), and bawaa (come) to the ahal (tent), and nakah (struck) it so that it napal (fall / be cast down), and hapak (turned) it upside down, so that the ahal (tent) napal (fall / be cast down) flat."

His rai (neigbor/another person) inah (answer / respond), "This is nothing other than the charab (sword) of Gadaiwan (Gideon) the ban (son) of Yawaash (Joash), a ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel). Alahayam nathan (give) delivered Madayan (Midian) into his yad (hand), with all the machanah (army)."

It was so, when Gadaiwan (Gideon) shamai (hearken / hear) the masapar (telling) of the chalawam (dream), and its shabar (interpretation), that he shachah (worshiped); and he shawab (turn back / repent) into the machanah (camp) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and amar (spoke), "qawam (rise up); for Yahawah nathan (give) delivered the machanah (army) of Madayan (Midian) into your yad (hand)!"

He chatzah (divided) the shalawash (three) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) into shalawash (three) raashayam (companies), and he nathan (give) into the yad (hand) of all of them shawaparawath (trumpets), and rayaq (empty) kadayam (pitchers), with torches thawak (midst) the kadayam (pitchers).

He amar (spoke) to them, "Watch me, and ishah (make) likewise. Behold, when I bawaa (come) to the outermost part of the machanah (camp), it shall be that, as I ishah (make), so you shall ishah (make).

When I thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn), I and all who are with me, then thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawaparawath (trumpets) also on sabayab (surrounding) side of all the machanah (camp), and shout, ‘For Yahawah and for Gadaiwan (Gideon)!'"

So Gadaiwan (Gideon), and the maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) who were with him, bawaa (come) to the outermost part of the machanah (camp) in the raash (head) of the thayakawan (middle) ashamarah (watch), when they had but qawam (rise up) qawam (rise up) the shamar (keep/guard): and they thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawaparawath (trumpets), and napatz (broke) in pieces the kadayam (pitchers) that were in their yad (hand).

The shalawash (three) raashayam (companies) thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawaparawath (trumpets), and shabar (broke) the kadayam (pitchers), and chazaq (held) the torches in their shamaawal (left hand) yad (hand), and the shawaparawath (trumpets) in their yamayan (right hand) yad (hand) with which to thaqai (blow / sound alarm); and they shouted, "The charab (sword) of Yahawah and of Gadaiwan (Gideon)!"
They ayash (man / husband) imad (stood) in his sabayab (surrounding) around the machanah (camp); and all the machanah (army) rawatz (ran); and they rawai (shouted), and nawas (put) them to flight.

They thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shawaparawath (trumpets), and Yahawah shawam (place / establish / appoint) every ayash (man / husband) charab (sword) against his rai (neigbor/another person), and against all the machanah (army); and the machanah (army) nawas (fled) as far as Bayathahashatah (Beth Shittah) toward Tzararah (Zererah), as far as the shapah (border) of Abalamachawalah (Abel Meholah), by Tabath (Tabbath).

The ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) were tzaiq (gathered) together out of Napathalay (Naphtali), and out of Ashar (Asher), and out of all Manashah (Manasseh), and radap (pursued) achar (other) Madayan (Midian).

Gadaiwan (Gideon) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) throughout all the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), amar (spoke), "yarad (come) down qaraah (against) Madayan (Midian), and lakad (take) before them the mayam (Waters), as far as Bayathabarah (Beth Barah), even the Yaradan (Jordan)!" So all the ayash (man / husband) of Aparayam (Ephraim) were tzaiq (gathered) together, and lakad (took) the mayam (Waters) as far as Bayathabarah (Beth Barah), even the Yaradan (Jordan).

They lakad (took) the shanayam (two) sharay (princes) of Madayan (Midian), Irab (Oreb) and Zaab (Zeeb); and they harag (kill) Irab (Oreb) at the tzawar (rock) of Irab (Oreb), and Zaab (Zeeb) they harag (kill) at the yaqab (winepress) of Zaab (Zeeb), and radap (pursued) Madayan (Midian): and they bawaa (come) the raash (head) of Irab (Oreb) and Zaab (Zeeb) to Gadaiwan (Gideon) ibar (beyond) the Yaradan (Jordan).

The ayash (man / husband) of Aparayam (Ephraim) amar (spoke) to him, "mah (why) have you treated us this mah (way), that you didn't qaraa (called) us, when you halak (move) to lacham (fight) with Madayan (Midian)?" They rebuked him chazaqah (sharply).

He amar (spoke) to them, "What ishah (make) I now done in comparison with you? Isn't the gleaning of the grapes of Aparayam (Ephraim) tawab (good / proper function) than the batzayar (vintage) of Abayaizar (Abiezer)?

Alahayam nathan (give) delivered into your yad (hand) the sharay (princes) of Madayan (Midian), Irab (Oreb) and Zaab (Zeeb)! What was I yakal (able) to ishah (make) in comparison with you?" Then their rawach (spirit / wind) was rapah (abated) toward him, when he had dabar (word / matter) that.

Gadaiwan (Gideon) bawaa (come) to the Yaradan (Jordan), and ibar (pass over/through) over, he, and the shalawash (three) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) who were with him, iyap (faint), yet radap (pursuing).

He amar (spoke) to the anashay (men) of Sakawath (Succoth), "Please nathan (give) loaves of lacham (bread) to the im (nation / people) who ragal (feet / foot) me; for they are iyap (faint), and I am radap (pursuing) achar (other) Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna), the malakay (kings) of Madayan (Midian)."

The sharay (princes) of Sakawath (Succoth) amar (spoke), "Are the kap (hands) of Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna) now in your yad (hand), that we should nathan (give) lacham (bread) to your tzabaa (troop)?"

Gadaiwan (Gideon) amar (spoke), "Therefore when Yahawah nathan (give) delivered Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna) into my yad (hand), then I will dawash (tear) your bashar (flesh) with the qawatzay (thorns) of the madabar (wilderness) and with baraqanayam (briers)."

He ilah (go up / offer) up there to Panawaal (Penuel), and dabar (word / matter) to them in the same way; and the anashay (men) of Panawaal (Penuel) inah (answer / respond) him as the anashay (men) of Sakawath (Succoth) had inah (answer / respond).

He amar (spoke) also to the anashay (men) of Panawaal (Penuel), amar (spoke), "When I shawab (turn back / repent) again in shalawam (peace / safety), I will nathatz (break) down this magadal (tower)."

Now Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna) were in Qaraqar (Karkor), and their machanah (armies) with them, about chamash (fifteen) alap (thousand) men, all who were yathar (left) of all the machanah (army) of the banay (children) of the qadam (east); for there napal (fall / be cast down) one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband) who shalap (drew) charab (sword).

Gadaiwan (Gideon) ilah (go up / offer) up by the darak (way) of those who lived in ahalayam (tents) on the qadam (east) of Nabach (Nobah) and Yagabahah (Jogbehah), and nakah (struck) the machanah (army); for the machanah (army) was batach (secure).

Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna) nawas (fled); and he radap (pursued) achar (other) them; and he lakad (took) the shanayam (two) malakay (kings) of Madayan (Midian), Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna), and confused all the machanah (army).
Gadaiwan (Gideon) the ban (son) of Yawaash (Joash) shawab (turn back / repent) from the malachamah (battle) from the ascent of Heres.

He lakad (caught) a nair (young) man of the anashay (men) of Sakawath (Succoth), and inquired of him: and he kathab (write) for him the sharay (princes) of Sakawath (Succoth), and its zaqan (elders), seventy-seven anashay (men).

He bawaa (come) to the anashay (men) of Sakawath (Succoth), and amar (spoke), "See Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna), concerning whom you taunted me, amar (spoke), ‘Are the kap (hands) of Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna) now in your kap (hand), that we should nathan (give) lacham (bread) to your anashay (men) who are yaip (weary)?'"

He laqach (take / seize) the zaqanay (elders) of the iyar (city), and qawatzay (thorns) of the madabar (wilderness) and baraqanayam (briers), and with them he yadai (taught) the zaqanay (men) of Sakawath (Succoth).
He nathatz (broke) down the magadal (tower) of Panawaal (Penuel), and harag (kill) the anashay (men) of the iyar (city).

Then he amar (spoke) to Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna), "ayapah (what) kind of anashayam (men) were they whom you harag (kill) at Thabawar (Tabor)?" They amar (spoke), "They were kamaw (like) you. Achad (one) one thaar (resembled) the banay (children) of a malak (king)."
He amar (spoke), "They were my ach (brother/kinsman), the banay (sons) of my am (mother). As Yahawah chay (life), if you had chayah (saved) them alive, I would not harag (kill) you."

He amar (spoke) to Yathar (Jether) his bakawar (firstborn), "qawam (rise up) up, and harag (kill) them!" But the youth didn't shalap (draw) his charab (sword); for he was yaraa (fear / be afraid), because he was yet a youth.

Then Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna) amar (spoke), "qawam (rise up) and pagai (fall) on us; for as the ayash (man / husband) is, so is his gabawarah (strength)." Gadaiwan (Gideon) qawam (rise up), and harag (kill) Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna), and laqach (take / seize) the crescents that were on their gamal (camels)' tzawaaray (necks).

Then the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke) to Gadaiwan (Gideon), "mashal (rule/have dominion) over us, both you, and your ban (son), and your ban (son) ban (son) also; for you have yashai (salvation) us out of the yad (hand) of Madayan (Midian)."

Gadaiwan (Gideon) amar (spoke) to them, "I will not mashal (rule/have dominion) over you, neither shall my ban (son) mashal (rule/have dominion) over you. Yahawah shall mashal (rule/have dominion) over you."

Gadaiwan (Gideon) amar (spoke) to them, "I would make a shaalah (request) of you, that you nathan (give) give me every ayash (man / husband) the nazamay (earrings) of his shalal (spoil)." (For they had zahab (gold) nazamay (earrings), because they were Yashamaialay (Ishmaelites).)

They amar (spoke), "We will nathan (give) nathan (give) them." They parash (spread) a shamalah (garment), and every ayash (man / husband) shalak (threw) the nazam (earrings) of his shalal (spoil) into it.

The mashaqal (weight) of the zahab (gold) nazamay (earrings) that he shaal (requested) was one alap (thousand) and shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shekels of zahab (gold), besides the crescents, and the pendants, and the aragaman (purple) bagad (clothing) that was on the malakay (kings) of Madayan (Midian), and besides the inaqawath (chains) that were about their gamal (camels)' tzawaaray (necks).

Gadaiwan (Gideon) ishah (make) an apawad (ephod) of it, and yatzag (put) it in his iyar (city), even in Iparah (Ophrah): and all Yashar-Al (Israel) zanah (played) the prostitute achar (other) it there; and it became a mawaqash (snare) to Gadaiwan (Gideon), and to his bayath (house).

So Madayan (Midian) was kanai (subdued) panayam (face) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and they nashaa (lift) up their raash (head) no more. The aratz (Earth/land) had shaqat (rest) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years) in the yamay (days) of Gadaiwan (Gideon).
Yarabail (Jerubbaal) the ban (son) of Yawaash (Joash) yalak (went) and lived in his own bayath (house).
Gadaiwan (Gideon) had shabaiyam (seventy) banayam (sons) conceived from his yarak (body); for he rab (had) many wives.
His payalagash (concubine) who was in Shakam (Shechem), she also yalad (birth / begot) him a ban (son), and he shawam (place / establish / appoint) him Abayamalak (Abimelech).

Gadaiwan (Gideon) the ban (son) of Yawaash (Joash) mawath (death) in a tawab (good / proper function) shayabah (old age / white hair - due to age) age, and was qabar (bury) in the tomb of Yawaash (Joash) his ab (father), in Iparah (Ophrah) of the abayahaizaray (abiezrites).

It happened, as soon as Gadaiwan (Gideon) was mawath (death), that the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shawab (turn back / repent) again, and zanah (played) the prostitute achar (other) the Bail (Baals), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) Bailabarayath (Baal Berith) their Alahayam.

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) didn't zakar (remember) Yahawah their Alahayam, who had natzal (delivered) them out of the yad (hand) of all their ayab (enemy) on sabayab (surrounding) side;
Neither ishah (make) they show chasad (grace) to the bayath (house) of Yarabail (Jerubbaal), Gadaiwan (Gideon), according to all the goodness which he ishah (make) shown to Yashar-Al (Israel).

Abayamalak (Abimelech) the ban (son) of Yarabail (Jerubbaal) yalak (went) to Shakam (Shechem) to his am (mother) achay (brothers), and dabar (word / matter) with them, and with all the mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) of the bayath (house) of his am (mother) ab (father), amar (spoke),

"Please dabar (word / matter) in the azanay (ears) of all the bailay (men) of Shakam (Shechem), ‘Is it tawab (good / proper function) for you that all the banay (sons) of Yarabail (Jerubbaal), who are shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (man / husband), mashal (rule/have dominion) over you, or that achad (one) mashal (rule/have dominion) over you?' Zakar (remember) also that I am your itzam (bone) and your bashar (flesh)."

His am (mother) achay (brothers) dabar (word / matter) of him in the azanay (ears) of all the bailay (men) of Shakam (Shechem) all these dabarayam (words): and their lab (heart) natah (inclined) to achar (other) Abayamalak (Abimelech); for they amar (spoke), "He is our ach (brother/kinsman)."

They nathan (give) him shabaiyam (seventy) pieces of kasap (silver) out of the bayath (house) of Bailabarayath (Baal Berith), with which Abayamalak (Abimelech) shakar (hired) rayaq (vain) and pachaz (light) anashayam (fellows), who yalak (followed) him.

He bawaa (come) to his ab (father) bayath (house) at Iparah (Ophrah), and harag (kill) his ach (brother/kinsman) the banay (sons) of Yarabail (Jerubbaal), being shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (man / husband), on achad (one) aban (stone): but Yawatham (Jotham) the youngest ban (son) of Yarabail (Jerubbaal) was yathar (left); for he chabaa (hid) himself.

All the bailay (men) of Shakam (Shechem) asap (assembled) themselves together, and all the bayath (house) of Malawaa (Millo), and yalak (went) and malak (king) Abayamalak (Abimelech) malak (king), by the oak of the natzab (pillar) that was in Shakam (Shechem).

When they nagad (told) it to Yawatham (Jotham), he yalak (went) and imad (stood) on the raash (head) of har (mountain) Garazayam (Gerizim), and nashaa (lift) up his qawal (sound / voice), and qaraa (called), and amar (spoke) to them, "shamai (hearken / hear) to me, you bailay (men) of Shakam (Shechem), that Alahayam may shamai (hearken / hear) to you.
The itzayam (trees) halak (move) forth on a time to mashach (anoint) a malak (king) over them; and they amar (spoke) to the zayath (olive) tree, ‘malak (king) over us.'

"But the zayath (olive) tree amar (spoke) to them, ‘Should I chadal (leave) my dashan (fatness), with which by me they honor Alahayam and ayash (man / husband), and halak (move) to wave back and forth over the itzayam (trees)?'
"The itzayam (trees) amar (spoke) to the thaan (fig) tree, ‘yalak (come) and malak (king) over us.'

"But the thaan (fig) tree amar (spoke) to them, ‘Should I chadal (leave) my mathaq (sweetness), and my tawab (good / proper function) thanawabah (fruit), and halak (move) to wave back and forth over the itzayam (trees)?'
"The itzayam (trees) amar (spoke) to the gapan (vine), ‘yalak (come) and malak (king) over us.'

"The gapan (vine) amar (spoke) to them, ‘Should I chadal (leave) my new thayarawash (wine), which shamach (cheers) Alahayam and ayash (man / husband), and halak (move) to wave back and forth over the itzayam (trees)?'
"Then all the itzayam (trees) amar (spoke) to the atad (bramble), ‘yalak (come) and malak (king) over us.'

"The atad (bramble) amar (spoke) to the itzayam (trees), ‘If in amath (truth) you mashach (anoint) me malak (king) over you, then bawaa (come) and take chasah (refuge) in my tzal (shade); and if not, let ash (fire) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the atad (bramble), and akal (eat) the arazay (cedars) of Labanawan (Lebanon).'

"Now therefore, if you ishah (make) dealt truly and righteously, in that you have made Abayamalak (Abimelech) malak (king), and if you ishah (make) dealt tawab (good / proper function) with Yarabail (Jerubbaal) and his bayath (house), and ishah (make) done to him according to the gamawal (deserving) of his yad (hand)
(For my ab (father) lacham (fought) for you, and risked his napash (soul), and natzal (delivered) you out of the yad (hand) of Madayan (Midian):

And you have qawam (rise up) up against my ab (father) bayath (house) this yawam (day), and have harag (kill) his ban (son), shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (man / husband), on achad (one) aban (stone), and have made Abayamalak (Abimelech), the ban (son) of his female amah (servant), malak (king) over the bailay (men) of Shakam (Shechem), because he is your ach (brother/kinsman));

If you then ishah (make) dealt truly and righteously with Yarabail (Jerubbaal) and with his bayath (house) this yawam (day), then shamach (rejoice) in Abayamalak (Abimelech), and let him also shamach (rejoice) in you:

But if not, let ash (fire) yatzaa (go out / come out) out from Abayamalak (Abimelech), and akal (eat) the bailay (men) of Shakam (Shechem), and the bayath (house) of Malawaa (Millo); and let ash (fire) yatzaa (go out / come out) out from the bailay (men) of Shakam (Shechem), and from the bayath (house) of Malawaa (Millo), and akal (eat) Abayamalak (Abimelech)."
Yawatham (Jotham) barach (ran) away, and nawas (fled), and yalak (went) to Baar (Beer), and lived there, for panayam (face) of Abayamalak (Abimelech) his ach (brother/kinsman).
Abayamalak (Abimelech) was shawar (prince) over Yashar-Al (Israel) shalawash (three) shanayam (years).

Alahayam shalach (send) an rai (evil) rawach (spirit / wind) between Abayamalak (Abimelech) and the bailay (men) of Shakam (Shechem); and the bailay (men) of Shakam (Shechem) dealt bagad (treacherously) with Abayamalak (Abimelech):

That the chamas (violence) done to the shabaiyam (seventy) banay (sons) of Yarabail (Jerubbaal) might bawaa (come), and that their dam (blood) might be shawam (place / establish / appoint) on Abayamalak (Abimelech) their ach (brother/kinsman), who harag (kill) them, and on the bailay (men) of Shakam (Shechem), who chazaq (strengthened) his harag (kill) to kill his ach (brother/kinsman).

The bailay (men) of Shakam (Shechem) shawam (place / establish / appoint) an arab (ambush) for him on the raashay (tops) of the harayam (mountains), and they gazal (robbed) ibar (pass over/through) who came along that darak (way) by them: and it was nagad (told) Abayamalak (Abimelech).

Gail (Gaal) the ban (son) of Ibad (Ebed) bawaa (come) with his ach (brother/kinsman), and ibar (pass over/through) over to Shakam (Shechem); and the bailay (men) of Shakam (Shechem) batach (put) their trust in him.

They yatzaa (go out / come out) out into the shadah (field), and harvested their karam (vineyards), and darak (trod) the grapes, and ishah (make) festival, and bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of their Alahayam, and akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and qalal (cursed) Abayamalak (Abimelech).

Gail (Gaal) the ban (son) of Ibad (Ebed) amar (spoke), "Who is Abayamalak (Abimelech), and who is Shakam (Shechem), that we should ibad (servant) him? Isn't he the ban (son) of Yarabail (Jerubbaal)? And Zabal (Zebul) his officer? Ibad (servant) the ban (son) of Chamawar (Hamor) the ab (father) of Shakam (Shechem): but why should we ibad (servant) him?

Would that this im (nation / people) were under my yad (hand)! Then I would sawar (remove) Abayamalak (Abimelech)." He amar (spoke) to Abayamalak (Abimelech), "rabah (increase) your tzabaa (troop), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out!"

When Zabal (Zebul) the shar (prince / ruler) of the iyar (city) shamai (hearken / hear) the dabaray (words) of Gail (Gaal) the ban (son) of Ibad (Ebed), his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger).

He shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to Abayamalak (Abimelech) craftily, amar (spoke), "Behold, Gail (Gaal) the ban (son) of Ibad (Ebed) and his ach (brother/kinsman) bawaa (come) come to Shakam (Shechem); and behold, they incite the iyar (city) against you.
Now therefore, go up by layal (night), you and the im (nation / people) who are with you, and lie in arab (wait) in the shadah (field):

And it shall be, that in the baqar (morning), as soon as the shamash (sun) is up, you shall shakam (rise) early, and rush on the iyar (city); and behold, when he and the im (nation / people) who are with him yatzaa (go out / come out) out against you, then may you ishah (make) to them as you shall matzaa (find) occasion."

Abayamalak (Abimelech) qawam (rise up) up, and all the im (nation / people) who were with him, by layal (night), and they arab (laid) wait against Shakam (Shechem) in arabai (four) raashayam (companies).

Gail (Gaal) the ban (son) of Ibad (Ebed) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and imad (stood) in the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate) of the iyar (city): and Abayamalak (Abimelech) qawam (rise up) up, and the im (nation / people) who were with him, from the maarab (ambush).

When Gail (Gaal) raah (see) the im (nation / people), he amar (spoke) to Zabal (Zebul), "Behold, im (nation / people) are yarad (coming) down from the raashay (tops) of the harayam (mountains)." Zabal (Zebul) amar (spoke) to him, "You raah (see) the tzal (shadow) of the harayam (mountains) as if they were im (nation / people)."

Gail (Gaal) dabar (word / matter) again and dabar (word / matter), "Behold, im (nation / people) are yarad (coming) down by the tabawar (middle) of the aratz (Earth/land), and one raash (head) bawaa (come) by the darak (way) of the oak of Meonenim."

Then Zabal (Zebul) amar (spoke) to him, "apaw (now) where is your pah (mouth), that you amar (spoke), ‘Who is Abayamalak (Abimelech), that we should ibad (servant) him?' Isn't this the im (nation / people) that you have maas (despised)? Please yatzaa (go out / come out) out naa (now) and lacham (fight) with them."
Gail (Gaal) yatzaa (go out / come out) out panayam (face) the bailay (men) of Shakam (Shechem), and lacham (fought) with Abayamalak (Abimelech).
Abayamalak (Abimelech) radap (chased) him, and he nawas (fled) panayam (face) him, and many napal (fall / be cast down) chalal (wounded), even to the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate).
Abayamalak (Abimelech) lived at Arawamah (Arumah): and Zabal (Zebul) garash (drove) out Gail (Gaal) and his ach (brother/kinsman), that they should not yashab (inhabit/dwell) in Shakam (Shechem).
It happened on the next macharath (day), that the im (nation / people) yatzaa (go out / come out) out into the shadah (field); and they nagad (told) Abayamalak (Abimelech).

He laqach (take / seize) the im (nation / people), and chatzah (divided) them into shalawash (three) raashayam (companies), and arab (laid) wait in the shadah (field); and he raah (see), and behold, the im (nation / people) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the iyar (city); He qawam (rise up) up against them, and nakah (struck) them.

Abayamalak (Abimelech), and the raashayam (companies) that were with him, pashat (rushed) forward, and imad (stood) in the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate) of the iyar (city): and the shanayam (two) raashayam (companies) pashat (rushed) on all who were in the shadah (field), and nakah (struck) them.

Abayamalak (Abimelech) lacham (fought) against the iyar (city) all that yawam (day); and he lakad (took) the iyar (city), and harag (kill) the im (nation / people) who were therein: and he nathatz (beat) down the iyar (city), and zarai (sowed) it with malach (salt).
When all the bailay (men) of the magadal (tower) of Shakam (Shechem) shamai (hearken / hear) of it, they bawaa (come) into the stronghold of the bayath (house) of Barayath (Elberith).
It was nagad (told) Abayamalak (Abimelech) that all the bailay (men) of the magadal (tower) of Shakam (Shechem) were qabatz (gathered) together.

Abayamalak (Abimelech) ilah (go up / offer) up to har (mountain) Tzalamawan (Zalmon), he and all the im (nation / people) who were with him; and Abayamalak (Abimelech) laqach (take / seize) an axe in his yad (hand), and karath (cut) down a shawak (bough) from the itzayam (trees), and nashaa (lift) it up, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it on his shakam (shoulder): and he amar (spoke) to the im (nation / people) who were with him, "What you raah (see) seen me ishah (make), mahar (make) haste, and ishah (make) as I have done!"

All the im (nation / people) likewise ayash (man / husband) karath (cut) down his shawak (bough), and yalak (followed) Abayamalak (Abimelech), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them at the base of the stronghold, and yatzath (set) the stronghold on ash (fire) on them; so that all the im (nation / people) of the magadal (tower) of Shakam (Shechem) mawath (death) also, about a alap (thousand) anashay (men) and ayashah (woman / wife).
Then yalak (went) Abayamalak (Abimelech) to Thabatz (Thebez), and chanah (encamped) against Thabatz (Thebez), and lakad (took) it.

But there was a iz (strength / might / refuge) magadal (tower) thawak (midst) the iyar (city), and there nawas (fled) all the anashayam (men) and nashayam (women), and all they of the iyar (city), and sagar (shut) themselves in, and ilah (go up / offer) up to the gag (roof) of the magadal (tower).
Abayamalak (Abimelech) bawaa (come) to the magadal (tower), and lacham (fought) against it, and nagash (drew) near to the pathach (door) of the magadal (tower) to sharap (burn) it with ash (fire).
A achad (one) ayashah (woman / wife) shalak (cast) an upper rakab (millstone) on Abayamalak (Abimelech's) raash (head), and ratzatz (broke) his galagalath (skull).

Then he qaraa (called) maharah (hastily) to the nair (young) man his armor bearer, and amar (spoke) to him, "shalap (draw) your charab (sword), and mawath (death) me, that men not amar (spoke) of me, ‘A ayashah (woman / wife) harag (kill) him.' His nair (young) man thrust him daqar (through), and he mawath (death)."
When the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) raah (see) that Abayamalak (Abimelech) was mawath (death), they departed every ayash (man / husband) to his maqawam (place).
Thus Alahayam shawab (turn back / repent) the rai (wickedness) of Abayamalak (Abimelech), which he ishah (make) to his ab (father), in harag (kill) his shabaiyam (seventy) ach (brother/kinsman);

And all the rai (wickedness) of the rai (men) of Shakam (Shechem) did Alahayam shawab (turn back / repent) on their raash (head): and on them bawaa (come) the qalalah (curse) of Yawatham (Jotham) the ban (son) of Yarabail (Jerubbaal).

Achar (other) Abayamalak (Abimelech) there qawam (rise up) to yashai (salvation) Yashar-Al (Israel) Thawalai (Tola) the ban (son) of Pawaah (Puah), the ban (son) of Dawadaw (Dodo), a ayash (man / husband) of Yashashakar (Issachar); and he lived in Shamayar (Shamir) in the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim).
He shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel) isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three) shanah (years), and mawath (death), and was qabar (bury) in Shamayar (Shamir).
