Achar (other) him qawam (rise up) Yaayar (Jair), the Galaiday (Gileadite); and he shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel) isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) shanah (years).

He had shalawashayam (thirty) banayam (sons) who rakab (rode) on shalawashayam (thirty) donkey iyarayam (colts), and they had shalawashayam (thirty) cities, which are qaraa (called) Havvoth chawawathayaiyar (jair) to this yawam (day), which are in the aratz (Earth/land) of Galaid (Gilead).
Yaayar (Jair) mawath (death), and was qabar (bury) in Qamawan (Kamon).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) again ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, and ibad (servant) the Bail (Baals), and the Ishatharawath (Ashtaroth), and the Alahayam of Aram (Syria), and the Alahayam of Tzayadawan (Sidon), and the Alahayam of Mawaab (Moab), and the Alahayam of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), and the Alahayam of the Palashathay (Philistines); and they forsook Yahawah, and didn't ibad (servant) him.

The ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah was charah (hot with anger) against Yashar-Al (Israel), and he makar (sold) them into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and into the yad (hand) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon).

They troubled and ratzatz (oppressed) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) that year. For eighteen shanah (years), they ratzatz (oppressed) all the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) that were ibar (beyond) the Yaradan (Jordan) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the Amaray (Amorites), which is in Galaid (Gilead).

The banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) ibar (pass over/through) over the Yaradan (Jordan) to lacham (fight) also against Yahawadah (Judah), and against Banayamayan (Benjamin), and against the bayath (house) of Aparayam (Ephraim); so that Yashar-Al (Israel) was very yatzar (distressed).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) zaiq (cried) to Yahawah, amar (spoke), "We have chataa (sinned) against you, even because we have forsaken our Alahayam, and have ibad (servant) the Bail (Baals)."

Yahawah amar (spoke) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), "Didn't I save you from the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and from the Amaray (Amorites), from the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), and from the Palashathay (Philistines)?
The Tzayadanay (Sidonians) also, and the Imalaq (Amalekites), and the maiwan (maonites), lachatz (oppressed) you; and you tzaiq (cried) to me, and I yashai (salvation) you out of their yad (hand).
Yet you have forsaken me, and ibad (servant) other Alahayam: therefore I will yashai (salvation) you no more.
Yalak (go) and zaiq (cry) to the Alahayam which you have bachar (chosen). Let them yashai (salvation) you in the ith (time) of your tzarah (distress)!"

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke) to Yahawah, "We have chataa (sinned): ishah (make) you to us whatever seems tawab (good / proper function) to you; only natzal (deliver) us, please, this yawam (day)."
They sawar (put) away the foreign Alahayam from qarab (among / near) them, and ibad (servant) Yahawah; and his napash (soul) was qatzar (grieved) for the misery of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Then the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) were tzaiq (gathered) together, and chanah (encamped) in Galaid (Gilead). The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) asap (assembled) themselves together, and chanah (encamped) in Matzapah (Mizpah).

The im (nation / people), the sharay (princes) of Galaid (Gilead), amar (spoke) ayash (man / husband) to rai (neigbor/another person), "What ayash (man / husband) is he who will chalal (begin) to lacham (fight) against the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon)? He shall be raash (head) over all the yashabay (inhabitants) of Galaid (Gilead)."

Now Yapathach (Jephthah) the Galaiday (Gileadite) was a gabawar (mighty) man of valor, and he was the ban (son) of a prostitute: and Galaid (Gilead) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Yapathach (Jephthah).

Galaid (Gilead's) ayashah (woman / wife) yalad (birth / begot) him banayam (sons); and when his ayashah (woman / wife) banayam (sons) gadal (grew) up, they garash (drove) out Yapathach (Jephthah), and amar (spoke) to him, "You shall not nachal (inherit) in our ab (father) bayath (house); for you are the ban (son) of achar (other) ayashah (woman / wife)."

Then Yapathach (Jephthah) barach (fled) from his ach (brother/kinsman), and lived in the aratz (Earth/land) of Tawab (Tob): and there were laqat (gathered) rayaq (vain) anashayam (fellows) to Yapathach (Jephthah), and they yatzaa (go out / come out) out with him.
It happened after a yawam (day), that the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) made lacham (war) against Yashar-Al (Israel).

It was so, that when the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) made lacham (war) against Yashar-Al (Israel), the zaqanay (elders) of Galaid (Gilead) yalak (went) to laqach (take / seize) Yapathach (Jephthah) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Tawab (Tob);
And they amar (spoke) to Yapathach (Jephthah), "yalak (come) and be our chief, that we may lacham (fight) with the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon)."

Yapathach (Jephthah) amar (spoke) to the zaqanay (elders) of Galaid (Gilead), "Didn't you shanaa (hate) me, and garash (drive) me out of my ab (father) bayath (house)? Why bawaa (come) you come to me now when you are in tzar (oppressor / distressor)?"

The zaqanay (elders) of Galaid (Gilead) amar (spoke) to Yapathach (Jephthah), "Therefore we have shawab (turn back / repent) again to you now, that you may halak (move) with us, and lacham (fight) with the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon); and you shall be our raash (head) over all the yashabay (inhabitants) of Galaid (Gilead)."

Yapathach (Jephthah) amar (spoke) to the zaqanay (elders) of Galaid (Gilead), "If you shawab (turn back / repent) me home again to lacham (fight) with the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), and Yahawah nathan (give) them panayam (face) me, shall I be your raash (head)?"

The zaqanay (elders) of Galaid (Gilead) amar (spoke) to Yapathach (Jephthah), "Yahawah shall be shamai (hearken / hear) between us; surely according to your dabar (word / matter) so will we ishah (make)."

Then Yapathach (Jephthah) yalak (went) with the zaqanay (elders) of Galaid (Gilead), and the im (nation / people) shawam (place / establish / appoint) him raash (head) and chief over them: and Yapathach (Jephthah) dabar (word / matter) all his dabar (word / matter) panayam (face) Yahawah in Matzapah (Mizpah).

Yapathach (Jephthah) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to the malak (king) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), amar (spoke), "What bawaa (come) you to do with me, that you have come to me to lacham (fight) against my aratz (Earth/land)?"

The malak (king) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) amar (spoke) to the malaakay (messengers) of Yapathach (Jephthah), "Because Yashar-Al (Israel) laqach (take / seize) away my aratz (Earth/land), when he ilah (go up / offer) up out of Matzarayam (Egypt), from the Aranawan (Arnon) even to the Yabaq (Jabbok), and to the Yaradan (Jordan): now therefore shawab (turn back / repent) that territory again peaceably."
Yapathach (Jephthah) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) again to the malak (king) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon);

And he amar (spoke) to him, "Thus amar (spoke) Yapathach (Jephthah): Yashar-Al (Israel) didn't laqach (take / seize) away the aratz (Earth/land) of Mawaab (Moab), nor the aratz (Earth/land) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon),

But when they ilah (go up / offer) up from Matzarayam (Egypt), and Yashar-Al (Israel) yalak (went) through the madabar (wilderness) to the sawap (red) yam (sea/waters), and bawaa (come) to Qadash (Kadesh);

Then Yashar-Al (Israel) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to the malak (king) of Adawam (Edom), amar (spoke), ‘Please let me ibar (pass over/through) through your aratz (Earth/land);' but the malak (king) of Adawam (Edom) didn't shamai (hearken / hear). In the same way, he shalach (send) to the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab); but he would not: and Yashar-Al (Israel) stayed in Qadash (Kadesh).

Then they yalak (went) through the madabar (wilderness), and sabab (went) around the aratz (Earth/land) of Adawam (Edom), and the aratz (Earth/land) of Mawaab (Moab), and bawaa (come) by the mazarach (east) side of the aratz (Earth/land) of Mawaab (Moab), and they chanah (encamped) on the other ibar (side) of the Aranawan (Arnon); but they didn't bawaa (come) within the gabawal (border/boundary) of Mawaab (Moab), for the Aranawan (Arnon) was the gabawal (border/boundary) of Mawaab (Moab).

Yashar-Al (Israel) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to Sayachawan (Sihon) malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), the malak (king) of Chashabawan (Heshbon); and Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke) to him, ‘Please let us ibar (pass over/through) through your aratz (Earth/land) to my maqawam (place).'

But Sayachawan (Sihon) didn't aman (believe / have faith) Yashar-Al (Israel) to ibar (pass over/through) through his gabawal (border/boundary); but Sayachawan (Sihon) asap (gathered) all his im (nation / people) asap (together), and chanah (encamped) in Yahatz (Jahaz), and lacham (fought) against Yashar-Al (Israel).

Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), nathan (give) Sayachawan (Sihon) and all his im (nation / people) into the yad (hand) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and they nakah (struck) them: so Yashar-Al (Israel) yarash (possessed) all the aratz (Earth/land) of the Amaray (Amorites), the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of that aratz (Earth/land).

They yarash (possessed) all the gabawal (border/boundary) of the Amaray (Amorites), from the Aranawan (Arnon) even to the Yabaq (Jabbok), and from the madabar (wilderness) even to the Yaradan (Jordan).

So now Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), has yarash (dispossessed) the Amaray (Amorites) from panayam (face) his im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel), and should you yarash (possess) them?

Won't you yarash (possess) that which Kamawash (Chemosh) your Alahayam nayarash (gives) you to possess? So whoever Yahawah our Alahayam has yarash (dispossessed) from panayam (face) us, them will we yarash (possess).

Now are you anything tawab (good / proper function) than Balaq (Balak) the ban (son) of Tzapawar (Zippor), malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab)? Did he rayab (ever) rayab (strive) against Yashar-Al (Israel), or did he rayab (ever) lacham (fight) against them?

While Yashar-Al (Israel) lived in Chashabawan (Heshbon) and its banath (daughter), and in Irawair (Aroer) and its banath (daughter), and in all the irayam (cities) that are along by the yad (hand) of the Aranawan (Arnon), shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shanah (years); why didn't you natzal (recover) them within that ith (time)?

I therefore have not chataa (sinned) against you, but you ishah (make) me rai (wrong) to lacham (war) against me. Yahawah, the shapat (judge / judgement), be shapat (judge / judgement) this yawam (day) between the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) and the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon)."
However the malak (king) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) didn't shamai (hearken / hear) to the dabaray (words) of Yapathach (Jephthah) which he shalach (send) him.

Then the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah came on Yapathach (Jephthah), and he ibar (pass over/through) over Galaid (Gilead) and Manashah (Manasseh), and ibar (pass over/through) over Matzapah (Mizpeh) of Galaid (Gilead), and from Matzapah (Mizpeh) of Galaid (Gilead) he ibar (pass over/through) over to the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon).
Yapathach (Jephthah) nadar (make vow) a nadar (vow) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "If you will nathan (give) nathan (give) the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) into my yad (hand),

Then it shall be, that whatever yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from the dalathay (doors) of my bayath (house) to qaraah (meet) me, when I shawab (turn back / repent) in shalawam (peace / safety) from the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), it shall be Yahawah, and I will ilah (go up / offer) it up for a burnt ilah (offering)."
So Yapathach (Jephthah) ibar (pass over/through) over to the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) to lacham (fight) against them; and Yahawah nathan (give) them into his yad (hand).

He nakah (struck) them from Irawair (Aroer) until you bawaa (come) to Manayath (Minnith), even isharayam (twenty) iyar (cities), and to Abelcheramim, with a very gadawal (very great/important/mighty) makah (slaughter). So the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) were kanai (subdued) panayam (face) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Yapathach (Jephthah) bawaa (come) to Matzapah (Mizpah) to his bayath (house); and behold, his banath (daughter) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) him with tambourines and with machalawath (dances): and she was his only yachayad (child); besides her he had neither ban (son) aw (or) banath (daughter).

It happened, when he raah (see) her, that he qarai (tore) his clothes, and amar (spoke), "ahah (alas), my banath (daughter)! You have karai (brought) me very low, and you are one of those who ikar (trouble) me; for I have patzah (opened) my pah (mouth) to Yahawah, and I can't shawab (turn back / repent) back."

She amar (spoke) to him, "My ab (father), you have patzah (opened) your pah (mouth) to Yahawah; ishah (make) to me according to that which yatzaa (go out / come out) proceeded out of your pah (mouth), because Yahawah ishah (make) taken naqamah (vengeance) for you on your ayab (enemy), even on the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon)."

She amar (spoke) to her ab (father), "Let this thing be ishah (make) for me: let me rapah (alone) shanayam (two) chadashayam (months), that I may depart and yarad (go) down on the harayam (mountains), and bakah (bewail) my bathawalayam (virginity), I and my companions."

He amar (spoke), "yalak (go)." He shalach (send) her away for shanayam (two) chadashayam (months): and she departed, she and her raih (companions), and bakah (mourned) her bathawalayam (virginity) on the harayam (mountains).

It happened at the qatz (end) of shanayam (two) chadashayam (months), that she shawab (turn back / repent) to her ab (father), who ishah (make) with her according to his nadar (vow) which he had nadar (make vow): and she was a virgin. It was a chaq (statute) in Yashar-Al (Israel),

That the banawath (daughters) of Yashar-Al (Israel) yalak (went) yawam (day) to celebrate the banath (daughter) of Yapathach (Jephthah) the Galaiday (Gileadite) arabai (four) yamayam (days) in a shanah (year).

The ayash (man / husband) of Aparayam (Ephraim) were tzaiq (gathered) together, and ibar (pass over/through) northward; and they amar (spoke) to Yapathach (Jephthah), "Why ibar (pass over/through) you pass over to lacham (fight) against the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), and didn't qaraa (called) us to yalak (go) with you? We will sharap (burn) your bayath (house) around you with ash (fire)!"

Yapathach (Jephthah) amar (spoke) to them, "I and my im (nation / people) were at maad (great) strife with the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon); and when I zaiq (called) you, you didn't yashai (salvation) me out of their yad (hand).

When I raah (see) that you didn't yashai (salvation) me, I shawam (place / establish / appoint) my napash (soul) in my kap (hand), and ibar (pass over/through) over against the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), and Yahawah nathan (give) them into my yad (hand). Why then have you ilah (go up / offer) up to me this yawam (day), to lacham (fight) against me?"

Then Yapathach (Jephthah) qabatz (gathered) together all the anashay (men) of Galaid (Gilead), and lacham (fought) with Aparayam (Ephraim); and the anashay (men) of Galaid (Gilead) nakah (struck) Aparayam (Ephraim), because they amar (spoke), "You are palayatay (fugitives) of Aparayam (Ephraim), you Galaid (Gileadites), in the thawak (midst) of Aparayam (Ephraim), and in the thawak (midst) of Manashah (Manasseh)."

The Galaid (Gileadites) lakad (took) the maibarawath (fords) of the Yaradan (Jordan) against the Aparayam (Ephraimites). It was so, that when the palayatay (fugitives) of Aparayam (Ephraim) amar (spoke), "Let me ibar (pass over/through) over," the ibar (pass over/through) of Galaid (Gilead) amar (spoke) to him, "Are you an Aparathay (Ephraimite)?" If he amar (spoke), "No;"

Then they amar (spoke) to him, "Now amar (spoke) ‘shabal (shibboleth);'" and he amar (spoke) "sabalath (sibboleth);" for he couldn't manage to dabar (word / matter) it kawan (right): then they siezed him, and shachat (killed) him at the maibarawath (fords) of the Yaradan (Jordan). At that ith (time), arabaiyam (forty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) of Aparayam (Ephraim) napal (fall / be cast down).

Yapathach (Jephthah) shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel) shash (six) shanayam (years). Then Yapathach (Jephthah) the Galaiday (Gileadite) mawath (death), and was qabar (bury) in the iray (cities) of Galaid (Gilead).
Achar (other) him Abatzan (Ibzan) of Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem) shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel).

He had shalawashayam (thirty) banayam (sons); and shalawashayam (thirty) banawath (daughters) he shalach (send) chawatz (abroad), and shalawashayam (thirty) banawath (daughters) he bawaa (come) in from chawatz (abroad) for his banayam (sons). He shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel) shabai (seven) shanayam (years).
Abatzan (Ibzan) mawath (death), and was qabar (bury) at Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem).
Achar (other) him Ayalawan (Elon) the Zabawalanay (Zebulunite) shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel); and he shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel) ishar (ten) shanayam (years).
Ayalawan (Elon) the Zabawalanay (Zebulunite) mawath (death), and was qabar (bury) in Ayalawan (Aijalon) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Zabawalawan (Zebulun).
Achar (other) him Ibadawan (Abdon) the ban (son) of Halal (Hillel) the paraithawanay (pirathonite) shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel).

He had arabaiyam (forty) banayam (sons) and shalawashayam (thirty) banayam (sons)' sons, who rakab (rode) on shabaiyam (seventy) donkey iyaram (colts): and he shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel) shamanah (eight) shanayam (years).

Ibadawan (Abdon) the ban (son) of Halal (Hillel) the paraithawanay (pirathonite) mawath (death), and was qabar (bury) in Paraithawan (Pirathon) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Aparayam (Ephraim), in the har (mountain) country of the Imalaqay (Amalekites).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) again ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah; and Yahawah nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years).

There was a achad (one) ayash (man / husband) of Tzaraih (Zorah), of the mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) of the Danay (Danites), whose sham (name) was Manawach (Manoah); and his ayashah (woman / wife) was iqar (barren), and didn't yalad (birth / begot).

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah raah (see) to the ayashah (woman / wife), and amar (spoke) to her, "See now, you are iqar (barren), and don't yalad (birth / begot); but you shall harah (conceive), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son).
Now therefore please beware and shathah (drinks) no yayan (wine) nor strong shathah (drinks), and don't akal (eat) any tamaa (unclean) thing:

For, behold, you shall harah (conceive), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son); and no mawarah (razor) shall ilah (go up / offer) on his raash (head); for the nair (child) shall be a Nazirite to Alahayam from the batan (womb): and he shall chalal (begin) to yashai (salvation) Yashar-Al (Israel) out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines)."

Then the ayashah (woman / wife) bawaa (come) and amar (spoke) her ayash (man / husband), amar (spoke), "A ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam bawaa (come) to me, and his maraah (face) was like the maraah (face) of the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Alahayam, very awesome; and I didn't shaal (ask) him where he was from, neither did he nagad (tell) me his sham (name):

But he amar (spoke) to me, ‘Behold, you shall harah (conceive), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son); and now shakar (drink) no yayan (wine) nor strong shathah (drinks), and akal (eat) not any tamaah (unclean) thing; for the nair (child) shall be a Nazirite to Alahayam from the batan (womb) to the yawam (day) of his mawath (death).'"

Then Manawach (Manoah) entreated Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "Oh, Adawan, please let the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam whom you did shalach (send) bawaa (come) again to us, and yarah (teach) us what we shall ishah (make) to the nair (child) who shall be yalad (birth / begot)."

Alahayam shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of Manawach (Manoah); and the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Alahayam bawaa (come) again to the ayashah (woman / wife) as she yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the shadah (field): but Manawach (Manoah), her ayash (man / husband), wasn't with her.

The ayashah (woman / wife) mahar (made) haste, and rawatz (ran), and amar (spoke) her ayash (man / husband), and amar (spoke) to him, "Behold, the ayash (man / husband) has raah (see) to me, who bawaa (come) to me that yawam (day)."

Manawach (Manoah) qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) achar (other) his ayashah (woman / wife), and bawaa (come) to the ayash (man / husband), and amar (spoke) to him, "Are you the ayash (man / husband) who dabar (word / matter) to the ayashah (woman / wife)?" He amar (spoke), "I am."
Manawach (Manoah) amar (spoke), "Now let your dabar (word / matter) happen. What shall the nair (child's) mashapat (way) of maishah (life) and mission be?"
The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah amar (spoke) to Manawach (Manoah), "Of all that I amar (spoke) to the ayashah (woman / wife) let her beware.

She may not akal (eat) of anything that yatzaa (go out / come out) of the gapan (vine), neither let her shathah (drinks) yayan (wine) or strong shathah (drinks), nor akal (eat) any tamaah (unclean) thing; all that I tzawah (commanded) her let her shamar (keep/guard)."
Manawach (Manoah) amar (spoke) to the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah, "Please, let us itzar (detain) you, that we may make a young goat ready for you."

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah amar (spoke) to Manawach (Manoah), "Though you itzar (detain) me, I won't akal (eat) of your lacham (bread); and if you will ishah (make) a burnt ishah (make), you must ishah (make) it to Yahawah." For Manawach (Manoah) didn't yadai (know) that he was the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah.
Manawach (Manoah) amar (spoke) to the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah, "What is your sham (name), that when your dabar (word / matter) happen, we may honor you?"
The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, "Why do you shaal (ask) about my sham (name), since it is palaay (wonderful)?"

So Manawach (Manoah) laqach (take / seize) the young goat with the meal manachah (offering), and ilah (go up / offer) it on the tzawar (rock) to Yahawah. Then the angel ishah (make) a palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) thing as Manawach (Manoah) and his ayashah (woman / wife) raah (see) on.

For it happened, when the lahab (flame) ilah (go up / offer) up toward the sky from off the mazabach (altar), that the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah ilah (go up / offer) in the lahab (flame) of the mazabach (altar): and Manawach (Manoah) and his ayashah (woman / wife) raah (see) on; and they fell on their panayam (face) to the aratz (Earth/land).

But the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah didn't raah (see) to Manawach (Manoah) or to his ayashah (woman / wife) any more. Then Manawach (Manoah) yadai (knew) that he was the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah.
Manawach (Manoah) amar (spoke) to his ayashah (woman / wife), "We shall mawath (death) mawath (death), because we raah (see) seen Alahayam."

But his ayashah (woman / wife) amar (spoke) to him, "If Yahawah were chapatz (pleased) to mawath (death) us, he wouldn't have laqach (take / seize) a burnt ilah (offering) and a meal ilah (offering) at our yad (hand), neither would he raah (see) shown us all these things, nor would at this ith (time) have shamai (hearken / hear) such things as these."
The ayashah (woman / wife) yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son), and qaraa (called) him Shamashawan (Samson): and the nair (child) gadal (grew), and Yahawah barak (blessed) him.
The rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah chalal (began) to paim (move) him in Mahaneh Dan (Dan), between Tzaraih (Zorah) and Ashathaal (Eshtaol).
Shamashawan (Samson) yarad (went) down to Thamanah (Timnah), and raah (see) a ayashah (woman / wife) in Thamanah (Timnah) of the banawath (daughters) of the Palashathay (Philistines).

He ilah (go up / offer) up, and nagad (told) his ab (father) and his am (mother), and said, "I raah (see) seen a ayashah (woman / wife) in Thamanah (Timnah) of the banawath (daughters) of the Palashathay (Philistines): now therefore laqach (take / seize) her for me as ayashah (woman / wife)."

Then his ab (father) and his am (mother) amar (spoke) to him, "Is there ayan (NO ONE) a ayashah (woman / wife) among the banawath (daughters) of your ach (brother/kinsman), or among all my im (nation / people), that you halak (move) to laqach (take / seize) a ayashah (woman / wife) of the iral (uncircumcised) Palashathay (Philistines)?" Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke) to his ab (father), "laqach (take / seize) her for me; for she yashar (upright) me well."

But his ab (father) and his am (mother) didn't yadai (know) that it was of Yahawah; for he baqash (sought) an thaanah (occasion) against the Palashathay (Philistines). Now at that ith (time) the Palashathay (Philistines) mashal (rule/have dominion) rule over Yashar-Al (Israel).

Then yarad (went) Shamashawan (Samson) down, and his ab (father) and his am (mother), to Thamanah (Timnah), and bawaa (come) to the karamay (vineyards) of Thamanah (Timnah): and behold, a young aray (lion) shaag (roared) qaraah (against) him.

The rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah tzalach (came) mightily on him, and he tore him as he would have torn a young goat; and he had maawamah (nothing) in his yad (hand): but he didn't nagad (tell) his ab (father) or his am (mother) what he ishah (make) done.
He yarad (went) down, and dabar (word / matter) with the ayashah (woman / wife), and she yashar (upright) Shamashawan (Samson) well.

After a yawam (day) he shawab (turn back / repent) to laqach (take / seize) her; and he shawab (turn back / repent) sawar (aside) to raah (see) the carcass of the aray (lion): and raah (see), there was a idah (swarm) of dabawarayam (bees) in the gawayah (corpse) of the aray (lion), and dabash (honey).

He radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) it into his kap (hands), and yalak (went) on, akal (eat) as he halak (move); and he came to his ab (father) and am (mother), and nathan (give) to them, and they akal (eat): but he didn't nagad (tell) them that he radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) taken the dabash (honey) out of the gawayah (corpse) of the aray (lion).
His ab (father) yarad (went) down to the ayashah (woman / wife): and Shamashawan (Samson) ishah (make) there a mashathah (feast); for so used the bachawar (young) men to ishah (make).
It happened, when they raah (see) him, that they laqach (take / seize) shalawashayam (thirty) maraiyam (companions) to be with him.

Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke) to them, "Let me tell you a chayadah (riddle) now. If you can nagad (declare) it to me within the shabai (seven) yamay (days) of the mashathah (feast), and matzaa (find) it out, then I will nathan (give) you shalawashayam (thirty) sadayan (linen) garments and shalawashayam (thirty) chalapath (changes) of bagad (clothing);

But if you can't nagad (declare) it to me, then you shall nathan (give) me shalawashayam (thirty) sadayan (linen) garments and shalawashayam (thirty) chalayapawath (changes) of bagad (clothing)." They amar (spoke) to him, "chawad (put) forth your chayadah (riddle), that we may shamai (hearken / hear) it."

He amar (spoke) to them, "Out of the eater yatzaa (go out / come out) forth maakal (food). Out of the iz (strong) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth sweetness." They couldn't in shalawash (three) yamayam (days) nagad (declare) the chayadah (riddle).

It happened on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), that they amar (spoke) to Shamashawan (Samson's) ayashah (woman / wife), "pathah (entice) your ayash (man / husband), that he may nagad (declare) to us the chayadah (riddle), lest we sharap (burn) you and your ab (father) bayath (house) with ash (fire). Have you qaraa (called) us to impoverish us? Is it not so?"

Shamashawan (Samson's) ayashah (woman / wife) bakah (wept) before him, and amar (spoke), "You just shanaa (hate) me, and don't ahab (love) me. You have chawad (put) forth a chayadah (riddle) to the banay (children) of my im (nation / people), and haven't nagad (told) it me." He said to her, "Behold, I haven't amar (spoke) it my ab (father) nor my am (mother), and shall I nagad (tell) you?"

She bakah (wept) before him the shabai (seven) yamayam (days), while their mashathah (feast) hayah (came to pass): and it happened on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), that he nagad (told) her, because she tzawaq (pressed) him severely; and she nagad (told) the chayadah (riddle) to the banay (children) of her im (nation / people).

The anashay (men) of the iyar (city) amar (spoke) to him on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) before the charas (sun) bawaa (come) down, "What is sweeter than dabash (honey)? What is stronger than a aray (lion)?" He amar (spoke) to them, "If you hadn't charash (plowed) with my igalah (heifer), you wouldn't matzaa (have) found out my chayadah (riddle)."

The rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah tzalach (came) mightily on him, and he yarad (went) down to Ashaqalawan (Ashkelon), and nakah (struck) shalawashayam (thirty) ayash (man / husband) of them, and took their spoil, and nathan (give) the chalayapawath (changes) of clothing to those who nagad (declared) the chayadah (riddle). His ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger), and he ilah (go up / offer) up to his ab (father) bayath (house).
But Shamashawan (Samson's) ayashah (woman / wife) was given to his marai (companion), whom he had used as his raih (friend).

But it happened after a yawam (day), in the time of chatah (wheat) qatzayar (harvest), that Shamashawan (Samson) paqad (visit) his ayashah (woman / wife) with a young goat; and he amar (spoke), "I will bawaa (come) in to my ayashah (woman / wife) into the room." But her ab (father) wouldn't allow him to bawaa (come) in.

Her ab (father) amar (spoke), "I most certainly amar (spoke) that you had shanaa (hate) shanaa (hate) her; therefore I nathan (give) her to your marai (companion). Isn't her younger achawath (sister) more tawab (good / proper function) than she? Please take her, instead."
Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke) to them, "paim (this) time I will be naqah (clean/innocent) in regard of the Palashathay (Philistines), when I rai (harm) them."

Shamashawan (Samson) yalak (went) and lakad (caught) shalawash (three) maah (hundred) foxes, and laqach (take / seize) torches, and panah (turn) zanab (tail) to zanab (tail), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) a lapayad (torch) in the thawak (midst) between every shanayam (two) zanabawath (tails).

When he had bair (set) the lapayadayam (brands) on ash (fire), he shalach (send) them go into the standing grain of the Palashathay (Philistines), and burnt up both the gadayash (shocks) and the standing grain, and also the zayath (olive) groves.

Then the Palashathay (Philistines) amar (spoke), "Who ishah (make) done this?" They amar (spoke), "Shamashawan (Samson), the son-in-law of the Thamanay (Timnite), because he has laqach (take / seize) his ayashah (woman / wife), and nathan (give) her to his marai (companion)." The Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up, and burnt her and her ab (father) with ash (fire).
Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke) to them, "If you behave like zaath (this), naqam (surely) I will be avenged of you, and achar (other) that I will chadal (cease)."

He nakah (struck) them shawaq (hip) and yarak (thigh) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) makah (slaughter): and he yarad (went) down and lived in the cleft of the salai (rock) of Iyatam (Etam).
Then the Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up, and chanah (encamped) in Yahawadah (Judah), and natash (spread) themselves in Lachay (Lehi).

The ayash (man / husband) of Yahawadah (Judah) amar (spoke), "Why have you ilah (go up / offer) up amar (spoke) us?" They said, "We have ilah (go up / offer) up to asar (bind) Shamashawan (Samson), to ishah (make) to him as he ishah (make) done to us."

Then shalawash (three) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband) of Yahawadah (Judah) yarad (went) down to the cleft of the salai (rock) of Iyatam (Etam), and amar (spoke) to Shamashawan (Samson), "Don't you yadai (know) that the Palashathay (Philistines) are mashalayam (rulers) over us? What then is this that you ishah (make) done to us?" He amar (spoke) to them, "As they ishah (make) to me, so ishah (make) I done to them."

They amar (spoke) to him, "We have yarad (come) down to asar (bind) you, that we may nathan (give) you into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines)." Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke) to them, "shabai (swear / take oath) to me that you will not pagai (fall) on me yourselves."

They amar (spoke) to him, amar (spoke), "No; but we will asar (bind) you asar (fast), and nathan (give) you into their yad (hand); but mawath (death) we will not mawath (death) you." They asar (bound) him with shanayam (two) chadash (new) ibathayam (ropes), and ilah (go up / offer) him up from the salai (rock).

When he bawaa (come) to Lachay (Lehi), the Palashathay (Philistines) rawai (shouted) as they met him: and the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah tzalach (came) mightily on him, and the ibathayam (ropes) that were on his zarawai (arms) became as pashathah (flax) that was burnt with ash (fire), and his asawar (bands) dropped from off his yad (hand).
He matzaa (found) a fresh jawbone of a donkey, and shalach (send) forth his yad (hand), and laqach (take / seize) it, and nakah (struck) a alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband) therewith.

Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke), "With the jawbone of a donkey, chamarathayam (heaps) on chamarathayam (heaps); with the jawbone of a donkey I have nakah (struck) a alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband)."

It happened, when he kalah (complete / finish) made an end of dabar (word / matter), that he shalak (cast) away the jawbone out of his yad (hand); and that maqawam (place) was qaraa (called) Ramathalachay (Ramath Lehi).

He was very tzamaa (thirsty), and qaraa (called) on Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "You nathan (give) given this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thashawaih (deliverance) by the yad (hand) of your ibad (servant); and now shall I mawath (death) for tzamaa (thirst), and napal (fall / be cast down) into the yad (hand) of the iral (uncircumcised)?"

But Alahayam split the makathash (hollow) place that is in Lehi, and mayam (Waters) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of it. When he had shathah (drinks), his rawach (spirit / wind) shawab (turn back / repent) again, and he chayah (revived): therefore its sham (name) was qaraa (called) Iyanahaqawaraa (En Hakkore), which is in Lachay (Lehi), to this yawam (day).
He shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel) in the yamay (days) of the Palashathay (Philistines) isharayam (twenty) shanah (years).
Shamashawan (Samson) yalak (went) to Izah (Gaza), and raah (see) there a prostitute, and bawaa (come) in to her.

The izathay (gazites) were amar (spoke), "Shamashawan (Samson) is here!" They surrounded him, and arab (laid) wait for him all layal (night) in the shair (gate) of the iyar (city), and were charash (quiet) all the layal (night), amar (spoke), "Wait until baqar (morning) awar (light), then we will harag (kill) him."

Shamashawan (Samson) shakab (lay) until chatzay (midnight), and qawam (rise up) at chatzay (midnight), and achaz (laid) hold of the dalathawath (doors) of the shair (gate) of the iyar (city), and the shanayam (two) mazawazawath (posts), and plucked them up, barayach (bar) and all, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them on his kathap (shoulders), and carried them up to the raash (head) of the har (mountain) that is panayam (face) Chabarawan (Hebron).
It came to pass afterward, that he ahab (love) a ayashah (woman / wife) in the nachal (stream / river) of Shawaraq (Sorek), whose sham (name) was Dalayalah (Delilah).

The saranay (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up to her, and amar (spoke) to her, "pathah (entice) him, and raah (see) in which his gadawal (very great/important/mighty) kach (strength / mighty / power) lies, and by what means we may yakal (prevail) against him, that we may asar (bind) him to inah (oppress / afflict) him; and we will ayash (man / husband) nathan (give) you eleven hundred pieces of kasap (silver)."

Dalayalah (Delilah) amar (spoke) to Shamashawan (Samson), "Please nagad (tell) me where your gadawal (very great/important/mighty) kach (strength / mighty / power) lies, and what you might be asar (bound) to inah (oppress / afflict) you."

Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke) to her, "If they asar (bind) me with shabai (seven) lach (green) yatharayam (cords) that were never charab (dried), then shall I become chalah (afflict), and be as another adam (man)."

Then the saranay (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up to her shabai (seven) lach (green) yatharayam (cords) which had not been charab (dried), and she asar (bound) him with them.

Now she had an arab (ambush) waiting in the chadar (inner) room. She amar (spoke) to him, "The Palashathay (Philistines) are on you, Shamashawan (Samson)!" He nathaq (broke) the yatharayam (cords), as a string of nairath (tow) is nathaq (broken) when it touches the ash (fire). So his kach (strength / mighty / power) was not yadai (known).

Dalayalah (Delilah) amar (spoke) to Shamashawan (Samson), "Behold, you have hathal (mocked) me, and dabar (word / matter) me kazabayam (lies): now please nagad (tell) me with which you might be asar (bound)."

He amar (spoke) to her, "If they only asar (bind) me with chadash (new) ibathayam (ropes) with which no malaakah (work) has been done, then shall I become chalah (afflict), and be as another adam (man)."

So Dalayalah (Delilah) laqach (take / seize) chadash (new) ibathayam (ropes), and asar (bound) him therewith, and amar (spoke) to him, "The Palashathay (Philistines) are on you, Shamashawan (Samson)!" The arab (ambush) was waiting in the chadar (inner) room. He nathaq (broke) them off his zarawai (arms) like a chawat (thread).

Dalayalah (Delilah) amar (spoke) to Shamashawan (Samson), "Until hanah (here), you have hathal (mocked) me and dabar (word / matter) me kazabayam (lies). Nagad (tell) me with what you might be asar (bound)." He amar (spoke) to her, "If you weave the shabai (seven) machalapawath (locks) of my raash (head) with the masakath (web)."

She thaqai (blow / sound alarm) it with the yathad (pin), and amar (spoke) to him, "The Palashathay (Philistines) are on you, Shamashawan (Samson)!" He awakened out of his shanah (sleep), and plucked nasai (away) the yathad (pin) of the arag (beam), and the masakath (web).

She amar (spoke) to him, "ayak (how) can you amar (spoke), ‘I ahab (love) you,' when your lab (heart) is not with me? You have hathal (mocked) me these shalawash (three) paimayam (times), and have not nagad (told) me where your gadawal (very great/important/mighty) kach (strength / mighty / power) lies."
It happened, when she tzawaq (pressed) him yawam (day) with her dabar (word / matter), and alatz (urged) him, that his napash (soul) was qatzar (troubled) to mawath (death).

He nagad (told) her all his lab (heart), and said to her, "No mawarah (razor) has ever ilah (go up / offer) on my raash (head); for I have been a Nazirite to Alahayam from my am (mother) batan (womb). If I am galach (shaved), then my kach (strength / mighty / power) will sawar (go) from me, and I will become chalah (afflict), and be like any other adam (man)."

When Dalayalah (Delilah) raah (see) that he had nagad (told) her all his lab (heart), she shalach (send) and qaraa (called) for the saranay (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines), amar (spoke), "ilah (go up / offer) up paim (this) once, for he has nagad (told) me all his lab (heart)." Then the saranay (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up to her, and ilah (go up / offer) the kasap (money) in their yad (hand).

She made him sleep on her barak (blessed); and she qaraa (called) for a ayash (man / husband), and galach (shaved) off the shabai (seven) machalapawath (locks) of his raash (head); and she chalal (began) to inah (oppress / afflict) him, and his kach (strength / mighty / power) sawar (went) from him.

She amar (spoke), "The Palashathay (Philistines) are upon you, Shamashawan (Samson)!" He awoke out of his shanah (sleep), and amar (spoke), "I will yatzaa (go out / come out) out as at other paim (times), and nair (shake) myself free." But he didn't yadai (know) that Yahawah had sawar (departed) from him.

The Palashathay (Philistines) achaz (laid) hold on him, and naqar (put) out his iyan (eye); and they yarad (brought) him down to Izah (Gaza), and asar (bound) him with nachashathayam (fetters) of brass; and he tachan (ground) at the mill in the asar (prison).
However the shair (hair) of his raash (head) chalal (began) to tzamach (grow) again ashar (who/that) he was galach (shaved).

The saranay (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) asap (gathered) them together to zabach (offer) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) zabach (sacrifice) to Dagawan (Dagon) their Alahayam, and to shamachah (rejoice); for they amar (spoke), "Our Alahayam nathan (give) delivered Shamashawan (Samson) our ayab (enemy) into our yad (hand)."

When the im (nation / people) raah (see) him, they halal (praise) their Alahayam; for they amar (spoke), "Our Alahayam nathan (give) delivered our ayab (enemy) and the charab (destroyer) of our aratz (Earth/land), who has chalal (slain) many of us, into our yad (hand)."

It happened, when their lab (heart) were tawab (good / proper function), that they amar (spoke), "qaraa (called) for Shamashawan (Samson), that he may entertain us." They qaraa (called) for Shamashawan (Samson) out of the bayath (house); and he performed panayam (face) them. They imad (set) him between the imawadayam (pillars);

And Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke) to the nair (boy) who chazaq (held) him by the yad (hand), "Allow me to yamash (feel) the imadayam (pillars) whereupon the bayath (house) kawan (rests), that I may shain (lean) on them."

Now the bayath (house) was malaa (full) of anashayam (men) and nashayam (women); and all the saranay (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) were there; and there were on the gag (roof) about shalawash (three) alap (thousand) anashayam (men) and nashayam (women), who raah (see) while Shamashawan (Samson) performed.

Shamashawan (Samson) qaraa (called) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "Adawan Yahawah, zakar (remember) me, please, and chazaq (strengthen) me, please, only paim (this) once, Alahayam, that I may be at paim (once) naqam (avenged) of the Palashathay (Philistines) for my shanayam (two) iyan (eye)."

Shamashawan (Samson) lapath (took) hold of the shanayam (two) thawak (midst) imawaday (pillars) on which the bayath (house) rested, and leaned on them, the achad (one) with his right yamayan (right hand), and the other with his shamaawal (left hand).

Shamashawan (Samson) amar (spoke), "Let me mawath (death) with the Palashathay (Philistines)!" He natah (bowed) himself with all his kach (strength / mighty / power); and the bayath (house) napal (fall / be cast down) on the saranayam (lords), and on all the im (nation / people) who were therein. So the mawath (death) that he mawath (death) at his mawath (death) were more than those who he mawath (death) in his chay (life).

Then his ach (brother/kinsman) and all the bayath (house) of his ab (father) yarad (came) down, and nashaa (lift) him, and ilah (go up / offer) him up, and qabar (bury) him between Tzaraih (Zorah) and Ashathaal (Eshtaol) in the burial site of Manawach (Manoah) his ab (father). He shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel) isharayam (twenty) shanah (years).
There was a ayash (man / husband) of the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), whose sham (name) was Mayakahaw (Micah).

He amar (spoke) to his am (mother), "The eleven hundred pieces of kasap (silver) that were laqach (take / seize) from you, about which you uttered a alah (swear / adjure), and also amar (spoke) it in my azan (ear), behold, the kasap (silver) is with me; I laqach (take / seize) it." His am (mother) amar (spoke), "barak (blessed) be my ban (son) of Yahawah."

He shawab (turn back / repent) the eleven hundred pieces of kasap (silver) to his am (mother); and his am (mother) amar (spoke), "I most certainly qadash (set apart / make holy) the kasap (silver) to Yahawah from my yad (hand) for my ban (son), to ishah (make) an engraved pasal (image) and a molten pasal (image). Now therefore I will shawab (turn back / repent) it to you."

When he shawab (turn back / repent) the kasap (money) to his am (mother), his am (mother) laqach (take / seize) two maah (hundred) pieces of kasap (silver), and nathan (give) them to the tzarap (founder), who ishah (make) of it an engraved pasal (image) and a masakah (molten) image: and it was in the bayath (house) of Mayakahaw (Micah).

The ayash (man / husband) Mayakah (Micah) had a bayath (house) of Alahayam, and he ishah (make) an apawad (ephod), and tharapayam (teraphim), and malaa (consecrated) achad (one) of his ban (son), who became his kahan (priest).
In those yamayam (days) there was no malak (king) in Yashar-Al (Israel): every ayash (man / husband) ishah (make) that which was yashar (upright) in his own iyan (eye).
There was a nair (young) man out of Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem Judah), of the mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) of Yahawadah (Judah), who was a Lawayay (Levite); and he lived there.

The ayash (man / husband) departed out of the iyar (city), out of Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem Judah), to live where he could matzaa (find) a place, and he bawaa (come) to the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim) to the bayath (house) of Mayakah (Micah), as he traveled.

Mayakah (Micah) amar (spoke) to him, "ayan (NO ONE) did you bawaa (come) from?" He amar (spoke) to him, "I am a Lawayay (Levite) of Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem Judah), and I am looking for a halak (move) to live."

Mayakah (Micah) amar (spoke) to him, "yashab (inhabit/dwell) with me, and be to me a ab (father) and a kahan (priest), and I will nathan (give) you ishar (ten) pieces of kasap (silver) per yawam (day), a irak (suit) of bagad (clothing), and your food." So the Lawayay (Levite) yalak (went) in.
The Lawayay (Levite) was yaal (content) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) with the ayash (man / husband); and the young ayash (man / husband) was to him as nair (one) of his ban (son).
Mayakah (Micah) malaa (consecrated) the Lawayay (Levite), and the nair (young) man became his kahan (priest), and was in the bayath (house) of Mayakah (Micah).
Then Mayakah (Micah) amar (spoke), "Now yadai (know) I that Yahawah will do yatab (good) to me, since I have a Lawayay (Levite) to my kahan (priest)."

In those yamayam (days) there was no malak (king) in Yashar-Al (Israel): and in those yamayam (days) the shabat (tribe) of the Danay (Danites) baqash (sought) an nachalah (inheritance) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) in; for to that yawam (day), their nachalah (inheritance) napal (fall / be cast down) not fallen to them thawak (midst) the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

The banay (children) of Dan (Dan) shalach (send) of their mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) chamash (five) banay (men) from their whole number, banay (men) of valor, from Tzaraih (Zorah), and from Ashathaal (Eshtaol), to ragal (spy) out the aratz (Earth/land), and to chaqar (search) it; and they amar (spoke) to them, "yalak (go), explore the aratz (Earth/land)!" They bawaa (come) to the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), to the bayath (house) of Mayakah (Micah), and lawan (lodged) there.

When they were by the bayath (house) of Mayakah (Micah), they nakar (knew) the qawal (sound / voice) of the nair (young) man the Lawayay (Levite); and they sawar (turned) aside there, and amar (spoke) to him, "Who bawaa (come) you here? What ishah (make) you do in this place? What do you have here?"
He amar (spoke) to them, "zah (this / that / these) and zah (this / that / these) has Mayakah (Micah) dealt with me, and he has shakar (hired) me, and I am become his kahan (priest)."
They amar (spoke) to him, "Please ask shaal (counsel) of Alahayam, that we may yadai (know) whether our darak (way) which we halak (move) shall be prosperous."
The kahan (priest) amar (spoke) to them, "yalak (go) in shalawam (peace / safety). Your darak (way) in which you yalak (go) is nakach (before) Yahawah."

Then the chamash (five) anashayam (men) departed, and bawaa (come) to Layash (Laish), and raah (see) the im (nation / people) who were qarab (among / near), how they lived in security, in the mashapat (way) of the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), shaqat (quiet) and batach (secure); for there was none in the aratz (Earth/land), yarash (possessing) authority, that might kalam (put) them to shame in anything, and they were rachawaq (far) from the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), and had no dealings with any adam (man).
They bawaa (come) to their ach (brother/kinsman) to Tzaraih (Zorah) and Ashathaal (Eshtaol): and their ach (brother/kinsman) amar (spoke) to them, "What do you say?"

They amar (spoke), "qawam (rise up), and let us ilah (go up / offer) up against them; for we raah (see) seen the aratz (Earth/land), and behold, it is very tawab (good / proper function). Do you stand still? Don't be itzal (slothful) to yalak (go) and to bawaa (come) in to yarash (possess) the aratz (Earth/land).

When you bawaa (come), you shall bawaa (come) to a batach (secure) im (nation / people), and the aratz (Earth/land) is rachab (large); for Alahayam nathan (give) given it into your yad (hand), a maqawam (place) where there is no machasawar (want) of anything that is in the aratz (Earth/land)."

There nasai (set) forth from there of the mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) of the Danay (Danites), out of Tzaraih (Zorah) and out of Ashathaal (Eshtaol), shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) girt with kalay (weapons) of malachamah (war).

They ilah (go up / offer) up, and chanah (encamped) in Kiriath Qarayath-Yairayam (Jearim), in Yahawadah (Judah): therefore they qaraa (called) that maqawam (place) Machanahadan (Mahaneh Dan), to this yawam (day); behold, it is achar (other) Kiriath Qarayath-Yairayam (Jearim).
They ibar (pass over/through) there to the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), and bawaa (come) to the bayath (house) of Mayakah (Micah).

Then the chamash (five) anashayam (men) who halak (move) to ragal (spy) out the aratz (Earth/land) of Layash (Laish) inah (answer / respond), and amar (spoke) to their ach (brother/kinsman), "Do you yadai (know) that there is in these bathayam (houses) an apawad (ephod), and tharapayam (teraphim), and an engraved pasal (image), and a masakah (molten) image? Now therefore yadai (consider) what you ishah (make) to do."

They sawar (turned) aside there, and bawaa (come) to the bayath (house) of the nair (young) man the Lawayay (Levite), even to the bayath (house) of Mayakah (Micah), and shaal (asked) him of his welfare.

The shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) girt with their kalay (weapons) of malachamah (war), who were of the banay (children) of Dan (Dan), natzab (stood) by the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate).

The chamash (five) anashayam (men) who halak (move) to ragal (spy) out the aratz (Earth/land) ilah (go up / offer) up, and bawaa (come) in there, and laqach (take / seize) the engraved pasayal (image), and the apawad (ephod), and the tharapayam (teraphim), and the masakah (molten) image: and the kahan (priest) natzab (stood) by the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate) with the shash (six) maah (hundred) anashayam (men) girt with kalay (weapons) of malachamah (war).

When these bawaa (come) into Mayakah (Micah's) bayath (house), and laqach (take / seize) the engraved pasal (image), the apawad (ephod), and the tharapayam (teraphim), and the masakah (molten) image, the kahan (priest) amar (spoke) to them, "What are you ishah (make)?"

They amar (spoke) to him, "Hold your charash (peace), put your yad (hand) on your pah (mouth), and yalak (go) with us, and be to us a ab (father) and a kahan (priest). Is it tawab (good / proper function) for you to be kahan (priest) to the bayath (house) of achad (one) ayash (man / husband), or to be kahan (priest) to a shabat (tribe) and a mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) in Yashar-Al (Israel)?"

The kahan (priest) lab (heart) was yatab (glad), and he laqach (take / seize) the apawad (ephod), and the tharapayam (teraphim), and the engraved pasal (image), and bawaa (come) in the qarab (among / near) of the im (nation / people).
So they panah (turn) and departed, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the little tap (ones) and the livestock and the kabawadah (goods) panayam (face) them.

When they were a rachaq (good) way from the bayath (house) of Mayakah (Micah), the anashayam (men) who were in the bathayam (houses) near to Mayakah (Micah's) bayath (house) were zaiq (gathered) together, and overtook the banay (children) of Dan (Dan).
They qaraa (called) to the banay (children) of Dan (Dan). They sabab (turned) their panayam (face), and amar (spoke) to Mayakah (Micah), "What ails you, that you zaiq (come) with such a company?"

He amar (spoke), "You have laqach (take / seize) away my Alahayam which I ishah (make), and the kahan (priest), and have yalak (gone) away, and what more do I have? How then do you amar (spoke) to me, ‘What ails you?'"

The banay (children) of Dan (Dan) amar (spoke) to him, "Don't let your qawal (sound / voice) be shamai (hearken / hear) among us, lest mar (angry) anashayam (fellows) pagai (fall) on you, and you asap (lose) your napash (soul), with the lives of your bayath (house)."

The banay (children) of Dan (Dan) yalak (went) their darak (way): and when Mayakah (Micah) raah (see) that they were too chazaq (strong) for him, he panah (turn) and shawab (turn back / repent) back to his bayath (house).

They laqach (take / seize) that which Mayakah (Micah) ishah (make) made, and the kahan (priest) whom he bawaa (come), and came to Layash (Laish), to a im (nation / people) shaqat (quiet) and batach (secure), and nakah (struck) them with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword); and they burnt the iyar (city) with ash (fire).

There was no deliverer, because it was rachawaq (far) from Tzayadawan (Sidon), and they had no dealings with any adam (man); and it was in the imaq (valley) that lies by Bayatharachawab (Beth Rehob). They banah (build) the iyar (city), and lived therein.

They qaraa (called) the sham (name) of the iyar (city) Dan (Dan), after the sham (name) of Dan (Dan) their ab (father), who was yalad (birth / begot) to Yashar-Al (Israel): however the sham (name) of the iyar (city) was Layash (Laish) at the raashawan (first).

The banay (children) of Dan (Dan) qawam (rise up) up for themselves the engraved pasal (image): and Yawanathan (Jonathan), the ban (son) of Garasham (Gershom), the ban (son) of Manashah (Moses), he and his banay (sons) were kahanayam (priests) to the shabat (tribe) of the Danay (Danites) until the yawam (day) of the captivity of the aratz (Earth/land).
So they shawam (place / establish / appoint) them up Mayakah (Micah's) engraved pasal (image) which he ishah (make), all the yawam (day) that the bayath (house) of Alahayam was in Shayalah (Shiloh).

It happened in those yamayam (days), when there was no malak (king) in Yashar-Al (Israel), that there was a ayash (man / husband) Lawayay (Levite) living on the farther yarakah (side) of the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), who laqach (take / seize) to him a concubine out of Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem Judah).

His payalagash (concubine) zanah (played) the prostitute against him, and yalak (went) away from him to her ab (father) bayath (house) to Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem Judah), and was there the space of arabai (four) chadashayam (months).

Her ayash (man / husband) qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) achar (other) her, to dabar (word / matter) lab (heart) to her, to shawab (turn back / repent) her again, having his nair (servant) with him, and a tzamad (couple) of donkeys: and she bawaa (come) him into her ab (father) bayath (house); and when the ab (father) of the nairah (young) lady raah (see) him, he shamach (rejoiced) to qaraah (meet) him.

His father-in-law, the nairah (young) lady's ab (father), chazaq (retained) him; and he stayed with him shalawash (three) yamayam (days): so they akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and lawan (lodged) there.

It happened on the rabayaiy (fourth) yawam (day), that they arose shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and he qawam (rise up) up to depart: and the nairah (young) lady's ab (father) amar (spoke) to his son-in-law, "said (strengthen) your lab (heart) with a path (morsel) of lacham (bread), and afterward you shall go your yalak (way)."

So they yashab (inhabit/dwell) down, akal (eat), and shathah (drinks), shanayam (two) of them yachad (together): and the nairah (young) lady's ab (father) amar (spoke) to the ayash (man / husband), "yaal (please) be pleased to stay all lawan (night), and let your lab (heart) be yatab (merry)."
The ayash (man / husband) qawam (rise up) up to depart; but his father-in-law patzar (urged) him, and he lawan (lodged) there again.

He arose shakam (early) in the baqar (morning) on the chamayashay (fifth) yawam (day) to depart; and the nairah (young) lady's ab (father) amar (spoke), "Please said (strengthen) your labab (heart) and mahah (stay) until the yawam (day) declines;" and they shanayam (two) akal (eat).

When the ayash (man / husband) qawam (rise up) up to depart, he, and his payalagash (concubine), and his nair (servant), his father-in-law, the nairah (young) lady's ab (father), amar (spoke) to him, "Behold, now the yawam (day) rapah (draws) toward irab (evening), please stay all lawan (night): behold, the yawam (day) chanah (grows) to an end, lawan (lodge) here, that your labab (heart) may be yatab (merry); and machar (tomorrow) go on your darak (way) shakam (early), that you may halak (move) ahal (home)."

But the ayash (man / husband) wouldn't stay that lawan (night), but he qawam (rise up) up and departed, and bawaa (come) over nakach (against) Yabawas (Jebus) (the same is Yarawashalam (Jerusalem)): and there were with him a tzamad (couple) of donkeys chabash (saddled); his payalagash (concubine) also was with him.

When they were by Yabawas (Jebus), the yawam (day) was maad (far) radad (spent); and the nair (servant) amar (spoke) to his adawan (master / lord), "Please yalak (come) and let us sawar (turn) aside into this iyar (city) of the Yabawasay (Jebusites), and lawan (lodge) in it."

His adawan (master / lord) amar (spoke) to him, "We won't sawar (turn) aside into the iyar (city) of a nakaray (foreigner), that is not of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel); but we will ibar (pass over/through) over to Gabaih (Gibeah)."

He amar (spoke) to his nair (servant), "yalak (come) and let us qarab (come close) near to achad (one) of these maqamawath (places); and we will lawan (lodge) in Gabaih (Gibeah), or in Ramah (Ramah)."
So they ibar (pass over/through) on and went their yalak (way); and the shamash (sun) bawaa (come) down on them atzal (near) to Gabaih (Gibeah), which belongs to Banayamayan (Benjamin).

They sawar (turned) aside there, to bawaa (come) in to lawan (lodge) in Gabaih (Gibeah): and he bawaa (come) in, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) him down in the rachab (street) of the iyar (city); for there was no ayash (man / husband) who asap (took) them into his bayath (house) to lawan (lodge).

Behold, there bawaa (come) an zaqan (old) ayash (man / husband) from his maishah (work) out of the shadah (field) at irab (evening): now the ayash (man / husband) was of the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), and he lived in Gabaih (Gibeah); but the anashay (men) of the maqawam (place) were Banayamayanay (Benjamites).

He nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye), and raah (see) the arach (wayfaring) ayash (man / husband) in the rachab (street) of the iyar (city); and the zaqan (old) ayash (man / husband) amar (spoke), "Where are you yalak (going)? Ayan (NO ONE) did you bawaa (come) from?"

He amar (spoke) to him, "We are ibar (pass over/through) from Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem Judah) to the farther yarakah (side) of the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim). I am from there, and I yalak (went) to Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem Judah). I am halak (move) to the bayath (house) of Yahawah; and there is no ayash (man / husband) who asap (takes) me into his bayath (house).

Yet there is both thaban (straw) and masapawaa (provender) for our donkeys; and there is lacham (bread) and yayan (wine) also for me, and for your handmaid, and for the nair (young) man who is with your ibad (servant): there is no machasawar (want) of anything."

The zaqan (old) ayash (man / husband) amar (spoke), "shalawam (peace / safety) be to you; raq (concept: what comes out / spittle) let all your machasawar (wants) lawan (lie) on me; only don't lodge in the rachab (street)."
So he bawaa (come) him into his bayath (house), and gave the donkeys fodder; and they rachatz (washed) their ragal (feet / foot), and akal (eat) and shathah (drinks).

As they were making their lab (heart) yatab (merry), behold, the anashay (men) of the iyar (city), ayash (man / husband) base anashay (fellows), surrounded the bayath (house), dapaq (beating) at the dalath (door); and they amar (spoke) to the bail (master) of the bayath (house), the zaqan (old) ayash (man / husband), amar (spoke), "yatzaa (go out / come out) out the ayash (man / husband) who bawaa (come) into your bayath (house), that we may yadai (have) sex with him!"

The ayash (man / husband), the bail (master) of the bayath (house), yatzaa (go out / come out) out to them, and amar (spoke) to them, "No, my ach (brother/kinsman), please don't act so wickedly; achar (other) this ayash (man / husband) bawaa (come) come into my bayath (house), don't ishah (make) this nabalah (folly).

Behold, here is my bathawalah (virgin) banath (daughter) and his payalagash (concubine). I will yatzaa (go out / come out) them out now. Inah (oppress / afflict) them, and ishah (make) with them what seems tawab (good / proper function) to you; but to this ayash (man / husband) don't ishah (make) any such nabalah (folly)."

But the anashayam (men) wouldn't shamai (hearken / hear) to him: so the ayash (man / husband) laid hold of his payalagash (concubine), and yatzaa (go out / come out) her out to them; and they yadai (had) sex with her, and ilal (abused) her all layal (night) until the baqar (morning): and when the shachar (day) began to ilah (go up / offer), they shalach (send) her go.

Then bawaa (come) the ayashah (woman / wife) in the panah (turn) of the baqar (morning), and napal (fall / be cast down) down at the pathach (door) of the ayash (man / husband) bayath (house) where her Adawan was, until it was awar (light).

Her Adawan qawam (rise up) up in the baqar (morning), and pathach (opened) the dalathawath (doors) of the bayath (house), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out to yalak (go) his darak (way); and behold, the ayashah (woman / wife) his payalagash (concubine) was napal (fall / be cast down) down at the pathach (door) of the bayath (house), with her yad (hand) on the sap (threshold).

He amar (spoke) to her, "qawam (rise up) up, and yalak (let) us be going!" But no ayash (man / husband) inah (answer / respond). Then he laqach (take / seize) her up on the donkey; and the ayash (man / husband) qawam (rise up) up, and went to his maqawam (place).

When he bawaa (come) come into his bayath (house), he laqach (take / seize) a maakalath (knife), and laid chazaq (hold) on his payalagash (concubine), and nathach (divided) her, limb by limb, into shanayam (two) nathachayam (pieces), and shalach (send) her throughout all the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

It was so, that all who raah (see) it amar (spoke), "There was no such deed done nor raah (see) from the yawam (day) that the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) to this yawam (day)! Shawam (place / establish / appoint) it, iwatz (take) counsel, and dabar (word / matter)."

Then all the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and the idah (congregation) was qahal (assembled) as achad (one) ayash (man / husband), from Dan (Dan) even to Baar-Shabai (Beersheba), with the aratz (Earth/land) of Galaid (Gilead), to Yahawah at Matzapah (Mizpah).

The panawath (chiefs) of all the im (nation / people), even of all the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel), yatzab (presented) themselves in the qahal (assembly) of the im (nation / people) of Alahayam, arabai (four) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) footmen who shalap (drew) charab (sword).

(Now the banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) shamai (hearken / hear) that the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) had ilah (go up / offer) up to Matzapah (Mizpah).) The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke), "dabar (word / matter) us, how hayah (came to pass) this rai (wickedness) happen?"

The Lawayay (Levite), the ayash (man / husband) of the ayashah (woman / wife) who was ratzach (murdered), inah (answer / respond), "I bawaa (come) into Gabaih (Gibeah) that belongs to Banayamayan (Benjamin), I and my payalagash (concubine), to lawan (lodge).

The bailay (men) of Gabaih (Gibeah) qawam (rise up) against me, and surrounded the bayath (house) by layal (night). They damah (thought) to have harag (kill) me, and they inah (oppress / afflict) my payalagash (concubine), and she is mawath (death).

I achaz (took) my payalagash (concubine), and nathach (cut) her in pieces, and shalach (send) her throughout all the shadah (country) of the nachalah (inheritance) of Yashar-Al (Israel); for they ishah (make) committed lewdness and nabalah (folly) in Yashar-Al (Israel).
Behold, you banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), all of you, yahab (give) here your dabar (word / matter) and itzah (counsel)."

All the im (nation / people) qawam (rise up) as achad (one) ayash (man / husband), amar (spoke), "ayash (man / husband) of us will yalak (go) to his ahal (tent), neither will any of us sawar (turn) to his bayath (house).
But now this is the thing which we will ishah (make) to Gabaih (Gibeah): we will go up against it by gawaral (lot);

And we will laqach (take / seize) ishar (ten) anashayam (men) of one maah (hundred) throughout all the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and one maah (hundred) of one alap (thousand), and a alap (thousand) out of rababah (ten) thousand, to laqach (take / seize) food for the im (nation / people), that they may ishah (make), when they bawaa (come) to Gabai (Gibeah) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), according to all the nabalah (folly) that they ishah (make) worked in Yashar-Al (Israel)."
So all the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) were asap (gathered) against the iyar (city), chabar (knit) together as achad (one) ayash (man / husband).

The shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shalach (send) anashayam (men) through all the shabat (tribe) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), amar (spoke), "What rai (wickedness) is this that is hayah (came to pass) among you?

Now therefore nathan (give) up the anashayam (men), the base fellows, who are in Gabaih (Gibeah), that we may put them to mawath (death), and bair (put) away rai (evil) from Yashar-Al (Israel)." But Banayamayan (Benjamin) would not shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of their ach (brother/kinsman) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

The banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) asap (gathered) themselves together out of the irayam (cities) to Gabaih (Gibeah), to yatzaa (go out / come out) out to malachamah (battle) against the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

The banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) were paqad (visit) on that yawam (day) out of the irayam (cities) isharayam (twenty) - shash (six) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband) who shalap (drew) the charab (sword), besides the yashabay (inhabitants) of Gabaih (Gibeah), who were paqad (visit) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) bachar (chosen) ayash (man / husband).

Among all this im (nation / people) there were shabai (seven) maah (hundred) bachar (chosen) ayash (man / husband) yad (hand); everyone could qalai (sling) aban (stone) at a hair-breadth, and not chataa (miss).

The ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel), besides Banayamayan (Benjamin), were paqad (visit) arabai (four) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband) who shalap (drew) charab (sword): all these were ayash (man / husband) of malachamah (war).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) qawam (rise up), and went up to Bethel, and shaal (asked) counsel of Alahayam; and they amar (spoke), "Who shall ilah (go up / offer) up for us thachalah (first) to malachamah (battle) against the banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin)?" Yahawah amar (spoke), "Yahawadah (Judah) thachalah (first)."
The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) qawam (rise up) up in the baqar (morning), and chanah (encamped) against Gabaih (Gibeah).

The ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to malachamah (battle) against Banayamayan (Benjamin); and the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) set the malachamah (battle) in irak (array) against them at Gabaih (Gibeah).

The banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of Gabaih (Gibeah), and shachath (destroyed) down to the aratz (Earth/land) of the Yashar-Al (Israelites) on that yawam (day) isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband).

The im (nation / people), the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel), chazaq (encouraged) themselves, and set the malachamah (battle) again in irak (array) in the maqawam (place) where they irak (set) themselves in array the raashawan (first) yawam (day).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up and bakah (wept) panayam (face) Yahawah until irab (evening); and they shaal (asked) of Yahawah, amar (spoke), "Shall I again nagash (draw) near to malachamah (battle) against the banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) my ach (brother/kinsman)?" Yahawah amar (spoke), "ilah (go up / offer) up against him."
The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) qarab (come close) near against the banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) the shanay (second) yawam (day).

Banayamayan (Benjamin) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth qaraah (against) them out of Gabaih (Gibeah) the shanay (second) yawam (day), and shachath (destroyed) down to the aratz (Earth/land) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) again eighteen alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband); all these shalap (drew) the charab (sword).

Then all the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and all the im (nation / people), ilah (go up / offer) up, and bawaa (come) to Bethel, and bakah (wept), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) there panayam (face) Yahawah, and tzawam (fasted) that yawam (day) until irab (evening); and they ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilawath (offerings) and peace ilawath (offerings) panayam (face) Yahawah.
The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shaal (asked) of Yahawah (for the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Alahayam was there in those yamayam (days),

And Payanachas (Phinehas), the ban (son) of Alaizar (Eleazar), the ban (son) of Aharawan (Aaron), imad (stood) panayam (face) it in those yamayam (days)), amar (spoke), "Shall I yet again yatzaa (go out / come out) out to malachamah (battle) against the banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) my ach (brother/kinsman), or shall I chadal (cease)?" Yahawah amar (spoke), "ilah (go up / offer) up; for machar (tomorrow) I will nathan (give) him into your yad (hand)."
Yashar-Al (Israel) shawam (place / establish / appoint) ambushes all around Gabaih (Gibeah).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up against the banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), and irak (set) themselves in array against Gabaih (Gibeah), as at other paim (times).

The banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) yatzaa (go out / come out) out qaraah (against) the im (nation / people), and were nathaq (drawn) away from the iyar (city); and they chalal (began) to nakah (strike) and chalal (kill) of the im (nation / people), as at other paim (times), in the masalawath (highways), of which achad (one) ilah (go up / offer) up to Bethel, and the other to Gabaih (Gibeah), in the shadah (field), about shalawashayam (thirty) ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

The banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) amar (spoke), "They are nagap (struck) down panayam (face) us, as at the raashawan (first)." But the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke), "Let us nawas (flee), and nathaq (draw) them away from the iyar (city) to the masalawath (highways)."

All the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) qawam (rise up) up out of their maqawam (place), and irak (set) themselves in array at Bailathamar (Baal Tamar): and the ambushers of Yashar-Al (Israel) gayach (broke) forth out of their maqawam (place), even out of Maareh Geba.

There bawaa (come) over nagad (against) Gabaih (Gibeah) ishar (ten) alap (thousand) bachar (chosen) ayash (man / husband) out of all Yashar-Al (Israel), and the malachamah (battle) was severe; but they didn't yadai (know) that rai (evil) was close on them.

Yahawah nagap (struck) Banayamayan (Benjamin) panayam (face) Yashar-Al (Israel); and the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shachath (destroyed) of banayamayan (benjamin) that yawam (day) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) one maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband): all these shalap (drew) the charab (sword).

So the banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) raah (see) that they were nagap (struck); for the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) nathan (give) maqawam (place) to banayamayan (benjamin), because they batach (trusted) the ambushers whom they had shawam (place / establish / appoint) against Gabaih (Gibeah).
The ambushers hurried, and pashat (rushed) on Gabaih (Gibeah); and the ambushers mashak (drew) themselves along, and nakah (struck) all the iyar (city) with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword).

Now the appointed mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) between the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) and the ambushers was that they should rabah (make) a great cloud of ishan (smoke) ilah (go up / offer) up out of the iyar (city).

The ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) hapak (turned) in the malachamah (battle), and Banayamayan (Benjamin) chalal (began) to nakah (strike) and chalal (kill) of the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) about shalawashayam (thirty) ayash (man / husband); for they amar (spoke), "nagap (surely) they are nagap (struck) down panayam (face) us, as in the raashawan (first) malachamah (battle)."

But when the cloud chalal (began) to arise up out of the iyar (city) in a imawad (pillar) of ishan (smoke), the Benjamites panah (turn) achar (other) them; and behold, the whole of the iyar (city) ilah (go up / offer) up in kalayal (smoke) to the sky.

The ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) hapak (turned), and the ayash (man / husband) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) were bahal (dismayed); for they raah (see) that rai (evil) had nagai (come) on them.

Therefore they panah (turn) their backs panayam (face) the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) to the darak (way) of the madabar (wilderness); but the malachamah (battle) dabaq (followed) hard after them; and those who came out of the irayam (cities) shachath (destroyed) them in its thawak (midst).
They surrounded the Benjamites, radap (chased) them, and darak (trod) them down at their manawachah (resting) place, as far as over nakach (against) Gabaih (Gibeah) toward the sunrise.
There napal (fall / be cast down) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) eighteen alap (thousand) anashay (men); all these were anashay (men) of valor.

They panah (turn) and nawas (fled) toward the madabar (wilderness) to the salai (rock) of Ramawan (Rimmon): and they ilal (gleaned) of them in the masalawath (highways) chamash (five) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband), and dabaq (followed) hard achar (other) them to Gadaim (Gidom), and nakah (struck) of them two alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband).

So that all who napal (fall / be cast down) that yawam (day) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) were isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) anashay (men) who shalap (drew) the charab (sword); all these were anashay (men) of valor.

But shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) panah (turn) and nawas (fled) toward the madabar (wilderness) to the salai (rock) of Ramawan (Rimmon), and stayed in the salai (rock) of Ramawan (Rimmon) arabai (four) chadashayam (months).

The ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shawab (turn back / repent) again on the banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), and nakah (struck) them with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), both the entire iyar (city), and the livestock, and all that they matzaa (found): moreover all the irayam (cities) which they matzaa (found) they shalach (send) on ash (fire).

Now the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) had shabai (swear / take oath) in Matzapah (Mizpah), amar (spoke), "There shall not any of us nathan (give) his banath (daughter) to Banayamayan (Benjamin) as ayashah (woman / wife)."

The im (nation / people) bawaa (come) to Bethel, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) there until irab (evening) panayam (face) Alahayam, and nashaa (lift) up their qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept) severely.

They amar (spoke), "Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), why has this happened in Yashar-Al (Israel), that there should be today achad (one) shabat (tribe) paqad (visit) in Yashar-Al (Israel)?"

It happened on the next macharath (day) that the im (nation / people) shakam (rose) early, and banah (build) there an mazabach (altar), and ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilawath (offerings) and peace ilawath (offerings).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke), "Who is there among all the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel) who didn't ilah (go up / offer) up in the qahal (assembly) to Yahawah?" For they had made a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shabawaih (oath) concerning him who didn't ilah (go up / offer) up to Yahawah to Matzapah (Mizpah), amar (spoke), "He shall mawath (death) be put to mawath (death)."
