The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) grieved for Banayamayan (Benjamin) their ach (brother/kinsman), and amar (spoke), "There is achad (one) shabat (tribe) gadai (cut) off from Yashar-Al (Israel) this yawam (day).
How shall we provide wives for those who yathar (remain), since we have shabai (swear / take oath) by Yahawah that we will not nathan (give) them of our banath (daughter) to wives?"

They amar (spoke), "What achad (one) is there of the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel) who didn't ilah (go up / offer) up to Yahawah to Matzapah (Mizpah)?" Behold, there bawaa (come) ayash (man / husband) to the machanah (camp) from Yabash (Jabesh Gilead) to the qahal (assembly).
For when the im (nation / people) were paqad (visit), behold, there were ayash (man / husband) of the yawashabay (inhabitants) of Yabash (Jabesh Gilead) there.

The idah (congregation) shalach (send) there shanayam (two) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband) of the most ban (son), and tzawah (commanded) them, amar (spoke), "yalak (go) and nakah (strike) the yawashabay (inhabitants) of Yabash (Jabesh Gilead) with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), with the nashayam (women) and the little tap (ones).
This is the thing that you shall ishah (make): you shall utterly charam (destroy) every zakar (remember), and every ayashah (woman / wife) who has lain with a yadai (man)."

They matzaa (found) among the yawashabay (inhabitants) of Yabash (Jabesh Gilead) arabai (four) maah (hundred) nairah (young) bathawalah (virgins), who yadai (had) not known ayash (man / husband) by lying with him; and they bawaa (come) them to the machanah (camp) to Shayalah (Shiloh), which is in the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan).

The whole idah (congregation) shalach (send) and dabar (word / matter) to the banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) who were in the salai (rock) of Ramawan (Rimmon), and qaraa (called) shalawam (peace / safety) to them.

Banayamayan (Benjamin) shawab (turn back / repent) at that ith (time); and they nathan (give) them the nashayam (women) whom they had chayah (saved) alive of the nashayam (women) of Yabash (Jabesh Gilead): and yet so they weren't matzaa (enough) for them.
The im (nation / people) grieved for Banayamayan (Benjamin), because that Yahawah ishah (make) made a paratz (breach) in the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Then the zaqanay (elders) of the idah (congregation) amar (spoke), "How shall we ishah (make) wives for those who yathar (remain), since the nashayam (women) are destroyed out of Banayamayan (Benjamin)?"
They amar (spoke), "There must be an yarashah (inheritance) for those who are palayatah (escaped) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), that a shabat (tribe) not be machah (blotted) out from Yashar-Al (Israel).

However we may not nathan (give) them wives of our banath (daughter), for the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) had shabai (swear / take oath), amar (spoke), ‘arar (cursed) is he who nathan (give) a ayashah (woman / wife) to Banayamayan (Benjamin).'"

They amar (spoke), "Behold, there is a chag (feast/festival) of Yahawah from yawam (day) to year in Shayalah (Shiloh), which is on the tzapawan (north) of Bayath-Al (Bethel), on the east tzapawan (side) of the masalah (highway) that ilah (go up / offer) up from Bayath-Al (Bethel) to Shakam (Shechem), and on the nagab (south) of Labawanah (Lebonah)."
They tzawah (commanded) the banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), amar (spoke), "yalak (go) and lie in arab (wait) in the karamayam (vineyards),

And raah (see), and behold, if the banawath (daughters) of Shayalah (Shiloh) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to chawal (dance) in the machalawath (dances), then yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the karamayam (vineyards), and each ayash (man / husband) chatap (catch) his ayashah (woman / wife) of the banawath (daughters) of Shayalah (Shiloh), and halak (move) to the aratz (Earth/land) of Banayamayan (Benjamin).

It shall be, when their ab (father) or their ach (brother/kinsman) bawaa (come) to rayab (complain) to us, that we will amar (spoke) to them, ‘chanan (showing favor) them graciously to us, because we didn't laqach (take / seize) for each ayash (man / husband) his ayashah (woman / wife) in malachamah (battle), neither nathan (give) you give them to them, otherwise you would now be asham (guilty).'"

The banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) ishah (make) so, and nashaa (lift) them wives, according to their masapar (number), of those who chawal (danced), whom they carried off. They yalak (went) and shawab (turn back / repent) to their nachalah (inheritance), banah (build) the irayam (cities), and lived in them.

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) departed there at that ith (time), every ayash (man / husband) to his shabat (tribe) and to his mashapachah (tribe / clan / family), and they yatzaa (go out / come out) out from there every ayash (man / husband) to his nachalah (inheritance).
In those yamayam (days) there was no malak (king) in Yashar-Al (Israel): every ayash (man / husband) ishah (make) that which was yashar (upright) in his own iyan (eye).

It happened in the yamay (days) when the shapatayam (judges) shapat (judge / judgement), that there was a raib (famine) in the aratz (Earth/land). A certain ayash (man / husband) of Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem Judah) yalak (went) to live in the shadah (country) of Mawaab (Moab), he, and his ayashah (woman / wife), and his shanayam (two) ban (son).

The sham (name) of the ayash (man / husband) was Alayamalak (Elimelech), and the sham (name) of his ayashah (woman / wife) Naimay (Naomi), and the sham (name) of his shanayam (two) ban (son) Machalawan (Mahlon) and Kalayawan (Chilion), aparathayam (ephrathites) of Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem Judah). They bawaa (come) into the shadah (country) of Mawaab (Moab), and continued there.
Alayamalak (Elimelech), Naimay (Naomi's) ayash (man / husband), mawath (death); and she was shaar (left), and her shanayam (two) ban (son).

They nashaa (lift) them wives of the nashayam (women) of mawaabay (moab); the sham (name) of the achad (one) was Irapah (Orpah), and the sham (name) of the other Rawath (Ruth): and they lived there about ishar (ten) shanayam (years).
Machalawan (Mahlon) and Kalayawan (Chilion) shanayam (two) mawath (death), and the ayashah (woman / wife) was bereaved of her shanayam (two) yalad (birth / begot) and of her ayash (man / husband).

Then she qawam (rise up) with her daughters-in-law, that she might shawab (turn back / repent) from the shadah (country) of Mawaab (Moab): for she had shamai (hearken / hear) in the shadah (country) of Mawaab (Moab) how that Yahawah paqad (visit) visited his im (nation / people) in nathan (give) them lacham (bread).

She yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the maqawam (place) where she was, and her shanayam (two) daughters-in-law with her; and they yalak (went) on the darak (way) to shawab (turn back / repent) to the aratz (Earth/land) of Yahawadah (Judah).

Naimay (Naomi) amar (spoke) to her shanayam (two) daughters-in-law, "yalak (go), shawab (turn back / repent) ayashah (woman / wife) of you to her am (mother) bayath (house): Yahawah ishah (make) chasad (grace) with you, as you ishah (make) dealt with the mawath (death), and with me.

Yahawah nathan (give) you that you may matzaa (find) manawachah (rest), ayashah (woman / wife) of you in the bayath (house) of her ayash (man / husband)." Then she nashaq (kissed) them, and they nashaa (lift) up their qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept).
They amar (spoke) to her, "No, but we will shawab (turn back / repent) with you to your im (nation / people)."

Naimay (Naomi) amar (spoke), "shawab (turn back / repent) back, my banath (daughter). Why do you want to yalak (go) with me? Do I still have banayam (sons) in my maih (womb), that they may be your anashayam (husbands)?

Shawab (turn back / repent) back, my banath (daughter), yalak (go) your way; for I am too zaqan (old) to have a ayash (man / husband). If I should amar (spoke), ‘I yash (have) thaqawah (hope),' if I should even have a ayash (man / husband) tonight, and should also yalad (birth / begot) banayam (sons);

Would you then shabar (wait) until they were gadal (grown)? Would you then refrain from having ayash (man / husband)? No, my banath (daughter), for it grieves me much for your sakes, for the yad (hand) of Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) gone out against me."
They nashaa (lift) up their qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept) again: and Irapah (Orpah) nashaq (kissed) her mother-in-law, but Ruth dabaq (joined) with her.
She amar (spoke), "Behold, your sister-in-law has shawab (turn back / repent) back to her im (nation / people), and to her Alahayam. Follow your sister-in-law."

Ruth amar (spoke), "Don't pagai (entreat) me to izab (leave) you, and to shawab (turn back / repent) from achar (other) after you, for where you yalak (go), I will yalak (go); and where you lawan (lodge), I will lawan (lodge); your im (nation / people) shall be my im (nation / people), and your Alahayam my Alahayam;
Where you mawath (death), will I mawath (death), and there will I be qabar (bury). Yahawah ishah (make) so to me, and more also, if anything but mawath (death) parad (part) you and me."
When she raah (see) that she was steadfastly amatz (minded) to yalak (go) with her, she chadal (left) off dabar (word / matter) to her.

So they shanayam (two) yalak (went) until they bawaa (come) to Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem). It happened, when they bawaa (come) come to Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem), that all the iyar (city) was hawam (moved) about them, and they asked, "Is this Naimay (Naomi)?"
She amar (spoke) to them, "Don't qaraa (called) me Naimay (Naomi). Qaraa (called) me Maraa (Mara); for the Shaday has dealt very bitterly with me.

I halak (move) out malaa (full), and Yahawah has shawab (turn back / repent) me home again rayaqam (empty); why do you qaraa (called) me Naimay (Naomi), since Yahawah has inah (answer / respond) against me, and the Shaday has raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) me?"

So Naimay (Naomi) shawab (turn back / repent), and Ruth the Moabitess, her kalah (complete / finish), with her, who shawab (turn back / repent) out of the shadah (country) of Mawaab (Moab): and they bawaa (come) to Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem) in the thachalah (beginning) of shairah (barley) qatzayar (harvest).

Naimay (Naomi) had a kinsman of her ayash (man / husband), a gabawar (mighty) ayash (man / husband) of wealth, of the mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) of Alayamalak (Elimelech), and his sham (name) was Baiz (Boaz).

The Moabitess amar (spoke) to Naimay (Naomi), "yalak (let) me now go to the shadah (field), and laqat (glean) among the shabalayam (ears) of grain achar (other) him in whose iyan (eye) I shall matzaa (find) favor." She amar (spoke) to her, "yalak (go), my banath (daughter)."

She yalak (went), and bawaa (come) and laqat (gleaned) in the shadah (field) achar (other) the qatzarayam (reapers): and she happened to qarah (come) to the chalaqah (portion) of the shadah (field) belonging to Baiz (Boaz), who was of the mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) of Alayamalak (Elimelech).
Behold, Baiz (Boaz) bawaa (come) from Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem), and amar (spoke) to the qawatzarayam (reapers), "Yahawah be with you." They amar (spoke) him, "Yahawah barak (blessed) you."
Then Baiz (Boaz) amar (spoke) to his nair (servant) who was natzab (set) over the qawatzarayam (reapers), "Whose nairah (young) lady is this?"

The nair (servant) who was natzab (set) over the qawatzarayam (reapers) inah (answer / respond), "It is the Mawaabay (Moabite) lady who shawab (turn back / repent) back with Naimay (Naomi) out of the shadah (country) of Mawaab (Moab).

She amar (spoke), ‘Please let me laqat (glean) and asap (gather) achar (other) the qawatzarayam (reapers) among the sheaves.' So she bawaa (come), and has imad (continued) even from the baqar (morning) until now, except that she stayed a mait (little) in the bayath (house)."

Then Baiz (Boaz) amar (spoke) to Rawath (Ruth), "shamai (hearken / hear), my banath (daughter). Don't yalak (go) to laqat (glean) in achar (other) shadah (field), and don't ibar (pass over/through) from here, but stay here close to my nairah (maidens).

Let your iyan (eye) be on the shadah (field) that they qatzar (reap), and halak (move) achar (other) them. Haven't I tzawah (commanded) the nair (young) men not to nagai (touch) you? When you are tzamaa (thirsty), halak (move) to the kalayam (vessels), and shathah (drinks) from that which the nair (young) men have shaab (drawn)."

Then she napal (fall / be cast down) on her panayam (face), and shachah (bowed) herself to the aratz (Earth/land), and amar (spoke) to him, "Why matzaa (have) I found favor in your iyan (eye), that you should take nakar (knowledge) of me, since I am a nakaray (foreigner)?"

Baiz (Boaz) inah (answer / respond) her, "It has nagad (fully) been shown me, all that you ishah (make) done to your mother-in-law achar (other) the mawath (death) of your ayash (man / husband); and how you have izab (left) your ab (father) and your am (mother), and the aratz (Earth/land) of your birth, and have yalak (come) to a im (nation / people) that you didn't yadai (know) thamawal (before).

May Yahawah shalam (repay) your pail (work), and a shalam (full / whole / complete) mashakarath (reward) be given you from Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), under whose kanap (wings) you bawaa (come) come to take chasah (refuge)."

Then she amar (spoke), "Let me matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (eye), my Adawan, because you have nacham (turn away / repent) me, and because you have dabar (word / matter) lab (heart) to your handmaid, though I am not as achad (one) of your handmaidens."

At meal ith (time) Baiz (Boaz) amar (spoke) to her, "nagash (come) here, and akal (eat) of the lacham (bread), and tabal (dip) your path (morsel) in the chamatz (vinegar)." She yashab (inhabit/dwell) tzad (beside) the qawatzarayam (reapers), and they tzabat (reached) her qalay (parched) grain, and she akal (eat), and was shabai (satisfied), and yathar (left) some of it.
When she had qawam (rise up) up to laqat (glean), Baiz (Boaz) tzawah (commanded) his nair (young) men, amar (spoke), "Let her laqat (glean) even among the sheaves, and don't kalam (reproach) her.
Also pull out some for her from the bundles, and izab (leave) it, and let her laqat (glean), and don't gair (rebuke) her."
So she laqat (gleaned) in the shadah (field) until irab (evening); and she chabat (beat) out that which she had laqat (gleaned), and it was about an ayapah (ephah) of shairah (barley).

She nashaa (lift) it up, and bawaa (come) into the iyar (city); and her mother-in-law raah (see) what she had laqat (gleaned): and she yatzaa (go out / come out) out and nathan (give) to her that which she had yathar (left) after she was sufficed.

Her mother-in-law amar (spoke) to her, "Where have you laqat (gleaned) today? Ayapah (where) ishah (make) you worked? Barak (blessed) be he who noticed you." She showed her mother-in-law with whom she ishah (make) worked, and amar (spoke), "The ayash (man / husband) sham (name) with whom I ishah (make) today is Baiz (Boaz)."

Naimay (Naomi) amar (spoke) to her daughter-in-law, "barak (blessed) be he of Yahawah, who has not izab (left) off his chasad (grace) to the chay (life) and to the mawath (death)." Naimay (Naomi) amar (spoke) to her, "The ayash (man / husband) is a close relative to us, ayash (man / husband) of our gaal (near) kinsmen."
The Moabitess amar (spoke), "Yes, he amar (spoke) to me, ‘You shall stay dabaq (close) to my nair (young) men, until they kalah (complete / finish) ended all my qatzayar (harvest).'"

Naimay (Naomi) amar (spoke) to her kalah (complete / finish), "It is tawab (good / proper function), my banath (daughter), that you yatzaa (go out / come out) out with his nairah (maidens), and that they not pagai (meet) you in any other shadah (field)."

So she stayed dabaq (close) to the nairawath (maidens) of Baiz (Boaz), to laqat (glean) to the kalah (complete / finish) of shairah (barley) qatzayar (harvest) and of chatah (wheat) qatzayar (harvest); and she lived with her mother-in-law.
Naimay (Naomi) her mother-in-law amar (spoke) to her, "My banath (daughter), shall I not baqash (seek) manawach (rest) for you, that it may be yatab (well) with you?
Now isn't Baiz (Boaz) our kinsman, with whose nairah (maidens) you were? Behold, he zarah (winnows) shairah (barley) tonight in the garan (threshing) floor.

Therefore rachatz (wash) yourself, sawak (anoint) yourself, shawam (place / establish / appoint) dressed, and yarad (go) down to the garan (threshing) floor, but don't yadai (make) yourself known to the ayash (man / husband) until he kalah (complete / finish) finished akal (eat) and shathah (drinks).

It shall be, when he shakab (lies) down, that you shall yadai (mark) the maqawam (place) where he shall shakab (lie), and you shall bawaa (come) in, and galah (uncover) his maragalah (feet), and shakab (lay) down; then he will nagad (tell) you what you shall ishah (make)."
She amar (spoke) to her, "All that you amar (spoke) I will ishah (make)."
She yarad (went) down to the garan (threshing) floor, and ishah (make) according to all that her mother-in-law told her.

When Baiz (Boaz) had akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and his lab (heart) was yatab (merry), he bawaa (come) to shakab (lie) down at the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the iram (heap) of grain. She bawaa (come) lat (softly), galah (uncovered) his maragalah (feet), and shakab (laid) her down.
It happened at chatzay (midnight), that the ayash (man / husband) was startled and lapath (turned) himself; and behold, a ayashah (woman / wife) shakab (lay) at his maragalah (feet).
He amar (spoke), "Who are you?" She amar (spoke), "I am your handmaid. Therefore parash (spread) your kanap (skirt) over your handmaid; for you are a gaal (near) kinsman."

He amar (spoke), "barak (blessed) are you by Yahawah, my banath (daughter). You yatab (have) shown more chasad (grace) in the acharawan (latter) end than at the raashawan (beginning), inasmuch as you didn't yalak (follow) bachawar (young) men, whether dal (poor) or ishayar (rich).

Now, my banath (daughter), don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid); I will ishah (make) to you all that you amar (spoke); for all the shair (city) of my im (nation / people) does yadai (know) that you are a chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ayashah (woman / wife).
Now it is amanam (true) that I am a gaal (near) kinsman; however there is a gaal (kinsman) nearer than I.

Stay this layal (night), and it shall be in the baqar (morning), that if he will gaal (perform) for you the part of a kinsman, tawab (good / proper function); let him gaal (do) the kinsman's part. But if he chapatz (will) not gaal (do) the part of a kinsman for you, then will I gaal (do) the part of a kinsman for you, as Yahawah chay (life). Shakab (lie) down until the baqar (morning)."

She shakab (lay) at his maragalah (feet) until the baqar (morning). She qawam (rise up) up tarawam (before) ayash (man / husband) nakar (could) discern rai (neigbor/another person). For he amar (spoke), "yadai (let) it not be known that the ayashah (woman / wife) bawaa (come) to the garan (threshing) floor."

He amar (spoke), "yahab (bring) the mantle that is on you, and achaz (hold) it." She achaz (held) it; and he madad (measured) shash (six) measures of shairah (barley), and shayath (put / appoint / make) it on her; and he bawaa (come) into the iyar (city).
When she bawaa (come) to her mother-in-law, she amar (spoke), "How did it go, my banath (daughter)?" She amar (spoke) her all that the ayash (man / husband) ishah (make) done to her.
She amar (spoke), "He nathan (give) me these shash (six) measures of shairah (barley); for he amar (spoke), ‘Don't bawaa (come) rayaqam (empty) to your mother-in-law.'"

Then she amar (spoke), "yashab (inhabit/dwell) still, my banath (daughter), until you yadai (know) how the dabar (word / matter) will napal (fall / be cast down); for the ayash (man / husband) will not shaqat (rest), until he kalah (complete / finish) finished the thing this yawam (day)."

Now Baiz (Boaz) ilah (go up / offer) up to the shair (gate), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) down there. Behold, the gaal (near) kinsman of whom Baiz (Boaz) dabar (word / matter) ibar (pass over/through) by; to whom he dabar (word / matter), "ibar (pass over/through) over here, friend, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) down!" He sawar (turned) aside, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) down.
He laqach (take / seize) ishar (ten) anashayam (men) of the zaqanay (elders) of the iyar (city), and amar (spoke), "yashab (inhabit/dwell) down here." They yashab (inhabit/dwell) down.

He amar (spoke) to the gaal (near) kinsman, "Naimay (Naomi), who has shawab (turn back / repent) back out of the shadah (country) of Mawaab (Moab), is makar (selling) the chalaqah (parcel) of shadah (land), which was our ach (brother/kinsman) Alayamalak (Elimelech's).

I amar (spoke) to galah (disclose) it to you, amar (spoke), ‘qanah (buy) it before those who sit here, and before the zaqanay (elders) of my im (nation / people).' If you will gaal (redeem) it, gaal (redeem) it; but if you will not gaal (redeem) it, then nagad (tell) me, that I may yadai (know). For there is no one to gaal (redeem) it zawalah (besides) you; and I am achar (other) you." He amar (spoke), "I will gaal (redeem) it."

Then Baiz (Boaz) amar (spoke), "On the yawam (day) you qanah (buy) the shadah (field) from the yad (hand) of Naimay (Naomi), you must qanah (buy) it also from the Moabitess, the ayashah (woman / wife) of the mawath (death), to qawam (rise up) up the sham (name) of the mawath (death) on his nachalah (inheritance)."

The gaal (near) kinsman amar (spoke), "I can't gaal (redeem) it for myself, lest I shachath (mar) my own nachalah (inheritance). Take my gaalah (right) of yakal (redemption) for yourself; for I can't gaal (redeem) it."

Now this panayam (face) the custom in former time in Yashar-Al (Israel) concerning gaalah (redeeming) and concerning thamawarah (exchanging), to qawam (rise up) all things: a ayash (man / husband) took off his nail (shoe), and nathan (give) it to his neighbor; and this was the thaiwadah (way) of attestation in Yashar-Al (Israel).
So the gaal (near) kinsman amar (spoke) to Baiz (Boaz), "qanah (buy) it for yourself." He took off his nail (shoe).

Baiz (Boaz) amar (spoke) to the zaqanayam (elders), and to all the im (nation / people), "You are witnesses this yawam (day), that I have bought all that was Alayamalak (Elimelech's), and all that was Kalayawan (Chilion's) and Machalawan (Mahlon's), from the yad (hand) of Naimay (Naomi).

Rawath (Moreover) the Moabitess, the ayashah (woman / wife) of Machalawan (Mahlon), I have qanah (purchased) to be my ayashah (woman / wife), to qawam (rise up) up the sham (name) of the mawath (death) on his nachalah (inheritance), that the sham (name) of the mawath (death) not be karath (cut) off from im (with) his ach (brother/kinsman), and from the shair (gate) of his maqawam (place). You are witnesses this yawam (day)."

All the im (nation / people) who were in the shair (gate), and the zaqanayam (elders), amar (spoke), "We are witnesses. May Yahawah nathan (give) the ayashah (woman / wife) who bawaa (come) come into your bayath (house) like Rachal (Rachel) and like Laah (Leah), which shanayam (two) banah (build) the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel); and treat you chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) in Ephrathah, and be qaraa (called) in Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem).

Let your bayath (house) be like the bayath (house) of Paratz (Perez), whom Thamar (Tamar) yalad (birth / begot) to Yahawadah (Judah), of the zarai (seed) which Yahawah shall nathan (give) you of this nairah (young) woman."

So Baiz (Boaz) laqach (take / seize) Rawath (Ruth), and she became his ayashah (woman / wife); and he bawaa (come) in to her, and Yahawah nathan (give) her harawan (conception), and she yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son).

The nashayam (women) amar (spoke) to Naimay (Naomi), "barak (blessed) be Yahawah, who has not shabath (shabath / rest) you this yawam (day) without a gaal (near) kinsman; and let his sham (name) be qaraa (called) in Yashar-Al (Israel).

He shall be to you a restorer of napash (soul), and kawal (all) you in your shayabah (old age / white hair - due to age) age, for your kalah (complete / finish), who ahab (love) you, who is tawab (good / proper function) to you than shabai (seven) banayam (sons), has yalad (birth / begot) him."
Naimay (Naomi) laqach (take / seize) the yalad (birth / begot), and shayath (put / appoint / make) it in her chayaq (bosom), and became aman (believe / have faith) to it.

The women, her neighbors, gave him a sham (name), amar (spoke), "There is a ban (son) yalad (birth / begot) to Naimay (Naomi);" and they sham (name) him Iwabad (Obed). He is the ab (father) of Yashay (Jesse), the ab (father) of Dawad (David).
Now this is the history of the thawaladawath (generations) of Paratz (Perez): Paratz (Perez) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Chatzarawan (Hezron),
And Chatzarawan (Hezron) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Ram (Ram), and Ram (Ram) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Imayanadab (Amminadab),
And Imayanadab (Amminadab) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Nachashawan (Nahshon), and Nachashawan (Nahshon) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Shalamah (Salmon),
And Shalamawan (Salmon) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Baiz (Boaz), and Baiz (Boaz) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Iwabad (Obed),
And Iwabad (Obed) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Yashay (Jesse), and Yashay (Jesse) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Dawad (David).

Now there was a achad (one) ayash (man / husband) of Ramathayamatzawapayam (Ramathaim Zophim), of the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), and his sham (name) was Alaqanah (Elkanah), the ban (son) of Yaracham (Jeroham), the ban (son) of Alayahaw (Elihu), the ban (son) of Thachaw (Tohu), the ban (son) of Tzawap (Zuph), an Aparathay (Ephraimite):

And he had shanayam (two) wives; the sham (name) of the achad (one) was Chanah (Hannah), and the sham (name) of other Pananah (Peninnah): and Pananah (Peninnah) had yaladayam (children), but Chanah (Hannah) had no yaladayam (children).

Hawaa (which/who/that is) ayash (man / husband) ilah (go up / offer) up out of his iyar (city) from yawam (day) to year to shachah (worship) and to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) in Shayalah (Shiloh). The shanayam (two) banay (sons) of Ilay (Eli), Chapanay (Hophni) and Payanachas (Phinehas), kahanayam (priests) to Yahawah, were there.

When the yawam (day) came that Alaqanah (Elkanah) zabach (sacrificed), he nathan (give) to Pananah (Peninnah) his ayashah (woman / wife), and to all her ban (son) and her banath (daughter), manawath (portions):
But to Chanah (Hannah) he nathan (give) a double manah (portion); for he ahab (love) Chanah (Hannah), but Yahawah had sagar (shut) up her racham (womb).
Her rival kais (provoked) her severely, to raim (make) her fret, because Yahawah had sagar (shut) up her racham (womb).
As he ishah (make) so shanah (year) by shanah (year), when she ilah (go up / offer) up to the bayath (house) of Yahawah, so she kais (provoked) her; therefore she bakah (wept), and didn't akal (eat).

Alaqanah (Elkanah) her ayash (man / husband) amar (spoke) to her, "Chanah (Hannah), why do you bakah (weep)? Why don't you akal (eat)? Why is your labab (heart) grieved? Am I not tawab (good / proper function) to you than ishar (ten) banayam (sons)?"

So Chanah (Hannah) qawam (rise up) up achar (other) they had akal (eat) in Shayalah (Shiloh), and achar (other) they had shathah (drinks). Now Ilay (Eli) the kahan (priest) was sitting on his kasaa (seat) by the doorpost of the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah.
She was in bitterness of napash (soul), and palal (prayed) to Yahawah, and bakah (wept) bitterly.

She nadar (make vow) a nadar (vow), and amar (spoke), "Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), if you will raah (see) raah (see) on the inay (affliction) of your handmaid, and zakar (remember) me, and not shakach (forget) your handmaid, but will nathan (give) to your handmaid a boy, then I will nathan (give) him to Yahawah all the yamay (days) of his chay (life), and no mawarah (razor) shall ilah (go up / offer) on his raash (head)."
It happened, as she rabah (continued) palal (praying) panayam (face) Yahawah, that Ilay (Eli) Ilay (saw) her pah (mouth).

Now Chanah (Hannah) dabar (word / matter) in her lab (heart). Only her shapah (lips) nawai (moved), but her qawal (sound / voice) was not shamai (hearken / hear). Therefore Ilay (Eli) chashab (thought) she had been shakawar (drunken).
Ilay (Eli) amar (spoke) to her, "How long will you be shakar (drunken)? Sawar (put) away your yayan (wine) from you."

Chanah (Hannah) inah (answer / respond), "No, my Adawan, I am a ayashah (woman / wife) of a qashah (rough / hard) rawach (spirit / wind). I have shathah (drinks) neither yayan (wine) nor shakar (strong) drink, but I shapak (poured) out my napash (soul) panayam (face) Yahawah.
Don't nathan (give) your handmaid for a balayail (wicked) banath (daughter); for I have been dabar (word / matter) out of the rab (abundance) of my shayach (complaint) and my kais (provocation)."

Then Ilay (Eli) inah (answer / respond), "yalak (go) in shalawam (peace / safety); and may the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel) nathan (give) your shaalah (petition) that you have shaal (asked) of him."

She amar (spoke), "Let your handmaid matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (eye)." So the ayashah (woman / wife) yalak (went) her darak (way), and akal (eat); and her facial expression wasn't sad any more.

They shakam (rose) up in the baqar (morning) shakam (early), and shachah (worshiped) panayam (face) Yahawah, and shawab (turn back / repent), and bawaa (come) to their bayath (house) to Ramah (Ramah): and Alaqanah (Elkanah) yadai (knew) Chanah (Hannah) his ayashah (woman / wife); and Yahawah zakar (remember) her.

It happened, when the yawam (day) had thaqawapah (come), that Chanah (Hannah) harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son); and she qaraa (called) him Shamawaal (Samuel), saying, "Because I have shaal (asked) him of Yahawah."
The ayash (man / husband) Alaqanah (Elkanah), and all his bayath (house), ilah (go up / offer) up to zabach (offer) to Yahawah the yawam (day) zabach (sacrifice), and his nadar (vow).

But Chanah (Hannah) didn't ilah (go up / offer) up; for she amar (spoke) to her ayash (man / husband), "Not until the nair (child) is weaned; then I will bawaa (come) him, that he may raah (see) panayam (face) Yahawah, and stay there iwalam (forever)."

Alaqanah (Elkanah) her ayash (man / husband) amar (spoke) to her, "ishah (make) what seems tawab (good / proper function) to you. Wait until you have weaned him; only may Yahawah qawam (rise up) his dabar (word / matter)." So the ayashah (woman / wife) waited and yanaq (nursed) her ban (son), until she weaned him.

When she had weaned him, she ilah (go up / offer) him up with her, with shalawash (three) parayam (bulls), and achad (one) ayapah (ephah) of qamach (meal), and a nabal (bottle) of yayan (wine), and bawaa (come) him to Yahawah bayath (house) in Shayalah (Shiloh). The nair (child) was nair (young).
They shachat (killed) the par (bull), and bawaa (come) the nair (child) to Ilay (Eli).
She amar (spoke), "Oh, my Adawan, as your napash (soul) chay (life), my Adawan, I am the ayashah (woman / wife) who natzab (stood) by you here, palal (praying) to Yahawah.
For this nair (child) I palal (prayed); and Yahawah nathan (give) given me my shaalah (petition) which I shaal (asked) of him.
Therefore also I have granted him to Yahawah. As yawam (day) as he lives he is granted to Yahawah." He shachah (worshiped) Yahawah there.

Chanah (Hannah) palal (prayed), and amar (spoke): "My lab (heart) exults in Yahawah! My qaran (horn) is rawam (will lift up) in Yahawah. My pah (mouth) is enlarged over my ayab (enemy), because I shamach (rejoice) in your yashawaih (salvation).
There is no one as qadawash (holy) as Yahawah, For there is no one balathay (without) you, nor is there any tzawar (rock) like our Alahayam.

"Dabar (word / matter) no more so gabah (exceeding) gabah (proudly). Don't let arrogance yatzaa (go out / come out) out of your pah (mouth), For Yahawah is a Al of daih (knowledge). By him ilalawath (actions) are thakan (weighed).
"The qashath (bows) of the gabawar (mighty) men are chath (broken). Those who kashal (stumble / stagger) are armed with chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor).

Those who were shabai (full) have shakar (hired) themselves out for lacham (bread). Those who were raib (hungry) are satisfied. Yes, the iqar (barren) has yalad (birth / begot) shabai (seven). She who rab (has) many banayam (children) languishes.
"Yahawah mawath (death), and chayah (makes) alive. He yarad (brings) down to shaawal (Sheol / afterlife), and ilah (go up / offer) up.
Yahawah yarash (makes) poor, and ishar (makes) rich. He shapal (brings) low, he also rawam (will lift up) up.

He qawam (rise up) up the dal (poor) out of the ipar (dust). He rawam (will lift up) up the abayawan (needy) from the dunghill, To yashab (inhabit/dwell) them sit with nadayabayam (princes), and nachal (inherit) the kasaa (throne) of kabawad (glory). For the matzaqay (pillars) of the aratz (Earth/land) are Yahawah. He has shayath (put / appoint / make) the thabal (world) on them.

He will shamar (keep/guard) the ragalay (feet) of his chasayad (holy) ones, but the rashai (wicked) shall be put to damam (silence) in chashak (darkness); for no ayash (man / husband) shall gabar (prevail) by kach (strength / mighty / power).

Those who rayab (strive) with Yahawah shall be broken to pieces. He will raim (thunder) against them in the sky. "Yahawah will dayan (judge) the apasay (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land). He will nathan (give) iz (strength / might / refuge) to his malak (king), and rawam (will lift up) the qaran (horn) of his mashayach (anointed one)."
Alaqanah (Elkanah) yalak (went) to Ramah (Ramah) to his bayath (house). The nair (child) sharath (served) Yahawah panayam (face) Ilay (Eli) the kahan (priest).
Now the banay (sons) of Ilay (Eli) were base banay (men); they didn't yadai (know) Yahawah.

The mashapat (custom) of the kahanayam (priests) with the im (nation / people) was that when any ayash (man / husband) zabach (offered) zabach (sacrifice), the kahanayam (priests) nair (servant) bawaa (come), while the bashar (flesh) was bashal (boiling), with a fork of shalawash (three) shanayam (teeth) in his yad (hand);

And he nakah (struck) it into the kayawar (pan), or dawad (kettle), or qalachath (caldron), or parawar (pot); all that the fork ilah (go up / offer) up the kahan (priest) laqach (take / seize) therewith. So they ishah (make) in Shayalah (Shiloh) to all the Yashar-Al (Israelites) who bawaa (come) there.

Yes, before they burnt the chalab (fat), the kahan (priest) nair (servant) bawaa (come), and amar (spoke) to the ayash (man / husband) who zabach (sacrificed), "nathan (give) meat to tzalah (roast) for the kahan (priest); for he will not laqach (take / seize) bashal (boiled) meat from you, but chay (life)."

If the ayash (man / husband) amar (spoke) to him, "Let the chalab (fat) be qatar (burned) yawam (day), and then laqach (take / seize) as much as your napash (soul) amar (spoke);" then he would amar (spoke), "No, but you shall nathan (give) it to me now; and if not, I will laqach (take / seize) it by chazaqah (force)."

The chataah (sin) of the nair (young) men was very gadawal (very great/important/mighty) panayam (face) Yahawah; for the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) naatz (despised) the manachah (offering) of Yahawah.
But Shamawaal (Samuel) sharath (ministered) panayam (face) Yahawah, being a nair (child), clothed with a bad (linen) apawad (ephod).

Moreover his am (mother) ishah (make) him a qatan (small / young / least) maiyal (robe), and ilah (go up / offer) it to him from yawam (day) to yawam (day), when she ilah (go up / offer) up with her ayash (man / husband) to zabach (offer) the yawam (day) zabach (sacrifice).

Ilay (Eli) barak (blessed) Alaqanah (Elkanah) and his ayashah (woman / wife), and amar (spoke), "Yahawah shawam (place / establish / appoint) you zarai (seed) of this ayashah (woman / wife) for the shaalah (petition) which was shaal (asked) of Yahawah." They halak (move) to their own maqawam (place).

Yahawah paqad (visit) Chanah (Hannah), and she harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) shalawash (three) banayam (sons) and shanayam (two) banawath (daughters). The nair (child) Shamawaal (Samuel) gadal (grew) im (with) Yahawah.

Now Ilay (Eli) was very zaqan (old); and he shamai (hearken / hear) all that his ban (son) ishah (make) to all Yashar-Al (Israel), and how that they shakab (lay) with the nashayam (women) who served at the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
He amar (spoke) to them, "Why ishah (make) you do such things? For I shamai (hearken / hear) of your rai (evil) dealings from all this im (nation / people).
No, my ban (son); for it is no tawab (good / proper function) shamawaih (report) that I shamai (hearken / hear): you make Yahawah im (nation / people) disobey.

If one ayash (man / husband) chataa (sin) against ayash (man / husband), Alahayam shall palal (judge) him; but if a ayash (man / husband) chataa (sin) against Yahawah, who shall entreat for him?" Notwithstanding, they didn't shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of their ab (father), because Yahawah intended to mawath (death) them.
The nair (child) Shamawaal (Samuel) gadal (grew) on, and increased in favor both with Yahawah, and also with halak (move).

A ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam bawaa (come) to Ilay (Eli), and amar (spoke) to him, "Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘Did I galah (reveal) myself to the bayath (house) of your ab (father), when they were in Matzarayam (Egypt) in bondage to Paraih (Pharaoh's) bayath (house)?

Did I bachar (choose) him out of all the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel) to be my kahan (priest), to ilah (go up / offer) up to my mazabach (altar), to qatar (burn) qatarath (incense), to nashaa (lift) an apawad (ephod) panayam (face) me? Nathan (give) I give to the bayath (house) of your ab (father) all the offerings of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) made by ashah (fire / offering made by fire)?

Why do you bait (kick) at my zabach (sacrifice) and at my zabach (offering), which I have tzawah (commanded) in my maiwan (habitation), and honor your ban (son) above me, to baraa (created) yourselves fat with the best of all the manachah (offerings) of Yashar-Al (Israel) my im (nation / people)?'

"Therefore Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), naam (declares prophetically), ‘I naam (declares prophetically) amar (spoke) that your bayath (house), and the bayath (house) of your ab (father), should halak (move) panayam (face) me iwalam (forever).' But now Yahawah naam (declares prophetically), ‘Be it chalayalah (far) from me; for those who honor me I will honor, and those who bazah (despise) me shall be lightly qalal (esteemed).

Behold, the yamayam (days) bawaa (come), that I will gadai (cut) off your zarawai (arm), and the zarawai (arm) of your ab (father) bayath (house), that there shall not be an old zaqan (man) in your bayath (house).

You shall nabat (see) the tzar (oppressor / distressor) of my maiwan (habitation), in all the wealth which I shall yatab (give) Yashar-Al (Israel); and there shall not be an old zaqan (man) in your bayath (house) yawam (day).

The ayash (man / husband) of yours, whom I shall not karath (cut) off from my mazabach (altar), shall kalah (complete / finish) your iyan (eye), and adab (grieve) your napash (soul); and all the marabayath (increase) of your bayath (house) shall mawath (death) in the flower of their age.

"‘This shall be the awath (sign / mark / miracle) to you, that shall bawaa (come) on your shanayam (two) ban (son), on Chapanay (Hophni) and Payanachas (Phinehas): in achad (one) yawam (day) they shall shanayam (two) mawath (death).

I will qawam (rise up) me up a aman (believe / have faith) kahan (priest), that shall ishah (make) according to that which is in my labab (heart) and in my napash (soul). I will banah (build) him a aman (believe / have faith) bayath (house); and he shall halak (move) panayam (face) my mashayach (anointed one) yawam (day).

It shall happen, that everyone who is yathar (left) in your bayath (house) shall bawaa (come) and shachah (bow) down to him for a agawarah (piece) of kasap (silver) and a kakar (loaf) of lacham (bread), and shall amar (spoke), "Please put me into achad (one) of the kahanawath (priests)' offices, that I may akal (eat) a path (morsel) of lacham (bread)."'"

The nair (child) Shamawaal (Samuel) sharath (ministered) to Yahawah panayam (face) Ilay (Eli). The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah was yaqar (precious) in those yamayam (days); there was no frequent chazawan (vision).
It happened at that yawam (day), when Ilay (Eli) was shakab (laid) down in his maqawam (place) (now his iyan (eye) had chalal (begun) to grow kahah (dim), so that he yakal (could) not raah (see)),
And the nayar (lamp) of Alahayam hadn't yet kabah (gone) out, and Shamawaal (Samuel) had shakab (laid) down in the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, where the arawan (ark) of Alahayam was;
That Yahawah qaraa (called) Shamawaal (Samuel); and he amar (spoke), "Here I am."
He rawatz (ran) to Ilay (Eli), and amar (spoke), "Here I am; for you amar (spoke) me." He said, "I didn't qaraa (called); shakab (lie) down again." He yalak (went) and shakab (lay) down.

Yahawah qaraa (called) yet again, "Shamawaal (Samuel)!" Shamawaal (Samuel) qawam (rise up) and yalak (went) to Ilay (Eli), and amar (spoke), "Here I am; for you qaraa (called) me." He amar (spoke), "I didn't qaraa (called), my ban (son); shakab (lie) down again."
Now Shamawaal (Samuel) didn't yet yadai (know) Yahawah, neither was the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah yet galah (revealed) to him.

Yahawah qaraa (called) Shamawaal (Samuel) again the shalayashay (third) time. He qawam (rise up) and yalak (went) to Ilay (Eli), and amar (spoke), "Here I am; for you qaraa (called) me." Ilay (Eli) bayan (between) that Yahawah had qaraa (called) the nair (child).

Therefore Ilay (Eli) amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), "yalak (go), shakab (lie) down: and it shall be, if he qaraa (called) you, that you shall amar (spoke), ‘dabar (word / matter), Yahawah; for your ibad (servant) shamai (hearken / hear).'" So Shamawaal (Samuel) yalak (went) and shakab (lay) down in his maqawam (place).

Yahawah bawaa (come), and yatzab (stood), and qaraa (called) as at other paim (times), "Shamawaal (Samuel)! Shamawaal (Samuel)!" Then Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), "dabar (word / matter); for your ibad (servant) shamai (hearken / hear)."

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), "Behold, I will ishah (make) a thing in Yashar-Al (Israel), at which shanayam (two) the azan (ear) of everyone who shamai (hearken / hear) it shall tzalal (tingle).
In that yawam (day) I will qawam (rise up) against Ilay (Eli) all that I have dabar (word / matter) al (toward) his bayath (house), from the beginning even to the kalah (complete / finish).

For I have nagad (told) him that I will shapat (judge / judgement) his bayath (house) iwalam (forever), for the iwan (guilt/iniquity) which he yadai (knew), because his ban (son) brought a qalal (curse) on themselves, and he didn't kahah (restrain) them.

Therefore I have shabai (swear / take oath) to the bayath (house) of Ilay (Eli), that the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of Ilay (Eli's) bayath (house) shall not be removed with zabach (sacrifice) nor zabach (offering) iwalam (forever)."

Shamawaal (Samuel) shakab (lay) until the baqar (morning), and pathach (opened) the dalathawath (doors) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah. Shamawaal (Samuel) yaraa (fear / be afraid) to show Ilay (Eli) the maraah (vision).
Then Ilay (Eli) qaraa (called) Shamawaal (Samuel), and amar (spoke), "Shamawaal (Samuel), my ban (son)!" He amar (spoke), "Here I am."

He amar (spoke), "dabar (word / matter) is the thing that he has dabar (word / matter) to you? Please don't kachad (hide) it from me. Alahayam ishah (make) so to you, and more also, if you kachad (hide) anything from me of all the things that he dabar (word / matter) to you."
Shamawaal (Samuel) nagad (told) him every bit, and kachad (hid) nothing from him. He amar (spoke), "It is Yahawah. Let him ishah (make) what seems tawab (good / proper function) to him."
Shamawaal (Samuel) gadal (grew), and Yahawah was with him, and let none of his dabar (word / matter) napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land).
All Yashar-Al (Israel) from Dan (Dan) even to Baar-Shabai (Beersheba) yadai (knew) that Shamawaal (Samuel) was aman (believe / have faith) to be a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Yahawah.
Yahawah raah (see) again in Shayalah (Shiloh); for Yahawah galah (revealed) himself to Shamawaal (Samuel) in Shayalah (Shiloh) by the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah.

The dabar (word / matter) of Shamawaal (Samuel) came to all Yashar-Al (Israel). Now Yashar-Al (Israel) yatzaa (go out / come out) out il (over) the Palashathay (Philistines) to malachamah (battle), and chanah (encamped) beside Abanahaizar (Ebenezer): and the Palashathay (Philistines) chanah (encamped) in Apaq (Aphek).

The Palashathay (Philistines) irak (put) themselves in array panayam (face) Yashar-Al (Israel): and when they natash (joined) malachamah (battle), Yashar-Al (Israel) was nagap (struck) panayam (face) the Palashathay (Philistines); and they nakah (killed) of the mairakah (army) in the shadah (field) about arabai (four) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband).

When the im (nation / people) bawaa (come) come into the machanah (camp), the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke), "Why has Yahawah nagap (struck) us today panayam (face) the Palashathay (Philistines)? Let us laqach (take / seize) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah out of Shayalah (Shiloh) to us, that it may bawaa (come) qarab (among / near) us, and yashai (salvation) us out of the kap (hand) of our ayab (enemy)."

So the im (nation / people) shalach (send) to Shayalah (Shiloh); and they nashaa (lift) from there the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), who yashab (inhabit/dwell) above the karawab (cherubim): and the shanayam (two) banay (sons) of Ilay (Eli), Chapanay (Hophni) and Payanachas (Phinehas), were there with the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Alahayam.

When the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah bawaa (come) into the machanah (camp), all Yashar-Al (Israel) rawai (shouted) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) tharawaih (shout), so that the aratz (Earth/land) hawam (rang) again.

When the Palashathay (Philistines) shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the tharawaih (shout), they amar (spoke), "What does the qawal (sound / voice) of this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) tharawaih (shout) in the machanah (camp) of the ibarayam (hebrews) mean?" They yadai (understood) that the arawan (ark) of Yahawah bawaa (come) come into the machanah (camp).

The Palashathay (Philistines) were yaraa (fear / be afraid), for they amar (spoke), "Alahayam bawaa (come) come into the machanah (camp)." They amar (spoke), "away (woe) to us! For there has not been such a thing athamawal (before).

Away (woe) to us! Who shall natzal (deliver) us out of the yad (hand) of these adayar (mighty) Alahayam? These are the Alahayam that nakah (struck) the Matzarayam (Egyptians) with all kinds of makah (plagues) in the madabar (wilderness).

Be chazaq (strong), and behave like hathachazaqaw (men), O you Palashathay (Philistines), that you not be thaibadaw (servants) to the ibarayam (hebrews), as they have been to you. Strengthen yourselves like hathachazaqaw (men), and lacham (fight)!"

The Palashathay (Philistines) lacham (fought), and Yashar-Al (Israel) was nagap (struck), and they nawas (fled) every ayash (man / husband) to his ahal (tent): and there was a very gadawal (very great/important/mighty) makah (slaughter); for there napal (fall / be cast down) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand) footmen.
The arawan (ark) of Alahayam was laqach (take / seize); and the shanayam (two) banay (sons) of Ilay (Eli), Chapanay (Hophni) and Payanachas (Phinehas), were mawath (death).

There rawatz (ran) a ayash (man / husband) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) out of the mairakah (army), and bawaa (come) to Shayalah (Shiloh) the same yawam (day), with his mad (clothes) qarai (torn), and with adamah (earth) on his raash (head).

When he bawaa (come), behold, Ilay (Eli) was sitting on his kasaa (seat) by the road tzapah (watchman / keep watch); for his lab (heart) trembled for the arawan (ark) of Alahayam. When the ayash (man / husband) bawaa (come) into the iyar (city), and nagad (told) it, all the iyar (city) zaiq (cried) out.

When Ilay (Eli) shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the tzaiqah (crying), he amar (spoke), "What does the qawal (sound / voice) of this tumult mean?" The ayash (man / husband) hurried, and bawaa (come) and nagad (told) Ilay (Eli).
Now Ilay (Eli) was thashaiyam (ninety) - shamanah (eight) shanah (years) ban (son); and his iyan (eye) were qawam (rise up), so that he yakal (could) not raah (see).

The ayash (man / husband) amar (spoke) to Ilay (Eli), "I am he who bawaa (come) out of the mairakah (army), and I nawas (fled) today out of the mairakah (army)." He amar (spoke), "How dabar (word / matter) the matter go, my ban (son)?"

He who inah (answer / respond) the news answered, "Yashar-Al (Israel) has nawas (fled) panayam (face) the Palashathay (Philistines), and there has been also a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) magapah (slaughter) among the im (nation / people). Your shanayam (two) ban (son) also, Chapanay (Hophni) and Payanachas (Phinehas), are mawath (death), and the arawan (ark) of Alahayam has been captured."

It happened, when he zakar (remember) mention of the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, that Eli napal (fall / be cast down) from off his kasaa (seat) backward by the yad (hand) of the shair (gate); and his maparaqath (neck) shabar (broke), and he mawath (death); for he was an zaqan (old) ayash (man / husband), and kabad (heavy). He had shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years).

His kalah (complete / finish), Payanachas (Phinehas)' ayashah (woman / wife), was with harah (child), near to be yalad (birth / begot). When she shamai (hearken / hear) the shamawaih (news) that the arawan (ark) of Alahayam was laqach (take / seize), and that her father-in-law and her ayash (man / husband) were mawath (death), she karai (bowed) herself and gave yalad (birth / begot); for her tzayar (pains) hapak (came) on her.

About the ith (time) of her mawath (death) the women who natzab (stood) by her dabar (word / matter) to her, "Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid); for you have given yalad (birth / begot) to a ban (son)." But she didn't inah (answer / respond), neither did she shayath (put / appoint / make) it.

She qaraa (called) the nair (child) Ayakabawad (Ichabod), amar (spoke), "The kabawad (glory) has departed from Yashar-Al (Israel);" al (toward) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam was laqach (take / seize), and because of her father-in-law and her ayash (man / husband).
She amar (spoke), "The kabawad (glory) has departed from Yashar-Al (Israel); for the arawan (ark) of Alahayam is laqach (take / seize)."
Now the Palashathay (Philistines) had laqach (take / seize) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, and they bawaa (come) it from Abanahaizar (Ebenezer) to Ashadawad (Ashdod).
The Palashathay (Philistines) laqach (take / seize) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, and bawaa (come) it into the bayath (house) of Dagawan (Dagon), and yatzag (set) it by Dagawan (Dagon).

When they of ashadawaday (ashdod) arose shakam (early) on the next macharath (day), behold, Dagawan (Dagon) was napal (fall / be cast down) on his panayam (face) to the aratz (Earth/land) panayam (face) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah. They laqach (take / seize) Dagawan (Dagon), and shawab (turn back / repent) him in his maqawam (place) again.

When they arose shakam (early) on the next macharath (day) baqar (morning), behold, Dagawan (Dagon) was napal (fall / be cast down) on his panayam (face) to the aratz (Earth/land) panayam (face) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah; and the raash (head) of Dagawan (Dagon) and shanayam (two) the kapawath (palms) of his yad (hand) were karath (cut) off on the mapathan (threshold). Only Dagawan (Dagon's) torso was intact.

Therefore neither the kahanay (priests) of Dagawan (Dagon), nor any who bawaa (come) into Dagawan (Dagon's) bayath (house), darak (tread) on the mapathan (threshold) of Dagawan (Dagon) in Ashadawad (Ashdod), to this yawam (day).

But the yad (hand) of Yahawah was kabad (heavy) on them of ashadawaday (ashdod), and he shamam (destroyed) them, and nakah (struck) them with tumors, even Ashadawad (Ashdod) and its gabawal (border/boundary).

When the anashay (men) of Ashadawad (Ashdod) raah (see) that it was so, they amar (spoke), "The arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall not stay with us; for his yad (hand) is severe on us, and on Dagawan (Dagon) our Alahayam."

They shalach (send) therefore and asap (gathered) all the saranay (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) to them, and amar (spoke), "What shall we ishah (make) with the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel)?" They amar (spoke), "Let the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel) be sabab (carried) over to gath (gath)." They sabab (carried) the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel) there.

It was so, that achar (other) they had sabab (carried) it about, the yad (hand) of Yahawah was against the iyar (city) with a very gadawal (very great/important/mighty) mahawamah (confusion): and he nakah (struck) the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) of the iyar (city), both qatan (small / young / least) and gadawal (very great/important/mighty); and tumors broke out on them.

So they shalach (send) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam to Iqarawan (Ekron). It happened, as the arawan (ark) of Alahayam bawaa (come) to Iqarawan (Ekron), that the iqaranayam (ekronites) zaiq (cried) out, amar (spoke), "They have sabab (brought) about the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel) to us, to mawath (death) us and our im (nation / people)."

They shalach (send) therefore and asap (gathered) together all the saranay (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and they amar (spoke), "shalach (send) away the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), and shawab (turn back / repent) it go again to its own maqawam (place), that it not mawath (death) us and our im (nation / people)." For there was a mawath (death) mahawamah (confusion) throughout all the iyar (city); the yad (hand) of Alahayam was very kabad (heavy) there.
The anashayam (men) who didn't mawath (death) were nakah (struck) with the tumors; and the cry of the iyar (city) ilah (go up / offer) up to shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens).
The arawan (ark) of Yahawah was in the shadah (country) of the Palashathay (Philistines) shabai (seven) chadashayam (months).

The Palashathay (Philistines) qaraa (called) for the kahanayam (priests) and the diviners, amar (spoke), "What shall we ishah (make) with the arawan (ark) of Yahawah? Show us with which we shall shalach (send) it to its maqawam (place)."

They amar (spoke), "If you shalach (send) away the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), don't shalach (send) it rayaqam (empty); but by shawab (turn back / repent) means shawab (turn back / repent) him a asham (trespass) offering: then you shall be rapaa (healed), and it shall be yadai (known) to you why his yad (hand) is not sawar (removed) from you."

Then they amar (spoke), "What shall be the asham (trespass) offering which we shall shawab (turn back / repent) to him?" They amar (spoke), "chamash (five) zahab (gold) tumors, and chamash (five) zahab (gold) ikabaray (mice), for the masapar (number) of the saranay (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines); for achad (one) magapah (plague) was on you all, and on your saranay (lords).

Therefore you shall ishah (make) tzalamay (images) of your tumors, and tzalamay (images) of your ikabar (mice) that shachath (mar) the aratz (Earth/land); and you shall nathan (give) kabawad (glory) to the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel): perhaps he will lighten his yad (hand) from off you, and from off your Alahayam, and from off your aratz (Earth/land).

Why then kabad (do) you harden your labab (hearts), as the Matzaray (Egyptians) and Paraih (Pharaoh) kabad (hardened) their lab (heart)? When he had ilal (worked) wonderfully among them, didn't they shalach (send) the people go, and they departed?

"Now therefore laqach (take / seize) and ishah (make) yourselves a chadash (new) igalah (cart), and shanayam (two) milk parawath (cows), on which there has ilah (go up / offer) no il (over); and asar (tie) the parawath (cows) to the igalah (cart), and shawab (turn back / repent) their calves bayath (house) from them;

And laqach (take / seize) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, and nathan (give) it on the igalah (cart); and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the kalay (jewels) of zahab (gold), which you shawab (turn back / repent) him for a asham (trespass) offering, in a aragaz (coffer) by its tzad (side); and shalach (send) it away, that it may halak (move).

Raah (see); if it ilah (go up / offer) up by the darak (way) of its own gabawal (border/boundary) to Bayath-Shamash (Beth Shemesh), then he ishah (make) done us this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) rai (evil): but if not, then we shall yadai (know) that it is not his yad (hand) that nagai (struck) us; it was a maqarah (chance) that hayah (came to pass) to us."
The yaishaw (men) ishah (make) so, and laqach (take / seize) shanayam (two) milk parawath (cows), and asar (tied) them to the igalah (cart), and kalaa (shut) up their calves at bayath (house);

And they shawam (place / establish / appoint) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah on the igalah (cart), and the aragaz (coffer) with the ikabaray (mice) of zahab (gold) and the tzalamay (images) of their tumors.

The parawath (cows) took the yashar (upright) darak (way) by the darak (way) to Bayath-Shamash (Beth Shemesh); they halak (move) along the masalah (highway), gaih (lowing) as they halak (move), and didn't sawar (turn) aside to the right yamayan (right hand) or to the shamaawal (left hand); and the saranay (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) halak (move) achar (other) them to the gabawal (border/boundary) of Bayath-Shamash (Beth Shemesh).

They of Bayath-Shamash (Beth Shemesh) were qatzar (reaping) their chatah (wheat) qatzayar (harvest) in the imaq (valley); and they nashaa (lift) up their iyan (eye), and raah (see) the arawan (ark), and shamach (rejoiced) to raah (see) it.

The igalah (cart) bawaa (come) into the shadah (field) of Yahawashawai (Joshua) of Beth Shemesh, and imad (stood) there, where there was a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) aban (stone): and they split the itz (wood) of the igalah (cart), and ilah (go up / offer) up the parawath (cows) for a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah.

The Lawayay (Levites) yarad (took) down the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, and the aragaz (coffer) that was with it, in which the kalay (jewels) of zahab (gold) were, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them on the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) aban (stone): and the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) of Bayath-Shamash (Beth Shemesh) ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilawath (offerings) and zabach (sacrificed) zabachayam (sacrifices) the same yawam (day) to Yahawah.
When the chamash (five) saranay (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) raah (see) seen it, they shawab (turn back / repent) to Iqarawan (Ekron) the same yawam (day).

These are the zahab (gold) tumors which the Palashathay (Philistines) shawab (turn back / repent) for a asham (trespass) offering to Yahawah: for Ashadawad (Ashdod) achad (one), for Izah (Gaza) achad (one), for Ashaqalawan (Ashkelon) achad (one), for gath (gath) achad (one), for Iqarawan (Ekron) achad (one);

And the zahab (gold) ikabaray (mice), according to the masapar (number) of all the iray (cities) of the Palashathay (Philistines) belonging to the chamash (five) saranayam (lords), both of fortified iray (cities) and of country kapar (villages), even to the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) Abal (stone), whereon they yanach (set) down the arawan (ark) of Yahawah. That stone remains to this yawam (day) in the shadah (field) of Yahawashawai (Joshua) of Beth Shemesh.

He nakah (struck) of the anashay (men) of Bayath-Shamash (Beth Shemesh), because they raah (see) looked into the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, he nakah (struck) of the im (nation / people) chamashayam (fifty) alap (thousand) shabaiyam (seventy) anashay (men); and the im (nation / people) abal (mourned), because Yahawah had nakah (struck) the anashay (people) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) makah (slaughter).

The anashay (men) of Bayath-Shamash (Beth Shemesh) amar (spoke), "Who is yakal (able) to imad (stand) panayam (face) Yahawah, this qadawash (holy) Alahayam? To whom shall he ilah (go up / offer) up from us?"

They shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to the yawashabay (inhabitants) of Kiriath Qarayath-Yairayam (Jearim), amar (spoke), "The Palashathay (Philistines) have shawab (turn back / repent) back the arawan (ark) of Yahawah; yarad (come) down, and ilah (go up / offer) it up to yourselves."

The anashay (men) of Kiriath Qarayath-Yairayam (Jearim) bawaa (come), and ilah (go up / offer) up the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, and bawaa (come) it into the bayath (house) of Abayanadab (Abinadab) in the gabaih (hill), and qadash (set apart / make holy) Alaizar (Eleazar) his ban (son) to shamar (keep/guard) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah.

It happened, from the yawam (day) that the arawan (ark) stayed in Kiriath Qarayath-Yairayam (Jearim), that the yawam (day) was rabah (long); for it was isharayam (twenty) shanah (years): and all the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) nahah (lamented) achar (other) Yahawah.

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to all the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), amar (spoke), "If you do shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah with all your labab (heart), then sawar (put) away the foreign Alahayam and the Ishatharawath (Ashtaroth) from thawak (midst) you, and kawan (direct) your labab (hearts) to Yahawah, and ibad (servant) him only; and he will natzal (deliver) you out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines)."
Then the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) sawar (removed) the Bail (Baals) and the Ishatharawath (Ashtaroth), and ibad (servant) Yahawah only.
Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), "qabatz (gather) all Yashar-Al (Israel) to Mizpah, and I will palal (pray) for you to Yahawah."

They qabatz (gathered) together to Matzapah (Mizpah), and shaab (drew) mayam (Waters), and shapak (poured) it out panayam (face) Yahawah, and tzawam (fasted) on that yawam (day), and amar (spoke) there, "We have chataa (sinned) against Yahawah." Shamawaal (Samuel) shapat (judge / judgement) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) in Mizpah.

When the Palashathay (Philistines) shamai (hearken / hear) that the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) were qabatz (gathered) together at Mizpah, the saranay (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up against Yashar-Al (Israel). When the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shamai (hearken / hear) it, they were yaraa (fear / be afraid) of the Palashathay (Philistines).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), "Don't charash (cease) to zaiq (cry) to Yahawah our Alahayam for us, that he will yashai (salvation) us out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines)."

Shamawaal (Samuel) laqach (take / seize) a suckling talah (lamb), and ilah (go up / offer) it for a kalayal (whole) burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah: and Shamawaal (Samuel) zaiq (cried) to Yahawah for Yashar-Al (Israel); and Yahawah inah (answer / respond) him.

As Shamawaal (Samuel) was ilah (go up / offer) up the burnt ilah (offering), the Palashathay (Philistines) nagash (drew) near to malachamah (battle) against Yashar-Al (Israel); but Yahawah raim (thundered) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice) on that yawam (day) on the Palashathay (Philistines), and confused them; and they were nagap (struck) down panayam (face) Yashar-Al (Israel).

The anashay (men) of Yashar-Al (Israel) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of Matzapah (Mizpah), and radap (pursued) the Palashathay (Philistines), and nakah (struck) them, until they came under Bayathakar (Beth Kar).

Then Shamawaal (Samuel) laqach (take / seize) a aban (stone), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it between Matzapah (Mizpah) and Shan (Shen), and qaraa (called) its sham (name) Abanahaizar (Ebenezer), amar (spoke), "Yahawah izar (helped) us until now."

So the Palashathay (Philistines) were kanai (subdued), and they bawaa (come) no more within the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yashar-Al (Israel). The yad (hand) of Yahawah was against the Palashathay (Philistines) all the yamay (days) of Shamawaal (Samuel).

The irayam (cities) which the Palashathay (Philistines) had laqach (take / seize) from Yashar-Al (Israel) were shawab (turn back / repent) to Yashar-Al (Israel), from Iqarawan (Ekron) even to gath (gath); and Yashar-Al (Israel) natzal (recovered) its gabawal (border/boundary) out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines). There was shalawam (peace / safety) between Yashar-Al (Israel) and the Amaray (Amorites).
Shamawaal (Samuel) shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel) all the yamay (days) of his chay (life).

He halak (move) from shanah (year) to shanah (year) in sabab (circuit) to Bayath-Al (Bethel) and Galagal (Gilgal), and Matzapah (Mizpah); and he shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel) in all those maqawamawath (places).
His thashawabah (return) was to Ramah (Ramah), for there was his bayath (house); and there he shapat (judge / judgement) Yashar-Al (Israel): and he banah (build) there an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah.
It happened, when Shamawaal (Samuel) was zaqan (old), that he shawam (place / establish / appoint) his ban (son) shapatayam (judges) over Yashar-Al (Israel).
Now the sham (name) of his ban (son) was Yawaal (Joel); and the sham (name) of his mashanah (second), Abayah (Abijah): they were shapatayam (judges) in Baar-Shabai (Beersheba).
His ban (son) didn't halak (move) in his darak (ways), but natah (turned) aside achar (other) batzai (lucre), and laqach (take / seize) shachad (bribes), and natah (perverted) mashapat (justice).
Then all the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel) qabatz (gathered) themselves together, and bawaa (come) to Shamawaal (Samuel) to Ramah (Ramah);

And they amar (spoke) to him, "Behold, you are zaqan (old), and your ban (son) don't halak (move) in your darak (ways): now shawam (place / establish / appoint) us a malak (king) to shapat (judge / judgement) us like all the gawayam (nations)."
But the thing displeased Shamawaal (Samuel), when they amar (spoke), "nathan (give) us a malak (king) to shapat (judge / judgement) us." Shamawaal (Samuel) palal (prayed) to Yahawah.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), "shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of the im (nation / people) in all that they amar (spoke) you; for they have not maas (rejected) you, but they have maas (rejected) me, that I should not be malak (king) over them.

According to all the maishayam (works) which they ishah (make) done since the yawam (day) that I ilah (go up / offer) them up out of Matzarayam (Egypt) even to this yawam (day), in that they have forsaken me, and ibad (servant) other Alahayam, so ishah (make) they also to you.

Now therefore shamai (hearken / hear) to their qawal (sound / voice): however you shall iwad (admonish/bear witness against) iwad (admonish/bear witness against) to them, and shall show them the mashapat (way) of the malak (king) who shall malak (king) over them."
Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) all the dabaray (words) of Yahawah to the im (nation / people) who shaal (asked) of him a malak (king).

He amar (spoke), "This will be the mashapat (way) of the malak (king) who shall malak (king) over you: he will laqach (take / seize) your ban (son), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them to him, for his marakabah (chariots), and to be his horsemen; and they shall rawatz (run) panayam (face) his marakabah (chariots);

And he will shawam (place / establish / appoint) them to him for sharay (captains) of alapayam (thousands), and sharay (captains) of chamashayam (fifties); and he will assign some to charash (plow) his charayash (ground), and to qatzar (reap) his qatzayar (harvest), and to ishah (make) his kalay (instruments) of malachamah (war), and the kalay (instruments) of his rakab (chariots).
He will laqach (take / seize) your banath (daughter) to be perfumers, and to be tabachawath (cooks), and to be bakers.

He will laqach (take / seize) your shadah (fields), and your karam (vineyards), and your zayath (olive) groves, even their tawab (good / proper function), and nathan (give) them to his ibad (servant).
He will take the ishar (tenth) of your zarai (seed), and of your karam (vineyards), and nathan (give) to his sarayas (officers), and to his ibad (servant).

He will laqach (take / seize) your male ibad (servant), and your female ibad (servant), and your tawab (good / proper function) bachawar (young) men, and your donkeys, and ishah (make) them to his malaakah (work).
He will take the ishar (tenth) of your tzaan (flocks): and you shall be his ibadayam (servants).
You shall zaiq (cry) out in that yawam (day) panayam (face) of your malak (king) whom you shall have bachar (chosen) you; and Yahawah will not inah (answer / respond) you in that yawam (day)."
But the im (nation / people) maan (refused) to shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of Shamawaal (Samuel); and they amar (spoke), "No; but we will have a malak (king) over us,

That we also may be like all the gawayam (nations), and that our malak (king) may shapat (judge / judgement) us, and yatzaa (go out / come out) out panayam (face) us, and lacham (fight) our malachamah (battles)."
Shamawaal (Samuel) shamai (hearken / hear) all the dabaray (words) of the im (nation / people), and he dabar (word / matter) them in the azanay (ears) of Yahawah.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), "shamai (hearken / hear) to their qawal (sound / voice), and malak (king) them a malak (king)." Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to the anashay (men) of Yashar-Al (Israel), "Every ayash (man / husband) yalak (go) to his iyar (city)."

Now there was a ayash (man / husband) of Benjamin, whose sham (name) was Qayash (Kish), the ban (son) of Abayaal (Abiel), the ban (son) of Zeror, the ban (son) of Bakawarath (Becorath), the ban (son) of Apayach (Aphiah), the son of a Benjamite, a gabawar (mighty) ayash (man / husband) of valor.

He had a ban (son), whose sham (name) was Shaawal (Saul), an impressive bachawar (young) man; and there was not among the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) a tawab (good / proper function) ayash (man / husband) than he. From his shakam (shoulders) and upward he was gabah (higher) than any of the im (nation / people).

The donkeys of Qayash (Kish), Shaawal (Saul's) ab (father), were abad (destroy / perish). Qayash (Kish) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul) his ban (son), "laqach (take / seize) now achad (one) of the nairayam (servants) with you, and qawam (rise up), yalak (go) baqash (seek) the donkeys."

He ibar (pass over/through) through the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), and ibar (pass over/through) through the aratz (Earth/land) of Shalashah (Shalishah), but they didn't matzaa (find) them: then they ibar (pass over/through) through the aratz (Earth/land) of Shailayam (Shaalim), and there they weren't there: and he ibar (pass over/through) through the aratz (Earth/land) of the Benjamites, but they didn't matzaa (find) them.

When they bawaa (come) come to the aratz (Earth/land) of Tzawap (Zuph), Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to his nair (servant) who was with him, "yalak (come), and let us shawab (turn back / repent), lest my ab (father) stop caring about the donkeys, and be anxious for us."

He amar (spoke) to him, "See now, there is in this iyar (city) a ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, and he is a ayash (man / husband) who is held in honor. All that he dabar (word / matter) bawaa (come) bawaa (come) to pass. Now yalak (let) us go there. Perhaps he can nagad (tell) us concerning our darak (journey) whereon we halak (move)."

Then Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to his nair (servant), "But, behold, if we yalak (go), what shall we bawaa (come) the ayash (man / husband)? For the lacham (bread) is spent in our kalay (vessels), and there is not a thashawarah (present) to bawaa (come) to the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam. What do we have?"

The nair (servant) inah (answer / respond) Shaawal (Saul) again, and inah (answer / respond), "Behold, I matzaa (have) in my yad (hand) the rabai (fourth) part of a shaqal (shekel) of kasap (silver). I will nathan (give) that to the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, to nagad (tell) us our darak (way)."

(In earlier times in Yashar-Al (Israel), when a ayash (man / husband) yalak (went) to darash (inquire) of Alahayam, thus he amar (spoke), "yalak (come), and yalak (let) us go to the seer;" for he who is yawam (day) qaraa (called) a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) panayam (face) before qaraa (called) a Seer.)

Then Shaawal (Saul) dabar (word / matter) to his nair (servant), "tawab (good / proper function) amar (spoke). Yalak (come), yalak (let) us go." So they yalak (went) to the iyar (city) where the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam was.

As they ilah (go up / offer) up the ascent to the iyar (city), they matzaa (found) nairah (young) maidens yatzaa (go out / come out) out to shaab (draw) mayam (Waters), and amar (spoke) to them, "Is the seer here?"

They inah (answer / respond) them, and inah (answer / respond), "He is. Behold, he is panayam (face) you. Hurry now, for he bawaa (come) come today into the iyar (city); for the people have a zabach (sacrifice) today in the bamah (high) place.

As soon as you bawaa (come) come into the iyar (city), you shall immediately matzaa (find) him, before he ilaw (goes) up to the bamah (high) place to akal (eat); for the im (nation / people) will not akal (eat) until he bawaa (come), because he blesses the zabach (sacrifice). Afterwards those who are qaraa (called) akal (eat). Now therefore ilah (go up / offer) up; for at this yawam (day) you shall matzaa (find) him."

They ilah (go up / offer) up to the iyar (city). As they bawaa (come) within the iyar (city), behold, Shamawaal (Samuel) yatzaa (go out / come out) out toward them, to ilah (go up / offer) up to the bamah (high) place.
Now Yahawah had galah (revealed) to Shamawaal (Samuel) a yawam (day) panayam (face) Shaawal (Saul) bawaa (come), amar (spoke),

"Machar (tomorrow) about this ith (time) I will shalach (send) you a ayash (man / husband) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), and you shall mashach (anoint) him to be nagayad (prince) over my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel); and he shall yashai (salvation) my im (nation / people) out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines): for I raah (see) looked on my im (nation / people), because their tzaiqah (cry) bawaa (come) come to me."

When Shamawaal (Samuel) raah (see) Shaawal (Saul), Yahawah inah (answer / respond) to him, "Behold, the ayash (man / husband) of whom I amar (spoke) to you! This same shall have authority over my im (nation / people)."
Then Shaawal (Saul) nagash (drew) near to Shamawaal (Samuel) in the shair (gate), and amar (spoke), "Please nagad (tell) me ay (where) the seer's bayath (house) is."

Shamawaal (Samuel) inah (answer / respond) Shaawal (Saul), and inah (answer / respond), "I am the seer. Ilah (go up / offer) up panayam (face) me to the bamah (high) place, for you shall akal (eat) with me today. In the baqar (morning) I will shalach (send) you go, and will nagad (tell) you all that is in your labab (heart).

As for your donkeys who were abad (destroy / perish) shalawash (three) yamayam (days) ago, don't shawam (place / establish / appoint) your lab (heart) on them; for they are matzaa (found). For whom is all that is desirable in Yashar-Al (Israel)? Is it not for you, and for all your ab (father) bayath (house)?"

Shaawal (Saul) inah (answer / respond), "Am I not a Banayamayanay (Benjamite), of the smallest of the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel)? And my mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) the tzaiyar (least) of all the mashapachawath (families) of the shabat (tribe) of Banayamayan (Benjamin)? Why then do you dabar (word / matter) to me like this?"

Shamawaal (Samuel) laqach (take / seize) Shaawal (Saul) and his nair (servant), and bawaa (come) them into the guest room, and nathan (give) them sit in the best maqawam (place) among those who were qaraa (called), who were about shalawashayam (thirty) ayash (man / husband).
Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to the tabach (cook), "nathan (give) the manah (portion) which I nathan (give) you, of which I amar (spoke) to you, ‘shawam (place / establish / appoint) it aside.'"

The tabach (cook) rawam (will lift up) up the shawaq (thigh), and that which was on it, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it panayam (face) Shaawal (Saul). Samuel amar (spoke), "Behold, that which has been shaar (reserved)! Shawam (place / establish / appoint) it panayam (face) yourself and akal (eat); because for the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) time has it been shamar (keep/guard) for you, for I amar (spoke), ‘I have qaraa (called) the im (nation / people).'" So Shaawal (Saul) akal (eat) with Shamawaal (Samuel) that yawam (day).
When they had yarad (come) down from the bamah (high) place into the iyar (city), he dabar (word / matter) with Shaawal (Saul) on the housetop.

They arose shakam (early): and it happened about the ilah (go up / offer) of the shachar (day), that Shamawaal (Samuel) qaraa (called) to Shaawal (Saul) on the housetop, amar (spoke), "qawam (rise up) up, that I may shalach (send) you away." Shaawal (Saul) qawam (rise up), and they yatzaa (go out / come out) out shanayam (two) of them, he and Shamawaal (Samuel), chawatz (abroad).

As they were yarad (going) down at the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the iyar (city), Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "amar (spoke) the nair (servant) ibar (pass over/through) on panayam (face) us" (and he ibar (pass over/through) on), "but imad (stand) still yawam (day), that I may shamai (hearken / hear) you to hear the dabar (word / matter) of Alahayam."

Then Shamawaal (Samuel) laqach (take / seize) the pak (vial) of shaman (oil), and yatzaq (poured) it on his raash (head), and nashaq (kissed) him, and amar (spoke), "Isn't it that Yahawah has mashach (anointed) you to be nagayad (prince) over his nachalah (inheritance)?
