When you have departed from me today, then you shall matzaa (find) shanayam (two) anashayam (men) by Rachal (Rachel's) tomb, in the gabawal (border/boundary) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) at Tzalatzach (Zelzah); and they will amar (spoke) you, ‘The donkeys which you halak (move) to baqash (seek) matzaa (have) been found; and behold, your ab (father) has stopped dabar (word / matter) about the donkeys, and is anxious for you, amar (spoke), "What shall I ishah (make) for my ban (son)?"'

"Then you shall chalap (go) on halaah (forward) from there, and you shall bawaa (come) to the oak of Thabawar (Tabor); and shalawash (three) anashayam (men) shall matzaa (meet) you there ilah (go up / offer) up to Alahayam to Bayath-Al (Bethel), achad (one) nashaa (lift) shalawash (three) young goats, and another nashaa (lift) shalawash (three) loaves of lacham (bread), and another nashaa (lift) a nabal (bottle) of yayan (wine):
And they will greet you, and nathan (give) you shanayam (two) loaves of lacham (bread), which you shall laqach (take / seize) of their yad (hand).

"Achar (other) that you shall bawaa (come) to the gabaih (hill) of Alahayam, where is the natzayab (garrison) of the Palashathay (Philistines): and it shall happen, when you bawaa (come) come there to the iyar (city), that you shall pagai (meet) a chabal (band) of nabayaayam (prophets) yarad (coming) down from the bamah (high) place with a nabal (psaltery), and a tambourine, and a chalayal (pipe), and a kanawar (harp), panayam (face) them; and they will be nabaa (prophesying):
And the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah will tzalach (come) mightily on you, and you shall nabaa (prophesy) with them, and shall be hapak (turned) into achar (other) ayash (man / husband).
Let it be, when these athawath (signs) bawaa (come) come to you, that you ishah (make) as matzaa (occasion) shall yad (hand) you; for Alahayam is with you.

"You shall yarad (go) down panayam (face) me to Galagal (Gilgal); and behold, I will yarad (come) down to you, to ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilawath (offerings), and to ilah (go up / offer) zabach (sacrifices) of peace ilawath (offerings): you shall yachal (wait) shabai (seven) yamayam (days), until I bawaa (come) to you, and show you what you shall ishah (make)."

It was so, that when he had panah (turn) his shakam (back) to yalak (go) from Shamawaal (Samuel), Alahayam hapak (gave) him achar (other) lab (heart): and all those athawath (signs) happened that yawam (day).

When they bawaa (come) there to the gabaih (hill), behold, a chabal (band) of nabaayam (prophets) qaraa (called) him; and the rawach (spirit / wind) of Alahayam tzalach (came) mightily on him, and he nabaa (prophesied) thawak (midst) them.

It happened, when all who yadai (knew) him athamawal (before) raah (see) that, behold, he nabaa (prophesied) with the nabaayam (prophets), then the im (nation / people) amar (spoke) ayash (man / husband) to rai (neigbor/another person), "What is this that has come to the ban (son) of Qayash (Kish)? Is Shaawal (Saul) also among the nabaayam (prophets)?"
Ayash (man / husband) of the same place inah (answer / respond), "Who is their ab (father)?" Therefore it became a mashal (proverb), "Is Shaawal (Saul) also among the nabaayam (prophets)?"
When he kalah (complete / finish) made an end of nabaa (prophesying), he bawaa (come) to the bamah (high) place.

Shaawal (Saul's) dawad (uncle) amar (spoke) to him and to his nair (servant), "an (where) did you halak (move)?" He amar (spoke), "To baqash (seek) the donkeys. When we raah (see) that they were not found, we bawaa (come) to Shamawaal (Samuel)."
Shaawal (Saul's) dawad (uncle) amar (spoke), "Please nagad (tell) me what Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to you."

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to his dawad (uncle), "He amar (spoke) us nagad (plainly) that the donkeys were matzaa (found)." But dabar (word / matter) the matter of the malawakah (kingdom), of which Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), he didn't nagad (tell) him.
Shamawaal (Samuel) tzaiq (called) the im (nation / people) together to Yahawah to Matzapah (Mizpah);

And he amar (spoke) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), "Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), ‘I ilah (go up / offer) up Yashar-Al (Israel) out of Matzarayam (Egypt), and I natzal (delivered) you out of the yad (hand) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and out of the yad (hand) of all the mamalakawath (kingdoms) that lachatz (oppressed) you:'

But you have this yawam (day) maas (rejected) your Alahayam, who himself yashai (salvation) you out of all your rai (calamities) and your distresses; and you have amar (spoke) to him, ‘No! Shawam (place / establish / appoint) a malak (king) over us.' Now therefore yatzab (present) yourselves panayam (face) Yahawah by your shabat (tribes), and by your alap (thousands)."
So Shamawaal (Samuel) brought all the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel) qarab (come close), and the shabat (tribe) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) was lakad (taken).

He brought the shabat (tribe) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) qarab (come close) by their mashapachah (tribe / clan / family); and the mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) of the Matrites was lakad (taken); and Shaawal (Saul) the ban (son) of Qayash (Kish) was lakad (taken): but when they baqash (sought) him, he could not be matzaa (found).
Therefore they shaal (asked) of Yahawah further, "Is there yet a ayash (man / husband) to bawaa (come) here?" Yahawah amar (spoke), "Behold, he has chabaa (hidden) himself among the baggage."

They rawatz (ran) and laqach (take / seize) him there; and when he yatzab (stood) thawak (midst) the im (nation / people), he was gabah (higher) than any of the im (nation / people) from his shakam (shoulders) and upward.

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to all the im (nation / people), "You raah (see) him whom Yahawah has bachar (chosen), that there is none like him among all the im (nation / people)?" All the im (nation / people) rawai (shouted), and amar (spoke), "Let the malak (king) chayah (live)!"

Then Shamawaal (Samuel) dabar (word / matter) the im (nation / people) the regulations of the malawakah (kingdom), and kathab (write) it in a sapar (book / scribed document), and yanach (laid) it up panayam (face) Yahawah. Shamawaal (Samuel) shalach (send) all the im (nation / people) shalach (send), every ayash (man / husband) to his bayath (house).

Shaawal (Saul) also halak (move) to his bayath (house) to Gabaih (Gibeah); and there yalak (went) with him the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), whose lab (heart) Alahayam had nagai (touched).
But certain worthless fellows amar (spoke), "How shall this man yashai (salvation) us?" They bazah (despised) him, and bawaa (come) him no manachah (present). But he held his charash (peace).

Then Nachash (Nahash) the Imawanay (Ammonite) ilah (go up / offer) up, and chanah (encamped) against Yabash (Jabesh Gilead): and all the anashay (men) of Yabash (Jabesh) amar (spoke) to Nachash (Nahash), "karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with us, and we will ibad (servant) you."

Nachash (Nahash) the Imawanay (Ammonite) amar (spoke) to them, "On zaath (this) condition I will karath (cut) it with you, that all your yamayan (right hand) iyan (eye) be naqar (put) out; and I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) it for a charapah (reproach) on all Yashar-Al (Israel)."

The zaqanay (elders) of Yabash (Jabesh) amar (spoke) to him, "Give us shabai (seven) yamayam (days), that we may shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to all the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yashar-Al (Israel); and then, if there is no one to yashai (salvation) us, we will yatzaa (go out / come out) out to you."

Then the malaakayam (messengers) bawaa (come) to Gabaih (Gibeah) of Shaawal (Saul), and dabar (word / matter) these dabarayam (words) in the azanay (ears) of the im (nation / people): and all the im (nation / people) nashaa (lift) up their qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept).

Behold, Shaawal (Saul) bawaa (come) achar (other) the oxen out of the shadah (field); and Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "What ails the im (nation / people) that they bakah (weep)?" They sapar (book) him the dabaray (words) of the im (nation / people) of Yabash (Jabesh).

The rawach (spirit / wind) of Alahayam tzalach (came) mightily on Shaawal (Saul) when he shamai (hearken / hear) those dabarayam (words), and his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger) maad (greatly).

He laqach (take / seize) a tzamad (yoke) of oxen, and nathach (cut) them in pieces, and shalach (send) them throughout all the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yashar-Al (Israel) by the yad (hand) of malaakayam (messengers), amar (spoke), "Whoever doesn't yatzaa (go out / come out) forth achar (other) Shaawal (Saul) and achar (other) Shamawaal (Samuel), so shall it be ishah (make) to his oxen." The pachad (fear / dread) of Yahawah napal (fall / be cast down) on the im (nation / people), and they yatzaa (go out / come out) out as achad (one) ayash (man / husband).

He paqad (visit) them in Bazaq (Bezek); and the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) were shalawash (three) maah (hundred) alap (thousand), and the ayash (man / husband) of Yahawadah (Judah) shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand).

They amar (spoke) to the malaakayam (messengers) who bawaa (come), "Thus you shall amar (spoke) the anashay (men) of Yabash (Jabesh Gilead), ‘machar (tomorrow), by the time the shamash (sun) is cham (hot), you shall have thashawaih (deliverance).'" The malaakayam (messengers) bawaa (come) and nagad (told) the anashay (men) of Yabash (Jabesh); and they were shamach (glad).

Therefore the anashay (men) of Yabash (Jabesh) amar (spoke), "machar (tomorrow) we will yatzaa (go out / come out) out to you, and you shall ishah (make) with us all that seems tawab (good / proper function) to you."

It was so on the next macharath (day), that Shaawal (Saul) shawam (place / establish / appoint) the im (nation / people) in shalawash (three) raashayam (companies); and they bawaa (come) into the thawak (midst) of the machanah (camp) in the baqar (morning) ashamarah (watch), and nakah (struck) the Imawan (Ammonites) until the cham (heat) of the yawam (day): and it happened, that those who shaar (remained) were pawatz (scattered), so that no shanayam (two) of them were shaar (left) yachad (together).

The im (nation / people) amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), "Who is he who amar (spoke), ‘Shall Shaawal (Saul) malak (king) over us?' Nathan (give) those men, that we may put them to mawath (death)!"
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "There shall not a ayash (man / husband) be put to mawath (death) this yawam (day); for today Yahawah ishah (make) worked thashawaih (deliverance) in Yashar-Al (Israel)."
Then Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to the im (nation / people), "yalak (come), and yalak (let) us go to Galagal (Gilgal), and chadash (renew) the malawakah (kingdom) there."

All the im (nation / people) yalak (went) to Galagal (Gilgal); and there they made Shaawal (Saul) malak (king) panayam (face) Yahawah in Galagal (Gilgal); and there they zabach (offered) zabachayam (sacrifices) of shalam (peace) offerings panayam (face) Yahawah; and there Shaawal (Saul) and all the im (nation / people) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shamach (rejoiced) maad (greatly).

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to all Yashar-Al (Israel), "Behold, I have shamai (hearken / hear) to your qawal (sound / voice) in all that you amar (spoke) to me, and have malak (king) a malak (king) over you.

Now, behold, the malak (king) halak (move) panayam (face) you; and I am zaqan (old) and shayab (gray-headed); and behold, my ban (son) are with you: and I have halak (move) panayam (face) you from my naiwar (youth) to this yawam (day).

Here I am. Inah (answer / respond) against me before Yahawah, and before his mashayach (anointed one). Whose shawar (ox) have I laqach (take / seize)? Whose donkey have I laqach (take / seize)? Whom have I ishaq (defrauded)? Whom have I ratzatz (oppressed)? Of whose yad (hand) have I taken a kapar (ransom) to ilam (blind) my iyan (eye) therewith? I will shawab (turn back / repent) it to you."
They amar (spoke), "You have not ishaq (defrauded) us, nor ratzatz (oppressed) us, neither have you laqach (take / seize) anything of any ayash (man / husband) yad (hand)."

He amar (spoke) to them, "Yahawah is id (until / as far as) against you, and his mashayach (anointed one) is id (until / as far as) this yawam (day), that you matzaa (have) not found anything in my yad (hand)." They amar (spoke), "He is id (until / as far as)."

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to the im (nation / people), "It is Yahawah who ishah (make) Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron), and that ilah (go up / offer) your ab (father) up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

Now therefore yatzab (stand) still, that I may shapat (judge / judgement) with you panayam (face) Yahawah concerning all the tzadaqah (righteousness) acts of Yahawah, which he ishah (make) to you and to your ab (father).

"When Yaiqab (Jacob) bawaa (come) come into Matzarayam (Egypt), and your ab (father) zaiq (cried) to Yahawah, then Yahawah shalach (send) Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron), who brought your ab (father) out of Matzarayam (Egypt), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) them to dwell in this maqawam (place).

"But they shakach (forgot) Yahawah their Alahayam; and he makar (sold) them into the yad (hand) of Sayasaraa (Sisera), shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop) of Chatzawar (Hazor), and into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab); and they lacham (fought) against them.

They zaiq (cried) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), ‘We have chataa (sinned), because we have forsaken Yahawah, and have ibad (servant) the Bail (Baals) and the Ishatharawath (Ashtaroth): but now natzal (deliver) us out of the yad (hand) of our ayab (enemy), and we will ibad (servant) you.'

Yahawah shalach (send) Yarabail (Jerubbaal), and Badan (Bedan), and Yapathach (Jephthah), and Shamawaal (Samuel), and natzal (delivered) you out of the yad (hand) of your ayab (enemy) on sabayab (surrounding) side; and you lived in safety.

"When you raah (see) that Nachash (Nahash) the malak (king) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) bawaa (come) amar (spoke) you, you said to me, ‘No, but a malak (king) shall malak (king) over us;' when Yahawah your Alahayam was your malak (king).
Now therefore see the malak (king) whom you have bachar (chosen), and whom you have shaal (asked) for: and behold, Yahawah nathan (give) set a malak (king) over you.

If you will yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah, and ibad (servant) him, and shamai (hearken / hear) to his qawal (sound / voice), and not marah (rebel) against the commandment of Yahawah, then both you and also the malak (king) who malak (king) over you are followers of Yahawah your Alahayam.

But if you will not shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah, but marah (rebel) against the commandment of Yahawah, then will the yad (hand) of Yahawah be against you, as it was against your ab (father).
"Now gam (indeed / moreover) yatzab (stand) still and raah (see) this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thing, which Yahawah will ishah (make) before your iyan (eye).

Isn't it chatah (wheat) qatzayar (harvest) today? I will qaraa (called) to Yahawah, that he may nathan (give) qawal (sound / voice) and matar (rain); and you shall yadai (know) and raah (see) that your rai (wickedness) is rab (great), which you ishah (make) done in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, in shaal (asking) for a malak (king)."

So Shamawaal (Samuel) qaraa (called) to Yahawah; and Yahawah nathan (give) qawal (sound / voice) and matar (rain) that yawam (day): and all the im (nation / people) maad (greatly) yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah and Shamawaal (Samuel).

All the im (nation / people) amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), "palal (pray) for your ibad (servant) to Yahawah your Alahayam, that we not mawath (death); for we have yasap (added) to all our chataah (sin) this rai (evil), to shaal (ask) us a malak (king)."

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to the im (nation / people), "Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). You ishah (make) indeed done all this rai (evil); yet don't sawar (turn) aside from achar (other) Yahawah, but ibad (servant) Yahawah with all your labab (heart).
Don't sawar (turn) aside to go achar (other) thahaw (formless) things which can't yail (profit) nor natzal (deliver), for they are thahaw (formless).

For Yahawah will not natash (forsake) his im (nation / people) for his gadawal (very great/important/mighty) sham (name) sake, because it has yaal (pleased) Yahawah to ishah (make) you a im (nation / people) to himself.

Moreover as for me, chalayalah (far) be it from me that I should chataa (sin) against Yahawah in chadal (ceasing) to palal (pray) for you: but I will yarah (instruct) you in the tawab (good / proper function) and the yashar (upright) darak (way).
Only yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah, and ibad (servant) him in amath (truth) with all your labab (heart); for raah (see) how gadal (great) things he has done for you.
But if you shall still raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) wickedly, you shall be sapah (consumed), both you and your malak (king)."
Shaawal (Saul) malak (king) a year; and when he had malak (king) shanayam (two) shanayam (years) over Yashar-Al (Israel),

Shaawal (Saul) bachar (chose) for himself shalawash (three) alap (thousand) men of Yashar-Al (Israel), of which two alap (thousand) were with Shaawal (Saul) in Makamas (Michmash) and in the har (mountain) of Bayath-Al (Bethel), and one alap (thousand) were with Yawanathan (Jonathan) in Gabaih (Gibeah) of Banayamayan (Benjamin): and the yathar (rest) of the im (nation / people) he shalach (send) every ayash (man / husband) to his ahal (tent).

Yawanathan (Jonathan) nakah (struck) the natzayab (garrison) of the Palashathay (Philistines) that was in Gabai (Geba): and the Palashathay (Philistines) shamai (hearken / hear) of it. Shaawal (Saul) thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn) throughout all the aratz (Earth/land), amar (spoke), "Let the ibarayam (hebrews) shamai (hearken / hear)!"

All Yashar-Al (Israel) shamai (hearken / hear) that Shaawal (Saul) had nakah (struck) the natzayab (garrison) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and also that Yashar-Al (Israel) was had in baash (abomination) with the Palashathay (Philistines). The im (nation / people) were tzaiq (gathered) together achar (other) Shaawal (Saul) to Galagal (Gilgal).

The Palashathay (Philistines) asap (assembled) themselves together to lacham (fight) with Yashar-Al (Israel), shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand) rakab (chariots), and shash (six) alap (thousand) horsemen, and im (nation / people) as the chawal (sand) which is on the seashore in rab (multitude): and they ilah (go up / offer) up, and chanah (encamped) in Makamas (Michmash), qadamah (eastward) of Bayathaawan (Beth Aven).

When the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) raah (see) that they were in a tzar (oppressor / distressor) (for the im (nation / people) were nagash (distressed)), then the im (nation / people) chabaa (hid) themselves in mairawath (caves), and in chawachayam (thickets), and in salaiyam (rocks), and in coverts, and in barawath (pits).

Now some of the ibarayam (hebrews) ibar (pass over/through) gone over the Yaradan (Jordan) to the aratz (Earth/land) of Gad (Gad) and Galaid (Gilead); but as for Shaawal (Saul), he was yet in Galagal (Gilgal), and all the im (nation / people) achar (other) him charad (trembling).

He yachal (stayed) shabai (seven) yamayam (days), according to the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) set by Shamawaal (Samuel): but Shamawaal (Samuel) didn't bawaa (come) to Galagal (Gilgal); and the im (nation / people) were pawatz (scattered) from him.
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "nagash (bring) here the burnt ilah (offering) to me, and the shalam (peace) offerings." He ilah (go up / offer) the burnt ilah (offering).

It came to kalah (complete / finish) that as soon as he had made an end of ilah (go up / offer) the burnt ilah (go up / offer), behold, Shamawaal (Samuel) bawaa (come); and Shaawal (Saul) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraa (called) him, that he might greet him.

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), "What ishah (make) you done?" Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "Because I raah (see) that the im (nation / people) were napatz (scattered) from me, and that you didn't bawaa (come) within the yamayam (days) mawaid (Feast/Holy Day), and that the Palashathay (Philistines) asap (assembled) themselves together at Makamas (Michmash);

Therefore I amar (spoke), ‘Now the Palashathay (Philistines) will yarad (come) down on me to Galagal (Gilgal), and I haven't entreated the favor of Yahawah.' I apaq (forced) myself therefore, and ilah (go up / offer) the burnt ilah (offering)."

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "You have sakal (done) foolishly. You have not shamar (keep/guard) the matzawah (commandment) of Yahawah your Alahayam, which he tzawah (commanded) you; for now Yahawah would have kawan (established) your mamalakah (kingdom) on Yashar-Al (Israel) iwalam (forever).

But now your mamalakah (kingdom) shall not qawam (rise up). Yahawah has baqash (sought) for himself a ayash (man / husband) after his own labab (heart), and Yahawah has tzawah (appointed) him to be nagayad (prince) over his im (nation / people), because you have not shamar (keep/guard) that which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) you."

Shamawaal (Samuel) qawam (rise up), and ilah (go up / offer) from Galagal (Gilgal) to Gabaih (Gibeah) of Banayamayan (Benjamin). Shaawal (Saul) paqad (visit) the im (nation / people) who were matzaa (present) with him, about shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband).

Shaawal (Saul), and Yawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son), and the im (nation / people) who were matzaa (present) with them, stayed in Gabai (Geba) of Banayamayan (Benjamin): but the Palashathay (Philistines) chanah (encamped) in Makamas (Michmash).

The shachath (spoilers) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the machanah (camp) of the Palashathay (Philistines) in shalawash (three) raashayam (companies): achad (one) raash (head) panah (turn) to the darak (way) that leads to Iparah (Ophrah), to the aratz (Earth/land) of Shawail (Shual);

And another raash (head) panah (turn) the darak (way) to Bayathachawarawan (Beth Horon); and another raash (head) panah (turn) the darak (way) of the gabawal (border/boundary) that shaqap (looks) down on the gayaa (valley) of Tzabaiyam (Zeboim) toward the madabar (wilderness).

Now there was no charash (smith) matzaa (found) throughout all the aratz (Earth/land) of Yashar-Al (Israel); for the Palashathay (Philistines) amar (spoke), "Lest the ibarayam (hebrews) ishah (make) them charab (sword) or chanayath (spears);"
But all the Yashar-Al (Israelites) yarad (went) down to the Palashathay (Philistines), to latash (sharpen) every ayash (man / husband) his plowshare, macharashah (mattock), axe, and sickle;
Yet they had a patzayarah (file) for the macharashath (mattocks), and for the athayam (plowshares), and for the shalawash (three), and for the axes, and to natzab (set) the darabawan (goads).

So it came to pass in the yawam (day) of malachamah (battle), that there was neither charab (sword) nor chanayath (spear) matzaa (found) in the yad (hand) of any of the im (nation / people) who were with Shaawal (Saul) and Yawanathan (Jonathan): but with Shaawal (Saul) and with Yawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son) was there matzaa (found).
The matzab (garrison) of the Palashathay (Philistines) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to the maibar (pass) of Makamas (Michmash).

Now it fell on a yawam (day), that Yawanathan (Jonathan) the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to the nair (young) man who nashaa (lift) his armor, "yalak (come), and let us ibar (pass over/through) over to the Palashathay (Philistines)' matzab (garrison), that is on the other ibar (side)." But he didn't nagad (tell) his ab (father).

Shaawal (Saul) stayed in the uttermost part of Gabaih (Gibeah) under the ramawan (pomegranate) tree which is in Magarawan (Migron): and the im (nation / people) who were with him were about shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband);

And Achayah (Ahijah), the ban (son) of Achayatawab (Ahitub), Ayakabawad (Ichabod's) ach (brother/kinsman), the ban (son) of Payanachas (Phinehas), the ban (son) of Ilay (Eli), the kahan (priest) of Yahawah in Shayalah (Shiloh), nashaa (lift) an apawad (ephod). The im (nation / people) didn't yadai (know) that Yawanathan (Jonathan) was halak (move).

Between the passes, by which Yawanathan (Jonathan) baqash (sought) to ibar (pass over/through) over to the Palashathay (Philistines)' matzab (garrison), there was a rocky shan (crag) on the one ibar (side), and a rocky shan (crag) on the other ibar (side): and the sham (name) of the achad (one) was Bawatzatz (Bozez), and the sham (name) of the other Sanah (Seneh).
The achad (one) shan (crag) rose up on the tzapawan (north) in front of Makamas (Michmash), and the other on the nagab (south) in mawal (front) of Gabai (Geba).

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke) to the nair (young) man who nashaa (lift) his armor, "yalak (come), and let us ibar (pass over/through) over to the matzab (garrison) of these iral (uncircumcised). It may be that Yahawah will ishah (make) for us; for there is no maitzawar (restraint) on Yahawah to yashai (salvation) by many or by mait (few)."
His armor bearer amar (spoke) to him, "ishah (make) all that is in your labab (heart). Natah (turn) and, behold, I am with you according to your labab (heart)."
Then Yahawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke), "Behold, we will ibar (pass over/through) over to the ibarayam (men), and we will galah (reveal) ourselves to them.
If they amar (spoke) thus to us, ‘damam (wait) until we nagai (come) to you!' Then we will imad (stand) still in our place, and will not ilah (go up / offer) up to them.

But if they amar (spoke) this, ‘ilah (go up / offer) up to us!' Then we will ilah (go up / offer) up; for Yahawah nathan (give) delivered them into our yad (hand). This shall be the awath (sign / mark / miracle) to us."

Shanayam (two) of them galah (revealed) themselves to the matzab (garrison) of the Palashathay (Philistines): and the Palashathay (Philistines) amar (spoke), "Behold, the ibarayam (hebrews) are yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the charayam (holes) where they had chabaa (hidden) themselves!"

The anashay (men) of the matzabah (garrison) inah (answer / respond) Yawanathan (Jonathan) and his armor bearer, and amar (spoke), "ilah (go up / offer) up to us, and we yadai (will) show you something!" Yawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke) to his armor bearer, "ilah (go up / offer) up achar (other) me; for Yahawah nathan (give) delivered them into the yad (hand) of Yashar-Al (Israel)."

Yawanathan (Jonathan) ilah (go up / offer) up on his yad (hand) and on his ragal (feet / foot), and his armor bearer achar (other) him: and they napal (fall / be cast down) panayam (face) Yawanathan (Jonathan); and his armor bearer mawath (death) them achar (other) him.

That raashawan (first) makah (slaughter), which Yawanathan (Jonathan) and his armor bearer nakah (made), was about isharayam (twenty) ayash (man / husband), within as it were chatzay (half) a furrow's length in an mainah (acre) of shadah (land).

There was a charadah (trembling) in the machanah (camp), in the shadah (field), and among all the im (nation / people); the matzab (garrison), and the shachath (spoilers), they also charad (trembled); and the aratz (Earth/land) ragaz (quaked): so there was an alahayam (God) great charadah (trembling).
The watchmen of Shaawal (Saul) in Gabaih (Gibeah) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) raah (see); and behold, the hamawan (multitude) mawag (melted) away, and scattered.

Then Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to the im (nation / people) who were with him, "paqad (visit) now, and raah (see) who is missing from us." When they paqad (visit) counted, behold, Yawanathan (Jonathan) and his armor bearer were not there.
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Achayah (Ahijah), "Bring the arawan (ark) of Alahayam here." For the arawan (ark) of Alahayam was with the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) at that yawam (day).

It happened, while Shaawal (Saul) dabar (word / matter) to the kahan (priest), that the hamawan (tumult) that was in the machanah (camp) of the Palashathay (Philistines) yalak (went) on and rab (increased): and Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to the kahan (priest), "asap (withdraw) your yad (hand)!"

Shaawal (Saul) and all the im (nation / people) who were with him were zaiq (gathered) together, and bawaa (come) to the malachamah (battle): and behold, every ayash (man / husband) charab (sword) was against his rai (neigbor/another person): a very gadawal (very great/important/mighty) mahawamah (confusion).

Now the ibarayam (hebrews) who were with the Palashathay (Philistines) as athamawal (before), and who ilah (go up / offer) up with them into the machanah (camp), from all around, even they also turned to be with the Yashar-Al (Israelites) who were with Shaawal (Saul) and Yawanathan (Jonathan).

Likewise all the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) who had chabaa (hidden) themselves in the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), when they shamai (hearken / hear) that the Palashathay (Philistines) nawas (fled), even they also dabaq (followed) hard achar (other) them in the malachamah (battle).
So Yahawah yashai (salvation) Yashar-Al (Israel) that yawam (day): and the malachamah (battle) ibar (pass over/through) over by Bayathaawan (Beth Aven).

The ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) were nagash (distressed) that yawam (day); for Shaawal (Saul) had alah (swear / adjure) the im (nation / people), amar (spoke), "arar (cursed) is the ayash (man / husband) who akal (eat) any lacham (food) until it is irab (evening), and I am naqam (avenged) of my ayab (enemy)." So none of the im (nation / people) taim (tasted) lacham (food).
All the aratz (Earth/land) bawaa (come) into the yair (forest); and there was dabash (honey) on the shadah (ground).

When the im (nation / people) bawaa (come) come to the yair (forest), behold, the dabash (honey) halak (move): but no man nashag (put) his yad (hand) to his pah (mouth); for the im (nation / people) yaraa (fear / be afraid) the shabawaih (oath).

But Yawanathan (Jonathan) didn't shamai (hearken / hear) when his ab (father) commanded the im (nation / people) with the shabai (swear / take oath): therefore he shalach (send) forth the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the matah (staff / rod / tribe) who was in his yad (hand), and tabal (dipped) it in the yairah (honeycomb), and shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand) to his pah (mouth); and his iyan (eye) were enlightened.

Then ayash (man / husband) of the im (nation / people) inah (answer / respond), and amar (spoke), "Your ab (father) directly commanded the im (nation / people) with an shabai (swear / take oath), amar (spoke), ‘arar (cursed) is the ayash (man / husband) who akal (eat) lacham (food) this yawam (day).'" The im (nation / people) were iwap (flying).

Then Yawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke), "My ab (father) has ikar (troubled) the aratz (Earth/land). Please raah (see) how my iyan (eye) have been enlightened, because I taim (tasted) a mait (little) of this dabash (honey).

Ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) much more, if perhaps the im (nation / people) had akal (eat) akal (eat) today of the shalal (spoil) of their ayab (enemy) which they matzaa (found)? For now rabah (has) there been no great makah (slaughter) among the Palashathay (Philistines)."
They nakah (struck) of the Palashathay (Philistines) that yawam (day) from Makamas (Michmash) to Ayalawan (Aijalon). The im (nation / people) were very iwap (flying);

And the im (nation / people) ishah (make) on the shalal (spoil), and laqach (take / seize) tzaan (sheep), and cattle, and calves, and shachat (killed) them on the aratz (Earth/land); and the im (nation / people) akal (eat) them with the dam (blood).

Then they nagad (told) Shaawal (Saul), amar (spoke), "Behold, the im (nation / people) are chataa (sinning) against Yahawah, in that they akal (eat) meat with the dam (blood)." He amar (spoke), "You have dealt bagad (treacherously). Galal (roll) a large aban (stone) to me this yawam (day)!"

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "pawatz (disperse) yourselves among the im (nation / people), and amar (spoke) them, ‘nagash (bring) me here every ayash (man / husband) his shawar (ox), and every ayash (man / husband) his shah (sheep), and shachat (kill) them here, and akal (eat); and don't chataa (sin) against Yahawah in akal (eat) meat with the dam (blood).'" All the im (nation / people) nagash (brought) every ayash (man / husband) his shawar (ox) with him that layal (night), and shachat (killed) them there.
Shaawal (Saul) banah (build) an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah. This was the chalal (first) mazabach (altar) that he banah (build) to Yahawah.

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "yarad (let) us go down achar (other) the Palashathay (Philistines) by layal (night), and bazaz (take) spoil among them until the baqar (morning) awar (light), and shaar (let) us not leave a ayash (man / husband) of them." They amar (spoke), "ishah (make) whatever seems tawab (good / proper function) to you." Then the kahan (priest) amar (spoke), "Let us qarab (come close) near here to Alahayam."

Shaawal (Saul) shaal (asked) counsel of Alahayam, "Shall I yarad (go) down achar (other) the Palashathay (Philistines)? Will you nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of Yashar-Al (Israel)?" But he didn't inah (answer / respond) him that yawam (day).
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "nagash (draw) near here, all you panawath (chiefs) of the im (nation / people); and yadai (know) and raah (see) in which this chataah (sin) has been this yawam (day).

For, as Yahawah chay (life), who yashai (salvation) Yashar-Al (Israel), though it is in Yawanathan (Jonathan) my ban (son), he shall mawath (death) mawath (death)." But there was not a man among all the im (nation / people) who inah (answer / respond) him.

Then he amar (spoke) to all Yashar-Al (Israel), "You be on achad (one) ibar (side), and I and Yawanathan (Jonathan) my ban (son) will be on the other ibar (side)." The im (nation / people) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "ishah (make) what seems tawab (good / proper function) to you."

Therefore Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), "Show the right." Yawanathan (Jonathan) and Shaawal (Saul) were chosen; but the im (nation / people) yatzaa (go out / come out).
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "napal (fall / be cast down) lots between me and Yawanathan (Jonathan) my ban (son)." Yawanathan (Jonathan) was selected.

Then Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Yawanathan (Jonathan), "nagad (tell) me what you ishah (make) done!" Yawanathan (Jonathan) nagad (told) him, and said, "I certainly did taim (taste) a mait (little) dabash (honey) with the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the matah (staff / rod / tribe) that was in my yad (hand); and han (behold), I must mawath (death)."
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "Alahayam ishah (make) so and more also; for you shall mawath (death) mawath (death), Yawanathan (Jonathan)."

The im (nation / people) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "Shall Yawanathan (Jonathan) mawath (death), who ishah (make) worked this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) yashawaih (salvation) in Yashar-Al (Israel)? Chalayalah (far) from it! As Yahawah chay (life), there shall not one shairah (hair) of his raash (head) napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land); for he ishah (make) worked with Alahayam this yawam (day)!" So the im (nation / people) padah (rescued) Yawanathan (Jonathan), that he didn't mawath (death).
Then Shaawal (Saul) ilah (go up / offer) up from achar (other) the Palashathay (Philistines); and the Palashathay (Philistines) halak (move) to their own maqawam (place).

Now when Shaawal (Saul) had lakad (taken) the malawakah (kingdom) over Yashar-Al (Israel), he lacham (fought) against all his ayab (enemy) on sabayab (surrounding) side, against Mawaab (Moab), and against the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), and against Adawam (Edom), and against the malakay (kings) of Tzawabaa (Zobah), and against the Palashathay (Philistines): and wherever he panah (turn) himself, he defeated them.

He ishah (make) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), and nakah (struck) the Imalaq (Amalekites), and natzal (delivered) Yashar-Al (Israel) out of the yad (hand) of those who despoiled them.

Now the banay (sons) of Shaawal (Saul) were Yawanathan (Jonathan), and Yashaway (Ishvi), and Malakayashawai (Malchishua); and the sham (name) of his shanayam (two) banath (daughter) were these: the sham (name) of the bakayarah (firstborn) Marab (Merab), and the sham (name) of the younger Mayakal (Michal):

And the sham (name) of Shaawal (Saul's) ayashah (woman / wife) was Achayanaim (Ahinoam) the banath (daughter) of Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz). The sham (name) of the shar (prince / ruler) of his tzabaa (troop) was Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner), Shaawal (Saul's) dawad (uncle).
Qayash (Kish) was the ab (father) of Shaawal (Saul); and Nar (Ner) the ab (father) of Abanar (Abner) was the ban (son) of Abayaal (Abiel).

There was severe malachamah (war) against the Palashathay (Philistines) all the yamay (days) of Shaawal (Saul): and when Shaawal (Saul) raah (see) any gabawar (mighty) ayash (man / husband), or any chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ayash (man / husband), he asap (took) him to him.

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "Yahawah shalach (send) me to mashach (anoint) you to be malak (king) over his im (nation / people), over Yashar-Al (Israel). Now therefore shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of the dabaray (words) of Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), ‘I paqad (visit) marked that which Imalaq (Amalek) ishah (make) to Yashar-Al (Israel), how he shawam (place / establish / appoint) himself against him in the darak (way), when he ilah (go up / offer) up out of Matzarayam (Egypt).

Now yalak (go) and nakah (strike) Imalaq (Amalek), and utterly charam (destroy) all that they chamal (have), and don't spare them; but mawath (death) both ayash (man / husband) and ayashah (woman / wife), iwalal (infant) and yanaq (nursing) baby, shawar (ox) and shah (sheep), gamal (camel) and donkey.'"
Shaawal (Saul) summoned the im (nation / people), and paqad (visit) them in Talaayam (Telaim), two maah (hundred) alap (thousand) footmen, and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) men of Yahawadah (Judah).
Shaawal (Saul) bawaa (come) to the iyar (city) of Imalaq (Amalek), and rayab (laid) wait in the nachal (stream / river).

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to the Qayanay (Kenites), "yalak (go), sawar (depart), yarad (go) down from thawak (midst) the Imalaq (Amalekites), lest I asap (destroy) you with them; for you showed chasad (grace) to all the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), when they ilah (go up / offer) up out of Matzarayam (Egypt)." So the Qayanay (Kenites) sawar (departed) from thawak (midst) the Imalaqay (Amalekites).
Shaawal (Saul) nakah (struck) the Imalaq (Amalekites), from Chawayalah (Havilah) as you bawaa (come) to Shawar (Shur), that is panayam (face) Matzarayam (Egypt).
He thapash (took) Agag (Agag) the malak (king) of the Imalaq (Amalekites) chay (life), and charam (utterly) destroyed all the im (nation / people) with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword).

But Shaawal (Saul) and the im (nation / people) chamal (spared) Agag (Agag), and the mayatab (best) of the tzaan (sheep), and of the cattle, and of the mashanayam (fatlings), and the karayam (lambs), and all that was tawab (good / proper function), and wouldn't utterly charam (destroy) them: but everything that was namabazah (vile) and masas (refuse), that they charam (destroyed) utterly.
Then the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Shamawaal (Samuel), amar (spoke),

"It grieves me that I have malak (king) up Shaawal (Saul) to be malak (king); for he is shawab (turn back / repent) back from achar (other) me, and has not qawam (rise up) my commandments." Shamawaal (Samuel) was charah (hot with anger); and he zaiq (cried) to Yahawah all layal (night).

Shamawaal (Samuel) shakam (rose) early to qaraa (called) Shaawal (Saul) in the baqar (morning); and it was nagad (told) Shamawaal (Samuel), amar (spoke), "Shaawal (Saul) bawaa (come) to Karamal (Carmel), and behold, he natzab (set) up a monument for himself, and sabab (turned), and ibar (pass over/through) on, and yarad (went) down to Galagal (Gilgal)."
Shamawaal (Samuel) bawaa (come) to Shaawal (Saul); and Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to him, "You are barak (blessed) by Yahawah! I have qawam (rise up) the commandment of Yahawah."
Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), "Then what does this qawal (sound / voice) of the tzaan (sheep) in my azan (ear), and the qawal (sound / voice) of the cattle which I shamai (hearken / hear) mean?"

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "They bawaa (come) brought them from the Imalaqay (Amalekites); for the im (nation / people) chamal (spared) the mayatab (best) of the tzaan (sheep) and of the cattle, to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah your Alahayam. We charam (have) utterly destroyed the yathar (rest)."

Then Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "rapah (stay), and I will nagad (tell) you what Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) to me last layal (night)." He dabar (word / matter) to him, "dabar (word / matter) on."

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), "Though you were qatan (small / young / least) in your own iyan (eye), weren't you made the raash (head) of the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel)? Yahawah mashach (anointed) you malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel);

And Yahawah shalach (send) you on a darak (journey), and amar (spoke), ‘yalak (go), and utterly charam (destroy) the chataayam (sinners) the Imalaq (Amalekites), and lacham (fight) against them until they are kalah (complete / finish).'
Why then didn't you shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah, but took the shalal (spoils), and ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah?"

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), "But I have shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah, and have yalak (gone) the darak (way) which Yahawah shalach (send) me, and bawaa (come) brought Agag (Agag) the malak (king) of Imalaq (Amalek), and charam (have) utterly destroyed the Imalaq (Amalekites).

But the im (nation / people) laqach (take / seize) of the shalal (spoil), tzaan (sheep) and cattle, the raashayath (beginning) of the charam (devoted) things, to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah your Alahayam in Galagal (Gilgal)."

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), "Has Yahawah as great chapatz (delight) in burnt ilawath (offerings) and zabachayam (sacrifices), as in shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah? Behold, to shamai (hearken / hear) is tawab (good / proper function) than zabach (sacrifice), and to shamai (hearken / hear) than the chalab (fat) of ayalayam (rams).

For rebellion is as the chataah (sin) of qasam (witchcraft), and patzar (stubbornness) is as tharapayam (idolatry) and teraphim. Because you have maas (rejected) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, he has also maas (rejected) you from being malak (king)."

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), "I have chataa (sinned); for I ibar (pass over/through) transgressed the commandment of Yahawah, and your dabar (word / matter), because I yaraa (fear / be afraid) the im (nation / people), and shamai (hearken / hear) their qawal (sound / voice).
Now therefore, please nashaa (lift) my chataah (sin), and shawab (turn back / repent) again with me, that I may shachah (worship) Yahawah."

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "I will not shawab (turn back / repent) with you; for you have maas (rejected) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, and Yahawah has maas (rejected) you from being malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel)."
As Shamawaal (Samuel) sabab (turned) about to yalak (go) away, Saul grabbed the kanap (skirt) of his maiyal (robe), and it qarai (tore).

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to him, "Yahawah has qarai (torn) the mamalakawath (kingdom) of Yashar-Al (Israel) from you this yawam (day), and nathan (give) given it to a neighbor of yours who is tawab (good / proper function) than you.
Also the natzach (strength) of Yashar-Al (Israel) will not shaqar (lie) nor nacham (turn away / repent); for he is not a adam (man), that he should nacham (turn away / repent)."

Then he amar (spoke), "I have chataa (sinned): yet please honor me now before the zaqanay (elders) of my im (nation / people), and before Yashar-Al (Israel), and shawab (turn back / repent) back with me, that I may shachah (worship) Yahawah your Alahayam."
So Shamawaal (Samuel) shawab (turn back / repent) back with Shaawal (Saul); and Shaawal (Saul) shachah (worshiped) Yahawah.

Then Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), "nagash (bring) here to me Agag (Agag) the malak (king) of the Imalaq (Amalekites)!" Agag (Agag) yalak (came) to him cheerfully. Agag (Agag) amar (spoke), "akan (surely) the bitterness of mawath (death) is sawar (past)."

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), "As your charab (sword) has made nashayam (women) shakal (childless), so your am (mother) will be shakal (childless) among nashayam (women)!" Shamawaal (Samuel) cut Agag (Agag) in shasap (pieces) panayam (face) Yahawah in Galagal (Gilgal).
Then Shamawaal (Samuel) yalak (went) to Ramah (Ramah); and Shaawal (Saul) ilah (go up / offer) up to his bayath (house) to Gabaih (Gibeah) of Shaawal (Saul).

Shamawaal (Samuel) yasap (came) no more to raah (see) Shaawal (Saul) until the yawam (day) of his mawath (death); for Shamawaal (Samuel) abal (mourned) for Shaawal (Saul): and Yahawah grieved that he had made Shaawal (Saul) malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), "How long will you abal (mourn) for Shaawal (Saul), since I have maas (rejected) him from being malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel)? Malaa (fill) your qaran (horn) with shaman (oil), and yalak (go). I will shalach (send) you to Yashay (Jesse) the bayathahalachamay (bethlehemite); for I raah (see) provided a malak (king) for myself among his ban (son)."

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), "How can I yalak (go)? If Shaawal (Saul) shamai (hearken / hear) it, he will harag (kill) me." Yahawah amar (spoke), "laqach (take / seize) a baqar (morning) with you, and amar (spoke), I bawaa (come) come to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah.
Qaraa (called) Yashay (Jesse) to the zabach (sacrifice), and I yadai (will) show you what you shall ishah (make). You shall mashach (anoint) to me him whom I amar (spoke) to you."

Shamawaal (Samuel) ishah (make) that which Yahawah dabar (word / matter), and bawaa (come) to Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem). The zaqanay (elders) of the iyar (city) came to meet him charad (trembling), and amar (spoke), "Do you bawaa (come) peaceably?"

He amar (spoke), "Peaceably; I bawaa (come) come to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah. Qadash (set apart / make holy) yourselves, and bawaa (come) with me to the zabach (sacrifice)." He qadash (set apart / make holy) Yashay (Jesse) and his ban (son), and qaraa (called) them to the zabach (sacrifice).
It happened, when they bawaa (come) come, that he raah (see) at Alayaab (Eliab), and amar (spoke), "Surely Yahawah mashayach (anointed one) is before him."

But Yahawah amar (spoke) to Shamawaal (Samuel), "Don't nabat (look) on his maraah (face), or on the gabah (height) of his qawamah (stature); because I have maas (rejected) him: for I see not as adam (man) raah (see); for adam (man) raah (see) at the iyan (eye) appearance, but Yahawah raah (see) at the labab (heart)."
Then Yashay (Jesse) qaraa (called) Abayanadab (Abinadab), and ibar (pass over/through) him pass panayam (face) Shamawaal (Samuel). He amar (spoke), "Neither has Yahawah bachar (chosen) this one."
Then Yashay (Jesse) made Shamah (Shammah) to ibar (pass over/through) by. He amar (spoke), "Neither has Yahawah bachar (chosen) this one."

Yashay (Jesse) made shabai (seven) of his ban (son) to ibar (pass over/through) panayam (face) Shamawaal (Samuel). Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Yashay (Jesse), "Yahawah has not bachar (chosen) these."

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Yashay (Jesse), "Are thamam (all) your nairayam (children) here?" He amar (spoke), "There shaar (remains) yet the youngest, and behold, he is raih (keeping) the tzaan (sheep)." Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Yashay (Jesse), "shalach (send) and laqach (take / seize) him; for we will not sabab (sit) down until he bawaa (come) here."

He shalach (send), and bawaa (come) him in. Now he was adamanay (ruddy), and im (with) of a yapah (beautiful) iyan (eye), and goodly to look on. Yahawah amar (spoke), "qawam (rise up), mashach (anoint) him; for this is he."

Then Shamawaal (Samuel) laqach (take / seize) the qaran (horn) of shaman (oil), and mashach (anointed) him in the qarab (among / near) of his ach (brother/kinsman): and the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah tzalach (came) mightily on Dawad (David) from that yawam (day) mail (top/above). So Shamawaal (Samuel) qawam (rise up) up, and yalak (went) to Ramah (Ramah).
Now the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah sawar (departed) from Shaawal (Saul), and an rai (evil) rawach (spirit / wind) from Yahawah baith (troubled) him.
Shaawal (Saul's) ibaday (servants) amar (spoke) to him, "See now, an rai (evil) rawach (spirit / wind) from Alahayam baith (troubles) you.

Let our Adawan now command your ibad (servant) who are panayam (face) you, to baqash (seek) out a ayash (man / husband) who is a skillful nagan (player) on the kanawar (harp). It shall happen, when the rai (evil) rawach (spirit / wind) from Alahayam is on you, that he shall nagan (play) with his yad (hand), and you shall be tawab (good / proper function)."
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), "raah (see) me now a ayash (man / husband) who can nagan (play) yatab (well), and bawaa (come) him to me."

Then achad (one) of the young men inah (answer / respond), and amar (spoke), "raah (see), I have seen a ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse) the bayathahalachamay (bethlehemite), who is skillful in nagan (playing), a gabawar (mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) of valor, a ayash (man / husband) of malachamah (war), bayan (between) in dabar (word / matter), and a thaar (comely) ayash (man / husband); and Yahawah is with him."
Therefore Shaawal (Saul) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to Yashay (Jesse), and amar (spoke), "shalach (send) me Dawad (David) your ban (son), who is with the tzaan (sheep)."

Yashay (Jesse) laqach (take / seize) a donkey loaded with lacham (bread), and a naad (bottle) of yayan (wine), and a young goat, and shalach (send) them by Dawad (David) his ban (son) to Shaawal (Saul).
Dawad (David) bawaa (come) to Shaawal (Saul), and imad (stood) panayam (face) him. He ahab (love) him maad (greatly); and he became his armor bearer.
Shaawal (Saul) shalach (send) to Yashay (Jesse), amar (spoke), "Please let Dawad (David) imad (stand) panayam (face) me; for he matzaa (has) found favor in my iyan (eye)."

It happened, when the rawach (spirit / wind) from Alahayam was on Shaawal (Saul), that Dawad (David) laqach (take / seize) the kanawar (harp), and nagan (played) with his yad (hand): so Shaawal (Saul) was rawach (spirit / wind), and was tawab (good / proper function), and the rai (evil) rawach (spirit / wind) sawar (departed) from him.

Now the Palashathay (Philistines) asap (gathered) together their machanah (armies) to malachamah (battle); and they were asap (gathered) together at Shawakah (Socoh), which belongs to Yahawadah (Judah), and chanah (encamped) between Shawakah (Socoh) and Izaqah (Azekah), in Apasadamayam (Ephesdammim).

Shaawal (Saul) and the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) were asap (gathered) together, and chanah (encamped) in the imaq (valley) of Alah (Elah), and set the malachamah (battle) in irak (array) against the Palashathay (Philistines).

The Palashathay (Philistines) imad (stood) on the har (mountain) on the one side, and Yashar-Al (Israel) imad (stood) on the har (mountain) on the other side: and there was a gayaa (valley) between them.

There yatzaa (go out / come out) out a ayash (man / husband) out of the machanah (camp) of the Palashathay (Philistines), sham (name) Galayath (Goliath), of gath (gath), whose gabah (height) was shash (six) amawath (cubits) and a zarath (span).

He had a kawabai (helmet) of nachashath (brass) on his raash (head), and he was clad with a sharayawan (coat) of qashaqashath (mail); and the mashaqal (weight) of the sharayawan (coat) was chamash (five) alap (thousand) shaqalayam (shekels) of nachashath (brass).
He had nachashath (brass) shin armor on his ragal (feet / foot), and a javelin of nachashath (brass) between his kathap (shoulders).

The chatz (staff) of his chanayath (spear) was like a aragayam (weavers) manawar (beam); and his chanayath (spear's) lahabah (head) weighed shash (six) maah (hundred) shaqalayam (shekels) of barazal (iron): and his tzanah (shield) bearer halak (move) panayam (face) him.

He imad (stood) and qaraa (called) to the mairakath (armies) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and amar (spoke) to them, "Why yatzaa (go out / come out) you come out to set your malachamah (battle) in irak (array)? Am I not a Palashathay (Philistine), and you ibadayam (servants) to Shaawal (Saul)? Barah (choose) a ayash (man / husband) for yourselves, and yarad (let) him come down to me.

If he be yakal (able) to lacham (fight) with me, and nakah (kill) me, then will we be your ibadayam (servants); but if I yakal (prevail) against him, and nakah (kill) him, then you will be our ibadayam (servants), and ibad (servant) us."

The Palashathay (Philistine) amar (spoke), "I charap (defy) the mairakawath (armies) of Yashar-Al (Israel) this yawam (day)! Nathan (give) me a ayash (man / husband), that we may lacham (fight) yachad (together)!"

When Shaawal (Saul) and all Yashar-Al (Israel) shamai (hearken / hear) those dabaray (words) of the Palashathay (Philistine), they were chathath (dismayed), and maad (greatly) yaraa (fear / be afraid).

Now Dawad (David) was the ban (son) of that Ephrathite of Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem Judah), whose sham (name) was Yashay (Jesse); and he had shamanah (eight) banayam (sons): and the ayash (man / husband) was an old zaqan (man) in the yamay (days) of Shaawal (Saul), stricken among banayam (men).

The shalawash (three) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) banay (sons) of Yashay (Jesse) had yalak (gone) achar (other) Shaawal (Saul) to the malachamah (battle): and the sham (name) of his shalawash (three) banay (sons) who halak (move) to the malachamah (battle) were Alayaab (Eliab) the bakawar (firstborn), and mashanah (next) to him Abayanadab (Abinadab), and the shalayashay (third) Shamah (Shammah).
Dawad (David) was the youngest; and the shalawash (three) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) halak (move) Shaawal (Saul).
Now Dawad (David) halak (move) shawab (turn back / repent) and forth from Shaawal (Saul) to raih (feed) his ab (father) tzaan (sheep) at Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem).
The Palashathay (Philistine) nagash (drew) near shakam (morning) and irab (evening), and yatzab (presented) himself arabaiyam (forty) yawam (day).

Yashay (Jesse) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David) his ban (son), "Now laqach (take / seize) for your ach (brother/kinsman) an ayapah (ephah) of zah (this / that / these) qalay (parched) grain, and these ishar (ten) loaves, and carry them quickly to the machanah (camp) to your ach (brother/kinsman);

And bawaa (come) these ishar (ten) chalab (milk) to the shar (prince / ruler) of their alap (thousand), and paqad (visit) how your ach (brother/kinsman) are shalawam (peace / safety), and laqach (take / seize) back news."
Now Shaawal (Saul), and they, and all the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel), were in the imaq (valley) of Alah (Elah), lacham (fighting) with the Palashathay (Philistines).

Dawad (David) shakam (rose) up early in the baqar (morning), and natash (left) the tzaan (sheep) with a keeper, and nashaa (lift), and yalak (went), as Yashay (Jesse) had tzawah (commanded) him; and he bawaa (come) to the place of the wagons, as the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) which was yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to the mairakah (fight) rawai (shouted) for the malachamah (battle).
Yashar-Al (Israel) and the Palashathay (Philistines) irak (put) the battle in array, mairakah (army) against mairakah (army).
Dawad (David) natash (left) his baggage in the yad (hand) of the keeper of the baggage, and rawatz (ran) to the mairakah (army), and bawaa (come) and shaal (greeted) his ach (brother/kinsman).

As he dabar (word / matter) with them, behold, there ilah (go up / offer) up the ayash (man / husband), the Palashathay (Philistine) of gath (gath), Galayath (Goliath) by sham (name), out of the ranks of the Palashathay (Philistines), and dabar (word / matter) according to the same dabarayam (words): and Dawad (David) shamai (hearken / hear) them.
All the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel), when they raah (see) the ayash (man / husband), nawas (fled) from him, and were terrified.

The ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke), "raah (see) you seen this ayash (man / husband) who has ilah (go up / offer) up? He has surely ilah (go up / offer) up to charap (defy) Yashar-Al (Israel). It shall be, that the ayash (man / husband) who nakah (kills) him, the malak (king) will enrich him with gadawal (very great/important/mighty) riches, and will nathan (give) him his banath (daughter), and ishah (make) his ab (father) bayath (house) chapashay (free) in Yashar-Al (Israel)."

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to the anashayam (men) who imad (stood) by him, amar (spoke), "What shall be ishah (make) to the ayash (man / husband) who nakah (kills) halaz (this) Palashathay (Philistine), and sawar (takes) away the charapah (reproach) from Yashar-Al (Israel)? For who is this iral (uncircumcised) Palashathay (Philistine), that he should charap (defy) the mairakawath (armies) of the chay (life) Alahayam?"
The im (nation / people) amar (spoke) him in this dabar (word / matter), amar (spoke), "So shall it be ishah (make) to the ayash (man / husband) who nakah (kills) him."

Alayaab (Eliab) his gadawal (very great/important/mighty) ach (brother/kinsman) shamai (hearken / hear) when he dabar (word / matter) to the gadawal (very great/important/mighty); and Alayaab (Eliab's) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger) against Dawad (David), and he amar (spoke), "Why have you yarad (come) down? With whom have you natash (left) those mait (few) tzaan (sheep) in the madabar (wilderness)? I yadai (know) your zadawan (pride), and the rai (naughtiness) of your labab (heart); for you have yarad (come) down that you might raah (see) the malachamah (battle)."
Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "What ishah (make) I now done? Is there not a dabar (word / matter)?"
He sabab (turned) away from him mawal (toward) achar (other), and amar (spoke) like that again; and the im (nation / people) dabar (word / matter) him again the same dabar (word / matter).
When the dabarayam (words) were shamai (hearken / hear) which Dawad (David) dabar (word / matter), they nagad (rehearsed) them panayam (face) Shaawal (Saul); and he laqach (take / seize) for him.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "Let no adam (man's) lab (heart) napal (fall / be cast down) because of him. Your ibad (servant) will yalak (go) and lacham (fight) with this Palashathay (Philistine)."

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "You are not yakal (able) to yalak (go) against this Palashathay (Philistine) to lacham (fight) with him; for you are but a youth, and he a ayash (man / husband) of malachamah (war) from his naiwar (youth)."

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "Your ibad (servant) was raih (keeping) his ab (father) tzaan (sheep); and when a aray (lion) or a dab (bear) bawaa (come), and nashaa (lift) a shah (lamb) out of the idar (flock),

I yatzaa (go out / come out) out achar (other) him, and nakah (struck) him, and natzal (rescued) it out of his pah (mouth). When he qawam (rise up) against me, I chazaq (caught) him by his zaqan (beard), and nakah (struck) him, and mawath (death) him.

Your ibad (servant) nakah (struck) both the aray (lion) and the dab (bear). This iral (uncircumcised) Palashathay (Philistine) shall be as achad (one) of them, since he has charap (defied) the mairakath (armies) of the chay (life) Alahayam."

Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "Yahawah who natzal (delivered) me out of the paw of the aray (lion), and out of the paw of the dab (bear), he will natzal (deliver) me out of the yad (hand) of this Palashathay (Philistine)." Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "yalak (go); and Yahawah shall be with you."
Shaawal (Saul) dressed Dawad (David) with his clothing. He nathan (give) a qawabai (helmet) of nachashath (brass) on his raash (head), and he clad him with a sharayawan (coat) of mail.

Dawad (David) strapped his charab (sword) on his clothing, and he tried to move; for he had not tested it. Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "I can't yalak (go) with these; for I yakal (have) not tested them." Dawad (David) took them off.

He laqach (take / seize) his maqal (staff) in his yad (hand), and bachar (chose) for himself chamash (five) chalaq (smooth) abanayam (stones) out of the nachal (stream / river), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them in the raiyam (shepherds) kalay (bag) which he had, even in his wallet. His qalai (sling) was in his yad (hand); and he nagash (drew) near to the Palashathay (Philistine).
The Palashathay (Philistine) yalak (came) on and qarab (drew) near to Dawad (David); and the ayash (man / husband) who nashaa (lift) the tzanah (shield) went panayam (face) him.

When the Palashathay (Philistine) nabat (looked) about, and raah (see) Dawad (David), he bazah (disdained) him; for he was but a youth, and adamanay (ruddy), and withal of a yapah (fair) maraah (face).
The Palashathay (Philistine) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "Am I a kalab (dog), that you bawaa (come) to me with sticks?" The Palashathay (Philistine) qalal (cursed) Dawad (David) by his Alahayam.

The Palashathay (Philistine) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "yalak (come) to me, and I will nathan (give) your bashar (flesh) to the iwap (flying) of the sky, and to the animals of the shadah (field)."

Then Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to the Palashathay (Philistine), "You bawaa (come) to me with a charab (sword), and with a chanayath (spear), and with a javelin: but I bawaa (come) to you in the sham (name) of Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), the Alahayam of the tzabaawath (armies) of Yashar-Al (Israel), whom you have charap (defied).

Today, Yahawah will sagar (deliver) you into my yad (hand). I will nakah (strike) you, and sawar (take) your raash (head) from off you. I will nathan (give) the pagar (dead) bodies of the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines) this yawam (day) to the iwap (flying) of the sky, and to the wild animals of the aratz (Earth/land); that all the aratz (Earth/land) may yadai (know) that there is a Alahayam in Yashar-Al (Israel),

And that all this qahal (assembly) may yadai (know) that Yahawah doesn't yashai (salvation) with charab (sword) and chanayath (spear): for the malachamah (battle) is Yahawah, and he will nathan (give) you into our yad (hand)."

It happened, when the Palashathay (Philistine) qawam (rise up), and yalak (came) and qarab (come close) near to qaraa (called) Dawad (David), that Dawad (David) hurried, and rawatz (ran) toward the mairakah (army) to qaraa (called) the Palashathay (Philistine).

Dawad (David) shalach (send) his yad (hand) in his kalay (bag), laqach (take / seize) a aban (stone), and slung it, and nakah (struck) the Palashathay (Philistine) in his matzach (forehead); and the aban (stone) tabai (sank) into his matzach (forehead), and he napal (fall / be cast down) on his panayam (face) to the aratz (Earth/land).

So Dawad (David) chazaq (prevailed) over the Palashathay (Philistine) with a qalai (sling) and with a aban (stone), and nakah (struck) the Palashathay (Philistine), and mawath (death) him; but there was no charab (sword) in the yad (hand) of Dawad (David).

Then Dawad (David) rawatz (ran), and imad (stood) over the Palashathay (Philistine), and laqach (take / seize) his charab (sword), and shalap (drew) it out of its thair (razor), and mawath (death) him, and karath (cut) off his raash (head) therewith. When the Palashathay (Philistines) raah (see) that their gabawar (champion) was mawath (death), they nawas (fled).

The anashay (men) of Yashar-Al (Israel) and of Yahawadah (Judah) qawam (rise up), and rawai (shouted), and radap (pursued) the Palashathay (Philistines), until you bawaa (come) to Gai, and to the shairay (gates) of Iqarawan (Ekron). The chalal (wounded) of the Palashathay (Philistines) napal (fall / be cast down) down by the darak (way) to Shairayam (Shaaraim), even to gath (gath), and to Iqarawan (Ekron).
The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shawab (turn back / repent) from dalaq (chasing) achar (other) the Palashathay (Philistines), and they plundered their machanah (camp).

Dawad (David) laqach (take / seize) the raash (head) of the Palashathay (Philistine), and bawaa (come) it to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); but he shawam (place / establish / appoint) his armor in his ahal (tent).

When Shaawal (Saul) raah (see) Dawad (David) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth amar (spoke) the Palashathay (Philistine), he amar (spoke) to Abanar (Abner), the shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop), "Abanar (Abner), whose ban (son) is this youth?" Abanar (Abner) amar (spoke), "As your napash (soul) chay (life), O malak (king), I can't yadai (tell)."
The malak (king) amar (spoke), "Inquire whose ban (son) the young ilam (man) is!"

As Dawad (David) shawab (turn back / repent) from the nakah (slaughter) of the Palashathay (Philistine), Abanar (Abner) laqach (take / seize) him, and bawaa (come) him panayam (face) Shaawal (Saul) with the raash (head) of the Palashathay (Philistine) in his yad (hand).

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to him, "Whose ban (son) are you, you nair (young) man?" Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "I am the ban (son) of your ibad (servant) Yashay (Jesse) the bayathahalachamay (bethlehemite)."

It happened, when he kalah (complete / finish) made an end of dabar (word / matter) to Shaawal (Saul), that the napash (soul) of Yahawanathan (Jonathan) was qashar (knit) with the napash (soul) of Dawad (David), and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) ahab (love) him as his own napash (soul).
Shaawal (Saul) laqach (take / seize) him that yawam (day), and nathan (give) let him shawab (turn back / repent) no more home to his ab (father) shawab (turn back / repent).
Then Yahawanathan (Jonathan) and Dawad (David) karath (cut) a barayath (covenant), because he ahabah (loved) him as his own napash (soul).

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) pashat (stripped) himself of the maiyal (robe) that was on him, and nathan (give) it to Dawad (David), and his clothing, even to his charab (sword), and to his qashath (bow), and to his sash.

Dawad (David) yatzaa (go out / come out) out wherever Shaawal (Saul) shalach (send) him, and shakal (behaved) himself wisely: and Shaawal (Saul) shawam (place / establish / appoint) him over the anashay (men) of malachamah (war), and it was yatab (good) in the iyan (eye) of all the im (nation / people), and also in the iyan (eye) of Shaawal (Saul's) ibaday (servants).

It happened as they bawaa (come), when Dawad (David) shawab (turn back / repent) from the nakah (slaughter) of the Palashathay (Philistine), that the nashayam (women) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of all the iray (cities) of Yashar-Al (Israel), shayar (singing) and machawalah (dance), to qaraa (called) malak (king) Shaawal (Saul), with tambourines, with shamachah (joy), and with shalashayam (instruments) of music.

The nashayam (women) inah (answer / respond) one to another as they shachaq (played), and amar (spoke), "Shaawal (Saul) has nakah (slain) his alap (thousands), Dawad (David) his ten alap (thousands)."

Shaawal (Saul) was very charah (hot with anger), and this dabar (word / matter) displeased him; and he amar (spoke), "They nathan (give) ascribed to Dawad (David) rababah (ten) thousands, and to me they nathan (give) ascribed but alapayam (thousands). What can he have more but the malawakah (kingdom)?"
Shaawal (Saul) eyed Dawad (David) from that yawam (day) and halaah (forward).

It happened on the next macharath (day), that an rai (evil) rawach (spirit / wind) from Alahayam tzalach (came) mightily on Shaawal (Saul), and he nabaa (prophesied) in the thawak (midst) of the bayath (house). Dawad (David) nagan (played) with his yad (hand), as he did yawam (day) by day. Shaawal (Saul) had his chanayath (spear) in his yad (hand);
And Shaawal (Saul) threw the chanayath (spear); for he amar (spoke), "I will pin Dawad (David) even to the qayar (wall)!" Dawad (David) escaped from his panayam (face) paim (twice).
Shaawal (Saul) was yaraa (fear / be afraid) of Dawad (David), because Yahawah was with him, and was sawar (departed) from Shaawal (Saul).

Therefore Shaawal (Saul) sawar (removed) him from him, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) him his shar (prince / ruler) over a alap (thousand); and he yatzaa (go out / come out) out and bawaa (come) in panayam (face) the im (nation / people).
Dawad (David) shakal (behaved) himself wisely in all his darak (ways); and Yahawah was with him.
When Shaawal (Saul) raah (see) that he shakal (behaved) himself very shakal (wisely), he gawar (stood) in awe of him.
But all Yashar-Al (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah) ahab (love) Dawad (David); for he yatzaa (go out / come out) out and bawaa (come) in panayam (face) them.

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "Behold, my gadawal (very great/important/mighty) banath (daughter) Marab (Merab), I will nathan (give) her to you as ayashah (woman / wife). Only be ban (son) for me, and lacham (fight) Yahawah malachamawath (battles)." For Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "Don't let my yad (hand) be on him, but let the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines) be on him."

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "Who am I, and what is my chay (life), or my ab (father) mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) in Yashar-Al (Israel), that I should be son-in-law to the malak (king)?"

But it happened at the ith (time) when Marab (Merab), Shaawal (Saul's) banath (daughter), should nathan (give) been given to Dawad (David), that she was nathan (give) to Idarayaal (Adriel) the Meholathite as ayashah (woman / wife).
Mayakal (Michal), Shaawal (Saul's) banath (daughter), ahab (love) Dawad (David); and they nagad (told) Shaawal (Saul), and the thing yashar (upright) him.

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), I will nathan (give) her to him, that she may be a mawaqash (snare) to him, and that the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines) may be against him. Therefore Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "You shall this yawam (day) be my son-in-law a shanayam (two) time."

Shaawal (Saul) tzawah (commanded) his ibad (servant), "dabar (word / matter) with Dawad (David) lat (secretly), and amar (spoke), ‘Behold, the malak (king) chapatz (has) delight in you, and all his ibad (servant) ahab (love) you: now therefore be the malak (king) son-in-law.'"

Shaawal (Saul's) ibaday (servants) dabar (word / matter) those dabarayam (words) in the azanay (ears) of Dawad (David). Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "Does it seems to you a qalal (light) thing to be the malak (king) son-in-law, since I am a rawash (poor) ayash (man / husband), and qalah (lightly) esteemed?"
The ibaday (servants) of Shaawal (Saul) nagad (told) him, amar (spoke), "Dawad (David) nagad (spoke) like this."

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "You shall amar (spoke) Dawad (David), ‘The malak (king) chapatz (desires) no mahar (dowry) except one maah (hundred) iralawath (foreskins) of the Palashathay (Philistines), to be naqam (avenged) of the malak (king) ayabay (enemies).'" Now Shaawal (Saul) chashab (thought) to make Dawad (David) napal (fall / be cast down) by the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines).
When his ibad (servant) nagad (told) Dawad (David) these dabarayam (words), it dabar (word / matter) Dawad (David) well to be the malak (king) son-in-law. The yamayam (days) were not malaa (expired);

And Dawad (David) qawam (rise up) and yalak (went), he and his ayash (man / husband), and nakah (killed) of the Palashathay (Philistines) two maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband); and Dawad (David) bawaa (come) their iralah (foreskins), and they malaa (gave) them in full number to the malak (king), that he might be the malak (king) son-in-law. Shaawal (Saul) nathan (give) him Mayakal (Michal) his banath (daughter) as ayashah (woman / wife).
Shaawal (Saul) raah (see) and yadai (knew) that Yahawah was with Dawad (David); and Mayakal (Michal), Shaawal (Saul's) banath (daughter), ahab (love) him.
Shaawal (Saul) was yet the more yaraa (fear / be afraid) of Dawad (David); and Shaawal (Saul) was Dawad (David's) ayab (enemy) yawam (day).

Then the sharay (princes) of the Palashathay (Philistines) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth: and it happened, as often as they yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, that Dawad (David) shakal (behaved) himself more wisely than all the ibaday (servants) of Shaawal (Saul); so that his sham (name) was highly esteemed.

Shaawal (Saul) dabar (word / matter) to Yawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son), and to all his ibad (servant), that they should mawath (death) Dawad (David). But Jonathan, Saul's son, delighted much in David.

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) nagad (told) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), "Shaawal (Saul) my ab (father) baqash (seeks) to mawath (death) you. Now therefore, please shamar (keep/guard) care of yourself in the baqar (morning), and live in a sathar (secret / hidden) place, and chabaa (hide) yourself.

I will yatzaa (go out / come out) out and imad (stand) yad (hand) my ab (father) in the shadah (field) where you are, and I will dabar (word / matter) with my ab (father) about you; and if I raah (see) anything, I will nagad (tell) you."

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) dabar (word / matter) tawab (good / proper function) of Dawad (David) to Shaawal (Saul) his ab (father), and amar (spoke) to him, "Don't let the malak (king) chataa (sin) against his ibad (servant), against Dawad (David); because he has not chataa (sinned) against you, and because his maishah (works) have been very tawab (good / proper function) toward you;

For he shawam (place / establish / appoint) his napash (soul) in his kap (hand), and nakah (struck) the Palashathay (Philistine), and Yahawah ishah (make) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thashawaih (deliverance) for all Yashar-Al (Israel). You raah (see) it, and shamach (rejoiced). Why then will you chataa (sin) against naqay (innocent) dam (blood), to mawath (death) Dawad (David) chanam (without) a cause?"

Shaawal (Saul) shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawanathan (Jonathan): and Shaawal (Saul) shabai (swear / take oath), "As Yahawah chay (life), he shall not be put to mawath (death)."

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) qaraa (called) Dawad (David), and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) showed him all those things. Yahawanathan (Jonathan) bawaa (come) Dawad (David) to Shaawal (Saul), and he panayam (face) in his presence, as athamawal (before).

There was malachamah (war) again. Dawad (David) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and lacham (fought) with the Palashathay (Philistines), and nakah (killed) them with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) makah (slaughter); and they nawas (fled) panayam (face) him.

An rai (evil) rawach (spirit / wind) from Yahawah was on Shaawal (Saul), as he yashab (inhabit/dwell) in his bayath (house) with his chanayath (spear) in his yad (hand); and Dawad (David) was nagan (playing) with his yad (hand).

Shaawal (Saul) baqash (sought) to pin Dawad (David) even to the qayar (wall) with the chanayath (spear); but he patar (slipped) away out of Shaawal (Saul's) panayam (face), and he stuck the chanayath (spear) into the qayar (wall). Dawad (David) nawas (fled), and malat (escaped) that layal (night).

Shaawal (Saul) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to Dawad (David's) bayath (house), to shamar (keep/guard) him, and to mawath (death) him in the baqar (morning). Mayakal (Michal), Dawad (David's) ayashah (woman / wife), nagad (told) him, amar (spoke), "If you don't malat (save) your napash (soul) tonight, machar (tomorrow) you will be mawath (death)."
So Mayakal (Michal) yarad (let) Dawad (David) down through the chalawan (window). He yalak (went), barach (fled), and malat (escaped).

Mayakal (Michal) laqach (take / seize) the tharapayam (teraphim), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it in the matah (bed), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) a kabayar (pillow) of izayam (goats)' hair at its maraashah (head), and kasah (covered) it with the clothes.
When Shaawal (Saul) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to laqach (take / seize) Dawad (David), she amar (spoke), "He is chalah (afflict)."
Shaawal (Saul) shalach (send) the malaakayam (messengers) to raah (see) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), "ilah (go up / offer) him up to me in the matah (bed), that I may mawath (death) him."
When the malaakayam (messengers) bawaa (come) in, behold, the tharapayam (teraphim) was in the matah (bed), with the kabayar (pillow) of izayam (goats)' hair at its head.

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Mayakal (Michal), "Why have you ramah (deceived) me thus, and let my ayab (enemy) go, so that he is malat (escaped)?" Mayakal (Michal) amar (spoke) Shaawal (Saul), "He amar (spoke) to me, ‘shalach (send) me go! Why should I mawath (death) you?'"

Now Dawad (David) barach (fled), and malat (escaped), and bawaa (come) to Shamawaal (Samuel) to Ramah (Ramah), and nagad (told) him all that Shaawal (Saul) ishah (make) done to him. He and Shamawaal (Samuel) yalak (went) and lived in Nawayath (Naioth).
It was nagad (told) Shaawal (Saul), amar (spoke), "Behold, Dawad (David) is at Nawayath (Naioth) in Ramah (Ramah)."

Shaawal (Saul) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to laqach (take / seize) Dawad (David): and when they raah (see) the lahaqah (company) of the nabayaayam (prophets) nabaa (prophesying), and Shamawaal (Samuel) imad (standing) as natzab (head) over them, the rawach (spirit / wind) of Alahayam came on the malaakayam (messengers) of Shaawal (Saul), and they also nabaa (prophesied).

When it was nagad (told) Shaawal (Saul), he shalach (send) other malaakayam (messengers), and they also nabaa (prophesied). Shaawal (Saul) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) again the shalayashay (third) time, and they also nabaa (prophesied).

Then yalak (went) he also to Ramah (Ramah), and bawaa (come) to the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) bawar (well) that is in Shakaw (Secu): and he shaal (asked), "ayapah (where) are Shamawaal (Samuel) and Dawad (David)?" One amar (spoke), "Behold, they are at Nawayath (Naioth) in Ramah (Ramah)."
