He yalak (went) there to Nawayath (Naioth) in Ramah (Ramah). Then the rawach (spirit / wind) of Alahayam yalak (came) on him also, and he went on, and nabaa (prophesied), until he bawaa (come) to Nawayath (Naioth) in Ramah (Ramah).

He also pashat (stripped) off his clothes, and he also nabaa (prophesied) panayam (face) Shamawaal (Samuel), and napal (fall / be cast down) down irawam (naked) all that yawam (day) and all that layal (night). Therefore they amar (spoke), "Is Shaawal (Saul) also among the nabayaam (prophets)?"

Dawad (David) barach (fled) from Nawayath (Naioth) in Ramah (Ramah), and bawaa (come) and amar (spoke) panayam (face) Yahawanathan (Jonathan), "What ishah (make) I done? What is my iwan (guilt/iniquity)? What is my chataah (sin) panayam (face) your ab (father), that he baqash (seeks) my napash (soul)?"

He amar (spoke) to him, "chalayalah (far) from it; you shall not mawath (death). Behold, my ab (father) ishah (make) nothing either gadawal (very great/important/mighty) or qatan (small / young / least), but that he galah (discloses) it to me; and why should my ab (father) sathar (hide) this thing from me? It is not so."

Dawad (David) shabai (swear / take oath) moreover, and amar (spoke), "Your ab (father) yadai (knows) well that I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye); and he amar (spoke), ‘Don't let Yahawanathan (Jonathan) yadai (know) this, lest he be itzab (grieved):' but awalam (truly) as Yahawah chay (life), and as your napash (soul) chay (life), there is but a pashai (step) between me and mawath (death)."
Then Yahawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "Whatever your napash (soul) amar (spoke), I will even ishah (make) it for you."

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Yahawanathan (Jonathan), "Behold, machar (tomorrow) is the new chadash (month), and I should not yashab (inhabit/dwell) to akal (eat) with the malak (king); but shalach (send) me go, that I may sathar (hide) myself in the shadah (field) to the shalayashay (third) irab (evening) at evening.

If your ab (father) paqad (visit) me at paqad (visit), then amar (spoke), ‘Dawad (David) shaal (earnestly) shaal (asked) leave of me that he might rawatz (run) to Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem) his iyar (city); for it is the yawam (day) zabach (sacrifice) there for all the mashapachah (tribe / clan / family).'

If he amar (spoke), ‘It is tawab (good / proper function);' your ibad (servant) shall have shalawam (peace / safety): but if he be charah (hot with anger), then yadai (know) that rai (evil) is kalah (complete / finish) by him.

Therefore ishah (make) chasad (grace) with your ibad (servant); for you bawaa (come) brought your ibad (servant) into a barayath (covenant) of Yahawah with you: but if there is iwan (guilt/iniquity) in me, mawath (death) me yourself; for why should you bawaa (come) me to your ab (father)?"

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke), "chalayalah (far) be it from you; for if I should at all yadai (know) that rai (evil) were kalah (complete / finish) by my ab (father) to bawaa (come) on you, then wouldn't I nagad (tell) you that?"
Then Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Yahawanathan (Jonathan), "Who shall nagad (tell) me if perchance your ab (father) inah (answer / respond) you qashah (rough / hard)?"

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "yalak (come), and yatzaa (go out / come out) us go out into the shadah (field)." They shanayam (two) yatzaa (go out / come out) out into the shadah (field).

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "By Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), when I have chaqar (sounded) my ab (father) about this ith (time) machar (tomorrow), or the shalayashay (third) machar (day), behold, if there is tawab (good / proper function) toward Dawad (David), shall I not then shalach (send) to you, and disclose it to you?

Yahawah ishah (make) so to Yahawanathan (Jonathan), and more also, should it yatab (please) my ab (father) to do you rai (evil), if I don't galah (disclose) it to you, and shalach (send) you away, that you may halak (move) in shalawam (peace / safety): and Yahawah be with you, as he has been with my ab (father).
You shall not only am (mother) yet I chay (life) show me the loving chasad (grace) of Yahawah, that I not mawath (death);

But also you shall not karath (cut) off your chasad (grace) from my bayath (house) iwalam (forever); no, not when Yahawah has karath (cut) off the ayabay (enemies) of Dawad (David) everyone from the surface of the adamah (earth)."
So Yahawanathan (Jonathan) karath (cut) a covenant with the bayath (house) of Dawad (David), saying, "Yahawah will baqash (require) it at the yad (hand) of Dawad (David's) ayabay (enemies)."
Yahawanathan (Jonathan) caused Dawad (David) to shabai (swear / take oath) again, for the ahabah (love) that he had to him; for he ahab (love) him as he ahabah (loved) his own napash (soul).
Then Yahawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke) to him, "machar (tomorrow) is the new chadash (month): and you will be paqad (visit), because your mawashab (seat) will be paqad (visit).

When you have stayed shalash (three) days, you shall bawaa (come) down maad (quickly), and bawaa (come) to the maqawam (place) where you sathar (hid) yourself when this started, and shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) by the aban (stone) Azal (Ezel).
I will yarah (shoot) shalawash (three) chatzayam (arrows) on its tzad (side), as though I shalach (send) at a mataraa (mark).

Behold, I will shalach (send) the nair (boy), amar (spoke), ‘yalak (go), matzaa (find) the chatzayam (arrows)!' If I amar (spoke) the nair (boy), ‘Behold, the chatzayam (arrows) are on this side of you. Laqach (take / seize) them;' then bawaa (come); for there is shalawam (peace / safety) to you and no dabar (word / matter), as Yahawah chay (life).
But if I amar (spoke) this to the boy, ‘Behold, the chatzayam (arrows) are halaah (beyond) you;' then go your yalak (way); for Yahawah has shalach (send) you away.
Dabar (word / matter) the matter which you and I have dabar (word / matter) of, behold, Yahawah is between you and me iwalam (forever)."
So Dawad (David) sathar (hid) himself in the shadah (field): and when the new chadash (month) had come, the malak (king) yashab (inhabit/dwell) him down to akal (eat) lacham (food).

The malak (king) yashab (inhabit/dwell) on his mawashab (seat), as at other paim (times), even on the mawashab (seat) by the qayar (wall); and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) qawam (rise up) up, and Abanar (Abner) yashab (inhabit/dwell) by Shaawal (Saul's) tzad (side): but Dawad (David's) maqawam (place) was paqad (visit).

Nevertheless Shaawal (Saul) didn't dabar (word / matter) anything that yawam (day): for he amar (spoke), "maqarah (something) has happened to him. He is not tahawar (clean). Surely he is not tahawar (clean)."

It happened on the next macharath (day) after the new chadash (month), the shanay (second) day, that Dawad (David's) maqawam (place) was paqad (visit). Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Yahawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son), "Why doesn't the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse) bawaa (come) to lacham (eat), neither thamawal (yesterday), nor today?"
Yahawanathan (Jonathan) inah (answer / respond) Shaawal (Saul), "Dawad (David) shaal (earnestly) shaal (asked) leave of me to go to Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem).

He amar (spoke), ‘Please shalach (send) me go, for our mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) has a zabach (sacrifice) in the iyar (city). My ach (brother/kinsman) has tzawah (commanded) me to be there. Now, if I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye), please malat (let) me go away and raah (see) my ach (brother/kinsman).' Therefore he bawaa (come) not come to the malak (king) shalachan (table)."

Then Shaawal (Saul's) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger) against Yahawanathan (Jonathan), and he amar (spoke) to him, "You ban (son) of a iwah (perverse) maradawath (rebellious) woman, don't I yadai (know) that you have bachar (chosen) the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse) to your own bashath (shame), and to the bashath (shame) of your am (mother) irawah (nakedness)?

For as yawam (day) as the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse) chayay (life) on the adamah (earth), you shall not be kawan (established), nor your malakawath (kingdom). Therefore now shalach (send) and laqach (take / seize) him to me, for he shall ban (son) die!"
Yahawanathan (Jonathan) inah (answer / respond) Shaawal (Saul) his ab (father), and amar (spoke) to him, "Why should he be put to mawath (death)? What ishah (make) he done?"

Shaawal (Saul) tawal (cast) his chanayath (spear) at him to nakah (strike) him. By this Yahawanathan (Jonathan) yadai (knew) that his ab (father) kalah (complete / finish) determined to put Dawad (David) to mawath (death).

So Yahawanathan (Jonathan) qawam (rise up) from the shalachan (table) in charay (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and akal (eat) no lacham (food) the shanay (second) yawam (day) of the chadash (month); for he was itzab (grieved) for Dawad (David), because his ab (father) had kalam (done) him shame.

It happened in the baqar (morning), that Yahawanathan (Jonathan) yatzaa (go out / come out) out into the shadah (field) at the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) appointed with Dawad (David), and a qatan (small / young / least) nair (boy) with him.

He amar (spoke) to his nair (boy), "rawatz (run), matzaa (find) now the chatzayam (arrows) which I yarah (shoot)." As the nair (boy) rawatz (ran), he yarah (shot) an chatzay (arrow) ibar (pass over/through) him.

When the nair (boy) bawaa (come) come to the maqawam (place) of the chatzay (arrow) which Yahawanathan (Jonathan) had yarah (shot), Yahawanathan (Jonathan) qaraa (called) achar (other) the nair (boy), and amar (spoke), "Isn't the chatzay (arrow) halaah (beyond) you?"

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) qaraa (called) achar (other) the nair (boy), "Go fast! Hurry! Don't delay!" Yahawanathan (Jonathan's) nair (boy) laqat (gathered) up the chatzay (arrows), and bawaa (come) to his adawan (master / lord).
But the nair (boy) didn't yadai (know) anything. Only Yahawanathan (Jonathan) and Dawad (David) yadai (knew) the dabar (word / matter).
Yahawanathan (Jonathan) nathan (give) his kalay (weapons) to his nair (boy), and amar (spoke) to him, "yalak (go), bawaa (come) them to the iyar (city)."

As soon as the nair (boy) was bawaa (come), Dawad (David) qawam (rise up) out of the nagab (south), and napal (fall / be cast down) on his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land), and shachah (bowed) himself shalawash (three) paimayam (times). They nashaq (kissed) ayash (man / husband) rai (neigbor/another person), and bakah (wept) ayash (man / husband) with rai (neigbor/another person), and Dawad (David) bakah (wept) the most.

Yahawanathan (Jonathan) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "halak (move) in shalawam (peace / safety), because we have shanayam (two) shabai (swear / take oath) in the sham (name) of Yahawah, amar (spoke), ‘Yahawah shall be between me and you, and between my zarai (seed) and your zarai (seed), iwalam (forever).'" He arose and departed; and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) halak (move) into the city.
Then bawaa (come) David to Nob to Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech came to meet David trembling, and said to him, "Why are you alone, and no man with you?"

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Achayamalak (Ahimelech) the kahan (priest), "The king has amar (spoke) me a business, and has amar (spoke) to me, ‘Let no ayash (man / husband) know anything of the business about which I bawaa (come) you, and what I have amar (spoke) you; and I have amar (spoke) the young men to such and such a place.'
Now therefore what is under your hand? Amar (spoke) me five loaves of bread in my hand, or whatever there is present."
The priest answered David, and said, "There is no common lacham (bread) under my yad (hand), but there is holy lacham (bread); if only the young men have kept themselves from women."

Dawad (David) inah (answer / respond) the kahan (priest), and inah (answer / respond) to him, "Truly, ayashah (woman / wife) have been shamar (keep/guard) from us about these three qadash (set apart / make holy). When I came out, the vessels of the nair (young) men were qadash (set apart / make holy), though it was but a chal (common) journey. How much more then today shall their vessels be qadash (set apart / make holy)?"

So the kahan (priest) inah (answer / respond) him qadash (set apart / make holy) chal (bread); for there was no bread there but the show chal (bread), that was yatzaa (go out / come out) from thamawal (before) Yahawah, to yatzaa (go out / come out) hot chal (bread) in the yawam (day) when it was yatzaa (go out / come out) away.

Now a certain man of the servants of Yahawah (Saul) was there that yawam (day), detained panayam (face) Yahawah; and his shawam (place / establish / appoint) was Doeg the Edomite, the best of the herdsmen who belonged to Yahawah (Saul).
Yahawah (David) said to Ahimelech, "Isn't there here under your hand spear or sword? For I have neither brought my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king's business yawam (day) haste."

The priest amar (spoke), "The charab (sword) of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the valley of Elah, behold, it is here wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you will laqach (take / seize) that, laqach (take / seize) it; for there is no other except that here." Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "There is none like that. Amar (spoke) it to me."
Dawad (David) arose, and fled that day for fear of Saul, and nakah (went) to Achish the king of Gath.

The servants of Akayash (Achish) said to him, "Isn't this Dawad (David) the malak (king) of the land? Didn't they sing one to another about him in dances, saying, ‘Shaawal (Saul) has slain his thousands, Dawad (David) his ten thousands?'"
Dawad (David) laid up these words in his heart, and was very afraid of Akayash (Achish) the malak (king) of Gath.
He shawam (place / establish / appoint) his behavior panayam (face) them, and pretended to be mad in their hands, and scrabbled on the doors of the gate, and let his spittle fall down on his beard.
Then Achish said to his servants, "iyan (eye), you see the man is halal (praise). Why then il (over) you brought him to me?
Do I lack madmen, that you bawaa (come) brought this fellow to shagai (play) the madman in my presence? Shall this fellow bawaa (come) into my house?"

Dawad (David) therefore departed there, and malat (escaped) to the mairah (cave) of Idalam (Adullam). When his ach (brother/kinsman) and all his ab (father) bayath (house) shamai (hearken / hear) it, they yarad (went) down there to him.

Everyone who was in matzawaq (distress), and everyone who was in nashaa (lift), and everyone who was mar (discontented), qabatz (gathered) themselves to him; and he became shar (prince / ruler) over them: and there were with him about arabai (four) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband).

Dawad (David) yalak (went) there to Matzapah (Mizpeh) of Mawaab (Moab), and he amar (spoke) to the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab), "Please let my ab (father) and my am (mother) yatzaa (go out / come out) out with you, until I yadai (know) what Alahayam will ishah (make) for me."
He nachah (brought) them panayam (face) the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab); and they lived with him all the yawam (day) that Dawad (David) was in the stronghold.

The nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) Gad (Gad) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "Don't stay in the stronghold. Depart, and bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land) of Yahawadah (Judah)." Then Dawad (David) departed, and bawaa (come) into the yair (forest) of Charath (Hereth).

Shaawal (Saul) shamai (hearken / hear) that Dawad (David) was yadai (discovered), and the yadai (men) who were with him. Now Shaawal (Saul) was sitting in Gabaih (Gibeah), under the tamarisk ashal (tree) in Ramah, with his chanayath (spear) in his yad (hand), and all his ibad (servant) were natzab (standing) about him.

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant) who natzab (stood) about him, "shamai (hearken / hear) now, you Benjamites! Will the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse) nathan (give) everyone of you shadawath (fields) and karamayam (vineyards), will he shawam (place / establish / appoint) you all sharay (captains) of alapayam (thousands) and sharay (captains) of maawath (hundreds),

That all of you have qashar (conspired) against me, and there is none who galah (discloses) to me when my ban (son) karath (cut) a treaty with the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse), and there is none of you who is chalah (afflict) for me, or galah (discloses) to me that my ban (son) has qawam (rise up) up my ibad (servant) against me, to lie in arab (wait), as at this yawam (day)?"

Then Daag (Doeg) the Adawamay (Edomite), who natzab (stood) by the ibaday (servants) of Shaawal (Saul), amar (spoke) and amar (spoke), "I raah (see) the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse) bawaa (come) to Nab (Nob), to Achayamalak (Ahimelech) the ban (son) of Achayatawab (Ahitub).
He inquired of Yahawah for him, nathan (give) him food, and nathan (give) him the charab (sword) of Galayath (Goliath) the Palashathay (Philistine)."

Then the malak (king) shalach (send) to qaraa (called) Achayamalak (Ahimelech) the kahan (priest), the ban (son) of Achayatawab (Ahitub), and all his ab (father) bayath (house), the kahanayam (priests) who were in Nab (Nob): and they bawaa (come) all of them to the malak (king).
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "shamai (hearken / hear) now, you ban (son) of Achayatawab (Ahitub)." He amar (spoke), "Here I am, my Adawan."

Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to him, "Why have you qashar (conspired) against me, you and the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse), in that you nathan (give) given him lacham (bread), and a charab (sword), and have inquired of Alahayam for him, that he should qawam (rise up) against me, to lie in arab (wait), as at this yawam (day)?"

Then Achayamalak (Ahimelech) inah (answer / respond) the malak (king), and amar (spoke), "Who among all your ibad (servant) is so aman (believe / have faith) as Dawad (David), who is the malak (king) son-in-law, and is sawar (taken) into your council, and is honorable in your bayath (house)?

Have I today chalal (begun) to inquire of Alahayam for him? Be it chalayalah (far) from me! Don't let the malak (king) shawam (place / establish / appoint) anything to his ibad (servant), nor to all the bayath (house) of my ab (father); for your ibad (servant) yadai (knows) nothing of all this, qatan (small / young / least) or more."
The malak (king) amar (spoke), "You shall mawath (death) mawath (death), Achayamalak (Ahimelech), you, and all your ab (father) bayath (house)."

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to the rawatz (guard) who natzab (stood) about him, "sabab (turn), and mawath (death) the kahanay (priests) of Yahawah; because their yad (hand) also is with Dawad (David), and because they yadai (knew) that he barach (fled), and didn't galah (disclose) it to me." But the ibaday (servants) of the malak (king) wouldn't shalach (send) forth their yad (hand) to pagai (fall) on the kahanay (priests) of Yahawah.

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Daag (Doeg), "sabab (turn) and attack the kahanayam (priests)!" Daag (Doeg) the Adawamay (Edomite) sabab (turned), and he attacked the kahanayam (priests), and he mawath (death) on that yawam (day) shamanayam (eighty) - chamash (five) ayash (man / husband) who nashaa (lift) a bad (linen) apawad (ephod).

He nakah (struck) Nab (Nob), the iyar (city) of the kahanayam (priests), with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), both ayash (man / husband) and ayashah (woman / wife), iwalal (children) and yanaq (nursing) babies, and cattle and donkeys and shah (sheep), with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword).
Achad (one) of the ban (son) of Achayamalak (Ahimelech), the ban (son) of Achayatawab (Ahitub), sham (name) Abayathar (Abiathar), malat (escaped), and barach (fled) achar (other) Dawad (David).
Abayathar (Abiathar) nagad (told) Dawad (David) that Shaawal (Saul) had harag (kill) Yahawah kahanay (priests).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Abayathar (Abiathar), "I yadai (knew) on that yawam (day), when Daag (Doeg) the Adawamay (Edomite) was there, that he would nagad (surely) nagad (tell) Shaawal (Saul). I am responsible for the death of all the napash (soul) of your ab (father) bayath (house).
Stay with me, don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid); for he who baqash (seeks) my napash (soul) baqash (seeks) your napash (soul). For with me you shall be in mashamarath (duty / watch)."
Dawad (David) was nagad (told), "Behold, the Palashathay (Philistines) are lacham (fighting) against Qaiyalah (Keilah), and are shasah (robbing) the garan (threshing) floors."

Therefore Dawad (David) inquired of Yahawah, amar (spoke), "Shall I yalak (go) and nakah (strike) these Palashathay (Philistines)?" Yahawah amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "yalak (go) nakah (strike) the Palashathay (Philistines), and yashai (salvation) Qaiyalah (Keilah)."

Dawad (David's) anashay (men) amar (spoke) to him, "Behold, we are yaraa (fear / be afraid) here in Yahawadah (Judah): how much more then if we yalak (go) to Qaiyalah (Keilah) against the mairakawath (armies) of the Palashathay (Philistines)?"

Then Dawad (David) inquired of Yahawah yet again. Yahawah inah (answer / respond) him, and inah (answer / respond), "qawam (rise up), yarad (go) down to Qaiyalah (Keilah); for I will nathan (give) the Palashathay (Philistines) into your yad (hand)."

Dawad (David) and his ayash (man / husband) yalak (went) to Qaiyalah (Keilah), and lacham (fought) with the Palashathay (Philistines), and nahag (brought) away their livestock, and nakah (killed) them with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) makah (slaughter). So Dawad (David) yashai (salvation) the yashabay (inhabitants) of Qaiyalah (Keilah).

It happened, when Abayathar (Abiathar) the ban (son) of Achayamalak (Ahimelech) barach (fled) to Dawad (David) to Qaiyalah (Keilah), that he yarad (came) down with an apawad (ephod) in his yad (hand).

It was nagad (told) Shaawal (Saul) that Dawad (David) bawaa (come) come to Qaiyalah (Keilah). Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "Alahayam has nakar (delivered) him into my yad (hand); for he is sagar (shut) in, by bawaa (come) into a iyar (town) that has dalathayam (gates) and barayach (bars)."
Shaawal (Saul) summoned all the im (nation / people) to malachamah (war), to yarad (go) down to Qaiyalah (Keilah), to tzawar (besiege) Dawad (David) and his im (nation / people).
Dawad (David) yadai (knew) that Shaawal (Saul) was charash (devising) rai (mischief) amar (spoke) him; and he said to Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahan (priest), "Bring the apawad (ephod) here."

Then Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "O Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), your ibad (servant) has shamai (hearken / hear) shamai (hearken / hear) that Shaawal (Saul) baqash (seeks) to bawaa (come) to Qaiyalah (Keilah), to shachath (destroy) the iyar (city) for my sake.

Will the bailay (men) of Qaiyalah (Keilah) sagar (deliver) me up into his yad (hand)? Will Shaawal (Saul) yarad (come) down, as your ibad (servant) has shamai (hearken / hear)? Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), I beg you, nagad (tell) your ibad (servant)." Yahawah amar (spoke), "He will yarad (come) down."

Then Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "Will the bailay (men) of Qaiyalah (Keilah) sagar (deliver) me and my bailay (men) into the yad (hand) of Shaawal (Saul)?" Yahawah amar (spoke), "They will sagar (deliver) you up."

Then Dawad (David) and his ayash (man / husband), who were about shash (six) maah (hundred), qawam (rise up) and departed out of Qaiyalah (Keilah), and halak (move) wherever they could halak (move). It was nagad (told) Shaawal (Saul) that Dawad (David) was malat (escaped) from Qaiyalah (Keilah); and he gave up yatzaa (go out / come out) there.

Dawad (David) stayed in the madabar (wilderness) in the strongholds, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the har (mountain) country in the madabar (wilderness) of Zayap (Ziph). Shaawal (Saul) baqash (sought) him every yawam (day), but Alahayam didn't nathan (give) him into his yad (hand).

Dawad (David) raah (see) that Shaawal (Saul) yatzaa (go out / come out) come out to baqash (seek) his napash (soul). Dawad (David) was in the madabar (wilderness) of Zayap (Ziph) in the Charash (wood).
Yahawanathan (Jonathan), Shaawal (Saul's) ban (son), qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) to Dawad (David) into the Charash (woods), and chazaq (strengthened) his yad (hand) in Alahayam.

He amar (spoke) to him, "Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid); for the yad (hand) of Shaawal (Saul) my ab (father) shall not matzaa (find) you; and you shall be malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel), and I shall be mashanah (next) to you; and that also Shaawal (Saul) my ab (father) yadai (knows)."
They shanayam (two) karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) panayam (face) Yahawah: and Dawad (David) stayed in the Charash (woods), and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) halak (move) to his bayath (house).

Then the zapayam (ziphites) ilah (go up / offer) up to Shaawal (Saul) to Gabaih (Gibeah), amar (spoke), "Doesn't Dawad (David) sathar (hide) himself with us in the strongholds in the Charash (wood), in the gabaih (hill) of Chakayalah (Hachilah), which is on the yamayan (right hand) of the yashayamawan (desert)?

Now therefore, O malak (king), yarad (come) down, according to all the awah (desire) of your napash (soul) to yarad (come) down; and our part shall be to sagar (deliver) him up into the malak (king) yad (hand)."
Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "You are barak (blessed) by Yahawah; for you chamal (have) had compassion on me.

Please yalak (go) kawan (make) yet more yadai (sure), and know and raah (see) his maqawam (place) where his ragal (feet / foot) is, and who raah (see) seen him there; for it is amar (spoke) me that he iram (deals) very subtly.

Raah (see) therefore, and take yadai (knowledge) of all the lurking machabaayam (places) where he chabaa (hides) himself, and shawab (turn back / repent) again to me with kawan (certainty), and I will halak (move) with you: and it yash (shall) happen, if he is in the aratz (Earth/land), that I will chapash (search) him out among all the alapay (thousands) of Yahawadah (Judah)."

They qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) to Zayap (Ziph) panayam (face) Shaawal (Saul): but Dawad (David) and his ayash (man / husband) were in the madabar (wilderness) of maiwan (maon), in the irabah (arabah) on the yamayan (right hand) of the yashayamawan (desert).

Shaawal (Saul) and his ayash (man / husband) yalak (went) to baqash (seek) him. When Dawad (David) was nagad (told), he yarad (went) down to the salai (rock), and stayed in the madabar (wilderness) of maiwan (maon). When Shaawal (Saul) shamai (hearken / hear) that, he radap (pursued) Dawad (David) in the madabar (wilderness) of maiwan (maon).

Shaawal (Saul) yalak (went) on this tzad (side) of the har (mountain), and Dawad (David) and his zah (this / that / these) on that tzad (side) of the har (mountain): and Dawad (David) made chapaz (haste) to yalak (get) away for panayam (face) of Shaawal (Saul); for Shaawal (Saul) and his zah (this / that / these) surrounded Dawad (David) and his zah (this / that / these) to thapash (take) them.
But a malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) bawaa (come) to Shaawal (Saul), amar (spoke), "Hurry and yalak (come); for the Palashathay (Philistines) have pashat (made) a raid on the aratz (Earth/land)!"

So Shaawal (Saul) shawab (turn back / repent) from radap (pursuing) achar (other) Dawad (David), and yalak (went) il (over) the Palashathay (Philistines): therefore they qaraa (called) that maqawam (place) Salaihamachalaqawath (Sela Hammahlekoth).
Dawad (David) ilah (go up / offer) up from there, and lived in the strongholds of Iyan-Gaday (En Gedi).
It happened, when Saul was yashab (inhabit/dwell) from following the Philistines, that it was told him, saying, "Behold, Dawad (David) is in the wilderness of Iyan-Gaday (En Gedi)."
Then Shaawal (Saul) shawab (turn back / repent) three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and shawab (turn back / repent) to seek Dawad (David) and his men on the rocks of the wild goats.

He yalak (came) to the sheep pens by the yalak (way), where there was a cave; and Shaawal (Saul) yalak (went) in to relieve himself. Now Dawad (David) and his ayash (man / husband) were abiding in the innermost parts of the cave.

The ayash (man / husband) of Dawad (David) said to him, "Behold, the day of which Yahawah said to you, ‘Behold, I will deliver your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as it shall seem ayash (man / husband) to you.'" Then Dawad (David) arose, and cut off the skirt of Shaawal (Saul's) robe secretly.
It happened afterward, that Dawad (David's) heart nathan (give) him, because he had karath (cut) off Shaawal (Saul's) kanap (skirt).
He said to his men, "Yahawah forbid that I should hayah (came to pass) this thing to my Adawan, Yahawah anointed, to put forth my hand against him, since he is Yahawah anointed."

So Yahawah (David) checked his ayash (man / husband) with these dabar (word / matter), and didn't allow them to rise against Yahawah (Saul). Yahawah (Saul) rose up out of the cave, and ishah (make) on his way.

Dawad (David) also qawam (rise up) afterward, and yalak (went) out of the mairah (cave), and nathan (give) al (toward) Shaawal (Saul), dabar (word / matter), "My Adawan the king!" When Shaawal (Saul) looked behind him, Dawad (David) bowed with his face to the earth, and showed respect.
Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "Why do you listen to men's words, amar (spoke), ‘Behold, Dawad (David) seeks your hurt?'

Behold, this day your eyes have seen how that Yahawah had delivered you today into my hand in the cave. Some urged me to kill you; but I spared you; and I amar (spoke), I will not put forth my hand against my Adawan; for he is Yahawah anointed.

Moreover, my father, raah (see), yes, raah (see) the skirt of your robe in my yad (hand); for in that I cut off the skirt of your robe, and didn't harag (kill) you, know and raah (see) that there is neither evil nor disobedience in my yad (hand), and I have not sinned against you, though you hunt for my yawam (day) to raah (see) it.
May Yahawah judge between me and you, and may Yahawah avenge me of you; but my yad (hand) shall not be on you.
As the proverb of the ancients says, ‘Out of the wicked hayah (came to pass) forth wickedness;' but my yad (hand) shall not be on you.
Against whom has the king of Israel yatzaa (go out / come out) out? Whom do you pursue? A dead dog? A flea?
May Yahawah therefore be judge, and give sentence between me and you, and see, and plead my yatzaa (go out / come out), and deliver me out of your hand."

It came to pass, when Yahawah (David) hayah (came to pass) made an end of speaking these words to Yahawah (Saul), that Yahawah (Saul) said, "Is this your voice, my son Yahawah (David)?" Yahawah (Saul) lifted up his voice, and wept.
He amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "You are more righteous than I; for you have hayah (came to pass) good to me, whereas I have hayah (came to pass) evil to you.
You have amar (spoke) this day how you have dealt tawab (good / proper function) with me, because when Yahawah had delivered me up into your hand, you didn't kill me.
For if a ishah (make) finds his enemy, will he let him go away unharmed? Therefore may Yahawah reward you tawab (good / proper function) for that which you ishah (make) done to me this yawam (day).
Now, behold, I know that you shall kay (surely) be king, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be established in your matzaa (hand).
Yad (hand) now therefore to me by Yahawah, that you will not cut off my seed after me, and that you will not destroy my name out of my father's house."
Yahawah (David) shabai (swear / take oath) to Yahawah (Saul). Yahawah (Saul) went bayath (house); but Yahawah (David) and his men went up to the stronghold.

Shamawaal (Samuel) mawath (death); and all Yashar-Al (Israel) qabatz (gathered) themselves together, and sapad (lamented) him, and qabar (bury) him in his bayath (house) at Ramah (Ramah). Dawad (David) qawam (rise up), and yarad (went) down to the madabar (wilderness) of Paaran (Paran).

There was a ayash (man / husband) in maiwan (maon), whose maishah (possessions) were in Karamal (Carmel); and the ayash (man / husband) was very gadawal (very great/important/mighty), and he had shalawash (three) alap (thousand) tzaan (sheep), and a alap (thousand) izayam (goats): and he was gazaz (shearing) his tzaan (sheep) in Karamal (Carmel).

Now the sham (name) of the ayash (man / husband) was Nabal (Nabal); and the sham (name) of his ayashah (woman / wife) Abayagayal (Abigail); and the ayashah (woman / wife) was of tawab (good / proper function) shakal (understanding), and of a yapah (beautiful) thaar (face): but the ayash (man / husband) was qashah (rough / hard) and rai (evil) in his mailalayam (doings); and he was of the house of Caleb.
Dawad (David) shamai (hearken / hear) in the madabar (wilderness) that Nabal (Nabal) was gazaz (shearing) his tzaan (sheep).

Dawad (David) shalach (send) ishar (ten) nair (young) men, and Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to the nair (young) men, "ilah (go up / offer) up to Karamal (Carmel), and bawaa (come) to Nabal (Nabal), and shaal (greet) him in my sham (name).
You shall amar (spoke) him, ‘Long life to you! Shalawam (peace / safety) be to you, and shalawam (peace / safety) be to your bayath (house), and shalawam (peace / safety) be to all that you have.

Now I have shamai (hearken / hear) that you have gazazayam (shearers). Your raiyam (shepherds) have now been with us, and we didn't kalam (hurt) them, neither was there anything paqad (visit) from them, all the yawam (day) they were in Karamal (Carmel).

Shaal (ask) your nair (young) men, and they will nagad (tell) you. Therefore, let the nair (young) men matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (eye); for we bawaa (come) in a tawab (good / proper function) yawam (day). Please nathan (give) whatever yamatzaaw (comes) to your yad (hand), to your ibad (servant), and to your ban (son) Dawad (David).'"
When Dawad (David's) nair (young) men bawaa (come), they dabar (word / matter) to Nabal (Nabal) according to all those dabarayam (words) in the sham (name) of Dawad (David), and nawach (ceased).

Nabal (Nabal) inah (answer / respond) Dawad (David's) ibaday (servants), and inah (answer / respond), "Who is Dawad (David)? Who is the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse)? There are many ibaday (servants) who paratz (break) away from their adawan (master / lord) these yawam (day).

Shall I then laqach (take / seize) my lacham (bread), and my mayam (Waters), and my meat that I have tabach (killed) for my gazaz (shearers), and nathan (give) it to anashayam (men) who I don't yadai (know) where they come from?"
So Dawad (David's) nair (young) men hapak (turned) on their darak (way), and shawab (turn back / repent) back, and bawaa (come) and nagad (told) him according to all these dabarayam (words).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to his ayash (man / husband), "Every ayash (man / husband) chagar (put) on his charab (sword)!" Every ayash (man / husband) chagar (put) on his charab (sword). Dawad (David) also chagar (put) on his charab (sword). About arabai (four) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) achar (other) Dawad (David); and two maah (hundred) stayed by the baggage.

But achad (one) of the nair (young) men nagad (told) Abayagayal (Abigail), Nabal (Nabal's) ayashah (woman / wife), amar (spoke), "Behold, Dawad (David) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) out of the madabar (wilderness) to Greet our adawan (master / lord); and he iyat (railed) at them.

But the anashayam (men) were very tawab (good / proper function) to us, and we were not kalam (hurt), neither paqad (visit) we anything, as yawam (day) as we halak (move) with them, when we were in the shadah (fields).
They were a chawamah (wall) to us both by layal (night) and by yawamam (by day), all the yawam (day) we were with them raih (keeping) the tzaan (sheep).

Now therefore yadai (know) and raah (see) what you will ishah (make); for rai (evil) is kalah (complete / finish) against our adawan (master / lord), and against all his bayath (house); for he is such a worthless fellow that one can't dabar (word / matter) to him."

Then Abayagayal (Abigail) hurried and laqach (take / seize) two maah (hundred) loaves of bread, shanayam (two) nabalay (bottles) of yayan (wine), chamash (five) tzaan (sheep) ready ishah (make), chamash (five) saayam (measures) of qalay (parched) grain, one maah (hundred) clusters of tzamaqayam (raisins), and two maah (hundred) dabalayam (cakes) of figs, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them on donkeys.

She amar (spoke) to her nair (young) men, "ibar (pass over/through) on panayam (face) me. Behold, I bawaa (come) achar (other) you." But she didn't nagad (tell) her ayash (man / husband), Nabal (Nabal).

It was so, as she rakab (rode) on her donkey, and yarad (came) down by the sathar (secret / hidden) of the har (mountain), that behold, Dawad (David) and his ayash (man / husband) yarad (came) down toward her; and she pagash (met) them.

Now Dawad (David) had amar (spoke), "Surely in shaqar (vain) have I shamar (keep/guard) all that zah (this / that / these) fellow has in the madabar (wilderness), so that maawamah (nothing) was paqad (visit) of shawab (turn back / repent) that pertained to him. He has returned me rai (evil) for tawab (good / proper function).

Alahayam ishah (make) so to the ayabay (enemies) of Dawad (David), and more also, if I shaar (leave) of all that belongs to him by the baqar (morning) light so much as shathan (one) who urinates on a qayar (wall)."

When Abayagayal (Abigail) raah (see) Dawad (David), she hurried, and alighted from her donkey, and napal (fall / be cast down) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) Dawad (David) on her panayam (face), and shachah (bowed) herself to the aratz (Earth/land).

She napal (fall / be cast down) at his ragal (feet / foot), and amar (spoke), "On me, my Adawan, on me be the iwan (guilt/iniquity); and please let your handmaid dabar (word / matter) in your azan (ear). Shamai (hearken / hear) the dabaray (words) of your handmaid.

Please don't let my Adawan lab (heart) this worthless ayash (man / husband), even Nabal (Nabal); for as his sham (name) is, so is he. Nabal (Nabal) is his sham (name), and nabalah (folly) is with him; but I, your handmaid, didn't raah (see) the nair (young) men of my Adawan, whom you shalach (send).

Now therefore, my Adawan, as Yahawah chay (life), and as your napash (soul) chay (life), since Yahawah has withheld you from dam (blood) guiltiness, and from yashai (salvation) yourself with your own yad (hand), now therefore let your ayab (enemy), and those who baqash (seek) rai (evil) to my Adawan, be as Nabal (Nabal).
Now this barakah (present) which your shapachah (servant) bawaa (come) brought to my Adawan, nathan (give) it be given to the nair (young) men who halak (move) my Adawan.

Please nashaa (lift) the pashai (trespass) of your handmaid. For Yahawah will ishah (make) ishah (make) my Adawan a aman (believe / have faith) bayath (house), because my Adawan lacham (fights) the malachamawath (battles) of Yahawah; and rai (evil) shall not be matzaa (found) in you all your yawam (day).

Though adam (men) may qawam (rise up) up to radap (pursue) you, and to baqash (seek) your napash (soul), yet the napash (soul) of my Adawan shall be tzarar (bound) in the tzarawar (bundle) of chay (life) with Yahawah your Alahayam. He will qalai (sling) out the napash (soul) of your ayab (enemy), as from the hollow of a qalai (sling).

It shall come to pass, when Yahawah ishah (make) done to my Adawan according to all the tawab (good / proper function) that he has dabar (word / matter) concerning you, and shall have tzawah (appointed) you nagayad (prince) over Yashar-Al (Israel),

That this shall be no pawaqah (grief) to you, nor offense of lab (heart) to my Adawan, either that you have shapak (shed) dam (blood) chanam (without) cause, or that my Adawan has avenged himself. When Yahawah yatab (has) dealt well with my Adawan, then zakar (remember) your handmaid."
Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Abayagayal (Abigail), "barak (blessed) is Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), who shalach (send) you this yawam (day) to qaraa (called) me!

Barak (blessed) is your taim (discretion), and barak (blessed) are you, that have kalaa (kept) me this yawam (day) from dam (blood) guiltiness, and from yashai (salvation) myself with my own yad (hand).

For indeed, as Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), chay (life), who has withheld me from raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) you, lawalaa (unless) you had hurried and bawaa (come) to qaraa (called) me, surely there wouldn't have been yathar (left) to Nabal (Nabal) by the baqar (morning) awar (light) so much as shathan (one) who urinates on a qayar (wall)."

So Dawad (David) laqach (take / seize) of her yad (hand) that which she bawaa (come) brought him: and he amar (spoke) to her, "ilah (go up / offer) up in shalawam (peace / safety) to your bayath (house). Raah (see), I have shamai (hearken / hear) to your qawal (sound / voice), and have granted your request."

Abayagayal (Abigail) bawaa (come) to Nabal (Nabal); and behold, he held a mashathah (feast) in his bayath (house), like the mashathah (feast) of a malak (king). Nabal (Nabal's) lab (heart) was tawab (good / proper function) within him, for he was very shakawar (drunken). Therefore she nagad (told) him nothing, qatan (small / young / least) or more, until the baqar (morning) awar (light).

It happened in the baqar (morning), when the yayan (wine) was yatzaa (go out / come out) out of Nabal (Nabal), that his ayashah (woman / wife) nagad (told) him these things, and his lab (heart) mawath (death) qarab (among / near) him, and he became as a aban (stone).
It happened about ishar (ten) yamayam (days) after, that Yahawah nagap (struck) Nabal (Nabal), so that he mawath (death).

When Dawad (David) shamai (hearken / hear) that Nabal (Nabal) was mawath (death), he amar (spoke), "barak (blessed) is Yahawah, who has rayab (pleaded) the rayab (cause) of my charapah (reproach) from the yad (hand) of Nabal (Nabal), and has chashak (darkness) back his ibad (servant) from rai (evil). Yahawah has shawab (turn back / repent) the evildoing of Nabal (Nabal) on his own raash (head)." Dawad (David) shalach (send) and dabar (word / matter) concerning Abayagayal (Abigail), to laqach (take / seize) her to him as ayashah (woman / wife).

When the ibaday (servants) of Dawad (David) bawaa (come) come to Abayagayal (Abigail) to Karamal (Carmel), they dabar (word / matter) to her, amar (spoke), "Dawad (David) has shalach (send) us to you, to laqach (take / seize) you to him as ayashah (woman / wife)."

She qawam (rise up), and shachah (bowed) herself with her ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land), and amar (spoke), "Behold, your handmaid is a shapachah (servant) to rachatz (wash) the ragalay (feet) of the shapachah (servants) of my Adawan."

Abayagayal (Abigail) hurried, and qawam (rise up), and rakab (rode) on a donkey, with chamash (five) ladies of hers who ragal (feet / foot) her; and she halak (move) ragal (feet / foot) the malaakay (messengers) of Dawad (David), and became his ayashah (woman / wife).
Dawad (David) also laqach (take / seize) Achayanaim (Ahinoam) of Yazaraial (Jezreel); and they shanayam (two) became his wives.
Now Shaawal (Saul) nathan (give) given Mayakal (Michal) his banath (daughter), Dawad (David's) ayashah (woman / wife), to Palatay (Palti) the ban (son) of Layash (Laish), who was of Galayam (Gallim).

The zapayam (ziphites) bawaa (come) to Shaawal (Saul) to Gabaih (Gibeah), amar (spoke), "Doesn't Dawad (David) sathar (hide) himself in the gabaih (hill) of Chakayalah (Hachilah), which is panayam (face) the yashayamawan (desert)?"

Then Shaawal (Saul) qawam (rise up), and yarad (went) down to the madabar (wilderness) of Zayap (Ziph), having shalawash (three) alap (thousand) bachar (chosen) ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) with him, to baqash (seek) Dawad (David) in the madabar (wilderness) of Zayap (Ziph).

Shaawal (Saul) chanah (encamped) in the gabaih (hill) of Chakayalah (Hachilah), which is panayam (face) the yashayamawan (desert), by the darak (way). But Dawad (David) stayed in the madabar (wilderness), and he raah (see) that Shaawal (Saul) bawaa (come) achar (other) him into the madabar (wilderness).
Dawad (David) therefore shalach (send) out maragalayam (spies), and yadai (understood) that Shaawal (Saul) had certainly bawaa (come).

Dawad (David) qawam (rise up), and bawaa (come) to the maqawam (place) where Shaawal (Saul) had chanah (encamped); and Dawad (David) raah (see) the maqawam (place) where Shaawal (Saul) shakab (lay), and Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner), the shar (prince / ruler) of his tzabaa (troop): and Shaawal (Saul) shakab (lay) within the place of the wagons, and the im (nation / people) were chanah (encamped) around him.

Then inah (answer / respond) Dawad (David) and amar (spoke) to Achayamalak (Ahimelech) the Chathay (Hittite), and to Abayashay (Abishai) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah), ach (brother/kinsman) to Yawaab (Joab), amar (spoke), "Who will yarad (go) down with me to Shaawal (Saul) to the machanah (camp)?" Abayashay (Abishai) amar (spoke), "I will yarad (go) down with you."

So Dawad (David) and Abayashay (Abishai) bawaa (come) to the im (nation / people) by layal (night): and, behold, Shaawal (Saul) shakab (lay) yashan (sleeping) within the place of the wagons, with his chanayath (spear) maik (stuck) in the aratz (Earth/land) at his maraashah (head); and Abanar (Abner) and the im (nation / people) shakab (lay) around him.

Then Abayashay (Abishai) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "Alahayam has sagar (delivered) up your ayab (enemy) into your yad (hand) this yawam (day). Now therefore please let me nakah (strike) him with the chanayath (spear) to the aratz (Earth/land) at paim (one) stroke, and I will not strike him the shanah (second) time."

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Abayashay (Abishai), "Don't shachath (destroy) him; for who can shalach (send) forth his yad (hand) against Yahawah mashayach (anointed one), and be naqah (clean/innocent)?"

Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "As Yahawah chay (life), Yahawah will nagap (strike) him; or his yawam (day) shall bawaa (come) to mawath (death); or he shall bawaa (come) down into malachamah (battle) and sapah (perish).

Yahawah chalayalah (forbid) that I should shalach (send) forth my yad (hand) against Yahawah mashayach (anointed one); but now please laqach (take / seize) the chanayath (spear) that is at his maraashah (head), and the jar of mayam (Waters), and yalak (let) us go."

So Dawad (David) laqach (take / seize) the chanayath (spear) and the jar of mayam (Waters) from Shaawal (Saul's) raashath (head); and they yalak (went) away: and no man raah (see) it, nor yadai (knew) it, neither did any qawatz (awake); for they were all asleep, because a tharadamah (deep) sleep from Yahawah was napal (fall / be cast down) on them.

Then Dawad (David) ibar (pass over/through) over to the other ibar (side), and imad (stood) on the raash (head) of the har (mountain) rachawaq (afar) off; a rab (great) maqawam (place) being between them;

And Dawad (David) qaraa (called) to the im (nation / people), and to Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner), amar (spoke), "Don't you inah (answer / respond), Abanar (Abner)?" Then Abanar (Abner) inah (answer / respond), "Who are you who qaraa (called) to the malak (king)?"

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Abanar (Abner), "Aren't you a ayash (man / husband)? Who is like you in Yashar-Al (Israel)? Why then have you not shamar (keep/guard) watch over your Adawan, the malak (king)? For achad (one) of the im (nation / people) bawaa (come) in to shachath (destroy) the malak (king) your Adawan.

This thing isn't tawab (good / proper function) that you ishah (make) done. As Yahawah chay (life), you are ban (son) to mawath (death), because you have not shamar (keep/guard) watch over your Adawan, Yahawah mashayach (anointed one). Now raah (see) where the malak (king) chanayath (spear) is, and the jar of mayam (Waters) that was at his maraashah (head)."

Shaawal (Saul) nakar (knew) Dawad (David's) qawal (sound / voice), and amar (spoke), "Is this your qawal (sound / voice), my ban (son) Dawad (David)?" Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "It is my qawal (sound / voice), my Adawan, O malak (king)."
He amar (spoke), "Why does my Adawan radap (pursue) achar (other) his ibad (servant)? For what ishah (make) I done? Or what rai (evil) is in my yad (hand)?

Now therefore, please let my Adawan the malak (king) shamai (hearken / hear) the dabaray (words) of his ibad (servant). If it is so that Yahawah has sawath (stirred) you up against me, let him rawach (spirit / wind) an manachah (offering). But if it is the banay (children) of adam (men), they are arar (cursed) panayam (face) Yahawah; for they have garash (driven) me out this yawam (day) that I shouldn't cling to Yahawah nachalah (inheritance), amar (spoke), ‘yalak (go), ibad (servant) other Alahayam!'

Now therefore, don't let my dam (blood) napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land) away from the panayam (face) of Yahawah; for the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) yatzaa (go out / come out) come out to baqash (seek) a paraish (flea), as when one radap (hunts) a qaraa (called) in the harayam (mountains)."

Then Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "I have chataa (sinned). Shawab (turn back / repent), my ban (son) Dawad (David); for I will no more raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) you harm, because my napash (soul) was yaqar (precious) in your iyan (eye) this yawam (day). Behold, I have sakal (played) the fool, and have shagah (erred) rabah (exceedingly)."
Dawad (David) inah (answer / respond), "Behold the chanayath (spear), O malak (king)! Then let achad (one) of the nair (young) men ibar (pass over/through) over and laqach (take / seize) it.

Yahawah will shawab (turn back / repent) to every ayash (man / husband) his tzadaqah (righteousness) and his amawanah (faithfulness); because Yahawah nathan (give) you into my yad (hand) today, and I wouldn't shalach (send) forth my yad (hand) against Yahawah mashayach (anointed one).

Behold, as your napash (soul) was respected this yawam (day) in my iyanay (eyes), so let my napash (soul) be respected in the iyanay (eyes) of Yahawah, and let him natzal (deliver) me out of all oppression."

Then Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "You are barak (blessed), my ban (son) Dawad (David). You shall both ishah (make) mightily, and shall surely yakal (prevail)." So Dawad (David) yalak (went) his darak (way), and Shaawal (Saul) shawab (turn back / repent) to his maqawam (place).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) in his lab (heart), "I shall now sapah (perish) achad (one) yawam (day) by the yad (hand) of Shaawal (Saul). There is nothing tawab (good / proper function) for me kay (surely) that I should malat (escape) into the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines); and Shaawal (Saul) will yaash (despair) of me, to baqash (seek) me any more in all the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yashar-Al (Israel). So shall I malat (escape) out of his yad (hand)."

Dawad (David) qawam (rise up), and ibar (pass over/through) over, he and the shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) who were with him, to Akayash (Achish) the ban (son) of Maiwak (Maoch), malak (king) of gath (gath).

Dawad (David) lived with Akayash (Achish) at gath (gath), he and his ayash (man / husband), every ayash (man / husband) with his bayath (house), even Dawad (David) with his shanayam (two) wives, Achayanaim (Ahinoam) the yazaraialayath (jezreelitess), and Abayagayal (Abigail) the karamalayath (carmelitess), Nabal (Nabal's) ayashah (woman / wife).
It was nagad (told) Shaawal (Saul) that Dawad (David) was barach (fled) to gath (gath): and he baqash (sought) no more again for him.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Akayash (Achish), "If now I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye), nathan (give) them give me a maqawam (place) in achad (one) of the iray (cities) in the shadah (country), that I may yashab (inhabit/dwell) there. For why should your ibad (servant) yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the mamalakah (royal) iyar (city) with you?"
Then Akayash (Achish) nathan (give) him Tzaqalag (Ziklag) that yawam (day): why Tzaqalag (Ziklag) pertains to the malakay (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah) to this yawam (day).
The masapar (number) of the days that Dawad (David) lived in the shadah (country) of the Palashathay (Philistines) was a yawam (day) year and arabai (four) chadashayam (months).

Dawad (David) and his ayash (man / husband) ilah (go up / offer) up, and pashat (made) a raid on the Gashawaray (Geshurites), and the Girzites, and the Imalaqay (Amalekites); for those were the yashabawath (inhabitants) of the aratz (Earth/land), who were of iwalam (forever), as you bawaa (come) to Shawar (Shur), even to the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

Dawad (David) nakah (struck) the aratz (Earth/land), and saved neither ayash (man / husband) nor ayashah (woman / wife) chayah (alive), and laqach (take / seize) away the tzaan (sheep), and the cattle, and the donkeys, and the gamalayam (camels), and the bagad (clothing); and he shawab (turn back / repent), and bawaa (come) to Akayash (Achish).

Akayash (Achish) amar (spoke), "Against whom have you pashat (made) a raid today?" Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "Against the nagab (south) of Yahawadah (Judah), against the nagab (south) of the Yarachamaalay (Jerahmeelites), and against the nagab (south) of the Qayanay (Kenites)."

Dawad (David) chayah (saved) neither ayash (man / husband) nor ayashah (woman / wife) chayah (alive), to bawaa (come) them to gath (gath), amar (spoke), "Lest they should nagad (tell) of us, amar (spoke), ‘Dawad (David) this, and this has been his mashapat (way) all the yawam (day) he has lived in the shadah (country) of the Palashathay (Philistines).'"

Akayash (Achish) aman (believe / have faith) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), "He has made his im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel) baash (utterly) to abhor him. Therefore he shall be my ibad (servant) iwalam (forever)."

It happened in those yamayam (days), that the Palashathay (Philistines) qabatz (gathered) their machanah (armies) qabatz (together) for tzabaa (troop), to lacham (fight) with Yashar-Al (Israel). Akayash (Achish) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "yadai (know) yadai (assuredly) that you shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out with me in the machanah (army), you and your yadai (men)."

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Akayash (Achish), "Therefore you shall yadai (know) what your ibad (servant) will ishah (make)." Akayash (Achish) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "Therefore will I shawam (place / establish / appoint) you my bodyguard for yawam (day)."

Now Shamawaal (Samuel) was mawath (death), and all Yashar-Al (Israel) had sapad (lamented) him, and qabar (bury) him in Ramah (Ramah), even in his own iyar (city). Shaawal (Saul) had sawar (put) away those who had familiar abawath (spirits), and the yadainayam (wizards), out of the aratz (Earth/land).

The Palashathay (Philistines) qabatz (gathered) themselves together, and bawaa (come) and chanah (encamped) in Shawanam (Shunem): and Shaawal (Saul) qabatz (gathered) all Yashar-Al (Israel) qabatz (together), and they chanah (encamped) in Galabai (Gilboa).
When Shaawal (Saul) raah (see) the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines), he was yaraa (fear / be afraid), and his lab (heart) charad (trembled) maad (greatly).
When Shaawal (Saul) inquired of Yahawah, Yahawah didn't inah (answer / respond) him, neither by chalamawath (dreams), nor by awarayam (urim), nor by nabayaam (prophets).

Then Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), "baqash (seek) me a ayashah (woman / wife) who has a familiar awab (spirit), that I may yalak (go) to her, and darash (inquire) of her." His ibad (servant) amar (spoke) to him, "Behold, there is a ayashah (woman / wife) who has a familiar awab (spirit) at Iyan-Daar (Endor)."

Shaawal (Saul) disguised himself, and labash (put) on other bagad (clothing), and yalak (went), he and shanayam (two) acharayam (men) with him, and they bawaa (come) to the ayashah (woman / wife) by layal (night): and he amar (spoke), "Please qasam (divine) to me by the familiar awab (spirit), and ilah (go up / offer) me up whomever I shall amar (spoke) to you."

The ayashah (woman / wife) amar (spoke) to him, "Behold, you yadai (know) what Shaawal (Saul) ishah (make) done, how he has karath (cut) off those who have familiar abawath (spirits), and the yadainay (wizards), out of the aratz (Earth/land). Why then do you lay a naqash (snare) for my napash (soul), to cause me to mawath (death)?"
Shaawal (Saul) shabai (swear / take oath) to her by Yahawah, amar (spoke), "As Yahawah chay (life), no iwan (guilt/iniquity) shall qarah (happen) to you for this thing."
Then the ayashah (woman / wife) amar (spoke), "Whom shall I ilah (go up / offer) up to you?" He amar (spoke), "Bring Shamawaal (Samuel) up for me."

When the ayashah (woman / wife) raah (see) Shamawaal (Samuel), she zaiq (cried) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice); and the ayashah (woman / wife) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), amar (spoke), "Why have you ramah (deceived) me? For you are Shaawal (Saul)!"

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to her, "Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). For what do you raah (see)?" The ayashah (woman / wife) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "I raah (see) a Alahayam coming up out of the aratz (Earth/land)."

He amar (spoke) to her, "What does he look like?" She amar (spoke), "An zaqan (old) ayash (man / husband) ilah (go up / offer) up. He is itah (covered) with a maiyal (robe)." Shaawal (Saul) yadai (perceived) that it was Shamawaal (Samuel), and he qadad (bowed) with his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land), and showed respect.

Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke) to Shaawal (Saul), "Why have you disturbed me, to ilah (go up / offer) me up?" Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke), "I am very tzarar (distressed); for the Palashathay (Philistines) make lacham (war) against me, and Alahayam has sawar (departed) from me, and answers me no more, neither by nabayaam (prophets), nor by chalamawath (dreams). Therefore I have qaraa (called) you, that you may yadai (make) known to me what I shall ishah (make)."
Shamawaal (Samuel) amar (spoke), "Why then do you shaal (ask) of me, since Yahawah has sawar (departed) from you and has become your ir (adversary)?

Yahawah ishah (make) done to you as he dabar (word / matter) by me. Yahawah has qarai (torn) the mamalakah (kingdom) out of your yad (hand), and nathan (give) it to your neighbor, even to Dawad (David).

Ashar (who/that) you didn't obey the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah, and didn't ishah (make) his charawan (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) on Imalaq (Amalek), therefore Yahawah ishah (make) done this thing to you this yawam (day).

Moreover Yahawah will nathan (give) Yashar-Al (Israel) also with you into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines); and machar (tomorrow) you and your ban (son) will be with me. Yahawah will nathan (give) the machanah (army) of Yashar-Al (Israel) also into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines)."

Then Shaawal (Saul) napal (fall / be cast down) immediately his malaa (full) length on the aratz (Earth/land), and was terrified, because of the dabaray (words) of Shamawaal (Samuel). There was no kach (strength / mighty / power) in him; for he had akal (eat) no lacham (bread) all the yawam (day), nor all the layal (night).

The ayashah (woman / wife) bawaa (come) to Shaawal (Saul), and raah (see) that he was very bahal (troubled), and amar (spoke) to him, "Behold, your handmaid has shamai (hearken / hear) to your qawal (sound / voice), and I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) my napash (soul) in my kap (hand), and have shamai (hearken / hear) to your dabar (word / matter) which you dabar (word / matter) to me.

Now therefore, please shamai (hearken / hear) also to the qawal (sound / voice) of your handmaid, and let me shawam (place / establish / appoint) a path (morsel) of lacham (bread) panayam (face) you; and akal (eat), that you may have kach (strength / mighty / power), when you yalak (go) on your darak (way)."

But he maan (refused), and amar (spoke), I will not akal (eat). But his ibad (servant), together with the ayashah (woman / wife), constrained him; and he shamai (hearken / hear) to their qawal (sound / voice). So he qawam (rise up) from the aratz (Earth/land), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the matah (bed).

The ayashah (woman / wife) had a fattened igal (calf) in the bayath (house). She hurried and zabach (killed) it; and she laqach (take / seize) qamach (flour), and lawash (kneaded) it, and apah (baked) unleavened matzah (bread) of it.
She nagash (brought) it panayam (face) Shaawal (Saul), and panayam (face) his ibad (servant); and they akal (eat). Then they qawam (rise up) up, and yalak (went) away that layal (night).

Now the Palashathay (Philistines) qabatz (gathered) together all their machanah (armies) to Apaq (Aphek): and the Yashar-Al (Israelites) chanah (encamped) by the spring which is in Yazaraial (Jezreel).

The saranay (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines) ibar (pass over/through) on by maawath (hundreds), and by alapayam (thousands); and Dawad (David) and his ibarayam (men) ibar (pass over/through) on in the rear with Akayash (Achish).

Then the sharay (princes) of the Palashathay (Philistines) amar (spoke), "What about these ibarayam (hebrews)?" Akayash (Achish) amar (spoke) to the sharay (princes) of the Palashathay (Philistines), "Isn't this Dawad (David), the ibad (servant) of Shaawal (Saul) the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), who has been with me these yamayam (days), or rather these shanayam (years), and I matzaa (have) found no maawamah (fault) in him yawam (day) he napal (fall / be cast down) away to this yawam (day)?"

But the sharay (princes) of the Palashathay (Philistines) were qatzap (angry) with him; and the sharay (princes) of the Palashathay (Philistines) amar (spoke) to him, "shawab (turn back / repent) the ayash (man / husband) shawab (turn back / repent), that he may shawab (turn back / repent) back to his maqawam (place) where you paqad (visit) appointed him, and yarad (let) him not go down with us to malachamah (battle), lest in the malachamah (battle) he become an shatan (adversary) to us. For with what should this fellow ratzah (reconcile) himself to his Adawan? Should it not be with the raashay (heads) of these anashayam (men)?

Is not this Dawad (David), of whom they inah (answer / respond) one to another in machalawath (dances), amar (spoke), ‘Shaawal (Saul) has nakah (slain) his alap (thousands), Dawad (David) his rababah (ten) thousands?'"

Then Akayash (Achish) qaraa (called) Dawad (David), and amar (spoke) to him, "As Yahawah chay (life), you have been yashar (upright), and your yatzaa (go out / come out) out and your bawaa (come) in with me in the machanah (army) is tawab (good / proper function) in my iyan (eye); for I matzaa (have) not found rai (evil) in you since the yawam (day) of your bawaa (come) to me to this yawam (day). Nevertheless, the saranayam (lords) don't favor you.
Therefore now shawab (turn back / repent), and yalak (go) in shalawam (peace / safety), that you not rai (displease) the saranay (lords) of the Palashathay (Philistines)."

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Akayash (Achish), "But what ishah (make) I done? What matzaa (have) you found in your ibad (servant) so yawam (day) as I have been panayam (face) you to this yawam (day), that I may not bawaa (come) and lacham (fight) against the ayabay (enemies) of my Adawan the malak (king)?"

Akayash (Achish) inah (answer / respond) Dawad (David), "I yadai (know) that you are tawab (good / proper function) in my iyan (eye), as an malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Alahayam. Notwithstanding the sharay (princes) of the Palashathay (Philistines) have amar (spoke), ‘He shall not ilah (go up / offer) up with us to the malachamah (battle).'

Therefore now shakam (rise) up early in the baqar (morning) with the ibaday (servants) of your Adawan who bawaa (come) come with you; and as soon as you are up shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and have awar (light), depart."

So Dawad (David) shakam (rose) up early, he and his ayash (man / husband), to depart in the baqar (morning), to shawab (turn back / repent) into the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines). The Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up to Yazaraial (Jezreel).

It happened, when Dawad (David) and his ayash (man / husband) bawaa (come) come to Tzaqalag (Ziklag) on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), that the Imalaqay (Amalekites) had pashat (made) a raid on the nagab (south), and on Tzaqalag (Ziklag), and had nakah (struck) Tzaqalag (Ziklag), and sharap (burned) it with ash (fire),

And had shabah (taken) captive the nashayam (women) and all who were therein, both qatan (small / young / least) and gadawal (very great/important/mighty). They didn't mawath (death) any, but nahag (carried) them off, and yalak (went) their darak (way).

When Dawad (David) and his ayash (man / husband) bawaa (come) to the iyar (city), behold, it was sharap (burned) with ash (fire); and their wives, and their ban (son), and their banath (daughter), were shabah (taken) captive.

Then Dawad (David) and the im (nation / people) who were with him nashaa (lift) up their qawal (sound / voice) and bakah (wept), until they had no more kach (strength / mighty / power) to bakah (weep).

Dawad (David's) shanayam (two) wives were shabah (taken) captive, Achayanaim (Ahinoam) the yazaraialayath (jezreelitess), and Abayagayal (Abigail) the ayashah (woman / wife) of Nabal (Nabal) the karamalay (carmelite).

Dawad (David) was maad (greatly) yatzar (distressed); for the im (nation / people) amar (spoke) of saqal (stoning) him, because the napash (soul) of all the im (nation / people) was grieved, every ayash (man / husband) for his ban (son) and for his banath (daughter): but Dawad (David) chazaq (strengthened) himself in Yahawah his Alahayam.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahan (priest), the ban (son) of Achayamalak (Ahimelech), "Please nagash (bring) me here the apawad (ephod)." Abayathar (Abiathar) nagash (brought) the apawad (ephod) to Dawad (David).

Dawad (David) inquired of Yahawah, amar (spoke), "If I radap (pursue) achar (other) this gadawad (troop), shall I nashag (overtake) them?" He amar (spoke) him, "radap (pursue); for you shall nashag (surely) nashag (overtake) them, and shall natzal (without) fail natzal (recover) all."

So Dawad (David) yalak (went), he and the shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) who were with him, and bawaa (come) to the nachal (stream / river) Bashawar (Besor), where those who were yathar (left) behind imad (stayed).

But Dawad (David) radap (pursued), he and arabai (four) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband); for two maah (hundred) imad (stayed) behind, who were so pagar (faint) that they couldn't ibar (pass over/through) over the nachal (stream / river) Bashawar (Besor).

They matzaa (found) an Egyptian in the shadah (field), and laqach (take / seize) him to Dawad (David), and nathan (give) him lacham (bread), and he akal (eat); and they gave him mayam (Waters) to shaqah (drink).

They nathan (give) him a palach (piece) of a dabalah (fig cake) of figs, and shanayam (two) clusters of tzamaqayam (raisins). When he had akal (eat), his rawach (spirit / wind) shawab (turn back / repent) again to him; for he had akal (eat) no lacham (bread), nor shathah (drinks) any mayam (Waters), shalawash (three) yamayam (days) and shalawash (three) layalawath (nights).

Dawad (David) asked him, "To whom do you belong? Where are you from?" He amar (spoke), "I am a nair (young) man of Matzaray (Egypt), ibad (servant) to an Amalekite; and my adawan (master / lord) izab (left) me, because shalawash (three) yawam (day) ago I chalah (afflict) sick.

We pashat (made) a raid on the nagab (south) of the Karathay (Cherethites), and on that which belongs to Yahawadah (Judah), and on the nagab (south) of Kalab (Caleb); and we sharap (burned) Tzaqalag (Ziklag) with ash (fire)."

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to him, "Will you yarad (bring) me down to this gadawad (troop)?" He amar (spoke), "shabai (swear / take oath) to me by Alahayam that you will neither mawath (death) me, am (mother) sagar (deliver) me up into the yad (hand) of my adawan (master / lord), and I will yarad (bring) you down to this gadawad (troop)."

When he had yarad (brought) him down, behold, they were natash (spread) around over all the aratz (Earth/land), akal (eat), shathah (drinks), and chagag (dancing), because of all the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shalal (spoil) that they had laqach (take / seize) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Yahawadah (Judah).

Dawad (David) nakah (struck) them from the nashap (twilight) even to the irab (evening) of the next macharath (day). Not a ayash (man / husband) of them malat (escaped) from there, except arabai (four) maah (hundred) nair (young) ayash (man / husband), who rakab (rode) on gamalayam (camels) and nawas (fled).
Dawad (David) natzal (recovered) all that the Imalaq (Amalekites) had laqach (take / seize); and Dawad (David) natzal (rescued) his shanayam (two) wives.

There was nothing idar (lacking) to them, man (from) qatan (small / young / least) nor gadawal (very great/important/mighty), neither banayam (sons) nor banawath (daughters), neither shalal (spoil), nor anything that they had laqach (take / seize) to them. Dawad (David) laqach (take / seize) back all.

Dawad (David) laqach (take / seize) all the tzaan (flocks) and the baqar (morning), which they nahag (drove) panayam (face) hawaa (which/who/that is) other livestock, and amar (spoke), "This is Dawad (David's) shalal (spoil)."

Dawad (David) bawaa (come) to the two maah (hundred) anashayam (men), who were so pagar (faint) that they could not yalak (follow) Dawad (David), whom also they had yashab (inhabit/dwell) to stay at the nachal (stream / river) Bashawar (Besor); and they yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to qaraa (called) Dawad (David), and to qaraa (called) the im (nation / people) who were with him. When Dawad (David) nagash (came) near to the im (nation / people), he shaal (greeted) them.

Then all the rai (wicked) anashayam (men) and base anashayam (fellows), of those who halak (move) with Dawad (David), amar (spoke) and amar (spoke), "Because they didn't go with us, we will not nathan (give) them anything of the shalal (spoil) that we have natzal (recovered), except to every ayash (man / husband) his ayashah (woman / wife) and his ban (son), that he may nahag (lead) them away, and depart."

Then Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "You shall not ishah (make) so, my ach (brother/kinsman), with that which Yahawah nathan (give) given to us, who has shamar (keep/guard) us, and nathan (give) the gadawad (troop) that bawaa (come) against us into our yad (hand).

Who will shamai (hearken / hear) to you in this dabar (word / matter)? For as his share is who yarad (goes) down to the malachamah (battle), so shall his share be who yashab (inhabit/dwell) by the baggage: they shall share yachad (alike)."
It was so from that yawam (day) mail (top/above), that he shawam (place / establish / appoint) it a chaq (statute) and an mashapat (ordinance) for Yashar-Al (Israel) to this yawam (day).

When Dawad (David) bawaa (come) to Tzaqalag (Ziklag), he shalach (send) of the shalal (spoil) to the zaqanay (elders) of Yahawadah (Judah), even to his rai (neigbor/another person), amar (spoke), "Behold, a barakah (present) for you of the shalal (spoil) of the ayabay (enemies) of Yahawah."
He sent it to those who were in Bayath-Al (Bethel), and to those who were in Ramawath (Ramoth) of the ramawath (south), and to those who were in Yathayar (Jattir),
And to those who were in Irawair (Aroer), and to those who were in Shapamawath (Siphmoth), and to those who were in Ashathamai (Eshtemoa),
And to those who were in Rakal (Racal), and to those who were in the iray (cities) of the Yarachamaalay (Jerahmeelites), and to those who were in the iray (cities) of the Qayanay (Kenites),
And to those who were in Charamah (Hormah), and to those who were in Kawaraishan (Borashan), and to those who were in Ithak (Athach),
And to those who were in Chabarawan (Hebron), and to all the maqamawath (places) where Dawad (David) himself and his halak (move) used to stay.

Now the Palashathay (Philistines) lacham (fought) against Yashar-Al (Israel): and the anashay (men) of Yashar-Al (Israel) nawas (fled) from panayam (face) the Palashathay (Philistines), and napal (fall / be cast down) down chalal (slain) on har (mountain) Galabai (Gilboa).

The Palashathay (Philistines) dabaq (followed) hard on Shaawal (Saul) and on his banay (sons); and the Palashathay (Philistines) nakah (killed) Yahawanathan (Jonathan), and Abayanadab (Abinadab), and Malakayashawai (Malchishua), the banay (sons) of Shaawal (Saul).
The malachamah (battle) went hard against Shaawal (Saul), and the archers overtook him; and he was maad (greatly) distressed by reason of the archers.

Then Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to his armor bearer, "shalap (draw) your charab (sword), and thrust me daqar (through) with it, lest these iral (uncircumcised) bawaa (come) and thrust me daqar (through), and ilal (abuse) me!" But his armor bearer would not; for he was terrified. Therefore Shaawal (Saul) laqach (take / seize) his charab (sword), and napal (fall / be cast down) on it.
When his armor bearer raah (see) that Shaawal (Saul) was mawath (death), he likewise napal (fall / be cast down) on his charab (sword), and mawath (death) with him.
So Shaawal (Saul) mawath (death), and his shalawash (three) ban (son), and his armor bearer, and all his mawath (death), that same yawam (day) yachad (together).

When the anashay (men) of Yashar-Al (Israel) who were on the other ibar (side) of the imaq (valley), and those who were ibar (beyond) the Yaradan (Jordan), raah (see) that the anashay (men) of Yashar-Al (Israel) nawas (fled), and that Shaawal (Saul) and his ban (son) were mawath (death), they forsook the irayam (cities), and nawas (fled); and the Palashathay (Philistines) bawaa (come) and lived in them.

It happened on the next macharath (day), when the Palashathay (Philistines) bawaa (come) to pashat (strip) the chalal (slain), that they matzaa (found) Shaawal (Saul) and his shalawash (three) ban (son) napal (fall / be cast down) on har (mountain) Galabai (Gilboa).

They karath (cut) off his raash (head), and stripped off his armor, and shalach (send) into the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines) all around, to bashar (carry) the news to the bayath (house) of their itzab (idols), and to the im (nation / people).

They shawam (place / establish / appoint) his armor in the bayath (house) of the Ishatharawath (Ashtaroth); and they thaqai (blow / sound alarm) his gawayah (corpse) to the chawamah (wall) of Bayath-Shaan (Beth Shan).
When the yashabay (inhabitants) of Yabash (Jabesh Gilead) shamai (hearken / hear) concerning him that which the Palashathay (Philistines) ishah (make) done to Shaawal (Saul),

All the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ayash (man / husband) qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) all layal (night), and laqach (take / seize) the gawayah (corpse) of Shaawal (Saul) and the gawayath (bodies) of his ban (son) from the chawamah (wall) of Bayath-Shaan (Beth Shan); and they bawaa (come) to Yabash (Jabesh), and burnt them there.
They laqach (take / seize) their itzam (bones), and qabar (bury) them under the tamarisk ashal (tree) in Yabash (Jabesh), and tzawam (fasted) shabai (seven) yamayam (days).

It happened achar (other) the mawath (death) of Shaawal (Saul), when Dawad (David) was shawab (turn back / repent) from the nakah (slaughter) of the Imalaq (Amalekites), and Dawad (David) had stayed shanayam (two) yamayam (days) in Tzaqalag (Ziklag);

It happened on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), that behold, a ayash (man / husband) bawaa (come) out of the machanah (camp) from Shaawal (Saul), with his clothes qarai (torn), and adamah (earth) on his raash (head): and so it was, when he bawaa (come) to Dawad (David), that he napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land), and showed respect.
Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to him, "Where do you bawaa (come) from?" He amar (spoke) to him, "I have malat (escaped) out of the machanah (camp) of Yashar-Al (Israel)."

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to him, "mah (how) dabar (word / matter) it go? Please nagad (tell) me." He amar (spoke), "The im (nation / people) have nawas (fled) from the malachamah (battle), and many of the im (nation / people) also napal (fall / be cast down) fallen and are mawath (death); and Shaawal (Saul) and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son) are mawath (death) also."
Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to the nair (young) man who amar (spoke) him, "How do you yadai (know) that Shaawal (Saul) and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son) are mawath (death)?"

The nair (young) man who nagad (told) him said, "As I qarah (happened) by qaraa (called) on har (mountain) Galabai (Gilboa), behold, Shaawal (Saul) was shain (leaning) on his chanayath (spear); and behold, the rakab (chariots) and the horsemen dabaq (followed) hard after him.
When he panah (turn) achar (other) him, he saw me, and qaraa (called) to me. I amar (spoke), ‘Here I am.'
He amar (spoke) to me, ‘Who are you?' I amar (spoke) him, ‘I am an Imalaqay (Amalekite).'
He amar (spoke) to me, ‘Please imad (stand) beside me, and mawath (death) me; for shabatz (anguish) achaz (has) taken hold of me, because my napash (soul) is yet whole in me.'

So I imad (stood) beside him, and mawath (death) him, because I was yadai (sure) that he could not chayah (live) achar (other) that he napal (fall / be cast down) fallen. I laqach (take / seize) the nazar (crown / consecrate) that was on his raash (head), and the atzaidah (bracelet) that was on his zarawai (arm), and bawaa (come) brought them here to my Adawan."
Then Dawad (David) chazaq (took) hold on his clothes, and qarai (tore) them; and likewise all the chazaq (men) who were with him.

They sapad (mourned), and bakah (wept), and tzawam (fasted) until irab (evening), for Shaawal (Saul), and for Yahawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son), and for the im (nation / people) of Yahawah, and for the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel); because they were napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword).
Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to the nair (young) man who amar (spoke) him, "Where are you from?" He amar (spoke), "I am the ban (son) of a foreigner, an Imalaqay (Amalekite)."
Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to him, "How were you not yaraa (fear / be afraid) to shalach (send) forth your yad (hand) to shachath (destroy) Yahawah mashayach (anointed one)?"
Dawad (David) qaraa (called) achad (one) of the nair (young) men, and amar (spoke), "nagash (go) near, and pagai (fall) on him." He nakah (struck) him, so that he mawath (death).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to him, "Your dam (blood) be on your raash (head); for your pah (mouth) has inah (answer / respond) amar (spoke) you, saying, ‘I have mawath (death) Yahawah mashayach (anointed one).'"
