Dawad (David) qawan (lamented) with this qayanah (lamentation) over Shaawal (Saul) and over Yahawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son)

(And he commanded them to lamad (teach / instruct) the banay (children) of Yahawadah (Judah) the song of the qashath (bow): behold, it is kathab (write) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of Jashar):
"Your glory, Yashar-Al (Israel), is chalal (slain) on your bamah (high) places! How the gabawar (mighty) napal (fall / be cast down) fallen!

Don't nagad (tell) it in gath (gath). Don't bashar (publish) it in the chawatzath (streets) of Ashaqalawan (Ashkelon), lest the banawath (daughters) of the Palashathay (Philistines) shamach (rejoice), lest the banawath (daughters) of the iral (uncircumcised) ilaz (triumph).

You haray (mountains) of Galabai (Gilboa), let there be no tal (dew) nor matar (rain) on you, neither shaday (fields) of tharawamath (offerings); For there the magan (shield) of the gabawar (mighty) was gail (vilely) cast away, The magan (shield) of Shaawal (Saul) was not mashayach (anointed one) with shaman (oil).

From the dam (blood) of the chalal (slain), from the chalab (fat) of the gabawar (mighty), Yahawanathan (Jonathan's) qashath (bow) didn't shawag (turn) achawar (back). Shaawal (Saul's) charab (sword) didn't shawab (turn back / repent) rayaqam (empty).

Shaawal (Saul) and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) were lovely and naiyam (pleasant) in their chay (life). In their mawath (death), they were not parad (divided). They were qalal (swifter) than nasharayam (eagles). They were gabar (stronger) than arayawath (lions).

You banawath (daughters) of Yashar-Al (Israel), bakah (weep) over Shaawal (Saul), who labash (clothed) you in shanay (second) delicately, who ilah (go up / offer) iday (ornament / adornment) of zahab (gold) on your labawash (clothing).
How are the gabawar (mighty) napal (fall / be cast down) in the thawak (midst) of the malachamah (battle)! Yahawanathan (Jonathan) is chalal (slain) on your bamah (high) places.

I am tzarar (distressed) for you, my ach (brother/kinsman) Yahawanathan (Jonathan). You have been very naim (pleasant) to me. Your ahabah (love) to me was palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous), passing the ahabah (love) of nashayam (women).
How are the gabawar (mighty) napal (fall / be cast down), and the kalay (weapons) of malachamah (war) abad (destroy / perish)!"

It happened achar (other) this, that Dawad (David) inquired of Yahawah, amar (spoke), "Shall I ilah (go up / offer) up into any of the iray (cities) of Yahawadah (Judah)?" Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, "ilah (go up / offer) up." Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "Where shall I ilah (go up / offer) up?" He amar (spoke), "To Chabarawan (Hebron)."

So Dawad (David) ilah (go up / offer) up there, and his shanayam (two) wives also, Achayanaim (Ahinoam) the yazaraialayath (jezreelitess), and Abayagayal (Abigail) the ayashah (woman / wife) of Nabal (Nabal) the karamalay (carmelite).
Dawad (David) ilah (go up / offer) up his ayash (man / husband) who were with him, every ayash (man / husband) with his bayath (house). They lived in the iray (cities) of Chabarawan (Hebron).

The anashay (men) of Yahawadah (Judah) bawaa (come), and there they mashach (anointed) Dawad (David) malak (king) over the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah). They nagad (told) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), "The anashay (men) of Yabash (Jabesh Gilead) were those who qabar (bury) Shaawal (Saul)."

Dawad (David) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to the anashay (men) of Yabash (Jabesh Gilead), and amar (spoke) to them, "barak (blessed) are you by Yahawah, that you ishah (make) shown this chasad (grace) to your Adawan, even to Shaawal (Saul), and have qabar (bury) him.
Now may Yahawah show loving chasad (grace) and amath (truth) to you. I also will reward you for this tawab (good / proper function), because you ishah (make) done this thing.

Now therefore let your yad (hand) be chazaq (strong), and be ban (son); for Shaawal (Saul) your Adawan is mawath (death), and also the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) have mashach (anointed) me malak (king) over them."

Now Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner), shar (prince / ruler) of Shaawal (Saul's) tzabaa (troop), had laqach (take / seize) Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth) the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul), and ibar (pass over/through) him over to Machanayam (Mahanaim);

And he made him malak (king) over Galaid (Gilead), and over the ashawaray (ashurites), and over Yazaraial (Jezreel), and over Aparayam (Ephraim), and over Banayamayan (Benjamin), and over all Yashar-Al (Israel).

Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth), Shaawal (Saul's) ban (son), was arabaiyam (forty) shanayam (years) ban (son) when he began to malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel), and he malak (king) shanayam (two) shanayam (years). But the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) achar (other) Dawad (David).
The masapar (time) that Dawad (David) was malak (king) in Chabarawan (Hebron) over the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) was shabai (seven) shanayam (years) and shash (six) chadashayam (months).

Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner), and the ibaday (servants) of Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth) the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul), yatzaa (go out / come out) out from Machanayam (Mahanaim) to Gabaiwan (Gibeon).

Yawaab (Joab) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah), and the ibaday (servants) of Dawad (David), yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and pagash (met) them by the barakah (pool) of Gabaiwan (Gibeon); and they yashab (inhabit/dwell) down, the one on the one side of the barakah (pool), and the other on the other side of the barakah (pool).
Abanar (Abner) amar (spoke) to Yawaab (Joab), "Please let the nair (young) men qawam (rise up) and shachaq (play) panayam (face) us!" Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke), "Let them qawam (rise up)!"

Then they qawam (rise up) and ibar (pass over/through) over by masapar (number): shanayam (two) for Banayamayan (Benjamin), and for Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth) the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul), and shanayam (two) of the ibaday (servants) of Dawad (David).

They ayash (man / husband) chazaq (caught) his opponent by the raash (head), and thrust his charab (sword) in his rai (neigbor/another person) tzad (side); so they napal (fall / be cast down) down yachad (together): therefore that maqawam (place) was qaraa (called) Chalaqathahatzarayam (Helkath Hazzurim), which is in Gabaiwan (Gibeon).
The malachamah (battle) was very severe that yawam (day): and Abanar (Abner) was nagap (beaten), and the anashay (men) of Yashar-Al (Israel), panayam (face) the ibaday (servants) of Dawad (David).

The shalawash (three) banay (sons) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah) were there, Yawaab (Joab), and Abayashay (Abishai), and Ishahaal (Asahel): and Ishahaal (Asahel) was as qal (light) of ragal (feet / foot) as a shadah (wild) gazelle.

Ishahaal (Asahel) radap (pursued) achar (other) Abanar (Abner); and in yalak (going) he didn't natah (turn) to the right yamayan (right hand) nor to the shamaawal (left hand) from achar (other) Abanar (Abner).
Then Abanar (Abner) panah (turn) achar (other) him, and amar (spoke), "Is it you, Ishahaal (Asahel)?" He amar (spoke), "It is I."

Abanar (Abner) amar (spoke) to him, "natah (turn) aside to your right yamayan (right hand) or to your shamaawal (left hand), and grab achad (one) of the nair (young) men, and laqach (take / seize) his armor." But Ishahaal (Asahel) would not sawar (turn) aside from achar (other) him.

Abanar (Abner) amar (spoke) again to Ishahaal (Asahel), "sawar (turn) aside from achar (other) me. Why should I nakah (strike) you to the aratz (Earth/land)? How then should I nashaa (lift) up my panayam (face) to Yawaab (Joab) your ach (brother/kinsman)?"

However he maan (refused) to sawar (turn) aside. Therefore Abanar (Abner) with the achar (other) end of the chanayath (spear) nakah (struck) him in the body, so that the chanayath (spear) yatzaa (go out / come out) out achar (other) him; and he napal (fall / be cast down) down there, and mawath (death) in the same thachath (under). It happened, that as many as bawaa (come) to the maqawam (place) where Ishahaal (Asahel) napal (fall / be cast down) down and mawath (death) imad (stood) still.

But Yawaab (Joab) and Abayashay (Abishai) radap (pursued) achar (other) Abanar (Abner): and the shamash (sun) bawaa (come) down when they bawaa (come) come to the gabaih (hill) of Amah (Ammah), that lies panayam (face) Gayach (Giah) by the darak (way) of the madabar (wilderness) of Gabaiwan (Gibeon).

The banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) qabatz (gathered) themselves together achar (other) Abanar (Abner), and became achad (one) band, and imad (stood) on the raash (head) of a gabaih (hill).

Then Abanar (Abner) qaraa (called) to Yawaab (Joab), and amar (spoke), "Shall the charab (sword) akal (eat) natzach (forever)? Don't you yadai (know) that it will be bitterness in the acharawan (latter) end? How long shall it be then, before you ask the im (nation / people) to shawab (turn back / repent) from achar (other) their ach (brother/kinsman)?"

Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke), "As Alahayam chay (life), if you lawalaa (had) not dabar (word / matter), surely then in the baqar (morning) the im (nation / people) would have ilah (go up / offer) away, and not ayash (man / husband) achar (other) his ach (brother/kinsman)."

So Yawaab (Joab) thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn); and all the im (nation / people) imad (stood) still, and radap (pursued) achar (other) Yashar-Al (Israel) no more, neither lacham (fought) they any more.

Abanar (Abner) and his ayash (man / husband) halak (move) all that layal (night) through the irabah (arabah); and they ibar (pass over/through) over the Yaradan (Jordan), and yalak (went) through all Batharawan (Bithron), and bawaa (come) to Machanayam (Mahanaim).

Yawaab (Joab) shawab (turn back / repent) from achar (other) Abanar (Abner): and when he had qabatz (gathered) all the im (nation / people) qabatz (together), there paqad (visit) of Dawad (David's) ibaday (servants) nineteen ayash (man / husband) and Ishahaal (Asahel).

But the ibaday (servants) of Dawad (David) had nakah (struck) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), and of Abanar (Abner's) anashay (men), so that shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty) anashay (men) mawath (death).

They nashaa (lift) up Ishahaal (Asahel), and qabar (bury) him in the tomb of his ab (father), which was in Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem). Yawaab (Joab) and his ayash (man / husband) yalak (went) all layal (night), and the awar (light) broke on them at Chabarawan (Hebron).

Now there was arak (long) malachamah (war) between the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul) and the bayath (house) of Dawad (David): and Dawad (David) halak (move) chazaq (stronger) and chazaq (stronger), but the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul) halak (move) dal (weaker) and dal (weaker).
To Dawad (David) were banayam (sons) yalad (birth / begot) in Chabarawan (Hebron): and his bakawar (firstborn) was Amanawan (Amnon), of Achayanaim (Ahinoam) the yazaraialayath (jezreelitess);

And his mashanah (second), Kalaab (Chileab), of Abayagayal (Abigail) the ayashah (woman / wife) of Nabal (Nabal) the karamalay (carmelite); and the shalayashay (third), Abayashalawam (Absalom) the ban (son) of Maikah (Maacah) the banath (daughter) of Thalamay (Talmai) malak (king) of Gashawar (Geshur);
And the rabayaiy (fourth), Adanayah (Adonijah) the ban (son) of Chagayath (Haggith); and the chamayashay (fifth), Shapatayah (Shephatiah) the ban (son) of Abayatal (Abital);
And the shashay (sixth), Yatharaim (Ithream), of Igalah (Eglah), Dawad (David's) ayashah (woman / wife). These were yalad (birth / begot) to Dawad (David) in Chabarawan (Hebron).

It happened, while there was malachamah (war) between the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul) and the bayath (house) of Dawad (David), that Abanar (Abner) chazaq (made) himself strong in the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul).

Now Shaawal (Saul) had a payalagash (concubine), whose sham (name) was Ratzapah (Rizpah), the banath (daughter) of Ayah (Aiah): and Ishbosheth amar (spoke) to Abanar (Abner), "Why bawaa (come) you gone in to my ab (father) payalagash (concubine)?"

Then was Abanar (Abner) very charah (hot with anger) for the dabaray (words) of Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth), and amar (spoke), "Am I a kalab (dog's) raash (head) that belongs to Yahawadah (Judah)? Today I show chasad (grace) to the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul) your ab (father), to his ach (brother/kinsman), and to his marai (friends), and matzaa (have) not delivered you into the yad (hand) of Dawad (David); and yet you paqad (visit) me this yawam (day) with a iwan (guilt/iniquity) concerning this ayashah (woman / wife)!
Alahayam ishah (make) so to Abanar (Abner), and more also, if, as Yahawah has shabai (swear / take oath) to Dawad (David), I don't ishah (make) even so to him;

To transfer the mamalakah (kingdom) from the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul), and to qawam (rise up) up the kasaa (throne) of Dawad (David) over Yashar-Al (Israel) and over Yahawadah (Judah), from Dan (Dan) even to Baar-Shabai (Beersheba)."
He yakal (could) not shawab (turn back / repent) Abanar (Abner) another dabar (word / matter), because he yaraa (fear / be afraid) him.

Abanar (Abner) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to Dawad (David) on his behalf, amar (spoke), "Whose is the aratz (Earth/land)?" And amar (spoke), "karath (cut) your alliance with me, and behold, my yad (hand) shall be with you, to bring all Yashar-Al (Israel) around to you."

He amar (spoke), "tawab (good / proper function); I will karath (cut) a treaty with you; but achad (one) thing I shaal (require) of you. That is, you shall not raah (see) my panayam (face), unless you panayam (face) bawaa (come) Mayakal (Michal), Shaawal (Saul's) banath (daughter), when you bawaa (come) to raah (see) my panayam (face)."

Dawad (David) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth), Shaawal (Saul's) ban (son), amar (spoke), "nathan (give) me my ayashah (woman / wife) Mayakal (Michal), whom I pledged to be married to me for one maah (hundred) iralawath (foreskins) of the Palashathay (Philistines)."
Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth) shalach (send), and laqach (take / seize) her from her ayash (man / husband), even from Palatayaal (Paltiel) the ban (son) of Lawash (Laish).

Her ayash (man / husband) yalak (went) with her, weeping as he yalak (went), and achar (other) her to Bacharayam (Bahurim). Then Abanar (Abner) amar (spoke) to him, "yalak (go)! Shawab (turn back / repent)!" And he shawab (turn back / repent).

Abanar (Abner) hayah (came to pass) communication with the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel), amar (spoke), "In thamawal (times) shalashawam (past), you baqash (sought) for Dawad (David) to be malak (king) over you.

Now then ishah (make) it; for Yahawah has amar (spoke) of Dawad (David), amar (spoke), ‘By the yad (hand) of my ibad (servant) Dawad (David), I will yashai (salvation) my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel) out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and out of the yad (hand) of all their ayab (enemy).'"

Abanar (Abner) also dabar (word / matter) in the azanay (ears) of Banayamayan (Benjamin): and Abanar (Abner) yalak (went) also to dabar (word / matter) in the azanay (ears) of Dawad (David) in Chabarawan (Hebron) all that seemed tawab (good / proper function) to Yashar-Al (Israel), and to the whole bayath (house) of Banayamayan (Benjamin).

So Abanar (Abner) bawaa (come) to Dawad (David) to Chabarawan (Hebron), and isharayam (twenty) anashayam (men) with him. Dawad (David) ishah (make) Abanar (Abner) and the anashayam (men) who were with him a mashathah (feast).

Abanar (Abner) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "I will qawam (rise up) and yalak (go), and will qabatz (gather) all Yashar-Al (Israel) to my Adawan the malak (king), that they may karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with you, and that you may malak (king) over all that your napash (soul) awah (desires)." Dawad (David) shalach (send) Abanar (Abner) shalach (send); and he yalak (went) in shalawam (peace / safety).

Behold, the ibaday (servants) of Dawad (David) and Yawaab (Joab) bawaa (come) from a foray, and bawaa (come) in a rab (great) shalal (spoil) with them: but Abanar (Abner) was not with Dawad (David) in Chabarawan (Hebron); for he had shalach (send) him away, and he was yalak (gone) in shalawam (peace / safety).

When Yawaab (Joab) and all the tzabaa (troop) who was with him bawaa (come) come, they nagad (told) Yawaab (Joab), amar (spoke), Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner) bawaa (come) to the malak (king), and he has shalach (send) him away, and he is yalak (gone) in shalawam (peace / safety).

Then Yawaab (Joab) bawaa (come) to the malak (king), and amar (spoke), "What ishah (make) you done? Behold, Abanar (Abner) bawaa (come) to you. Why is it that you have shalach (send) him away, and he is halak (move) yalak (gone)?

You yadai (know) Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner), that he bawaa (come) to pathah (deceive) you, and to yadai (know) your mawatzaa (going) out and your mawabaa (coming) in, and to yadai (know) all that you ishah (make)."

When Yawaab (Joab) yatzaa (go out / come out) come out from Dawad (David), he shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) achar (other) Abanar (Abner), and they shawab (turn back / repent) him back from the bawar (well) of Sarah (Sirah); but Dawad (David) didn't yadai (know) it.

When Abanar (Abner) was shawab (turn back / repent) to Chabarawan (Hebron), Yawaab (Joab) natah (took) him aside into the midst of the shair (gate) to dabar (word / matter) with him shalay (quietly), and nakah (struck) him there in the body, so that he mawath (death), for the dam (blood) of Ishahaal (Asahel) his ach (brother/kinsman).

Afterward, when Dawad (David) shamai (hearken / hear) it, he amar (spoke), "I and my mamalakah (kingdom) are naqay (guiltless) before Yahawah iwalam (forever) of the dam (blood) of Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner).

Let it chawal (fall) on the raash (head) of Yawaab (Joab), and on all his ab (father) bayath (house). Let there not karath (cut) from the bayath (house) of Yawaab (Joab) one who zawab (flow) an issue, or who is a tzarai (leper), or who chazaq (leans) on a palak (staff), or who napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword), or who chasar (lacks) lacham (bread)."

So Yawaab (Joab) and Abayashay (Abishai) his ach (brother/kinsman) harag (kill) Abanar (Abner), because he had harag (kill) their ach (brother/kinsman) Ishahaal (Asahel) at Gabaiwan (Gibeon) in the malachamah (battle).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Yawaab (Joab), and to all the im (nation / people) who were with him, qarai (tear) your clothes, and clothe yourselves with sackcloth, and sapad (mourn) panayam (face) Abanar (Abner). Malak (king) Dawad (David) halak (move) the matah (bier).

They qabar (bury) Abanar (Abner) in Chabarawan (Hebron): and the malak (king) nashaa (lift) up his qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept) at the qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) of Abanar (Abner); and all the im (nation / people) bakah (wept).
The malak (king) qawan (lamented) for Abanar (Abner), and amar (spoke), "Should Abanar (Abner) mawath (death) as a nabal (fool) mawath (death)?

Your yad (hand) were not asar (bound), nor your ragal (feet / foot) nagash (put) into nachashathayam (fetters). As a man napal (fall / be cast down) panayam (face) the banay (children) of iwal (iniquity), so you napal (fall / be cast down)." All the im (nation / people) bakah (wept) again over him.

Kal (every) the im (nation / people) bawaa (come) to cause Dawad (David) to barah (eat) lacham (bread) while it was yet yawam (day); but Dawad (David) shabai (swear / take oath), amar (spoke), "Alahayam ishah (make) so to me, and more also, if I taim (taste) lacham (bread), or anything else, until the shamash (sun) bawaa (come) down."
All the im (nation / people) nakar (took) notice of it, and it yatab (pleased) them; as whatever the malak (king) ishah (make) yatab (pleased) all the im (nation / people).
So all the im (nation / people) and all Yashar-Al (Israel) yadai (understood) that yawam (day) that it was not of the malak (king) to mawath (death) Abanar (Abner) the ban (son) of Nar (Ner).

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), "Don't you yadai (know) that there a shar (prince / ruler) and a great gadawal (very great/important/mighty) napal (fall / be cast down) fallen this yawam (day) in Yashar-Al (Israel)?

I am this yawam (day) rak (weak), though mashach (anointed) malak (king); and these anashayam (men) the banay (sons) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah) are too qashah (rough / hard) for me. May Yahawah shalam (reward) the evildoer according to his ishah (make)."

When Shaawal (Saul's) ban (son) shamai (hearken / hear) that Abanar (Abner) was mawath (death) in Chabarawan (Hebron), his yad (hand) became rapah (feeble), and all the Yashar-Al (Israelites) were bahal (troubled).

Shaawal (Saul's) ban (son) hayah (came to pass) shanayam (two) anashayam (men) who were sharay (captains) of gadawadayam (bands): the sham (name) of the achad (one) was Bainah (Baanah), and the sham (name) of the other Rakab (Rechab), the banay (sons) of Ramawan (Rimmon) the Baarathay (Beerothite), of the banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) (for Baarawath (Beeroth) also is chashab (reckoned) to Banayamayan (Benjamin):
And the Baarathay (Beerothites) barach (fled) to Gathayam (Gittaim), and have lived as foreigners there until this yawam (day)).

Now Yahawanathan (Jonathan), Shaawal (Saul's) ban (son), had a ban (son) who was nakah (lame) of his ragalayam (feet). He was chamash (five) shanayam (years) ban (son) when the shamawaih (news) bawaa (come) of Shaawal (Saul) and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) out of Yazaraial (Jezreel); and his aman (believe / have faith) nashaa (lift) him up, and nawas (fled): and it happened, as she made chapaz (haste) to nawas (flee), that he napal (fall / be cast down), and pasach (became) lame. His sham (name) was Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth).

The banay (sons) of Ramawan (Rimmon) the Baarathay (Beerothite), Rakab (Rechab) and Bainah (Baanah), yalak (went), and bawaa (come) about the cham (heat) of the yawam (day) to the bayath (house) of Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth), as he shakab (took) his mashakab (rest) at tzahar (noon).

They bawaa (come) there into the thawak (midst) of the bayath (house), as though they would have laqach (take / seize) chatah (wheat); and they nakah (struck) him in the body: and Rakab (Rechab) and Bainah (Baanah) his ach (brother/kinsman) malat (escaped).

Now when they bawaa (come) into the bayath (house), as he shakab (lay) on his matah (bed) in his bedroom, they nakah (struck) him, and nakah (killed) him, and sawar (beheaded) him, and laqach (take / seize) his raash (head), and yalak (went) by the darak (way) of the irabah (arabah) all layal (night).

They bawaa (come) the raash (head) of Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth) to Dawad (David) to Chabarawan (Hebron), and amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "Behold, the raash (head) of Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth), the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul), your ayab (enemy), who baqash (sought) your napash (soul)! Yahawah nathan (give) naqamah (avenged) my Adawan the malak (king) this yawam (day) of Shaawal (Saul), and of his zarai (seed)."

Dawad (David) inah (answer / respond) Rakab (Rechab) and Bainah (Baanah) his ach (brother/kinsman), the banay (sons) of Ramawan (Rimmon) the Baarathay (Beerothite), and amar (spoke) to them, "As Yahawah chay (life), who has padah (redeemed) my napash (soul) out of all tzarah (adversity),

When someone nagad (told) me, ‘Behold, Shaawal (Saul) is mawath (death),' iyan (eye) to have brought bashar (good) news, I took achaz (hold) of him, and harag (kill) him in Tzaqalag (Ziklag), which was the reward I nathan (give) him for his news.

How much more, when rashai (wicked) anashayam (men) have harag (kill) a tzadayaq (righteous) ayash (man / husband) in his own bayath (house) on his mashakab (bed), shall I not now baqash (require) his dam (blood) of your yad (hand), and bair (take) you away from the aratz (Earth/land)?"

Dawad (David) tzawah (commanded) his nair (young) men, and they harag (kill) them, and qatzatz (cut) off their yad (hand) and their ragal (feet / foot), and hanged them up beside the barakah (pool) in Chabarawan (Hebron). But they laqach (take / seize) the raash (head) of Ayashabashath (Ishbosheth), and qabar (bury) it in the qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) of Abanar (Abner) in Chabarawan (Hebron).
Then bawaa (come) all the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel) to Dawad (David) to Chabarawan (Hebron), and amar (spoke), amar (spoke), "Behold, we are your itzam (bone) and your bashar (flesh).

In athamawal (times) past, when Shaawal (Saul) was malak (king) over us, it was you who yatzaa (go out / come out) out and bawaa (come) in Yashar-Al (Israel). Yahawah amar (spoke) to you, ‘You shall be raih (shepherd) of my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel), and you shall be nagayad (prince) over Yashar-Al (Israel).'"

So all the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel) bawaa (come) to the malak (king) to Chabarawan (Hebron); and malak (king) Dawad (David) karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with them in Chabarawan (Hebron) panayam (face) Yahawah; and they mashach (anointed) Dawad (David) malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel).
Dawad (David) was shalawashayam (thirty) shanah (years) ban (son) when he began to malak (king), and he malak (king) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years).

In Chabarawan (Hebron) he malak (king) over Yahawadah (Judah) shabai (seven) shanayam (years) and shash (six) chadashayam (months); and in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) he malak (king) thirty-three shanayam (years) over all Yashar-Al (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah).

The malak (king) and his ayash (man / husband) yalak (went) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) against the Yabawasay (Jebusites), the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the aratz (Earth/land), who amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), amar (spoke), "Unless you sawar (take) away the iwar (blind) and the pasach (lame), you shall not bawaa (come) in here;" amar (spoke), "Dawad (David) can't bawaa (come) in here."
Nevertheless Dawad (David) lakad (took) the stronghold of Tzayawan (Zion); the same is the iyar (city) of Dawad (David).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) on that yawam (day), "Whoever nakah (strikes) the Yabawasay (Jebusites), let him nagai (get) up to the watercourse, and strike the pasach (lame) and the iwar (blind), who are shanaa (hate) by Dawad (David's) napash (soul)." Therefore they amar (spoke), "The iwar (blind) and the pasach (lame) can't bawaa (come) into the bayath (house)."
Dawad (David) lived in the stronghold, and qaraa (called) it the iyar (city) of Dawad (David). Dawad (David) banah (build) around from Malawaa (Millo) and inward.
Dawad (David) yalak (grew) greater and halak (move); for Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies), was with him.

Chayaram (Hiram) malak (king) of Tzar (Tyre) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to Dawad (David), and araz (cedar) itzay (trees), and charashay (carpenters), and qayar (masons); and they banah (build) Dawad (David) a bayath (house).

Dawad (David) yadai (perceived) that Yahawah had kawan (established) him malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel), and that he had nashaa (lift) his mamalakah (kingdom) for his im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel's) sake.

Dawad (David) laqach (take / seize) him more palagashayam (concubines) and wives out of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), achar (other) he bawaa (come) come from Chabarawan (Hebron); and there were yet banayam (sons) and banawath (daughters) yalad (birth / begot) to Dawad (David).
These are the shamawath (names) of those who were yalawad (born) to him in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem): Shamawai (Shammua), and Shawabab (Shobab), and Nathan (Nathan), and Shalamah (Solomon),
And Yabachar (Ibhar), and Alayashawai (Elishua), and Napag (Nepheg), and Yapayai (Japhia),
And Alayashamai (Elishama), and Alayadai (Eliada), and Alayapalat (Eliphelet).

When the Palashathay (Philistines) shamai (hearken / hear) that they had mashach (anointed) Dawad (David) malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel), all the Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up to baqash (seek) Dawad (David); and Dawad (David) shamai (hearken / hear) of it, and yarad (went) down to the stronghold.
Now the Palashathay (Philistines) bawaa (come) come and natash (spread) themselves in the imaq (valley) of Rapaa (Rephaim).

Dawad (David) inquired of Yahawah, amar (spoke), "Shall I ilah (go up / offer) up against the Palashathay (Philistines)? Will you nathan (give) them into my yad (hand)?" Yahawah amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "ilah (go up / offer) up; for I will certainly nathan (give) the Palashathay (Philistines) into your yad (hand)."

Dawad (David) bawaa (come) to Baal Perazim, and Dawad (David) nakah (struck) them there; and he amar (spoke), "Yahawah has paratz (broken) my ayab (enemy) panayam (face) me, like the paratz (breach) of mayam (Waters)." Therefore he qaraa (called) the sham (name) of that maqawam (place) Baal Perazim.
They izab (left) their itzab (images) there; and Dawad (David) and his ayash (man / husband) nashaa (lift) them away.
The Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up yet again, and natash (spread) themselves in the imaq (valley) of Rapaa (Rephaim).
When Dawad (David) inquired of Yahawah, he amar (spoke), "You shall not ilah (go up / offer) up. Circle around achar (other) them, and attack them over mawal (against) the bakaa (mulberry) trees.

It shall be, when you shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of marching in the raashay (tops) of the bakaa (mulberry) trees, that then you shall stir yourself up; for then Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) gone out panayam (face) you to nakah (strike) the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines)."
Dawad (David) ishah (make) so, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) him, and nakah (struck) the Palashathay (Philistines) from Gabai (Geba) until you bawaa (come) to Gazar (Gezer).
Dawad (David) again asap (gathered) together all the bachar (chosen) men of Yashar-Al (Israel), shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand).

Dawad (David) qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) with all the im (nation / people) who were with him, from Bailayayahawadah (Baale Judah), to ilah (go up / offer) up from there the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, which is qaraa (called) by the sham (name), even the sham (name) of Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) above the karawab (cherubim).

They rakab (set) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam on a chadash (new) igalah (cart), and nashaa (lift) it out of the bayath (house) of Abayanadab (Abinadab) that was in the Gabaih (hill): and Izaa (Uzzah) and Achayaw (Ahio), the banay (sons) of Abayanadab (Abinadab), nahag (drove) the chadash (new) igalah (cart).

They nashaa (lift) it out of the bayath (house) of Abayanadab (Abinadab), which was in the Gabaih (hill), with the arawan (ark) of Alahayam: and Achayaw (Ahio) halak (move) panayam (face) the arawan (ark).

Dawad (David) and all the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shachaq (played) panayam (face) Yahawah with all kinds of instruments made of barawash (fir) itz (wood), and with kanarawath (harps), and with stringed instruments, and with tambourines, and with castanets, and with tzalatzalayam (cymbals).
When they bawaa (come) to the garan (threshing) floor of Nakawan (Nacon), Izaa (Uzzah) shalach (send) for the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, and achaz (took) hold of it; for the cattle shamat (stumbled).

The ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah was charah (hot with anger) against Izaa (Uzzah); and Alahayam nakah (struck) him there for his shal (error); and there he mawath (death) by the arawan (ark) of Alahayam.
Dawad (David) was charah (hot with anger), because Yahawah had broken paratz (forth) on Izaa (Uzzah); and he qaraa (called) that maqawam (place) Perez Izaa (Uzzah), to this yawam (day).
Dawad (David) was yaraa (fear / be afraid) of Yahawah that yawam (day); and he amar (spoke), "How shall the arawan (ark) of Yahawah bawaa (come) to me?"

So Dawad (David) would not move the arawan (ark) of Yahawah to be with him in the iyar (city) of Dawad (David); but Dawad (David) natah (carried) it aside into the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom) the Gathay (Gittite).

The arawan (ark) of Yahawah yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom) the Gathay (Gittite) shalawash (three) chadashayam (months): and Yahawah barak (blessed) Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom), and all his bayath (house).

It was nagad (told) malak (king) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), "Yahawah has barak (blessed) the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom), and all that pertains to him, because of the arawan (ark) of Alahayam." Dawad (David) yalak (went) and ilah (go up / offer) up the arawan (ark) of Alahayam from the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom) into the iyar (city) of Dawad (David) with shamachah (joy).
It was so, that, when those who nashaa (lift) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah had tzaid (gone) shash (six) tzaidayam (paces), he zabach (sacrificed) an shawar (ox) and a fattened calf.
Dawad (David) karar (danced) panayam (face) Yahawah with all his iz (strength / might / refuge); and Dawad (David) was clothed in a bad (linen) apawad (ephod).

So Dawad (David) and all the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up the arawan (ark) of Yahawah with tharawaih (shouting), and with the qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn).

It was so, as the arawan (ark) of Yahawah bawaa (come) into the iyar (city) of Dawad (David), that Mayakal (Michal) the banath (daughter) of Shaawal (Saul) shaqap (looked) out at the chalawan (window), and raah (see) malak (king) Dawad (David) pazaz (leaping) and karar (dancing) panayam (face) Yahawah; and she bazah (despised) him in her lab (heart).

They bawaa (come) in the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, and yatzag (set) it in its maqawam (place), in the thawak (midst) of the ahal (tent) that Dawad (David) had natah (pitched) for it; and Dawad (David) ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilawath (offerings) and peace ilawath (offerings) panayam (face) Yahawah.

When Dawad (David) kalah (complete / finish) made an end of ilah (go up / offer) the burnt ilah (offering) and the shalam (peace) offerings, he barak (blessed) the im (nation / people) in the sham (name) of Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies).

He chalaq (gave) to all the im (nation / people), even among the whole multitude of Yashar-Al (Israel), both to ayash (man / husband) and ayashah (woman / wife), to everyone a portion of lacham (bread), dates, and raisins. So all the im (nation / people) departed everyone to his bayath (house).

Then Dawad (David) shawab (turn back / repent) to barak (blessed) his bayath (house). Mayakal (Michal) the banath (daughter) of Shaawal (Saul) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) Dawad (David), and amar (spoke), "How kabad (glorious) the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) was today, who galah (uncovered) himself today in the iyanay (eyes) of the handmaids of his ibad (servant), as achad (one) of the rayaq (vain) fellows galah (shamelessly) galah (uncovers) himself!"

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Mayakal (Michal), "It panayam (face) before Yahawah, who bachar (chose) me above your ab (father), and above all his bayath (house), to tzawah (appoint) me nagayad (prince) over the im (nation / people) of Yahawah, over Yashar-Al (Israel). Therefore will I celebrate panayam (face) Yahawah.
I will be yet more qalal (vile) than zaath (this), and will be shapal (base) in my own iyan (eye). But of the handmaids of whom you have amar (spoke), they shall honor me."
Mayakal (Michal) the banath (daughter) of Shaawal (Saul) had no yalad (birth / begot) to the yawam (day) of her mawath (death).
It happened, when the malak (king) lived in his bayath (house), and Yahawah had given him nawach (rest) from all his ayab (enemy) all around,

That the malak (king) amar (spoke) to Nathan (Nathan) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), "raah (see) now, I yashab (inhabit/dwell) in a bayath (house) of araz (cedar), but the arawan (ark) of Alahayam yashab (inhabit/dwell) thawak (midst) yarayaih (curtains)."
Nathan (Nathan) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "yalak (go), ishah (make) all that is in your labab (heart); for Yahawah is with you."
It happened the same layal (night), that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Nathan (Nathan), amar (spoke),
"Yalak (go) and amar (spoke) my ibad (servant) Dawad (David), ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "Shall you banah (build) me a bayath (house) for me to yashab (inhabit/dwell) in?

For I have not lived in a bayath (house) since the yawam (day) that I ilah (go up / offer) up the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) out of Matzarayam (Egypt), even to this yawam (day), but have halak (move) around in a ahal (tent) and in a mashakan (tabernacle).

In all halak (move) in which I have walked with all the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), did I dabar (word / matter) a dabar (word / matter) to any of the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel), whom I tzawah (commanded) to be raih (shepherd) of my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel), amar (spoke), ‘Why have you not banah (build) me a bayath (house) of araz (cedar)?'"'

Now therefore you shall amar (spoke) my ibad (servant) Dawad (David) this, ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), "I laqach (take / seize) you from the tzaan (sheep) pen, from achar (other) the tzaan (sheep), that you should be nagayad (prince) over my im (nation / people), over Yashar-Al (Israel).

I have been with you wherever you halak (move), and have karath (cut) off all your ayab (enemy) from panayam (face) you. I will ishah (make) you a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) sham (name), like the sham (name) of the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) ones who are in the aratz (Earth/land).

I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) a maqawam (place) for my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel), and will natai (plant) them, that they may shakan (place) in their own place, and be ragaz (moved) no more; neither shall the banay (children) of iwal (wickedness) inah (oppress / afflict) them any more, as at the raashawan (first),

And as from the yawam (day) that I tzawah (commanded) shapatayam (judges) to be over my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel). I will cause you to nawach (rest) from all your ayab (enemy). Moreover Yahawah nagad (tells) you that Yahawah will make you a bayath (house).

When your yawam (day) are malaa (fulfilled), and you shall sleep with your ab (father), I will qawam (rise up) up your zarai (seed) achar (other) you, who shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out of your maih (bowels), and I will kawan (establish) his mamalakah (kingdom).
He shall banah (build) a bayath (house) for my sham (name), and I will kawan (establish) the kasaa (throne) of his mamalakah (kingdom) iwalam (forever).

I will be his ab (father), and he shall be my ban (son). If he commits iwah (iniquity), I will yakach (chasten) him with the shabat (rod) of banay (men), and with the nagaiy (stripes) of the banay (children) of adam (men);
But my loving chasad (grace) shall not sawar (depart) from him, as I sawar (took) it from Shaawal (Saul), whom I sawar (put) away panayam (face) you.
Your bayath (house) and your mamalakah (kingdom) shall be made sure iwalam (forever) panayam (face) you. Your kasaa (throne) shall be kawan (established) iwalam (forever)."'"
According to all these dabarayam (words), and according to all this chazayawan (vision), so Nathan (Nathan) dabar (word / matter) to Dawad (David).

Then Dawad (David) the malak (king) bawaa (come) in, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) panayam (face) Yahawah; and he amar (spoke), "Who am I, Adanay Yahawah, and what is my bayath (house), that you bawaa (come) brought me thus far?

This was yet a qatan (small / young / least) thing in your iyan (eye), Adanay Yahawah; but you have dabar (word / matter) also of your ibad (servant) bayath (house) for a rachawaq (great) while to come; and this after the thawarah (Torah / Instruction) of adam (men), Adanay Yahawah!
What more can Dawad (David) dabar (word / matter) to you? For you yadai (know) your ibad (servant), Adanay Yahawah.
For your dabar (word / matter) sake, and according to your own lab (heart), you ishah (make) worked all this gadawalah (greatness), to make your ibad (servant) yadai (know) it.

Therefore you are gadal (great), Yahawah Alahayam. For there is none like you, neither is there any Alahayam zawalah (besides) you, according to all that we have shamai (hearken / hear) with our azan (ear).

What achad (one) gaway (heathen / nation) in the aratz (Earth/land) is like your im (nation / people), even like Yashar-Al (Israel), whom Alahayam halak (move) to padah (redeem) to himself for a im (nation / people), and to shawam (place / establish / appoint) himself a sham (name), and to ishah (make) gadawalah (great) things for you, and awesome things for your aratz (Earth/land), panayam (face) your im (nation / people), whom you padah (redeem) to yourself out of Matzarayam (Egypt), from the gawayam (nations) and their Alahayam?
You kawan (established) for yourself your im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel) to be a im (nation / people) to you iwalam (forever); and you, Yahawah, hayah (came to pass) their Alahayam.

Now, Yahawah Alahayam, the dabar (word / matter) that you have dabar (word / matter) concerning your ibad (servant), and concerning his bayath (house), qawam (rise up) it iwalam (forever), and ishah (make) as you have dabar (word / matter).

Let your sham (name) be gadal (magnified) iwalam (forever), amar (spoke), ‘Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) is Alahayam over Yashar-Al (Israel); and the bayath (house) of your ibad (servant) Dawad (David) shall be kawan (established) panayam (face) you.'

For you, Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), have galah (revealed) to your ibad (servant), amar (spoke), ‘I will banah (build) you a bayath (house).' Therefore your ibad (servant) matzaa (has) found in his lab (heart) to palal (pray) this thapalah (prayer) to you.
"Now, O Adanay Yahawah, you are Alahayam, and your dabar (word / matter) are amath (truth), and you have dabar (word / matter) this tawab (good / proper function) thing to your ibad (servant).

Now therefore let it yaal (please) you to barak (blessed) the bayath (house) of your ibad (servant), that it may continue iwalam (forever) panayam (face) you; for you, Adanay Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it. Let the bayath (house) of your ibad (servant) be barak (blessed) iwalam (forever) with your barakah (blessing)."

Achar (other) this it happened that Dawad (David) nakah (struck) the Palashathay (Philistines), and kanai (subdued) them: and Dawad (David) laqach (take / seize) the bridle of the mother city out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines).

He nakah (struck) Mawaab (Moab), and madad (measured) them with the chabal (line), making them to shakab (lie) down on the aratz (Earth/land); and he madad (measured) shanayam (two) chabalayam (lines) to put to mawath (death), and one malaa (full) chabal (line) to chayah (keep) alive. The Mawaab (Moabites) became ibadayam (servants) to Dawad (David), and nashaa (lift) tribute.

Dawad (David) nakah (struck) also Hadadaizar (Hadadezer) the ban (son) of Rachab (Rehob), malak (king) of Tzawabaa (Zobah), as he yalak (went) to shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand) at the nahar (river).

Dawad (David) lakad (took) from him one alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) horsemen, and isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) footmen: and Dawad (David) hamstrung all the rakab (chariot) horses, but yathar (reserved) of them for one maah (hundred) rakab (chariots).

When the Aram (Syrians) of Damashaq (Damascus) bawaa (come) to izar (help) Hadadaizar (Hadadezer) malak (king) of Tzawabaa (Zobah), Dawad (David) nakah (struck) of the Aram (Syrians) shanayam (two) and isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband).

Then Dawad (David) shawam (place / establish / appoint) natzabayam (garrisons) in Aram (Syria) of Damashaq (Damascus); and the Aram (Syrians) became ibadayam (servants) to Dawad (David), and nashaa (lift) tribute. Yahawah gave yashai (salvation) to Dawad (David) wherever he halak (move).
Dawad (David) laqach (take / seize) the shalatay (shields) of zahab (gold) that were on the ibaday (servants) of Hadadaizar (Hadadezer), and bawaa (come) them to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).
From Batach (Betah) and from Barawathah (Berothai), iray (cities) of Hadadaizar (Hadadezer), malak (king) Dawad (David) laqach (take / seize) maad (exceeding) much nachashath (brass).
When Thaiw (Toi) malak (king) of Chamath (Hamath) shamai (hearken / hear) that Dawad (David) had nakah (struck) all the chayal (army) of Hadadaizar (Hadadezer),

Then Thaiw (Toi) shalach (send) Yawaram (Joram) his ban (son) to malak (king) Dawad (David), to shaal (greet) him, and to barak (blessed) him, because he had lacham (fought) against Hadadaizar (Hadadezer) and nakah (struck) him: for Hadadaizar (Hadadezer) had wars with Thaiw (Toi). Joram brought with him kalay (vessels) of kasap (silver), and kalay (vessels) of zahab (gold), and kalay (vessels) of nachashath (brass):

Malak (king) Dawad (David) also qadash (set apart / make holy) these to Yahawah, with the kasap (silver) and zahab (gold) that he qadash (set apart / make holy) of all the gawayam (nations) which he kabash (subdued);

Of Aram (Syria), and of Mawaab (Moab), and of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), and of the Palashathay (Philistines), and of Imalaq (Amalek), and of the shalal (spoil) of Hadadaizar (Hadadezer), ban (son) of Rachab (Rehob), malak (king) of Tzawabaa (Zobah).
Dawad (David) earned a reputation when he shawab (turn back / repent) from nakah (smiting) the Aram (Syrians) in the gayaa (valley) of malach (salt), even eighteen alap (thousand) men.

He shawam (place / establish / appoint) natzabayam (garrisons) in Adawam (Edom); throughout all Adawam (Edom) shawam (place / establish / appoint) he natzabayam (garrisons), and all the Adawam (Edomites) became ibadayam (servants) to Dawad (David). Yahawah gave yashai (salvation) to Dawad (David) wherever he halak (move).
Dawad (David) malak (king) over all Yashar-Al (Israel); and Dawad (David) ishah (make) tzadaqah (righteousness) and mashapat (righteousness) to all his im (nation / people).
Yawaab (Joab) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah) was over the tzabaa (troop); and Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the ban (son) of Achayalawad (Ahilud) was zakar (remember);
And Tzadawaq (Zadok) the ban (son) of Achayatawab (Ahitub), and Achayamalak (Ahimelech) the ban (son) of Abayathar (Abiathar), were kahanayam (priests); and Sharayah (Seraiah) was sapar (book);
And Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) was over the Karathay (Cherethites) and the Palathay (Pelethites); and Dawad (David's) banay (sons) were kahan (priest) ministers.
Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "Is there yet any who is yathar (left) of the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul), that I may show him chasad (grace) for Yahawanathan (Jonathan's) sake?"

There was of the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul) a ibad (servant) whose sham (name) was Tzayabaa (Ziba), and they qaraa (called) him to Dawad (David); and the malak (king) amar (spoke) to him, "Are you Tzayabaa (Ziba)?" He amar (spoke), "Your ibad (servant) is he."

The malak (king) amar (spoke), "Is there not yet any of the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul), that I may show the chasad (grace) of Alahayam to him?" Tzayabaa (Ziba) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "Yahawanathan (Jonathan) has yet a ban (son), who is nakah (lame) of his ragalayam (feet)."

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to him, "ayapah (where) is he?" Tzayabaa (Ziba) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "Behold, he is in the bayath (house) of Makayar (Machir) the ban (son) of Imayaal (Ammiel), in Laadabar (Lo Debar)."
Then malak (king) Dawad (David) shalach (send), and laqach (take / seize) him out of the bayath (house) of Makayar (Machir) the ban (son) of Imayaal (Ammiel), from Laadabar (Lo Debar).

Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth), the ban (son) of Yahawanathan (Jonathan), the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul), bawaa (come) to Dawad (David), and napal (fall / be cast down) on his panayam (face), and showed respect. Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth)." He amar (spoke), "Behold, your ibad (servant)!"

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to him, "Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of him; for I will ishah (make) show you chasad (grace) for Yahawanathan (Jonathan) your ab (father) sake, and will shawab (turn back / repent) to you all the shadah (land) of Shaawal (Saul) your ab (father). You shall akal (eat) lacham (bread) at my shalachan (table) continually."
He shachah (bowed) down, and amar (spoke), "What is your ibad (servant), that you should panah (turn) on such a mawath (death) kalab (dog) as I am?"

Then the malak (king) qaraa (called) to Tzayabaa (Ziba), Shaawal (Saul's) nair (servant), and amar (spoke) to him, "All that hayah (came to pass) to Shaawal (Saul) and to all his bayath (house) nathan (give) I given to your adawan (master / lord) ban (son).

You shall ibad (servant) the adamah (land) for him, you, and your banayam (sons), and your ibadayam (servants); and you shall bawaa (come) in the harvest, that your adawan (master / lord) ban (son) may have lacham (bread) to akal (eat): but Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth) your adawan (master / lord) ban (son) shall akal (eat) lacham (bread) thamayad (always) at my shalachan (table)." Now Tzayabaa (Ziba) had chamash (fifteen) banayam (sons) and isharayam (twenty) ibadayam (servants).

Then Tzayabaa (Ziba) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "According to all that my Adawan the malak (king) tzawah (commands) his ibad (servant), so your shall ibad (servant) ishah (make)." So Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth) akal (eat) at the king's shalachan (table), like achad (one) of the malak (king) banay (sons).

Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth) had a qatan (small / young / least) ban (son), whose sham (name) was Mayakaa (Mica). All that lived in the bayath (house) of Tzayabaa (Ziba) were ibadayam (servants) to Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth).
So Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth) lived in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); for he akal (eat) continually at the malak (king) shalachan (table). He was pasach (lame) in shanayam (two) his ragal (feet / foot).
It happened achar (other) this, that the malak (king) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) mawath (death), and Chanawan (Hanun) his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "I will show chasad (grace) to Chanawan (Hanun) the ban (son) of Nachash (Nahash), as his ab (father) showed chasad (grace) to me." So Dawad (David) shalach (send) by his ibaday (servants) to nacham (turn away / repent) him concerning his ab (father). Dawad (David's) ibaday (servants) bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon).

But the sharay (princes) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) amar (spoke) to Chanawan (Hanun) their Adawan, "Do you iyan (eye) that Dawad (David) honors your ab (father), in that he has shalach (send) comforters to you? Hasn't Dawad (David) shalach (send) his ibad (servant) to you to chaqar (search) the iyar (city), and to ragal (spy) it out, and to hapak (overthrow) it?"

So Chanawan (Hanun) laqach (take / seize) Dawad (David's) ibaday (servants), and galach (shaved) off the one chatzay (half) of their zaqan (beards), and karath (cut) off their madaw (garments) in the chatzay (middle), even to their shathah (drinks), and shalach (send) them away.

When they nagad (told) it to Dawad (David), he shalach (send) to qaraah (meet) them; for the anashayam (men) were maad (greatly) kalam (ashamed). The malak (king) amar (spoke), "Wait at Yarayachaw (Jericho) until your zaqan (beards) have tzamach (grown), and then shawab (turn back / repent)."

When the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) raah (see) that they were become baash (odious) to Dawad (David), the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) shalach (send) and shakar (hired) the Aram (Syrians) of Bayatharachawab (Beth Rehob), and the Aram (Syrians) of Tzawabaa (Zobah), isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) footmen, and the malak (king) of Maikah (Maacah) with one alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband), and the ayash (man / husband) of Tob ishar (-teen) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband).
When Dawad (David) shamai (hearken / hear) of it, he shalach (send) Yawaab (Joab), and all the tzabaa (troop) of the gabawar (mighty) men.

The banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and put the malachamah (battle) in irak (array) at the entrance of the shair (gate): and the Aram (Syrians) of Tzawabaa (Zobah) and of Rachab (Rehob), and the men of Maikah (Tob) and Maacah, were by themselves in the shadah (field).

Now when Yawaab (Joab) raah (see) that the malachamah (battle) panayam (face) set panayam (face) him before and achawar (behind), he bachar (chose) of all the choice men of Yashar-Al (Israel), and irak (put) them in array qaraah (against) the Aram (Syrians):

The yathar (rest) of the im (nation / people) he nathan (give) into the yad (hand) of Abayashay (Abishai) his ach (brother/kinsman); and he irak (put) them in array qaraah (against) the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon).

He amar (spoke), "If the Aram (Syrians) are too chazaq (strong) for me, then you shall chazaq (help) me; but if the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) are too chazaq (strong) for you, then I will halak (move) and yashai (salvation) you.
Be courageous, and let us be chazaq (strong) for our im (nation / people), and for the iray (cities) of our Alahayam; and Yahawah ishah (make) that which seems tawab (good / proper function) to him."
So Yawaab (Joab) and the im (nation / people) who were with him nagash (drew) near to the malachamah (battle) against the Aram (Syrians): and they nawas (fled) panayam (face) him.

When the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) raah (see) that the Aram (Syrians) had nawas (fled), they likewise nawas (fled) panayam (face) Abayashay (Abishai), and bawaa (come) into the iyar (city). Then Yawaab (Joab) shawab (turn back / repent) from the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), and bawaa (come) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).
When the Aram (Syrians) raah (see) that they were defeated by Yashar-Al (Israel), they asap (gathered) themselves yachad (together).

Hadadezer shalach (send), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out the Aram (Syrians) who were ibar (beyond) the nahar (river): and they bawaa (come) to Chayalam (Helam), with Shawabak (Shobach) the shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop) of Hadadezer at their panayam (face).

It was nagad (told) Dawad (David); and he asap (gathered) all Yashar-Al (Israel) asap (together), and ibar (pass over/through) over the Yaradan (Jordan), and bawaa (come) to Chayalam (Helam). The Aram (Syrians) irak (set) themselves in array qaraah (against) Dawad (David), and lacham (fought) with him.

The Aram (Syrians) nawas (fled) panayam (face) Yashar-Al (Israel); and Dawad (David) harag (kill) of the Aram (Syrians) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) charioteers, and arabaiyam (forty) alap (thousand) horsemen, and nakah (struck) Shawabak (Shobach) the shar (prince / ruler) of their tzabaa (troop), so that he mawath (death) there.

When all the malakayam (kings) who were ibaday (servants) to Hadadezer raah (see) that they were defeated panayam (face) Yashar-Al (Israel), they made shalam (peace) with Yashar-Al (Israel), and ibad (servant) them. So the Aram (Syrians) yaraa (fear / be afraid) to yashai (salvation) the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) any more.

It happened, at the thashawabah (return) of the shanah (year), at the ith (time) when malaakayam (kings) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, that Dawad (David) shalach (send) Yawaab (Joab), and his ibad (servant) with him, and all Yashar-Al (Israel); and they shachath (destroyed) the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), and tzawar (besieged) Rabah (Rabbah). But Dawad (David) stayed at Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

It happened at irab (evening), that Dawad (David) qawam (rise up) from off his mashakab (bed), and halak (move) on the gag (roof) of the malak (king) bayath (house): and from the gag (roof) he raah (see) a ayashah (woman / wife) rachatz (bathing); and the ayashah (woman / wife) was very tawab (good / proper function) to maraah (look) on.

Dawad (David) shalach (send) and darash (inquired) after the ayashah (woman / wife). One amar (spoke), "Isn't this Bathashabai (Bathsheba), the banath (daughter) of Alayaim (Eliam), the ayashah (woman / wife) of Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite)?"

Dawad (David) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers), and laqach (take / seize) her; and she bawaa (come) in to him, and he shakab (lay) with her (for she was qadash (set apart / make holy) from her tamaah (uncleanness)); and she shawab (turn back / repent) to her bayath (house).
The ayashah (woman / wife) harah (conceived); and she shalach (send) and nagad (told) Dawad (David), and amar (spoke), "I am with harah (child)."
Dawad (David) shalach (send) to Yawaab (Joab), "shalach (send) me Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite)." Yawaab (Joab) shalach (send) Awarayah (Uriah) to Dawad (David).

When Awarayah (Uriah) bawaa (come) come to him, Dawad (David) shaal (asked) of him how Yawaab (Joab) shalawam (peace / safety), and how the im (nation / people) shalawam (peace / safety), and how the malachamah (war) shalawam (peace / safety).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Awarayah (Uriah), "yarad (go) down to your bayath (house), and rachatz (wash) your ragal (feet / foot)." Awarayah (Uriah) departed out of the malak (king) bayath (house), and a mashaath (gift) from the malak (king) was sent achar (other) him.
But Awarayah (Uriah) shakab (slept) at the pathach (door) of the malak (king) bayath (house) with all the ibaday (servants) of his Adawan, and didn't yarad (go) down to his bayath (house).

When they had nagad (told) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), "Awarayah (Uriah) didn't yarad (go) down to his bayath (house)," Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Awarayah (Uriah), "Haven't you bawaa (come) from a darak (journey)? Why didn't you yarad (go) down to your bayath (house)?"

Awarayah (Uriah) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "The arawan (ark), Yashar-Al (Israel), and Yahawadah (Judah), are staying in sakawath (tents); and my Adawan Yawaab (Joab), and the ibaday (servants) of my Adawan, are chanah (encamped) in the panayam (face) shadah (field). Shall I then bawaa (come) into my bayath (house) to akal (eat) and to shathah (drinks), and to shakab (lie) with my ayashah (woman / wife)? As you chay (life), and as your napash (soul) chay (life), I will not ishah (make) this thing!"

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Awarayah (Uriah), "Stay here today also, and machar (tomorrow) I will shalach (send) you depart." So Awarayah (Uriah) stayed in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) that yawam (day), and the next yawam (day).

When Dawad (David) had qaraa (called) him, he akal (eat) and shathah (drinks) panayam (face) him; and he shakar (made) him drunk. At irab (evening), he yatzaa (go out / come out) out to shakab (lie) on his mashakab (bed) with the ibaday (servants) of his Adawan, but didn't yarad (go) down to his bayath (house).
It happened in the baqar (morning), that Dawad (David) kathab (write) a sapar (book / scribed document) to Yawaab (Joab), and shalach (send) it by the yad (hand) of Awarayah (Uriah).

He kathab (write) in the sapar (book / scribed document), amar (spoke), "Send Awarayah (Uriah) to the panayam (face) of the chazaq (hottest) malachamah (battle), and retreat from him, that he may be nakah (struck), and mawath (death)."

It happened, when Yawaab (Joab) shamar (keep/guard) watch on the iyar (city), that he nathan (give) Awarayah (Uriah) to the maqawam (place) where he yadai (knew) that chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) yadai (men) were.

The anashay (men) of the iyar (city) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and lacham (fought) with Yawaab (Joab). Some of the im (nation / people) napal (fall / be cast down), even of the ibaday (servants) of Dawad (David); and Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite) mawath (death) also.
Then Yawaab (Joab) shalach (send) and nagad (told) Dawad (David) all the things concerning the malachamah (war);

And he tzawah (commanded) the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah), amar (spoke), "When you kalah (complete / finish) finished dabar (word / matter) all the things concerning the malachamah (war) to the malak (king),

It shall be that, if the malak (king) chamah (wrath) arise, and he asks you, ‘Why did you nagash (go) so near to the iyar (city) to lacham (fight)? Didn't you yadai (know) that they would yarah (shoot) from the chawamah (wall)?

Who nakah (struck) Abayamalak (Abimelech) the ban (son) of Yarabashath (Jerubbesheth)? Didn't a ayashah (woman / wife) shalak (cast) an upper rakab (millstone) on him from the chawamah (wall), so that he mawath (death) at Thabatz (Thebez)? Why did you nagash (go) so near the chawamah (wall)?' Then you shall amar (spoke), ‘Your ibad (servant) Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite) is mawath (death) also.'"
So the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) yalak (went), and bawaa (come) and showed Dawad (David) all that Yawaab (Joab) had shalach (send) him for.

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "The anashayam (men) gabar (prevailed) against us, and yatzaa (go out / come out) out to us into the shadah (field), and we were on them even to the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate).

The shooters yarah (shot) at your ibaday (servants) from off the chawamah (wall); and some of the malak (king) ibaday (servants) are mawath (death), and your ibad (servant) Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite) is mawath (death) also."

Then Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah), "Thus you shall amar (spoke) Yawaab (Joab), ‘Don't let this thing displease you, for the charab (sword) akal (eat) one as zah (this / that / these) as another. Make your malachamah (battle) chazaq (stronger) against the iyar (city), and haras (overthrow) it.' Chazaq (encourage) him."
When the ayashah (woman / wife) of Awarayah (Uriah) shamai (hearken / hear) that Awarayah (Uriah) her ayash (man / husband) was mawath (death), she made lamentation for her bail (husband).

When the abal (mourning) was past, Dawad (David) shalach (send) and asap (took) her home to his bayath (house), and she became his ayashah (woman / wife), and yalad (birth / begot) him a ban (son). But the thing that Dawad (David) ishah (make) done displeased Yahawah.

Yahawah shalach (send) Nathan (Nathan) to Dawad (David). He bawaa (come) to him, and amar (spoke) to him, "There were shanayam (two) anashayam (men) in achad (one) iyar (city); the achad (one) ishayar (rich), and the other rawash (poor).
The ishayar (rich) maad (man) had very many tzaan (flocks) and baqar (morning),

But the rawash (poor) achad (one) had nothing, except one qatan (small / young / least) ewe kabashah (lamb), which he had bought and raised. It grew up yachad (together) with him, and with his ban (son). It akal (eat) of his own food, shathah (drinks) of his own kawas (cup), and shakab (lay) in his chayaq (bosom), and was to him like a banath (daughter).

A traveler bawaa (come) to the ishayar (rich) ayash (man / husband), and he chamal (spared) to laqach (take / seize) of his own tzaan (flock) and of his own baqar (morning), to ishah (make) for the arach (wayfaring) man who bawaa (come) come to him, but laqach (take / seize) the rawash (poor) ayash (man / husband) kabashah (lamb), and ishah (make) it for the ayash (man / husband) who bawaa (come) come to him."

Dawad (David's) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was maad (greatly) charah (hot with anger) against the ayash (man / husband), and he amar (spoke) to Nathan (Nathan), "As Yahawah chay (life), the ayash (man / husband) who ishah (make) done this is ban (son) to mawath (death)!

He shall shalam (restore) the kabashah (lamb) arabaithayam (fourfold), iqab (award / effect after the cause) he ishah (make) this thing, and iqab (award / effect after the cause) he chamal (had) no pity!"

Nathan (Nathan) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "You are the ayash (man / husband). This is what Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), amar (spoke): ‘I mashach (anointed) you malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel), and I natzal (delivered) you out of the yad (hand) of Shaawal (Saul).

I nathan (give) you your adawan (master / lord) bayath (house), and your adawan (master / lord) wives into your chayaq (bosom), and nathan (give) you the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) and of Yahawadah (Judah); and if that would have been too mait (little), I would have yasap (added) to you many more such things.

Why have you bazah (despised) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, to ishah (make) that which is rai (evil) in his iyan (eye)? You have nakah (struck) Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite) with the charab (sword), and have laqach (take / seize) his ayashah (woman / wife) to be your ayashah (woman / wife), and have harag (kill) him with the charab (sword) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon).

Now therefore the charab (sword) will never sawar (depart) from your bayath (house), iqab (award / effect after the cause) you have bazah (despised) me, and have laqach (take / seize) the ayashah (woman / wife) of Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite) to be your ayashah (woman / wife).'

"This is what Yahawah amar (spoke): ‘Behold, I will qawam (rise up) up rai (evil) against you out of your own bayath (house); and I will laqach (take / seize) your wives before your iyanay (eyes), and nathan (give) them to your neighbor, and he will shakab (lie) with your wives in the iyan (eye) of this shamash (sun).
For you ishah (make) it secretly, but I will ishah (make) this thing before all Yashar-Al (Israel), and before the shamash (sun).'"

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Nathan (Nathan), "I have chataa (sinned) against Yahawah." Nathan (Nathan) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "Yahawah also ibar (pass over/through) put away your chataah (sin). You will not mawath (death).

However, dabar (word / matter) by this deed you have given naatz (great) occasion to Yahawah ayabay (enemies) to naatz (blaspheme), the ban (son) also who is yalawad (born) to you shall mawath (death) mawath (death)."

Nathan (Nathan) departed to his bayath (house). Yahawah nagap (struck) the yalad (birth / begot) that Awarayah (Uriah's) ayashah (woman / wife) yalad (birth / begot) to Dawad (David), and it was very anash (sick).
Dawad (David) therefore baqash (begged) Alahayam for the nair (child); and Dawad (David) tzawam (fasted), and bawaa (come) in, and shakab (lay) all lawan (night) on the aratz (Earth/land).
The zaqanay (elders) of his bayath (house) qawam (rise up) beside him, to qawam (rise up) him up from the aratz (Earth/land): but he would not, neither did he barah (eat) lacham (bread) with them.

It happened on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), that the yalad (birth / begot) mawath (death). The ibaday (servants) of Dawad (David) yaraa (fear / be afraid) to nagad (tell) him that the yalad (birth / begot) was mawath (death); for they amar (spoke), "Behold, while the yalad (birth / begot) was yet chay (life), we amar (spoke) to him, and he didn't shamai (hearken / hear) to our qawal (sound / voice). How will he then rai (harm) himself, if we amar (spoke) him that the yalad (birth / begot) is mawath (death)?"

But when Dawad (David) raah (see) that his ibad (servant) were lachash (whispering) together, Dawad (David) bayan (between) that the yalad (birth / begot) was mawath (death); and Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), "Is the yalad (birth / begot) mawath (death)?" They amar (spoke), "He is mawath (death)."

Then Dawad (David) qawam (rise up) from the aratz (Earth/land), and rachatz (washed), and sawak (anointed) himself, and chalap (changed) his shamalah (clothing); and he bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and shachah (worshiped): then he bawaa (come) to his own bayath (house); and when he shaal (required), they shawam (place / establish / appoint) lacham (bread) before him, and he akal (eat).

Then his ibad (servant) amar (spoke) to him, "dabar (word / matter) is this that you ishah (make) done? You tzawam (fasted) and bakah (wept) for the yalad (birth / begot) while he was chay (life); but when the yalad (birth / begot) was mawath (death), you qawam (rise up) up and akal (eat) lacham (bread)."

He amar (spoke), "While the yalad (birth / begot) was yet chay (life), I tzawam (fasted) and bakah (wept); for I amar (spoke), ‘Who yadai (knows) whether Yahawah will not be gracious to me, that the yalad (birth / begot) may chay (life)?'
But now he is mawath (death), why should I tzawam (fast)? Yakal (can) I shawab (turn back / repent) him back again? I shall halak (move) to him, but he will not shawab (turn back / repent) to me."

Dawad (David) nacham (turn away / repent) Bathashabai (Bathsheba) his ayashah (woman / wife), and bawaa (come) in to her, and shakab (lay) with her. She yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son), and he qaraa (called) his sham (name) Shalamah (Solomon). Yahawah ahab (love) him;
And he shalach (send) by the yad (hand) of Nathan (Nathan) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy); and he sham (name) him Yadayadayah (Jedidiah), for Yahawah sake.
Now Yawaab (Joab) lacham (fought) against Rabah (Rabbah) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), and lakad (took) the malawakah (royal) iyar (city).
Yawaab (Joab) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to Dawad (David), and amar (spoke), "I have lacham (fought) against Rabah (Rabbah). Yes, I have lakad (taken) the iyar (city) of mayam (Waters).

Now therefore asap (gather) the yathar (rest) of the im (nation / people) asap (together), and chanah (encamp) against the iyar (city), and lakad (take) it; lest I lakad (take) the iyar (city), and it be qaraa (called) after my sham (name)."
Dawad (David) asap (gathered) all the im (nation / people) asap (together), and yalak (went) to Rabah (Rabbah), and lacham (fought) against it, and lakad (took) it.

He laqach (take / seize) the itarah (crown) of their malak (king) from off his raash (head); and its mashaqal (weight) was a kakar (talent) of zahab (gold), and in it were yaqar (precious) aban (stone); and it was set on Dawad (David's) raash (head). He yatzaa (go out / come out) out the shalal (spoil) of the iyar (city), maad (exceeding) much.

He yatzaa (go out / come out) out the im (nation / people) who were therein, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them under magarah (saws), and under barazal (iron) picks, and under magazarath (axes) of barazal (iron), and ibar (pass over/through) them pass through the brick kiln: and he ishah (make) so to all the iray (cities) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon). Dawad (David) and all the im (nation / people) shawab (turn back / repent) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

It happened achar (other) this, that Abayashalawam (Absalom) the ban (son) of Dawad (David) had a yapah (beautiful) achawath (sister), whose sham (name) was Thamar (Tamar); and Amanawan (Amnon) the ban (son) of Dawad (David) ahab (love) her.

Amanawan (Amnon) was so troubled that he chalah (afflict) sick because of his achawath (sister) Thamar (Tamar); for she was a bathawalah (virgin); and it seemed palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) to Amanawan (Amnon) to ishah (make) anything to her.

But Amanawan (Amnon) had a rai (neigbor/another person), whose sham (name) was Yawanadab (Jonadab), the ban (son) of Shamaih (Shimeah), Dawad (David's) ach (brother/kinsman); and Yawanadab (Jonadab) was a very subtle ayash (man / husband).

He amar (spoke) to him, "Why, ban (son) of the malak (king), are you so sad from baqar (morning) to baqar (morning)? Won't you nagad (tell) me?" Amanawan (Amnon) amar (spoke) to him, "I ahab (love) Thamar (Tamar), my ach (brother/kinsman) Abayashalawam (Absalom's) achawath (sister)."

Yahawanadab (Jonadab) amar (spoke) to him, "shakab (lay) down on your mashakab (bed), and pretend to be chalah (afflict). When your ab (father) bawaa (come) to raah (see) you, amar (spoke) him, ‘Please let my achawath (sister) Thamar (Tamar) bawaa (come) and give me lacham (bread) to eat, and ishah (make) the lacham (food) in my iyan (eye), that I may raah (see) it, and akal (eat) it from her yad (hand).'"

So Amanawan (Amnon) shakab (lay) down and faked being chalah (afflict). When the malak (king) bawaa (come) to raah (see) him, Amanawan (Amnon) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "Please let my achawath (sister) Thamar (Tamar) bawaa (come), and labab (make) me a shanayam (two) of lababawath (cakes) in my iyan (eye), that I may barah (eat) from her yad (hand)."
Then Dawad (David) shalach (send) bayath (house) to Thamar (Tamar), amar (spoke), "yalak (go) now to your ach (brother/kinsman) Amanawan (Amnon's) bayath (house), and ishah (make) food for him."

So Thamar (Tamar) yalak (went) to her ach (brother/kinsman) Amanawan (Amnon's) bayath (house); and he was shakab (laid) down. She laqach (take / seize) batzaq (dough), and lawash (kneaded) it, and labab (made) cakes in his iyan (eye), and bashal (baked) the labab (cakes).

She laqach (take / seize) the masharath (pan), and yatzaq (poured) them out panayam (face) him; but he maan (refused) to akal (eat). Amanawan (Amnon) amar (spoke), "Have all ayash (man / husband) leave me." Every ayash (man / husband) yatzaa (go out / come out) out from him.

Amanawan (Amnon) amar (spoke) to Thamar (Tamar), "bawaa (come) the food into the room, that I may barah (eat) from your yad (hand)." Thamar (Tamar) laqach (take / seize) the lababawath (cakes) which she ishah (make) made, and bawaa (come) them into the room to Amanawan (Amnon) her ach (brother/kinsman).
When she had nagash (brought) them near to him to akal (eat), he chazaq (took) hold of her, and amar (spoke) to her, "bawaa (come), shakab (lie) with me, my achawath (sister)!"
She amar (spoke) him, "No, my ach (brother/kinsman), do not inah (oppress / afflict) me! For no such thing ought to be ishah (make) in Yashar-Al (Israel). Don't you ishah (make) this nabalah (folly).

I, where would I yalak (carry) my charapah (shame)? And as for you, you will be as achad (one) of the nabalayam (fools) in Yashar-Al (Israel). Now therefore, please dabar (word / matter) to the malak (king); for he will not manai (withhold) me from you."
However he would not shamai (hearken / hear) to her qawal (sound / voice); but being chazaq (stronger) than she, he inah (oppress / afflict) her, and shakab (lay) with her.

Then Amanawan (Amnon) shanaa (hate) her with exceeding great hatred; for the hatred with which he shanaa (hate) her was greater than the ahabah (love) with which he had ahab (love) her. Amanawan (Amnon) amar (spoke) to her, "qawam (rise up), be yalak (gone)!"

She amar (spoke) to him, "Not so, awadawath (because) this rai (great) wrong in shalach (send) me away is worse than the other that you ishah (make) to me!" But he would not shamai (hearken / hear) to her.

Then he qaraa (called) his nair (servant) who sharath (ministered) to him, and amar (spoke), "shalach (send) now this chawatz (woman) out from me, and nail (bolt) the dalath (door) achar (other) her."

She had a kathanath (garment) of various colors on her; for with such maiyalayam (robes) were the malak (king) banawath (daughters) who were bathawalath (virgins) dressed. Then his sharath (servant) yatzaa (go out / come out) her out, and nail (bolted) the dalath (door) achar (other) her.

Thamar (Tamar) put ashes on her raash (head), and qarai (tore) her kathanath (garment) of various colors that was on her; and she shawam (place / establish / appoint) her yad (hand) on her raash (head), and yalak (went) her way, zaiq (crying) aloud as she went.

Abayashalawam (Absalom) her ach (brother/kinsman) amar (spoke) to her, "Has Amanawan (Amnon) your ach (brother/kinsman) been with you? But now hold your charash (peace), my achawath (sister). He is your ach (brother/kinsman). Don't shayath (put / appoint / make) this thing to heart." So Thamar (Tamar) yashab (inhabit/dwell) shamam (desolate) in her ach (brother/kinsman) Abayashalawam (Absalom's) bayath (house).
But when malak (king) Dawad (David) shamai (hearken / hear) of all these things, he was very charah (hot with anger).

Abayashalawam (Absalom) dabar (word / matter) to Amanawan (Amnon) neither tawab (good / proper function) nor rai (bad); for Abayashalawam (Absalom) shanaa (hate) Amanawan (Amnon), dabar (word / matter) he had inah (oppress / afflict) his achawath (sister) Thamar (Tamar).

It happened after yawam (day) full shanathayam (years), that Abayashalawam (Absalom) had sheepshearers in Bailachatzawar (Baal Hazor), which is beside Aparayam (Ephraim): and Abayashalawam (Absalom) qaraa (called) all the malak (king) banay (sons).

Abayashalawam (Absalom) bawaa (come) to the malak (king), and amar (spoke), "See now, your ibad (servant) has sheepshearers. Please yalak (let) the malak (king) and his ibad (servant) yalak (go) with your ibad (servant)."

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Abayashalawam (Absalom), "No, my ban (son), yalak (let) us not all go, lest we be burdensome to you." He paratz (pressed) him; however he would not yalak (go), but barak (blessed) him.

Then Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke), "If not, please let my ach (brother/kinsman) Amanawan (Amnon) yalak (go) with us." The malak (king) amar (spoke) to him, "Why should he yalak (go) with you?"
But Abayashalawam (Absalom) paratz (pressed) him, and he let Amanawan (Amnon) and all the malak (king) banay (sons) shalach (send) with him.

Abayashalawam (Absalom) tzawah (commanded) his nair (servants), amar (spoke), "raah (see) now, when Amanawan (Amnon's) lab (heart) is tawab (good / proper function) with yayan (wine); and when I amar (spoke) you, ‘nakah (strike) Amanawan (Amnon),' then mawath (death) him. Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). Haven't I tzawah (commanded) you? Be courageous, and be ban (son)!"

The nairay (servants) of Abayashalawam (Absalom) ishah (make) to Amanawan (Amnon) as Abayashalawam (Absalom) had tzawah (commanded). Then all the malak (king) banay (sons) qawam (rise up), and every ayash (man / husband) qawam (rise up) up on his parad (mule), and nawas (fled).

It happened, while they were in the darak (way), that the shamawaih (news) bawaa (come) to Dawad (David), amar (spoke), "Abayashalawam (Absalom) has nakah (slain) all the malak (king) banay (sons), and there is not achad (one) of them yathar (left)!"

Then the malak (king) qawam (rise up), and qarai (tore) his bagadayam (garments), and shakab (lay) on the aratz (Earth/land); and all his ibad (servant) natzab (stood) by with their clothes qarai (torn).

Yawanadab (Jonadab), the ban (son) of Shamaih (Shimeah), Dawad (David's) ach (brother/kinsman), inah (answer / respond), "Don't let my Adawan amar (spoke) that they have mawath (death) all the nair (young) men the malak (king) banay (sons); for Amanawan (Amnon) only is mawath (death); for by the pah (appointment) of Abayashalawam (Absalom) this has been shawam (place / establish / appoint) from the yawam (day) that he inah (oppress / afflict) his achawath (sister) Thamar (Tamar).

Now therefore don't let my Adawan the malak (king) shawam (place / establish / appoint) the thing to his lab (heart), to amar (spoke) that all the malak (king) banay (sons) are mawath (death); for Amanawan (Amnon) only is mawath (death)."
