But Abayashalawam (Absalom) barach (fled). The nair (young) man who kept the tzapah (watchman / keep watch) nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye), and raah (see), and behold, many im (nation / people) were coming by darak (way) of the hillside achar (other) him.
Yawanadab (Jonadab) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "Behold, the malak (king) banay (sons) are bawaa (come)! It is as your ibad (servant) dabar (word / matter)."

It happened, as soon as he kalah (complete / finish) finished dabar (word / matter), that behold, the malak (king) banay (sons) bawaa (come), and nashaa (lift) up their qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept). The malak (king) also and all his ibad (servant) bakah (wept) bitterly.

But Abayashalawam (Absalom) barach (fled), and yalak (went) to Thalamay (Talmai) the ban (son) of Imayachawar (Ammihur), malak (king) of Gashawar (Geshur). David abal (mourned) for his ban (son) every yawam (day).
So Abayashalawam (Absalom) barach (fled), and yalak (went) to Gashawar (Geshur), and was there shalawash (three) shanayam (years).

Malak (king) Dawad (David) kalah (complete / finish) to yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to Abayashalawam (Absalom): for he was nacham (turn away / repent) concerning Amanawan (Amnon), since he was mawath (death).
Now Yawaab (Joab) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah) yadai (perceived) that the malak (king) lab (heart) was toward Abayashalawam (Absalom).

Yawaab (Joab) shalach (send) to Thaqawai (Tekoa), and laqach (take / seize) there a chakam (wise) ayashah (woman / wife), and amar (spoke) to her, "Please act like a mourner, and labash (put) on abal (mourning) bagad (clothing), please, and don't sawak (anoint) yourself with shaman (oil), but be as a ayashah (woman / wife) who has abal (mourned) a rab (long) yawam (day) for the mawath (death).
Bawaa (come) in to the malak (king), and dabar (word / matter) like this to him." So Yawaab (Joab) shawam (place / establish / appoint) the dabarayam (words) in her pah (mouth).

When the ayashah (woman / wife) of Tekoa amar (spoke) to the malak (king), she napal (fall / be cast down) on her ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land), showed respect, and amar (spoke), "yashai (salvation), O malak (king)!"
The malak (king) amar (spoke) to her, "What ails you?" She amar (spoke), "Truly I am a alamanah (widow), and my ayash (man / husband) is mawath (death).

Your handmaid had shanayam (two) banayam (sons), and they shanayam (two) fought together in the shadah (field), and there was no one to natzal (part) them, but the achad (one) nakah (struck) the other, and nakah (killed) him.

Behold, the whole mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) has qawam (rise up) against your handmaid, and they amar (spoke), ‘nathan (give) him who nakah (struck) his ach (brother/kinsman), that we may mawath (death) him for the napash (soul) of his ach (brother/kinsman) whom he harag (kill), and so shamad (destroy) the heir also.' Thus they would kabah (quench) my gachal (coal) which is shawam (place / establish / appoint), and would shawam (place / establish / appoint) to my ayash (man / husband) neither sham (name) nor shaarayath (remainder) on the surface of the adamah (earth)."
The malak (king) amar (spoke) to the ayashah (woman / wife), "yalak (go) to your bayath (house), and I will give a tzawah (command) concerning you."

The ayashah (woman / wife) of Tekoa amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "My Adawan, O malak (king), the iwan (guilt/iniquity) be on me, and on my ab (father) bayath (house); and the malak (king) and his kasaa (throne) be naqay (guiltless)."
The malak (king) amar (spoke), "Whoever amar (spoke) anything to you, bawaa (come) him to me, and he shall not nagai (touch) you any more."

Then she amar (spoke), "Please let the malak (king) zakar (remember) Yahawah your Alahayam, that the gaal (avenger) of dam (blood) shachath (destroy) not any more, lest they shamad (destroy) my ban (son)." He amar (spoke), "As Yahawah chay (life), not one shairah (hair) of your ban (son) shall napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land)."
Then the ayashah (woman / wife) amar (spoke), "Please let your handmaid dabar (word / matter) a dabar (word / matter) to my Adawan the malak (king)." He amar (spoke), "dabar (word / matter) on."

The ayashah (woman / wife) amar (spoke), "Why then have you chashab (devised) such a thing against the im (nation / people) of Alahayam? For in dabar (word / matter) this dabar (word / matter) the malak (king) is as one who is asham (guilty), in that the malak (king) shawab (turn back / repent) not bring home again his nadach (banished) one.

For we mawath (death) mawath (death), and are as mayam (Waters) spilled on the aratz (Earth/land), which can't be asap (gathered) up again; neither does Alahayam nashaa (lift) away napash (soul), but chashab (devises) machashabawath (means), that he who is nadach (banished) not be an nadach (outcast) from him.

Now therefore seeing that I bawaa (come) come to dabar (word / matter) this dabar (word / matter) to my Adawan the malak (king), it is because the im (nation / people) have made me yaraa (fear / be afraid): and your handmaid amar (spoke), ‘I will now dabar (word / matter) to the malak (king); it may be that the malak (king) will ishah (make) the dabar (word / matter) of his amah (servant).'

For the malak (king) will shamai (hearken / hear), to natzal (deliver) his amah (servant) out of the kap (hand) of the ayash (man / husband) who would shamad (destroy) me and my ban (son) yachad (together) out of the nachalah (inheritance) of Alahayam.

Then your handmaid amar (spoke), ‘Please let the dabar (word / matter) of my Adawan the malak (king) bring manawachah (rest); for as an malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Alahayam, so is my Adawan the malak (king) to shamai (hearken / hear) tawab (good / proper function) and rai (bad). May Yahawah, your Alahayam, be with you.'"

Then the malak (king) inah (answer / respond) the ayashah (woman / wife), "Please don't kachad (hide) anything from me that I shaal (ask) you." The ayashah (woman / wife) amar (spoke), "Let my Adawan the malak (king) now dabar (word / matter)."

The malak (king) amar (spoke), "Is the yad (hand) of Yawaab (Joab) with you in all this?" The ayashah (woman / wife) inah (answer / respond), "As your napash (soul) chay (life), my Adawan the malak (king), no napash (soul) ash (fire) turn to the right yaman (hand) or to the shamaal (left) from anything that my Adawan the malak (king) has dabar (word / matter); for your ibad (servant) Yawaab (Joab), he urged me, and he shawam (place / establish / appoint) all these dabarayam (words) in the pah (mouth) of your handmaid;

To sabab (change) the panayam (face) of the dabar (word / matter) has your ibad (servant) Yawaab (Joab) ishah (make) this thing. My Adawan is chakam (wise), according to the chakamah (wisdom) of an malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Alahayam, to yadai (know) all things that are in the aratz (Earth/land)."

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Yawaab (Joab), "Behold now, I ishah (make) done this thing. Yalak (go) therefore, shawab (turn back / repent) the nair (young) man Abayashalawam (Absalom) shawab (turn back / repent)."

Yawaab (Joab) napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land) on his panayam (face), showed respect, and barak (blessed) the malak (king). Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke), "Today your ibad (servant) yadai (knows) that I matzaa (have) found favor in your iyan (eye), my Adawan, malak (king), in that the malak (king) ishah (make) performed the dabar (word / matter) of his ibad (servant)."
So Yawaab (Joab) qawam (rise up) and yalak (went) to Gashawar (Geshur), and bawaa (come) Abayashalawam (Absalom) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

The malak (king) amar (spoke), "Let him sabab (return) to his own bayath (house), but raah (see) him not see my panayam (face)." So Abayashalawam (Absalom) sabab (returned) to his own bayath (house), and didn't raah (see) the malak (king) panayam (face).

Now in all Yashar-Al (Israel) there was ayash (man / husband) to be so much halal (praise) as Abayashalawam (Absalom) for his yapah (beauty): from the kap (sole) of his ragal (feet / foot) even to the qadaqad (crown) of his head there was no maawam (blemish) in him.

When he cut the hair of his raash (head) (yawam (day) it was at every year's qatz (end) that he cut it; because it was kabad (heavy) on him, therefore he cut it); he shaqal (weighed) the shair (hair) of his raash (head) at two maah (hundred) shaqalayam (shekels), after the malak (king) aban (stone).

To Abayashalawam (Absalom) there were yalad (birth / begot) shalawash (three) banayam (sons), and achad (one) banath (daughter), whose sham (name) was Thamar (Tamar): she was a ayashah (woman / wife) of a yapah (beautiful) maraah (face).
Abayashalawam (Absalom) lived yawam (day) full shanathayam (years) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); and he didn't raah (see) the malak (king) panayam (face).

Then Abayashalawam (Absalom) shalach (send) for Yawaab (Joab), to shalach (send) him to the malak (king); but he would not bawaa (come) to him: and he shalach (send) again a shanay (second) time, but he would not bawaa (come).

Therefore he amar (spoke) to his ibaday (servants), "raah (see), Yawaab (Joab's) chalaqah (field) is al (toward) yad (hand), and he has shairah (barley) there. Yalak (go) and yatzath (set) it on ash (fire)." Abayashalawam (Absalom's) ibaday (servants) yatzath (set) the chalaqah (field) on ash (fire).

Then Yawaab (Joab) qawam (rise up), and bawaa (come) to Abayashalawam (Absalom) to his bayath (house), and amar (spoke) to him, "Why have your ibad (servant) yatzath (set) my chalaqah (field) on ash (fire)?"

Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke) Yawaab (Joab), "Behold, I shalach (send) to you, amar (spoke), ‘bawaa (come) here, that I may shalach (send) you to the malak (king), to amar (spoke), "Why bawaa (come) I come from Gashawar (Geshur)? It would be tawab (good / proper function) for me to be there still. Now therefore raah (see) me see the malak (king) panayam (face); and if there is iwan (guilt/iniquity) in me, let him mawath (death) me."'"

So Yawaab (Joab) bawaa (come) to the malak (king), and nagad (told) him; and when he had qaraa (called) for Abayashalawam (Absalom), he bawaa (come) to the malak (king), and shachah (bowed) himself on his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land) panayam (face) the malak (king): and the malak (king) nashaq (kissed) Abayashalawam (Absalom).

It happened achar (other) this, that Abayashalawam (Absalom) ishah (make) him a marakabah (chariot) and sasayam (horses), and chamashayam (fifty) ayash (man / husband) to rawatz (run) panayam (face) him.

Abayashalawam (Absalom) shakam (rose) up early, and imad (stood) yad (hand) the darak (way) of the shair (gate). It was so, that when any ayash (man / husband) had a rayab (suit) which should bawaa (come) to the malak (king) for mashapat (judgment), then Abayashalawam (Absalom) qaraa (called) to him, and amar (spoke), "ay (what) iyar (city) are you from?" He amar (spoke), "Your ibad (servant) is of achad (one) of the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel)."

Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke) to him, "raah (see), your dabar (word / matter) are tawab (good / proper function) and nakach (right); but there is no man deputized by the malak (king) to shamai (hearken / hear) you."

Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke) moreover, "Oh that I were shawam (place / establish / appoint) shapat (judge / judgement) in the aratz (Earth/land), that every ayash (man / husband) who has any rayab (suit) or cause might bawaa (come) to me, and I would tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) him justice!"
It was so, that when any ayash (man / husband) qarab (come close) near to shachah (do) him obeisance, he shalach (send) forth his yad (hand), and chazaq (took) hold of him, and nashaq (kissed) him.

Abayashalawam (Absalom) ishah (make) this sort of thing to all Yashar-Al (Israel) who bawaa (come) to the malak (king) for mashapat (judgment). So Abayashalawam (Absalom) ganab (stole) the lab (heart) of the ishah (make) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

It happened at the qatz (end) of arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years), that Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "Please yalak (let) me go and shalam (pay) my nadar (vow), which I have nadar (make vow) to Yahawah, in Chabarawan (Hebron).

For your ibad (servant) nadar (make vow) a nadar (vow) while I stayed at Gashawar (Geshur) in Aram (Syria), amar (spoke), ‘If Yahawah shall indeed shawab (turn back / repent) me again to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), then I will ibad (servant) Yahawah.'"
The malak (king) amar (spoke) to him, "yalak (go) in shalawam (peace / safety)." So he qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) to Chabarawan (Hebron).

But Abayashalawam (Absalom) shalach (send) maragalayam (spies) throughout all the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel), amar (spoke), "As soon as you shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn), then you shall amar (spoke), ‘Abayashalawam (Absalom) is malak (king) in Chabarawan (Hebron)!'"

Two maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) halak (move) with Abayashalawam (Absalom) out of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), who were qaraa (called), and halak (move) in their tham (simplicity); and they didn't yadai (know) anything.

Abayashalawam (Absalom) shalach (send) for Achayathapal (Ahithophel) the gayalanay (gilonite), Dawad (David's) yaitz (counselor), from his iyar (city), even from Galah (Giloh), while he was zabach (offering) the zabachayam (sacrifices). The qashar (conspiracy) was amayatz (strong); for the im (nation / people) rab (increased) halak (move) with Abayashalawam (Absalom).
A nagad (messenger) bawaa (come) to Dawad (David), amar (spoke), "The lab (heart) of the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) are achar (other) Abayashalawam (Absalom)."

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to all his ibad (servant) who were with him at Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), "qawam (rise up), and let us barach (flee); for else none of us shall palayatah (escape) from Abayashalawam (Absalom). Mahar (make) speed to depart, lest he nashag (overtake) us mahar (quickly), and nadach (bring) down rai (evil) on us, and nakah (strike) the iyar (city) with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword)."
The malak (king) ibaday (servants) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "Behold, your ibaday (servants) are ready to do whatever my Adawan the malak (king) bachar (chooses)."

The malak (king) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and all his bayath (house) ragal (feet / foot) him. The malak (king) izab (left) ishar (ten) nashayam (women), who were palagashayam (concubines), to shamar (keep/guard) the bayath (house).
The malak (king) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and all the im (nation / people) ragal (feet / foot) him; and they imad (stayed) in Beth Merhak.

All his ibad (servant) ibar (pass over/through) on yad (hand) him; and all the Karathay (Cherethites), and all the Palathay (Pelethites), and all the Gathay (Gittites), shash (six) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) who bawaa (come) ragal (feet / foot) him from gath (gath), ibar (pass over/through) on panayam (face) the malak (king).

Then the malak (king) amar (spoke) to Athay (Ittai) the Gathay (Gittite), "Why do you also yalak (go) with us? Shawab (turn back / repent), and stay with the malak (king); for you are a nakaray (foreigner), and also an galah (exile). Return to your own maqawam (place).

Whereas you bawaa (come) but thamawal (yesterday), should I this yawam (day) yalak (make) you go up and down with us, since I halak (move) where I may? Shawab (turn back / repent), and shawab (turn back / repent) back your ach (brother/kinsman). Chasad (grace) and amath (truth) be with you."

Athay (Ittai) inah (answer / respond) the malak (king), and inah (answer / respond), "As Yahawah chayayam (lives), and as my Adawan the malak (king) chayayam (lives), surely in what maqawam (place) my Adawan the malak (king) shall is, whether for mawath (death) or for chay (life), even there also will your ibad (servant) be."

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Athay (Ittai), "yalak (go) and ibar (pass over/through) over." Athay (Ittai) the Gathay (Gittite) ibar (pass over/through) over, and all his ibar (pass over/through), and all the little tap (ones) who were with him.

All the aratz (Earth/land) bakah (wept) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice), and all the im (nation / people) ibar (pass over/through) over: the malak (king) also himself ibar (pass over/through) over the nachal (stream / river) Qadarawan (Kidron), and all the im (nation / people) ibar (pass over/through) over, panayam (face) the darak (way) of the madabar (wilderness).

Behold, Tzadawaq (Zadok) also came, and all the Lawayay (Levites) with him, nashaa (lift) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Alahayam; and they yatzaq (set) down the arawan (ark) of Alahayam; and Abayathar (Abiathar) ilah (go up / offer) up, until all the im (nation / people) finished ibar (pass over/through) out of the iyar (city).

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Tzadawaq (Zadok), "shawab (turn back / repent) back the arawan (ark) of Alahayam into the iyar (city). If I matzaa (find) favor in the iyanay (eyes) of Yahawah, he will shawab (turn back / repent) me again, and show me both it, and his nawah (habitation);
But if he amar (spoke) thus, ‘I chapatz (have) no delight in you;' behold, here am I. Let him ishah (make) to me as seems tawab (good / proper function) to him."

The malak (king) amar (spoke) also to Tzadawaq (Zadok) the kahan (priest), "Aren't you a seer? Shawab (turn back / repent) into the iyar (city) in shalawam (peace / safety), and your shanayam (two) ban (son) with you, Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) your ban (son), and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) the ban (son) of Abayathar (Abiathar).
Raah (see), I will mahah (stay) at the fords of the madabar (wilderness), until dabar (word / matter) bawaa (come) from you to inform me."
Tzadawaq (Zadok) therefore and Abayathar (Abiathar) shawab (turn back / repent) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam again to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); and they stayed there.

Dawad (David) ilah (go up / offer) up by the ascent of the Mount of zayathayam (olives), and bakah (wept) as he ilah (go up / offer) up; and he had his raash (head) chapah (covered), and halak (move) yachap (barefoot): and all the im (nation / people) who were with him chapah (covered) every ayash (man / husband) his raash (head), and they ilah (go up / offer) up, bakah (weeping) as they ilah (go up / offer) up.

Someone nagad (told) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), "Achayathapal (Ahithophel) is among the conspirators with Abayashalawam (Absalom)." Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "Yahawah, please turn the itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal (Ahithophel) into foolishness."

It happened that when Dawad (David) bawaa (come) come to the raash (head), where Alahayam was shachah (worshiped), behold, Chawashay (Hushai) the arakay (archite) came to qaraah (meet) him with his kathanath (coat) qarai (torn), and adamah (earth) on his raash (head).
Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to him, "If you ibar (pass over/through) on with me, then you will be a mashaa (burden) to me;

But if you shawab (turn back / repent) to the iyar (city), and amar (spoke) Abayashalawam (Absalom), ‘I will be your ibad (servant), O malak (king). As I have been your ab (father) ibad (servant) in az (time) past, so will I now be your ibad (servant); then will you parar (defeat) for me the itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal (Ahithophel).'

Don't you have Tzadawaq (Zadok) and Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahanayam (priests) there with you? Therefore it shall be, that whatever thing you shall shamai (hearken / hear) out of the malak (king) bayath (house), you shall nagad (tell) it to Tzadawaq (Zadok) and Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahanayam (priests).

Behold, they have there with them their shanayam (two) ban (son), Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz), Tzadawaq (Zadok's) son, and Yahawanathan (Jonathan), Abayathar (Abiathar's) yad (hand); and by them you shall shalach (send) to me everything that you shall shamai (hearken / hear)."
So Chawashay (Hushai), Dawad (David's) raih (friend), bawaa (come) into the iyar (city); and Abayashalawam (Absalom) bawaa (come) into Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

When Dawad (David) was a mait (little) past the raash (head), behold, Tzayabaa (Ziba) the nair (servant) of Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth) qaraa (called) him, with a tzamad (couple) of donkeys chabash (saddled), and on them two maah (hundred) loaves of lacham (bread), and one maah (hundred) clusters of tzamawaqayam (raisins), and one maah (hundred) qayatz (summer) fruits, and a nabal (bottle) of yayan (wine).

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Tzayabaa (Ziba), What do you mean by these? Tzayabaa (Ziba) amar (spoke), The donkeys are for the malak (king) bayath (house) to rakab (ride) on; and the lacham (bread) and qayatz (summer) fruit for the nair (young) men to akal (eat); and the yayan (wine), that such as are yaip (faint) in the madabar (wilderness) may shathah (drinks).

The malak (king) amar (spoke), "Where is your adawan (master / lord) ban (son)?" Tzayabaa (Ziba) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "Behold, he is staying in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); for he amar (spoke), ‘Today the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) will shawab (turn back / repent) me the mamalakawath (kingdom) of my ab (father).'"

Then the malak (king) amar (spoke) to Tzayabaa (Ziba), "Behold, all that pertains to Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth) is yours." Tzayabaa (Ziba) amar (spoke), "I shachah (do) obeisance. Let me matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (eye), my Adawan, O malak (king)."

When malak (king) Dawad (David) bawaa (come) to Bacharayam (Bahurim), behold, a ayash (man / husband) of the mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) of the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, whose sham (name) was Shamaiy (Shimei), the ban (son) of Garaa (Gera). He yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and qalal (cursed) still as he yatzaa (go out / come out).

He saqal (cast) abanayam (stones) at Dawad (David), and at all the ibaday (servants) of malak (king) Dawad (David), and all the im (nation / people) and all the gabawar (mighty) men were on his right yamayan (right hand) and on his shamaawal (left hand).
Shamaiy (Shimei) amar (spoke) when he qalal (cursed), "Be yatzaa (go out / come out), be yatzaa (go out / come out), you ayash (man / husband) of dam (blood), and base ayash (man / husband)!

Yahawah has shawab (turn back / repent) on you all the dam (blood) of the bayath (house) of Shaawal (Saul), in whose place you have malak (king)! Yahawah nathan (give) delivered the malawakah (kingdom) into the yad (hand) of Abayashalawam (Absalom) your ban (son)! Behold, you are caught by your own rai (mischief), because you are a ayash (man / husband) of dam (blood)!"

Then Abayashay (Abishai) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "Why should this mawath (death) kalab (dog) qalal (curse) my Adawan the malak (king)? Please let me ibar (pass over/through) over and sawar (take) off his raash (head)."

The malak (king) amar (spoke), "What have I to do with you, you banay (sons) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah)? Because he qalal (curses), and because Yahawah has amar (spoke) to him, ‘qalal (curse) Dawad (David);' who then shall amar (spoke), ‘Why ishah (make) you done so?'"

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Abayashay (Abishai), and to all his ibad (servant), "Behold, my ban (son), who yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from my maih (bowels), baqash (seeks) my napash (soul). How much more this Banayamayanay (Benjamite), now? Leave him yanach (alone), and let him qalal (curse); for Yahawah has invited him.
It may be that Yahawah will raah (see) on the wrong done to me, and that Yahawah will repay me tawab (good / proper function) for the qalalah (cursing) of me today."

So Dawad (David) and his ayash (man / husband) yalak (went) by the darak (way); and Shamaiy (Shimei) halak (move) along on the hillside opposite him, and qalal (cursed) as he halak (move), saqal (threw) abanayam (stones) at him, and saqal (threw) ipar (dust).
The malak (king), and all the im (nation / people) who were with him, bawaa (come) iyap (weary); and he napash (soul) himself there.
Abayashalawam (Absalom), and all the im (nation / people), the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel), bawaa (come) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and Achayathapal (Ahithophel) with him.

It happened, when Chawashay (Hushai) the arakay (archite), Dawad (David's) raih (friend), bawaa (come) come to Abayashalawam (Absalom), that Chawashay (Hushai) amar (spoke) to Abayashalawam (Absalom), "Long chayah (live) the malak (king)! Long chayah (live) the malak (king)!"
Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke) to Chawashay (Hushai), "Is this your chasad (grace) to your rai (neigbor/another person)? Why didn't you halak (move) with your rai (neigbor/another person)?"

Chawashay (Hushai) amar (spoke) to Abayashalawam (Absalom), "No; but whomever Yahawah, and this im (nation / people), and all the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) have bachar (chosen), his will I be, and with him I will stay.
Again, whom should I ibad (servant)? Shouldn't I panayam (face) in the presence of his ban (son)? As I have ibad (servant) in your ab (father) panayam (face), so will I be in your panayam (face)."
Then Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke) to Achayathapal (Ahithophel), "yahab (give) your itzah (counsel) what we shall ishah (make)."

Achayathapal (Ahithophel) amar (spoke) to Abayashalawam (Absalom), "bawaa (come) in to your ab (father) palagashay (concubines), that he has yanach (left) to shamar (keep/guard) the bayath (house). Then all Yashar-Al (Israel) will shamai (hearken / hear) that you are baash (abhorred) by your ab (father). Then the yaday (hands) of all who are with you will be chazaq (strong)."

So they natah (spread) Abayashalawam (Absalom) a ahal (tent) on the gag (top) of the house; and Abayashalawam (Absalom) bawaa (come) in to his ab (father) palagashay (concubines) in the iyan (eye) of all Yashar-Al (Israel).

The itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal (Ahithophel), which he yaitz (gave) in those yamayam (days), was as if a man inquired at the dabar (word / matter) of Alahayam: so was all the itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal (Ahithophel) both with Dawad (David) and with Abayashalawam (Absalom).

Moreover Achayathapal (Ahithophel) amar (spoke) to Abayashalawam (Absalom), "Let me now bachar (choose) shanayam (two) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband), and I will qawam (rise up) and radap (pursue) achar (other) Dawad (David) tonight.

I will bawaa (come) on him while he is yagai (weary) and exhausted, and will make him charad (afraid). All the im (nation / people) who are with him shall nawas (flee). I will nakah (strike) the malak (king) only;

And I will shawab (turn back / repent) back all the im (nation / people) to you. The ayash (man / husband) whom you baqash (seek) is as if shawab (turn back / repent) returned. All the im (nation / people) shall be in shalawam (peace / safety)."
The dabar (word / matter) yashar (upright) Abayashalawam (Absalom) iyan (eye), and all the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel).
Then Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke), "Now qaraa (called) Chawashay (Hushai) the arakay (archite) also, and shamai (hearken / hear) us hear likewise what he pah (says)."

When Chawashay (Hushai) bawaa (come) come to Abayashalawam (Absalom), Abayashalawam (Absalom) amar (spoke) to him, amar (spoke), "Achayathapal (Ahithophel) has dabar (word / matter) like this. Shall we ishah (make) dabar (word / matter) he says? If not, dabar (word / matter) up."
Chawashay (Hushai) amar (spoke) to Abayashalawam (Absalom), "The itzah (counsel) that Achayathapal (Ahithophel) has yaitz (given) paim (this) time is not tawab (good / proper function)."

Chawashay (Hushai) amar (spoke) moreover, "You yadai (know) your ab (father) and his yadai (men), that they are gabawar (mighty) men, and they are fierce in their napash (soul), like a dab (bear) robbed of her cubs in the shadah (field). Your ab (father) is a ayash (man / husband) of malachamah (war), and will not lawan (lodge) with the im (nation / people).

Behold, he is now chabaa (hidden) in some pachath (pit), or in some other maqawam (place). It will happen, when some of them napal (fall / be cast down) fallen at the thachalah (first), that whoever shamai (hearken / hear) it will amar (spoke), ‘There is a magapah (slaughter) among the im (nation / people) who achar (other) Abayashalawam (Absalom)!'

Even he who is ban (son), whose lab (heart) is as the lab (heart) of a aray (lion), will masas (utterly) masas (melt); for all Yashar-Al (Israel) yadai (knows) that your ab (father) is a gabawar (mighty) man, and those who are with him are chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) banay (men).

But I yaitz (counsel) that all Yashar-Al (Israel) be asap (gathered) asap (together) to you, from Dan (Dan) even to Baar-Shabai (Beersheba), as the chawal (sand) that is by the yam (sea/waters) for rab (multitude); and that you halak (move) to qarab (battle) in your own panayam (face).

So shall we bawaa (come) on him in some maqawam (place) where he shall be matzaa (found), and we will matzaa (light) on him as the tal (dew) napal (fall / be cast down) on the adamah (ground); and of him and of all the achad (one) who are with him we will not yathar (leave) so much as achad (one).

Moreover, if he be gone into a iyar (city), then shall all Yashar-Al (Israel) nashaa (lift) chabalayam (ropes) to that iyar (city), and we will sachab (draw) it into the nachal (stream / river), until there isn't gam (indeed / moreover) small tzarawar (stone) matzaa (found) there."

Abayashalawam (Absalom) and all the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke), "The itzah (counsel) of Chawashay (Hushai) the arakay (archite) is tawab (good / proper function) than the itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal (Ahithophel)." For Yahawah had ordained to parar (defeat) the tawab (good / proper function) itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal (Ahithophel), to the intent that Yahawah might bawaa (come) rai (evil) on Abayashalawam (Absalom).

Then Chawashay (Hushai) amar (spoke) to Tzadawaq (Zadok) and to Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahanayam (priests), "Achayathapal (Ahithophel) yaitz (counseled) Abayashalawam (Absalom) and the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel) that way; and I have yaitz (counseled) this way.

Now therefore shalach (send) maharah (quickly), and nagad (tell) Dawad (David), amar (spoke), ‘Don't lawan (lodge) this layal (night) at the fords of the madabar (wilderness), but by ibar (pass over/through) means ibar (pass over/through) over; lest the malak (king) be balai (swallowed) up, and all the im (nation / people) who are with him.'"

Now Yahawanathan (Jonathan) and Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) were imad (staying) by Iyanaragal (En Rogel); and a female shapachah (servant) used to halak (move) and nagad (tell) them; and they halak (move) and nagad (told) malak (king) Dawad (David). For they yakal (might) not be raah (see) to bawaa (come) into the iyar (city).

But a nair (boy) raah (see) them, and nagad (told) Abayashalawam (Absalom). Then they shanayam (two) yalak (went) away maharah (quickly), and bawaa (come) to the bayath (house) of a ayash (man / husband) in Bacharayam (Bahurim), who had a baar (well) in his chatzar (court); and they yarad (went) down there.

The ayashah (woman / wife) laqach (take / seize) and parash (spread) the masak (covering) over the baar (well's) panayam (face), and shatach (spread) out bruised grain on it; and nothing was yadai (known).

Abayashalawam (Absalom's) ibaday (servants) bawaa (come) to the ayashah (woman / wife) to the bayath (house); and they amar (spoke), "Where are Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) and Yahawanathan (Jonathan)?" The ayashah (woman / wife) amar (spoke) to them, "They ibar (pass over/through) gone over the mayakal (brook) of mayam (Waters)." When they had baqash (sought) and could not matzaa (find) them, they shawab (turn back / repent) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

It happened, achar (other) they had departed, that they ilah (go up / offer) up out of the baar (well), and yalak (went) and nagad (told) malak (king) Dawad (David); and they said to Dawad (David), "qawam (rise up) and pass maharah (quickly) over the mayam (Waters); for thus has Achayathapal (Ahithophel) counseled against you."

Then Dawad (David) qawam (rise up), and all the im (nation / people) who were with him, and they ibar (pass over/through) over the Yaradan (Jordan). By the baqar (morning) awar (light) there idar (lacked) not achad (one) of them who ibar (pass over/through) not gone over the Yaradan (Jordan).

When Achayathapal (Ahithophel) raah (see) that his itzah (counsel) was not ishah (make), he chabash (saddled) his donkey, and qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) home, to his iyar (city), and set his yalak (house) in tzawah (order), and hanged himself; and he mawath (death), and was qabar (bury) in the tomb of his ab (father).

Then Dawad (David) bawaa (come) to Machanayam (Mahanaim). Abayashalawam (Absalom) ibar (pass over/through) over the Yaradan (Jordan), he and all the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) with him.

Abayashalawam (Absalom) shawam (place / establish / appoint) Imashaa (Amasa) over the tzabaa (troop) instead of Yawaab (Joab). Now Imashaa (Amasa) was the ban (son) of a ayash (man / husband), whose sham (name) was Yatharaa (Ithra) the Yasharaalay (Israelite), who bawaa (come) in to Abayagayal (Abigail) the banath (daughter) of Nachash (Nahash), achawath (sister) to Tzarawayah (Zeruiah), Yawaab (Joab's) am (mother).
Yashar-Al (Israel) and Abayashalawam (Absalom) chanah (encamped) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Galaid (Gilead).

It happened, when Dawad (David) bawaa (come) come to Machanayam (Mahanaim), that Shabay (Shobi) the ban (son) of Nachash (Nahash) of Rabah (Rabbah) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), and Makayar (Machir) the ban (son) of Imayaal (Ammiel) of Laadabar (Lodebar), and Barazalay (Barzillai) the Galaiday (Gileadite) of Ragalayam (Rogelim),
Brought mashakab (beds), basins, yatzar (earthen) kalay (vessels), chatah (wheat), shairah (barley), qamach (meal), qalay (parched) grain, pawal (beans), lentils, roasted grain,

Dabash (honey), chamaah (butter), tzaan (sheep), and shapah (cheese) of the baqar (morning), for Dawad (David), and for the im (nation / people) who were with him, to akal (eat): for they amar (spoke), "The im (nation / people) are raib (hungry), and iyap (weary), and thirsty, in the madabar (wilderness)."

Dawad (David) paqad (visit) the im (nation / people) who were with him, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) sharay (captains) of alapayam (thousands) and sharay (captains) of maawath (hundreds) over them.

Dawad (David) shalach (send) forth the im (nation / people), a shalayashay (third) part under the yad (hand) of Yawaab (Joab), and a shalayashay (third) part under the yad (hand) of Abayashay (Abishai) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah), Yawaab (Joab's) ach (brother/kinsman), and a shalayashay (third) part under the yad (hand) of Athay (Ittai) the Gathay (Gittite). The malak (king) amar (spoke) to the im (nation / people), "I will yatzaa (go out / come out) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth with you anay (myself) also."

But the im (nation / people) amar (spoke), "You shall not yatzaa (go out / come out) forth; for if we nawas (flee) nawas (away), they will not shawam (place / establish / appoint) for us; neither if chatzay (half) of us mawath (death), will they shawam (place / establish / appoint) for us. But you are kamaw (worth) ishar (ten) alap (thousand) of us. Therefore now it is tawab (good / proper function) that you are ready to izar (help) us out of the iyar (city)."

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to them, "I will ishah (make) what seems yatab (best) to you." The malak (king) imad (stood) yad (hand) the shair (gate), and all the im (nation / people) yatab (went) out by maawath (hundreds) and by alapayam (thousands).

The malak (king) tzawah (commanded) Yawaab (Joab) and Abayashay (Abishai) and Athay (Ittai), amar (spoke), "Deal at (gently) for my sake with the nair (young) man, even with Abayashalawam (Absalom)." All the im (nation / people) shamai (hearken / hear) when the malak (king) tzawah (commanded) all the sharayam (captains) dabar (word / matter) Abayashalawam (Absalom).
So the im (nation / people) yatzaa (go out / come out) out into the shadah (field) qaraah (against) Yashar-Al (Israel): and the malachamah (battle) was in the yair (forest) of Aparayam (Ephraim).

The im (nation / people) of Yashar-Al (Israel) were nagap (struck) there panayam (face) the ibaday (servants) of Dawad (David), and there was a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) magapah (slaughter) there that yawam (day) of isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) men.

For the malachamah (battle) was there pawatz (spread) over the surface of all the aratz (Earth/land); and the yair (forest) akal (eat) more im (nation / people) that yawam (day) than the charab (sword) akal (eat).

Abayashalawam (Absalom) qaraa (called) to meet the panay (servants) of Dawad (David). Abayashalawam (Absalom) was rakab (riding) on his parad (mule), and the parad (mule) bawaa (come) under the shawabak (thick) boughs of a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) alah (oak / terebinth), and his raash (head) chazaq (caught) hold of the alah (oak / terebinth), and he was nathan (give) up between the sky and aratz (Earth/land); and the parad (mule) that was under him ibar (pass over/through) on.
A achad (one) ayash (man / husband) raah (see) it, and nagad (told) Yawaab (Joab), and said, "raah (see), I saw Abayashalawam (Absalom) thalah (hanging) in an alah (oak / terebinth)."

Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke) to the ayash (man / husband) who amar (spoke) him, "raah (see), you saw it, and why didn't you nakah (strike) him there to the aratz (Earth/land)? I nathan (give) have given you ishar (ten) pieces of kasap (silver), and a sash."

The ayash (man / husband) amar (spoke) to Yawaab (Joab), "lawaa (do not) I should shaqal (receive) a alap (thousand) pieces of kasap (silver) in my kap (hand), I still wouldn't shalach (send) forth my kap (hand) against the malak (king) ban (son); for in our azan (ear) the malak (king) tzawah (commanded) you and Abayashay (Abishai) and Athay (Ittai), amar (spoke), ‘Beware that none touch the nair (young) man Abayashalawam (Absalom).'

Aw (or) if I ishah (make) dealt falsely against his napash (soul) (and there is no dabar (word / matter) kachad (hidden) from the malak (king)), then you yourself would have yatzab (set) yourself against me."

Then Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke), "I'm not going to yachal (wait) like this with you." He laqach (take / seize) shalawash (three) shabatayam (darts) in his kap (hand), and thaqai (blow / sound alarm) them through the lab (heart) of Abayashalawam (Absalom), while he was yet chay (life) in the midst of the alah (oak / terebinth).
Ishar (ten) nair (young) men who nashaa (lift) Yawaab (Joab's) armor surrounded and nakah (struck) Abayashalawam (Absalom), and nakah (killed) him.

Yawaab (Joab) thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn), and the im (nation / people) shawab (turn back / repent) from radap (pursuing) achar (other) Yashar-Al (Israel); for Yawaab (Joab) chashak (darkness) back the im (nation / people).

They laqach (take / seize) Abayashalawam (Absalom), and shalak (cast) him into the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) pachath (pit) in the yair (forest), and raised over him a very gadawal (very great/important/mighty) gal (heap) of abanayam (stones). Then all Yashar-Al (Israel) nawas (fled) everyone to his ahal (tent).

Now Abayashalawam (Absalom) in his chay (life) had laqach (take / seize) and natzab (reared) up for himself the matzabath (pillar), which is in the malak (king) imaq (dale); for he amar (spoke), "I have no ban (son) to keep my sham (name) in memory." He qaraa (called) the matzabath (pillar) after his own sham (name); and it is qaraa (called) Abayashalawam (Absalom's) monument, to this yawam (day).

Then Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) the ban (son) of Tzadawaq (Zadok) amar (spoke), "Let me now rawatz (run), and bashar (bear) the malak (king) news, how that Yahawah has shapat (judge / judgement) him of his yad (hand)."

Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke) to him, "You shall not be the bearer of news this yawam (day), but you shall bashar (bear) news achar (other) yawam (day). But today you shall bashar (bear) no news, because the malak (king) ban (son) is mawath (death)."

Then Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke) to the Kawashay (Cushite), "yalak (go), nagad (tell) the malak (king) what you raah (see) seen!" The Kawashay (Cushite) shachah (bowed) himself to Yawaab (Joab), and rawatz (ran).

Then Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) the ban (son) of Tzadawaq (Zadok) amar (spoke) yet again to Yawaab (Joab), "But come mah (what) may, please let me also rawatz (run) achar (other) the Kawashay (Cushite)." Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke), "Why do you want to rawatz (run), my ban (son), since that you will matzaa (have) no reward for the news?"

"But come what may," he amar (spoke), "I will rawatz (run)." He amar (spoke) to him, "rawatz (run)!" Then Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) rawatz (ran) by the darak (way) of the kakar (plain), and outran the Kawashay (Cushite).

Now Dawad (David) was sitting between the shanayam (two) shairayam (gates): and the tzapah (watchman / keep watch) yalak (went) up to the gag (roof) of the shair (gate) to the chawamah (wall), and nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye), and raah (see), and, behold, a ayash (man / husband) running rawatz (alone).

The tzapah (watchman / keep watch) qaraa (called), and nagad (told) the malak (king). The malak (king) said, "If he is bashawarah (alone), there is news in his pah (mouth)." He yalak (came) closer and closer.

The tzapah (watchman / keep watch) raah (see) achar (other) ayash (man / husband) running; and the tzapah (watchman / keep watch) qaraa (called) to the shawair (porter), and amar (spoke), "Behold, a ayash (man / husband) running alone!" The malak (king) amar (spoke), "He also bashar (brings) news."

The tzapah (watchman / keep watch) amar (spoke), "I raah (see) the marawatzah (running) of the raashawan (first) one is like the marawatzah (running) of Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) the ban (son) of Tzadawaq (Zadok)." The malak (king) amar (spoke), "He is a tawab (good / proper function) ayash (man / husband), and bawaa (come) with tawab (good / proper function) news."

Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) qaraa (called), and amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "shalawam (peace / safety) is well." He shachah (bowed) himself before the malak (king) with his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land), and amar (spoke), "barak (blessed) is Yahawah your Alahayam, who has sagar (delivered) up the anashayam (men) who lifted up their yad (hand) against my Adawan the malak (king)!"

The malak (king) amar (spoke), "Is it shalawam (peace / safety) with the nair (young) man Abayashalawam (Absalom)?" Achayamaitz (Ahimaaz) amar (spoke), "When Yawaab (Joab) shalach (send) the malak (king) ibad (servant), even me your ibad (servant), I raah (see) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) hamawan (tumult), but I don't yadai (know) what it was."
The malak (king) amar (spoke), "sabab (turn) aside, and yatzab (stand) here." He sabab (turned) aside, and imad (stood) still.

Behold, the Kawashay (Cushite) bawaa (come). The Kawashay (Cushite) amar (spoke), "News for my Adawan the malak (king); for Yahawah has shapat (judge / judgement) you this yawam (day) of all those who qawam (rise up) up against you."

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to the Kawashay (Cushite), "Is it shalawam (peace / safety) with the nair (young) man Abayashalawam (Absalom)?" The Kawashay (Cushite) amar (spoke), "May the ayabay (enemies) of my Adawan the malak (king), and all who qawam (rise up) up against you to do you rai (harm), be as that nair (young) man is."

The malak (king) was much ragaz (moved), and ilah (go up / offer) up to the room over the shair (gate), and bakah (wept). As he yalak (went), he amar (spoke), "My ban (son) Abayashalawam (Absalom)! My ban (son), my ban (son) Abayashalawam (Absalom)! I wish I had mawath (death) for you, Abayashalawam (Absalom), my ban (son), my ban (son)!"
It was amar (spoke) Joab, "Behold, the malak (king) bakah (weeps) and bakah (mourns) for Abayashalawam (Absalom)."
The victory that day was turned into bakah (mourning) to all the people; for the people heard it said that day, "The malak (king) grieves for his son."
The im (nation / people) sneaked into the city that yawam (day), as im (nation / people) who are ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.
The king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, "My son Absalom, Absalom, my son, my son!"

Joab zaiq (came) into the house to the malak (king), and said, "You have shamed this day the panayam (face) of all your ban (son), who this day have saved your life, and the lives of your ban (son) and of your ban (son), and the lives of your wives, and the lives of your concubines;

In that you love those who hate you, and hate those who love you. For you have amar (spoke) this yawam (day), that princes and ibad (servant) are nothing to you. For today I perceive that if Absalom had yawam (day), and kal (every) we had died this yawam (day), then it would have panayam (face) you well.

Now therefore arise, ayan (NO ONE) out, and nagad (speak) to comfort your ibadayam (servants); for I swear by Yahawah, if you don't ayan (NO ONE) out, not a yadai (man) will stay with you this night. That would be worse to you than all the evil that yadai (has) happened to you from your youth until now."

Then the king qawam (rise up), and sat in the gate. They dabar (word / matter) to all the ayash (man / husband), dabar (word / matter), "Behold, the king is sitting in the gate." All the ayash (man / husband) bawaa (come) ath (entirety) the king. Now Israel had fled every ayash (man / husband) to his tent.

All the im (nation / people) were at strife throughout all the tribes of Yashar-Al (Israel), amar (spoke), "The malak (king) delivered us out of the hand of our qawam (rise up), and he saved us out of the hand of the Philistines; and now he has nawas (fled) out of the land from Absalom.
Abayashalawam (Absalom), whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle. Now therefore why don't you amar (spoke) a word of bringing the malak (king) back?"

Malak (king) David shawab (turn back / repent) to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, shawab (turn back / repent), "charash (speak) to the elders of Judah, shawab (turn back / repent), ‘Why are you the last to shawab (turn back / repent) the malak (king) shawab (turn back / repent) to his house? Since the speech of all Israel il (over) come to the malak (king), to return him to his house.
You are my brothers, you are my bone and my flesh. Why then are you the acharawan (last) to shawab (turn back / repent) back the malak (king)?'

Shawab (turn back / repent) to Amasa, ‘Aren't you my itzam (bone) and my bashar (flesh)? Alahayam hayah (came to pass) so to me, and more also, if you aren't captain of the army before me shawab (turn back / repent) in the room of Joab.'"
He bowed the heart of all the ishah (make) of Judah, even as one ishah (make); so that they sent to the king, saying, "Return, you and all your servants."

So the malak (king) shawab (turn back / repent), and shawab (turn back / repent) to the Jordan. Yahawadah (Judah) shawab (turn back / repent) to Gilgal, to natah (go) to meet the malak (king), to shalach (send) the malak (king) over the Jordan.
Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite, who was of Bahurim, hurried and shawab (turn back / repent) down with the ibar (pass over/through) of Yahawadah (Judah) to qaraah (meet) malak (king) David.

There were a thousand ayash (man / husband) of banayamayanay (benjamin) with him, and Ziba the ban (son) of the house of Saul, and his fifteen ban (son) and his twenty ban (son) with him; and they yarad (went) through the Jordan in the presence of the malak (king).

A ferry boat tzalach (went) to bring over the malak (king) bayath (house), and to do what he thought ayash (man / husband). Shimei the ban (son) of Gera fell down panayam (face) the malak (king), when he had come over the Yaradan (Jordan).

He said to the malak (king), "Don't let my Adawan impute iniquity to me, nor remember that which your ban (son) ibar (pass over/through) perversely the day that my Adawan the malak (king) ibar (pass over/through) out of Jerusalem, that the malak (king) should ibar (pass over/through) it to his heart.

For your ibad (servant) knows that I have iwan (guilt/iniquity). Therefore, behold, I yatzaa (go out / come out) come this yawam (day) the first of all the house of Joseph to yatzaa (go out / come out) down to meet my Adawan the malak (king)."
But Abishai the son of Zeruiah yadai (answered), "Shall Shimei not be put to death for this, because he cursed Yahawah anointed?"

Yahawah (David) amar (spoke), "What have I to do with you, you ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah), that you should this day be adversaries to me? Shall there any ban (son) be put to mawath (death) this day in Abayashay (Israel)? For don't I know that I am this day king over Abayashay (Israel)?"
The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Shimei, "You shall not mawath (death)." The malak (king) swore to him.

Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the malak (king); and he had laa (NOT) groomed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from the day the malak (king) departed until the day he came home in peace.
It happened, when he bawaa (come) come to Jerusalem to qaraah (meet) the malak (king), that the malak (king) said to him, "Why didn't you yarad (go) with me, Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth)?"

He amar (spoke), "My Adawan, O malak (king), my servant deceived me. For your servant amar (spoke), I will saddle me a donkey, that I may ride thereon, and bawaa (come) with the malak (king); because your servant is lame.
He has slandered your ibad (servant) to my Adawan the malak (king); but my Adawan the malak (king) is as an angel of Alahayam. Do therefore what is good in your eyes.

For all my father's house were but dead ishah (make) before my Adawan the malak (king); yet you ishah (make) your ibad (servant) among those who ate at your own table. What right therefore ishah (make) I yet that I should cry any more to the malak (king)?"
The malak (king) said to him, "Why do you speak any more of your matters? I say, you and Ziba divide the land."
Mephibosheth amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "Yes, let him chalaq (take) all, because my Adawan the malak (king) chalaq (has) come in peace to his own house."
Barzillai the Gileadite bawaa (come) down from Rogelim; and he bawaa (come) over the Jordan with the malak (king), to conduct him over the Jordan.

Now Barazalay (Barzillai) was a very ibar (pass over/through) man, even eighty years old: and he had provided the malak (king) with sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; for he was a very great ibar (pass over/through).
The malak (king) said to Barazalay (Barzillai), "ban (son) over with me, and I will kawal (all) you with me in Jerusalem."
Barazalay (Barzillai) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should ibar (pass over/through) up with the malak (king) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem)?

I am this yawam (day) eighty shanay (years) yawam (day). Can I discern between mah (good) and bad? Can your servant taste what I eat or what I drink? Can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women? Why then should your servant be yet a burden to my Adawan the malak (king)?
Your ibad (servant) would but just go over the Jordan with the malak (king). Why should the malak (king) repay me with such a reward?

Please let your ibad (servant) ibar (pass over/through) back again, that I may die in my own city, by the grave of my father and my mother. But behold, your ibad (servant) Chimham; let him ibar (pass over/through) over with my Adawan the malak (king); and ibar (pass over/through) to him what shall seem mah (good) to you."

The malak (king) shawab (turn back / repent), "Kamaham (Chimham) shall ibar (pass over/through) over with me, and I will ishah (make) to him that which shall seem tawab (good / proper function) to you. Whatever you require of me, that I will ishah (make) for you."

All the people ibar (pass over/through) over the Kamaham (Jordan), and the malak (king) ibar (pass over/through) over. Then the malak (king) kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned to his own kal (every).

So the malak (king) ibar (pass over/through) over to Gilgal, and Chimham ibar (pass over/through) over with him. All the im (nation / people) of Judah ibar (pass over/through) the malak (king) over, and also half the im (nation / people) of Israel.

Behold, all the yaibaraw (men) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ibar (pass over/through) to the malak (king), and said to the malak (king), "Why have our brothers the yaibaraw (men) of Yahawadah (Judah) stolen you away, and ibar (pass over/through) the malak (king), and his household, over the Kamaham (Jordan), and all David's yaibaraw (men) with him?"

All the anashay (men) of Yahawadah (Judah) amar (spoke) the anashay (men) of Yashar-Al (Israel), "Because the malak (king) is a close relative to us. Why then are you angry about this matter? Have we bawaa (come) at kal (every) at the malak (king) cost? Or has he bawaa (come) us any gift?"

The ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) inah (answer / respond) the ayash (man / husband) of Yahawadah (Judah), and inah (answer / respond), "We have ten dabar (word / matter) in the malak (king), and we have also more claim to David than you. Why then did you despise us, that our dabar (word / matter) should not be first had in inah (answer / respond) back our malak (king)?" The dabar (word / matter) of the ayash (man / husband) of Yahawadah (Judah) were fiercer than the dabar (word / matter) of the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

There qaraa (called) to be there a base ayash (man / husband), whose sham (name) was shabai (sheba), the ban (son) of Bakaray (Bichri), a Benjamite: and he thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn), and amar (spoke), "We have no chalaq (portion) in Dawad (David), neither have we nachalah (inheritance) in the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse). Ayash (man / husband) ayash (man / husband) to his ahal (tents), Yashar-Al (Israel)!"

So all the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up from achar (other) Dawad (David), and achar (other) shabai (sheba) the ban (son) of Bakaray (Bichri); but the ayash (man / husband) of Yahawadah (Judah) dabaq (joined) with their malak (king), from the Yaradan (Jordan) even to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

Dawad (David) bawaa (come) to his bayath (house) at Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); and the malak (king) laqach (take / seize) the ishar (ten) nashayam (women) his palagashayam (concubines), whom he had yanach (left) to shamar (keep/guard) the bayath (house), and nathan (give) them in custody, and kawal (all) them with sustenance, but didn't bawaa (come) in to them. So they were tzarar (shut) up to the yawam (day) of their mawath (death), chayawath (living) in alamanawath (widowhood).
Then the malak (king) amar (spoke) to Imashaa (Amasa), "zaiq (call) me the ayash (man / husband) of Yahawadah (Judah) together within shalawash (three) yamayam (days), and be here imad (present)."
So Imashaa (Amasa) yalak (went) to zaiq (call) the men of Yahawadah (Judah) together; but he stayed longer than the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) time which he had yaid (appointed) him.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Abayashay (Abishai), "Now shabai (sheba) the ban (son) of Bakaray (Bichri) will do us more harm than Abayashalawam (Absalom) did. Laqach (take / seize) your Adawan ibaday (servants), and radap (pursue) achar (other) him, lest he matzaa (get) himself batzar (fortified) irayam (cities), and natzal (escape) out of our iyan (eye)."

There yatzaa (go out / come out) out achar (other) him Yawaab (Joab's) anashay (men), and the Karathay (Cherethites) and the Palathay (Pelethites), and all the gabawar (mighty) men; and they yatzaa (go out / come out) out of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), to radap (pursue) achar (other) shabai (sheba) the ban (son) of Bakaray (Bichri).

When they were at the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) aban (stone) which is in Gabaiwan (Gibeon), Imashaa (Amasa) bawaa (come) to panayam (face) them. Yawaab (Joab) was clothed in his apparel of war that he had put on, and on it was a sash with a charab (sword) tzamad (fastened) on his waist in its thair (razor); and as he yatzaa (go out / come out) forth it yatzaa (go out / come out) out.

Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke) to Imashaa (Amasa), "Is it shalawam (peace / safety) with you, my ach (brother/kinsman)?" Yawaab (Joab) achaz (took) Imashaa (Amasa) by the zaqan (beard) with his yamayan (right hand) yad (hand) to nashaq (kiss) him.

But Imashaa (Amasa) shamar (keep/guard) no heed to the charab (sword) that was in Yawaab (Joab's) yad (hand). So he nakah (struck) him with it in the body, and shapak (shed) out his maih (bowels) to the aratz (Earth/land), and didn't shanah (strike) him again; and he mawath (death). Yawaab (Joab) and Abayashay (Abishai) his ach (brother/kinsman) radap (pursued) achar (other) shabai (sheba) the ban (son) of Bakaray (Bichri).

There imad (stood) by him ayash (man / husband) of Yawaab (Joab's) nair (young) men, and amar (spoke), "He who favors Yawaab (Joab), and he who is for Dawad (David), let him achar (other) Yawaab (Joab)!"

Imashaa (Amasa) lay galal (wallowing) in his dam (blood) in the thawak (midst) of the masalah (highway). When the ayash (man / husband) raah (see) that all the im (nation / people) imad (stood) still, he sabab (carried) Imashaa (Amasa) out of the masalah (highway) into the shadah (field), and shalak (cast) a bagad (garment) over him, when he raah (see) that everyone who bawaa (come) by him imad (stood) still.

When he was yagah (removed) out of the masalah (highway), all the ayash (man / husband) ibar (pass over/through) on achar (other) Yawaab (Joab), to radap (pursue) achar (other) shabai (sheba) the ban (son) of Bakaray (Bichri).

He ibar (pass over/through) through all the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel) to Abal (Abel), and to Bayathamaikah (Beth Maacah), and all the barayam (berites): and they were qalah (gathered) together, and bawaa (come) also achar (other) him.

They bawaa (come) and tzawar (besieged) him in Abal (Abel) of Bayathamaikah (Beth Maacah), and they shapak (cast) up a mound against the iyar (city), and it imad (stood) against the chayal (rampart); and all the im (nation / people) who were with Yawaab (Joab) shachath (battered) the chawamah (wall), to napal (fall / be cast down) it down.

Then a chakam (wise) ayashah (woman / wife) qaraa (called) out of the iyar (city), "shamai (hearken / hear), shamai (hearken / hear)! Please amar (spoke) to Yawaab (Joab), ‘qarab (come close) near here, that I may dabar (word / matter) with you.'"

He qarab (come close) near to her; and the ayashah (woman / wife) amar (spoke), "Are you Yawaab (Joab)?" He amar (spoke), "I am." Then she amar (spoke) to him, "shamai (hearken / hear) the dabaray (words) of your handmaid." He amar (spoke), "I do shamai (hearken / hear)."
Then she amar (spoke), amar (spoke), "They were used to dabar (word / matter) in raashawan (old) times, ‘They shall shaal (surely) shaal (ask) counsel at Abal (Abel);' and so they settled it.

I am among those who are shalam (peaceable) and aman (believe / have faith) in Yashar-Al (Israel). You baqash (seek) to mawath (death) a iyar (city) and a am (mother) in Yashar-Al (Israel). Why will you balai (swallow) up the nachalah (inheritance) of Yahawah?"
Yawaab (Joab) inah (answer / respond), "chalayalah (far) be it, chalayalah (far) be it from me, that I should balai (swallow) up or shachath (destroy).

The dabar (word / matter) is not so. But a ayash (man / husband) of the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim), shabai (sheba) the ban (son) of Bakaray (Bichri) by sham (name), has nashaa (lift) up his yad (hand) against the malak (king), even against Dawad (David). Nathan (give) him only, and I will depart from the iyar (city)." The ayashah (woman / wife) amar (spoke) to Yawaab (Joab), "Behold, his raash (head) shall be shalak (thrown) to you over the chawamah (wall)."

Then the ayashah (woman / wife) bawaa (come) to all the im (nation / people) in her chakamah (wisdom). They karath (cut) off the raash (head) of shabai (sheba) the ban (son) of Bakaray (Bichri), and shalak (threw) it out to Yawaab (Joab). He thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn), and they were pawatz (dispersed) from the iyar (city), every ayash (man / husband) to his ahal (tent). Yawaab (Joab) shawab (turn back / repent) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) to the malak (king).

Now Yawaab (Joab) was over all the tzabaa (troop) of Yashar-Al (Israel); and Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) was over the Karay (Cherethites) and over the Palathay (Pelethites);
And Adaram (Adoram) was over the men subject to forced mas (labor); and Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the ban (son) of Achayalawad (Ahilud) was the zakar (remember);
And Shayaa (Sheva) was sapar (book); and Tzadawaq (Zadok) and Abayathar (Abiathar) were kahanayam (priests);
And also Iyaraa (Ira) the yaaray (jairite) was kahan (priest) minister to Dawad (David).

There was a raib (famine) in the yamay (days) of Dawad (David) shalawash (three) shanayam (years), shanah (year) achar (other) shanah (year); and Dawad (David) baqash (sought) the panayam (face) of Yahawah. Yahawah amar (spoke), "It is for Shaawal (Saul), and for his bloody bayath (house), because he put to mawath (death) the Gabainay (Gibeonites)."

The malak (king) qaraa (called) the Gabainay (Gibeonites), and amar (spoke) to them (now the Gabainay (Gibeonites) were not of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), but of the yathar (remnant) of the Amaray (Amorites); and the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) had shabai (swear / take oath) to them: and Shaawal (Saul) baqash (sought) to nakah (kill) them in his qanaa (jealous) for the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah));

And Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to the Gabainay (Gibeonites), "What shall I ishah (make) for you? And with what shall I make kapar (atonement), that you may barak (blessed) the nachalah (inheritance) of Yahawah?"

The Gabainay (Gibeonites) amar (spoke) to him, "It is no matter of kasap (silver) or zahab (gold) between us and Shaawal (Saul), or his bayath (house); neither is it for us to put any ayash (man / husband) to mawath (death) in Yashar-Al (Israel)." He amar (spoke), "Whatever you amar (spoke), that will I ishah (make) for you."

They amar (spoke) to the malak (king), "The ayash (man / husband) who kalah (complete / finish) us, and who damah (devised) against us, that we should be destroyed from yatzab (remaining) in any of the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yashar-Al (Israel),

Let shabai (seven) anashayam (men) of his ban (son) be nathan (give) to us, and we will yaqai (hang) them up to Yahawah in Gabaih (Gibeah) of Shaawal (Saul), the bachayar (chosen) of Yahawah." The malak (king) amar (spoke), "I will nathan (give) them."

But the malak (king) chamal (spared) Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth), the ban (son) of Yahawanathan (Jonathan) the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul), because of Yahawah shabawaih (oath) that was between them, between Dawad (David) and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) the ban (son) of Shaawal (Saul).

But the malak (king) laqach (take / seize) the shanayam (two) banay (sons) of Ratzapah (Rizpah) the banath (daughter) of Ayah (Aiah), whom she yalad (birth / begot) to Shaawal (Saul), Aramanay (Armoni) and Mapayabashath (Mephibosheth); and the chamash (five) banay (sons) of Mayakal (Michal) the banath (daughter) of Shaawal (Saul), whom she yalad (birth / begot) to Idarayaal (Adriel) the ban (son) of Barazalay (Barzillai) the Meholathite.

He nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of the Gabainay (Gibeonites), and they hanged them in the har (mountain) panayam (face) Yahawah, and all shabai (seven) of them napal (fall / be cast down) yachad (together). They were put to mawath (death) in the yamay (days) of qatzayar (harvest), in the raashawan (first) days, at the thachalah (beginning) of shairah (barley) qatzayar (harvest).

Ratzapah (Rizpah) the banath (daughter) of Ayah (Aiah) laqach (take / seize) sackcloth, and natah (spread) it for her on the tzawar (rock), from the thachalah (beginning) of qatzayar (harvest) until mayam (Waters) was nathak (poured) on them from the sky. She allowed neither the iwap (flying) of the sky to nawach (rest) on them by yawamam (by day), nor the animals of the shadah (field) by layal (night).
It was nagad (told) Dawad (David) what Ratzapah (Rizpah) the banath (daughter) of Ayah (Aiah), the payalagash (concubine) of Shaawal (Saul), ishah (make) done.

Dawad (David) yalak (went) and laqach (take / seize) the itzamawath (bones) of Shaawal (Saul) and the itzamawath (bones) of Yahawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son) from the bailay (men) of Yabash (Jabesh Gilead), who had ganab (stolen) them from the rachab (street) of Bayath-Shaan (Beth Shan), where the Palashathay (Philistines) had hanged them, in the yawam (day) that the Palashathay (Philistines) nakah (killed) Shaawal (Saul) in Galabai (Gilboa);

And he ilah (go up / offer) up from there the itzamawath (bones) of Shaawal (Saul) and the itzamawath (bones) of Yahawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son): and they asap (gathered) the itzamawath (bones) of those who were hanged.

They qabar (bury) the itzamawath (bones) of Shaawal (Saul) and Yahawanathan (Jonathan) his ban (son) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Banayamayan (Benjamin) in Tzalai (Zela), in the tomb of Qayash (Kish) his ab (father): and they ishah (make) all that the malak (king) tzawah (commanded). Achar (other) that Alahayam was entreated for the aratz (Earth/land).

The Palashathay (Philistines) had malachamah (war) again with Yashar-Al (Israel); and Dawad (David) yarad (went) down, and his ibad (servant) with him, and lacham (fought) against the Palashathay (Philistines). Dawad (David) grew iwap (flying);

And Yashabawabanab (Ishbibenob), who was of the yalayaday (sons) of the Rapaa (giant), the mashaqal (weight) of whose qayan (spear) was shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shekels of nachashath (brass) in mashaqal (weight), he being armed with a chadash (new) sword, amar (spoke) to have nakah (slain) Dawad (David).

But Abayashay (Abishai) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah) izar (helped) him, and nakah (struck) the Palashathay (Philistine), and mawath (death) him. Then the ban (son) of Dawad (David) shabai (swear / take oath) to him, amar (spoke), "You shall yatzaa (go out / come out) no more out with us to malachamah (battle), that you don't kabah (quench) the nayar (lamp) of Yashar-Al (Israel)."

It came to pass achar (other) this, that there was again malachamah (war) with the Palashathay (Philistines) at Gab (Gob): then Sabakay (Sibbecai) the chashathay (hushathite) nakah (killed) Sap (Saph), who was of the yaladay (sons) of the Rapaa (giant).

There was again malachamah (war) with the Palashathay (Philistines) at Gab (Gob); and Alachanan (Elhanan) the ban (son) of Yairayaaragayam (Jaareoregim) the bayathahalachamay (bethlehemite) nakah (killed) Galayath (Goliath) the gathay (gittite's) brother, the itz (staff) of whose chanayath (spear) was like a aragayam (weavers) manawar (beam).

There was again malachamah (war) at gath (gath), where there was a ayash (man / husband) of great madawan (stature), who had on every yad (hand) shash (six) atzabaith (fingers), and on every ragal (feet / foot) shash (six) atzabaith (toes), arabai (four) and isharayam (twenty) in masapar (number); and he also was yalad (birth / begot) to the Rapaa (giant).
When he charap (defied) Yashar-Al (Israel), Yahawanathan (Jonathan) the ban (son) of Shamaiy (Shimei), Dawad (David's) ach (brother/kinsman), nakah (killed) him.

These arabai (four) were yalad (birth / begot) to the Rapaa (giant) in gath (gath); and they napal (fall / be cast down) by the yad (hand) of Dawad (David), and by the yad (hand) of his ibad (servant).

Dawad (David) dabar (word / matter) to Yahawah the dabaray (words) of this shayar (song) in the yawam (day) that Yahawah natzal (delivered) him out of the kap (hand) of all his ayab (enemy), and out of the kap (hand) of Shaawal (Saul):
And he amar (spoke), "Yahawah is my salai (rock), my matzawad (fortress), and my deliverer, even mine;

Alahayam, my tzawar (rock), in him I will take chasah (refuge); my magan (shield), and the qaran (horn) of my yashai (salvation), my high tower, and my manawas (refuge). My savior, you yashai (salvation) me from chamas (violence).
I will qaraa (called) on Yahawah, who is halal (praise) to be praised: So shall I be yashai (salvation) from my ayab (enemy).
For the mashabaray (waves) of mawath (death) surrounded me. The nachalay (floods) of ungodliness made me baith (afraid).
The chabalay (cords) of shaawal (Sheol / afterlife) were around me. The maqashay (snares) of mawath (death) caught me.

In my tzar (oppressor / distressor) I qaraa (called) on Yahawah. Yes, I qaraa (called) to my Alahayam. He shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice) out of his hayakal (temple). My cry came into his azan (ear).

Then the aratz (Earth/land) gaish (shook) and raish (trembled). The mawasadawath (foundations) of shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) ragaz (quaked) and were gaish (shaken), because he was charah (hot with anger).
Ishan (smoke) ilah (go up / offer) up out of his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting). Ash (fire) out of his pah (mouth) akal (eat). Gachalayam (coals) were bair (kindled) by it.
He natah (bowed) the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) also, and yarad (came) down. Irapal (thick) darkness was under his ragal (feet / foot).
He rakab (rode) on a karawab (cherub), and iwap (flying). Yes, he was raah (see) on the kanapay (wings) of the rawach (spirit / wind).
He shayath (put / appoint / make) chashak (darkness) sakawath (pavilions) around himself: gathering of mayam (Waters), and ib (thick) clouds of the shachaqayam (skies).
At the nagah (brightness) before him, gachalay (coals) of ash (fire) were bair (kindled).
Yahawah raim (thundered) from shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens). The Most ilayawan (Ilayawan) nathan (give) his qawal (sound / voice).
He shalach (send) out chatzayam (arrows), and pawatz (scattered) them; baraq (lightning), and confused them.

Then the apaqay (channels) of the yam (sea/waters) raah (see). The masadawath (foundations) of the thabal (world) were laid bare by the gairah (rebuke) of Yahawah, At the nashamah (breathing thing) of the rawach (spirit / wind) of his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).
He shalach (send) from on marawam (high) and he laqach (take / seize) me. He mashah (Moses) me out of many mayam (Waters).
He natzal (delivered) me from my iz (strong) ayab (enemy), from those who shanaa (hate) me, for they were too amatz (mighty) for me.
They qadam (came) on me in the yawam (day) of my ayad (calamity), but Yahawah was my support.
He also yatzaa (go out / come out) me out into a marachab (large) place. He chalatz (delivered) me, because he chapatz (delighted) in me.
Yahawah gamal (rewarded) me according to my tzadaqah (righteousness). He shawab (turn back / repent) me according to the bar (cleanness) of my yad (hand).
For I have shamar (keep/guard) the darakay (ways) of Yahawah, and have not wickedly departed from my Alahayam.
For all his mashapat (ordinances) were before me. As for his chaqah (statutes), I did not sawar (depart) from them.
I was also thamayam (complete / whole) toward him. I shamar (keep/guard) myself from my iwan (guilt/iniquity).
Therefore Yahawah has shawab (turn back / repent) me according to my tzadaqah (righteousness), According to my bar (cleanness) in his eyesight.
With the chasayad (merciful) you will show yourself chasad (grace). With the thamayam (complete / whole) gabawar (man) you will show yourself thamayam (complete / whole).
With the barar (pure) you will show yourself barar (pure). With the iqash (crooked) you will show yourself shrewd.
You will yashai (salvation) the inay (afflicted) im (nation / people), But your iyan (eye) are on the rawam (will lift up), that you may shapal (bring) them down.
For you are my nayar (lamp), Yahawah. Yahawah will nagah (light) up my chashak (darkness).
For by you, I rawatz (run) against a gadawad (troop). By my Alahayam, I dalag (leap) over a shawar (wall).
As for Al, his darak (way) is thamayam (complete / whole). The amarah (sayings) of Yahawah is tested. He is a magan (shield) to all those who take chasah (refuge) in him.
For who is Al, balaiday (besides) Yahawah? Who is a tzawar (rock), balaiday (besides) our Alahayam?
Al is my maiwaz (stronghold / fortress / protection) fortress. He nathar (makes) my darak (way) thamayam (complete / whole).
He shawah (makes) his ragal (feet / foot) shawah (like) ayalawath (hinds)' feet, and imad (sets) me on my bamah (high) places.
He teaches my yad (hand) to malachamah (war), so that my zarawai (arms) bend a qashath (bow) of nachawashah (brass).
You nathan (give) also given me the magan (shield) of your yashai (salvation). Your inah (oppress / afflict) rabah (has) made me great.
You have enlarged my tzaid (steps) under me. My qarasal (feet) have not maid (slipped).
I have radap (pursued) my ayab (enemy) and destroyed them. I didn't shawab (turn back / repent) again until they were kalah (complete / finish).
I napal (fall / be cast down) consumed them, and machatz (crush / shatter) them through, so that they can't qawam (rise up). Yes, they napal (fall / be cast down) fallen under my ragal (feet / foot).
For you have armed me with chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) for the malachamah (battle). You have karai (subdued) under me those who qawam (rise up) up against me.
You nathan (give) also made my ayab (enemy) turn their irap (neck) to me, that I might tzamath (cut) off those who shanaa (hate) me.
They shaih (looked), but there was none to yashai (salvation); even to Yahawah, but he didn't inah (answer / respond) them.
Then I shachaq (beat) them as small as the ipar (dust) of the aratz (Earth/land). I crushed them as the tayat (mire) of the chawatzawath (streets), and raqai (spread) them abroad.

You also have palat (delivered) me from the rayabay (strivings) of my im (nation / people). You have shamar (keep/guard) me to be the raash (head) of the gawayam (nations). A im (nation / people) whom I yadai (have) not known will ibad (servant) me.
The foreigners will kachash (submit) themselves to me. As soon as they shamai (hearken / hear) of me, they will shamai (hearken / hear) me.
The foreigners will nabal (fade) away, and will come trembling out of their masagarath (close) places.
Yahawah chay (life)! Barak (blessed) be my tzawar (rock)! Rawam (will lift up) be Alahayam, the tzawar (rock) of my yashai (salvation),
Even the Al who executes vengeance for me, who yarad (brings) down imayam (peoples) under me,

Who yatzaa (go out / come out) me away from my ayab (enemy). Yes, you rawam (will lift up) me up above those who qawam (rise up) up against me. You natzal (deliver) me from the chamas (violent) ayash (man / husband).
Therefore I will give yadah (thanks) to you, Yahawah, among the gawayam (nations). Will sing zamar (praises) to your sham (name).
He gives great yashawaih (salvation) to his malak (king), and shows loving chasad (grace) to his mashayach (anointed one), to Dawad (David) and to his zarai (seed), forevermore."

Now these are the acharawan (last) dabaray (words) of Dawad (David). Dawad (David) the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse) naam (declares prophetically), the gabar (man) who was qawam (rise up) on il (over) naam (declares prophetically), the mashayach (anointed one) of the Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob), the naiyam (sweet) zamayar (psalmist) of Yashar-Al (Israel):
"The rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah dabar (word / matter) by me. His malah (word) was on my lashawan (tongue / language).

The Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke), the tzawar (rock) of Yashar-Al (Israel) dabar (word / matter) to me, ‘One who mashal (rule/have dominion) over adam (men) righteously, who mashal (rule/have dominion) in the yaraah (fear) of Alahayam,

Shall be as the awar (light) of the baqar (morning), when the shamash (sun) zarach (rises), a baqar (morning) laa (NOT) ibawath (clouds), when the tender dashaa (grass) springs out of the aratz (Earth/land), through clear nagah (shining) after matar (rain).'

Most certainly my bayath (house) is not so with Al, yet he has shawam (place / establish / appoint) with me an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant), irak (ordered) in all things, and shamar (keep/guard), for it is all my yashai (salvation), and all my chapatz (desire), although he doesn't tzamach (make) it grow.
But all of the balayail (ungodly) shall be as qawatz (thorns) to be nadad (thrust) away, because they can't be laqach (take / seize) with the yad (hand),

But the ayash (man / husband) who touches them must be armed with barazal (iron) and the itz (staff) of a chanayath (spear). They shall be sharap (utterly) sharap (burned) with ash (fire) in their shabath (shabath / rest)."

These are the shamawath (names) of the gabawar (mighty) men whom Dawad (David) had: Josheb Basshebeth a Tahchemonite, raash (head) of the shalashay (captains); the same was Idayanaw (Adino) the itzan (eznite), against shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) chalal (slain) at achad (one) paim (time).

Achar (other) him was Alaizar (Eleazar) the ban (son) of Dawadaw (Dodai) the son of an Achawachay (Ahohite), one of the shalawash (three) gabawar (mighty) men with Dawad (David), when they charap (defied) the Palashathay (Philistines) who were there asap (gathered) together to malachamah (battle), and the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) were ilah (go up / offer) away.

He qawam (rise up), and nakah (struck) the Palashathay (Philistines) kay (surely) his yad (hand) was yagai (weary), and his yad (hand) froze to the charab (sword); and Yahawah ishah (make) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thashawaih (deliverance) that yawam (day); and the im (nation / people) shawab (turn back / repent) achar (other) him only to take pashat (spoil).

Achar (other) him was Shammah the ban (son) of Agaa (Agee) a hararay (hararite). The Palashathay (Philistines) were asap (gathered) together into a chay (life), where there was a plot of shadah (ground) full of lentils; and the im (nation / people) nawas (fled) from the Palashathay (Philistines).

But he yatzab (stood) in the thawak (midst) of the plot, and natzal (defended) it, and nakah (killed) the Palashathay (Philistines); and Yahawah ishah (make) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thashawaih (deliverance).

Three of the shalawashayam (thirty) raash (head) men yarad (went) down, and bawaa (come) to Dawad (David) in the qatzayar (harvest) time to the mairah (cave) of Idalam (Adullam); and the chay (life) of the Palashathay (Philistines) was chanah (encamped) in the imaq (valley) of Rapaa (Rephaim).
Dawad (David) was then in the stronghold; and the matzab (garrison) of the Palashathay (Philistines) was then in Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem).
