In the isharayam (twenty) - shabai (seven) shanah (year) of Asaa (Asa) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Zamaray (Zimri) malak (king) shabai (seven) yamayam (days) in Tharatzah (Tirzah). Now the im (nation / people) were chanah (encamped) against Gabathawan (Gibbethon), which belonged to the Palashathay (Philistines).

The im (nation / people) who were chanah (encamped) shamai (hearken / hear) amar (spoke), Zamaray (Zimri) has qashar (conspired), and has also nakah (struck) the malak (king): therefore all Yashar-Al (Israel) made Imaray (Omri), the shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop), malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel) that yawam (day) in the machanah (camp).
Imaray (Omri) ilah (go up / offer) up from Gabathawan (Gibbethon), and all Yashar-Al (Israel) with him, and they tzawar (besieged) Tharatzah (Tirzah).

It happened, when Zamaray (Zimri) raah (see) that the iyar (city) was lakad (taken), that he bawaa (come) into the aramawan (castle) of the malak (king) bayath (house), and burnt the malak (king) bayath (house) over him with ash (fire), and mawath (death),

For his chataah (sin) which he chataa (sinned) in ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, in yalak (walking) in the darak (way) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam), and in his chataah (sin) which he ishah (make), to make Yashar-Al (Israel) to chataa (sin).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabaray (acts) of Zamaray (Zimri), and his qashar (treason) that he committed, aren't they kathab (write) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabaray (chronicles) of the malakay (kings) of Yashar-Al (Israel)?

Then were the im (nation / people) of Yashar-Al (Israel) chalaq (divided) into chatzay (two) parts: chatzay (half) of the im (nation / people) hayah (came to pass) Thabanay (Tibni) the ban (son) of Gayanath (Ginath), to make him malak (king); and chatzay (half) achar (other) Imaray (Omri).

But the im (nation / people) who achar (other) Imaray (Omri) chazaq (prevailed) ath (entirety) the im (nation / people) who achar (other) Thabanay (Tibni) the ban (son) of Gayanath (Ginath): so Thabanay (Tibni) mawath (death), and Imaray (Omri) malak (king).

In the shalawashayam (thirty) - achad (one) shanah (year) of Asaa (Asa) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Imaray (Omri) began to malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel) for shanayam (two) shanayam (years). He malak (king) shash (six) shanayam (years) in Tharatzah (Tirzah).

He bought the har (mountain) Shamarawan (Samaria) of Shamar (Shemer) for two kakarayam (talents) of kasap (silver); and he banah (build) on the har (mountain), and qaraa (called) the sham (name) of the iyar (city) which he banah (build), after the sham (name) of Shamar (Shemer), the adawan (master / lord) of the har (mountain), Shamarawan (Samaria).
Imaray (Omri) ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, and dealt wickedly above all who were panayam (face) him.

For he yalak (walked) in all the darak (way) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Nabat (Nebat), and in his chataah (sin) with which he made Yashar-Al (Israel) to chataa (sin), to provoke Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), to kais (anger) with their habal (vanities).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabaray (acts) of Imaray (Omri) which he ishah (make), and his gabawarah (might) that he showed, aren't they kathab (write) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabaray (chronicles) of the malakay (kings) of Yashar-Al (Israel)?
So Imaray (Omri) shakab (slept) with his ab (father), and was qabar (bury) in Shamarawan (Samaria); and Achaab (Ahab) his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.

In the shalawashayam (thirty) - shamanah (eighth) shanah (year) of Asaa (Asa) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) began Achaab (Ahab) the ban (son) of Imaray (Omri) to malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel): and Achaab (Ahab) the ban (son) of Imaray (Omri) malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel) in Shamarawan (Samaria) isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) shanah (years).
Achaab (Ahab) the ban (son) of Imaray (Omri) ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah above all that were panayam (face) him.

It happened, as if it had been a qalal (light) thing for him to yalak (walk) in the chataawath (sins) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Nabat (Nebat), that he laqach (take / seize) as ayashah (woman / wife) Ayazabal (Jezebel) the banath (daughter) of Athabail (Ethbaal) malak (king) of the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), and yalak (went) and ibad (servant) Bail (Baal), and shachah (worshiped) him.
He qawam (rise up) up an mazabach (altar) for Bail (Baal) in the bayath (house) of Bail (Baal), which he had banah (build) in Shamarawan (Samaria).

Achaab (Ahab) ishah (make) the Asharah (Asherah); and Achaab (Ahab) ishah (make) yet more to provoke Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), to kais (anger) than all the malakay (kings) of Yashar-Al (Israel) who were panayam (face) him.

In his yawam (day) Chayaal (Hiel) the bayathahaalay (bethelite) banah (build) Yarayachaw (Jericho): he yasad (laid) its foundation with the loss of Abayaram (Abiram) his bakawar (firstborn), and natzab (set) up its dalath (gates) with the loss of his youngest son Shagawab (Segub), according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, which he dabar (word / matter) by Yahawashawai (Joshua) the ban (son) of Nawan (Nun).

Alayah (Elijah) the thashabay (tishbite), who was of the thashabay (foreigners) of Galaid (Gilead), amar (spoke) to Achaab (Ahab), "As Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), chay (life), panayam (face) whom I imad (stand), there shall not be tal (dew) nor matar (rain) these shanayam (years), but pah (according) to my dabar (word / matter)."
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to him, amar (spoke),
"Yalak (go) away from here, panah (turn) eastward, and sathar (hide) yourself by the nachal (stream / river) Karayath (Cherith), that is panayam (face) the Yaradan (Jordan).
It shall be, that you shall shathah (drinks) of the nachal (stream / river). I have tzawah (commanded) the irabayam (ravens) to kawal (all) you there."

So he yalak (went) and ishah (make) according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah; for he yalak (went) and lived by the nachal (stream / river) Karayath (Cherith), that is panayam (face) the Yaradan (Jordan).

The irabayam (ravens) bawaa (come) him lacham (bread) and bashar (flesh) in the baqar (morning), and lacham (bread) and bashar (flesh) in the irab (evening); and he shathah (drinks) of the nachal (stream / river).
It happened qatz (after) a yawam (day), that the nachal (stream / river) yabash (dry land) up, because there was no gasham (rain) in the aratz (Earth/land).
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to him, amar (spoke),
"Qawam (rise up), yalak (go) to Tzarapath (Zarephath), which belongs to Tzayadawan (Sidon), and stay there. Behold, I have tzawah (commanded) a alamanah (widow) there to kawal (all) you."

So he qawam (rise up) and yalak (went) to Tzarapath (Zarephath); and when he bawaa (come) to the pathach (gate) of the iyar (city), behold, a alamanah (widow) was there qashash (gathering) itzayam (sticks): and he qaraa (called) to her, and amar (spoke), "Please laqach (take / seize) me a mait (little) mayam (Waters) in a kalay (vessel), that I may shathah (drinks)."
As she was yalak (going) to laqach (take / seize) it, he qaraa (called) to her, and amar (spoke), "Please laqach (take / seize) me a path (morsel) of lacham (bread) in your yad (hand)."

She amar (spoke), "As Yahawah your Alahayam chay (life), I don't yash (have) a maiwag (cake), but a handful of qamach (meal) in the jar, and a mait (little) shaman (oil) in the jar. Behold, I am qashash (gathering) shanayam (two) itzayam (sticks), that I may bawaa (come) in and bake it for me and my ban (son), that we may akal (eat) it, and mawath (death)."

Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to her, "Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). Bawaa (come) and ishah (make) as you have dabar (word / matter); but ishah (make) me of it a qatan (small / young / least) igah (cake) raashawan (first), and yatzaa (go out / come out) it out to me, and acharawan (afterward) ishah (make) some for you and for your ban (son).

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), ‘The jar of qamach (meal) shall not empty, neither shall the jar of shaman (oil) chasar (fail), until the yawam (day) that Yahawah nathan (give) gasham (rain) on the adamah (earth).'"
She yalak (went) and ishah (make) according to the dabar (word / matter) of Alayah (Elijah): and she, and he, and her bayath (house), akal (eat) many yamayam (days).
The jar of qamach (meal) didn't empty, neither did the jar of shaman (oil) chasar (fail), according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, which he dabar (word / matter) by Alayah (Elijah).

It happened achar (other) these things, that the ban (son) of the ayashah (woman / wife), the bailah (mistress) of the bayath (house), chalah (afflict) sick; and his chalay (sickness) was so severe, that there was no nashamah (breathing thing) yathar (left) in him.

She amar (spoke) to Alayah (Elijah), "What have I to do with you, you ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam? You bawaa (come) come to me to zakar (remember) my iwan (guilt/iniquity) to memory, and to mawath (death) my ban (son)!"

He amar (spoke) to her, "nathan (give) me your ban (son)." He laqach (take / seize) him out of her chayaq (bosom), and ilah (go up / offer) him up into the room where he stayed, and shakab (laid) him on his own matah (bed).

He qaraa (called) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "Yahawah my Alahayam, have you also brought raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) on the alamanah (widow) with whom I stay, by mawath (death) her ban (son)?"

He madad (stretched) himself on the yalad (birth / begot) shalawash (three) paimayam (times), and qaraa (called) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "Yahawah my Alahayam, please let this yalad (birth / begot) napash (soul) shawab (turn back / repent) into him again."

Yahawah shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of Alayah (Elijah); and the napash (soul) of the yalad (birth / begot) shawab (turn back / repent) into him again, and he chayah (revived).

Alayah (Elijah) laqach (take / seize) the yalad (birth / begot), and yarad (brought) him down out of the room into the bayath (house), and nathan (give) him to his am (mother); and Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke), "raah (see), your ban (son) chay (life)."

The ayashah (woman / wife) amar (spoke) to Alayah (Elijah), "zah (this / that / these) I yadai (know) that you are a ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, and that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah in your pah (mouth) is amath (truth)."

It happened after many yamayam (days), that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Alayah (Elijah), in the shalayashay (third) shanah (year), amar (spoke), "yalak (go), show yourself to Achaab (Ahab); and I will nathan (give) matar (rain) on the adamah (earth)."
Alayah (Elijah) yalak (went) to show himself to Achaab (Ahab). The raib (famine) was severe in Shamarawan (Samaria).
Achaab (Ahab) qaraa (called) Ibadayah (Obadiah), who was over the bayath (house). (Now Ibadayah (Obadiah) yaraa (feared) Yahawah maad (greatly):

For it was so, when Ayazabal (Jezebel) karath (cut) off the nabayaay (prophets) of Yahawah, that Ibadayah (Obadiah) laqach (take / seize) one maah (hundred) nabayaay (prophets), and chabaa (hid) them by ayash (man / husband) in a mairah (cave), and kawal (all) them with lacham (bread) and mayam (Waters).)

Achaab (Ahab) amar (spoke) to Ibadayah (Obadiah), "yalak (go) through the aratz (Earth/land), to all the maiyanay (springs) of mayam (Waters), and to all the nachalayam (brooks). Perhaps we may matzaa (find) chatzayar (grass) and chayah (save) the sawas (horses) and parad (mules) chayah (alive), that we not karath (cut) all the animals."

So they chalaq (divided) the aratz (Earth/land) between them to ibar (pass over/through) throughout it: Achaab (Ahab) halak (move) achad (one) darak (way) by himself, and Ibadayah (Obadiah) halak (move) another darak (way) by himself.

As Ibadayah (Obadiah) was in the darak (way), behold, Alayah (Elijah) qaraah (met) him: and he recognized him, and napal (fall / be cast down) on his panayam (face), and amar (spoke), "Is it you, my Adawan Alayah (Elijah)?"
He amar (spoke) him, "It is I. Yalak (go), amar (spoke) your Adawan, ‘Behold, Alayah (Elijah) is here!'"
He amar (spoke), "Wherein have I chataa (sinned), that you nathan (give) deliver your ibad (servant) into the yad (hand) of Achaab (Ahab), to mawath (death) me?

As Yahawah your Alahayam chay (life), there is no gaway (heathen / nation) or mamalakah (kingdom), ashar (who/that) my Adawan has not shalach (send) to baqash (seek) you. When they amar (spoke), ‘He is not here,' he took an shabai (swear / take oath) of the mamalakah (kingdom) and gaway (heathen / nation), that they didn't matzaa (find) you.
Now you amar (spoke), ‘yalak (go), amar (spoke) your Adawan, "Behold, Alayah (Elijah) is here."'

It will happen, as soon as I am yalak (gone) from you, that the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah will nashaa (lift) you I don't yadai (know) where; and so when I bawaa (come) and nagad (tell) Achaab (Ahab), and he can't matzaa (find) you, he will harag (kill) me. But I, your ibad (servant), have yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah from my naiwar (youth).

Wasn't it nagad (told) my Adawan what I ishah (make) when Ayazabal (Jezebel) harag (kill) the nabayaay (prophets) of Yahawah, how I chabaa (hid) one maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) of Yahawah nabayaay (prophets) with chamashayam (fifty) to a mairah (cave), and kawal (all) them with lacham (bread) and mayam (Waters)?
Now you amar (spoke), ‘yalak (go), amar (spoke) your Adawan, "Behold, Alayah (Elijah) is here;"' and he will harag (kill) me."
Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke), "As Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) chay (life), panayam (face) whom I imad (stand), I will raah (see) show myself to him today."
So Ibadayah (Obadiah) yalak (went) to qaraah (meet) Achaab (Ahab), and nagad (told) him; and Achaab (Ahab) yalak (went) to qaraah (meet) Alayah (Elijah).
It happened, when Achaab (Ahab) raah (see) Alayah (Elijah), that Achaab (Ahab) amar (spoke) to him, "Is that you, you troubler of Yashar-Al (Israel)?"

He amar (spoke), "I have not ikar (troubled) Yashar-Al (Israel); but you, and your ab (father) bayath (house), in that you have forsaken the matzawath (commandments) of Yahawah, and you have yalak (followed) the Bail (Baals).

Now therefore shalach (send), and qabatz (gather) to me all Yashar-Al (Israel) to har (mountain) Karamal (Carmel), and arabai (four) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) of the nabayaay (prophets) of Bail (Baal), and arabai (four) maah (hundred) of the nabayaay (prophets) of the Asharah (Asherah), who akal (eat) at Ayazabal (Jezebel's) shalachan (table)."
So Achaab (Ahab) shalach (send) to all the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and qabatz (gathered) the nabayaayam (prophets) qabatz (together) to har (mountain) Karamal (Carmel).

Alayah (Elijah) nagash (came) near to all the im (nation / people), and amar (spoke), "How long will you waver between the shanayam (two) sides? If Yahawah is Alahayam, yalak (follow) him; but if Bail (Baal), then yalak (follow) him." The im (nation / people) inah (answer / respond) him not a dabar (word / matter).

Then Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to the im (nation / people), "I, even I only, am yathar (left) a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Yahawah; but Bail (Baal's) nabayaay (prophets) are arabai (four) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) ayash (man / husband).

Nathan (give) them therefore give us shanayam (two) parayam (bulls); and let them bachar (choose) achad (one) par (bull) for themselves, and nathach (cut) it in pieces, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it on the itz (wood), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) no ash (fire) under; and I will ishah (make) the other par (bull), and nathan (give) it on the itz (wood), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) no ash (fire) under it.

You qaraa (called) on the sham (name) of your Alahayam, and I will qaraa (called) on the sham (name) of Yahawah. The Alahayam who inah (answer / respond) by ash (fire), let him be Alahayam." All the im (nation / people) inah (answer / respond), "It is tawab (good / proper function) inah (answer / respond)."

Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to the nabayaay (prophets) of Bail (Baal), "bachar (choose) achad (one) par (bull) for yourselves, and ishah (make) it raashawan (first); for you are many; and qaraa (called) on the sham (name) of your Alahayam, but shawam (place / establish / appoint) no ash (fire) under it."

They laqach (take / seize) the par (bull) which was nathan (give) them, and they ishah (make) it, and qaraa (called) on the sham (name) of Bail (Baal) from baqar (morning) even until tzahar (noon), amar (spoke), Bail (Baal), inah (answer / respond) us. But there was no qawal (sound / voice), nor any who inah (answer / respond). They pasach (leaped) about the mazabach (altar) which was ishah (make).

It happened at tzahar (noon), that Alayah (Elijah) hathal (mocked) them, and amar (spoke), "qaraa (called) gadawal (very great/important/mighty); for he is a Alahayam. Either he is musing, or he has gone aside, or he is on a darak (journey), or perhaps he sleeps and must be awakened."
They qaraa (called) qawal (sound / voice), and gadad (cut) themselves in their mashapat (way) with knives and lances, until the dam (blood) shapak (gushed) out on them.

It was so, when tzahar (midday) was past, that they nabaa (prophesied) until the time of the ilah (go up / offer) of the ilah (go up / offer); but there was neither qawal (sound / voice), nor any to inah (answer / respond), nor any who qashab (regarded).

Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to all the im (nation / people), "nagash (come) near to me;" and all the im (nation / people) nagash (came) near to him. He rapaa (repaired) the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah that was haras (thrown) down.

Alayah (Elijah) laqach (take / seize) shanayam (two) abanayam (stones), according to the masapar (number) of the shabatay (tribes) of the banay (sons) of Yaiqab (Jacob), to whom the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came, amar (spoke), "Yashar-Al (Israel) shall be your sham (name)."

With the abanayam (stones) he banah (build) an mazabach (altar) in the sham (name) of Yahawah. He ishah (make) a thailah (trench) around the mazabach (altar), large enough to bayath (house) two saathayam (measures) of zarai (seed).

He irak (put) the itz (wood) in irak (order), and nathach (cut) the par (bull) in pieces, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it on the itz (wood). He said, "Fill four jars with water, and pour it on the burnt offering, and on the itz (wood)."
He amar (spoke), "Do it a shanah (second) time;" and they did it the shanah (second) time. He amar (spoke), "shanah (do) it a third time;" and they did it the shalash (three) time.
The mayam (Waters) yalak (ran) around the mazabach (altar); and he also malaa (filled) the thailah (trench) with mayam (Waters).

It happened at the time of the ilah (go up / offer) of the manachah (offering), that Alayah (Elijah) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) nagash (came) near, and amar (spoke), "Yahawah, the Alahayam of Abaraham (Abraham), of Yatzachaq (Isaac), and of Yashar-Al (Israel), yadai (let) it be known this yawam (day) that you are Alahayam in Yashar-Al (Israel), and that I am your ibad (servant), and that I ishah (make) done all these things at your dabar (word / matter).

Inah (answer / respond) me, Yahawah, inah (answer / respond) me, that this im (nation / people) may yadai (know) that you, Yahawah, are Alahayam, and that you have sabab (turned) their lab (heart) sabab (back) again."

Then the ash (fire) of Yahawah napal (fall / be cast down), and akal (eat) the burnt ilah (offering), and the itz (wood), and the abanayam (stones), and the ipar (dust), and lachak (licked) up the mayam (Waters) that was in the thailah (trench).
When all the im (nation / people) raah (see) it, they napal (fall / be cast down) on their panayam (face). They amar (spoke), "Yahawah, he is Alahayam! Yahawah, he is Alahayam!"

Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to them, "Seize the nabayaay (prophets) of Bail (Baal)! Don't let ayash (man / husband) of them malat (escape)!" They seized them. Alayah (Elijah) yarad (brought) them down to the nachal (stream / river) Qayashawan (Kishon), and shachat (killed) them there.
Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to Achaab (Ahab), "ilah (go up / offer) up, akal (eat) and shathah (drinks); for there is the qawal (sound / voice) of hamawan (abundance) of gasham (rain)."

So Achaab (Ahab) ilah (go up / offer) up to akal (eat) and to shathah (drinks). Alayah (Elijah) ilah (go up / offer) up to the raash (head) of Karamal (Carmel); and he bowed himself down on the aratz (Earth/land), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) his panayam (face) between his barak (blessed).

He amar (spoke) to his nair (servant), "ilah (go up / offer) up now, nabat (look) darak (toward) the yam (sea/waters)." He ilah (go up / offer) up, and nabat (looked), and amar (spoke), "There is maawamah (nothing)." He amar (spoke), "shawab (turn back / repent) again" shabai (seven) paimayam (times).

It happened at the shabayaiy (seventh) time, that he amar (spoke), "Behold, a qatan (small / young / least) ib (cloud), like a ayash (man / husband) kap (hand), is ilah (go up / offer) out of the yam (sea/waters)." He amar (spoke), "ilah (go up / offer) up, amar (spoke) Achaab (Ahab), ‘Get asar (ready) and yarad (go) down, so that the gasham (rain) doesn't itzar (stop) you.'"

It happened in a little kah (while), that the sky grew qadar (black) with ibayam (clouds) and rawach (spirit / wind), and there was a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) gasham (rain). Achaab (Ahab) rakab (rode), and yalak (went) to Yazaraial (Jezreel).
The yad (hand) of Yahawah was on Alayah (Elijah); and he tucked his cloak into his belt and rawatz (ran) panayam (face) Achaab (Ahab) to the entrance of Yazaraial (Jezreel).
Achaab (Ahab) nagad (told) Ayazabal (Jezebel) all that Alayah (Elijah) ishah (make) done, and how he had harag (kill) all the nabayaayam (prophets) with the charab (sword).

Then Ayazabal (Jezebel) shalach (send) a malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to Alayah (Elijah), amar (spoke), "So let the Alahayam ishah (make) to me, and more also, if I don't shawam (place / establish / appoint) your napash (soul) as the napash (soul) of achad (one) of them by machar (tomorrow) about this ith (time)!"

When he raah (see) that, he qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) for his napash (soul), and bawaa (come) to Baar-Shabai (Beersheba), which belongs to Yahawadah (Judah), and yanach (left) his nair (servant) there.

But he himself halak (move) a yawam (day) darak (journey) into the madabar (wilderness), and bawaa (come) and yashab (inhabit/dwell) down under a ratham (juniper) tree: and he shaal (requested) for himself that he might mawath (death), and amar (spoke), "It is rab (enough). Now, O Yahawah, laqach (take / seize) away my napash (soul); for I am not tawab (good / proper function) than my ab (father)."
He shakab (lay) down and yashan (slept) under a ratham (juniper) tree; and behold, an malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) nagai (touched) him, and amar (spoke) to him, "qawam (rise up) and akal (eat)!"

He nabat (looked), and behold, there was at his maraashah (head) a igah (cake) baked on the ratzapayam (coals), and a jar of mayam (Waters). He akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and shakab (lay) down again.

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah shawab (turn back / repent) again the shanay (second) time, and nagai (touched) him, and amar (spoke), "qawam (rise up) and akal (eat), darak (because) the journey is rab (too) great for you."

He qawam (rise up), and akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and yalak (went) in the kach (strength / mighty / power) of that food arabaiyam (forty) yawam (day) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights) to Charab (Horeb) the har (mountain) of Alahayam.

He bawaa (come) there to a mairah (cave), and lawan (lodged) there; and behold, the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to him, and he amar (spoke) to him, "What are you doing here, Alayah (Elijah)?"

He amar (spoke), "I have been very qanaa (jealous) for Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies); for the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) have forsaken your barayath (covenant), haras (thrown) down your mazabach (altars), and harag (kill) your nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) with the charab (sword). I, even I only, am yathar (left); and they baqash (seek) my napash (soul), to laqach (take / seize) it away."

He amar (spoke), "yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and imad (stand) on the har (mountain) panayam (face) Yahawah." Behold, Yahawah ibar (pass over/through) by, and a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and chazaq (strong) rawach (spirit / wind) paraq (tore) the harayam (mountains), and shabar (broke) in pieces the salaiyam (rocks) panayam (face) Yahawah; but Yahawah was not in the rawach (spirit / wind). Achar (other) the rawach (spirit / wind) an raish (earthquake); but Yahawah was not in the raish (earthquake).
Achar (other) the raish (earthquake) a ash (fire) passed; but Yahawah was not in the ash (fire): and achar (other) the ash (fire) a still daq (small) qawal (sound / voice).

It was so, when Alayah (Elijah) shamai (hearken / hear) it, that he lawat (wrapped) his panayam (face) in his adarath (mantle), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and imad (stood) in the entrance of the mairah (cave). Behold, a qawal (sound / voice) came to him, and amar (spoke), "What are you doing here, Alayah (Elijah)?"

He amar (spoke), "I have been very qanaa (jealous) for Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies); for the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) have forsaken your barayath (covenant), haras (thrown) down your mazabach (altars), and harag (kill) your nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) with the charab (sword). I, even I only, am yathar (left); and they baqash (seek) my napash (soul), to laqach (take / seize) it away."

Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, "yalak (go), shawab (turn back / repent) on your darak (way) to the madabar (wilderness) of Damashaq (Damascus). When you arrive, you shall mashach (anoint) Chazaal (Hazael) to be malak (king) over Aram (Syria).

You shall mashach (anoint) Yahawaa (Jehu) the ban (son) of Namashay (Nimshi) to be malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel); and you shall mashach (anoint) Alayashai (Elisha) the ban (son) of Shapat (Shaphat) of Abalamachawalah (Abel Meholah) to be nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) in your place.

It shall happen, that he who malat (escapes) from the charab (sword) of Chazaal (Hazael), Yahawaa (Jehu) will mawath (death); and he who malat (escapes) from the charab (sword) of Yahawaa (Jehu), Alayashai (Elisha) will mawath (death).

Yet will I shaar (leave) shabai (seven) alap (thousand) in Yashar-Al (Israel), all the barakayam (knees) which have not karai (bowed) to Bail (Baal), and every pah (mouth) which has not nashaq (kissed) him."

So he departed there, and matzaa (found) Alayashai (Elisha) the ban (son) of Shapat (Shaphat), who was charash (plowing), with shanayam (two) tzamad (yoke) of oxen panayam (face) him, and he with the shanayam (two): and Alayah (Elijah) ibar (pass over/through) over to him, and shalak (cast) his adarath (mantle) on him.

He izab (left) the oxen, and rawatz (ran) achar (other) Alayah (Elijah), and amar (spoke), "Let me please nashaq (kiss) my ab (father) and my am (mother), and then I will yalak (follow) you." He amar (spoke) to him, "yalak (go) back again; for what ishah (make) I done to you?"

He shawab (turn back / repent) from achar (other) him, and laqach (take / seize) the tzamad (yoke) of oxen, and zabach (killed) them, and bashal (boiled) their bashar (flesh) with the kalay (instruments) of the oxen, and nathan (give) to the im (nation / people), and they akal (eat). Then he qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) achar (other) Alayah (Elijah), and sharath (served) him.

Banahadad (Ben Hadad) the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) qabatz (gathered) all his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) qabatz (together); and there were shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) malak (king) with him, and sawas (horses) and rakab (chariots): and he ilah (go up / offer) up and tzawar (besieged) Shamarawan (Samaria), and lacham (fought) against it.
He shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to Achaab (Ahab) malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), into the iyar (city), and said to him, "Thus says Ben Hadad,
‘Your kasap (silver) and your zahab (gold) is mine. Your wives also and your ban (son), even the tawab (good / proper function), are mine.'"
The malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) inah (answer / respond), "It is according to your amar (spoke), my Adawan, O malak (king). I am yours, and all that I have."

The malaakayam (messengers) shawab (turn back / repent) again, and amar (spoke), "Banahadad (Ben Hadad) yaamaraw (says), ‘I shalach (send) amar (spoke) to you, saying, "You shall nathan (give) me your kasap (silver), and your zahab (gold), and your wives, and your ban (son);

But I will shalach (send) my ibad (servant) to you machar (tomorrow) about this ith (time), and they shall chapash (search) your bayath (house), and the bathay (houses) of your ibad (servant); and it shall be, that whatever is machamad (pleasant) in your iyan (eye), they shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) it in their yad (hand), and laqach (take / seize) it away."'"

Then the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) qaraa (called) all the zaqanay (elders) of the aratz (Earth/land), and amar (spoke), "Please notice how this man baqash (seeks) rai (mischief); for he shalach (send) to me for my wives, and for my ban (son), and for my kasap (silver), and for my zahab (gold); and I didn't manai (deny) him."
All the zaqanayam (elders) and all the im (nation / people) amar (spoke) to him, "Don't shamai (hearken / hear), neither abah (be willing / desire)."

Therefore he amar (spoke) to the malaakay (messengers) of Banahadad (Ben Hadad), "amar (spoke) my Adawan the malak (king), ‘All that you shalach (send) for to your ibad (servant) at the raashawan (first) I will ishah (make); but this thing I cannot ishah (make).'" The malaakay (messengers) departed, and shawab (turn back / repent) him shawab (turn back / repent) the dabar (word / matter).

Banahadad (Ben Hadad) shalach (send) to him, and amar (spoke), "The Alahayam ishah (make) so to me, and more also, if the ipar (dust) of Shamarawan (Samaria) shall sapaq (suffice) for shailayam (handfuls) for all the im (nation / people) who ragal (feet / foot) me."
The malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) inah (answer / respond), "dabar (word / matter) him, ‘Don't let him who chagar (puts) on his armor brag like he who takes it off.'"

It happened, when Ben Hadad shamai (hearken / hear) this dabar (word / matter), as he was shathah (drinks), he and the malakayam (kings), in the sakawath (pavilions), that he amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), "Prepare to attack!" They prepared to attack the iyar (city).

Behold, a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) nagash (came) near to Achaab (Ahab) malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and amar (spoke), "Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘raah (see) you seen all this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) hamawan (multitude)? Behold, I will nathan (give) it into your yad (hand) this yawam (day); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.'"

Achaab (Ahab) amar (spoke), "By whom?" He amar (spoke), "Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘By the nair (young) men of the sharay (princes) of the madayanawath (provinces).'" Then he amar (spoke), "Who shall begin the malachamah (battle)?" He amar (spoke), "You."

Then he mustered the nair (young) men of the sharay (princes) of the madayanawath (provinces), and they were shanayam (two) maah (hundred) and shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two). Achar (other) them, he mustered all the im (nation / people), even all the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), being shabai (seven) alap (thousand).

They yatzaa (go out / come out) out at tzahar (noon). But Banahadad (Ben Hadad) was shathah (drinks) himself shakawar (drunk) in the sakawath (pavilions), he and the malakayam (kings), the shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) malakayam (kings) who izar (helped) him.

The nair (young) men of the sharay (princes) of the madayanawath (provinces) yatzaa (go out / come out) out raashawan (first); and Banahadad (Ben Hadad) shalach (send) out, and they nagad (told) him, amar (spoke), "anashayam (men) are yatzaa (go out / come out) out from Shamarawan (Samaria)."

He amar (spoke), "If they yatzaa (go out / come out) come out for shalawam (peace / safety), thapash (take) them chay (life); or if they yatzaa (go out / come out) come out for malachamah (war), thapash (take) them chay (life)."

So these yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the iyar (city), the nair (young) men of the sharay (princes) of the madayanawath (provinces), and the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) which achar (other) them.

They ayash (man / husband) nakah (killed) his ayash (man / husband). The Aram (Syrians) nawas (fled), and Yashar-Al (Israel) radap (pursued) them. Banahadad (Ben Hadad) the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) malat (escaped) on a sawas (horse) with horsemen.

The malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and nakah (struck) the sawas (horses) and rakab (chariots), and nakah (killed) the Aram (Syrians) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) makah (slaughter).

The nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) nagash (came) near to the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and amar (spoke) to him, "yalak (go), chazaq (strengthen) yourself, and yadai (mark), and raah (see) what you ishah (make); for at the thashawabah (return) of the shanah (year) the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) will ilah (go up / offer) up against you."

The ibaday (servants) of the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) amar (spoke) to him, "Their Alahayam is a Alahayam of the harayam (hills); therefore they were chazaq (stronger) than we. But let us lacham (fight) against them in the mayashawar (plain), and laa (NOT) we shall be chazaq (stronger) than they.
Ishah (make) this thing: sawar (take) the malakayam (kings) away, every ayash (man / husband) out of his maqawam (place), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) pachawath (captains) in their place.

Muster an chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), like the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) that you napal (fall / be cast down) lost, sawas (horse) for sawas (horse), and rakab (chariot) for rakab (chariot). We will lacham (fight) against them in the mayashawar (plain), and surely we will be chazaq (stronger) than them." He shamai (hearken / hear) to their qawal (sound / voice), and ishah (make) so.

It happened at the thashawabah (return) of the shanah (year), that Banahadad (Ben Hadad) mustered the Aram (Syrians), and ilah (go up / offer) up to Apaq (Aphek), to malachamah (fight) against Yashar-Al (Israel).

The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) were mustered, and were kawal (all), and yalak (went) qaraah (against) them. The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) chanah (encamped) before them like shanayam (two) chashap (little) flocks of young izayam (goats); but the Aram (Syrians) malaa (filled) the aratz (Earth/land).

A ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam nagash (came) near and amar (spoke) to the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and amar (spoke), "Thus amaraw (says) Yahawah, ‘Because the Aram (Syrians) have amar (spoke), "Yahawah is a Alahayam of the harayam (hills), but he is not a Alahayam of the imaqayam (valleys);" therefore I will nathan (give) all this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) hamawan (multitude) into your yad (hand), and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.'"

They chanah (encamped) alah (these) over nakach (against) the other shabai (seven) yamayam (days). So it was, that in the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) the malachamah (battle) was qarab (come close); and the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) nakah (killed) one maah (hundred) alap (thousand) footmen of the Aram (Syrians) in achad (one) yawam (day).

But the yathar (rest) nawas (fled) to Apaq (Aphek), into the iyar (city); and the chawamah (wall) napal (fall / be cast down) on isharayam (twenty) - shabai (seven) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband) who were yathar (left). Banahadad (Ben Hadad) nawas (fled), and bawaa (come) into the iyar (city), into an chadar (inner) room.

His ibad (servant) amar (spoke) to him, "See now, we have shamai (hearken / hear) that the malakay (kings) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) are chasad (grace) malakay (kings). Please let us shawam (place / establish / appoint) sackcloth on our bodies, and chabalayam (ropes) on our raash (head), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out to the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel). Maybe he will chayah (save) your napash (soul)."

So they chagar (put) sackcloth on their bodies and chabalayam (ropes) on their raash (head), and bawaa (come) to the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and amar (spoke), "Your ibad (servant) Banahadad (Ben Hadad) yaamaraw (says), ‘Please chayah (let) me live.'" He amar (spoke), "Is he still chay (life)? He is my ach (brother/kinsman)."

Now the anashayam (men) nachash (observed) diligently, and hurried to take this phrase; and they amar (spoke), "Your ach (brother/kinsman) Banahadad (Ben Hadad)." Then he amar (spoke), "bawaa (come), laqach (take / seize) him." Then Banahadad (Ben Hadad) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to him; and he ilah (go up / offer) him to come up into the marakabah (chariot).

Ben Hadad amar (spoke) to him, "The irayam (cities) which my ab (father) laqach (take / seize) from your ab (father) I will shawab (turn back / repent). You shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) chawatzawath (streets) for yourself in Damashaq (Damascus), as my ab (father) shawam (place / establish / appoint) in Shamarawan (Samaria)." "I," said Ahab, "will shalach (send) you go with this barayath (covenant)." So he karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with him, and shalach (send) him go.

A achad (one) ayash (man / husband) of the banay (sons) of the nabayaayam (prophets) amar (spoke) to his rai (neigbor/another person) by the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, "Please nakah (strike) me!" The ayash (man / husband) maan (refused) to nakah (strike) him.

Then he amar (spoke) to him, "Because you have not shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah, behold, as soon as you are departed from me, a aray (lion) shall nakah (kill) you." As soon as he was departed from him, a aray (lion) matzaa (found) him, and nakah (killed) him.
Then he matzaa (found) achar (other) ayash (man / husband), and amar (spoke), "Please nakah (strike) me." The ayash (man / husband) nakah (struck) him, nakah (smiting) and patzai (wounding) him.
So the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) departed, and waited for the malak (king) by the darak (way), and disguised himself with his headband over his iyan (eye).

As the malak (king) ibar (pass over/through) by, he tzaiq (cried) to the malak (king); and he amar (spoke), "Your ibad (servant) yatzaa (go out / come out) out into the qarab (among / near) of the malachamah (battle); and behold, a ayash (man / husband) sawar (turned) aside, and bawaa (come) a ayash (man / husband) to me, and amar (spoke), ‘Guard this ayash (man / husband)! If by any paqad (visit) he be paqad (visit), then your napash (soul) shall be for his napash (soul), or else you shall shaqal (pay) a kakar (talent) of kasap (silver).'

As your ibad (servant) was ishah (make) here and there, he was ayan (NO ONE)." The malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke) to him, "So your mashapat (judgment) shall be; you yourself have charatz (decided) it."
He hurried, and took the headband sawar (away) from his iyan (eye); and the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) recognized that he was of the nabaayam (prophets).

He amar (spoke) to him, "Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘Because you have shalach (send) go out of your yad (hand) the ayash (man / husband) whom I charam (had) devoted to destruction, therefore your napash (soul) shall go for his napash (soul), and your im (nation / people) for his im (nation / people).'"
The malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) yalak (went) to his bayath (house) sullen and angry, and bawaa (come) to Shamarawan (Samaria).

It happened achar (other) these things, that Nabawath (Naboth) the yazaraialay (jezreelite) had a karam (vineyard), which was in Yazaraial (Jezreel), hard by the hayakal (palace) of Achaab (Ahab) malak (king) of Shamarawan (Samaria).

Achaab (Ahab) dabar (word / matter) to Nabawath (Naboth), amar (spoke), "nathan (give) me your karam (vineyard), that I may have it for a gan (garden) of yaraq (herbs), because it is qarawab (near) to my bayath (house); and I will nathan (give) you for it a tawab (good / proper function) karam (vineyard) than it. Or, if it seems tawab (good / proper function) to you, I will nathan (give) you its machayar (worth) in kasap (money)."
Nabawath (Naboth) amar (spoke) to Achaab (Ahab), "May Yahawah chalayalah (forbid) me, that I should nathan (give) the nachalah (inheritance) of my ab (father) to you!"

Achaab (Ahab) bawaa (come) into his bayath (house) sullen and angry because of the dabar (word / matter) which Nabawath (Naboth) the yazaraialay (jezreelite) had dabar (word / matter) to him; for he had amar (spoke), "I will not nathan (give) you the nachalah (inheritance) of my ab (father)." He shakab (laid) himself down on his matah (bed), and sabab (turned) away his panayam (face), and would akal (eat) no lacham (bread).
But Ayazabal (Jezebel) his ayashah (woman / wife) bawaa (come) to him, and dabar (word / matter) to him, "Why is your rawach (spirit / wind) so sar (sad), that you akal (eat) no lacham (bread)?"

He dabar (word / matter) to her, "Because I dabar (word / matter) to Nabawath (Naboth) the yazaraialay (jezreelite), and dabar (word / matter) to him, ‘nathan (give) me your karam (vineyard) for kasap (money); or else, if it chapatz (pleases) you, I will nathan (give) you another karam (vineyard) for it.' He amar (spoke), ‘I will not nathan (give) you my karam (vineyard).'"

Ayazabal (Jezebel) his ayashah (woman / wife) amar (spoke) to him, "ishah (make) you now govern the malawakah (kingdom) of Yashar-Al (Israel)? Qawam (rise up), and akal (eat) lacham (bread), and let your lab (heart) be yatab (merry). I will nathan (give) you the karam (vineyard) of Nabawath (Naboth) the yazaraialay (jezreelite)."

So she kathab (write) saparayam (letters) in Achaab (Ahab's) sham (name), and chatham (sealed) them with his chawatham (seal), and shalach (send) the saparayam (letters) to the zaqanayam (elders) and to the charayam (nobles) who were in his iyar (city), who lived with Nabawath (Naboth).
She kathab (write) in the saparayam (letters), amar (spoke), "qaraa (called) a tzawam (fast), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) Nabawath (Naboth) on raash (head) among the im (nation / people).

Yashab (inhabit/dwell) shanayam (two) anashayam (men), base fellows, before him, and let them iwad (admonish/bear witness against) amar (spoke) him, saying, ‘You barak (blessed) Alahayam and the malak (king)!' Then yatzaa (go out / come out) him out, and saqal (stone) him to mawath (death)."

The yaishaw (men) of his iyar (city), even the zaqanayam (elders) and the charayam (nobles) who lived in his iyar (city), ishah (make) as Ayazabal (Jezebel) had shalach (send) to them, according as it was kathab (write) in the saparayam (letters) which she had shalach (send) to them.
They qaraa (called) a tzawam (fast), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) Nabawath (Naboth) on raash (head) among the im (nation / people).

The shanayam (two) anashayam (men), the base fellows, bawaa (come) in and yashab (inhabit/dwell) before him. The base anashayam (fellows) iwad (admonish/bear witness against) against him, even against Nabawath (Naboth), in the presence of the im (nation / people), amar (spoke), "Nabawath (Naboth) barak (blessed) Alahayam and the malak (king)!" Then they yatzaa (go out / come out) him out of the iyar (city), and saqal (stoned) him to mawath (death) with abanayam (stones).
Then they shalach (send) to Ayazabal (Jezebel), amar (spoke), "Nabawath (Naboth) has been saqal (stoned), and is mawath (death)."

It happened, when Ayazabal (Jezebel) shamai (hearken / hear) that Nabawath (Naboth) was saqal (stoned), and was mawath (death), that Ayazabal (Jezebel) amar (spoke) to Achaab (Ahab), "qawam (rise up), take yarash (possession) of the karam (vineyard) of Nabawath (Naboth) the yazaraialay (jezreelite), which he maan (refused) to nathan (give) you for kasap (money); for Nabawath (Naboth) is not chay (life), but mawath (death)."

It happened, when Achaab (Ahab) shamai (hearken / hear) that Nabawath (Naboth) was mawath (death), that Achaab (Ahab) qawam (rise up) up to yarad (go) down to the karam (vineyard) of Nabawath (Naboth) the yazaraialay (jezreelite), to take yarash (possession) of it.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Alayah (Elijah) the thashabay (tishbite), amar (spoke),

"Qawam (rise up), yarad (go) down to qaraah (meet) Achaab (Ahab) malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), who dwells in Shamarawan (Samaria). Behold, he is in the karam (vineyard) of Nabawath (Naboth), where he has yarad (gone) down to take yarash (possession) of it.

You shall dabar (word / matter) to him, amar (spoke), ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "Have you ratzach (killed) and also taken yarash (possession)?"' You shall dabar (word / matter) to him, amar (spoke), ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "In the maqawam (place) where kalabayam (dogs) laqaq (licked) the dam (blood) of Nabawath (Naboth), kalabayam (dogs) will laqaq (lick) your dam (blood), even yours."'"

Achaab (Ahab) amar (spoke) to Alayah (Elijah), "matzaa (have) you found me, my ayab (enemy)?" He amar (spoke), "I matzaa (have) found you, because you have makar (sold) yourself to ishah (make) that which is rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah.

Behold, I will bawaa (come) rai (evil) on you, and will utterly sweep you bair (away) and will karath (cut) off from Achaab (Ahab) everyone who urinates against a qayar (wall), and him who is itzar (shut) up and him who is izab (left) at large in Yashar-Al (Israel).

I will nathan (give) your bayath (house) like the bayath (house) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Nabat (Nebat), and like the bayath (house) of Baishaa (Baasha) the ban (son) of Achayah (Ahijah) for the kais (provocation) with which you have provoked me to kais (anger), and have made Yashar-Al (Israel) to chataa (sin)."
Yahawah also dabar (word / matter) of Ayazabal (Jezebel), amar (spoke), "The kalabayam (dogs) shall akal (eat) Ayazabal (Jezebel) by the chayal (rampart) of Yazaraial (Jezreel).
The kalabayam (dogs) will akal (eat) he who mawath (death) of Achaab (Ahab) in the iyar (city); and the iwap (flying) of the sky will akal (eat) he who mawath (death) in the shadah (field)."

But there was none like Achaab (Ahab), who makar (sold) himself to ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, whom Ayazabal (Jezebel) his ayashah (woman / wife) sawath (stirred) up.

He did very thaib (abominably) in yalak (following) galalayam (idols), according to all that the Amaray (Amorites) ishah (make), whom Yahawah yarash (cast) out panayam (face) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

It happened, when Achaab (Ahab) shamai (hearken / hear) those dabarayam (words), that he qarai (tore) his clothes, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) sackcloth on his bashar (flesh), and tzawam (fasted), and shakab (lay) in sackcloth, and halak (move) at (softly).
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Alayah (Elijah) the thashabay (tishbite), amar (spoke),

"Raah (see) how Achaab (Ahab) kanai (humbles) panayam (face) before me? Yain (because) he kanai (humbles) panayam (face) before me, I will not bawaa (come) the rai (evil) in his yamay (days); but in his ban (son) yamay (days) will I bawaa (come) the rai (evil) on his bayath (house)."
They yashab (inhabit/dwell) shalawash (three) shanayam (years) without malachamah (war) between Aram (Syria) and Yashar-Al (Israel).
It happened in the shalayashay (third) shanah (year), that Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) yarad (came) down to the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

The malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), "You yadai (know) that Ramath-Galaid (Ramoth) Galaid (Gilead) is ours, and we are still, and don't laqach (take / seize) it out of the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Aram (Syria)?"

He amar (spoke) to Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat), "Will you yalak (go) with me to malachamah (battle) to Ramath-Galaid (Ramoth Gilead)?" Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) amar (spoke) to the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), "I am as you are, my im (nation / people) as your im (nation / people), my sawas (horses) as your sawas (horses)."
Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) amar (spoke) to the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), "Please darash (inquire) yawam (day) for the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah."

Then the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) qabatz (gathered) the nabayaayam (prophets) qabatz (together), about arabai (four) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband), and amar (spoke) to them, "Shall I yalak (go) against Ramath-Galaid (Ramoth Gilead) to malachamah (battle), or shall I chadal (forbear)?" They amar (spoke), "ilah (go up / offer) up; for the Adanay will nathan (give) it into the yad (hand) of the malak (king)."
But Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) amar (spoke), "Isn't there here a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Yahawah, that we may darash (inquire) of him?"

The malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke) to Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat), "There is yet achad (one) ayash (man / husband) by whom we may darash (inquire) of Yahawah, Mayakayahaw (Micaiah) the ban (son) of Yamalaa (Imlah); but I shanaa (hate) him; for he does not nabaa (prophesy) tawab (good / proper function) concerning me, but rai (evil)." Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) amar (spoke), "Don't let the malak (king) amar (spoke) so."
Then the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) qaraa (called) an sarayas (officer), and amar (spoke), "mahar (quickly) get Mayakayahaw (Micaiah) the ban (son) of Yamalaa (Imlah)."

Now the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) and Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) were sitting ayash (man / husband) on his kasaa (throne), labash (arrayed) in their bagadayam (robes), in an open garan (place) at the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate) of Shamarawan (Samaria); and all the nabayaayam (prophets) were prophesying panayam (face) them.

Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah) the ban (son) of Kanainah (Chenaanah) ishah (make) him qaranay (horns) of barazal (iron), and amar (spoke), "Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘With these you shall nagach (push) the Aram (Syrians), until they are kalah (complete / finish).'"

All the nabaayam (prophets) nabaa (prophesied) so, amar (spoke), "ilah (go up / offer) up to Ramath-Galaid (Ramoth Gilead), and tzalach (prosper); for Yahawah will nathan (give) it into the yad (hand) of the malak (king)."

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) who halak (move) to qaraa (called) Mayakayahaw (Micaiah) dabar (word / matter) to him, amar (spoke), "See now, the nabayaayam (prophets) declare tawab (good / proper function) to the malak (king) with achad (one) pah (mouth). Please let your dabar (word / matter) be like the dabar (word / matter) of achad (one) of them, and dabar (word / matter) tawab (good / proper function)."
Mayakayahaw (Micaiah) amar (spoke), "As Yahawah chay (life), what Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, that I will dabar (word / matter)."

When he bawaa (come) come to the malak (king), the malak (king) amar (spoke) to him, "Mayakayahaw (Micaiah), shall we yalak (go) to Ramath-Galaid (Ramoth Gilead) to malachamah (battle), or shall we chadal (forbear)?" He amar (spoke) him, "ilah (go up / offer) up and tzalach (prosper); and Yahawah will nathan (give) it into the yad (hand) of the malak (king)."

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to him, "How many paimayam (times) do I have to shabai (swear / take oath) you that you dabar (word / matter) to me nothing but the amath (truth) in the sham (name) of Yahawah?"

He amar (spoke), "I raah (see) all Yashar-Al (Israel) pawatz (scattered) on the harayam (mountains), as tzaan (sheep) that have no raih (shepherd). Yahawah amar (spoke), ‘These have no adawan (master / lord). Let them ayash (man / husband) shawab (turn back / repent) to his bayath (house) in shalawam (peace / safety).'"

The malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke) to Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat), "Didn't I amar (spoke) you that he would not nabaa (prophesy) tawab (good / proper function) concerning me, but rai (evil)?"

Micaiah amar (spoke), "Therefore shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah. I raah (see) Yahawah sitting on his kasaa (throne), and all the tzabaa (troop) of shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) imad (standing) by him on his right yamayan (right hand) and on his shamaawal (left hand).

Yahawah amar (spoke), ‘Who shall pathah (entice) Achaab (Ahab), that he may ilah (go up / offer) up and napal (fall / be cast down) at Ramath-Galaid (Ramoth Gilead)?' One amar (spoke) kah (one) thing; and another amar (spoke) another.
A rawach (spirit / wind) yatzaa (go out / come out) out and imad (stood) panayam (face) Yahawah, and amar (spoke), ‘I will pathah (entice) him.'

Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, ‘How?' He amar (spoke), ‘I will yatzaa (go out / come out) out and will be a shaqar (lying) rawach (spirit / wind) in the pah (mouth) of all his nabayaa (prophet/prophecy).' He amar (spoke), ‘You will pathah (entice) him, and will also yakal (prevail). Yatzaa (go out / come out) out and ishah (make) so.'

Now therefore, behold, Yahawah nathan (give) put a shaqar (lying) rawach (spirit / wind) in the pah (mouth) of all these your nabayaa (prophet/prophecy); and Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) rai (evil) concerning you."

Then Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah) the ban (son) of Kanainah (Chenaanah) nagash (came) near, and nakah (struck) Mayakayahaw (Micaiah) on the lachay (cheek), and amar (spoke), "Which ay (way) did the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah ibar (pass over/through) from me to dabar (word / matter) to you?"
Mayakayahaw (Micaiah) amar (spoke), "raah (see), you will see on that yawam (day), when you bawaa (come) into an chadar (inner) room to chabah (hide) yourself."

The malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke), "laqach (take / seize) Mayakayahaw (Micaiah), and shawab (turn back / repent) him back to Amawan (Amon) the shar (prince / ruler) of the iyar (city), and to Yawaash (Joash) the malak (king) ban (son).

Amar (spoke), ‘Thus amar (spoke) the malak (king), "shawam (place / establish / appoint) this fellow in the bayath (house), and akal (eat) him with lacham (bread) of lachatz (affliction) and with mayam (Waters) of lachatz (affliction), until I bawaa (come) in shalawam (peace / safety)."'"

Mayakayahaw (Micaiah) amar (spoke), "If you shawab (turn back / repent) at shawab (turn back / repent) in shalawam (peace / safety), Yahawah has not dabar (word / matter) by me." He amar (spoke), "shamai (hearken / hear), all you imayam (people)!"
So the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) and Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) ilah (go up / offer) up to Ramath-Galaid (Ramoth Gilead).

The malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke) to Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat), "I will disguise myself, and bawaa (come) into the malachamah (battle); but you labash (put) on your bagad (robes)." The malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) disguised himself, and bawaa (come) into the malachamah (battle).

Now the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) had tzawah (commanded) the shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) sharay (captains) of his rakab (chariots), amar (spoke), lacham (fight) neither with qatan (small / young / least) nor gadawal (very great/important/mighty), except only with the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

It happened, when the sharay (captains) of the rakab (chariots) raah (see) Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat), that they amar (spoke), "Surely that is the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel)!" And they sawar (turned) aside to lacham (fight) against him. Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) zaiq (cried) out.
It happened, when the sharay (captains) of the rakab (chariots) raah (see) that it was not the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), that they shawab (turn back / repent) back from achar (other) him.

A certain ayash (man / husband) mashak (drew) his qashath (bow) at random, and nakah (struck) the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) between the dabaqayam (joints) of the armor. Therefore he amar (spoke) to the rakab (driver) of his chariot, "hapak (turn) your yad (hand), and yatzaa (go out / come out) me out of the machanah (battle); for I am severely chalah (afflict)."

The malachamah (battle) ilah (go up / offer) that yawam (day). The malak (king) was propped up in his marakabah (chariot) facing the Aram (Syrians), and mawath (death) at irab (evening). The dam (blood) yatzaq (ran) out of the makah (wound) into the chayaq (bottom) of the rakab (chariot).

A ranah (cry) ibar (pass over/through) throughout the machanah (army) about the bawaa (come) down of the shamash (sun), amar (spoke), "Every ayash (man / husband) to his iyar (city), and every ayash (man / husband) to his aratz (Earth/land)!"
So the malak (king) mawath (death), and was bawaa (come) to Shamarawan (Samaria); and they qabar (bury) the malak (king) in Shamarawan (Samaria).

They shatap (washed) the rakab (chariot) by the barakah (pool) of Shamarawan (Samaria); and the kalabayam (dogs) laqaq (licked) up his dam (blood) where the prostitutes rachatz (washed) themselves; according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah which he dabar (word / matter).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabaray (acts) of Achaab (Ahab), and all that he ishah (make), and the shan (ivory) bayath (house) which he banah (build), and all the irayam (cities) that he banah (build), aren't they kathab (write) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabaray (chronicles) of the malakay (kings) of Yashar-Al (Israel)?
So Achaab (Ahab) shakab (slept) with his ab (father); and Achazayah (Ahaziah) his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.
Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the ban (son) of Asaa (Asa) began to malak (king) over Yahawadah (Judah) in the arabai (four) shanah (year) of Achaab (Ahab) malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) was shalawashayam (thirty) - chamash (five) shanah (years) ban (son) when he began to malak (king); and he malak (king) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) shanah (years) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem). His am (mother) sham (name) was Izawabah (Azubah) the banath (daughter) of Shalachay (Shilhi).

He yalak (walked) in all the darak (way) of Asaa (Asa) his ab (father); He didn't sawar (turn) aside from it, ishah (make) that which was yashar (upright) in the iyanay (eyes) of Yahawah: however the high places were not sawar (taken) away; the people still ishah (make) and burnt incense in the high places.
Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
Now the rest of the acts of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat), and his might that he showed, and how he warred, aren't they written in the book of the chronicles of the malak (king) of Judah?
The yathar (remnant) of the sodomites, that remained in the yamayam (days) of his father Asa, he ishah (make) away out of the land.
There was no king in Edom: a deputy was king.
Jehoshaphat made ships of Tarshish to ayan (NO ONE) to Ophir for gold: but they didn't ayan (NO ONE); for the ships were broken at Ezion Geber.
Then Ahaziah the son of Ahab said to Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat), "Let my servants yalak (go) with your servants in the anayawath (ships)." But Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) would not.
Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father; Jehoram his ban (son) reigned in his place.
Ahaziah the ban (son) of Ahab began to malak (king) over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) malak (king) of Judah, and he malak (king) two years over Israel.

He did that which was evil in the sight of Yahawah, and walked in the way of his father, and in the way of his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam the ban (son) of Nebat, in which he made Yashar-Al (Israel) to sin.
He ishah (make) Baal, and worshiped him, and provoked to anger Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), according to all that his ab (father) ishah (make) done.
Mawaab (Moab) pashai (rebelled) against Yashar-Al (Israel) achar (other) the mawath (death) of Achaab (Ahab).

Achazayah (Ahaziah) napal (fall / be cast down) down through the shabakah (lattice) in his upper room that was in Shamarawan (Samaria), and was chalah (afflict). So he shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers), and amar (spoke) to them, "yalak (go), darash (inquire) of Bailazabawab (Baal Zebub), the Alahayam of Iqarawan (Ekron), whether I will chayah (recover) of this chalay (sickness)."

But the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Alayah (Elijah) the thashabay (tishbite), "qawam (rise up), ilah (go up / offer) up to qaraah (meet) the malaakay (messengers) of the malak (king) of Shamarawan (Samaria), and dabar (word / matter) them, ‘Is it because there is no Alahayam in Yashar-Al (Israel), that you halak (move) to darash (inquire) of Bailazabawab (Baal Zebub), the Alahayam of Iqarawan (Ekron)?

Now therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "You shall not yarad (come) down from the matah (bed) where you have ilah (go up / offer) up, but shall mawath (death) mawath (death)."'" Alayah (Elijah) departed.
The malaakayam (messengers) shawab (turn back / repent) to him, and he amar (spoke) to them, "Why is it that you have shawab (turn back / repent)?"

They amar (spoke) to him, "A ayash (man / husband) ilah (go up / offer) up to qaraah (meet) us, and amar (spoke) to us, ‘yalak (go), shawab (turn back / repent) to the malak (king) who shalach (send) you, and dabar (word / matter) him, "Thus dabaratham (says) Yahawah, ‘Is it because there is no Alahayam in Yashar-Al (Israel), that you shalach (send) to darash (inquire) of Bailazabawab (Baal Zebub), the Alahayam of Iqarawan (Ekron)? Therefore you shall not yarad (come) down from the matah (bed) where you have ilah (go up / offer) up, but shall mawath (death) mawath (death).'"'"
He dabar (word / matter) to them, "What kind of ayash (man / husband) was he who ilah (go up / offer) up to qaraah (meet) you, and dabar (word / matter) you these dabarayam (words)?"
They amar (spoke) him, "He was a shair (hair) bail (man), and wearing a iwar (leather) belt around his waist." He amar (spoke), "It is Alayah (Elijah) the thashabay (tishbite)."

Then the malak (king) shalach (send) a shar (prince / ruler) of chamashayam (fifty) with his chamashayam (fifty) to him. He ilah (go up / offer) up to him; and behold, he was sitting on the raash (head) of the har (mountain). He dabar (word / matter) to him, "ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, the malak (king) has dabar (word / matter), ‘yarad (come) down!'"

Alayah (Elijah) inah (answer / respond) to the shar (prince / ruler) of chamashayam (fifty), "If I am a ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, let ash (fire) yarad (come) down from the sky, and akal (eat) you and your chamashayam (fifty)!" Ash (fire) yarad (came) down from the sky, and akal (eat) him and his chamashayam (fifty).

Again he shalach (send) to him achar (other) shar (prince / ruler) of chamashayam (fifty) and his chamashayam (fifty). He inah (answer / respond) him, "ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, the malak (king) has inah (answer / respond), ‘yarad (come) down maharah (quickly)!'"

Alayah (Elijah) inah (answer / respond) them, "If I am a ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, let ash (fire) yarad (come) down from the sky, and akal (eat) you and your chamashayam (fifty)!" The ash (fire) of Alahayam yarad (came) down from the sky, and akal (eat) him and his chamashayam (fifty).

Again he shalach (send) the shar (prince / ruler) of a shalayashay (third) chamashayam (fifty) with his chamashayam (fifty). The shalayashay (third) shar (prince / ruler) of chamashayam (fifty) ilah (go up / offer) up, and bawaa (come) and karai (fell) on his barak (blessed) before Alayah (Elijah), and begged him, and dabar (word / matter) to him, "ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, please let my napash (soul), and the napash (soul) of these chamashayam (fifty) your ibad (servant), be yaqar (precious) in your iyan (eye).

Behold, ash (fire) yarad (came) down from the sky, and akal (eat) the shanayam (two) raashawan (former) sharay (captains) of chamashayam (fifty) with their chamashayam (fifties). But now let my napash (soul) be yaqar (precious) in your iyan (eye)."

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Alayah (Elijah), "yarad (go) down with him. Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of him." He qawam (rise up), and yarad (went) down with him to the malak (king).

He dabar (word / matter) to him, "Thus dabar (word / matter) Yahawah, ‘Because you have shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to darash (inquire) of Bailazabawab (Baal Zebub), the Alahayam of Iqarawan (Ekron), is it because there is no Alahayam in Yashar-Al (Israel) to darash (inquire) of his dabar (word / matter)? Therefore you shall not yarad (come) down from the matah (bed) where you have ilah (go up / offer) up, but shall mawath (death) mawath (death).'"

So he mawath (death) according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah which Alayah (Elijah) had dabar (word / matter). Yahawaram (Jehoram) began to malak (king) in his place in the shanayam (two) shanah (year) of Yahawaram (Jehoram) the ban (son) of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah); because he had no ban (son).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabaray (acts) of Achazayah (Ahaziah) which he ishah (make), aren't they kathab (write) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabaray (chronicles) of the malakay (kings) of Yashar-Al (Israel)?

It happened, when Yahawah would ilah (go up / offer) up Alayah (Elijah) by a sair (whirlwind) into shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), that Alayah (Elijah) yalak (went) with Alayashai (Elisha) from Galagal (Gilgal).

Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to Alayashai (Elisha), "Please wait here, for Yahawah has shalach (send) me as far as Bayath-Al (Bethel)." Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke), "As Yahawah chay (life), and as your napash (soul) chay (life), I will not izab (leave) you." So they yarad (went) down to Bayath-Al (Bethel).

The banay (sons) of the nabayaayam (prophets) who were at Bayath-Al (Bethel) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to Alayashai (Elisha), and amar (spoke) to him, "Do you yadai (know) that Yahawah will laqach (take / seize) away your adawan (master / lord) from your raash (head) today?" He amar (spoke), "Yes, I yadai (know) it; hold your chashah (peace)."

Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to him, "Alayashai (Elisha), please wait here, for Yahawah has shalach (send) me to Yarayachaw (Jericho)." He amar (spoke), "As Yahawah chay (life), and as your napash (soul) chay (life), I will not izab (leave) you." So they bawaa (come) to Yarayachaw (Jericho).

The banay (sons) of the nabayaayam (prophets) who were at Yarayachaw (Jericho) nagash (came) near to Alayashai (Elisha), and amar (spoke) to him, "Do you yadai (know) that Yahawah will laqach (take / seize) away your adawan (master / lord) from your raash (head) today?" He amar (spoke), "Yes, I yadai (know) it. Hold your chashah (peace)."

Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to him, "Please wait here, for Yahawah has shalach (send) me to the Yaradan (Jordan)." He amar (spoke), "As Yahawah chay (life), and as your napash (soul) chay (life), I will not izab (leave) you." They shanayam (two) yalak (went) on.

Chamashayam (fifty) ayash (man / husband) of the banay (sons) of the nabayaayam (prophets) halak (move), and imad (stood) opposite them at a distance; and they shanayam (two) imad (stood) by the Yaradan (Jordan).

Alayah (Elijah) laqach (take / seize) his adarath (mantle), and galam (wrapped) it together, and nakah (struck) the mayam (Waters), and they were chatzah (divided) here and there, so that they shanayam (two) ibar (pass over/through) over on dry charabah (ground).

It happened, when they ibar (pass over/through) gone over, that Alayah (Elijah) amar (spoke) to Alayashai (Elisha), "shaal (ask) what I shall ishah (make) for you, before I am laqach (take / seize) from you." Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke), "Please let a shanayam (two) pah (portion) of your rawach (spirit / wind) be on me."
He amar (spoke), "You have shaal (asked) a qashah (rough / hard) thing. If you raah (see) me when I am laqach (take / seize) from you, it shall be so for you; but if not, it shall not be so."

It happened, as they still halak (move) on, and dabar (word / matter), that behold, a rakab (chariot) of ash (fire) and sawasay (horses) of ash (fire) parad (separated) them; and Alayah (Elijah) ilah (go up / offer) up by a sair (whirlwind) into shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens).

Alayashai (Elisha) raah (see) it, and he tzaiq (cried), "My ab (father), my ab (father), the rakab (chariots) of Yashar-Al (Israel) and its horsemen!" He raah (see) him no more: and he chazaq (took) hold of his own clothes, and qarai (tore) them in shanayam (two) qaraiyam (pieces).

He rawam (will lift up) up also the adarath (mantle) of Alayah (Elijah) that napal (fall / be cast down) from him, and shawab (turn back / repent) back, and imad (stood) by the shapah (bank) of the Yaradan (Jordan).

He laqach (take / seize) the adarath (mantle) of Alayah (Elijah) that napal (fall / be cast down) from him, and nakah (struck) the mayam (Waters), and amar (spoke), "Where is Yahawah, the Alahayam of Alayah (Elijah)?" When he also had nakah (struck) the mayam (Waters), they were chatzah (divided) here and there; and Alayashai (Elisha) ibar (pass over/through) over.

When the banay (sons) of the nabayaayam (prophets) who were at Yarayachaw (Jericho) over against him raah (see) him, they amar (spoke), "The rawach (spirit / wind) of Alayah (Elijah) nawach (rests) on Alayashai (Elisha)." They bawaa (come) to qaraah (meet) him, and shachah (bowed) themselves to the aratz (Earth/land) before him.

They amar (spoke) to him, "See now, there are with your ibad (servant) chamashayam (fifty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) banay (men). Please yalak (let) them go and baqash (seek) your adawan (master / lord). Perhaps the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah has nashaa (lift) him up, and put him on some har (mountain), or into some gayaa (valley). He amar (spoke), "You shall not shalach (send) them."

When they patzar (urged) him until he was bawash (ashamed), he amar (spoke), "shalach (send) them." They shalach (send) therefore chamashayam (fifty) ayash (man / husband); and they searched for shalawash (three) yamayam (days), but didn't matzaa (find) him.
They shawab (turn back / repent) back to him, while he stayed at Yarayachaw (Jericho); and he amar (spoke) to them, "Didn't I amar (spoke) you, ‘Don't yalak (go)?'"

The anashay (men) of the iyar (city) amar (spoke) to Alayashai (Elisha), "Behold, please, the mawashab (situation) of this iyar (city) is tawab (good / proper function), as my Adawan raah (see); but the mayam (Waters) is rai (bad), and the aratz (Earth/land) shakal (miscarries)."
He amar (spoke), "laqach (take / seize) me a chadash (new) jar, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) malach (salt) in it." They laqach (take / seize) it to him.

He yatzaa (go out / come out) out to the mawatzaa (spring) of the mayam (Waters), and shalak (threw) malach (salt) into it, and amar (spoke), "Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘I have rapaa (healed) these mayam (Waters). There shall not be from there any more mawath (death) or shakal (miscarrying).'"
So the mayam (Waters) were rapaa (healed) to this yawam (day), according to the dabar (word / matter) of Alayashai (Elisha) which he dabar (word / matter).

He ilah (go up / offer) up from there to Bayath-Al (Bethel). As he was ilah (go up / offer) up by the darak (way), some youths yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the iyar (city) and qalas (mocked) him, and amar (spoke) to him, "ilah (go up / offer) up, you baldy! Ilah (go up / offer) up, you baldhead!"

He raah (see) achar (other) him and raah (see) them, and qalal (cursed) them in the sham (name) of Yahawah. Shanayam (two) female dabayam (bears) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the yair (woods), and mauled arabaiyam (forty) - shanayam (two) of those youths.
He yalak (went) from there to har (mountain) Karamal (Carmel), and from there he shawab (turn back / repent) to Shamarawan (Samaria).

Now Yahawaram (Jehoram) the ban (son) of Achaab (Ahab) began to malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel) in Shamarawan (Samaria) in the eighteenth shanah (year) of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and malak (king) shanayam (two) shanah (years).

He ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, but not like his ab (father), and like his am (mother); for he sawar (put) away the matzabah (pillar) of Bail (Baal) that his ab (father) ishah (make) made.
Nevertheless he held to the chataawath (sins) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Nabat (Nebat), with which he made Yashar-Al (Israel) to chataa (sin); he didn't sawar (depart) from it.

Now Mayashai (Mesha) malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab) was a sheep breeder; and he shawab (turn back / repent) to the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) the tzamar (wool) of one maah (hundred) alap (thousand) karayam (lambs), and of one maah (hundred) alap (thousand) ayalayam (rams).
But it happened, when Achaab (Ahab) was mawath (death), that the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab) pashai (rebelled) against the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel).
Malak (king) Yahawaram (Jehoram) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of Shamarawan (Samaria) at that yawam (day), and mustered all Yashar-Al (Israel).

He yalak (went) and shalach (send) to Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), amar (spoke), "The malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab) has pashai (rebelled) against me. Will you yalak (go) with me against Mawaab (Moab) to malachamah (battle)?" He amar (spoke), "I will ilah (go up / offer) up. I am as you are, my im (nation / people) as your im (nation / people), my sawas (horses) as your sawas (horses)."
He amar (spoke), "Which darak (way) shall we ilah (go up / offer) up?" He amar (spoke), "The darak (way) of the madabar (wilderness) of Adawam (Edom)."

So the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) yalak (went), and the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and the malak (king) of Adawam (Edom); and they sabab (made) a circuit of shabai (seven) yamayam (days)' darak (journey). There was no mayam (Waters) for the machanah (army), nor for the animals that ragal (feet / foot) them.

The malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke), "ahah (alas)! For Yahawah has qaraa (called) these shalawash (three) malakayam (kings) together to nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of Mawaab (Moab)."

But Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) amar (spoke), "Isn't there here a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of Yahawah, that we may darash (inquire) of Yahawah by him?" Achad (one) of the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel's) ibaday (servants) inah (answer / respond), "Alayashai (Elisha) the ban (son) of Shapat (Shaphat) is here, who yatzaq (poured) mayam (Waters) on the yaday (hands) of Alayah (Elijah)."

Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) amar (spoke), "The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah is with him." So the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) and Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) and the malak (king) of Adawam (Edom) yarad (went) down to him.

Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke) to the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), "What have I to do with you? Yalak (go) to the nabayaay (prophets) of your ab (father), and to the nabayaay (prophets) of your am (mother)." The malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke) to him, "No; for Yahawah has qaraa (called) these shalawash (three) malakayam (kings) together to nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of Mawaab (Moab)."

Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke), "As Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) chay (life), panayam (face) whom I imad (stand), surely, were it not that I nashaa (lift) the panayam (face) of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), I would not nabat (look) toward you, nor raah (see) you.
But now laqach (take / seize) me a minstrel." It happened, when the minstrel nagan (played), that the yad (hand) of Yahawah came on him.
He amar (spoke), "Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘ishah (make) this nachal (stream / river) full of trenches.'

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘You will not raah (see) rawach (spirit / wind), neither will you raah (see) gasham (rain); yet that nachal (stream / river) shall be malaa (filled) with mayam (Waters), and you will shathah (drinks), both you and your livestock and your animals.
This is but a qalal (light) thing in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah. He will also nathan (give) the Mawaab (Moabites) into your yad (hand).

You shall nakah (strike) every fortified iyar (city), and every mabachawar (choice) iyar (city), and shall napal (fall / be cast down) every tawab (good / proper function) itz (tree), and satham (stop) all maiyanay (springs) of mayam (Waters), and kaab (mar) every tawab (good / proper function) chalaqah (piece) of land with abanayam (stones).'"

It happened in the baqar (morning), about the time of ilah (go up / offer) the ilah (go up / offer), that behold, mayam (Waters) bawaa (come) by the darak (way) of Adawam (Edom), and the aratz (Earth/land) was malaa (filled) with mayam (Waters).

Now when all the Mawaab (Moabites) shamai (hearken / hear) that the malakayam (kings) had ilah (go up / offer) up to lacham (fight) against them, they tzaiq (gathered) themselves together, all who were chagar (able) to put on armor, and upward, and imad (stood) on the gabawal (border/boundary).

They shakam (rose) up early in the baqar (morning), and the shamash (sun) shone on the mayam (Waters), and the Mawaab (Moabites) raah (see) the mayam (Waters) over nagad (against) them as adam (red) as dam (blood).

They amar (spoke), "This is dam (blood). The malakayam (kings) are charab (surely) charab (destroyed), and they have struck ayash (man / husband) other. Now therefore, Mawaab (Moab), to the shalal (spoil)!"

When they bawaa (come) to the machanah (camp) of Yashar-Al (Israel), the Yashar-Al (Israelites) qawam (rise up) up and nakah (struck) the Mawaab (Moabites), so that they nawas (fled) panayam (face) them; and they nakah (went) forward into the land nakah (smiting) the Mawaab (Moabites).

They haras (beat) down the irayam (cities); and on every tawab (good / proper function) chalaqah (piece) of land they shalak (cast) every ayash (man / husband) his aban (stone), and malaa (filled) it; and they satham (stopped) all the maiyan (springs) of mayam (Waters), and felled all the tawab (good / proper function) itz (trees), until in Qayaracharash (Kir Hareseth) only they shaar (left) its aban (stone); however the men armed with slings sabab (went) about it, and nakah (struck) it.
