When the malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab) raah (see) that the malachamah (battle) was too severe for him, he laqach (take / seize) with him shabai (seven) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) who shalap (drew) charab (sword), to baqai (break) through to the malak (king) of Adawam (Edom); but they yakal (could) not.

Then he laqach (take / seize) his bakawar (eldest) ban (son) who would have malak (king) in his place, and ilah (go up / offer) him for a burnt ilah (offering) on the chawamah (wall). There was gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qatzap (wrath) against Yashar-Al (Israel): and they departed from him, and shawab (turn back / repent) to their own aratz (Earth/land).

Now there tzaiq (cried) a achad (one) ayashah (woman / wife) of the wives of the banay (sons) of the nabayaayam (prophets) to Alayashai (Elisha), amar (spoke), "Your ibad (servant) my ayash (man / husband) is mawath (death). You yadai (know) that your ibad (servant) yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah. Now the nashah (creditor) bawaa (come) come to laqach (take / seize) for himself my shanayam (two) yalad (birth / begot) to be ibadayam (slaves)."

Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke) to her, "What shall I ishah (make) for you? Nagad (tell) me: what yash (do) you have in the bayath (house)?" She amar (spoke), "Your handmaid has nothing in the bayath (house), except a asawak (pot) of shaman (oil)."
Then he amar (spoke), "yalak (go), shaal (borrow) containers from of all your neighbors, even rayaq (empty) containers. Don't mait (borrow) just a few.

You shall bawaa (come) in, and sagar (shut) the dalath (door) on you and on your ban (son), and yatzaq (pour) out into all those containers; and you shall nasai (set) aside that which is malaa (full)."
So she yalak (went) from him, and sagar (shut) the dalath (door) on her and on her ban (son); they nagash (brought) the containers to her, and she yatzaq (poured) out.

It happened, when the containers were malaa (full), that she amar (spoke) to her ban (son), "nagash (bring) me kalay (another) container." He amar (spoke) to her, "There isn't kalay (another) container." The shaman (oil) stopped flowing.

Then she bawaa (come) and nagad (told) the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam. He amar (spoke), "yalak (go), makar (sell) the shaman (oil), and shalam (pay) your nashay (debt); and you and your ban (son) chayah (live) on the yathar (rest)."

It fell on a yawam (day), that Alayashai (Elisha) ibar (pass over/through) to Shawanam (Shunem), where there was a prominent ayashah (woman / wife); and she persuaded him to akal (eat) lacham (bread). So it was, that as often as he ibar (pass over/through) by, he sawar (turned) in there to akal (eat) lacham (bread).
She amar (spoke) to her ayash (man / husband), "See now, I yadai (perceive) that this is a qadawash (holy) ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, that passes by us continually.

Please let us ishah (make) a qatan (small / young / least) room on the qayar (wall). Let us shawam (place / establish / appoint) for him there a matah (bed), a shalachan (table), a chair, and a manawarah (lamp) stand. It shall be, when he bawaa (come) to us, that he shall sawar (turn) in there."
One yawam (day) he bawaa (come) there, and he sawar (turned) into the room and shakab (lay) there.
He amar (spoke) to Gayachazay (Gehazi) his nair (servant), "qaraa (called) this Shunammite." When he had qaraa (called) her, she imad (stood) panayam (face) him.

He amar (spoke) to him, "amar (spoke) now to her, ‘Behold, you have cared for us with all this charadah (care). What is to be ishah (make) for you? Would you like to be dabar (word / matter) for to the malak (king), or to the shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop)?'" She amar (spoke), "I yashab (inhabit/dwell) thawak (midst) my own im (nation / people)."
He amar (spoke), "What then is to be ishah (make) for her?" Gayachazay (Gehazi) amar (spoke), "Most certainly she has no ban (son), and her ayash (man / husband) is zaqan (old)."
He amar (spoke), "qaraa (called) her." When he had qaraa (called) her, she imad (stood) in the pathach (door).

He amar (spoke), "At this mawaid (Feast/Holy Day), when the ith (time) comes around, you will chabaq (embrace) a ban (son)." She amar (spoke), "No, my Adawan, you ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, do not kazab (lie) to your handmaid."

The ayashah (woman / wife) harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son) at that mawaid (Feast/Holy Day), when the ith (time) came around, as Alayashai (Elisha) had dabar (word / matter) to her.
When the yalad (birth / begot) was gadal (grown), it happened one yawam (day) that he yatzaa (go out / come out) out to his ab (father) to the qatzarayam (reapers).
He amar (spoke) to his ab (father), "My raash (head)! My raash (head)!" He amar (spoke) to his nair (servant), "nashaa (lift) him to his am (mother)."
When he had nashaa (lift) him, and bawaa (come) him to his am (mother), he yashab (inhabit/dwell) on her barak (blessed) until tzahar (noon), and then mawath (death).
She ilah (go up / offer) up and shakab (laid) him on the matah (bed) of the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, and sagar (shut) the door on him, and yatzaa (go out / come out) out.

She qaraa (called) to her ayash (man / husband), and amar (spoke), "Please shalach (send) me achad (one) of the nairayam (servants), and achad (one) of the donkeys, that I may rawatz (run) to the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, and shawab (turn back / repent) again."
He amar (spoke), "Why would you want halak (move) to him today? It is neither new chadash (month) nor shabath (shabath / rest)." She amar (spoke), "It's alright."
Then she chabash (saddled) a donkey, and amar (spoke) to her nair (servant), "nahag (drive), and yalak (go) forward! Don't slow down for me, unless I ask you to."

So she yalak (went), and bawaa (come) to the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam to har (mountain) Karamal (Carmel). It happened, when the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam raah (see) her afar off, that he amar (spoke) to Gayachazay (Gehazi) his nair (servant), "Behold, there is the Shunammite.

Please rawatz (run) now to qaraah (meet) her, and ask her, ‘Is it shalawam (peace / safety) with you? Is it shalawam (peace / safety) with your ayash (man / husband)? Is it shalawam (peace / safety) with the yalad (birth / begot)?'" She amar (spoke), "It is shalawam (peace / safety)."

When she bawaa (come) to the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam to the har (mountain), she chazaq (caught) hold of his ragal (feet / foot). Gayachazay (Gehazi) nagash (came) near to hadap (thrust) her away; but the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam amar (spoke), "Leave her rapah (alone); for her napash (soul) is troubled within her; and Yahawah has ilam (hidden) it from me, and has not nagad (told) me."
Then she amar (spoke), "Did I shaal (desire) a ban (son) of my Adawan? Didn't I amar (spoke), Do not shalah (deceive) me?"

Then he amar (spoke) to Gayachazay (Gehazi), "Tuck your cloak into your belt, laqach (take / seize) my mashainah (staff) in your yad (hand), and go your yalak (way). If you matzaa (meet) any ayash (man / husband), don't greet him; and if anyone greets you, don't inah (answer / respond) him again. Then shawam (place / establish / appoint) my mashainah (staff) on the panayam (face) of the nair (child)."
The am (mother) of the nair (child) amar (spoke), "As Yahawah chay (life), and as your napash (soul) chay (life), I will not izab (leave) you." He qawam (rise up), and yalak (followed) her.

Gayachazay (Gehazi) ibar (pass over/through) on panayam (face) them, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the mashainah (staff) on the panayam (face) of the nair (child); but there was neither qawal (sound / voice), nor qashab (hearing). Therefore he shawab (turn back / repent) to qaraah (meet) him, and nagad (told) him, amar (spoke), "The nair (child) has not awakened."
When Alayashai (Elisha) bawaa (come) come into the bayath (house), behold, the nair (child) was mawath (death), and shakab (laid) on his matah (bed).
He bawaa (come) in therefore, and sagar (shut) the dalath (door) on them shanayam (two), and palal (prayed) to Yahawah.

He ilah (go up / offer) up, and shakab (lay) on the yalad (birth / begot), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) his pah (mouth) on his pah (mouth), and his iyan (eye) on his iyan (eye), and his kap (hands) on his kap (hands). He gahar (stretched) himself on him; and the bashar (flesh) of the yalad (birth / begot) grew chamam (warm).

Then he shawab (turn back / repent), and yalak (walked) in the bayath (house) achad (one) back and forth; and ilah (go up / offer) up, and gahar (stretched) himself on him. Then the nair (child) zarar (sneezed) shabai (seven) paimayam (times), and the nair (child) paqach (opened) his iyan (eye).

He qaraa (called) Gayachazay (Gehazi), and amar (spoke), "qaraa (called) this Shunammite!" So he qaraa (called) her. When she bawaa (come) come in to him, he amar (spoke), "nashaa (lift) up your ban (son)."

Then she bawaa (come) in, and napal (fall / be cast down) at his ragal (feet / foot), and shachah (bowed) herself to the aratz (Earth/land); and she nashaa (lift) up her ban (son), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out.

Alayashai (Elisha) shawab (turn back / repent) again to Galagal (Gilgal). There was a raib (famine) in the aratz (Earth/land); and the banay (sons) of the nabayaayam (prophets) were sitting panayam (face) him; and he amar (spoke) to his nair (servant), "shapath (set) on the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) sayar (pot), and bashal (boil) stew for the banay (sons) of the nabayaayam (prophets)."

Achad (one) yatzaa (go out / come out) out into the shadah (field) to laqat (gather) arath (herbs), and matzaa (found) a shadah (wild) gapan (vine), and laqat (gathered) of it shadah (wild) paqaith (gourds) his bagad (lap) malaa (full), and bawaa (come) and palach (shred) them into the sayar (pot) of stew; for they didn't recognize them.

So they yatzaq (poured) out for the anashayam (men) to akal (eat). It happened, as they were akal (eat) of the stew, that they tzaiq (cried) out, and amar (spoke), "ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, there is mawath (death) in the sayar (pot)!" They yakal (could) not akal (eat) of it.

But he amar (spoke), "Then laqach (take / seize) qamach (meal)." He shalak (cast) it into the sayar (pot); and he amar (spoke), "yatzaq (pour) out for the im (nation / people), that they may akal (eat)." There was no dabar (word / matter) in the sayar (pot).

A ayash (man / husband) from Baal Shalishah bawaa (come), and bawaa (come) the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam lacham (bread) of the bakawar (first) bakawarayam (fruits), isharayam (twenty) loaves of shairah (barley), and fresh karamal (ears) of grain in his sack. He amar (spoke), "nathan (give) to the im (nation / people), that they may akal (eat)."

His sharath (servant) amar (spoke), "What, should I nathan (give) this panayam (face) a maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband)?" But he amar (spoke), "nathan (give) the im (nation / people), that they may akal (eat); for thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘They will akal (eat), and will have some yathar (left) over.'"
So he nathan (give) it panayam (face) them, and they akal (eat), and yathar (left) some of it, according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah.

Now Naiman (Naaman), shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop) of the malak (king) of Aram (Syria), was a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) ayash (man / husband) with his adawan (master / lord), and nashaa (lift), because by him Yahawah nathan (give) given thashawaih (deliverance) to Aram (Syria): he was also a gabawar (mighty) ayash (man / husband) of valor, but he was a tzarai (leper).

The Aram (Syrians) yatzaa (go out / come out) gone out in gadawadayam (bands), and had shabah (brought) away captive out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Yashar-Al (Israel) a qatan (small / young / least) nairah (maiden); and she waited on Naiman (Naaman's) ayashah (woman / wife).
She amar (spoke) to her gabarath (mistress), "I wish that my Adawan were with the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) who is in Shamarawan (Samaria)! Then he would heal him of his tzaraith (leprosy)."
Someone bawaa (come) in, and nagad (told) his Adawan, amar (spoke), "The nairah (maiden) who is from the aratz (Earth/land) of Yashar-Al (Israel) dabar (word / matter) this."

The malak (king) of Aram (Syria) amar (spoke), "bawaa (come) now, and I will shalach (send) a sapar (book / scribed document) to the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel)." He departed, and laqach (take / seize) with him ishar (ten) kakaray (talents) of kasap (silver), and shash (six) alap (thousand) pieces of zahab (gold), and ishar (ten) chalayapawath (changes) of bagad (clothing).

He bawaa (come) the sapar (book / scribed document) to the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), amar (spoke), "Now when this sapar (book / scribed document) bawaa (come) come to you, behold, I have shalach (send) Naiman (Naaman) my ibad (servant) to you, that you may heal him of his tzaraith (leprosy)."

It happened, when the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) had qaraa (called) the sapar (book / scribed document), that he qarai (tore) his clothes, and amar (spoke), "Am I Alahayam, to mawath (death) and to chayah (make) alive, that this zah (this / that / these) shalach (send) to me to heal a ayash (man / husband) of his tzaraith (leprosy)? But please yadai (consider) and raah (see) how he anah (seeks) a quarrel against me."

It was so, when Alayashai (Elisha) the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam shamai (hearken / hear) that the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) had qarai (torn) his clothes, that he shalach (send) to the malak (king), amar (spoke), "Why have you qarai (torn) your clothes? Bawaa (come) him come now to me, and he shall yadai (know) that there is a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) in Yashar-Al (Israel)."
So Naiman (Naaman) bawaa (come) with his sawas (horses) and with his rakab (chariots), and imad (stood) at the pathach (door) of the bayath (house) of Alayashai (Elisha).

Alayashai (Elisha) shalach (send) a malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to him, amar (spoke), "halak (move) and rachatz (wash) in the Yaradan (Jordan) shabai (seven) paimayam (times), and your bashar (flesh) shall shawab (turn back / repent) again to you, and you shall be tahar (clean)."

But Naiman (Naaman) was qatzap (angry), and yalak (went) away, and amar (spoke), "Behold, I amar (spoke), ‘He will yatzaa (go out / come out) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to me, and imad (stand), and qaraa (called) on the sham (name) of Yahawah his Alahayam, and nawap (wave) his yad (hand) over the maqawam (place), and heal the tzarai (leper).'

Abanah (Aren't Abanah) and Parapar (Pharpar), the naharawath (rivers) of Damashaq (Damascus), tawab (good / proper function) than all the mayamay (waters) of Yashar-Al (Israel)? Couldn't I rachatz (wash) in them, and be tahar (clean)?" So he panah (turn) and yalak (went) away in a chamah (rage).

His ibad (servant) nagash (came) near, and dabar (word / matter) to him, and amar (spoke), "My ab (father), if the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) had asked you do some gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thing, wouldn't you ishah (make) done it? Ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) much rather then, when he yaamaraw (says) to you, ‘rachatz (wash), and be tahar (clean)?'"

Then yarad (went) he down, and tabal (dipped) himself shabai (seven) paimayam (times) in the Yaradan (Jordan), according to the dabar (word / matter) of the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam; and his bashar (flesh) was shawab (turn back / repent) like the bashar (flesh) of a qatan (small / young / least) nair (child), and he was tahar (clean).

He shawab (turn back / repent) to the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, he and all his machanah (company), and bawaa (come), and imad (stood) panayam (face) him; and he amar (spoke), "See now, I yadai (know) that there is no Alahayam in all the aratz (Earth/land), but in Yashar-Al (Israel). Now therefore, please laqach (take / seize) a barakah (gift) from your ibad (servant)."
But he amar (spoke), "As Yahawah chay (life), panayam (face) whom I imad (stand), I will laqach (take / seize) none." He patzar (urged) him to laqach (take / seize) it; but he maan (refused).

Naiman (Naaman) amar (spoke), "If not, then, please let tzamad (two) paradayam (mules)' mashaa (burden) of adamah (earth) be nathan (give) to your ibad (servant); for your ibad (servant) will from now on ishah (make) neither burnt ilah (offering) nor zabach (sacrifice) to other Alahayam, but to Yahawah.

In this thing may Yahawah salach (forgive/pardon/make clean) your ibad (servant): when my adawan (master / lord) bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of Ramawan (Rimmon) to shachah (worship) there, and he shain (leans) on my yad (hand), and I shachah (bow) myself in the bayath (house) of Ramawan (Rimmon). When I shachah (bow) myself in the bayath (house) of Ramawan (Rimmon), may Yahawah salach (forgive/pardon/make clean) your ibad (servant) in this thing."
He amar (spoke) to him, "yalak (go) in shalawam (peace / safety)." So he departed from him a kabarah (little) aratz (Earth/land).

But Gayachazay (Gehazi) the nair (servant) of Alayashai (Elisha) the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, amar (spoke), "Behold, my adawan (master / lord) has chashak (darkness) this Naiman (Naaman) the Aramay (Syrian), in not laqach (take / seize) at his yad (hand) that which he bawaa (come). As Yahawah chay (life), I will rawatz (run) achar (other) him, and laqach (take / seize) something from him."

So Gayachazay (Gehazi) radap (followed) achar (other) Naiman (Naaman). When Naiman (Naaman) raah (see) rawatz (one) running achar (other) him, he came down from the marakabah (chariot) to qaraah (meet) him, and amar (spoke), "Is shalawam (peace / safety) well?"

He amar (spoke), "shalawam (peace / safety) is well. My adawan (master / lord) has shalach (send) me, amar (spoke), ‘Behold, even now shanayam (two) nair (young) men of the banay (sons) of the nabayaayam (prophets) bawaa (come) come to me from the har (mountain) country of Aparayam (Ephraim). Please nathan (give) them a kakar (talent) of kasap (silver) and shanayam (two) chalapawath (changes) of bagad (clothing).'"

Naiman (Naaman) amar (spoke), "Be yaal (pleased) to laqach (take / seize) two kakarayam (talents)." He paratz (urged) him, and tzarar (bound) shanayam (two) kakarayam (talents) of kasap (silver) in shanayam (two) charatayam (bags), with shanayam (two) chalapawath (changes) of bagad (clothing), and nathan (give) them on shanayam (two) of his nair (servants); and they nashaa (lift) them panayam (face) him.
When he bawaa (come) to the hill, he laqach (take / seize) them from their yad (hand), and stored them in the bayath (house). Then he let the anashayam (men) shalach (send), and they departed.

But he bawaa (come) in, and imad (stood) before his adawan (master / lord). Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke) to him, "an (where) did you come from, Gayachazay (Gehazi)?" He amar (spoke), "Your ibad (servant) halak (move) nowhere."

He amar (spoke) to him, "Didn't my lab (heart) halak (move) with you, when the ayash (man / husband) hapak (turned) from his marakabah (chariot) to qaraah (meet) you? Is it a ith (time) to laqach (take / seize) kasap (money), and to laqach (take / seize) bagadayam (garments), and zayath (olive) groves and karamayam (vineyards), and tzaan (sheep) and cattle, and male ibadayam (servants) and female shapachawath (servants)?

Therefore the tzaraith (leprosy) of Naiman (Naaman) will cling to you and to your zarai (seed) iwalam (forever)." He yatzaa (go out / come out) out from his panayam (face) a tzarai (leper), as white as shalag (snow).
The banay (sons) of the nabayaayam (prophets) amar (spoke) to Alayashai (Elisha), "See now, the maqawam (place) where we yashab (inhabit/dwell) before you is too tzar (oppressor / distressor) for us.

Please yalak (let) us go to the Yaradan (Jordan), and every ayash (man / husband) laqach (take / seize) a qawarah (beam) from there, and let us ishah (make) us a maqawam (place) there, where we may yashab (inhabit/dwell)." He amar (spoke), "yalak (go)!"
Achad (one) amar (spoke), "yaal (please) be pleased to yalak (go) with your ibad (servant)." He amar (spoke), "I will yalak (go)."
So he yalak (went) with them. When they bawaa (come) to the Yaradan (Jordan), they gazar (cut) down itz (wood).

But as achad (one) was napal (fall / be cast down) a qawarah (beam), the axe barazal (head) napal (fall / be cast down) into the mayam (Waters). Then he tzaiq (cried), and amar (spoke), "ahah (alas), my adawan (master / lord)! For it was shaal (borrowed)."

The ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam asked, "an (where) did it napal (fall / be cast down)?" He showed him the maqawam (place). He qatzab (cut) down a itz (stick), shalak (threw) it in there, and made the barazal (iron) float.
He amar (spoke), "rawam (will lift up) it." So he shalach (send) out his yad (hand) and laqach (take / seize) it.

Now the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) was lacham (warring) against Yashar-Al (Israel); and he took yaitz (counsel) with his ibad (servant), amar (spoke), "My thachanah (camp) will be in such and such a maqawam (place)."

The ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam shalach (send) to the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), amar (spoke), "Beware that you not ibar (pass over/through) such a maqawam (place); for the Aram (Syrians) are nachath (coming) down there."

The malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shalach (send) to the maqawam (place) which the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam amar (spoke) him and zahar (warn) him of; and he shamar (keep/guard) himself there, not achad (one) nor shanayam (two).

The lab (heart) of the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) was very sair (troubled) about this. He qaraa (called) his ibad (servant), and amar (spoke) to them, "Won't you show me which of us is for the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel)?"

Achad (one) of his ibad (servant) amar (spoke), "No, my Adawan, O malak (king); but Alayashai (Elisha), the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) who is in Yashar-Al (Israel), nagad (tells) the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) the dabarayam (words) that you dabar (word / matter) in your bedroom."
He amar (spoke), "yalak (go) and raah (see) ayakah (where) he is, that I may shalach (send) and laqach (take / seize) him." It was nagad (told) him, amar (spoke), "Behold, he is in Dathan (Dothan)."

Therefore he shalach (send) sawasayam (horses), rakab (chariots), and a kabad (great) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) there. They bawaa (come) by layal (night), and surrounded the iyar (city).

When the sharath (servant) of the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam had qawam (rise up) shakam (early), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out, behold, an chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) with sawas (horses) and rakab (chariots) was around the iyar (city). His nair (servant) amar (spoke) to him, "ahah (alas), my adawan (master / lord)! What shall we ishah (make)?"
He amar (spoke), "Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid); for those who are with us are more than those who are with them."

Alayashai (Elisha) palal (prayed), and amar (spoke), "Yahawah, please paqach (open) his iyanay (eyes), that he may raah (see)." Yahawah paqach (opened) the iyanay (eyes) of the nair (young) man; and he raah (see): and behold, the har (mountain) was malaa (full) of sawasayam (horses) and rakab (chariots) of ash (fire) around Alayashai (Elisha).

When they yarad (came) down to him, Alayashai (Elisha) palal (prayed) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "Please nakah (strike) this gaway (heathen / nation) with sanawar (blindness)." He nakah (struck) them with sanawar (blindness) according to the dabar (word / matter) of Alayashai (Elisha).

Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke) to them, "This is not the darak (way), neither is zah (this / that / these) the iyar (city). Yalak (follow) me, and I will yalak (bring) you to the ayash (man / husband) whom you baqash (seek)." He yalak (led) them to Shamarawan (Samaria).

It happened, when they bawaa (come) come into Shamarawan (Samaria), that Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke), "Yahawah, paqach (open) the iyanay (eyes) of these men, that they may raah (see)." Yahawah paqach (opened) their iyanay (eyes), and they raah (see); and behold, they were in the thawak (midst) of Shamarawan (Samaria).
The malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke) to Alayashai (Elisha), when he raah (see) them, "My ab (father), shall I nakah (strike) them? Shall I nakah (strike) them?"

He amar (spoke), "You shall not nakah (strike) them. Would you nakah (strike) those whom you have shabah (taken) captive with your charab (sword) and with your qashath (bow)? Shawam (place / establish / appoint) lacham (bread) and mayam (Waters) panayam (face) them, that they may akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and yalak (go) to their adawan (master / lord)."

He karah (prepared) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) feast for them. When they had akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), he shalach (send) them away, and they yalak (went) to their adawan (master / lord). The gadawaday (bands) of Aram (Syria) stopped raiding the aratz (Earth/land) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

It happened achar (other) this, that Banahadad (Benhadad) malak (king) of Aram (Syria) qabatz (gathered) all his machanah (army), and ilah (go up / offer) up and tzawar (besieged) Shamarawan (Samaria).

There was a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) raib (famine) in Shamarawan (Samaria). Behold, they tzawar (besieged) it, until a donkey's raash (head) was sold for shamanayam (eighty) pieces of kasap (silver), and the rabai (fourth) part of a kab of yawanayam (doves) dung for chamash (five) pieces of kasap (silver).

As the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) was ibar (pass over/through) by on the chawamah (wall), a ayashah (woman / wife) tzaiq (cried) to him, amar (spoke), "yashai (salvation), my Adawan, O malak (king)!"
He amar (spoke), "If Yahawah doesn't yashai (salvation) you, from ayan (NO ONE) could I yashai (salvation) you? From of the garan (threshing) floor, or from the yaqab (winepress)?"

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to her, "What ails you?" She amar (spoke), "This ayashah (woman / wife) amar (spoke) to me, ‘nathan (give) your ban (son), that we may akal (eat) him today, and we will akal (eat) my ban (son) machar (tomorrow).'

So we bashal (boiled) my ban (son), and akal (eat) him: and I amar (spoke) to her on the achar (other) yawam (day), ‘nathan (give) your ban (son), that we may akal (eat) him;' and she has chabaa (hidden) her ban (son)."

It happened, when the malak (king) shamai (hearken / hear) the dabaray (words) of the ayashah (woman / wife), that he qarai (tore) his clothes (now he was ibar (pass over/through) by on the chawamah (wall)); and the im (nation / people) raah (see), and behold, he had sackcloth underneath on his bashar (flesh).
Then he amar (spoke), "Alahayam ishah (make) so to me, and more also, if the raash (head) of Alayashai (Elisha) the ban (son) of Shapat (Shaphat) shall imad (stay) on him this yawam (day)."

But Alayashai (Elisha) was sitting in his bayath (house), and the zaqanayam (elders) were sitting with him. Then the king shalach (send) a ayash (man / husband) from panayam (face) him; but before the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) bawaa (come) to him, he amar (spoke) to the zaqanayam (elders), "Do you raah (see) how this ban (son) of a ratzach (murderer) has shalach (send) to sawar (take) away my raash (head)? Raah (see), when the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) bawaa (come), sagar (shut) the dalath (door), and hold the dalath (door) shut against him. Isn't the qawal (sound / voice) of his adawan (master / lord) ragalay (feet) achar (other) him?"

While he was still dabar (word / matter) with them, behold, the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) yarad (came) down to him. Then he amar (spoke), "Behold, this rai (evil) is from Yahawah. Why should I yachal (wait) for Yahawah any longer?"

Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke), "shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah. Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘machar (tomorrow) about this ith (time) a saah (measure) of fine salath (flour) will be sold for a shaqal (shekel), and two saathayam (measures) of shairah (barley) for a shaqal (shekel), in the shair (gate) of Shamarawan (Samaria).'"

Then the shalayash (captain) on whose yad (hand) the malak (king) shain (leaned) inah (answer / respond) the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, and amar (spoke), "Behold, if Yahawah ishah (make) arabawath (windows) in shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), could this thing be?" He amar (spoke), "raah (see), you shall see it with your iyan (eye), but shall not akal (eat) of it."

Now there were arabai (four) tzarai (leprous) anashayam (men) at the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate). They amar (spoke) ayash (man / husband) to rai (neigbor/another person), "Why do we yashab (inhabit/dwell) here until we mawath (death)?

If we amar (spoke), ‘We will bawaa (come) into the iyar (city),' then the raib (famine) is in the iyar (city), and we shall mawath (death) there. If we yashab (inhabit/dwell) still here, we also mawath (death). Now therefore yalak (come), and napal (fall / be cast down) us surrender to the machanah (army) of the Aram (Syrians). If they chayah (save) us alive, we will chayah (live); and if they mawath (death) us, we will only mawath (death)."

They qawam (rise up) up in the nashap (twilight), to bawaa (come) to the machanah (camp) of the Aram (Syrians). When they bawaa (come) come to the outermost part of the machanah (camp) of the Aram (Syrians), behold, there was no ayash (man / husband) there.

For the Adanay had made the machanah (army) of the Aram (Syrians) to shamai (hearken / hear) a qawal (sound / voice) of rakab (chariots), and a qawal (sound / voice) of sawas (horses), even the qawal (sound / voice) of a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor): and they amar (spoke) ayash (man / husband) to ach (brother/kinsman), Behold, the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) has shakar (hired) against us the malakay (kings) of the Chathay (Hittites), and the malakay (kings) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians), to bawaa (come) on us.

Therefore they qawam (rise up) and nawas (fled) in the nashap (twilight), and izab (left) their ahal (tents), and their sawas (horses), and their donkeys, even the machanah (camp) as it was, and nawas (fled) for their napash (soul).

When these matzaraiyam (lepers) bawaa (come) to the outermost part of the machanah (camp), they bawaa (come) into achad (one) ahal (tent), and akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and nashaa (lift) there kasap (silver), and zahab (gold), and bagad (clothing), and yalak (went) and taman (hid) it. Then they shawab (turn back / repent) back, and bawaa (come) into achar (other) ahal (tent), and nashaa (lift) there also, and yalak (went) and taman (hid) it.

Then they amar (spoke) ayash (man / husband) to rai (neigbor/another person), "We aren't ishah (make) right. This yawam (day) is a yawam (day) of bashawarah (good) news, and we chashah (keep) silent. If we chakah (wait) until the baqar (morning) awar (light), iwan (guilt/iniquity) will overtake us. Now therefore matzaa (come), yalak (let) us go and nagad (tell) the malak (king) bayath (house)."

So they bawaa (come) and qaraa (called) to the shawair (porter) of the iyar (city); and they nagad (told) them, amar (spoke), "We bawaa (come) to the machanah (camp) of the Aram (Syrians), and, behold, there was no ayash (man / husband) there, neither qawal (sound / voice) of adam (man), but the sawas (horses) asar (tied), and the donkeys asar (tied), and the ahalayam (tents) as they were."
He qaraa (called) the shairayam (porters); and they nagad (told) it to the malak (king) bayath (house) panayamah (within).

The malak (king) qawam (rise up) in the layal (night), and amar (spoke) to his ibad (servant), "I will now show you what the Aram (Syrians) ishah (make) done to us. They yadai (know) that we are raib (hungry). Therefore are they yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the machanah (camp) to chabah (hide) themselves in the shadah (field), amar (spoke), ‘When they yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the iyar (city), we shall thapash (take) them chay (life), and bawaa (come) into the iyar (city).'"

Achad (one) of his ibad (servant) inah (answer / respond), "Please let some laqach (take / seize) chamash (five) of the sawasayam (horses) that shaar (remain), which are shaar (left) in the city. Behold, they are like all the hamawan (multitude) of Yashar-Al (Israel) who are shaar (left) in it. Behold, they are like all the hamawan (multitude) of Yashar-Al (Israel) who are thamam (consumed). Shalach (send) us send and raah (see)."

They laqach (take / seize) therefore shanayam (two) rakab (chariots) with sawasayam (horses); and the malak (king) shalach (send) achar (other) the machanah (army) of the Aram (Syrians), amar (spoke), "yalak (go) and raah (see)."

They yalak (went) achar (other) them to the Yaradan (Jordan); and behold, all the darak (way) malaa (was) full of bagadayam (garments) and kalayam (vessels), which the Aram (Syrians) had shalak (cast) away in their chapaz (haste). The malaakayam (messengers) shawab (turn back / repent), and nagad (told) the malak (king).

The im (nation / people) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and plundered the machanah (camp) of the Aram (Syrians). So a saah (measure) of fine salath (flour) was sold for a shaqal (shekel), and two saathayam (measures) of shairah (barley) for a shaqal (shekel), according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah.

The malak (king) paqad (visit) the shalayash (captain) on whose yad (hand) he shain (leaned) to be in charge of the shair (gate): and the im (nation / people) ramas (trod) on him in the shair (gate), and he mawath (death) as the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam had dabar (word / matter), who dabar (word / matter) when the malak (king) yarad (came) down to him.

It happened, as the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam had dabar (word / matter) to the malak (king), amar (spoke), "Two saathayam (measures) of shairah (barley) for a shaqal (shekel), and a saah (measure) of fine salath (flour) for a shaqal (shekel), shall be machar (tomorrow) about this ith (time) in the shair (gate) of Shamarawan (Samaria);"

And that shalayash (captain) inah (answer / respond) the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, and amar (spoke), "Now, behold, if Yahawah should ishah (make) arabawath (windows) in shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), might such a thing be?" And he amar (spoke), "raah (see), you shall see it with your iyan (eye), but shall not akal (eat) of it."
It happened like that to him; for the im (nation / people) ramas (trod) on him in the shair (gate), and he mawath (death).

Now Alayashai (Elisha) had dabar (word / matter) to the ayashah (woman / wife), whose ban (son) he had restored to chayah (life), amar (spoke), "qawam (rise up), and yalak (go), you and your bayath (house), and stay for a while wherever you can; for Yahawah has qaraa (called) for a raib (famine). It shall also bawaa (come) on the aratz (Earth/land) shabai (seven) shanayam (years)."

The ayashah (woman / wife) qawam (rise up), and ishah (make) according to the dabar (word / matter) of the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam. She yalak (went) with her bayath (house), and lived in the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines) shabai (seven) shanayam (years).

It happened at the shabai (seven) shanayam (years)' qatzah (end / extremity / border), that the ayashah (woman / wife) shawab (turn back / repent) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines). Then she yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to tzaiq (cry) to the malak (king) for her bayath (house) and for her shadah (land).

Now the malak (king) was dabar (word / matter) with Gayachazay (Gehazi) the nair (servant) of the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, amar (spoke), "Please sapar (book) me all the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) things that Alayashai (Elisha) ishah (make) done."

It happened, as he was sapar (book) the malak (king) how he had chayah (restored) to chayah (life) him who was mawath (death), that behold, the ayashah (woman / wife), whose ban (son) he had restored to chayah (life), tzaiq (cried) to the malak (king) for her bayath (house) and for her shadah (land). Gayachazay (Gehazi) amar (spoke), "My Adawan, O malak (king), this is the ayashah (woman / wife), and this is her ban (son), whom Alayashai (Elisha) restored to chayah (life)."

When the malak (king) shaal (asked) the ayashah (woman / wife), she sapar (book) him. So the malak (king) nathan (give) to her a achad (one) sarayas (officer), amar (spoke), "shawab (turn back / repent) all that was hers, and all the thabawaath (fruits) of the shadah (field) since the yawam (day) that she izab (left) the aratz (Earth/land), even until now."

Alayashai (Elisha) bawaa (come) to Damashaq (Damascus); and Banahadad (Benhadad) the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) was chalah (afflict). It was nagad (told) him, amar (spoke), "The ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam bawaa (come) come here."

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Chazaal (Hazael), "laqach (take / seize) a manachah (present) in your yad (hand), and yalak (go), qaraah (meet) the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam, and darash (inquire) of Yahawah by him, amar (spoke), ‘Will I chayah (recover) from this chalay (sickness)?'"

So Chazaal (Hazael) yalak (went) to qaraah (meet) him, and laqach (take / seize) a manachah (present) with him, even of every tawab (good / proper function) thing of Damashaq (Damascus), arabaiyam (forty) gamal (camels)' mashaa (burden), and bawaa (come) and imad (stood) panayam (face) him, and amar (spoke), "Your ban (son) Banahadad (Benhadad) malak (king) of Aram (Syria) has shalach (send) me to you, amar (spoke), ‘Will I chayah (recover) from this chalay (sickness)?'"
Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke) to him, "yalak (go), amar (spoke) him, ‘You shall chayah (surely) chayah (recover);' however Yahawah raah (see) shown me that he shall mawath (death) mawath (death)."
He settled his gaze steadfastly on him, until he was bawash (ashamed). Then the ayash (man / husband) of Alahayam bakah (wept).

Chazaal (Hazael) amar (spoke), "Why do you bakah (weep), my Adawan?" He amar (spoke), "Because I yadai (know) the rai (evil) that you will ishah (make) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel). You will shalach (send) their strongholds on ash (fire), and you will harag (kill) their bachawar (young) men with the charab (sword), and will ratash (dash) in pieces their iwalal (little) ones, and baqai (rip) up their harah (women) with child."

Chazaal (Hazael) amar (spoke), "But what is your ibad (servant), who is but a kalab (dog), that he should ishah (make) this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thing?" Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke), "Yahawah raah (see) shown me that you will be malak (king) over Aram (Syria)."

Then he departed from Alayashai (Elisha), and bawaa (come) to his adawan (master / lord), who amar (spoke) to him, "What did Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke) to you?" He amar (spoke), "He amar (spoke) me that you would chayah (surely) chayah (recover)."

It happened on the next macharath (day), that he laqach (take / seize) a makabar (thick) cloth, tabal (dipped) it in mayam (Waters), and parash (spread) it on his panayam (face), so that he mawath (death). Then Chazaal (Hazael) malak (king) in his place.

In the chamash (fifth) shanah (year) of Yawaram (Joram) the ban (son) of Achaab (Ahab) malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) being malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) then, Yahawaram (Jehoram) the ban (son) of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) began to malak (king).
He was shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) shanah (years) ban (son) when he began to malak (king). He malak (king) shamanah (eight) shanah (years) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

He yalak (walked) in the darak (way) of the malakay (kings) of Yashar-Al (Israel), as ishah (make) the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab); for he had the banath (daughter) of Achaab (Ahab) as ayashah (woman / wife). He ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah.

However Yahawah would not shachath (destroy) Yahawadah (Judah), for Dawad (David) his ibad (servant) sake, as he amar (spoke) him to nathan (give) to him a nayar (lamp) for his ban (son) yamayam (always).
In his yawam (day) Adawam (Edom) pashai (revolted) from under the yad (hand) of Yahawadah (Judah), and malak (king) a malak (king) over themselves.

Then Yawaram (Joram) ibar (pass over/through) over to Tzaiyar (Zair), and all his rakab (chariots) with him: and he qawam (rise up) up by layal (night), and nakah (struck) the Adawam (Edomites) who surrounded him, and the sharay (captains) of the rakab (chariots); and the im (nation / people) nawas (fled) to their ahal (tents).
So Adawam (Edom) pashai (revolted) from under the yad (hand) of Yahawadah (Judah) to this yawam (day). Then Labanah (Libnah) pashai (revolted) at the same ith (time).

The yathar (rest) of the dabaray (acts) of Yawaram (Joram), and all that he ishah (make), aren't they kathab (write) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabaray (chronicles) of the malakay (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)?
Yawaram (Joram) shakab (slept) with his ab (father), and was qabar (bury) with his ab (father) in the iyar (city) of Dawad (David); and Achazayah (Ahaziah) his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.

In the twelfth shanah (year) of Yawaram (Joram) the ban (son) of Achaab (Ahab) malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), Achazayah (Ahaziah) the ban (son) of Yahawaram (Jehoram) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) began to malak (king).

Isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) shanah (years) ban (son) was Achazayah (Ahaziah) when he began to malak (king); and he malak (king) achad (one) shanah (year) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem). His am (mother) sham (name) was Ithalayah (Athaliah) the banath (daughter) of Imaray (Omri) malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

He yalak (walked) in the darak (way) of the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab), and ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, as did the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab); for he was the son-in-law of the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab).

He yalak (went) with Yawaram (Joram) the ban (son) of Achaab (Ahab) to malachamah (war) against Chazaal (Hazael) malak (king) of Aram (Syria) at Ramath-Galaid (Ramoth Gilead): and the Aramay (Syrians) wounded Yawaram (Joram).

Malak (king) Yawaram (Joram) shawab (turn back / repent) to be rapaa (healed) in Yazaraial (Jezreel) of the makayam (wounds) which the Aramay (Syrians) had nakah (given) him at Ramah (Ramah), when he lacham (fought) against Chazaal (Hazael) malak (king) of Aram (Syria). Achazayah (Ahaziah) the ban (son) of Yahawaram (Jehoram) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) yarad (went) down to raah (see) Yawaram (Joram) the ban (son) of Achaab (Ahab) in Yazaraial (Jezreel), because he was chalah (afflict).

Alayashai (Elisha) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) qaraa (called) achad (one) of the banay (sons) of the nabayaayam (prophets), and amar (spoke) to him, "chagar (put) your belt on your waist, laqach (take / seize) this pak (vial) of shaman (oil) in your yad (hand), and yalak (go) to Ramath-Galaid (Ramoth Gilead).

When you bawaa (come) there, find Yahawaa (Jehu) the ban (son) of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the ban (son) of Namashay (Nimshi), and bawaa (come) in, and make him qawam (rise up) up from thawak (midst) his ach (brother/kinsman), and bawaa (come) him to an chadar (inner) room.

Then laqach (take / seize) the pak (vial) of shaman (oil), and yatzaq (pour) it on his raash (head), and amar (spoke), ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "I have mashach (anointed) you malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel)."' Then pathach (open) the dalath (door), nawas (flee), and don't chakah (wait)."
So the nair (young) man, even the nair (young) man the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), yalak (went) to Ramath-Galaid (Ramoth Gilead).

When he bawaa (come), behold, the sharay (captains) of the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) were sitting. Then he amar (spoke), "I have a dabar (word / matter) for you, shar (prince / ruler)." Yahawaa (Jehu) amar (spoke), "To which of us all?" He amar (spoke), "To you, O shar (prince / ruler)."

He qawam (rise up), and bawaa (come) into the bayath (house). Then he yatzaq (poured) the shaman (oil) on his raash (head), and amar (spoke) to him, "Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), ‘I have mashach (anointed) you malak (king) over the im (nation / people) of Yahawah, even over Yashar-Al (Israel).

You shall nakah (strike) the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab) your adawan (master / lord), that I may naqam (avenge) the dam (blood) of my ibaday (servants) the nabayaayam (prophets), and the dam (blood) of all the ibaday (servants) of Yahawah, at the yad (hand) of Ayazabal (Jezebel).

For the whole bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab) shall abad (destroy / perish). I will karath (cut) off from Achaab (Ahab) everyone who urinates against a qayar (wall), both him who is itzar (shut) up and him who is izab (left) at large in Yashar-Al (Israel).

I will nathan (give) the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab) like the bayath (house) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Nabat (Nebat), and like the bayath (house) of Baishaa (Baasha) the ban (son) of Achayah (Ahijah).

The kalabayam (dogs) will akal (eat) Ayazabal (Jezebel) on the plot of ground of Yazaraial (Jezreel), and there shall be none to qabar (bury) her.'" He pathach (opened) the dalath (door), and nawas (fled).

Then Yahawaa (Jehu) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to the ibaday (servants) of his Adawan: and one amar (spoke) to him, "Is shalawam (peace / safety) well? Why did this shagai (mad) fellow bawaa (come) to you?" He amar (spoke) to them, "You yadai (know) the ayash (man / husband) and what his shayach (talk) was."

They amar (spoke), "That is a shaqar (lie). Nagad (tell) us now." He amar (spoke), "He amar (spoke) to me, ‘Thus yaamaraw (says) Yahawah, I have mashach (anointed) you malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel).'"

Then they hurried, and laqach (take / seize) every ayash (man / husband) his bagad (garment), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it under him on the garam (top) of the mailawath (stairs), and thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn), amar (spoke), "Yahawaa (Jehu) is malak (king)."

So Yahawaa (Jehu) the ban (son) of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the ban (son) of Namashay (Nimshi) qashar (conspired) against Yawaram (Joram). (Now Yawaram (Joram) was shamar (keep/guard) Ramath-Galaid (Ramoth Gilead), he and all Yashar-Al (Israel), panayam (face) of Chazaal (Hazael) malak (king) of Aram (Syria);

But malak (king) Yahawaram (Joram) was shawab (turn back / repent) to be rapaa (healed) in Yazaraial (Jezreel) of the makayam (wounds) which the Aramay (Syrians) had nakah (given) him, when he lacham (fought) with Chazaal (Hazael) malak (king) of Aram (Syria).) Yahawaa (Jehu) amar (spoke), "If this is your thinking, then let no al (not) palayat (escape) and yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the iyar (city), to yalak (go) to nagad (tell) it in Yazaraial (Jezreel)."

So Yahawaa (Jehu) rakab (rode) in a chariot, and yalak (went) to Yazaraial (Jezreel); for Yawaram (Joram) shakab (lay) there. Achazayah (Ahaziah) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) had yarad (come) down to raah (see) Yawaram (Joram).

Now the tzapah (watchman / keep watch) was imad (standing) on the magadal (tower) in Yazaraial (Jezreel), and he raah (see) the shapaih (company) of Yahawaa (Jehu) as he bawaa (come), and amar (spoke), "I raah (see) a shapaih (company)." Yahawaram (Joram) amar (spoke), "laqach (take / seize) a rakab (horseman), and shalach (send) to qaraah (meet) them, and let him amar (spoke), ‘Is it shalawam (peace / safety)?'"

So there yalak (went) one on rakab (horseback) to qaraah (meet) him, and amar (spoke), "Thus amar (spoke) the malak (king), ‘Is it shalawam (peace / safety)?'" Yahawaa (Jehu) amar (spoke), "What do you have to do with shalawam (peace / safety)? Fall in achar (other) me!" The tzapah (watchman / keep watch) said, "The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) bawaa (come) to them, but he isn't shawab (turn back / repent) back."

Then he shalach (send) out a shanay (second) on rakab (horseback), who bawaa (come) to them, and amar (spoke), "Thus amar (spoke) the malak (king), ‘Is it shalawam (peace / safety)?'" Yahawaa (Jehu) amar (spoke), "What do you have to do with shalawam (peace / safety)? Fall in achar (other) me!"

The tzapah (watchman / keep watch) said, "He bawaa (come) to them, and isn't shawab (turn back / repent) back. The manahag (driving) is like the manahag (driving) of Yahawaa (Jehu) the ban (son) of Namashay (Nimshi); for he nahag (drives) shagaiwan (furiously)."

Yahawaram (Joram) amar (spoke), "Get asar (ready)!" They got his rakab (chariot) asar (ready). Yahawaram (Joram) malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) and Achazayah (Ahaziah) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, ayash (man / husband) in his rakab (chariot), and they yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) Yahawaa (Jehu), and matzaa (found) him in the chalaqah (portion) of Nabawath (Naboth) the yazaraialay (jezreelite).

It happened, when Yahawaram (Joram) raah (see) Yahawaa (Jehu), that he amar (spoke), "Is it shalawam (peace / safety), Yahawaa (Jehu)?" He amar (spoke), "What shalawam (peace / safety), so id (until / as far as) as the prostitution of your am (mother) Ayazabal (Jezebel) and her kashap (witchcraft) rab (abound)?"
Yahawaram (Joram) hapak (turned) his yad (hand), and nawas (fled), and amar (spoke) to Achazayah (Ahaziah), "There is treason, Achazayah (Ahaziah)!"

Yahawaa (Jehu) drew his qashath (bow) with his malaa (full) yad (hand), and nakah (struck) Yahawaram (Joram) between his zarawai (arms); and the chatzay (arrow) yatzaa (go out / come out) out at his lab (heart), and he karai (sunk) down in his rakab (chariot).

Then Jehu amar (spoke) to Badaqar (Bidkar) his shalayash (captain), "Pick him up, and shalak (throw) him in the plot of the shadah (field) of Nabawath (Naboth) the yazaraialay (jezreelite); for zakar (remember) how, when you and I rakab (rode) tzamad (together) achar (other) Achaab (Ahab) his ab (father), Yahawah nashaa (lift) this mashaa (burden) on him:

‘Raah (see) I have seen amash (yesterday) the dam (blood) of Nabawath (Naboth), and the dam (blood) of his ban (son),' naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah; ‘and I will shalam (repay) you in this plot of ground,' naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah. Now therefore nashaa (lift) and shalak (cast) him onto the plot of ground, according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah."

But when Achazayah (Ahaziah) the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) raah (see) this, he nawas (fled) by the darak (way) of the gan (garden) bayath (house). Yahawaa (Jehu) radap (followed) achar (other) him, and amar (spoke), "nakah (strike) him also in the marakabah (chariot)!" They struck him at the mailah (ascent) of Gawar (Gur), which is by Yabalaim (Ibleam). He nawas (fled) to Magadawan (Megiddo), and mawath (death) there.
His ibad (servant) rakab (carried) him in a chariot to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and qabar (bury) him in his tomb with his ab (father) in the iyar (city) of Dawad (David).
In the ishar (-teen) shanah (year) of Yawaram (Joram) the ban (son) of Achaab (Ahab) began Achazayah (Ahaziah) to malak (king) over Yahawadah (Judah).

When Yahawaa (Jehu) bawaa (come) come to Yazaraial (Jezreel), Ayazabal (Jezebel) shamai (hearken / hear) of it; and she shawam (place / establish / appoint) her iyan (eye), and attired her raash (head), and shaqap (looked) out at the chalawan (window).
As Yahawaa (Jehu) bawaa (come) in at the shair (gate), she amar (spoke), "Do you come in shalawam (peace / safety), Zamaray (Zimri), you harag (kill) of your adawan (master / lord)?"
He nashaa (lift) up his panayam (face) to the chalawan (window), and amar (spoke), "Who is on my side? Who?" Shanayam (two) or shalawash (three) sarayasayam (eunuchs) shaqap (looked) out at him.

He amar (spoke), "shamat (throw) her down!" So they shamat (threw) her down; and some of her dam (blood) was nazah (sprinkled) on the qayar (wall), and on the sawasayam (horses). Then he ramas (trampled) her under foot.

When he bawaa (come) come in, he akal (eat) and shathah (drinks); and he amar (spoke), "paqad (visit) now to this arar (cursed) woman, and qabar (bury) her; for she is a malak (king) banath (daughter)."
They yalak (went) to qabar (bury) her; but they matzaa (found) no more of her am (mother) the galagalath (skull), and the ragalayam (feet), and the kapawath (palms) of her yadayam (hands).

Therefore they shawab (turn back / repent) back, and nagad (told) him. He amar (spoke), "This is the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, which he dabar (word / matter) by his ibad (servant) Alayah (Elijah) the thashabay (tishbite), amar (spoke), ‘The kalabayam (dogs) will akal (eat) the bashar (flesh) of Ayazabal (Jezebel) on the plot of Yazaraial (Jezreel),

And the nabalah (body) of Ayazabal (Jezebel) shall be as daman (dung) on the panayam (face) of the shadah (field) in the chalaq (portion) of Yazaraial (Jezreel), so that they shall not amar (spoke), "This is Ayazabal (Jezebel)."'"

Now Achaab (Ahab) had shabaiyam (seventy) banayam (sons) in Shamarawan (Samaria). Yahawaa (Jehu) kathab (write) saparayam (letters), and shalach (send) to Shamarawan (Samaria), to the sharay (rulers) of Yazaraial (Jezreel), even the zaqanayam (elders), and to those who aman (believe / have faith) up the sons of Achaab (Ahab), amar (spoke),

"Now as soon as this sapar (book / scribed document) bawaa (come) to you, since your adawan (master / lord) banay (sons) are with you, and there are with you rakab (chariots) and sawasayam (horses), a fortified iyar (city) also, and armor.

Select the tawab (good / proper function) and fittest of your adawan (master / lord) banay (sons), shawam (place / establish / appoint) him on his ab (father) kasaa (throne), and lacham (fight) for your adawan (master / lord) bayath (house)."
But they were maad (exceedingly) yaraa (fear / be afraid), and amar (spoke), "Behold, the shanayam (two) malakayam (kings) didn't imad (stand) panayam (face) him! How then shall we imad (stand)?"

He who was over the bayath (house), and he who was over the iyar (city), the zaqanayam (elders) also, and those who raised the children, shalach (send) to Yahawaa (Jehu), amar (spoke), "We are your ibad (servant), and will ishah (make) all that you ask us. We will not make any man malak (king). You ishah (make) that which is tawab (good / proper function) in your iyan (eye)."

Then he kathab (write) a sapar (book / scribed document) the shanay (second) time to them, amar (spoke), "If you are on my side, and if you will shamai (hearken / hear) to my qawal (sound / voice), laqach (take / seize) the raashay (heads) of the raashay (men) your adawan (master / lord) banay (sons), and bawaa (come) to me to Yazaraial (Jezreel) by machar (tomorrow) this ith (time)." Now the malak (king) banay (sons), being shabaiyam (seventy) anashay (persons), were with the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) men of the iyar (city), who gadal (brought) them up.

It happened, when the sapar (book / scribed document) bawaa (come) to them, that they laqach (take / seize) the malak (king) banay (sons), and shachat (killed) them, even shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (man / husband), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) their raash (head) in dawadayam (baskets), and shalach (send) them to him to Yazaraial (Jezreel).

A malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) bawaa (come), and nagad (told) him, "They bawaa (come) brought the raashay (heads) of the malak (king) banay (sons)." He amar (spoke), "shawam (place / establish / appoint) them in shanayam (two) tzabarayam (heaps) at the pathach (entrance) of the shair (gate) until the baqar (morning)."

It happened in the baqar (morning), that he yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and imad (stood), and amar (spoke) to all the im (nation / people), "You are tzadayaq (righteous). Behold, I qashar (conspired) against my adawan (master / lord), and harag (kill) him; but who nakah (struck) all these?

Yadai (know) apaw (now) that nothing shall napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land) of the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, which Yahawah dabar (word / matter) concerning the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab). For Yahawah ishah (make) done that which he dabar (word / matter) by his ibad (servant) Alayah (Elijah)."

So Yahawaa (Jehu) nakah (struck) all that shaar (remained) of the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab) in Yazaraial (Jezreel), with all his gadawal (very great/important/mighty) men, his yadai (familiar) friends, and his kahan (priest), until he shaar (left) him none sharayad (remaining).
He qawam (rise up) and departed, and yalak (went) to Shamarawan (Samaria). As he was at the raih (shearing) bayathaiqad (house) of the shepherds on the darak (way),

Yahawaa (Jehu) matzaa (met) with the achay (brothers) of Achazayah (Ahaziah) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and amar (spoke), "Who are you?" They amar (spoke), "We are the achay (brothers) of Achazayah (Ahaziah). We are yarad (going) down to greet the banay (children) of the malak (king) and the banay (children) of the gabayarah (queen)."

He amar (spoke), "thapash (take) them chay (life)!" They thapash (took) them chay (life), and shachat (killed) them at the bawar (pit) of the shearing bayathaiqad (house), even arabaiyam (forty) - shanayam (two) ayash (man / husband). He didn't shaar (leave) any of them.

When he had departed from there, he met Yahawanadab (Jehonadab) the ban (son) of Rakab (Rechab) coming to qaraah (meet) him. He greeted him, and amar (spoke) to him, "Is your labab (heart) yashar (upright), as my labab (heart) is with your labab (heart)?" Yahawanadab (Jehonadab) amar (spoke), "It is." "If it is, nathan (give) me your yad (hand)." He nathan (give) him his yad (hand); and he ilah (go up / offer) him up to him into the marakabah (chariot).
He amar (spoke), "yalak (come) with me, and raah (see) my qanaah (zeal) for Yahawah." So they rakab (made) him ride in his rakab (chariot).

When he bawaa (come) to Shamarawan (Samaria), he nakah (struck) all who shaar (remained) to Achaab (Ahab) in Shamarawan (Samaria), until he had destroyed him, according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, which he dabar (word / matter) to Alayah (Elijah).

Yahawaa (Jehu) qabatz (gathered) all the im (nation / people) qabatz (together), and amar (spoke) to them, "Achaab (Ahab) ibad (servant) Bail (Baal) a mait (little); but Yahawaa (Jehu) will ibad (servant) him much.

Now therefore qaraa (called) to me all the nabayaay (prophets) of Bail (Baal), all of his ibaday (worshippers), and all of his kahan (priest). Let ayash (man / husband) be absent; for I have a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) zabach (sacrifice) to Bail (Baal). Whoever is absent, he shall not chayah (live)." But Yahawaa (Jehu) ishah (make) it in subtlety, intending that he might abad (destroy / perish) the ibaday (worshippers) of Bail (Baal).
Yahawaa (Jehu) amar (spoke), "qadash (set apart / make holy) a solemn itzarah (assembly) for Bail (Baal)!" They qaraa (called) it.

Yahawaa (Jehu) shalach (send) through all Yashar-Al (Israel); and all the ibaday (worshippers) of Bail (Baal) bawaa (come), so that there was not a ayash (man / husband) shaar (left) that didn't bawaa (come). They bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of Bail (Baal); and the bayath (house) of Bail (Baal) was malaa (filled) from one pah (end) to another.
He amar (spoke) to him who was over the malathachah (vestry), "yatzaa (go out / come out) out robes for all the ibaday (worshippers) of Bail (Baal)!" He brought robes out to them.

Yahawaa (Jehu) bawaa (come) with Yahawanadab (Jehonadab) the ban (son) of Rakab (Rechab) into the bayath (house) of Bail (Baal). Then he amar (spoke) to the ibaday (worshippers) of Bail (Baal), "chapash (search), and raah (see) that there are here with you none of the ibaday (servants) of Yahawah, but the ibaday (worshippers) of Bail (Baal) only."

They bawaa (come) in to ishah (make) zabachayam (sacrifices) and burnt ilawath (offerings). Now Yahawaa (Jehu) had shawam (place / establish / appoint) him shamanayam (eighty) anashayam (men) outside, and amar (spoke), "If any of the ishah (make) whom I bawaa (come) into your yad (hand) malat (escape), he who lets him go, his napash (soul) shall be for the napash (soul) of him."

It happened, as soon as he kalah (complete / finish) made an end of ilah (offering) the burnt ishah (make), that Yahawaa (Jehu) amar (spoke) to the rawatz (guard) and to the shalashayam (captains), "bawaa (come) in, and nakah (kill) them! Let ayash (man / husband) yatzaa (go out / come out)." They nakah (struck) them with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword); and the rawatz (guard) and the shalashayam (captains) shalak (cast) them out, and yalak (went) to the iyar (city) of the bayath (house) of Bail (Baal).
They yatzaa (go out / come out) out the matzabawath (pillars) that were in the bayath (house) of Bail (Baal), and sharap (burned) them.
They nathatz (broke) down the matzabah (pillar) of Bail (Baal), and nathatz (broke) down the bayath (house) of Bail (Baal), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it a latrine, to this yawam (day).
Thus Yahawaa (Jehu) destroyed Bail (Baal) out of Yashar-Al (Israel).

However from the chataay (sins) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Nabat (Nebat), with which he made Yashar-Al (Israel) to chataa (sin), Yahawaa (Jehu) didn't sawar (depart) from achar (other) them, the zahab (gold) calves that were in Bayath-Al (Bethel), and that were in Dan (Dan).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to Yahawaa (Jehu), "Because you have tawab (good / proper function) well in ishah (make) that which is yashar (upright) in my iyan (eye), and ishah (make) done to the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab) according to all that was in my labab (heart), your banay (sons) of the rabayaiy (fourth) generation shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the kasaa (throne) of Yashar-Al (Israel)."

But Yahawaa (Jehu) shamar (keep/guard) no heed to yalak (walk) in the thawarah (instruction) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), with all his labab (heart). He didn't sawar (depart) from the chataawath (sins) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam), with which he made Yashar-Al (Israel) to chataa (sin).

In those yamayam (days) Yahawah chalal (began) to qatzah (end / extremity / border) off from Yashar-Al (Israel); and Chazaal (Hazael) nakah (struck) them in all the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yashar-Al (Israel);

From the Yaradan (Jordan) eastward, all the aratz (Earth/land) of Galaid (Gilead), the Gaday (Gadites), and the Raawabanay (Reubenites), and the Manashay (Manassites), from Irawair (Aroer), which is by the nachal (stream / river) of the Aranawan (Arnon), even Galaid (Gilead) and Bashan (Bashan).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabaray (acts) of Yahawaa (Jehu), and all that he ishah (make), and all his gabawarah (might), aren't they kathab (write) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabaray (chronicles) of the malakay (kings) of Yashar-Al (Israel)?
Yahawaa (Jehu) shakab (slept) with his ab (father); and they qabar (bury) him in Shamarawan (Samaria). Yahawaachaz (Jehoahaz) his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.
The yawam (day) that Yahawaa (Jehu) malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel) in Shamarawan (Samaria) was isharayam (twenty) - shamanah (eight) shanah (years).

Now when Ithalayah (Athaliah) the am (mother) of Achazayah (Ahaziah) raah (see) that her ban (son) was mawath (death), she qawam (rise up) and abad (destroy / perish) all the zarai (seed) mamalakah (royal).

But Yahawashabai (Jehosheba), the banath (daughter) of malak (king) Yawaram (Joram), achawath (sister) of Achazayah (Ahaziah), laqach (take / seize) Yawaash (Joash) the ban (son) of Achazayah (Ahaziah), and ganab (stole) him away from thawak (midst) the malak (king) banay (sons) who were mawath (death), even him and his yanaq (nurse), and put them in the bedroom; and they sathar (hid) him from Ithalayah (Athaliah), so that he was not mawath (death);
He was with her chabaa (hidden) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah shash (six) shanayam (years). Ithalayah (Athaliah) malak (king) over the aratz (Earth/land).

In the shabayaiy (seventh) shanah (year) Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) shalach (send) and laqach (take / seize) the karay (captains) over maayawath (hundreds) of the Carites and of the rawatz (guard), and bawaa (come) them to him into the bayath (house) of Yahawah; and he karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with them, and took an shabai (swear / take oath) of them in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and showed them the malak (king) ban (son).

He tzawah (commanded) them, amar (spoke), "This is the thing that you shall ishah (make): a shalayashay (third) part of you, who bawaa (come) in on the shabath (shabath / rest), shall be keepers of the mashamarath (duty / watch) of the malak (king) bayath (house);

A shalayashay (third) part shall be at the shair (gate) Sawar (Sur); and a shalayashay (third) part at the shair (gate) achar (other) the rawatz (guard). So you shall shamar (keep/guard) the mashamarath (duty / watch) of the bayath (house), and be a barrier.

The shanayam (two) companies of you, even all who yatzaa (go out / come out) out on the shabath (shabath / rest), shall shamar (keep/guard) the mashamarath (duty / watch) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah around the malak (king).

You shall surround the malak (king), sabayab (surrounding) ayash (man / husband) with his kalay (weapons) in his yad (hand); and he who bawaa (come) within the ranks, let him be mawath (death). Be with the malak (king) when he yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and when he bawaa (come) in."

The sharay (captains) over maayawath (hundreds) ishah (make) according to all that Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) the kahan (priest) tzawah (commanded); and they laqach (take / seize) every ayash (man / husband) his yaishaw (men), those who were to bawaa (come) in on the shabath (shabath / rest), with those who were to yatzaa (go out / come out) out on the shabath (shabath / rest), and bawaa (come) to Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) the kahan (priest).

The kahan (priest) nathan (give) to the sharay (captains) over maayawath (hundreds) the chanayath (spears) and shalatayam (shields) that had been malak (king) Dawad (David's), which were in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

The rawatz (guard) imad (stood), every ayash (man / husband) with his kalay (weapons) in his yad (hand), from the yamanay (right) kathap (side) of the bayath (house) to the shamaalay (left) kathap (side) of the bayath (house), along by the mazabach (altar) and the bayath (house), around the malak (king).

Then he yatzaa (go out / come out) out the malak (king) ban (son), and nathan (give) the nazar (crown / consecrate) on him, and gave him the idawath (testimony); and they made him malak (king), and mashach (anointed) him; and they nakah (clapped) their kap (hands), and amar (spoke), "Long chayah (live) the malak (king)!"

When Ithalayah (Athaliah) shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the rawatz (guard) and of the im (nation / people), she bawaa (come) to the im (nation / people) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah:

And she raah (see), and behold, the malak (king) imad (stood) by the imawad (pillar), as the tradition was, and the sharayam (captains) and the chatzatzarawath (trumpets) by the malak (king); and all the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land) shamach (rejoiced), and thaqai (blow / sound alarm) chatzatzarawath (trumpets). Then Ithalayah (Athaliah) qarai (tore) her clothes, and qaraa (called), "qashar (treason)! Qashar (treason)!"

Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) the kahan (priest) tzawah (commanded) the sharay (captains) of mayaawath (hundreds) who were set over the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), and amar (spoke) to them, "yatzaa (go out / come out) her out between the ranks. Mawath (death) him who bawaa (come) her with the charab (sword)." For the kahan (priest) amar (spoke), "Don't let her be mawath (death) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah."

So they shawam (place / establish / appoint) yad (hand) for her; and she bawaa (come) by the darak (way) of the sawasayam (horses)' mabawaa (entry) to the malak (king) bayath (house). She was mawath (death) there.

Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) between Yahawah and the malak (king) and the im (nation / people), that they should be Yahawah im (nation / people); between the malak (king) also and the im (nation / people).

All the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land) bawaa (come) to the bayath (house) of Bail (Baal), and nathatz (broke) it down; his mazabachawath (altars) and his tzalam (likeness) shabar (broke) they in pieces yatab (thoroughly), and harag (kill) Mathan (Mattan) the kahan (priest) of Bail (Baal) panayam (face) the mazabachawath (altars). The kahan (priest) shawam (place / establish / appoint) kahan (priest) over the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

He laqach (take / seize) the karay (captains) over maawath (hundreds), and the Carites, and the rawatz (guard), and all the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land); and they yarad (brought) down the malak (king) from the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and bawaa (come) by the darak (way) of the shair (gate) of the rawatz (guard) to the malakayam (kings) bayath (house). He yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the kasaa (throne) of the malakayam (kings).

So all the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land) shamach (rejoiced), and the iyar (city) was shaqat (quiet). Ithalayah (Athaliah) they had mawath (death) with the charab (sword) at the malak (king) bayath (house).
Yahawaash (Jehoash) was shabai (seven) shanah (years) ban (son) when he began to malak (king).
In the shabai (seven) shanah (year) of Jehu began Yahawaash (Jehoash) to malak (king); and he malak (king) forty shanayam (years) in Jerusalem: and his mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.
Yahawaash (Jehoash) did that which was right in the eyes of Yahawah all his arabaiyam (forty) in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
However the high places were not ishah (make) away; the people still ishah (make) and burnt incense in the high places.

Jehoash said to the priests, "All the money of the holy things that is sawar (brought) into the bamah (house) of Yahawah, in current money, the money of the persons for whom each bamah (man) is rated, and all the money that it comes into any bamawath (mans) heart to sawar (bring) into the bamah (house) of Yahawah,
Let the kahanayam (priests) bawaa (come) it to them, every ayash (man / husband) from his acquaintance; and they shall repair the breaches of the bayath (house), wherever any breach shall be found."
But it was so, that in the three and twentieth year of king Jehoash the kahanayam (priests) had not chazaq (repaired) the breaches of the bayath (house).

Then malak (king) Yahawaash (Jehoash) called for Jehoiada the kahan (priest), and for the other kahanayam (priests), and said to them, "Why don't you chazaq (repair) the breaches of the bayath (house)? Now therefore chazaq (take) no more money from your treasurers, but deliver it for the breaches of the bayath (house)."
The kahanayam (priests) consented that they should laqach (take / seize) no more kasap (money) from the people, ayan (NO ONE) chazaq (repair) the breaches of the bayath (house).

But Jehoiada the kahan (priest) laqach (take / seize) a chest, and bored a hole in its lid, and set it beside the altar, on the right side as one comes into the bayath (house) of Yahawah: and the kahanayam (priests) who kept the threshold put therein all the kasap (money) that was laqach (take / seize) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

It was so, when they atzal (saw) that there was much kasap (money) in the arawan (chest), that the king's scribe and the ayash (man / husband) kahan (priest) nathan (give) up, and they nathan (give) up in bags and nathan (give) the kasap (money) that was found in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

They gave the kasap (money) that was weighed out into the matzaa (hands) of those who hayah (came to pass) the ilah (go up / offer), who hayah (came to pass) the oversight of the bayath (house) of Yahawah: and they paid it out to the carpenters and the builders, who ilah (go up / offer) on the bayath (house) of Yahawah,

And to the charashay (masons) and the stone cutters, and for buying itz (timber) and cut stone to banah (build) the breaches of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and for all that was yatzaa (go out / come out) out for the bayath (house) to banah (build) it.

But there were not gadar (made) for the bayath (house) of Yahawah cups of silver, snuffers, basins, trumpets, any vessels of gold, or vessels of silver, of the money that was yatzaa (go out / come out) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah;
For they bawaa (come) that to those who did the ishah (make), and repaired therewith the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
Moreover they didn't demand an accounting from the ishay (men) into whose hand they nathan (give) the money to nathan (give) to those who did the malaakah (work); for they dealt faithfully.
The kasap (money) for the trespass offerings, and the kasap (money) for the ishah (make) offerings, was not nathan (give) into the house of Yahawah: it was the priests'.
Then Hazael king of Syria bawaa (come) up, and fought against Gath, and bawaa (come) it; and Hazael bawaa (come) his face to bawaa (come) up to Jerusalem.

Jehoash malak (king) of Gath (Judah) ilah (go up / offer) all the gath (holy) things that Jehoshaphat and Jehoram and Ahaziah, his fathers, malak (king) of Gath (Judah), had dedicated, and his own gath (holy) things, and all the gold that was found in the treasures of the gath (house) of Yahawah, and of the malak (king) gath (house), and sent it to Chazaal (Hazael) malak (king) of Aram (Syria): and he ilah (go up / offer) away from Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).
Now the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, aren't they written in the book of the chronicles of the malakay (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)?
His servants arose, and made a conspiracy, and struck Yawaash (Joash) at the house of Millo, on the way that ishah (make) down to Silla.

For Jozacar the son of Shimeath, and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his ibad (servant), nakah (struck) him, and he died; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David: and Amaziah his son reigned in his place.

In the shalawash (three) and isharayam (twenty) shanah (year) of Yawaash (Joash) the ban (son) of Achazayah (Ahaziah), malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Yahawaachaz (Jehoahaz) the ban (son) of Yahawaa (Jehu) began to malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel) in Shamarawan (Samaria) for seventeen shanah (years).

He ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, and yalak (followed) the chataath (sins) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Nabat (Nebat), with which he made Yashar-Al (Israel) to chataa (sin); he didn't sawar (depart) from it.

The ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah was charah (hot with anger) against Yashar-Al (Israel), and he nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of Chazaal (Hazael) malak (king) of Aram (Syria), and into the yad (hand) of Banahadad (Benhadad) the ban (son) of Chazaal (Hazael), yawam (day).

Yahawaachaz (Jehoahaz) begged Yahawah, and Yahawah shamai (hearken / hear) to him; for he raah (see) the lachatz (oppression) of Yashar-Al (Israel), how that the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) lachatz (oppressed) them.

(Yahawah nathan (give) Yashar-Al (Israel) a savior, so that they yatzaa (go out / come out) out from under the yad (hand) of the Aram (Syrians); and the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) lived in their ahal (tents) as shalashawam (before).

Nevertheless they didn't sawar (depart) from the chataawath (sins) of the bayath (house) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam), with which he made Yashar-Al (Israel) to chataa (sin), but halak (move) therein: and there imad (remained) the Asharah (Asherah) also in Shamarawan (Samaria).)

For he didn't shaar (leave) to Yahawaachaz (Jehoahaz) of the im (nation / people) any more than chamashayam (fifty) horsemen, and ishar (ten) rakab (chariots), and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) footmen; for the malak (king) of Aram (Syria) abad (destroy / perish) them, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them like the ipar (dust) in dawash (threshing).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabaray (acts) of Yahawaachaz (Jehoahaz), and all that he ishah (make), and his gabawarah (might), aren't they kathab (write) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabaray (chronicles) of the malakay (kings) of Yashar-Al (Israel)?
Yahawaachaz (Jehoahaz) shakab (slept) with his ab (father); and they qabar (bury) him in Shamarawan (Samaria): and Yawaash (Joash) his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.

In the shalawashayam (thirty) - shabai (seven) shanah (year) of Yawaash (Joash) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Yahawaash (Jehoash) the ban (son) of Yahawaachaz (Jehoahaz) began to malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel) in Shamarawan (Samaria) for sixteen shanah (years).

He ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah; he didn't sawar (depart) from all the chataawath (sins) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Nabat (Nebat), with which he made Yashar-Al (Israel) to chataa (sin); but he halak (move) therein.

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabaray (acts) of Yawaash (Joash), and all that he ishah (make), and his gabawarah (might) with which he lacham (fought) against Amatzayah (Amaziah) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), aren't they kathab (write) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabaray (chronicles) of the malakay (kings) of Yashar-Al (Israel)?

Yawaash (Joash) shakab (slept) with his ab (father); and Yarabaim (Jeroboam) yashab (inhabit/dwell) on his kasaa (throne): and Yawaash (Joash) was qabar (bury) in Shamarawan (Samaria) with the malakay (kings) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Now Alayashai (Elisha) was chalah (afflict) sick of his chalay (sickness) of which he mawath (death): and Yawaash (Joash) the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) yarad (came) down to him, and bakah (wept) over him, and amar (spoke), "My ab (father), my ab (father), the rakab (chariots) of Yashar-Al (Israel) and its horsemen!"
Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke) to him, "laqach (take / seize) qashath (bow) and chatzayam (arrows);" and he laqach (take / seize) to him qashath (bow) and chatzayam (arrows).

He amar (spoke) to the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), "rakab (put) your yad (hand) on the qashath (bow);" and he rakab (put) his yad (hand) on it. Alayashai (Elisha) shawam (place / establish / appoint) his yaday (hands) on the malak (king) yaday (hands).

He amar (spoke), "pathach (open) the chalawan (window) eastward;" and he pathach (opened) it. Then Alayashai (Elisha) amar (spoke), "yarah (shoot)!" And he yarah (shot). He amar (spoke), "Yahawah chatz (arrow) of thashawaih (deliverance), even the chatz (arrow) of thashawaih (deliverance) over Aram (Syria); for you shall nakah (strike) the Aram (Syrians) in Apaq (Aphek), until you kalah (complete / finish) consumed them."

He amar (spoke), "laqach (take / seize) the chatzayam (arrows);" and he laqach (take / seize) them. He amar (spoke) to the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), "nakah (strike) the aratz (Earth/land);" and he nakah (struck) shalawash (three) times, and stopped.
