Atzal (Azel) had shash (six) banayam (sons), whose sham (name) are these: Izarayaqam (Azrikam), Bakaraw (Bocheru), and Yashamaial (Ishmael), and Shairayah (Sheariah), and Ibadayah (Obadiah), and Chanan (Hanan). All these were the banayam (sons) of Atzal (Azel).
The banay (sons) of Ishaq (Eshek) his ach (brother/kinsman): Awalam (Ulam) his bakawar (firstborn), Yaiwash (Jeush) the shanay (second), and Alayapalat (Eliphelet) the shalayashay (third).

The banay (sons) of Awalam (Ulam) were gabawar (mighty) banay (men) of valor, darakay (archers), and rabah (had) many banay (sons), and banay (sons)' banay (sons), one maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty). All these were of the banay (sons) of Banayamayan (Benjamin).

So all Yashar-Al (Israel) were yachash (reckoned) by genealogies; and behold, they are kathab (write) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the malakay (kings) of Yashar-Al (Israel): and Yahawadah (Judah) was galah (carried) away captive to Babal (Babylon) for their disobedience.

Now the raashawan (first) yawashabayam (inhabitants) who lived in their achazah (possessions) in their iyar (cities) were Yashar-Al (Israel), the kahanayam (priests), the Lawayay (Levites), and the nathayan (nethinim).

In Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) lived of the banay (children) of Yahawadah (Judah), and of the banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), and of the banay (children) of Aparayam (Ephraim) and Manashah (Manasseh):

Iwathay (Uthai) the ban (son) of Imayahawad (Ammihud), the ban (son) of Imaray (Omri), the ban (son) of Amaray (Imri), the ban (son) of Bani, of the banay (children) of Paratz (Perez) the ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah).
Of the Shayalawanay (Shilonites): Ishayah (Asaiah) the bakawar (firstborn), and his ban (son).
Of the banay (sons) of Zarach (Zerah): Yaiwaal (Jeuel), and their ach (brother/kinsman), shash (six) maah (hundred) thashaiyam (ninety).
Of the banay (sons) of Banayamayan (Benjamin): Salaw (Sallu) the ban (son) of Mashalam (Meshullam), the ban (son) of Hawadawayah (Hodaviah), the ban (son) of Sanawaah (Hassenuah),

And Yabanayah (Ibneiah) the ban (son) of Yaracham (Jeroham), and Alah (Elah) the ban (son) of Izay (Uzzi), the ban (son) of Makaray (Michri), and Mashalam (Meshullam) the ban (son) of Shapatayah (Shephatiah), the ban (son) of Raiwaal (Reuel), the ban (son) of Yabanayah (Ibnijah);

And their ach (brother/kinsman), according to their thawaladah (generation), thashai (nine) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) - shash (six). All these anashayam (men) were raashay (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (house).
Of the kahanayam (priests): Yadaiyah (Jedaiah), and Yahawayarayab (Jehoiarib), Yakayan (Jachin),

And Izarayah (Azariah) the ban (son) of Chalaqayah (Hilkiah), the ban (son) of Mashalam (Meshullam), the ban (son) of Tzadawaq (Zadok), the ban (son) of Marayawath (Meraioth), the ban (son) of Achayatawab (Ahitub), the nagayad (ruler) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam;

And Idayah (Adaiah) the ban (son) of Yaracham (Jeroham), the ban (son) of Pashachawar (Pashhur), the ban (son) of Malakayah (Malchijah), and Maishay (Maasai) the ban (son) of Idayaal (Adiel), the ban (son) of Yachazarah (Jahzerah), the ban (son) of Mashalam (Meshullam), the ban (son) of Mashalamayath (Meshillemith), the ban (son) of Amar (Immer);

And their ach (brother/kinsman), raashayam (heads) of their ab (father)' bayath (house), one alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty); very chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) gabawaray (men) for the malaakah (work) of the ibadah (service) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam.

Of the Lawayay (Levites): Shamaiyah (Shemaiah) the ban (son) of Chashawab (Hasshub), the ban (son) of Izarayaqam (Azrikam), the ban (son) of Chashabayah (Hashabiah), of the banay (sons) of Mararay (Merari);
And Baqabaqar (Bakbakkar), Charash (Heresh), and Galal (Galal), and Mathanayah (Mattaniah) the ban (son) of Mayakaa (Mica), the ban (son) of Zakaray (Zichri), the ban (son) of Asap (Asaph),

And Ibadayah (Obadiah) the ban (son) of Shamaiyah (Shemaiah), the ban (son) of Galal (Galal), the ban (son) of Yadawathawan (Jeduthun), and Barakayah (Berechiah) the ban (son) of Asaa (Asa), the ban (son) of Alaqanah (Elkanah), who lived in the chatzaray (villages) of the Natapathay (Netophathites).
The shairayam (porters): Shalawam (Shallum), and Iqawab (Akkub), and Talamawan (Talmon), and Achayaman (Ahiman), and their ach (brother/kinsman) (Shalawam (Shallum) was the raash (head)),
Who previously served in the malak (king) shair (gate) eastward: they were the shairayam (porters) for the machanah (camp) of the banay (children) of Laway (Levi).

Shalawam (Shallum) the ban (son) of Qawaraa (Kore), the ban (son) of Abayasap (Ebiasaph), the ban (son) of Qarach (Korah), and his ach (brother/kinsman), of his ab (father) bayath (house), the qarachayam (korahites), were over the malaakah (work) of the ibadah (service), keepers of the sapayam (thresholds) of the ahal (tent): and their ab (father) had been over the machanah (camp) of Yahawah, keepers of the mabawaa (entry).
Payanachas (Phinehas) the ban (son) of Alaizar (Eleazar) was nagayad (ruler) over them in panayam (face) past, and Yahawah was with him.
Zakarayah (Zechariah) the ban (son) of Mashalamayah (Meshelemiah) was shawair (porter) of the pathach (door) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

All these who were barar (chosen) to be shairayam (porters) in the sapayam (thresholds) were two maah (hundred) and shanayam (two). These were yachash (reckoned) by genealogy in their chatzar (villages), whom Dawad (David) and Shamawaal (Samuel) the seer yasad (ordained) in their amawanah (office) of trust.
So they and their ban (son) had the oversight of the shairayam (gates) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, even the bayath (house) of the ahal (tent), by mashamarawath (wards).
On the arabai (four) rawachawath (sides) were the shairayam (porters), toward the mazarach (east), yam (sea/waters), tzapawan (north), and nagab (south).
Their ach (brother/kinsman), in their chatzar (villages), were to bawaa (come) in every shabai (seven) yamayam (days) from ith (time) to ith (time) to be with them:

For the arabai (four) gabawar (chief) shairayam (porters), who were Lawayay (Levites), were in an amawanah (office) of trust, and were over the rooms and over the atzarawath (treasuries) in the bayath (house) of Alahayam.
They lawan (lodged) around the bayath (house) of Alahayam, because that duty was on them; and to them pertained its opening baqar (morning) by morning.
Certain of them were in il (over) of the kalay (vessels) of service; for by count were these bawaa (come) in and by count were these yatzaa (go out / come out) out.

Some of them also were manah (appointed) over the kalay (furniture), and over all the kalayam (vessels) of the qadash (set apart / make holy), and over the fine salath (flour), and the yayan (wine), and the shaman (oil), and the labawanah (frankincense), and the bashamayam (spices).
Some of the banay (sons) of the kahanayam (priests) raqach (prepared) the confection of the bashamayam (spices).

Mathathayah (Mattithiah), one of the Lawayay (Levites), who was the bakawar (firstborn) of Shalawam (Shallum) the qarachay (korahite), had the amawanah (office) of trust over the things that were baked in chabathayam (pans).
Some of their ach (brother/kinsman), of the banay (sons) of the Qahathay (Kohathites), were over the show lacham (bread), to kawan (prepare) it every shabath (shabath / rest).

These are the singers, raashay (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households of the Lawayay (Levites), who lived in the rooms and were patayar (free) from other service; for they were employed in their malaakah (work) yawamam (by day) and layal (night).
These were raashay (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households of the Lawayay (Levites), throughout their thawaladah (generation), raash (head) men: these lived at Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).
In Gabaiwan (Gibeon) there lived the ab (father) of Gabaiwan (Gibeon), Yaiyaal (Jeiel), whose ayashah (woman / wife) sham (name) was Maikah (Maacah):
And his bakawar (firstborn) ban (son) Ibadawan (Abdon), and Tzawar (Zur), and Qayash (Kish), and Bail (Baal), and Nar (Ner), and Nadab (Nadab),
And Gadar (Gedor), and Achayaw (Ahio), and Zakarayah (Zechariah), and Maqalawath (Mikloth).
Maqalawath (Mikloth) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Shamaam (Shimeam). They also lived with their ach (brother/kinsman) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), over against their ach (brother/kinsman).

Nar (Ner) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Qayash (Kish); and Qayash (Kish) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Shaawal (Saul); and Shaawal (Saul) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Yahawanathan (Jonathan), and Malakayashawai (Malchishua), and Abayanadab (Abinadab), and Ashabail (Eshbaal).
The ban (son) of Yahawanathan (Jonathan) was Marayababail (Merib Baal); and Marayababail (Merib Baal) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Mayakah (Micah).
The banay (sons) of Mayakah (Micah): Payathawan (Pithon), and malak (king), and Thacharai (Tahrea), and Ahaz.

Achaz (Ahaz) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Yairah (Jarah); and Yairah (Jarah) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Ilamath (Alemeth), and Izamawath (Azmaveth), and Zamaray (Zimri); and Zamaray (Zimri) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Mawatzaa (Moza);
And Mawatzaa (Moza) became the yalad (birth / begot) of Banaia (Binea); and Rapayah (Rephaiah) his ban (son), Alaishah (Eleasah) his ban (son), Atzal (Azel) his ban (son).

Atzal (Azel) had shash (six) banayam (sons), whose sham (name) are these: Izarayaqam (Azrikam), Bakaraw (Bocheru), and Yashamaial (Ishmael), and Shairayah (Sheariah), and Ibadayah (Obadiah), and Chanan (Hanan): these were the banayam (sons) of Atzal (Azel).

Now the Palashathay (Philistines) lacham (fought) against Yashar-Al (Israel): and the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) nawas (fled) from panayam (face) the Palashathay (Philistines), and napal (fall / be cast down) down chalal (slain) on har (mountain) Galabai (Gilboa).

The Palashathay (Philistines) dabaq (followed) hard achar (other) Shaawal (Saul) and achar (other) his banay (sons); and the Palashathay (Philistines) nakah (killed) Yawanathan (Jonathan), and Abayanadab (Abinadab), and Malakayashawai (Malchishua), the banay (sons) of Shaawal (Saul).
The malachamah (battle) went hard against Shaawal (Saul), and the mawarayam (archers) overtook him; and he was distressed by reason of the mawarayam (archers).

Then Shaawal (Saul) amar (spoke) to his armor bearer, "shalap (draw) your charab (sword), and thrust me through with it, lest these iral (uncircumcised) bawaa (come) and ilal (abuse) me." But his armor bearer would not; for he was terrified. Therefore Shaawal (Saul) laqach (take / seize) his charab (sword), and napal (fall / be cast down) on it.
When his armor bearer raah (see) that Shaawal (Saul) was mawath (death), he likewise napal (fall / be cast down) on his charab (sword), and mawath (death).
So Shaawal (Saul) mawath (death), and his shalawash (three) ban (son); and all his bayath (house) mawath (death) yachad (together).

When all the ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) who were in the imaq (valley) raah (see) that they nawas (fled), and that Shaawal (Saul) and his ban (son) were mawath (death), they forsook their iyar (cities), and nawas (fled); and the Palashathay (Philistines) bawaa (come) and lived in them.

It happened on the next macharath (day), when the Palashathay (Philistines) bawaa (come) to pashat (strip) the chalal (slain), that they matzaa (found) Shaawal (Saul) and his ban (son) napal (fall / be cast down) on har (mountain) Galabai (Gilboa).

They pashat (stripped) him, and nashaa (lift) his raash (head), and his armor, and shalach (send) into the aratz (Earth/land) of the Palashathay (Philistines) all around, to bashar (carry) the news to their itzab (idols), and to the im (nation / people).
They shawam (place / establish / appoint) his armor in the bayath (house) of their Alahayam, and thaqai (blow / sound alarm) his galagalath (head) in the bayath (house) of Dagawan (Dagon).
When all Yabash (Jabesh Gilead) shamai (hearken / hear) all that the Palashathay (Philistines) ishah (make) done to Shaawal (Saul),

All the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ayash (man / husband) qawam (rise up), and nashaa (lift) away the gawapah (body) of Shaawal (Saul), and the gawapath (bodies) of his ban (son), and bawaa (come) them to Yabash (Jabesh), and qabar (bury) their itzam (bones) under the alah (oak / terebinth) in Yabash (Jabesh), and tzawam (fasted) shabai (seven) yamayam (days).

So Shaawal (Saul) mawath (death) for his mail (top/above) which he mail (top/above) against Yahawah, because of the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, which he didn't shamar (keep/guard); and also because he shaal (asked) counsel of one who had a familiar awab (spirit), to darash (inquire),
And didn't darash (inquire) of Yahawah: therefore he mawath (death) him, and sabab (turned) the malawakah (kingdom) to Dawad (David) the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse).
Then all Yashar-Al (Israel) qabatz (gathered) themselves to Dawad (David) to Chabarawan (Hebron), amar (spoke), "Behold, we are your itzam (bone) and your bashar (flesh).

In thamawal (times) shalashawam (past), even when Shaawal (Saul) was malak (king), it was you who yatzaa (go out / come out) out and bawaa (come) in Yashar-Al (Israel). Yahawah your Alahayam amar (spoke) to you, ‘You shall be raih (shepherd) of my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel), and you shall be nagayad (prince) over my gam (indeed / moreover) Yashar-Al (Israel).'"

So all the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel) bawaa (come) to the malak (king) to Chabarawan (Hebron); and Dawad (David) karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with them in Chabarawan (Hebron) panayam (face) Yahawah; and they mashach (anointed) Dawad (David) malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel), according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah by Shamawaal (Samuel).

Dawad (David) and all Yashar-Al (Israel) yalak (went) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) (the same is Yabawas (Jebus)); and the Yabawasay (Jebusites), the yashabay (inhabitants) of the aratz (Earth/land), were there.

The yashabay (inhabitants) of Yabawas (Jebus) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "You shall not bawaa (come) in here." Nevertheless Dawad (David) lakad (took) the stronghold of Tzayawan (Zion). The same is the iyar (city) of Dawad (David).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "Whoever nakah (strikes) the Yabawasay (Jebusites) raashawan (first) shall be raash (head) and shar (prince / ruler)." Yawaab (Joab) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah) ilah (go up / offer) up raashawan (first), and was made raash (head).
Dawad (David) lived in the stronghold; therefore they qaraa (called) it the iyar (city) of Dawad (David).
He banah (build) the iyar (city) all around, from Malawaa (Millo) even around; and Yawaab (Joab) chayah (repaired) the shaar (rest) of the iyar (city).
Dawad (David) yalak (grew) halak (move) and halak (move); for Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) was with him.

Now these are the raash (head) of the gabawar (mighty) men whom Dawad (David) had, who showed themselves chazaq (strong) with him in his malakawath (kingdom), together with all Yashar-Al (Israel), to make him malak (king), according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah concerning Yashar-Al (Israel).

This is the masapar (number) of the gabawar (mighty) men whom Dawad (David) had: Yashabaim (Jashobeam), the son of a Chakamawanay (Hachmonite), the raash (head) of the shalawashayam (thirty); he iwar (rouse / awaken) up his chanayath (spear) against shalawash (three) maah (hundred) and chalal (killed) them at achad (one) paim (time).
Achar (other) him was Alaizar (Eleazar) the ban (son) of Dawadaw (Dodo), the Achawachay (Ahohite), who was one of the shalawash (three) gabawar (mighty) men.

He was with Dawad (David) at Pasadamayam (Pasdammim), and there the Palashathay (Philistines) were asap (gathered) together to malachamah (battle), where there was a plot of shadah (ground) malaa (full) of shairah (barley); and the im (nation / people) nawas (fled) from panayam (face) the Palashathay (Philistines).

They yatzab (stood) in the thawak (midst) of the plot, and natzal (defended) it, and nakah (killed) the Palashathay (Philistines); and Yahawah natzal (saved) them by a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thashawaih (deliverance).

Shalawash (three) of the shalawashayam (thirty) raash (head) men yarad (went) down to the tzawar (rock) to Dawad (David), into the mairah (cave) of Idalam (Adullam); and the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines) were chanah (encamped) in the imaq (valley) of Rapaa (Rephaim).
Dawad (David) was then in the stronghold, and the natzayab (garrison) of the Palashathay (Philistines) was then in Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem).
Dawad (David) awah (longed), and amar (spoke), "Oh that one would give me mayam (Waters) to shaqah (drink) of the bawar (well) of Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem), which is by the shair (gate)!"

The shalawash (three) baqai (broke) through the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and shaab (drew) mayam (Waters) out of the bawar (well) of Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem), that was by the shair (gate), and nashaa (lift) it, and bawaa (come) it to Dawad (David): but Dawad (David) would not shathah (drinks) of it, but nasak (poured) it out to Yahawah,

And amar (spoke), "My Alahayam chalayalah (forbid) it me, that I should ishah (make) zaath (this)! Shall I shathah (drinks) the dam (blood) of these ishaw (men) who napash (soul) put their lives in jeopardy?" For they risked their lives to bawaa (come) it. Therefore he would not shathah (drinks) it. The shalawash (three) gabawar (mighty) ishaw (men) did these things.

Abayashay (Abishai), the ach (brother/kinsman) of Yawaab (Joab), he was raash (head) of the shalawash (three); for he iwar (rouse / awaken) up his chanayath (spear) against shalawash (three) maah (hundred) and chalal (killed) them, and had a sham (name) among the shalawash (three).
Of the shalawash (three), he was more honorable than the shanayam (two), and was made their shar (prince / ruler): however he didn't bawaa (come) to the shalawash (three).

Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada), the ban (son) of a chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ayash (man / husband) of Qabatzaal (Kabzeel), who had done rab (mighty) pailayam (deeds), he nakah (killed) the shanayam (two) Arayaal (sons) of Ariel of Mawaab (Moab): he yarad (went) down also and nakah (killed) a aray (lion) in the midst of a bawar (pit) in yawam (day) of shalag (snow).

He nakah (killed) an Matzaray (Egyptian), a ayash (man / husband) of great madah (stature), chamash (five) amah (cubits) high; and in the Matzaray (Egyptian's) yad (hand) was a chanayath (spear) like a aragayam (weavers) manawar (beam); and he yarad (went) down to him with a shabat (staff), and gazal (plucked) the chanayath (spear) out of the Matzaray (Egyptian's) yad (hand), and harag (kill) him with his own chanayath (spear).
Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) ishah (make) these things, and had a sham (name) among the shalawash (three) gabawar (mighty) men.

Han (behold), he was more honorable than the shalawashayam (thirty), but he didn't bawaa (come) to the shalawash (three): and Dawad (David) shawam (place / establish / appoint) him over his mashamaith (guard).

Also the gabawar (mighty) men of the chayalayam (armies): Ishahaal (Asahel) the ach (brother/kinsman) of Yawaab (Joab), Alachanan (Elhanan) the ban (son) of Dawadaw (Dodo) of Bayath-Lacham (Bethlehem),
Shamawath (Shammoth) the harawaray (harorite), Chalatz (Helez) the palawanay (pelonite),
Iyaraa (Ira) the ban (son) of Iqash (Ikkesh) the Thaqawaiy (Tekoite), Abayaizar (Abiezer) the Inathathay (Anathothite),
Sabakay (Sibbecai) the chashathay (hushathite), Iyalay (Ilai) the Achawachay (Ahohite),
Maharay (Maharai) the Natapathay (Netophathite), Chalad (Heled) the ban (son) of Bainah (Baanah) the Natapathay (Netophathite),
Athay (Ithai) the ban (son) of Rayabay (Ribai) of Gabaih (Gibeah) of the banay (children) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), Banayah (Benaiah) the paraithawanay (pirathonite),
Chawaray (Hurai) of the nachalay (brooks) of Gaish (Gaash), Abayaal (Abiel) the Arbathite,
Izamawath (Azmaveth) the bacharawamay (baharumite), Alayachabaa (Eliahba) the shailabanay (shaalbonite),
The banay (sons) of Hasham (Hashem) the gazawanay (gizonite), Yawanathan (Jonathan) the ban (son) of Shagaa (Shagee) the hararay (hararite),
Achayaam (Ahiam) the ban (son) of Shakar (Sacar) the hararay (hararite), Alayapal (Eliphal) the ban (son) of Awar (Ur),
Chapar (Hepher) the makarathay (mecherathite), Achayah (Ahijah) the palawanay (pelonite),
Chatzaraw (Hezro) the karamalay (carmelite), Nairay (Naarai) the ban (son) of Azabay (Ezbai),
Yawaal (Joel) the ach (brother/kinsman) of Nathan (Nathan), Mabachar (Mibhar) the ban (son) of Hagri,
Tzalaq (Zelek) the Imawanay (Ammonite), Nacharay (Naharai) the barathay (berothite), the armor bearer of Yawaab (Joab) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah),
Iyaraa (Ira) the yatharay (ithrite), Garab (Gareb) the yatharay (ithrite),
Awarayah (Uriah) the Chathay (Hittite), Zabad (Zabad) the ban (son) of Achalay (Ahlai),
Idayanaa (Adina) the ban (son) of Shayazaa (Shiza) the Raawabanay (Reubenite), a raash (head) of the Raawabanay (Reubenites), and shalawashayam (thirty) with him,
Chanan (Hanan) the ban (son) of Maikah (Maacah), and Yawashapat (Joshaphat) the mathanay (mithnite),
Izayaa (Uzzia) the ishatharathay (ashterathite), Shamai (Shama) and Yaiyaal (Jeiel) the banay (sons) of Chawatham (Hotham) the irairay (aroerite),
Yadayaial (Jediael) the ban (son) of Shamaray (Shimri), and Yawachaa (Joha) his ach (brother/kinsman), the thayatzay (tizite),
Alayaal (Eliel) the machawayam (mahavite), and Yarayabay (Jeribai), and Yawashawayah (Joshaviah), the banay (sons) of Alanaim (Elnaam), and Yathamah (Ithmah) the Mawaabay (Moabite),
Alayaal (Eliel), and Iwabad (Obed), and Yaishayaal (Jaasiel) the Matzabayah (Mezobaite).

Now these are those who bawaa (come) to Dawad (David) to Tzaqalag (Ziklag), while he yet itzar (kept) himself close panayam (face) of Shaawal (Saul) the ban (son) of Qayash (Kish); and they were among the gabawar (mighty) men, his helpers in malachamah (war).

They were nashaq (armed) with qashath (bows), and could use both the right yaman (hand) and the shamaal (left) in slinging abanayam (stones) and in shooting chatzayam (arrows) from the qashath (bow): they were of Shaawal (Saul's) achay (brothers) of Banayamayan (Benjamin).

The raash (head) was Achayaizar (Ahiezer); then Yawaash (Joash), the banay (sons) of Shamaih (Shemaah) the gabaithay (gibeathite), and Yazawaal (Jeziel), and Palat (Pelet), the banay (sons) of Izamawath (Azmaveth), and Barakah (Beracah), and Yahawaa (Jehu) the Inathathay (Anathothite),

And Yashamaiyah (Ishmaiah) the Gabainay (Gibeonite), a gabawar (mighty) man among the shalawashayam (thirty), and over the shalawashayam (thirty), and Jeremiah, and Jahaziel, and Johanan, and Jozabad the Gederathite,
Eluzai, and Jerimoth, and Bealiah, and Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite,
Elkanah, and Isshiah, and Azarel, and Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korahites,
And Joelah, and Zebadiah, the qarachayam (sons) of Jeroham of Gedor.

Of the Gadites there separated themselves to David to the stronghold in the wilderness, ban (son) banay (men) of valor, banay (men) trained for war, that could handle shield and spear; whose yawaialah (faces) were like the yawaialah (faces) of lions, and they were as swift as the roes on the mountains;
Ezer the gabawar (chief), Obadiah the second, Eliab the third,
Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,
Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,
Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth,
Jeremiah the tenth, Machbannai the eleventh.
These of the sons of Gad were captains of the army: he who was least was equal to one hundred, and the greatest to one ishar (-teen).
These are those who went over the Jordan in the ban (son) month, when it had overflowed all its banks; and they put to flight all them of the valleys, both toward the east, and toward the west.
There ibar (pass over/through) of the children of Benjamin and Judah to the stronghold to David.

Dawad (David) bawaa (come) out to ban (son) them, and answered them, "If you bawaa (come) come peaceably to me to help me, my heart shall be knit to you; but if you have come to betray me to my adversaries, since there is no wrong in my hands, may the Alahayam of our fathers look thereon, and rebuke it."

Then the Spirit yatzaa (go out / come out) on Amasai, who was ab (father) of the thirty, and he said, "We are yours, Dawad (David), and on your side, you son of Jesse: shalawam (peace / safety), shalawam (peace / safety) be to you, and shalawam (peace / safety) be to your helpers; for your Alahayam helps you." Then Dawad (David) received them, and made them captains of the band.

Of Manasseh also there fell away some to Dawad (David), when he labash (came) with the Philistines against Saul to battle; but they didn't izar (help) them; for the lords of the Philistines nathan (give) him away after consultation, saying, "He will fall away to his master Saul to the jeopardy of our raashay (heads)."

As he bawaa (come) to Ziklag, there napal (fall / be cast down) to him of Manashah (Manasseh), Adnah, and Jozabad, and Jediael, and Michael, and Jozabad, and Elihu, and Zillethai, raash (head) of thousands who were of Manashah (Manasseh).
They helped David against the raash (head) of rovers: for they were all mighty men of valor, and were raashay (captains) in the army.
For from hayah (came to pass) to hayah (came to pass) men hayah (came to pass) to Dawad (David) to izar (help) him, until there was a great gadawad (army), like the gadawad (army) of Alahayam.
These are the numbers of the heads of those who were armed for bawaa (come), who bawaa (come) to Dawad (David) to Hebron, to turn the kingdom of Saul to him, according to the word of Yahawah.
The children of Judah who bore shield and spear were six thousand and eight hundred, chalatz (armed) for tzabaa (troop).
Of the banay (children) of Simeon, ban (son) men of valor for the tzabaa (troop), seven alap (thousand) and one maah (hundred).
Of the banay (children) of Levi four alap (thousand) and six maah (hundred).
Jehoiada was the leader of the household of Aaron; and with him were three alap (thousand) and seven maah (hundred),
And Zadok, a young man mighty of valor, and of his father's house twenty - two nagayad (captains).
Of the nair (children) of Benjamin, the brothers of Saul, three shanayam (two): for hitherto the greatest part of them had kept their allegiance to the bayath (house) of Saul.
Of the banay (children) of Ephraim twenty alap (thousand) eight hundred, ban (son) banay (men) of valor, famous men in their fathers' bayath (house).
Of the half-tribe of Manasseh eighteen alap (thousand), who were mentioned by sham (name), to ban (son) and make David king.
Of the children of Issachar, men who had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do, their heads were two hundred; and all their brothers were at their commandment.

Of Zebulun, such as were able to go out in the army, who could ishah (make) the battle in array, with all kinds of instruments of war, fifty thousand, and who could command and were not of double heart.
Of Naphtali one alap (thousand) captains, and with them with shield and spear thirty - seven alap (thousand).
Of the Danites who could set the battle in array, twenty - eight alap (thousand) six hundred.
Of Asher, such as were able to go out in the army, who could irak (set) the malachamah (battle) in array, forty alap (thousand).

On the other side of the Jordan, of the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and of the half - tribe of Manasseh, with all kinds of instruments of tzabaa (troop) for the malachamah (battle), one hundred twenty alap (thousand).

All these being men of malachamah (war), who could order the battle array, came with a perfect shabat (heart) to Hebron, to make David shabat (king) over all Israel: and all the rest also of Israel were of one shabat (heart) to make David shabat (king).
They were there with Dawad (David) three days, bawaa (come) and drinking; for their brothers had shalam (full / whole / complete) preparation for them.

Moreover those who were near to them, as far as Issachar and Zebulun and Naphtali, brought bread on donkeys, and on camels, and on mules, and on oxen, akal (eat) of meal, cakes of figs, and clusters of raisins, and wine, and oil, and cattle, and sheep in abundance: for there was joy in Israel.
Dawad (David) yaitz (consulted) with the sharay (captains) of alapayam (thousands) and of maawath (hundreds), even with every nagayad (leader).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to all the qahal (assembly) of Yashar-Al (Israel), "If it seems tawab (good / proper function) to you, and if it is of Yahawah our Alahayam, shalach (send) us send paratz (abroad) everywhere to our ach (brother/kinsman) who are shaar (left) in all the aratz (Earth/land) of Yashar-Al (Israel), with whom the kahanayam (priests) and Lawayay (Levites) are in their iray (cities) that have magarash (suburbs), that they may qabatz (gather) themselves to us;
And let us sabab (bring) again the arawan (ark) of our Alahayam to us. For we didn't darash (seek) it in the yamay (days) of Shaawal (Saul)."
All the qahal (assembly) amar (spoke) that they would ishah (make) so; for the thing was yashar (upright) in the iyanay (eyes) of all the im (nation / people).

So Dawad (David) qahal (assembled) all Yashar-Al (Israel) together, from the Shayachawar (Shihor) the brook of Matzarayam (Egypt) even to the entrance of Chamath (Hamath), to bawaa (come) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam from Kiriath Qarayath-Yairayam (Jearim).

Dawad (David) ilah (go up / offer) up, and all Yashar-Al (Israel), to Bailah (Baalah), that is, to Kiriath Qarayath-Yairayam (Jearim), which belonged to Yahawadah (Judah), to ilah (go up / offer) up from there the arawan (ark) of Alahayam Yahawah that yashab (inhabit/dwell) above the karawab (cherubim), that is qaraa (called) by the sham (name).

They rakab (carried) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam on a chadash (new) igalah (cart), and brought it out of the bayath (house) of Abayanadab (Abinadab): and Izaa (Uzza) and Achayaw (Ahio) nahag (drove) the igalah (cart).

Dawad (David) and all Yashar-Al (Israel) shachaq (played) panayam (face) Alahayam with all their iz (strength / might / refuge), even with shayarayam (songs), and with kanarawath (harps), and with stringed instruments, and with tambourines, and with matzalathayam (cymbals), and with chatzatzarawath (trumpets).
When they bawaa (come) to the garan (threshing) floor of Kayadawan (Chidon), Izaa (Uzza) shalach (send) forth his yad (hand) to achaz (hold) the arawan (ark); for the oxen shamat (stumbled).

The ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah was charah (hot with anger) against Izaa (Uzza), and he nakah (struck) him, because he shalach (send) forth his yad (hand) to the arawan (ark); and there he mawath (death) panayam (face) Alahayam.
Dawad (David) was charah (hot with anger), because Yahawah had broken paratz (forth) on Izaa (Uzza); and he qaraa (called) that maqawam (place) Perez Izaa (Uzza), to this yawam (day).
Dawad (David) was yaraa (fear / be afraid) of Alahayam that yawam (day), amar (spoke), "hayak (how) shall I bawaa (come) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam home to me?"
So Dawad (David) didn't move the arawan (ark) to him into the iyar (city) of Dawad (David), but natah (carried) it aside into the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom) the Gathay (Gittite).

The arawan (ark) of Alahayam yashab (inhabit/dwell) with the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom) in his bayath (house) shalawash (three) chadashayam (months): and Yahawah barak (blessed) the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom), and all that he had.

Chayaram (Hiram) malak (king) of Tzar (Tyre) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to Dawad (David), and araz (cedar) itzay (trees), and qayar (masons), and charashay (carpenters), to banah (build) him a bayath (house).

Dawad (David) yadai (perceived) that Yahawah had kawan (established) him malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel); for his malakawath (kingdom) was nashaa (lift) on mail (top/above), for his im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel's) sake.
Dawad (David) laqach (take / seize) more wives at Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); and Dawad (David) became the yalad (birth / begot) of more banayam (sons) and banawath (daughters).
These are the shamawath (names) of the yalawadayam (children) whom he had in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem): Shamawai (Shammua), and Shawabab (Shobab), Nathan (Nathan), and Shalamah (Solomon),
And Yabachar (Ibhar), and Alayashawai (Elishua), and Alayapalat (Elpelet),
And Nagah (Nogah), and Napag (Nepheg), and Yapayai (Japhia),
And Alayashamai (Elishama), and Bailayadai (Beeliada), and Alayapalat (Eliphelet).

When the Palashathay (Philistines) shamai (hearken / hear) that Dawad (David) was mashach (anointed) malak (king) over all Yashar-Al (Israel), all the Palashathay (Philistines) ilah (go up / offer) up to baqash (seek) Dawad (David): and Dawad (David) shamai (hearken / hear) of it, and yatzaa (go out / come out) out panayam (face) them.
Now the Palashathay (Philistines) bawaa (come) come and pashat (made) a raid in the imaq (valley) of Rapaa (Rephaim).

Dawad (David) inquired of Alahayam, amar (spoke), "Shall I ilah (go up / offer) up against the Palashathay (Philistines)? Will you nathan (give) them into my yad (hand)?" Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, "ilah (go up / offer) up; for I will nathan (give) them into your yad (hand)."

So they ilah (go up / offer) up to Bailaparatzayam (Baal Perazim), and Dawad (David) nakah (struck) them there; and Dawad (David) amar (spoke), Alahayam has paratz (broken) my ayab (enemy) by my yad (hand), like the paratz (breach) of mayam (Waters). Therefore they qaraa (called) the sham (name) of that maqawam (place) Bailaparatzayam (Baal Perazim).
They izab (left) their Alahayam there; and Dawad (David) amar (spoke) commandment, and they were sharap (burned) with ash (fire).
The Palashathay (Philistines) yet again pashat (made) a raid in the imaq (valley).

Dawad (David) inquired again of Alahayam; and Alahayam amar (spoke) to him, "You shall not ilah (go up / offer) up achar (other) them. Sabab (turn) away from them, and bawaa (come) on them over mawal (against) the bakaa (mulberry) trees.

It shall be, when you shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of marching in the raashay (tops) of the bakaa (mulberry) trees, that then you shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out to malachamah (battle); for Alahayam yatzaa (go out / come out) gone out panayam (face) you to nakah (strike) the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines)."
Dawad (David) ishah (make) as Alahayam tzawah (commanded) him: and they nakah (struck) the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines) from Gabaiwan (Gibeon) even to Gazar (Gezer).
The sham (name) of Dawad (David) yatzaa (go out / come out) out into all aratzawath (lands); and Yahawah nathan (give) the pachad (fear / dread) of him on all gawayam (nations).
David ishah (make) him bathayam (houses) in the iyar (city) of Dawad (David); and he kawan (prepared) a maqawam (place) for the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, and natah (pitched) for it a ahal (tent).

Then Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "No one ought to nashaa (lift) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam but the Lawayay (Levites). For Yahawah has bachar (chosen) them to nashaa (lift) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, and to sharath (minister) to him iwalam (forever)."

Dawad (David) qahal (assembled) all Yashar-Al (Israel) at Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), to ilah (go up / offer) up the arawan (ark) of Yahawah to its maqawam (place), which he had kawan (prepared) for it.
Dawad (David) asap (gathered) together the banay (sons) of Aharawan (Aaron), and the Lawayay (Levites):
Of the banay (sons) of Qahath (Kohath), Awarayaal (Uriel) the shar (prince / ruler), and his ach (brother/kinsman) one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty);
Of the banay (sons) of Mararay (Merari), Ishayah (Asaiah) the shar (prince / ruler), and his ach (brother/kinsman) two maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty);
Of the banay (sons) of Garashawan (Gershom), Yawaal (Joel) the shar (prince / ruler), and his ach (brother/kinsman) one maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty);
Of the banay (sons) of Alayatzapan (Elizaphan), Shamaiyah (Shemaiah) the shar (prince / ruler), and his ach (brother/kinsman) two maah (hundred);
Of the banay (sons) of Chabarawan (Hebron), Alayaal (Eliel) the shar (prince / ruler), and his ach (brother/kinsman) shamanayam (eighty);
Of the banay (sons) of Izayaal (Uzziel), Imayanadab (Amminadab) the shar (prince / ruler), and his ach (brother/kinsman) one maah (hundred) shanayam (two).

Dawad (David) qaraa (called) for Tzadawaq (Zadok) and Abayathar (Abiathar) the kahanayam (priests), and for the Lawayay (Levites), for Awarayaal (Uriel), Ishayah (Asaiah), and Yawaal (Joel), Shamaiyah (Shemaiah), and Alayaal (Eliel), and Imayanadab (Amminadab),

And amar (spoke) to them, "You are the raashay (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' households of the Lawayay (Levites). Qadash (set apart / make holy) yourselves, both you and your ach (brother/kinsman), that you may ilah (go up / offer) up the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), to the place that I have kawan (prepared) for it.
For because you didn't carry it at raashawan (first), Yahawah our Alahayam made paratz (broke) out against us, because we didn't darash (seek) him according to the mashapat (ordinance)."
So the kahanayam (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites) qadash (set apart / make holy) themselves to ilah (go up / offer) up the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel).

The banay (children) of the Lawayay (Levites) nashaa (lift) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam on their kathap (shoulders) with the poles thereon, as Mashah (Moses) tzawah (commanded) according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to the shar (prince / ruler) of the Lawayay (Levites) to imad (appoint) their ach (brother/kinsman) the singers, with kalay (instruments) of music, stringed kalay (instruments) and kanarawath (harps) and matzalathayam (cymbals), shamai (hearken / hear) aloud and rawam (will lift up) up the qawal (sound / voice) with shamachah (joy).

So the Lawayay (Levites) imad (appointed) Hayaman (Heman) the ban (son) of Yawaal (Joel); and of his ach (brother/kinsman), Asap (Asaph) the ban (son) of Barakayah (Berechiah); and of the banay (sons) of Mararay (Merari) their ach (brother/kinsman), Ayathan (Ethan) the ban (son) of Qawashayahaw (Kushaiah);

And with them their ach (brother/kinsman) of the mashanah (second) degree, Zakarayah (Zechariah), Ban (Ben), and Yaizayaal (Jaaziel), and Shamayaramawath (Shemiramoth), and Yachayaal (Jehiel), and Inay (Unni), Alayaab (Eliab), and Banayah (Benaiah), and Maishayah (Maaseiah), and Mathathayah (Mattithiah), and Alayapalahaw (Eliphelehu), and Maqanayahaw (Mikneiah), and Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom), and Yaiyaal (Jeiel), the shairayam (doorkeepers).
So the singers, Hayaman (Heman), Asap (Asaph), and Ayathan (Ethan), were given matzalathayam (cymbals) of nachashath (brass) to shamai (hearken / hear) aloud;

And Zakarayah (Zechariah), and Izayaal (Aziel), and Shamayaramawath (Shemiramoth), and Yachayaal (Jehiel), and Inay (Unni), and Alayaab (Eliab), and Maishayah (Maaseiah), and Banayah (Benaiah), with stringed instruments set to ilamawath (alamoth);

And Mathathayah (Mattithiah), and Alayapalahaw (Eliphelehu), and Maqanayahaw (Mikneiah), and Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom), and Yaiyaal (Jeiel), and Izazayahaw (Azaziah), with kanarawath (harps) tuned to the eight-stringed lyre, to lead.
Kananayah (Chenaniah), shar (prince / ruler) of the Lawayay (Levites), was over the mashaa (song): he yasar (instructed) about the mashaa (song), because he was skillful.
Barakayah (Berechiah) and Alaqanah (Elkanah) were shairayam (doorkeepers) for the arawan (ark).

Shabanayah (Shebaniah), and Yawashapat (Joshaphat), and Nathanaal (Nethanel), and Imashay (Amasai), and Zakarayah (Zechariah), and Banayah (Benaiah), and Alayaizar (Eliezer), the kahanayam (priests), chatzar (blew) the chatzatzarawath (trumpets) panayam (face) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam: and Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom) and Yachayah (Jehiah) were shairayam (doorkeepers) for the arawan (ark).

So Dawad (David), and the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and the sharay (captains) over alapayam (thousands), halak (move) to ilah (go up / offer) up the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah out of the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom) with shamachah (joy).

It happened, when Alahayam izar (helped) the Lawayay (Levites) who nashaa (lift) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, that they zabach (sacrificed) shabai (seven) parayam (bulls) and shabai (seven) ayalayam (rams).

Dawad (David) was karabal (clothed) with a maiyal (robe) of bawatz (fine) linen, and all the Lawayay (Levites) who nashaa (lift) the arawan (ark), and the singers, and Kananayah (Chenaniah) the shar (prince / ruler) of the mashaa (song) with the singers: and Dawad (David) had on him an apawad (ephod) of bad (linen).

Thus all Yashar-Al (Israel) ilah (go up / offer) up the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah with tharawaih (shouting), and with qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn), and with chatzatzarawath (trumpets), and with matzalathayam (cymbals), shamai (hearken / hear) aloud with stringed instruments and kanarawath (harps).

It happened, as the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah bawaa (come) to the iyar (city) of Dawad (David), that Mayakal (Michal) the banath (daughter) of Shaawal (Saul) shaqap (looked) out at the chalawan (window), and raah (see) malak (king) Dawad (David) raqad (dancing) and shachaq (playing); and she bazah (despised) him in her lab (heart).

They bawaa (come) in the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, and yatzag (set) it in the thawak (midst) of the ahal (tent) that Dawad (David) had natah (pitched) for it: and they qarab (come close) burnt ilawath (offerings) and shalam (peace) offerings panayam (face) Alahayam.

When Dawad (David) kalah (complete / finish) made an end of ilah (go up / offer) the burnt ilah (offering) and the shalam (peace) offerings, he barak (blessed) the im (nation / people) in the sham (name) of Yahawah.

He dealt to everyone of Yashar-Al (Israel), both ayash (man / husband) and ayashah (woman / wife), to ayash (man / husband) one a kakar (loaf) of lacham (bread), and a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins.

He nathan (give) certain of the Lawayay (Levites) to sharath (minister) panayam (face) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, and to celebrate and to yadah (thank) and halal (praise) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel):

Asap (Asaph) the raash (head), and mashanah (second) to him Zakarayah (Zechariah), Yaiyaal (Jeiel), and Shamayaramawath (Shemiramoth), and Yachayaal (Jehiel), and Mathathayah (Mattithiah), and Alayaab (Eliab), and Banayah (Benaiah), and Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom), and Yaiyaal (Jeiel), with stringed instruments and with kanarawath (harps); and Asap (Asaph) with matzalathayam (cymbals), shamai (hearken / hear) aloud;
And Banayah (Benaiah) and Yachazayaal (Jahaziel) the kahanayam (priests) with chatzatzarawath (trumpets) continually, panayam (face) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Alahayam.
Then on that yawam (day) Dawad (David) raash (head) nathan (give) to give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah, by the yad (hand) of Asap (Asaph) and his ach (brother/kinsman).
Oh give hawadaw (thanks) to Yahawah. Qaraa (called) on his sham (name). Make his ilayalah (doings) yadai (known) among the imayam (peoples).
Shayar (sing) to him. Sing zamaraw (praises) to him. Tell of all his marvelous palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous).
Glory in his qadash (set apart / make holy) sham (name). Let the lab (heart) of those who baqash (seek) Yahawah shamach (rejoice).
Darash (seek) Yahawah and his iz (strength / might / refuge). Baqash (seek) his panayam (face) thamayad (forever) more.
Zakar (remember) his palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) ishah (make) that he has done, his mawapath (wonders), and the mashapatay (judgments) of his pah (mouth),
You zarai (seed) of Yashar-Al (Israel) his ibad (servant), you banay (children) of Yaiqab (Jacob), his bachayar (chosen) ones.
He is Yahawah our Alahayam. His mashapat (judgments) are in all the aratz (Earth/land).
Zakar (remember) his barayath (covenant) iwalam (forever), the dabar (word / matter) which he tzawah (commanded) to a alap (thousand) dawar (generation / age / period),
The karath (cut) which he made with Abaraham (Abraham), his shabawaih (oath) to Yatzachaq (Isaac).
He imad (confirmed) the same to Yaiqab (Jacob) for a chaq (statute), and to Yashar-Al (Israel) for an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant),
Amar (spoke), "I will nathan (give) you the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), The chabal (lot) of your nachalah (inheritance),"
When you were but a masapar (few) men in number, yes, very mait (few), and foreigners were in it.
They halak (move) about from gaway (heathen / nation) to gaway (heathen / nation), from one mamalakah (kingdom) to achar (other) im (nation / people).
He allowed no ayash (man / husband) to ishaq (do) them wrong. Yes, he yakach (reproved) malakayam (kings) for their sakes,
"Don't nagai (touch) my mashayach (anointed one) ones! Do my nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) no raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil)!"
Shayar (sing) to Yahawah, all the aratz (Earth/land)! Display his yashawaih (salvation) from yawam (day) to yawam (day).
Sapar (book) his kabawad (glory) among the gawayam (nations), and his marvelous palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) among all the imayam (peoples).
For gadawal (very great/important/mighty) is Yahawah, and maad (greatly) to be halal (praise). He also is to be yaraa (fear / be afraid) above all Alahayam.
For all the Alahayam of the imayam (peoples) are alayalayam (idols), but Yahawah ishah (make) the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens).
Honor and hawad (majesty) are panayam (face) him. Iz (strength / might / refuge) and chadawah (gladness) are in his maqawam (place).
Yahab (ascribe) to Yahawah, you relatives of the imayam (peoples), yahab (ascribe) to Yahawah kabawad (glory) and iz (strength / might / refuge)!

Yahab (ascribe) to Yahawah the kabawad (glory) due to his sham (name). Nashaa (lift) an manachah (offering), and bawaa (come) panayam (face) him. Shachah (worship) Yahawah in qadash (set apart / make holy) array.
Chawal (tremble) panayam (face) him, all the aratz (Earth/land). The thabal (world) also is kawan (established) that it can't be mawat (moved).
Let the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) be shamach (glad), and let the aratz (Earth/land) gayal (rejoice)! Let them amar (spoke) among the gawayam (nations), "Yahawah malak (king)!"
Let the yam (sea/waters) raim (roar), and its fullness! Let the shadah (field) exult, and all that is therein!
Then the itzay (trees) of the yair (forest) will ranan (sing) for joy panayam (face) Yahawah, for he bawaa (come) to shapat (judge / judgement) the aratz (Earth/land).
Oh give hawadaw (thanks) to Yahawah, for he is tawab (good / proper function), for his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever).

Amar (spoke), "yashai (salvation) us, Alahayam of our yashai (salvation)! Qabatz (gather) us together and natzal (deliver) us from the gawayam (nations), to give yadah (thanks) to your qadash (set apart / make holy) sham (name), to shabach (triumph) in your thahalah (praise)."

Barak (blessed) be Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), from iwalam (forever) even to iwalam (forever). All the im (nation / people) amar (spoke), "aman (believe / have faith)," and halal (praise) Yahawah.

So he izab (left) there, panayam (face) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, Asap (Asaph) and his ach (brother/kinsman), to sharath (minister) panayam (face) the arawan (ark) continually, as every yawam (day) dabar (word / matter) yawam (day);

And Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom) with their ach (brother/kinsman), shashayam (sixty) - shamanah (eight); Ibadaadawam (Obed-Edom) also the ban (son) of Yadawathawan (Jeduthun) and Chasah (Hosah) to be shairayam (doorkeepers);

And Tzadawaq (Zadok) the kahan (priest), and his ach (brother/kinsman) the kahanayam (priests), panayam (face) the mashakan (tabernacle) of Yahawah in the bamah (high) place that was at Gabaiwan (Gibeon),

To ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilawath (offerings) to Yahawah on the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering) continually baqar (morning) and irab (evening), even according to all that is kathab (write) in the thawarah (instruction) of Yahawah, which he tzawah (commanded) to Yashar-Al (Israel);

And with them Hayaman (Heman) and Yadawathawan (Jeduthun), and the shaar (rest) who were barar (chosen), who were mentioned by sham (name), to give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah, because his loving chasad (grace) endures iwalam (forever);

And with them Hayaman (Heman) and Yadawathawan (Jeduthun) with chatzatzarawath (trumpets) and matzalathayam (cymbals) for those that should shamai (hearken / hear) aloud, and with kalay (instruments) for the shayar (song) of Alahayam; and the banay (sons) of Yadawathawan (Jeduthun) to be at the shair (gate).
All the im (nation / people) departed every ayash (man / husband) to his bayath (house): and Dawad (David) sabab (returned) to barak (blessed) his bayath (house).

It happened, when Dawad (David) lived in his bayath (house), that Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Nathan (Nathan) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), "Behold, I yashab (inhabit/dwell) in a bayath (house) of araz (cedar), but the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah is under yarayaiwath (curtains)."
Nathan (Nathan) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "ishah (make) all that is in your labab (heart); for Alahayam is with you."
It happened the same layal (night), that the dabar (word / matter) of Alahayam came to Nathan (Nathan), amar (spoke),
"Yalak (go) and amar (spoke) Dawad (David) my ibad (servant), ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "You shall not banah (build) me a bayath (house) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) in;

For I have not lived in a bayath (house) since the yawam (day) that I ilah (go up / offer) up Yashar-Al (Israel), to this yawam (day), but have gone from ahal (tent) to ahal (tent), and from one mashakan (tent) to another.

In all halak (move) in which I have walked with all Yashar-Al (Israel), did I dabar (word / matter) a dabar (word / matter) with any of the shapatay (judges) of Yashar-Al (Israel), whom I tzawah (commanded) to be raih (shepherd) of my im (nation / people), amar (spoke), ‘Why have you not banah (build) me a bayath (house) of araz (cedar)?'"'

"Now therefore, you shall amar (spoke) my ibad (servant) Dawad (David), ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), "I laqach (take / seize) you from the sheep pen, from achar (other) the tzaan (sheep), that you should be nagayad (prince) over my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel).

I have been with you wherever you have halak (move), and have karath (cut) off all your ayab (enemy) from panayam (face) you. I will ishah (make) you a sham (name), like the sham (name) of the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) ones who are in the aratz (Earth/land).

I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) a maqawam (place) for my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel), and will natai (plant) them, that they may shakan (place) in their own place, and be ragaz (moved) no more; neither shall the banay (children) of iwal (wickedness) balah (waste) them any more, as at the raashawan (first),

And from the yawam (day) that I tzawah (commanded) shapatayam (judges) to be over my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel); and I will kanai (subdue) all your ayab (enemy). Moreover I nagad (tell) you that Yahawah will banah (build) you a bayath (house).

It shall happen, when your yawam (day) are malaa (fulfilled) that you must yalak (go) to be with your ab (father), that I will qawam (rise up) up your zarai (seed) achar (other) you, who shall be of your ban (son); and I will kawan (establish) his malakawath (kingdom).
He shall banah (build) me a bayath (house), and I will kawan (establish) his kasaa (throne) iwalam (forever).
I will be his ab (father), and he shall be my ban (son). I will not sawar (take) my loving chasad (grace) sawar (away) from him, as I sawar (took) it from him that panayam (face) before you;
But I will settle him in my bayath (house) and in my malakawath (kingdom) iwalam (forever). His kasaa (throne) shall be kawan (established) iwalam (forever)."'"
According to all these dabarayam (words), and according to all this chazawan (vision), so Nathan (Nathan) dabar (word / matter) to Dawad (David).

Then Dawad (David) the malak (king) bawaa (come) in, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) panayam (face) Yahawah; and he amar (spoke), "Who am I, Yahawah Alahayam, and what is my bayath (house), that you bawaa (come) brought me thus far?

This was a qatan (small / young / least) thing in your iyan (eye), Alahayam; but you have dabar (word / matter) of your ibad (servant) bayath (house) for a rachawaq (great) while to come, and raah (see) respected me according to the thawar (estate) of a adam (man) of high mailah (ascent/climbing up), Yahawah Alahayam.
What can Dawad (David) say yet more to you concerning the honor which is done to your ibad (servant)? For you yadai (know) your ibad (servant).
Yahawah, for your ibad (servant) sake, and according to your own lab (heart), you ishah (make) worked all this gadawalah (greatness), to yadai (make) known all these gadawalah (great) things.
Yahawah, there is none like you, neither is there any Alahayam zawalah (besides) you, according to all that we have shamai (hearken / hear) with our azan (ear).

What achad (one) gaway (heathen / nation) in the aratz (Earth/land) is like your im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel), whom Alahayam halak (move) to padah (redeem) to himself for a im (nation / people), to shawam (place / establish / appoint) you a sham (name) by gadawalah (great) and awesome things, in garash (driving) out gawayam (nations) from panayam (face) your im (nation / people), whom you padah (redeem) out of Matzarayam (Egypt)?
For your im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel) you nathan (give) your own im (nation / people) iwalam (forever); and you, Yahawah, became their Alahayam.

Now, Yahawah, let the dabar (word / matter) that you have dabar (word / matter) concerning your ibad (servant), and concerning his bayath (house), be aman (believe / have faith) iwalam (forever), and ishah (make) as you have dabar (word / matter).

Let your sham (name) be aman (believe / have faith) and gadal (magnified) iwalam (forever), amar (spoke), ‘Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) is the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), even a Alahayam to Yashar-Al (Israel). The bayath (house) of Dawad (David) your ibad (servant) is kawan (established) panayam (face) you.'

For you, my Alahayam, have galah (revealed) to your ibad (servant) that you will banah (build) him a bayath (house). Therefore your ibad (servant) matzaa (has) found courage to palal (pray) panayam (face) you.
Now, Yahawah, you are Alahayam, and have dabar (word / matter) this tawab (good / proper function) thing to your ibad (servant).

Now it has yaal (pleased) you to barak (blessed) the bayath (house) of your ibad (servant), that it may continue iwalam (forever) panayam (face) you; for you, Yahawah, have barak (blessed), and it is barak (blessed) iwalam (forever)."

Achar (other) this it happened, that Dawad (David) nakah (struck) the Palashathay (Philistines), and kanai (subdued) them, and laqach (take / seize) gath (gath) and its banath (daughter) out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines).
He nakah (struck) Mawaab (Moab); and the Mawaab (Moabites) became ibadayam (servants) to Dawad (David), and nashaa (lift) tribute.
Dawad (David) nakah (struck) Hadadezer malak (king) of Tzawabaa (Zobah) to Chamath (Hamath), as he yalak (went) to natzab (establish) his yad (hand) by the nahar (river) Parath (Euphrates).

Dawad (David) lakad (took) from him one alap (thousand) rakab (chariots), and shabai (seven) alap (thousand) horsemen, and isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) footmen; and Dawad (David) hamstrung all the rakab (chariot) horses, but yathar (reserved) of them for one maah (hundred) rakab (chariots).
When the Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck of the Syrians twenty-two thousand men.

Then Dawad (David) shawam (place / establish / appoint) garrisons in Aram (Syria) of Damascus; and the Aram (Syrians) became ibadayam (servants) to Dawad (David), and nashaa (lift) tribute. Yahawah gave yashai (salvation) to Dawad (David) wherever he halak (move).
Dawad (David) laqach (take / seize) the shalatay (shields) of zahab (gold) that were on the ibaday (servants) of Hadadezer, and bawaa (come) them to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

From Tabachath (Tibhath) and from Kawan (Cun), iray (cities) of Hadadezer, Dawad (David) laqach (take / seize) very much nachashath (brass), with which Shalamah (Solomon) ishah (make) the bronze yam (sea/waters), and the imawadayam (pillars), and the kalay (vessels) of nachashath (brass).
When Thaiw (Tou) malak (king) of Chamath (Hamath) shamai (hearken / hear) that Dawad (David) had nakah (struck) all the chayal (army) of Hadadezer malak (king) of Tzawabaa (Zobah),

He shalach (send) Hadawaram (Hadoram) his ban (son) to malak (king) Dawad (David), to shaal (greet) him, and to barak (blessed) him, because he had lacham (fought) against Hadadezer and nakah (struck) him; (for Hadadezer had wars with Thaiw (Tou);) and he had with him all kinds of kalay (vessels) of zahab (gold) and kasap (silver) and nachashath (brass).

Malak (king) Dawad (David) also qadash (set apart / make holy) these to Yahawah, with the kasap (silver) and the zahab (gold) that he nashaa (lift) away from all the gawayam (nations); from Adawam (Edom), and from Mawaab (Moab), and from the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), and from the Palashathay (Philistines), and from Imalaq (Amalek).
Moreover Abayashay (Abishai) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah) nakah (struck) of the Adawam (Edomites) in the gayaa (valley) of malach (salt) eighteen alap (thousand).

He shawam (place / establish / appoint) natzayabayam (garrisons) in Adawam (Edom); and all the Adawam (Edomites) became ibadayam (servants) to Dawad (David). Yahawah gave yashai (salvation) to Dawad (David) wherever he halak (move).
Dawad (David) malak (king) over all Yashar-Al (Israel); and he ishah (make) mashapat (justice) and tzadaqah (righteousness) to all his im (nation / people).
Yawaab (Joab) the ban (son) of Tzarawayah (Zeruiah) was over the tzabaa (troop); and Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat) the ban (son) of Achayalawad (Ahilud) was zakar (remember);
And Tzadawaq (Zadok) the ban (son) of Achayatawab (Ahitub), and Abayamalak (Abimelech) the ban (son) of Abayathar (Abiathar), were kahanayam (priests); and Shawashaa (Shavsha) was sapar (book);

And Banayah (Benaiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayadai (Jehoiada) was over the Karathay (Cherethites) and the Palathay (Pelethites); and the banay (sons) of Dawad (David) were chief yad (hand) the malak (king).
It happened achar (other) this, that Nachash (Nahash) the malak (king) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) mawath (death), and his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.

Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "I will show chasad (grace) to Chanawan (Hanun) the ban (son) of Nachash (Nahash), because his ab (father) showed chasad (grace) to me." So Dawad (David) shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to nacham (turn away / repent) him concerning his ab (father). Dawad (David's) ibaday (servants) bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) to Chanawan (Hanun), to nacham (turn away / repent) him.

But the sharay (princes) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) amar (spoke) to Chanawan (Hanun), "Do you iyan (eye) that Dawad (David) honors your ab (father), in that he has shalach (send) comforters to you? Haven't his ibad (servant) bawaa (come) to you to chaqar (search), to hapak (overthrow), and to ragal (spy) out the aratz (Earth/land)?"

So Chanawan (Hanun) laqach (take / seize) Dawad (David's) ibaday (servants), and galach (shaved) them, and karath (cut) off their madaw (garments) in the chatzay (middle), even to their mapashaih (buttocks), and shalach (send) them away.

Then there yalak (went) certain persons, and nagad (told) Dawad (David) how the anashayam (men) were served. He shalach (send) to qaraah (meet) them; for the anashayam (men) were maad (greatly) kalam (ashamed). The malak (king) amar (spoke), "Stay at Yarayachaw (Jericho) until your zaqan (beards) have tzamach (grown), and then shawab (turn back / repent)."

When the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) raah (see) that they baash (had) made themselves odious to Dawad (David), Chanawan (Hanun) and the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) shalach (send) one alap (thousand) kakar (talents) of kasap (silver) to shakar (hire) them rakab (chariots) and horsemen out of Aramanaharayam (Mesopotamia), and out of Aram (Arammaacah), and out of Tzawabaa (Zobah).

So they shakar (hired) for themselves shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) rakab (chariots), and the malak (king) of Maikah (Maacah) and his im (nation / people), who bawaa (come) and chanah (encamped) panayam (face) May-Dabaa (Medeba). The banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) asap (gathered) themselves together from their iyar (cities), and bawaa (come) to malachamah (battle).
When Dawad (David) shamai (hearken / hear) of it, he shalach (send) Yawaab (Joab), and all the tzabaa (troop) of the gabawar (mighty) men.

The banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and put the malachamah (battle) in irak (array) at the pathach (gate) of the iyar (city): and the malakayam (kings) who bawaa (come) come were by themselves in the shadah (field).

Now when Yawaab (Joab) raah (see) that the malachamah (battle) panayam (face) set against him before and achawar (behind), he bachar (chose) of all the choice men of Yashar-Al (Israel), and irak (put) them in array qaraah (against) the Aram (Syrians).

The yathar (rest) of the im (nation / people) he nathan (give) into the yad (hand) of Abayashay (Abishai) his ach (brother/kinsman); and they irak (put) themselves in array qaraah (against) the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon).

He amar (spoke), "If the Aram (Syrians) are too chazaq (strong) for me, then you are to thashawaih (deliverance) me; but if the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) are too chazaq (strong) for you, then I will yashai (salvation) you.
Be courageous, and let us be chazaq (strong) for our im (nation / people), and for the iray (cities) of our Alahayam. May Yahawah ishah (make) that which seems tawab (good / proper function) to him."
So Yawaab (Joab) and the im (nation / people) who were with him nagash (drew) near panayam (face) the Aram (Syrians) to the malachamah (battle); and they nawas (fled) panayam (face) him.

When the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) raah (see) that the Aram (Syrians) had nawas (fled), they likewise nawas (fled) panayam (face) Abayashay (Abishai) his ach (brother/kinsman), and bawaa (come) into the iyar (city). Then Yawaab (Joab) bawaa (come) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

When the Aram (Syrians) raah (see) that they were defeated by Yashar-Al (Israel), they shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers), and yatzaa (go out / come out) forth the Aram (Syrians) who were ibar (beyond) the nahar (river), with Shawapak (Shophach) the shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop) of Hadadezer at their panayam (face).

It was nagad (told) Dawad (David); and he asap (gathered) all Yashar-Al (Israel) together, and ibar (pass over/through) over the Yaradan (Jordan), and bawaa (come) on them, and irak (set) the battle in array against them. So when Dawad (David) had put the malachamah (battle) in irak (array) qaraah (against) the Aram (Syrians), they lacham (fought) with him.

The Aram (Syrians) nawas (fled) panayam (face) Yashar-Al (Israel); and Dawad (David) harag (kill) of the Aram (Syrians) the men of shabai (seven) alap (thousand) rakab (chariots), and arabaiyam (forty) alap (thousand) footmen, and mawath (death) Shawapak (Shophach) the shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop).

When the ibaday (servants) of Hadadezer raah (see) that they were defeated by Yashar-Al (Israel), they made shalam (peace) with Dawad (David), and ibad (servant) him: neither would the Aram (Syrians) yashai (salvation) the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) any more.

It happened, at the ith (time) of the thashawabah (return) of the shanah (year), at the ith (time) when malakayam (kings) yatzaa (go out / come out) out, that Yawaab (Joab) nahag (led) forth the tzabaa (troop), and shachath (wasted) the aratz (Earth/land) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), and bawaa (come) and tzawar (besieged) Rabah (Rabbah). But Dawad (David) stayed at Yarawashalam (Jerusalem). Yawaab (Joab) nakah (struck) Rabah (Rabbah), and overthrew it.

Dawad (David) laqach (take / seize) the itarah (crown) of their malak (king) from off his raash (head), and matzaa (found) it to weigh a kakar (talent) of zahab (gold), and there were yaqar (precious) aban (stone) in it; and it was set on Dawad (David's) raash (head): and he yatzaa (go out / come out) forth the shalal (spoil) of the iyar (city), maad (exceeding) much.

He yatzaa (go out / come out) forth the im (nation / people) who were therein, and shawar (cut) them with magarawath (saws), and with barazal (iron) picks, and with magarawath (axes). Dawad (David) ishah (make) so to all the iray (cities) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon). Dawad (David) and all the im (nation / people) shawab (turn back / repent) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

It happened achar (other) this, that there arose malachamah (war) at Gazar (Gezer) with the Palashathay (Philistines): then Sabakay (Sibbecai) the chashathay (hushathite) nakah (killed) Sapay (Sippai), of the yaladay (sons) of the Rapaa (giant); and they were kanai (subdued).

There was again malachamah (war) with the Palashathay (Philistines); and Alachanan (Elhanan) the ban (son) of Yaiwar (Jair) nakah (killed) Lachamay (Lahmi) the ach (brother/kinsman) of Galayath (Goliath) the Gathay (Gittite), the itz (staff) of whose chanayath (spear) was like a aragayam (weavers) manawar (beam).

There was again malachamah (war) at gath (gath), where there was a ayash (man / husband) of great madah (stature), whose atzabai (fingers) and atzabai (toes) were isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four), shash (six) on each hand, and shash (six) on each foot; and he also was yalad (birth / begot) to the Rapaa (giant).
When he charap (defied) Yashar-Al (Israel), Yahawanathan (Jonathan) the ban (son) of Shamaia (Shimea) Dawad (David's) ach (brother/kinsman) nakah (killed) him.
These were yalad (birth / begot) to the Rapaa (giant) in gath (gath); and they napal (fall / be cast down) by the yad (hand) of Dawad (David), and by the yad (hand) of his ibad (servant).
Shatan (satan) imad (stood) up against Yashar-Al (Israel), and sawath (moved) Dawad (David) to manah (number) Yashar-Al (Israel).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Yawaab (Joab) and to the sharay (princes) of the im (nation / people), "yalak (go), sapar (book) Yashar-Al (Israel) from Baar-Shabai (Beersheba) even to Dan (Dan); and bawaa (come) me word, that I may yadai (know) the sum of them."

Yawaab (Joab) amar (spoke), "May Yahawah make his im (nation / people) a maah (hundred) paimayam (times) as many as they are. But, my Adawan the malak (king), aren't they all my Adawan ibadayam (servants)? Why does my Adawan baqash (require) this thing? Why will he be a cause of ashamah (guilt) to Yashar-Al (Israel)?"

Nevertheless the malak (king) dabar (word / matter) chazaq (prevailed) against Yawaab (Joab). Therefore Yawaab (Joab) departed, and halak (move) throughout all Yashar-Al (Israel), and bawaa (come) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

Yawaab (Joab) nathan (give) up the sum of the mapaqad (numbering) of the im (nation / people) to Dawad (David). All those of Yashar-Al (Israel) were alap (one) million one maah (hundred) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband) who shalap (drew) charab (sword): and in Yahawadah (Judah) were arabai (four) maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband) who shalap (drew) charab (sword).
But he didn't paqad (visit) Laway (Levi) and Banayamayan (Benjamin) thawak (midst) them; for the malak (king) dabar (word / matter) was thaib (abominable) to Yawaab (Joab).
Alahayam was displeased with this thing; therefore he nakah (struck) Yashar-Al (Israel).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Alahayam, "I have chataa (sinned) maad (greatly), in that I ishah (make) done this thing. But now, ibar (pass over/through) away, I beg you, the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of your ibad (servant); for I have done very foolishly."
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to Gad (Gad), Dawad (David's) chazah (seer), amar (spoke),

"Yalak (go) and dabar (word / matter) to Dawad (David), amar (spoke), ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "I natah (offer) you shalawash (three) things. Bachar (choose) achad (one) of them, that I may ishah (make) it to you."'"
So Gad (Gad) bawaa (come) to Dawad (David), and amar (spoke) to him, "Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘qabal (take) your choice:

Either shalawash (three) shanayam (years) of raib (famine); or shalawash (three) chadashayam (months) to be sapah (consumed) panayam (face) your tzar (oppressor / distressor), while the charab (sword) of your ayab (enemy) nashag (overtakes) you; or else shalawash (three) yamayam (days) the charab (sword) of Yahawah, even dabar (word / matter) in the aratz (Earth/land), and the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah shachath (destroying) throughout all the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yashar-Al (Israel). Now therefore raah (see) dabar (word / matter) answer I shall shawab (turn back / repent) to him who shalach (send) me.'"

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Gad (Gad), "I am in tzar (oppressor / distressor). Napal (fall / be cast down) me fall, I pray, into the yad (hand) of Yahawah; for his racham (show mercy / love) are very rab (great). Napal (fall / be cast down) me not fall into the yad (hand) of adam (man)."
So Yahawah nathan (give) a dabar (word / matter) on Yashar-Al (Israel); and shabaiyam (seventy) alap (thousand) ayash (man / husband) of Yashar-Al (Israel) napal (fall / be cast down).

Alahayam shalach (send) an malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) to shachath (destroy) it. As he was about to shachath (destroy), Yahawah raah (see), and he relented of the disaster, and amar (spoke) to the shachath (destroying) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah), "It is rab (enough); now rapah (stay) your yad (hand)." The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah was imad (standing) by the garan (threshing) floor of Aranan (Ornan) the Yabawasay (Jebusite).

Dawad (David) nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye), and raah (see) the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah imad (standing) between aratz (Earth/land) and the sky, having a shalap (drawn) charab (sword) in his yad (hand) natah (stretched) out over Yarawashalam (Jerusalem). Then Dawad (David) and the zaqanayam (elders), kasah (clothed) in sackcloth, napal (fall / be cast down) on their panayam (face).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Alahayam, "Isn't it I who commanded the im (nation / people) to be manah (numbered)? It is even I who have chataa (sinned) and raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) very wickedly; but these tzaan (sheep), what ishah (make) they done? Please let your yad (hand), O Yahawah my Alahayam, be against me, and against my ab (father) bayath (house); but not against your im (nation / people), that they should be magapah (plagued)."

Then the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah commanded Gad (Gad) to amar (spoke) Dawad (David) that Dawad (David) should ilah (go up / offer) up, and qawam (rise up) an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah in the garan (threshing) floor of Aranan (Ornan) the Yabawasay (Jebusite).
Dawad (David) ilah (go up / offer) up at the dabar (word / matter) of Gad (Gad), which he dabar (word / matter) in the sham (name) of Yahawah.

Aranan (Ornan) shawab (turn back / repent) back, and raah (see) the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah); and his arabai (four) ban (son) who were with him chabaa (hid) themselves. Now Aranan (Ornan) was dawash (threshing) chatah (wheat).

As Dawad (David) bawaa (come) to Aranan (Ornan), Aranan (Ornan) nabat (looked) and nabat (saw) Dawad (David), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the garan (threshing) floor, and shachah (bowed) himself to Dawad (David) with his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to the aratz (Earth/land).

Then Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Aranan (Ornan), "nathan (give) me the maqawam (place) of this garan (threshing) floor, that I may banah (build) thereon an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah. You shall sell it to me for the malaa (full) kasap (price), that the magapah (plague) may be itzar (stopped) from afflicting the im (nation / people)."

Aranan (Ornan) amar (spoke) to Dawad (David), "laqach (take / seize) it for yourself, and let my Adawan the malak (king) ishah (make) that which is tawab (good / proper function) in his iyan (eye). Raah (see), I nathan (give) the oxen for burnt ilawath (offerings), and the mawarag (threshing) instruments for itz (wood), and the chatah (wheat) for the meal manachah (offering). I nathan (give) it all."

Malak (king) Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Aranan (Ornan), "No; but I will most certainly qanah (buy) it for the malaa (full) kasap (price). For I will not nashaa (lift) that which is yours for Yahawah, nor ilah (go up / offer) a burnt ilah (offering) chanam (without) cost."
So Dawad (David) nathan (give) to Aranan (Ornan) shash (six) maah (hundred) shaqalay (shekels) of zahab (gold) by mashaqal (weight) for the maqawam (place).

Dawad (David) banah (build) an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah there, and ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilawath (offerings) and peace ilawath (offerings), and qaraa (called) on Yahawah; and he inah (answer / respond) him from the sky by ash (fire) on the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering).
Yahawah commanded the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah); and he shawab (turn back / repent) up his charab (sword) again into its nadan (sheath).

At that ith (time), when Dawad (David) raah (see) that Yahawah had inah (answer / respond) him in the garan (threshing) floor of Aranan (Ornan) the Yabawasay (Jebusite), then he zabach (sacrificed) there.

For the mashakan (tabernacle) of Yahawah, which Mashah (Moses) ishah (make) in the madabar (wilderness), and the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering), were at that ith (time) in the bamah (high) place at Gabaiwan (Gibeon).

But Dawad (David) couldn't yalak (go) panayam (face) it to darash (inquire) of Alahayam; for he was baith (afraid) panayam (face) of the charab (sword) of the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah.
Then Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "This is the bayath (house) of Yahawah Alahayam, and this is the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering) for Yashar-Al (Israel)."

Dawad (David) amar (spoke) orders to kanas (gather) together the foreigners who were in the aratz (Earth/land) of Yashar-Al (Israel); and he imad (set) chatzabayam (masons) to chatzab (cut) worked abanay (stones) to banah (build) the bayath (house) of Alahayam.

Dawad (David) kawan (prepared) barazal (iron) in rab (abundance) for the masamarayam (nails) for the dalathawath (doors) of the shairayam (gates), and for the machabarawath (couplings); and nachashath (brass) in rab (abundance) without mashaqal (weight);
And araz (cedar) itzay (trees) without rab (number): for the Tzayadanay (Sidonians) and they of tzaray (tyre) bawaa (come) araz (cedar) itzay (trees) in abundance to Dawad (David).

Dawad (David) amar (spoke), "Shalamah (Solomon) my ban (son) is nair (young) and rak (tender), and the bayath (house) that is to be banah (build) for Yahawah must be mail (top/above) magnificent, of sham (name) and of glory throughout all aratzawath (countries). I will therefore kawan (make) preparation for it." So Dawad (David) kawan (prepared) rab (abundantly) panayam (face) his mawath (death).
Then he qaraa (called) for Shalamah (Solomon) his ban (son), and tzawah (commanded) him to banah (build) a bayath (house) for Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel).
Dawad (David) amar (spoke) to Shalamah (Solomon) his ban (son), "As for me, it was in my labab (heart) to banah (build) a bayath (house) to the sham (name) of Yahawah my Alahayam.

But the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke), ‘You have shapak (shed) dam (blood) rab (abundantly), and ishah (make) made gadawal (very great/important/mighty) malachamawath (wars). You shall not banah (build) a bayath (house) to my sham (name), because you have shapak (shed) much dam (blood) on the aratz (Earth/land) in my panayam (face).

Behold, a ban (son) shall be yalad (birth / begot) to you, who shall be a ayash (man / husband) of manawachah (rest). I will give him nawach (rest) from all his ayab (enemy) all around; for his sham (name) shall be Shalamah (Solomon), and I will nathan (give) shalawam (peace / safety) and shaqat (quietness) to Yashar-Al (Israel) in his yawam (day).

He shall banah (build) a bayath (house) for my sham (name); and he shall be my ban (son), and I will be his ab (father); and I will kawan (establish) the kasaa (throne) of his malakawath (kingdom) over Yashar-Al (Israel) for iwalam (forever).'
Now, my ban (son), may Yahawah be with you and tzalach (prosper) you, and banah (build) the bayath (house) of Yahawah your Alahayam, as he has dabar (word / matter) concerning you.

May Yahawah nathan (give) you shakal (discretion) and bayanah (understanding), and tzawah (put) you in charge of Yashar-Al (Israel); that so you may shamar (keep/guard) the thawarah (instruction) of Yahawah your Alahayam.

Then you will tzalach (prosper), if you shamar (keep/guard) to ishah (make) the chaqayam (statutes) and the mashapatayam (ordinances) which Yahawah tzawah (gave) Mashah (Moses) concerning Yashar-Al (Israel). Be chazaq (strong), and amatz (courageous). Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), neither be chathath (dismayed).

Now, behold, in my inay (affliction) I have kawan (prepared) for the bayath (house) of Yahawah one maah (hundred) alap (thousand) kakarayam (talents) of zahab (gold), alap (one) million kakarayam (talents) of kasap (silver), and nachashath (brass) and barazal (iron) without mashaqal (weight); for it is in rab (abundance). I have also kawan (prepared) itz (timber) and aban (stone); and you may yasap (add) to them.
There are also workmen with you in rab (abundance), cutters and charashay (workers) of aban (stone) and itz (timber), and all kinds of chakam (men) who are skillful in every kind of malaakah (work):
Of the zahab (gold), the kasap (silver), and the nachashath (brass), and the barazal (iron), there is no masapar (number). Qawam (rise up) and be ishah (make), and may Yahawah be with you."
Dawad (David) also tzawah (commanded) all the sharay (princes) of Yashar-Al (Israel) to izar (help) Shalamah (Solomon) his ban (son), saying,
