The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Asathar (Esther) the malakah (queen), "The Yahawaday (Jews) have harag (kill) and abad (destroy / perish) chamash (five) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) in the citadel of Shawashan (Susa), including the ishar (ten) banay (sons) of Haman (Haman); what then ishah (make) they done in the shaar (rest) of the malak (king) madayanawath (provinces)! Now what is your shaalah (petition)? It shall be nathan (give) you. What is your iwad (more/again) baqashah (request)? It shall be ishah (make)."

Then Asathar (Esther) amar (spoke), "If it pleases the malak (king), nathan (give) it be granted to the Yahawaday (Jews) who are in Shawashan (Shushan) to ishah (make) machar (tomorrow) also according to this yawam (day) dath (decree), and let Haman (Haman's) ishar (ten) banay (sons) be hanged on the itz (gallows)."
The malak (king) commanded this to be ishah (make). A decree was nathan (give) out in Shawashan (Shushan); and they hanged Haman (Haman's) ishar (ten) banay (sons).

The Yahawaday (Jews) who were in Shawashan (Shushan) qahal (gathered) themselves together on the fourteenth yawam (day) also of the chadash (month) Adar (Adar), and harag (kill) shalawash (three) maah (hundred) ayash (man / husband) in Shawashan (Shushan); but they didn't shalach (send) their yad (hand) on the bazah (spoil).

The other Yahawaday (Jews) who were in the malak (king) madayanawath (provinces) qahal (gathered) themselves together, defended their lives, had nawach (rest) from their ayab (enemy), and harag (kill) shabaiyam (seventy) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) of those who shanaa (hate) them; but they didn't shalach (send) their yad (hand) on the plunder.

This was done on the thirteenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month) Adar (Adar); and on the fourteenth day of that month they nawach (rested) and ishah (make) it a yawam (day) of mashathah (feasting) and shamachah (gladness).

But the Yahawaday (Jews) who were in Shawashan (Shushan) qahal (assembled) together on the thirteenth and on the fourteenth chamash (days) of the month; and on the fifteenth day of that month, they nawach (rested), and ishah (make) it a yawam (day) of mashathah (feasting) and shamachah (gladness).

Therefore the Yahawaday (Jews) of the parawazayam (villages), who live in the parazah (unwalled) iray (towns), ishah (make) the fourteenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month) Adar (Adar) a day of shamachah (gladness) and mashathah (feasting), a tawab (good / proper function) yawam (day), and a yawam (day) of mashalawach (sending) presents of food to ayash (man / husband) rai (neigbor/another person).

Maradakay (Mordecai) kathab (write) these things, and shalach (send) saparayam (letters) to all the Yahawaday (Jews) who were in all the madayanawath (provinces) of the malak (king) Achashawarawash (Ahasuerus), both qarawab (near) and rachawaq (far),
To qawam (rise up) them that they should ishah (make) the fourteenth and fifteenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month) Adar (Adar) yearly,

As the yamayam (days) in which the Yahawaday (Jews) had nawach (rest) from their ayab (enemy), and the chadash (month) which was hapak (turned) to them from yagawan (sorrow) to shamachah (gladness), and from abal (mourning) into a tawab (good / proper function) yawam (day); that they should ishah (make) them yamayam (days) of mashathah (feasting) and shamachah (gladness), and of mashalawach (sending) presents of food to ayash (man / husband) rai (neigbor/another person), and mathanawath (gifts) to the abayawan (needy).
The Yahawaday (Jews) accepted the custom that they had chalal (begun), as Maradakay (Mordecai) had kathab (write) to them;

Because Haman (Haman) the ban (son) of Madathaa (Hammedatha), the agagay (agagite), the tzarar (enemy) of all the Yahawaday (Jews), had plotted against the Yahawaday (Jews) to abad (destroy / perish) them, and napal (fall / be cast down) cast "Pawar (Pur)," that is the gawaral (lot), to hamam (consume) them, and to abad (destroy / perish) them;

But when this became known to the malak (king), he commanded by sapar (book / scribed document) that his rai (wicked) machashabah (device), which he had chashab (devised) against the Yahawaday (Jews), should shawab (turn back / repent) on his own raash (head), and that he and his ban (son) should be hanged on the itz (gallows).

Therefore they qaraa (called) these yamayam (days) "Pawar (Purim)," from the sham (name) "Pawar (Pur)." Therefore because of all the dabaray (words) of this agarath (letter), and of that which they raah (see) seen concerning kakah (this) matter, and that which had nagai (come) to them,

The Yahawaday (Jews) qawam (rise up), and imposed on themselves, and on their descendants, and on all those who lawah (joined) themselves to them, so that it should not ibar (pass over/through), that they would ishah (make) these shanayam (two) yamayam (days) according to what was written, and according to its appointed zaman (time), every shanah (year);

And that these yamayam (days) should be zakar (remember) and ishah (make) throughout every dawar (generation / age / period), every mashapachah (tribe / clan / family), every madayanah (province), and every iyar (city); and that these yamayam (days) of Pawar (Purim) should not ibar (pass over/through) from thawak (midst) the Yahawaday (Jews), nor their zakar (remember) sawap (perish) from their zarai (seed).

Then Asathar (Esther) the malakah (queen), the banath (daughter) of Abayahayal (Abihail), and Maradakay (Mordecai) the Yahawaday (Jew), kathab (write) with all thaqap (authority) to qawam (rise up) this shanay (second) agarath (letter) of Pawar (Purim).

He shalach (send) saparayam (letters) to all the Yahawaday (Jews), to the maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shabai (seven) madayanah (provinces) of the malakawath (kingdom) of Achashawarawash (Ahasuerus), with dabaray (words) of shalawam (peace / safety) and amath (truth),

To qawam (rise up) these yamay (days) of Pawar (Purim) in their appointed zaman (times), as Maradakay (Mordecai) the Yahawaday (Jew) and Asathar (Esther) the malakah (queen) had qawam (rise up), and as they had imposed upon themselves and their descendants, in the dabar (word / matter) of the tzamawath (fastings) and their zaiq (cry).
The commandment of Asathar (Esther) qawam (rise up) these dabaray (matters) of Pawar (Purim); and it was kathab (write) in the sapar (book / scribed document).
Malak (king) Achashawarawash (Ahasuerus) shawam (place / establish / appoint) a mas (tribute) on the aratz (Earth/land), and on the ayay (islands) of the yam (sea/waters).

All the maishah (acts) of his thaqap (power) and of his gabawarah (might), and the full account of the gadawalah (greatness) of Maradakay (Mordecai), to which the malak (king) gadal (advanced) him, aren't they kathab (write) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of the dabaray (chronicles) of the malakay (kings) of Maday (Media) and Paras (Persia)?

For Maradakay (Mordecai) the Yahawaday (Jew) was mashanah (next) to malak (king) Achashawarawash (Ahasuerus), and gadawal (very great/important/mighty) among the Yahawaday (Jews), and ratzah (accepted) by the rab (multitude) of his ach (brother/kinsman), darash (seeking) the tawab (good / proper function) of his im (nation / people), and dabar (word / matter) shalawam (peace / safety) to all his descendants.

There was a ayash (man / husband) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Iwatz (Uz), whose sham (name) was Ayawab (Job). That ayash (man / husband) was blameless and yashar (upright), and ayash (man / husband) who yaraa (feared) Alahayam, and sawar (turned) away from rai (evil).
There were yalad (birth / begot) to him shabai (seven) banayam (sons) and shalawash (three) banawath (daughters).

His maqanah (possessions) also were shabai (seven) alap (thousand) tzaan (sheep), shalawash (three) alap (thousand) gamalayam (camels), chamash (five) maah (hundred) tzamad (yoke) of oxen, chamash (five) maah (hundred) female donkeys, and a very rab (great) ibadah (household); so that this ayash (man / husband) was the greatest of all the banay (children) of the qadam (east).

His ban (son) halak (move) and held a mashathah (feast) in the house of ayash (man / husband) ayash (man / husband) on his birthday; and they shalach (send) and qaraa (called) for their shalawash (three) achawath (sisters) to akal (eat) and to shathah (drinks) with them.

It was so, when the yamay (days) of their mashathah (feasting) had run their course, that Ayawab (Job) shalach (send) and qadash (set apart / make holy) them, and shakam (rose) up early in the baqar (morning), and ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilawath (offerings) according to the masapar (number) of them all. For Ayawab (Job) amar (spoke), "It awalay (perhaps) be that my ban (son) have chataa (sinned), and renounced Alahayam in their labab (hearts)." Ayawab (Job) ishah (make) this yawam (day).
Now it happened on the yawam (day) when Alahayam banay (sons) bawaa (come) to yatzab (present) themselves before Yahawah, that shatan (satan) also bawaa (come) thawak (midst) them.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to shatan (satan), "ayan (NO ONE) bawaa (come) you come from?" Then shatan (satan) inah (answer / respond) Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "From shawat (going) back and forth in the aratz (Earth/land), and from halak (move) up and down in it."

Yahawah amar (spoke) to shatan (satan), "Have you shawam (place / establish / appoint) my ibad (servant), Ayawab (Job)? For there is none like him in the aratz (Earth/land), a blameless and an yashar (upright) ayash (man / husband), ayash (man / husband) who yaraa (fears) Alahayam, and turns away from rai (evil)."
Then shatan (satan) inah (answer / respond) Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "Does Ayawab (Job) yaraa (fear / be afraid) Alahayam for chanam (nothing)?

Haven't you made a shawak (hedge) around him, and around his bayath (house), and around all that he has, on sabayab (surrounding) side? You have barak (blessed) the maishah (work) of his yad (hand), and his maqanah (substance) is paratz (increased) in the aratz (Earth/land).
But shalach (send) forth your yad (hand) now, and nagai (touch) barak (blessed) that he has, and he will renounce you to your panayam (face)."

Yahawah amar (spoke) to shatan (satan), "Behold, all that he has is in your yad (hand). Only on himself don't shalach (send) forth your yad (hand)." So shatan (satan) shalach (send) forth from the panayam (face) of Yahawah.
It fell on a yawam (day) when his ban (son) and his banath (daughter) were akal (eat) and shathah (drinks) yayan (wine) in their bakawar (eldest) ach (brother/kinsman) bayath (house),
That there bawaa (come) a malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) to Ayawab (Job), and amar (spoke), "The oxen were charash (plowing), and the donkeys raih (feeding) yad (hand) them,

And the Shabaa (Sabeans) attacked, and laqach (take / seize) them away. Yes, they have nakah (killed) the nairayam (servants) with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), and I malat (alone) have escaped to nagad (tell) you."

While he was still dabar (word / matter), there also bawaa (come) another, and amar (spoke), "The ash (fire) of Alahayam napal (fall / be cast down) fallen from the sky, and has bair (burned) up the tzaan (sheep) and the nairayam (servants), and akal (eat) them, and I malat (alone) have escaped to nagad (tell) you."

While he was still dabar (word / matter), there bawaa (come) also another, and amar (spoke), "The Kashaday (Chaldeans) shawam (place / establish / appoint) shalawash (three) raashayam (bands), and swept down on the gamalayam (camels), and have laqach (take / seize) them away, yes, and nakah (killed) the nairayam (servants) with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword); and I malat (alone) have escaped to nagad (tell) you."

While he was still dabar (word / matter), there bawaa (come) also another, and amar (spoke), "Your ban (son) and your banath (daughter) were akal (eat) and shathah (drinks) yayan (wine) in their bakawar (eldest) ach (brother/kinsman) bayath (house),

And behold, there bawaa (come) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) rawach (spirit / wind) from the madabar (wilderness), and nagai (struck) the arabai (four) panawath (corners) of the bayath (house), and it napal (fall / be cast down) on the nair (young) men, and they are mawath (death). I malat (alone) have escaped to nagad (tell) you."
Then Ayawab (Job) qawam (rise up), and qarai (tore) his maiyal (robe), and gazaz (shaved) his raash (head), and napal (fall / be cast down) down on the aratz (Earth/land), and shachah (worshiped).

He amar (spoke), "irawam (naked) I yatzaa (go out / come out) out of my am (mother) batan (womb), and irawam (naked) shall I shawab (turn back / repent) there. Yahawah nathan (give), and Yahawah has laqach (take / seize) away. Barak (blessed) be the sham (name) of Yahawah."
In all this, Ayawab (Job) did not chataa (sin), nor nathan (give) Alahayam with wrongdoing.

Again it happened on the yawam (day) when the Alahayam banay (sons) bawaa (come) to yatzab (present) themselves before Yahawah, that shatan (satan) bawaa (come) also thawak (midst) them to yatzab (present) himself before Yahawah.

Yahawah amar (spoke) to shatan (satan), "ay (where) bawaa (come) you come from?" Shatan (satan) inah (answer / respond) Yahawah, and inah (answer / respond), "From shawat (going) back and forth in the aratz (Earth/land), and from halak (move) up and down in it."

Yahawah amar (spoke) to shatan (satan), "Have you lab (heart) my ibad (servant) Ayawab (Job)? For there is none like him in the aratz (Earth/land), a blameless and an yashar (upright) ayash (man / husband), one who yaraa (fears) Alahayam, and sawar (turns) away from rai (evil). He still chazaq (maintains) his thamah (integrity), although you incited me against him, to ruin him chanam (without) cause."
Shatan (satan) inah (answer / respond) Yahawah, and inah (answer / respond), "iwar (skin) for iwar (skin). Yes, all that a ayash (man / husband) nathan (give) he will give for his napash (soul).
But shalach (send) forth your yad (hand) now, and nagai (touch) his itzam (bone) and his bashar (flesh), and he will renounce you to your panayam (face)."
Yahawah amar (spoke) to shatan (satan), "Behold, he is in your yad (hand). Only spare his napash (soul)."

So shatan (satan) yatzaa (go out / come out) yatzaa (go out / come out) from the panayam (face) of Yahawah, and nakah (struck) Ayawab (Job) with painful sores from the kap (sole) of his ragal (feet / foot) to his qadaqad (head).
He laqach (take / seize) for himself a charash (potsherd) to garad (scrape) himself with, and he yashab (inhabit/dwell) thawak (midst) the ashes.
Then his ayashah (woman / wife) amar (spoke) to him, "Do you still chazaq (maintain) your thamah (integrity)? Renounce Alahayam, and mawath (death)."

But he amar (spoke) to her, "You dabar (word / matter) as achad (one) of the foolish nabalawath (women) would dabar (word / matter). Gam (indeed / moreover)? Shall we qabal (receive) tawab (good / proper function) at the hand of Alahayam, and shall we not qabal (receive) rai (evil)?" In all this Ayawab (Job) didn't chataa (sin) with his shapah (lips).

Now when Ayawab (Job's) shalawash (three) raiy (friends) shamai (hearken / hear) of all this rai (evil) that bawaa (come) come on him, they ayash (man / husband) bawaa (come) from his own maqawam (place): Alayapaz (Eliphaz) the thayamanay (temanite), Baladad (Bildad) the shawachay (shuhite), and Tzawapar (Zophar) the naimathay (naamathite), and they made an appointment yachad (together) to bawaa (come) to sympathize with him and to nacham (turn away / repent) him.

When they nashaa (lift) up their iyan (eye) from a distance, and didn't recognize him, they nashaa (lift) their qawal (sound / voice), and bakah (wept); and they ayash (man / husband) qarai (tore) his maiyal (robe), and zaraq (sprinkled) ipar (dust) on their raash (head) toward the sky.

So they yashab (inhabit/dwell) down with him on the aratz (Earth/land) shabai (seven) yamayam (days) and shabai (seven) layalawath (nights), and none dabar (word / matter) a dabar (word / matter) to him, for they raah (see) that his kaab (grief) was very gadal (great).
Achar (other) this Ayawab (Job) pathach (opened) his pah (mouth), and qalal (cursed) the yawam (day) of his birth.
Then Ayawab (Job) inah (answer / respond) and amar (spoke):
"Let the yawam (day) abad (destroy / perish) in which I was yalad (birth / begot), the layal (night) which amar (spoke), ‘There is a boy harah (conceived).'
Let that yawam (day) be chashak (darkness). Don't let Alawah from mail (top/above) darash (seek) for it, neither let the naharah (light) yapai (shine) on it.
Let chashak (darkness) and the shadow of tzalamawath (death) claim it for their own. Let a inanah (cloud) shakan (place) on it. Let all that makes black the yawam (day) baith (terrify) it.

As for that layal (night), let thick apal (darkness) laqach (take / seize) on it. Let it not rejoice among the yamay (days) of the shanah (year). Bawaa (come) it not come into the masapar (number) of the yarachayam (months).
Behold, let that layal (night) be barren. Let no rananah (joyful) voice bawaa (come) therein.
Let them naqab (curse) it who arar (curse) the yawam (day), who are ithayad (ready) to rouse up lawayathan (leviathan).

Let the kawakabay (stars) of its nashap (twilight) be chashak (darkness). Let it qawah (gather/wait) for awar (light), but raah (see) none, neither let it see the ipaipay (eyelids) of the shachar (morning),
Because it didn't sagar (shut) up the dalathay (doors) of my mother's batan (womb), nor did it sathar (hide) imal (trouble) from my iyan (eye).
"Why didn't I mawath (death) from the racham (womb)? Why didn't I gawai (give) up the spirit when my batan (mother) yatzaa (go out / come out) me?
Why did the barakayam (knees) receive me? Or why the shad (breast), that I should yanaq (nurse)?
For now should I have shakab (lain) down and been shaqat (quiet). I should have yashan (slept), then I would have been at nawach (rest),
With malakayam (kings) and yaitzay (counselors) of the aratz (Earth/land), who banah (build) up charabah (waste) places for themselves;
Or with sharayam (princes) who had zahab (gold), who malaa (filled) their bayath (house) with kasap (silver):
Or as a taman (hidden) napal (fall / be cast down) birth I had not been, as ilalayam (infants) who never raah (see) awar (light).
There the rashai (wicked) chadal (cease) from ragaz (troubling). There the yagayai (weary) are at nawach (rest).
There the asayarayam (prisoners) are at shaan (ease) yachad (together). They don't shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the nagash (taskmaster).
The qatan (small / young / least) and the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) are there. The ibad (servant) is chapashay (free) from his adawan (master / lord).
"Why is awar (light) nathan (give) to him who is in imal (misery), chay (life) to the mar (bitter) in napash (soul),
Who chakah (long) for mawath (death), but it doesn't come; and chapar (dig) for it more than for matamawan (hidden) treasures,
Who shamach (rejoice) gayal (exceedingly), and are shawash (glad), when they can matzaa (find) the qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher)?
Why is light given to a gabar (man) whose darak (way) is sathar (hidden), whom Alawah has sakak (hedged) in?
For my anachah (sighing) bawaa (come) panayam (face) I lacham (eat). My groanings are nathak (poured) out like mayam (Waters).
For the thing which I pachad (fear / dread) athah (you (masc)) on me, That which I am yagar (afraid) of bawaa (come) to me.
I am not at ease, neither am I shaqat (quiet), neither have I shaqat (rest); but ragaz (trouble) bawaa (come)."
Then Alayapaz (Eliphaz) the thayamanay (temanite) inah (answer / respond),
"If someone ventures to dabar (word / matter) with you, will you be laah (grieved)? But who yakal (can) itzar (withhold) himself from malah (speaking)?
Behold, you have yasar (instructed) many, you have chazaq (strengthened) the rapah (weak) yadayam (hands).
Your malah (words) have supported him who was kashal (stumble / stagger), You have amatz (made) firm the karai (feeble) barakayam (knees).
But now it bawaa (come) come to you, and you laah (faint). It touches you, and you are bahal (troubled).
Isn't your piety your kasalah (confidence)? Isn't the tham (integrity) of your darak (ways) your thaqawah (hope)?
"Zakar (remember), now, whoever abad (destroy / perish), being naqay (innocent)? Or ayapah (where) were the yashar (upright) kachad (cut) off?
According to what I raah (see) seen, those who charash (plow) awan (iniquity), and zarai (sow) imal (trouble), qatzar (reap) the same.
By the nashamah (breathing thing) of Alawah they abad (destroy / perish). By the rawach (spirit / wind) of his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) are they kalah (complete / finish).
The shaagah (roaring) of the aray (lion), and the qawal (sound / voice) of the fierce shachal (lion), the shanay (teeth) of the young kapayarayam (lions), are nathai (broken).
The old layash (lion) perishes for balay (lack) of tarap (prey). The cubs of the labayaa (lioness) are parad (scattered) abroad.
"Now a thing was ganab (secretly) brought to me. My azan (ear) laqach (take / seize) a whisper of it.
In thoughts from the chazayanawath (visions) of the layal (night), when tharadamah (deep) sleep napal (fall / be cast down) on anashayam (men),
Pachad (fear / dread) qaraa (called) on me, and raid (trembling), which made rab (all) my itzam (bones) pachad (fear / dread).
Then a rawach (spirit / wind) chalap (passed) before my panayam (face). The shairah (hair) of my bashar (flesh) samar (stood) up.

It imad (stood) still, but I couldn't nakar (discern) its maraah (appearance). A maraah (form) was before my iyan (eye). Damamah (silence), then I shamai (hearken / hear) a qawal (sound / voice), saying,
‘Shall mortal anawash (man) be more tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) than Alawah? Shall a gabar (man) be more pure than his Maker?
Behold, he puts no aman (believe / have faith) in his ibad (servant). He shawam (place / establish / appoint) his malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) with error.

Ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) much more, those who shakan (place) in bathay (houses) of chamar (clay), whose yasawad (foundation) is in the ipar (dust), who are dakaa (crushed) panayam (face) the ish (made)!
Between baqar (morning) and irab (evening) they are kathath (destroyed). They abad (destroy / perish) natzach (forever) without any shawam (place / establish / appoint) it.
Isn't their tent yathar (cord) plucked up within them? They mawath (death), and that without chakamah (wisdom).'
"Qaraa (called) now; is there any who will inah (answer / respond) you? To which of the qadawash (holy) ones will you panah (turn)?
For resentment harag (kill) the awayal (foolish) man, and qanaah (jealousy) mawath (death) the simple.
I raah (see) seen the awayal (foolish) sharash (taking) root, but pathaawam (suddenly) I qabab (cursed) his nawah (habitation).
His ban (son) are rachaq (far) from yashai (salvation). They are dakaa (crushed) in the shair (gate). Neither is there any to natzal (deliver) them,
Whose qatzayar (harvest) the raib (hungry) akal (eat) up, and take it even out of the tzanayam (thorns). The snare gapes for their chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor).
For awan (affliction) doesn't yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from the ipar (dust), neither does imal (trouble) tzamach (spring) out of the adamah (ground);
But adam (man) is yalad (birth / begot) to imal (trouble), as the banay (sparks) iwap (flying) gabah (upward).
"But as for me, I would seek Alahayam. I would shawam (place / establish / appoint) my dabarah (cause) to Alahayam,
Who ishah (make) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) things that can't be fathomed, palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) things without masapar (number);
Who nathan (give) matar (rain) on the aratz (Earth/land), and shalach (send) mayam (Waters) on the chawatzawath (fields);
So that he shawam (place / establish / appoint) up on marawam (high) those who are shapal (low), those who qadar (mourn) are shagab (exalted) to yashai (salvation).
He parar (frustrates) the machashabawath (devices) of the irawam (crafty), So that their yad (hand) can't ishah (make) their thawashayah (enterprise).
He lakad (takes) the chakam (wise) in their own iram (craftiness); the itzah (counsel) of the cunning is mahar (carried) headlong.
They pagash (meet) with chashak (darkness) in the yawamam (by day) time, and mashash (grope) at noonday as in the layal (night).
But he yashai (salvation) from the charab (sword) of their pah (mouth), even the abayawan (needy) from the yad (hand) of the chazaq (mighty).
So the dal (poor) has thaqawah (hope), and injustice qapatz (shuts) her pah (mouth).
"Behold, ashar (who/that) is the anawash (man) whom Alawah yakach (corrects). Therefore do not maas (despise) the mawasar (chastening) of the Shaday.
For he wounds, and chabash (binds) up. He injures, and his yad (hand) rapaa (make) whole.
He will natzal (deliver) you in shash (six) tzarawath (troubles); yes, in shabai (seven) no rai (evil) shall nagai (touch) you.
In raib (famine) he will padah (redeem) you from mawath (death); in malachamah (war), from the yad (hand) of the charab (sword).
You shall be chabaa (hidden) from the shawat (scourge) of the lashawan (tongue / language), neither shall you be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of shad (destruction) when it bawaa (come).
At shad (destruction) and kapan (famine) you shall shachaq (laugh), neither shall you be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of the animals of the aratz (Earth/land).
For you shall be allied with the abanay (stones) of the shadah (field). The animals of the shadah (field) shall be at shalam (peace) with you.
You shall yadai (know) that your ahal (tent) is in shalawam (peace / safety). You shall paqad (visit) your nawah (habitation), and shall chataa (miss) nothing.
You shall yadai (know) also that your zarai (seed) shall be rab (great), Your tzaatzaa (offspring) as the ishab (grass) of the aratz (Earth/land).
You shall bawaa (come) to your qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) in a kalach (full) age, like a gadayash (shock) of grain ilah (go up / offer) in its ith (season).
Look this, we have chaqar (searched) it, so it is. Shamai (hearken / hear) it, and yadai (know) it for your good."
Then Ayawab (Job) inah (answer / respond),
"Oh that my anguish were shaqal (weighed), and all my hayah (came to pass) nashaa (lift) in the maazanayam (balances)!
For now it would be kabad (heavier) than the chawal (sand) of the yamayam (seas), therefore have my dabar (word / matter) been rash.
For the chatzay (arrows) of the Shaday are within me. My rawach (spirit / wind) shathah (drinks) up their chamah (poison). The baiwathay (terrors) of Alawah irak (set) themselves in array against me.
Does the paraa (wild) donkey nahaq (bray) when he has dashaa (grass)? Or does the shawar (ox) gaih (low) over his balayal (fodder)?
Can that which has no flavor be akal (eat) without malach (salt)? Or is there any taim (taste) in the rayar (white) of an chalamawath (egg)?
My napash (soul) maan (refuses) to nagai (touch) them. They are as loathsome lacham (food) to me.
"Oh that I might bawaa (come) my shaalah (request), that Alawah nathan (give) grant the thing that I thaqawah (long) for,
Even that it yaal (would) please Alawah to dakaa (crush) me; that he would let nathar (loose) his yad (hand), and batzai (cut) me off!
Be it still my consolation, yes, let me exult in chayal (pain) that doesn't chamal (spare), that I have not denied the amaray (words) of the qadawash (holy) One.
What is my kach (strength / mighty / power), that I should yachal (wait)? What is my qatz (end), that I should be patient?
Is my kach (strength / mighty / power) the kach (strength / mighty / power) of abanayam (stones)? Or is my bashar (flesh) of nachawash (brass)?
Isn't it that I have no izarah (help) in me, That thawashayah (wisdom) is nadach (driven) quite from me?
"To him who is ready to faint, chasad (grace) should be shown from his rai (neigbor/another person); even to him who izab (forsakes) the yaraah (fear) of the Shaday.
My ach (brother/kinsman) have dealt bagad (deceitfully) as a nachal (stream / river), as the apayaq (channel) of nachalayam (brooks) that ibar (pass over/through) away;
Which are qadar (black) by reason of the qarach (ice), in which the shalag (snow) ilam (hides) itself.
In the dry ith (season), they tzamath (vanish). When it is cham (hot), they are daik (consumed) out of their maqawam (place).
The caravans that travel beside them lapath (turn) aside. They ilah (go up / offer) up into the thahaw (formless), and abad (destroy / perish).
The caravans of Thayamaa (Tema) nabat (looked). The halayakath (companies) of Shabaa (Sheba) qawah (gather/wait) for them.
They were distressed because they were batach (confident). They bawaa (come) there, and were chapar (confounded).
For now you are nothing. You raah (see) a terror, and are yaraa (fear / be afraid).
Did I amar (spoke), ‘yahab (give) to me?' Or, ‘Offer a present for me from your kach (strength / mighty / power)?'
Or, ‘malat (deliver) me from the tzar (oppressor / distressor) yad (hand)?' Or, ‘padah (redeem) me from the yad (hand) of the irayatzayam (oppressors)?'
"Yarah (teach) me, and I will hold my charash (peace). Bayan (between) me to understand wherein I have shagah (erred).
How maratz (forcible) are amaray (words) of yashar (upright)! But your reproof, what does it yakach (reprove)?
Do you intend to yakach (reprove) malayam (words), since the speeches of one who is yaash (desperate) are as rawach (spirit / wind)?
Yes, you would even napal (fall / be cast down) lots for the yathawam (fatherless), and karah (make) merchandise of your rai (neigbor/another person).
Now therefore be yaal (pleased) to panah (turn) at me, for surely I shall not kazab (lie) to your face.
Please shawab (turn back / repent). Let there be no injustice. Yes, shawab (turn back / repent) again. My tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) is righteous.
Is there injustice on my lashawan (tongue / language)? Can't my chak (taste) bayan (between) hawah (calamity / destruction) things?
"Isn't a anawash (man) forced to labor on aratz (Earth/land)? Aren't his yamay (days) like the yamay (days) of a shakayar (hired) hand?
As a ibad (servant) who earnestly shaap (desires) the tzal (shadow), as a shakayar (hireling) who qawah (gather/wait) for his wages,
So am I nachal (made) to possess yarachay (months) of misery, imal (wearisome) layalawath (nights) are manah (appointed) to me.
When I shakab (lie) down, I amar (spoke), ‘When shall I qawam (rise up), and the irab (evening) be madad (gone)?' I toss and nadad (turn) until the dawning of the nashap (day).
My bashar (flesh) is labash (clothed) with ramah (worms) and gawash (clods) of ipar (dust). My iwar (skin) closes up, and ragai (breaks) out afresh.
My yawam (day) are qalal (swifter) than a arag (weaver's) shuttle, and are kalah (complete / finish) apas (without) thaqawah (hope).
Oh zakar (remember) that my chay (life) is a rawach (spirit / wind). My iyan (eye) shall no more raah (see) tawab (good / proper function).
The iyan (eye) of him who shawar (sees) me shall shawar (see) me no more. Your iyan (eye) shall be on me, but I shall not be.
As the inan (cloud) is kalah (complete / finish) and vanishes yalak (away), so he who yarad (goes) down to shaawal (Sheol / afterlife) shall ilah (go up / offer) up no more.
He shall shawab (turn back / repent) no more to his bayath (house), neither shall his maqawam (place) nakar (know) him any more.

"Therefore I will not chashak (darkness) silent. I will dabar (word / matter) in the tzar (oppressor / distressor) of my rawach (spirit / wind). I will shayach (meditate) in the bitterness of my napash (soul).
Am I a yam (sea/waters), or a thanayan (sea) monster, that you shawam (place / establish / appoint) a mashamar (guard) over me?
When I amar (spoke), ‘My irash (bed) shall nacham (turn away / repent) me. My mashakab (couch) shall nashaa (lift) my shayach (complaint);'
Then you chathath (scare) me with chalamawath (dreams), and baith (terrify) me through chazayanawath (visions):
So that my napash (soul) bachar (chooses) machanaq (strangling), mawath (death) rather than my itzam (bones).
I maas (loathe) my chayah (life). I don't want to live iwalam (forever). Leave me chadal (alone), for my yawam (day) are but a habal (breath).
What is anawash (man), that you should gadal (magnify) him, that you should shayath (put / appoint / make) your lab (heart) on him,
That you should paqad (visit) him every baqar (morning), and test him every ragai (in an instance)?
Mah (how) long will you not shaih (look) away from me, nor leave me rapah (alone) until I balai (swallow) down my spittle?

If I have chataa (sinned), what pail (do) I do to you, you natzar (watcher) of adam (men)? Why have you shawam (place / establish / appoint) me as a mapagai (mark) for you, so that I am a mashaa (burden) to myself?

Why do you not nashaa (lift) my disobedience, and ibar (pass over/through) away my iwan (guilt/iniquity)? For now shall I shakab (lie) down in the ipar (dust). You will shachar (seek) me diligently, but I shall not be."
Then Baladad (Bildad) the shawachay (shuhite) inah (answer / respond),
"How id (until / as far as) will you malal (speak) these things? Shall the amaray (words) of your pah (mouth) be a kabayar (mighty) rawach (spirit / wind)?
Does Al iwath (pervert) mashapat (justice)? Or does the Shaday iwath (pervert) tzadaq (righteous / just / fair)?
If your ban (son) have chataa (sinned) against him, He has delivered them into the shalach (send) of their disobedience.
If you want to shachar (seek) Al shachar (diligently), chanan (showing favor) your supplication to the Shaday.
If you were zak (pure) and yashar (upright), surely now he would awaken for you, and make the nawah (habitation) of your tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) shalam (prosperous).
Though your raashayath (beginning) was matzair (small), yet your acharayath (latter) end would maad (greatly) shagah (increase).
"Please inquire of raashawan (past) dawar (generation / age / period). Find out about the learning of their ab (father).
(For we are but of thamawal (yesterday), and yadai (know) nothing, because our yawam (day) on aratz (Earth/land) are a tzal (shadow).)
Shall they not yarah (teach) you, amar (spoke) you, and yatzaa (go out / come out) malayam (words) out of their lab (heart)?
"Can the papyrus gaah (grow) up without batzah (mire)? Can the rushes shagah (grow) balay (without) mayam (Waters)?
While it is yet in its ab (father), not qatap (cut) down, it yabash (dry land) panayam (face) any other reed.
So are the arachawath (paths) of shakach (all) who forget Al. The thaqawah (hope) of the godless man shall abad (destroy / perish),
Whose kasal (confidence) shall break apart, Whose mabatach (trust) is a ikabayash (spider's) bayath (house).
He shall shain (lean) on his bayath (house), but it shall not imad (stand). He shall cling to it, but it shall not qawam (rise up).
He is ratab (green) panayam (face) the shamash (sun). His shoots yatzaa (go out / come out) forth over his ganah (garden).
His sharash (roots) are sabak (wrapped) around the rock pile. He chazah (sees) the bayath (house) of abanayam (stones).
If he is balai (destroyed) from his maqawam (place), then it shall kachash (deny) him, saying, ‘I raah (see) not seen you.'
Behold, this is the mashawash (joy) of his darak (way): out of the ipar (earth), others shall tzamach (spring).
"Behold, Al will not maas (cast) away a blameless chazaq (man), neither will he uphold the evildoers.
He will still malaa (fill) your pah (mouth) with shachawaq (laughter/joking matter), your shapah (lips) with tharawaih (shouting).
Those who shanaa (hate) you shall be labash (clothed) with bashath (shame). The ahal (tent) of the rashai (wicked) shall be no more."
Then Ayawab (Job) inah (answer / respond),
"Truly I yadai (know) that it is so, but how can anawash (man) be tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) with Al?
If he is pleased to rayab (contend) with him, he can't inah (answer / respond) him achad (one) time in a alap (thousand).
Alahayam who is wise in labab (heart), and amayatz (mighty) in kach (strength / mighty / power): who qashah (rough / hard) hardened himself against him, and shalam (prospered)?
He ithaq (removes) the harayam (mountains), and they don't yadai (know) it, when he overturns them in his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).
He ragaz (shakes) the aratz (Earth/land) out of its maqawam (place). Its imawad (pillar) palatz (tremble).
He commands the charas (sun), and it doesn't zarach (rise), and chatham (seals) up the kawakabayam (stars).
He natah (alone) stretches out the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and darak (treads) on the bamathay (waves) of the yam (sea/waters).
He ishah (make) the Bear, kasayal (orion), and the kayamah (pleiades), and the rooms of the thayaman (south).
He ishah (make) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) things ayan (NO ONE) chaqar (finding) out; yes, palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) things without masapar (number).
Behold, he ibar (pass over/through) by me, and I don't raah (see) him. He passes on also, but I don't bayan (between) him.
Behold, he snatches chathap (away). Who can shawab (turn back / repent) him? Who will ask him, ‘What are you ishah (make)?'
"Alawah will not shawab (turn back / repent) his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting). The helpers of rahab (rahab) shachach (stoop) under him.
How much less shall I inah (answer / respond) him, And bachar (choose) my dabar (word / matter) to argue with him?
Though I were tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), yet I wouldn't inah (answer / respond) him. I would chanan (showing favor) supplication to my shapat (judge / judgement).
If I had qaraa (called), and he had inah (answer / respond) me, yet I wouldn't aman (believe / have faith) that he listened to my qawal (sound / voice).
For he shawap (breaks) me with a shairah (storm), and rabah (multiplies) my patzai (wounds) chanam (without) cause.
He will not allow me to catch my rawach (spirit / wind), but shabai (fills) me with mamarar (bitterness).
If it is a matter of kach (strength / mighty / power), behold, he is amayatz (mighty)! If of mashapat (justice), ‘Who,' says he, ‘will summon me?'
Though I am tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), my own pah (mouth) shall rashai (condemn) me. Though I am blameless, it shall iqash (prove) me perverse.
I am blameless. I don't yadai (respect) myself. I maas (despise) my napash (soul).
"It is all the same. Therefore I amar (spoke) he kalah (complete / finish) the blameless and the rashai (wicked).
If the shawat (scourge) mawath (death) pathaawam (suddenly), he will laig (mock) at the masah (trial) of the naqay (innocent).
The aratz (Earth/land) is nathan (give) into the yad (hand) of the rashai (wicked). He kasah (covers) the panay (faces) of its shapat (judge / judgement). If not he, then who is it?
"Now my yawam (day) are qalal (swifter) than a runner. They barach (flee) away, they raah (see) no tawab (good / proper function),
They have chalap (passed) away as the abah (be willing / desire) anayawath (ships), as the nashar (eagle) that swoops on the akal (prey).
If I amar (spoke), ‘I will shakach (forget) my shayach (complaint), I will put off my sad panayam (face), and cheer up;'
I am yagar (afraid) of all my itzabath (sorrows), I yadai (know) that you will not hold me naqah (clean/innocent).
I shall be rashai (condemned). Why then do I yagai (labor) in habal (vain)?
If I rachatz (wash) myself with snow, and cleanse my kap (hands) with lye,
Yet you will tabal (plunge) me in the shachath (ditch). My own shalamah (dress / garment) shall thaib (abhor) me.
For he is not a ayash (man / husband), as I am, that I should inah (answer / respond) him, that we should bawaa (come) yachad (together) in mashapat (judgment).
There is no umpire between us, that might shayath (put / appoint / make) his yad (hand) on us shanayam (two).
Let him sawar (take) his shabat (rod) sawar (away) from me. Let his ayamah (terror) not make me afraid;
Then I would dabar (word / matter), and not yaraa (fear / be afraid) him, for I am not so in myself.
"My napash (soul) is naqat (weary) of my chay (life). I will give free course to my shayach (complaint). I will dabar (word / matter) in the bitterness of my napash (soul).
I will amar (spoke) Alawah, ‘rashai (do) not condemn me. Show me why you rayab (contend) with me.

Is it tawab (good / proper function) to you that you should ishaq (oppress), that you should maas (despise) the yagayai (work) of your kap (hands), and smile on the itzah (counsel) of the rashai (wicked)?
Do you have iyanay (eyes) of bashar (flesh)? Or do you raah (see) as anawash (man) raah (see)?
Are your yamay (days) as the yamay (days) of anawash (mortals), or your shanah (years) as anawash (man's) shanah (years),
That you inquire after my iwan (guilt/iniquity), and darash (search) after my chataah (sin)?
Although you daith (know) that I am not rashai (wicked), there is no one who can natzal (deliver) out of your yad (hand).
"‘Your yad (hand) have framed me and ishah (make) me yachad (altogether), yet you balai (destroy) me.
Zakar (remember), I beg you, that you ishah (make) fashioned me as chamar (clay). Will you shawab (turn back / repent) me into ipar (dust) again?
Haven't you nathak (poured) me out like chalab (milk), and qapaa (curdled) me like gabanah (cheese)?
You have labash (clothed) me with iwar (skin) and bashar (flesh), and knit me together with itzamawath (bones) and gayadayam (sinews).
You ishah (make) granted me chay (life) and loving chasad (grace). Your paqadah (visitation) has shamar (keep/guard) my rawach (spirit / wind).
Yet you tzapan (hid) these things in your labab (heart). I yadai (know) that this is with you:
If I chataa (sin), then you shamar (keep/guard) me. You will not naqah (clean/innocent) me from my iwan (guilt/iniquity).

If I am rashai (wicked), alalay (woe) to me. If I am tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), I still shall not nashaa (lift) up my raash (head), being filled with disgrace, and conscious of my inay (affliction).
If my gaah (head) is held high, you tzawad (hunt) me like a shachal (lion). Again you show yourself powerful to me.
You chadash (renew) your witnesses against me, and rabah (increase) your kais (indignation) on me. Chalayapawath (changes) and tzabaa (troop) are with me.
"‘Why, then, yatzaa (go out / come out) you brought me forth out of the racham (womb)? I wish I had gawai (given) up the spirit, and no iyan (eye) raah (see) seen me.
I should have been as though I had not been. I should have been yabal (carried) from the batan (womb) to the qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher).
Aren't my yawam (day) mait (few)? Chadal (cease) then. Leave me shayath (put / appoint / make), that I may find a mait (little) balag (comfort),
Before I yalak (go) where I shall not shawab (turn back / repent) from, to the aratz (Earth/land) of chashak (darkness) and of the shadow of tzalamawath (death);
The aratz (Earth/land) dark as midnight, of the shadow of tzalamawath (death), without any sadar (order), where the yapai (light) is as midnight.'"
Then Tzawapar (Zophar), the naimathay (naamathite), inah (answer / respond),
"Shouldn't the rab (multitude) of dabarayam (words) be inah (answer / respond)? Should a ayash (man / husband) full of shapah (talk) be justified?
Should your boastings make mathayam (men) hold their charash (peace)? When you laig (mock), shall no man make you kalam (ashamed)?
For you amar (spoke), ‘My laqach (doctrine) is zak (pure). I am bar (clean) in your iyan (eye).'
But oh that Alawah would dabar (word / matter), and pathach (open) his shapah (lips) against you,

That he would show you the thailamawath (secrets) of chakamah (wisdom)! For true chakamah (wisdom) has kapal (two) sides. Yadai (know) therefore that Alawah exacts of you less than your iwan (guilt/iniquity) deserves.
"Can you fathom the mystery of Alawah? Or can you probe the limits of the Shaday?
They are gabah (high) as shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens). What can you pail (do)? They are deeper than shaawal (Sheol / afterlife). What yadai (can) you know?
Its mad (measure) is longer than the aratz (Earth/land), and broader than the yam (sea/waters).
If he passes by, or confines, or convenes a court, then who can oppose him?
For he yadai (knows) shawaa (vanity) mathay (men). He raah (see) awan (iniquity) also, even though he doesn't bayan (between) it.
An empty-headed ayash (man / husband) becomes labab (wise) when a adam (man) is yalad (birth / begot) as a paraa (wild) donkey's iyar (colt).
"If you kawan (set) your lab (heart) aright, parash (stretch) out your kap (hands) toward him.
If awan (iniquity) is in your yad (hand), rachaq (put) it far away. Don't let iwal (unrighteousness) shakan (place) in your ahal (tents).
Surely then you shall nashaa (lift) up your panayam (face) without maawam (spot); Yes, you shall be steadfast, and shall not yaraa (fear / be afraid):
For you shall shakach (forget) your misery. You shall zakar (remember) it as mayam (Waters) that are ibar (pass over/through) away.
Chalad (life) shall be qawam (rise up) than the noonday. Though there is iwap (flying), it shall be as the baqar (morning).
You shall be batach (secure), because there is thaqawah (hope). Yes, you shall chapar (search), and shall take your shakab (rest) in safety.
Also you shall rabatz (lie) down, and none shall make you charad (afraid). Yes, many shall court your favor.

But the iyanay (eyes) of the rashai (wicked) shall kalah (complete / finish). They shall have no abad (destroy / perish) to flee. Their thaqawah (hope) shall be the mapach (giving) up of the napash (soul)."
Then Ayawab (Job) inah (answer / respond),
"No amanam (doubt), but you are the im (nation / people), and chakamah (wisdom) shall mawath (death) with you.
But I have labab (understanding) as well as you; I am not napal (fall / be cast down) to you. Yes, who doesn't know such things as these?

I am like shachawaq (laughter/joking matter) who is a joke to his neighbor, I, who qaraa (called) on Alawah, and he inah (answer / respond). The tzadayaq (righteous), the blameless shachawaq (laughter/joking matter) is a joke.
In the ishathawath (thought) of him who is at shaanan (ease) there is contempt for misfortune. It is kawan (ready) for them whose ragal (feet / foot) mawaiday (slips).
The ahalayam (tents) of shadadayam (robbers) shalah (prosper). Those who ragaz (provoke) Al are batachawath (secure), who bawaa (come) their Alawah in their yad (hand).
"But shaal (ask) the animals, now, and they shall yarah (teach) you; the iwap (flying) of the sky, and they shall nagad (tell) you.
Or shayach (meditate) to the aratz (Earth/land), and it shall yarah (teach) you. The dag (fish) of the yam (sea/waters) shall sapar (book) to you.
Who doesn't yadai (know) that in all these, the yad (hand) of Yahawah ishah (make) done this,
In whose yad (hand) is the napash (soul) of every chay (life) thing, and the rawach (spirit / wind) of all ayash (man / husband)?
Doesn't the azan (ear) bachan (try) malayan (words), even as the palate taim (tastes) its akal (food)?
With yashayash (aged) men is chakamah (wisdom), in arak (length) of yamayam (days) thabawan (understanding).
"With Alahayam is wisdom and gabawarah (might). He has itzah (counsel) and thabawan (understanding).
Behold, he haras (breaks) down, and it can't be banah (build) again. He imprisons a ayash (man / husband), and there can be no release.
Behold, he itzar (withholds) the mayam (Waters), and they yabash (dry land) up. Again, he shalach (send) them out, and they overturn the aratz (Earth/land).
With him is iz (strength / might / refuge) and thawashayah (wisdom). The shagag (deceived) and the deceiver are his.
He yalak (leads) yawaitzayam (counselors) away shawalal (stripped). He makes shapatayam (judges) halal (praise).
He loosens the mawasar (bond) of malakayam (kings). He asar (binds) their waist with a belt.
He yalak (leads) kahanayam (priests) away shawalal (stripped), and overthrows the ayathan (mighty).
He sawar (removes) the shapah (speech) of those who are aman (believe / have faith), and laqach (take / seize) away the taim (understanding) of the zaqanayam (elders).
He pours bawaz (contempt) on nadayabayam (princes), and loosens the belt of the strong.
He galah (uncovers) imaq (deep) things out of chashak (darkness), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out to awar (light) the shadow of tzalamawath (death).
He shagaa (increases) the gawayam (nations), and he abad (destroy / perish) them. He shatach (enlarges) the gawayam (nations), and he nachah (leads) them captive.

He sawar (takes) away lab (heart) from the raashay (chiefs) of the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land), and thaih (causes) them to wander in a thahaw (formless) where there is no darak (way).
They mashash (grope) in the chashak (darkness) without awar (light). He thaih (makes) them stagger like a drunken shakawar (man).
"Behold, my iyan (eye) raah (see) seen all this. My azan (ear) has shamai (hearken / hear) and bayan (between) it.
What you daith (know), I yadai (know) also. I am not napal (fall / be cast down) to you.
"Awalam (surely) I would dabar (word / matter) to the Shaday. I chapatz (desire) to yakach (reason) with Al.
But you are tapalay (forgers) of shaqar (lies). You are all rapaay (physicians) of no alayal (value).
Oh that you would be completely charash (silent)! Then you would be wise.
Shamai (hearken / hear) now my thawakachah (reasoning). Listen to the rabawath (pleadings) of my shapah (lips).
Will you dabar (word / matter) iwal (unrighteously) for Al, and dabar (word / matter) deceitfully for him?
Will you show partiality to him? Will you rayab (contend) for Al?
Is it tawab (good / proper function) that he should chaqar (search) you out? Or as anawash (one) thahathalaw (deceives) a man, will you hathal (deceive) him?
He will yakach (surely) yakach (reprove) you if you secretly show partiality.
Shall not his majesty make you baith (afraid), And his pachad (fear / dread) napal (fall / be cast down) on you?
Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, Your defenses are defenses of chamar (clay).
"Be charash (silent), leave me alone, that I may dabar (word / matter). Let ibar (pass over/through) on me what will.
Why should I nashaa (lift) my bashar (flesh) in my shan (teeth), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) my napash (soul) in my kap (hand)?
Han (behold), he will qatal (kill) me. I yachal (have) no hope. Nevertheless, I will yakach (maintain) my darak (ways) panayam (face) him.
This also shall be my yashawaih (salvation), that a godless man shall not bawaa (come) panayam (face) him.
Shamai (hearken / hear) shamai (hearken / hear) my speech. Let my achawah (declaration) be in your azan (ear).
See now, I have irak (set) my cause in order. I yadai (know) that I am tzadaq (righteous / just / fair).
Who is he who will rayab (contend) with me? For then would I hold my charash (peace) and gawai (give) up the spirit.
"Only don't ishah (make) shanayam (two) things to me; then I will not sathar (hide) myself from your panayam (face):
Rachaq (withdraw) your kap (hand) rachaq (far) from me; and don't let your ayamah (terror) make me afraid.
Then qaraa (called), and I will inah (answer / respond); or let me dabar (word / matter), and you shawab (turn back / repent) me.
How many are my iwanawath (iniquities) and chataawath (sins)? Yadai (make) me know my disobedience and my chataah (sin).
Why sathar (hide) you your panayam (face), and chashab (hold) me for your ayab (enemy)?
Will you harass a nadap (driven) ilah (leaf)? Will you radap (pursue) the yabash (dry land) qash (stubble)?
For you kathab (write) mararah (bitter) things against me, and yarash (make) me inherit the iwanawath (iniquities) of my naiwar (youth):

You also shawam (place / establish / appoint) my ragal (feet / foot) in the sad (stocks), and shamar (keep/guard) all my arach (paths). You chaqah (set) a bound to the soles of my ragal (feet / foot),
Though I am decaying like a rotten thing, like a bagad (garment) that is ish (made) - akal (eat).
"Adam (man), who is yalad (birth / begot) of a ayashah (woman / wife), is of qatzar (few) yamayam (days), and shabai (full) of ragaz (trouble).
He yatzaa (go out / come out) forth like a tzayatz (flower), and is namal (cut) down. He also barach (flees) like a tzal (shadow), and doesn't imad (continue).
Do you paqach (open) your iyan (eye) on such a zah (this / that / these), and bawaa (come) me into mashapat (judgment) with you?
Who can nathan (give) a tahawar (clean) thing out of an tamaa (unclean)? Not achad (one).

Am (mother) his yawam (day) are charatz (determined), the masapar (number) of his chadash (month) is with you, and you ishah (make) appointed his chaq (statute) that he can't ibar (pass over/through);
Shaih (look) away from him, that he may chadal (rest), until he shall ratzah (accomplish), as a shakayar (hireling), his yawam (day).
"For there is thaqawah (hope) for a itz (tree), If it is karath (cut) down, that it will chalap (sprout) again, that the tender yawanaqath (branch) of it will not chadal (cease).
Though its sharash (root) grows zaqan (old) in the aratz (Earth/land), and its gazai (stock) mawath (death) in the ipar (ground),
Yet through the rayach (smell) of mayam (Waters) it will parach (bud), and ishah (make) forth qatzayar (boughs) like a natai (plant).
But gabar (man) mawath (death), and is laid low. Yes, adam (man) gawai (gives) up the spirit, and where is he?
As the mayam (Waters) azal (fail) from the yam (sea/waters), and the nahar (river) charab (wastes) and yabash (dry land) up,
So ayash (man / husband) shakab (lies) down and doesn't qawam (rise up). Until the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) are no more, they shall not qawatz (awake), nor be roused out of their shanah (sleep).

"Oh that you would tzapan (hide) me in shaawal (Sheol / afterlife), that you would sathar (keep) me secret, until your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) is shawab (turn back / repent), that you would shayath (put / appoint / make) me a chaq (statute) time, and zakar (remember) me!
If a gabar (man) mawath (death), shall he chayah (live) again? All the yamay (days) of my tzabaa (troop) would I yachal (wait), until my release should bawaa (come).
You would qaraa (called), and I would inah (answer / respond) you. You would have a kasap (desire) to the maishah (work) of your yad (hand).
But now you sapar (book) my tzaid (steps). Don't you shamar (keep/guard) over my chataah (sin)?
My disobedience is chatham (sealed) up in a tzarawar (bag). You fasten up my iwan (guilt/iniquity).
"But the har (mountain) napal (fall / be cast down) nabal (comes) to nothing. The tzawar (rock) is ithaq (removed) out of its maqawam (place);

The mayam (Waters) shachaq (wear) the abanayam (stones). The torrents of it shatap (wash) away the ipar (dust) of the aratz (Earth/land). So you abad (destroy / perish) the thaqawah (hope) of anawash (man).
You natzach (forever) thaqap (prevail) against him, and he departs. You shanah (change) his panayam (face), and shalach (send) him away.
His ban (son) kabad (come) to honor, and he doesn't yadai (know) it. They are tzair (brought) low, but he doesn't bayan (between) it of them.
But his bashar (flesh) on him kaab (has) pain, and his napash (soul) inside him abal (mourns)."
Then Alayapaz (Eliphaz) the thayamanay (temanite) inah (answer / respond),
"Should a wise chakam (man) inah (answer / respond) with rawach (spirit / wind) daith (knowledge), and malaa (fill) himself with the east qadayam (wind)?
Should he yakach (reason) with unprofitable dabar (word / matter), or with speeches with which he can do no yail (good)?
Yes, you do away with yaraah (fear), and hinder devotion panayam (face) Al.
For your iwan (guilt/iniquity) teaches your pah (mouth), and you bachar (choose) the lashawan (tongue / language) of the irawam (crafty).
Your own pah (mouth) rashai (condemns) you, and not I. Yes, your own shapah (lips) inah (answer / respond) against you.
"Are you the raashawan (first) adam (man) who was yalad (birth / begot)? Or were you chawal (brought) panayam (face) before the gabaiwath (hills)?
Have you shamai (hearken / hear) the sawad (secret) counsel of Alawah? Garai (do) you limit chakamah (wisdom) to yourself?
What do you yadai (know), that we don't yadai (know)? What do you bayan (between), which is not in us?
With us are both the shayab (gray-headed) and the very yashayash (aged) men, much yawam (day) than your ab (father).
Are the thanachamawath (consolations) of Al too mait (small) for you, even the dabar (word / matter) that is gentle toward you?
Why does your lab (heart) laqach (take / seize) you away? Why do your iyan (eye) flash,
That you shawab (turn back / repent) your rawach (spirit / wind) against Al, and let such malayan (words) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of your pah (mouth)?
What is anawash (man), that he should be zakah (clean)? What is he who is yalad (birth / begot) of a ayashah (woman / wife), that he should be tzadaq (righteous / just / fair)?
Behold, he puts no aman (believe / have faith) in his qadawash (holy) ones. Yes, the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) are not zakak (clean) in his iyan (eye);
How much less ayash (man / husband) who is thaib (abominable) and corrupt, a ayash (man / husband) who shathah (drinks) iwal (iniquity) like mayam (Waters)!
"I will chawah (show) you, shamai (hearken / hear) to me; that which I have chazah (seen) I will sapar (book):
(Which chakam (wise) men have nagad (told) by their ab (father), and have not kachad (hidden) it;
To whom alone the aratz (Earth/land) was nathan (give), and no stranger ibar (pass over/through) thawak (midst) them):
The rashai (wicked) chawal (man) writhes in pain all his yamay (days), even the masapar (number) of shanayam (years) that are tzapan (laid) up for the irayatz (oppressor).
A qawal (sound / voice) of pachadayam (terrors) is in his azan (ear). In prosperity the shadad (destroyer) shall bawaa (come) on him.
He doesn't aman (believe / have faith) that he shall shawab (turn back / repent) out of chashak (darkness). He is tzapah (watchman / keep watch) for by the charab (sword).
He nadad (wanders) abroad for lacham (bread), saying, ‘Where is it?' He yadai (knows) that the yawam (day) of chashak (darkness) is kawan (ready) at his yad (hand).
Tzar (oppressor / distressor) and matzawaqah (anguish) make him baith (afraid). They thaqap (prevail) against him, as a malak (king) ithayad (ready) to the kayadawar (battle).
Because he has natah (stretched) out his yad (hand) against Al, and behaves himself proudly against the Shaday;
He rawatz (runs) at him with a stiff tzawaar (neck), with the ibay (thick) gabay (shields) of his magan (shield);
Because he has kasah (covered) his panayam (face) with his chalab (fatness), and ishah (make) fat on his thighs.
He shakan (place) lived in kachad (desolate) irayam (cities), in bathayam (houses) which no one yashab (inhabit/dwell), which were ithad (ready) to become galayam (heaps).
He shall not be ishar (rich), neither shall his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) qawam (rise up), neither shall their natah (possessions) be extended on the aratz (Earth/land).
He shall not sawar (depart) out of chashak (darkness). The shalahabath (flame) shall yabash (dry land) up his branches. By the rawach (spirit / wind) of Alahayam mouth shall he sawar (go) away.
Let him not aman (believe / have faith) in emptiness, thaih (deceiving) himself; for emptiness shall be his reward.
It shall be malaa (accomplished) laa (NOT) his yawam (day). His kapah (branch) shall not be rainan (green).
He shall chamas (shake) off his basar (unripe) grape as the gapan (vine), and shall shalak (cast) off his natzah (flower) as the zayath (olive) tree.
For the idah (company) of the godless shall be barren, and ash (fire) shall akal (eat) the ahalay (tents) of shachad (bribery).
They harah (conceive) imal (mischief), and yalad (birth / begot) forth awan (iniquity). Their batan (heart) kawan (prepares) maramah (deceit)."
Then Ayawab (Job) inah (answer / respond),
"I have shamai (hearken / hear) many such things. You are all imal (miserable) comforters!
Shall rawach (spirit / wind) dabaray (words) have an qatz (end)? Or what provokes you that you inah (answer / respond)?

I also could dabar (word / matter) as you do. If your napash (soul) were in my napash (soul) place, I could chabar (join) malayam (words) together against you, and nawai (shake) my raash (head) at you,
But I would amatz (strengthen) you with my pah (mouth). The solace of my shapah (lips) would relieve you.
"Though I dabar (word / matter), my kaab (grief) is not subsided. Though I chadal (forbear), what am I halak (move)?
But now, Alahayam, you have surely worn me out. You have shamam (made) desolate all my idah (company).
You have shriveled me up. This is a id (until / as far as) against me. My kachash (leanness) qawam (rise up) up against me. It inah (answer / respond) to my panayam (face).

He has tarap (torn) me in his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and persecuted me. He has charaq (gnashed) on me with his shan (teeth). My tzar (oppressor / distressor) latash (sharpens) his iyan (eye) on me.
They have pair (gaped) on me with their pah (mouth). They have nakah (struck) me on the lachay (cheek) charapah (reproachfully). They malaa (gather) themselves yachad (together) against me.
Al sagar (delivers) me to the iwayal (ungodly), and casts me into the yaday (hands) of the rashai (wicked).
I was at shalaw (ease), and he parar (broke) me apart. Yes, he achaz (has) taken me by the irap (neck), and pawatz (dashed) me to pieces. He has also qawam (rise up) me up for his target.
His rab (archers) surround me. He splits my kalayah (kidneys) apart, and does not chamal (spare). He shapak (pours) out my mararah (gall) on the aratz (Earth/land).
He paratz (breaks) me with paratz (breach) on paratz (breach). He rawatz (runs) on me like a gabawar (giant).
I have thapar (sewed) sackcloth on my galad (skin), and have thrust my qaran (horn) in the ipar (dust).
My panayam (face) is chamar (red) with bakay (weeping). Deep tzalamawath (darkness) is on my ipaip (eyelids).
Although there is no chamas (violence) in my kap (hands), and my thapalah (prayer) is zak (pure).
"Aratz (Earth/land), don't kasah (cover) my dam (blood). Let my zaiq (cry) have no maqawam (place) to rest.
Even now, behold, my id (until / as far as) is in shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens). He who vouches for me is on marawam (high).
My rai (neigbor/another person) scoff at me. My iyan (eye) dalap (pour) out tears to Alawah,
That he would yakach (maintain) the right of a gabar (man) with Alawah, of a son of adam (man) with his neighbor!
For when a masapar (few) shanawath (years) have athah (you (masc)), I shall go the arach (way) of no shawab (turn back / repent).
"My rawach (spirit / wind) is consumed. My yawam (day) are zaik (extinct), And the qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) is ready for me.
Surely there are hathalayam (mockers) with me. My iyan (eye) lawan (dwells) on their marah (provocation).
"Now shawam (place / establish / appoint) a irab (evening), be collateral for me with yourself. Who is there who will thaqai (blow / sound alarm) yad (hand) with me?
For you have tzapan (hidden) their lab (heart) from shakal (understanding), Therefore you shall not rawam (will lift up) them.
He who nagad (denounces) his raiyam (friends) for a prey, Even the iyanay (eyes) of his ban (son) shall kalah (complete / finish).
"But he has yatzag (made) me a mashal (byword) of the imayam (people). They spit in my thapath (face).
My iyan (eye) also is kahah (dim) by reason of kais (sorrow). All my yatzar (members) are as a tzal (shadow).
Yashar (upright) men shall be shamam (astonished) at this. The naqay (innocent) shall iwar (rouse / awaken) up himself against the godless.
Yet shall the tzadayaq (righteous) achaz (hold) on his darak (way). He who has tahar (clean) yadayam (hands) shall grow amatz (stronger) and stronger.
But as for you shawab (turn back / repent), come on now again; I shall not matzaa (find) a wise chakam (man) among you.
My yawam (day) are past, my plans are nathaq (broken) off, as are the mawarashay (thoughts) of my labab (heart).
They shawam (place / establish / appoint) the layal (night) into yawam (day), saying ‘The awar (light) is qarawab (near)' in the panayam (face) of chashak (darkness).
If I qawah (gather/wait) for shaawal (Sheol / afterlife) as my bayath (house), if I have rapad (spread) my yatzawai (couch) in the chashak (darkness),
If I have qaraa (called) to shachath (corruption), ‘You are my ab (father);' to the ramah (worm), ‘My am (mother),' and ‘my achawath (sister);'
Apaw (where) then is my thaqawah (hope)? As for my thaqawah (hope), who shall shawar (see) it?
Shall it yarad (go) down with me to the gates of shaawal (Sheol / afterlife), or descend yachad (together) into the ipar (dust)?"
Then Baladad (Bildad) the shawachay (shuhite) inah (answer / respond),
"Id (until / as far as) long will you hunt for malayan (words)? Bayan (between), and afterwards we will dabar (word / matter).
Why are we chashab (counted) as animals, which have become tamah (unclean) in your iyan (eye)?

You who tarap (tear) yourself in your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), shall the aratz (Earth/land) be forsaken for you? Or shall the tzawar (rock) be ithaq (removed) out of its maqawam (place)?
"Yes, the awar (light) of the rashai (wicked) shall be daik (put) out, The shabayab (spark) of his ash (fire) shall not nagah (shine).
The awar (light) shall be chashak (darkness) in his ahal (tent). His nayar (lamp) above him shall be daik (put) out.
The tzaiday (steps) of his awan (strength) shall be shortened. His own itzah (counsel) shall shalak (cast) him down.
For he is shalach (send) into a rashath (net) by his own ragal (feet / foot), and he wanders into its mesh.
A pach (snare / trap) will achaz (take) him by the iqab (heel). A trap will chazaq (catch) him.
A noose is taman (hidden) for him in the aratz (Earth/land), a malakadath (trap) for him in the nathayab (way).
Balahawath (terrors) shall make him baith (afraid) on sabayab (surrounding) side, and shall chase him at his heels.
His awan (strength) shall be famished. Ayad (calamity) shall be kawan (ready) at his tzalai (side).
The members of his body shall be akal (eat). The bakawar (firstborn) of mawath (death) shall akal (eat) his members.
He shall be nathaq (rooted) out of his ahal (tent) where he mabatach (trusts). He shall be tzaid (brought) to the malak (king) of balahawath (terrors).
There shall shakan (place) in his ahal (tent) that which is balay (none) of his. Sulfur shall be zarah (scattered) on his nawah (habitation).
His sharash (roots) shall be yabash (dry land) up beneath. Mail (top/above) shall his qatzayar (branch) be namal (cut) off.
His zakar (remember) shall abad (destroy / perish) from the aratz (Earth/land). He shall have no sham (name) in the panayam (face).
He shall be hadap (driven) from awar (light) into chashak (darkness), and nadad (chased) out of the thabal (world).
He shall have neither nayan (son) nor grandson among his im (nation / people), nor any sharayad (remaining) magawar (where) he lived.
Those who acharawan (come) after shall be shamam (astonished) at his yawam (day), as those who qadamawanay (went) before were frightened.
Surely such are the mashakanawath (dwellings) of the iwal (unrighteous). This is the maqawam (place) of him who doesn't yadai (know) Al."
Then Ayawab (Job) inah (answer / respond),
"How long will you torment me, and dakaa (crush) me with malayam (words)?
You have kalam (reproached) me ishar (ten) paimayam (times). You aren't bawash (ashamed) that you attack me.
If it is amanam (true) that I have shagah (erred), my mashawagah (error) lawan (remains) with myself.
If amanam (indeed) you will gadal (magnify) yourselves against me, and yakach (plead) against me my charapah (reproach);
Yadai (know) apaw (now) that Alawah has iwath (subverted) me, and has surrounded me with his matzawad (net).
"Behold, I tzaiq (cry) out of chamas (wrong), but I am not inah (answer / respond). I shawai (cry) for help, but there is no mashapat (justice).
He has walled up my arach (way) so that I can't ibar (pass over/through), and has shawam (place / establish / appoint) chashak (darkness) in my nathayab (paths).
He has pashat (stripped) me of my kabawad (glory), and sawar (taken) the itarah (crown) from my itarah (head).
He has nathatz (broken) me down on sabayab (surrounding) side, and I am yalak (gone). My thaqawah (hope) he has plucked up like a itz (tree).
He has also charah (hot with anger) his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) against me. He chashab (counts) me among his tzar (oppressor / distressor).
His gadawad (troops) bawaa (come) on yachad (together), build a siege ramp against me, and chanah (encamp) around my ahal (tent).
"He has rachaq (put) my ach (brother/kinsman) rachaq (far) from me. My yadai (acquaintances) are wholly zawar (estranged) from me.
My relatives have gone away. My yadai (familiar) friends have shakach (forgotten) me.
Those who gawar (dwell) in my bayath (house), and my amah (maids), chashab (count) me for a stranger. I am an nakaray (alien) in their iyan (eye).
I qaraa (called) to my ibad (servant), and he inah (answer / respond) me no answer. I beg him with my pah (mouth).
My rawach (spirit / wind) is offensive to my ayashah (woman / wife). I am loathsome to the banay (children) of my own batan (mother).
Even iwayal (young) children maas (despise) me. If I qawam (rise up), they dabar (word / matter) against me.
All my familiar mathay (friends) thaib (abhor) me. They whom I ahab (love) have hapak (turned) against me.
My itzam (bones) dabaq (stick) to my iwar (skin) and to my bashar (flesh). I have malat (escaped) by the iwar (skin) of my shan (teeth).
"Chanan (showing favor) pity on me, chanan (showing favor) pity on me, you my rai (neigbor/another person); for the yad (hand) of Alawah has nagai (touched) me.
Why do you radap (persecute) me as Al, and are not shabai (satisfied) with my bashar (flesh)?
"Oh that my malah (words) were apaw (now) kathab (write)! Oh that they were inscribed in a sapar (book / scribed document)!
That with an barazal (iron) it (pen) and iwaparath (lead) they were engraved in the tzawar (rock) id (until / as far as)!
But as for me, I yadai (know) that my gaal (redeemer) chay (life). In the end, he will qawam (rise up) upon the ipar (earth).
Achar (other) my iwar (skin) is naqap (destroyed), then in my bashar (flesh) shall I chazah (see) Alawah,
Whom I, even I, shall chazah (see) on my side. My iyan (eye) shall raah (see), and not as a stranger. "My kalayah (heart) is kalah (complete / finish) chayaq (within) me.
If you amar (spoke), ‘How we will radap (persecute) him!' Because the sharash (root) of the dabar (word / matter) is matzaa (found) in me,
Be gawar (afraid) of the charab (sword), for chamah (wrath) brings the iwanawath (punishments) of the charab (sword), that you may yadai (know) there is a dayan (judge)."
Then Tzawapar (Zophar) the naimathay (naamathite) inah (answer / respond),
"Therefore do my thoughts shawab (turn back / repent) answer to me, even by reason of my chawash (haste) that is in me.
I have shamai (hearken / hear) the reproof which puts me to kalamah (shame). The rawach (spirit / wind) of my bayanah (understanding) inah (answer / respond) me.
Don't you yadai (know) this from id (until / as far as) time, since adam (man) was shawam (place / establish / appoint) on aratz (Earth/land),
That the rananah (triumphing) of the rashai (wicked) is qarawab (short), the shamachah (joy) of the godless but for a ragai (in an instance)?
Though his height ilah (go up / offer) up to the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and his raash (head) nagai (reach) to the ib (clouds),
Yet he shall abad (destroy / perish) natzach (forever) like his own galal (dung). Those who raah (see) seen him shall amar (spoke), ‘ay (where) is he?'
He shall iwap (flying) away as a chalawam (dream), and shall not be matzaa (found). Yes, he shall be nadad (chased) away like a chazayawan (vision) of the layal (night).
The iyan (eye) which shazap (saw) him shall see him no more, neither shall his maqawam (place) any more see him.
His ban (son) shall seek the favor of the dal (poor). His yad (hand) shall shawab (turn back / repent) back his wealth.
His itzam (bones) are malaa (full) of his ilawam (youth), but youth shall shakab (lie) down with him in the ipar (dust).
"Though rai (wickedness) is mathaq (sweet) in his pah (mouth), though he kachad (hide) it under his lashawan (tongue / language),
Though he chamal (spare) it, and will not let it go, but manai (keep) it still thawak (midst) his chak (mouth);
Yet his lacham (food) in his maih (bowels) is hapak (turned). It is cobra venom qarab (among / near) him.
He has balai (swallowed) down riches, and he shall qawaa (vomit) them up again. Al will yarash (cast) them out of his batan (belly).
He shall yanaq (suck) cobra raash (head). The apaih (viper's) lashawan (tongue / language) shall harag (kill) him.
He shall not raah (see) at the palagawath (rivers), the flowing streams of dabash (honey) and chamaah (butter).

That for which he labored he shall shawab (turn back / repent), and shall not balai (swallow) it down. According to the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) that he has gotten, he shall not ilas (rejoice).
For he has ratzatz (oppressed) and forsaken the dal (poor). He has violently gazal (taken) away a bayath (house), and he shall not banah (build) it up.
"Because he yadai (knew) no shalaw (quietness) batan (within) him, he shall not malat (save) anything of that in which he chamad (delights).
There was nothing sharayad (left) that he didn't devour, therefore his prosperity shall not endure.
In the fullness of his sapaq (sufficiency), distress shall overtake him. The yad (hand) of everyone who is in imal (misery) shall bawaa (come) on him.

When he is about to malaa (fill) his batan (belly), Alahayam will cast the charawan (fierceness) of his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) on him. It will matar (rain) on him lachawam (while) he is eating.
He shall barach (flee) from the barazal (iron) nashaq (weapon). The bronze qashath (arrow) shall chalap (strike) him through.
He shalap (draws) it yatzaa (go out / come out), and it comes out of his gawah (body). Yes, the baraq (glittering) point halak (move) out of his liver. Amayam (terrors) are on him.
All chashak (darkness) is taman (laid) up for his treasures. An unfanned ash (fire) shall akal (eat) him. It shall consume that which is sharayad (left) in his ahal (tent).
The shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) shall galah (reveal) his iwan (guilt/iniquity). The aratz (Earth/land) shall qawam (rise up) up against him.
The yabawal (increase) of his bayath (house) shall depart. They shall rush nagar (away) in the yawam (day) of his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).
This is the chalaq (portion) of a rashai (wicked) adam (man) from Alahayam, the nachalah (heritage) amar (spoke) to him by Al."
Then Ayawab (Job) inah (answer / respond),
"Shamai (hearken / hear) shamai (hearken / hear) to my speech. Let this be your thanachawam (consolation).
Allow me, and I also will dabar (word / matter); achar (other) I have dabar (word / matter), laig (mock) on.
As for me, is my shayach (complaint) to adam (man)? Why shouldn't I be impatient?
Panah (turn) at me, and be shamam (astonished). Shawam (place / establish / appoint) your yad (hand) on your pah (mouth).
When I zakar (remember), I am bahal (troubled). Palatzawath (horror) achaz (takes) hold of my bashar (flesh).
"Why do the rashai (wicked) chayah (live), ithaq (become) old, yes, and grow gabar (mighty) in chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor)?
Their zarai (child) is kawan (established) with them in their panayam (face), their tzaatzaa (offspring) before their iyan (eye).
Their bayath (house) are shalawam (peace / safety) from pachad (fear / dread), neither is the shabat (rod) of Alawah upon them.
Their shawar (bulls) breed without gail (fail). Their parah (cows) palat (calve), and don't shakal (miscarry).
They shalach (send) forth their iwayal (little) ones like a tzaan (flock). Their yalad (birth / begot) raqad (dance).
They sing to the tambourine and kanawar (harp), and shamach (rejoice) at the qawal (sound / voice) of the pipe.
They balah (spend) their yawam (day) in tawab (good / proper function). In an ragai (in an instance) they nachath (go) down to shaawal (Sheol / afterlife).
They amar (spoke) Al, ‘sawar (depart) from us, for we don't want to daith (know) about your darak (ways).
What is the Shaday, that we should ibad (servant) him? What yail (profit) should we have, if we pagai (pray) to him?'
Behold, their prosperity is not in their yad (hand). The itzah (counsel) of the rashai (wicked) is rachaq (far) from me.

"How often is it that the nayar (lamp) of the rashai (wicked) is daik (put) out, that their ayad (calamity) bawaa (come) on them, that Alahayam distributes chabalayam (sorrows) in his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting)?
How often is it that they are as thaban (stubble) panayam (face) the rawach (spirit / wind), as matz (chaff) that the sawapah (storm) ganab (carries) away?
You say, ‘Alawah tzapan (lays) up his awan (iniquity) for his ban (son).' Let him shalam (recompense) it to himself, that he may yadai (know) it.
Let his own iyan (eye) raah (see) his kayad (destruction). Let him shathah (drinks) of the chamah (wrath) of the Shaday.
For what does he care for his bayath (house) achar (other) him, when the masapar (number) of his chadash (month) is chatzatz (cut) off?
"Shall any lamad (teach / instruct) Al daith (knowledge), since he shapat (judge / judgement) those who are rawam (will lift up)?
One mawath (death) in his tham (full) itzam (strength), shalaanan (being) wholly at ease and shalaw (quiet).
His pails are malaa (full) of chalab (milk). The mach (marrow) of his itzam (bones) is shaqah (moistened).
Another mawath (death) in bitterness of napash (soul), and never tastes of tawab (good / proper function).
They shakab (lie) down yachad (alike) in the ipar (dust). The ramah (worm) kasah (covers) them.
"Behold, I yadai (know) your machashabah (thoughts), the mazamawath (devices) with which you would chamas (wrong) me.
For you amar (spoke), ‘Where is the bayath (house) of the nadayab (prince)? Where is the mashakan (tent) in which the rashai (wicked) lived?'
Haven't you shaal (asked) wayfaring iwabaray (men)? Don't you nakar (know) their evidences,
That the rai (evil) man is chashak (darkness) to the yawam (day) of ayad (calamity), That they are yabal (led) forth to the yawam (day) of ibarah (wrath)?
Who shall nagad (declare) his darak (way) to his panayam (face)? Who shall shalam (repay) him what he ishah (make) done?
Yet he will be borne to the qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher). Men shall keep shaqad (watch) over the gadayash (tomb).
The ragabay (clods) of the nachal (stream / river) shall be mathaq (sweet) to him. All adam (men) shall mashak (draw) achar (other) him, as there were innumerable panayam (face) him.
So how can you nacham (turn away / repent) me with nonsense, because in your thashawabah (answers) there shaar (remains) only mail (top/above)?"
Then Alayapaz (Eliphaz) the thayamanay (temanite) inah (answer / respond),
"Can a gabar (man) be sakan (profitable) to Al? Kay (surely) he who is shakal (wise) is sakan (profitable) to himself.
