Is it any chapatz (pleasure) to the Shaday, that you are tzadaq (righteous / just / fair)? Or does it benefit him, that you make your darak (ways) thamam (perfect)?
Is it for your piety that he yakach (reproves) you, that he bawaa (come) with you into mashapat (judgment)?
Isn't your rai (wickedness) rab (great)? Neither is there any qatz (end) to your iwan (guilt/iniquity).
For you have taken chabal (pledges) from your ach (brother/kinsman) for chanam (nothing), and pashat (stripped) the irawam (naked) of their bagad (clothing).
You haven't given mayam (Waters) to the iyap (weary) to shaqah (drink), and you have withheld lacham (bread) from the raib (hungry).
But as for the zarawai (mighty) ayash (man / husband), he had the aratz (Earth/land). The nashaa (lift) man, he lived in it.
You have shalach (send) alamanawath (widows) away rayaqam (empty), and the zaraiwath (arms) of the yathawam (fatherless) have been dakaa (broken).
Therefore pachayam (snares) are around you. Pathaawam (sudden) pachad (fear / dread) bahal (troubles) you,
Or chashak (darkness), so that you can not raah (see), and floods of mayam (Waters) kasah (cover) you.
"Isn't Alawah in the gabah (heights) of shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens)? Raah (see) the gabah (height) of the kawakabayam (stars), how rawam (will lift up) they are!
You amar (spoke), ‘What does Al yadai (know)? Can he shapat (judge / judgement) through the irapal (thick) darkness?
Ib (thick) clouds are a sathar (secret / hidden) to him, so that he doesn't raah (see). He halak (move) on the vault of the sky.'
Will you shamar (keep/guard) the iwalam (forever) arach (way), which awan (wicked) mathay (men) have darak (trodden),
Who were snatched away before their ith (time), whose yasawad (foundation) was yatzaq (poured) out as a stream,
Who amar (spoke) to Al, ‘sawar (depart) from us;' and, ‘What can the Shaday pail (do) for us?'
Yet he malaa (filled) their bayath (house) with tawab (good / proper function) things, but the itzah (counsel) of the rashai (wicked) is rachaq (far) from me.
The tzadayaq (righteous) raah (see) it, and are shamach (glad). The naqay (innocent) ridicule them,
Saying, ‘am (mother) those who rose up against us are kachad (cut) off. The ash (fire) has akal (eat) their yathar (remnant).'
"Sakan (acquaint) yourself with him, now, and be at shalam (peace). Thereby tawab (good / proper function) shall bawaa (come) to you.
Please laqach (take / seize) instruction from his pah (mouth), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) up his amar (spoke) in your labab (heart).
If you shawab (turn back / repent) to the Shaday, you shall be banah (build) up, if you rachaq (put) away iwal (unrighteousness) rachaq (far) from your ahal (tents).
Shayath (put / appoint / make) your treasure in the ipar (dust), the gold of Awapayar (Ophir) among the tzawar (stones) of the nachalayam (brooks).
The Shaday will be your treasure, and precious kasap (silver) to you.
For then you will inag (delight) yourself in the Shaday, and shall nashaa (lift) up your panayam (face) to Alawah.
You shall make your ithar (prayer) to him, and he will shamai (hearken / hear) you. You shall shalam (pay) your nadar (vow).
You shall also gazar (decree) a thing, and it shall be qawam (rise up) to you. Awar (light) shall nagah (shine) on your darak (ways).
When they shapal (cast) down, you shall amar (spoke), ‘be lifted up.' He will yashai (salvation) the shach (humble) person.
He will even malat (deliver) him who is not naqay (innocent). Yes, he shall be malat (delivered) through the bar (cleanness) of your kap (hands)."
Then Ayawab (Job) inah (answer / respond),
"Even today my shayach (complaint) is rebellious. His yad (hand) is kabad (heavy) in spite of my anachah (groaning).
Oh that I yadai (knew) where I might matzaa (find) him! That I might bawaa (come) even to his thakawanah (seat)!
I would set my cause in irak (order) panayam (face) him, and malaa (fill) my pah (mouth) with thawakachawath (arguments).
I would yadai (know) the malayam (words) which he would inah (answer / respond) me, and bayan (between) what he would amar (spoke) me.
Would he rayab (contend) with me in the greatness of his kach (strength / mighty / power)? No, but he would listen to me.
There the yashar (upright) might yakach (reason) with him, so I should be palat (delivered) natzach (forever) from my shapat (judge / judgement).
"If I halak (move) qadam (east), he is not there; if west, I can't find him;
He ishah (make) to the north, but I can't chazah (see) him. He itap (turns) yamayan (right hand), but I can't catch a glimpse of him.
But he yadai (knows) the darak (way) that I imad (take). When he has bachan (tried) me, I shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth like zahab (gold).
My ragal (feet / foot) achaz (has) held fast to his ashar (who/that). I have shamar (keep/guard) his darak (way), and not natah (turned) aside.
I haven't mawash (gone) back from the matzawah (commandment) of his shapah (lips). I have treasured up the amaray (words) of his pah (mouth) more than my chaq (statute) food.
But he stands achad (one), and who can oppose him? What his napash (soul) awah (desires), even that he ishah (make).
For he shalam (performs) that which is chaq (statute) for me. Many such things are with him.
Therefore I am terrified at his panayam (face). When I bayan (between), I am pachad (fear / dread) of him.
For Al has made my lab (heart) rakak (faint). The Shaday has terrified me.
Because I was not tzamath (cut) off panayam (face) the chashak (darkness), neither did he kasah (cover) the thick apal (darkness) from my panayam (face).
"Why aren't ithayam (times) tzapan (laid) up by the Shaday? Why don't those who yadai (know) him chazah (see) his yawam (day)?
There are people who nashag (remove) the gabalawath (landmarks). They violently gazal (take) away idar (flocks), and raih (feed) them.
They nahag (drive) away the donkey of the yathawam (fatherless), and they take the alamanah (widow's) shawar (ox) for a chabal (pledge).
They natah (turn) the abayawan (needy) out of the darak (way). The abayawan (poor) of the aratz (Earth/land) yachad (all) chabaa (hide) themselves.

Behold, as paraa (wild) donkeys in the madabar (desert), they yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to their pail (work), shachar (seeking) diligently for food. The irabah (wilderness) yields them lacham (bread) for their nairayam (children).
They qatzar (cut) their balayal (provender) in the shadah (field). They glean the karam (vineyard) of the rashai (wicked).
They lie all lawan (night) irawam (naked) without labawash (clothing), and have no kasawath (covering) in the qarah (cold).
They are ratab (wet) with the zaram (showers) of the harayam (mountains), and chabaq (embrace) the tzawar (rock) for lack of a machasah (shelter).
There are those who gazal (pluck) the yathawam (fatherless) from the shad (breast), and take a chabal (pledge) of the inay (poor),
So that they halak (move) around irawam (naked) without labawash (clothing). Being raib (hungry), they nashaa (lift) the sheaves.
They make tzahar (oil) bayan (between) the shawar (walls) of these men. They darak (tread) yaqab (wine) presses, and tzamaa (suffer) thirst.

From out of the populous iyar (city), mathayam (men) naaq (groan). The napash (soul) of the chalal (wounded) shawai (cries) out, yet Alawah doesn't shawam (place / establish / appoint) the thapalah (folly).
"These are of those who marad (rebel) against the awar (light). They don't nakar (know) its darak (ways), nor stay in its nathayab (paths).
The ratzach (murderer) qawam (rise up) with the awar (light). He qatal (kills) the inay (poor) and inay (needy). In the layal (night) he is like a ganab (thief).
The iyan (eye) also of the naap (adulterer) shamar (keep/guard) for the nashap (twilight), amar (spoke), ‘No iyan (eye) shall shawar (see) me.' He sathar (secret / hidden) his panayam (face).
In the chashak (darkness) they chathar (dig) through bathayam (houses). They shut themselves up in the yawamam (by day). They don't yadai (know) the awar (light).
For the baqar (morning) is to yachad (all) of them like thick tzalamawath (darkness), for they nakar (know) the balahawath (terrors) of the thick tzalamawath (darkness).
"They are foam on the surface of the panay (waters). Their chalaqah (portion) is qalal (cursed) in the aratz (Earth/land). They don't panah (turn) into the darak (way) of the karamayam (vineyards).
Tzayah (drought) and cham (heat) gazal (consume) the shalag (snow) mayamay (waters), so does shaawal (Sheol / afterlife) those who have chataa (sinned).

The racham (womb) shall shakach (forget) him. The ramah (worm) shall mathaq (feed) sweetly on him. He shall be no more zakar (remember). Iwal (unrighteousness) shall be shabar (broken) as a itz (tree).
He raih (devours) the iqar (barren) who don't yalad (birth / begot). He shows no yatab (kindness) to the alamanah (widow).
Yet Alahayam preserves the abayar (mighty) by his kach (strength / mighty / power). He qawam (rise up) up who has no aman (believe / have faith) of chay (life).
Alahayam gives them security, and they shain (rest) in it. His iyan (eye) are on their darak (ways).

They are ramam (exalted); yet a mait (little) while, and they are gone. Yes, they are makak (brought) low, they are qapatz (taken) out of the qapatz (way) as all others, and are namal (cut) off as the raash (head) of the shabal (ears) of grain.
If it isn't so apaw (now), who will prove me a kazab (liar), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) my speech worth al (not)?"
Then Baladad (Bildad) the shawachay (shuhite) inah (answer / respond),
"Mashal (rule/have dominion) and pachad (fear / dread) are with him. He ishah (make) shalawam (peace / safety) in his marawam (high) places.
Can his gadawad (armies) be counted? On whom does his awar (light) not qawam (rise up)?
How then can anawash (man) be tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) with Al? Or how can he who is yalad (birth / begot) of a ayashah (woman / wife) be zakah (clean)?
Behold, even the yarach (moon) has no brightness, and the kawakabayam (stars) are not zakak (pure) in his iyan (eye);
How much less anawash (man), who is a ramah (worm), the ban (son) of adam (man), who is a thawalai (worm)!"
Then Ayawab (Job) inah (answer / respond),
"How have you izar (helped) him who is without kach (strength / mighty / power)! How have you yashai (salvation) the zarawai (arm) that has no iz (strength / might / refuge)!
How have you counseled him who has no chakamah (wisdom), and rab (plentifully) yadai (declared) sound thawashayah (knowledge)!
To whom have you nagad (uttered) malayan (words)? Whose nashamah (breathing thing) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from you?
"Those who are rapaa (deceased) chawal (tremble), those beneath the mayam (Waters) and all that live in them.
Shaawal (Sheol / afterlife) is irawam (naked) before Alahayam, and Abaddon has no kasawath (covering).
He stretches out the tzapawan (north) over thahaw (formless) space, and thalah (hangs) the aratz (Earth/land) on balayamah (nothing).
He tzarar (binds) up the mayam (Waters) in his ib (thick) clouds, and the inan (cloud) is not baqai (burst) under them.
He encloses the panayam (face) of his kasaa (throne), and parashaz (spreads) his inan (cloud) on it.
He has described a boundary on the surface of the panay (waters), and to the confines of awar (light) and chashak (darkness).
The imawaday (pillars) of shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) rawap (tremble) and are thamah (astonished) at his gairah (rebuke).
He stirs up the yam (sea/waters) with his kach (strength / mighty / power), and by his thabawan (understanding) he machatz (crush / shatter) through rahab (rahab).
By his rawach (spirit / wind) the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) are shaparah (garnished). His yad (hand) has pierced the swift nachash (serpent).
Behold, these are but the outskirts of his darak (ways). How small a whisper do we shamai (hearken / hear) of him! But the raim (thunder) of his gabawarah (power) who can bayan (between)?"
Ayawab (Job) again took up his mashal (parable), and amar (spoke),
"As Al chay (life), who has sawar (taken) away my mashapat (right), the Shaday, who has made my napash (soul) marar (bitter).
(For the length of my nashamah (breathing thing) is still in me, and the rawach (spirit / wind) of Alawah is in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting));
Surely my shapah (lips) shall not dabar (word / matter) iwal (unrighteousness), neither shall my lashawan (tongue / language) hagah (utter) ramayah (deceit).
Chalayalah (far) be it from me that I should justify you. Until I gawai (die) I will not sawar (put) away my thamah (integrity) from me.
I chazaq (hold) fast to my tzadaqah (righteousness), and will not rapah (let) it go. My labab (heart) shall not charap (reproach) me so yawam (day) as I live.
"Let my ayab (enemy) be as the rashai (wicked). Let him who qawam (rise up) up against me be as the iwal (unrighteous).
For what is the thaqawah (hope) of the godless, when he is batzai (cut) off, when Alawah shalah (takes) away his napash (soul)?
Will Al shamai (hearken / hear) his tzaiqah (cry) when tzarah (trouble) bawaa (come) on him?
Will he inag (delight) himself in the Shaday, and qaraa (called) on Alawah at all ith (times)?
I will yarah (teach) you about the yad (hand) of Al. That which is with the Shaday will I not kachad (conceal).
Chazah (behold), all of you have seen it yourselves; why then have you become habal (altogether) habal (vain)?
"This is the chalaq (portion) of a rashai (wicked) adam (man) with Al, the nachalah (heritage) of irayatzayam (oppressors), which they laqach (take / seize) from the Shaday.
If his ban (son) are rabah (multiplied), it is for the charab (sword). His tzaatzaa (offspring) shall not be shabai (satisfied) with lacham (bread).
Those who sharayad (remain) of him shall be qabar (bury) in mawath (death). His alamanah (widows) shall bakah (make) no lamentation.
Though he tzabar (heap) up kasap (silver) as the ipar (dust), and kawan (prepare) clothing as the chamar (clay);
He may kawan (prepare) it, but the tzadayaq (righteous) shall labash (put) it on, and the naqay (innocent) shall chalaq (divide) the kasap (silver).
He banah (build) his bayath (house) as the ish (made), as a sakah (booth) which the natzar (watchman) ishah (make).
He shakab (lies) down ishayar (rich), but he shall not do so again. He paqach (opens) his iyan (eye), and he is not.
Balahawath (terrors) nashag (overtake) him like mayam (Waters). A sawapah (storm) ganab (steals) him away in the layal (night).
The qadayam (east) wind nashaa (lift) him away, and he departs. It sweeps him out of his maqawam (place).
For it shalak (hurls) at him, and does not chamal (spare), as he barach (flees) away from his yad (hand).
Men shall sapaq (clap) their kap (hands) at him, and shall sharaq (hiss) him out of his maqawam (place).
"Surely there is a mine for kasap (silver), and a maqawam (place) for zahab (gold) which they zaqaq (refine).
Barazal (iron) is laqach (take / seize) out of the ipar (earth), and copper is smelted out of the ore.
Man shawam (place / establish / appoint) an qatz (end) to chashak (darkness), and searches out, to the furthest bound, the aban (stone) of apal (obscurity) and of thick tzalamawath (darkness).
He paratz (breaks) open a shaft away from where gawar (people) live. They are shakach (forgotten) by the ragal (feet / foot). They hang far from anawash (men), they swing back and forth.
As for the aratz (Earth/land), out of it yatzaa (go out / come out) lacham (bread); Underneath it is hapak (turned) up as it were by ash (fire).
Sapayar (sapphires) come from its rocks. It has ipar (dust) of zahab (gold).
That nathayab (path) no iyat (bird) of prey yadai (knows), neither has the falcon's iyan (eye) shazap (seen) it.
The proud animals have not darak (trodden) it, nor has the fierce shachal (lion) idah (passed) by there.
He shalach (send) forth his yad (hand) on the chalamayash (flinty) rock, and he overturns the harayam (mountains) by the sharash (roots).
He baqai (cuts) out channels among the tzawarawath (rocks). His iyan (eye) raah (see) every yaqar (precious) thing.
He chabash (binds) the streams that they don't trickle. The thing that is thailamah (hidden) he yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to awar (light).
"But ayan (NO ONE) shall chakamah (wisdom) be matzaa (found)? Where is the maqawam (place) of bayanah (understanding)?
Anawash (man) doesn't yadai (know) its irak (price); Neither is it matzaa (found) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life).
The thahawam (depths) amar (spoke), ‘It isn't in me.' The yam (sea/waters) amar (spoke), ‘It isn't with me.'
It can't be nathan (give) for sagawar (gold), neither shall kasap (silver) be shaqal (weighed) for its machayar (price).
It can't be salah (valued) with the katham (gold) of Awapayar (Ophir), with the yaqar (precious) shaham (Onyx), or the sapayar (sapphire).
Zahab (gold) and glass can't irak (equal) it, neither shall it be thamawarah (exchanged) for kalay (jewels) of paz (fine) gold.
No zakar (remember) shall be made of raamah (coral) or of crystal. Yes, the mashak (price) of chakamah (wisdom) is above panayanayam (rubies).
The patadah (topaz) of Kawash (Ethiopia) shall not irak (equal) it, Neither shall it be salah (valued) with tahawar (pure) katham (gold).
Ayan (NO ONE) then does chakamah (wisdom) bawaa (come) from? Where is the maqawam (place) of bayanah (understanding)?
Seeing it is ilam (hidden) from the iyanay (eyes) of all chay (life), and sathar (kept) close from the iwap (flying) of the sky.
Abadawan (destruction) and mawath (death) amar (spoke), ‘We have shamai (hearken / hear) a rumor of it with our azan (ear).'
"Alahayam bayan (between) its darak (way), and he yadai (knows) its maqawam (place).
For he nabat (looks) to the ends of the aratz (Earth/land), and raah (see) under the whole sky.
He establishes the force of the rawach (spirit / wind). Yes, he measures out the mayam (Waters) by madah (measure).
When he ishah (make) a chaq (statute) for the matar (rain), and a darak (way) for the chazayaz (lightning) of the qawal (sound / voice);
Then he raah (see) it, and sapar (book) it. He kawan (established) it, yes, and chaqar (searched) it out.
To adam (man) he amar (spoke), ‘Behold, the yaraah (fear) of the Adanay, that is chakamah (wisdom). To sawar (depart) from rai (evil) is bayanah (understanding).'"
Ayawab (Job) again took up his mashal (parable), and amar (spoke),
"Oh that I were as in the yarachay (months) of qadam (old), as in the yamay (days) when Alawah shamar (keep/guard) over me;
When his nayar (lamp) halal (praise) on my raash (head), and by his awar (light) I yalak (walked) through chashak (darkness),
As I was in the ripeness of my yamay (days), when the friendship of Alawah was in my ahal (tent),
When the Shaday was yet with me, and my nair (children) were around me,
When my halayak (steps) were rachatz (washed) with chamaah (butter), and the tzawar (rock) tzawaq (poured) out palagay (streams) of shaman (oil) for me,
When I yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to the qarath (city) shair (gate), when I kawan (prepared) my mawashab (seat) in the rachab (street).
The nair (young) men raah (see) me and chabaa (hid) themselves. The yashayash (aged) qawam (rise up) up and imad (stood).
The sharayam (princes) itzar (refrained) from malah (talking), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) their kap (hand) on their pah (mouth).
The chabaa (voice) of the nagayadayam (nobles) was hushed, and their lashawan (tongue / language) dabaq (stuck) to the roof of their chak (mouth).
For when the azan (ear) shamai (hearken / hear) me, then it ashar (who/that) me; and when the iyan (eye) raah (see) me, it commended me:
Because I malat (delivered) the inay (poor) who shawai (cried), and the yathawam (fatherless) also, who had none to izar (help) him,
The barakah (blessing) of him who was ready to abad (destroy / perish) bawaa (come) on me, and I caused the alamanah (widow's) lab (heart) to ranan (sing) for joy.
I labash (put) on tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and it labash (clothed) me. My mashapat (justice) was as a maiyal (robe) and a tzanayap (diadem).
I was iyanayam (eyes) to the iwar (blind), and ragalayam (feet) to the pasach (lame).
I was a ab (father) to the abayawan (needy). The rayab (cause) of him who I didn't yadai (know), I chaqar (searched) out.
I shabar (broke) the mathalaiwath (jaws) of the iwal (unrighteous), and shalak (plucked) the tarap (prey) out of his shan (teeth).
Then I amar (spoke), ‘I shall gawai (die) in my own qan (house), I shall number my yamayam (days) as the chawal (sand).
My sharash (root) is spread out to the mayam (Waters). The tal (dew) lies all lawan (night) on my qatzayar (branch).
My kabawad (glory) is chadash (fresh) in me. My qashath (bow) is chalap (renewed) in my yad (hand).'
"Men listened to me, yachal (waited), and damam (kept) silence for my itzah (counsel).
Achar (other) my dabar (word / matter) they didn't shanah (speak) again. My speech fell on them.
They yachal (waited) for me as for the matar (rain). Their pah (mouths) drank as with the spring malaqawash (rain).
I smiled on them when they had no confidence. They didn't reject the awar (light) of my panayam (face).
I bachar (chose) out their darak (way), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) as raash (head). I lived as a malak (king) in the gadawad (army), as one who nacham (turn away / repent) the mourners.
"But now those who are younger than I shachaq (have) me in derision, whose ab (father) I would have maas (disdained) to shayath (put / appoint / make) with my tzaan (sheep) kalabay (dogs).
Of mah (what) use is the kach (strength / mighty / power) of their yad (hand) to me, men in whom ripe kalach (age) abad (destroy / perish) perished?
They are gaunt from lack and kapan (famine). They gnaw the tzayah (dry) ground, in the gloom of mashawaah (waste) and shawaa (vanity).
They qatap (pluck) salt herbs by the bushes. The sharash (roots) of the broom are their lacham (food).
They are garash (driven) out from the midst of men. They rawai (cry) after them as after a ganab (thief);
So that they shakan (place) in frightful nachalayam (valleys), and in charay (holes) of the ipar (earth) and of the kapayam (rocks).
Among the bushes they nahaq (bray); and under the charawal (nettles) they are sapach (gathered) together.
They are banay (children) of nabal (fools), yes, banay (children) of sham (name) men. They were flogged out of the aratz (Earth/land).
"Now I have become their nagayanah (song). Yes, I am a malah (byword) to them.
They thaib (abhor) me, they stand aloof from me, and don't hesitate to raq (concept: what comes out / spittle) in my panayam (face).
For he pathach (has) untied his yathar (cord), and inah (oppress / afflict) me; and they have thrown off restraint panayam (face) me.
On my yamayan (right hand) hand qawam (rise up) the rabble. They thrust aside my ragal (feet / foot), They salal (cast) up against me their arachawath (ways) of ayad (destruction).
They nathas (mar) my nathayab (path), They yail (set) forward my hawah (calamity / destruction), without anyone's izar (help).
As through a rachab (wide) paratz (breach) they athah (you (masc)), in the midst of the ruin they galal (roll) themselves in.
Balahawath (terrors) have hapak (turned) on me. They radap (chase) my honor as the rawach (spirit / wind). My yashawaih (salvation) ibar (pass over/through) passed away as a ib (cloud).
"Now my napash (soul) is shapak (poured) out within me. Yamay (days) of inay (affliction) achaz (have) taken hold on me.
In the layal (night) season my itzam (bones) are naqar (pierced) in me, and the pains that gnaw me take no shakab (rest).
By rab (great) kach (strength / mighty / power) is my labawash (garment) disfigured. It azar (binds) me about as the pah (collar) of my kathanath (coat).
He has yarah (cast) me into the chamar (mire). I have mashal (speak in proverb/parable) like ipar (dust) and ashes.
I shawai (cry) to you, and you do not inah (answer / respond) me. I imad (stand) up, and you gaze at me.
You have hapak (turned) to be akazar (cruel) to me. With the itzam (might) of your yad (hand) you persecute me.
You nashaa (lift) me up to the rawach (spirit / wind), and drive me with it. You mawag (dissolve) me in the storm.
For I yadai (know) that you will shawab (turn back / repent) me to mawath (death), To the bayath (house) mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) for all chay (life).
"However doesn't one shalach (send) out a yad (hand) in his fall? Or in his calamity therefore shawai (cry) for help?
Didn't I bakah (weep) for him who was in qashah (rough / hard)? Wasn't my napash (soul) igam (grieved) for the abayawan (needy)?
When I qawah (gather/wait) for tawab (good / proper function), then rai (evil) bawaa (come); When I yachal (waited) for awar (light), there bawaa (come) apal (darkness).
My maih (heart) is troubled, and doesn't damam (rest). Yamay (days) of inay (affliction) have qadam (come) on me.
I halak (move) qadar (mourning) without the chamah (sun). I qawam (rise up) up in the qahal (assembly), and shawai (cry) for help.
I am a ach (brother/kinsman) to jackals, and a rai (neigbor/another person) to ostriches.
My iwar (skin) grows shachar (black) and peels from me. My itzam (bones) are charar (burned) with charab (heat).
Therefore my kanawar (harp) has turned to abal (mourning), and my pipe into the qawal (sound / voice) of those who bakah (weep).
"I karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with my iyan (eye), how then should I bayan (between) lustfully at a young bathawalah (woman)?
For what is the chalaq (portion) from Alawah mail (top/above), and the nachalah (heritage) from the Shaday on marawam (high)?
Is it not ayad (calamity) to the iwal (unrighteous), and disaster to the pailay (workers) of awan (iniquity)?
Doesn't he raah (see) my darak (ways), and sapar (book) all my tzaid (steps)?
"If I have halak (move) with falsehood, and my ragal (feet / foot) has hurried to maramah (deceit)
(Let me be shaqal (weighed) in an even maazan (balance), that Alawah may yadai (know) my thamah (integrity));
If my ashar (who/that) has natah (turned) out of the darak (way), if my lab (heart) halak (move) achar (other) my iyan (eye), if any defilement has dabaq (stuck) to my kap (hands),
Then let me zarai (sow), and let achar (other) akal (eat). Yes, let the produce of my field be sharash (rooted) out.
"If my lab (heart) has been pathah (enticed) to a ayashah (woman / wife), and I have arab (laid) wait at my neighbor's pathach (door),
Then let my ayashah (woman / wife) tachan (grind) for achar (other), and let others sleep with her.
For that would be a zamah (heinous) crime. Yes, it would be an iwan (guilt/iniquity) to be punished by the palayalayam (judges):
For it is a ash (fire) that akal (eat) to abadawan (destruction), and would sharash (root) out all my thabawaah (increase).
"If I have maas (despised) the cause of my male amah (servant) or of my female servant, when they rayab (contended) with me;
What then shall I ishah (make) when Al qawam (rise up) up? When he paqad (visit), what shall I shawab (turn back / repent) him?
Didn't he who ishah (make) me in the batan (womb) ishah (make) him? Didn't achad (one) kawan (fashion) us in the racham (womb)?
"If I have withheld the dal (poor) from their chapatz (desire), or have caused the iyanay (eyes) of the alamanah (widow) to kalah (complete / finish),
Or have akal (eat) my path (morsel) alone, and the yathawam (fatherless) has not akal (eat) of it
(No, from my naiwar (youth) he gadal (grew) up with me as with a ab (father), her have I nachah (guided) from my am (mother) batan (womb));
If I raah (see) seen any abad (destroy / perish) for want of labawash (clothing), or that the abayawan (needy) had no kasawath (covering);
If his chalatz (heart) hasn't barak (blessed) me, if he hasn't been chamam (warmed) with my kabash (sheep's) gaz (fleece);
If I have nawap (lifted) up my yad (hand) against the yathawam (fatherless), because I raah (see) my izarah (help) in the shair (gate),
Then napal (fall / be cast down) my shoulder fall from the shakamah (shoulder) blade, and my azarawai (arm) be shabar (broken) from the qanah (bone).
For ayad (calamity) from Al is a pachad (fear / dread) to me. Because his majesty, I yakal (can) do nothing.
"If I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) zahab (gold) my kasal (hope), and have amar (spoke) to the katham (fine) gold, ‘You are my mabatach (confidence);'
If I shamach (have) rejoiced because my wealth was rab (great), and because my yad (hand) matzaa (had) gotten much;
If I raah (see) seen the awar (light) when it shined, or the yarach (moon) halak (move) in splendor,
And my lab (heart) has been secretly pathah (enticed), and my yad (hand) threw a nashaq (kiss) from my pah (mouth),
This also would be an iwan (guilt/iniquity) to be punished by the palayalay (judges); for I should have kachash (denied) the Al who is mail (top/above).
"If I shamach (have) rejoiced at the payad (destruction) of him who shanaa (hate) me, or iwar (rouse / awaken) up myself when rai (evil) matzaa (found) him;
(Yes, I nathan (give) not allowed my chak (mouth) to chataa (sin) by shaal (asking) his napash (soul) with a alah (curse / oath));
If the mathay (men) of my ahal (tent) have not amar (spoke), ‘Who can find one who shabai (has) not been filled with his meat?'
(The foreigner has not lawan (lodged) in the chawatz (street), but I pathach (have) opened my dalath (doors) to the traveler);
If like Adam (Adam) I have kasah (covered) my pashai (transgressions), by taman (hiding) my iwan (guilt/iniquity) in my chab (heart),

Because I iratz (feared) the rab (great) hamawan (multitude), and the bawaz (contempt) of mashapachawath (families) chathath (terrified) me, so that I damam (kept) silence, and didn't yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the pathach (door)—
Oh that I had one to shamai (hearken / hear) me! (Behold, here is my signature, let the Shaday inah (answer / respond) me); let the accuser kathab (write) my indictment!
Surely I would nashaa (lift) it on my shakam (shoulder); and I would inad (bind) it to me as a itarah (crown).
I would nagad (declare) to him the masapar (number) of my tzaid (steps). As a nagayad (prince) would I qarab (come close) near to him.
If my adamah (land) zaiq (cries) out against me, and its thalam (furrows) bakah (weep) together;
If I have akal (eat) its kach (strength / mighty / power) without kasap (money), or bail (have) caused its owners to napach (lose) their napash (soul),
Let briars yatzaa (go out / come out) instead of chatah (wheat), and stinkweed instead of shairah (barley)." The dabaray (words) of Ayawab (Job) are thamam (ended).
So these shalawash (three) anashayam (men) shabath (shabath / rest) to inah (answer / respond) Ayawab (Job), because he was tzadayaq (righteous) in his own iyan (eye).

Then the ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Alayahaw (Elihu) the ban (son) of Barakaal (Barachel), the bawazay (buzite), of the mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) of Ram (Ram), was charah (hot with anger) against Ayawab (Job). His ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger) because he justified himself rather than Alahayam.

Also his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger) against his shalawash (three) rai (neigbor/another person), because they matzaa (had) found no mainah (answer), and yet had rashai (condemned) Ayawab (Job).
Now Alayahaw (Elihu) had chakah (waited) to dabar (word / matter) to Ayawab (Job), because they were zaqan (elder) than he.

When Alayahaw (Elihu) raah (see) that there was no mainah (answer) in the pah (mouth) of these shalawash (three) anashayam (men), his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) was charah (hot with anger).

Alayahaw (Elihu) the ban (son) of Barakaal (Barachel) the bawazay (buzite) inah (answer / respond), "I am tzaiyar (young), and you are very yashayash (old); Therefore I held back, and didn't dare chawah (show) you my dai (opinion).
I amar (spoke), ‘yamayam (days) should dabar (word / matter), and rab (multitude) of shanayam (years) should yadai (teach) chakamah (wisdom).'
But there is a rawach (spirit / wind) in anawash (man), and the nashamah (breathing thing) of the Shaday gives them bayan (between).
It is not the rab (great) who are chakam (wise), nor the zaqan (aged) who bayan (between) mashapat (justice).
Therefore I amar (spoke), ‘shamai (hearken / hear) to me; I also will chawah (show) my dai (opinion).'
"Behold, I yachal (waited) for your dabar (word / matter), and I listened for your thabawan (reasoning), while you chaqar (searched) out what to malah (say).
Yes, I bayan (between) you my full attention, but there was no one who yakach (convinced) Ayawab (Job), or who inah (answer / respond) his amar (spoke), among you.
Beware lest you amar (spoke), ‘We matzaa (have) found chakamah (wisdom), Al may refute him, not ayash (man / husband);'
For he has not irak (directed) his malayan (words) against me; neither will I shawab (turn back / repent) him with your speeches.
"They are chathath (amazed). They inah (answer / respond) no more. They don't have a malah (word) to say.
Shall I yachal (wait), because they don't dabar (word / matter), because they imad (stand) still, and inah (answer / respond) no more?
I also will inah (answer / respond) my chalaq (part), and I also will chawah (show) my dai (opinion).
For I am malaa (full) of malayam (words). The rawach (spirit / wind) batan (within) me tzawaq (constrains) me.
Behold, my breast is as yayan (wine) which pathach (has) no vent; like chadash (new) wineskins it is baqai (ready) to burst.
I will dabar (word / matter), that I may be rawach (spirit / wind). I will pathach (open) my shapah (lips) and inah (answer / respond).
Please don't let me nashaa (lift) any ayash (man / husband) panayam (face), neither will I kanah (give) flattering titles to any adam (man).
For I don't yadai (know) how to kanah (give) flattering titles; or else my Maker would mait (soon) nashaa (lift) me away.
"However, Ayawab (Job), please shamai (hearken / hear) my speech, and shamai (hearken / hear) to all my dabar (word / matter).
See now, I pathach (have) opened my pah (mouth). My lashawan (tongue / language) has dabar (word / matter) in my chak (mouth).
My amar (spoke) shall utter the yashar (upright) of my lab (heart). That which my shapah (lips) daith (know) they shall malal (speak) sincerely.
The rawach (spirit / wind) of Al ishah (make) made me, and the nashamah (breathing thing) of the Shaday gives me chayah (life).
If you yakal (can), shawab (turn back / repent) me. Irak (set) your words in order panayam (face) me, and yatzab (stand) forth.
Behold, I am toward Al even as you are. I am also qaratz (formed) out of the chamar (clay).
Behold, my ayamah (terror) shall not make you baith (afraid), neither shall my pressure be kabad (heavy) on you.
"Surely you have amar (spoke) in my azan (ear), I have shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of your malayan (words), saying,
‘I am zak (clean), without disobedience. I am chap (innocent), neither is there iwan (guilt/iniquity) in me.
Behold, he matzaa (finds) thanawaawath (occasions) against me. He chashab (counts) me for his ayab (enemy).
He shawam (place / establish / appoint) my ragal (feet / foot) in the sad (stocks). He shamar (keep/guard) all my arach (paths).'
"Behold, I will inah (answer / respond) you. In this you are not tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), for Alawah is rabah (greater) than anawash (man).
Why do you rayab (strive) against him, because he doesn't inah (answer / respond) account of any of his dabar (word / matter)?
For Al dabar (word / matter) achad (one), yes shanayam (two), though shawar (man) pays no attention.
In a chalawam (dream), in a chazayawan (vision) of the layal (night), when tharadamah (deep) sleep napal (fall / be cast down) on anashayam (men), in thanawamah (slumbering) on the mashakab (bed);
Then he galah (opens) the azan (ear) of anashayam (men), and chatham (seals) their masar (instruction),
That he may sawar (withdraw) adam (man) from his purpose, and kasah (hide) gawah (pride) from gabar (man).
He chashak (darkness) back his napash (soul) from the shachath (pit), and his chay (life) from ibar (pass over/through) by the shalach (sword).
He is yakach (chastened) also with makaab (pain) on his mashakab (bed), with continual strife in his itzam (bones);
So that his chay (life) zaham (abhors) lacham (bread), and his napash (soul) thaawah (dainty) maakal (food).
His bashar (flesh) is so kalah (complete / finish) away, that it can't be raay (seen). His itzam (bones) that were not raah (see) shapay (stick) out.
Yes, his napash (soul) qarab (come close) near to the shachath (pit), and his chay (life) to the mamathayam (destroyers).
"If there is beside him an malaak (angel / messenger of Yah), an lawatz (interpreter), achad (one) among a alap (thousand), to show to adam (man) what is yashar (upright) for him;
Then Alahayam is gracious to him, and amar (spoke), ‘padai (deliver) him from yarad (going) down to the shachath (pit), I matzaa (have) found a kapar (ransom).'
His bashar (flesh) shall be fresher than a nair (child's). He shawab (turn back / repent) to the yamay (days) of his ilawam (youth).
He ithar (prays) to Alawah, and he is favorable to him, so that he raah (see) his panayam (face) with tharawaih (joy). He shawab (turn back / repent) to anawash (man) his tzadaqah (righteousness).
He sings before anashayam (men), and amar (spoke), ‘I have chataa (sinned), and iwah (perverted) that which was yashar (upright), and it didn't shawah (profit) me.
He has padah (redeemed) my napash (soul) from ibar (pass over/through) into the shachath (pit). My chay (life) shall raah (see) the awar (light).'
"Behold, Al pail (works) all these things, paim (twice), yes three times, with a gabar (man),
To shawab (turn back / repent) back his napash (soul) from the shachath (pit), that he may be enlightened with the awar (light) of the chay (life).
Qashab (mark) well, Ayawab (Job), and shamai (hearken / hear) to me. Hold your charash (peace), and I will dabar (word / matter).
If you yash (have) anything to malah (say), shawab (turn back / repent) me. Dabar (word / matter), for I chapatz (desire) to justify you.
If not, shamai (hearken / hear) to me. Hold your charash (peace), and I will alap (teach) you chakamah (wisdom)."
Moreover Alayahaw (Elihu) inah (answer / respond),
"Shamai (hearken / hear) my malah (words), you chakam (wise) men. Azan (ear) ear to me, you who have yadai (knowledge).
For the azan (ear) bachan (tries) malayan (words), as the palate taim (tastes) akal (eat).
Let us bachar (choose) for us that which is mashapat (right). Yadai (let) us know among ourselves what is tawab (good / proper function).
For Ayawab (Job) has amar (spoke), ‘I am tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), Al has sawar (taken) away my mashapat (right):
Notwithstanding my mashapat (right) I am considered a kazab (liar). My chatz (wound) is anash (incurable), though I am without disobedience.'
What gabar (man) is like Ayawab (Job), who shathah (drinks) laig (scorn) like mayam (Waters),
Who arach (goes) in chabarah (company) with the pailay (workers) of awan (iniquity), and yalak (walks) with rashai (wicked) anashay (men)?
For he has amar (spoke), ‘It sakan (profits) a gabar (man) nothing that he should ratzah (delight) himself with Alahayam.'

"Therefore shamai (hearken / hear) to me, you anashay (men) of labab (understanding): chalayalah (far) be it from Al, that he should do rashai (wickedness), from the Shaday, that he should commit iwal (iniquity).
For the pail (work) of a adam (man) he will shalam (render) to him, and cause every ayash (man / husband) to matzaa (find) according to his arach (ways).
Yes amanam (surely), Al will not rashai (do) wickedly, neither will the Shaday iwath (pervert) mashapat (justice).
Who put him in paqad (visit) of the aratz (Earth/land)? Or who has shawam (place / establish / appoint) him over the whole thabal (world)?
If he shawam (place / establish / appoint) his lab (heart) on himself, If he asap (gathered) to himself his rawach (spirit / wind) and his nashamah (breathing thing),
All bashar (flesh) would gawai (perish) yachad (together), and adam (man) would shawab (turn back / repent) again to ipar (dust).
"If now you have bayanah (understanding), shamai (hearken / hear) this. Listen to the qawal (sound / voice) of my malah (words).
Shall even one who shanaa (hate) mashapat (justice) chabash (govern)? Will you rashai (condemn) him who is tzadayaq (righteous) and kabayar (mighty)?—
Who amar (spoke) to a malak (king), ‘Vile!' Or to nadayabayam (nobles), ‘balayail (wicked)!'?
Who doesn't nashaa (lift) the panay (persons) of sharayam (princes), nor nakar (respects) the shawai (rich) more panayam (face) the dal (poor); for they all are the maishah (work) of his yad (hand).

In a ragai (in an instance) they mawath (death), even at chatzawath (midnight). The im (nation / people) are gaish (shaken) and ibar (pass over/through) away. The abayar (mighty) are ibar (pass over/through) away without a yad (hand).
"For his iyan (eye) are on the darakay (ways) of a ayash (man / husband). He raah (see) all his goings.
There is no chashak (darkness), nor thick gloom, where the pailay (workers) of awan (iniquity) may sathar (hide) themselves.
For he doesn't need to consider a ayash (man / husband) further, that he should halak (move) before Al in mashapat (judgment).
He raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) in pieces kabayar (mighty) men in ways past chaqar (finding) out, and imad (sets) others in their place.
Therefore he takes nakar (knowledge) of their maibad (works). He overturns them in the layal (night), so that they are dakaa (destroyed).
He sapaq (strikes) them as rashai (wicked) men in the maqawam (place) raah (see) of others;
Because they sawar (turned) aside from achar (other) him, and wouldn't pay attention to any of his darak (ways),
So that they caused the tzaiqah (cry) of the dal (poor) to bawaa (come) to him. He shamai (hearken / hear) the tzaiqah (cry) of the inay (afflicted).

When he shaqat (gives) quietness, who then can rashai (condemn)? When he sathar (hides) his panayam (face), who then can shawar (see) him? Alike whether to a gaway (heathen / nation), or to a adam (man),
That the godless man may not malak (king), that there be no mawaqash (one) to ensnare the im (nation / people).
"For has any amar (spoke) to Al, ‘I am guilty, but I will not chabal (offend) any more.
Yarah (teach) me that which I don't chazah (see). If I have pail (done) iwal (iniquity), I will yasap (do) it no more'?
Shall his shalam (recompense) be as you desire, that you refuse it? For you must bachar (choose), and not I. Therefore dabar (word / matter) what you yadai (know).
Anashay (men) of labab (understanding) will amar (spoke) me, yes, every chakam (wise) gabar (man) who shamai (hearken / hear) me:
‘Ayawab (Job) dabar (word / matter) without daith (knowledge). His dabar (word / matter) are without shakal (wisdom).'
I wish that were bachan (tried) to the natzach (end), because of his thashawabah (answering) like awan (wicked) anashay (men).
For he yasap (adds) pashai (rebellion) to his chataah (sin). He sapaq (claps) his hands among us, and rabah (multiplies) his amar (spoke) against Al."
Moreover Alayahaw (Elihu) inah (answer / respond),
"Do you chashab (think) this to be your mashapat (right), or do you amar (spoke), ‘My tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) is more than Al,'
That you ask, ‘What sakan (advantage) will it be to you? What yail (profit) shall I have, more than if I had chataah (sin)?'
I will shawab (turn back / repent) you, and your rai (neigbor/another person) with you.
Nabat (look) to the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and raah (see). Shawar (see) the shachaqayam (skies), which are gabah (higher) than you.
If you have chataa (sinned), what effect pail (do) you have against him? If your pashai (transgressions) are rabab (multiplied), what ishah (make) you do to him?
If you are tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), what nathan (give) you give him? Or what does he laqach (take / seize) from your yad (hand)?
Your rashai (wickedness) may hurt a ayash (man / husband) as you are, and your tzadaqah (righteousness) may profit a ban (son) of adam (man).
"By reason of the rab (multitude) of ishawaqayam (oppressions) they shawai (cry) out. They zaiq (cry) for zarawai (help) by reason of the arm of the rab (mighty).
But none amar (spoke), ‘Where is Alawah my Maker, who nathan (give) zamarawath (songs) in the layal (night),
Who teaches us more than the animals of the aratz (Earth/land), and chakam (makes) us wiser than the iwap (flying) of the sky?'
There they tzaiq (cry), but none inah (answer / respond) answer, panayam (face) of the gaawan (pride) of rai (evil) men.
Surely Al will not shamai (hearken / hear) an empty cry, neither will the Shaday shawar (regard) it.
Ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) much less when you amar (spoke) you don't shawar (see) him. The dayan (judge) is panayam (face) him, and you chawal (wait) for him!
But now, because he paqad (visit) not visited in his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), neither does he maad (greatly) yadai (regard) arrogance.
Therefore Ayawab (Job) patzah (opens) his pah (mouth) with empty talk, and he kabar (multiplies) malayan (words) balay (without) daith (knowledge)."
Alayahaw (Elihu) also yasap (continued), and amar (spoke),
"Bear with me a zaiyar (little), and I will chawah (show) you; for I still have something to malah (say) on Alawah behalf.
I will get my dai (knowledge) from rachawaq (afar), and will nathan (give) tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) to my pail (maker).
For truly my malah (words) are not shaqar (false). One who is thamayam (complete / whole) in daih (knowledge) is with you.
"Behold, Al is kabayar (mighty), and doesn't maas (despise) anyone. He is kabayar (mighty) in kach (strength / mighty / power) of lab (heart).
He doesn't preserve the chayah (life) of the rashai (wicked), but nathan (give) to the inay (afflicted) their mashapat (right).

He doesn't garai (withdraw) his iyan (eye) from the tzadayaq (righteous), but with malakayam (kings) on the kasaa (throne), he yashab (inhabit/dwell) them natzach (forever), and they are gabah (exalted).
If they are asar (bound) in zaqayam (fetters), and are lakad (taken) in the chabalay (cords) of inay (afflictions),
Then he shows them their pail (work), and their pashai (transgressions), that they have behaved themselves proudly.
He also galah (opens) their azan (ear) to mawasar (instruction), and commands that they shawab (turn back / repent) from awan (iniquity).
If they shamai (hearken / hear) and ibad (servant) him, they shall kalah (complete / finish) their yawam (day) in tawab (good / proper function), and their shanah (years) in naiyamayam (pleasures).
But if they don't shamai (hearken / hear), they shall ibar (pass over/through) by the shalach (sword); they shall gawai (die) without daith (knowledge).
"But those who are godless in lab (heart) shawam (place / establish / appoint) up ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting). They don't shawai (cry) for help when he asar (binds) them.
They mawath (death) in nair (youth). Their chay (life) perishes among the qadash (set apart / make holy).
He chalatz (delivers) the inay (afflicted) by their inay (affliction), and galah (opens) their azan (ear) in lachatz (oppression).

Yes, he would have allured you out of distress, into a rachab (broad) place, thachath (under) there is no restriction. That which is nachath (set) on your shalachan (table) would be malaa (full) of dashan (fatness).
"But you are malaa (full) of the dayan (judge) of the rashai (wicked). Dayan (judge) and dayan (judge) thamak (take) hold of you.
Don't let riches sawath (entice) you to chamah (wrath), neither let the rab (great) size of a kapar (bribe) natah (turn) you aside.
Would your wealth sustain you in distress, or all the kach (strength / mighty / power) of your kach (strength / mighty / power)?
Don't shaap (desire) the layal (night), when imayam (people) are ilah (go up / offer) off in their place.
Shamar (keep/guard) heed, don't panah (turn) awan (iniquity); for you have bachar (chosen) this rather than inay (affliction).
Behold, Al is shagab (exalted) in his kach (strength / mighty / power). Who is a teacher like him?
Who paqad (visit) prescribed his darak (way) for him? Or who can amar (spoke), ‘You have pail (committed) iwal (unrighteousness)?'
"Zakar (remember) that you shagaa (magnify) his pail (work), whereof shararaw (men) have shayar (sung).
All adam (men) have chazah (looked) thereon. Adam (man) chazaw (sees) it rachawaq (afar) off.
Behold, Al is shagayaa (great), and we don't yadai (know) him. The masapar (number) of his shanah (years) is unsearchable.
For he draws up the natapay (drops) of mayam (Waters), which distill in matar (rain) from his ad (vapor),
Which the shachaqayam (skies) pour down and which nazal (drop) on adam (man) abundantly.
Yes, can any bayan (between) the maparash (spreading) of the ib (clouds), and the thunderings of his sakah (pavilion)?
Behold, he parash (spreads) his awar (light) around him. He kasah (covers) the sharash (bottom) of the yam (sea/waters).
For by these he dayan (judge) the imayam (people). He nathan (give) akal (food) in makabayar (abundance).
He kasah (covers) his kapayam (hands) with the awar (light), and tzawah (commands) it to strike the mark.
Its rai (noise) nagad (tells) about him, and the livestock also concerning the storm that ilah (go up / offer) up.
"Yes, at zaath (this) my lab (heart) charad (trembles), and is nathar (moved) out of its maqawam (place).
Shamai (hearken / hear), oh, shamai (hearken / hear) the ragaz (noise) of his ragaz (voice), the qawal (sound / voice) that yatzaa (go out / come out) out of his pah (mouth).
He sends it forth under the whole sky, and his awar (light) to the kanapawath (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land).

Achar (other) it a qawal (sound / voice) shaag (roars). He raim (thunders) with the qawal (sound / voice) of his gaawan (majesty). He doesn't hold back anything when his qawal (sound / voice) is shamai (hearken / hear).
Al raim (thunders) marvelously with his qawal (sound / voice). He ishah (make) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) things, which we can't yadai (comprehend).
For he amar (spoke) to the shalag (snow), ‘Fall on the aratz (Earth/land);' likewise to the shower of gasham (rain), and to the showers of his iz (strength / might / refuge) gasham (rain).
He chatham (seals) up the yad (hand) of every adam (man), that all adam (men) whom he yadai (has) made may know it.
Then the animals bawaa (come) cover, and shakan (place) in their arab (dens).
Out of its room bawaa (come) the sawapah (storm), and qarah (cold) out of the mazarah (north).
By the nashamah (breathing thing) of Al, ice is nathan (give), and the rachab (breadth) of the mayam (Waters) is frozen.
Yes, he loads the ib (thick) cloud with moisture. He pawatz (spreads) abroad the ib (cloud) of his awar (light).
It is hapak (turned) around by his guidance, that they may pail (do) whatever he tzawah (commands) them on the surface of the habitable thabal (world),
Whether it is for shabat (correction), or for his aratz (Earth/land), or for loving chasad (grace), that he causes it to matzaa (come).
"Listen to this, Ayawab (Job). Imad (stand) still, and bayan (between) the palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) works of Al.
Do you yadai (know) how Alawah controls them, and causes the awar (light) of his inan (cloud) to yapai (shine)?
Do you yadai (know) the workings of the ib (clouds), the wondrous mapalaawath (works) of him who is thamayam (complete / whole) in dai (knowledge)?
You whose bagad (clothing) is cham (warm), when the aratz (Earth/land) is still by reason of the darawam (south) wind?
Can you, with him, raqai (spread) out the shachaq (sky), which is chazaq (strong) as a yatzaq (cast) metal mirror?
Yadai (teach) us what we shall amar (spoke) him, for we can't make our case by panayam (face) of chashak (darkness).
Shall it be sapar (book) him that I would dabar (word / matter)? Or should a ayash (man / husband) wish that he were balai (swallowed) up?
Now men don't raah (see) the awar (light) which is bahayar (bright) in the shachaqayam (skies), but the rawach (spirit / wind) passes, and clears them.
Out of the tzapawan (north) athah (you (masc)) zahab (gold) splendor. With Alawah is awesome hawad (majesty).
We can't reach the Shaday. He is exalted in kach (strength / mighty / power). In mashapat (justice) and rab (great) tzadaqah (righteousness), he will not oppress.
Therefore anashayam (men) revere him. He doesn't raah (see) any who are chakam (wise) of lab (heart)."
Then Yahawah inah (answer / respond) Ayawab (Job) out of the sair (whirlwind),
"Who is this who chashak (darkness) itzah (counsel) by malayan (words) without daith (knowledge)?
Brace yourself like a gabar (man), for I will question you, then you yadai (answer) me!
"Ayapah (where) were you when I yasad (laid) the foundations of the aratz (Earth/land)? Nagad (declare), if you yadai (have) bayanah (understanding).
Who shawam (place / establish / appoint) its mamad (measures), if you yadai (know)? Or who natah (stretched) the qaw (line) on it?
Whereupon were its adan (foundations) tabai (fastened)? Or who yarah (laid) its cornerstone,
When the baqar (morning) kawakabay (stars) ranan (sang) yachad (together), and all the banay (sons) of Alahayam rawai (shouted) for joy?
"Or who sakak (shut) up the yam (sea/waters) with dalathayam (doors), when it gayach (broke) forth from the racham (womb),
When I shawam (place / establish / appoint) inan (cloud) its labawash (garment), and wrapped it in irapal (thick) darkness,
Marked out for it my chaq (statute), shawam (place / establish / appoint) barayach (bars) and dalathayam (doors),
And amar (spoke), ‘Here you may bawaa (come), but no yasap (further). Here your gaawan (proud) gal (waves) shall be shayath (put / appoint / make)?'
"Have you tzawah (commanded) the baqar (morning) in your yawam (day), and caused the dawn to yadai (know) its maqawam (place);
That it might achaz (take) hold of the kanapawath (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land), and shake the rashai (wicked) out of it?
It is hapak (changed) as chamar (clay) under the chawatham (seal), and yathayatzabaw (stands) forth as a labawash (garment).
From the rashai (wicked), their awar (light) is withheld. The rawam (will lift up) zarawai (arm) is shabar (broken).
"Bawaa (come) you entered into the nabakay (springs) of the yam (sea/waters)? Or have you halak (move) in the recesses of the thahawam (depths)?
Have the shairay (gates) of mawath (death) been galah (revealed) to you? Or raah (see) you seen the shairay (gates) of the shadow of tzalamawath (death)?
Bayan (between) you comprehended the aratz (Earth/land) in its rachab (breadth)? Nagad (declare), if you yadai (know) it all.
"What is the darak (way) to the shakan (place) of awar (light)? As for chashak (darkness), where is its maqawam (place),
That you should laqach (take / seize) it to its gabawal (border/boundary), that you should bayan (between) the nathayabawath (paths) to its bayath (house)?
Surely you yadai (know), for you were yalad (birth / begot) then, and the masapar (number) of your yawam (day) is rab (great)!
Bawaa (come) you entered the atzarawath (treasuries) of the shalag (snow), or raah (see) you seen the atzarawath (treasures) of the barad (hail),
Which I have chashak (darkness) against the ith (time) of tzar (oppressor / distressor), against the yawam (day) of qarab (battle) and qarab (war)?
By ay (what) darak (way) is the awar (light) distributed, or the east qadayam (wind) pawatz (scattered) on the aratz (Earth/land)?
Who has cut a channel for the shatap (flood) water, or the darak (path) for the thunderstorm;
To cause it to matar (rain) on a aratz (Earth/land) where no ayash (man / husband) is; on the madabar (wilderness), in which there is no adam (man);
To shabai (satisfy) the mashawaah (waste) and shawaa (vanity) mawatzaa (ground), to cause the tender dashaa (grass) to tzamach (spring) forth?
Does the matar (rain) yash (have) a ab (father)? Or who yalad (birth / begot) the agalay (drops) of tal (dew)?
Out of whose batan (womb) yatzaa (go out / come out) the qarach (ice)? The gray kapawar (frost) of the sky, who has given yalad (birth / begot) to it?
The mayam (Waters) become hard like aban (stone), when the surface of the thahawam (depths) is lakad (frozen).
"Can you qashar (bind) the cluster of the kayamah (pleiades), or loosen the cords of kasayal (orion)?
Can you yatzaa (go out / come out) forth the Mazarah (constellations) in their ith (season)? Or can you nachah (guide) the Bear with her cubs?
Do you yadai (know) the chaqawath (laws) of the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens)? Can you establish its mashatar (dominion) over the aratz (Earth/land)?
"Can you rawam (will lift up) up your qawal (sound / voice) to the ib (clouds), That shapaih (abundance) of mayam (Waters) may kasah (cover) you?
Can you shalach (send) forth baraqayam (lightnings), that they may yalak (go)? Do they amar (spoke) to you, ‘Here we are?'
Who has shayath (put / appoint / make) chakamah (wisdom) in the tachah (inward) parts? Or who nathan (give) given bayanah (understanding) to the shakaway (mind)?
Who can sapar (book) the shachaqayam (clouds) by chakamah (wisdom)? Or who can pour out the nabalay (bottles) of the sky,
When the ipar (dust) yatzaq (runs) into a mass, and the ragabayam (clods) of earth dabaq (stick) together?
"Can you tzawad (hunt) the tarap (prey) for the labayaa (lioness), or malaa (satisfy) the chay (life) of the young kapayarayam (lions),
When they crouch in their maiwanawath (dens), and arab (lie) in wait in the thicket?
Who kawan (provides) for the irab (evening) his prey, when his yalad (birth / begot) ones shawai (cry) to Al, and thaih (wander) for balay (lack) of akal (food)?
"Do you yadai (know) the ith (time) when the salai (mountain) yailay (goats) give yalad (birth / begot)? Do you shamar (keep/guard) when the doe chawal (bears) fawns?
Can you sapar (book) the yarachayam (months) that they fulfill? Or do you yadai (know) the ith (time) when they give birth?
They karai (bow) themselves, they palach (bring) forth their yalad (birth / begot), they end their labor chabal (pains).
Their ban (son) ones become strong. They rabah (grow) up in the open field. They yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and don't shawab (turn back / repent) again.
"Who has shalach (send) the paraa (wild) donkey chapashay (free)? Or who pathach (has) loosened the masarawath (bonds) of the swift donkey,
Whose bayath (house) I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) the irabah (wilderness), and the malachah (salt) land his mashakan (dwelling) place?
He shachaq (scorns) the hamawan (tumult) of the qarayah (city / town), neither does he shamai (hearken / hear) the thashaah (shouting) of the nagash (driver).
The yathawar (range) of the harayam (mountains) is his maraih (pasture), He searches achar (other) every yarawaq (green) thing.
"Will the wild ox be abah (be willing / desire) to ibad (servant) you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?
Can you hold the wild ox in the thalam (furrow) with his harness? Or will he till the imaqayam (valleys) achar (other) you?
Will you batach (trust) him, because his kach (strength / mighty / power) is rab (great)? Or will you izab (leave) to him your yagayai (labor)?
Will you confide in him, that he will shawab (turn back / repent) home your zarai (seed), and asap (gather) the grain of your garan (threshing) floor?
"The kanap (wings) of the ostrich wave proudly; but are they the abarah (feathers) and plumage of nawatzah (love)?
For she izab (leaves) her bayatzah (eggs) on the aratz (Earth/land), chamam (warms) them in the ipar (dust),
And shakach (forgets) that the ragal (feet / foot) may zawar (crush) them, or that the shadah (wild) animal may trample them.
She deals harshly with her ban (son) ones, as if they were not hers. Though her yagayai (labor) is in rayaq (vain), she is without pachad (fear / dread),
Because Alawah has nashah (deprived) her of chakamah (wisdom), neither chalaq (has) he imparted to her bayanah (understanding).
When she maraa (lifts) up herself on marawam (high), she shachaq (scorns) the sawas (horse) and his rider.
"Nathan (give) you given the sawas (horse) gabawarah (might)? Have you labash (clothed) his tzawaar (neck) with a quivering mane?
Have you raish (made) him to leap as a arabah (locust)? The glory of his nachar (snorting) is awesome.
He yachaparaw (paws) in the imaq (valley), and shawash (rejoices) in his kach (strength / mighty / power). He yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) the nashaq (armed) men.
He shachaq (mocks) at pachad (fear / dread), and is not chathath (dismayed), neither does he shawab (turn back / repent) back from the charab (sword).
The ashapah (quiver) ranah (rattles) against him, the flashing chanayath (spear) and the javelin.
He eats up the aratz (Earth/land) with raish (fierceness) and ragaz (rage), neither does he stand still at the qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn).

As often as the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn) sounds he snorts, ‘haach (aha)!' He rawach (spirit / wind) the malachamah (battle) rachawaq (afar) off, the raim (thunder) of the sharayam (captains), and the tharawaih (shouting).
"Is it by your bayanah (wisdom) that the natz (hawk) soars, and stretches her kanap (wings) toward the thayaman (south)?
Is it at your command that the nashar (eagle) gabah (mounts) up, and rawam (will lift up) his qan (nest) on rawam (will lift up)?
On the cliff he shakan (place), and makes his home, on the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.
From there he spies out the akal (prey). His iyan (eye) nabat (see) it rachawaq (afar) off.
His aparach (young) ones also ilai (suck) up dam (blood). Where the chalal (slain) are, there he is."
Moreover Yahweh answered Job,
"Shall he who argues contend with the Almighty? He who argues with God, let him answer it."
Then answered Yahweh,
"Behold, I am of small account. What shall I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.
I have spoken once, and I will not answer; Yes, twice, but I will proceed no further."
Then Yahweh answered out of the whirlwind,
"Now brace yourself like a man. I will question you, and you will answer me.
Will you even annul my judgment? Will you condemn me, that you may be justified?
Or do you have an arm like God? Can you thunder with a voice like him?
"Now deck yourself with excellency and dignity. Array yourself with honor and majesty.
Pour out the fury of your anger. Look at everyone who is proud, and bring him low.
Look at everyone who is proud, and humble him. Crush the wicked in their place.
Hide them in the dust together. Bind their faces in the hidden place.
Then I will also admit to you that your own right hand can save you.
"See now, behemoth, which I made as well as you. He eats grass as an ox.
Look now, his strength is in his thighs. His force is in the muscles of his belly.
He moves his tail like a cedar. The sinews of his thighs are knit together.
His bones are like tubes of brass. His limbs are like bars of iron.
He is the chief of the ways of God. He who made him gives him his sword.
Surely the mountains produce food for him, where all the animals of the field play.
He lies under the lotus trees, in the covert of the reed, and the marsh.
The lotuses cover him with their shade. The willows of the brook surround him.
Behold, if a river overflows, he doesn't tremble. He is confident, though the Jordan swells even to his mouth.
Shall any take him when he is on the watch, or pierce through his nose with a snare?
Can you draw out Leviathan with a fishhook, or press down his tongue with a cord?
Can you put a rope into his nose, or pierce his jaw through with a hook?
Will he shalam (make) many petitions to you, or will he speak soft words to you?
Will he make a covenant with you, that you should take him for a servant forever?
Will you play with him as with a bird? Or will you bind him for your girls?
Will traders barter for him? Will they part him among the merchants?
Can you fill his skin with barbed irons, or his head with fish spears?
Lay your hand on him. Remember the battle, and do so no more.
Behold, the hope of him is in vain. Won't one be cast down even at the sight of him?
None is so fierce that he dare stir him up. Who then is he who can stand iyan (eye) me?
Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Everything under the heavens is mine.
"I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, nor his mighty strength, nor his goodly frame.
Who can strip off his outer garment? Who shall yatzaa (go out / come out) within his jaws?
Who can panayam (face) the doors of his panayam (face)? Around his teeth is terror.
Strong scales are his pride, shut up together with a dabaq (close) seal.
One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.
They are joined one to another. They stick together, so that they can't be pulled apart.
His sneezing flashes out light. His eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
Out of his mouth go burning torches. Sparks of fire leap forth.
Out of his nostrils a smoke goes, as of a boiling pot over a fire of reeds.
His breath kindles coals. A flame goes forth from his mouth.
There is strength in his neck. Terror dances before him.
The flakes of his flesh are joined together. They are firm on him. They can't be moved.
His heart is as firm as a stone, yes, firm as the lower millstone.
When he raises himself up, the mighty are afraid. They retreat before his thrashing.
If one attacks him with the sword, it can't prevail; nor the spear, the dart, nor the pointed shaft.
He chashab (counts) barazal (iron) as thaban (straw); and nachawashah (brass) as raqabawan (rotten) itz (wood).
The ban (son) can't barach (make) him flee. Aban (stone) hapak (stones) are like chaff to him.
Clubs are chashab (counted) as qash (stubble). He shachaq (laughs) at the raish (rushing) of the javelin.
His undersides are like chadawad (sharp) charash (potsherds), leaving a trail in the mud like a charawatz (threshing) sledge.
He makes the matzawalah (deep) to rathach (boil) like a sayar (pot). He shawam (place / establish / appoint) the yam (sea/waters) like a maraqachah (pot) of ointment.
He makes a nathayab (path) awar (light) achar (other) him. One would chashab (think) the thahawam (depths) had white hair.
On ipar (earth) there is not his equal, that is ishah (make) balay (without) chath (fear).
He raah (see) everything that is gabah (high). He is malak (king) over all the ban (son) of shachatz (pride)."
Then Ayawab (Job) inah (answer / respond) Yahawah,
"I yadai (know) that you yakal (can) do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be batzar (restrained).

You asked, ‘Who is this who ilam (hides) itzah (counsel) without daith (knowledge)?' Therefore I have nagad (uttered) that which I did not bayan (between), things palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) wonderful for me, which I didn't yadai (know).
You said, ‘shamai (hearken / hear), now, and I will dabar (word / matter); I will question you, and you yadai (will) answer me.'
I had shamai (hearken / hear) of you by the shamai (hearing) of the azan (ear), but now my iyan (eye) raah (see) you.
Therefore I maas (abhor) myself, and nacham (turn away / repent) in ipar (dust) and ashes."

It was so, that achar (other) Yahawah had dabar (word / matter) these dabarayam (words) to Ayawab (Job), Yahawah amar (spoke) to Alayapaz (Eliphaz) the thayamanay (temanite), "My ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) is charah (hot with anger) against you, and against your shanayam (two) rai (neigbor/another person); for you have not dabar (word / matter) of me the thing that is kawan (right), as my ibad (servant) Ayawab (Job) has.

Now therefore, laqach (take / seize) to yourselves shabai (seven) parayam (bulls) and shabai (seven) ayalayam (rams), and yalak (go) to my ibad (servant) Ayawab (Job), and ilah (go up / offer) up for yourselves a burnt ilah (offering); and my ibad (servant) Ayawab (Job) shall palal (pray) for you, for I will nashaa (lift) him, that I not ishah (make) with you according to your nabalah (folly). For you have not dabar (word / matter) of me the thing that is kawan (right), as my ibad (servant) Ayawab (Job) has."

So Alayapaz (Eliphaz) the thayamanay (temanite) and Baladad (Bildad) the shawachay (shuhite) and Tzawapar (Zophar) the naimathay (naamathite) yalak (went), and ishah (make) what Yahawah commanded them, and Yahawah nashaa (lift) Job.

Yahawah shawab (turn back / repent) the shabawath (captivity) of Ayawab (Job), when he palal (prayed) for his rai (neigbor/another person). Yahawah yasap (gave) Ayawab (Job) mashanah (twice) as much as he had before.

Then bawaa (come) there to him all his ach (brother/kinsman), and all his achawath (sisters), and all those who yadai (had) been of his acquaintance panayam (face), and akal (eat) lacham (bread) with him in his bayath (house). They nacham (turn away / repent) him, and consoled him concerning all the rai (evil) that Yahawah bawaa (come) brought on him. Everyone also nathan (give) him a qashayatah (piece) of money, and everyone a ring of zahab (gold).

So Yahawah barak (blessed) the acharayath (latter) end of Ayawab (Job) more than his raashayath (beginning). He had fourteen alap (thousand) tzaan (sheep), shash (six) alap (thousand) gamalayam (camels), one alap (thousand) tzamad (yoke) of oxen, and a alap (thousand) female donkeys.
He had also shabainah (seven) banayam (sons) and shalawash (three) banawath (daughters).

He qaraa (called) the sham (name) of the achad (one), Yamayamah (Jemimah); and the sham (name) of the shanay (second), Qatzayaih (Keziah); and the sham (name) of the shalayashay (third), Qaranahapawak (Keren Happuch).

In all the aratz (Earth/land) were no nashayam (women) matzaa (found) so yapah (beautiful) as the banawath (daughters) of Ayawab (Job). Their ab (father) nathan (give) them an nachalah (inheritance) thawak (midst) their ach (brother/kinsman).

Achar (other) this Ayawab (Job) chayah (lived) one maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years), and raah (see) his banay (sons), and his banay (sons)' banay (sons), to arabai (four) darawath (generations).
So Ayawab (Job) mawath (death), being zaqan (old) and shabai (full) of yamayam (days).

Ashar (who/that) is the ayash (man / husband) who doesn't halak (move) in the itzah (counsel) of the rashai (wicked), nor imad (stand) in the darak (way) of chataayam (sinners), nor yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the mawashab (seat) of latzayam (scoffers);
But his chapatz (delight) is in Yahawah thawarah (instruction). On his thawarah (instruction) he hagah (meditates) yawamam (by day) and layal (night).

He will be like a itz (tree) shathal (planted) by the palagay (streams) of mayam (Waters), that nathan (give) forth its paray (fruit) in its ith (season), whose ilah (leaf) also nabal (does) not wither. Whatever he ishah (make) shall tzalach (prosper).
The rashai (wicked) are not so, but are like the matz (chaff) which the rawach (spirit / wind) nadap (drives) away.
Therefore the rashai (wicked) shall not qawam (rise up) in the mashapat (judgment), nor chataayam (sinners) in the idah (congregation) of the tzadayaq (righteous).
For Yahawah yadai (knows) the darak (way) of the tzadayaq (righteous), but the darak (way) of the rashai (wicked) shall abad (destroy / perish).
Why do the gawayam (nations) ragash (rage), and the laamayam (peoples) plot a rayaq (vain) thing?

The malakay (kings) of the aratz (Earth/land) take a yatzab (stand), and the rawazanayam (rulers) take yasad (counsel) yachad (together), against Yahawah, and against his mashayach (anointed one), saying,
"Let's nathaq (break) their mawasar (bonds) apart, and shalak (cast) their cords from us."
He who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) will shachaq (laugh). The Adanay will laig (have) them in derision.
Then he will dabar (word / matter) to them in his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and terrify them in his charawan (wrath):
"Yet I have nasak (set) my malak (king) on my qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain) of Tzayawan (Zion)."
I will sapar (book) of the chaq (statute). Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, "You are my ban (son). Today I have become your yalad (birth / begot).
Shaal (ask) of me, and I will nathan (give) the gawayam (nations) for your nachalah (inheritance), the apas (uttermost) parts of the aratz (Earth/land) for your achazah (possession).
You shall raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) them with a shabat (rod) of barazal (iron). You shall napatz (dash) them in pieces like a yatzar (potter's) kalay (vessel)."
Now therefore be shakal (wise), you malakayam (kings). Be yasar (instructed), you shapatay (judges) of the aratz (Earth/land).
Ibad (servant) Yahawah with yaraah (fear), and gayal (rejoice) with raid (trembling).

Give sincere homage to the bar (son), lest he be anap (angry), and you abad (destroy / perish) in the darak (way), for his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) will mait (soon) be bair (kindled). Ashar (who/that) are all those who take chasah (refuge) in him.
Yahawah, how my tzar (oppressor / distressor) have rabab (increased)! Many are those who qawam (rise up) up against me.
Many there are who amar (spoke) of my napash (soul), "There is no yashawaih (salvation) for him in Alahayam." Salah (selah).
But you, Yahawah, are a magan (shield) around me, my kabawad (glory), and the one who rawam (will lift up) up my raash (head).
I qaraa (called) to Yahawah with my qawal (sound / voice), and he inah (answer / respond) me out of his qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain). Salah (selah).
I shakab (laid) myself down and yashan (slept). I awakened; for Yahawah samak (sustains) me.
I will not be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of rababawath (tens) of thousands of im (nation / people) who have shayath (put / appoint / make) themselves against me on sabayab (surrounding) side.

Qawam (rise up), Yahawah! Yashai (salvation) me, my Alahayam! For you have nakah (struck) all of my ayab (enemy) on the lachay (cheek) bone. You have shabar (broken) the shanay (teeth) of the rashai (wicked).
Yashawaih (salvation) belongs to Yahawah. Your barakah (blessing) be on your im (nation / people). Salah (selah).

Inah (answer / respond) me when I qaraa (called), Alahayam of my tzadaq (righteous / just / fair). Give me relief from my tzar (oppressor / distressor). Have chanan (showing favor) on me, and shamai (hearken / hear) my thapalah (prayer).

You banay (sons) of ayash (man / husband), id (until / as far as) long shall my kabawad (glory) be turned into dishonor? Will you ahab (love) rayaq (vanity), and baqash (seek) after falsehood? Salah (selah).
But yadai (know) that Yahawah has palah (set) apart for himself him who is chasayad (godly): Yahawah will shamai (hearken / hear) when I qaraa (called) to him.
Ragaz (stand) in awe, and don't chataa (sin). Search your own labab (heart) on your mashakab (bed), and be still. Salah (selah).
Zabach (offer) the zabachay (sacrifices) of tzadaq (righteous / just / fair). Batach (put) your trust in Yahawah.
Many amar (spoke), "Who will show us any tawab (good / proper function)?" Yahawah, let the awar (light) of your panayam (face) shine on us.
You nathan (give) put shamachah (gladness) in my lab (heart), more than when their grain and their new thayarawash (wine) are rabab (increased).
In shalawam (peace / safety) I will yachad (both) shakab (lay) myself down and sleep, for you, Yahawah badad (alone), yashab (inhabit/dwell) me live in safety.
Azan (ear) ear to my amar (spoke), Yahawah. Bayan (between) my hagayag (meditation).
Listen to the qawal (sound / voice) of my shawai (cry), my malak (king) and my Alahayam; for to you do I palal (pray).

Yahawah, in the baqar (morning) you shall shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice). In the baqar (morning) I will irak (lay) my requests before you, and will tzapah (watchman / keep watch) expectantly.
For you are not a Al who chapatz (has) pleasure in rashai (wickedness). Rai (evil) can't live with you.
The arrogant shall not yatzab (stand) in your iyan (eye). You shanaa (hate) all pailay (workers) of awan (iniquity).
You will abad (destroy / perish) those who dabar (word / matter) kazab (lies). Yahawah thaib (abhors) the bloodthirsty and deceitful ayash (man / husband).

But as for me, in the rab (abundance) of your loving chasad (grace) I will bawaa (come) into your bayath (house). I will shachah (bow) toward your qadash (set apart / make holy) hayakal (temple) in reverence of you.
Nachah (lead) me, Yahawah, in your tzadaqah (righteousness) because of my sharar (enemies). Make your darak (way) yashar (upright) before my panayam (face).

For there is no kawan (faithfulness) in their pah (mouth). Their qarab (among / near) is destruction. Their garawan (throat) is an pathach (open) tomb. They chalaq (flatter) with their lashawan (tongue / language).

Asham (hold) them guilty, Alahayam. Napal (fall / be cast down) them fall by their own mawaitzah (counsels); nadach (thrust) them out in the rab (multitude) of their pashai (transgressions), for they have marah (rebelled) against you.

But let all those who take chasah (refuge) in you shamach (rejoice), Let them iwalam (forever) ranan (shout) for joy, because you sakak (defend) them. Let them also who ahab (love) your sham (name) be ilatz (joyful) in you.
For you will barak (blessed) the tzadayaq (righteous). Yahawah, you will surround him with favor as with a tzanah (shield).
Yahawah, don't yakach (rebuke) me in your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), neither discipline me in your chamah (wrath).
Have chanan (showing favor) on me, Yahawah, for I am faint. Yahawah, rapaa (heal) me, for my itzam (bones) are bahal (troubled).
My napash (soul) is also in maad (great) anguish. But you, Yahawah —how long?
Shawab (turn back / repent), Yahawah. Chalatz (deliver) my napash (soul), and yashai (salvation) me for your loving chasad (grace)' sake.
For in mawath (death) there is no zakar (remember) of you. In shaawal (Sheol / afterlife), who shall give you yadah (thanks)?
I am yagai (weary) with my anachah (groaning). Every layal (night) I flood my matah (bed). I drench my irash (couch) with my damaih (tears).
My iyan (eye) wastes away because of kais (grief). It grows ithaq (old) because of all my tzarar (adversaries).
Sawar (depart) from me, all you pailay (workers) of awan (iniquity), for Yahawah has shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of my bakay (weeping).
Yahawah has shamai (hearken / hear) my thachanah (supplication). Yahawah laqach (take / seize) my thapalah (prayer).
May all my ayab (enemy) be bawash (ashamed) and bahal (dismayed). They shall shawab (turn back / repent) back, they shall be disgraced ragai (in an instance).
Yahawah, my Alahayam, I take chasah (refuge) in you. Yashai (salvation) me from all those who radap (pursue) me, and natzal (deliver) me,
Lest they tarap (tear) apart my napash (soul) like a aray (lion), ripping it in paraq (pieces), while there is none to natzal (deliver).
Yahawah, my Alahayam, if I ishah (make) done this, if there is iwal (iniquity) in my kap (hands),
If I have gamal (rewarded) rai (evil) to him who was at shalam (peace) with me (yes, if I have chalatz (delivered) him who rayaqam (without) cause was my tzarar (adversary)),

Let the ayab (enemy) radap (pursue) my napash (soul), and nashag (overtake) it; yes, let him tread my chay (life) down to the aratz (Earth/land), and shakan (place) my kabawad (glory) in the ipar (dust). Salah (selah).
