But I am inay (poor) and abayawan (needy). May the Adanay chashab (think) about me. You are my izarah (help) and my deliverer. Don't achar (other), my Alahayam.
Ashar (who/that) is he who shakal (considers) the dal (poor). Yahawah will malat (deliver) him in the yawam (day) of rai (evil).
Yahawah will shamar (keep/guard) him, and chayah (keep) him alive. He shall be ashar (who/that) on the aratz (Earth/land), and he will not surrender him to the napash (soul) of his ayab (enemy).
Yahawah will sustain him on his sickbed, and hapak (restore) him from his irash (bed) of illness.
I amar (spoke), "Yahawah, have chanan (showing favor) on me! Rapaa (heal) me, for I have chataa (sinned) against you."
My ayab (enemy) amar (spoke) rai (evil) against me: "When will he mawath (death), and his sham (name) abad (destroy / perish)?"

If he bawaa (come) to raah (see) me, he dabar (word / matter) falsehood. His lab (heart) qabatz (gathers) awan (iniquity) to itself. When he yatzaa (go out / come out) chawatz (abroad), he dabar (word / matter) it.
All who shanaa (hate) me lachash (whisper) yachad (together) against me. They chashab (imagine) the rai (worst) for me.
"An balayail (evil) dabar (word / matter)," they say, "has afflicted him. Now that he shakab (lies) he shall qawam (rise up) up no more."
Yes, my own shalawam (peace / safety) friend, in whom I batach (trusted), who akal (eat) lacham (bread) with me, has gadal (lifted) up his iqab (heel) against me.
But you, Yahawah, have chanan (showing favor) on me, and qawam (rise up) me up, that I may shalam (repay) them.
By this I yadai (know) that you chapatz (delight) in me, because my ayab (enemy) doesn't rawai (triumph) over me.
As for me, you uphold me in my tham (integrity), and natzab (set) me in your panayam (face) iwalam (forever).
Barak (blessed) be Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), from iwalam (forever) and to iwalam (forever)! Aman (believe / have faith) and aman (believe / have faith).
As the deer irag (pants) for the mayam (Waters) apayaqay (brooks), so my napash (soul) irag (pants) after you, Alahayam.
My napash (soul) tzamaa (thirsts) for Alahayam, for the chay (life) Al. When shall I bawaa (come) and raah (see) panayam (face) Alahayam?
My damaih (tears) have been my lacham (food) yawamam (by day) and layal (night), yawam (day) they continually ask me, "Where is your Alahayam?"

These things I zakar (remember), and shapak (pour) out my napash (soul) within me, how I used to ibar (pass over/through) with the crowd, and led them to the bayath (house) of Alahayam, with the qawal (sound / voice) of ranah (joy) and thawadah (praise), a hamawan (multitude) chagag (keeping) a holy day.
Why are you in despair, my napash (soul)? Why are you disturbed within me? Yachal (hope) in Alahayam! For I shall still yadah (praise) him for the yashawaih (salvation) help of his panayam (face).

My Alahayam, my napash (soul) is in despair within me. Therefore I zakar (remember) you from the aratz (Earth/land) of the Yaradan (Jordan), the heights of Charamawanayam (Hermon), from the har (mountain) matzair (mizar).
Thahawam (depths) qaraa (called) to thahawam (depths) at the qawal (sound / voice) of your waterfalls. All your mashabar (waves) and your gal (billows) ibar (pass over/through) swept over me.
Yahawah will tzawah (command) his loving chasad (grace) in the yawamam (by day). In the layal (night) his shayar (song) shall be with me: a thapalah (prayer) to the Al of my chay (life).
I will ask Al, my salai (rock), "Why have you shakach (forgotten) me? Why do I yalak (go) qadar (mourning) because of the lachatz (oppression) of the ayab (enemy)?"
As with a ratzach (sword) in my itzam (bones), my tzarar (adversaries) charap (reproach) me, yawam (day) they continually ask me, "Where is your Alahayam?"

Why are you in despair, my napash (soul)? Why are you disturbed within me? Yachal (hope) in Alahayam! For I shall still yadah (praise) him, the yashawaih (salvation) help of my panayam (face), and my Alahayam.
Vindicate me, Alahayam, and rayab (plead) my rayab (cause) against an ungodly gaway (heathen / nation). Oh, palat (deliver) me from deceitful and iwal (wicked) ayash (man / husband).
For you are the Alahayam of my maiwaz (stronghold / fortress / protection). Why have you rejected me? Why do I halak (move) qadar (mourning) because of the lachatz (oppression) of the ayab (enemy)?
Oh, shalach (send) out your awar (light) and your amath (truth). Let them nachah (lead) me. Bawaa (come) them bring me to your qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain), To your mashakan (tents).
Then I will bawaa (come) to the mazabach (altar) of Alahayam, to Al, my shamachah (exceeding) gayal (joy). I will yadah (praise) you on the kanawar (harp), Alahayam, my Alahayam.
Why are you in despair, my napash (soul)? Why are you disturbed within me? Yachal (hope) in Alahayam! For I shall still yadah (praise) him: my Savior, my helper, and my Alahayam.
We have shamai (hearken / hear) with our azan (ear), Alahayam; our ab (father) have sapar (book) us, what pail (work) you pail (did) in their yamay (days), in the yamay (days) of qadam (old).
You yarash (drove) out the gawayam (nations) with your yad (hand), but you natai (planted) them. You raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) the laamayam (peoples), but you shalach (send) them abroad.

For they didn't yarash (get) the aratz (Earth/land) in yarash (possession) by their own charab (sword), neither did their own zarawai (arm) yashai (salvation) them; but your right yamayan (right hand), and your zarawai (arm), and the awar (light) of your panayam (face), because you were favorable to them.
You are my malak (king), Alahayam. Tzawah (command) victories for Yaiqab (Jacob)!
Through you, will we nagach (push) down our tzar (oppressor / distressor). Through your sham (name), will we bawas (tread) them under who qawam (rise up) up against us.
For I will not batach (trust) in my qashath (bow), neither shall my charab (sword) yashai (salvation) me.
But you have yashai (salvation) us from our tzar (oppressor / distressor), and have bawash (shamed) those who shanaa (hate) us.
In Alahayam we have halal (praise) our boast all yawam (day) long, we will give nawadah (thanks) to your sham (name) iwalam (forever). Salah (selah).
But now you rejected us, and brought us to dishonor, and don't yatzaa (go out / come out) out with our tzabaa (troop).
You make us shawab (turn back / repent) achawar (back) from the tzar (oppressor / distressor). Those who shanaa (hate) us take shasah (spoil) for themselves.
You nathan (give) made us like tzaan (sheep) for maakal (food), and have zarah (scattered) us among the gawayam (nations).
You makar (sell) your im (nation / people) for nothing, and have gained nothing from their sale.
You shawam (place / establish / appoint) us a charapah (reproach) to our neighbors, a scoffing and a qalas (derision) to those who are around us.
You shawam (place / establish / appoint) us a mashal (byword) among the gawayam (nations), a manawad (shaking) of the raash (head) among the amayam (peoples).
All bashath (day) long my dishonor is before me, and bashath (shame) kasah (covers) my panayam (face),
At the taunt of charap (one) who reproaches and verbally abuses, panayam (face) of the ayab (enemy) and the avenger.
All this bawaa (come) come on us, yet have we not shakach (forgotten) you, Neither have we been false to your barayath (covenant).
Our lab (heart) has not sawag (turned) achawar (back), neither have our ashar (who/that) strayed from your arach (path),
Though you have crushed us in the haunt of jackals, and kasah (covered) us with the shadow of tzalamawath (death).
If we have shakach (forgotten) the sham (name) of our Alahayam, or parash (spread) forth our kap (hands) to a zawar (strange) Al;
Won't Alahayam chaqar (search) this out? For he yadai (knows) the thailamawath (secrets) of the lab (heart).
Yes, for your sake we are harag (kill) all yawam (day) long. We are chashab (regarded) as tzaan (sheep) for the tabachah (slaughter).
Iwar (rouse / awaken) up! Why do you sleep, Adanay? Arise! Don't reject us natzach (forever).
Why do you sathar (hide) your panayam (face), and shakach (forget) our inay (affliction) and our lachatz (oppression)?
For our napash (soul) is shawach (bowed) down to the ipar (dust). Our batan (body) clings to the aratz (Earth/land).
Qawam (rise up) up to izarah (help) us. Padah (redeem) us for your loving chasad (grace)' sake.
My lab (heart) overflows with a noble theme. I recite my verses for the malak (king). My lashawan (tongue / language) is like the it (pen) of a skillful sapar (book).
You are the most excellent of the banay (sons) of adam (men). Chan (favor) has yatzaq (anointed) your shapah (lips), therefore Alahayam has barak (blessed) you iwalam (forever).
Strap your charab (sword) on your yarak (thigh), gabawar (mighty) hawad (one): your splendor and your hadar (glory / majesty / splendor).

In your hadar (glory / majesty / splendor) rakab (ride) on victoriously on behalf of amath (truth), humility, and tzadaq (righteous / just / fair). Let your right yamayan (right hand) display awesome deeds.
Your chatz (arrows) are shanan (sharp). The imayam (nations) napal (fall / be cast down) under you, with arrows in the lab (heart) of the malak (king) awayabay (enemies).
Your kasaa (throne), Alahayam, is id (until / as far as) and iwalam (forever). A scepter of mayashawar (equity) is the scepter of your malakawath (kingdom).

You have ahab (love) tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and shanaa (hate) rashai (wickedness). Therefore Alahayam, your Alahayam, has mashach (anointed) you with the shaman (oil) of shashawan (gladness) above your chabar (fellows).
All your bagad (garments) smell like mar (myrrh), ahalawath (aloes), and qatzayaih (cassia). Out of shan (ivory) hayakalay (palaces) man (from) instruments shamach (have) made you glad.
Malakayam (kings)' banawath (daughters) are among your honorable yaqar (women). At your right yamayan (right hand) the shagal (queen) natzab (stands) in katham (gold) of Awapayar (Ophir).
Shamai (hearken / hear), banath (daughter), raah (see), and natah (turn) your azan (ear). Shakach (forget) your own im (nation / people), and also your ab (father) bayath (house).
So the malak (king) will awah (desire) your yapay (beauty), honor him, for he is your Adawan.
The banath (daughter) of Tzar (Tyre) comes with a manachah (gift). The ishayar (rich) among the im (nation / people) entreat your favor.
The banath (daughter) inside is kabawadah (all) glorious. Her labawash (clothing) is interwoven with zahab (gold).
She shall be yabal (led) to the malak (king) in embroidered raqamah (work). The bathawalawath (virgins), her raih (companions) who achar (other) her, shall be bawaa (come) to you.
With shamachah (gladness) and gayal (rejoicing) they shall be yabal (led). They shall bawaa (come) into the malak (king) hayakal (palace).
Your ban (son) will take the place of your ab (father). You shall shayath (put / appoint / make) them sharayam (princes) in all the aratz (Earth/land).
I will make your sham (name) to be zakar (remember) in all dawar (generation / age / period). Therefore the imayam (peoples) shall give you yadah (thanks) iwalam (forever) and iwalam (forever).
Alahayam is our machasah (refuge) and iz (strength / might / refuge), a very matzaa (present) izarah (help) in tzarah (trouble).
Therefore we won't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), though the aratz (Earth/land) mawar (changes), though the harayam (mountains) are mawat (shaken) into the lab (heart) of the yamayam (seas);
Though its mayam (Waters) hamah (great uproar) and are chamar (troubled), though the harayam (mountains) raish (tremble) with their gaawah (swelling). Salah (selah).
There is a nahar (river), the palag (streams) of which make the iyar (city) of Alahayam shamach (glad), the qadawash (holy) place of the mashakanay (tents) of the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan).
Alahayam is in her qarab (among / near). She shall not be mawat (moved). Alahayam will izar (help) her at dawn.
The gawayam (nations) hamah (great uproar). The mamalakawath (kingdoms) were mawat (moved). He nathan (give) his qawal (sound / voice), and the aratz (Earth/land) mawag (melted).
Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) is with us. The Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob) is our refuge. Salah (selah).
Yalak (come), chazah (see) Yahawah mapailawath (works), what shamawath (desolations) he has shawam (place / establish / appoint) in the aratz (Earth/land).

He makes malachamawath (wars) shabath (shabath / rest) to the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land). He shabar (breaks) the qashath (bow), and shatters the chanayath (spear). He sharap (burns) the igalawath (chariots) in the ash (fire).
"Be still, and yadai (know) that I am Alahayam. I will be rawam (will lift up) among the gawayam (nations). I will be rawam (will lift up) in the aratz (Earth/land)."
Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) is with us. The Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob) is our refuge. Mashagab (selah).
Oh thaqai (blow / sound alarm) your kap (hands), all you imayam (nations). Rawai (shout) to Alahayam with the qawal (sound / voice) of ranah (triumph)!
For Yahawah Most ilayawan (Ilayawan) is awesome. He is a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) malak (king) over all the aratz (Earth/land).
He dabar (word / matter) imayam (nations) under us, and imayam (peoples) under our ragal (feet / foot).
He bachar (chooses) our nachalah (inheritance) for us, the glory of Yaiqab (Jacob) whom he ahab (love). Salah (selah).
Alahayam has ilah (go up / offer) up with a tharawaih (shout), Yahawah with the qawal (sound / voice) of a shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn).
Sing zamar (praise) to Alahayam, sing zamaraw (praises). Sing zamaraw (praises) to our malak (king), sing zamaraw (praises).
For Alahayam is the malak (king) of all the aratz (Earth/land). Sing zamaraw (praises) with shakal (understanding).
Alahayam malak (king) over the gawayam (nations). Alahayam yashab (inhabit/dwell) on his qadash (set apart / make holy) kasaa (throne).

The nadayabay (princes) of the imayam (peoples) are asap (gathered) together, the imayam (people) of the Alahayam of Abaraham (Abraham). For the maganay (shields) of the aratz (Earth/land) belong to Alahayam. He is maad (greatly) ilah (go up / offer)!
Gadawal (very great/important/mighty) is Yahawah, and maad (greatly) to be halal (praise), in the iyar (city) of our Alahayam, in his qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain).

Yapah (beautiful) in elevation, the mashawash (joy) of the whole aratz (Earth/land), is har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion), on the tzapawan (north) yarakathay (sides), the qarayah (city / town) of the rab (great) malak (king).
Alahayam yadai (has) shown himself in her citadels as a refuge.
For, behold, the malakayam (kings) yaid (assembled) themselves, they ibar (pass over/through) by yachad (together).
They raah (see) it, then they were thamah (amazed). They were bahal (dismayed). They hurried away.
Raid (trembling) achaz (took) hold of them there, chayal (pain), as of a yalad (birth / begot) in travail.
With the qadayam (east) rawach (spirit / wind), you shabar (break) the anayawath (ships) of Tharashayash (Tarshish).

As we have shamai (hearken / hear), so we raah (see) seen, in the iyar (city) of Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), in the iyar (city) of our Alahayam. Alahayam will kawan (establish) it iwalam (forever). Salah (selah).
We have damah (thought) about your loving chasad (grace), Alahayam, in the qarab (among / near) of your hayakal (temple).
As is your sham (name), Alahayam, so is your thahalah (praise) to the qatzaway (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land). Your right yamayan (right hand) is malaa (full) of tzadaq (righteous / just / fair).
Let har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion) be gayal (glad)! Let the banawath (daughters) of Yahawadah (Judah) gayal (rejoice), Because of your mashapat (judgments).
Sabab (walk) about Tzayawan (Zion), and naqap (go) around her. Sapar (book) its magadal (towers).
Shayath (put / appoint / make) lab (heart) her chayalah (bulwarks). Pasag (consider) her aramawan (palaces), that you may sapar (book) it to the next dawar (generation / age / period).
For this Alahayam is our Alahayam iwalam (forever) and iwalam (forever). He will be our nahag (guide) even to mawath (death).
Shamai (hearken / hear) this, all you imayam (peoples). Shamai (hearken / hear), all you yashabay (inhabitants) of the chalad (world),
Both low and high, ishayar (rich) and abayawan (poor) yachad (together).
My pah (mouth) will dabar (word / matter) words of chakamawath (wisdom). My lab (heart) shall utter thabawan (understanding).
I will natah (incline) my azan (ear) to a mashal (proverb). I will pathach (open) my chayadah (riddle) on the kanawar (harp).
Why should I yaraa (fear / be afraid) in the yamay (days) of rai (evil), when iwan (guilt/iniquity) at my iqab (heels) surrounds me?
Those who batach (trust) in their wealth, and halal (praise) in the rab (multitude) of their riches—
Ayash (man / husband) of them can by any padah (means) padah (redeem) his ach (brother/kinsman), nor nathan (give) Alahayam a kapar (ransom) for him.
For the padayawam (redemption) of their napash (soul) is costly, no payment is iwalam (forever) enough,
That he should chayah (live) on natzach (forever), that he should not raah (see) shachath (corruption).
For he raah (see) that chakam (wise) men mawath (death); yachad (likewise) the kasayal (fool) and the senseless abad (destroy / perish), and izab (leave) their wealth to others.

Their qarab (among / near) thought is that their bayath (house) will endure iwalam (forever), and their mashakan (dwelling) places to all dawar (generation / age / period). They qaraa (called) their adamawath (lands) after themselves.
But adam (man), despite his riches, doesn't lawan (endure). He is mashal (speak in proverb/parable) the animals that damah (perish).
This is the destiny of those who are foolish, and of those who ratzah (approve) their pah (sayings). Salah (selah).

They are appointed as a tzaan (flock) for shaawal (Sheol / afterlife). Mawath (death) shall be their raih (shepherd). The yashar (upright) shall radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) dominion over them in the baqar (morning). Their beauty shall decay in shaawal (Sheol / afterlife), far from their mansion.
But Alahayam will padah (redeem) my napash (soul) from the yad (hand) of shaawal (Sheol / afterlife), for he will laqach (take / seize) me. Salah (selah).
Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) when a ayash (man / husband) is ishar (made) rich, when the kabawad (glory) of his bayath (house) is rabah (increased).
For when he mawath (death) he shall laqach (take / seize) nothing away. His kabawad (glory) shall not descend achar (other) him.
Though while he chay (life) he barak (blessed) his napash (soul)— and men yadah (praise) you when you yatab (do) well for yourself—
He shall bawaa (come) to the dawar (generation / age / period) of his ab (father). They shall laa (NOT) raah (see) the awar (light).
A adam (man) who has riches without bayan (between), is mashal (speak in proverb/parable) the animals that damah (perish).
The al (Alahayam) One, Alahayam, Yahawah, dabar (word / matter), and qaraa (called) the aratz (Earth/land) from sunrise to sunset.
Out of Tzayawan (Zion), the makalal (perfection) of yapay (beauty), Alahayam yapai (shines) forth.
Our Alahayam bawaa (come), and does not charash (keep) silent. A ash (fire) akal (eat) panayam (face) him. It is very stormy around him.
He qaraa (called) to the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) il (over), to the aratz (Earth/land), that he may dayan (judge) his im (nation / people):
"Asap (gather) my chasayad (saints) together to me, those who have karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with me by zabach (sacrifice)."
The shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) shall nagad (declare) his tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), for Alahayam himself is shapat (judge / judgement). Salah (selah).
"Shamai (hearken / hear), my im (nation / people), and I will dabar (word / matter); Yashar-Al (Israel), and I will testify against you. I am Alahayam, your Alahayam.
I don't yakach (rebuke) you for your zabach (sacrifices). Your burnt ilah (offerings) are continually before me.
I have no need for a par (bull) from your stall, nor male ithawadayam (goats) from your pens.
For every animal of the yair (forest) is mine, and the livestock on a alap (thousand) hararay (hills).
I yadai (know) all the iwap (flying) of the harayam (mountains). The zayaz (wild) animals of the shadah (field) are imad (mine).
If I were raib (hungry), I would not amar (spoke) you, for the thabal (world) is mine, and malaa (all) that is in it.
Will I akal (eat) the bashar (flesh) of abayarayam (bulls), or shathah (drinks) the dam (blood) of ithawadayam (goats)?
Zabach (offer) to Alahayam the thawadah (sacrifice) of thanksgiving. Shalam (pay) your nadar (vow) to the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan).
Qaraa (called) on me in the yawam (day) of tzarah (trouble). I will chalatz (deliver) you, and you will honor me."
But to the rashai (wicked) Alahayam amar (spoke), "What right do you have to sapar (book) my chaq (statute), that you have nashaa (lift) my barayath (covenant) on your lips,
Since you shanaa (hate) mawasar (instruction), and shalak (throw) my dabar (word / matter) achar (other) you?
When you raah (see) a ganab (thief), you ratzah (consented) with him, and have participated with manaapayam (adulterers).
"You shalach (send) your pah (mouth) to rai (evil). Your lashawan (tongue / language) tzamad (frames) maramah (deceit).
You yashab (inhabit/dwell) and dabar (word / matter) against your ach (brother/kinsman). You slander your own am (mother) ban (son).
You ishah (make) done these things, and I charash (kept) silent. You damah (thought) that I was just like you. I will yakach (rebuke) you, and accuse you in front of your iyan (eye).
"Now bayan (between) this, you who shakach (forget) Alawah, lest I tarap (tear) you into pieces, and there be none to natzal (deliver).
Whoever zabach (offers) the thawadah (sacrifice) of thanksgiving kabad (glorifies) me, and prepares his darak (way) so that I will show Alahayam yashai (salvation) to him."

Have chanan (showing favor) on me, Alahayam, according to your loving chasad (grace). According to the rab (multitude) of your tender racham (show mercy / love), machah (blot) out my pashai (transgressions).
Kabas (wash) me rabah (thoroughly) from my iwan (guilt/iniquity). Tahar (cleanse) me from my chataah (sin).
For I yadai (know) my pashai (transgressions). My chataah (sin) is constantly before me.

Against you, and you only, have I chataa (sinned), and ishah (make) that which is rai (evil) in your iyan (eye); that you may be proved right when you dabar (word / matter), and justified when you shapat (judge / judgement).
Behold, I was chawal (brought) forth in iwan (guilt/iniquity). In chataa (sin) my am (mother) yacham (conceived) me.
Behold, you chapatz (desire) amath (truth) in the tachah (inward) parts. You yadai (teach) me chakamah (wisdom) in the inmost place.
Chataa (purify) me with azawab (hyssop), and I will be tahar (clean). Kabas (wash) me, and I will be laban (whiter) than shalag (snow).
Shamai (hearken / hear) me hear shashawan (joy) and shashawan (gladness), That the itzamawath (bones) which you have dakah (broken) may gayal (rejoice).
Sathar (hide) your panayam (face) from my chataa (sins), and machah (blot) out all of my iwan (guilt/iniquity).
Baraa (created) in me a tahawar (clean) lab (heart), O Alahayam. Chadash (renew) a kawan (right) rawach (spirit / wind) qarab (among / near) me.
Don't shalak (throw) me from your panayam (face), and don't laqach (take / seize) your qadash (set apart / make holy) rawach (spirit / wind) from me.
Shawab (turn back / repent) to me the shashawan (joy) of your yashai (salvation). Samak (uphold) me with a nadayab (willing) rawach (spirit / wind).
Then I will lamad (teach / instruct) transgressors your darak (ways). Chataayam (sinners) shall be shawab (turn back / repent) to you.
Natzal (deliver) me from bloodguiltiness, O Alahayam, the Alahayam of my thashawaih (deliverance). My lashawan (tongue / language) shall ranan (sing) aloud of your tzadaqah (righteousness).
Adanay, pathach (open) my shapah (lips). My pah (mouth) shall nagad (declare) your thahalah (praise).
For you don't chapatz (delight) in zabach (sacrifice), or else I nathan (give) give it. You ratzah (have) no pleasure in burnt ilah (offering).
The zabachay (sacrifices) of Alahayam are a shabar (broken) rawach (spirit / wind). A shabar (broken) and dakah (contrite) lab (heart), O Alahayam, you will not bazah (despise).
Do well in your yatab (good) ratzawan (pleasure) to Tzayawan (Zion). Banah (build) the chawamawath (walls) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

Then you chapatz (will) delight in the zabachay (sacrifices) of tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), in burnt ilah (offerings) and in kalayal (whole) burnt ilah (offerings). Then they will ilah (go up / offer) parayam (bulls) on your mazabach (altar).
Why do you halal (praise) of rai (mischief), gabawar (mighty) man? Al loving chasad (grace) endures yawam (day).
Your lashawan (tongue / language) plots destruction, like a latash (sharp) thair (razor), ishah (make) deceitfully.
You ahab (love) rai (evil) more than tawab (good / proper function), shaqar (lying) rather than dabar (word / matter) the tzadaq (righteous / just / fair). Salah (selah).
You ahab (love) all balai (devouring) dabaray (words), you deceitful lashawan (tongue / language).

Al will likewise nathatz (destroy) you natzach (forever). He will chathah (take) you up, and nasach (pluck) you out of your ahal (tent), and sharash (root) you out of the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life). Salah (selah).
The tzadayaq (righteous) also will raah (see) it, and yaraa (fear / be afraid), and shachaq (laugh) at him, saying,

"Behold, this is the gabar (man) who didn't shawam (place / establish / appoint) Alahayam his maiwaz (stronghold / fortress / protection), but batach (trusted) in the rab (abundance) of his riches, and izaz (strengthened) himself in his hawah (calamity / destruction)."
But as for me, I am like a rainan (green) zayath (olive) tree in Alahayam bayath (house). I batach (trust) in Alahayam loving chasad (grace) iwalam (forever) and id (until / as far as).

I will give you yadah (thanks) iwalam (forever), because you ishah (make) done it. I will hope in your sham (name), for it is tawab (good / proper function), in the presence of your chasayad (saints).

The nabal (fool) has amar (spoke) in his lab (heart), "There is no Alahayam." They are shachath (corrupt), and have thaib (done) abominable iwal (iniquity). There is no one who ishah (make) tawab (good / proper function).
Alahayam shaqap (looks) down from shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) on the banay (children) of adam (men), to raah (see) if there are any who shakal (understood), who darash (seek) after Alahayam.
Every one of them has sawag (gone) back. They have alach (become) filthy yachad (together). There is no one who ishah (make) tawab (good / proper function), no, not achad (one).
Have the pailay (workers) of awan (iniquity) no yadai (knowledge), who akal (eat) up my im (nation / people) as they akal (eat) lacham (bread), and don't qaraa (called) on Alahayam?

There they were in pachad (fear / dread) pachad (fear / dread), where no pachad (fear / dread) was, for Alahayam has pazar (scattered) the itzamawath (bones) of him who chanah (encamps) against you. You have bawash (put) them to shame, because Alahayam has maas (rejected) them.

Oh that the yashawaih (salvation) of Yashar-Al (Israel) would come out of Tzayawan (Zion)! When Alahayam shawab (turn back / repent) back his im (nation / people) from shabawath (captivity), then Yaiqab (Jacob) shall gayal (rejoice), and Yashar-Al (Israel) shall be shamach (glad).
Yashai (salvation) me, Alahayam, by your sham (name). Vindicate me in your gabawarah (might).
Shamai (hearken / hear) my thapalah (prayer), Alahayam. Listen to the amaray (words) of my pah (mouth).

For strangers have qawam (rise up) up against me. Irayatz (violent) men have baqash (sought) after my napash (soul). They haven't shawam (place / establish / appoint) Alahayam before them. Salah (selah).
Behold, Alahayam is my helper. The Adanay is the napash (soul) who sustains my napash (soul).
He will repay the rai (evil) to my sharar (enemies). Tzamath (destroy) them in your amath (truth).
With a free will nadabah (voluntary / freewill offering), I will zabach (sacrifice) to you. I will give yadah (thanks) to your sham (name), Yahawah, for it is tawab (good / proper function).
For he has natzal (delivered) me out of all tzarah (trouble). My iyan (eye) raah (see) seen triumph over my ayab (enemy).
Listen to my thapalah (prayer), Alahayam. Don't ilam (hide) yourself from my thachanah (supplication).
Qashab (attend) to me, and inah (answer / respond) me. I am restless in my shayach (complaint), and moan,

Because of the qawal (sound / voice) of the ayab (enemy), panayam (face) of the iqah (oppression) of the rashai (wicked). For they bring suffering on me. In ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) they hold a grudge shatam (against) me.
My lab (heart) is severely chawal (pained) qarab (among / near) me. The ayamawath (terrors) of mawath (death) napal (fall / be cast down) fallen on me.
Yaraah (fearfulness) and raid (trembling) bawaa (come) come on me. Palatzawath (horror) has kasah (overwhelmed) me.
I amar (spoke), "Oh that I had abar (wings) like a yawanah (dove)! Then I would iwap (flying) away, and be at shakan (place).
Behold, then I would nadad (wander) rachaq (far) off. I would lawan (lodge) in the madabar (wilderness)." Salah (selah).
"I would hurry to a shelter from the stormy rawach (spirit / wind) and saih (storm)."
Confuse them, Adanay, and palag (confound) their lashawan (tongue / language), for I raah (see) seen chamas (violence) and rayab (strife) in the iyar (city).
Yawamam (by day) and layal (night) they prowl around on its chawamah (walls). Malice and abuse are also qarab (among / near) her.
Destructive forces are qarab (among / near) her. Threats and lies don't depart from her rachab (streets).

For it was not an ayab (enemy) who insulted me, then I could have endured it. Neither was it he who shanaa (hate) me who raised himself up against me, then I would have sathar (hidden) myself from him.
But it was you, a anawash (man) like me, my companion, and my yadai (familiar) friend.
We mathaq (took) sweet fellowship yachad (together). We halak (move) in Alahayam bayath (house) with ragash (company).

Let yashayamah (death) come suddenly on them. Yarad (let) them go down chay (life) into shaawal (Sheol / afterlife). For rai (wickedness) is in their magawar (dwelling), in their qarab (among / near).
As for me, I will qaraa (called) on Alahayam. Yahawah will yashai (salvation) me.
Irab (evening), baqar (morning), and at tzahar (noon), I will cry out in distress. He will shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice).
He has padah (redeemed) my napash (soul) in shalawam (peace / safety) from the qarab (battle) that was against me, although there are many who oppose me.
Al, who is enthroned qadam (forever), will shamai (hearken / hear), and inah (oppress / afflict) them. Salah (selah). They never chalayapah (change), who don't yaraa (fear / be afraid) Alahayam.
He raises his yad (hand) against his shalawam (peace / safety). He has violated his barayath (covenant).

His pah (mouth) was chalaq (smooth) as machamaah (butter), but his lab (heart) was qarab (war). His dabar (word / matter) were rakak (softer) than shaman (oil), yet they were drawn pathachawath (swords).
Shalak (cast) your yahab (burden) on Yahawah, and he will kawal (all) you. He will iwalam (forever) allow the tzadayaq (righteous) to be mawat (moved).

But you, Alahayam, will yarad (bring) them down into the baar (pit) of shachath (destruction). Bloodthirsty and deceitful anashay (men) shall not chatzah (live) out half their yawam (day), but I will batach (trust) in you.
Be chanan (showing favor) to me, Alahayam, for anawash (man) wants to shaap (swallow) me up. All yawam (day) long, he attacks and oppresses me.
My sharar (enemies) want to shaap (swallow) me up all yawam (day) long, for they are many who lacham (fight) proudly against me.
When I am yaraa (fear / be afraid), I will batach (put) my trust in you.
In Alahayam, I halal (praise) his dabar (word / matter). In Alahayam, I batach (put) my trust. I will not be yaraa (fear / be afraid). What can bashar (flesh) ishah (make) to me?
All yawam (day) long they twist my dabar (word / matter). All their machashabah (thoughts) are against me for rai (evil).
They conspire and tzapan (lurk), shamar (keep/guard) my iqab (steps), they are eager to take my napash (soul).
Shall they palat (escape) by awan (iniquity)? In ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) yarad (cast) down the imayam (peoples), Alahayam.
You sapar (book) my nawad (wanderings). You shawam (place / establish / appoint) my damaih (tears) into your naad (bottle). Aren't they in your sapar (book / scribed document)?
Then my ayab (enemy) shall shawab (turn back / repent) achawar (back) in the yawam (day) that I qaraa (called). I yadai (know) this, that Alahayam is for me.
In Alahayam, I will halal (praise) his dabar (word / matter). In Yahawah, I will halal (praise) his dabar (word / matter).
I have batach (put) my trust in Alahayam. I will not be yaraa (fear / be afraid). What can adam (man) ishah (make) to me?
Your nadar (vow) are on me, Alahayam. I will shalam (give) thank thawadath (offerings) to you.

For you have natzal (delivered) my napash (soul) from mawath (death), and prevented my ragal (feet / foot) from dachay (falling), that I may halak (move) panayam (face) Alahayam in the awar (light) of the chay (life).

Be chanan (showing favor) to me, Alahayam, be chanan (showing favor) to me, for my napash (soul) takes chasah (refuge) in you. Yes, in the tzal (shadow) of your kanap (wings), I will take chasah (refuge), until disaster ibar (pass over/through) passed.
I qaraa (called) out to Alahayam Most ilayawan (Ilayawan), to Al who accomplishes my requests for me.

He will shalach (send) from shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and yashai (salvation) me, he rebukes the shaap (one) who is pursuing me. Salah (selah). Alahayam will shalach (send) out his loving chasad (grace) and his amath (truth).

My napash (soul) is thawak (midst) labaam (lions). I shakab (lie) among those who are set on lahat (fire), even the banay (sons) of adam (men), whose shan (teeth) are chanayath (spears) and chatzayam (arrows), and their lashawan (tongue / language) a chad (sharp) charab (sword).
Be rawam (will lift up), Alahayam, above the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens)! Let your kabawad (glory) be above all the aratz (Earth/land)!

They have kawan (prepared) a rashath (net) for my paim (steps). My napash (soul) is kapap (bowed) down. They karah (dig) a shayachah (pit) panayam (face) me. They napal (fall / be cast down) into its thawak (midst) themselves. Salah (selah).
My lab (heart) is steadfast, Alahayam, my lab (heart) is steadfast. I will shayar (sing), yes, I will sing zamar (praises).
Iwar (rouse / awaken) up, my kabawad (glory)! Iwar (rouse / awaken) up, nabal (psaltery) and harp! I will iwar (rouse / awaken) up the dawn.
I will give yadah (thanks) to you, Adanay, among the imayam (peoples). I will zamar (sing) praises to you among the amayam (nations).
For your gadawal (very great/important/mighty) loving chasad (grace) reaches to the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and your amath (truth) to the shachaqayam (skies).
Be rawam (will lift up), Alahayam, above the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens). Let your kabawad (glory) be over all the aratz (Earth/land).
Do you indeed dabar (word / matter) tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), silent alam (ones)? Do you shapat (judge / judgement) blamelessly, you banay (sons) of adam (men)?
No, in your lab (heart) you plot injustice. You measure out the chamas (violence) of your yad (hand) in the aratz (Earth/land).
The rashai (wicked) zawar (go) astray from the racham (womb). They are wayward as soon as they are batan (born), dabar (word / matter) kazab (lies).
Their chamah (poison) is damawath (like) the chamah (poison) of a snake; like a charash (deaf) cobra that atam (stops) its azan (ear),
Which doesn't shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of malachashayam (charmers), no matter how skillful the chabar (charmer) may be.
Haras (break) their shan (teeth), Alahayam, in their pah (mouth). Nathatz (break) out the malathaih (great) teeth of the young kapayarayam (lions), Yahawah.
Let them vanish as mayam (Waters) that flows maas (away). When they darak (draw) the bow, let their chatz (arrows) be made blunt.
Let them be like a shabalawal (snail) which thamas (melts) and passes halak (move), like the stillborn child, who has not chazah (seen) the shamash (sun).
Before your sayar (pots) can bayan (between) the heat of the atad (thorns), he will sweep away the green and the burning alike.
The tzadayaq (righteous) shall shamach (rejoice) when he chazah (sees) the naqam (vengeance). He shall rachatz (wash) his paim (feet) in the dam (blood) of the rashai (wicked);
So that adam (men) shall amar (spoke), "Most certainly there is a paray (reward) for the tzadayaq (righteous). Most certainly there is a Alahayam who shapatayam (judges) the aratz (Earth/land)."
Natzal (deliver) me from my ayab (enemy), my Alahayam. Shagab (set) me on high from those who qawam (rise up) up against me.
Natzal (deliver) me from the pailay (workers) of awan (iniquity). Yashai (salvation) me from the bloodthirsty anashay (men).
For, behold, they lie in arab (wait) for my napash (soul). The iz (mighty) gawar (gather) themselves together against me, not for my disobedience, nor for my chataah (sin), Yahawah.
I have done no wrong, yet they are kawan (ready) to attack me. Iwar (rouse / awaken) up, raah (see), and qaraah (help) me!

You, Yahawah Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies), the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), rouse yourself to paqad (visit) the gawayam (nations). Show no chanan (showing favor) to the awan (wicked) traitors. Salah (selah).
They shawab (turn back / repent) at irab (evening), howling like kalab (dogs), and prowl around the iyar (city).
Behold, they spew with their pah (mouth). Charabawath (swords) are in their shapah (lips), "For," they say, "who shamai (hearken / hear) us?"
But you, Yahawah, shachaq (laugh) at them. You scoff at all the gawayam (nations).
Oh, my iz (strength / might / refuge), I shamar (keep/guard) for you, for Alahayam is my high tower.
My Alahayam will qadam (go) before me with his loving chasad (grace). Alahayam will raah (see) me look at my sharar (enemies) in triumph.

Don't harag (kill) them, or my im (nation / people) may shakach (forget). Nawai (scatter) them by your chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), and yarad (bring) them down, Adanay our magan (shield).

For the chataah (sin) of their pah (mouth), and the dabar (word / matter) of their shapah (lips), let them be lakad (caught) in their gaawan (pride), for the alah (curse / oath) and kachash (lies) which they utter.

Kalah (complete / finish) them in chamah (wrath). Kalah (complete / finish) them, and they yadai (will) be no more. Let them know that Alahayam mashal (rule/have dominion) in Yaiqab (Jacob), to the apasay (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land). Salah (selah).
At irab (evening) let them shawab (turn back / repent). Let them howl like a kalab (dog), and sabab (go) around the iyar (city).
They shall nawai (wander) up and down for akal (eat), and wait all night if they aren't shabai (satisfied).

But I will shayar (sing) of your iz (strength / might / refuge). Yes, I will ranan (sing) aloud of your loving chasad (grace) in the baqar (morning). For you have been my high tower, a manawas (refuge) in the yawam (day) of my tzar (oppressor / distressor).
To you, my iz (strength / might / refuge), I will zamar (sing) praises. For Alahayam is my high tower, the Alahayam of my chasad (grace).
Alahayam, you have rejected us. You have paratz (broken) us down. You have been anap (angry). Shawab (turn back / repent) us, again.
You have made the aratz (Earth/land) raish (tremble). You have torn it. Mend its fractures, for it quakes.
You raah (see) shown your im (nation / people) qashah (rough / hard) things. You have shaqah (made) us drink the yayan (wine) that makes us stagger.
You nathan (give) given a nas (banner) to those who yaraa (fear) you, that it may be nawas (displayed) panayam (face) of the qashat (truth). Salah (selah).
So that your yadayad (beloved) may be chalatz (delivered), chalatz (save) with your right yamayan (right hand), and inah (oppress / afflict) us.

Alahayam has dabar (word / matter) from his qadash (set apart / make holy): "I will ilaz (triumph). I will chalaq (divide) Shakam (Shechem), and madad (measure) out the imaq (valley) of Sakawath (Succoth).
Galaid (Gilead) is mine, and Manashah (Manasseh) is mine. Aparayam (Ephraim) also is the defense of my raash (head). Yahawadah (Judah) is my scepter.
Mawaab (Moab) is my wash basin. I will shalak (throw) my nail (shoe) on Adawam (Edom). I rawai (shout) in triumph over Palashath (Philistia)."
Who will yabal (bring) me into the matzawar (strong) iyar (city)? Who has nachah (led) me to Adawam (Edom)?
Haven't you, Alahayam, rejected us? You don't go out with our armies, Alahayam.
Yahab (give) us izarah (help) against the tzar (oppressor / distressor), for the thashawaih (deliverance) of adam (man) is shawaa (vanity).
Through Alahayam we shall ishah (make) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), for it is he who will bawas (tread) down our tzar (oppressor / distressor).
Shamai (hearken / hear) my ranah (cry), Alahayam. Listen to my thapalah (prayer).

From the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land), I will qaraa (called) to you, when my lab (heart) is itap (overwhelmed). Nachah (lead) me to the tzawar (rock) that is higher than I.
For you have been a machasah (refuge) for me, a iz (strength / might / refuge) magadal (tower) from the ayab (enemy).
I will gawar (dwell) in your ahal (tent) iwalam (forever). I will take chasah (refuge) in the shelter of your kanap (wings). Salah (selah).
For you, Alahayam, have shamai (hearken / hear) my nadar (vow). You nathan (give) given me the yarashah (heritage) of those who yaraa (fear) your sham (name).
You will yasap (prolong) the malak (king) yawam (day); his shanah (years) shall be for dawar (generation / age / period).
He shall be enthroned in Alahayam panayam (face) iwalam (forever). Appoint your loving chasad (grace) and amath (truth), that they may natzar (preserve) him.
So I will zamar (sing) praise to your sham (name) id (until / as far as), that I may fulfill my nadar (vow) yawam (day).
My napash (soul) dawamayah (rests) in Alahayam alone. My yashawaih (salvation) is from him.
He alone is my tzawar (rock) and my yashawaih (salvation), my fortress— I will never be greatly mawat (shaken).
How long will you assault a ayash (man / husband), would all of you throw him down, Like a leaning qayar (wall), like a dachah (tottering) gadar (fence)?
They fully intend to throw him down from his lofty place. They ratzah (delight) in kazab (lies). They barak (blessed) with their pah (mouth), but they qalal (curse) inwardly. Salah (selah).
My napash (soul), damam (wait) in silence for Alahayam alone, for my thaqawah (expectation) is from him.
He alone is my tzawar (rock) and my yashawaih (salvation), my fortress. I will not be mawat (shaken).
With Alahayam is my yashai (salvation) and my honor. The tzawar (rock) of my iz (strength / might / refuge), and my machasah (refuge), is in Alahayam.
Batach (trust) in him at all ith (times), you im (nation / people). Shapak (pour) out your labab (heart) panayam (face) him. Alahayam is a machasah (refuge) for us. Salah (selah).

Surely adam (men) of low degree are just a habal (breath), and ayash (man / husband) of high degree are a kazab (lie). In the maazanayam (balances) they will go up. They are yachad (together) lighter than a habal (breath).
Don't batach (trust) in ishaq (oppression). Don't habal (become) vain in gazal (robbery). If riches nawab (increase), don't shayath (put / appoint / make) your lab (heart) on them.
Alahayam has dabar (word / matter) achad (one); shanayam (two) I have shamai (hearken / hear) zaw (this), that iz (strength / might / refuge) belongs to Alahayam.
Also to you, Adanay, belongs loving chasad (grace), for you shalam (reward) every ayash (man / husband) according to his maishah (work).

Alahayam, you are my Alahayam. I will earnestly shachar (seek) you. My napash (soul) tzamaa (thirsts) for you. My bashar (flesh) kamah (longs) for you, in a tzayah (dry) and iyap (weary) aratz (Earth/land), balay (where) there is no mayam (Waters).
So I have chazah (seen) you in the kabawad (sanctuary), watching your iz (strength / might / refuge) and your kabawad (glory).
Because your loving chasad (grace) is tawab (good / proper function) than chay (life), my shapah (lips) shall shabach (praise) you.
So I will barak (blessed) you while I chay (life). I will nashaa (lift) up my kap (hands) in your sham (name).
My napash (soul) shall be shabai (satisfied) as with the richest food. My pah (mouth) shall halal (praise) you with rananah (joyful) shapathay (lips),
When I zakar (remember) you on my yatzawai (bed), and think about you in the ashamarah (night) watches.
For you have been my izarah (help). I will ranan (rejoice) in the tzal (shadow) of your kanap (wings).
My napash (soul) stays dabaq (close) to you. Your right yamayan (right hand) thamak (holds) me up.
But those who baqash (seek) my napash (soul), to shawaa (vanity) it, shall bawaa (come) into the lower thachathayawath (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land).
They shall be given over to the yad (hand) of the sword. They shall be jackal food.

But the malak (king) shall shamach (rejoice) in Alahayam. Everyone who shabai (swear / take oath) by him will halal (praise) him, for the pah (mouth) of those who dabar (word / matter) shaqar (lies) shall be silenced.
Shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice), Alahayam, in my shayach (complaint). Natzar (preserve) my chay (life) from pachad (fear / dread) of the ayab (enemy).
Sathar (hide) me from the conspiracy of the raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil), from the noisy crowd of the ones pail (doing) awan (evil);
Who shanan (sharpen) their lashawan (tongue / language) like a charab (sword), and aim their chatz (arrows), deadly dabar (word / matter),
To yarah (shoot) innocent men from ambushes. They yarah (shoot) at him pathaawam (suddenly) and fearlessly.
They chazaq (encourage) themselves in rai (evil) plans. They sapar (book) about taman (laying) mawaqashayam (snares) secretly. They amar (spoke), "Who will raah (see) them?"
They plot injustice, saying, "We thamam (have) made a perfect plan!" Surely ayash (man / husband) qarab (among / near) and qarab (among / near) are cunning.
But Alahayam will yarah (shoot) at them. They will be pathaawam (suddenly) struck down with an chatz (arrow).
Their own lashawan (tongue / language) shall kashal (stumble / stagger) them. All who raah (see) them will shake their yathanadadaw (heads).
All mankind shall be yaraa (fear / be afraid). They shall nagad (declare) the pail (work) of Alahayam, and shall shakal (wisely) ponder what he has maishah (done).
The tzadayaq (righteous) shall be shamach (glad) in Yahawah, and shall take chasah (refuge) in him. All the yashar (upright) in lab (heart) shall halal (praise) him!
Thahalah (praise) waits for you, Alahayam, in Tzayawan (Zion). To you shall nadar (vow) be shalam (performed).
You who shamai (hearken / hear) thapalah (prayer), to you all men will bawaa (come).
Dabaray (sins) overwhelmed me, but you atoned for our pashai (transgressions).

Ashar (who/that) is one whom you bachar (choose), and cause to qarab (come close) near, that he may live in your chatzar (courts). We will be shabai (filled) with the goodness of your bayath (house), your qadawash (holy) hayakal (temple).

By awesome deeds of tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), you inah (answer / respond) us, Alahayam of our yashai (salvation). You who are the mabatach (hope) of all the qatzaway (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land), of those who are rachawaq (far) away on the yam (sea/waters);
Who by his kach (strength / mighty / power) forms the harayam (mountains), having armed yourself with gabawarah (strength);
Who stills the roaring of the yamayam (seas), the roaring of their gal (waves), and the turmoil of the laamayam (nations).

They also who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in faraway places are yaraa (fear / be afraid) at your awath (sign / mark / miracle). You call the baqar (morning) dawn and the irab (evening) with songs of ranan (joy).

You paqad (visit) the aratz (Earth/land), and shawaq (water) it. You greatly enrich it. The palag (river) of Alahayam is malaa (full) of mayam (Waters). You kawan (provide) them grain, for so you have kawan (ordained) it.
You drench its thalam (furrows). You nachath (level) its thalam (ridges). You soften it with rabayabayam (showers). You barak (blessed) it with a crop.
You itar (crown) the shanah (year) with your bounty. Your carts overflow with abundance.
The madabar (wilderness) grasslands overflow. The gabaiwath (hills) are clothed with gayal (gladness).
The karayam (pastures) are covered with tzaan (flocks). The imaqayam (valleys) also are clothed with grain. They rawai (shout) for joy! They also shayar (sing).
Rawai (make) a joyful shout to Alahayam, all the aratz (Earth/land)!
Zamar (sing) to the kabawad (glory) of his sham (name)! Offer kabawad (glory) and thahalah (praise)!
Amar (spoke) Alahayam, "How awesome are your maishah (deeds)! Through the greatness of your iz (strength / might / refuge), your ayab (enemy) kachash (submit) themselves to you.
All the aratz (Earth/land) will shachah (worship) you, and will zamar (sing) to you; they will zamar (sing) to your sham (name)." Salah (selah).
Yalak (come), and raah (see) Alahayam deeds— awesome mapail (work) on behalf of the banay (children) of adam (men).
He hapak (turned) the yam (sea/waters) into yabashah (dry land) land. They ibar (pass over/through) through the nahar (river) on ragal (feet / foot). There, we shamach (rejoiced) in him.

He mashal (rule/have dominion) by his gabawarah (might) iwalam (forever). His iyan (eye) tzapah (watchman / keep watch) the gawayam (nations). Don't let the sarar (rebellious) rawam (will lift up) up against him. Salah (selah).
Barak (blessed) our Alahayam, you imayam (peoples)! Make the qawal (sound / voice) of his thahalah (praise) shamai (hearken / hear),
Who shawam (place / establish / appoint) our napash (soul) among the chay (life), and doesn't allow our ragal (feet / foot) to be mawat (moved).
For you, Alahayam, have tested us. You have tzarap (refined) us, as kasap (silver) is tzarap (refined).
You bawaa (come) us into prison. You shawam (place / establish / appoint) a burden on our backs.
You allowed anawash (men) to rakab (ride) over our raash (head). We bawaa (come) through ash (fire) and through mayam (Waters), but you yatzaa (go out / come out) us to the place of abundance.
I will bawaa (come) into your bayath (house) with burnt iwalawath (offerings). I will shalam (pay) my nadar (vow) to you,
Which my shapah (lips) promised, and my pah (mouth) spoke, when I was in tzar (oppressor / distressor).

I will ilah (go up / offer) to you burnt ilawath (offerings) of fat animals, with the qatarath (offering) of ayalayam (rams), I will ishah (make) baqar (morning) with ithawadayam (goats). Salah (selah).
Yalak (come), and shamai (hearken / hear), all you who yaraa (fear) Alahayam. I will sapar (book) what he ishah (make) done for my napash (soul).
I qaraa (called) to him with my pah (mouth). He was rawamam (extolled) with my lashawan (tongue / language).
If I cherished sin in my lab (heart), the Adanay wouldn't have listened.
But most akan (certainly), Alahayam has shamai (hearken / hear). He has shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of my thapalah (prayer).
Barak (blessed) be Alahayam, who has not sawar (turned) away my thapalah (prayer), nor his loving chasad (grace) from me.
May Alahayam be chanan (showing favor) to us, barak (blessed) us, and cause his panayam (face) to awar (light) on us. Salah (selah).
That your darak (way) may be yadai (known) on aratz (Earth/land), and your yashawaih (salvation) among all gawayam (nations),
Let the imayam (peoples) yadah (praise) you, Alahayam. Let all the imayam (peoples) yadah (praise) you.

Oh let the laamayam (nations) be shamach (glad) and ranan (sing) for joy, for you will shapat (judge / judgement) the imayam (peoples) with mayashawar (equity), and nachah (govern) the laamayam (nations) on aratz (Earth/land). Salah (selah).
Let the imayam (peoples) yadah (praise) you, Alahayam. Let all the imayam (peoples) yadah (praise) you.
The aratz (Earth/land) nathan (give) yielded its yabawal (increase). Alahayam, even our own Alahayam, will barak (blessed) us.
Alahayam will barak (blessed) us. All the apasay (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land) shall yaraa (fear / be afraid) him.
Let Alahayam qawam (rise up)! Let his ayab (enemy) be pawatz (scattered)! Let them who shanaa (hate) him also nawas (flee) panayam (face) him.

As ishan (smoke) is nadap (driven) away, so nadap (drive) them away. As dawanag (wax) masas (melts) panayam (face) the ash (fire), so let the rashai (wicked) abad (destroy / perish) at the panayam (face) of Alahayam.
But let the tzadayaq (righteous) be shamach (glad). Let them ilatz (rejoice) panayam (face) Alahayam. Yes, let them shawash (rejoice) with shamachah (gladness).
Shayar (sing) to Alahayam! Sing zamaraw (praises) to his sham (name)! Salal (extol) him who rakab (rides) on the clouds: to Yah, his sham (name)! Ilaz (rejoice) panayam (face) him!
A ab (father) of the yathawam (fatherless), and a defender of the alamanawath (widows), is Alahayam in his qadash (set apart / make holy) maiwan (habitation).

Alahayam yashab (inhabit/dwell) the lonely in bayath (house). He yatzaa (go out / come out) out the asayarayam (prisoners) with singing, but the sarar (rebellious) shakan (place) in a sun-scorched tzachayachah (land).
Alahayam, when you yatzaa (go out / come out) forth panayam (face) your im (nation / people), when you tzaid (marched) through the yashayamawan (wilderness)... Salah (selah).
The aratz (Earth/land) raish (trembled). The sky also poured down rain at the panayam (face) of the Alahayam of Sayanay (Sinai)— at the panayam (face) of Alahayam, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel).
You, Alahayam, nawap (sent) a nadabah (voluntary / freewill offering) gasham (rain). You kawan (confirmed) your nachalah (inheritance), when it was laah (weary).
Your chay (life) lived therein. You, Alahayam, kawan (prepared) your goodness for the inay (poor).
The Adanay announced the amar (spoke). The mabasharawath (ones) who proclaim it are a rab (great) tzabaa (troop).
"Malakay (kings) of tzabaawath (armies) nadad (flee)! They nadad (flee)!" She who waits at bayath (house) chalaq (divides) the shalal (spoil),
While you sleep among the campfires, the kanapay (wings) of a yawanah (dove) sheathed with kasap (silver), her kanapay (feathers) with shining charawatz (gold).
When the Shaday parash (scattered) malakayam (kings) in her, it shalag (snow) on Tzalamawan (Zalmon).
The har (mountain) of Bashan are majestic har (mountain). The har (mountain) of Bashan (Bashan) are rugged.
Why do you look in envy, you rugged harayam (mountains), at the har (mountain) where Alahayam chooses to yashab (inhabit/dwell)? Yes, Yahawah will shakan (place) there natzach (forever).

The rakab (chariots) of Alahayam are rabathayam (tens) of thousands and rabathayam (thousands) of shanaan (thousands). The Adanay is among them, from Sayanay (Sinai), into the qadash (set apart / make holy).

You have ilah (go up / offer) on marawam (high). You have led shabay (away) shabay (captives). You have laqach (take / seize) mathanawath (gifts) among adam (men), yes, among the sarar (rebellious) also, that Yah Alahayam might shakan (place) there.
Barak (blessed) be the Adanay, who yawam (day) imas (bears) our burdens, even the Al who is our yashawaih (salvation). Salah (selah).
Al is to us a Al of deliverance. To Yahawah, the Adanay, belongs escape from mawath (death).
But Alahayam will machatz (crush / shatter) through the raash (head) of his ayab (enemy), the shair (hair) qadaqad (scalp) of such a halak (move) as still continues in his asham (guiltiness).
The Adanay amar (spoke), "I will shawab (turn back / repent) you again from Bashan (Bashan), I will shawab (turn back / repent) you again from the matzalawath (depths) of the yam (sea/waters);

That you may crush them, machatz (crush / shatter) your ragal (feet / foot) in dam (blood), that the lashawan (tongue / language) of your kalab (dogs) may have their portion from your ayabayam (enemies)."
They raah (see) seen your processions, Alahayam, even the processions of my Al, my malak (king), into the qadash (set apart / make holy).
The singers qadam (went) before, the minstrels achar (other) after, in the thawak (midst) of the ladies thapap (playing) with tambourines,
"Barak (blessed) Alahayam in the maqahalawath (congregations), even the Adanay in the maqawar (assembly) of Yashar-Al (Israel)!"

There is tzaiyar (little) Banayamayan (Benjamin), their radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue), the sharay (princes) of Yahawadah (Judah), their ragamah (council), the sharay (princes) of Zabawalawan (Zebulun), and the sharay (princes) of Napathalay (Naphtali).
Your Alahayam has tzawah (commanded) your iz (strength / might / refuge). Izaz (strengthen), Alahayam, that which you have pail (done) for us.
Because of your hayakal (temple) at Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), malakayam (kings) shall yabal (bring) shay (presents) to you.

Gair (rebuke) the wild animal of the qanah (reeds), the idah (multitude) of the abayarayam (bulls), with the calves of the imayam (peoples). Being rapas (humbled), may it bring bars of kasap (silver). Bazar (scatter) the imayam (nations) that chapatz (delight) in qarab (war).
Chashamanayam (princes) shall athah (you (masc)) out of Matzarayam (Egypt). Kawash (Ethiopia) shall hurry to stretch out her yad (hand) to Alahayam.
Shayar (sing) to Alahayam, you mamalakawath (kingdoms) of the aratz (Earth/land)! Sing zamaraw (praises) to the Adanay! Salah (selah).

To him who rakab (rides) on the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) of shamay (heavens), which are of qadam (old); behold, he nathan (give) his qawal (sound / voice), a iz (strength / might / refuge) qawal (sound / voice).
Nathan (give) iz (strength / might / refuge) to Alahayam! His gaawah (excellency) is over Yashar-Al (Israel), his iz (strength / might / refuge) is in the shachaqayam (skies).

You are awesome, Alahayam, in your maqadash (sanctuaries). The Al of Yashar-Al (Israel) nathan (give) iz (strength / might / refuge) and iz (strength / might / refuge) to his im (nation / people). Barak (blessed) be to Alahayam!
Yashai (salvation) me, Alahayam, for the mayam (Waters) bawaa (come) come up to my neck!
I tabai (sink) in matzawalah (deep) yawan (mire), where there is no foothold. I bawaa (come) come into maimaq (deep) mayam (Waters), where the shabal (floods) shatap (overflow) me.
I am yagai (weary) with my qaraa (called). My garawan (throat) is charar (dry). My iyan (eye) kalah (complete / finish), looking for my Alahayam.

Those who shanaa (hate) me chanam (without) a cause are more than the shairawath (hairs) of my raash (head). Those who want to tzamath (cut) me off, being my ayab (enemy) shaqar (wrongfully), are itzam (mighty). I have to shawab (turn back / repent) what I didn't gazal (take) away.
Alahayam, you yadai (know) my awalath (foolishness). My ashamah (sins) aren't kachad (hidden) from you.

Don't let those who qawah (gather/wait) for you be bawash (shamed) through me, Adanay Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies). Don't let those who baqash (seek) you be brought to dishonor through me, Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel).
Because for your sake, I have nashaa (lift) charapah (reproach). Kalamah (shame) has kasah (covered) my panayam (face).
I have become a stranger to my ach (brother/kinsman), an nakaray (alien) to my am (mother) banay (children).
For the qanaah (zeal) of your bayath (house) akal (eat) me. The reproaches of those who charap (reproach) you napal (fall / be cast down) fallen on me.
When I bakah (wept) and I tzawam (fasted), that was to my charapah (reproach).
When I nathan (give) sackcloth my labawash (clothing), I became a mashal (byword) to them.
Those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the shair (gate) shayach (meditate) about me. I am the nagayanah (song) of the drunkards.

But as for me, my thapalah (prayer) is to you, Yahawah, in an ratzawan (acceptable) ith (time). Alahayam, in the rab (abundance) of your loving chasad (grace), inah (answer / respond) me in the amath (truth) of your yashai (salvation).
Natzal (deliver) me out of the tayat (mire), and don't let me tabai (sink). Let me be natzal (delivered) from those who shanaa (hate) me, and out of the maimaq (deep) mayam (Waters).
Don't let the mayam (Waters) waters shatap (overwhelm) me, neither let the matzawalah (deep) balai (swallow) me up. Don't let the baar (pit) atar (shut) its pah (mouth) on me.
Inah (answer / respond) me, Yahawah, for your loving chasad (grace) is tawab (good / proper function). According to the rab (multitude) of your tender racham (show mercy / love), panah (turn) to me.
Don't sathar (hide) your panayam (face) from your ibad (servant), for I am in tzarar (distress). Inah (answer / respond) me mahar (speedily)!
Qarab (come close) near to my napash (soul), and gaal (redeem) it. Padah (ransom) me because of my ayab (enemy).
You yadai (know) my charapah (reproach), my charapah (shame), and my dishonor. My tzarar (adversaries) are all before you.

Charapah (reproach) has shabar (broken) my lab (heart), and I am nawash (full) of heaviness. I qawah (gather/wait) for some to nawad (take) pity, but there was none; for comforters, but I matzaa (found) none.
They also nathan (give) me raash (head) for my food. In my tzamaa (thirst), they gave me chamatz (vinegar) to shaqah (drink).
Let their shalachan (table) panayam (face) them become a pach (snare / trap). May it become a retribution and a mawaqash (trap).
Let their iyan (eye) be chashak (darkness), so that they can't raah (see). Let their backs be continually bent.
Shapak (pour) out your zaim (indignation) on them. Let the charawan (fierceness) of your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) nashag (overtake) them.
Let their tayarah (habitation) be shamam (desolate). Let no one yashab (inhabit/dwell) in their ahal (tents).
For they radap (persecute) him whom you have wounded. They sapar (book) of the makaab (sorrow) of those whom you have hurt.
Nathan (give) them with crime upon crime. Don't bawaa (come) them come into your tzadaqah (righteousness).
Let them be machah (blotted) out of the sapar (book / scribed document) of chay (life), and not be kathab (write) with the tzadayaq (righteous).
But I am in pain and distress. Let your yashawaih (salvation), Alahayam, protect me.
I will halal (praise) the sham (name) of Alahayam with a shayar (song), and will gadal (magnify) him with thanksgiving.
It will yatab (please) Yahawah yatab (better) than an shawar (ox), or a shawar (bull) that has qaran (horns) and paras (hoofs).
The inaw (humble) raah (see) seen it, and are shamach (glad). You who darash (seek) after Alahayam, let your labab (heart) chayah (live).
For Yahawah shamai (hearken / hear) the abayawan (needy), and doesn't bazah (despise) his captive asayar (people).
Let shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) and aratz (Earth/land) halal (praise) him; the yamayam (seas), and everything that ramash (moves) therein!
For Alahayam will yashai (salvation) Tzayawan (Zion), and banah (build) the iray (cities) of Yahawadah (Judah). They shall settle there, and own it.
The zarai (children) also of his ibad (servant) shall nachal (inherit) it. Those who ahab (love) his sham (name) shall shakan (place) therein.
Hurry, Alahayam, to natzal (deliver) me. Come quickly to izarah (help) me, Yahawah.
Let them be disappointed and chapar (confounded) who baqash (seek) my napash (soul). Let those who chapatz (desire) my ruin be sawag (turned) achawar (back) in disgrace.
Shawab (turn back / repent) them be turned iqab (award / effect after the cause) of their bashath (shame) Who amar (spoke), "haach (aha)! Haach (aha)!"
Let all those who baqash (seek) you shawash (rejoice) and be shamach (glad) in you. Let those who ahab (love) your yashawaih (salvation) continually amar (spoke), "Let Alahayam be exalted!"
But I am inay (poor) and abayawan (needy). Come to me quickly, Alahayam. You are my izar (help) and my deliverer. Yahawah, don't achar (other).
In you, Yahawah, I take chasah (refuge). Al (not) let me be disappointed.
Natzal (deliver) me in your tzadaqah (righteousness), and rescue me. Natah (turn) your azan (ear) to me, and yashai (salvation) me.
Be to me a tzawar (rock) of refuge to which I may thamayad (always) bawaa (come). Give the tzawah (command) to yashai (salvation) me, for you are my salai (rock) and my matzawad (fortress).
Rescue me, my Alahayam, from the yad (hand) of the rashai (wicked), from the yad (hand) of the unrighteous and chamatz (cruel) man.
For you are my thaqawah (hope), Adanay Yahawah; my mabatach (confidence) from my naiwar (youth).
I have relied on you from the batan (womb). You are he who gazah (took) me out of my am (mother) maih (womb). I will thamayad (always) thahalah (praise) you.
I am a marvel to many, but you are my iz (strength / might / refuge) machasah (refuge).
My pah (mouth) shall be malaa (filled) with your thahalah (praise), with your honor all the yawam (day).
Don't reject me in my zaqanah (old) age. Don't izab (forsake) me when my kach (strength / mighty / power) kalah (complete / finish).
For my ayab (enemy) amar (spoke) about me. Those who shamar (keep/guard) for my napash (soul) conspire yachad (together),
Amar (spoke), "Alahayam has forsaken him. Radap (pursue) and thapash (take) him, for no one will natzal (rescue) him."
Alahayam, don't be rachaq (far) from me. My Alahayam, hurry to izarah (help) me.
Let my accusers be disappointed and kalah (complete / finish). Let them be itah (covered) with disgrace and scorn who want to rai (harm) me.
But I will thamayad (always) yachal (hope), and will yasap (add) to all of your thahalah (praise).
My pah (mouth) will sapar (book) about your tzadaqah (righteousness), and of your thashawaih (deliverance) all yawam (day), though I don't yadai (know) its full measure.
I will bawaa (come) with the gabawarah (mighty) acts of the Adanay Yahawah. I will zakar (remember) mention of your tzadaqah (righteousness), even of yours alone.
Alahayam, you have lamad (teach / instruct) me from my naiwar (youth). Until now, I have nagad (declared) your wondrous palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous).

Yes, even when I am zaqanah (old) and gray-haired, Alahayam, don't izab (forsake) me, until I have nagad (declared) your zarawai (strength) to the next dawar (generation / age / period), your gabawarah (might) to everyone who is to bawaa (come).
Your tzadaqah (righteousness) also, Alahayam, reaches to the marawam (heavens); you ishah (make) done gadawal (very great/important/mighty) things. Alahayam, who is like you?

You, who raah (see) shown us many and bitter tzarawath (troubles), you will shawab (turn back / repent) me chayah (live). You will ilah (go up / offer) us up again from the thahamawath (depths) of the aratz (Earth/land).
Rabah (increase) my honor, and nacham (turn away / repent) me again.
I will also yadah (praise) you with the harp for your amath (truth), my Alahayam. I zamar (sing) kanawar (praises) to you with the lyre, qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel).
My shapah (lips) shall ranan (shout) for joy! My napash (soul), which you have padah (redeemed), sings zamar (praises) to you!

My lashawan (tongue / language) will also hagah (talk) about your tzadaqah (righteousness) all yawam (day) bawash (long), for they are disappointed, and they are bawash (confounded), who want to rai (harm) me.
Alahayam, nathan (give) the malak (king) your mashapat (justice); your tzadaqah (righteousness) to the malak (king) ban (son).
He will dayan (judge) your im (nation / people) with tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and your inay (poor) with mashapat (justice).
The harayam (mountains) shall nashaa (lift) prosperity to the im (nation / people). The gabaiwath (hills) bring the fruit of tzadaqah (righteousness).

He will shapat (judge / judgement) the inay (poor) of the im (nation / people). He will yashai (salvation) the banay (children) of the abayawan (needy), and will break the oppressor in dakaa (pieces).
They shall yaraa (fear / be afraid) you while the shamash (sun) panay (endures); and as long as the yarach (moon), throughout all dawarayam (generations).
He will yarad (come) down like matar (rain) on the gaz (mown) grass, as rabayabayam (showers) that zarazayap (water) the aratz (Earth/land).
In his yawam (day), the tzadayaq (righteous) shall parach (flourish), and rab (abundance) of shalawam (peace / safety), until the yarach (moon) is no more.
He shall radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) dominion also from yam (sea/waters) to yam (sea/waters), from the nahar (river) to the apasay (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land).
Those who dwell in the tzayay (wilderness) shall karai (bow) panayam (face) him. His ayab (enemy) shall lachak (lick) the ipar (dust).

The malakay (kings) of Tharashayash (Tarshish) and of the ayayam (islands) will shawab (turn back / repent) tribute. The malakay (kings) of Shabaa (Sheba) and Sabaa (Seba) shall qarab (come close) ashakar (gifts).
Yes, all malakayam (kings) shall shachah (fall) down before him. All gawayam (nations) shall ibad (servant) him.
For he will natzal (deliver) the abayawan (needy) when he shawai (cries); the inay (poor), who has no helper.
He will have chawas (pity) on the dal (poor) and dal (needy). He will yashai (salvation) the napashawath (souls) of the abayawan (needy).
He will gaal (redeem) their napash (soul) from oppression and chamas (violence). Their dam (blood) will be yaqar (precious) in his iyan (eye).
They shall chayah (live), and to him shall be nathan (give) of the zahab (gold) of Shabaa (Sheba). Men shall palal (pray) for him continually. They shall barak (blessed) him all yawam (day) long.
Abundance of grain shall be throughout the aratz (Earth/land). Its paray (fruit) sways like Labanawan (Lebanon). Let it tzawatz (flourish), thriving like the ishab (grass) of the aratz (Earth/land).
His sham (name) endures iwalam (forever). His sham (name) continues as long as the shamash (sun). Men shall be barak (blessed) by him. All gawayam (nations) will ashar (who/that) him blessed.
Barak (blessed) be to Yahawah Alahayam, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), who alone ishah (make) palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) deeds.

Barak (blessed) be his kabawad (glorious) sham (name) iwalam (forever)! Let the whole aratz (Earth/land) be malaa (filled) with his kabawad (glory)! Aman (believe / have faith) and aman (believe / have faith).
This kalaw (ends) the thapalawath (prayers) by Dawad (David), the ban (son) of Yashay (Jesse).
Surely Alahayam is tawab (good / proper function) to Yashar-Al (Israel), to those who are bar (pure) in labab (heart).
But as for me, my ragal (feet / foot) were mait (almost) natah (gone). My ashar (who/that) had nearly shapak (slipped).
For I was qanaa (jealous) of the arrogant, when I raah (see) the prosperity of the rashai (wicked).
For there are no struggles in their mawath (death), but their awal (strength) is barayaa (firm).
They are free from burdens of anawash (men), neither are they nagai (plagued) im (with) other adam (men).
Therefore gaawah (pride) is like a inaq (chain) around their neck. Chamas (violence) itap (covers) them like a garment.
Their iyan (eye) bulge with chalab (fat). Their labab (minds) ibar (pass over/through) the limits of mashakayath (idol / carved image).
They scoff and dabar (word / matter) with malice. In arrogance, they threaten ishaq (oppression).
They have shathath (set) their pah (mouth) in the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens). Their lashawan (tongue / language) halak (move) through the aratz (Earth/land).
Therefore their im (nation / people) shawab (turn back / repent) to them, and they drink up may (waters) of abundance.
They amar (spoke), "How does Al yadai (know)? Is there daih (knowledge) in the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan)?"
Behold, these are the rashai (wicked). Being iwalam (forever) at shalaw (ease), they shagah (increase) in riches.
Surely in rayaq (vain) I have zakah (cleansed) my labab (heart), and rachatz (washed) my kap (hands) in innocence,
For all yawam (day) long have I been nagai (plagued), and punished every baqar (morning).
If I had amar (spoke), "I will amar (spoke) kamaw (thus);" behold, I would have betrayed the dawar (generation / age / period) of your ban (son).
When I tried to yadai (understand) this, it was too imal (painful) for me;
Until I bawaa (come) Al maqadash (sanctuary), and bayan (between) their acharayath (latter) end.
Surely you shayath (put / appoint / make) them in chalaqah (slippery) places. You napal (fall / be cast down) them down to mashawaah (destruction).
How they are ragai (in an instance) destroyed! They are completely swept away with balahawath (terrors).
As a chalawam (dream) when one qawatz (wakes) up, so, Adanay, when you iwar (rouse / awaken), you will bazah (despise) their fantasies.
For my labab (soul) was chamatz (grieved). I was embittered in my kalayah (heart).
I was so senseless and yadai (ignorant). I was a brute bahamah (beast) before you.
Nevertheless, I am continually with you. You achaz (have) held my yamayan (right hand) yad (hand).
You will nachah (guide) me with your itzah (counsel), and afterward laqach (take / seize) me to kabawad (glory).
Whom do I have in shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens)? There is no one on aratz (Earth/land) whom I chapatz (desire) besides you.
My shaar (flesh) and my labab (heart) kalah (complete / finish), but Alahayam is the tzawar (strength) of my labab (heart) and my chalaq (portion) iwalam (forever).
For, behold, those who are rachaq (far) from you shall abad (destroy / perish). You have tzamath (destroyed) all those who are unfaithful to you.

But it is tawab (good / proper function) for me to come close to Alahayam. I have shayath (put / appoint / make) the Adanay Yahawah my machasah (refuge), that I may sapar (book) of all your malaakah (works).
Alahayam, why have you rejected us natzach (forever)? Why does your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) smolder against the tzaan (sheep) of your maraiyath (pasture)?

Zakar (remember) your idah (congregation), which you qanah (purchased) of qadam (old), which you have gaal (redeemed) to be the tribe of your nachalah (inheritance); har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion), in which you shakan (place) lived.
Rawam (will lift up) up your paim (feet) to the natzach (perpetual) ruins, all the raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) that the ayab (enemy) has done in the qadash (set apart / make holy).
Your tzarar (adversaries) have shaag (roared) in the qarab (among / near) of your mawaid (Feast/Holy Day). They have shawam (place / establish / appoint) up their standards as athawath (signs).
They behaved like men wielding axes, cutting through a sabak (thicket) of itz (trees).
Now they break all its pathawach (carved) work down with hatchet and kayalapath (hammers).
They have burned your maqadash (sanctuary) to the aratz (Earth/land). They have chalal (profaned) the mashakan (dwelling) place of your sham (name).
They amar (spoke) in their lab (heart), "We will yanah (crush) them completely." They have sharap (burned) up all the mawaiday (places) in the aratz (Earth/land) where Al was worshiped.
We raah (see) no miraculous awath (sign / mark / miracle). There is no longer any nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), neither is there among us anyone who yadai (knows) id (until / as far as) long.
How long, Alahayam, shall the tzar (oppressor / distressor) charap (reproach)? Shall the ayab (enemy) naatz (blaspheme) your sham (name) natzach (forever)?
Why shawab (turn back / repent) you draw back your yad (hand), even your right yad (hand)? Kalah (complete / finish) it out of your pocket and consume them!
Yet Alahayam is my malak (king) of qadam (old), pail (working) yashawaih (salvation) in the qarab (among / near) of the aratz (Earth/land).
You parar (divided) the yam (sea/waters) by your iz (strength / might / refuge). You shabar (broke) the raashay (heads) of the thanayan (sea) monsters in the mayam (Waters).
You ratzatz (broke) the raashay (heads) of lawayathan (leviathan) in pieces. You nathan (give) him as maakal (food) to im (nation / people) and tzayay (desert) creatures.
You opened up maiyan (spring) and nachal (stream / river). You yabash (dry land) up ayathan (mighty) naharawath (rivers).
The yawam (day) is yours, the layal (night) is also yours. You have kawan (prepared) the maawar (Maawar / Luminary) and the shamash (sun).
You have natzab (set) all the boundaries of the aratz (Earth/land). You have yatzar (made) qayatz (summer) and charap (winter).
Zakar (remember) this, that the ayab (enemy) has mocked you, Yahawah. Foolish im (nation / people) have naatz (blasphemed) your sham (name).
Don't nathan (give) the napash (soul) of your thawar (dove) to wild chay (life). Don't shakach (forget) the chay (life) of your inay (poor) natzach (forever).
Honor your barayath (covenant), for haunts of chamas (violence) fill the machashak (dark) naawath (places) of the aratz (Earth/land).
Don't let the dak (oppressed) shawab (turn back / repent) kalam (ashamed). Let the inay (poor) and abayawan (needy) halal (praise) your sham (name).
Qawam (rise up), Alahayam! Rayab (plead) your own rayab (cause). Zakar (remember) how the foolish nabal (man) mocks you all yawam (day).
Don't shakach (forget) the qawal (sound / voice) of your tzarar (adversaries). The shaawan (tumult) of those who qawam (rise up) up against you ilah (go up / offer) continually.

We give hawadayanaw (thanks) to you, Alahayam. We give hawadayanaw (thanks), for your sham (name) is qarawab (near). Men sapar (book) about your wondrous palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous).
When I choose the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) time, I will shapat (judge / judgement) blamelessly.
The aratz (Earth/land) and all its yashab (inhabit/dwell) quake. I firmly hold its imawad (pillar). Salah (selah).
I amar (spoke) to the arrogant, "Don't halal (praise)!" I said to the rashai (wicked), "Don't rawam (will lift up) up the qaran (horn).
Don't rawam (will lift up) up your qaran (horn) on marawam (high). Don't dabar (word / matter) with a ithaq (stiff) tzawaar (neck)."
For neither from the mawatzaa (east), nor from the mairab (west), nor yet from the madabar (south), comes exaltation.
But Alahayam is the shapat (judge / judgement). He shapal (puts) down one, and rawam (will lift up) up another.

For in the yad (hand) of Yahawah there is a kawas (cup), full of foaming yayan (wine) mixed with spices. He pours it out. Indeed the rashai (wicked) of the aratz (Earth/land) drink and shathah (drinks) it to its very shamar (keep/guard).
But I will nagad (declare) this iwalam (forever): I will sing zamar (praises) to the Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob).
