I will cut off all the qaranay (horns) of the rashai (wicked), but the qaranay (horns) of the tzadayaq (righteous) shall be rawam (will lift up) up.
In Yahawadah (Judah), Alahayam is yadai (known). His sham (name) is gadawal (very great/important/mighty) in Yashar-Al (Israel).
His sak (tabernacle) is also in Shalam (Salem); His dwelling maiwanah (place) in Tzayawan (Zion).
There he shabar (broke) the flaming rashapay (arrows) of the bow, the magan (shield), and the charab (sword), and the weapons of malachamah (war). Salah (selah).
Awar (light) are you, and adayar (excellent), more than hararay (mountains) of game.
Abayar (valiant) men lie plundered, they have nawam (slept) their last shanah (sleep). None of the anashay (men) of chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) can lift their yad (hand).
At your gairah (rebuke), Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob), both rakab (chariot) and sawas (horse) are radam (cast) into a deep sleep.
You, even you, are to be yaraa (fear / be afraid). Who can imad (stand) in your panayam (face) when you are angry?
You pronounced dayan (judge) from shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens). The aratz (Earth/land) yaraa (fear / be afraid), and was silent,
When Alahayam qawam (rise up) to mashapat (judgment), to yashai (salvation) all the afflicted ones of the aratz (Earth/land). Salah (selah).
Surely the chamah (wrath) of adam (man) yadah (praises) you. The survivors of your chamah (wrath) are chagar (restrained).
Make nadaraw (vows) to Yahawah your Alahayam, and fulfill them! Let all of his neighbors yabal (bring) shay (presents) to him who is to be mawaraa (feared).
He will batzar (cut) off the rawach (spirit / wind) of nagayadayam (princes). He is yaraa (fear / be afraid) by the malakay (kings) of the aratz (Earth/land).
My tzaiq (cry) goes to Alahayam! Indeed, I qawal (sound / voice) to Alahayam for help, and for him to listen to me.

In the yawam (day) of my tzarah (trouble) I darash (sought) the Adanay. My yad (hand) was stretched out in the layal (night), and didn't get tired. My napash (soul) maan (refused) to be nacham (turn away / repent).
I zakar (remember) Alahayam, and I groan. I shayach (meditate), and my rawach (spirit / wind) is itap (overwhelmed). Salah (selah).
You achaz (hold) my eyelids open. I am so paim (troubled) that I can't dabar (word / matter).
I have chashab (considered) the yamayam (days) of qadam (old), the shanawath (years) of iwalam (forever) times.
I zakar (remember) my nagayanah (song) in the layal (night). I consider in my own labab (heart); my rawach (spirit / wind) diligently inquires:
"Will the Adanay reject us iwalam (forever)? Will he be favorable no more?
Has his loving chasad (grace) vanished natzach (forever)? Does his amar (spoke) gamar (fail) for dawar (generation / age / period)?
Has Al shakach (forgotten) to be chanawath (gracious)? Has he, in ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), withheld his racham (show mercy / love)?" Salah (selah).
Then I amar (spoke), "I will appeal to this: the shanah (years) of the right yamayan (right hand) of the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan)."
I will zakar (remember) Yah deeds; for I will zakar (remember) your palaa (wonders) of qadam (old).
I will also hagah (meditate) on all your pail (work), and consider your ilayalah (doings).
Your darak (way), Alahayam, is in the qadash (set apart / make holy). What Alahayam is gadawal (very great/important/mighty) like Al?
You are the Al who ishah (make) palaa (wonders). You have made your iz (strength / might / refuge) yadai (known) among the imayam (peoples).
You have gaal (redeemed) your im (nation / people) with your zarawai (arm), the banay (sons) of Yaiqab (Jacob) and Yawasap (Joseph). Salah (selah).
The mayam (Waters) raah (see) you, Alahayam. The mayam (Waters) raah (see) you, and they writhed. The thahamawath (depths) also convulsed.
The ibawath (clouds) zaram (poured) out mayam (Waters). The shachaqayam (skies) resounded with qawal (sound / voice). Your chatzatz (arrows) also flashed around.
The qawal (sound / voice) of your raim (thunder) was in the whirlwind. The baraqayam (lightnings) awar (light) up the thabal (world). The thabal (earth) ragaz (trembled) and raish (shook).
Your darak (way) was through the yam (sea/waters); your shabayal (paths) through the rab (great) mayam (Waters). Your iqab (footsteps) were not yadai (known).
You nachah (led) your im (nation / people) like a tzaan (flock), by the yad (hand) of Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron).
Azan (ear) my teaching, my im (nation / people). Natah (turn) your azan (ear) to the amaray (words) of my pah (mouth).
I will pathach (open) my pah (mouth) in a mashal (parable). I will nabai (utter) chayadah (dark) sayings of qadam (old),
Which we have shamai (hearken / hear) and yadai (known), and our ab (father) have sapar (book) us.

We will not kachad (hide) them from their ban (son), sapar (book) to the dawar (generation / age / period) to acharawan (come) the thahalawath (praises) of Yahawah, his izawaz (strength), and his wondrous palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) that he ishah (make) done.

For he qawam (rise up) a idawath (testimony) in Yaiqab (Jacob), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) a teaching in Yashar-Al (Israel), which he tzawah (commanded) our ab (father), that they should yadai (make) them known to their ban (son);

That the dawar (generation / age / period) to acharawan (come) might yadai (know), even the banayam (children) who should be yalad (birth / begot); who should qawam (rise up) and sapar (book) their banayam (children),
That they might shawam (place / establish / appoint) their kasal (hope) in Alahayam, and not shakach (forget) the mailalay (works) of Al, but natzar (keep) his matzawah (commandments),

And might not be as their ab (father), a sarar (stubborn) and rebellious dawar (generation / age / period), a dawar (generation / age / period) that didn't kawan (make) their lab (heart) loyal, whose rawach (spirit / wind) was not steadfast with Al.
The banay (children) of Aparayam (Ephraim), being nashaq (armed) and ramah (carrying) qashath (bows), hapak (turned) back in the yawam (day) of qarab (battle).
They didn't shamar (keep/guard) Alahayam barayath (covenant), and maan (refused) to yalak (walk) in his thawarah (instruction).
They shakach (forgot) his ilayalah (doings), his wondrous ilayalah (works) that he raah (see) shown them.
He ishah (make) marvelous things in the nagad (sight) of their ab (father), in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), in the shadah (field) of Tzain (Zoan).
He split the yam (sea/waters), and ibar (pass over/through) them to pass through. He made the mayam (Waters) natzab (stand) as a nad (heap).
In the yawamam (by day) he also nachah (led) them with a inan (cloud), and all layal (night) with a awar (light) of ash (fire).
He split tzarayam (rocks) in the madabar (wilderness), and shaqah (gave) them drink abundantly as out of the thahamawath (depths).
He yatzaa (go out / come out) nawazalayam (streams) also out of the salai (rock), and caused mayam (Waters) to yarad (run) down like naharawath (rivers).
Yet they still went on to chataa (sin) marah (against) him, to rebel against the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan) in the desert.
They nasah (tempted) Al in their labab (heart) by shaal (asking) akal (food) according to their napash (soul).
Yes, they dabar (word / matter) against Alahayam. They dabar (word / matter), "yakal (can) Al irak (prepare) a shalachan (table) in the madabar (wilderness)?

Behold, he nakah (struck) the tzawar (rock), so that mayam (Waters) zawab (flow) out, and nachalayam (streams) shatap (overflowed). Yakal (can) he nathan (give) lacham (bread) also? Will he kawan (provide) shaar (flesh) for his im (nation / people)?"

Therefore Yahawah shamai (hearken / hear), and was angry. A ash (fire) was nashaq (kindled) against Yaiqab (Jacob), ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) also ilah (go up / offer) up against Yashar-Al (Israel),
Because they didn't aman (believe / have faith) in Alahayam, and didn't batach (trust) in his yashawaih (salvation).
Yet he tzawah (commanded) the shachaqayam (skies) mail (top/above), and pathach (opened) the dalathay (doors) of shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens).
He matar (rained) down man (from) on them to akal (eat), and nathan (give) them food from the sky.
Ayash (man / husband) akal (eat) the lacham (bread) of abayarayam (angels). He shalach (send) them lacham (food) to the shabai (full).
He caused the east qadayam (wind) to nasai (blow) in the sky. By his iz (strength / might / refuge) he nahag (guided) the south thayaman (wind).
He matar (rained) also shaar (flesh) on them as the ipar (dust); kanap (winged) iwap (flying) as the chawal (sand) of the yamayam (seas).
He napal (fall / be cast down) them fall in the qarab (among / near) of their machanah (camp), around their mashakan (habitations).
So they akal (eat), and were maad (well) shabai (filled). He bawaa (come) them their own thaawah (desire).
They didn't zawar (turn) from their cravings. Their akal (food) was yet in their pah (mouths),
When the ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Alahayam ilah (go up / offer) up against them, harag (kill) some of their fattest, and struck down the bachawar (young) men of Yashar-Al (Israel).
For all this they still chataa (sinned), and didn't aman (believe / have faith) in his wondrous palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous).
Therefore he kalah (complete / finish) their yawam (day) in habal (vanity), and their shanah (years) in bahalah (terror).
When he harag (kill) them, then they darash (inquired) after him. They shawab (turn back / repent) and sought Al earnestly.
They zakar (remember) that Alahayam was their tzawar (rock), the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan) Al, their gaal (redeemer).
But they pathah (flattered) him with their pah (mouth), and lied to him with their lashawan (tongue / language).
For their lab (heart) was not kawan (right) with him, neither were they aman (believe / have faith) in his barayath (covenant).

But he, being rachawam (merciful), kapar (forgave) iwan (guilt/iniquity), and didn't shachath (destroy) them. Yes, many times he shawab (turn back / repent) his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) shawab (turn back / repent), and didn't iwar (rouse / awaken) up all his chamah (wrath).
He zakar (remember) that they were but bashar (flesh), a rawach (spirit / wind) that passes halak (move), and doesn't shawab (turn back / repent) again.
Mah (how) often they marah (rebelled) against him in the madabar (wilderness), and itzab (grieved) him in the yashayamawan (desert)!
They shawab (turn back / repent) again and nasah (tempted) Al, and provoked the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel).
They didn't zakar (remember) his yad (hand), nor the yawam (day) when he padah (redeemed) them from the tzar (oppressor / distressor);
How he shawam (place / establish / appoint) his awath (sign / mark / miracle) in Matzarayam (Egypt), his awath (sign / mark / miracle) in the shadah (field) of Tzain (Zoan),
He hapak (turned) their yaar (rivers) into dam (blood), and their yaar (streams), so that they could not shathah (drinks).
He shalach (send) among them irab (evening) of flies, which akal (eat) them; and tzaparadai (frogs), which shachath (destroyed) them.
He nathan (give) also their yabawal (increase) to the chasayal (caterpillar), and their yagayai (labor) to the arabah (locust).
He harag (kill) their gapan (vines) with barad (hail), their shaqamah (sycamore) fig trees with chanamal (frost).
He sagar (gave) over their livestock also to the barad (hail), and their maqanah (flocks) to rashap (hot) thunderbolts.
He threw on them the charawan (fierceness) of his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), ibarah (wrath), zaim (indignation), and tzarah (trouble), and a band of malaakay (angels) of rai (evil).

He palas (made) a nathayab (path) for his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting). He didn't chashak (darkness) their napash (soul) from mawath (death), but sagar (gave) their chay (life) over to the dabar (word / matter),
And nakah (struck) all the bakawar (firstborn) in Matzarayam (Egypt), the raashayath (beginning) of their awan (strength) in the ahalay (tents) of Cham (Ham).
But he led nasai (forth) his own im (nation / people) like tzaan (sheep), and nahag (guided) them in the madabar (wilderness) like a idar (flock).
He nachah (led) them safely, so that they weren't pachad (fear / dread), but the yam (sea/waters) kasah (overwhelmed) their ayab (enemy).
He bawaa (come) them to the gabawal (border/boundary) of his qadash (set apart / make holy), to this har (mountain), which his right yamayan (right hand) had taken.

He also garash (drove) out the gawayam (nations) panayam (face) them, allotted them for an nachalah (inheritance) by chabal (line), and made the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel) to shakan (place) in their ahal (tents).
Yet they nasah (tempted) and marah (rebelled) against the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan) Alahayam, and didn't shamar (keep/guard) his idah (testimonies);
But sawag (turned) back, and dealt bagad (treacherously) like their ab (father). They were hapak (turned) aside like a deceitful qashath (bow).
For they provoked him to kais (anger) with their bamah (high) places, and qanaa (jealous) him to jealousy with their engraved pasayal (images).
When Alahayam shamai (hearken / hear) this, he was angry, and maad (greatly) maas (abhorred) Yashar-Al (Israel);
So that he forsook the mashakan (tent) of Shayalah (Shiloh), the mashakan (tent) which he shakan (place) among adam (men);
And nathan (give) his iz (strength / might / refuge) into shabay (captivity), his glory into the tzar (oppressor / distressor) yad (hand).
He also sagar (gave) his im (nation / people) over to the charab (sword), and was angry with his nachalah (inheritance).
Ash (fire) akal (eat) their bachawar (young) men. Their bathawalah (virgins) had no wedding song.
Their kahan (priest) napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword), and their alamanah (widows) couldn't bakah (weep).
Then the Adanay awakened as yashan (one) out of sleep, like a gabawar (mighty) man who ranan (shouts) by reason of yayan (wine).
He nakah (struck) his tzar (oppressor / distressor) backward. He nathan (give) them to a iwalam (forever) charapah (reproach).
Moreover he maas (rejected) the ahal (tent) of Yawasap (Joseph), and didn't bachar (choose) the shabat (tribe) of Aparayam (Ephraim),
But bachar (chose) the shabat (tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah), har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion) which he ahab (love).
He banah (build) his maqadash (sanctuary) like the heights, like the aratz (Earth/land) which he has yasad (established) iwalam (forever).
He also bachar (chose) Dawad (David) his ibad (servant), and laqach (take / seize) him from the makalaath (sheepfolds);

From achar (other) the ewes that have their iwal (young), he bawaa (come) him to be the raih (shepherd) of Yaiqab (Jacob), his im (nation / people), and Yashar-Al (Israel), his nachalah (inheritance).
So he was their raih (shepherd) according to the tham (integrity) of his labab (heart), and nachah (guided) them by the skillfulness of his kap (hands).

Alahayam, the gawayam (nations) bawaa (come) come into your nachalah (inheritance). They have tamaa (defiled) your qadash (set apart / make holy) hayakal (temple). They have shawam (place / establish / appoint) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) in iyayam (heaps).

They nathan (give) given the nabalah (dead) bodies of your ibad (servant) to be maakal (food) for the iwap (flying) of the sky, the bashar (flesh) of your chasayad (saints) to the animals of the aratz (Earth/land).
Their dam (blood) they have shapak (shed) like mayam (Waters) around Yarawashalam (Jerusalem). There was no one to qabar (bury) them.
We have become a charapah (reproach) to our neighbors, a scoffing and qalas (derision) to those who are around us.
How long, Yahawah? Will you be anap (angry) natzach (forever)? Will your qanaah (jealousy) bair (burn) like ash (fire)?
Shapak (pour) out your chamah (wrath) on the gawayam (nations) that don't yadai (know) you; on the mamalakawath (kingdoms) that don't qaraa (called) on your sham (name);
For they have akal (eat) Yaiqab (Jacob), and shamam (destroyed) his homeland.
Don't hold the iwanath (iniquities) of our raashanayam (forefathers) against us. Let your tender racham (show mercy / love) mahar (speedily) qadam (meet) us, for we are in desperate need.
Izar (help) us, Alahayam of our yashai (salvation), for the kabawad (glory) of your sham (name). Natzal (deliver) us, and kapar (forgive) our chataah (sin), for your sham (name) sake.

Why should the gawayam (nations) amar (spoke), "Where is their Alahayam?" Yadai (let) it be known among the gawayam (nations), before our iyan (eye), that naqamah (vengeance) for your ibad (servant)' dam (blood) is being shapak (poured) out.

Let the anaqah (sighing) of the asayar (prisoner) bawaa (come) panayam (face) you. According to the gadal (greatness) of your zarawai (power), yathar (preserve) those who are sentenced to thamawathah (death).
Shawab (turn back / repent) back to our neighbors shabaithayam (seven) times into their chayaq (bosom) their charapah (reproach) with which they have charap (reproached) you, Adanay.

So we, your im (nation / people) and tzaan (sheep) of your maraiyath (pasture), will give you nawadah (thanks) iwalam (forever). We will thahalah (praise) you iwalam (forever), to all dawar (generation / age / period).
Azan (ear) us, raih (shepherd) of Yashar-Al (Israel), you who nahag (lead) Yawasap (Joseph) like a tzaan (flock), you who yashab (inhabit/dwell) above the karawab (cherubim), yapai (shine) forth.
Panayam (face) Aparayam (Ephraim) and Banayamayan (Benjamin) and Manashah (Manasseh), iwar (rouse / awaken) up your gabawarah (might)! Yalak (come) to yashawaih (salvation) us!
Shawab (turn back / repent) us again, Alahayam. Cause your panayam (face) to awar (light), and we will be yashai (salvation).
Yahawah Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies), How long will you be ishan (angry) against the thapalah (prayer) of your im (nation / people)?
You have akal (eat) them with the lacham (bread) of damaiwath (tears), and given them damaiwath (tears) to shaqah (drink) in large shalayash (measure).
You shawam (place / establish / appoint) us a source of madawan (contention) to our neighbors. Our ayab (enemy) laig (laugh) among themselves.
Shawab (turn back / repent) us again, Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies). Cause your panayam (face) to awar (light), and we will be yashai (salvation).
You nasai (brought) a gapan (vine) out of Matzarayam (Egypt). You garash (drove) out the gawayam (nations), and natai (planted) it.
You cleared the panayam (face) for it. It took sharash (deep) sharash (root), and malaa (filled) the aratz (Earth/land).
The harayam (mountains) were kasah (covered) with its tzal (shadow). Its inap (boughs) were like Al arazay (cedars).
It shalach (send) out its branches to the yam (sea/waters), Its shoots to the nahar (river).
Why have you paratz (broken) down its gadar (walls), so that ibar (pass over/through) those who pass by the darak (way) arah (pluck) it?
The chazayar (boar) out of the yair (wood) ravages it. The zayaz (wild) animals of the shadah (field) raih (feed) on it.
Shawab (turn back / repent) again, we beg you, Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies). Nabat (look) down from shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and raah (see), and paqad (visit) this gapan (vine),
The stock which your right yamayan (right hand) natai (planted), the ban (son) that you amatz (made) strong for yourself.
It's sharap (burned) with ash (fire). It's kasach (cut) down. They abad (destroy / perish) at your gairah (rebuke).
Let your yad (hand) be on the ayash (man / husband) of your right yamayan (right hand), on the ban (son) of adam (man) whom you amatz (made) strong for yourself.
So we will not sawag (turn) away from you. Chayah (revive) us, and we will qaraa (called) on your sham (name).
Shawab (turn back / repent) us again, Yahawah Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies). Cause your panayam (face) to awar (light), and we will be yashai (salvation).
Ranan (sing) aloud to Alahayam, our iz (strength / might / refuge)! Rawai (make) a joyful shout to the Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob)!
Nashaa (lift) a song, and nathan (give) here the tambourine, the naiyam (pleasant) lyre with the harp.
Thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn) at the New chadash (month), at the full chadash (month), on our chag (feast/festival) yawam (day).
For it is a chaq (statute) for Yashar-Al (Israel), an mashapat (ordinance) of the Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob).

He shawam (place / establish / appoint) it in Yahawasap (Joseph) for a idawath (testimony), when he yatzaa (go out / come out) out over the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), I shamai (hearken / hear) a shapah (language) that I didn't yadai (know).
"I sawar (removed) his shakam (shoulder) from the sabal (burden). His kap (hands) were freed from the dawad (basket).

You qaraa (called) in tzarah (trouble), and I chalatz (delivered) you. I inah (answer / respond) you in the sathar (secret / hidden) place of raim (thunder). I tested you at the may (waters) of Marayabah (Meribah)." Salah (selah).
"Shamai (hearken / hear), my im (nation / people), and I will iwad (admonish/bear witness against) to you, Yashar-Al (Israel), if you would shamai (hearken / hear) to me!
There shall be no zawar (strange) Al in you, neither shall you shachah (worship) any foreign Al.
I am Yahawah, your Alahayam, who ilah (go up / offer) you up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt). Open your pah (mouth) rachab (wide), and I will malaa (fill) it.
But my im (nation / people) didn't shamai (hearken / hear) to my qawal (sound / voice). Yashar-Al (Israel) desired none of me.
So I shalach (send) them go after the stubbornness of their lab (heart), that they might yalak (walk) in their own mawaitzah (counsels).
Oh that my im (nation / people) would shamai (hearken / hear) to me, that Yashar-Al (Israel) would halak (move) in my darak (ways)!
I would mait (soon) kanai (subdue) their ayab (enemy), and shawab (turn back / repent) my yad (hand) against their tzar (oppressor / distressor).
The haters of Yahawah would cringe before him, and their punishment would last iwalam (forever).
But he would have also akal (eat) them with the chalab (finest) of the chatah (wheat). I will shabai (satisfy) you with dabash (honey) out of the tzawar (rock)."
Alahayam presides in the al (Alahayam) idah (assembly). He shapat (judge / judgement) qarab (among / near) the Alahayam.
"How long will you shapat (judge / judgement) iwal (unjustly), and show partiality to the rashai (wicked)?" Salah (selah).
"Shapat (judge / judgement) the weak, the dal (poor), and the yathawam (fatherless). Maintain the rights of the inay (poor) and oppressed.
Rescue the weak and abayawan (needy). Palat (deliver) them out of the yad (hand) of the rashai (wicked)."
They don't yadai (know), neither do they bayan (between). They halak (move) back and forth in chashakah (darkness). All the mawasaday (foundations) of the aratz (Earth/land) are mawat (shaken).
I amar (spoke), "You are Alahayam, all of you are banay (sons) of the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan).
Akan (nevertheless) you shall mawath (death) like adam (men), and napal (fall / be cast down) like achad (one) of the sharayam (rulers)."
Qawam (rise up), Alahayam, shapat (judge / judgement) the aratz (Earth/land), for you nachal (inherit) all of the gawayam (nations).
Alahayam, don't keep silent. Don't keep silent, and don't be still, Al.
For, behold, your ayab (enemy) are stirred up. Those who shanaa (hate) you have nashaa (lift) up their raash (head).
They conspire with cunning against your im (nation / people). They plot against your cherished tzapan (ones).
"Yalak (come)," they amar (spoke), "and let's kachad (destroy) them as a gaway (heathen / nation), that the sham (name) of Yashar-Al (Israel) may be zakar (remember) no more."
For they have conspired yachad (together) with one lab (heart). They form an alliance against you.
The ahalay (tents) of Adawam (Edom) and the Yashamaialay (Ishmaelites); Mawaab (Moab), and the Hagaray (Hagrites);
Gabal (Gebal), Imawan (Ammon), and Imalaq (Amalek); Palashath (Philistia) with the yashabay (inhabitants) of Tzar (Tyre);
Ashawar (Assyria) also is lawah (joined) with them. They have zarawai (helped) the banay (children) of Lawat (Lot). Salah (selah).
Ishah (make) to them as you did to Madayan (Midian), as to Sayasaraa (Sisera), as to Yabayan (Jabin), at the nachal (stream / river) Qayashawan (Kishon);
Who shamad (perished) at Iyan-Daar (Endor), who became as daman (dung) for the adamah (earth).
Shayath (put / appoint / make) their nadayab (nobles) like Irab (Oreb) and Zaab (Zeeb); yes, all their nasayak (princes) like Zabach (Zebah) and Tzalamanai (Zalmunna);
Who amar (spoke), "Let us take yarash (possession) of Alahayam pasturelands."
My Alahayam, shayath (put / appoint / make) them like tumbleweed; like chaff panayam (face) the rawach (spirit / wind).
As the ash (fire) that bair (burns) the yair (forest), as the lahabah (flame) that lahat (sets) the harayam (mountains) on lahat (fire),
So radap (pursue) them with your sair (tempest), and terrify them with your sawapah (storm).
Malaa (fill) their panayam (face) with qalawan (confusion), that they may baqash (seek) your sham (name), Yahawah.
Let them be disappointed and bahal (dismayed) id (until / as far as). Yes, let them be chapar (confounded) and abad (destroy / perish);
That they may yadai (know) that you alone, whose sham (name) is Yahawah, are the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan) over all the aratz (Earth/land).
How lovely are your mashakan (dwellings), Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies)!
My napash (soul) kasap (longs), and even kalah (complete / finish) for the chatzarawath (courts) of Yahawah. My lab (heart) and my bashar (flesh) ranan (cry) out for the chay (life) Al.

Yes, the tzapawar (sparrow) matzaa (has) found a bayath (house), and the darawar (swallow) a qan (nest) for herself, where she may have her aparach (young), near your mazabach (altars), Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), my malak (king), and my Alahayam.
Ashar (who/that) are those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in your bayath (house). They are always halal (praise) you. Salah (selah).
Ashar (who/that) are those whose iz (strength / might / refuge) is in you; who have set their labab (hearts) on a pilgrimage.

Ibar (pass over/through) through the imaq (valley) of Weeping, they shayath (put / appoint / make) it a place of maiyan (springs). Yes, the autumn mawarah (rain) itah (covers) it with barakawath (blessings).
They yalak (go) from chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) to chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor). Everyone of them raah (see) before Alahayam in Tzayawan (Zion).
Yahawah, Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies), shamai (hearken / hear) my thapalah (prayer). Shamai (hearken / hear), Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob). Salah (selah).
Raah (see), Alahayam our magan (shield), nabat (look) at the panayam (face) of your mashayach (anointed one).

For a yawam (day) in your chatzar (courts) is tawab (good / proper function) than a alap (thousand). I would bachar (rather) be a sapap (doorkeeper) in the bayath (house) of my Alahayam, than to dawar (dwell) in the ahalay (tents) of rashai (wickedness).

For Yahawah Alahayam is a shamash (sun) and a magan (shield). Yahawah will nathan (give) chan (favor) and kabawad (glory). He manai (withholds) no tawab (good / proper function) thing from those who halak (move) blamelessly.
Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), ashar (who/that) is the adam (man) who batach (trusts) in you.
Yahawah, you ratzah (have) been favorable to your aratz (Earth/land). You have shawab (turn back / repent) the fortunes of Yaiqab (Jacob).
You have nashaa (lift) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of your im (nation / people). You have kasah (covered) all their chataah (sin). Salah (selah).
You have asap (taken) away all your ibarah (wrath). You have shawab (turn back / repent) from the charawan (fierceness) of your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).
Shawab (turn back / repent) us, Alahayam of our yashai (salvation), and cause your kais (indignation) toward us to parar (cease).
Will you be anap (angry) with us iwalam (forever)? Will you mashak (draw) out your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) to all dawar (generation / age / period)?
Won't you chayah (revive) us again, that your im (nation / people) may shamach (rejoice) in you?
Show us your loving chasad (grace), Yahawah. Nathan (give) us your yashai (salvation).

I will shamai (hearken / hear) what Al, Yahawah, will dabar (word / matter), for he will dabar (word / matter) shalawam (peace / safety) to his im (nation / people), his chasayad (saints); but let them not shawab (turn back / repent) again to kasalah (folly).
Surely his yashai (salvation) is qarawab (near) those who yaraa (fear) him, that kabawad (glory) may shakan (place) in our aratz (Earth/land).
Chasad (grace) and amath (truth) pagash (meet) together. Tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) and shalawam (peace / safety) have nashaq (kissed) each other.
Amath (truth) tzamach (springs) out of the aratz (Earth/land). Tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) has shaqap (looked) down from shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens).
Yes, Yahawah will nathan (give) that which is tawab (good / proper function). Our aratz (Earth/land) will nathan (give) its yabawal (increase).
Tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) halak (move) panayam (face) him, And prepares the darak (way) for his paim (steps).
Hear, Yahawah, and inah (answer / respond) me, for I am inay (poor) and inay (needy).
Shamar (keep/guard) my napash (soul), for I am chasayad (godly). You, my Alahayam, yashai (salvation) your ibad (servant) who batach (trusts) in you.
Be chanan (showing favor) to me, Adanay, for I qaraa (called) to you all yawam (day) long.
Bring shamach (joy) to the napash (soul) of your ibad (servant), for to you, Adanay, do I nashaa (lift) up my napash (soul).
For you, Adanay, are tawab (good / proper function), and salach (ready) to forgive; abundant in loving chasad (grace) to all those who qaraa (called) on you.
Azan (ear), Yahawah, my thapalah (prayer). Listen to the qawal (sound / voice) of my petitions.
In the yawam (day) of my tzarah (trouble) I will qaraa (called) on you, for you will inah (answer / respond) me.
There is no one like you among the Alahayam, Adanay, nor any maishah (deeds) like your deeds.
All gawayam (nations) you ishah (make) made will bawaa (come) and shachah (worship) panayam (face) you, Adanay. They shall kabad (glorify) your sham (name).
For you are gadawal (very great/important/mighty), and ishah (make) palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) things. You are Alahayam alone.
Yarah (teach) me your darak (way), Yahawah. I will halak (move) in your amath (truth). Make my labab (heart) undivided to yaraa (fear / be afraid) your sham (name).
I will yadah (praise) you, Adanay my Alahayam, with my whole labab (heart). I will kabad (glorify) your sham (name) forevermore.
For your loving chasad (grace) is gadawal (very great/important/mighty) toward me. You have natzal (delivered) my napash (soul) from the lowest shaawal (Sheol / afterlife).

Alahayam, the zad (proud) have qawam (rise up) up against me. A idah (company) of irayatz (violent) men have baqash (sought) after my napash (soul), and they don't shawam (place / establish / appoint) regard for you before them.
But you, Adanay, are a rachawam (merciful) and chanawan (gracious) Al, arak (slow) to rab (anger), and abundant in loving chasad (grace) and amath (truth).
Panah (turn) to me, and have chanan (showing favor) on me! Nathan (give) your iz (strength / might / refuge) to your ibad (servant). Yashai (salvation) the ban (son) of your handmaid.

Show me a awath (sign / mark / miracle) of your goodness, that those who shanaa (hate) me may raah (see) it, and be bawash (shamed), because you, Yahawah, have izar (helped) me, and nacham (turn away / repent) me.
His yasawadah (foundation) is in the qadash (set apart / make holy) hararay (mountains).
Yahawah ahab (love) the shairay (gates) of Tzayawan (Zion) more than all the mashakanawath (dwellings) of Yaiqab (Jacob).
Kabad (glorious) things are dabar (word / matter) about you, iyar (city) of Alahayam. Salah (selah).

I will zakar (remember) Rahab (Rahab) and Babal (Babylon) among those who yadai (acknowledge) me. Behold, Palashath (Philistia), Tzar (Tyre), and also Kawash (Ethiopia): "This one was yalad (birth / begot) there."
Yes, of Tzayawan (Zion) it will be amar (spoke), "This one and that one was yalad (birth / begot) in her;" the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan) himself will kawan (establish) her.
Yahawah will sapar (book), when he kathab (write) up the imayam (peoples), "This one was yalad (birth / begot) there." Salah (selah).
Those who shayar (sing) as well as those who dance say, "All my maiyan (springs) are in you."
Yahawah, the Alahayam of my yashawaih (salvation), I have tzaiq (cried) yawam (day) and layal (night) before you.
Let my thapalah (prayer) bawaa (come) into your panayam (face). Natah (turn) your azan (ear) to my ranah (cry).
For my napash (soul) is shabai (full) of raiwath (troubles). My chay (life) hagayaiw (draws) near to shaawal (Sheol / afterlife).
I am chashab (counted) among those who yarad (go) down into the bawar (pit). I am like a gabar (man) who has no help,
Set apart among the mawath (death), like the chalal (slain) who shakab (lie) in the qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher), whom you zakar (remember) no more. They are gazar (cut) off from your yad (hand).
You have shayath (put / appoint / make) me in the lowest bawar (pit), in the darkest matzalawath (depths).
Your chamah (wrath) samak (lies) heavily on me. You have inah (oppress / afflict) me with all your mashabar (waves). Salah (selah).
You have taken my yadai (friends) from me. You have shayath (put / appoint / make) me an thawaibah (abomination) to them. I am confined, and I can't yatzaa (go out / come out).
My iyan (eye) are dim from grief. I have qaraa (called) on you yawam (day), Yahawah. I have shatach (spread) out my kap (hands) to you.
Ishah (make) you show palaa (wonders) to the mawath (death)? Do the rapaa (dead) qawam (rise up) up and yadah (praise) you? Salah (selah).
Is your loving chasad (grace) sapar (book) in the qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher)? Or your amawanah (faithfulness) in abadawan (destruction)?
Are your palaa (wonders) yadai (made) known in the chashak (darkness)? Or your tzadaqah (righteousness) in the aratz (Earth/land) of nashayah (forgetfulness)?
But to you, Yahawah, I have shawai (cried). In the baqar (morning), my thapalah (prayer) qadam (comes) before you.
Yahawah, why do you reject my napash (soul)? Why do you sathar (hide) your panayam (face) from me?
I am inay (afflicted) and ready to gawai (die) from my nair (youth) up. While I nashaa (lift) your ayamah (terrors), I am pawan (distracted).
Your fierce charawan (wrath) ibar (pass over/through) gone over me. Your baiwathayam (terrors) have tzamath (cut) me off.
They sabab (came) around me like mayam (Waters) all yawam (day) long. They completely engulfed me.
You have put lover and rai (neigbor/another person) rachaq (far) from me, and my yadai (friends) into machashak (darkness).
I will shayar (sing) of the loving chasad (grace) of Yahawah iwalam (forever). With my pah (mouth), I yadai (will) make known your amawanah (faithfulness) to all dawar (generation / age / period).
I amar (spoke) declare, "chasad (grace) stands firm iwalam (forever). You kawan (established) the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens). Your amawanah (faithfulness) is in them."
"I have karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with my bachayar (chosen) one, I have shabai (swear / take oath) to Dawad (David), my ibad (servant),
‘I will kawan (establish) your zarai (seed) id (until / as far as), and banah (build) up your kasaa (throne) to all dawar (generation / age / period).'" Salah (selah).
The shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) will yadah (praise) your palaa (wonders), Yahawah; your amawanah (faithfulness) also in the qahal (assembly) of the qadawash (holy) ones.
For who in the shachaq (skies) can be irak (compared) to Yahawah? Who among the banay (sons) of the heavenly beings is damah (like) Yahawah,
A very awesome Al in the council of the qadawash (holy) ones, to be yaraa (fear / be afraid) above all those who are around him?
Yahawah, Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies), who is a chasayan (mighty) one, like you? Yah, your amawanah (faithfulness) is around you.
You mashal (rule/have dominion) the gaawath (pride) of the yam (sea/waters). When its gal (waves) shawaa (vanity) up, you calm them.
You have dakaa (broken) Rahab (Rahab) in dakaa (pieces), like one of the chalal (slain). You have pazar (scattered) your ayab (enemy) with your iz (strength / might / refuge) zarawai (arm).
The shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) are yours. The aratz (Earth/land) also is yours; the thabal (world) and its fullness. You have founded them.
The tzapawan (north) and the yamayan (right hand), you have baraa (created) them. Thabawar (Tabor) and Charamawan (Hermon) ranan (rejoice) in your sham (name).
You have a gabawarah (mighty) zarawai (arm). Your yad (hand) is izaz (strong), and your right yad (hand) is rawam (will lift up).

Tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) and tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) are the makawan (foundation) of your kasaa (throne). Loving chasad (grace) and amath (truth) qadam (go) before your panayam (face).
Ashar (who/that) are the im (nation / people) who learn to acclaim you. They halak (move) in the awar (light) of your panayam (face), Yahawah.
In your sham (name) they gayal (rejoice) all yawam (day). In your tzadaqah (righteousness), they are rawam (will lift up).
For you are the glory of their iz (strength / might / refuge). In your favor, our qaran (horn) will be rawam (will lift up).
For our magan (shield) belongs to Yahawah; our malak (king) to the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Then you dabar (word / matter) in chazawan (vision) to your chasayad (saints), and amar (spoke), "I have bestowed izar (strength) on the warrior. I have rawam (will lift up) a young gabawar (man) from the im (nation / people).
I matzaa (have) found Dawad (David), my ibad (servant). I have mashach (anointed) him with my qadash (set apart / make holy) shaman (oil),
With whom my yad (hand) shall be kawan (established). My zarawai (arm) will also amatz (strengthen) him.
No ayab (enemy) will tax him. No iwal (wicked) ban (son) will oppress him.
I will kathath (beat) down his tzar (oppressor / distressor) panayam (face) him, and nagap (strike) those who shanaa (hate) him.
But my amawanah (faithfulness) and my loving chasad (grace) will be with him. In my sham (name), his qaran (horn) will be rawam (will lift up).
I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) his yad (hand) also on the yam (sea/waters), and his right yamayan (right hand) on the naharawath (rivers).
He will qaraa (called) to me, ‘You are my ab (father), my Al, and the tzawar (rock) of my yashawaih (salvation)!'
I will also nathan (give) him my bakawar (firstborn), the highest of the malakay (kings) of the aratz (Earth/land).
I will shamar (keep/guard) my loving chasad (grace) for him forevermore. My barayath (covenant) will stand firm with him.
I will also shawam (place / establish / appoint) his zarai (seed) endure id (until / as far as), and his kasaa (throne) as the yamay (days) of shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens).
If his ban (son) izab (forsake) my thawarah (instruction), and don't yalak (walk) in my mashapat (ordinances);
If they chalal (break) my chaqah (statutes), and don't shamar (keep/guard) my matzawah (commandments);
Then I will paqad (visit) their pashai (sin) with the shabat (rod), and their iwan (guilt/iniquity) with nagaiyam (stripes).
But I will not completely pawar (take) my loving chasad (grace) from him, nor allow my amawanah (faithfulness) to shaqar (fail).
I will not chalal (break) my barayath (covenant), nor shanah (alter) what my shapah (lips) have uttered.
Achad (one) have I shabai (swear / take oath) by my qadash (set apart / make holy), I will not kazab (lie) to Dawad (David).
His zarai (seed) will endure iwalam (forever), his kasaa (throne) like the shamash (sun) before me.
It will be kawan (established) iwalam (forever) like the yarach (moon), the aman (believe / have faith) id (until / as far as) in the shachaq (sky)." Salah (selah).
But you have rejected and spurned. You ibar (pass over/through) been angry with your mashayach (anointed one).
You have renounced the barayath (covenant) of your ibad (servant). You have chalal (defiled) his nazar (crown / consecrate) in the dust.
You have paratz (broken) down all his gadarah (hedges). You have shawam (place / establish / appoint) his strongholds to machathah (ruin).
Ibar (pass over/through) who pass by the darak (way) rob him. He has become a charapah (reproach) to his neighbors.
You have rawam (will lift up) the right yamayan (right hand) of his tzar (oppressor / distressor). You have made all of his ayab (enemy) shamach (rejoice).
Yes, you shawab (turn back / repent) back the tzawar (edge) of his charab (sword), and haven't supported him in malachamah (battle).
You have ended his splendor, and thrown his kasaa (throne) down to the aratz (Earth/land).
You have shortened the yamay (days) of his ilawam (youth). You have itah (covered) him with bawashah (shame). Salah (selah).
How long, Yahawah? Will you sathar (hide) yourself natzach (forever)? Will your chamah (wrath) bair (burn) like ash (fire)?
Zakar (remember) how chalad (short) my time is! For what shawaa (vanity) have you created all the banay (children) of banay (men)!
What gabar (man) is he who shall chayah (live) and not raah (see) mawath (death), who shall malat (deliver) his napash (soul) from the yad (hand) of shaawal (Sheol / afterlife)? Salah (selah).
Adanay, where are your raashawan (former) chasad (grace) kindnesses, which you shabai (swear / take oath) to Dawad (David) in your amawanah (faithfulness)?
Zakar (remember), Adanay, the charapah (reproach) of your ibad (servant), how I nashaa (lift) in my chayaq (heart) the taunts of all the rab (mighty) imayam (peoples),
With which your ayab (enemy) have mocked, Yahawah, with which they have mocked the iqabawath (footsteps) of your mashayach (anointed one) one.
Barak (blessed) be Yahawah forevermore. Aman (believe / have faith), and aman (believe / have faith).
Adanay, you have been our maiwan (dwelling) place for all dawar (generation / age / period).

Before the harayam (mountains) were yalad (birth / begot) forth, before you had chawal (formed) the aratz (Earth/land) and the thabal (world), even from iwalam (forever) to iwalam (forever), you are Al.
You shawab (turn back / repent) anawash (man) to dakaa (destruction), saying, "shawab (turn back / repent), you banay (children) of adam (men)."
For a alap (thousand) shanayam (years) in your iyan (eye) are just like yesterday when it is past, like a ashamarah (watch) in the layal (night).
You sweep them away as they shanah (sleep). In the baqar (morning) they chalap (sprout) like new chatzayar (grass).
In the baqar (morning) it sprouts and springs up. By irab (evening), it is yabash (dry land) and dry.
For we are kalah (complete / finish) in your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting). We are bahal (troubled) in your chamah (wrath).
You have shayath (put / appoint / make) our iwan (guilt/iniquity) before you, our ilam (secret) sins in the maawar (Maawar / Luminary) of your panayam (face).
For all our yawam (day) have panah (turn) away in your ibarah (wrath). We kalah (complete / finish) our shanah (years) to an end as a sigh.

The yamay (days) of our shanah (years) are shabaiyam (seventy), or even by reason of gabawarah (strength) shamanayam (eighty) shanah (years); yet their pride is but imal (labor) and awan (sorrow), for it passes quickly, and we iwap (flying) away.
Who yadai (knows) the iz (strength / might / refuge) of your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), your ibarah (wrath) according to the yaraah (fear) that is due to you?
So yadai (teach) us to manah (number) our yawam (day), that we may gain a labab (heart) of chakamah (wisdom).
Relent, Yahawah! How long? Have compassion on your ibad (servant)!
Shabai (satisfy) us in the baqar (morning) with your loving chasad (grace), that we may ranan (rejoice) and be shamach (glad) all our yawam (day).
Shamach (make) us glad for as many yamawath (days) as you have inah (oppress / afflict) us, for as many shanawath (years) as we raah (see) seen rai (evil).
Let your pail (work) raah (see) to your ibad (servant); your glory to their ban (son).
Let the favor of the Adawan our Alahayam be on us; kawan (establish) the maishah (work) of our yad (hand) for us; yes, kawan (establish) the maishah (work) of our yad (hand).
He who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the sathar (secret / hidden) place of the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan) will lawan (rest) in the tzal (shadow) of the Shaday.
I will amar (spoke) of Yahawah, "He is my machasah (refuge) and my matzawad (fortress); my Alahayam, in whom I batach (trust)."
For he will natzal (deliver) you from the pach (snare / trap) of the yaqawash (fowler), and from the deadly dabar (word / matter).
He will sakak (cover) you with his abarah (feathers). Under his kanap (wings) you will take chasah (refuge). His amath (truth) is your tzanah (shield) and rampart.
You shall not be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of the pachad (fear / dread) by layal (night), nor of the chatz (arrow) that iwap (flying) by yawamam (by day);
Nor of the dabar (word / matter) that halak (move) in apal (darkness), nor of the qatab (destruction) that shawad (wastes) at noonday.
A thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand; but it will not come near you.
You will only look with your eyes, and see the recompense of the wicked.
Because you have made Yahweh your refuge, and the Ilayawan your dwelling place,
No evil shall happen to you, neither shall any plague come near your dwelling.
For he will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all your ways.
They will bear you up in their hands, so that you won't dash your foot against a stone.
You will tread on the lion and cobra. You will trample the young lion and the serpent underfoot.
"Because he has set his love on me, therefore I will deliver him. I will set him on high, because he has known my name.
He will call on me, and I will answer him. I will be with him in trouble. I will deliver him, and honor him.
I will satisfy him with long life, and show him my salvation."
It is a tawab (good / proper function) thing to give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah, to sing zamar (praises) to your sham (name), Most ilayawan (Ilayawan);
To proclaim your loving chasad (grace) in the baqar (morning), and your amawanah (faithfulness) every layal (night),
With the ten-stringed lute, with the harp, and with the melody of the lyre.
For you, Yahawah, shamach (have) made me glad through your pail (work). I will ranan (triumph) in the maishay (works) of your yad (hand).
How gadal (great) are your maishah (works), Yahawah! Your machashabah (thoughts) are very imaq (deep).
A senseless ayash (man / husband) doesn't yadai (know), neither does a kasayal (fool) bayan (between) this:
Though the rashai (wicked) parach (spring) up as the ishab (grass), and all the evildoers tzawatz (flourish), they will be destroyed id (until / as far as).
But you, Yahawah, are on marawam (high) forevermore.
For, behold, your ayab (enemy), Yahawah, for, behold, your ayab (enemy) shall abad (destroy / perish). All the evildoers will be parad (scattered).
But you have exalted my qaran (horn) like that of the wild ox. I am balal (anointed) with fresh shaman (oil).
My iyan (eye) nabat (has) also seen my shawar (enemies). My azan (ear) have shamai (hearken / hear) of the raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) qamayam (enemies) who rise up against me.
The tzadayaq (righteous) shall parach (flourish) like the thamar (palm) tree. He will shagah (grow) like a araz (cedar) in Labanawan (Lebanon).
They are shathal (planted) in Yahawah bayath (house). They will parach (flourish) in our Alahayam chatzarawath (courts).
They will still nawab (bring) forth fruit in shayabah (old age / white hair - due to age) age. They will be full of sap and rainan (green),
To show that Yahawah is yashar (upright). He is my tzawar (rock), and there is no iwal (unrighteousness) in him.
Yahawah malak (king)! He is labash (clothed) with gaawath (majesty)! Yahawah is armed with iz (strength / might / refuge). The thabal (world) also is kawan (established). It can't be mawat (moved).
Your kasaa (throne) is kawan (established) from long ago. You are from iwalam (forever).
The naharawath (floods) have nashaa (lift) up, Yahawah, the naharawath (floods) have nashaa (lift) up their qawal (sound / voice). The naharawath (floods) nashaa (lift) up their dakay (waves).
Above the qalawath (voices) of many mayam (Waters), the adayar (mighty) breakers of the yam (sea/waters), Yahawah on marawam (high) is adayar (mighty).
Your idah (statutes) stand firm. Qadash (set apart / make holy) adorns your bayath (house), Yahawah, forevermore.
Yahawah, you Al to whom naqamah (vengeance) belongs, you Al to whom naqamah (vengeance) belongs, yapai (shine) forth.
Nashaa (lift) up, you shapat (judge / judgement) of the aratz (Earth/land). Shawab (turn back / repent) back the gaah (proud) what they deserve.
Yahawah, how long will the rashai (wicked), how long will the rashai (wicked) ilaz (triumph)?
They nabai (pour) out arrogant yadabaraw (words). All the evildoers amar (spoke).
They break your im (nation / people) in yadakaaw (pieces), Yahawah, and inah (oppress / afflict) your nachalah (heritage).
They harag (kill) the alamanah (widow) and the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner), and ratzach (murder) the yathawam (fatherless).
They amar (spoke), "Yah will not raah (see), neither will Yaiqab (Jacob's) Alahayam bayan (between)."
Bayan (between), you senseless among the im (nation / people); you kasayalayam (fools), when will you be shakal (wise)?
He who implanted the azan (ear), won't he shamai (hearken / hear)? He who yatzar (formed) the iyan (eye), won't he nabat (see)?
He who disciplines the gawayam (nations), won't he punish? He who teaches adam (man) daith (knows).
Yahawah yadai (knows) the machashabawath (thoughts) of adam (man), that they are futile.
Ashar (who/that) is the gabar (man) whom you discipline, Yah, and lamad (teach / instruct) out of your thawarah (instruction);
That you may give him shaqat (rest) from the yamay (days) of rai (adversity), until the shachath (pit) is karah (dug) for the rashai (wicked).
For Yahawah won't reject his im (nation / people), neither will he izab (forsake) his nachalah (inheritance).
For mashapat (judgment) will shawab (turn back / repent) to tzadaq (righteous / just / fair). All the yashar (upright) in lab (heart) shall achar (other) it.
Who will qawam (rise up) up for me against the raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil)? Who will yatzab (stand) up for me against the evildoers?
Lawalaa (unless) Yahawah had been my izarah (help), my napash (soul) would have mait (soon) lived in dawamah (silence).
When I amar (spoke), "My ragal (feet / foot) is mawat (slipping)!" Your loving chasad (grace), Yahawah, said (held) me up.
In the rab (multitude) of my sharaip (thoughts) qarab (among / near) me, your thanachawam (comforts) shaii (delight) my napash (soul).
Shall the kasaa (throne) of hawah (calamity / destruction) chabar (have) fellowship with you, which brings about imal (mischief) by chaq (statute)?
They gadad (gather) themselves together against the napash (soul) of the tzadayaq (righteous), and rashai (condemn) the naqay (innocent) dam (blood).
But Yahawah has been my high tower, my Alahayam, the tzawar (rock) of my machasah (refuge).
He has shawab (turn back / repent) on them their own awan (iniquity), and will tzamath (cut) them off in their own rai (wickedness). Yahawah, our Alahayam, will tzamath (cut) them off.
Oh yalak (come), let's ranan (sing) to Yahawah. Let's rawai (shout) aloud to the tzawar (rock) of our yashai (salvation)!
Let's qadam (come) panayam (face) his presence with thanksgiving. Let's extol him with zamarawath (songs)!
For Yahawah is a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) Al, a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) malak (king) above all Al.
In his yad (hand) are the machaqar (deep) places of the aratz (Earth/land). The heights of the harayam (mountains) are also his.
The yam (sea/waters) is his, and he ishah (make) it. His yad (hand) yatzar (formed) the dry yabashath (land).
Oh bawaa (come), let's shachah (worship) and karai (bow) down. Let's barak (blessed) panayam (face) Yahawah, our Maker,
For he is our Alahayam. We are the im (nation / people) of his maraiyath (pasture), and the tzaan (sheep) in his care. Today, oh that you would shamai (hearken / hear) his qawal (sound / voice)!
Don't harden your labab (heart), as at marayabah (meribah), as in the yawam (day) of Massah in the madabar (wilderness),
When your ab (father) nasah (tempted) me, tested me, and raah (see) my pail (work).

Arabaiyam (forty) shanah (long) years I was grieved with that dawar (generation / age / period), and amar (spoke), "It is a im (nation / people) that thaiy (errs) in their labab (heart). They yadai (have) not known my darak (ways)."
Therefore I shabai (swear / take oath) in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), "They won't bawaa (come) into my manawachah (rest)."
Shayar (sing) to Yahawah a chadash (new) shayar (song)! Shayar (sing) to Yahawah, all the aratz (Earth/land).
Shayar (sing) to Yahawah! Barak (blessed) his sham (name)! Proclaim his yashawaih (salvation) from yawam (day) to yawam (day)!
Sapar (book) his kabawad (glory) among the gawayam (nations), his palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) works among all the imayam (peoples).
For gadawal (very great/important/mighty) is Yahawah, and maad (greatly) to be halal (praise)! He is to be yaraa (fear / be afraid) above all Alahayam.
For all the Alahayam of the imayam (peoples) are alayalayam (idols), but Yahawah ishah (make) the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens).
Honor and hadar (glory / majesty / splendor) are panayam (face) him. Iz (strength / might / refuge) and thapaarah (beauty) are in his maqadash (sanctuary).
Yahab (ascribe) to Yahawah, you mashapachawath (families) of imayam (nations), yahab (ascribe) to Yahawah kabawad (glory) and iz (strength / might / refuge).
Yahab (ascribe) to Yahawah the kabawad (glory) due to his sham (name). Nashaa (lift) an manachah (offering), and bawaa (come) into his chatzar (courts).
Shachah (worship) Yahawah in qadash (set apart / make holy) array. Chawal (tremble) panayam (face) him, all the aratz (Earth/land).

Amar (spoke) among the gawayam (nations), "Yahawah malak (king)." The thabal (world) is also kawan (established). It can't be mawat (moved). He will dayan (judge) the imayam (peoples) with mayashar (equity).
Let the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) be gayal (glad), and let the aratz (Earth/land) shamach (rejoice). Let the yam (sea/waters) raim (roar), and its fullness!
Let the shadah (field) and all that is in it exult! Then all the itzay (trees) of the yair (woods) shall ranan (sing) for joy

Panayam (face) Yahawah; for he bawaa (come), for he bawaa (come) to shapat (judge / judgement) the aratz (Earth/land). He will shapat (judge / judgement) the thabal (world) with tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), the imayam (peoples) with his amawanah (truth).
Yahawah malak (king)! Let the aratz (Earth/land) gayal (rejoice)! Let the rab (multitude) of ayayam (islands) be shamach (glad)!
Inan (cloud) and irapal (darkness) are around him. Tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) and mashapat (justice) are the makawan (foundation) of his kasaa (throne).
A ash (fire) yalak (goes) panayam (face) him, and lahat (burns) up his tzar (oppressor / distressor) on sabayab (surrounding) side.
His baraq (lightning) haayaraw (lights) up the thabal (world). The thabal (earth) raah (see), and chawal (trembles).
The harayam (mountains) masas (melt) like dawanag (wax) at the panayam (face) of Yahawah, at the panayam (face) of the Adawan of the whole aratz (Earth/land).
The shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) nagad (declare) his tzadaq (righteous / just / fair). All the imayam (peoples) raah (see) seen his kabawad (glory).
Let all them be bawash (shamed) who ibad (servant) engraved pasal (image), who halal (praise) in their alayalayam (idols). Shachah (worship) him, all you Alahayam!
Tzayawan (Zion) shamai (hearken / hear) and was shamach (glad). The banawath (daughters) of Yahawadah (Judah) gayal (rejoiced), because of your mashapat (judgments), Yahawah.
For you, Yahawah, are most ilayawan (Ilayawan) above all the aratz (Earth/land). You are ilah (go up / offer) maad (far) above all Alahayam.
You who ahab (love) Yahawah, shanaa (hate) rai (evil). He shamar (keep/guard) the napashawath (souls) of his chasayad (saints). He natzal (delivers) them out of the yad (hand) of the rashai (wicked).
Awar (light) is zarai (sown) for the tzadayaq (righteous), and shamachah (gladness) for the yashar (upright) in lab (heart).
Be shamach (glad) in Yahawah, you tzadayaq (righteous) people! Give hawadaw (thanks) to his qadash (set apart / make holy) zakar (remember).

Shayar (sing) to Yahawah a chadash (new) shayar (song), for he ishah (make) done palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) things! His right yamayan (right hand), and his qadash (set apart / make holy) zarawai (arm), have worked yashai (salvation) for him.
Yahawah yadai (has) made known his yashawaih (salvation). He has openly shown his tzadaqah (righteousness) in the iyan (eye) of the gawayam (nations).

He has zakar (remember) his loving chasad (grace) and his amawanah (faithfulness) toward the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel). All the apasay (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land) raah (see) seen the yashawaih (salvation) of our Alahayam.
Rawai (make) a joyful noise to Yahawah, all the aratz (Earth/land)! Burst out and sing for ranan (joy), yes, sing zamaraw (praises)!
Zamar (sing) praises to Yahawah with the kanawar (harp), with the kanawar (harp) and the qawal (sound / voice) of zamarah (melody).
With chatzatzarawath (trumpets) and qawal (sound / voice) of the ram's shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn), rawai (make) a joyful noise panayam (face) the malak (king), Yahawah.
Let the yam (sea/waters) raim (roar) with its fullness; the thabal (world), and those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein.
Let the naharawath (rivers) machaa (clap) their kap (hands). Let the harayam (mountains) ranan (sing) for joy yachad (together).

Let them sing panayam (face) Yahawah, for he bawaa (come) to shapat (judge / judgement) the aratz (Earth/land). He will shapat (judge / judgement) the thabal (world) with tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and the imayam (peoples) with mayashar (equity).
Yahawah malak (king)! Let the imayam (peoples) ragaz (tremble). He yashab (inhabit/dwell) enthroned among the karawab (cherubim). Let the aratz (Earth/land) be nawat (moved).
Yahawah is gadawal (very great/important/mighty) in Tzayawan (Zion). He is rawam (will lift up) above all the imayam (peoples).
Let them yadah (praise) your gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and awesome sham (name). He is qadawash (holy)!

The malak (king) iz (strength / might / refuge) also ahab (love) mashapat (justice). You do kawan (establish) mayashar (equity). You ishah (make) mashapat (justice) and tzadaqah (righteousness) in Yaiqab (Jacob).
Rawam (will lift up) Yahawah our Alahayam. Shachah (worship) at his footstool. He is qadawash (holy)!

Mashah (Moses) and Aharawan (Aaron) were among his kahan (priest), Shamawaal (Samuel) among those who qaraa (called) on his sham (name); they qaraa (called) on Yahawah, and he inah (answer / respond) them.
He dabar (word / matter) to them in the imawad (pillar) of inan (cloud). They shamar (keep/guard) his idah (testimonies), the chaq (statute) that he nathan (give) them.
You inah (answer / respond) them, Yahawah our Alahayam. You are a Al who nashaa (lift) them, although you naqam (took) vengeance for their ilayalah (doings).
Rawam (will lift up) Yahawah, our Alahayam. Shachah (worship) at his qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain), for Yahawah, our Alahayam, is qadawash (holy)!
Rawai (shout) for joy to Yahawah, all you aratz (Earth/land)!
Ibad (servant) Yahawah with shamachah (gladness). Bawaa (come) panayam (face) his presence with rananah (singing).
Yadai (know) that Yahawah, he is Alahayam. It is he who ishah (make) made us, and we are his. We are his im (nation / people), and the tzaan (sheep) of his maraiyath (pasture).
Bawaa (come) into his shair (gates) with thanksgiving, into his chatzar (courts) with thahalah (praise). Give hawadaw (thanks) to him, and barak (blessed) his sham (name).
For Yahawah is tawab (good / proper function). His loving tawab (good / proper function) endures iwalam (forever), his amawanah (faithfulness) to all dawar (generation / age / period).
I will shayar (sing) of loving chasad (grace) and mashapat (justice). To you, Yahawah, I will sing zamar (praises).
I will be careful to live a blameless darak (life). When will you bawaa (come) to me? I will halak (move) qarab (among / near) my bayath (house) with a blameless labab (heart).
I will shayath (put / appoint / make) no vile thing before my iyan (eye). I shanaa (hate) the deeds of faithless men. They will not cling to me.
A iqash (perverse) labab (heart) will be far from me. I yadai (will) have nothing to do with rai (evil).
I will silence whoever secretly lashan (slanders) his neighbor. I won't tolerate iyan (eye) who is haughty and conceited.

My iyan (eye) will be on the aman (believe / have faith) of the aratz (Earth/land), that they may yashab (inhabit/dwell) with me. He who halak (move) in a thamayam (complete / whole) darak (way), he will sharath (serve) me.
He who practices ramayah (deceit) won't yashab (inhabit/dwell) qarab (among / near) my bayath (house). He who dabar (word / matter) falsehood won't be kawan (established) before my iyan (eye).
Baqar (morning) by morning, I will tzamath (destroy) all the rashai (wicked) of the aratz (Earth/land); to karath (cut) off all the pailay (workers) of awan (iniquity) from Yahawah iyar (city).
Shamai (hearken / hear) my thapalah (prayer), Yahawah! Let my cry bawaa (come) to you.

Don't sathar (hide) your panayam (face) from me in the yawam (day) of my tzar (oppressor / distressor). Natah (turn) your azan (ear) to me. Inah (answer / respond) me mahar (quickly) in the yawam (day) when I qaraa (called).
For my yawam (day) kalah (complete / finish) away like ishan (smoke). My itzam (bones) are charar (burned) as a torch.
My lab (heart) is blighted like ishab (grass), and yabash (dry land), for I shakach (forget) to akal (eat) my lacham (bread).
By reason of the qawal (sound / voice) of my anachah (groaning), my itzam (bones) stick to my bashar (flesh).
I am damah (like) a pelican of the madabar (wilderness). I have become as an kawas (owl) of the charabah (waste) places.
I shaqad (watch), and have become like a tzapawar (sparrow) that is badad (alone) on the housetop.
My ayab (enemy) charap (reproach) me all yawam (day). Those who are halal (praise) at me use my name as a curse.
For I have akal (eat) ashes like lacham (bread), and mixed my shaqaw (drink) with tears,
Panayam (face) of your zaim (indignation) and your qatzap (wrath), for you have nashaa (lift) me up, and shalak (thrown) me away.
My yawam (day) are like a long tzal (shadow). I have yabash (dry land) like ishab (grass).
But you, Yahawah, will yashab (inhabit/dwell) iwalam (forever); your renown yashab (inhabit/dwell) to all dawar (generation / age / period).
You will qawam (rise up) and have racham (show mercy / love) on Tzayawan (Zion); for it is ith (time) to chanan (showing favor) pity on her. Yes, the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) time bawaa (come) come.
For your ibad (servant) ratzah (take) pleasure in her aban (stone), and chanan (showing favor) pity on her ipar (dust).
So the gawayam (nations) will yaraa (fear / be afraid) the sham (name) of Yahawah; all the malakay (kings) of the aratz (Earth/land) your kabawad (glory).
For Yahawah has banah (build) up Tzayawan (Zion). He has raah (see) in his kabawad (glory).
He has responded to the thapalah (prayer) of the irair (destitute), and has not bazah (despised) their thapalah (prayer).
This will be kathab (write) for the dawar (generation / age / period) to acharawan (come). A im (nation / people) which will be baraa (created) will halal (praise) Yah.
For he has shaqap (looked) down from the marawam (height) of his qadash (set apart / make holy). From shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), Yahawah nabat (saw) the aratz (Earth/land);
To shamai (hearken / hear) the groans of the asayar (prisoner); to pathach (free) those who are condemned to thamawathah (death);
That men may sapar (book) the sham (name) of Yahawah in Tzayawan (Zion), and his thahalah (praise) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem);
When the imayam (peoples) are qabatz (gathered) yachad (together), the mamalakawath (kingdoms), to ibad (servant) Yahawah.
He inah (oppress / afflict) my kach (strength / mighty / power) darak (along) the course. He shortened my yawam (day).
I amar (spoke), "My Al, don't ilah (go up / offer) me away in the chatzay (midst) of my yawam (day). Your shanah (years) are throughout all dawarayam (generations).
Of panayam (face), you yasad (laid) the foundation of the aratz (Earth/land). The shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) are the maishah (work) of your yad (hand).
They will abad (destroy / perish), but you will imad (endure). Yes, all of them will wear out like a bagad (garment). You will chalap (change) them like a cloak, and they will be chalap (changed).
But you are the same. Your shanah (years) will thamam (have) no end.
The banay (children) of your ibad (servant) will shakan (place). Their zarai (seed) will be kawan (established) panayam (face) you."
Barak (blessed) Yahawah, my napash (soul)! All that is qarab (among / near) me, praise his qadash (set apart / make holy) sham (name)!
Barak (blessed) Yahawah, my napash (soul), and don't shakach (forget) all his gamawal (benefits);
Who salach (forgive/pardon/make clean) all your iwan (guilt/iniquity); who rapaa (heals) all your thachalawaa (diseases);
Who gaal (redeems) your chay (life) from shachath (destruction); who itar (crowns) you with loving chasad (grace) and tender rachamayam (mercies);
Who shabai (satisfies) your desire with tawab (good / proper function) things, so that your naiwar (youth) is chadash (renewed) like the nashar (eagle's).
Yahawah ishah (make) tzadaqah (righteousness) acts, and mashapat (justice) for all who are ishaq (oppressed).
He yadai (made) known his darak (ways) to Mashah (Moses), his ilayalah (deeds) to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).
Yahawah is rachawam (merciful) and chanawan (gracious), arak (slow) to ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and abundant in loving chasad (grace).
He will not natzach (always) accuse; neither will he stay angry iwalam (forever).
He ishah (make) not dealt with us according to our chataa (sins), nor repaid us for our iwan (guilt/iniquity).
For as the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) are gabah (high) above the aratz (Earth/land), so gabar (great) is his loving chasad (grace) toward those who yaraa (fear) him.
As rachaq (far) as the mazarach (east) is from the mairab (west), so rachaq (far) has he removed our pashai (transgressions) from us.
Like a ab (father) racham (show mercy / love) compassion on his banayam (children), so Yahawah racham (show mercy / love) compassion on those who yaraa (fear) him.
For he yadai (knows) how we are made. He zakar (remember) that we are ipar (dust).
As for anawash (man), his yawam (day) are like chatzayar (grass). As a tzayatz (flower) of the shadah (field), so he flourishes.
For the rawach (spirit / wind) passes over it, and it is gone. Its maqawam (place) remembers it no more.
But Yahawah loving chasad (grace) is from iwalam (forever) to iwalam (forever) with those who yaraa (fear) him, his tzadaqah (righteousness) to banay (childrens) banay (children);
To those who shamar (keep/guard) his barayath (covenant), to those who zakar (remember) to obey his paqawad (precepts).
Yahawah has kawan (established) his kasaa (throne) in the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens). His malakawath (kingdom) mashal (rule/have dominion) over all.

Barak (blessed) Yahawah, you malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of his, who are gabawar (mighty) in kach (strength / mighty / power), who ishah (make) his dabar (word / matter), shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of his dabar (word / matter).
Barak (blessed) Yahawah, all you tzabaa (troop) of his, you sharath (servants) of his, who ishah (make) his ratzawan (pleasure).
Barak (blessed) Yahawah, all you maishah (works) of his, in all maqamawath (places) of his mamashalah (dominion). Barak (blessed) Yahawah, my napash (soul)!
Barak (blessed) Yahawah, my napash (soul). Yahawah, my Alahayam, you are very gadal (great). You are labash (clothed) with honor and hadar (glory / majesty / splendor).
He itah (covers) himself with awar (light) as with a shalamah (dress / garment). He stretches out the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) like a yarayaih (curtain).

He qarah (lays) the beams of his rooms in the mayam (Waters). He shawam (place / establish / appoint) the ibayam (clouds) his rakawab (chariot). He halak (move) on the kanapay (wings) of the rawach (spirit / wind).
He ishah (make) his malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) rawachawath (winds); his sharath (servants) lahat (flames) of ash (fire).
He yasad (laid) the makawan (foundations) of the aratz (Earth/land), that it should not be mawat (moved) iwalam (forever).
You kasah (covered) it with the thahawam (depths) as with a cloak. The mayam (Waters) imad (stood) above the harayam (mountains).
At your gairah (rebuke) they nawas (fled). At the qawal (sound / voice) of your raim (thunder) they hurried away.
The harayam (mountains) ilah (go up / offer), the baqaiwath (valleys) yarad (sank) down, to the maqawam (place) which you had assigned to them.
You have shawam (place / establish / appoint) a boundary that they may not ibar (pass over/through) over; that they don't shawab (turn back / repent) again to kasah (cover) the aratz (Earth/land).
He shalach (send) forth maiyanayam (springs) into the nachalayam (valleys). They halak (move) among the harayam (mountains).
They shaqah (give) drink to every animal of the shadah (field). The paraa (wild) donkeys shabar (quench) their tzamaa (thirst).
The iwap (flying) of the sky nest by them. They nathan (give) bayan (between) the branches.
He shaqah (waters) the harayam (mountains) from his rooms. The aratz (Earth/land) is shabai (filled) with the paray (fruit) of your maishah (works).
He causes the chatzayar (grass) to tzamach (grow) for the livestock, and plants for adam (man) to cultivate, that he may yatzaa (go out / come out) forth lacham (food) out of the aratz (Earth/land):

Yayan (wine) that shamach (makes) glad the labab (heart) of anawash (man), shaman (oil) to make his panayam (face) to tzahal (shine), and lacham (bread) that said (strengthens) anawash (man's) labab (heart).
Yahawah itzay (trees) are well watered, the arazay (cedars) of Labanawan (Lebanon), which he has natai (planted);
Where the tzaparayam (birds) qanan (make) their nests. The chasayadah (stork) makes its bayath (house) in the barawash (fir) trees.
The gabah (high) harayam (mountains) are for the yail (wild) goats. The salaiyam (rocks) are a machasah (refuge) for the Shapan (rock) badgers.
He ishah (make) the yarach (moon) for mawaidayam (seasons). The shamash (sun) yadai (knows) when to set.
You shayath (put / appoint / make) chashak (darkness), and it is layal (night), in which all the animals of the yair (forest) prowl.
The young kapayarayam (lions) shaag (roar) after their tarap (prey), and baqash (seek) their akal (food) from Al.
The shamash (sun) zarach (rises), and they steal asap (away), and rabatz (lay) down in their maiwanah (dens).
Adam (man) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to his pail (work), to his ibadah (labor) until the irab (evening).
Yahawah, how many are your maishah (works)! In chakamah (wisdom) ishah (make) you made them all. The aratz (Earth/land) is malaa (full) of your riches.
There is the yam (sea/waters), gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and rachab (wide), in which are innumerable living things, both qatan (small / young / least) and large animals.
There the anayawath (ships) halak (move), and lawayathan (leviathan), whom you yatzar (formed) to shachaq (play) there.
These all shabar (wait) for you, that you may nathan (give) them their akal (food) in due ith (season).
You nathan (give) to them; they laqat (gather). You pathach (open) your yad (hand); they are shabai (satisfied) with tawab (good / proper function).
You sathar (hide) your panayam (face): they are bahal (troubled); you asap (take) away their rawach (spirit / wind): they gawai (die), and shawab (turn back / repent) to the ipar (dust).
You shalach (send) forth your rawach (spirit / wind): they are baraa (created). You chadash (renew) the panayam (face) of the adamah (ground).
Let the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah endure iwalam (forever). Let Yahawah shamach (rejoice) in his maishah (works).
He nabat (looks) at the aratz (Earth/land), and it raid (trembles). He touches the harayam (mountains), and they ishan (smoke).
I will shayar (sing) to Yahawah as long as I chay (life). I will zamar (sing) praise to my Alahayam iwad (more/again) I have any being.
Let your shayach (meditation) be irab (evening) to him. I will shamach (rejoice) in Yahawah.
Let chataayam (sinners) be thamam (consumed) out of the aratz (Earth/land). Let the rashai (wicked) be no more. Barak (blessed) Yahawah, my napash (soul). Halal (praise) Yah!
Give hawadaw (thanks) to Yahawah! Qaraa (called) on his sham (name)! Make his ilayalah (doings) yadai (known) among the imayam (peoples).
Shayar (sing) to him, sing zamaraw (praises) to him! Tell of all his marvelous palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous).
Glory in his qadash (set apart / make holy) sham (name). Let the lab (heart) of those who baqash (seek) Yahawah shamach (rejoice).
Darash (seek) Yahawah and his iz (strength / might / refuge). Baqash (seek) his panayam (face) thamayad (forever) more.
Zakar (remember) his marvelous palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) that he ishah (make) done; his mawapath (wonders), and the mashapatay (judgments) of his pah (mouth),
You zarai (seed) of Abaraham (Abraham), his ibad (servant), you banay (children) of Yaiqab (Jacob), his bachayar (chosen) ones.
He is Yahawah, our Alahayam. His mashapat (judgments) are in all the aratz (Earth/land).
He has zakar (remember) his barayath (covenant) iwalam (forever), the dabar (word / matter) which he tzawah (commanded) to a alap (thousand) dawar (generation / age / period),
The karath (cut) which he made with Abaraham (Abraham), his shabawaih (oath) to Yashachaq (Isaac),
And imad (confirmed) the same to Yaiqab (Jacob) for a chaq (statute); to Yashar-Al (Israel) for an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant),
Amar (spoke), "To you I will nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (Canaan), the chabal (lot) of your nachalah (inheritance);"
When they were but a math (few) men in masapar (number), yes, very mait (few), and foreigners in it.
They halak (move) about from gaway (heathen / nation) to nation, from one mamalakah (kingdom) to achar (other) im (nation / people).
He allowed no adam (one) to ishaq (do) them wrong. Yes, he yakach (reproved) malakayam (kings) for their sakes,
"Don't nagai (touch) my mashayach (anointed one) ones! Do my nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) no raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil)!"
He qaraa (called) for a raib (famine) on the aratz (Earth/land). He shabar (destroyed) the lacham (food) supplies.
He shalach (send) a ayash (man / husband) panayam (face) them. Yawasap (Joseph) was makar (sold) for a ibad (servant).
They bruised his ragal (feet / foot) with shackles. His neck was locked in barazal (irons),
Until the ith (time) that his dabar (word / matter) happened, and Yahawah amarah (sayings) proved him true.
The malak (king) shalach (send) and freed him; even the mashal (rule/have dominion) of imayam (peoples), and pathach (let) him go free.
He shawam (place / establish / appoint) him Adawan of his bayath (house), and mashal (rule/have dominion) of all of his qanayan (possessions);
To discipline his shar (prince / ruler) at his napash (soul), and to teach his zaqan (elders) chakam (wisdom).
Yashar-Al (Israel) also bawaa (come) into Matzarayam (Egypt). Yaiqab (Jacob) lived in the aratz (Earth/land) of Cham (Ham).
He parah (increased) his im (nation / people) maad (greatly), and itzam (made) them stronger than their tzar (oppressor / distressor).
He hapak (turned) their lab (heart) to shanaa (hate) his im (nation / people), to nakal (conspire) against his ibad (servant).
He shalach (send) Mashah (Moses), his ibad (servant), and Aharawan (Aaron), whom he had bachar (chosen).
They performed awath (sign / mark / miracle) among them, and mapathayam (wonders) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Cham (Ham).
He shalach (send) chashak (darkness), and made it chashak (darkness). They didn't marah (rebel) against his dabar (word / matter).
He hapak (turned) their mayam (Waters) into dam (blood), and mawath (death) their dagah (fish).
Their aratz (Earth/land) swarmed with tzaparadaiyam (frogs), even in the rooms of their malak (king).
He amar (spoke), and irab (evening) of flies bawaa (come), and kan (for sure) in all their gabawal (border/boundary).
He nathan (give) them barad (hail) for gasham (rain), with lightning in their aratz (Earth/land).
He nakah (struck) their gapan (vines) and also their thaan (fig) trees, and shattered the itz (trees) of their country.
He amar (spoke), and the arabah (locusts) bawaa (come), and the grasshoppers, without masapar (number),
Akal (eat) up every plant in their aratz (Earth/land); and akal (eat) up the paray (fruit) of their aratz (Earth/land).
He nakah (struck) also all the bakawar (firstborn) in their aratz (Earth/land), the raashayath (beginning) fruits of all their manhood.
He yatzaa (go out / come out) them forth with kasap (silver) and zahab (gold). There was not one kashal (stumble / stagger) person among his shabat (tribes).
Matzarayam (Egypt) was shamach (glad) when they departed, for the pachad (fear / dread) of them napal (fall / be cast down) fallen on them.
He parash (spread) a inan (cloud) for a masak (covering), ash (fire) to give awar (light) in the layal (night).
They shaal (asked), and he bawaa (come) shalaw (quails), and shabai (satisfied) them with the lacham (bread) of the sky.
He pathach (opened) the tzawar (rock), and mayam (Waters) zawab (flow) out. They halak (move) as a nahar (river) in the tzayah (dry) places.
For he zakar (remember) his qadash (set apart / make holy) dabar (word / matter), and Abaraham (Abraham), his ibad (servant).
He yatzaa (go out / come out) forth his im (nation / people) with shashawan (joy), his bachayar (chosen) with ranah (singing).
He nathan (give) them the aratzawath (lands) of the gawayam (nations). They took the imal (labor) of the laamayam (peoples) in yarash (possession),
That they might shamar (keep/guard) his chaq (statute), and shamar (keep/guard) his thawarah (instruction). Halal (praise) Yah!
Halal (praise) Yahawah! Give hawadaw (thanks) to Yahawah, for he is tawab (good / proper function), for his loving tawab (good / proper function) endures iwalam (forever).
