Yes, if you qaraa (called) out for discernment, and nathan (give) up your qawal (sound / voice) for thabawan (understanding);
If you baqash (seek) her as kasap (silver), and chapash (search) for her as for matamawan (hidden) treasures:
Then you will bayan (between) the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah, and matzaa (find) the daith (knowledge) of Alahayam.
For Yahawah nathan (give) chakamah (wisdom). Out of his pah (mouth) comes daith (knowledge) and thabawan (understanding).
He tzapan (lays) up sound thawashayah (wisdom) for the yashar (upright). He is a magan (shield) to those who halak (move) in tham (integrity);
That he may guard the arachawath (paths) of mashapat (justice), and shamar (keep/guard) the darak (way) of his chasayad (saints).
Then you will bayan (between) tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) and mashapat (justice), mayashar (equity) and every tawab (good / proper function) maigal (path).
For chakamah (wisdom) will bawaa (come) into your lab (heart). Daith (knowledge) will be naim (pleasant) to your napash (soul).
Mazamah (discretion) will shamar (keep/guard) over you. Thabawan (understanding) will shamar (keep/guard) you,
To natzal (deliver) you from the darak (way) of rai (evil), from the ayash (man / husband) who dabar (word / matter) thahapakah (perverse) things;
Who izab (forsake) the arachawath (paths) of yashar (upright), to yalak (walk) in the darakay (ways) of chashak (darkness);
Who shamach (rejoice) to ishah (make) rai (evil), and delight in the perverseness of rai (evil);
Who are iqash (crooked) in their arach (ways), and wayward in their maigal (paths):
To natzal (deliver) you from the zawar (strange) ayashah (woman / wife), even from the nakaray (foreigner) who chalaq (flatters) with her amar (spoke);
Who izab (forsakes) the alawap (friend) of her naiwar (youth), and shakach (forgets) the barayath (covenant) of her Alahayam:
For her bayath (house) leads down to mawath (death), her maigal (paths) to the rapaa (dead).
None who bawaa (come) to her shawab (turn back / repent) again, neither do they nashag (attain) to the arachawath (paths) of chay (life):
That you may yalak (walk) in the darak (way) of tawab (good / proper function) men, and shamar (keep/guard) the arachawath (paths) of the tzadayaq (righteous).
For the yashar (upright) will shakan (place) in the aratz (Earth/land). The thamayam (complete / whole) will yathar (remain) in it.
But the rashai (wicked) will be karath (cut) off from the aratz (Earth/land). The bagad (treacherous) will be nasach (rooted) out of it.
My ban (son), don't shakach (forget) my teaching; but let your lab (heart) natzar (keep) my matzawah (commandments):
For arak (length) of yamayam (days), and shanawath (years) of chay (life), and shalawam (peace / safety), will they yasap (add) to you.
Don't let chasad (grace) and amath (truth) izab (forsake) you. Qashar (bind) them around your garagarawath (neck). Kathab (write) them on the tablet of your lab (heart).
So you will matzaa (find) favor, and tawab (good / proper function) shakal (understanding) in the iyan (eye) of Alahayam and adam (man).
Batach (trust) in Yahawah with all your lab (heart), and don't shain (lean) on your own bayanah (understanding).
In all your darak (ways) yadai (acknowledge) him, and he will make your arach (paths) yashar (upright).
Don't be chakam (wise) in your own iyan (eye). Yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah, and sawar (depart) from rai (evil).
It will be rapaawath (health) to your body, and nourishment to your itzam (bones).
Honor Yahawah with your hawan (substance), with the raashayath (beginning) fruits of all your thabawaah (increase):
So your asam (barns) will be malaa (filled) with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new thayarawash (wine).
My ban (son), don't maas (despise) Yahawah mawasar (discipline), neither be qawatz (weary) of his thawakachah (reproof):
For whom Yahawah ahab (love), he yakach (reproves); even as a ab (father) reproves the ban (son) in whom he ratzah (delights).
Ashar (who/that) is the adam (man) who matzaa (finds) chakamah (wisdom), the adam (man) who pawaq (gets) thabawan (understanding).
For her sachar (good) profit is tawab (good / proper function) than getting kasap (silver), and her thabawaah (return) is better than fine charawatz (gold).
She is more yaqar (precious) than panayayam (rubies). None of the things you can chapatz (desire) are to be shawah (compared) to her.
Arak (length) of yamayam (days) is in her right yamayan (right hand). In her left shamaawal (left hand) are riches and honor.
Her darak (ways) are darak (ways) of naim (pleasantness). All her nathayab (paths) are shalawam (peace / safety).
She is a itz (tree) of chay (life) to those who lay chazaq (hold) of her. Ashar (who/that) is everyone who thamak (retains) her.
By chakamah (wisdom) Yahawah founded the aratz (Earth/land). By chakamah (understanding), he kawan (established) the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens).
By his daith (knowledge), the thahawamawath (depths) were baqai (broken) up, and the shachaqayam (skies) raip (drop) down the tal (dew).
My ban (son), let them not depart from your iyan (eye). Natzar (keep) sound thawashayah (wisdom) and discretion:
So they will be chay (life) to your napash (soul), and chan (favor) for your garagarawath (neck).
Then you shall yalak (walk) in your darak (way) securely. Your ragal (feet / foot) won't nagap (stumble).
When you shakab (lie) down, you will not be pachad (fear / dread). Yes, you will shakab (lie) down, and your shanah (sleep) will be irab (evening).
Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of pathaawam (sudden) pachad (fear / dread), neither of the shawaa (vanity) of the rashai (wicked), when it bawaa (come):
For Yahawah will be your kasal (confidence), and will shamar (keep/guard) your ragal (feet / foot) from lakad (being) taken.
Don't manai (withhold) tawab (good / proper function) from bail (those) to whom it is due, when it is in the al (Alahayam) of your yad (hand) to ishah (make) it.
Don't amar (spoke) to your neighbor, "yalak (go), and shawab (turn back / repent) again; machar (tomorrow) I will nathan (give) it to you," when you yash (have) it by you.
Don't charash (devise) rai (evil) against your neighbor, since he yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely by you.
Don't rayab (strive) with a adam (man) chanam (without) cause, if he has gamal (done) you no rai (harm).
Don't qanaa (jealous) the ayash (man / husband) of violence. Bachar (choose) none of his darak (ways).
For the lawaz (perverse) is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, but his friendship is with the yashar (upright).
Yahawah maarah (curse) is in the bayath (house) of the rashai (wicked), but he blesses the nawah (habitation) of the tzadayaq (righteous).
Surely he latzayam (mocks) the latzayam (mockers), but he nathan (give) chan (favor) to the inay (humble).
The chakam (wise) will nachal (inherit) kabawad (glory), but qalawan (shame) will be the rawam (will lift up) of kasayalayam (fools).
Shamai (hearken / hear), banayam (sons), to a ab (father) mawasar (instruction). Pay attention and yadai (know) bayanah (understanding);
For I nathan (give) you sound laqach (learning). Don't izab (forsake) my thawarah (instruction).
For I was a ban (son) to my ab (father), rak (tender) and an only child in the panayam (face) of my am (mother).
He yarah (taught) me, and amar (spoke) to me: "Let your lab (heart) thamak (retain) my dabar (word / matter). Shamar (keep/guard) my matzawah (commandments), and chayah (live).
Qanah (get) chakamah (wisdom). Qanah (get) bayanah (understanding). Don't shakach (forget), neither swerve from the amaray (words) of my pah (mouth).
Don't izab (forsake) her, and she will shamar (keep/guard) you. Ahab (love) her, and she will natzar (keep) you.
Chakamah (wisdom) is supreme. Qanah (get) chakamah (wisdom). Yes, though it costs all your qanayan (possessions), get bayanah (understanding).
Esteem her, and she will salal (exalt) you. She will kabad (bring) you to honor, when you chabaq (embrace) her.
She will nathan (give) to your raash (head) a garland of chan (favor). She will magan (deliver) a itarah (crown) of splendor to you."
Shamai (hearken / hear), my ban (son), and laqach (take / seize) my amar (spoke). The shanawath (years) of your chay (life) will be many.
I have yarah (taught) you in the darak (way) of chakamah (wisdom). I have darak (led) you in yashar (upright) maigalay (paths).
When you yalak (go), your tzaid (steps) will not be hampered. When you rawatz (run), you will not kashal (stumble / stagger).
Chazaq (take) firm hold of mawasar (instruction). Don't rapah (let) her go. Natzar (keep) her, for she is your chay (life).
Don't bawaa (come) into the arach (path) of the rashai (wicked). Don't walk in the darak (way) of rai (evil) men.
Parai (avoid) it, and don't ibar (pass over/through) by it. Shatah (turn) from it, and ibar (pass over/through) on.
For they don't sleep, unless they do raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil). Their shanah (sleep) is gazal (taken) away, unless they kashal (stumble / stagger) someone fall.
For they lacham (eat) the lacham (bread) of rashai (wickedness), and shathah (drinks) the yayan (wine) of chamas (violence).
But the arach (path) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is like the dawning awar (light), that awar (light) more and more until the kawan (perfect) yawam (day).
The darak (way) of the rashai (wicked) is like apalah (darkness). They don't yadai (know) what they kashal (stumble / stagger) over.
My ban (son), qashab (attend) to my dabar (word / matter). Natah (turn) your azan (ear) to my amar (spoke).
Let them not depart from your iyan (eye). Shamar (keep/guard) them in the thawak (midst) of your thawak (midst).
For they are chay (life) to those who matzaa (find) them, and marapaa (health) to their whole bashar (flesh).
Natzar (keep) your lab (heart) with all mashamar (diligence), for out of it is the wellspring of chay (life).
Sawar (put) away from yourself a perverse pah (mouth). Put corrupt shapathayam (lips) rachaq (far) from you.
Let your iyan (eye) nabat (look) nakach (straight) ahead. Fix your gaze directly before you.
Make the maigal (path) of your ragal (feet / foot) level. Let all of your darak (ways) be kawan (established).
Don't natah (turn) to the right yamayan (right hand) nor to the shamaawal (left hand). Sawar (remove) your ragal (feet / foot) from rai (evil).
My ban (son), pay attention to my chakamah (wisdom). Natah (turn) your azan (ear) to my thabawan (understanding):
That you may maintain mazamah (discretion), that your shapah (lips) may natzar (preserve) daith (knowledge).
For the shapathay (lips) of an adulteress drip honey. Her chak (mouth) is smoother than shaman (oil),
But in the acharayath (end) she is as mar (bitter) as lainah (wormwood), and as chad (sharp) as a pah (two-edged) charab (sword).
Her ragal (feet / foot) yarad (go) down to mawath (death). Her tzaid (steps) lead thamak (straight) to shaawal (Sheol / afterlife).
She gives no thought to the maigal (way) of chay (life). Her maigal (ways) are crooked, and she doesn't yadai (know) it.
Now therefore, my banayam (sons), shamai (hearken / hear) to me. Don't sawar (depart) from the amaray (words) of my pah (mouth).
Rachaq (remove) your darak (way) rachaq (far) from her. Don't qarab (come close) near the pathach (door) of her bayath (house),
Lest you nathan (give) your honor to others, and your shanah (years) to the akazaray (cruel) one;
Lest strangers feast on your kach (strength / mighty / power), and your itzab (labors) enrich another nakaray (man's) bayath (house).
You will groan at your acharayath (latter) end, when your bashar (flesh) and your bashar (flesh) are kalah (complete / finish),
And amar (spoke), "How I have shanaa (hate) mawasar (instruction), and my lab (heart) naatz (despised) thawakachah (reproof);
Neither have I shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of my teachers, nor natah (turned) my azan (ear) to those who lamad (teach / instruct) me!
I have come to the brink of utter ruin, in the thawak (midst) of the gathered qahal (assembly)."
Shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters) out of your own bawar (cistern), running nazal (water) out of your own baar (well).
Should your maiyan (springs) overflow in the rachabawath (streets), palagay (streams) of mayam (Waters) in the public squares?
Let them be for yourself zawar (alone), not for strangers with you.
Let your maqawar (spring) be barak (blessed). Shamach (rejoice) in the ayashah (woman / wife) of your naiwar (youth).
A ahab (love) doe and a graceful deer— let her dad (breasts) rawah (satisfy) you at all ith (times). Be captivated thamayad (always) with her ahabah (love).
For why should you, my ban (son), be captivated with an adulteress? Why chabaq (embrace) the chayaq (bosom) of another?
For the darakay (ways) of ayash (man / husband) are nakach (before) the iyanay (eyes) of Yahawah. He examines all his maigal (paths).
The iwan (guilt/iniquity) deeds of the rashai (wicked) ensnare him. The chabalay (cords) of his chataah (sin) thamak (hold) him firmly.
He will mawath (death) for lack of mawasar (instruction). In the greatness of his awalath (folly), he will shagah (go) astray.
My ban (son), if you have become collateral for your neighbor, if you have thaqai (blow / sound alarm) your kap (hands) in pledge for a stranger;
You are trapped by the amaray (words) of your pah (mouth). You are ensnared with the amaray (words) of your pah (mouth).

Ishah (make) this apaw (now), my ban (son), and natzal (deliver) yourself, since you bawaa (come) come into the kap (hand) of your neighbor. Yalak (go), rapas (humble) yourself. Press your plea with your neighbor.
Nathan (give) no shanah (sleep) to your iyan (eye), nor thanawamah (slumber) to your ipaip (eyelids).
Free yourself, like a gazelle from the yad (hand) of the hunter, like a tzapawar (bird) from the snare of the yaqawash (fowler).
Yalak (go) to the namalah (ant), you itzal (sluggard). Raah (see) her darak (ways), and be chakam (wise);
Which having no chief, shatar (overseer), or mashal (rule/have dominion),
Kawan (provides) her lacham (bread) in the qayatz (summer), and agar (gathers) her maakal (food) in the qatzayar (harvest).
How long will you sleep, itzal (sluggard)? When will you qawam (rise up) out of your shanah (sleep)?
A mait (little) shanah (sleep), a mait (little) thanawamah (slumber), a mait (little) chabaq (folding) of the yadayam (hands) to sleep:
So your rayash (poverty) will bawaa (come) as a robber, and your scarcity as an magan (shield) ayash (man / husband).
A worthless adam (person), a ayash (man / husband) of awan (iniquity), is he who halak (move) with a perverse pah (mouth);
Who qaratz (winks) with his iyan (eye), who signals with his ragal (feet / foot), who motions with his atzabai (fingers);
In whose lab (heart) is perverseness, who devises rai (evil) ith (continually), who ith (always) shalach (send) madan (discord).
Therefore his ayad (calamity) will bawaa (come) pathaawam (suddenly). He will be shabar (broken) pathai (suddenly), and that without marapaa (remedy).
There are shash (six) things which Yahawah shanaa (hate); yes, shabai (seven) which are an thawaibah (abomination) to him:
Rawam (will lift up) iyanayam (eyes), a shaqar (lying) lashawan (tongue / language), yadayam (hands) that shapak (shed) naqay (innocent) dam (blood);
A lab (heart) that charash (devises) awan (wicked) schemes, ragalayam (feet) that are mahar (swift) in running to rai (mischief),
A shaqar (false) id (until / as far as) who pawach (utters) kazabayam (lies), and he who shalach (send) madan (discord) among achayam (brothers).
My ban (son), natzar (keep) your ab (father) matzawah (commandment), and don't natash (forsake) your am (mother) teaching.
Qashar (bind) them continually on your lab (heart). Inad (tie) them around your garagarawath (neck).
When you halak (move), it will nachah (lead) you. When you sleep, it will shamar (keep/guard) over you. When you qawatz (awake), it will shayach (meditate) with you.
For the matzawah (commandment) is a nayar (lamp), and the thawarah (instruction) is awar (light). Thawakachawath (reproofs) of mawasar (instruction) are the darak (way) of darak (life),
To shamar (keep/guard) you from the immoral ayashah (woman / wife), from the chalaqah (flattery) of the wayward wife's lashawan (tongue / language).
Don't chamad (lust) after her yapay (beauty) in your labab (heart), neither let her captivate you with her ipaip (eyelids).
For a prostitute reduces you to a kakar (piece) of lacham (bread). The adulteress tzawad (hunts) for your yaqar (precious) napash (soul).
Can a ayash (man / husband) scoop ash (fire) into his chayaq (lap), and his clothes not be sharap (burned)?
Or can ayash (man / husband) halak (move) on hot gachalayam (coals), and his ragal (feet / foot) not be scorched?
So is he who bawaa (come) in to his neighbor's ayashah (woman / wife). Whoever touches her will not be naqah (clean/innocent).
Men don't bawaz (despise) a ganab (thief), if he ganab (steals) to malaa (satisfy) himself when he is raib (hungry):
But if he is matzaa (found), he shall shalam (restore) shabaithayam (seven) times. He shall nathan (give) all the hawan (wealth) of his bayath (house).
He who naap (commits) adultery with a ayashah (woman / wife) is chasar (void) of lab (heart). He who ishah (make) it shachath (destroys) his own napash (soul).
He will matzaa (get) nagai (wounds) and dishonor. His charapah (reproach) will not be machah (wiped) away.
For qanaah (jealousy) arouses the fury of the gabar (husband). He won't chamal (spare) in the yawam (day) of naqam (vengeance).
He won't nashaa (lift) any kapar (ransom), neither will he abah (be willing / desire) content, though you rabah (give) many shachad (gifts).
My ban (son), shamar (keep/guard) my amar (spoke). Tzapan (lay) up my matzawah (commandments) within you.
Shamar (keep/guard) my matzawah (commandments) and chayah (live)! Guard my teaching as the ayashawan (apple) of your iyan (eye).
Qashar (bind) them on your atzabai (fingers). Kathab (write) them on the tablet of your lab (heart).
Amar (spoke) chakamah (wisdom), "You are my achawath (sister)." Qaraa (called) chakamah (understanding) your relative,
That they may shamar (keep/guard) you from the zawar (strange) ayashah (woman / wife), from the nakaray (foreigner) who chalaq (flatters) with her amar (spoke).
For at the chalawan (window) of my bayath (house), I shaqap (looked) out through my ashanab (lattice).
I raah (see) among the pathay (simple) ones. I bayan (between) among the banayam (youths) a nair (young) man chasar (void) of lab (heart),
Ibar (pass over/through) through the shawaq (street) atzal (near) her panah (corner / cornerstone), he tzaid (went) the darak (way) to her bayath (house),
In the nashap (twilight), in the yawam (day) of the ayashawan (day), in the middle of the layal (night) and in the apalah (darkness).
Behold, there a ayashah (woman / wife) qaraah (met) him with the shayath (attire) of a prostitute, and with crafty intent.
She is hamah (great uproar) and defiant. Her ragal (feet / foot) don't stay in her bayath (house).
Paim (now) she is in the rachabawath (streets), paim (now) in the squares, and lurking at every panah (corner / cornerstone).
So she chazaq (caught) him, and nashaq (kissed) him. With an izaz (impudent) panayam (face) she amar (spoke) to him:
"Sacrifices of shalam (peace) zabachay (offerings) are with me. This yawam (day) I have shalam (paid) my nadar (vow).
Therefore I yatzaa (go out / come out) out to qaraah (meet) you, to shachar (diligently) seek your panayam (face), and I matzaa (have) found you.
I have spread my irash (couch) with carpets of tapestry, with striped cloths of the yarn of Matzarayam (Egypt).
I have nawap (perfumed) my mashakab (bed) with mar (myrrh), ahalayam (aloes), and qanamawan (cinnamon).
Yalak (come), let's take our rawah (fill) of dawad (loving) until the baqar (morning). Let's ilas (solace) ourselves with ahab (love).
For my ayash (man / husband) isn't at bayath (house). He has halak (move) on a rachawaq (long) darak (journey).
He has laqach (take / seize) a tzarawar (bag) of kasap (money) with him. He will bawaa (come) bayath (house) at the yawam (day) kasaa (moon)."
With persuasive laqach (words), she led him astray. With the flattering of her shapah (lips), she seduced him.
He halak (move) her immediately, as an shawar (ox) bawaa (come) to the tabach (slaughter), as a awayal (fool) stepping into a noose.
Until an chatz (arrow) palach (strikes) through his kabad (liver), as a tzapawar (bird) hurries to the pach (snare / trap), and doesn't yadai (know) that it will cost his napash (soul).
Now therefore, banayam (sons), shamai (hearken / hear) to me. Pay attention to the amaray (words) of my pah (mouth).
Don't let your lab (heart) shatah (turn) to her darak (ways). Don't thaih (go) astray in her nathayab (paths),
For she napal (fall / be cast down) thrown down many chalal (wounded). Yes, all her harag (kill) are a itzawam (mighty) army.
Her bayath (house) is the darak (way) to shaawal (Sheol / afterlife), yarad (going) down to the rooms of mawath (death).
Doesn't chakamah (wisdom) qaraa (called) out? Doesn't chakamah (understanding) raise her qawal (sound / voice)?
On the raash (head) of marawam (high) places by the darak (way), where the nathayabawath (paths) meet, she natzab (stands).
Beside the shairayam (gates), at the pah (entry) of the qarath (city), at the pah (entry) pathachayam (doors), she ranan (cries) aloud:
"To you ayashayam (men), I qaraa (called)! I send my qawal (sound / voice) to the banay (sons) of mankind.
You pathay (simple), bayan (between) iramah (prudence). You kasayalayam (fools), be of an iramah (understanding) lab (heart).
Shamai (hearken / hear), for I will dabar (word / matter) nagayad (excellent) things. The mapathach (opening) of my shapah (lips) is for mayashar (right) things.
For my chak (mouth) hagah (speaks) amath (truth). Rashai (wickedness) is an thawaibah (abomination) to my shapah (lips).
All the amaray (words) of my pah (mouth) are in tzadaq (righteous / just / fair). There is nothing crooked or perverse in them.
They are all nakach (plain) to him who bayan (between), yashar (upright) to those who matzaa (find) daith (knowledge).
Laqach (take / seize) my mawasar (instruction) rather than kasap (silver); daith (knowledge) bachar (rather) than choice charawatz (gold).
For chakamah (wisdom) is tawab (good / proper function) than panayanayam (rubies). All the things that may be chapatz (desired) can't be shawah (compared) to it.
"I, chakamah (wisdom), have made iramah (prudence) my shakan (place). Matzaa (find) out daith (knowledge) and discretion.
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is to shanaa (hate) rai (evil). I shanaa (hate) gaah (pride), arrogance, the rai (evil) darak (way), and the thahapakah (perverse) pah (mouth).
Itzah (counsel) and sound thawashayah (knowledge) are mine. I have thawashayah (understanding) and gabawarah (power).
By me malakayam (kings) malak (king), and rawazanayam (princes) chaqaq (lawgiver) tzadaq (righteous / just / fair).
By me sharayam (princes) sharar (rule); nadayabayam (nobles), and all the righteous shapatay (rulers) of the earth.
I ahab (love) those who ahab (love) me. Those who shachar (seek) me diligently will matzaa (find) me.
With me are riches, honor, enduring hawan (wealth), and prosperity.
My paray (fruit) is tawab (good / proper function) than charawatz (gold), yes, than paz (fine) gold; my yield than choice kasap (silver).
I halak (move) in the arach (way) of tzadaqah (righteousness), in the thawak (midst) of the nathayabawath (paths) of mashapat (justice);
That I may nachal (give) wealth to those who ahab (love) me. I malaa (fill) their awatzar (treasuries).
"Yahawah qanah (possessed) me in the raashayath (beginning) of his mapail (work), qadam (before) his deeds of old.
I was nasak (set) up from iwalam (forever), from the raash (head), qadam (before) the aratz (Earth/land) existed.
When there were no thahamawath (depths), I was chawal (brought) forth, when there were no maiyanawath (springs) kabad (abounding) with mayam (Waters).
Before the harayam (mountains) were tabai (settled) in place, panayam (face) the gabaiwath (hills), I was chawal (brought) forth;
While as yet he ishah (make) not made the aratz (Earth/land), nor the chawatzawath (fields), nor the raash (head) of the ipar (dust) of the thabal (world).
When he kawan (established) the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), I was there; when he chaqaq (lawgiver) a chawag (circle) on the surface of the thahawam (depths),
When he amatz (established) the shachaqayam (clouds) mail (top/above), when the springs of the thahawam (depths) became izaz (strong),

When he shawam (place / establish / appoint) to the yam (sea/waters) its boundary, that the mayam (Waters) should not violate his commandment, when he marked out the mawasaday (foundations) of the aratz (Earth/land);
Then I was the craftsman by his side. I was a shaishai (delight) yawam (day) by day, ith (always) shachaq (rejoicing) panayam (face) him,
Shachaq (rejoicing) in his whole aratz (Earth/land). My shaishai (delight) was with the banay (sons) of adam (men).
"Now therefore, my banayam (sons), shamai (hearken / hear) to me, for ashar (who/that) are those who shamar (keep/guard) my darak (ways).
Shamai (hearken / hear) mawasar (instruction), and be chakam (wise). Don't parai (refuse) it.
Ashar (who/that) is the adam (man) who shamai (hearken / hear) me, shaqad (watching) yawam (day) at my dalath (gates), shamar (keep/guard) at my pathach (door) mazawazath (posts).
For whoever matzaay (finds) me, matzaay (finds) chay (life), and will pawaq (obtain) favor from Yahawah.
But he who chataa (sins) against me chamas (wrongs) his own napash (soul). All those who shanaa (hate) me ahab (love) mawath (death)."
Chakamawath (wisdom) has banah (build) her bayath (house). She has carved out her shabai (seven) imawad (pillar).
She has prepared her meat. She has mixed her yayan (wine). She has also irak (set) her shalachan (table).
She has shalach (send) out her nairah (maidens). She qaraa (called) from the highest maramay (places) of the qarath (city):
"Whoever is pathay (simple), let him sawar (turn) in here!" As for him who is chasar (void) of lab (heart), she amar (spoke) to him,
"Yalak (come), lacham (eat) some of my lacham (bread), shathah (drinks) some of the yayan (wine) which I have mixed!
Izab (leave) your pathay (simple) ways, and chayah (live). Walk in the darak (way) of bayanah (understanding)."
He who yasar (corrects) a lawatz (mocker) invites insult. He who yakach (reproves) a rashai (wicked) maawam (man) invites abuse.
Don't yakach (reprove) a lawatz (scoffer), lest he shanaa (hate) you. Yakach (reprove) a wise chakam (man), and he will ahab (love) you.
Instruct a chakam (wise) chakam (man), and he will be still wiser. Yadai (teach) a tzadayaq (righteous) man, and he will yasap (increase) in laqach (learning).
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is the thachalah (beginning) of chakamah (wisdom). The daith (knowledge) of the qadawash (holy) One is bayanah (understanding).
For by me your yawam (day) will be rabah (multiplied). The shanawath (years) of your chay (life) will be yasap (increased).
If you are chakam (wise), you are chakam (wise) for yourself. If you lawatz (mock), you alone will nashaa (lift) it.
The kasayalawath (foolish) ayashah (woman / wife) is hamah (great uproar), Undisciplined, and yadai (knows) mah (nothing).
She yashab (inhabit/dwell) at the pathach (door) of her bayath (house), on a kasaa (seat) in the marawam (high) places of the qarath (city),
To qaraa (called) to those who ibar (pass over/through) by, who go yashar (upright) on their arach (ways),
"Whoever is pathay (simple), let him sawar (turn) in here." As for him who is chasar (void) of lab (heart), she amar (spoke) to him,
"Ganab (stolen) mayam (Waters) is mathaq (sweet). Lacham (food) eaten in sathar (secret / hidden) is naim (pleasant)."
But he doesn't yadai (know) that the rapaa (dead) are there, that her qaraa (called) are in the imaqay (depths) of shaawal (Sheol / afterlife).
The mashalay (proverbs) of Shalamah (Solomon). A chakam (wise) ban (son) shamach (makes) a glad ab (father); but a kasayal (foolish) ban (son) brings grief to his am (mother).
Awatzarawath (treasures) of rashai (wickedness) yail (profit) nothing, but tzadaqah (righteousness) natzal (delivers) from mawath (death).
Yahawah will not allow the napash (soul) of the tzadayaq (righteous) to go raib (hungry), but he hadap (thrusts) away the desire of the rashai (wicked).
He becomes rawash (poor) who ishah (make) with a lazy kap (hand), but the yad (hand) of the charawatz (diligent) brings wealth.
He who agar (gathers) in qayatz (summer) is a shakal (wise) ban (son), but he who sleeps during the qatzayar (harvest) is a ban (son) who bawash (causes) shame.
Barakawath (blessings) are on the raash (head) of the tzadayaq (righteous), but chamas (violence) kasah (covers) the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked).
The zakar (remember) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is blessed, but the sham (name) of the rashai (wicked) will raqab (rot).
The chakam (wise) in lab (heart) laqach (take / seize) matzawath (commandments), but a chattering awayal (fool) will labat (fall).
He who yalak (walks) blamelessly yalak (walks) batach (surely), but he who iqash (perverts) his darak (ways) yadai (will) be found out.
One qaratz (winking) with the iyan (eye) nathan (give) itzabath (sorrow), but a chattering awayal (fool) will labat (fall).
The pah (mouth) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is a maqawar (spring) of chay (life), but chamas (violence) kasah (covers) the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked).
Hatred iwar (rouse / awaken) up madan (strife), but ahabah (love) kasah (covers) all wrongs.
Chakamah (wisdom) is matzaa (found) on the shapathay (lips) of him who bayan (between) discernment, but a shabat (rod) is for the gaw (back) of him who is chasar (void) of lab (heart).
Chakam (wise) men tzapan (lay) up daith (knowledge), but the pah (mouth) of the awayal (foolish) is qarawab (near) machathah (ruin).
The ishayar (rich) man's hawan (wealth) is his iz (strength / might / refuge) qarayah (city / town). The machathah (destruction) of the dal (poor) is their rayash (poverty).
The pailah (labor) of the tzadayaq (righteous) leads to chay (life). The thabawaah (increase) of the rashai (wicked) leads to chataah (sin).
He is in the arach (way) of chay (life) who shamar (keep/guard) mawasar (correction), but he who izab (forsakes) thawakachah (reproof) leads others thaih (astray).
He who kasah (hides) hatred has shaqar (lying) shapathay (lips). He who yatzaa (go out / come out) a dabah (slander) is a kasayal (fool).
In the rab (multitude) of dabarayam (words) there is no lack of disobedience, but he who restrains his shapah (lips) does shakal (wisely).
The lashawan (tongue / language) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is like choice kasap (silver). The lab (heart) of the rashai (wicked) is of mait (little) worth.
The shapathay (lips) of the tzadayaq (righteous) raih (feed) many, but the awayal (foolish) mawath (death) for chasar (lack) of lab (heart).
Yahawah barakah (blessing) brings wealth, and he yasap (adds) no trouble to it.
It is a kasayal (fool's) pleasure to ishah (make) zamah (wickedness), but chakamah (wisdom) is a ayash (man / husband) of thabawan (understanding's) pleasure.
What the rashai (wicked) magawarah (fear), will overtake them, but the thaawah (desire) of the tzadayaq (righteous) will be nathan (give).
When the sawapah (whirlwind) passes, the rashai (wicked) is no more; but the tzadayaq (righteous) stand firm iwalam (forever).
As chamatz (vinegar) to the shanayam (teeth), and as ishan (smoke) to the iyanayam (eyes), so is the itzal (sluggard) to those who shalach (send) him.
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah yasap (prolongs) yamayam (days), but the shanawath (years) of the rashai (wicked) shall be shortened.
The prospect of the tzadayaq (righteous) is shamachah (joy), but the thaqawah (hope) of the rashai (wicked) will abad (destroy / perish).
The darak (way) of Yahawah is a stronghold to the tham (upright), but it is a machathah (destruction) to the pailay (workers) of awan (iniquity).
The tzadayaq (righteous) will iwalam (forever) be mawat (removed), but the rashai (wicked) will not shakan (place) in the aratz (Earth/land).
The pah (mouth) of the tzadayaq (righteous) nawab (brings) forth chakamah (wisdom), but the thahapakah (perverse) lashawan (tongue / language) will be karath (cut) off.
The shapathay (lips) of the tzadayaq (righteous) yadai (know) what is ratzawan (acceptable), but the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked) is thahapakah (perverse).
A maramah (false) maazan (balance) is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, but accurate aban (stone) are his ratzawan (delight).
When zadawan (pride) bawaa (come), then bawaa (come) qalawan (shame), but with humility bawaa (come) chakamah (wisdom).
The thamah (integrity) of the yashar (upright) shall nachah (guide) them, but the salap (perverseness) of the bagad (treacherous) shall shadad (destroy) them.
Riches don't yail (profit) in the yawam (day) of ibarah (wrath), but tzadaqah (righteousness) natzal (delivers) from mawath (death).
The tzadaqah (righteousness) of the blameless will yashar (upright) his darak (way), but the rashai (wicked) shall napal (fall / be cast down) by his own rashaih (wickedness).
The tzadaqah (righteousness) of the yashar (upright) shall natzal (deliver) them, but the bagad (unfaithful) will be trapped by hawah (calamity / destruction) desires.
When a rashai (wicked) adam (man) mawath (death), thaqawah (hope) perishes, and thaqawah (expectation) of awan (power) comes to nothing.
A tzadayaq (righteous) person is chalatz (delivered) out of tzarah (trouble), and the rashai (wicked) takes his place.
With his pah (mouth) the godless man shachath (destroys) his neighbor, but the tzadayaq (righteous) will be chalatz (delivered) through daith (knowledge).
When it tawab (good / proper function) well with the tzadayaq (righteous), the qarayah (city / town) ilatz (rejoices). When the rashai (wicked) abad (destroy / perish), there is ranah (shouting).
By the barakah (blessing) of the yashar (upright), the qarath (city) is rawam (will lift up), but it is overthrown by the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked).
One who bawaz (despises) his neighbor is chasar (void) of lab (heart), but a ayash (man / husband) of thabawan (understanding) holds his charash (peace).
Halak (move) who brings gossip betrays a confidence, but aman (believe / have faith) who is of a trustworthy rawach (spirit / wind) is kasah (one) who keeps a secret.
Where there is no wise guidance, the im (nation / people) napal (fall / be cast down), but in the rab (multitude) of yaitz (counselors) there is thashawaih (deliverance).
He who is collateral for a stranger will suffer for it, but he who refuses pledges of collateral is batach (secure).
A chan (favor) ayashah (woman / wife) obtains honor, but irayatz (violent) men obtain riches.
The chasad (grace) ayash (man / husband) gamal (does) good to his own napash (soul), but he who is akazaray (cruel) ikar (troubles) his own shaar (flesh).
Rashai (wicked) ishah (make) earn shaqar (deceitful) pailah (wages), but one who zarai (sows) tzadaqah (righteousness) reaps a amath (truth) shakar (reward).
He who is truly tzadaqah (righteousness) gets chay (life). He who radap (pursues) rai (evil) gets mawath (death).
Those who are iqash (perverse) in lab (heart) are an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, but those whose darak (ways) are blameless are his ratzawan (delight).
Most certainly, the rai (evil) man will not be naqah (clean/innocent), but the zarai (seed) of the tzadayaq (righteous) will be malat (delivered).
Like a zahab (gold) ring in a pig's ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), is a yapah (beautiful) ayashah (woman / wife) who lacks taim (discretion).
The thaawah (desire) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is only tawab (good / proper function). The thaqawah (expectation) of the rashai (wicked) is ibarah (wrath).
There is one who pazar (scatters), and yasap (increases) yet more. There is yashar (upright) who withholds more than is appropriate, but gains machasawar (poverty).
The barakah (liberal) napash (soul) shall be dashan (made) fat. He who rawah (waters) shall be watered also himself.
Laam (people) naqab (curse) someone who manai (withholds) grain, but barakah (blessing) will be on the raash (head) of him who shabar (sells) it.
He who shachar (diligently) seeks tawab (good / proper function) shachar (seeks) favor, but he who searches after rai (evil), it shall bawaa (come) to him.
He who batach (trusts) in his riches will napal (fall / be cast down), but the tzadayaq (righteous) shall parach (flourish) as the green ilah (leaf).
He who ikar (troubles) his own bayath (house) shall nachal (inherit) the rawach (spirit / wind). The awayal (foolish) shall be ibad (servant) to the chakam (wise) of lab (heart).
The paray (fruit) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is a itz (tree) of chay (life). He who is chakam (wise) laqach (take / seize) napashawath (souls).
Behold, the tzadayaq (righteous) shall be repaid in the aratz (Earth/land); how much more the rashai (wicked) and the chataa (sinner)!
Whoever ahab (love) mawasar (correction) ahab (love) daith (knowledge), but he who shanaa (hate) thawakachah (reproof) is stupid.
A tawab (good / proper function) man shall pawaq (obtain) favor from Yahawah, but he will rashai (condemn) a ayash (man / husband) of wicked mazamawath (devices).
A adam (man) shall not be kawan (established) by rashai (wickedness), but the sharash (root) of the tzadayaq (righteous) shall not be mawat (moved).
A chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ayashah (woman / wife) is the itarah (crown) of her bail (husband), but a disgraceful wife is as raqab (rottenness) in his itzam (bones).
The machashabawath (thoughts) of the tzadayaq (righteous) are mashapat (just), but the advice of the rashai (wicked) is deceitful.
The dabaray (words) of the rashai (wicked) are about lying in arab (wait) for dam (blood), but the pah (speech) of the yashar (upright) natzal (rescues) them.
The rashai (wicked) are overthrown, and are no more, but the bayath (house) of the tzadayaq (righteous) shall imad (stand).
A ayash (man / husband) shall be halal (praise) pah (according) to his shakal (wisdom), but he who has a warped lab (heart) shall be bawaz (despised).
Tawab (good / proper function) is he who is qalah (lightly) esteemed, and has a ibad (servant), than he who honors himself, and chasar (lacks) lacham (bread).
A tzadayaq (righteous) yadai (man) respects the napash (soul) of his animal, but the tender rachamay (mercies) of the rashai (wicked) are akazaray (cruel).
He who ibad (servant) his adamah (land) shall shabai (have) plenty of lacham (bread), but he who radap (chases) fantasies is chasar (void) of lab (heart).
The rashai (wicked) chamad (desires) the plunder of rai (evil) men, but the sharash (root) of the tzadayaq (righteous) flourishes.
An rai (evil) man is mawaqash (trapped) by sinfulness of shapathayam (lips), but the tzadayaq (righteous) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out of tzarah (trouble).

A ayash (man / husband) shall be shabai (satisfied) with tawab (good / proper function) by the paray (fruit) of his pah (mouth). The gamawal (work) of a adam (man's) yaday (hands) shall be shawab (turn back / repent) to him.
The darak (way) of a awayal (fool) is yashar (upright) in his own iyan (eye), but he who is chakam (wise) shamai (hearken / hear) to itzah (counsel).
A awayal (fool) shows his annoyance the same yawam (day), but kasah (one) who overlooks an insult is irawam (prudent).
He who is truthful testifies honestly, but a shaqar (false) id (until / as far as) lies.
There is one who bataa (speaks) rashly like the madaqarah (piercing) of a charab (sword), but the lashawan (tongue / language) of the chakam (wise) heals.
Amath (truth) shapah (lips) will be kawan (established) id (until / as far as), but a shaqar (lying) lashawan (tongue / language) is only momentary.
Maramah (deceit) is in the lab (heart) of those who plot rai (evil), but shamachah (joy) comes to the promoters of shalawam (peace / safety).
No awan (mischief) shall anah (happen) to the tzadayaq (righteous), but the rashai (wicked) shall be malaa (filled) with rai (evil).
Shaqar (lying) shapathay (lips) are an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, but those who ishah (make) the amawanah (truth) are his ratzawan (delight).
A irawam (prudent) adam (man) keeps his daith (knowledge), but the lab (heart) of kasayalayam (fools) qaraa (called) awalath (foolishness).
The yad (hand) of the charawatz (diligent) ones shall mashal (rule/have dominion), but laziness ends in slave labor.
Anxiety in a ayash (man / husband) lab (heart) weighs it down, but a kind dabar (word / matter) shamach (makes) it glad.
A tzadayaq (righteous) person is cautious in friendship, but the darak (way) of the rashai (wicked) leads them astray.
The ramayah (slothful) man doesn't charak (roast) his game, but the hawan (possessions) of charawatz (diligent) adam (men) are prized.
In the arach (way) of tzadaqah (righteousness) is chay (life); in its nathayab (path) there is no mawath (death).
A chakam (wise) ban (son) listens to his ab (father) mawasar (instruction), but a lawatz (scoffer) doesn't shamai (hearken / hear) to gairah (rebuke).
By the paray (fruit) of his lips, a ayash (man / husband) enjoys tawab (good / proper function) things; but the unfaithful crave chamas (violence).
He who guards his pah (mouth) guards his napash (soul). One who pashaq (opens) wide his shapah (lips) comes to machathah (ruin).
The napash (soul) of the itzal (sluggard) awah (desires), and napash (soul) nothing, but the desire of the charawatz (diligent) shall be fully satisfied.
A tzadayaq (righteous) man shanaa (hate) lies, but a rashai (wicked) man chapar (brings) shame and disgrace.
Tzadaqah (righteousness) guards the darak (way) of tham (integrity), but rashaih (wickedness) salap (overthrows) the chataah (sin).
There are some who pretend to be ishar (rich), yet have nothing. There are some who pretend to be rawash (poor), yet rab (have) great hawan (wealth).
The kapar (ransom) of a ayash (man / husband) napash (soul) is his riches, but the rawash (poor) shamai (hearken / hear) no threats.
The awar (light) of the tzadayaq (righteous) shines brightly, but the nayar (lamp) of the rashai (wicked) is snuffed out.
Zadawan (pride) only breeds quarrels, but with ones who yaitz (take) advice is chakamah (wisdom).
Hawan (wealth) gained dishonestly dwindles away, but he who qabatz (gathers) by yad (hand) rabah (makes) it grow.
Thawachalath (hope) mashak (deferred) makes the lab (heart) chalah (afflict), but when longing is fulfilled, it is a itz (tree) of chay (life).
Whoever bawaz (despises) instruction will pay for it, but he who respects a command will be shalam (rewarded).
The teaching of the chakam (wise) is a maqawar (spring) of chay (life), to sawar (turn) from the maqashay (snares) of mawath (death).
Tawab (good / proper function) shakal (understanding) wins favor; but the darak (way) of the bagad (unfaithful) is ayathan (hard).
Every irawam (prudent) ishah (make) acts from daith (knowledge), but a kasayal (fool) exposes awalath (folly).
A rashai (wicked) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) napal (fall / be cast down) into rai (trouble), but a trustworthy envoy gains marapaa (healing).
Rayash (poverty) and qalawan (shame) come to him who parai (refuses) mawasar (discipline), but he who shamar (keep/guard) mawasar (correction) shall be honored.
Longing fulfilled is irab (evening) to the napash (soul), but kasayalayam (fools) detest sawar (turning) from rai (evil).
One who halak (move) with chakam (wise) men grows chakam (wise), but a raih (companion) of kasayalayam (fools) suffers harm.
Misfortune radap (pursues) chataayam (sinners), but tawab (good / proper function) shalam (rewards) the tzadayaq (righteous).
A tawab (good / proper function) man leaves an nachal (inheritance) to his banay (childrens) banay (children), but the wealth of the chataa (sinner) is stored for the tzadayaq (righteous).
An rab (abundance) of akal (food) is in rawash (poor) nayar (people's) fields, but injustice sweeps it away.
One who chashak (darkness) the shabat (rod) shanaa (hate) his ban (son), but one who ahab (love) him is careful to mawasar (discipline) him.
The tzadayaq (righteous) napash (soul) akal (eat) to the shabai (satisfying) of his napash (soul), but the batan (belly) of the rashai (wicked) goes hungry.
Chakamawath (every) wise ayashah (woman / wife) banah (build) her bayath (house), but the foolish haras (one) tears it down with her own yad (hand).
He who halak (move) in his yashar (upright) yaraa (fears) Yahawah, but he who is lawaz (perverse) in his darak (ways) bazah (despises) him.
The awayal (fool's) pah (talk) brings a chatar (rod) to his back, but the shapathay (lips) of the chakam (wise) protect them.
Where no alapayam (oxen) are, the abawas (crib) is bar (clean), but much thabawaah (increase) is by the kach (strength / mighty / power) of the shawar (ox).
A truthful id (until / as far as) will not kazab (lie), but a shaqar (false) id (until / as far as) pours out kazab (lies).
A lawatz (scoffer) baqash (seeks) chakamah (wisdom), and doesn't find it, but daith (knowledge) comes easily to a bayan (between) person.
Stay away from a kasayal (foolish) ayash (man / husband), for you won't find daith (knowledge) on his shapathay (lips).
The chakamah (wisdom) of the irawam (prudent) is to bayan (between) about his darak (way), but the awalath (folly) of kasayalayam (fools) is maramah (deceit).
Awalayam (fools) lawatz (mock) at making atonement for asham (sins), but among the yashar (upright) there is good ratzawan (will).
The lab (heart) yadai (knows) its napash (soul) marah (bitterness) and joy; he will not share these with a stranger.
The bayath (house) of the rashai (wicked) will be overthrown, but the ahal (tent) of the yashar (upright) will parach (flourish).
There is a darak (way) which seems yashar (upright) to a ayash (man / husband), but in the acharayath (end) it leads to mawath (death).
Even in shachawaq (laughter/joking matter) the lab (heart) may be kaab (sorrowful), and shamachah (mirth) may acharayath (end) in thawagah (heaviness).
The unfaithful will be repaid for his own darak (ways); likewise a tawab (good / proper function) ayash (man / husband) will be rewarded for his ways.
A pathay (simple) man aman (believe / have faith) everything, but the irawam (prudent) bayan (between) carefully considers his ashar (who/that).
A chakam (wise) man yaraa (fears), and shuns rai (evil), but the kasayal (fool) is hotheaded and reckless.
He who is quick to become angry will ishah (make) awalath (folly), and a crafty ayash (man / husband) is shanaa (hate).
The pathay (simple) nachal (inherit) awalath (folly), but the irawam (prudent) are kathar (crowned) with daith (knowledge).
The rai (evil) shachach (bow) down panayam (face) the tawab (good / proper function), and the rashai (wicked) at the shairay (gates) of the tzadayaq (righteous).
The rawash (poor) person is shunned even by his own neighbor, but the ishayar (rich) person rab (has) many ahabay (friends).
He who bawaz (despises) his neighbor chataa (sins), but ashar (who/that) is he who chanan (showing favor) pity on the inay (poor).
Don't they thaih (go) astray who plot rai (evil)? But chasad (grace) and amath (truth) belong to those who plan tawab (good / proper function).
In all hard itzab (work) there is mawathar (profit), but the dabar (word / matter) of the shapathayam (lips) leads only to machasawar (poverty).
The itarah (crown) of the chakam (wise) is their riches, but the awalath (folly) of kasayalayam (fools) crowns them with awalath (folly).
A truthful id (until / as far as) natzal (saves) napashawath (souls), but a maramah (false) witness is deceitful.
In the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is a secure fortress, and he will be a machasah (refuge) for his ban (son).
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is a maqawar (fountain) of chay (life), sawar (turning) people from the maqashay (snares) of mawath (death).
In the rab (multitude) of im (nation / people) is the malak (king) glory, but in the lack of laam (people) is the machathah (destruction) of the razawan (prince).
He who is arak (slow) to ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) rab (has) great thabawan (understanding), but he who has a quick temper displays awalath (folly).
The chay (life) of the bashar (flesh) is a lab (heart) at marapaa (peace), but qanaah (envy) rots the itzamawath (bones).
He who oppresses the dal (poor) shows contempt for his Maker, but he who is kind to the abayawan (needy) honors him.
The rashai (wicked) is brought down in his rai (calamity), but in mawath (death), the tzadayaq (righteous) chasah (has) a refuge.
Chakamah (wisdom) nawach (rests) in the lab (heart) of one who has bayan (between), and is even yadai (made) known in the qarab (among / near) part of kasayalayam (fools).
Tzadaqah (righteousness) rawam (will lift up) a gaway (heathen / nation), but chataah (sin) is a disgrace to any laamayam (people).
The malak (king) favor is toward a ibad (servant) who deals shakal (wisely), but his ibarah (wrath) is toward one who bawash (causes) shame.
A gentle mainah (answer) shawab (turn back / repent) away chamah (wrath), but a harsh dabar (word / matter) ilah (go up / offer) up ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).
The lashawan (tongue / language) of the chakam (wise) commends daith (knowledge), but the pah (mouth) of kasayalayam (fools) gush out awalath (folly).
Yahawah iyanay (eyes) are everywhere, keeping tzapah (watchman / keep watch) on the rai (evil) and the tawab (good / proper function).
A gentle lashawan (tongue / language) is a itz (tree) of chay (life), but deceit in it crushes the rawach (spirit / wind).
A awayal (fool) naatz (despises) his ab (father) mawasar (correction), but he who shamar (keep/guard) thawakachah (reproof) shows prudence.
In the bayath (house) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is much chasan (treasure), but the income of the rashai (wicked) brings ikar (trouble).
The shapathay (lips) of the chakam (wise) zarah (spread) daith (knowledge); not so with the lab (heart) of kasayalayam (fools).
The zabach (sacrifice) made by the rashai (wicked) is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, but the thapalah (prayer) of the yashar (upright) is his ratzawan (delight).
The darak (way) of the rashai (wicked) is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, but he ahab (love) him who radap (follows) after tzadaqah (righteousness).
There is stern mawasar (discipline) for one who izab (forsakes) the arach (way): whoever shanaa (hate) thawakachah (reproof) shall mawath (death).
Shaawal (Sheol / afterlife) and abadawan (abaddon) are before Yahawah— how much more then the labawath (hearts) of the banay (children) of adam (men)!
A lawatz (scoffer) doesn't ahab (love) to be yakach (reproved); he will not yalak (go) to the chakam (wise).
A shamach (glad) lab (heart) yatab (makes) a cheerful panayam (face); but an aching lab (heart) nakaa (breaks) the rawach (spirit / wind).
The lab (heart) of one who has bayan (between) baqash (seeks) daith (knowledge), but the panay (mouths) of kasayalayam (fools) raih (feed) on awalath (folly).
All the yamay (days) of the inay (afflicted) are wretched, but one who has a tawab (good / proper function) lab (heart) enjoys a thamayad (continual) mashathah (feast).
Tawab (good / proper function) is mait (little), with the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah, than rab (great) awatzar (treasure) with mahawamah (trouble).
Tawab (good / proper function) is a arachah (dinner) of yaraq (herbs), where ahabah (love) is, than a fattened calf with hatred.
A chamah (wrathful) ayash (man / husband) garah (stirs) up madawan (contention), but one who is arak (slow) to ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) appeases rayab (strife).
The darak (way) of the itzal (sluggard) is like a chadaq (thorn) patch, but the arach (path) of the yashar (upright) is a highway.
A chakam (wise) ban (son) makes a ab (father) shamach (glad), but a kasayal (foolish) adam (man) bazah (despises) his am (mother).
Awalath (folly) is shamachah (joy) to one who is chasar (void) of lab (heart), but a ayash (man / husband) of thabawan (understanding) keeps his yalak (way) yashar (upright).
Where there is no sawad (counsel), plans parar (fail); but in a rab (multitude) of yawaitzayam (counselors) they are qawam (rise up).
Shamachah (joy) comes to a ayash (man / husband) with the reply of his pah (mouth). How tawab (good / proper function) is a dabar (word / matter) at the right ith (time)!
The arach (path) of chay (life) leads upward for the shakal (wise), to keep him from going matah (downward) to shaawal (Sheol / afterlife).
Yahawah will uproot the bayath (house) of the gaah (proud), but he will keep the alamanah (widow's) gabawal (border/boundary) intact.
Yahawah detests the machashabawath (thoughts) of the rai (wicked), but the thoughts of the tahawar (pure) are pleasing.
He who is batzai (greedy) for batzai (gain) ikar (troubles) his own bayath (house), but he who shanaa (hate) bribes will chayah (live).
The lab (heart) of the tzadayaq (righteous) weighs inah (answer / respond), but the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked) gushes out rai (evil).
Yahawah is rachawaq (far) from the rashai (wicked), but he shamai (hearken / hear) the thapalah (prayer) of the tzadayaq (righteous).
The maawar (Maawar / Luminary) of the iyanayam (eyes) shamach (rejoices) the lab (heart). Tawab (good / proper function) shamawaih (news) gives health to the itzam (bones).
The azan (ear) that shamai (hearken / hear) to thawakachah (reproof) chayayam (lives), and will be at home qarab (among / near) the chakam (wise).
He who parai (refuses) mawasar (correction) maas (despises) his own napash (soul), but he who shamai (hearken / hear) to thawakachah (reproof) qanah (gets) lab (heart).
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah teaches chakamah (wisdom). Panayam (face) honor is inawah (humility).
The plans of the lab (heart) belong to adam (man), but the mainah (answer) of the lashawan (tongue / language) is from Yahawah.
All the darakay (ways) of a ayash (man / husband) are zak (clean) in his own iyan (eye); but Yahawah thakan (weighs) the motives.
Galal (commit) your maishah (deeds) to Yahawah, and your plans shall succeed.
Yahawah has pail (made) everything for its own end— yes, even the rashai (wicked) for the yawam (day) of rashai (evil).
Everyone who is gabah (proud) in lab (heart) is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah: they shall certainly not be naqah (clean/innocent).
By chasad (grace) and amath (truth) iwan (guilt/iniquity) is atoned for. By the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah men sawar (depart) from rai (evil).
When a ayash (man / husband) darakay (ways) ratzah (please) Yahawah, he makes even his ayab (enemy) to be at shalam (peace) with him.
Tawab (good / proper function) is a mait (little) with tzadaqah (righteousness), than rab (great) thabawaawath (revenues) with injustice.
A adam (man's) lab (heart) plans his course, but Yahawah kawan (directs) his tzaid (steps).
Inspired qasam (judgments) are on the shapathay (lips) of the malak (king). He shall not betray his pah (mouth).
Honest maazanay (balances) and palas (scales) are Yahawah; all the abanay (weights) in the kayas (bag) are his maishah (work).
It is an thawaibah (abomination) for malakayam (kings) to ishah (make) wrong, for the kasaa (throne) is kawan (established) by tzadaqah (righteousness).
Tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) shapathay (lips) are the ratzawan (delight) of malakayam (kings). They value one who dabar (word / matter) the yashar (upright).
The malak (king) chamah (wrath) is a malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of mawath (death), but a chakam (wise) ayash (man / husband) will kapar (pacify) it.
In the awar (light) of the malak (king) panayam (face) is chay (life). His favor is like a ib (cloud) of the spring malaqawash (rain).
How much tawab (good / proper function) it is to qanah (get) chakamah (wisdom) than charawatz (gold)! Yes, to qanah (get) bayanah (understanding) is to be bachar (chosen) rather than kasap (silver).
The masalah (highway) of the yashar (upright) is to sawar (depart) from rai (evil). He who natzar (keeps) his darak (way) shamar (keep/guard) his napash (soul).
Gaawan (pride) goes panayam (face) shabar (destruction), and a gabah (haughty) rawach (spirit / wind) panayam (face) a kashalawan (fall).
It is tawab (good / proper function) to be of a inay (lowly) rawach (spirit / wind) with the poor, than to chalaq (divide) the plunder with the gaah (proud).
He who heeds the dabar (word / matter) matzaa (finds) tawab (good / proper function). Whoever batach (trusts) in Yahawah is ashar (who/that).
The chakam (wise) in lab (heart) shall be qaraa (called) bayan (between). Pleasantness of the shapathayam (lips) promotes instruction.
Shakal (understanding) is a maqawar (fountain) of chay (life) to one who bail (has) it, but the punishment of awalayam (fools) is their awalath (folly).
The lab (heart) of the chakam (wise) shakal (instructs) his pah (mouth), and yasap (adds) laqach (learning) to his shapah (lips).
Naim (pleasant) amaray (words) are a tzawap (honeycomb), mathawaq (sweet) to the napash (soul), and marapaa (health) to the itzam (bones).
There is a darak (way) which seems yashar (upright) to a ayash (man / husband), but in the acharayath (end) it leads to mawath (death).
The appetite of the laboring napash (soul) imal (labors) for him; for his pah (mouth) urges him on.
A worthless ayash (man / husband) devises rai (mischief). His shapah (speech) is like a scorching ash (fire).
A thahapakah (perverse) ayash (man / husband) stirs up madawan (strife). A naragan (whisperer) parad (separates) close alawap (friends).
A ayash (man / husband) of chamas (violence) pathah (entices) his neighbor, and yalak (leads) him in a darak (way) that is not tawab (good / proper function).
Itzah (one) who winks his iyan (eye) to plot perversities, qaratz (one) who compresses his shapah (lips), is bent on rai (evil).
Shayabah (old age / white hair - due to age) hair is a itarah (crown) of glory. It is attained by a darak (life) of tzadaqah (righteousness).

One who is arak (slow) to ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) is tawab (good / proper function) than the gabawar (mighty); one who mashal (rule/have dominion) his rawach (spirit / wind), than he who lakad (takes) a iyar (city).
The gawaral (lot) is tawal (cast) into the chayaq (lap), but its every decision is from Yahawah.
Tawab (good / proper function) is a charab (dry) path (morsel) with shalawah (quietness), than a bayath (house) malaa (full) of feasting with rayab (strife).

A ibad (servant) who deals shakal (wisely) will mashal (rule/have dominion) over a ban (son) who bawash (causes) shame, and shall chalaq (have) a part in the nachalah (inheritance) thawak (midst) the achayam (brothers).
The refining matzarap (pot) is for kasap (silver), and the kawar (furnace) for zahab (gold), but Yahawah tests the labawath (hearts).
An evildoer qashab (heeds) awan (wicked) shapah (lips). A shaqar (liar) azan (ear) ear to a hawah (calamity / destruction) lashawan (tongue / language).
Whoever laig (mocks) the rawash (poor) reproaches his Maker. He who is shamach (glad) at ayad (calamity) shall not be naqah (clean/innocent).
Banay (childrens) banay (children) are the itarah (crown) of zaqan (old) men; the glory of banay (children) are their parents.
Arrogant shapah (speech) isn't fitting for a nabal (fool), much less do shaqar (lying) shapah (lips) fit a nadayab (prince).
A shachad (bribe) is a chan (favor) aban (stone) in the iyanay (eyes) of him who bail (gives) it; wherever he panah (turn), he shakal (prospers).
He who kasah (covers) an offense promotes ahabah (love); but he who shanah (repeats) a dabar (word / matter) parad (separates) best alawap (friends).
A gairah (rebuke) nachath (enters) deeper into bayan (between) who has understanding than a maah (hundred) lashes into a kasayal (fool).
An rai (evil) man baqash (seeks) only rebellion; therefore a akazaray (cruel) malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) shall be shalach (send) against him.
Let a dab (bear) robbed of her cubs pagash (meet) a ayash (man / husband), al (not) than a kasayal (fool) in his awalath (folly).
Whoever shawab (turn back / repent) rai (evil) for tawab (good / proper function), rai (evil) shall not depart from his bayath (house).
The raashayath (beginning) of madawan (strife) is like breaching a dam, therefore stop rayab (contention) panayam (face) quarreling breaks out.
He who justifies the rashai (wicked), and he who rashai (condemns) the tzadayaq (righteous), shanayam (two) of them alike are an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah.
Why is there money in the yad (hand) of a kasayal (fool) to qanah (buy) chakamah (wisdom), since he has no lab (heart)?
A rai (neigbor/another person) ahab (love) at all ith (times); and a ach (brother/kinsman) is yalad (birth / begot) for tzarah (adversity).
A adam (man) chasar (void) of lab (heart) thaqai (blow / sound alarm) kap (hands), and becomes collateral in the panayam (face) of his neighbor.
He who ahab (love) disobedience ahab (love) matzah (strife). One who builds a gabah (high) pathach (gate) baqash (seeks) shabar (destruction).

One who has a iqash (perverse) lab (heart) doesn't matzaa (find) tawab (good / proper function), and hapak (one) who has a deceitful lashawan (tongue / language) napal (fall / be cast down) into rai (trouble).
He who becomes the yalad (birth / begot) of a kasayal (fool) grieves. The ab (father) of a nabal (fool) shamach (has) no joy.
A cheerful lab (heart) makes yatab (good) gahah (medicine), but a crushed rawach (spirit / wind) yabash (dry land) up the garam (bones).
A rashai (wicked) man laqach (take / seize) a shachad (bribe) in secret, to natah (pervert) the arachawath (ways) of mashapat (justice).
Chakamah (wisdom) is before the panayam (face) of one who has understanding, but the iyanay (eyes) of a kasayal (fool) wander to the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land).
A kasayal (foolish) ban (son) brings kais (grief) to his ab (father), and mamar (bitterness) to her who yalad (birth / begot) him.
Also to inash (punish) the tzadayaq (righteous) is not tawab (good / proper function), nor to flog officials for their integrity.
He who chashak (darkness) his amar (spoke) yadai (has) daith (knowledge). He who is even tempered is a ayash (man / husband) of thabawan (understanding).
Even a awayal (fool), when he charash (keeps) silent, is chashab (counted) chakam (wise). When he atam (shuts) his shapah (lips), he is bayan (between) to be discerning.
An unfriendly baqash (man) pursues selfishness, and defies all sound thawashayah (judgment).
A kasayal (fool) chapatz (has) no delight in thabawan (understanding), but only in galah (revealing) his own opinion.
When rashai (wickedness) bawaa (come), bawaz (contempt) also bawaa (come), and with charapah (shame) comes disgrace.
The dabaray (words) of a ayash (man / husband) pah (mouth) are like imaq (deep) mayam (Waters). The maqawar (fountain) of chakamah (wisdom) is like a nabai (flowing) nachal (stream / river).
To be partial to the panay (faces) of the rashai (wicked) is not tawab (good / proper function), nor to deprive the innocent of mashapat (justice).
A kasayal (fool's) shapathay (lips) bawaa (come) into rayab (strife), and his pah (mouth) qaraa (called) beatings.
A kasayal (fool's) pah (mouth) is his machathah (destruction), and his shapah (lips) are a mawaqash (snare) to his napash (soul).
The dabaray (words) of a gossip are like dainty morsels: they yarad (go) down into a person's chadar (innermost) parts.
One who is rapah (slack) in his malaakah (work) is ach (brother/kinsman) to him who is a bail (master) of destruction.
The sham (name) of Yahawah is a iz (strength / might / refuge) magadal (tower): the tzadayaq (righteous) rawatz (run) to him, and are shagab (safe).
The ishayar (rich) man's hawan (wealth) is his iz (strength / might / refuge) qarayah (city / town), like an unscalable chawamah (wall) in his own imagination.
Panayam (face) shabar (destruction) the lab (heart) of ayash (man / husband) is gabah (proud), but panayam (face) honor is inawah (humility).
He who gives shawab (turn back / repent) before he shamai (hearken / hear), that is awalath (folly) and kalamah (shame) to him.
A ayash (man / husband) rawach (spirit / wind) will kawal (all) him in machalah (sickness), but a crushed rawach (spirit / wind), who can nashaa (lift)?
The lab (heart) of the bayan (between) qanah (gets) daith (knowledge). The azan (ear) of the chakam (wise) baqash (seeks) daith (knowledge).
A adam (man's) mathan (gift) rachab (makes) room for him, and nachah (brings) him panayam (face) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) men.
He who pleads his rayab (cause) raashawan (first) seems right; until rai (neigbor/another person) bawaa (come) and questions him.
The gawaral (lot) settles disputes, and keeps itzawam (strong) parad (ones) apart.
A ach (brother/kinsman) pashai (offended) is more difficult than a fortified qarayah (city / town); and disputes are like the barayach (bars) of a aramawan (castle).
A ayash (man / husband) stomach is shabai (filled) with the paray (fruit) of his pah (mouth). With the harvest of his lips he is shabai (satisfied).
Mawath (death) and chay (life) are in the yad (hand) of the lashawan (tongue / language); those who ahab (love) it will akal (eat) its paray (fruit).
Whoever matzaa (finds) a ayashah (woman / wife) matzaa (finds) a tawab (good / proper function) thing, and pawaq (obtains) favor of Yahawah.
The rawash (poor) plead for thachanawan (mercy), but the ishayar (rich) inah (answer / respond) harshly.
A ayash (man / husband) of many raiyam (companions) may be ruined, but there is a ahab (love) who dabaq (sticks) closer than a ach (brother/kinsman).
Tawab (good / proper function) is the rawash (poor) who halak (move) in his tham (integrity) than he who is iqash (perverse) in his shapah (lips) and is a kasayal (fool).
It isn't tawab (good / proper function) to napash (soul) zeal without daith (knowledge); nor being hasty with one's ragalayam (feet) and chataa (missing) the way.
The awalath (foolishness) of adam (man) subverts his darak (way); his lab (heart) rages against Yahawah.
Hawan (wealth) yasap (adds) many raiyam (friends), but the dal (poor) is parad (separated) from his rai (neigbor/another person).
A shaqar (false) id (until / as far as) shall not be naqah (clean/innocent). He who pours out kazabayam (lies) shall not malat (go) free.
Many will entreat the favor of a nadayab (ruler), and everyone is a rai (neigbor/another person) to a ayash (man / husband) who gives mathan (gifts).
All the relatives of the rawash (poor) shun him: how much more do his marai (friends) avoid him! He radap (pursues) them with pleas, but they are gone.
He who qanah (gets) lab (heart) ahab (love) his own napash (soul). He who shamar (keep/guard) thabawan (understanding) shall matzaa (find) tawab (good / proper function).
A shaqar (false) id (until / as far as) shall not be naqah (clean/innocent). He who pawach (utters) kazabayam (lies) shall abad (destroy / perish).
Thainawag (delicate) living is not appropriate for a kasayal (fool), much less for a ibad (servant) to mashal (rule/have dominion) rule over sharayam (princes).
The shakal (discretion) of a adam (man) arak (makes) him slow to ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting). It is his glory to overlook an offense.
The malak (king) zaip (wrath) is like the naham (roaring) of a kapayar (lion), but his favor is like tal (dew) on the ishab (grass).
A kasayal (foolish) ban (son) is the hawah (calamity / destruction) of his ab (father). A ayashah (woman / wife) quarrels are a tarad (continual) dripping.
Bayath (house) and riches are an nachalah (inheritance) from abawath (fathers), but a shakal (prudent) ayashah (woman / wife) is from Yahawah.
Itzalah (slothfulness) napal (fall / be cast down) into a tharadamah (deep) sleep. The ramayah (idle) napash (soul) shall raib (suffer) hunger.
He who shamar (keep/guard) the matzawah (commandment) shamar (keep/guard) his napash (soul), but he who is contemptuous in his darak (ways) shall mawath (death).
He who chanan (showing favor) pity on the dal (poor) lawah (lends) to Yahawah; he will shalam (reward) him.
Discipline your ban (son), for there is thaqawah (hope); don't be a willing party to his mawath (death).
A hot - tempered garal (man) must pay the penalty, for if you natzal (rescue) him, you must yasap (do) it again.
Shamai (hearken / hear) to itzah (counsel) and qabal (receive) mawasar (instruction), that you may be chakam (wise) in your acharayath (latter) end.
There are many plans in a ayash (man / husband) lab (heart), but Yahawah itzah (counsel) will prevail.
That which makes a adam (man) to be thaawah (desired) is his chasad (grace). A rawash (poor) man is tawab (good / proper function) than a kazab (liar).
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah leads to chay (life), then contentment; he lawan (rests) and will not be touched by rai (trouble).
The itzal (sluggard) buries his yad (hand) in the tzalachath (dish); he will not so much as shawab (turn back / repent) it to his pah (mouth) again.
Flog a lawatz (scoffer), and the pathay (simple) will learn prudence; yakach (rebuke) one who has bayan (between), and he will gain daith (knowledge).
He who robs his ab (father) and barach (drives) away his am (mother), is a ban (son) who bawash (causes) shame and chapar (brings) reproach.
If you stop shamai (hearken / hear) to mawasar (instruction), my ban (son), you will stray from the amaray (words) of daith (knowledge).
A corrupt id (until / as far as) lawatz (mocks) mashapat (justice), and the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked) gulps down rashai (iniquity).
Penalties are kawan (prepared) for latzayam (scoffers), and beatings for the gaw (backs) of kasayalayam (fools).
Yayan (wine) is a lawatz (mocker), and beer is a brawler. Whoever is led shagah (astray) by them is not chakam (wise).
The ayamah (terror) of a malak (king) is like the naham (roaring) of a kapayar (lion). He who provokes him to ibar (pass over/through) forfeits his own napash (soul).
It is an honor for a ayash (man / husband) to keep aloof from rayab (strife); but every awayal (fool) will be quarreling.
The itzal (sluggard) will not charash (plow) by reason of the charap (winter); therefore he shall shaal (beg) in qatzayar (harvest), and have nothing.
Itzah (counsel) in the lab (heart) of ayash (man / husband) is like imaq (deep) mayam (Waters); but a ayash (man / husband) of thabawan (understanding) will dalah (draw) it out.
Many adam (men) claim to be ayash (man / husband) of unfailing chasad (grace), but who can matzaa (find) a amawan (faithful) ayash (man / husband)?
A tzadayaq (righteous) halak (move) walks in tham (integrity). Ashar (who/that) are his ban (son) achar (other) him.
A malak (king) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the kasaa (throne) of dayan (judge) zarah (scatters) away all rai (evil) with his iyan (eye).
Who can amar (spoke), "I have made my lab (heart) pure. I am zakah (clean) and without chataah (sin)?"
Differing aban (stone) and differing ayapah (measures), shanayam (two) of them gam (indeed / moreover) are an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah.
Even a nair (child) makes himself nakar (known) by his mailal (doings), whether his pail (work) is zak (pure), and whether it is yashar (upright).
The shamai (hearken / hear) azan (ear), and the seeing iyan (eye), Yahawah ishah (make) made even shanayam (two) of them.
Don't ahab (love) shanah (sleep), lest you yarash (come) to poverty. Paqach (open) your iyan (eye), and you shall be shabai (satisfied) with lacham (bread).
"It's no rai (good), it's no rai (good)," amar (spoke) the qanah (buyer); but when he is azal (gone) his way, then he halal (praise).
There is zahab (gold) and rab (abundance) of panayanayam (rubies); but the shapathay (lips) of daith (knowledge) are a rare kalay (jewel).
Laqach (take / seize) the bagad (garment) of one who irab (evening) up collateral for a stranger; and hold him in chabal (pledge) for a wayward nakaray (woman).
Fraudulent lacham (food) is irab (evening) to a ayash (man / husband), but afterwards his pah (mouth) is malaa (filled) with chatzatz (gravel).
Plans are kawan (established) by thachabalah (advice); by wise guidance you wage malachamah (war)!
He who halak (move) about as a rakayal (tale-bearer) galah (reveals) sawad (secrets); therefore don't keep company with him who opens wide his shapah (lips).
Whoever qalal (curses) his ab (father) or his am (mother), his nayar (lamp) shall be daik (put) out in blackness of chashak (darkness).
An nachalah (inheritance) quickly gained at the raashawan (beginning), won't be barak (blessed) in the acharayath (end).
Don't amar (spoke), "I will shalam (pay) back rai (evil)." Qawah (gather/wait) for Yahawah, and he will yashai (salvation) you.
Yahawah detests differing aban (stone), and dishonest scales are not pleasing.
A gabar (man's) matzaiday (steps) are from Yahawah; how then can adam (man) bayan (between) his darak (way)?
It is a mawaqash (snare) to a adam (man) to make a rash dedication, then later to consider his nadarayam (vows).
A chakam (wise) malak (king) zarah (winnows) out the rashai (wicked), and drives the threshing awapan (wheel) over them.
The nashamah (breathing thing) of adam (man) is Yahawah nayar (lamp), chapash (searching) all his chadar (innermost) chadaray (parts).
Chasad (grace) and amath (truth) natzar (keep) the malak (king) safe. His kasaa (throne) is sustained by chasad (grace).
The glory of bachawar (young) men is their kach (strength / mighty / power). The splendor of zaqan (old) men is their shayabah (old age / white hair - due to age) hair.
Patzai (wounding) blows cleanse away rai (evil), and beatings purge the chadar (innermost) chadaray (parts).
The malak (king) lab (heart) is in Yahawah yad (hand) like the watercourses. He natah (turns) it wherever he chapatz (desires).
Every darak (way) of a ayash (man / husband) is yashar (upright) in his own iyan (eye), but Yahawah thakan (weighs) the labawath (hearts).
To ishah (make) tzadaqah (righteousness) and tzadaqah (righteousness) is more bachar (acceptable) to Yahawah than zabach (sacrifice).
A rawam (will lift up) iyan (eye), and a rachab (proud) lab (heart), the nayar (lamp) of the rashai (wicked), is chataah (sin).
The plans of the charawatz (diligent) surely lead to mawathar (profit); and everyone who is hasty surely rushes to machasawar (poverty).
Pail (getting) awatzarawath (treasures) by a shaqar (lying) lashawan (tongue / language) is a fleeting vapor for those who baqash (seek) mawath (death).
The violence of the rashai (wicked) will drive them away, because they maan (refuse) to ishah (make) what is mashapat (right).
The darak (way) of the guilty is devious, but the conduct of the innocent is yashar (upright).
It is tawab (good / proper function) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the panah (corner / cornerstone) of the housetop, than to share a bayath (house) with a madayan (contentious) ayashah (woman / wife).
The napash (soul) of the rashai (wicked) awah (desires) rai (evil); his neighbor finds no chanan (showing favor) in his iyan (eye).
When the lawatz (mocker) is inash (punished), the pathay (simple) gains chakam (wisdom). When the chakam (wise) is shakal (instructed), he laqach (take / seize) daith (knowledge).
The tzadayaq (righteous) One shakal (considers) the bayath (house) of the rashai (wicked), and brings the rashai (wicked) to ruin.
Whoever atam (stops) his azan (ear) at the zaiq (cry) of the dal (poor), he will also qaraa (called) out, but shall not be inah (answer / respond).
A mathan (gift) in sathar (secret / hidden) kapah (pacifies) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting); and a shachad (bribe) in the cloak, iz (strong) chamah (wrath).
It is shamachah (joy) to the tzadayaq (righteous) to ishah (make) mashapat (justice); but it is a machathah (destruction) to the pailay (workers) of awan (iniquity).
The adam (man) who thaih (wanders) out of the darak (way) of shakal (understanding) shall nawach (rest) in the qahal (assembly) of the rapaa (dead).
He who ahab (love) shamachah (pleasure) shall be a machasawar (poor) ayash (man / husband). He who ahab (love) yayan (wine) and shaman (oil) shall not be ishar (rich).
The rashai (wicked) is a kapar (ransom) for the tzadayaq (righteous); the bagad (treacherous) for the tzadayaq (righteous).
It is tawab (good / proper function) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) in a desert land, than with a madawan (contentious) and fretful ayashah (woman / wife).
There is chamad (precious) awatzar (treasure) and shaman (oil) in the nawah (habitation) of the chakam (wise); but a kasayal (foolish) adam (man) balai (swallows) it up.
He who radap (follows) after tzadaqah (righteousness) and chasad (grace) matzaa (finds) chay (life), tzadaqah (righteousness), and honor.
A chakam (wise) man ilah (go up / offer) the iyar (city) of the gabawar (mighty), and yarad (brings) down the iz (strength / might / refuge) of its mabatach (confidence).
Whoever guards his pah (mouth) and his lashawan (tongue / language) shamar (keep/guard) his napash (soul) from tzarawath (troubles).
The zad (proud) and haughty man, "scoffer" is his sham (name); he ishah (make) in the arrogance of zadawan (pride).
The thaawah (desire) of the itzal (sluggard) mawath (death) him, for his yad (hand) maan (refuse) to ishah (make).
There are those who awah (covet) thaawah (greedily) all yawam (day) long; but the tzadayaq (righteous) nathan (give) and don't chashak (darkness).
The zabach (sacrifice) of the rashai (wicked) is an thawaibah (abomination): how much more, when he bawaa (come) it with a zamah (wicked) mind!
A kazab (false) id (until / as far as) will abad (destroy / perish), and a ayash (man / husband) who shamai (hearken / hear) dabar (word / matter) to eternity.
A rashai (wicked) ayash (man / husband) izaz (hardens) his panayam (face); but as for the yashar (upright), he establishes his darak (ways).
There is no chakamah (wisdom) nor thabawan (understanding) nor itzah (counsel) against Yahawah.
The sawas (horse) is kawan (prepared) for the yawam (day) of malachamah (battle); but thashawaih (deliverance) is with Yahawah.
A good sham (name) is more desirable than rab (great) riches, and tawab (good / proper function) favor is better than kasap (silver) and zahab (gold).
The ishayar (rich) and the rawash (poor) have this in common: Yahawah is the maker of them all.
A irawam (prudent) man raah (see) danger, and sathar (hides) himself; but the pathay (simple) ibar (pass over/through) on, and suffer for it.
The result of inawah (humility) and the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is wealth, honor, and chay (life).
Tzanayam (thorns) and pachayam (snares) are in the darak (path) of the iqash (wicked): whoever guards his napash (soul) stays from them.
Chanak (train) up a nair (child) in the darak (way) he should go, and when he is zaqan (old) he will not sawar (depart) from it.
The ishayar (rich) mashal (rule/have dominion) over the rawash (poor). The lawah (borrower) is ibad (servant) to the lender.
He who zarai (sows) iwal (wickedness) qatzar (reaps) trouble, and the shabat (rod) of his fury will be kalah (complete / finish).
He who has a generous iyan (eye) will be barak (blessed); for he shares his lacham (food) with the dal (poor).
Garash (drive) out the lawatz (mocker), and dayan (judge) will yatzaa (go out / come out) out; yes, quarrels and insults will stop.
