He who ahab (love) purity of lab (heart) and speaks gracefully is the malak (king) rai (neigbor/another person).
The iyanay (eyes) of Yahawah watch over daith (knowledge); but he frustrates the dabaray (words) of the bagad (unfaithful).
The itzal (sluggard) amar (spoke), "There is a aray (lion) outside! I will be ratzach (killed) in the rachabawath (streets)!"
The pah (mouth) of an adulteress is a imaq (deep) shawachah (pit): he who is under Yahawah zaim (wrath) will napal (fall / be cast down) into it.
Awalath (folly) is qashar (bound) up in the lab (heart) of a nair (child): the shabat (rod) of mawasar (discipline) rachaq (drives) it far from him.
Whoever oppresses the dal (poor) for his own rabah (increase) and whoever nathan (give) to the ishayar (rich), both come to machasawar (poverty).
Natah (turn) your azan (ear), and listen to the dabaray (words) of the chakam (wise). Shayath (put / appoint / make) your lab (heart) to my teaching.
For it is a naiyam (pleasant) thing if you shamar (keep/guard) them batan (within) you, if yachad (all) of them are kawan (ready) on your shapah (lips).
That your mabatach (trust) may be in Yahawah, I yadai (teach) you today, even you.
Haven't I kathab (write) to you thirty excellent things of mawaitzah (counsel) and daith (knowledge),
To yadai (teach) you amath (truth), reliable amaray (words), to give sound shawab (turn back / repent) to the ones who shalach (send) you?
Don't exploit the dal (poor), because he is dal (poor); and don't dakaa (crush) the inay (needy) in court;
For Yahawah will rayab (plead) their case, and plunder the napash (soul) of those who plunder them.
Don't befriend a hot-tempered bail (man), and don't associate with bail (one) who harbors chamah (anger):
Lest you alap (learn) his arach (ways), and ensnare your napash (soul).
Don't you be one of those who thaqai (blow / sound alarm) kap (hands), of those who are collateral for mashaawath (debts).
If you don't have means to shalam (pay), why should he laqach (take / seize) away your mashakab (bed) from under you?
Don't move the iwalam (forever) boundary gabawal (border/boundary), which your ab (father) ishah (make) set up.
Do you chazah (see) a ayash (man / husband) skilled in his malaakah (work)? He will yatzab (serve) malakayam (kings). He won't yatzab (serve) obscure men.
When you yashab (inhabit/dwell) to lacham (eat) with a mashal (rule/have dominion), bayan (between) bayan (between) what is panayam (face) you;
Shawam (place / establish / appoint) a shakayan (knife) to your lai (throat), if you are a bail (man) given to napash (soul).
Don't be awah (desirous) of his mataim (dainties), since they are kazab (deceitful) lacham (food).
Don't yagai (weary) yourself to be ishar (rich). In your bayanah (wisdom), show restraint.
Why do you iwap (flying) your iyan (eye) on that which is not? For it ishah (make) sprouts kanapayam (wings) like an nashar (eagle) and iwap (flying) in the sky.
Don't lacham (eat) the lacham (food) of him who has a stingy iyan (eye), and don't crave his delicacies:
For as he shair (thinks) about the cost, so he is. "Akal (eat) and shathah (drinks)!" He amar (spoke) to you, but his lab (heart) is not with you.
The path (morsel) which you have akal (eat) you shall qawaa (vomit) up, and shachath (lose) your naiyam (good) dabar (word / matter).
Don't dabar (word / matter) in the azanay (ears) of a kasayal (fool), for he will bawaz (despise) the shakal (wisdom) of your malah (words).
Don't move the iwalam (forever) boundary gabawal (border/boundary). Don't encroach on the shaday (fields) of the yathawam (fatherless):
For their Defender is chazaq (strong). He will rayab (plead) their case against you.
Bawaa (come) your lab (heart) to mawasar (instruction), and your azan (ear) to the amaray (words) of daith (knowledge).
Don't manai (withhold) mawasar (correction) from a nair (child). If you nakah (punish) him with the shabat (rod), he will not mawath (death).
Nakah (punish) him with the shabat (rod), and natzal (save) his napash (soul) from shaawal (Sheol / afterlife).
My ban (son), if your lab (heart) is chakam (wise), then my lab (heart) will be shamach (glad), even anay (mine):
Yes, my kalayah (heart) will ilaz (rejoice), when your shapah (lips) dabar (word / matter) what is mayashar (right).
Don't let your lab (heart) qanaa (jealous) chataayam (sinners); but rather yaraah (fear) Yahawah all the yawam (day) long.
Indeed surely there is a future thaqawah (hope), and your hope will not be karath (cut) off.
Shamai (hearken / hear), my ban (son), and be chakam (wise), and keep your lab (heart) on the right darak (path)!
Don't be among yayan (ones) drinking too much zalal (wine), or those who gorge themselves on meat:
For the sabaa (drunkard) and the zalal (glutton) shall become yarash (poor); and nawamah (drowsiness) labash (clothes) them in qaraiyam (rags).
Shamai (hearken / hear) to your ab (father) who gave you yalad (birth / begot), and don't bawaz (despise) your am (mother) when she is zaqan (old).
Qanah (buy) the amath (truth), and don't makar (sell) it. Get chakamah (wisdom), mawasar (discipline), and bayanah (understanding).
The ab (father) of the tzadayaq (righteous) has great gayal (joy). Whoever yalad (birth / begot) a chakam (wise) child delights in him.
Let your ab (father) and your am (mother) be shamach (glad)! Let her who yalad (birth / begot) you gayal (rejoice)!
My ban (son), nathan (give) me your lab (heart); and let your iyan (eye) keep in my darak (ways).
For a prostitute is a imaq (deep) shawachah (pit); and a wayward wife is a tzar (oppressor / distressor) baar (well).
Yes, she lies in arab (wait) like a robber, and yasap (increases) the bagad (unfaithful) among adam (men).
Who has away (woe)? Who has abaway (sorrow)? Who has strife? Who has shayach (complaints)? Who has needless bruises? Who has bloodshot iyanayam (eyes)?
Those who achar (other) long at the yayan (wine); those who bawaa (come) to chaqar (seek) out mixed mamasak (wine).
Don't raah (see) at the yayan (wine) when it is adam (red), when it sparkles in the kayas (cup), when it halak (move) down smoothly.
In the acharayath (end), it nashak (bites) like a snake, and poisons like a viper.
Your iyan (eye) will raah (see) zawar (strange) things, and your lab (heart) will imagine confusing things.
Yes, you will be as he who shakab (lies) down in the lab (heart) of the yam (sea/waters), or as he who shakab (lies) on raash (head) of the rigging:
"They hit me, and I was not hurt! They halam (beat) me, and I don't yadai (feel) it! When will I qawatz (wake) up? I can do it again. I can find another."
Don't be qanaa (jealous) of rai (evil) anashay (men); neither awah (desire) to be with them:
For their lab (heart) plot violence, and their shapah (lips) dabar (word / matter) about imal (mischief).
Through chakamah (wisdom) a bayath (house) is banah (build); by thabawan (understanding) it is kawan (established);
By daith (knowledge) the rooms are malaa (filled) with all rare and beautiful treasure.
A chakam (wise) gabar (man) has great kach (strength / mighty / power); and a knowledgeable ayash (man / husband) amatz (increases) kach (strength / mighty / power);
For by wise guidance you wage your malachamah (war); and thashawaih (deliverance) is in many advisors.
Chakamawath (wisdom) is rawam (will lift up) high for a awayal (fool): he doesn't pathach (open) his pah (mouth) in the shair (gate).
Chashab (one) who plots to do raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) will be qaraa (called) a schemer.
The schemes of awalath (folly) are chataah (sin). The lawatz (mocker) is detested by adam (men).
If you falter in the yawam (day) of tzarah (trouble), your kach (strength / mighty / power) is tzar (oppressor / distressor).
Natzal (rescue) those who are being led away to mawath (death)! Indeed, chashak (darkness) back those who are staggering to the harag (kill)!

If you amar (spoke), "Behold, we didn't yadai (know) this;" doesn't he who thakan (weighs) the labawath (hearts) bayan (between) it? He who natzar (keeps) your napash (soul), doesn't he yadai (know) it? Shall he not shawab (turn back / repent) to every adam (man) according to his pail (work)?
My ban (son), akal (eat) dabash (honey), for it is tawab (good / proper function); the droppings of the napath (honeycomb), which are mathawaq (sweet) to your chak (taste):

So you shall yadai (know) chakamah (wisdom) to be to your napash (soul); if you matzaa (have) found it, then there yash (will) be a acharayath (reward), your thaqawah (hope) will not be karath (cut) off.
Don't arab (lay) in wait, rashai (wicked) man, against the nawah (habitation) of the tzadayaq (righteous). Don't shadad (destroy) his rabatz (resting) place:
For a tzadayaq (righteous) man napal (fall / be cast down) shabai (seven) times, and qawam (rise up) up again; but the rashai (wicked) are kashal (stumble / stagger) by rai (calamity).
Don't shamach (rejoice) when your ayab (enemy) napal (fall / be cast down). Don't let your lab (heart) be gayal (glad) when he is kashal (stumble / stagger);
Lest Yahawah raah (see) it, and it raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) him, and he shawab (turn back / repent) away his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) from him.
Don't charah (hot with anger) yourself because of evildoers; neither be qanaa (jealous) of the rashai (wicked):
For there will be no acharayath (reward) to the rai (evil) man; and the nayar (lamp) of the rashai (wicked) shall be snuffed out.
My ban (son), yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah and the malak (king). Don't join those who are rebellious:
For their ayad (calamity) will qawam (rise up) pathaawam (suddenly); the payad (destruction) from them both—who yadai (knows)?
These also are sayings of the chakam (wise). To show partiality in mashapat (judgment) is not tawab (good / proper function).
He who amar (spoke) to the rashai (wicked), "You are tzadayaq (righteous);" imayam (peoples) shall naqab (curse) him, and imayam (nations) shall zaim (abhor) him—
But it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and a rich barakah (blessing) will bawaa (come) on them.
An honest dabar (word / matter) is like a nashaq (kiss) on the shapathayam (lips).
Kawan (prepare) your malaakah (work) outside, and get your shadah (fields) ithad (ready). Afterwards, banah (build) your bayath (house).
Don't be a id (until / as far as) against your neighbor chanam (without) cause. Don't pathah (deceive) with your shapah (lips).
Don't amar (spoke), "I will ishah (make) to him as he ishah (make) done to me; I will shawab (turn back / repent) to the ayash (man / husband) according to his pail (work)."
I ibar (pass over/through) by the shadah (field) of the sluggard, by the karam (vineyard) of the adam (man) chasar (void) of lab (heart);
Behold, it was all ilah (go up / offer) over with qamashanayam (thorns). Its surface was kasah (covered) with charalayam (nettles), and its aban (stone) gadar (wall) was haras (broken) down.
Then I chazah (saw), and shayath (put / appoint / make) well. I raah (see), and laqach (take / seize) mawasar (instruction):
A mait (little) shanah (sleep), a mait (little) thanawamah (slumber), a mait (little) chabaq (folding) of the yadayam (hands) to sleep;
So your rayash (poverty) will bawaa (come) as a robber, and your machasawar (want) as an magan (shield) ayash (man / husband).
These also are mashalay (proverbs) of Shalamah (Solomon), which the anashay (men) of Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) ithaq (copied) out.
It is the kabawad (glory) of Alahayam to sathar (conceal) a thing, but the kabawad (glory) of malakayam (kings) is to chaqar (search) out a dabar (word / matter).
As the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) for rawam (will lift up), and the aratz (Earth/land) for imaq (depth), so the lab (heart) of malakayam (kings) are unsearchable.
Take hagah (away) the sayag (dross) from the kasap (silver), and material yatzaa (go out / come out) out for the refiner;
Take hagah (away) the rashai (wicked) from the malak (king) panayam (face), and his kasaa (throne) will be kawan (established) in tzadaq (righteous / just / fair).
Don't exalt yourself in the panayam (face) of the malak (king), or claim a maqawam (place) among gadawal (very great/important/mighty) men;

For it is tawab (good / proper function) that it be amar (spoke) to you, "ilah (go up / offer) up here," than that you should be shapal (put) lower in the panayam (face) of the nadayab (prince), whom your iyan (eye) raah (see) seen.
Don't be hasty in yatzaa (go out / come out) charges to court. What will you ishah (make) in the acharayath (end) when your neighbor kalam (shames) you?
Rayab (debate) your case with your neighbor, and don't betray the confidence of achar (other);
Lest one who shamai (hearken / hear) it chasad (grace) you to shame, and your bad reputation never depart.
A dabar (word / matter) fitly dabar (word / matter) is like thapawachay (apples) of zahab (gold) in settings of kasap (silver).
As an nazam (earring) of zahab (gold), and an chalay (ornament) of katham (fine) gold, so is a chakam (wise) yakach (reprover) to an shamai (hearken / hear) azan (ear).

As the tzanah (cold) of shalag (snow) in the yawam (day) of qatzayar (harvest), so is a aman (believe / have faith) tzayar (messenger) to those who shalach (send) him; for he refreshes the napash (soul) of his adawan (master / lord).
As nashayaayam (clouds) and rawach (spirit / wind) without gasham (rain), so is he who halal (praise) of mathath (gifts) deceptively.
By patience a qatzayan (ruler) is pathah (persuaded). A rak (soft) lashawan (tongue / language) shabar (breaks) the garam (bone).
Matzaa (have) you found dabash (honey)? Akal (eat) as much as is day (sufficient) for you, lest you eat too much, and qawaa (vomit) it.
Let your ragal (feet / foot) be seldom in your neighbor's bayath (house), lest he be shabai (weary) of you, and shanaa (hate) you.
A ayash (man / husband) who inah (answer / respond) shaqar (false) id (until / as far as) against his neighbor is like a club, a charab (sword), or a shanan (sharp) chatz (arrow).
Mabatach (confidence) in someone bagad (unfaithful) in yawam (day) of tzarah (trouble) is like a bad shan (tooth), or a lame ragal (feet / foot).
As one who idah (takes) away a bagad (garment) in qarah (cold) yawam (day), or chamatz (vinegar) on soda, so is one who shayar (sings) sharayam (songs) to a rai (heavy) lab (heart).
If your shanaa (hate) is raib (hungry), give him lacham (food) to akal (eat). If he is thirsty, give him mayam (Waters) to shaqah (drink):
For you will chathah (heap) gachalayam (coals) of fire on his raash (head), and Yahawah will shalam (reward) you.
The tzapawan (north) rawach (spirit / wind) chawal (brings) forth gasham (rain): so a sathar (secret / hidden) lashawan (tongue / language) brings an zaim (angry) panayam (face).
It is tawab (good / proper function) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the panah (corner / cornerstone) of the housetop, than to share a bayath (house) with a madawan (contentious) ayashah (woman / wife).
Like qar (cold) mayam (Waters) to a iyap (thirsty) napash (soul), so is tawab (good / proper function) shamawaih (news) from a marachaq (far) aratz (Earth/land).
Like a muddied maiyan (spring), and a polluted maqawar (well), so is a tzadayaq (righteous) mawat (man) who gives way panayam (face) the rashai (wicked).
It is not tawab (good / proper function) to akal (eat) much dabash (honey); nor is it honorable to seek kabawad (one's) own honor.
Like a iyar (city) that is paratz (broken) down and without chawamah (walls) is a ayash (man / husband) whose rawach (spirit / wind) is without restraint.
Like shalag (snow) in qayatz (summer), and as matar (rain) in qatzayar (harvest), so honor is not fitting for a kasayal (fool).
Like a fluttering tzapawar (sparrow), like a darting darawar (swallow), so the undeserved qalalah (curse) doesn't bawaa (come) to bawaa (come).
A shawat (whip) is for the sawas (horse), a mathag (bridle) for the donkey, and a shabat (rod) for the gaw (back) of kasayalayam (fools)!
Don't inah (answer / respond) a kasayal (fool) according to his awalath (folly), lest you also be shawah (like) him.
Inah (answer / respond) a kasayal (fool) according to his awalath (folly), lest he be chakam (wise) in his own iyan (eye).
One who shalach (send) a dabar (word / matter) by the yad (hand) of a kasayal (fool) is qatzah (end / extremity / border) off ragalayam (feet) and shathah (drinks) chamas (violence).
Like the shaqayam (legs) of the pasach (lame) that hang loose: so is a mashal (parable) in the pah (mouth) of kasayalayam (fools).
As one who binds a aban (stone) in a maragamah (sling), so is he who nathan (give) honor to a kasayal (fool).
Like a thornbush that ilah (go up / offer) into the yad (hand) of a drunkard, so is a mashal (parable) in the pah (mouth) of kasayalayam (fools).
As an archer who wounds all, so is he who shakar (hires) a kasayal (fool) or he who shakar (hires) those who ibar (pass over/through) by.
As a kalab (dog) that shawab (turn back / repent) to his qaa (vomit), so is a kasayal (fool) who shanah (repeats) his awalath (folly).
Do you raah (see) a ayash (man / husband) chakam (wise) in his own iyan (eye)? There is more thaqawah (hope) for a kasayal (fool) than for him.
The itzal (sluggard) amar (spoke), "There is a shachal (lion) in the road! A fierce shachal (lion) roams the rachabawath (streets)!"
As the dalath (door) sabab (turns) on its tzayar (hinges), so does the itzal (sluggard) on his matah (bed).
The itzal (sluggard) buries his yad (hand) in the tzalachath (dish). He is too lazy to shawab (turn back / repent) it back to his pah (mouth).
The itzal (sluggard) is wiser in his own iyan (eye) than shabai (seven) men who shawab (turn back / repent) with taim (discretion).
Like chazaq (one) who grabs a kalab (dog's) azanay (ears) is ibar (pass over/through) who passes by and ibar (pass over/through) in a quarrel not his own.
Like a madman who yarah (shoots) torches, chatzayam (arrows), and mawath (death),
Is the ayash (man / husband) who ramah (deceives) his neighbor and amar (spoke), "Am I not joking?"
For lack of itz (wood) a ash (fire) kabah (goes) out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.
As pacham (coals) are to hot embers, and itz (wood) to ash (fire), so is a madawan (contentious) ayash (man / husband) to charar (kindling) rayab (strife).
The dabaray (words) of a naragan (whisperer) are as dainty morsels, they yarad (go) down into the innermost chadaray (parts).
Like kasap (silver) sayag (dross) on an charash (earthen) vessel are the shapathayam (lips) of a fervent one with an rai (evil) lab (heart).
A malicious nakar (man) disguises himself with his shapah (lips), but he harbors maramah (evil) in his qarab (among / near).
When his speech is charming, don't aman (believe / have faith) him; for there are shabai (seven) thawaibawath (abominations) in his lab (heart).
His malice may be kasah (concealed) by deception, but his rai (wickedness) will be exposed in the qahal (assembly).
Whoever karah (digs) a shachath (pit) shall napal (fall / be cast down) into it. Whoever galal (rolls) a aban (stone), it will shawab (turn back / repent) back on him.
A shaqar (lying) lashawan (tongue / language) shanaa (hate) those it hurts; and a chalaq (flattering) pah (mouth) ishah (make) madachah (ruin).
Don't halal (praise) about machar (tomorrow); for you don't yadai (know) what a machar (day) may yalad (birth / begot) forth.
Let another zawar (man) halal (praise) you, and not your own pah (mouth); a stranger, and not your own shapah (lips).
A aban (stone) is kabad (heavy), and chawal (sand) is a burden; but a awayal (fool's) kais (provocation) is kabad (heavier) than shanayam (two).
Chamah (wrath) is akazarayawath (cruel), and ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) is overwhelming; but who is able to imad (stand) panayam (face) qanaah (jealousy)?
Tawab (good / proper function) is galah (open) thawakachah (rebuke) than sathar (hidden) ahabah (love).
Aman (believe / have faith) are the patzaiy (wounds) of a ahab (love); although the kisses of an shanaa (hate) are profuse.
A shabai (full) napash (soul) loathes a napath (honeycomb); but to a raib (hungry) napash (soul), every mar (bitter) thing is mathawaq (sweet).
As a tzapawar (bird) that nadad (wanders) from her qan (nest), so is a ayash (man / husband) who nadad (wanders) from his maqawam (place).
Qatarath (perfume) and incense bring shamach (joy) to the lab (heart); so does earnest itzah (counsel) from a man's rai (neigbor/another person).

Don't izab (forsake) your rai (neigbor/another person) and your ab (father) rai (neigbor/another person). Don't bawaa (come) to your ach (brother/kinsman) bayath (house) in the yawam (day) of your disaster: tawab (good / proper function) is a neighbor who is qarawab (near) than a distant ach (brother/kinsman).
Be chakam (wise), my ban (son), and bring shamach (joy) to my lab (heart), then I can shawab (turn back / repent) my tormentor.
A irawam (prudent) man raah (see) danger and takes refuge; but the pathay (simple) ibar (pass over/through) on, and suffer for it.
Laqach (take / seize) his bagad (garment) when he irab (evening) up collateral for a stranger. Hold it for a wayward nakaray (woman)!
He who blesses his neighbor with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice) shakam (early) in the shakam (morning), it will be taken as a qalalah (curse) by him.
A tarad (continual) dalap (dropping) on a sagarayad (rainy) yawam (day) and a madawan (contentious) ayashah (woman / wife) are alike:
Restraining her is like restraining the rawach (spirit / wind), or like grasping shaman (oil) in his right yamayan (right hand).
Barazal (iron) chadad (sharpens) barazal (iron); so a ayash (man / husband) chadad (sharpens) his rai (neigbor/another person) panayam (face).
Whoever tends the thaan (fig) tree shall akal (eat) its paray (fruit). He who shamar (keep/guard) after his adawan (master / lord) shall be honored.
As mayam (Waters) reflects a panayam (face), so a adam (man's) lab (heart) reflects the adam (man).
Shaawal (Sheol / afterlife) and Abaddon are laa (NOT) shabai (satisfied); and a adam (man's) iyanay (eyes) are never shabai (satisfied).
The crucible is for kasap (silver), and the kawar (furnace) for zahab (gold); but ayash (man / husband) is refined by his mahalal (praise).
Though you grind a awayal (fool) in a makathash (mortar) with a ilay (went up) along with grain, yet his awalath (foolishness) will not be sawar (removed) from him.
Yadai (know) well the panayam (face) of your tzaan (flocks), and pay attention to your idarayam (herds):
For riches are not iwalam (forever), nor does even the nazar (crown / consecrate) endure to all dawar (generation / age / period).
The chatzayar (hay) is removed, and the new growth raah (see), the grasses of the harayam (hills) are asap (gathered) in.
The kabashayam (lambs) are for your labawash (clothing), and the ithawadayam (goats) are the machayar (price) of a shadah (field).
There will be plenty of izayam (goats)' chalab (milk) for your lacham (food), for your bayath (house) lacham (food), and for the nourishment of your nairah (servant) girls.
The rashai (wicked) nawas (flee) when no one radap (pursues); but the tzadayaq (righteous) are as batach (bold) as a kapayar (lion).
In pashai (rebellion), a aratz (Earth/land) rab (has) many shar (prince / ruler), but order is maintained by a adam (man) of bayan (between) and yadai (knowledge).
A rawash (needy) gabar (man) who oppresses the dal (poor) is like a driving matar (rain) which leaves no crops.
Those who izab (forsake) the thawarah (instruction) halal (praise) the rashai (wicked); but those who shamar (keep/guard) the thawarah (instruction) garah (contend) with them.
Rai (evil) anashay (men) don't bayan (between) mashapat (justice); but those who baqash (seek) Yahawah bayan (between) it fully.
Tawab (good / proper function) is the rawash (poor) who halak (move) in his tham (integrity), than he who is iqash (perverse) in his darakayam (ways), and he is ishayar (rich).
Whoever natzar (keeps) the thawarah (instruction) is a bayan (between) ban (son); but he who is a raih (companion) of zawalalayam (gluttons) kalam (shames) his ab (father).
He who rabah (increases) his hawan (wealth) by excessive interest qabatz (gathers) it for one who chanan (showing favor) pity on the dal (poor).
He who sawar (turns) away his azan (ear) from shamai (hearken / hear) the thawarah (instruction), even his thapalah (prayer) is an thawaibah (abomination).

Whoever causes the yashar (upright) to shagah (go) astray in an rai (evil) darak (way), he will napal (fall / be cast down) into his own trap; but the blameless will nachal (inherit) tawab (good / proper function).
The ishayar (rich) ayash (man / husband) is chakam (wise) in his own iyan (eye); but the dal (poor) who has bayan (between) sees through him.
When the tzadayaq (righteous) ilatz (triumph), there is rab (great) glory; but when the rashai (wicked) qawam (rise up), adam (men) chapash (hide) themselves.
He who kasah (conceals) his pashai (sins) doesn't tzalach (prosper), but whoever confesses and renounces them finds racham (show mercy / love).
Ashar (who/that) is the adam (man) who thamayad (always) pachad (fear / dread); but qashah (rough / hard) who hardens his lab (heart) napal (fall / be cast down) into rai (trouble).
As a naham (roaring) aray (lion) or a charging dab (bear), so is a rashai (wicked) mashal (rule/have dominion) over helpless im (nation / people).
A tyrannical nagayad (ruler) chasar (lacks) thabawan (judgment). One who shanaay (hates) ill-gotten gain will have arak (long) yamayam (days).
A adam (man) who is tormented by napash (soul) dam (blood) will be a fugitive until bawar (death); no thamak (one) will support him.
Whoever halak (move) blamelessly is kept yashai (salvation); but one with iqash (perverse) darakayam (ways) will napal (fall / be cast down) suddenly.
One who ibad (servant) his adamah (land) will shabai (have) an abundance of lacham (food); but one who radap (chases) fantasies will have his fill of rayash (poverty).
A amawanah (faithful) ayash (man / husband) is rich with barakawath (blessings); but awatz (one) who is eager to be ishar (rich) will not go naqah (clean/innocent).
To show partiality is not tawab (good / proper function); yet a gabar (man) will do wrong for a path (piece) of lacham (bread).
A stingy iyan (eye) hurries after riches, and doesn't yadai (know) that chasar (poverty) waits for him.
One who yakach (rebukes) a adam (man) will afterward matzaa (find) more favor than one who chalaq (flatters) with the lashawan (tongue / language).
Whoever gazal (robs) his ab (father) or his am (mother), and amar (spoke), "It's not wrong." He is a partner with a destroyer.
Napash (soul) who is greedy garah (stirs) up madawan (strife); but one who batach (trusts) in Yahawah will dashan (prosper).
One who batach (trusts) in himself is a kasayal (fool); but one who halak (move) in chakamah (wisdom) is kept safe.
One who nathan (give) to the rawash (poor) has no machasawar (lack); but ilam (one) who closes his iyan (eye) will rab (have) many maarawath (curses).
When the rashai (wicked) qawam (rise up), adam (men) sathar (hide) themselves; but when they abad (destroy / perish), the tzadayaq (righteous) thrive.
He who is often thawakachah (rebuked) and stiffens his irap (neck) will be shabar (destroyed) pathai (suddenly), with no marapaa (remedy).
When the tzadayaq (righteous) thrive, the im (nation / people) shamach (rejoice); but when the rashai (wicked) mashal (rule/have dominion), the im (nation / people) anach (groan).
Ayash (man / husband) ahab (love) chakamah (wisdom) brings shamach (joy) to his ab (father); but a raih (companion) of prostitutes squanders his hawan (wealth).
The malak (king) by mashapat (justice) makes the aratz (Earth/land) stable, but he who takes bribes tears it down.
A gabar (man) who chalaq (flatters) his neighbor parash (spreads) a rashath (net) for his paim (feet).
An rai (evil) ayash (man / husband) is mawaqash (snared) by his pashai (sin), but the tzadayaq (righteous) can ranan (sing) and be shamach (glad).
The tzadayaq (righteous) care about dayan (judge) for the dal (poor). The rashai (wicked) aren't concerned about daith (knowledge).
Mockers stir up a qarayah (city / town), but chakam (wise) men shawab (turn back / repent) away ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).
If a chakam (wise) ayash (man / husband) goes to court with a awayal (foolish) ayash (man / husband), the fool ragaz (rages) or scoffs, and there is no nachath (peace).
The bloodthirsty shanaa (hate) a tham (man) of integrity; and they baqash (seek) the napash (soul) of the yashar (upright).
A kasayal (fool) vents all of his rawach (spirit / wind), but a chakam (wise) shabach (man) brings himself under control.
If a mashal (rule/have dominion) listens to lies, all of his officials are rashai (wicked).
The rawash (poor) ayash (man / husband) and the oppressor have this in common: Yahawah gives iyan (eye) to the iyanay (eyes) of shanayam (two).
The malak (king) who fairly shapat (judge / judgement) the dal (poor), his kasaa (throne) shall be kawan (established) id (until / as far as).
The shabat (rod) of thawakachah (correction) nathan (give) chakamah (wisdom), but a nair (child) shalach (send) to himself bawash (causes) shame to his am (mother).
When the rashai (wicked) rabah (increase), pashai (sin) rabah (increases); but the tzadayaq (righteous) will raah (see) their downfall.
Yasar (correct) your ban (son), and he will nawach (give) you peace; yes, he will nathan (give) maidan (delight) to your napash (soul).
Where there is no revelation, the im (nation / people) cast off restraint; but one who shamar (keep/guard) the thawarah (instruction) is ashar (who/that).
A ibad (servant) can't be yasar (corrected) by dabarayam (words). Though he bayan (between), yet he will not respond.
Do you chazah (see) a ayash (man / husband) who is hasty in his dabar (word / matter)? There is more thaqawah (hope) for a kasayal (fool) than for him.
He who pampers his ibad (servant) from nair (youth) will have him become a manawan (son) in the acharayath (end).
An angry ayash (man / husband) garah (stirs) up madawan (strife), and a chamah (wrathful) bail (man) rab (abounds) in pashai (sin).
A adam (man's) gaawah (pride) shapal (brings) him low, but shapal (one) of lowly rawach (spirit / wind) gains honor.
Whoever is an accomplice of a ganab (thief) is an shanaa (hate) of his own napash (soul). He takes an alah (curse / oath), but dares not testify.
The charadah (fear) of adam (man) proves to be a mawaqash (snare), but whoever batach (puts) his trust in Yahawah is kept shagab (safe).
Many baqash (seek) the mashal (rule/have dominion) favor, but a ayash (man / husband) mashapat (justice) comes from Yahawah.
A dishonest ayash (man / husband) detests the tzadayaq (righteous), and the yashar (upright) in their darak (ways) detest the rashai (wicked).
The dabaray (words) of Agawar (Agur) the ban (son) of Yaqah (Jakeh), the oracle: the gabar (man) naam (declares prophetically) to Ayathayaal (Ithiel), to Ayathayaal (Ithiel) and Akal (Ucal):
"Surely I am the most ignorant ayash (man / husband), and don't have a ayash (man / husband) bayanah (understanding).
I have not lamad (teach / instruct) chakamah (wisdom), neither do I yadai (have) the daith (knowledge) of the qadawash (holy) One.

Who has ilah (go up / offer) up into shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and descended? Who has asap (gathered) the rawach (spirit / wind) in his chapan (fists)? Who has tzarar (bound) the mayam (Waters) in his shamalah (garment)? Who has qawam (rise up) all the apasay (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land)? What is his sham (name), and what is his ban (son) sham (name), if you yadai (know)?
"Every amarah (sayings) of Alawah is flawless. He is a magan (shield) to those who take chasah (refuge) in him.
Don't you yasap (add) to his dabar (word / matter), lest he yakach (reprove) you, and you be kazab (found) a liar.
"Shanayam (two) things I have shaal (asked) of you; don't manai (deny) me before I mawath (death):
Rachaq (remove) far from me falsehood and lies. Nathan (give) me neither rayash (poverty) nor riches. Tarap (feed) me with the lacham (food) that is needful for me;
Lest I be shabai (full), kachash (deny) you, and amar (spoke), ‘Who is Yahawah?' Or lest I be yarash (poor), and ganab (steal), and so dishonor the sham (name) of my Alahayam.
"Don't lashan (slander) a ibad (servant) to his adawan (master / lord), lest he qalal (curse) you, and you be asham (held) guilty.
There is a dawar (generation / age / period) that qalal (curses) their ab (father), and doesn't barak (blessed) their am (mother).
There is a dawar (generation / age / period) that is tahawar (pure) in their own iyan (eye), yet are not rachatz (washed) from their tzawaah (filthiness).
There is a dawar (generation / age / period), oh how rawam (will lift up) are their iyan (eye)! Their ipaip (eyelids) are nashaa (lift) up.

There is a dawar (generation / age / period) whose shan (teeth) are like charabawath (swords), and their mathalaih (jaws) like knives, to akal (eat) the inay (poor) from the aratz (Earth/land), and the abayawan (needy) from among adam (men).

"The leach has shanayam (two) banawath (daughters): ‘yahab (give), yahab (give).' "There are shalawash (three) things that are never shabai (satisfied); arabai (four) that don't say, ‘hawan (enough):'

Shaawal (Sheol / afterlife), the itzar (barren) racham (show mercy / love); the aratz (Earth/land) that is not shabai (satisfied) with mayam (Waters); and the ash (fire) that doesn't amar (spoke), ‘hawan (enough).'

"The iyan (eye) that laig (mocks) at his ab (father), and scorns obedience to his am (mother): the irabay (ravens) of the nachal (stream / river) shall naqar (pick) it out, the ban (son) nashar (eagles) shall akal (eat) it.
"There are shalawash (three) things which are palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) amazing for me, arabai (four) which I don't yadai (understand):

The darak (way) of an nashar (eagle) in the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens); the darak (way) of a nachash (serpent) on a tzawar (rock); the darak (way) of a anayah (ship) in the lab (heart) of the yam (sea/waters); and the darak (way) of a gabar (man) with a maiden.
"So is the darak (way) of an adulterous ayashah (woman / wife): she akal (eat) and machah (wipes) her pah (mouth), and amar (spoke), ‘I have pail (done) nothing wrong.'
"For shalawash (three) things the aratz (Earth/land) ragaz (tremble), and under arabai (four), it can't nashaa (lift) up:
For a ibad (servant) when he is malak (king); a nabal (fool) when he is shabai (filled) with lacham (food);
For an unloved woman when she is bail (married); and a handmaid who is heir to her gabarath (mistress).
"There are arabai (four) things which are qatan (small / young / least) on the aratz (Earth/land), but they are exceedingly chakam (wise):
The namalayam (ants) are not a iz (strong) im (nation / people), yet they kawan (provide) their lacham (food) in the qayatz (summer).
The Shapan (conies) are but a itzawam (feeble) im (nation / people), yet shawam (place / establish / appoint) they their bayath (house) in the salai (rocks).
The arabah (locusts) have no malak (king), yet they advance in ranks.
You can thapash (catch) a lizard with your yadayam (hands), yet it is in malak (king)' hayakalay (palaces).
"There are shalawash (three) things which are stately in their march, arabai (four) which are stately in yalak (going):
The layash (lion), which is mightiest among animals, and doesn't shawab (turn back / repent) away for any;
The mathan (greyhound), the male thayash (goat) also; and the malak (king) against whom there is no alaqawam (rising) up.
"If you have nabal (done) foolishly in nashaa (lift) up yourself, or if you have zamam (thought) evil, put your yad (hand) over your pah (mouth).

For as the mayatz (churning) of chalab (milk) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth chamaah (butter), and the mayatz (wringing) of the ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth dam (blood); so the mayatz (forcing) of ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth rayab (strife)."
The dabaray (words) of malak (king) Lamawaal (Lemuel); the oracle which his am (mother) yasar (taught) him.
"Oh, my bar (son)! Oh, bar (son) of my batan (womb)! Oh, bar (son) of my nadar (vow)!
Don't nathan (give) your chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) to nashayam (women), nor your darak (ways) to that which machah (destroys) malakayan (kings).
It is not for malakayam (kings), Lamawaal (Lemuel); it is not for malakayam (kings) to shathah (drinks) yayan (wine); nor for rawazanayam (princes) to say, ‘Where is shakar (strong) drink?'
Lest they shathah (drinks), and shakach (forget) the chaqaq (lawgiver), and shanah (pervert) the dayan (judge) due to anyone who is ban (son).
Nathan (give) shakar (strong) drink to him who is ready to abad (destroy / perish); and yayan (wine) to the mar (bitter) in napash (soul):
Let him shathah (drinks), and shakach (forget) his rayash (poverty), and zakar (remember) his misery no more.
Pathach (open) your pah (mouth) for the mute, in the dayan (judge) of all who are left desolate.
Pathach (open) your pah (mouth), shapat (judge / judgement) righteously, and dayan (judge) justice to the inay (poor) and abayawan (needy)."
Who can matzaa (find) a chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) ayashah (woman / wife)? For her makar (price) is rachawaq (far) above panayanayam (rubies).
The lab (heart) of her bail (husband) batach (trusts) in her. He shall have no chasar (lack) of gain.
She gamal (does) him tawab (good / proper function), and not rai (harm), all the yamay (days) of her chay (life).
She darash (seeks) tzamar (wool) and pashathah (flax), and ishah (make) eagerly with her kap (hands).
She is like the sachar (merchant) anayawath (ships). She bawaa (come) her lacham (bread) from afar.
She qawam (rise up) also while it is yet layal (night), nathan (give) food to her bayath (house), and chaq (statute) for her nairah (servant) girls.
She zamam (considers) a shadah (field), and laqach (take / seize) it. With the paray (fruit) of her kap (hands), she natai (plants) a karam (vineyard).
She arms her waist with iz (strength / might / refuge), and makes her zarawai (arms) iz (strength / might / refuge).
She taim (perceives) that her sachar (merchandise) is profitable. Her nayar (lamp) doesn't kabah (go) out by layal (night).
She shalach (send) her yad (hand) to the palak (distaff), and her kap (hands) thamak (hold) the kayashawar (spindle).
She parash (opens) her arms to the inay (poor); yes, she extends her yad (hand) to the abayawan (needy).
She is not yaraa (fear / be afraid) of the shalag (snow) for her bayath (house); for all her bayath (house) are labash (clothed) with shanay (second).
She ishah (make) for herself carpets of marabad (tapestry). Her labawash (clothing) is shash (six) linen and aragaman (purple).
Her bail (husband) is yadai (respected) in the shairayam (gates), when he yashab (inhabit/dwell) among the zaqanay (elders) of the aratz (Earth/land).
She ishah (make) sadayan (linen) garments and makar (sells) them, and nathan (give) sashes to the kanainay (Canaanite).
Iz (strength / might / refuge) and dignity are her labawash (clothing). She shachaq (laughs) at the yawam (day) to acharawan (come).
She pathach (opens) her pah (mouth) with chakamah (wisdom). Chasad (grace) instruction is on her lashawan (tongue / language).
She tzapah (watchman / keep watch) well to the halayakawath (ways) of her bayath (house), and doesn't akal (eat) the lacham (bread) of itzalawath (idleness).
Her ban (son) qawam (rise up) up and ashar (who/that) her blessed. Her bail (husband) also halal (praise) her:
"Many women ishah (make) noble things, but you ilah (go up / offer) them all."
Charm is shaqar (deceitful), and yapay (beauty) is habal (vain); but a ayashah (woman / wife) who yaraa (fears) Yahawah, she shall be halal (praise).
Nathan (give) her of the paray (fruit) of her yad (hand)! Let her maishah (works) halal (praise) her in the shairayam (gates)!
The dabaray (words) of the qahalath (preacher), the ban (son) of Dawad (David), malak (king) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem):
"Habal (vanity) of habalayam (vanities)," amar (spoke) the qahalath (preacher); "habal (vanity) of habalayam (vanities), all is habal (vanity)."
What does adam (man) gain from all his imal (labor) in which he imal (labors) under the shamash (sun)?
One dawar (generation / age / period) halak (move), and another dawar (generation / age / period) bawaa (come); but the aratz (Earth/land) imad (remains) iwalam (forever).
The shamash (sun) also zarach (rises), and the shamash (sun) bawaa (come) down, and hurries to its maqawam (place) where it zarach (rises).

The rawach (spirit / wind) halak (move) toward the darawam (south), and sabab (turns) around to the tzapawan (north). It sabab (turns) around halak (move) as it goes, and the rawach (spirit / wind) shawab (turn back / repent) again to its courses.
All the nachalayam (rivers) halak (move) into the yam (sea/waters), yet the yam (sea/waters) is not malaa (full). To the maqawam (place) where the nachalayam (rivers) flow, there they flow again.
All things are yagai (full) of weariness beyond dabar (word / matter). The iyan (eye) is not shabai (satisfied) with seeing, nor the azan (ear) shabai (filled) with shamai (hearken / hear).
That which ishah (make) been is that which shall be; and that which has been done is that which shall be ishah (make): and there is no chadash (new) thing under the shamash (sun).
Is there a thing of which it may be amar (spoke), "raah (see), this is chadash (new)?" It has been long ago, in the ages which were panayam (face) us.
There is no memory of the raashawan (former); neither shall there be any memory of the acharawan (latter) that are to come, among those that shall acharawan (come) after.
I, the qahalath (preacher), was malak (king) over Yashar-Al (Israel) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

I nathan (give) my lab (heart) to darash (seek) and to thawar (search) out by chakamah (wisdom) concerning all that is ishah (make) under the sky. It is a rai (heavy) burden that Alahayam nathan (give) given to the banay (sons) of adam (men) to be inah (oppress / afflict) with.
I raah (see) seen all the maishayam (works) that are ishah (make) under the shamash (sun); and behold, all is habal (vanity) and a chasing after rawach (spirit / wind).
That which is iwath (crooked) can't be made thaqan (straight); and that which is lacking can't be manah (counted).

I dabar (word / matter) to myself, "Behold, I have obtained for myself gadal (great) chakamah (wisdom) above all who were panayam (face) me in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem). Yes, my lab (heart) rabah (has) had great raah (see) of chakamah (wisdom) and daith (knowledge)."

I nathan (give) my lab (heart) to yadai (know) chakamah (wisdom), and to yadai (know) hawalalah (madness) and sakalawath (folly). I yadai (perceived) that this also was a chasing after rawach (spirit / wind).
For in much chakamah (wisdom) is much kais (grief); and he who yasap (increases) daith (knowledge) yasap (increases) makaab (sorrow).
I amar (spoke) in my lab (heart), "yalak (come) now, I will test you with shamachah (mirth): therefore raah (see) tawab (good / proper function);" and behold, this also was habal (vanity).
I amar (spoke) of shachawaq (laughter/joking matter), "It is foolishness;" and of shamachah (mirth), "What ishah (make) it accomplish?"

I thawar (searched) in my lab (heart) how to cheer my flesh with yayan (wine), my lab (heart) yet nahag (guiding) me with chakamah (wisdom), and how to achaz (lay) hold of sakalawath (folly), until I might raah (see) what it was tawab (good / proper function) for the banay (sons) of adam (men) that they should ishah (make) under shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) masapar (all) the yamay (days) of their chay (life).
I gadal (made) myself great maishah (works). I banah (build) myself bathayam (houses). I natai (planted) myself karamayam (vineyards).
I ishah (make) myself ganawath (gardens) and parks, and I natai (planted) itz (trees) in them of all kinds of paray (fruit).
I ishah (make) myself barakawath (pools) of mayam (Waters), to shaqah (water) from it the yair (forest) where trees were reared.

I bought male ibadayam (servants) and female shapachawath (servants), and had banay (servants) born in my bayath (house). I also rabah (had) great maqanah (possessions) of tzaan (herds) and flocks, above all who were panayam (face) me in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem);

I also kanas (gathered) kasap (silver) and zahab (gold) for myself, and the treasure of malakayam (kings) and of the madayanawath (provinces). I ishah (make) myself male and female singers, and the thainawagath (delights) of the banay (sons) of men—musical shadawath (instruments), and that of all sorts.
So I was gadal (great), and yasap (increased) more panayam (face) all who were before me in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem). My chakamah (wisdom) also imad (remained) with me.

Whatever my iyan (eye) shaal (desired), I didn't atzal (keep) from them. I didn't manai (withhold) my lab (heart) from any shamachah (joy), for my lab (heart) shamach (rejoiced) because of all my imal (labor), and this was my chalaq (portion) from all my imal (labor).

Then I panah (turn) at all the maishah (works) that my yad (hand) ishah (make) worked, and at the imal (labor) that I had imal (labored) to ishah (make); and behold, all was habal (vanity) and a chasing after rawach (spirit / wind), and there was no yatharawan (profit) under the shamash (sun).
I panah (turn) myself to raah (see) chakamah (wisdom), hawalalah (madness), and sakalawath (folly): for what can the malak (king) successor ishah (make)? Just that which has been done long ago.
Then I raah (see) that chakamah (wisdom) excels sakalawath (folly), as far as awar (light) excels chashak (darkness).
The wise chakam (man's) iyan (eye) are in his raash (head), and the kasayal (fool) halak (move) in darkness—and yet I yadai (perceived) that achad (one) maqarah (event) qarah (happens) to them all.

Then I amar (spoke) in my lab (heart), "As it happens to the kasayal (fool), so will it qarah (happen) even to me; and why was I then more chakam (wise)?" Then I dabar (word / matter) in my lab (heart) that this also is habal (vanity).

For of the chakam (wise) im (with), even as of the kasayal (fool), there is no memory for iwalam (forever), since in the yamayam (days) to bawaa (come) shakach (all) will have been long forgotten. Indeed, the chakam (wise) mawath (death) must die just like the kasayal (fool)!
So I shanaa (hate) chay (life), because the maishah (work) that is ishah (make) under the shamash (sun) was rai (grievous) to me; for all is habal (vanity) and a chasing after rawach (spirit / wind).
I shanaa (hate) all my imal (labor) in which I imal (labored) under the shamash (sun), because I must yanach (leave) it to the adam (man) who comes achar (other) me.

Who yadai (knows) whether he will be a chakam (wise) man or a sakal (fool)? Yet he will shalat (have) rule over all of my imal (labor) in which I have imal (labored), and in which I have shown myself chakam (wise) under the shamash (sun). This also is habal (vanity).
Therefore I began to cause my lab (heart) to yaash (despair) concerning all the imal (labor) in which I had imal (labored) under the shamash (sun).

For there is a adam (man) whose imal (labor) is with chakamah (wisdom), with daith (knowledge), and with skillfulness; yet he shall nathan (give) it for his chalaq (portion) to a adam (man) who has not labored for it. This also is habal (vanity) and a rab (great) rai (evil).
For what hawaa (which/who/that is) a adam (man) of all his imal (labor), and of the striving of his lab (heart), in which he imal (labors) under the shamash (sun)?
For all his yawam (day) are makaabayam (sorrows), and his inayan (travail) is kais (grief); yes, even in the layal (night) his lab (heart) takes no shakab (rest). This also is habal (vanity).

There is nothing tawab (good / proper function) for a adam (man) than that he should akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and make his napash (soul) raah (see) tawab (good / proper function) in his imal (labor). Zah (this / that / these) also I raah (see), that it is from the yad (hand) of Alahayam.
For who can akal (eat), or who can have enjoyment, more than I?

For to the adam (man) who pleases him, Alahayam gives chakamah (wisdom), daith (knowledge), and shamachah (joy); but to the chataa (sinner) he nathan (give) inayan (travail), to asap (gather) and to kanas (heap) up, that he may nathan (give) to him who pleases Alahayam. This also is habal (vanity) and a chasing after rawach (spirit / wind).
For everything there is a zaman (season), and a zaman (time) for every chapatz (purpose) under shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens):
A ith (time) to be yalad (birth / begot), and a ith (time) to mawath (death); a ith (time) to natai (plant), and a ith (time) to iqar (pluck) up that which is natai (planted);
A ith (time) to harag (kill), and a ith (time) to rapaa (heal); a ith (time) to paratz (break) down, and a ith (time) to banah (build) up;
A ith (time) to bakah (weep), and a ith (time) to shachaq (laugh); a ith (time) to sapad (mourn), and a ith (time) to raqad (dance);

A ith (time) to shalak (cast) away abanayam (stones), and a ith (time) to kanas (gather) abanayam (stones) together; a ith (time) to chabaq (embrace), and a ith (time) to rachaq (refrain) from chabaq (embracing);
A ith (time) to baqash (seek), and a ith (time) to abad (destroy / perish); a ith (time) to shamar (keep/guard), and a ith (time) to shalak (cast) away;
A ith (time) to qarai (tear), and a ith (time) to thapar (sew); a ith (time) to chashah (keep) silence, and a ith (time) to dabar (word / matter);
A ith (time) to ahab (love), and a ith (time) to shanaa (hate); a ith (time) for malachamah (war), and a ith (time) for shalawam (peace / safety).
What yatharawan (profit) has he who ishah (make) in that in which he imal (labors)?
I raah (see) seen the burden which Alahayam nathan (give) given to the banay (sons) of adam (men) to be inah (oppress / afflict) with.

He ishah (make) made everything yapah (beautiful) in its ith (time). He nathan (give) also set eternity in their lab (heart), yet so that adam (man) can't matzaa (find) out the maishah (work) that Alahayam has done from the raash (head) even to the sawap (end).
I yadai (know) that there is nothing tawab (good / proper function) for them than to shamach (rejoice), and to ishah (make) tawab (good / proper function) as long as they chay (life).
Also that every adam (man) should akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and raah (see) tawab (good / proper function) in all his imal (labor), is the mathath (gift) of Alahayam.

I yadai (know) that whatever Alahayam ishah (make), it shall be iwalam (forever). Ayan (NO ONE) can be yasap (added) to it, nor anything taken from it; and Alahayam ishah (make) done it, that men should yaraa (fear / be afraid) panayam (face) him.
That which is has been long ago, and that which is to be has been long ago: and Alahayam baqash (seeks) again that which is passed away.

Moreover I raah (see) under the shamash (sun), in the maqawam (place) of mashapat (justice), that rashai (wickedness) was there; and in the maqawam (place) of tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), that rashai (wickedness) was there.

I amar (spoke) in my lab (heart), "Alahayam will shapat (judge / judgement) the tzadayaq (righteous) and the rashai (wicked); for there is a ith (time) there for every chapatz (purpose) and for every maishah (work)."
I amar (spoke) in my lab (heart), "As for the banay (sons) of adam (men), Alahayam tests them, so that they may raah (see) that they themselves are like animals.

For that which happens to the banay (sons) of adam (men) happens to animals. Even achad (one) thing happens to them. As the one mawath (death), so the other mawath (death). Yes, they have all achad (one) rawach (spirit / wind); and adam (man) has no advantage over the animals: for all is habal (vanity).
All halak (move) to achad (one) maqawam (place). All are from the ipar (dust), and all shawab (turn back / repent) to ipar (dust) again.

Who yadai (knows) the rawach (spirit / wind) of ban (son), whether it ilah (go up / offer) upward, and the rawach (spirit / wind) of the animal, whether it yarad (goes) matah (downward) to the aratz (Earth/land)?"

Therefore I raah (see) that there is nothing tawab (good / proper function), than that a adam (man) should shamach (rejoice) in his maishah (works); for that is his chalaq (portion): for who can bawaa (come) him to raah (see) what will be achar (other) him?

Then I shawab (turn back / repent) and raah (see) all the ishaqayam (oppressions) that are ishah (make) under the shamash (sun): and behold, the damaih (tears) of those who were ishaq (oppressed), and they had no comforter; and on the yad (hand) of their oppressors there was kach (strength / mighty / power); but they had no comforter.
Therefore I shabach (praised) the mawath (death) who have been long mawath (death) more than the chay (life) who are yet chay (life).
Yes, tawab (good / proper function) than them shanayam (two) is him who has not yet been, who raah (see) not seen the rai (evil) maishah (work) that is ishah (make) under the shamash (sun).
Then I raah (see) all the imal (labor) and achievement that is the qanaah (envy) of a ayash (man / husband) neighbor. This also is habal (vanity) and a striving after rawach (spirit / wind).
The kasayal (fool) chabaq (folds) his yad (hand) together and ruins himself.
Tawab (good / proper function) is a kap (handful), with nachath (quietness), than chapan (two) handfuls with imal (labor) and chasing after rawach (spirit / wind).
Then I shawab (turn back / repent) and raah (see) habal (vanity) under the shamash (sun).

There is achad (one) who is shanay (second), and he has neither ban (son) nor ach (brother/kinsman). There is no qatz (end) to all of his imal (labor), neither are his iyan (eye) shabai (satisfied) with wealth. "For whom then, do I imal (labor), and deprive my napash (soul) of enjoyment?" This also is habal (vanity). Yes, it is a miserable inayan (business).
Shanayam (two) are tawab (good / proper function) than achad (one), because they yash (have) a tawab (good / proper function) shakar (reward) for their imal (labor).

For if they napal (fall / be cast down), the achad (one) will qawam (rise up) up his chabar (fellow); but ay (woe) to him who is achad (one) when he yapalaw (falls), and doesn't have shanay (second) to qawam (rise up) him up.
Again, if shanayam (two) shakab (lie) together, then they have warmth; but how can achad (one) keep yacham (warm) alone?
If a achad (one) thaqap (prevails) against one who is alone, shanayam (two) shall withstand him; and a threefold chawat (cord) is not maharah (quickly) nathaq (broken).
Tawab (good / proper function) is a masakan (poor) and chakam (wise) youth than an zaqan (old) and kasayal (foolish) malak (king) who doesn't yadai (know) how to receive admonition any more.
For out of asar (prison) he yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to be malak (king); yes, even in his malakawath (kingdom) he was yalad (birth / begot) rawash (poor).
I raah (see) all the chay (life) who halak (move) under the shamash (sun), that they were with the youth, the other, who succeeded him.

There was no qatz (end) of all the im (nation / people), even of all them over whom he was—yet those who acharawan (come) after shall not shamach (rejoice) in him. Surely this also is habal (vanity) and a chasing after rawach (spirit / wind).

Guard your steps when you yatzaa (go out / come out) to Alahayam house; for to draw near to listen is better than to give the sacrifice of fools, for they don't know that they dabar (word / matter) evil.
Don't be rash with your mouth, and don't let your heart be hasty to utter anything before Alahayam; for Alahayam is in heaven, and you on earth. Therefore let your dabarayam (words) be few.
For as a dream comes with a multitude of cares, so a kasayalayam (fools) speech with a multitude of words.
When you nadar (make vow) a nadar (make vow) to Alahayam, don't defer to shalam (pay) it; for he has no tawab (good / proper function) in fools. Shalam (pay) that which you nadar (make vow).
It is better that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not nathan (give).

Don't allow your mouth to lead you into sin. Don't protest before the messenger that this was a mistake. Why should Alahayam be angry at your voice, and destroy the dabar (word / matter) of your hands?
For in the multitude of dreams there are vanities, as well as in many words: but you must fear Alahayam.

If you see the oppression of the poor, and the violent taking away of justice and righteousness in a district, don't marvel at the matter: for one official is eyed by a higher one; and there are officials over them.
Moreover the profit of the earth is for all. The king profits from the field.
He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he who loves rabah (abundance), with rabah (increase): this also is vanity.
When goods rabah (increase), those who akal (eat) them are rabah (increased); and what advantage is there to its owner, am (mother) to feast on them with his eyes?
The sleep of a laboring rai (man) is sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the abundance of the ishar (wealth / riches) will not allow him to sleep.
There is a rai (grievous) rai (evil) which I abad (destroy / perish) seen under the sun: wealth kept by its owner to his rai (harm).
Those riches perish by misfortune, and if he has fathered a son, there is maawamah (nothing) in his yad (hand).
As he bawaa (come) forth from his mother's womb, naked shall he yalak (go) again as he bawaa (come), and shall bawaa (come) kal (every) for his labor, which he may yalak (carry) away in his hand.
This also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go. And what profit does he have who labors for the wind?
All his yamay (days) he also akal (eat) in darkness, he is frustrated, and has sickness and wrath.

Behold, that which I have seen to be good and proper is for one to akal (eat) and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his imal (labor), in which he imal (labors) under the sun, gam (indeed / moreover) the days of his life which Alahayam nathan (give) given him; for this is his chalaq (portion).

Every man also to whom Alahayam rabah (has) given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat of it, and to rabah (take) his portion, and to shamachah (rejoice) in his labor — this is the gift of Alahayam.
For he shall not often reflect on the yawam (day) of his chay (life); because Alahayam occupies him with the shamachah (joy) of his lab (heart).
There is an rai (evil) which I raah (see) seen under the shamash (sun), and it is heavy on adam (men):

A ayash (man / husband) to whom Alahayam nathan (give) riches, wealth, and honor, so that he chasar (lacks) nothing for his napash (soul) of all that he awah (desires), yet Alahayam gives him no shalat (power) to akal (eat) of it, but an alien akal (eat) it. This is habal (vanity), and it is an rai (evil) chalay (disease).

If a ayash (man / husband) yalad (birth / begot) a maah (hundred) children, and chayah (lives) many shanayam (years), so that the yamay (days) of his shanayam (years) are many, but his napash (soul) is not shabai (filled) with tawab (good / proper function), and moreover he has no qabawarah (burial); I amar (spoke), that a stillborn child is tawab (good / proper function) than he:
For it bawaa (come) in habal (vanity), and departs in chashak (darkness), and its sham (name) is kasah (covered) with chashak (darkness).
Moreover it raah (see) not seen the shamash (sun) nor yadai (known) it. Zah (this / that / these) has nachath (rest) rather zah (this / that / these) the other.

Yes, alaw (though) he chayah (live) a alap (thousand) shanayam (years) paim (twice) told, and yet fails to raah (see) tawab (good / proper function), don't all halak (move) to achad (one) maqawam (place)?
All the imal (labor) of adam (man) is for his pah (mouth), and yet the napash (soul) is not malaa (filled).
For what advantage has the chakam (wise) more than the kasayal (fool)? What has the inay (poor) yadai (man), that knows how to halak (move) before the chay (life)?
Tawab (good / proper function) is the maraah (sight) of the iyanayam (eyes) than the halak (move) of the napash (soul). This also is habal (vanity) and a chasing after rawach (spirit / wind).
Whatever has been, its qaraa (called) was given long ago; and it is yadai (known) what adam (man) is; neither yakal (can) he contend with him who is mightier than he.
For there are many dabarayam (words) that rabah (create) habal (vanity). What does that yawathar (profit) adam (man)?

For who yadai (knows) what is tawab (good / proper function) for adam (man) in chay (life), masapar (all) the yamay (days) of his habal (vain) chay (life) which he ishah (make) like a tzal (shadow)? For who can nagad (tell) a adam (man) what will be achar (other) him under the shamash (sun)?
A good sham (name) is tawab (good / proper function) than tawab (good / proper function) perfume; and the yawam (day) of mawath (death) better than the yawam (day) of one's yalad (birth / begot).

It is tawab (good / proper function) to yalak (go) to the bayath (house) of abal (mourning) than to yalak (go) to the bayath (house) of mashathah (feasting): for that is the sawap (end) of all adam (men), and the chay (life) should nathan (give) this to lab (heart).
Kais (sorrow) is tawab (good / proper function) than shachawaq (laughter/joking matter); for by the rai (sadness) of the panayam (face) the lab (heart) is made yatab (good).
The lab (heart) of the chakam (wise) is in the bayath (house) of abal (mourning); but the lab (heart) of kasayalayam (fools) is in the bayath (house) of shamachah (mirth).

It is tawab (good / proper function) to shamai (hearken / hear) the gairah (rebuke) of the chakam (wise), than for a ayash (man / husband) to shamai (hearken / hear) the shayar (song) of kasayalayam (fools).
For as the qawal (sound / voice) of sayarayam (thorns) under a sayar (pot), so is the shachawaq (laughter/joking matter) of the kasayal (fool). This also is habal (vanity).
Surely ishaq (extortion) makes the wise chakam (man) foolish; and a bribe abad (destroy / perish) the lab (heart).

Tawab (good / proper function) is the acharayath (end) of a thing than its raashayath (beginning). The arak (patient) in rawach (spirit / wind) is tawab (good / proper function) than the gabah (proud) in rawach (spirit / wind).
Don't be hasty in your rawach (spirit / wind) to be kais (angry), for kais (anger) nawach (rests) in the chayaq (bosom) of kasayalayam (fools).
Don't amar (spoke), "Why were the raashawan (former) yamayam (days) tawab (good / proper function) than these?" For you do not shaal (ask) chakamah (wisely) about this.
Chakamah (wisdom) is as tawab (good / proper function) as an nachalah (inheritance). Yes, it is more excellent for those who raah (see) the shamash (sun).

For chakamah (wisdom) is a defense, even as kasap (money) is a defense; but the yatharawan (excellency) of daith (knowledge) is that chakamah (wisdom) preserves the chayah (life) of him who bail (has) it.
Raah (see) the maishah (work) of Alahayam, for who yakal (can) make that thaqan (straight), which he has made iwath (crooked)?

In the yawam (day) of tawab (good / proper function) be tawab (good / proper function), and in the yawam (day) of rai (adversity) raah (see); yes, Alahayam ishah (make) made the imah (one) side by side with the other, to the dabarah (end) that adam (man) should not matzaa (find) out anything achar (other) him.

All this raah (see) I seen in my yamay (days) of habal (vanity): there is a tzadayaq (righteous) abad (destroy / perish) who perishes in his tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and there is a rashai (wicked) man who arak (lives) long in his evildoing.
Don't be overly tzadayaq (righteous), neither make yourself overly chakam (wise). Why should you shamam (destroy) yourself?
Don't be too rashai (wicked), neither be sakal (foolish). Why should you mawath (death) before your ith (time)?

It is tawab (good / proper function) that you should achaz (take) hold of zah (this / that / these). Yes, also from that don't yanach (withdraw) your yad (hand); for he who yaraa (fears) Alahayam will yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from them all.
Chakamah (wisdom) is a izaz (strength) to the chakam (wise) man more than ishar (ten) shalayatayam (rulers) who are in a iyar (city).
Surely there is not a tzadayaq (righteous) adam (man) on aratz (Earth/land), who ishah (make) tawab (good / proper function) and doesn't chataa (sin).
Also don't nathan (give) lab (heart) to all dabarayam (words) that are dabar (word / matter), lest you shamai (hearken / hear) your ibad (servant) qalal (curse) you;
For often your own lab (heart) yadai (knows) that you yourself have likewise qalal (cursed) others.
All zah (this / that / these) have I nasah (proved) in chakamah (wisdom). I amar (spoke), "I will be chakam (wise);" but it was rachawaq (far) from me.
That which is, is rachawaq (far) off and exceedingly imaq (deep). Who can matzaa (find) it out?

I sabab (turned) around, and my lab (heart) sought to yadai (know) and to thawar (search) out, and to seek chakamah (wisdom) and the scheme of things, and to yadai (know) that rashai (wickedness) is stupidity, and that sakalawath (foolishness) is hawalalah (madness).

I matzaa (find) more mar (bitter) than mawath (death) the ayashah (woman / wife) whose lab (heart) is matzawadayam (snares) and traps, whose yad (hand) are chains. Whoever pleases Alahayam shall malat (escape) from her; but the chataa (sinner) will be ensnared by her.
"Raah (see), I matzaa (have) found this," amar (spoke) the qahalath (preacher), "achad (one) to another, to matzaa (find) out the scheme;

Which my napash (soul) still baqash (seeks); but I matzaa (have) not found. Achad (one) adam (man) among a alap (thousand) matzaa (have) I found; but I matzaa (have) not found a ayashah (woman / wife) among all those.
Raah (see), this only matzaa (have) I found: that Alahayam ishah (make) adam (man) yashar (upright); but they search for many schemes."

Who is like the chakam (wise) yadai (man)? And who knows the pashar (interpretation) of a thing? A adam (man's) chakamah (wisdom) makes his panayam (face) awar (light), and the hardness of his panayam (face) is shanaa (hate).
I say, "shamar (keep/guard) the malak (king) command!" Because of the shabawaih (oath) to Alahayam.
Don't be hasty to yalak (go) out of his panayam (face). Don't persist in an rai (evil) thing, for he ishah (make) whatever pleases him,
For the malak (king) dabar (word / matter) is supreme. Who can amar (spoke) to him, "What are you ishah (make)?"
Whoever shamar (keep/guard) the matzawah (commandment) shall not yadai (come) to rai (harm), and his wise lab (heart) yadai (will) know the ith (time) and procedure.
For there is a ith (time) and procedure for every chapatz (purpose), although the rai (misery) of adam (man) is heavy on him.
For he doesn't yadai (know) that which will be; for who can nagad (tell) him how it will be?

There is no adam (man) who has shalayat (power) over the rawach (spirit / wind) to contain the rawach (spirit / wind); neither does he have shalatawan (power) over the yawam (day) of mawath (death). There is no mashalachath (discharge) in malachamah (war); neither shall rashai (wickedness) malat (deliver) bail (those) who practice it.

All this raah (see) I seen, and nathan (give) my lab (heart) to every maishah (work) that is ishah (make) under the shamash (sun). There is a ith (time) in which one adam (man) has shalat (power) over another to his rai (hurt).

So I raah (see) the rashai (wicked) qabar (bury). Bawaa (come) they came also from maqawam (place). They bawaa (come) and were shakach (forgotten) in the iyar (city) where they ishah (make) this. This also is habal (vanity).

Because pathagam (sentence) against an rai (evil) maishah (work) is not ishah (make) maharah (speedily), therefore the lab (heart) of the banay (sons) of adam (men) is fully malaa (set) in them to ishah (make) rai (evil).

Though a chataa (sinner) ishah (make) crimes a maah (hundred) times, and arak (lives) long, yet surely I yadai (know) that it will be tawab (good / proper function) with those who yaraa (fear / be afraid) Alahayam, who are reverent panayam (face) him.
But it shall not be tawab (good / proper function) with the rashai (wicked), neither shall he arak (lengthen) yamayam (days) like a tzal (shadow); panayam (face) he doesn't yaraa (fear) Alahayam.

There is a habal (vanity) which is ishah (make) on the aratz (Earth/land), that there are tzadayaq (righteous) men to whom it nagai (happens) according to the maishah (work) of the rashai (wicked). Again, there are rashai (wicked) men to whom it nagai (happens) according to the maishah (work) of the tzadayaq (righteous). I amar (spoke) that this also is habal (vanity).

Then I shabach (commended) shamachah (mirth), because a adam (man) has no tawab (good / proper function) thing under the shamash (sun), than to akal (eat), and to shathah (drinks), and to be shamach (joyful): for that will accompany him in his imal (labor) all the yamay (days) of his chay (life) which Alahayam nathan (give) given him under the shamash (sun).

When I nathan (give) my lab (heart) to yadai (know) chakamah (wisdom), and to raah (see) the inayan (business) that is ishah (make) on the aratz (Earth/land) (for also there is that neither yawam (day) nor layal (night) raah (see) shanah (sleep) with his iyan (eye)),

Then I raah (see) all the maishah (work) of Alahayam, that adam (man) can't matzaa (find) out the maishah (work) that is ishah (make) under the shamash (sun), ashar (who/that) however much a adam (man) imal (labors) to baqash (seek) it out, yet he won't matzaa (find) it. Yes even though a chakam (wise) man amar (spoke) he yadai (can) comprehend it, he won't be yakal (able) to matzaa (find) it.

For all this I nathan (give) to my lab (heart), even to explore all this: that the tzadayaq (righteous), and the chakam (wise), and their ibad (servant), are in the yad (hand) of Alahayam; whether it is ahabah (love) or hatred, adam (man) doesn't yadai (know) it; all is panayam (face) them.

All things come achad (one) to all. There is one maqarah (event) to the tzadayaq (righteous) and to the rashai (wicked); to the tawab (good / proper function), to the tahawar (clean), to the tamaa (unclean), to him who zabach (sacrifices), and to him who doesn't zabach (sacrifice). As is the tawab (good / proper function), so is the chataa (sinner); he who shabai (swear / take oath) an oath, as he who yaraa (fear / be afraid) an shabawaih (oath).

This is an rai (evil) in all that is ishah (make) under the shamash (sun), that there is achad (one) maqarah (event) to all: yes also, the lab (heart) of the banay (sons) of adam (men) is malaa (full) of rai (evil), and hawalalah (madness) is in their labab (heart) while they chay (life), and achar (other) that they go to the mawath (death).
For to him who is bachar (joined) with all the chay (life) there is batachawan (hope); for a chay (life) kalab (dog) is tawab (good / proper function) than a mawath (death) aray (lion).

For the chay (life) yadai (know) that they will mawath (death), but the mawath (death) don't yadai (know) anything, neither do they have any more a shakar (reward); for their zakar (remember) is shakach (forgotten).

Also their ahabah (love), their hatred, and their qanaah (envy) abad (destroy / perish) perished long ago; neither have they any more a chalaq (portion) iwalam (forever) in anything that is ishah (make) under the shamash (sun).

Go your yalak (way) — akal (eat) your lacham (bread) with shamachah (joy), and shathah (drinks) your yayan (wine) with a tawab (good / proper function) lab (heart); for Alahayam has kabar (already) ratzah (accepted) your maishah (works).
Let your bagad (garments) be ith (always) laban (white), and don't let your raash (head) chasar (lack) shaman (oil).

Chay (life) raah (see) with the ayashah (woman / wife) whom you ahab (love) all the yamay (days) of your chay (life) of habal (vanity), which he nathan (give) given you under the shamash (sun), all your yamay (days) of habal (vanity): for that is your chalaq (portion) in chay (life), and in your imal (labor) in which you imal (labor) under the shamash (sun).

Whatever your yad (hand) matzaa (finds) to ishah (make), ishah (make) it with your kach (strength / mighty / power); for there is no maishah (work), nor chashabawan (device), nor daith (knowledge), nor chakamah (wisdom), in shaawal (Sheol / afterlife), where you are halak (move).

I shawab (turn back / repent), and raah (see) under the shamash (sun), that the marawatz (race) is not to the qal (swift), nor the malachamah (battle) to the gabawar (strong), neither yet lacham (bread) to the chakam (wise), nor yet riches to men of bayan (between), nor yet favor to yadaiyam (men) of skill; but ith (time) and pagai (chance) qarah (happen) to them all.

For adam (man) also doesn't yadai (know) his ith (time). As the dag (fish) that are achaz (taken) in an rai (evil) matzawad (net), and as the tzaparayam (birds) that are achaz (caught) in the pach (snare / trap), even so are the banay (sons) of adam (men) yaqash (snared) in an rai (evil) ith (time), when it napal (fall / be cast down) pathaawam (suddenly) on them.
I raah (see) also seen chakamah (wisdom) under the shamash (sun) in zah (this / that / these) way, and it seemed gadawal (very great/important/mighty) to me.

There was a qatan (small / young / least) iyar (city), and mait (few) anashayam (men) within it; and a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) malak (king) bawaa (come) against it, sabab (besieged) it, and banah (build) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) matzawadayam (bulwarks) against it.

Now a masakan (poor) chakam (wise) ayash (man / husband) was matzaa (found) in it, and he by his chakam (wisdom) malat (delivered) the iyar (city); yet no adam (man) zakar (remember) that same masakan (poor) adam (man).

Then I amar (spoke), "chakamah (wisdom) is tawab (good / proper function) than gabawarah (strength)." Nevertheless the masakan (poor) man's chakamah (wisdom) is bazah (despised), and his dabar (word / matter) are not shamai (hearken / hear).
The dabaray (words) of the chakam (wise) shamai (hearken / hear) in nachath (quiet) are better than the zaiq (cry) of him who mashal (rule/have dominion) among kasayalayam (fools).
Chakamah (wisdom) is tawab (good / proper function) than kalay (weapons) of qarab (war); but achad (one) chataa (sinner) abad (destroy / perish) much tawab (good / proper function).
Mawath (death) zabawabay (flies) cause the shaman (oil) of the perfumer to nabai (send) forth an baash (evil) odor; so does a mait (little) sakalawath (folly) outweigh chakamah (wisdom) and honor.
A wise chakam (man's) lab (heart) is at his right yamayan (right hand), but a kasayal (fool's) lab (heart) at his shamaawal (left hand).
Yes also, when the sakal (fool) halak (move) by the darak (way), his lab (heart) chasar (fails) him, and he amar (spoke) to everyone that he is a sakal (fool).

If the rawach (spirit / wind) of the mashal (rule/have dominion) ilah (go up / offer) up against you, don't yanach (leave) your maqawam (place); for gentleness yanach (lays) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) offenses to chataa (rest).
There is an rai (evil) which I raah (see) seen under the shamash (sun), the sort of shagagah (error) which yatzaa (go out / come out) from the shalayat (ruler).
Sakal (folly) is nathan (give) in rab (great) marawam (dignity), and the ishayar (rich) yashab (inhabit/dwell) in a shapal (low) place.
I raah (see) seen ibadayam (servants) on sawasayam (horses), and sharayam (princes) halak (move) like ibadayam (servants) on the aratz (Earth/land).
He who chapar (digs) a gawamatz (pit) may napal (fall / be cast down) into it; and whoever paratz (breaks) through a gadar (wall) may be bitten by a snake.
Whoever carves out abanayam (stones) may be injured by them. Whoever splits itz (wood) may be sakan (endangered) thereby.
If the axe is qahah (blunt), and qalal (one) doesn't sharpen the panayam (face), then he must use more chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor); but skill brings success.
If the snake nashak (bites) before it is lachash (charmed), then is there no yatharawan (profit) for the charmer's lashawan (tongue / language).
The dabaray (words) of a wise chakam (man's) pah (mouth) are chan (favor); but a kasayal (fool) is balai (swallowed) by his own shapathawath (lips).
The thachalah (beginning) of the dabaray (words) of his pah (mouth) is sakalawath (foolishness); and the acharayath (end) of his pah (talk) is rai (mischievous) hawalalawath (madness).
A sakal (fool) also rabah (multiplies) dabarayam (words). Adam (man) doesn't yadai (know) what will be; and that which will be achar (other) him, who can nagad (tell) him?
The imal (labor) of kasayalayam (fools) yagai (wearies) every one of them; for he doesn't yadai (know) how to yalak (go) to the iyar (city).
Ay (woe) to you, aratz (Earth/land), when your malak (king) is a nair (child), and your shar (prince / ruler) akal (eat) in the baqar (morning)!

Ashar (who/that) are you, aratz (Earth/land), when your malak (king) is the ban (son) of chawarayam (nobles), and your shar (prince / ruler) akal (eat) in due ith (season), for gabawarah (strength), and not for shathay (drunkenness)!
By itzalah (slothfulness) the roof sinks in; and through shapalawath (idleness) of the yadayam (hands) the bayath (house) leaks.
A feast is ishah (make) for shachawaq (laughter/joking matter), and yayan (wine) shamach (makes) the life glad; and kasap (money) is the inah (answer / respond) for all things.

Don't qalal (curse) the malak (king), no, not in your madai (thoughts); and don't qalal (curse) the ishayar (rich) in your bedroom: for a iwap (flying) of the sky may yalak (carry) your qawal (sound / voice), and that which bail (has) kanapayam (wings) may nagad (tell) the dabar (word / matter).
Shalach (send) your lacham (bread) on the mayam (Waters); for you shall matzaa (find) it after many yamayam (days).
Nathan (give) a chalaq (portion) to shabai (seven), yes, even to shamanah (eight); for you don't yadai (know) what rai (evil) will be on the aratz (Earth/land).

If the ibayam (clouds) are malaa (full) of gasham (rain), they rawaq (empty) themselves on the aratz (Earth/land); and if a itz (tree) napal (fall / be cast down) toward the darawam (south), or toward the tzapawan (north), in the maqawam (place) where the itz (tree) napal (fall / be cast down), there shall it be.
He who shamar (keep/guard) the rawach (spirit / wind) won't zarai (sow); and he who raah (see) the ibayam (clouds) won't qatzar (reap).

As you don't yadai (know) what is the darak (way) of the rawach (spirit / wind), nor how the itzamayam (bones) grow in the batan (womb) of her who is with malaa (child); even so you don't yadai (know) the maishah (work) of Alahayam who ishah (make) all.

In the baqar (morning) zarai (sow) your zarai (seed), and in the irab (evening) don't yanach (withhold) your yad (hand); for you don't yadai (know) which will kashar (prosper), whether this or that, or whether they shanayam (two) will be equally tawab (good / proper function).
