Truly the awar (light) is mathawaq (sweet), and a tawab (good / proper function) thing it is for the iyanayam (eyes) to raah (see) the shamash (sun).

Yes, if a adam (man) chayah (lives) many shanayam (years), let him shamach (rejoice) in them all; but let him zakar (remember) the yamay (days) of chashak (darkness), for they shall be many. All that bawaa (come) is habal (vanity).

Shamach (rejoice), bachawar (young) man, in your yaladawath (youth), and let your lab (heart) shamach (cheer) you in the yamay (days) of your bacharawath (youth), and halak (move) in the darakay (ways) of your lab (heart), and in the maraah (sight) of your maraay (eyes); but yadai (know) that for all these things Alahayam will bawaa (come) you into mashapat (judgment).
Therefore sawar (remove) kais (sorrow) from your lab (heart), and ibar (pass over/through) away rai (evil) from your bashar (flesh); for shacharawath (youth) and the dawn of life are habal (vanity).

Zakar (remember) also your Creator in the yamay (days) of your bacharawath (youth), before the rai (evil) yamay (days) bawaa (come), and the shanayam (years) nagai (draw) near, when you will amar (spoke), "I have no chapatz (pleasure) in them;"
Before the shamash (sun), the awar (light), the yarach (moon), and the kawakabayam (stars) are chashak (darkness), and the ibayam (clouds) shawab (turn back / repent) achar (other) the gasham (rain);

In the yawam (day) when the keepers of the bayath (house) shall zawai (tremble), and the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) anashay (men) shall iwath (bow) themselves, and the tachanawath (grinders) batal (cease) because they are mait (few), and those who raah (see) out of the arabawath (windows) are chashak (darkness),

And the dalathayam (doors) shall be sagar (shut) in the shawaq (street); when the qawal (sound / voice) of the tachanah (grinding) is shapal (low), and one shall qawam (rise up) up at the qawal (sound / voice) of a tzapawar (bird), and all the banawath (daughters) of music shall be shachach (brought) low;

Yes, they shall be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of gabah (heights), and terrors will be in the darak (way); and the shaqad (almond) tree shall blossom, and the grasshopper shall be a sabal (burden), and abayawanah (desire) shall parar (fail); because adam (man) halak (move) to his iwalam (forever) bayath (house), and the sapadayam (mourners) sabab (go) about the shawaq (streets):

Laa (NOT) the kasap (silver) chabal (cord) is severed, or the zahab (gold) galah (spring / basin / bowl) is ratzatz (broken), or the kad (pitcher) is shabar (broken) at the mabawai (spring), or the galagal (wheel) ratzatz (broken) at the bawar (cistern),
And the ipar (dust) shawab (turn back / repent) to the aratz (Earth/land) as it was, and the rawach (spirit / wind) shawab (turn back / repent) to Alahayam who nathan (give) it.
"Habal (vanity) of habalayam (vanities)," amar (spoke) the qahalath (preacher). "All is habal (vanity)!"

Further, because the qahalath (preacher) was chakam (wise), he still lamad (teach / instruct) the im (nation / people) daith (knowledge). Yes, he pondered, chaqar (sought) out, and thaqan (set) in order many mashalayam (proverbs).
The qahalath (preacher) baqash (sought) to matzaa (find) out chapatz (acceptable) dabaray (words), and that which was kathab (write) blamelessly, dabaray (words) of amath (truth).

The dabaray (words) of the chakam (wise) are like darabanawath (goads); and like mashamarawath (nails) well natai (fastened) are words from the bailay (masters) of asapawath (assemblies), which are nathan (give) from achad (one) raih (shepherd).
Furthermore, my ban (son), be zahar (warn): of ishah (make) many saparayam (books) there is no qatz (end); and much lahag (study) is a yagaih (weariness) of the bashar (flesh).

This is the sawap (end) of the dabar (word / matter). All has been shamai (hearken / hear). Yaraa (fear / be afraid) Alahayam, and shamar (keep/guard) his matzawah (commandments); for this is the whole duty of adam (man).
For Alahayam will bawaa (come) every maishah (work) into mashapat (judgment), with every ilam (hidden) thing, whether it is tawab (good / proper function), or whether it is rai (evil).
The shayar (song) of shayarayam (songs), which is Shalamah (Solomon's). Beloved
Let him nashaq (kiss) me with the kisses of his pah (mouth); for your dawad (love) is tawab (good / proper function) than yayan (wine).
Your shaman (oils) have a pleasing fragrance. Your sham (name) is shaman (oil) rawaq (poured) forth, therefore the ilamawath (virgins) ahab (love) you.

Take me achar (other) with you. Let us hurry. The malak (king) bawaa (come) brought me into his rooms. Friends We will be gayal (glad) and shamach (rejoice) in you. We will zakar (remember) your dawad (love) more than yayan (wine)! Beloved They are mayashar (right) to ahab (love) you.
I am dark, but lovely, you banawath (daughters) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), like Qadar (Kedar's) ahalay (tents), like Shalamah (Solomon's) yarayaiwath (curtains).

Don't raah (see) at me because I am dark, because the shamash (sun) has scorched me. My am (mother) banay (sons) were charar (angry) with me. They shawam (place / establish / appoint) me natar (keeper) of the karamayam (vineyards). I haven't natar (kept) my own karam (vineyard).

Nagad (tell) me, you whom my napash (soul) ahab (love), where you graze your flock, where you rabatz (rest) them at tzahar (noon); For why should I be as one who is veiled beside the idaray (flocks) of your chabar (companions)? Lover
If you don't yadai (know), most yapah (beautiful) among nashayam (women), follow the tracks of the tzaan (sheep). Graze your young goats beside the raiyam (shepherds)' mashakanawath (tents).
I have damah (compared) you, my raiyah (love), to a steed in Paraih (Pharaoh's) rakabay (chariots).
Your lachay (cheeks) are naah (beautiful) with earrings, your tzawaar (neck) with strings of jewels.
We will ishah (make) you earrings of zahab (gold), with naqadawath (studs) of kasap (silver). Beloved
While the malak (king) sat at his masab (table), my perfume spread its fragrance.
My dawad (beloved) is to me a sachet of mar (myrrh), that lawan (lies) between my shad (breasts).
My dawad (beloved) is to me a ashakawal (cluster) of henna blossoms from the karamay (vineyards) of Iyan-Gaday (En Gedi). Lover
Behold, you are yapah (beautiful), my raiyah (love). Behold, you are yapah (beautiful). Your iyan (eye) are yawanayam (doves). Beloved
Behold, you are yapah (beautiful), my dawad (beloved), yes, naiyam (pleasant); and our irash (couch) is verdant. Lover
The qarawath (beams) of our bayath (house) are arazayam (cedars). Our rachayat (rafters) are barawathayam (firs).
I am a chabatzalath (rose) of Sharawan (Sharon), a shawashan (lily) of the imaqayam (valleys). Lover
As a shawashan (lily) among chawachayam (thorns), so is my raiyah (love) among the banawath (daughters). Beloved

As the thapawach (apple) tree among the itzay (trees) of the yair (wood), so is my dawad (beloved) among the banayam (sons). I yashab (inhabit/dwell) down under his tzal (shadow) with great chamad (delight), his paray (fruit) was mathawaq (sweet) to my chak (taste).
He bawaa (come) me to the banquet hall. His dagal (banner) over me is ahabah (love).
Strengthen me with raisins, refresh me with thapawachayam (apples); For I am faint with ahabah (love).
His left shamaawal (left hand) is under my raash (head). His right yamayan (right hand) chabaq (embraces) me.

I shabai (swear / take oath) you, banawath (daughters) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), by the tzabaawath (roes), or by the ayalawath (hinds) of the shadah (field), that you not iwar (rouse / awaken) up, nor awaken ahabah (love), until it so chapatz (desires).
The qawal (sound / voice) of my dawad (beloved)! Behold, he bawaa (come), dalag (leaping) on the harayam (mountains), qapatz (skipping) on the gabaiwath (hills).

My dawad (beloved) is damah (like) a tzabay (roe) or a ipar (young) ayal (hart). Behold, he imad (stands) achar (other) our kathal (wall)! He shagach (looks) in at the chalanawath (windows). He glances through the charak (lattice).
My dawad (beloved) inah (answer / respond), and amar (spoke) to me, "qawam (rise up) up, my raiyah (love), my yapah (beautiful) one, and yalak (come) away.
For, behold, the sathaw (winter) is past. The gasham (rain) is over and halak (move).

The natzanayam (flowers) raah (see) on the aratz (Earth/land). The ith (time) of the qawal (sound / voice) has nagai (come), and the qawal (sound / voice) of the turtledove is shamai (hearken / hear) in our aratz (Earth/land).

The thaan (fig) tree ripens her pag (green) figs. The gapanayam (vines) are in blossom. They nathan (give) forth their fragrance. Qawam (rise up), my raiyah (love), my yapah (beautiful) one, and yalak (come) away." Lover

My yawanah (dove) in the chagaway (clefts) of the salai (rock), In the sathar (secret / hidden) madaragah (places) of the mountainside, raah (see) me see your maraah (face). Shamai (hearken / hear) me hear your qawal (sound / voice); for your qawal (sound / voice) is irab (evening), and your maraah (face) is lovely.
Achaz (catch) for us the foxes, the qatan (small / young / least) foxes that chabal (spoil) the karamayam (vineyards); for our karamayam (vineyards) are in blossom. Beloved
My dawad (beloved) is mine, and I am his. He browses among the shawashanayam (lilies).

Until the yawam (day) is cool, and the tzalalayam (shadows) nawas (flee) away, sabab (turn), my dawad (beloved), and be damah (like) a tzabay (roe) or a ipar (young) ayal (hart) on the haray (mountains) of bathar (bether).
By layal (night) on my mashakab (bed), I baqash (sought) him whom my napash (soul) ahab (love). I baqash (sought) him, but I didn't matzaa (find) him.

I will qawam (rise up) up now, and sabab (go) about the iyar (city); in the shawaqayam (streets) and in the squares I will baqash (seek) him whom my napash (soul) ahab (love). I baqash (sought) him, but I didn't matzaa (find) him.
The watchmen who sabab (go) about the iyar (city) matzaa (found) me; "raah (see) you seen him whom my napash (soul) ahab (love)?"

I had scarcely ibar (pass over/through) from them, when I matzaa (found) him whom my napash (soul) ahab (love). I achaz (held) him, and would not rapah (let) him go, until I bawaa (come) brought him into my am (mother) bayath (house), into the room of her who harah (conceived) me.

I shabai (swear / take oath) you, banawath (daughters) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), by the tzabaawath (roes), or by the ayalawath (hinds) of the shadah (field), that you not iwar (rouse / awaken) up, nor awaken ahabah (love), until it so chapatz (desires).

Who is this who ilah (go up / offer) up from the madabar (wilderness) like thayamarawath (pillars) of ishan (smoke), perfumed with mar (myrrh) and labawanah (frankincense), with all spices of the rakal (merchant)?
Behold, it is Shalamah (Solomon's) carriage! Shashayam (sixty) gabawar (mighty) men are around it, of the gabawar (mighty) men of Yashar-Al (Israel).

They all achaz (handle) the charab (sword), and are lamad (teach / instruct) in malachamah (war). Every ayash (man / husband) has his charab (sword) on his yarak (thigh), because of pachad (fear / dread) in the layal (night).
Malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon) ishah (make) himself a carriage of the itz (wood) of Labanawan (Lebanon).

He ishah (make) its imawad (pillar) of kasap (silver), its rapayadah (bottom) of zahab (gold), its seat of aragaman (purple), its thawak (midst) being ratzap (paved) with ahabah (love), from the banawath (daughters) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

Yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, you banawath (daughters) of Tzayawan (Zion), and raah (see) malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon), with the itarah (crown) with which his am (mother) has itar (crowned) him, in the yawam (day) of his weddings, in the yawam (day) of the shamachah (gladness) of his lab (heart). Lover

Behold, you are yapah (beautiful), my raiyah (love). Behold, you are yapah (beautiful). Your iyan (eye) are yawanayam (doves) behind your tzamah (veil). Your shair (hair) is as a idar (flock) of izayam (goats), that descend from har (mountain) Galaid (Gilead).

Your shan (teeth) are like a newly qatzab (shorn) idar (flock), which have ilah (go up / offer) up from the rachatzah (washing), where every one of them has mathaayamawath (twins). None is shakawal (bereaved) among them.
Your shapah (lips) are like shanay (second) chawat (thread). Your madabar (mouth) is lovely. Your raqah (temples) are like a palach (piece) of a ramawan (pomegranate) behind your tzamah (veil).

Your tzawaar (neck) is like Dawad (David's) magadal (tower) banah (build) for an armory, whereon a alap (thousand) magan (shield) thalah (hang), all the shalatay (shields) of the gabawar (mighty) men.
Your shanayam (two) shad (breasts) are like shanayam (two) fawns that are thaawamay (twins) of a roe, which raih (feed) among the shawashanayam (lilies).
Until the yawam (day) is cool, and the tzalalayam (shadows) nawas (flee) away, I will yalak (go) to the har (mountain) of mar (myrrh), to the gabaih (hill) of labawanah (frankincense).
You are all yapah (beautiful), my raiyah (love). There is no maawam (spot) in you.

Bawaa (come) with me from Labanawan (Lebanon), my kalah (complete / finish), with me from Labanawan (Lebanon). Shawar (look) from the raash (head) of Amanah (Amana), from the raash (head) of Shanayar (Senir) and Charamawan (Hermon), from the arayawath (lions)' mainawath (dens), from the hararay (mountains) of the namarayam (leopards).

You have ravished my labab (heart), my achawath (sister), my kalah (complete / finish). You have ravished my labab (heart) with achad (one) of your iyan (eye), with achad (one) inaq (chain) of your tzawaar (neck).

How yapah (beautiful) is your dawad (love), my achawath (sister), my kalah (complete / finish)! How much tawab (good / proper function) is your dawad (love) than yayan (wine)! The fragrance of your perfumes than all kinds of bashamayam (spices)!

Your shapah (lips), my kalah (complete / finish), drip like the napath (honeycomb). Dabash (honey) and chalab (milk) are under your lashawan (tongue / language). The rayach (smell) of your shalamah (dress / garment) is like the rayach (smell) of Labanawan (Lebanon).
A nail (locked) up gan (garden) is my achawath (sister), my kalah (complete / finish); a nail (locked) up gal (spring), a chatham (sealed) maiyan (fountain).
Your shoots are an paradas (orchard) of ramawanayam (pomegranates), with magad (precious) paray (fruits): henna with narad (spikenard) plants,

Narad (spikenard) and karakam (saffron), qanah (calamus) and qanamawan (cinnamon), with every kind of labawanah (incense) itz (tree); mar (myrrh) and ahalawath (aloes), with all the best bashamayam (spices),
A maiyan (fountain) of ganayam (gardens), a baar (well) of chay (life) mayam (Waters), nazal (flowing) streams from Labanawan (Lebanon). Beloved

Iwar (rouse / awaken), north tzapawan (wind); and bawaa (come), you thayaman (south)! Pawach (blow) on my gan (garden), that its basham (spices) may nazal (flow) out. Let my dawad (beloved) bawaa (come) into his gan (garden), and taste his magad (precious) paray (fruits).

I bawaa (come) come into my gan (garden), my achawath (sister), my kalah (complete / finish). I have arah (gathered) my mar (myrrh) with my basham (spice); I have akal (eat) my yair (honeycomb) with my honey; I have shathah (drinks) my yayan (wine) with my chalab (milk). Friends akal (eat), raiyam (friends)! Shathah (drinks), yes, shakar (drink) abundantly, dawad (beloved). Beloved

I was yashan (asleep), but my lab (heart) was iwar (rouse / awaken). It is the qawal (sound / voice) of my dawad (beloved) who dapaq (knocks): "pathach (open) to me, my achawath (sister), my raiyah (love), my yawanah (dove), my tham (undefiled); for my raash (head) is malaa (filled) with tal (dew), and my hair with the dampness of the layal (night)."
I have taken off my kathanath (robe). Indeed, must I labash (put) it on? I have rachatz (washed) my ragal (feet / foot). Indeed, must I soil them?
My dawad (beloved) thrust his yad (hand) in man (from) the latch opening. My maih (heart) pounded for him.
I qawam (rise up) up to pathach (open) for my dawad (beloved). My yad (hand) dripped with mar (myrrh), my atzabai (fingers) with liquid mar (myrrh), on the handles of the manaiwal (lock).

I pathach (opened) to my dawad (beloved); but my dawad (beloved) left; and ibar (pass over/through) gone away. My napash (soul) yatzaa (go out / come out) out when he dabar (word / matter). I looked for him, but I didn't matzaa (find) him. I qaraa (called) him, but he didn't inah (answer / respond).
The watchmen who sabab (go) about the iyar (city) matzaa (found) me. They nakah (beat) me. They bruised me. The keepers of the chamawath (walls) took my cloak nashaa (lift) from me.
I shabai (swear / take oath) you, banawath (daughters) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), If you matzaa (find) my dawad (beloved), that you nagad (tell) him that I am faint with ahabah (love). Friends

How is your dawad (beloved) better than another dawad (beloved), you fairest among nashayam (women)? How is your dawad (beloved) better than another dawad (beloved), that you do so shabai (swear / take oath) us? Beloved
My dawad (beloved) is tzach (white) and adam (ruddy). The best among rababah (ten) thousand.
His raash (head) is like the purest paz (gold). His hair is thalathal (bushy), shachar (black) as a irab (evening).
His iyan (eye) are like yawanayam (doves) beside the mayam (Waters) apayaqay (brooks), rachatz (washed) with chalab (milk), mounted like jewels.
His lachay (cheeks) are like a irawagah (bed) of basham (spices) with towers of perfumes. His shapah (lips) are like shawashanayam (lilies), natap (dropping) liquid mar (myrrh).
His yad (hand) are like galayalay (rings) of zahab (gold) malaa (set) with tharashayash (beryl). His body is like shan (ivory) ishath (work) ilap (overlaid) with sapayarayam (sapphires).

His shawaq (legs) are like imawaday (pillars) of shash (six) yasad (set) on adanay (sockets) of paz (fine) gold. His maraah (appearance) is like Labanawan (Lebanon), bachar (excellent) as the arazayam (cedars).
His chak (mouth) is sweetness; yes, he is altogether machamad (lovely). This is my dawad (beloved), and this is my rai (neigbor/another person), banawath (daughters) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).
Where has your dawad (beloved) halak (move), you fairest among nashayam (women)? Where has your dawad (beloved) panah (turn), that we may baqash (seek) him with you? Beloved
My dawad (beloved) has yarad (gone) down to his gan (garden), to the irawagawath (beds) of basham (spices), to raih (feed) in the ganayam (gardens), and to laqat (gather) shawashanayam (lilies).
I am my dawad (beloved's), and my dawad (beloved) is mine. He browses among the shawashanayam (lilies),
You are yapah (beautiful), my raiyah (love), as Tharatzah (Tirzah), lovely as Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), awesome as an army with nadagalawath (banners).
Sabab (turn) away your iyan (eye) from me, for they have rahab (overcome) me. Your shair (hair) is like a idar (flock) of izayam (goats), that lie along the side of Galaid (Gilead).

Your shan (teeth) are like a idar (flock) of rachalayam (ewes), which have ilah (go up / offer) up from the rachatzah (washing); of which every one has mathaayamawath (twins); none is shakawal (bereaved) among them.
Your raqah (temples) are like a palach (piece) of a ramawan (pomegranate) behind your tzamah (veil).
There are shashayam (sixty) malakawath (queens), shamanayam (eighty) payalagashayam (concubines), and ilamawath (virgins) without masapar (number).

My yawanah (dove), my tham (perfect) achad (one), is unique. She is her am (mother) only achad (one). She is the favorite one of her who yalad (birth / begot) her. The banawath (daughters) raah (see) her, and ashar (who/that) her blessed; the malakawath (queens) and the payalagashayam (concubines), and they halal (praise) her.
Who is she who shaqap (looks) forth as the shachar (morning), yapah (beautiful) as the labanah (moon), bar (clear) as the chamah (sun), and awesome as an army with nadagalawath (banners)?

I yarad (went) down into the agawaz (nut) tree grove, to raah (see) the green plants of the nachal (stream / river), to raah (see) whether the gapan (vine) nawatz (budded), and the ramanayam (pomegranates) were in flower.
Without realizing it, my napash (soul) shawam (place / establish / appoint) me with my royal napash (soul) marakabawath (chariots). Friends

Shawab (turn back / repent), shawab (turn back / repent), Shulammite! Shawab (turn back / repent), shawab (turn back / repent), that we may gaze at you. Lover Why do you desire to gaze at the Shulammite, as at the machawalah (dance) of Mahanaim?
How beautiful are your feet in sandals, prince's daughter! Your rounded thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a skillful workman.
Your body is like a round goblet, no mixed wine is wanting. Your waist is like a heap of wheat, set about with lilies.
Your two breasts are like two fawns, that are twins of a roe.
Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are like the pools in Heshbon by the gate of Bathrabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.
Your head on you is like Carmel. The hair of your head like purple. The king is held captive in its tresses.
How beautiful and how pleasant you are, love, for delights!
This, your stature, is like a palm tree, your breasts like its fruit.

I said, "I will climb up into the thamar (palm) tree. I will take hold of its fruit." Let your shad (breasts) be like ashakalawath (clusters) of the vine, the smell of your breath like apples, Beloved
Your mouth like the best wine, that ilah (go up / offer) down smoothly for my beloved, gliding through the lips of those who are asleep.
I am my dawad (beloved's). His desire is toward me.
Come, my dawad (beloved), let us go forth into the field. Let us lodge in the villages.
Let's go early up to the vineyards. Yalak (let's) see whether the vine has budded, its blossom is open, and the pomegranates are in flower. There I will give you my dawad (love).
The mandrakes nathan (give) forth fragrance. At our doors are all kinds of precious fruits, new and old, which I have stored up for you, my dawad (beloved).

Oh that you were like my ach (brother/kinsman), who yanaq (nursed) from the shaday (breasts) of my am (mother)! If I matzaa (found) you outside, I would nashaq (kiss) you; yes, and no one would bawaz (despise) me.

I would nahag (lead) you, bawaa (come) you into my am (mother) bayath (house), who would lamad (teach / instruct) me. I would have you shaqah (drink) raqach (spiced) yayan (wine), of the isayas (juice) of my ramawan (pomegranate).
His left shamaawal (left hand) would be under my raash (head). His right yamayan (right hand) would chabaq (embrace) me.
I shabai (swear / take oath) you, banawath (daughters) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), that you not iwar (rouse / awaken) up, nor awaken ahabah (love), until it so chapatz (desires). Friends

Who is this who ilah (go up / offer) up from the madabar (wilderness), rapaq (leaning) on her dawad (beloved)? Under the thapawach (apple) tree I aroused you. There your am (mother) conceived you. There she was in yalad (birth / begot) and bore you.

Shawam (place / establish / appoint) me as a chawatham (seal) on your lab (heart), as a chawatham (seal) on your zarawai (arm); for ahabah (love) is iz (strong) as mawath (death). Qanaah (jealousy) is as qashah (rough / hard) as shaawal (Sheol / afterlife). Its flashes are flashes of ash (fire), a very flame of Yahawah.

Many mayam (Waters) can't kabah (quench) ahabah (love), neither can naharawath (floods) shatap (drown) it. If a ayash (man / husband) nathan (give) give all the hawan (wealth) of his bayath (house) for ahabah (love), he would be bawaz (utterly) scorned. Friends

We have a qatan (small / young / least) achawath (sister). She has no shadayam (breasts). What shall we ishah (make) for our achawath (sister) in the yawam (day) when she is to be dabar (word / matter) for?
If she is a chawamah (wall), we will banah (build) on her a turret of kasap (silver). If she is a dalath (door), we will enclose her with lawach (boards) of araz (cedar). Beloved
I am a chawamah (wall), and my shad (breasts) like magadalawath (towers), then I was in his iyan (eye) like one who matzaa (found) shalawam (peace / safety).

Shalamah (Solomon) had a karam (vineyard) at Bailahamawan (Baal Hamon). He leased out the karam (vineyard) to natarayam (keepers). Ayash (man / husband) was to bawaa (come) a alap (thousand) shekels of kasap (silver) for its paray (fruit).
My own karam (vineyard) is panayam (face) me. The alap (thousand) are for you, Shalamah (Solomon); two maah (hundred) for those who tend its paray (fruit). Lover
You who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the ganayam (gardens), with friends in attendance, let me qashab (hear) your qawal (sound / voice)! Beloved
Come barach (away), my dawad (beloved)! Be damah (like) a gazelle or a ipar (young) stag on the haray (mountains) of bashamayam (spices)!

The chazawan (vision) of Yashaiyah (Isaiah) the ban (son) of Amawatz (Amoz), which he chazah (saw) concerning Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), in the yamay (days) of Izayah (Uzziah), Yawatham (Jotham), Achaz (Ahaz), and Chazaqayah (Hezekiah), malakay (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah).

Shamai (hearken / hear), shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and listen, aratz (Earth/land); for Yahawah has dabar (word / matter): "I have gadal (nourished) and rawam (will lift up) up banayam (children), and they have pashai (rebelled) against me.
The shawar (ox) yadai (knows) his owner, and the donkey his bail (master's) abawas (crib); but Yashar-Al (Israel) doesn't yadai (know), my im (nation / people) don't bayan (between)."

Haway (Alas/Woe!) Sinful gaway (heathen / nation), a im (nation / people) loaded with iwan (guilt/iniquity), a zarai (seed) of evildoers, zarai (children) who deal corruptly! They have forsaken Yahawah. They have naatz (despised) the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel). They are zawar (estranged) and backward.
Why should you be nakah (beaten) more, that you sarah (revolt) more and more? The whole raash (head) is chalay (sick), and the whole labab (heart) daway (faint).

From the kap (sole) of the ragal (feet / foot) even to the raash (head) there is no matham (soundness) in it: patzai (wounds), welts, and open makah (sores). They haven't been zawar (closed), neither bandaged, neither soothed with shaman (oil).

Your aratz (Earth/land) is shamamah (desolate). Your iyar (cities) are sharap (burned) with ash (fire). Strangers akal (eat) your adamah (land) in your presence, and it is shamamah (desolate), as mahapakah (overthrown) by strangers.
The banath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion) is yathar (left) like a shelter in a karam (vineyard), like a hut in a field of melons, like a natzar (besieged) iyar (city).

Lawalaa (unless) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) had yathar (left) to us a very mait (small) sharayad (remnant), we would hayah (came to pass) been as Sadam (Sodom); we would have been damah (like) Imarah (Gomorrah).

Shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, you qatzayanay (rulers) of Sadam (Sodom)! Listen to the thawarah (instruction) of our Alahayam, you im (nation / people) of Imarah (Gomorrah)!

"Mah (what) are the rab (multitude) of your zabach (sacrifices) to me?," amar (spoke) Yahawah. "I shabai (have) had enough of the burnt ilawath (offerings) of ayalayam (rams), and the chalab (fat) of fed animals. I don't chapatz (delight) in the dam (blood) of parayam (bulls), or of kabashayam (lambs), or of male ithawadayam (goats).
When you bawaa (come) to raah (see) panayam (face) me, who has baqash (required) this at your yad (hand), to ramas (trample) my chatzar (courts)?

Bawaa (come) no more shawaa (vanity) manachah (offerings). Qatarath (incense) is an thawaibah (abomination) to me; new chadash (month), shabath (shabath / rest), and maqaraa (convocations): I can't bear with awan (evil) maqaraa (assemblies).
My napash (soul) shanaa (hate) your New chadash (month) and your mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) feasts. They are a burden to me. I am laah (weary) of nashaa (lift) them.

When you parash (spread) forth your kap (hands), I will ilam (hide) my iyan (eye) from you. Yes, when you rabah (make) many thapalah (prayers), I will not shamai (hearken / hear). Your yad (hand) are malaa (full) of dam (blood).
Rachatz (wash) yourselves, make yourself zakah (clean). Sawar (put) away the rai (evil) of your mailal (doings) from before my iyan (eye). Chadal (cease) to do raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil).

Lamad (teach / instruct) to yatab (do) well. Darash (seek) mashapat (justice). Ashar (who/that) the chamawatz (oppressed). Shapat (judge / judgement) the yathawam (fatherless). Rayab (plead) for the alamanah (widow)."

"Yalak (come) now, and let us yakach (reason) together," amar (spoke) Yahawah: "Though your chataa (sins) be as shanay (second), they shall be as laban (white) as shalag (snow). Though they be adam (red) like thawalai (crimson), they shall be as tzamar (wool).
If you are abah (be willing / desire) and shamai (hearken / hear), you shall akal (eat) the tawab (good / proper function) of the aratz (Earth/land);
But if you maan (refuse) and marah (rebel), you shall be akal (eat) with the charab (sword); for the pah (mouth) of Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) it."

How the aman (believe / have faith) qarayah (city / town) has become a prostitute! She was full of mashapat (justice); tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) lawan (lodged) in her, but now maratzachayam (murderers).
Your kasap (silver) has become sayag (dross), your sabaa (wine) mahal (mixed) with mayam (Waters).

Your shar (prince / ruler) are sarar (rebellious), and chabaray (companions) of thieves. Everyone ahab (love) shachad (bribes), and radap (follows) after shalamanayam (rewards). They don't shapat (judge / judgement) the yathawam (fatherless), neither does the rayab (cause) of the alamanah (widow) bawaa (come) to them.

Therefore the Adawan, Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), the abayar (mighty) One of Yashar-Al (Israel), naam (declares prophetically): "haway (Alas/Woe!), I will get relief from my tzar (oppressor / distressor), and naqam (avenge) myself of my ayab (enemy);
And I will shawab (turn back / repent) my yad (hand) on you, thoroughly tzarap (purge) away your sayag (dross), and will sawar (take) away all your badayal (divide).

I will shawab (turn back / repent) your shapat (judge / judgement) as at the raashawan (first), and your yaitz (counselors) as at the thachalah (beginning). Afterward you shall be qaraa (called) ‘The iyar (city) of tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), a aman (believe / have faith) town.'
Tzayawan (Zion) shall be padah (redeemed) with mashapat (justice), and her shawab (turn back / repent) with tzadaqah (righteousness).
But the shabar (destruction) of transgressors and chataayam (sinners) shall be yachad (together), and those who izab (forsake) Yahawah shall be kalah (complete / finish).
For they shall be bawash (ashamed) of the ayalayam (oaks) which you have chamad (desired), and you shall be chapar (confounded) for the ganawath (gardens) that you have bachar (chosen).
For you shall be as an alah (oak / terebinth) whose ilah (leaf) nabal (fades), and as a ganah (garden) that has no mayam (Waters).
The chasan (strong) will be like tinder, and his pail (work) like a nayatzawatz (spark). They will shanayam (two) bair (burn) yachad (together), and no one will kabah (quench) them."
This is dabar (word / matter) Yashaiyah (Isaiah) the ban (son) of Amawatz (Amoz) chazah (saw) concerning Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

It shall happen in the acharayath (latter) yamayam (days), that the har (mountain) of Yahawah bayath (house) shall be kawan (established) on the raash (head) of the harayam (mountains), and shall be nashaa (lift) above the gabaiwath (hills); and all gawayam (nations) shall nahar (flow) to it.

Many imayam (peoples) shall halak (move) and amar (spoke), "yalak (come), let's ilah (go up / offer) up to the har (mountain) of Yahawah, to the bayath (house) of the Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob); and he will yarah (teach) us of his darak (ways), and we will yalak (walk) in his arach (paths)." For out of Tzayawan (Zion) the thawarah (instruction) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah from Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

He will shapat (judge / judgement) between the gawayam (nations), and will decide concerning many gawayam (peoples); and they shall kathath (beat) their charab (sword) into athayam (plowshares), and their chanayath (spears) into mazamarah (pruning) hooks. Gaway (heathen / nation) shall not nashaa (lift) up charab (sword) against gaway (heathen / nation), neither shall they lamad (teach / instruct) malachamah (war) any more.
Bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob), yalak (come), and yalak (let) us walk in the awar (light) of Yahawah.

For you have forsaken your im (nation / people), the bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob), because they are malaa (filled) from the qadam (east), with those who practice divination like the Palashathay (Philistines), and they clasp hands with the yaladay (children) of nakarayam (foreigners).

Their aratz (Earth/land) is malaa (full) of kasap (silver) and zahab (gold), neither is there any qatzah (end / extremity / border) of their awatzar (treasures). Their aratz (Earth/land) also is malaa (full) of sawasayam (horses), neither is there any qatzah (end / extremity / border) of their marakabah (chariots).
Their aratz (Earth/land) also is malaa (full) of alayalayam (idols). They shachah (worship) the maishah (work) of their own yad (hand), that which their own atzabai (fingers) ishah (make) made.
Adam (man) is shachach (brought) low, and mankind is shapal (humbled); therefore don't nashaa (lift) them.
Bawaa (come) into the tzawar (rock), and taman (hide) in the ipar (dust), from panayam (face) the pachad (fear / dread) of Yahawah, and from the glory of his gaawan (majesty).

The gabahawath (lofty) iyanay (looks) of adam (man) will be shapal (brought) low, the rawam (will lift up) of adam (men) will be shachach (bowed) down, and Yahawah alone will be shagab (exalted) in that yawam (day).
For there will be a yawam (day) of Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) for all that is gaah (proud) and haughty, and for all that is nashaa (lift) up; and it shall be shapal (brought) low:
For all the arazay (cedars) of Labanawan (Lebanon), that are rawam (will lift up) and nashaa (lift) up, for all the alawanay (oaks) of Bashan (Bashan),
For all the rawam (will lift up) harayam (mountains), for all the gabaiwath (hills) that are nashaa (lift) up,
For every gabah (lofty) magadal (tower), for every batzar (fortified) chawamah (wall),
For all the anayawath (ships) of Tharashayash (Tarshish), and for all chamadah (pleasant) imagery.

The gabahawath (loftiness) of adam (man) shall be shachach (bowed) down, and the rawam (will lift up) of adam (men) shall be shapal (brought) low; and Yahawah alone shall be shagab (exalted) in that yawam (day).
The alayalayam (idols) shall kalayal (utterly) chalap (pass) away.

Men shall bawaa (come) into the mairawath (caves) of the tzarayam (rocks), and into the holes of the ipar (earth), from panayam (face) the pachad (fear / dread) of Yahawah, and from the glory of his gaawan (majesty), when he qawam (rise up) to shake the aratz (Earth/land) mightily.

In that yawam (day), adam (men) shall shalak (cast) away their alayalay (idols) of kasap (silver), and their alayalay (idols) of zahab (gold), which ishah (make) been made for themselves to shachah (worship), to the chapar (moles) and to the italapayam (bats);

To bawaa (come) into the caverns of the tzarayam (rocks), and into the naqarawath (clefts) of the ragged salaiyam (rocks), from panayam (face) the pachad (fear / dread) of Yahawah, and from the glory of his gaawan (majesty), when he qawam (rise up) to shake the aratz (Earth/land) mightily.
Stop trusting in adam (man), whose nashamah (breathing thing) is in his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting); for of what chashab (account) is he?

For, behold, the Adawan, Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), sawar (takes) away from Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) and from Yahawadah (Judah) supply and support, the whole supply of lacham (bread), and the kal (every) supply of mayam (Waters);
The gabawar (mighty) man, the ayash (man / husband) of malachamah (war), the shapat (judge / judgement), the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), the diviner, the zaqan (elder),
The shar (prince / ruler) of chamashayam (fifty), the nashaa (lift) panayam (face), the yaitz (counselor), the skilled craftsman, and the clever enchanter.
I will nathan (give) nairayam (boys) to be their shar (prince / ruler), and nairayam (children) shall mashal (rule/have dominion) over them.

The im (nation / people) will be nagash (oppressed), everyone by ayash (man / husband), and everyone by his neighbor. The nair (child) will rahab (behave) himself proudly against the zaqan (old) man, and the qalah (base) against the honorable.

Indeed a ayash (man / husband) shall thapash (take) hold of his ach (brother/kinsman) in the bayath (house) of his ab (father), saying, "You have shamalah (clothing), you be our qatzayan (ruler), and let this makashalah (ruin) be under your yad (hand)."

In that yawam (day) he will cry out, amar (spoke), "I will not be a chabash (healer); for in my bayath (house) is neither lacham (bread) nor shamalah (clothing). You shall not shawam (place / establish / appoint) me qatzayan (ruler) of the im (nation / people)."

For Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) is kashal (stumble / stagger), and Yahawadah (Judah) is napal (fall / be cast down); because their lashawan (tongue / language) and their mailal (doings) are against Yahawah, to marah (provoke) the inay (eyes) of his kabawad (glory).

The look of their panayam (face) inah (answer / respond) against them. They parade their chataah (sin) like Sadam (Sodom). They don't kachad (hide) it. Away (woe) to their napash (soul)! For they have brought disaster upon themselves.
Amar (spoke) the tzadayaq (righteous) "tawab (good / proper function)!" For they shall akal (eat) the paray (fruit) of their deeds.
Away (woe) to the rashai (wicked)! Disaster is upon them; for the deeds of his yad (hand) will be paid back to him.

As for my im (nation / people), ilal (children) are their nagash (oppressors), and nashayam (women) mashal (rule/have dominion) over them. My im (nation / people), those who ashar (who/that) you thaih (cause) you to err, and balai (destroy) the darak (way) of your arach (paths).
Yahawah natzab (stands) up to rayab (contend), and imad (stands) to dayan (judge) the imayam (peoples).

Yahawah will bawaa (come) into mashapat (judgment) with the zaqanay (elders) of his im (nation / people), and their leaders: "It is you who have bair (eaten) up the karam (vineyard). The gazalah (spoil) of the inay (poor) is in your bayath (house).
What do you mean that you dakaa (crush) my im (nation / people), and tachan (grind) the panayam (face) of the inay (poor)?" Naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies).

Moreover Yahawah amar (spoke), "yain (because) the banawath (daughters) of Tzayawan (Zion) are gabah (haughty), and yalak (walk) with natah (outstretched) garawan (necks) and flirting iyanayam (eyes), halak (move) to trip as they yalak (go), jingling ornaments on their ragal (feet / foot);
Therefore the Adanay brings sores on the qadaqad (crown) of the head of the women of Tzayawan (Zion), and Yahawah will make their scalps bald."
In that yawam (day) the Adanay will sawar (take) away the thapaarah (beauty) of their anklets, the headbands, the crescent necklaces,
The earrings, the shayarawath (bracelets), the railawath (veils),
The headdresses, the ankle chains, the sashes, the perfume bottles, the charms,
The signet tabaiwath (rings), the ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) tabaiwath (rings),
The fine robes, the capes, the cloaks, the purses,
The galayawan (hand) mirrors, the sadayan (fine) linen garments, the tiaras, and the shawls.

It shall happen that instead of basham (sweet) spices, there shall be maq (rottenness); instead of a belt, a rope; instead of maishah (well) set maqashah (hair), qarachah (baldness); instead of a robe, a wearing of sackcloth; and branding instead of yapay (beauty).
Your math (men) shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword), and your gabawarah (mighty) in the malachamah (war).
Her pathach (gates) shall anah (lament) and abal (mourn); and she shall be naqah (clean/innocent) and yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the aratz (Earth/land).

Shabai (seven) nashayam (women) shall chazaq (take) hold of achad (one) ayash (man / husband) in that yawam (day), amar (spoke), "We will akal (eat) our own lacham (bread), and labash (wear) our own shamalah (clothing): only let us be qaraa (called) by your sham (name). Asap (take) away our charapah (reproach)."

In that yawam (day), Yahawah tzamach (branch) will be tzabay (beautiful) and kabawad (glorious), and the paray (fruit) of the aratz (Earth/land) will be the beauty and glory of the survivors of Yashar-Al (Israel).

It will happen, that he who is shaar (left) in Tzayawan (Zion), and he who yathar (remains) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), shall be amar (spoke) qadawash (holy), even everyone who is kathab (write) among the chay (life) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem);

When the Adanay shall have rachatz (washed) away the tzawaah (filth) of the banawath (daughters) of Tzayawan (Zion), and shall have dawach (purged) the dam (blood) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) from its qarab (among / near), by the rawach (spirit / wind) of mashapat (justice), and by the rawach (spirit / wind) of bair (burning).

Yahawah will baraa (created) over the whole makawan (habitation) of har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion), and over her maqaraa (assemblies), a inan (cloud) and ishan (smoke) by yawamam (by day), and the nagah (shining) of a lahabah (flaming) ash (fire) by layal (night); for over all the kabawad (glory) will be a canopy.
There will be a sakah (pavilion) for a tzal (shade) in the yawamam (by day) from the charab (heat), and for a machasah (refuge) and for a shelter from zaram (storm) and from matar (rain).
Let me shayar (sing) for my well yadayad (beloved) a shayar (song) of my dawad (beloved) about his karam (vineyard). My yadayad (beloved) had a karam (vineyard) on a very ban (son) qaran (horn).

He dug it up, gathered out its saqal (stones), natai (planted) it with the choicest vine, banah (build) a magadal (tower) in its thawak (midst), and also chatzab (cut) out a yaqab (winepress) therein. He qawah (gather/wait) for it to ishah (make) inabayam (grapes), but it ishah (make) baashayam (wild) grapes.
"Now, yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) and ayash (man / husband) of Yahawadah (Judah), please shapat (judge / judgement) between me and my karam (vineyard).

What could ishah (make) been done more to my karam (vineyard), that I ishah (make) not done in it? Madawai (for what reason?), when I qawah (gather/wait) for it to ishah (make) inabayam (grapes), ishah (make) it yield baashayam (wild) grapes?

Now I yadai (will) tell you what I will ishah (make) to my karam (vineyard). I will sawar (take) away its mashawakah (hedge), and it will be bair (eaten) up. I will paratz (break) down its gadar (wall) of it, and it will be trampled down.

I will shayath (put / appoint / make) it a wasteland. It won't be zamar (pruned) nor hoed, but it will ilah (go up / offer) shamayar (briers) and shayath (thorns). I will also tzawah (command) the ibayam (clouds) that they matar (rain) no matar (rain) on it."

For the karam (vineyard) of Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) is the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and the ayash (man / husband) of Yahawadah (Judah) his pleasant natai (plant): and he qawah (gather/wait) for mashapat (justice), but, behold, mashapach (oppression); for tzadaqah (righteousness), but, behold, a tzaiqah (cry) of distress.

Haway (Alas/Woe!) To those who nagai (join) bayath (house) to bayath (house), who lay shadah (field) to shadah (field), until there is no maqawam (place), and you are yashab (inhabit/dwell) to dwell alone in the qarab (among / near) of the aratz (Earth/land)!

In my azan (ear), Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) says: "laa (NOT) many bathayam (houses) will be shamah (desolate), even gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and tawab (good / proper function), unoccupied.
For ishar (ten) tzamaday (acres) of karam (vineyard) shall ishah (make) achad (one) bath (bath / liquid measure), and a chamar (homer) of zarai (seed) shall ishah (make) an ayapah (ephah)."

Haway (Alas/Woe!) To those who shakam (rise) up early in the baqar (morning), that they may radap (follow) shakar (strong) drink; who achar (other) late into the nashap (night), until yayan (wine) dalaq (inflames) them!

The kanawar (harp), lyre, tambourine, and flute, with yayan (wine), are at their mashathah (feasts); but they don't nabat (respect) the pail (work) of Yahawah, neither raah (see) they considered the operation of his yad (hand).

Therefore my im (nation / people) galah (go) into captivity for lack of daith (knowledge). Their honorable mathay (men) are raib (famished), and their hamawan (multitudes) are parched with tzamaa (thirst).

Therefore shaawal (Sheol / afterlife) has enlarged its desire, and pair (opened) its pah (mouth) without chaq (statute); and their glory, their hamawan (multitude), their shaawan (pomp), and he who rejoices among them, descend into it.
So adam (man) is shachach (brought) low, mankind is shapal (humbled), and the iyanay (eyes) of the arrogant ones are shapal (humbled);
But Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) is gabah (exalted) in mashapat (justice), and Al the qadawash (holy) One is qadash (set apart / make holy) in tzadaqah (righteousness).
Then the kabashayam (lambs) will graze as in their pasture, and garayam (strangers) will akal (eat) the ruins of the rich.
Haway (Alas/Woe!) To those who mashak (draw) iwan (guilt/iniquity) with chabalay (cords) of falsehood, and chataah (sin) as with igalah (cart) ibath (rope);

Who amar (spoke), "Let him mahar (make) speed, let him chawash (hasten) his maishah (work), that we may raah (see) it; and let the itzah (counsel) of the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel) qarab (come close) near and bawaa (come), that we may yadai (know) it!"

Haway (Alas/Woe!) To those who amar (spoke) rai (evil) tawab (good / proper function), and tawab (good / proper function) rai (evil); who shawam (place / establish / appoint) chashak (darkness) for awar (light), and awar (light) for chashak (darkness); who shawam (place / establish / appoint) mar (bitter) for mathawaq (sweet), and mathawaq (sweet) for mar (bitter)!
Haway (Alas/Woe!) To those who are chakam (wise) in their own iyan (eye), and bayan (between) in their own panayam (face)!
Haway (Alas/Woe!) To those who are gabawar (mighty) to shathah (drinks) yayan (wine), and champions at mixing shakar (strong) drink;
Who acquit the rashai (guilty) for a shachad (bribe), but deny tzadaqah (righteousness) for the innocent!

Therefore as the tongue of ash (fire) akal (eat) the qash (stubble), and as the dry grass sinks down in the lashawan (tongue / language), so their sharash (root) shall be as maq (rottenness), and their parach (blossom) shall ilah (go up / offer) up as abaq (dust); because they have maas (rejected) the thawarah (instruction) of Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), and naatz (despised) the amarah (sayings) of the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Therefore Yahawah ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) charah (hot with anger) against his im (nation / people), and he has natah (stretched) out his yad (hand) against them, and has nakah (struck) them. The harayam (mountains) ragaz (tremble), and their nabalah (dead) bodies are as refuse in the qarab (among / near) of the chawatzawath (streets). For all this, his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) is not shawab (turn back / repent) away, but his yad (hand) is still natah (stretched) out.

He will nashaa (lift) up a nas (banner) to the gawayam (nations) from rachawaq (far), and he will whistle for them from the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land). Behold, they will bawaa (come) maharah (speedily) and qal (swiftly).

None shall be iyap (weary) nor kashal (stumble / stagger) among them; none shall nawam (slumber) nor sleep; neither shall the belt of their waist be untied, nor the sharawak (latchet) of their nail (shoes) be nathaq (broken):

Whose chatz (arrows) are shanan (sharp), and all their qashath (bows) bent. Their sawas (horses)' parasawath (hoofs) will be chashab (like) tzar (oppressor / distressor), and their galagal (wheels) like a sawapah (whirlwind).

Their shaagah (roaring) will be like a labayaa (lioness). They will shaag (roar) like young kapayarayam (lions). Yes, they shall naham (roar), and seize their tarap (prey) and palat (carry) it off, and there will be no one to natzal (deliver).

They will naham (roar) against them in that yawam (day) like the nahamah (roaring) of the yam (sea/waters). If one nabat (looks) to the aratz (Earth/land) behold, chashak (darkness) and tzar (oppressor / distressor). The awar (light) is chashak (darkness) in its clouds.

In the shanah (year) that malak (king) Izayah (Uzziah) mawath (death), I raah (see) the Adanay sitting on a kasaa (throne), rawam (will lift up) and nashaa (lift) up; and his shawal (train) malaa (filled) the hayakal (temple).

Mail (top/above) him imad (stood) the seraphim. Achad (one) one had shash (six) kanapayam (wings). With shanayam (two) he kasah (covered) his panayam (face). With shanayam (two) he kasah (covered) his ragal (feet / foot). With shanayam (two) he iwap (flying).

One qaraa (called) to another, and amar (spoke), "qadawash (holy), qadawash (holy), qadawash (holy), is Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies)! The whole aratz (Earth/land) is malaa (full) of his kabawad (glory)!"
The foundations of the sapayam (thresholds) nawai (shook) at the qawal (sound / voice) of him who qaraa (called), and the bayath (house) was malaa (filled) with ishan (smoke).

Then I amar (spoke), "away (woe) is me! For I am damah (undone), because I am a ayash (man / husband) of tamaa (unclean) shapathayam (lips), and I yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the thawak (midst) of a im (nation / people) of tamaa (unclean) shapathayam (lips): for my iyan (eye) raah (see) seen the malak (king), Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies)!"
Then achad (one) of the seraphim iwap (flying) to me, having a ratzapah (live) coal in his yad (hand), which he had laqach (take / seize) with the malaqachayam (tongs) from off the mazabach (altar).

He nagai (touched) my pah (mouth) with it, and amar (spoke), "Behold, this has nagai (touched) your shapah (lips); and your iwan (guilt/iniquity) is sawar (taken) away, and your chataah (sin) kapar (forgiven)."
I shamai (hearken / hear) the Adanay qawal (sound / voice), amar (spoke), "Whom shall I shalach (send), and who will yalak (go) for us?" Then I amar (spoke), "Here I am. Shalach (send) me!"

He amar (spoke), "yalak (go), and amar (spoke) this im (nation / people), ‘You shamai (hearken / hear) shamai (hearken / hear), but don't bayan (between); and you raah (see) raah (see), but don't yadai (perceive).'

Make the lab (heart) of this im (nation / people) shaman (fat). Make their azan (ear) kabad (heavy), and shaii (shut) their iyan (eye); lest they raah (see) with their iyan (eye), and shamai (hearken / hear) with their azan (ear), and bayan (between) with their labab (heart), and shawab (turn back / repent) again, and be rapaa (healed)."

Then I amar (spoke), "Adanay, how long?" He amar (spoke), "Until irayam (cities) are shaah (waste) without yashab (inhabit/dwell), and bathayam (houses) without adam (man), and the adamah (land) becomes utterly shaah (waste),
And Yahawah has rachaq (removed) adam (men) rachaq (far) away, and the forsaken places are many in the qarab (among / near) of the aratz (Earth/land).

If there is a ishayaray (tenth) left in it, that also will in shawab (turn back / repent) be consumed: as a terebinth, and as an alawan (oak), whose stock remains when they are felled; so the qadash (set apart / make holy) zarai (seed) is its stock."

It happened in the yamay (days) of Achaz (Ahaz) the ban (son) of Yawatham (Jotham), the ban (son) of Izayah (Uzziah), malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), that Ratzayan (Rezin) the malak (king) of Aram (Syria), and Paqach (Pekah) the ban (son) of Ramalayahaw (Remaliah), malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), ilah (go up / offer) up to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) to malachamah (war) against it, but yakal (could) not lacham (prevail) against it.

It was nagad (told) the bayath (house) of Dawad (David), amar (spoke), "Aram (Syria) is allied with Aparayam (Ephraim)." His labab (heart) trembled, and the labab (heart) of his im (nation / people), as the itzay (trees) of the yair (forest) tremble with the rawach (spirit / wind).

Then Yahawah amar (spoke) to Yashaiyah (Isaiah), "yatzaa (go out / come out) out now to qaraah (meet) Achaz (Ahaz), you, and Shaarayashawab (Shearjashub) your ban (son), at the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the thailah (conduit) of the ilayawan (Ilayawan) barakah (pool), on the masalah (highway) of the kabas (fuller's) shadah (field).

Amar (spoke) him, ‘Be careful, and keep calm. Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), neither let your heart be rakak (faint) because of these shanayam (two) zanabawath (tails) of ishan (smoking) torches, for the charay (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Ratzayan (Rezin) and Aram (Syria), and of the ban (son) of Ramalayahaw (Remaliah).
Because Aram (Syria), Aparayam (Ephraim), and the ban (son) of Ramalayahaw (Remaliah), have plotted rai (evil) amar (spoke) you, saying,

"Let's ilah (go up / offer) up against Yahawadah (Judah), and tear it apart, and let's baqai (divide) it among ourselves, and malak (king) up a malak (king) in its thawak (midst), even the ban (son) of Tabaal (Tabeel)."
Kah (this) is what the Adanay Yahawah amar (spoke): "It shall not qawam (rise up), neither shall it happen."

For the raash (head) of Aram (Syria) is Damashaq (Damascus), and the raash (head) of Damashaq (Damascus) is Ratzayan (Rezin); and within shashayam (sixty) - chamash (five) shanah (years) Aparayam (Ephraim) shall be broken in pieces, so that it shall not be a im (nation / people);

And the raash (head) of Aparayam (Ephraim) is Shamarawan (Samaria), and the raash (head) of Shamarawan (Samaria) is Ramalayahaw (Remaliah's) ban (son). If you will not aman (believe / have faith), aman (believe / have faith) you shall not be established.'"
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) again to Achaz (Ahaz), amar (spoke),
"Shaal (ask) a awath (sign / mark / miracle) of Yahawah your Alahayam; shaal (ask) it either in the imaq (depth), or in the gabah (height) mail (top/above)."
But Achaz (Ahaz) amar (spoke), "I will not shaal (ask), neither will I nasah (tempt) Yahawah."
He amar (spoke), "shamai (hearken / hear) now, bayath (house) of Dawad (David). Is it not enough for you to try the patience of anashayam (men), that you will try the patience of my Alahayam also?

Therefore the Adanay himself will nathan (give) you a awath (sign / mark / miracle). Behold, the ilamah (virgin) will harah (conceive), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son), and shall qaraa (called) his sham (name) Imanawaal (Immanuel).
He shall akal (eat) chamaah (butter) and dabash (honey) when he yadai (knows) to maas (refuse) the rai (evil), and bachar (choose) the tawab (good / proper function).

For before the nair (child) yadai (knows) to maas (refuse) the rai (evil), and bachar (choose) the tawab (good / proper function), the adamah (land) whose shanayam (two) malak (king) you qawatz (abhor) shall be forsaken.

Yahawah will bawaa (come) on you, on your im (nation / people), and on your ab (father) bayath (house), yamayam (days) that bawaa (come) not come, from the yawam (day) that Aparayam (Ephraim) sawar (departed) from Yahawadah (Judah); even the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria).

It will happen in that yawam (day) that Yahawah will whistle for the zabawab (fly) that is in the uttermost part of the yaaray (rivers) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and for the dabawarah (bee) that is in the aratz (Earth/land) of Ashawar (Assyria).
They shall bawaa (come), and shall all nawach (rest) in the bathah (desolate) nachalay (valleys), in the clefts of the salaiyam (rocks), on all naitzawatz (thorn) hedges, and on all pastures.

In that yawam (day) the Adanay will galach (shave) with a thair (razor) that is shakayarah (hired) in the parts ibar (beyond) the nahar (river), even with the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria), the raash (head) and the shair (hair) of the ragalayam (feet); and it shall also sapah (consume) the zaqan (beard).
It shall happen in that yawam (day) that a ayash (man / husband) shall chayah (keep) alive a young igalah (cow), and shanayam (two) tzaan (sheep);

And it shall happen, that because of the rab (abundance) of chalab (milk) which they shall give he shall akal (eat) chamaah (butter): for everyone will akal (eat) chamaah (butter) and dabash (honey) that is yathar (left) in the midst of the aratz (Earth/land).

It will happen in that yawam (day) that every maqawam (place) where there were a alap (thousand) gapan (vines) at a alap (thousand) kasap (silver) shekels, shall be for shamayar (briers) and shayath (thorns).
People will bawaa (come) there with chatzayam (arrows) and with qashath (bow), because all the aratz (Earth/land) will be shamayar (briers) and shayath (thorns).

All the harayam (hills) that were cultivated with the hoe, you shall not bawaa (come) there for yaraah (fear) of shamayar (briers) and shayath (thorns); but it shall be for the mashalawach (sending) forth of oxen, and for the maramas (treading) of shah (sheep)."
Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, "laqach (take / seize) a large tablet, and kathab (write) on it with a anawash (man's) charat (pen), ‘For Maharashalalachashabaz (Maher Shalal Hash Baz);'

And I will iwad (admonish/bear witness against) for myself aman (believe / have faith) witnesses to iwad (admonish/bear witness against): Awarayah (Uriah) the kahan (priest), and Zakarayah (Zechariah) the ban (son) of Yabarakayahaw (Jeberechiah)."

I qarab (come close) to the nabayaah (prophetess), and she harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son). Then Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, "qaraa (called) his sham (name) ‘Maharashalalachashabaz (Maher Shalal Hash Baz).'

For before the nair (child) yadai (knows) how to qaraa (called), ‘My ab (father),' and, ‘My am (mother),' the riches of Damashaq (Damascus) and the shalal (spoil) of Shamarawan (Samaria) will be nashaa (lift) away by the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria)."
Yahawah dabar (word / matter) to me yet again, amar (spoke),

"Yain (because) this im (nation / people) have maas (refused) the may (waters) of shalach (shiloah) that halak (move) at (softly), and mashawash (rejoice) in Ratzayan (Rezin) and Ramalayahaw (Remaliah's) ban (son);

Now therefore, behold, the Adanay ilah (go up / offer) upon them the itzawam (mighty) flood may (waters) of the nahar (river): the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria) and all his kabawad (glory). It will ilah (go up / offer) up over all its apayaq (channels), and halak (move) over all its gadah (banks).

It will sweep onward into Yahawadah (Judah). It will shatap (overflow) and ibar (pass over/through) through; it will nagai (reach) even to the tzawaar (neck); and the matah (stretching) out of its kanap (wings) will malaa (fill) the rachab (breadth) of your aratz (Earth/land), Imanawaal (Immanuel).
Make an uproar, you imayam (peoples), and be broken in pieces! Listen, kal (every) you from marachaq (far) aratz (Earth/land): dress for battle, and be shattered! Dress for battle, and be shattered!
Iwatz (take) itzah (counsel) iwatz (together), and it will be parar (brought) to nothing; dabar (word / matter) the dabar (word / matter), and it will not qawam (rise up): for Al is with us."
For Yahawah amar (spoke) thus to me with a chazaqah (strong) yad (hand), and yasar (instructed) me not to yalak (walk) in the darak (way) of this im (nation / people), amar (spoke),

"Don't amar (spoke), ‘A qashar (conspiracy)!' Concerning all about which this im (nation / people) amar (spoke), ‘A qashar (conspiracy)!' Neither yaraa (fear / be afraid) their threats, nor be terrorized.
Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) is who you must respect as holy. He is the one you must mawaraa (fear). He is the one you must iratz (dread).
He will be a maqadash (sanctuary), but for shanayam (two) bathay (houses) of Yashar-Al (Israel), he will be a trap and a mawaqash (snare) for the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).
Many will kashal (stumble / stagger) over it, napal (fall / be cast down), be shabar (broken), be yaqash (snared), and be captured."
Wrap up the thaiwadah (testimony). Chatham (seal) the thawarah (instruction) among my lamawad (disciples).
I will chakah (wait) for Yahawah, who sathar (hides) his panayam (face) from the bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and I will qawah (gather/wait) for him.

Behold, I and the yaladayam (children) whom Yahawah nathan (give) given me are for athawath (signs) and for mawapathayam (wonders) in Yashar-Al (Israel) from Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), who shakan (place) in har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion).

When they amar (spoke) you, "Consult with those who have familiar abawath (spirits) and with the yadainayam (wizards), who chirp and who hagah (mutter):" shouldn't a im (nation / people) consult with their Alahayam? Should they consult the mawath (death) on behalf of the chay (life)?
Turn to the thawarah (instruction) and to the thaiwadah (testimony)! If they don't amar (spoke) according to this dabar (word / matter), surely there is no shachar (morning) for them.

They will ibar (pass over/through) through it, very distressed and raib (hungry); and it will happen that when they are raib (hungry), they will worry, and qalal (curse) by their malak (king) and by their Alahayam. They will panah (turn) their mail (top/above) upward,
And nabat (look) to the aratz (Earth/land), and see tzarah (distress), chashakah (darkness), and the gloom of tzawaq (anguish). They will be nadach (driven) into thick apalah (darkness).

But there shall be no more gloom for her who was in anguish. In the former time, he brought into contempt the aratz (Earth/land) of Zebulun and the aratz (Earth/land) of Naphtali; but in the latter time he raah (see) made it glorious, by the aratz (Earth/land) of the sea, il (over) the Jordan, Galilee of the im (nation / people).
The gaway (heathen / nation) who walked in darkness rabah (have) seen a rabah (great) light. Those who lived in the land of the shadow of death, on them the light has shined.
You have multiplied the nation. You have increased their joy. They rejoice before you according to the joy in harvest, as men rejoice when they divide the spoil.
For the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, you have broken as in the hayah (came to pass) of Midian.
For all the armor of the armed yalad (birth / begot) in the noisy battle, and the garments rolled in blood, will be for burning, fuel for the fire.

For to us a child is ishah (make). To us a son is given; and the masharah (government) will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty Al, Everlasting Father, Prince of shalawam (peace / safety).

Of the increase of his government and of peace there shall be no end, on the throne of David, and on his kingdom, to establish it, and to uphold it with justice and with righteousness from that time on, even forever. The zeal of Yahawah of Armies will perform this.
The Adanay sent a word into Jacob, and it falls on Israel.
All the people will know, including Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria, who say in pride and in arrogance of heart,
"The bricks il (over) fallen, but we will build with cut stone. The sycamore fig trees have been cut down, but we will put cedars in their place."
Therefore Yahawah will shawab (turn back / repent) up on high against him the adversaries of Rezin, and will stir up his enemies,
The Syrians in front, and the Philistines behind; and they will devour Israel with open mouth. For all this, his anger is not shawab (turn back / repent) away, but his hand is stretched out still.
Yet the people have not turned to him who struck them, neither have they sought Yahawah of Armies.
Therefore Yahawah will cut off from Israel raash (head) and zanab (tail), palm branch and reed, in one day.
The elder and the honorable zah (this / that / these) is the head, and the prophet who teaches lies is the tail.
For those who lead this people lead them astray; and those who are led by them are dabar (word / matter).

Therefore the Adanay will not rejoice over their young men, neither will he have compassion on their fatherless and widows; for everyone is profane and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks folly. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
For wickedness burns like a ash (fire). It devours the briers and thorns; yes, it kindles in the thickets of the forest, and they roll upward in a column of smoke.
Through the wrath of Yahawah of Armies, the land is burnt up; and the ayash (man / husband) are the fuel for the fire. No ayash (man / husband) spares his brother.
One will devour on the right yad (hand), and be hungry; and he will eat on the left yad (hand), and they will not be satisfied. Everyone will eat the flesh of his own arm:

Manashah (Manasseh), Aparayam (Ephraim); and Aparayam (Ephraim), Manashah (Manasseh); and they yachad (together) shall be against Yahawadah (Judah). For all this his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) is not shawab (turn back / repent) away, but his yad (hand) is natah (stretched) out still.
Haway (Alas/Woe!) To those who chaqaq (lawgiver) awan (unrighteous) chaqaqay (decrees), and to the writers who kathab (write) oppressive decrees;

To deprive the dal (needy) from dayan (judge), and to gazal (rob) the inay (poor) among my im (nation / people) of their mashapat (rights), that alamanawath (widows) may be their shalal (spoil), and that they may make the yathawam (fatherless) their bazaz (prey)!

What will you ishah (make) in the yawam (day) of paqadah (visitation), and in the shawaa (vanity) which will bawaa (come) from afar? To whom will you nawas (flee) for izarah (help)? Where will you izab (leave) your wealth?

They will only karai (bow) down under the asayar (prisoners), and will napal (fall / be cast down) under the harag (kill). For all this his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) is not shawab (turn back / repent) away, but his yad (hand) is natah (stretched) out still.
Alas Ashawar (Assyrian), the shabat (rod) of my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), the matah (staff / rod / tribe) in whose yad (hand) is my zaim (indignation)!

I will shalach (send) him against a profane gaway (heathen / nation), and against the im (nation / people) who ibarah (anger) me will I give him a tzawah (command) to take the shalal (spoil) and to bazaz (take) the baz (prey), and to shawam (place / establish / appoint) them down like the chamar (mire) of the chawatzawath (streets).
However he doesn't damah (mean) so, neither does his labab (heart) chashab (think) so; but it is in his labab (heart) to shamad (destroy), and to karath (cut) off not a mait (few) gawayam (nations).
For he amar (spoke), "Aren't yachad (all) of my shar (prince / ruler) malakayam (kings)?
Isn't Kalanah (Calno) like Karakamayash (Carchemish)? Isn't Chamath (Hamath) like Arapad (Arpad)? Isn't Shamarawan (Samaria) like Damashaq (Damascus)?"
As my yad (hand) matzaa (has) found the mamalakath (kingdoms) of the alayal (idols), whose engraved pasayal (images) exceeded those of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) and of Shamarawan (Samaria);
Shall I not, as I ishah (make) done to Shamarawan (Samaria) and her alayal (idols), so ishah (make) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) and her itzab (idols)?

Therefore it will happen that, when the Adanay has batzai (performed) his whole maishah (work) on har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion) and on Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), I will paqad (visit) the paray (fruit) of the willful proud labab (heart) of the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria), and the insolence of his haughty iyan (eye).

For he has amar (spoke), "By the kach (strength / mighty / power) of my yad (hand) I ishah (make) done it, and by my chakamah (wisdom); for I have chakamah (understanding): and I have sawar (removed) the boundaries of the imayam (peoples), and have shasah (robbed) their treasures. Like a abayar (valiant) man I have yarad (brought) down their yawashabayam (rulers).

My yad (hand) matzaa (has) found the riches of the imayam (peoples) like a qan (nest), and like one asap (gathers) bayatzayam (eggs) that are abandoned, have I asap (gathered) all the aratz (Earth/land). There was no one who nadad (moved) their kanap (wing), or that patzah (opened) their pah (mouth), or chirped."

Should an axe brag against him who chops with it? Should a mashawar (saw) exalt itself above him who saws with it? As if a shabat (rod) should nawap (lift) those who rawam (will lift up) it up, or as if a matah (staff / rod / tribe) should rawam (will lift up) up someone who is not itz (wood).

Therefore the Adawan, Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), will shalach (send) among his mashaman (fat) ones razawan (leanness); and under his kabawad (glory) a yaqawad (burning) will be yaqad (kindled) like the burning of ash (fire).

The awar (light) of Yashar-Al (Israel) will be for a ash (fire), and his qadawash (holy) One for a lahabah (flame); and it will bair (burn) and akal (eat) his shayath (thorns) and his shamayar (briers) in achad (one) yawam (day).

He will kalah (complete / finish) the kabawad (glory) of his yair (forest), and of his karamal (fruitful) field, both napash (soul) and bashar (flesh). It will be as when a standard bearer masas (faints).
The shaar (remnant) of the itz (trees) of his yair (forest) shall be masapar (few), so that a nair (child) could kathab (write) their number.

It will come to pass in that yawam (day) that the shaar (remnant) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and those who have palayatah (escaped) from the bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob) will no more again shain (lean) on him who nakah (struck) them, but shall shain (lean) on Yahawah, the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel), in amath (truth).
A shaar (remnant) will shawab (turn back / repent), even the shaar (remnant) of Yaiqab (Jacob), to the gabawar (mighty) Al.

For though your im (nation / people), Yashar-Al (Israel), are like the chawal (sand) of the yam (sea/waters), only a shaar (remnant) of them will shawab (turn back / repent). A destruction is charatz (determined), shatap (overflowing) with tzadaqah (righteousness).
For the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), will ishah (make) a kalah (complete / finish) end, and that charatz (determined), in the qarab (among / near) of all the aratz (Earth/land).

Therefore the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), amar (spoke) "My im (nation / people) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in Tzayawan (Zion), don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of the Ashawar (Assyrian), though he nakah (strike) you with the shabat (rod), and nashaa (lift) up his matah (staff / rod / tribe) against you, as Matzarayam (Egypt) did.

For yet a very mait (little) while, and the zaim (indignation) against you will be kalah (complete / finish), and my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) will be directed to his thabalayath (destruction)."

Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) will iwar (rouse / awaken) up a shawat (scourge) against him, as in the makah (slaughter) of Madayan (Midian) at the tzawar (rock) of Irab (Oreb). His matah (staff / rod / tribe) will be over the yam (sea/waters), and he will nashaa (lift) it up like he did against Matzarayam (Egypt).

It will happen in that yawam (day), that his sabal (burden) will sawar (depart) from off your shakam (shoulder), and his il (over) from off your tzawaar (neck), and the il (over) shall be chabal (destroyed) panayam (face) of the anointing shaman (oil).
He bawaa (come) come to Iy (Aiath). He ibar (pass over/through) passed through Magarawan (Migron). At Makamas (Michmash) he stores his baggage.

They ibar (pass over/through) gone over the maibar (pass). They have taken up their malawan (lodging) at Gabai (Geba). Ramah (Ramah) charad (trembles). Gabaih (Gibeah) of Shaawal (Saul) has nawas (fled).
Qawal (sound / voice) tzahal (aloud) with your qawal (sound / voice), banath (daughter) of Galayam (Gallim)! Listen, Laishah! You inay (poor) Inathawath (Anathoth)!
Madamanah (Madmenah) is a fugitive. The yashabay (inhabitants) of Gabayam (Gebim) iwaz (flee) for safety.
This very yawam (day) he will halt at Nab (Nob). He nawap (shakes) his yad (hand) at the har (mountain) of the banath (daughter) of Zion, the gabaih (hill) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).
Behold, the Adawan, Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), will lop the paarah (boughs) with mairatzah (terror). The qawamah (tall) will be gadai (cut) down, and the gabah (lofty) will be brought low.
He will naqap (cut) down the sabakay (thickets) of the yair (forest) with barazal (iron), and Labanawan (Lebanon) will napal (fall / be cast down) by the adayar (mighty) One.
A shoot will yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the gazai (stock) of Yashay (Jesse), and a natzar (branch) out of his sharash (roots) will parah (bear) fruit.

The rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah will nawach (rest) on him: the rawach (spirit / wind) of chakamah (wisdom) and chakamah (understanding), the rawach (spirit / wind) of itzah (counsel) and gabawarah (might), the rawach (spirit / wind) of daith (knowledge) and of the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah.
His delight will be in the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah. He will not shapat (judge / judgement) by the maraah (sight) of his maraah (eyes), neither decide by the mashamai (hearing) of his azan (ear);

But with tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) he will shapat (judge / judgement) the dal (poor), and decide with mayashawar (equity) for the inaw (humble) of the aratz (Earth/land). He will nakah (strike) the aratz (Earth/land) with the shabat (rod) of his pah (mouth); and with the rawach (spirit / wind) of his shapah (lips) he will mawath (death) the rashai (wicked).
Tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) will be the belt of his waist, and amawanah (faithfulness) the belt of his waist.

The zaab (wolf) will live with the kabash (lamb), and the namar (leopard) will rabatz (lie) down with the young goat; The igal (calf), the young kapayar (lion), and the fattened igal (calf) yachad (together); and a qatan (small / young / least) nair (child) will nahag (lead) them.
The parah (cow) and the dab (bear) will graze. Their yalad (birth / begot) ones will rabatz (lie) down yachad (together). The aray (lion) will akal (eat) thaban (straw) like the baqar (morning).
The yanaq (nursing) child will shaii (play) near a cobra's chawar (hole), and the weaned child will hadah (put) his yad (hand) on the viper's maawarah (den).

They will not raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) nor shachath (destroy) in all my qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain); for the aratz (Earth/land) will be malaa (full) of the daih (knowledge) of Yahawah, as the mayam (Waters) kasah (cover) the yam (sea/waters).

It will happen in that yawam (day) that the gawayam (nations) will darash (seek) the sharash (root) of Yashay (Jesse), who imad (stands) as a nas (banner) of the imayam (peoples); and his manawachah (resting) place will be kabawad (glorious).

It will happen in that yawam (day) that the Adanay will set his yad (hand) again the shanay (second) time to qanah (recover) the shaar (remnant) that is shaar (left) of his im (nation / people) from Ashawar (Assyria), from Matzarayam (Egypt), from Patharawas (Pathros), from Kawash (Cush), from Iyalam (Elam), from Shanair (Shinar), from Chamath (Hamath), and from the ayay (islands) of the yam (sea/waters).

He will nashaa (lift) up a nas (banner) for the gawayam (nations), and will asap (assemble) the nadachay (outcasts) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and qabatz (gather) together the napatz (dispersed) of Yahawadah (Judah) from the arabai (four) kanapawath (corners) of the aratz (Earth/land).

The qanaah (envy) also of Aparayam (Ephraim) will sawar (depart), and those who persecute Yahawadah (Judah) will be karath (cut) off. Aparayam (Ephraim) won't qanaa (jealous) Yahawadah (Judah), and Yahawadah (Judah) won't persecute Aparayam (Ephraim).

They will iwap (flying) down on the kathap (shoulders) of the Palashathay (Philistines) on the yam (sea/waters). Yachad (together) they will plunder the banay (children) of the qadam (east). They will extend their yad (hand) over Adawam (Edom) and Mawaab (Moab), and the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon) will mashamaith (obey) them.

Yahawah will utterly charam (destroy) the lashawan (tongue / language) of the Matzarayam (Egyptian) yam (sea/waters); and with his scorching rawach (spirit / wind) he will nawap (wave) his yad (hand) over the nahar (river), and will split it into shabai (seven) nachalayam (streams), and cause men to march over in sandals.

There will be a masalah (highway) for the shaar (remnant) that is shaar (left) of his im (nation / people) from Ashawar (Assyria), like there was for Yashar-Al (Israel) in the yawam (day) that he ilah (go up / offer) up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

In that yawam (day) you will amar (spoke), "I will give yadah (thanks) to you, Yahawah; for though you were anap (angry) with me, your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) has shawab (turn back / repent) away and you nacham (turn away / repent) me.

Behold, Al is my yashawaih (salvation). I will batach (trust), and will not be pachad (fear / dread); for Yah, Yahawah, is my iz (strength / might / refuge) and zamarath (song); and he has become my yashawaih (salvation)."
Therefore with shashawan (joy) you will shaab (draw) mayam (Waters) out of the maiyanay (wells) of yashawaih (salvation).

In that yawam (day) you will amar (spoke), "Give hawadaw (thanks) to Yahawah! Qaraa (called) on his sham (name). Yadai (declare) his ilayalah (doings) among the imayam (peoples). Proclaim that his sham (name) is shagab (exalted)!
Zamar (sing) to Yahawah, for he ishah (make) done gaawath (excellent) things! Yadai (let) this be known in all the aratz (Earth/land)!

Tzahal (cry) aloud and ranan (shout), you yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Tzayawan (Zion); for the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel) is gadawal (very great/important/mighty) in the qarab (among / near) of you!"
The mashaa (burden) of Babal (Babylon), which Yashaiyah (Isaiah) the ban (son) of Amawatz (Amoz) chazah (saw):

Nashaa (lift) up a nas (banner) on the bare har (mountain)! Rawam (will lift up) up your qawal (sound / voice) to them! Nawap (wave) your yad (hand), that they may bawaa (come) into the pathachay (gates) of the nadayabayam (nobles).

I have tzawah (commanded) my qadash (set apart / make holy) ones; yes, I have qaraa (called) my gabawar (mighty) men for my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), even my gaawah (proudly) exulting ilayazay (ones).
