For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah to me, "As the aray (lion) and the young kapayar (lion) growling over his tarap (prey), if a malaa (multitude) of raiyam (shepherds) is qaraa (called) together against him, will not be chathath (dismayed) at their qawal (sound / voice), nor inah (oppress / afflict) himself for their hamawan (noise), so Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) will yarad (come) down to tzabaa (troop) on har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion) and on its heights.
As tzaparayam (birds) hovering, so Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) will protect Yarawashalam (Jerusalem). He will protect and natzal (deliver) it. He will pasach (pass) over and malat (preserve) it."
Shawab (turn back / repent) to him from whom you imaq (have) deeply sarah (revolted), banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

For in that yawam (day) everyone shall maas (cast) away his alayalay (idols) of kasap (silver) and his alayalay (idols) of zahab (gold) — chataa (sin) which your own yad (hand) ishah (make) made for you.

"The Ashawar (Assyrian) will napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword), not of ayash (man / husband); and the charab (sword), not of mankind, shall akal (eat) him. He will nawas (flee) from the charab (sword), and his bachawar (young) men will become subject to forced mas (labor).

His salai (rock) will ibar (pass over/through) away by reason of magawar (terror), and his shar (prince / ruler) will be afraid of the nas (banner)," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, whose awar (light) is in Tzayawan (Zion), and his thanawar (furnace) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).
Behold, a malak (king) shall malak (king) in tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and sharayam (princes) shall sharar (rule) in mashapat (justice).

A ayash (man / husband) shall be as a machabaa (hiding) place from the rawach (spirit / wind), and a sathar (secret / hidden) from the zaram (storm), as palagay (streams) of mayam (Waters) in a tzayawan (dry) place, as the tzal (shade) of a large salai (rock) in a iyap (weary) aratz (Earth/land).
The iyanay (eyes) of those who raah (see) will not be shaih (dim), and the azanay (ears) of those who shamai (hearken / hear) will listen.

The labab (heart) of the mahar (rash) will bayan (between) yadai (knowledge), and the lashawan (tongue / language) of the ilagayam (stammerers) will be mahar (ready) to dabar (word / matter) tzach (plainly).
The nabal (fool) will no longer be qaraa (called) nadayab (noble), nor the scoundrel be highly respected.

For the nabal (fool) will dabar (word / matter) nabalah (folly), and his lab (heart) will ishah (make) awan (iniquity), to practice profanity, and to dabar (word / matter) thawaih (error) against Yahawah, To make rawaq (empty) the napash (soul) of the raib (hungry), and to cause the mashaqah (drink) of the thirsty to chasar (fail).

The kalay (ways) of the scoundrel are rai (evil). He yaitz (devises) zamah (wicked) devices to chabal (destroy) the inaw (humble) with shaqar (lying) amaray (words), even when the abayawan (needy) dabar (word / matter) mashapat (right).
But the nadayab (noble) yaitz (devises) nadayab (noble) things; and he will continue in nadayab (noble) things.

Qawam (rise up) up, you nashayam (women) who are at shaanan (ease)! Shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice)! You batach (careless) banawath (daughters), azan (ear) ear to my amarah (sayings)!
For yamayam (days) beyond a shanah (year) you will be ragaz (troubled), you batach (careless) women; for the batzayar (vintage) shall kalah (complete / finish). The harvest won't bawaa (come).
Charad (tremble), you women who are at shaanan (ease)! Be ragaz (troubled), you batach (careless) ones! Pashat (strip) yourselves, irar (make) yourselves naked, and put sackcloth on your waist.
Beat your shadayam (breasts) for the chamad (pleasant) shaday (fields), for the parah (fruitful) gapan (vine).
Qawatz (thorns) and briars will ilah (go up / offer) up on my im (nation / people) adamah (land); yes, on all the bathay (houses) of mashawash (joy) in the ilayaz (joyous) qarayah (city / town).

For the aramawan (palace) will be forsaken. The populous iyar (city) will be deserted. The hill and the watchtower will be for mairawath (dens) id (until / as far as), a delight for paraa (wild) donkeys, a maraih (pasture) of idarayam (flocks);

Until the rawach (spirit / wind) is irah (poured) on us from on marawam (high), and the madabar (wilderness) becomes a karamal (fruitful) field, and the karamal (fruitful) field is chashab (considered) a yair (forest).
Then mashapat (justice) will shakan (place) in the madabar (wilderness); and tzadaqah (righteousness) will yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the karamal (fruitful) field.
The maishah (work) of tzadaqah (righteousness) will be shalawam (peace / safety); and the ibadah (effect) of tzadaqah (righteousness), shaqat (quietness) and batach (confidence) iwalam (forever).
My im (nation / people) will live in a peaceful nawah (habitation), in safe mashakanawath (dwellings), and in shaanan (quiet) manawachah (resting) places.
Though barad (hail) flattens the yair (forest), and the iyar (city) is leveled completely.
Ashar (who/that) are you who zarai (sow) beside all mayam (Waters), who shalach (send) out the ragal (feet / foot) of the shawar (ox) and the donkey.

Haway (Alas/Woe!) To you who shadad (destroy), but you weren't shadad (destroyed); and who betray, but nobody betrayed you! When you thamam (have) finished shadad (destroying), you will be shadad (destroyed); and when you have nalah (made) an end of betrayal, you will be betrayed.
Yahawah, be gracious to us. We have qawah (gather/wait) for you. Be our zarawai (strength) every baqar (morning), our yashawaih (salvation) also in the ith (time) of tzarah (trouble).
At the qawal (sound / voice) of the thunder, the imayam (peoples) have nadad (fled). When you lift yourself up, the gawayam (nations) are napatz (scattered).
Your shalal (spoil) will be asap (gathered) as the chasayal (caterpillar) gathers. Men will leap on it as gabayam (locusts) leap.
Yahawah is shagab (exalted), for he shakan (place) on marawam (high). He malaa (has) filled Tzayawan (Zion) with mashapat (justice) and tzadaqah (righteousness).
There will be amawanah (stability) in your ith (times), abundance of yashawaih (salvation), chakamah (wisdom), and daith (knowledge). The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is your awatzar (treasure).
Behold, their araal (valiant) ones tzaiq (cry) outside; the malaakay (ambassadors) of shalawam (peace / safety) bakah (weep) bitterly.

The masalawath (highways) are shamam (desolate). The traveling ibar (pass over/through) shabath (shabath / rest). The barayath (covenant) is parar (broken). He has maas (despised) the irayam (cities). He doesn't respect anawash (man).

The aratz (Earth/land) abal (mourns) and languishes. Labanawan (Lebanon) is chapar (confounded) and qamal (withers) away. Sharawan (Sharon) is like a irabah (desert), and Bashan (Bashan) and Karamal (Carmel) are stripped bare.
"Now I will qawam (rise up)," amar (spoke) Yahawah; "Now I will nashaa (lift) myself up. Now I will be nashaa (lift).
You will harah (conceive) chashash (chaff). You will yalad (birth / begot) forth qash (stubble). Your rawach (spirit / wind) is a ash (fire) that will akal (eat) you.
The imayam (peoples) will be like the burning of shayad (lime), like qawatzayam (thorns) that are kasach (cut) down and yatzath (burned) in the ash (fire).
Shamai (hearken / hear), you who are rachawaq (far) off, what I ishah (make) done; and, you who are qarawab (near), yadai (acknowledge) my gabawarah (might)."

The chataayam (sinners) in Tzayawan (Zion) are pachad (fear / dread). Trembling achaz (has) seized the godless gawar (ones). Who among us can live with the akal (eat) ash (fire)? Who among us can live with iwalam (forever) mawaqad (burning)?

He who halak (move) righteously, and dabar (word / matter) blamelessly; He who maas (despises) the batzai (gain) of maishaqawath (oppressions), who gestures with his kap (hands), refusing to thamak (take) a shachad (bribe), who atam (stops) his azan (ear) from shamai (hearken / hear) of dam (blood), and itzam (shuts) his iyan (eye) from raah (see) at rai (evil)—
He will shakan (place) on marawam (high). His place of defense will be the fortress of salaiyam (rocks). His lacham (bread) will be supplied. His mayam (Waters) will be aman (believe / have faith).
Your iyan (eye) will chazah (see) the malak (king) in his yapay (beauty). They will raah (see) a distant aratz (Earth/land).
Your lab (heart) will hagah (meditate) on the ayamah (terror). Where is he who sapar (book)? Where is he who shaqal (weighed)? Where is he who sapar (book) the magadalayam (towers)?

You will no longer raah (see) the yaiz (fierce) im (nation / people), a im (nation / people) of a deep shapah (speech) that you can't comprehend, with a strange lashawan (tongue / language) that you can't understand.

Chazah (look) at Tzayawan (Zion), the qarayah (city / town) of our mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) festivals. Your iyan (eye) will raah (see) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), a shaanan (quiet) nawah (habitation), a ahal (tent) that won't be removed. Its yathad (stakes) will never be plucked up, nor will any of its chabal (cords) be nathaq (broken).

But there Yahawah will be with us in majesty, a maqawam (place) of rachab (broad) naharayam (rivers) and yaarayam (streams), in which no anay (galley) with shayat (oars) will yalak (go), neither will any adayar (gallant) tzay (ship) ibar (pass over/through) by there.
For Yahawah is our shapat (judge / judgement). Yahawah is our chaqaq (lawgiver). Yahawah is our malak (king). He will yashai (salvation) us.

Your rigging is untied. They couldn't chazaq (strengthen) the kan (for sure) of their tharan (mast). They couldn't parash (spread) the nas (sail). Then the id (until / as far as) of a marabah (great) shalal (spoil) was chalaq (divided). The pasach (lame) bazaz (took) the baz (prey).
The shakan (place) won't amar (spoke), "I am chalah (afflict)." The im (nation / people) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein will be nashaa (lift) their iwan (guilt/iniquity).

Qarab (come close) near, you gawayam (nations), to shamai (hearken / hear)! Listen, you laamayam (peoples). Let the aratz (Earth/land) and malaa (all) it contains shamai (hearken / hear); the thabal (world), and everything that comes from it.
For Yahawah is enraged against all the gawayam (nations), and angry with all their tzabaa (troop). He charam (has) utterly destroyed them. He nathan (give) given them over for tabach (slaughter).
Their chalal (slain) will also be shalak (cast) out, and the stench of their pagar (dead) bodies will ilah (go up / offer) up; and the harayam (mountains) will masas (melt) in their dam (blood).

All of the tzabaa (troop) of the sky will be maqaq (dissolved). The sky will be galal (rolled) up like a sapar (book / scribed document), and all its tzabaa (troop) will nabal (fade) away, as a ilah (leaf) nabal (fades) from off a gapan (vine) or a thaan (fig) tree.
For my charab (sword) has rawah (drunk) its fill in the sky. Behold, it will yarad (come) down on Adawam (Edom), and on the im (nation / people) of my charam (curse), for mashapat (judgment).

Yahawah charab (sword) is malaa (filled) with dam (blood). It is covered with dashan (fat), with the dam (blood) of karayam (lambs) and ithawadayam (goats), with the chalab (fat) of the kalayawath (kidneys) of ayalayam (rams); for Yahawah has a zabach (sacrifice) in Batzarah (Bozrah), And a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) tabach (slaughter) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Adawam (Edom).

The wild oxen will yarad (come) down with them, and the young parayam (bulls) with the abayar (mighty) bulls; and their aratz (Earth/land) will be rawah (drunken) with dam (blood), and their ipar (dust) dashan (made) greasy with chalab (fat).
For Yahawah has a yawam (day) of naqam (vengeance), a shanah (year) of shalawam (peace / safety) for the rayab (cause) of Tzayawan (Zion).
Its nachal (stream / river) will be hapak (turned) into zapath (pitch), its ipar (dust) into sulfur, And its aratz (Earth/land) will become bair (burning) zapath (pitch).

It won't be kabah (quenched) layal (night) nor yawamam (by day). Its ishan (smoke) will ilah (go up / offer) up iwalam (forever). From dawar (generation / age / period) to dawar (generation / age / period), it will charab (lie) waste. No one will ibar (pass over/through) through it natzach (forever) and natzach (ever).

But the pelican and the porcupine will yarash (possess) it. The yanashawap (owl) and the irab (evening) will shakan (place) in it. He will natah (stretch) the qaw (line) of thahaw (formless) over it, and the plumb qaw (line) of bahaw (void).
They shall qaraa (called) its char (nobles) to the malawakah (kingdom), but none shall be there; and all its shar (prince / ruler) shall be apas (nothing).

Sayarayam (thorns) will ilah (go up / offer) up in its aramawan (palaces), qamawash (nettles) and chawach (thistles) in its fortresses; and it will be a nawah (habitation) of jackals, a chatzayar (court) for ostriches.

The tzayay (wild) animals of the desert will pagash (meet) with the wolves, and the wild shaiyar (goat) will qaraa (called) to his rai (neigbor/another person). Yes, the layalayath (night creature) creature shall settle there, and shall matzaa (find) herself a place of manawach (rest).

The arrow snake will qanan (make) her nest there, and malat (lay), baqai (hatch), and dagar (gather) under her tzal (shade). Yes, the kites will be qabatz (gathered) there, ayashah (woman / wife) one with her raiwath (mate).

Darash (search) in the sapar (book / scribed document) of Yahawah, and qaraa (called): not achad (one) of these will be missing. Ayashah (woman / wife) will paqad (visit) her raiwath (mate). For my pah (mouth) has tzawah (commanded), and his rawach (spirit / wind) has qabatz (gathered) them.

He napal (fall / be cast down) cast the gawaral (lot) for them, and his yad (hand) chalaq (has) divided it to them with a measuring qaw (line). They shall yarash (possess) it iwalam (forever). From dawar (generation / age / period) to dawar (generation / age / period) they will shakan (place) in it.
The madabar (wilderness) and the dry tzayah (land) will be shawash (glad). The irabah (desert) will gayal (rejoice) and parach (blossom) like a chabatzalath (rose).

It will parach (blossom) parach (abundantly), and gayal (rejoice) even with gayalah (joy) and ranan (singing). Labanawan (Lebanon's) kabawad (glory) Lebanon will be nathan (give) to it, the excellence of Karamal (Carmel) and Sharawan (Sharon). They will raah (see) Yahawah kabawad (glory), the excellence of our Alahayam.
Chazaq (strengthen) the rapah (weak) yadayam (hands), and amatz (make) firm the kashal (stumble / stagger) barakayam (knees).

Amar (spoke) those who have a mahar (fearful) lab (heart), "Be chazaq (strong). Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). Behold, your Alahayam will bawaa (come) with naqam (vengeance), Alahayam retribution. He will bawaa (come) and yashai (salvation) you.
Then the iyanay (eyes) of the iwar (blind) will be paqach (opened), and the azanay (ears) of the charash (deaf) will be pathach (unstopped).

Then the pasach (lame) man will dalag (leap) like a deer, and the lashawan (tongue / language) of the mute will ranan (sing); for mayam (Waters) will baqai (break) out in the madabar (wilderness), and nachalayam (streams) in the irabah (desert).

The burning sand will become a agam (pool), and the thirsty tzamaawan (ground) mabawaiy (springs) of mayam (Waters). Chatzayar (grass) with qanah (reeds) and rushes will be in the nawah (habitation) of jackals, rabatz (where) they lay.

A masalawal (highway) will be there, a road, and it will be qaraa (called) The qadash (set apart / make holy) darak (way). The tamaa (unclean) shall not ibar (pass over/through) over it, but it will be for those who walk in the Way. Wicked awayalayam (fools) will not thaih (go) there.
No aray (lion) will be there, nor will any parayatz (ravenous) animal ilah (go up / offer) up on it. They will not be matzaa (found) there; but the gaal (redeemed) will halak (move) there.

The Yahawah padah (ransomed) ones will shawab (turn back / repent), and bawaa (come) with ranah (singing) to Tzayawan (Zion); and iwalam (forever) shamachah (joy) will be on their raash (head). They will obtain shamachah (gladness) and shashawan (joy), and yagawan (sorrow) and anachah (sighing) will nawas (flee) away."

Now it happened in the fourteenth shanah (year) of malak (king) Chazaqayah (Hezekiah), that Sanacharayab (Sennacherib) malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria) attacked all of the batzar (fortified) iray (cities) of Yahawadah (Judah), and captured them.

The malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria) shalach (send) Rabashaqah (Rabshakeh) from Lakayash (Lachish) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) to malak (king) Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) with a large chayal (army). He imad (stood) by the aqueduct from the ilayawan (Ilayawan) barakah (pool) in the kabas (fuller's) shadah (field) masalah (highway).

Then Alayaqayam (Eliakim) the ban (son) of Chalaqayah (Hilkiah), who was over the bayath (house), and Shabanaa (Shebna) the sapar (book), and Yawaach (Joah), the ban (son) of Asap (Asaph), the zakar (remember) yatzaa (go out / come out) out to him.

Rabashaqah (Rabshakeh) amar (spoke) to them, "Now amar (spoke) Chazaqayah (Hezekiah), ‘Thus amaraw (says) the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) malak (king), the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria), "What batachawan (confidence) is this in which you trust?

I amar (spoke) that your itzah (counsel) and gabawarah (strength) for the malachamah (war) are only vain dabar (word / matter). Now in whom do you batach (trust), that you have marad (rebelled) against me?

Behold, you batach (trust) in the mashainah (staff) of this ratzatz (bruised) qanah (reed), even in Matzarayam (Egypt), which if a ayash (man / husband) samak (leans) on it, it will bawaa (come) into his kap (hand) and naqab (pierce) it. So is Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt) to all who batach (trust) in him.

But if you amar (spoke) me, ‘We batach (trust) in Yahawah our Alahayam,' isn't that he whose bamah (high) places and whose mazabach (altars) Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) has sawar (taken) away, and has amar (spoke) to Yahawadah (Judah) and to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), ‘You shall shachah (worship) panayam (face) this mazabach (altar)?'"

Now therefore, please make a irab (evening) to my adawan (master / lord) the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria), and I will nathan (give) you two alap (thousand) sawasayam (horses), if you are yakal (able) on your part to nathan (give) riders on them.

How then can you shawab (turn back / repent) away the panayam (face) of achad (one) pachah (captain) of the qatan (small / young / least) of my adawan (master / lord) ibaday (servants), and batach (put) your trust on Matzarayam (Egypt) for rakab (chariots) and for horsemen?

Have I ilah (go up / offer) up now balaiday (without) Yahawah against this aratz (Earth/land) to shachath (destroy) it? Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, "ilah (go up / offer) up against this aratz (Earth/land), and shachath (destroy) it."'"

Then Alayaqayam (Eliakim), Shabanaa (Shebna) and Yawaach (Joah) amar (spoke) to Rabashaqah (Rabshakeh), "Please dabar (word / matter) to your ibad (servant) in Aramaic, for we shamai (hearken / hear) it; and don't dabar (word / matter) to us in the Yahawadayath (Jews)' language in the azan (ear) of the im (nation / people) who are on the chawamah (wall)."

But Rabashaqah (Rabshakeh) amar (spoke), "Has my adawan (master / lord) shalach (send) me only to your adawan (master / lord) and to you, to dabar (word / matter) these dabarayam (words), and not to the anashayam (men) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the chawamah (wall), who will akal (eat) their own charaa (dung) and shathah (drinks) their own urine with you?"

Then Rabashaqah (Rabshakeh) imad (stood), and qaraa (called) out with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice) in the Yahawadayath (Jews)' language, and amar (spoke), "shamai (hearken / hear) the dabaray (words) of the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) malak (king), the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria)!
Thus amar (spoke) the malak (king), ‘Don't let Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) nashaa (lift) you; for he will not be yakal (able) to natzal (deliver) you.

Don't let Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) batach (make) you trust in Yahawah, amar (spoke), "Yahawah will natzal (surely) natzal (deliver) us. This iyar (city) won't be nathan (give) into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria)."'

Don't shamai (hearken / hear) to Chazaqayah (Hezekiah), for thus amar (spoke) the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria), ‘ishah (make) your barakah (peace) with me, and yatzaa (go out / come out) out to me; and ayash (man / husband) of you akal (eat) from his gapan (vine), and ayash (man / husband) one from his thaan (fig) tree, and ayash (man / husband) one of you shathah (drinks) the may (waters) of his own bawar (cistern);

Until I bawaa (come) and laqach (take / seize) you away to a aratz (Earth/land) like your own aratz (Earth/land), a aratz (Earth/land) of grain and new thayarawash (wine), a aratz (Earth/land) of lacham (bread) and karamayam (vineyards).

Beware lest Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) sawath (persuade) you, amar (spoke), "Yahawah will natzal (deliver) us." Have any of the Alahayam of the gawayam (nations) natzal (delivered) their aratz (Earth/land) from the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria)?
Where are the Alahayam of Chamath (Hamath) and Arapad (Arpad)? Where are the Alahayam of Saparawayam (Sepharvaim)? Have they natzal (delivered) Shamarawan (Samaria) from my yad (hand)?

Who are they among all the Alahayam of these aratzawath (countries) that have natzal (delivered) their aratz (Earth/land) out of my yad (hand), that Yahawah should natzal (deliver) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) out of my yad (hand)?'"
But they remained charash (silent), and inah (answer / respond) nothing in reply, for the malak (king) matzawah (commandment) was, "Don't dabar (word / matter) him."

Then Alayaqayam (Eliakim) the ban (son) of Chalaqayah (Hilkiah), who was over the bayath (house), and Shabanaa (Shebna) the sapar (book), and Yawaach (Joah), the ban (son) of Asap (Asaph), the zakar (remember), bawaa (come) to Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) with their clothes qarai (torn), and nagad (told) him the dabaray (words) of Rabashaqah (Rabshakeh).

It happened, when malak (king) Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) shamai (hearken / hear) it, that he qarai (tore) his clothes, kasah (covered) himself with sackcloth, and bawaa (come) into Yahawah bayath (house).

He shalach (send) Alayaqayam (Eliakim), who was over the bayath (house), and Shabanaa (Shebna) the sapar (book), and the zaqanay (elders) of the kahanayam (priests), kasah (covered) with sackcloth, to Yashaiyah (Isaiah) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), the ban (son) of Amawatz (Amoz).

They amar (spoke) to him, "Thus yaamaraw (says) Chazaqayah (Hezekiah), ‘This yawam (day) is a yawam (day) of tzarah (trouble), and of thawakachah (rebuke), and of rejection; for the banayam (children) bawaa (come) come to the mashabar (birth), and there is no kach (strength / mighty / power) to yalad (birth / begot) forth.

It may be Yahawah your Alahayam will shamai (hearken / hear) the dabaray (words) of Rabashaqah (Rabshakeh), whom the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria) his adawan (master / lord) has shalach (send) to charap (defy) the chay (life) Alahayam, and will yakach (rebuke) the dabaray (words) which Yahawah your Alahayam has shamai (hearken / hear). Therefore nashaa (lift) up your thapalah (prayer) for the shaarayath (remnant) that is matzaa (left).'"
So the ibaday (servants) of malak (king) Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) bawaa (come) to Yashaiyah (Isaiah).

Yashaiyah (Isaiah) amar (spoke) to them, "amar (spoke) your adawan (master / lord), ‘Thus thaamaraw (says) Yahawah, "Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of the dabarayam (words) that you have shamai (hearken / hear), with which the nairay (servants) of the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria) have gadap (blasphemed) me.

Behold, I will nathan (give) a rawach (spirit / wind) in him and he will shamai (hearken / hear) shamawaih (news), and will shawab (turn back / repent) to his own aratz (Earth/land). I will napal (fall / be cast down) him to fall by the charab (sword) in his own aratz (Earth/land)."'"

So Rabashaqah (Rabshakeh) shawab (turn back / repent), and matzaa (found) the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria) lacham (warring) against Labanah (Libnah), for he had shamai (hearken / hear) that he was departed from Lakayash (Lachish).

He shamai (hearken / hear) news concerning Tharahaqah (Tirhakah) malak (king) of Kawash (Ethiopia), "He yatzaa (go out / come out) come out to lacham (fight) against you." When he shamai (hearken / hear) it, he shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to Chazaqayah (Hezekiah), amar (spoke),

"Thus you shall amar (spoke) to Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), amar (spoke), ‘Don't let your Alahayam in whom you batach (trust) nashaa (lift) you, amar (spoke), "Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) won't be nathan (give) into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria)."

Behold, you have shamai (hearken / hear) what the malakay (kings) of Ashawar (Assyria) ishah (make) done to all aratzawath (lands), by charam (destroying) them utterly. Shall you be natzal (delivered)?

Have the Alahayam of the gawayam (nations) natzal (delivered) them, which my ab (father) have shachath (destroyed), Gawazan (Gozan), Charan (Haran), Ratzap (Rezeph), and the banay (children) of Idan (Eden) who were in Thalaashar (Telassar)?
Where is the malak (king) of Chamath (Hamath), and the malak (king) of Arapad (Arpad), and the malak (king) of the iyar (city) of Saparawayam (Sepharvaim), of Hanai (Hena), and Iwah (Ivvah)?'"

Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) laqach (take / seize) the sapar (book / scribed document) from the yad (hand) of the malaakayam (messengers) and qaraa (called) it. Then Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) ilah (go up / offer) up to Yahawah bayath (house), and parash (spread) it panayam (face) Yahawah.
Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) palal (prayed) to Yahawah, amar (spoke),

"Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), who is enthroned among the karawab (cherubim), you are the Alahayam, even you alone, of all the mamalakawath (kingdoms) of the aratz (Earth/land). You ishah (make) made shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) and aratz (Earth/land).

Natah (turn) your azan (ear), Yahawah, and shamai (hearken / hear). Paqach (open) your iyan (eye), Yahawah, and raah (see). Shamai (hearken / hear) all of the dabaray (words) of Sanacharayab (Sennacherib), who has shalach (send) to charap (defy) the chay (life) Alahayam.
Truly, Yahawah, the malakay (kings) of Ashawar (Assyria) have charab (destroyed) all the aratzawath (countries) and their aratz (Earth/land),

And nathan (give) cast their Alahayam into the ash (fire); for they were no Alahayam, but the maishah (work) of adam (men's) yaday (hands), itz (wood) and aban (stone); therefore they abad (destroy / perish) destroyed them.
Now therefore, Yahawah our Alahayam, yashai (salvation) us from his yad (hand), that all the mamalakawath (kingdoms) of the aratz (Earth/land) may yadai (know) that you are Yahawah, even you only."

Then Yashaiyah (Isaiah) the ban (son) of Amawatz (Amoz) shalach (send) to Chazaqayah (Hezekiah), amar (spoke), "Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), ‘Because you have palal (prayed) to me against Sanacharayab (Sennacherib) malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria),

This is the dabar (word / matter) which Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) concerning him. The bathawalah (virgin) banath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion) has bazah (despised) you and ridiculed you. The banath (daughter) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) has nawai (shaken) her raash (head) at you.

Whom have you charap (defied) and gadap (blasphemed)? Against whom have you rawam (will lift up) your qawal (sound / voice) and nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye) on marawam (high)? Against the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel).

By your ibad (servant), have you charap (defied) the Adanay, and have amar (spoke), "With the rab (multitude) of my rakab (chariots) I have ilah (go up / offer) up to the marawam (height) of the harayam (mountains), to the innermost yarakathay (parts) of Labanawan (Lebanon). I will karath (cut) down its qawamah (tall) araz (cedars) and its mabachar (choice) barawash (fir) trees. I will bawaa (come) into its farthest marawam (height), the yair (forest) of its Karamal (fruitful) field.
I have qawar (dug) and shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters), and with the kap (sole) of my paim (feet) I will charab (dry) up all the yaaray (rivers) of Matzawar (Egypt)."

Have you not shamai (hearken / hear) how I ishah (make) done it rachawaq (long) ago, and yatzar (formed) it in qadam (ancient) yamay (times)? Now I bawaa (come) brought it to pass, that it should be yours to shaah (destroy) batzar (fortified) irayam (cities), turning them into ruinous galayam (heaps).

Therefore their yashab (inhabit/dwell) had little yad (hand). They were chathath (dismayed) and bawash (confounded). They were like the ishab (grass) of the shadah (field), and like the yaraq (green) dashaa (herb), like the chatzayar (grass) on the housetops, and like a field panayam (face) its crop has qamah (grown).
But I yadai (know) your sitting down, your yatzaa (go out / come out) out, your bawaa (come) in, and your ragaz (raging) against me.

Because of your ragaz (raging) against me, and because your arrogance has ilah (go up / offer) up into my azan (ear), therefore will I shawam (place / establish / appoint) my chach (hook) in your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) and my mathag (bridle) in your shapah (lips), and I will shawab (turn back / repent) you back by the darak (way) by which you bawaa (come).

This shall be the awath (sign / mark / miracle) to you. You will akal (eat) this shanah (year) that which sapayach (grows) of itself, and in the shanay (second) shanah (year) that which springs from the same; and in the shalayashay (third) shanah (year) zarai (sow) and qatzar (reap) and natai (plant) karamayam (vineyards), and akal (eat) their paray (fruit).
The shaar (remnant) that is palayatah (escaped) of the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) will again take sharash (root) matah (downward), and ishah (make) paray (fruit) upward.

For out of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) a shaarayath (remnant) will yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and survivors will palayatah (escape) from har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion). The qanaah (zeal) of Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) will ishah (make) this.'

Therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah concerning the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria), ‘He will not bawaa (come) to this iyar (city), nor yarah (shoot) an chatz (arrow) there, neither will he qadam (come) before it with magan (shield), nor shapak (cast) up a mound against it.
By the darak (way) that he bawaa (come), by the same he shall shawab (turn back / repent), and he shall not bawaa (come) to this iyar (city),' naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.
‘For I will ganan (defend) this iyar (city) to yashai (salvation) it, for my own sake, and for my ibad (servant) Dawad (David's) sake.'"

The malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) out and nakah (struck) one maah (hundred) and shamanayam (eighty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) men in the machanah (camp) of the Ashawar (Assyrians). When men arose shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), behold, these were all mawath (death) pagarayam (bodies).
So Sanacharayab (Sennacherib) malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria) departed, yalak (went) shawab (turn back / repent), returned to Nayanawah (Nineveh), and stayed there.

It happened, as he was shachah (worshipping) in the bayath (house) of Nasarak (Nisroch) his Alahayam, that Adaramalak (Adrammelech) and Sharaatzar (Sharezer) his ban (son) nakah (struck) him with the charab (sword); and they malat (escaped) into the aratz (Earth/land) of Ararat (Ararat). Asarachadawan (Esar Haddon) his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.

In those yamayam (days) was Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) chalah (afflict) and near mawath (death). Yashaiyah (Isaiah) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), the ban (son) of Amawatz (Amoz), bawaa (come) to him, and amar (spoke) to him, "Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, ‘Set your bayath (house) in tzawah (order), for you will mawath (death), and not chayah (live).'"
Then Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) sabab (turned) his panayam (face) to the qayar (wall) and palal (prayed) to Yahawah,

And amar (spoke), "zakar (remember) now, Yahawah, I beg you, how I have halak (move) panayam (face) you in amath (truth) and with a shalam (full / whole / complete) lab (heart), and ishah (make) done that which is tawab (good / proper function) in your iyan (eye)." Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) bakah (wept) bitterly.
Then the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Yashaiyah (Isaiah), amar (spoke),

"Halak (move), and amar (spoke) Chazaqayah (Hezekiah), ‘Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Dawad (David) your ab (father), "I have shamai (hearken / hear) your thapalah (prayer). I raah (see) seen your damaih (tears). Behold, I will yasap (add) chamash (fifteen) shanah (years) to your yawam (day).
I will natzal (deliver) you and this iyar (city) out of the kap (hand) of the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria), and I will ganan (defend) this iyar (city).
This shall be the awath (sign / mark / miracle) to you from Yahawah, that Yahawah will ishah (make) this thing that he has dabar (word / matter).

Behold, I will cause the tzal (shadow) on the sundial, which has yarad (gone) down on the sundial of Achaz (Ahaz) with the sun, to shawab (turn back / repent) backward ishar (ten) mailawath (steps). So the shamash (sun) shawab (turn back / repent) ishar (ten) mailawath (steps) on the sundial on which it had yarad (gone) down."'"
The makathab (writing) of Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), when he had been chalah (afflict), and had chayah (recovered) of his chalay (sickness).
I amar (spoke), "In the middle of my yawam (day) I yalak (go) into the shairay (gates) of shaawal (Sheol / afterlife). I am deprived of the yathar (residue) of my shanah (years)."
I amar (spoke), "I won't raah (see) Yah, Yah in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life). I will nabat (see) adam (man) no more with the yawashabay (inhabitants) of the chadal (world).

My dwelling is nasai (removed), and is galah (carried) away from me like a shepherd's ahal (tent). I have rolled up, like a arag (weaver), my chay (life). He will batzai (cut) me off from the loom. From yawam (day) even to layal (night) you will shalam (make) an end of me.
I waited patiently until baqar (morning). He shabar (breaks) all my itzam (bones) like a aray (lion). From yawam (day) even to layal (night) you will shalam (make) an end of me.
I tzapap (chattered) like a igawar (swallow) or a sawas (crane). I moaned like a yawanah (dove). My iyan (eye) weaken looking marawam (upward). Adawan, I am ishaqah (oppressed). Be my security."
What will I dabar (word / matter)? He has both amar (spoke) to me, and himself ishah (make) done it. I will walk carefully all my shanah (years) because of the anguish of my napash (soul).
Adanay, men chayah (live) by these things; and my rawach (spirit / wind) finds chay (life) in all of them: you chalam (dream) me, and cause me to chayah (live).

Behold, for shalawam (peace / safety) I had mar (great) anguish, but you have in chashaq (love) for my napash (soul) delivered it from the shachath (pit) of balay (corruption); for you have shalak (cast) all my chataa (sins) achar (other) your gaw (back).
For shaawal (Sheol / afterlife) can't yadah (praise) you. Mawath (death) can't halal (praise) you. Those who yarad (go) down into the bawar (pit) can't shabar (hope) for your amath (truth).
The chay (life), the chay (life), he shall yadah (praise) you, as I do this yawam (day). The ab (father) shall yadai (make) known your amath (truth) to the banayam (children).
Yahawah will yashai (salvation) me. Therefore we will sing my naganawathay (songs) with nagan (stringed) instruments all the yamay (days) of our chay (life) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
Now Yashaiyah (Isaiah) had amar (spoke), "Let them nashaa (lift) a dabalah (fig cake) of thaanayam (figs), and marach (lay) it for a poultice on the shachayan (boil), and he shall chayah (recover)."
Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) also had amar (spoke), "What is the awath (sign / mark / miracle) that I will ilah (go up / offer) up to the bayath (house) of Yahawah?"

At that ith (time), Merodach Balaadan (Baladan) the ban (son) of Balaadan (Baladan), malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), shalach (send) saparayam (letters) and a manachah (present) to Chazaqayah (Hezekiah); for he shamai (hearken / hear) that he had been chalah (afflict), and had chazaq (recovered).

Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) was pleased with them, and showed them the bayath (house) of his nakath (precious) things, the kasap (silver), and the zahab (gold), the bashamayam (spices), and the tawab (good / proper function) shaman (oil), and all the bayath (house) of his armor, and all that was matzaa (found) in his awatzar (treasures). There was nothing in his bayath (house), nor in all his mamashalah (dominion), that Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) didn't show them.

Then Yashaiyah (Isaiah) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) bawaa (come) to malak (king) Chazaqayah (Hezekiah), and asked him, "What did these anashayam (men) amar (spoke)? Ayan (NO ONE) did they bawaa (come) from to you?" Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) amar (spoke), "They bawaa (come) come from a aratz (Earth/land) rachawaq (far) from me, even from Babal (Babylon)."

Then he asked, "What raah (see) they seen in your bayath (house)?" Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) amar (spoke), "They raah (see) seen all that is in my bayath (house). There is nothing among my awatzar (treasures) that I raah (see) not shown them."
Then Yashaiyah (Isaiah) amar (spoke) to Chazaqayah (Hezekiah), "shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies):

‘Behold, the yamayam (days) are bawaa (come) when all that is in your bayath (house), and that which your ab (father) have atzar (stored) up until this yawam (day), will be nashaa (lift) to Babal (Babylon). Nothing will be yathar (left),' amar (spoke) Yahawah.

‘They will laqach (take / seize) away your ban (son) who will yatzaa (go out / come out) from you, whom you shall yalad (birth / begot), and they will be sarayasayam (eunuchs) in the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon's) hayakal (palace).'"

Then Chazaqayah (Hezekiah) amar (spoke) to Yashaiyah (Isaiah), "Yahawah dabar (word / matter) which you have dabar (word / matter) is tawab (good / proper function)." He amar (spoke) moreover, "For there will be shalawam (peace / safety) and amath (truth) in my yawam (day)."
"Nacham (turn away / repent), nacham (turn away / repent) my im (nation / people)," amar (spoke) your Alahayam.

"Dabar (word / matter) lab (heart) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); and qaraa (called) out to her that her tzabaa (troop) is malaa (accomplished), that her iwan (guilt/iniquity) is ratzah (pardoned), that she has laqach (take / seize) of Yahawah yad (hand) kapal (double) for all her chataah (sin)."

The qawal (sound / voice) of one who qaraa (called) out, "panah (turn) the darak (way) of Yahawah in the irabah (wilderness)! Yashar (upright) a level masalah (highway) in the irabah (desert) for our Alahayam.

Every gayaa (valley) shall be nashaa (lift), and every har (mountain) and gabaih (hill) shall be shapal (made) low. The uneven shall be made mayashawar (level), and the rakas (rough) places a baqaih (plain).
The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah shall be galah (revealed), and all bashar (flesh) shall raah (see) it yachad (together); for the pah (mouth) of Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) it."

The qawal (sound / voice) of one amar (spoke), "qaraa (called)!" One amar (spoke), "What shall I qaraa (called)?" "All bashar (flesh) is like chatzayar (grass), and all its glory is like the tzayatz (flower) of the shadah (field).

The chatzayar (grass) yabash (dry land), the tzayatz (flower) nabal (fades), because Yahawah rawach (spirit / wind) nashab (blows) on it. Akan (surely) the im (nation / people) are like chatzayar (grass).
The chatzayar (grass) yabash (dry land), the tzayatz (flower) nabal (fades); but the dabar (word / matter) of our Alahayam qawam (rise up) iwalam (forever)."

You who tell bashar (good) news to Tzayawan (Zion), ilah (go up / offer) up on a gabah (high) har (mountain). You who tell bashar (good) news to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), rawam (will lift up) up your qawal (sound / voice) with kach (strength / mighty / power). Rawam (will lift up) it up. Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). Amar (spoke) to the iray (cities) of Yahawadah (Judah), "Behold, your Alahayam!"

Behold, the Adanay Yahawah will bawaa (come) as a chazaq (mighty) one, and his zarawai (arm) will mashal (rule/have dominion) for him. Behold, his shakar (reward) is with him, and his recompense panayam (face) him.

He will raih (feed) his idar (flock) like a raih (shepherd). He will qabatz (gather) the talaayam (lambs) in his zarawai (arm), and nashaa (lift) them in his chayaq (bosom). He will nahal (gently) lead those who have their iwal (young).

Who has madad (measured) the mayam (Waters) in the hollow of his shail (hand), and marked off the sky with his zarath (span), and calculated the ipar (dust) of the aratz (Earth/land) in a shalayash (measure), and shaqal (weighed) the harayam (mountains) in palas (scales), and the gabaiwath (hills) in a maazan (balance)?
Who has thakan (directed) the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah, or yadai (has) taught him as his counselor?

Who did he take yaitz (counsel) with, and who bayan (between) him, and lamad (teach / instruct) him in the arach (path) of mashapat (justice), and lamad (teach / instruct) him daith (knowledge), and showed him the darak (way) of thabawan (understanding)?

Behold, the gawayam (nations) are like a mar (drop) in a dalay (bucket), and are chashab (regarded) as a speck of shachaq (dust) on a maazan (balance). Behold, he lifts up the ayayam (islands) like a very daq (little) thing.
Labanawan (Lebanon) is not day (sufficient) to bair (burn), nor its animals day (sufficient) for a burnt ilah (offering).
All the gawayam (nations) are chashab (like) nothing before him. They are regarded by him as apas (less) than nothing, and thahaw (formless).
To whom then will you damah (liken) Al? Or what damawath (likeness) will you irak (compare) to him?
A charash (workman) has cast an pasal (image), and the tzarap (goldsmith) overlays it with zahab (gold), and tzarap (casts) kasap (silver) rathaqawath (chains) for it.

He who is too sakan (impoverished) for such an tharawamah (offering) bachar (chooses) a itz (tree) that will not raqab (rot). He baqash (seeks) a skillful charash (workman) to kawan (set) up an engraved pasal (image) for him that will not be mawat (moved).

Haven't you yadai (known)? Haven't you shamai (hearken / hear), yet? Haven't you been nagad (told) from the raash (head)? Haven't you bayan (between) from the mawasadawath (foundations) of the aratz (Earth/land)?

It is he who yashab (inhabit/dwell) above the chawag (circle) of the aratz (Earth/land), and its yashab (inhabit/dwell) are like grasshoppers; who stretches out the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) like a daq (curtain), and mathach (spreads) them out like a ahal (tent) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) in;
Who nathan (give) rawazanayam (princes) to nothing; who ishah (make) the shapatay (judges) of the aratz (Earth/land) like meaningless.

They are natai (planted) scarcely. They are zarai (sown) scarcely. Their gazai (stock) has scarcely sharash (taken) root in the aratz (Earth/land). He merely nashap (blows) on them, and they yabash (dry land), and the sair (whirlwind) nashaa (lift) them away as qash (stubble).
"To whom then will you damah (liken) me? Who is my shawah (equal)?" Amar (spoke) the qadawash (holy) One.

Nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye) on marawam (high), and raah (see) who has baraa (created) these, who yatzaa (go out / come out) out their tzabaa (troop) by masapar (number). He qaraa (called) them all by sham (name). By the greatness of his awan (might), and because he is amayatz (strong) in kach (strength / mighty / power), Not ayash (man / husband) is idar (lacking).

Why do you amar (spoke), Yaiqab (Jacob), and dabar (word / matter), Yashar-Al (Israel), "My darak (way) is sathar (hidden) from Yahawah, and the mashapat (justice) due me is disregarded by my Alahayam?"

Haven't you yadai (known)? Haven't you shamai (hearken / hear)? The iwalam (forever) Alahayam, Yahawah, The Creator of the ends of the aratz (Earth/land), doesn't yaip (faint). He isn't yagai (weary). His thabawan (understanding) is unsearchable.
He nathan (give) kach (strength / mighty / power) to the weak. He rabah (increases) the itzamah (strength) of him who has no awan (might).
Even the youths yaip (faint) and get yagai (weary), and the bachawar (young) men kashal (stumble / stagger) kashal (stumble / stagger);

But those who qawah (gather/wait) for Yahawah will chalap (renew) their kach (strength / mighty / power). They will ilah (go up / offer) up with abar (wings) like nasharayam (eagles). They will rawatz (run), and not be yagai (weary). They will yalak (walk), and not yaip (faint).

"Charash (keep) silent before me, ayayam (islands), and let the laamayam (peoples) chalap (renew) their kach (strength / mighty / power). Let them nagash (come) near, then let them dabar (word / matter). Let's meet yachad (together) for mashapat (judgment).

Who has iwar (rouse / awaken) up one from the mazarach (east)? Who qaraa (called) him to his ragal (feet / foot) in tzadaq (righteous / just / fair)? He nathan (give) over gawayam (nations) to him, and radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) him rule over malakayam (kings). He nathan (give) them like the ipar (dust) to his charab (sword), like the nadap (driven) qash (stubble) to his qashath (bow).
He radap (pursues) them, and passes by safely, Even by a arach (way) that he bawaa (come) not gone with his ragal (feet / foot).
Who has pail (worked) and ishah (make) it, qaraa (called) the darawath (generations) from the raash (head)? I, Yahawah, the raashawan (first), and with the acharawan (last), I am he."
The ayayam (islands) raah (see) seen, and yaraa (fear / be afraid). The ends of the aratz (Earth/land) charad (tremble). They qarab (come close), and athah (you (masc)).
Everyone yaizaraw (helps) his neighbor. They amar (spoke) to their ach (brother/kinsman), "Be chazaq (strong)!"

So the charash (carpenter) chazaq (encourages) the tzarap (goldsmith). He who smoothes with the patayash (hammer) encourages him who strikes the paim (anvil), amar (spoke) of the dabaq (soldering), "It is tawab (good / proper function);" and he chazaq (fastens) it with masamarayam (nails), that it might not totter.
"But you, Yashar-Al (Israel), my ibad (servant), Yaiqab (Jacob) whom I have bachar (chosen), the zarai (seed) of Abaraham (Abraham) my ahab (love),

You whom I have chazaq (taken) hold of from the ends of the aratz (Earth/land), and qaraa (called) from its corners, and amar (spoke) to you, ‘You are my ibad (servant), I have bachar (chosen) you and not maas (cast) you away;'

Don't you be yaraa (fear / be afraid), for I am with you. Don't be shaih (dismayed), for I am your Alahayam. I will amatz (strengthen) you. Yes, I will izar (help) you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right yamayan (right hand) of my tzadaq (righteous / just / fair).
Behold, all those who are charah (hot with anger) against you will be disappointed and kalam (confounded). Those who rayab (strive) with you will be like nothing, and shall abad (destroy / perish).
You will baqash (seek) them, and won't matzaa (find) them, even those who contend with you. Those who malachamah (war) against you will be as apas (nothing), as a non-existent thing.
For I, Yahawah your Alahayam, will chazaq (hold) your right yamayan (right hand), amar (spoke) to you, ‘Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). I will izar (help) you.'

Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), you thawalai (worm) Yaiqab (Jacob), and you mathay (men) of Yashar-Al (Israel). I will izar (help) you," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, "and your gaal (redeemer) is the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Behold, I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) you into a chadash (new) charawatz (sharp) mawarag (threshing) instrument with payapayawath (teeth). You will dawash (thresh) the harayam (mountains), and daqaq (beat) them small, and will shawam (place / establish / appoint) the gabaiwath (hills) like matz (chaff).

You will zarah (winnow) them, and the rawach (spirit / wind) will nashaa (lift) them away, and the sair (whirlwind) will pawatz (scatter) them. You will gayal (rejoice) in Yahawah. You will glory in the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel).

The inay (poor) and abayawan (needy) baqash (seek) mayam (Waters), and there is none. Their lashawan (tongue / language) nashath (fails) for tzamaa (thirst). I, Yahawah, will inah (answer / respond) them. I, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), will not izab (forsake) them.

I will pathach (open) naharawath (rivers) on the bare heights, and maiyanawath (springs) in the thawak (midst) of the baqaiwath (valleys). I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) the madabar (wilderness) a agam (pool) of mayam (Waters), and the tzayah (dry) aratz (Earth/land) mawatzaay (springs) of mayam (Waters).

I will nathan (give) araz (cedar), acacia, hadas (myrtle), and shaman (oil) trees in the madabar (wilderness). I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) fir itz (trees), thadahar (pine), and box trees yachad (together) in the irabah (desert);

That they may raah (see), yadai (know), shawam (place / establish / appoint), and shakal (understand) yachad (together), that the yad (hand) of Yahawah ishah (make) done this, and the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel) has baraa (created) it.
Qarab (come close) your rayab (cause)," amar (spoke) Yahawah. "Nagash (bring) forth your itzawamah (bulwark / argument) reasons," amar (spoke) the malak (king) of Yaiqab (Jacob).

"Let them announce, and nagad (declare) to us what shall qarah (happen). Nagad (declare) the raashawan (former) things, what they are, that we may shawam (place / establish / appoint) them, and yadai (know) the acharayath (latter) end of them; or show us things to bawaa (come).

Nagad (declare) the things that are to athah (you (masc)) achawar (hereafter), that we may yadai (know) that you are Alahayam. Yes, do yatab (good), or do raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil), that we may be shaih (dismayed), and raah (see) it yachad (together).
Behold, you are of ayan (NO ONE), and your pail (work) is of nothing. He who bachar (chooses) you is an thawaibah (abomination).

"I have iwar (rouse / awaken) up one from the tzapawan (north), and he has athah (you (masc)); from the mazarach (rising) of the shamash (sun), one who qaraa (called) on my sham (name); and he shall bawaa (come) on saganayam (rulers) as on mortar, and as the yatzar (potter) ramas (treads) tayat (clay).

Who has nagad (declared) it from the raash (head), that we may yadai (know)? And panayam (face), that we may amar (spoke), ‘He is right?' Nagad (surely), there is no one who declares. Shamai (hearken / hear), there is no one who shows. Shamai (hearken / hear), there is no one who hears your amar (spoke).
I am the raashawan (first) to say to Tzayawan (Zion), ‘hanah (Behold), look at them;' and I will nathan (give) one who brings bashar (good) news to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).
When I raah (see), there is no ayash (man / husband); even among them there is no yaitz (counselor) who, when I shaal (ask) of them, can shawab (turn back / repent) a dabar (word / matter).
Behold, all of them, their maishah (works) are awan (vanity) and apas (nothing). Their molten nasak (images) are rawach (spirit / wind) and thahaw (formless).

"Behold, my ibad (servant), whom I uphold; my bachayar (chosen), in whom my napash (soul) ratzah (delights)— I nathan (give) put my rawach (spirit / wind) on him. He will yatzaa (go out / come out) mashapat (justice) to the gawayam (nations).
He will not shout, nor nashaa (lift) his qawal (sound / voice), nor shamai (hearken / hear) it to be heard in the chawatz (street).
He won't shabar (break) a ratzatz (bruised) qanah (reed). He won't kabah (quench) a dimly burning wick. He will faithfully yatzaa (go out / come out) mashapat (justice).

He will not kahah (fail) nor be ratzatz (discouraged), until he has shawam (place / establish / appoint) mashapat (justice) in the aratz (Earth/land), and the ayayam (islands) will yachal (wait) for his thawarah (instruction)."

Thus amar (spoke) Al Yahawah, he who baraa (created) the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) and natah (stretched) them out, he who raqai (spread) out the aratz (Earth/land) and that which comes out of it, he who nathan (give) nashamah (breathing thing) to its im (nation / people) and rawach (spirit / wind) to those who halak (move) in it.

"I, Yahawah, have qaraa (called) you in tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and will chazaq (hold) your yad (hand), and will natzar (keep) you, and nathan (give) you a barayath (covenant) for the im (nation / people), as a awar (light) for the gawayam (nations);
To paqach (open) the iwar (blind) iyanayam (eyes), to bring the asayar (prisoners) out of the dungeon, and those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in chashak (darkness) out of the kalaa (prison).
"I am Yahawah. That is my sham (name). I will not nathan (give) my kabawad (glory) to achar (other), nor my thahalah (praise) to engraved pasayalayam (images).
Behold, the raashawan (former) things bawaa (come) happened, and I nagad (declare) chadash (new) things. I shamai (hearken / hear) you about them before they come up."

Shayar (sing) to Yahawah a chadash (new) shayar (song), and his thahalah (praise) from the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land), you who yarad (go) down to the yam (sea/waters), and malaa (all) that is therein, the ayayam (islands) and their yashab (inhabit/dwell).

Let the madabar (wilderness) and its iyar (cities) nashaa (lift) their voices, with the chatzarayam (villages) that Qadar (Kedar) yashabay (inhabits). Let the yashabay (inhabitants) of Sela ranan (sing). Let them tzawach (shout) from the raash (head) of the harayam (mountains)!
Let them shawam (place / establish / appoint) kabawad (glory) to Yahawah, and nagad (declare) his thahalah (praise) in the ayayam (islands).

Yahawah will yatzaa (go out / come out) out like a gabawar (mighty) man. He will iwar (rouse / awaken) up qanaah (zeal) like a ayash (man / husband) of malachamah (war). He will raise a war rawai (cry). Yes, he will shout aloud. He will triumph over his ayab (enemy).

"I have been chashah (silent) a iwalam (forever) time. I have been charash (quiet) and apaq (restrained) myself. Now I will paih (cry) out like a travailing yalad (birth / begot). I will yachad (both) gasp and shaap (pant).

I will charab (destroy) harayam (mountains) and gabaiwath (hills), and yabash (dry land) up all their ishab (herbs). I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) the naharawath (rivers) ayayam (islands), and will yabash (dry land) up the agamayam (pools).

I will yalak (bring) the iwar (blind) by a darak (way) that they don't yadai (know). I will darak (lead) them in nathayabawath (paths) that they don't yadai (know). I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) machashak (darkness) awar (light) panayam (face) them, and maiqash (crooked) places mayashawar (straight). I will ishah (make) these things, and I will not izab (forsake) them.
"Those who batach (trust) in engraved pasal (image), who amar (spoke) molten pasal (image), ‘You are our Alahayam' will be sawag (turned) achawar (back). They will be utterly disappointed.
"Shamai (hearken / hear), you charash (deaf), and nabat (look), you iwar (blind), that you may raah (see).

Who is iwar (blind), but my ibad (servant)? Or who is as charash (deaf) as my malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) whom I shalach (send)? Who is as iwar (blind) as he who is at shalam (peace), and as iwar (blind) as Yahawah ibad (servant)?
You raah (see) many things, but don't shamar (keep/guard). His azanayam (ears) are paqach (open), but he doesn't shamai (hearken / hear).
It chapatz (pleased) Yahawah, for his tzadaq (righteous / just / fair)' sake, to gadal (magnify) the thawarah (instruction), and make it honorable.

But this is a bazaz (robbed) and plundered im (nation / people). All of them are pachach (snared) in chawarayam (holes), and they are chabaa (hidden) in kalaayam (prisons). They have become a baz (prey), and no one natzal (delivers); and a mashasah (spoil), and no one amar (spoke), ‘shawab (turn back / repent) them!'
Who is there among you who will azan (ear) ear to this? Who will listen and shamai (hearken / hear) for the achawar (time) to come?

Who nathan (give) Yaiqab (Jacob) as plunder, and Yashar-Al (Israel) to the bazazayam (robbers)? Didn't Yahawah, he against whom we have chataa (sinned)? For they would not halak (move) in his darak (ways), and they disobeyed his thawarah (instruction).

Therefore he shapak (poured) the fierceness of his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) on him, and the izawaz (strength) of malachamah (battle); and it set him on lahat (fire) all around, but he didn't yadai (know); and it bair (burned) him, but he didn't shawam (place / establish / appoint) it to lab (heart)."

But now thus amar (spoke) Yahawah who baraa (created) you, Yaiqab (Jacob), and he who yatzar (formed) you, Yashar-Al (Israel): "Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), for I have gaal (redeemed) you. I have qaraa (called) you by your sham (name). You are mine.

When you ibar (pass over/through) through the mayam (Waters), I will be with you; and ibar (pass over/through) the naharawath (rivers), they will not shatap (overflow) you. When you yalak (walk) bamaw (through) the ash (fire), you will not be kawah (burned), and lahabah (flame) will not scorch you.

For I am Yahawah your Alahayam, the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel), your Savior. I nathan (give) given Matzarayam (Egypt) as your kapar (ransom), Kawash (Ethiopia) and Sabaa (Seba) in your place.

Since you have been yaqar (precious) and honored in my iyan (eye), and I have ahab (love) you; therefore I will nathan (give) adam (people) in your place, and laamayam (nations) instead of your napash (soul).
Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid); for I am with you. I will bawaa (come) your zarai (seed) from the mazarach (east), and qabatz (gather) you from the mairab (west).

I will amar (spoke) the tzapawan (north), ‘nathan (give) them up!' And tell the thayaman (south), ‘Don't hold them back! Bawaa (come) my ban (son) from rachawaq (far), and my banath (daughter) from the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land)—
Everyone who is qaraa (called) by my sham (name), and whom I have baraa (created) for my kabawad (glory), whom I have yatzar (formed), yes, whom I ishah (make) made.'"
Yatzaa (go out / come out) out the iwar (blind) im (nation / people) who yash (have) iyanayam (eyes), and the charash (deaf) who have azanayam (ears).

Let all the gawayam (nations) be qabatz (gathered) yachad (together), and let the laamayam (peoples) be asap (assembled). Who among them can nagad (declare) this, and show us raashawan (former) things? Nathan (give) them bring their witnesses, that they may be justified; or shamai (hearken / hear) them hear, and amar (spoke), "That is amath (truth)."

"You are my witnesses," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, "With my ibad (servant) whom I have bachar (chosen); that you may yadai (know) and aman (believe / have faith) me, and bayan (between) that I am he. Panayam (face) me there was no Al yatzar (formed), neither will there be achar (other) me.
I myself am Yahawah; and balaiday (besides) me there is no savior.

I have nagad (declared), I have yashai (salvation), and I have shown; and there was no zawar (strange) Alahayam among you. Therefore you are my witnesses," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, "and I am Al.
Yes, since the yawam (day) was I am he; and there is no one who can natzal (deliver) out of my yad (hand). I will pail (work), and who can shawab (turn back / repent) it?"

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, your gaal (redeemer), the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel): "For your sake, I have shalach (send) to Babal (Babylon), and I will bring all of them down as fugitives, even the Kashaday (Chaldeans), in the anayawath (ships) of their ranah (rejoicing).
I am Yahawah, your qadawash (holy) One, the Creator of Yashar-Al (Israel), your malak (king)."
Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, who nathan (give) a darak (way) in the yam (sea/waters), and a nathayab (path) in the iz (mighty) mayam (Waters);

Who yatzaa (go out / come out) forth the rakab (chariot) and sawas (horse), the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) and the izawaz (mighty) man (they shakab (lie) down yachad (together), they shall not qawam (rise up); they are daik (extinct), they are kabah (quenched) like a wick):
"Don't zakar (remember) the raashawan (former) things, and don't bayan (between) the things of qadamawanay (old).

Behold, I will ishah (make) a chadash (new) thing. It tzamach (springs) forth now. Don't you yadai (know) it? I will even shawam (place / establish / appoint) a darak (way) in the madabar (wilderness), and naharawath (rivers) in the yashayamawan (desert).

The animals of the shadah (field) shall honor me, the jackals and the ostriches; because I nathan (give) mayam (Waters) in the madabar (wilderness) and naharawath (rivers) in the yashayamawan (desert), to shaqah (give) drink to my im (nation / people), my bachayar (chosen),
The im (nation / people) which I yatzar (formed) for myself, that they might set sapar (book) my thahalah (praise).
Yet you have not qaraa (called) on me, Yaiqab (Jacob); but you have been yagai (weary) of me, Yashar-Al (Israel).

You bawaa (come) not brought me of your shah (sheep) for burnt ilah (offerings); neither kabad (have) you honored me with your zabach (sacrifices). I have not burdened you with manachah (offerings), nor yagai (wearied) you with labawanah (frankincense).

You have bought me no sweet qanah (cane) with kasap (money), nor have you rawah (filled) me with the chalab (fat) of your zabach (sacrifices); but you have burdened me with your chataah (sin). You have yagai (wearied) me with your iwan (guilt/iniquity).
I, even I, am he who machah (blots) out your pashai (transgressions) for my own sake; and I will not zakar (remember) your chataah (sin).
Zakar (remember) me in remembrance. Let us shapat (judge / judgement) yachad (together). Set sapar (book) your case, that you may be justified.
Your raashawan (first) ab (father) chataa (sinned), and your lawatz (teachers) have pashai (transgressed) against me.
Therefore I will chalal (profane) the sharay (princes) of the qadash (set apart / make holy); and I will nathan (give) Yaiqab (Jacob) a charam (curse), and Yashar-Al (Israel) an insult."
Yet shamai (hearken / hear) now, Yaiqab (Jacob) my ibad (servant), and Yashar-Al (Israel), whom I have bachar (chosen).

This is what Yahawah who ishah (make) you, and yatzar (formed) you from the batan (womb), who will izar (help) you amar (spoke): "Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), Yaiqab (Jacob) my ibad (servant); and you, Yasharawan (Jeshurun), whom I have bachar (chosen).

For I will yatzaq (pour) mayam (Waters) on him who is thirsty, and nazalayam (streams) on the dry yabashah (dry land). I will yatzaq (pour) my rawach (spirit / wind) on your zarai (seed), and my barakah (blessing) on your tzaatzaa (offspring):
And they will tzamach (spring) up bayan (between) the chatzayar (grass), as irabayam (willows) by the yabalay (watercourses).

One will amar (spoke), ‘I am Yahawah;' and another will be qaraa (called) by the sham (name) of Yaiqab (Jacob); and another will kathab (write) with his yad (hand) ‘to Yahawah,' and honor the sham (name) of Yashar-Al (Israel)."

This is what Yahawah, the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and his gaal (redeemer), Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), amar (spoke): "I am the raashawan (first), and I am the acharawan (last); and balaiday (besides) me there is no Alahayam.

Who is like me? Who will qaraa (called), and will nagad (declare) it, and irak (set) it in order for me, since I established the iwalam (forever) im (nation / people)? Let them nagad (declare) the things that are bawaa (come), and that will happen.

Don't pachad (fear / dread), neither be rahah (afraid). Haven't I nagad (declared) it to you long ago, and shown it? You are my witnesses. Is there a Alawah balaiday (besides) me? Indeed, there is not. I don't yadai (know) any other tzawar (rock)."

Everyone who yatzaray (makes) an engraved pasal (image) is thahaw (formless). The things that they delight in will not yail (profit). Their own witnesses don't raah (see), nor yadai (know), that they may be disappointed.
Who has yatzar (fashioned) a Al, or molds an pasal (image) that is profitable for balathay (without)?

Behold, all his chabar (fellows) will be disappointed; and the workmen are mere adam (men). Let them all be qabatz (gathered) together. Let them imad (stand) up. They will pachad (fear / dread). They will be bawash (put) to shame yachad (together).

The blacksmith takes an axe, pail (works) in the pacham (coals), yatzar (fashions) it with maqabawath (hammers), and pail (works) it with his strong zarawai (arm). He is raib (hungry), and his kach (strength / mighty / power) ayan (NO ONE); he shathah (drinks) no mayam (Waters), and is yaip (faint).

The charash (carpenter) stretches out a qaw (line). He thaar (marks) it out with a pencil. He shapes it with maqatzaiwath (planes). He thaar (marks) it out with compasses, and shapes it like the thabanayath (figure) of a ayash (man / husband), with the thapaarah (beauty) of a adam (man), to reside in a bayath (house).

He karath (cut) down arazayam (cedars) for himself, and laqach (take / seize) the tharazah (cypress) and the alawan (oak), and amatz (strengthens) for himself one among the itzay (trees) of the yair (forest). He natai (plants) a fir tree, and the gasham (rain) nourishes it.

Then it will be for a adam (man) to bair (burn); and he laqach (take / seize) some of it, and chamam (warms) himself. Yes, he bair (burns) it, and apah (bakes) lacham (bread). Yes, he pail (makes) a Al, and shachah (worships) it; he ishah (make) it an engraved pasal (image), and sagad (falls) down to it.

He sharap (burns) chatzay (part) of it in the ash (fire). With chatzay (part) of it, he akal (eat) meat. He tzalay (roasts) a tzalah (roast), and is shabai (satisfied). Yes, he chamam (warms) himself, and amar (spoke), "haach (aha)! I am chamam (warm). I raah (see) seen the awar (light)."

The shaarayath (rest) of it he ishah (make) into a Al, even his engraved pasal (image). He bows down to it and shachah (worships), and palal (prays) to it, and amar (spoke), "natzal (deliver) me; for you are my Al!"
They don't yadai (know), neither do they bayan (between): for he has shut their iyan (eye), that they can't raah (see); and their lab (heart), that they can't shakal (understand).

No lab (heart) thinks, neither is there daith (knowledge) nor thabawan (understanding) to amar (spoke), "I have sharap (burned) chatzay (part) of it in the ash (fire). Yes, I have also apah (baked) lacham (bread) on its gachal (coals). I have tzalah (roasted) meat and akal (eat) it. Shall I ishah (make) the yathar (rest) of it into an thawaibah (abomination)? Shall I bow down to a itz (tree) trunk?"

He raih (feeds) on ashes. A hathal (deceived) lab (heart) has natah (turned) him aside; and he can't natzal (deliver) his napash (soul), nor amar (spoke), "Isn't there a shaqar (lie) in my right yamayan (right hand)?"

Zakar (remember) these things, Yaiqab (Jacob) and Yashar-Al (Israel); for you are my ibad (servant). I have yatzar (formed) you. You are my ibad (servant). Yashar-Al (Israel), you will not be nashah (forgotten) by me.
I have machah (blotted) out, as a ib (thick) cloud, your pashai (transgressions), and, as a inan (cloud), your chataah (sin). Shawab (turn back / repent) to me, for I have gaal (redeemed) you.

Ranan (sing), you shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), for Yahawah ishah (make) done it! Rawai (shout), you lower thachathayawath (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land)! Patzach (break) out into ranah (singing), you harayam (mountains), O yair (forest), all of your itz (trees), for Yahawah has gaal (redeemed) Yaiqab (Jacob), and will paar (glorify) himself in Yashar-Al (Israel).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, your gaal (redeemer), and he who yatzar (formed) you from the batan (womb): "I am Yahawah, who ishah (make) all things; who natah (alone) stretches out the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens); who natah (spreads) out the aratz (Earth/land) by myself;

Who parar (frustrates) the athawath (signs) of the badayam (liars), and makes diviners halal (praise); who shawab (turn back / repent) chakam (wise) men backward, and makes their daith (knowledge) foolish;

Who qawam (rise up) the dabar (word / matter) of his ibad (servant), and shalam (performs) the itzah (counsel) of his malaak (angel / messenger of Yah); who amar (spoke) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), ‘She will be yashab (inhabit/dwell);' and of the iray (cities) of Yahawadah (Judah), ‘They will be banah (build),' and ‘I will qawam (rise up) up its charabah (waste) places;'
Who amar (spoke) to the tzawalah (deep), ‘Be charab (dry),' and ‘I will yabash (dry land) up your nahar (rivers);'

Who amar (spoke) of Kawarash (Cyrus), ‘He is my shepherd, and shall shalam (perform) all my chapatz (pleasure),' even amar (spoke) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), ‘She will be banah (build);' and of the hayakal (temple), ‘Your yasad (foundation) will be laid.'"

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah to his mashayach (anointed one), to Kawarash (Cyrus), whose right yamayan (right hand) I have chazaq (held), to radad (subdue) gawayam (nations) panayam (face) him, and strip malakayam (kings) of their armor; to pathach (open) the dalathayam (doors) panayam (face) him, and the dalathayam (gates) shall not be sagar (shut):

"I will yalak (go) panayam (face) you, and yashar (upright) the rough hadawarayam (places) smooth. I will break the dalathawath (doors) of nachawashah (brass) in shabar (pieces), and gadai (cut) apart the barayachay (bars) of barazal (iron).

I will nathan (give) you the awatzarawath (treasures) of chashak (darkness), and matamawan (hidden) riches of masathar (secret) places, that you may yadai (know) that it is I, Yahawah, who qaraa (called) you by your sham (name), even the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel).

For Yaiqab (Jacob) my ibad (servant) sake, and Yashar-Al (Israel) my bachayar (chosen), I have qaraa (called) you by your sham (name). I have kanah (surnamed) you, though you yadai (have) not known me.
I am Yahawah, and there is none else. Zawalah (besides) me, there is no Alahayam. I will strengthen you, though you yadai (have) not known me;
That they may yadai (know) from the mazarach (rising) of the shamash (sun), and from the mairab (west), that there is apas (none) balaiday (besides) me. I am Yahawah, and there is no one else.

I yatzar (form) the awar (light), and baraa (created) chashak (darkness). I ishah (make) shalawam (peace / safety), and baraa (created) rai (calamity). I am Yahawah, who ishah (make) all these things.

Raip (distil), you shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), from mail (top/above), and let the shachaqayam (skies) nazal (pour) down tzadaq (righteous / just / fair). Let the aratz (Earth/land) pathach (open), that it may parah (bring) forth yashai (salvation), and let it cause tzadaqah (righteousness) to tzamach (spring) up with it. I, Yahawah, have baraa (created) it.

Haway (Alas/Woe!) To him who rayab (strives) with his yatzar (maker)— a clay pot among the clay pots of the adamah (earth)! Shall the chamar (clay) ask him who yatzar (fashions) it, ‘What are you ishah (make)?' Or your pail (work), ‘He has no yadayam (hands)?'
Haway (Alas/Woe!) To him who amar (spoke) to a ab (father), ‘What have you become the yalad (birth / begot) of?' Or to a ayashah (woman / wife), ‘To what have you given birth?'"

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel), and his yatzar (maker): "You shaal (ask) me about the things that are to athah (you (masc)), concerning my ban (son), and you tzawah (command) me concerning the pail (work) of my yad (hand)!

I ishah (make) made the aratz (Earth/land), and baraa (created) adam (man) on it. I, even my yad (hand), have natah (stretched) out the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens); and I have tzawah (commanded) all their tzabaa (troop).

I have iwar (rouse / awaken) him up in tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and I will make yashar (upright) all his darak (ways). He shall banah (build) my iyar (city), and he shall let my exiles shalach (send) free, not for machayar (price) nor shachad (reward)," amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: "The yagayai (labor) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and the sachar (merchandise) of Kawash (Ethiopia), and the Sabaay (Sabeans), anashay (men) of madah (stature), shall ibar (pass over/through) over to you, and they shall be yours. They will yalak (go) achar (other) you. They shall ibar (pass over/through) over in zaqayam (chains); and they will shachah (bow) down to you. They will palal (make) supplication to you: ‘Surely Alahayam is in you; and there is apas (none) else. There is no other Alahayam.
Most akan (certainly) you are a Al who sathar (hidden) yourself, Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), the Savior.'"
They will be disappointed, yes, kalam (confounded), all of them. Those who are charashay (makers) of tzayarayam (idols) will halak (move) into kalamah (confusion) yachad (together).
Yashar-Al (Israel) will be yashai (salvation) by Yahawah with an iwalam (forever) thashawaih (deliverance). You will not be disappointed nor bawash (confounded) to ages id (until / as far as).

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah who baraa (created) the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), the Alahayam who yatzar (formed) the aratz (Earth/land) and ishah (make) it, who kawan (established) it and didn't baraa (created) it a thahaw (formless), who yatzar (formed) it to be yashab (inhabit/dwell): "I am Yahawah; and there is no other.

I have not dabar (word / matter) in sathar (secret / hidden), in a maqawam (place) of the aratz (Earth/land) of chashak (darkness). I didn't amar (spoke) to the zarai (seed) of Yaiqab (Jacob), ‘baqash (seek) me in thahaw (formless).' I, Yahawah, dabar (word / matter) tzadaq (righteous / just / fair). I nagad (declare) things that are mayashar (right).

"Qabatz (assemble) yourselves and bawaa (come). Nagash (draw) near yachad (together), you who have palayat (escaped) from the gawayam (nations). Those have no yadai (knowledge) who nashaa (lift) the itz (wood) of their engraved pasal (image), and palal (pray) to a Al that can't yashai (salvation).

Nagad (declare) and nagash (present) it. Yes, let them take yaitz (counsel) yachad (together). Who has shown this from qadam (ancient) time? Who has nagad (declared) it of old? Haven't I, Yahawah? There is no other Alahayam balaiday (besides) me, a tzadayaq (righteous) Al and a Savior; There is no ayan (NO ONE) zawalah (besides) me.
"Panah (turn) to me, and be yashai (salvation), all the apasay (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land); for I am Al, and there is no other.

I have shabai (swear / take oath) by myself, the dabar (word / matter) yatzaa (go out / come out) gone out of my pah (mouth) in tzadaqah (righteousness), and will not shawab (turn back / repent), that to me every barak (blessed) shall karai (bow), every lashawan (tongue / language) shall take an shabai (swear / take oath).

They will amar (spoke) of me, ‘There is tzadaqah (righteousness) and iz (strength / might / refuge) only in Yahawah.'" Even to him shall men bawaa (come); and all those who were charah (hot with anger) against him shall be disappointed.
In Yahawah shall all the zarai (seed) of Yashar-Al (Israel) be justified, and shall glory.

Bal (Bel) karai (bows) down, Nabaw (Nebo) qaras (stoops); their itzab (idols) are on the animals, and on the livestock: the things that you carried about are made a imas (load), a mashaa (burden) to the iyap (weary).
They qaras (stoop), they karai (bow) down yachad (together); they yakal (could) not malat (deliver) the mashaa (burden), but themselves have halak (move) into shabay (captivity).

"Shamai (hearken / hear) to me, bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and all the shaarayath (remnant) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), that have been imas (borne) from their birth, that have been nashaa (lift) from the racham (show mercy / love);

And even to zaqanah (old) age I am he, and even to shayabah (old age / white hair - due to age) hairs will I sabal (carry) you. I ishah (make) made, and I will nashaa (lift); yes, I will sabal (carry), and will malat (deliver).
"To whom will you damah (liken) me, and shawah (make) me equal, and mashal (speak in proverb/parable) me, that we may be damah (like)?

Some pour out zahab (gold) from the kayas (bag), and shaqal (weigh) kasap (silver) in the qanah (balance). They shakar (hire) a tzarap (goldsmith), and he ishah (make) it a Al. They sagad (fall) down—yes, they shachah (worship).

They nashaa (lift) it on the kathap (shoulder), they sabal (carry) it, and yanach (set) it in its place, and it imad (stands), from its maqawam (place) it shall not move: yes, one may tzaiq (cry) to it, yet it can not inah (answer / respond), nor yashai (salvation) him out of his tzarah (trouble).
"Zakar (remember) this, and ayash (man / husband) yourselves men; shawab (turn back / repent) it again to lab (heart), you transgressors.
Zakar (remember) the raashawan (former) things of iwalam (forever): for I am Al, and there is none else; I am Alahayam, and there is apas (none) kamaw (like) me;

Nagad (declaring) the acharayath (end) from the raashayath (beginning), and from qadam (ancient) times things that are not yet ishah (make); amar (spoke), My itzah (counsel) shall qawam (rise up), and I will ishah (make) all my chapatz (pleasure);

Qaraa (called) a iyat (ravenous) bird from the mazarach (east), the ayash (man / husband) of my itzah (counsel) from a marachaq (far) aratz (Earth/land); yes, I have dabar (word / matter), I will also bawaa (come) it to pass; I have yatzar (purposed), I will also ishah (make) it.
Shamai (hearken / hear) to me, you abayar (stout-hearted), who are rachawaq (far) from tzadaqah (righteousness):

I qarab (come close) near my tzadaqah (righteousness), it shall not be rachaq (far) off, and my thashawaih (deliverance) shall not wait; and I will nathan (give) thashawaih (deliverance) in Tzayawan (Zion) for Yashar-Al (Israel) my glory.

"Yarad (come) down, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the ipar (dust), bathawalah (virgin) banath (daughter) of Babal (Babylon); yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the aratz (Earth/land) without a kasaa (throne), banath (daughter) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans): for you shall no more be qaraa (called) rak (tender) and inag (delicate).

Laqach (take / seize) the millstones, and tachan (grind) qamach (meal); galah (remove) your tzamah (veil), strip off the train, galah (uncover) the shawaq (leg), ibar (pass over/through) through the naharawath (rivers).
