Your irawah (nakedness) shall be galah (uncovered), yes, your charapah (shame) shall be raah (see): I will laqach (take / seize) naqam (vengeance), and will spare no adam (man)."
Our gaal (redeemer), Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) is his sham (name), the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel).

"Yashab (inhabit/dwell) in silence, and bawaa (come) into chashak (darkness), banath (daughter) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans); for you shall no more be qaraa (called) the gabarath (mistress) of mamalakawath (kingdoms).

I was qatzap (angry) with my im (nation / people), I chalal (profaned) my nachalah (inheritance), and nathan (give) them into your yad (hand): you showed them no racham (show mercy / love); on the zaqan (aged) you have very kabad (heavily) laid your il (over).

You amar (spoke), ‘I shall be a gabarath (mistress) iwalam (forever);' so that you shawam (place / establish / appoint) not lay these things to your lab (heart), nor did you zakar (remember) the acharayath (latter) end of it.

"Now therefore shamai (hearken / hear) this, you who are idayan (given) to pleasures, who yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely, who amar (spoke) in your labab (heart), ‘I am, and there is apas (none) else besides me; I shall not yashab (inhabit/dwell) as a alamanah (widow), neither shall I yadai (know) the shakawal (loss) of children:'

But these shanayam (two) things shall bawaa (come) to you in a ragai (in an instance) in achad (one) yawam (day), the shakawal (loss) of children, and alaman (widowhood); in their tham (full) measure shall they bawaa (come) on you, in the rab (multitude) of your kashap (sorceries), and the maad (great) itzamah (abundance) of your chabar (enchantments).

For you have batach (trusted) in your rai (wickedness); you have amar (spoke), No one raah (see) me; your chakamah (wisdom) and your daith (knowledge), it has shawab (turn back / repent) you, and you have amar (spoke) in your lab (heart), I am, and there is apas (none) else besides me.

Therefore rai (evil) will bawaa (come) on you; you won't yadai (know) when it dawns: and hawah (calamity / destruction) will napal (fall / be cast down) on you; you will not be yakal (able) to kapar (put) it away: and shawaa (vanity) shall bawaa (come) on you pathaawam (suddenly), which you don't yadai (know).

"Imad (stand) now with your chabar (enchantments), and with the rab (multitude) of your kashap (sorceries), in which you have labored from your naiwar (youth); if so be you shall be yakal (able) to yail (profit), if so be you may iratz (prevail).

You are laah (wearied) in the rab (multitude) of your itzah (counsels): let now the habaraw (astrologers), the chazayam (stargazers), the chadash (month) mawadayaim (prognosticators), imad (stand) up, and yashai (salvation) you from the things that shall bawaa (come) on you.

Behold, they shall be as qash (stubble); the ash (fire) shall sharap (burn) them; they shall not natzal (deliver) themselves from the yad (hand) of the lahabah (flame): it shall not be a gachal (coal) to chamam (warm) at, nor a awar (light) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) before.

Thus shall the things be to you in which you have labored: those who have sachar (trafficked) with you from your naiwar (youth) shall thaih (wander) everyone to his ibar (quarter); there shall be none to yashai (salvation) you.

"Shamai (hearken / hear) this, bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob), you who are qaraa (called) by the sham (name) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and yatzaa (go out / come out) come forth out of the may (waters) of Yahawadah (Judah); who shabai (swear / take oath) by the sham (name) of Yahawah, and zakar (remember) mention of the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), but not in amath (truth), nor in tzadaqah (righteousness)

(For they qaraa (called) themselves of the qadash (set apart / make holy) iyar (city), and samak (stay) themselves on the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel); Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) is his sham (name)):

I have nagad (declared) the raashawan (former) things from of az (old); yes, they yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of my pah (mouth), and I showed them: pathaawam (suddenly) I ishah (make) them, and they happened.
Because I daith (knew) that you are qashah (rough / hard), and your irap (neck) is an barazal (iron) gayad (sinew), and your matzach (brow) nachawashah (brass);

Therefore I have nagad (declared) it to you from of az (old); before it bawaa (come) to pass I showed it to you; lest you should amar (spoke), ‘My itzab (idol) ishah (make) done them, and my engraved pasal (image), and my molten nasak (image), has tzawah (commanded) them.'

You have shamai (hearken / hear) it; chazah (see) all this; and you, will you not nagad (declare) it? "I have shown you new things from ithah (now / present moment) time, even natzar (hidden) things, which you yadai (have) not known.
They are baraa (created) now, and not from of panayam (face); and before this yawam (day) you didn't shamai (hearken / hear) them; lest you should amar (spoke), ‘Behold, I yadai (knew) them.'

Yes, you didn't shamai (hearken / hear); yes, you didn't yadai (know); yes, from of old your azan (ear) was not pathach (opened): for I yadai (knew) that you dealt very bagad (treacherously), and was qaraa (called) a transgressor from the batan (womb).
For my sham (name) sake will I arak (defer) my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and for my thahalah (praise) will I chatam (refrain) for you, that I not karath (cut) you off.
Behold, I have tzarap (refined) you, but not as kasap (silver); I have bachar (chosen) you in the kawar (furnace) of inay (affliction).
For my own sake, for my own sake, will I ishah (make) it; for how should my name be chalal (profaned)? I will not nathan (give) my kabawad (glory) to achar (other).
"Shamai (hearken / hear) to me, O Yaiqab (Jacob), and Yashar-Al (Israel) my qaraa (called): I am he; I am the raashawan (first), I also am the acharawan (last).

Yes, my yad (hand) has yasad (laid) the foundation of the aratz (Earth/land), and my right yamayan (right hand) has spread out the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens): when I qaraa (called) to them, they imad (stand) up yachad (together).

"Qabatz (assemble) yourselves, all you, and shamai (hearken / hear); who among them has nagad (declared) these things? He whom Yahawah ahab (love) shall ishah (make) his chapatz (pleasure) on Babal (Babylon), and his zarawai (arm) shall be on the Kashaday (Chaldeans).
I, even I, have dabar (word / matter); yes, I have qaraa (called) him; I bawaa (come) brought him, and he shall make his darak (way) prosperous.

"Qarab (come close) qarab (come close) to me and shamai (hearken / hear) this: "From the raash (head) I have not dabar (word / matter) in sathar (secret / hidden); from the ith (time) that it was, there am I." Now the Adanay Yahawah has shalach (send) me, with his rawach (spirit / wind).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, your gaal (redeemer), the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel): I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who teaches you to yail (profit), who darak (leads) you by the darak (way) that you should yalak (go).

Oh that you had listened to my matzawah (commandments)! Then your shalawam (peace / safety) would have been like a nahar (river), and your tzadaqah (righteousness) like the galay (waves) of the yam (sea/waters):
Your zarai (seed) also had been as the chawal (sand), and the tzaatzaa (offspring) of your body like its grains: his sham (name) would not be karath (cut) off nor destroyed from panayam (face) me.

Yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from Babal (Babylon), barach (flee) from the Kashaday (Chaldeans); with a qawal (sound / voice) of ranah (singing) nagad (declare), shamai (hearken / hear) this, yatzaa (go out / come out) it even to the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land): amar (spoke), Yahawah has gaal (redeemed) his ibad (servant) Yaiqab (Jacob).

They didn't tzamaa (thirst) when he yalak (led) them through the deserts; he caused the mayam (Waters) to nazal (flow) out of the tzawar (rock) for them; he split the tzawar (rock) also, and the mayam (Waters) zawab (flow) out.
"There is no shalawam (peace / safety)," amar (spoke) Yahawah, "for the rashai (wicked)."

Shamai (hearken / hear), ayayam (islands), to me; and listen, you laamayam (peoples), from rachawaq (far): Yahawah has qaraa (called) me from the batan (womb); from the maiy (bowels) of my am (mother) has he zakar (remember) mention of my sham (name):

And he has shawam (place / establish / appoint) my pah (mouth) like a chad (sharp) charab (sword); in the tzal (shadow) of his yad (hand), he has chabaa (hidden) me: and he has shawam (place / establish / appoint) me a barar (polished) chatz (shaft); in his ashapah (quiver) has he sathar (kept) me close:
And he amar (spoke) to me, "You are my ibad (servant); Yashar-Al (Israel), in whom I will be paar (glorified)."

But I amar (spoke), "I have labored in rayaq (vain), I kalah (complete / finish) spent my kach (strength / mighty / power) for thahaw (formless) and habal (vanity); yet akan (surely) the mashapat (justice) due to me is with Yahawah, and my pailah (reward) with my Alahayam."

Now amar (spoke) Yahawah who yatzar (formed) me from the batan (womb) to be his ibad (servant), to shawab (turn back / repent) Yaiqab (Jacob) again to him, and that Yashar-Al (Israel) be asap (gathered) to him (for I am honorable in the iyanay (eyes) of Yahawah, and my Alahayam has become my iz (strength / might / refuge));

Yes, he amar (spoke), "It is too qalal (light) a thing that you should be my ibad (servant) to qawam (rise up) up the shabatay (tribes) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and to shawab (turn back / repent) the natzayar (preserved) of Yashar-Al (Israel): I will also nathan (give) you for a awar (light) to the gawayam (nations), that you may be my yashawaih (salvation) to the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land)."

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the gaal (redeemer) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and his qadawash (holy) One, to him whom napash (soul) bazah (despises), to him whom the gaway (heathen / nation) thaib (abhors), to a ibad (servant) of mashalayam (rulers): "malakayam (kings) shall raah (see) and qawam (rise up); sharayam (princes), and they shall shachah (worship); because of Yahawah who is aman (believe / have faith), even the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel), who has bachar (chosen) you."

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "In an ratzawan (acceptable) ith (time) have I inah (answer / respond) you, and in a yawam (day) of yashawaih (salvation) have I izar (helped) you; and I will natzar (preserve) you, and nathan (give) you for a barayath (covenant) of the im (nation / people), to qawam (rise up) up the aratz (Earth/land), to nachal (make) them inherit the shamam (desolate) nachalah (heritage):

Amar (spoke) to those who are asar (bound), ‘yatzaa (go out / come out) out!'; to those who are in chashak (darkness), ‘Show yourselves!' "They shall raih (feed) in the darakayam (ways), and on all bare heights shall be their maraiyath (pasture).

They shall not raib (hunger) nor tzamaa (thirst); neither shall the sharab (heat) nor shamash (sun) nakah (strike) them: for he who has racham (show mercy / love) on them will nahag (lead) them, even by mabawaiy (springs) of mayam (Waters) he will nahal (guide) them.
I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) all my har (mountain) a darak (way), and my masalah (highways) shall be rawam (will lift up).
Behold, these shall bawaa (come) from rachawaq (far); and behold, these from the tzapawan (north) and from the yam (sea/waters); and these from the aratz (Earth/land) of Sayanayam (Sinim)."

Ranan (sing), shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens); and be gayal (joyful), aratz (Earth/land); and patzach (break) forth into ranah (singing), harayam (mountains): for Yahawah has nacham (turn away / repent) his im (nation / people), and will racham (show mercy / love) compassion on his inay (afflicted).
But Tzayawan (Zion) amar (spoke), "Yahawah has forsaken me, and the Adawan has shakach (forgotten) me."

"Can a ayashah (woman / wife) shakach (forget) her nursing iwal (child), that she should not racham (show mercy / love) compassion on the ban (son) of her batan (womb)? Yes, these may shakach (forget), yet I will not shakach (forget) you!
Behold, I have engraved you on the palms of my kapayam (hands); your chawamah (walls) are continually before me.
Your ban (son) mahar (make) haste; your destroyers and those who charab (made) you waste shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from you.

Nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye) all around, and raah (see): all these qabatz (gather) themselves together, and bawaa (come) to you. As I chay (life)," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, "you shall surely labash (clothe) yourself with them all as with an iday (ornament / adornment), and dress yourself with them, like a kalah (complete / finish).

"For, as for your charabah (waste) and your shamam (desolate) places, and your aratz (Earth/land) that has been destroyed, surely now you shall be too small for the yashab (inhabit/dwell), and those who balai (swallowed) you up shall be rachaq (far) away.

The banay (children) of your bereavement shall yet amar (spoke) in your azan (ear), The maqawam (place) is too tzar (oppressor / distressor) for me; nagash (give) maqawam (place) to me that I may yashab (inhabit/dwell).

Then you will amar (spoke) in your labab (heart), ‘Who has conceived these for me, since I have been shakal (bereaved) of my children, and am galamawad (solitary), an galah (exile), and wandering sawar (back) and forth? Who has gadal (brought) up these? Behold, I was shaar (left) alone; these, ayapah (where) were they?'"

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, "Behold, I will nashaa (lift) up my yad (hand) to the gawayam (nations), and rawam (will lift up) up my nas (banner) to the imayam (peoples); and they shall bawaa (come) your ban (son) in their bosom, and your banath (daughter) shall be nashaa (lift) on their kathap (shoulders).

Malakayam (kings) shall be your aman (believe / have faith) fathers, and their sharah (queens) your yanaq (nursing) mothers: they shall shachah (bow) down to you with their apayam (faces) to the aratz (Earth/land), and lachak (lick) the ipar (dust) of your ragal (feet / foot); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah; and those who qawah (gather/wait) for me shall not be disappointed."
Shall the malaqawach (prey) be laqach (take / seize) from the gabawar (mighty), or the tzadayaq (righteous) shabay (captives) be malat (delivered)?

But thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "Even the shabay (captives) of the gabawar (mighty) shall be laqach (take / seize) away, and the malaqawach (prey) of the irayatz (terrible) shall be malat (delivered); for I will rayab (contend) with him who rayab (contends) with you, and I will yashai (salvation) your ban (son).

I will akal (eat) those who yanah (oppress) you with their own bashar (flesh); and they shall be shakar (drunken) with their own dam (blood), as with sweet isayas (wine): and all bashar (flesh) shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, am your Savior, and your gaal (redeemer), the abayar (mighty) One of Yaiqab (Jacob)."

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "Where is the sapar (book / scribed document) of your am (mother) karayathawath (divorce), with which I have shalach (send) her away? Or which of my nashah (creditors) is it to whom I have makar (sold) you? Behold, for your iwan (guilt/iniquity) were you makar (sold), and for your pashai (transgressions) was your am (mother) shalach (send) away.

Why, when I bawaa (come), was there no ayash (man / husband)? When I qaraa (called), was there none to inah (answer / respond)? Is my yad (hand) shortened at qatzar (all), that it can't padawath (redeem)? Or have I no kach (strength / mighty / power) to natzal (deliver)? Behold, at my gairah (rebuke) I charab (dry) up the yam (sea/waters), I shawam (place / establish / appoint) the naharawath (rivers) a madabar (wilderness): their dagah (fish) baash (stink), because there is no mayam (Waters), and mawath (death) for tzamaa (thirst).
I labash (clothe) the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) with qadarawath (blackness), and I shawam (place / establish / appoint) sackcloth their kasawath (covering)."

The Adanay Yahawah nathan (give) given me the lashawan (tongue / language) of those who are lamawad (taught), that I may yadai (know) how to sustain with dabar (word / matter) him who is yaip (weary): he wakens baqar (morning) by baqar (morning), he wakens my azan (ear) to shamai (hearken / hear) as those who are lamawad (taught).
The Adanay Yahawah pathach (has) opened my azan (ear), and I was not rebellious, neither sawag (turned) away backward.

I nathan (give) my gaw (back) to the strikers, and my lachay (cheeks) to those who marat (plucked) off the hair; I didn't sathar (hide) my panayam (face) from kalamah (shame) and raq (concept: what comes out / spittle).

For the Adanay Yahawah will izar (help) me; therefore I have not been kalam (confounded): therefore have I shawam (place / establish / appoint) my panayam (face) like a chalamayash (flint), and I yadai (know) that I shall not be disappointed.
He is qarawab (near) who justifies me; who will bring charges against me? Let us imad (stand) up yachad (together): who is my bail (adversary)? Let him nagash (come) near to me.
Behold, the Adanay Yahawah will izar (help) me; who is he who shall rashai (condemn) me? Behold, all they shall balah (wax) old as a bagad (garment), the ish (made) shall akal (eat) them up.

Who is among you who yaraa (fears) Yahawah, who shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of his ibad (servant)? He who halak (move) in chashakah (darkness), and has no nagah (light), let him batach (trust) in the sham (name) of Yahawah, and shain (rely) on his Alahayam.

Behold, all you who qadach (kindle) a ash (fire), who adorn yourselves with torches around yourselves; yalak (walk) in the awar (light) of your ash (fire), and among the brands that you have bair (kindled). You shall have this of my yad (hand); you shall shakab (lie) down in maitzabah (sorrow).

"Shamai (hearken / hear) to me, you who radap (follow) after tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), you who baqash (seek) Yahawah: nabat (look) to the tzawar (rock) you were chatzab (cut) from, and to the hold of the bawar (pit) you were naqar (dug) from.

Nabat (look) to Abaraham (Abraham) your ab (father), and to Sharah (Sarah) who chawal (bore) you; for when he was but achad (one) I qaraa (called) him, and I barak (blessed) him, and rabah (made) him many.

For Yahawah has nacham (turn away / repent) Tzayawan (Zion); he has nacham (turn away / repent) all her charabah (waste) places, and has shawam (place / establish / appoint) her madabar (wilderness) like Idan (Eden), and her irabah (desert) like the gan (garden) of Yahawah; shashawan (joy) and shamachah (gladness) shall be matzaa (found) therein, thanksgiving, and the qawal (sound / voice) of zamarah (melody).

"Qashab (attend) to me, my imayam (people); and azan (ear) ear to me, my laam (nation): for a thawarah (instruction) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from me, and I will establish my mashapat (justice) for a awar (light) of the imayam (peoples).

My tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) is qarawab (near), my yashai (salvation) is yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and my zarawai (arms) shall shapat (judge / judgement) the imayam (peoples); the ayayam (islands) shall qawah (gather/wait) for me, and on my zarawai (arm) shall they yachal (trust).

Nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye) to the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and nabat (look) on the aratz (Earth/land) beneath; for the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) shall malach (vanish) away like ishan (smoke), and the aratz (Earth/land) shall balah (wax) old like a bagad (garment); and those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein shall mawath (death) in the same kan (for sure): but my yashawaih (salvation) shall be iwalam (forever), and my tzadaqah (righteousness) shall not be chathath (abolished).

"Shamai (hearken / hear) to me, you who yadai (know) tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), the im (nation / people) in whose lab (heart) is my thawarah (instruction); don't yaraa (fear / be afraid) the charapah (reproach) of anawash (men), neither be chathath (dismayed) at their insults.

For the ish (made) shall akal (eat) them up like a bagad (garment), and the worm shall akal (eat) them like tzamar (wool); but my tzadaqah (righteousness) shall be iwalam (forever), and my yashawaih (salvation) to all dawarayam (generations)."

Iwar (rouse / awaken), iwar (rouse / awaken), labash (put) on iz (strength / might / refuge), zarawai (arm) of Yahawah; iwar (rouse / awaken), as in the yamay (days) of iwalam (forever), the darawath (generations) of qadam (ancient) times. Isn't it you who chatzab (cut) Rahab (Rahab) in pieces, who pierced the thanayan (monster)?

Isn't it you who charab (dried) up the yam (sea/waters), the may (waters) of the rab (great) thahawam (depths); who shawam (place / establish / appoint) the maimaqay (depths) of the yam (sea/waters) a darak (way) for the gaal (redeemed) to ibar (pass over/through) over?

The padah (ransomed) of Yahawah shall shawab (turn back / repent), and bawaa (come) with ranah (singing) to Tzayawan (Zion); and iwalam (forever) shamachah (joy) shall be on their raash (head). They shall obtain shashawan (gladness) and shamachah (joy). Yagawan (sorrow) and anachah (sighing) shall nawas (flee) away.

"I, even I, am he who nacham (turn away / repent) you: who are you, that you are yaraa (fear / be afraid) of anawash (man) who shall mawath (death), and of the ban (son) of adam (man) who shall be nathan (give) as chatzayar (grass);

And have shakach (forgotten) Yahawah your Maker, who natah (stretched) forth the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and yasad (laid) the foundations of the aratz (Earth/land); and pachad (fear / dread) continually all the yawam (day) panayam (face) of the fury of the oppressor, when he kawan (makes) ready to shachath (destroy)? And where is the fury of the oppressor?
The tzaih (captive) exile shall mahar (speedily) be pathach (freed); and he shall not mawath (death) and go down into the shachath (pit), neither shall his lacham (bread) chasar (fail).
For I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who stirs up the yam (sea/waters), so that its gal (waves) hamah (great uproar): Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) is his sham (name).

I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) my dabar (word / matter) in your pah (mouth), and have kasah (covered) you in the tzal (shadow) of my yad (hand), that I may natai (plant) the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and yasad (lay) the foundations of the aratz (Earth/land), and amar (spoke) Tzayawan (Zion), ‘You are my im (nation / people).'"

Iwar (rouse / awaken), iwar (rouse / awaken), qawam (rise up) up, Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), that have shathah (drinks) at the yad (hand) of Yahawah the kawas (cup) of his chamah (wrath); you have shathah (drinks) the bowl of the kawas (cup) of staggering, and drained it.

There is none to nahal (guide) her among all the banayam (sons) whom she has yalad (birth / begot) forth; neither is there any who chazaq (takes) her by the yad (hand) among all the banayam (sons) who she has gadal (brought) up.

These shanayam (two) things have qaraa (called) to you. Who will nawad (bemoan) you? Shad (desolation) and shabar (destruction), and the raib (famine) and the charab (sword); how shall I nacham (turn away / repent) you?

Your ban (son) have ilap (fainted), they shakab (lie) at the raash (head) of all the chawatzawath (streets), as an antelope in a makamar (net); they are malaa (full) of the chamah (wrath) of Yahawah, the gairah (rebuke) of your Alahayam.
Therefore shamai (hearken / hear) now this, you inay (afflicted), and shakar (drunken), but not with yayan (wine):

Thus amar (spoke) your Adawan Yahawah, and your Alahayam who rayab (pleads) the cause of his im (nation / people), "Behold, I have laqach (take / seize) out of your yad (hand) the kawas (cup) of staggering, even the bowl of the kawas (cup) of my chamah (wrath); you shall no more shathah (drinks) it again:

And I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) it into the yad (hand) of those who yagah (afflict) you, who have amar (spoke) to your napash (soul), ‘shachah (bow) down, that we may walk over you;' and you have shawam (place / establish / appoint) your gaw (back) as the aratz (Earth/land), and as the chawatz (street), to those who walk over."

Iwar (rouse / awaken), iwar (rouse / awaken), labash (put) on your iz (strength / might / refuge), Tzayawan (Zion); labash (put) on your thapaarah (beautiful) bagaday (garments), Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), the qadash (set apart / make holy) iyar (city): for yasap (henceforth) there shall no more bawaa (come) into you the iral (uncircumcised) and the tamaa (unclean).

Nair (shake) yourself from the ipar (dust)! Qawam (rise up), yashab (inhabit/dwell) up, Yarawashalam (Jerusalem)! Release yourself from the mawasaray (bonds) of your tzawaar (neck), shabay (captive) banath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion)!
For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "You were makar (sold) for chanam (nothing); and you shall be gaal (redeemed) without kasap (money)."

For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, "My im (nation / people) yarad (went) down at the raashawan (first) into Matzarayam (Egypt) to live there: and the Ashawar (Assyrian) has ishaq (oppressed) them apas (without) cause.

"Now therefore, what do I do here," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, "seeing that my im (nation / people) are laqach (take / seize) away for chanam (nothing)? Those who mashal (rule/have dominion) over them mock," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, "and my sham (name) continually all the yawam (day) is naatz (blasphemed).
Therefore my im (nation / people) shall yadai (know) my sham (name). Therefore they shall know in that yawam (day) that I am he who dabar (word / matter); behold, it is I."

How naah (beautiful) on the harayam (mountains) are the ragalay (feet) of him who brings bashar (good) news, who publishes shalawam (peace / safety), who brings bashar (good) news of tawab (good / proper function), who publishes yashawaih (salvation), who amar (spoke) to Tzayawan (Zion), "Your Alahayam malak (king)!"

The qawal (sound / voice) of your watchmen! They nashaa (lift) up the qawal (sound / voice), yachad (together) do they ranan (sing); for they shall raah (see) iyan (eye) to iyan (eye), when Yahawah shawab (turn back / repent) to Tzayawan (Zion).

Patzach (break) forth into joy, ranan (sing) yachad (together), you charabah (waste) places of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); for Yahawah has nacham (turn away / repent) his im (nation / people), he has gaal (redeemed) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

Yahawah has chashap (made) bare his qadash (set apart / make holy) zarawai (arm) in the iyanay (eyes) of all the gawayam (nations); and all the apasay (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land) raah (see) seen the yashawaih (salvation) of our Alahayam.

Sawar (depart), sawar (depart), yatzaa (go out / come out) out from there, nagai (touch) no tamaa (unclean) thing! Yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the thawak (midst) of her! Barar (cleanse) yourselves, you who nashaa (lift) the kalay (vessels) of Yahawah.

For you shall not yatzaa (go out / come out) out in chapazawan (haste), neither shall you halak (move) by manawasah (flight): for Yahawah will halak (move) panayam (face) you; and the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel) will be your rear guard.
Behold, my ibad (servant) shall deal shakal (wisely), he shall be rawam (will lift up) and nashaa (lift) up, and shall be very gabah (high).
Like as many were shamam (astonished) at you (his maraah (appearance) was mashachath (marred) more than any ayash (man / husband), and his thaar (form) more than the banay (sons) of adam (men)),

So shall he nazah (sprinkle) many gawayam (nations); malakayam (kings) shall qapatz (shut) their pah (mouths) at him: for that which had not been sapar (book) them shall they raah (see); and that which they had not shamai (hearken / hear) shall they bayan (between).
Who has aman (believe / have faith) our message? To whom has the zarawai (arm) of Yahawah been galah (revealed)?

For he ilah (go up / offer) up panayam (face) him as a yawanaq (tender) plant, and as a sharash (root) out of tzayah (dry) aratz (Earth/land). He has no thaar (good) looks or hadar (glory / majesty / splendor). When we raah (see) him, there is no beauty that we should chamad (desire) him.

He was bazah (despised), and chadal (rejected) by ayashayam (men); a ayash (man / husband) of suffering, and acquainted with chalay (disease). He was bazah (despised) as one from whom men hide their panayam (face); and we didn't respect him.
Akan (surely) he has nashaa (lift) our chalay (sickness), and sabal (carried) our suffering; yet we chashab (considered) him nagai (plagued), nakah (struck) by Alahayam, and inah (oppress / afflict).

But he was pierced for our pashai (transgressions). He was dakaa (crushed) for our iwan (guilt/iniquity). The punishment that brought our shalawam (peace / safety) was on him; and by his chabawarah (wounds) we are rapaa (healed).
All we like tzaan (sheep) have thaih (gone) astray. Everyone has panah (turn) to his own darak (way); and Yahawah has pagai (laid) on him the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of us all.

He was nagash (oppressed), yet when he was inah (oppress / afflict) he didn't pathach (open) his pah (mouth). As a shah (lamb) that is yabal (led) to the tabach (slaughter), and as a rachal (sheep) that panayam (face) its gazaz (shearers) is mute, so he didn't pathach (open) his pah (mouth).

He was laqach (take / seize) away by itzar (oppression) and mashapat (judgment); and as for his dawar (generation / age / period), who considered that he was gazar (cut) off out of the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life) and nagai (stricken) for the disobedience of my im (nation / people)?

They nathan (give) his qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) with the rashai (wicked), and with a ishayar (rich) man in his mawath (death); although he ishah (make) done no chamas (violence), neither was any maramah (deceit) in his pah (mouth).

Yet it chapatz (pleased) Yahawah to dakaa (bruise) him. He has caused him to suffer. When you shawam (place / establish / appoint) his napash (soul) an offering for asham (sin), he shall raah (see) his zarai (seed). He shall prolong his yamayam (days), and the chapatz (pleasure) of Yahawah shall tzalach (prosper) in his yad (hand).

After the suffering of his napash (soul), he will raah (see) the light and be shabai (satisfied). My tzadayaq (righteous) ibad (servant) will justify many by the daith (knowledge) of himself; and he will sabal (bear) their iwan (guilt/iniquity).

Therefore will I chalaq (divide) him a portion with the rab (great), and he shall chalaq (divide) the shalal (spoil) with the itzawam (strong); because he irah (poured) out his napash (soul) to mawath (death), and was manah (numbered) with the transgressors; yet he nashaa (lift) the chataa (sin) of many, and pagai (made) intercession for the transgressors.

"Ranan (sing), iqar (barren), you who didn't yalad (birth / begot); patzach (break) forth into ranah (singing), and tzahal (cry) aloud, you who did not chawal (travail) with child: for more are the banay (children) of the shamam (desolate) than the banay (children) of the bail (married) wife," amar (spoke) Yahawah.

"Enlarge the maqawam (place) of your ahal (tent), and natah (let) them stretch forth the yarayaiwath (curtains) of your mashakan (habitations); don't chashak (darkness): arak (lengthen) your mayathar (cords), and chazaq (strengthen) your yathad (stakes).

For you shall spread out on the right yamayan (right hand) and on the shamaawal (left hand); and your zarai (seed) shall yarash (possess) the gawayam (nations), and shamam (make) the desolate irayam (cities) to be yashab (inhabit/dwell).

"Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid); for you shall not be bawash (ashamed): neither be kalam (confounded); for you shall not be disappointed: for you shall shakach (forget) the chapar (shame) of your ilawam (youth); and the charapah (reproach) of your alamanawath (widowhood) you shall zakar (remember) no more.

For your Maker is your bail (husband); Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) is his sham (name): and the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel) is your gaal (redeemer); the Alahayam of the whole aratz (Earth/land) shall he be qaraa (called).

For Yahawah has qaraa (called) you as a ayashah (woman / wife) forsaken and itzab (grieved) in rawach (spirit / wind), even a ayashah (woman / wife) of naiwar (youth), when she is maas (cast) off," amar (spoke) your Alahayam.
"For a qatan (small / young / least) ragai (in an instance) have I forsaken you; but with gadawal (very great/important/mighty) rachamayam (mercies) will I qabatz (gather) you.

In overflowing qatzap (wrath) I sathar (hid) my panayam (face) from you for a ragai (in an instance); but with iwalam (forever) loving chasad (grace) will I have racham (show mercy / love) on you," amar (spoke) Yahawah your gaal (redeemer).

"For this is like the may (waters) of Nach (Noah) to me; for as I have shabai (swear / take oath) that the may (waters) of Nach (Noah) shall no more ibar (pass over/through) over the aratz (Earth/land), so have I shabai (swear / take oath) that I will not be qatzap (angry) with you, nor gair (rebuke) you.

For the harayam (mountains) may depart, and the gabaiwath (hills) be mawat (removed); but my loving chasad (grace) shall not depart from you, neither shall my barayath (covenant) of shalawam (peace / safety) be mawat (removed)," amar (spoke) Yahawah who has racham (show mercy / love) on you.

"You inay (afflicted), tossed with storms, and not nacham (turn away / repent), behold, I will set your aban (stone) in beautiful colors, and rabatz (lay) your yasad (foundations) with sapayarayam (sapphires).
I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) your pinnacles of rubies, and your shair (gates) of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious abanay (stones).
All your ban (son) shall be lamawad (taught) of Yahawah; and rab (great) shall be the shalawam (peace / safety) of your ban (son).

In tzadaqah (righteousness) you shall be kawan (established): you shall be rachaq (far) from ishaq (oppression), for you shall not be yaraa (fear / be afraid); and from machathah (terror), for it shall not qarab (come close) near you.
Behold, they may gawar (gather) together, but not by me: whoever shall gawar (gather) together against you shall napal (fall / be cast down) because of you.

"Behold, I have baraa (created) the charash (smith) who napach (blows) the ash (fire) of pacham (coals), and yatzaa (go out / come out) forth a kalay (weapon) for his maishah (work); and I have baraa (created) the shachath (waster) to chabal (destroy).

No kalay (weapon) that is yatzar (formed) against you will prevail; and you will rashai (condemn) every lashawan (tongue / language) that qawam (rise up) against you in mashapat (judgment). This is the nachalah (heritage) of the ibaday (servants) of Yahawah, and their tzadaqah (righteousness) which is of me," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

"Come, everyone who tzamaa (thirsts), to the mayam (Waters)! Yalak (come), he who has no kasap (money), shabar (buy), and akal (eat)! Yes, yalak (come), shabar (buy) yayan (wine) and chalab (milk) without kasap (money) and without machayar (price).

Why do you shaqal (spend) kasap (money) for that which is not lacham (bread)? And your yagayai (labor) for that which doesn't shabaih (seven)? Shamai (hearken / hear) shamai (hearken / hear) to me, and akal (eat) you that which is tawab (good / proper function), and let your napash (soul) inag (delight) itself in dashan (fatness).

Natah (turn) your azan (ear), and yalak (come) to me; shamai (hearken / hear), and your napash (soul) shall chayah (live): and I will karath (cut) an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant) with you, even the aman (believe / have faith) chasaday (mercies) of Dawad (David).
Behold, I nathan (give) given him for a id (until / as far as) to the laawamayam (peoples), a nagayad (leader) and commander to the laawamayam (peoples).

Behold, you shall qaraa (called) a gaway (heathen / nation) that you don't yadai (know); and a gaway (heathen / nation) that didn't yadai (know) you shall rawatz (run) to you, because of Yahawah your Alahayam, and for the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel); for he has paar (glorified) you."
Darash (seek) Yahawah while he may be matzaa (found); qaraa (called) you on him while he is qarawab (near):

Let the rashai (wicked) izab (forsake) his darak (way), and the awan (unrighteous) ayash (man / husband) his machashabah (thoughts); and let him shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah, and he will have racham (show mercy / love) on him; and to our Alahayam, for he will abundantly salach (forgive/pardon/make clean).
"For my machashabah (thoughts) are not your machashabah (thoughts), neither are your darak (ways) my darak (ways)," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

"For as the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) are gabah (higher) than the aratz (Earth/land), so are my darak (ways) gabah (higher) than your darak (ways), and my machashabah (thoughts) than your machashabah (thoughts).

For as the gasham (rain) yarad (comes) down and the shalag (snow) from the sky, and doesn't shawab (turn back / repent) there, but rawah (waters) the aratz (Earth/land), and makes it yalad (birth / begot) forth and tzamach (bud), and nathan (give) zarai (seed) to the zarai (sower) and lacham (bread) to the eater;

So shall my dabar (word / matter) be that yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of my pah (mouth): it shall not shawab (turn back / repent) to me rayaqam (void), but it shall ishah (make) that which I please, and it shall tzalach (prosper) in the thing I shalach (send) it to do.

For you shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out with shamachah (joy), and be yabal (led) forth with shalawam (peace / safety): the harayam (mountains) and the gabaiwath (hills) shall patzach (break) forth panayam (face) you into ranah (singing); and all the itzay (trees) of the shadah (fields) shall machaa (clap) their kap (hands).

Instead of the naitzawatz (thorn) shall ilah (go up / offer) up the barawash (fir) tree; and instead of the sarapad (brier) shall ilah (go up / offer) up the hadas (myrtle) tree: and it shall be to Yahawah for a sham (name), for an iwalam (forever) awath (sign / mark / miracle) that shall not be karath (cut) off."

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "shamar (keep/guard) mashapat (justice), and ishah (make) tzadaqah (righteousness); for my yashawaih (salvation) is qarawab (near) to bawaa (come), and my tzadaqah (righteousness) to be galah (revealed).

Ashar (who/that) is the anawash (man) who ishah (make) this, and the ban (son) of adam (man) who chazaq (holds) it fast; who shamar (keep/guard) the shabath (shabath / rest) from chalal (profaning) it, and shamar (keep/guard) his yad (hand) from ishah (make) any rai (evil)."

Neither let the foreigner, who has lawah (joined) himself to Yahawah, amar (spoke), amar (spoke), "Yahawah will surely badal (separated) me from his im (nation / people);" neither let the sarayas (eunuch) amar (spoke), "Behold, I am a yabash (dry land) itz (tree)."

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "To the sarayasayam (eunuchs) who shamar (keep/guard) my shabath (shabath / rest), and bachar (choose) the things that please me, and chazaq (hold) fast my barayath (covenant):

To them I will nathan (give) in my bayath (house) and within my chawamah (walls) a yad (hand) and a sham (name) tawab (good / proper function) than of banayam (sons) and of banawath (daughters); I will nathan (give) them an iwalam (forever) sham (name), that shall not be karath (cut) off.

Also the foreigners who lawah (join) themselves to Yahawah, to sharath (minister) to him, and to ahab (love) the sham (name) of Yahawah, to be his ibadayam (servants), everyone who shamar (keep/guard) the shabath (shabath / rest) from chalal (profaning) it, and machazayaqayam (holds) fast my barayath (covenant);

Even them will I bawaa (come) to my qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain), and shamach (make) them joyful in my bayath (house) of thapalah (prayer): their burnt ilah (offerings) and their zabach (sacrifices) shall be accepted on my mazabach (altar); for my bayath (house) shall be qaraa (called) a bayath (house) of thapalah (prayer) for all imayam (peoples)."

The Adanay Yahawah, who qabatz (gathers) the nadachay (outcasts) of Yashar-Al (Israel), naam (declares prophetically), "Yet will I qabatz (gather) others to him, besides his own who are qabatz (gathered)."
All you animals of the shadah (field), athah (you (masc)) to akal (eat), all you animals in the yair (forest).
His watchmen are iwar (blind), they are all without yadai (knowledge); they are all mute kalabayam (dogs), they can't nabach (bark); dreaming, lying down, ahab (love) to nawam (slumber).

Yes, the kalabayam (dogs) are iz (greedy), they yadai (can) never yadai (have) shabaih (seven); and these are raiyam (shepherds) who can't bayan (between): they have all panah (turn) to their own darak (way), ayash (man / husband) one to his batzai (gain), from every qatzah (end / extremity / border).

"Athah (you (masc))," say they, "I will laqach (take / seize) yayan (wine), and we will sabaa (fill) ourselves with shakar (strong) drink; and machar (tomorrow) shall be as this machar (day), maad (great) beyond measure."

The tzadayaq (righteous) perishes, and no ayash (man / husband) shawam (place / establish / appoint) it to lab (heart); and chasad (grace) anashay (men) are asap (taken) away, none bayan (between) that the tzadayaq (righteous) is asap (taken) away from the rai (evil).
He bawaa (come) into shalawam (peace / safety); they nawach (rest) in their mashakab (beds), each one who halak (move) in his nakach (uprightness).
"But qarab (come close) near here, you banay (sons) of the sorceress, the zarai (seed) of the naap (adulterer) and the prostitute.

Against whom do you inag (sport) yourselves? Against whom do you rachab (make) a wide pah (mouth), and stick out your lashawan (tongue / language)? Aren't you yaladay (children) of disobedience, a zarai (seed) of falsehood,
You who inflame yourselves among the oaks, under every rainan (green) itz (tree); who shachat (kill) the yaladayam (children) in the nachalayam (valleys), under the clefts of the salaiyam (rocks)?

Among the chalaq (smooth) stones of the nachal (stream / river) is your chalaq (portion); they, they are your gawaral (lot); you have even shapak (poured) a drink nasak (offering) to them. You have ilah (go up / offer) an manachah (offering). Shall I be appeased for these things?
On a nashaa (lift) and gabah (lofty) har (mountain) you have shawam (place / establish / appoint) your mashakab (bed); there also you ilah (go up / offer) up to zabach (offer) zabach (sacrifice).

Achar (other) the dalath (doors) and the mazawazah (posts) you have shawam (place / establish / appoint) up your zakarawan (memorial): for you have galah (uncovered) to someone besides me, and have ilah (go up / offer) up; you have enlarged your mashakab (bed), and karath (cut) you a covenant with them: you ahab (love) their mashakab (bed) yad (hand) you chazah (saw) it.

You shawar (went) to the malak (king) with shaman (oil), and rabah (increased) your raqach (perfumes), and shalach (send) your tzayar (ambassadors) rachawaq (far) off, and shapal (debased) yourself even to shaawal (Sheol / afterlife).
You were yagai (wearied) with the length of your darak (way); yet you didn't amar (spoke), ‘It is in vain.' You matzaa (found) a reviving of your yad (hand); therefore you weren't faint.

"Of whom have you been daag (afraid) and in yaraa (fear / be afraid), that you kazab (lie), and have not zakar (remember) me, nor shawam (place / establish / appoint) it to your lab (heart)? Haven't I held my chashah (peace) even of iwalam (forever) time, and you don't yaraa (fear / be afraid) me?
I will nagad (declare) your tzadaqah (righteousness); and as for your maishah (works), they shall not yail (profit) you.

When you zaiq (cry), let those who you have gathered natzal (deliver) you; but the rawach (spirit / wind) shall laqach (take / seize) them, a habal (breath) shall nashaa (lift) them all away: but he who laqach (take / seize) chasah (refuge) in me shall nachal (possess) the aratz (Earth/land), and shall yarash (inherit) my qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain)."
He will amar (spoke), "salal (cast) up, salal (cast) up, panah (turn) the darak (way), rawam (will lift up) up the makashawal (stumbling-block) out of the darak (way) of my im (nation / people)."

For thus amar (spoke) the rawam (will lift up) and nashaa (lift) One who shakan (place) id (until / as far as), whose sham (name) is qadawash (holy): "I shakan (place) in the marawam (high) and qadawash (holy) place, with him also who is of a dakaa (contrite) and shapal (humble) rawach (spirit / wind), to chayah (revive) the rawach (spirit / wind) of the shapal (humble), and to chayah (revive) the lab (heart) of the dakaa (contrite).

For I will not rayab (contend) iwalam (forever), neither will I be natzach (always) qatzap (angry); for the rawach (spirit / wind) would itap (faint) panayam (face) me, and the nashamawath (souls) who I ishah (make) made.

For the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of his batzai (covetousness) was I qatzap (angry), and nakah (struck) him; I sathar (hid) myself and was qatzap (angry); and he yalak (went) on shawabab (backsliding) in the darak (way) of his lab (heart).
I raah (see) seen his darak (ways), and will rapaa (heal) him: I will nachah (lead) him also, and shalam (restore) nachamayam (comforts) to him and to his mourners.

I baraa (created) the nawab (fruit) of the shapathayam (lips): shalawam (peace / safety), shalawam (peace / safety), to him who is rachawaq (far) off and to him who is qarawab (near)," amar (spoke) Yahawah; "and I will rapaa (heal) them."
But the rashai (wicked) are like the garash (troubled) yam (sea/waters); for it can't shaqat (rest), and its mayam (Waters) garash (cast) up rapash (mire) and tayat (dirt).
"There is no shalawam (peace / safety)," amar (spoke) my Alahayam, "for the rashai (wicked)."

"Qaraa (called) garawan (aloud), don't chashak (darkness), rawam (will lift up) up your qawal (sound / voice) like a shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn), and nagad (declare) to my im (nation / people) their disobedience, and to the bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob) their chataah (sin).

Yet they darash (seek) me yawam (day), and chapatz (delight) to daith (know) my darak (ways): as a gaway (heathen / nation) that ishah (make) tzadaqah (righteousness), and didn't izab (forsake) the mashapat (ordinance) of their Alahayam, they shaal (ask) of me righteous tzadaq (righteous / just / fair); they chapatz (delight) to qarabah (draw) near to Alahayam.

‘Why have we tzawam (fasted),' say they, ‘and you don't raah (see)? Why have we inah (oppress / afflict) our napash (soul), and you take no yadai (knowledge)?' "Behold, in the yawam (day) of your tzawam (fast) you matzaa (find) chapatz (pleasure), and nagash (exact) all your itzab (labors).

Behold, you tzawam (fast) for rayab (strife) and rayab (contention), and to nakah (strike) with the agarap (fist) of rashai (wickedness): you don't tzawam (fast) this yawam (day) so as to make your qawal (sound / voice) to be shamai (hearken / hear) on marawam (high).

Is such the tzawam (fast) that I have bachar (chosen)? The yawam (day) for a adam (man) to inah (oppress / afflict) his napash (soul)? Is it to kapap (bow) down his raash (head) as a agamawan (rush), and to yatzai (spread) sackcloth and ashes under him? Will you qaraa (called) zah (this / that / these) a tzawam (fast), and an ratzawan (acceptable) yawam (day) to Yahawah?

"Isn't this the tzawam (fast) that I have bachar (chosen): to release the bonds of rashai (wickedness), to nathar (undo) the bands of the mawatah (yoke), and to let the ratzatz (oppressed) shalach (send) chapashay (free), and that you nathaq (break) every mawatah (yoke)?

Isn't it to distribute your lacham (bread) to the raib (hungry), and that you bawaa (come) the inay (poor) who are marawad (cast) out to your bayath (house)? When you raah (see) the irawam (naked), that you kasah (cover) him; and that you not ilam (hide) yourself from your own bashar (flesh)?

Then your awar (light) shall baqai (break) forth as the shachar (morning), and your healing shall tzamach (spring) forth maharah (speedily); and your tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) shall halak (move) panayam (face) you; the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah shall be your rear guard.

Then you shall qaraa (called), and Yahawah will inah (answer / respond); you shall shawai (cry), and he will amar (spoke), ‘Here I am.' "If you sawar (take) away from the thawak (midst) of you the mawatah (yoke), the shalach (send) forth of the atzabai (finger), and dabar (word / matter) wickedly;

And if you pawaq (draw) out your napash (soul) to the raib (hungry), and shabai (satisfy) the inah (oppress / afflict) napash (soul): then your awar (light) shall zarach (rise) in apalah (darkness), and your chashak (darkness) be as the noonday;

And Yahawah will nachah (guide) you continually, and shabai (satisfy) your napash (soul) in dry places, and chalatz (make) strong your itzam (bones); and you shall be like a rawah (watered) gan (garden), and like a mawatzaa (spring) of mayam (Waters), whose mayam (Waters) don't kazab (fail).

Those who shall be of you shall banah (build) the iwalam (forever) charabah (waste) places; you shall qawam (rise up) up the mawasaday (foundations) of many dawar (generation / age / period); and you shall be qaraa (called) The gadar (repairer) of the paratz (breach), The restorer of nathayabawath (paths) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) in.

"If you shawab (turn back / repent) away your ragal (feet / foot) from the shabath (shabath / rest), from ishah (make) your chapatz (pleasure) on my qadash (set apart / make holy) yawam (day); and qaraa (called) the shabath (shabath / rest) a inag (delight), and the qadawash (holy) of Yahawah honorable; and shall honor it, not ishah (make) your own darak (ways), nor matzaa (finding) your own chapatz (pleasure), nor dabar (word / matter) your own dabar (word / matter):

Then you shall inag (delight) yourself in Yahawah; and I will rakab (make) you to ride on the bamah (high) places of the aratz (Earth/land); and I will akal (eat) you with the nachalah (heritage) of Yaiqab (Jacob) your ab (father):" for the pah (mouth) of Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) it.
Han (behold), Yahawah yad (hand) is not shortened, that it can't yashai (salvation); neither his azan (ear) kabad (heavy), that it can't shamai (hearken / hear):

But your iwan (guilt/iniquity) have badal (separated) bayan (between) you and your Alahayam, and your chataah (sin) have sathar (hidden) his panayam (face) from you, so that he will not shamai (hearken / hear).

For your kap (hands) are gaal (defiled) with dam (blood), and your atzabai (fingers) with iwan (guilt/iniquity); your shapah (lips) have dabar (word / matter) shaqar (lies), your lashawan (tongue / language) hagah (mutters) iwal (wickedness).

None sues in tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and none shapat (judge / judgement) in amawanah (truth): they batach (trust) in thahaw (formless), and dabar (word / matter) shawaa (vanity); they harah (conceive) imal (mischief), and yalad (birth / begot) forth awan (iniquity).

They baqai (hatch) tzapai (adders)' bayatzay (eggs), and weave the ikabayash (spider's) qawar (web): he who akal (eat) of their bayatzay (eggs) mawath (death); and that which is zawarah (crushed) baqaiw (breaks) out into a apaih (viper).

Their qawar (webs) shall not become bagad (garments), neither shall they kasah (cover) themselves with their maishay (works): their maishay (works) are maishay (works) of awan (iniquity), and the pail (act) of chamas (violence) is in their kap (hands).

Their ragal (feet / foot) rawatz (run) to rai (evil), and they mahar (make) haste to shapak (shed) naqay (innocent) dam (blood): their machashabawath (thoughts) are machashabawath (thoughts) of awan (iniquity); shad (desolation) and shabar (destruction) are in their masalah (paths).

The darak (way) of shalawam (peace / safety) they don't yadai (know); and there is no mashapat (justice) in their maigal (goings): they have iqash (made) them crooked nathayab (paths); whoever darak (goes) therein does not yadai (know) shalawam (peace / safety).

Therefore is mashapat (justice) rachaq (far) from us, neither does tzadaqah (righteousness) nashag (overtake) us: we qawah (gather/wait) for awar (light), but, behold, chashak (darkness); for nagahah (brightness), but we halak (move) in obscurity.

We gashash (grope) for the qayar (wall) like the iwar (blind); yes, we gashash (grope) as those who have no iyanayam (eyes): we kashal (stumble / stagger) at noonday as in the nashap (twilight); among those who are lusty we are as mawath (death) men.

We hamah (great uproar) all like dabayam (bears), and moan bitterly like yawanayam (doves): we qawah (gather/wait) for mashapat (justice), but there is none; for yashawaih (salvation), but it is rachaq (far) off from us.

For our pashai (transgressions) are rabah (multiplied) before you, and our chataah (sin) inah (answer / respond) against us; for our pashai (transgressions) are with us, and as for our iwan (guilt/iniquity), we yadai (know) them:

Pashai (transgressing) and kachash (denying) Yahawah, and nasag (turning) away from following our Alahayam, dabar (word / matter) ishaq (oppression) and sarah (revolt), harah (conceiving) and hagah (uttering) from the lab (heart) dabaray (words) of falsehood.

Mashapat (justice) is nasag (turned) away backward, and tzadaqah (righteousness) imad (stands) rachawaq (afar) off; for amath (truth) is kashal (stumble / stagger) in the rachab (street), and nakachah (uprightness) can't bawaa (come).
Yes, amath (truth) is idar (lacking); and he who sawar (departs) from rai (evil) shalal (makes) himself a prey. Yahawah raah (see) it, and it displeased him that there was no mashapat (justice).

He raah (see) that there was no ayash (man / husband), and shamam (wondered) that there was no pagai (intercessor): therefore his own zarawai (arm) brought yashai (salvation) to him; and his tzadaqah (righteousness), it upheld him.

He labash (put) on tzadaqah (righteousness) as a sharayawan (breastplate), and a kawabai (helmet) of yashawaih (salvation) on his raash (head); and he labash (put) on bagaday (garments) of naqam (vengeance) for thalabashath (clothing), and was itah (clad) with qanaah (zeal) as a maiyal (mantle).

Il (over) to their gamalawath (deeds), accordingly he will shalam (repay), chamah (wrath) to his tzar (oppressor / distressor), gamawal (recompense) to his ayab (enemy); to the ayayam (islands) he will shalam (repay) gamawal (recompense).

So shall they yaraa (fear / be afraid) the sham (name) of Yahawah from the mairab (west), and his kabawad (glory) from the mazarach (rising) of the shamash (sun); for he will bawaa (come) as a rushing stream, which the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah drives.
"A gaal (redeemer) will bawaa (come) to Tzayawan (Zion), and to those who shawab (turn back / repent) from disobedience in Yaiqab (Jacob)," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

"As for me, this is my barayath (covenant) with them," amar (spoke) Yahawah. "My rawach (spirit / wind) who is on you, and my dabar (word / matter) which I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) in your pah (mouth), shall not depart out of your pah (mouth), nor out of the pah (mouth) of your zarai (seed), nor out of the pah (mouth) of your zarai (seed's) zarai (seed)," amar (spoke) Yahawah, "from henceforth and iwalam (forever)."
"Qawam (rise up), awar (light); for your awar (light) bawaa (come) come, and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah is zarach (risen) on you.

For, behold, chashak (darkness) shall kasah (cover) the aratz (Earth/land), and irapal (gross) darkness the laamayam (peoples); but Yahawah will arise on you, and his kabawad (glory) shall be raah (see) on you.
Gawayam (nations) shall halak (move) to your awar (light), and malakayam (kings) to the nagah (brightness) of your zarach (rising).

"Nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye) all around, and raah (see): they all qabatz (gather) themselves together, they bawaa (come) to you; your ban (son) shall bawaa (come) from rachawaq (far), and your banath (daughter) shall be carried in the arms.

Then you shall raah (see) and be radiant, and your labab (heart) shall thrill and be enlarged; because the hamawan (abundance) of the yam (sea/waters) shall be hapak (turned) to you, the wealth of the gawayam (nations) shall bawaa (come) to you.

The shapaih (multitude) of gamalayam (camels) shall kasah (cover) you, the bakaray (dromedaries) of Madayan (Midian) and Iyapah (Ephah); all they from Shabaa (Sheba) shall bawaa (come); they shall nashaa (lift) zahab (gold) and labawanah (frankincense), and shall proclaim the thahalath (praises) of Yahawah.

All the tzaan (flocks) of Qadar (Kedar) shall be qabatz (gathered) together to you, the ayalay (rams) of Nabayawath (Nebaioth) shall sharath (minister) to you; they shall ilah (go up / offer) up with acceptance on my mazabach (altar); and I will paar (glorify) the bayath (house) of my glory.
"Who are these who iwap (flying) as a ib (cloud), and as the yawanayam (doves) to their arabah (windows)?

Surely the ayayam (islands) shall qawah (gather/wait) for me, and the anayawath (ships) of Tharashayash (Tarshish) raashawan (first), to bawaa (come) your ban (son) from rachawaq (far), their kasap (silver) and their zahab (gold) with them, for the sham (name) of Yahawah your Alahayam, and for the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel), because he has paar (glorified) you.

"Foreigners shall banah (build) up your chawamah (walls), and their malak (king) shall sharath (minister) to you: for in my qatzap (wrath) I nakah (struck) you, but in my favor have I had racham (show mercy / love) on you.

Your shair (gates) also shall be pathach (open) continually; they shall not be sagar (shut) yawamam (by day) nor layal (night); that men may bawaa (come) to you the wealth of the gawayam (nations), and their malak (king) nahag (led) captive.
For that gaway (heathen / nation) and mamalakah (kingdom) that will not ibad (servant) you shall abad (destroy / perish); yes, those gawayam (nations) shall be utterly charab (wasted).

"The kabawad (glory) of Labanawan (Lebanon) shall bawaa (come) to you, the barawash (fir) tree, the thadahar (pine), and the box tree yachad (together), to paar (beautify) the maqawam (place) of my maqadash (sanctuary); and I will make the maqawam (place) of my ragal (feet / foot) kabad (glorious).

The banay (sons) of those who inah (oppress / afflict) you shall halak (move) shachach (bending) to you; and all those who naatz (despised) you shall shachah (bow) themselves down at the kapawath (soles) of your ragal (feet / foot); and they shall qaraa (called) you The iyar (city) of Yahawah, The Tzayawan (Zion) of the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel).

"Thachath (under) you have been forsaken and shanaa (hate), so that no ibar (pass over/through) passed through you, I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) you an iwalam (forever) gaawan (excellency), a mashawash (joy) of many dawar (generation / age / period).

You shall also drink the chalab (milk) of the gawayam (nations), and shall yanaq (nurse) from malak (king) shad (breasts); and you shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, am your Savior, and your gaal (redeemer), the abayar (mighty) One of Yaiqab (Jacob).

For nachashath (brass) I will bawaa (come) zahab (gold), and for barazal (iron) I will bawaa (come) kasap (silver), and for itz (wood) nachashath (brass), and for abanayam (stones) barazal (iron). I will also shawam (place / establish / appoint) your paqadah (officers) shalawam (peace / safety), and tzadaqah (righteousness) your nagash (ruler).

Chamas (violence) shall no more be shamai (hearken / hear) in your aratz (Earth/land), shad (desolation) nor shabar (destruction) within your gabawal (border/boundary); but you shall qaraa (called) your chawamah (walls) yashawaih (salvation), and your shair (gates) thahalah (praise).

The shamash (sun) shall be no more your awar (light) by yawamam (by day); neither for nagah (brightness) shall the yarach (moon) give awar (light) to you: but Yahawah will be to you an iwalam (forever) awar (light), and your Alahayam your glory.

Your shamash (sun) shall no more bawaa (come) down, neither shall your yarach (moon) asap (withdraw) itself; for Yahawah will be your iwalam (forever) awar (light), and the yamay (days) of your abal (mourning) shall be shalam (ended).

Your im (nation / people) also shall be all tzadayaq (righteous); they shall yarash (inherit) the aratz (Earth/land) iwalam (forever), the natzar (branch) of my matai (planting), the maishah (work) of my yad (hand), that I may be paar (glorified).
The qatan (small / young / least) one shall become a alap (thousand), and the tzaiyar (small) one a itzawam (strong) gaway (heathen / nation); I, Yahawah, will chawash (hasten) it in its ith (time)."

The rawach (spirit / wind) of the Adanay Yahawah is on me; because Yahawah has mashach (anointed) me to preach bashar (good) news to the inaw (humble). He has shalach (send) me to chabash (bind) up the shabar (brokenhearted), to qaraa (called) darawar (liberty) to the shabawayam (captives), and release to those who are asar (bound);
To qaraa (called) the shanah (year) of Yahawah favor, and the yawam (day) of naqam (vengeance) of our Alahayam; to nacham (turn away / repent) all who abal (mourn);

To shawam (place / establish / appoint) to those who abal (mourn) in Tzayawan (Zion), to nathan (give) to them a garland for ashes, the shaman (oil) of shashawan (joy) for abal (mourning), the maitah (garment) of thahalah (praise) for the rawach (spirit / wind) of kahah (heaviness); that they may be qaraa (called) ayalay (trees) of tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), the matai (planting) of Yahawah, that he may be paar (glorified).

They shall banah (build) the iwalam (forever) charabawath (wastes), they shall qawam (rise up) up the raashawan (former) desolations, and they shall chadash (repair) the charab (waste) iray (cities), the desolations of many dawar (generation / age / period).
Strangers shall imad (stand) and raih (feed) your tzaan (flocks), and foreigners shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers.

But you shall be qaraa (called) the kahanay (priests) of Yahawah; men will amar (spoke) you the masharathay (ministers) of our Alahayam: you will akal (eat) the wealth of the gawayam (nations), and you will yamar (boast) in their kabawad (glory).

Instead of your bashath (shame) you shall have mashanah (double); and instead of dishonor they shall ranan (rejoice) in their chalaq (portion): therefore in their aratz (Earth/land) they shall yarash (possess) mashanah (double); iwalam (forever) shamachah (joy) shall be to them.

"For I, Yahawah, ahab (love) mashapat (justice), I shanaa (hate) gazal (robbery) with ilah (iniquity); and I will nathan (give) them their recompense in amath (truth), and I will karath (cut) an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant) with them.

Their zarai (seed) shall be yadai (known) among the gawayam (nations), and their tzaatzaa (offspring) thawak (midst) the imayam (peoples); all who raah (see) them shall nakar (acknowledge) them, that they are the zarai (seed) which Yahawah has barak (blessed)."

I will shawash (greatly) shawash (rejoice) in Yahawah, my napash (soul) shall be gayal (joyful) in my Alahayam; for he has labash (clothed) me with the bagaday (garments) of yashai (salvation), he has yait (covered) me with the maiyal (robe) of tzadaqah (righteousness), as a chathan (bridegroom) kahan (priest) himself with a garland, and as a kalah (complete / finish) idah (adorns) herself with her kalay (jewels).

For as the aratz (Earth/land) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth its tzamach (bud), and as the ganah (garden) causes the things that are zarawai (sown) in it to tzamach (spring) forth; so the Adanay Yahawah will cause tzadaqah (righteousness) and thahalah (praise) to tzamach (spring) forth before all the gawayam (nations).

For Tzayawan (Zion's) sake will I not hold my chashah (peace), and for Yarawashalam (Jerusalem's) sake I will not shaqat (rest), until her tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth as nagah (brightness), and her yashawaih (salvation) as a lapayad (lamp) that bair (burns).

The gawayam (nations) shall raah (see) your tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and all malakayam (kings) your kabawad (glory), and you shall be qaraa (called) by a chadash (new) naqab (name), which the pah (mouth) of Yahawah shall sham (name).
You shall also be a itarah (crown) of thapaarah (beauty) in the yad (hand) of Yahawah, and a malawakah (royal) tzanayap (diadem) in the kap (hand) of your Alahayam.

You shall no more be amar (spoke) Forsaken; neither shall your aratz (Earth/land) any more be amar (spoke) shamamah (desolate): but you shall be qaraa (called) Chapatzayabah (Hephzibah), and your aratz (Earth/land) Beulah; for Yahawah chapatz (delights) in you, and your aratz (Earth/land) shall be bail (married).

For as a bachawar (young) man bail (marries) a bathawalah (virgin), so your ban (son) shall bail (marry) you; and as the chathan (bridegroom) mashawash (rejoices) over the kalah (complete / finish), so your Alahayam will shawash (rejoice) over you.

I paqad (visit) set watchmen on your chawamah (walls), Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); they shall thamayad (never) hold their chashah (peace) yawam (day) nor layal (night): you who zakar (remember) on Yahawah, take no damay (rest),
And nathan (give) him no damay (rest), until he establishes, and until he shawam (place / establish / appoint) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) a thahalah (praise) in the aratz (Earth/land).

Yahawah has shabai (swear / take oath) by his right yamayan (right hand), and by the zarawai (arm) of his iz (strength / might / refuge), "am (mother) I will no more nathan (give) your grain to be maakal (food) for your ayab (enemy); and foreigners shall not shathah (drinks) your new thayarawash (wine), for which you have labored:

But those who have garnered it shall akal (eat) it, and halal (praise) Yahawah; and those who have qabatz (gathered) it shall shathah (drinks) it in the chatzarawath (courts) of my qadash (set apart / make holy)."

Ibar (pass over/through) through, ibar (pass over/through) through the shairayam (gates)! Panah (turn) the darak (way) of the imayam (people)! Salal (cast) up, salal (cast) up the masalah (highway)! Saqal (gather) out the aban (stone)! Rawam (will lift up) up a nas (banner) for the imayam (peoples).

Behold, Yahawah has shamai (hearken / hear) to the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land), "amar (spoke) to the banath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion), ‘Behold, your yashai (salvation) bawaa (come). Behold, his shakar (reward) is with him, and his recompense panayam (face) him.'"

They shall qaraa (called) them The qadash (set apart / make holy) im (nation / people), The gaal (redeemed) of Yahawah: and you shall be qaraa (called) darash (sought) out, A iyar (city) not forsaken.

Who is this who bawaa (come) from Adawam (Edom), with chamatz (dyed) bagadayam (garments) from Batzarah (Bozrah)? This who is hadar (glorious) in his labawash (clothing), marching in the greatness of his kach (strength / mighty / power)? "It is I who dabar (word / matter) in tzadaqah (righteousness), rab (mighty) to yashai (salvation)."
Why are you adam (red) in your labawash (clothing), and your bagad (garments) like him who darak (treads) in the gath (wine) vat?

"I have darak (trodden) the pawarah (winepress) alone; and of the imayam (peoples) there was no man with me: yes, I darak (trod) them in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and ramas (trampled) them in my chamah (wrath); and their lifeblood is nazah (sprinkled) on my bagad (garments), and I have gaal (stained) all my clothing.
For the yawam (day) of naqam (vengeance) was in my lab (heart), and the shanah (year) of my gaal (redeemed) bawaa (come) come.

I nabat (looked), and there was none to izar (help); and I shamam (wondered) that there was none to samak (uphold): therefore my own zarawai (arm) brought yashai (salvation) to me; and my chamah (wrath), it upheld me.
I bawas (trod) down the imayam (peoples) in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and shakar (made) them drunk in my chamah (wrath), and I poured out their lifeblood on the aratz (Earth/land)."

I will zakar (remember) mention of the chasad (grace) kindnesses of Yahawah and the thahalath (praises) of Yahawah, according to all that Yahawah has gamal (bestowed) on us, and the rab (great) goodness toward the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), which he has gamal (bestowed) on them according to his racham (show mercy / love), and according to the rab (multitude) of his chasad (grace) kindnesses.
For he amar (spoke), "Surely, they are my im (nation / people), banayam (children) who will not shaqar (deal) falsely:" so he was their Savior.

In all their tzarah (affliction) he was tzar (oppressor / distressor), and the malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) of his panayam (face) yashai (salvation) them: in his ahabah (love) and in his chamalah (pity) he gaal (redeemed) them; and he natal (bore) them, and nashaa (lift) them all the yamay (days) of iwalam (forever).

But they marah (rebelled), and itzab (grieved) his qadash (set apart / make holy) rawach (spirit / wind): therefore he was hapak (turned) to be their ayab (enemy), and he himself lacham (fought) against them.

Then he zakar (remember) the yamay (days) of iwalam (forever), Mashah (Moses) and his im (nation / people), saying, "Where is he who ilah (go up / offer) them up out of the yam (sea/waters) with the raiy (shepherds) of his tzaan (flock)? Where is he who shawam (place / establish / appoint) his qadash (set apart / make holy) rawach (spirit / wind) in their qarab (among / near)?

Who caused his thapaarah (glorious) zarawai (arm) to yalak (go) at the right yamayan (right hand) of Mashah (Moses)? Who baqai (divided) the mayam (Waters) panayam (face) them, to ishah (make) himself an iwalam (forever) sham (name)?
Who yalak (led) them through the thahamawath (depths), as a sawas (horse) in the madabar (wilderness), so that they didn't kashal (stumble / stagger)?

As the livestock that yarad (go) down into the baqaih (valley), the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah caused them to nawach (rest); so you nahag (led) your im (nation / people), to ishah (make) yourself a thapaarah (glorious) sham (name).

Raah (see) down from shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and raah (see) from the zabawal (habitation) of your qadash (set apart / make holy) and of your glory: where are your qanaah (zeal) and your gabawarah (mighty) acts? The yearning of your maih (heart) and your compassion is apaq (restrained) toward me.

For you are our ab (father), though Abaraham (Abraham) doesn't know us, and Yashar-Al (Israel) does not nakar (acknowledge) us: you, Yahawah, are our ab (father); our gaal (redeemer) from iwalam (forever) is your sham (name).

O Yahawah, why do you thaih (make) us to err from your darak (ways), and qashach (harden) our lab (heart) from your yaraah (fear)? Shawab (turn back / repent) for your ibad (servant)' sake, the shabatay (tribes) of your nachalah (inheritance).
Your qadash (set apart / make holy) im (nation / people) yarash (possessed) it but a matzair (little) while: our tzar (oppressor / distressor) have bawas (trodden) down your maqadash (sanctuary).
We have become as they over whom you iwalam (forever) mashal (rule/have dominion) rule, as those who were not qaraa (called) by your sham (name).
Oh that you would tear the heavens, that you would yadai (come) down, that the mountains might quake at your panayam (face),
As when har (mountain) kindles the brushwood, and the har (mountain) causes the waters to boil; to make your name known to your adversaries, that the nations may tremble at your panayam (face)!
When you ishah (make) awesome things which we didn't iyan (eye) for, you came down, the mountains quaked at your iyan (eye).
For from of iwalam (forever) men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither has the eye seen a Alahayam besides you, who ishah (make) for him who waits for him.

You meet him who rejoices and works tzadaqah (righteousness), those who remember you in your nahay (ways). Behold, you were angry, and we iwan (guilt/iniquity). We have been in iwan (guilt/iniquity) for a long time; and shall we be saved?
For we have all become as one who is unclean, and all our righteousness is as a polluted garment: and we all fade as a leaf; and our iwan (guilt/iniquity), like the wind, chazaq (take) us away.
There is none who calls on your ab (father), who stirs up himself to take hold of you; for you have hidden your face from us, and have consumed us by yad (hand) of our iniquities.
But now, Yahawah, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you our potter; and we all are the work of your hand.
Don't be furious, Yahawah, neither remember iniquity forever: see, look, we beg you, we are all your people.
Your qadash (set apart / make holy) cities are become a wilderness, Zion has become a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.
Our holy and our beautiful house, where our fathers praised you, is burned with fire; and all our pleasant places are laid waste.
Will you refrain yourself for these things, Yahawah? Will you hold your chashah (peace), and inah (oppress / afflict) us very severely?

"I am darash (inquired) of by those who didn't shaal (ask); I am matzaa (found) by those who didn't baqash (seek) me: I amar (spoke), See me, see me, to a gaway (heathen / nation) that was not qaraa (called) by my sham (name).

I have parash (spread) out my yad (hand) all the yawam (day) to a sarar (rebellious) im (nation / people), who halak (move) in a darak (way) that is not tawab (good / proper function), achar (other) their own machashabah (thoughts);
A im (nation / people) who kais (provoke) me to my panayam (face) continually, zabach (sacrificing) in ganawath (gardens), and qatar (burning) incense on labanayam (bricks);

Who yashab (inhabit/dwell) among the qabarayam (graves), and lawan (lodge) in the secret places; who akal (eat) pig's bashar (flesh), and paraq (broth) of pagawal (abominable) things is in their kalay (vessels);

Who amar (spoke), qarab (come close) by yourself, don't nagash (come) near to me, for I am holier than you. These are a ishan (smoke) in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), a ash (fire) that yaqad (burns) all the yawam (day).
"Behold, it is kathab (write) panayam (face) me: I will not chashah (keep) silence, but will shalam (recompense), yes, I will shalam (recompense) into their chayaq (bosom),

Your own iwanath (iniquities), and the iwanath (iniquities) of your ab (father) yachad (together)," amar (spoke) Yahawah, "who have qatar (burned) incense on the harayam (mountains), and charap (blasphemed) me on the gabaiwath (hills); therefore will I raashawan (first) madad (measure) their pailah (work) into their chayaq (bosom)."

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, "As the new thayarawash (wine) is matzaa (found) in the ashakawal (cluster), and one amar (spoke), ‘Don't shachath (destroy) it, for a barakah (blessing) is in it:' so will I ishah (make) for my ibad (servant)' sake, that I may not shachath (destroy) them all.

I will yatzaa (go out / come out) forth a zarai (seed) out of Yaiqab (Jacob), and out of Yahawadah (Judah) an inheritor of my har (mountain); and my bachayar (chosen) shall yarash (inherit) it, and my ibad (servant) shall shakan (place) there.

Sharawan (Sharon) shall be a nawah (habitation) of tzaan (flocks), and the imaq (valley) of Ikawar (Achor) a place for baqar (morning) to rabatz (lie) down in, for my im (nation / people) who have darash (sought) me.

"But you who izab (forsake) Yahawah, who shakach (forget) my qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain), who irak (prepare) a shalachan (table) for Fortune, and who malaa (fill) up mixed mamasak (wine) to Manay (Destiny);

I will destine you to the charab (sword), and you shall all karai (bow) down to the tabach (slaughter); because when I qaraa (called), you didn't inah (answer / respond); when I dabar (word / matter), you didn't shamai (hearken / hear); but you ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in my iyan (eye), and bachar (chose) that in which I didn't chapatz (delight)."

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, "Behold, my ibad (servant) shall akal (eat), but you shall be raib (hungry); behold, my ibad (servant) shall shathah (drinks), but you shall be tzamaa (thirsty); behold, my ibad (servant) shall shamach (rejoice), but you shall be disappointed;

Behold, my ibad (servant) shall ranan (sing) for tawab (good / proper function) of lab (heart), but you shall tzaiq (cry) for kaab (sorrow) of lab (heart), and shall wail for anguish of rawach (spirit / wind).

You shall yanach (leave) your sham (name) for a shabawaih (curse) to my bachayar (chosen); and the Adanay Yahawah will mawath (death) you; and he will qaraa (called) his ibad (servant) by achar (other) sham (name):

So that he who blesses himself in the aratz (Earth/land) shall barak (blessed) himself in the Alahayam of aman (believe / have faith); and he who shabai (swear / take oath) in the aratz (Earth/land) shall shabai (swear / take oath) by the Alahayam of aman (believe / have faith); because the raashawan (former) tzarawath (troubles) are shakach (forgotten), and because they are sathar (hidden) from my iyan (eye).

"For, behold, I baraa (created) chadash (new) shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) and a chadash (new) aratz (Earth/land); and the raashawan (former) things shall not be zakar (remember), nor ilah (go up / offer) into lab (heart).

But be you shawash (glad) and gayal (rejoice) id (until / as far as) in that which I baraa (created); for, behold, I baraa (created) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) a gayalah (rejoicing), and her im (nation / people) a mashawash (joy).

I will gayal (rejoice) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and shawash (joy) in my im (nation / people); and there shall be shamai (hearken / hear) in her no more the qawal (sound / voice) of bakay (weeping) and the qawal (sound / voice) of zaiq (crying).

"There shall be no more there an iwal (infant) of yamayam (days), nor an old zaqan (man) who malaa (has) not filled his yamayam (days); for the nair (child) shall mawath (death) one maah (hundred) shanah (years) ban (son), and the chataa (sinner) being one maah (hundred) shanah (years) ban (son) shall be qalal (accursed).
They shall banah (build) bathayam (houses), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) them; and they shall natai (plant) karamayam (vineyards), and akal (eat) their paray (fruit).

They shall not banah (build), and achar (other) yashab (inhabit/dwell); they shall not natai (plant), and achar (other) akal (eat): for as the yamay (days) of a itz (tree) shall be the yamay (days) of my im (nation / people), and my bachayar (chosen) shall balah (long) enjoy the maishah (work) of their yad (hand).
They shall not yagai (labor) in rayaq (vain), nor yalad (birth / begot) forth for calamity; for they are the zarai (seed) of the barak (blessed) of Yahawah, and their tzaatzaa (offspring) with them.
