But, Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), who shapat (judge / judgement) righteously, who tests the kalayah (heart) and the lab (heart), I shall raah (see) your naqamah (vengeance) on them; for to you have I galah (revealed) my rayab (cause).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah concerning the anashay (men) of Inathawath (Anathoth), who baqash (seek) your napash (soul), amar (spoke), You shall not nabaa (prophesy) in the sham (name) of Yahawah, that you not mawath (death) by our yad (hand);

Therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), Behold, I will paqad (visit) them: the bachawar (young) men shall mawath (death) by the charab (sword); their ban (son) and their banath (daughter) shall mawath (death) by raib (famine);
And there shall be no shaarayath (remnant) to them: for I will bawaa (come) rai (evil) on the rai (men) of Inathawath (Anathoth), even the shanah (year) of their paqadah (visitation).

You are tzadayaq (righteous), Yahawah, when I rayab (contend) with you; yet I would reason the cause with you: why does the darak (way) of the rashai (wicked) tzalach (prosper)? Why are all they at ease who deal very bagad (treacherously)?

You have natai (planted) them, yes, they have sharash (taken) root; they yalak (grow), yes, they ishah (make) forth paray (fruit): you are qarawab (near) in their pah (mouth), and rachawaq (far) from their kalayah (heart).

But you, Yahawah, yadai (know) me; you raah (see) me, and bachan (try) my lab (heart) toward you: nathaq (pull) them out like tzaan (sheep) for the tabachah (slaughter), and qadash (set apart / make holy) them for the yawam (day) of haragah (slaughter).

How long shall the aratz (Earth/land) abal (mourn), and the ishab (herbs) of the whole shadah (country) yabash (dry land)? For the rai (wickedness) of those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein, the animals are sapah (consumed), and the iwap (flying); because they amar (spoke), He shall not raah (see) our acharayath (latter) end.

If you have rawatz (run) with the footmen, and they have laah (wearied) you, then how can you thacharah (contend) with sawasayam (horses)? And though in a aratz (Earth/land) of shalawam (peace / safety) you are batach (secure), yet how will you ishah (make) in the pride of the Yaradan (Jordan)?

For even your ach (brother/kinsman), and the bayath (house) of your ab (father), even they have dealt bagad (treacherously) with you; even they have qaraa (called) aloud achar (other) you: don't aman (believe / have faith) them, though they dabar (word / matter) tawab (good / proper function) words to you.
I have forsaken my bayath (house), I have natash (cast) off my nachalah (heritage); I nathan (give) given the yadadawath (dearly) beloved of my napash (soul) into the kap (hand) of her ayab (enemy).
My nachalah (heritage) has become to me as a aray (lion) in the yair (forest): she nathan (give) uttered her voice against me; therefore I have shanaa (hate) her.

Is my nachalah (heritage) to me as a tzabawai (speckled) iyat (bird) of prey? Are the iyat (birds) of prey against her all around? Yalak (go), asap (assemble) all the animals of the shadah (field), athah (you (masc)) them to akalah (devour).

Many raiyam (shepherds) have shachath (destroyed) my karam (vineyard), they have bawas (trodden) my chalaqah (portion) under bawas (foot), they nathan (give) made my chamadah (pleasant) chalaqah (portion) a shamamah (desolate) madabar (wilderness).

They have shawam (place / establish / appoint) it a desolation; it abal (mourns) to me, being shamamah (desolate); the whole aratz (Earth/land) is shamam (made) desolate, because no ayash (man / husband) shawam (place / establish / appoint) it to lab (heart).

Shadadayam (destroyers) bawaa (come) come on all the bare heights in the madabar (wilderness); for the charab (sword) of Yahawah akal (eat) from the one qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land) even to the other qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land): no bashar (flesh) has shalawam (peace / safety).

They have zarai (sown) chatah (wheat), and have qatzar (reaped) qatzayam (thorns); they have chalah (afflict) themselves to pain, and yail (profit) nothing: and you shall be bawash (ashamed) of your thabawaah (fruits), because of the charawan (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah against all my rai (evil) neighbors, who nagai (touch) the nachalah (inheritance) which I have caused my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel) to nachal (inherit): behold, I will nathash (pluck) them up from off their adamah (land), and will nathash (pluck) up the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) from thawak (midst) them.

It shall happen, achar (other) that I have nathash (plucked) them up, I will shawab (turn back / repent) and racham (show mercy / love) compassion on them; and I will shawab (turn back / repent) them again, every ayash (man / husband) to his nachalah (heritage), and every ayash (man / husband) to his aratz (Earth/land).

It shall happen, if they will lamad (teach / instruct) lamad (teach / instruct) the darakay (ways) of my im (nation / people), to shabai (swear / take oath) by my sham (name), As Yahawah chay (life); even as they lamad (teach / instruct) my im (nation / people) to shabai (swear / take oath) by Bail (Baal); then shall they be banah (build) up in the thawak (midst) of my im (nation / people).
But if they will not shamai (hearken / hear), then will I nathash (pluck) up that gaway (heathen / nation), nathash (plucking) up and destroying it, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah to me, halak (move), and qanah (buy) yourself a pashathah (linen) belt, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it on your waist, and don't bawaa (come) it in mayam (Waters).
So I bought a belt according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) it on my waist.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me the shanay (second) time, amar (spoke),
Laqach (take / seize) the belt that you have bought, which is on your waist, and qawam (rise up), yalak (go) to the Parath (Euphrates), and taman (hide) it there in a cleft of the salai (rock).
So I yalak (went), and taman (hid) it by the Parath (Euphrates), as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) me.

It happened qatz (after) many yamayam (days), that Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, qawam (rise up), yalak (go) to the Parath (Euphrates), and laqach (take / seize) the belt from there, which I tzawah (commanded) you to taman (hide) there.

Then I yalak (went) to the Parath (Euphrates), and chapar (dug), and laqach (take / seize) the belt from the maqawam (place) where I had taman (hidden) it; and behold, the belt was shachath (marred), it was tzalach (profitable) for nothing.
Then the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, In this way I will shachath (mar) the gaawan (pride) of Yahawadah (Judah), and the rab (great) gaawan (pride) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

This rai (evil) im (nation / people), who maan (refuse) to shamai (hearken / hear) my dabar (word / matter), who halak (move) in the stubbornness of their lab (heart), and are yalak (gone) achar (other) other Alahayam to ibad (servant) them, and to shachah (worship) them, shall even be as this belt, which is tzalach (profitable) for nothing.

For as the belt clings to the waist of a ayash (man / husband), so have I caused to cling to me the whole bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) and the whole bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah; that they may be to me for a im (nation / people), and for a sham (name), and for a thahalah (praise), and for a glory: but they would not shamai (hearken / hear).

Therefore you shall amar (spoke) to them this dabar (word / matter): Thus amaraw (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), Every nabal (bottle) shall be malaa (filled) with yayan (wine): and they shall amar (spoke) you, Do we not yadai (certainly) yadai (know) that every nabal (bottle) shall be malaa (filled) with yayan (wine)?

Then you shall amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, Behold, I will malaa (fill) all the yashabay (inhabitants) of this aratz (Earth/land), even the malakayam (kings) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) on Dawad (David's) kasaa (throne), and the kahanayam (priests), and the nabayaayam (prophets), and all the yashabay (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), with shakarawan (drunkenness).

I will napatz (dash) them ayash (man / husband) against ach (brother/kinsman), even the abawath (fathers) and the banayam (sons) yachad (together), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah: I will not chamal (pity), nor chawas (spare), nor racham (show mercy / love) compassion, that I should not shachath (destroy) them.
Shamai (hearken / hear), and azan (ear) ear; don't be gabah (proud); for Yahawah has dabar (word / matter).

Nathan (give) kabawad (glory) to Yahawah your Alahayam, before he causes chashak (darkness), and before your ragal (feet / foot) nagap (stumble) on the nashap (dark) haray (mountains), and, while you qawah (gather/wait) for awar (light), he shawam (place / establish / appoint) it into the shadow of tzalamawath (death), and shayath (put / appoint / make) it irapal (gross) darkness.

But if you will not shamai (hearken / hear) it, my napash (soul) shall bakah (weep) in masathar (secret) for your gawah (pride); and my iyan (eye) shall damai (weep) bitterly, and yarad (run) down with damaih (tears), because Yahawah idar (flock) is shabah (taken) captive.

Amar (spoke) to the malak (king) and to the gabayarah (queen) mother, shapal (humble) yourselves, yashab (inhabit/dwell) down; for your headdresses have yarad (come) down, even the itarah (crown) of your glory.

The iray (cities) of the nagab (south) are sagar (shut) up, and there is none to pathach (open) them: Yahawadah (Judah) is galah (carried) away captive, shalawam (peace / safety) of it; it is wholly galah (carried) away captive.
Nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye), and raah (see) those who bawaa (come) from the tzapawan (north): where is the idar (flock) that was nathan (give) you, your thapaarah (beautiful) tzaan (flock)?

What will you amar (spoke), when he shall paqad (visit) over you as raash (head) those whom you have yourself lamad (teach / instruct) to be alapayam (friends) to you? Shall not chabalayam (sorrows) achaz (take) hold of you, as of a ayashah (woman / wife) in yalad (birth / begot)?

If you amar (spoke) in your labab (heart), Why are these things qaraa (called) on me? For the greatness of your iwan (guilt/iniquity) are your shawal (skirts) galah (uncovered), and your iqab (heels) suffer chamas (violence).

Can the Kawashay (Ethiopian) hapak (change) his iwar (skin), or the namar (leopard) his chabarabarah (spots)? Then may you also do yatab (good), who are lamawad (accustomed) to do raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil).
Therefore will I pawatz (scatter) them, as the qash (stubble) that passes ibar (pass over/through), by the rawach (spirit / wind) of the madabar (wilderness).
This is your gawaral (lot), the manah (portion) mad (measured) to you from me, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah; because you have shakach (forgotten) me, and batach (trusted) in falsehood.
Therefore will I also chashap (uncover) your shawal (skirts) on your panayam (face), and your qalawan (shame) shall raah (see).

I raah (see) seen your shaqawatz (abominations), even your naap (adulteries), and your matzahalah (neighing), the lewdness of your prostitution, on the gabaiwath (hills) in the shadah (field). Away (woe) to you, Yarawashalam (Jerusalem)! You will not be made tahar (clean); how iwad (more/again) shall it yet be?
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah that came to Yaramayah (Jeremiah) dabar (word / matter) the batzarath (drought).

Yahawadah (Judah) abal (mourns), and its shair (gates) amal (languish), they sit in qadar (black) on the aratz (Earth/land); and the tzawachah (cry) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) is ilah (go up / offer) up.

Their adayar (nobles) shalach (send) their tzaiyar (little) ones to the mayam (Waters): they bawaa (come) to the cisterns, and matzaa (find) no mayam (Waters); they shawab (turn back / repent) with their kalay (vessels) rayaqam (empty); they are disappointed and bawash (confounded), and chapah (cover) their raash (head).
Because of the adamah (ground) which is cracked, because no gasham (rain) has been in the aratz (Earth/land), the plowmen are disappointed, they chapah (cover) their raash (head).
Yes, the ayalath (hind) also in the shadah (field) yalad (birth / begot), and izab (forsakes) her young, because there is no dashaa (grass).
The paraa (wild) donkeys imad (stand) on the bare heights, they shaap (pant) for rawach (spirit / wind) like jackals; their iyan (eye) kalah (complete / finish), because there is no herbage.
Though our iwan (guilt/iniquity) inah (answer / respond) against us, ishah (make) for your sham (name) sake, Yahawah; for our mashawabah (backslidings) are many; we have chataa (sinned) against you.

You maqawah (gathering / collection) of Yashar-Al (Israel), its Savior in the ith (time) of tzarah (trouble), why should you be as a foreigner in the aratz (Earth/land), and as a arach (wayfaring) man who natah (turns) aside to stay for a lawan (night)?

Why should you be like a scared ayash (man / husband), as a gabawar (mighty) man who can't yashai (salvation)? Yet you, Yahawah, are in the qarab (among / near) of us, and we are qaraa (called) by your sham (name); don't yanach (leave) us.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah to this im (nation / people), Even so have they ahab (love) to nawai (wander); they have not chashak (darkness) their ragal (feet / foot): therefore Yahawah does not ratzah (accept) them; now he will zakar (remember) their iwan (guilt/iniquity), and paqad (visit) their chataah (sin).
Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, Don't palal (pray) for this im (nation / people) for their tawab (good / proper function).

When they tzawam (fast), I will not shamai (hearken / hear) their ranah (cry); and when they ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilah (offering) and meal manachah (offering), I will not ratzah (accept) them; but I will kalah (complete / finish) them by the charab (sword), and by the raib (famine), and by the dabar (word / matter).

Then I amar (spoke), ahah (ah), Adanay Yahawah! Behold, the nabaayam (prophets) amar (spoke) them, You shall not raah (see) the charab (sword), neither shall you have raib (famine); but I will nathan (give) you amath (truth) shalawam (peace / safety) in this maqawam (place).

Then Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, The nabaayam (prophets) nabaa (prophesy) shaqar (lies) in my sham (name); I didn't shalach (send) them, neither have I tzawah (commanded) them, neither dabar (word / matter) I to them: they nabaa (prophesy) to you a shaqar (lying) chazawan (vision), and qasam (divination), and a thing of nothing, and the tharamah (deceit) of their own lab (heart).

Therefore thus amarayam (says) Yahawah concerning the nabaayam (prophets) who nabaa (prophesy) in my sham (name), and I didn't shalach (send) them, yet they amar (spoke), charab (sword) and raib (famine) shall not be in this aratz (Earth/land): By charab (sword) and raib (famine) shall those nabaayam (prophets) be thamam (consumed).

The im (nation / people) to whom they nabaa (prophesy) shall be shalak (cast) out in the chatzawath (streets) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) panayam (face) of the raib (famine) and the charab (sword); and they shall have none to qabar (bury) them—them, their wives, nor their ban (son), nor their banath (daughter): for I will shapak (pour) their rai (wickedness) on them.

You shall amar (spoke) this dabar (word / matter) to them, Let my iyan (eye) yarad (run) down with damaih (tears) layal (night) and yawamam (by day), and let them not damah (cease); for the bathawalah (virgin) banath (daughter) of my im (nation / people) is shabar (broken) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shabar (breach), with a very chalah (afflict) makah (wound).

If I yatzaa (go out / come out) forth into the shadah (field), then, behold, the chalal (slain) with the charab (sword)! And if I bawaa (come) into the iyar (city), then, behold, those who are thachalawaa (sick) with raib (famine)! For both the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) and the kahan (priest) sachar (go) about in the aratz (Earth/land), and have no yadai (knowledge).

Have you maas (utterly) maas (rejected) Yahawadah (Judah)? Has your napash (soul) loathed Tzayawan (Zion)? Why have you nakah (struck) us, and there is no marapaa (healing) for us? We qawah (gather/wait) for shalawam (peace / safety), but no tawab (good / proper function) came; and for a ith (time) of marapaa (healing), and behold, baithah (dismay)!
We yadai (acknowledge), Yahawah, our rashai (wickedness), and the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of our ab (father); for we have chataa (sinned) against you.
Do not naatz (abhor) us, for your sham (name) sake; nabal (do) not disgrace the kasaa (throne) of your kabawad (glory): zakar (remember), don't parar (break) your barayath (covenant) with us.

Are there any among the habalay (vanities) of the gawayam (nations) that can cause gasham (rain)? Or can the sky nathan (give) rababayam (showers)? Aren't you he, Yahawah our Alahayam? Therefore we will qawah (gather/wait) for you; for you ishah (make) made all these things.

Then Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, Though Mashah (Moses) and Shamawaal (Samuel) imad (stood) panayam (face) me, yet my napash (soul) would not be toward this im (nation / people): shalach (send) them out of my panayam (face), and yatzaa (go out / come out) them go forth.

It shall happen, when they amar (spoke) you, Where shall we yatzaa (go out / come out) forth? Then you shall amar (spoke) them, Thus yaamaraw (says) Yahawah: Such as are for mawath (death), to mawath (death); and such as are for the charab (sword), to the charab (sword); and such as are for the raib (famine), to the raib (famine); and such as are for shabay (captivity), to shabay (captivity).

I will paqad (visit) over them arabai (four) mashapachawath (kinds), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah: the charab (sword) to harag (kill), and the kalabayam (dogs) to sachab (tear), and the iwap (flying) of the sky, and the animals of the aratz (Earth/land), to akal (eat) and to shachath (destroy).

I will nathan (give) them to be tossed back and forth among all the mamalakawath (kingdoms) of the aratz (Earth/land), galal (because) of Manashah (Manasseh), the ban (son) of Chazaqayah (Hezekiah), malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), for that which he ishah (make) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).
For who will chamal (have) pity on you, Yarawashalam (Jerusalem)? Or who will nawad (bemoan) you? Or who will sawar (turn) aside to shaal (ask) of your shalawam (peace / safety)?

You have rejected me, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, you have yalak (gone) backward: therefore have I natah (stretched) out my yad (hand) against you, and shachath (destroyed) you; I am laah (weary) with nacham (turn away / repent).

I have zarah (winnowed) them with a zarah (fan) in the shairay (gates) of the aratz (Earth/land); I have shakal (bereaved) them of children, I abad (destroy / perish) destroyed my im (nation / people); they didn't shawab (turn back / repent) from their darak (ways).

Their alamanah (widows) are itzam (increased) to me above the chawal (sand) of the yamayam (seas); I bawaa (come) brought on them against the am (mother) of the bachawar (young) men a shadad (destroyer) at noonday: I have caused anguish and bahalawath (terrors) to napal (fall / be cast down) on her pathaawam (suddenly).

She who has yalad (birth / begot) shabai (seven) languishes; she has napach (given) up the napash (soul); her shamash (sun) is bawaa (come) down while it was yet yawamam (by day); she has been disappointed and chapar (confounded): and their shaarayath (residue) will I nathan (give) to the charab (sword) panayam (face) their ayab (enemy), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

Away (woe) is me, my am (mother), that you have yalad (birth / begot) me a ayash (man / husband) of rayab (strife) and a ayash (man / husband) of madawan (contention) to the whole aratz (Earth/land)! I have not nashah (lent), neither have men lent to me; yet everyone of them qalal (curses) me.

Yahawah amar (spoke), Most certainly I will strengthen you for tawab (good / proper function); most certainly I will cause the ayab (enemy) to pagai (make) supplication to you in the ith (time) of rai (evil) and in the ith (time) of tzarah (affliction).
Can one raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) barazal (iron), even barazal (iron) from the tzapawan (north), and nachashath (brass)?

Your chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) and your awatzar (treasures) will I nathan (give) for a baz (spoil) without machayar (price), and that for all your chataah (sin), even in all your gabawal (border/boundary).

I will ibar (pass over/through) them to pass with your ayab (enemy) into a aratz (Earth/land) which you don't yadai (know); for a ash (fire) is qadach (kindled) in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), which shall yaqad (burn) on you.

Yahawah, you yadai (know); zakar (remember) me, and paqad (visit) me, and naqam (avenge) me of my persecutors; don't laqach (take / seize) me away in your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting): yadai (know) that for your sake I have nashaa (lift) charapah (reproach).

Your dabar (word / matter) were matzaa (found), and I akal (eat) them; and your dabar (word / matter) were to me a shashawan (joy) and the shamachah (rejoicing) of my labab (heart): for I am qaraa (called) by your sham (name), Yahawah, Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies).

I didn't yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the sawad (assembly) of those who shachaq (make) merry, nor ilaz (rejoiced); I yashab (inhabit/dwell) badad (alone) panayam (face) of your yad (hand); for you malaa (have) filled me with zaim (indignation).

Why is my kaab (pain) natzach (perpetual), and my makah (wound) anash (incurable), which maan (refuses) to be rapaa (healed)? Will you indeed be to me as a deceitful brook, as mayam (Waters) that aman (believe / have faith)?

Therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, If you shawab (turn back / repent), then will I shawab (turn back / repent) you again, that you may imad (stand) panayam (face) me; and if you yatzaa (go out / come out) forth the yaqar (precious) from the zalal (vile), you shall be as my pah (mouth): they shall shawab (turn back / repent) to you, but you shall not shawab (turn back / repent) to them.

I will nathan (give) you to this im (nation / people) a batzar (fortified) bronze chawamah (wall); and they shall lacham (fight) against you, but they shall not yakal (prevail) against you; for I am with you to yashai (salvation) you and to natzal (deliver) you, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.
I will natzal (deliver) you out of the yad (hand) of the rai (wicked), and I will padah (redeem) you out of the kap (hand) of the irayatz (terrible).
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came also to me, amar (spoke),
You shall not laqach (take / seize) a ayashah (woman / wife), neither shall you have banayam (sons) or banawath (daughters), in this maqawam (place).

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah concerning the banayam (sons) and concerning the banawath (daughters) who are yalad (birth / begot) in this maqawam (place), and concerning their am (mother) who yalad (birth / begot) them, and concerning their ab (father) who became their ab (father) in this aratz (Earth/land):

They shall mawath (death) thachalawaa (grievous) mamawathay (deaths): they shall not be sapad (lamented), neither shall they be qabar (bury); they shall be as daman (dung) on the surface of the adamah (ground); and they shall be kalah (complete / finish) by the charab (sword), and by raib (famine); and their nabalah (dead) bodies shall be maakal (food) for the iwap (flying) of the sky, and for the animals of the aratz (Earth/land).

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, Don't bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of marazach (mourning), neither yalak (go) to sapad (lament), neither nawad (bemoan) them; for I have asap (taken) away my shalawam (peace / safety) from this im (nation / people), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, even loving chasad (grace) and tender rachamayam (mercies).

Both gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and qatan (small / young / least) shall mawath (death) in this aratz (Earth/land); they shall not be qabar (bury), neither shall men sapad (lament) for them, nor gadad (cut) themselves, nor qarach (make) themselves bald for them;

Neither shall men break bread for them in abal (mourning), to nacham (turn away / repent) them for the mawath (death); neither shall men give them the kawas (cup) of thanachawam (consolation) to shaqah (drink) for their ab (father) or for their am (mother).
You shall not bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of mashathah (feasting) to yashab (inhabit/dwell) with them, to akal (eat) and to shathah (drinks).

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel): Behold, I will shabath (shabath / rest) to cease out of this maqawam (place), before your iyan (eye) and in your yawam (day), the qawal (sound / voice) of shashawan (mirth) and the qawal (sound / voice) of shamachah (gladness), the qawal (sound / voice) of the chathan (bridegroom) and the qawal (sound / voice) of the kalah (complete / finish).

It shall happen, when you shall show this im (nation / people) all these dabarayam (words), and they shall amar (spoke) you, Why has Yahawah dabar (word / matter) all this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) rai (evil) against us? Or what is our iwan (guilt/iniquity)? Or what is our chataah (sin) that we have chataa (committed) against Yahawah our Alahayam?

Then you shall amar (spoke) them, Because your ab (father) have forsaken me, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, and have yalak (walked) achar (other) other Alahayam, and have ibad (servant) them, and have shachah (worshiped) them, and have forsaken me, and have not shamar (keep/guard) my thawarah (instruction);

And you ishah (make) done raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) more than your ab (father); for, han (behold), you halak (move) ayash (man / husband) one achar (other) the stubbornness of his rai (evil) lab (heart), so that you don't shamai (hearken / hear) to me:

Therefore will I tawal (cast) you forth out of this aratz (Earth/land) into the aratz (Earth/land) that you yadai (have) not known, neither you nor your ab (father); and there you shall ibad (servant) other Alahayam yawamam (by day) and layal (night); for I will show you no favor.

Therefore, behold, the yamayam (days) bawaa (come), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, that it shall no more be amar (spoke), As Yahawah chay (life), who ilah (go up / offer) up the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt);

But, As Yahawah chay (life), who ilah (go up / offer) up the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) from the aratz (Earth/land) of the tzapawan (north), and from all the aratzawath (countries) where he had nadach (driven) them. I will shawab (turn back / repent) them again into their adamah (land) that I nathan (give) to their ab (father).

Behold, I will shalach (send) for many fishermen, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, and they shall dayag (fish) them up; and afterward I will shalach (send) for many tzayadayam (hunters), and they shall tzawad (hunt) them from every har (mountain), and from every gabaih (hill), and out of the clefts of the salaiyam (rocks).
For my iyan (eye) are on all their darak (ways); they are not sathar (hidden) from my panayam (face), neither is their iwan (guilt/iniquity) concealed from my iyan (eye).

Raashawan (first) I will shalam (recompense) their iwan (guilt/iniquity) and their chataah (sin) mashanah (double), because they have chalal (polluted) my aratz (Earth/land) with the carcasses of their shaqawatz (detestable) things, and malaa (have) filled my nachalah (inheritance) with their thawaibah (abominations).

Yahawah, my iz (strength / might / refuge), and my stronghold, and my manawas (refuge) in the yawam (day) of tzarah (affliction), to you shall the gawayam (nations) bawaa (come) from the apas (ends) of the aratz (Earth/land), and shall amar (spoke), Our ab (father) nachal (have) inherited nothing but shaqar (lies), habal (vanity) and things in which there is no yail (profit).
Shall a adam (man) ishah (make) to himself Alahayam, which yet are no Alahayam?

Therefore, behold, I yadai (will) cause them to know, paim (this) once yadai (will) I cause them to know my yad (hand) and my gabawarah (might); and they shall yadai (know) that my sham (name) is Yahawah.

The chataah (sin) of Yahawadah (Judah) is kathab (write) with a it (pen) of barazal (iron), and with the tzaparan (point) of a shamayar (diamond): it is engraved on the tablet of their lab (heart), and on the qaranawath (horns) of your mazabach (altars);
While their ban (son) zakar (remember) their mazabach (altars) and their Asharah (Asherim) by the rainan (green) itz (trees) on the gabah (high) gabaiwath (hills).

My harar (mountain) in the shadah (field), I will nathan (give) your chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) and all your awatzar (treasures) for a baz (spoil), and your bamah (high) places, because of chataah (sin), throughout all your gabawal (border/boundary).

You, even of yourself, shall shamat (discontinue) from your nachalah (heritage) that I nathan (give) you; and I will cause you to ibad (servant) your ayab (enemy) in the aratz (Earth/land) which you don't yadai (know): for you have qadach (kindled) a ash (fire) in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) which shall yaqad (burn) iwalam (forever).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: arar (cursed) is the gabar (man) who batach (trusts) in adam (man), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) bashar (flesh) his zarawai (arm), and whose lab (heart) sawar (departs) from Yahawah.

For he shall be like the heath in the irabah (desert), and shall not raah (see) when tawab (good / proper function) bawaa (come), but shall shakan (place) the charar (parched) places in the madabar (wilderness), a malachah (salt) aratz (Earth/land) and not yashab (inhabit/dwell).
Barak (blessed) is the gabar (man) who batach (trusts) in Yahawah, and whose mabatach (trust) Yahawah is.

For he shall be as a itz (tree) shathal (planted) by the mayam (Waters), who shalach (send) out its sharash (roots) by the yawabal (river), and shall not yaraa (fear / be afraid) when cham (heat) bawaa (come), but its ilah (leaf) shall be rainan (green); and shall not be daag (careful) in the shanah (year) of batzarath (drought), neither shall mawash (cease) from ishah (make) paray (fruit).
The lab (heart) is iqab (deceitful) above all things, and it is exceedingly corrupt: who yadai (can) know it?

I, Yahawah, chaqar (search) the lab (heart), I bachan (try) the lab (heart), even to nathan (give) every ayash (man / husband) according to his darak (ways), according to the paray (fruit) of his mailal (doings).

As the qaraa (called) that dagar (sits) on eggs which she has not laid, so is he who ishah (make) riches, and not by mashapat (right); in the chatzay (midst) of his yawam (day) they shall izab (leave) him, and at his acharayath (end) he shall be a nabal (fool).
A kabawad (glorious) kasaa (throne), set on marawam (high) from the raashawan (beginning), is the maqawam (place) of our maqadash (sanctuary).

Yahawah, the maqawah (gathering / collection) of Yashar-Al (Israel), all who izab (forsake) you shall be disappointed. Those who depart from me shall be kathab (write) in the aratz (Earth/land), because they have forsaken Yahawah, the maqawar (spring) of chay (life) mayam (Waters).
Rapaa (heal) me, O Yahawah, and I shall be rapaa (healed); yashai (salvation) me, and I shall be yashai (salvation): for you are my thahalah (praise).
Behold, they amar (spoke) me, Where is the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah? Bawaa (come) it come now.

As for me, I have not hurried from being a raih (shepherd) achar (other) you; neither have I awah (desired) the anash (woeful) yawam (day); you yadai (know): that which mawatzaa (came) out of my shapah (lips) was nakach (before) your panayam (face).
Don't be a machathah (terror) to me: you are my machasah (refuge) in the yawam (day) of rai (evil).

Let them be disappointed who radap (persecute) me, but let not me be disappointed; let them be chathath (dismayed), but don't let me be chathath (dismayed); bawaa (come) on them the yawam (day) of rai (evil), and shabar (destroy) them with mashanah (double) shabarawan (destruction).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah to me: halak (move), and imad (stand) in the shair (gate) of the banay (children) of the im (nation / people), through which the malakay (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah) bawaa (come) in, and by which they yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and in all the shairay (gates) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem);

And amar (spoke) them, shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, you malakay (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah), and all Yahawadah (Judah), and all the yashabay (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), that bawaa (come) in by these shairayam (gates):

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, shamar (keep/guard) heed to yourselves, and nashaa (lift) no mashaa (burden) on the shabath (shabath / rest) yawam (day), nor bawaa (come) it in by the shairay (gates) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem);

Neither yatzaa (go out / come out) forth a mashaa (burden) out of your bayath (house) on the shabath (shabath / rest) yawam (day) qadash (set apart / make holy), neither ishah (make) any malaakah (work): but make the shabath (shabath / rest) yawam (day), as I tzawah (commanded) your ab (father).

But they didn't listen, neither natah (turn) their azan (ear), but made their irap (neck) qashah (rough / hard), that they might not shamai (hearken / hear), and might not laqach (take / seize) mawasar (instruction).

It shall happen, if you shamai (hearken / hear) shamai (hearken / hear) to me, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, to bawaa (come) in no mashaa (burden) through the shairay (gates) of this iyar (city) on the shabath (shabath / rest) yawam (day), but to make the shabath (shabath / rest) yawam (day) qadash (set apart / make holy), to ishah (make) no malaakah (work) therein;

Then shall there bawaa (come) in by the shairay (gates) of this iyar (city) malakayam (kings) and sharayam (princes) sitting on the kasaa (throne) of Dawad (David), rakab (riding) in rakab (chariots) and on sawasayam (horses), they, and their sharayam (princes), the ayash (man / husband) of Yahawadah (Judah), and the yashabayam (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); and this iyar (city) shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) iwalam (forever).

They shall bawaa (come) from the iray (cities) of Yahawadah (Judah), and from the sabayabawath (places) around Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and from the aratz (Earth/land) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), and from the lowland, and from the har (mountain) country, and from the nagab (south), bawaa (come) burnt ilah (offerings), and zabach (sacrifices), and meal manachah (offerings), and labawanah (frankincense), and bawaa (come) thawadah (sacrifices) of thanksgiving, to the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

But if you will not shamai (hearken / hear) to me to make the shabath (shabath / rest) yawam (day) qadash (set apart / make holy), and not to nashaa (lift) a mashaa (burden) and bawaa (come) in at the shairay (gates) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) on the shabath (shabath / rest) yawam (day); then will I yatzath (kindle) a ash (fire) in its shairay (gates), and it shall akal (eat) the aramanawath (palaces) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and it shall not be kabah (quenched).
The dabar (word / matter) which came to Yaramayah (Jeremiah) from Yahawah, amar (spoke),
Qawam (rise up), and yarad (go) down to the yatzar (potter's) bayath (house), and there I will shamai (hearken / hear) you to hear my dabar (word / matter).
Then I yarad (went) down to the yatzar (potter's) bayath (house), and hanah (Behold), he was ishah (make) a malaakah (work) on the abanayam (wheels).

When the kalay (vessel) that he ishah (make) of the chamar (clay) was shachath (marred) in the yad (hand) of the yatzar (potter), he ishah (make) it again achar (other) kalay (vessel), as seemed yashar (upright) to the yatzar (potter) to ishah (make) it.
Then the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), can't I ishah (make) with you as this yatzar (potter)? Naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah. Behold, as the chamar (clay) in the yatzar (potter's) yad (hand), so are you in my yad (hand), bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

At what ragai (in an instance) I shall dabar (word / matter) concerning a gaway (heathen / nation), and concerning a mamalakah (kingdom), to nathash (pluck) up and to nathatz (break) down and to abad (destroy / perish) it;

If that gaway (heathen / nation), concerning which I have dabar (word / matter), shawab (turn back / repent) from their rai (evil), I will nacham (turn away / repent) of the rai (evil) that I chashab (thought) to ishah (make) to them.
At what ragai (in an instance) I shall dabar (word / matter) concerning a gaway (heathen / nation), and concerning a mamalakah (kingdom), to banah (build) and to natai (plant) it;

If they ishah (make) that which is rai (evil) in my iyan (eye), that they not shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice), then I will nacham (turn away / repent) of the tawab (good / proper function), with which I amar (spoke) I would yatab (benefit) them.

Now therefore, amar (spoke) to the ayash (man / husband) of Yahawadah (Judah), and to the yawashabay (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: Behold, I yatzar (frame) rai (evil) against you, and chashab (devise) a machashabah (device) against you: shawab (turn back / repent) you now everyone from his rai (evil) darak (way), and yatab (amend) your darak (ways) and your mailal (doings).
But they amar (spoke), It is in vain; for we will yalak (walk) achar (other) our own machashabah (devices), and we will ishah (make) everyone after the stubbornness of his rai (evil) lab (heart).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: shaal (ask) now among the gawayam (nations), who has shamai (hearken / hear) such things; the bathawalah (virgin) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ishah (make) done a very shairawarah (horrible) thing.
Shall the shalag (snow) of Labanawan (Lebanon) izab (fail) from the tzawar (rock) of the shadah (field)? Shall the qar (cold) mayam (Waters) that nazal (flow) down from afar be dried up?

For my im (nation / people) have shakach (forgotten) me, they have qatar (burned) incense to shawaa (vanity) Alahayam; and they have been made to stumble in their darak (ways), in the iwalam (forever) shabayalay (paths), to yalak (walk) in byways, in a darak (way) not built up;

To shawam (place / establish / appoint) their aratz (Earth/land) an shamah (astonishment), and a iwalam (forever) sharawaqah (hissing); everyone who passes thereby shall be shamam (astonished), and nawad (shake) his raash (head).

I will pawatz (scatter) them as with an qadayam (east) rawach (spirit / wind) panayam (face) the ayab (enemy); I will show them the irap (neck), and not the panayam (face), in the yawam (day) of their ayad (calamity).

Then they amar (spoke), yalak (come), and let us chashab (devise) machashabawath (devices) against Yaramayah (Jeremiah); for the thawarah (instruction) shall not abad (destroy / perish) from the kahan (priest), nor itzah (counsel) from the chakam (wise), nor the dabar (word / matter) from the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy). Yalak (come), and let us nakah (strike) him with the lashawan (tongue / language), and let us not qashab (give) heed to any of his dabar (word / matter).
Qashab (give) heed to me, Yahawah, and shamai (hearken / hear) to the qawal (sound / voice) of those who contend with me.

Shall rai (evil) be shalam (recompensed) for tawab (good / proper function)? For they have karah (dug) a shawachah (pit) for my napash (soul). Zakar (remember) how I imad (stood) panayam (face) you to dabar (word / matter) tawab (good / proper function) for them, to shawab (turn back / repent) away your chamah (wrath) from them.

Therefore nathan (give) up their ban (son) to the raib (famine), and give them over to the yad (hand) of the charab (sword); and let their wives become childless, and alamanawath (widows); and let their ban (son) be slain of mawath (death), and their bachawar (young) men nakah (struck) of the charab (sword) in malachamah (battle).

Let a zaiq (cry) be shamai (hearken / hear) from their bayath (house), when you shall bawaa (come) a gadawad (troop) pathaawam (suddenly) on them; for they have karah (dug) a shayachah (pit) to lakad (take) me, and taman (hid) pachayam (snares) for my ragal (feet / foot).

Yet, Yahawah, you yadai (know) all their itzah (counsel) against me to kill me; don't kapar (forgive) their iwan (guilt/iniquity), neither machah (blot) out their chataah (sin) from your panayam (face); but let them be kashal (stumble / stagger) panayam (face) you; ishah (make) you with them in the ith (time) of your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, halak (move), and qanah (buy) a yatzar (potter's) charash (earthen) baqabaq (bottle), and take some of the zaqanay (elders) of the im (nation / people), and of the zaqanay (elders) of the kahanayam (priests);

And yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to the gayaa (valley) of the ban (son) of Hanam (Hinnom), which is by the entry of the shair (gate) Harsith, and qaraa (called) there the dabarayam (words) that I shall dabar (word / matter) you;

And amar (spoke), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, malakay (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah), and yashabay (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem): thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), Behold, I will bawaa (come) rai (evil) on this maqawam (place), which whoever shamaiw (hears), his azan (ear) shall tzalal (tingle).

Because they have forsaken me, and have nakar (estranged) this maqawam (place), and have qatar (burned) incense in it to other Alahayam, that they didn't yadai (know), they and their ab (father) and the malakay (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah); and malaa (have) filled this maqawam (place) with the dam (blood) of naqayam (innocents),

And have banah (build) the bamah (high) places of Bail (Baal), to sharap (burn) their ban (son) in the ash (fire) for burnt ilawath (offerings) to Bail (Baal); which I didn't tzawah (command), nor dabar (word / matter) it, neither ilah (go up / offer) it into my lab (heart):

Therefore, behold, the yamayam (days) bawaa (come), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, that this maqawam (place) shall no more be qaraa (called) Thapath (Topheth), nor The gayaa (valley) of the ban (son) of Hanam (Hinnom), but The gayaa (valley) of haragah (slaughter).

I will baqaq (make) void the itzah (counsel) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) in this maqawam (place); and I will napal (fall / be cast down) them to fall by the charab (sword) panayam (face) their ayab (enemy), and by the yad (hand) of those who baqash (seek) their napash (soul): and their nabalah (dead) bodies will I nathan (give) to be maakal (food) for the iwap (flying) of the sky, and for the animals of the aratz (Earth/land).

I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) this iyar (city) an shamah (astonishment), and a sharaqah (hissing); everyone who passes thereby shall be shamam (astonished) and sharaq (hiss) because of all its makah (plagues).

I will cause them to akal (eat) the bashar (flesh) of their ban (son) and the bashar (flesh) of their banath (daughter); and they shall akal (eat) everyone the bashar (flesh) of his rai (neigbor/another person), in the matzawar (siege) and in the matzawaq (distress), with which their ayab (enemy), and those who baqash (seek) their napash (soul), shall tzawaq (distress) them.
Then you shall shabar (break) the baqabaq (bottle) in the iyan (eye) of the anashayam (men) who halak (move) with you,

And shall amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies): Even so will I shabar (break) this im (nation / people) and this iyar (city), as one shabar (breaks) a yatzar (potter's) kalay (vessel), that can't be rapaa (made) whole again; and they shall qabar (bury) in Thapath (Topheth), until there is no maqawam (place) to qabar (bury).
Thus will I ishah (make) to this maqawam (place), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, and to its yashab (inhabit/dwell), even nathan (give) this iyar (city) as Thapath (Topheth):

And the bathay (houses) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and the bathay (houses) of the malakay (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah), which are tamaa (defiled), shall be as the maqawam (place) of Thapath (Topheth), even all the bathay (houses) on whose gag (roofs) they have qatar (burned) incense to all the tzabaa (troop) of the sky, and have nasak (poured) out drink nasakayam (offerings) to other Alahayam.

Then bawaa (come) Yaramayah (Jeremiah) from Thapath (Topheth), where Yahawah had shalach (send) him to nabaa (prophesy); and he imad (stood) in the chatzar (court) of Yahawah bayath (house), and amar (spoke) to all the im (nation / people):

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), Behold, I will bawaa (come) on this iyar (city) and on all its iyar (towns) all the rai (evil) that I have dabar (word / matter) against it; because they have made their irap (neck) qashah (rough / hard), that they may not shamai (hearken / hear) my dabar (word / matter).

Now Pashachawar (Pashhur), the ban (son) of Amar (Immer) the kahan (priest), who paqayad (was) chief officer in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, shamai (hearken / hear) Yaramayah (Jeremiah) nabaa (prophesying) these things.

Then Pashachawar (Pashhur) nakah (struck) Yaramayah (Jeremiah) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and nathan (give) him in the mahapakath (stocks) that were in the ilayawan (Ilayawan) shair (gate) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), which was in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

It happened on the next macharath (day), that Pashachawar (Pashhur) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth Yaramayah (Jeremiah) out of the mahapakath (stocks). Then Yaramayah (Jeremiah) amar (spoke) to him, Yahawah has not qaraa (called) your sham (name) Pashachawar (Pashhur), but magawaramasabayab (magormissabib).

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, Behold, I will nathan (give) you a magawar (terror) to yourself, and to all your ahab (love); and they shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword) of their ayab (enemy), and your iyan (eye) shall raah (see) it; and I will nathan (give) all Yahawadah (Judah) into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), and he shall galah (carry) them captive to Babal (Babylon), and shall nakah (kill) them with the charab (sword).

Moreover I will nathan (give) all the riches of this iyar (city), and all its gains, and all the yaqar (precious) things of it, yes, all the awatzarawath (treasures) of the malakay (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah) will I nathan (give) into the yad (hand) of their ayab (enemy); and they shall make them a bazaz (prey), and laqach (take / seize) them, and bawaa (come) them to Babal (Babylon).

You, Pashachawar (Pashhur), and all who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in your bayath (house) shall yalak (go) into shabay (captivity); and you shall bawaa (come) to Babal (Babylon), and there you shall mawath (death), and there you shall be qabar (bury), you, and all your ahab (love), to whom you have nabaa (prophesied) falsely.

Yahawah, you have pathah (persuaded) me, and I was pathah (persuaded); you are chazaq (stronger) than I, and yakal (have) prevailed: I am become a laughing-stock all the yawam (day), every one laig (mocks) me.

For as often as I dabar (word / matter), I qaraa (called) out; I qaraa (called), chamas (violence) and destruction! Because the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah is made a charapah (reproach) to me, and a qalas (derision), all the yawam (day).

If I amar (spoke), I will not zakar (remember) mention of him, nor dabar (word / matter) any more in his sham (name), then there is in my lab (heart) as it were a bair (burning) ash (fire) itzar (shut) up in my itzam (bones), and I am laah (weary) with kawal (all), and I can't.

For I have shamai (hearken / hear) the dabah (defaming) of many, magawar (terror) on sabayab (surrounding) side. Nagad (denounce), and we will nagad (denounce) him, say all my familiar friends, those who shamar (keep/guard) for my fall; perhaps he will be pathah (persuaded), and we shall yakal (prevail) against him, and we shall laqach (take / seize) our naqamah (revenge) on him.

But Yahawah is with me as an awesome gabawar (mighty) irayatz (one): therefore my persecutors shall kashal (stumble / stagger), and they shall not yakal (prevail); they shall be maad (utterly) disappointed, because they shakal (have) not dealt wisely, even with an iwalam (forever) dishonor which shall never be shakach (forgotten).

But, Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), who tests the tzadayaq (righteous), who raah (see) the kalayah (heart) and the lab (heart), raah (see) me see your naqamah (vengeance) on them; for to you have I galah (revealed) my rayab (cause).
Shayar (sing) to Yahawah, halal (praise) Yahawah; for he has natzal (delivered) the napash (soul) of the abayawan (needy) from the yad (hand) of evildoers.
Arar (cursed) is the yawam (day) in which I was yalad (birth / begot): don't let the yawam (day) in which my am (mother) yalad (birth / begot) me be barak (blessed).
Arar (cursed) is the ayash (man / husband) who bashar (brought) news to my ab (father), amar (spoke), A boy is yalad (birth / begot) to you; shamach (making) him very shamach (glad).

Let that ayash (man / husband) be as the irayam (cities) which Yahawah overthrew, and didn't nacham (turn away / repent): and shamai (hearken / hear) him hear a zaiq (cry) in the baqar (morning), and tharawaih (shouting) at noontime;
Because he didn't mawath (death) me from the racham (womb); and so my am (mother) would have been my qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher), and her racham (womb) iwalam (forever) harah (great).
Why yatzaa (go out / come out) I forth out of the racham (womb) to raah (see) imal (labor) and yagawan (sorrow), that my yawam (day) should be kalah (complete / finish) with bashath (shame)?

The dabar (word / matter) which came to Yaramayah (Jeremiah) from Yahawah, when malak (king) Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah) shalach (send) to him Pashachawar (Pashhur) the ban (son) of Malakayah (Malchijah), and Tzapanayah (Zephaniah) the ban (son) of Maishayah (Maaseiah), the kahan (priest), amar (spoke),

Please darash (inquire) of Yahawah for us; for Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) makes lacham (war) against us: perhaps Yahawah will ishah (make) with us according to all his wondrous palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous), that he may ilah (go up / offer) up from us.
Then Yaramayah (Jeremiah) amar (spoke) to them, You shall amar (spoke) Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah):

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), Behold, I will sabab (turn) back the kalay (weapons) of malachamah (war) that are in your yad (hand), with which you lacham (fight) against the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), and against the Kashaday (Chaldeans) who tzawar (besiege) you, chawatz (without) the chawamah (walls); and I will asap (gather) them into the thawak (midst) of this iyar (city).

I myself will lacham (fight) against you with an natah (outstretched) yad (hand) and with a chazaq (strong) zarawai (arm), even in ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and in chamah (wrath), and in gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qatzap (indignation).
I will nakah (strike) the yawashabay (inhabitants) of this iyar (city), both adam (man) and animal: they shall mawath (death) of a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) dabar (word / matter).

Afterward, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, I will nathan (give) Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and his ibad (servant), and the im (nation / people), even such as are shaar (left) in this iyar (city) from the dabar (word / matter), from the charab (sword), and from the raib (famine), into the yad (hand) of Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), and into the yad (hand) of their ayab (enemy), and into the yad (hand) of those who baqash (seek) their napash (soul): and he shall nakah (strike) them with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword); he shall not chawas (spare) them, neither chamal (have) pity, nor have racham (show mercy / love).
To this im (nation / people) you shall amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: Behold, I nathan (give) panayam (face) you the darak (way) of chay (life) and the darak (way) of mawath (death).

He who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in this iyar (city) shall mawath (death) by the charab (sword), and by the raib (famine), and by the dabar (word / matter); but he who yatzaa (go out / come out) out, and passes over to the Kashaday (Chaldeans) who tzawar (besiege) you, he shall chayah (live), and his napash (soul) shall be to him for a shalal (prey).

For I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) my panayam (face) on this iyar (city) for rai (evil), and not for tawab (good / proper function), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah: it shall be nathan (give) into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), and he shall sharap (burn) it with ash (fire).
Touching the bayath (house) of the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah:

Bayath (house) of Dawad (David), thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, Execute mashapat (justice) in the baqar (morning), and natzal (deliver) him who is gazal (robbed) out of the yad (hand) of the oppressor, lest my chamah (wrath) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth like ash (fire), and bair (burn) so that none can kabah (quench) it, panayam (face) of the rai (evil) of your mailal (doings).

Behold, I am against you, O yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the imaq (valley), and of the tzawar (rock) of the mayashawar (plain), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah; you that amar (spoke), Who shall nachath (come) down bawaa (come) us? Or who shall enter into our maiwanah (habitations)?

I will paqad (visit) you according to the paray (fruit) of your mailal (doings), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah; and I will yatzath (kindle) a ash (fire) in her yair (forest), and it shall akal (eat) all that is around her.
Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: yarad (go) down to the bayath (house) of the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and dabar (word / matter) there this dabar (word / matter),

Amar (spoke), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), who yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the kasaa (throne) of Dawad (David), you, and your ibad (servant), and your im (nation / people) who bawaa (come) in by these shairayam (gates).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: ishah (make) mashapat (justice) and tzadaqah (righteousness), and natzal (deliver) him who is gazal (robbed) out of the yad (hand) of the ishawaq (oppressor): and yanah (do) no wrong, chamas (do) no violence, to the foreigner, the yathawam (fatherless), nor the alamanah (widow); neither shapak (shed) naqay (innocent) dam (blood) in this maqawam (place).

For if you ishah (make) this thing ishah (make), then shall there bawaa (come) in by the shairay (gates) of this bayath (house) malakayam (kings) sitting on the kasaa (throne) of Dawad (David), rakab (riding) in rakab (chariots) and on sawasayam (horses), he, and his ibad (servant), and his im (nation / people).
But if you will not shamai (hearken / hear) these dabarayam (words), I shabai (swear / take oath) by myself, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, that this bayath (house) shall become a desolation.

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah concerning the bayath (house) of the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah): You are Galaid (Gilead) to me, the raash (head) of Labanawan (Lebanon). Yet surely I will shayath (put / appoint / make) you a madabar (wilderness), irayam (cities) which are not yashab (inhabit/dwell).

I will qadash (set apart / make holy) destroyers against you, everyone with his kalay (weapons); and they shall karath (cut) down your mabachar (choice) araz (cedars), and napal (fall / be cast down) them into the ash (fire).

Many gawayam (nations) shall ibar (pass over/through) by this iyar (city), and they shall amar (spoke) every ayash (man / husband) to his neighbor, Why has Yahawah ishah (make) thus to this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) iyar (city)?
Then they shall amar (spoke), Because they forsook the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah their Alahayam, and shachah (worshiped) other Alahayam, and ibad (servant) them.

Don't bakah (weep) for the mawath (death), neither nawad (bemoan) him; but bakah (weep) bitterly for him who halak (move) away; for he shall shawab (turn back / repent) no more, nor raah (see) his mawaladath (kindred / native land) aratz (Earth/land).

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah touching Shalawam (Shallum) the ban (son) of Yaashayah (Josiah), malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), who malak (king) instead of Yaashayah (Josiah) his ab (father), and who yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of this maqawam (place): He shall not shawab (turn back / repent) there any more.
But in the maqawam (place) where they have galah (led) him captive, there shall he mawath (death), and he shall raah (see) this aratz (Earth/land) no more.

Haway (Alas/Woe!) To him who banah (build) his bayath (house) by unrighteousness, and his rooms by injustice; who uses his neighbor's ibad (servant) chanam (without) wages, and doesn't nathan (give) him his hire;

Who amar (spoke), I will banah (build) me a madah (wide) bayath (house) and spacious rooms, and qarai (cuts) him out chalawan (windows); and it is ceiling with araz (cedar), and mashach (painted) with vermilion.

Shall you malak (king), because you strive to excel in araz (cedar)? Didn't your ab (father) akal (eat) and shathah (drinks), and ishah (make) mashapat (justice) and tzadaqah (righteousness)? Then it was tawab (good / proper function) with him.
He dayan (judge) the dayan (judge) of the inay (poor) and abayawan (needy); then it was tawab (good / proper function). Wasn't this to daith (know) me? Naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

But your iyan (eye) and your lab (heart) are not but for your batzai (covetousness), and for shapak (shedding) naqay (innocent) dam (blood), and for ishaq (oppression), and for maratzah (violence), to ishah (make) it.

Therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah concerning Yahawayaqayam (Jehoiakim) the ban (son) of Yaashayah (Josiah), malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah): they shall not sapad (lament) for him, saying, haway (Alas/Woe!) My ach (brother/kinsman)! Or, haway (Alas/Woe!) Achawath (sister)! They shall not sapad (lament) for him, saying haway (Alas/Woe!) Adawan! Or, haway (Alas/Woe!) His glory!
He shall be qabar (bury) with the qabawarah (burial) of a donkey, sachab (drawn) and shalak (cast) forth halaah (beyond) the shairay (gates) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

Ilah (go up / offer) up to Labanawan (Lebanon), and tzaiq (cry); and nathan (give) up your qawal (sound / voice) in Bashan (Bashan), and tzaiq (cry) from Abarim; for all your lovers are shabar (destroyed).

I dabar (word / matter) to you in your shalawah (prosperity); but you amar (spoke), I will not shamai (hearken / hear). This has been your darak (way) from your naiwar (youth), that you didn't shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice).

The rawach (spirit / wind) shall raih (feed) all your raih (shepherds), and your lovers shall yalak (go) into shabay (captivity): surely then you will be bawash (ashamed) and kalam (confounded) for all your rai (wickedness).

Yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Labanawan (Lebanon), who qanan (makes) your nest in the arazayam (cedars), how greatly to be chanan (showing favor) you will be when chabalayam (pangs) bawaa (come) on you, the chayal (pain) as of a yalad (birth / begot) in travail!

As I chay (life), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, though Kanayahaw (Coniah) the ban (son) of Yahawayaqayam (Jehoiakim) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) were the chawatham (signet) on my yamayan (right hand) yad (hand), yet would I nathaq (pluck) you there;

And I will nathan (give) you into the yad (hand) of those who baqash (seek) your napash (soul), and into the yad (hand) of them of whom you are yagawar (afraid), even into the yad (hand) of Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), and into the yad (hand) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans).
I will tawal (cast) you out, and your am (mother) who yalad (birth / begot) you, into achar (other) aratz (Earth/land), where you were not yalad (birth / begot); and there you will mawath (death).
But to the aratz (Earth/land) whereunto their nashaa (lift) longs to shawab (turn back / repent), there shall they not shawab (turn back / repent).

Is this ayash (man / husband) Kanayahaw (Coniah) a bazah (despised) napatz (broken) vessel? Is he a kalay (vessel) in which none chapatz (delights)? Why are they shalak (cast) out, he and his zarai (seed), and are tawal (cast) into the aratz (Earth/land) which they don't yadai (know)?
O aratz (Earth/land), aratz (Earth/land), aratz (Earth/land), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, kathab (write) you this ayash (man / husband) irayaray (childless), a gabar (man) who shall not tzalach (prosper) in his yawam (day); for no more shall a ayash (man / husband) of his zarai (seed) tzalach (prosper), sitting on the kasaa (throne) of Dawad (David), and mashal (rule/have dominion) in Yahawadah (Judah).
Haway (Alas/Woe!) To the raiyam (shepherds) who abad (destroy / perish) and pawatz (scatter) the tzaan (sheep) of my maraiyath (pasture)! Naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

Therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), against the raiyam (shepherds) who raih (feed) my im (nation / people): You have pawatz (scattered) my tzaan (flock), and nadach (driven) them away, and paqad (visit) not visited them; behold, I will paqad (visit) on you the rai (evil) of your mailal (doings), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

I will qabatz (gather) the shaarayath (remnant) of my tzaan (flock) out of all the aratzawath (countries) where I have nadach (driven) them, and will shawab (turn back / repent) them again to their nawah (habitation); and they shall be parah (fruitful) and rabah (multiply).

I will qawam (rise up) up raiyam (shepherds) over them, who shall raih (feed) them; and they shall yaraa (fear / be afraid) no more, nor be chathath (dismayed), neither shall any be paqad (visit), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

Behold, the yamayam (days) bawaa (come), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, that I will qawam (rise up) to Dawad (David) a tzadayaq (righteous) tzamach (branch), and he shall malak (king) as malak (king) and deal shakal (wisely), and shall ishah (make) mashapat (justice) and tzadaqah (righteousness) in the aratz (Earth/land).

In his yawam (day) Yahawadah (Judah) shall be yashai (salvation), and Yashar-Al (Israel) shall shakan (place) safely; and this is his sham (name) by which he shall be qaraa (called): Yahawah our righteousness.

Therefore, behold, the yamayam (days) bawaa (come), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, that they shall no more amar (spoke), As Yahawah chay (life), who ilah (go up / offer) up the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt);

But, As Yahawah chay (life), who ilah (go up / offer) up and who bawaa (come) the zarai (seed) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) out of the tzapawan (north) aratz (Earth/land), and from all the aratzawath (countries) where I had nadach (driven) them. They shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) in their own adamah (land).

Concerning the nabaayam (prophets). My lab (heart) qarab (among / near) me is shabar (broken), all my itzam (bones) rachap (hover); I am like a shakawar (drunken) ayash (man / husband), and like a gabar (man) whom yayan (wine) ibar (pass over/through) overcome, panayam (face) of Yahawah, and because of his qadash (set apart / make holy) dabaray (words).

For the aratz (Earth/land) is malaa (full) of manaapayam (adulterers); for panayam (face) of alah (curse / oath) the aratz (Earth/land) abal (mourns); the naawath (pastures) of the madabar (wilderness) are yabash (dry land) up. Their marawatzah (course) is rai (evil), and their gabawarah (might) is not right;
For both nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) and kahan (priest) are chanap (profane); yes, in my bayath (house) matzaa (have) I found their rai (wickedness), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

Therefore their darak (way) shall be to them as chalaqalaqah (slippery) places in the apalah (darkness): they shall be dachah (driven) on, and napal (fall / be cast down) therein; for I will bawaa (come) rai (evil) on them, even the shanah (year) of their paqadah (visitation), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.
I raah (see) seen thapalah (folly) in the nabayaay (prophets) of Shamarawan (Samaria); they nabaa (prophesied) by Bail (Baal), and caused my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel) to thaih (err).

In the nabaay (prophets) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) also I raah (see) seen a shairawarah (horrible) thing: they naap (commit) adultery, and halak (move) in shaqar (lies); and they chazaq (strengthen) the yaday (hands) of evildoers, so that ayash (man / husband) does shawab (turn back / repent) from his rai (wickedness): they are all of them become to me as Sadam (Sodom), and its yashab (inhabit/dwell) as Imarah (Gomorrah).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) concerning the nabaayam (prophets): Behold, I will akal (eat) them with lainah (wormwood), and shaqah (make) them drink the mayam (Waters) of raash (head); for from the nabaayam (prophets) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) is ungodliness yatzaa (go out / come out) forth into all the aratz (Earth/land).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), Don't shamai (hearken / hear) to the dabaray (words) of the nabaayam (prophets) who nabaa (prophesy) to you: they teach you vanity; they dabar (word / matter) a chazawan (vision) of their own lab (heart), and not out of the pah (mouth) of Yahawah.

They amar (spoke) continually to those who naatz (despise) me, Yahawah has dabar (word / matter), You shall have shalawam (peace / safety); and to everyone who halak (move) in the stubbornness of his own lab (heart) they amar (spoke), No rai (evil) shall bawaa (come) on you.

For who has imad (stood) in the council of Yahawah, that he should raah (see) and shamai (hearken / hear) his dabar (word / matter)? Who has qashab (marked) my dabar (word / matter), and shamai (hearken / hear) it?
Behold, the sair (storm) of Yahawah, his chamah (wrath), yatzaa (go out / come out) gone forth. Yes, a whirling sair (storm). It shall burst on the raash (head) of the rashai (wicked).

The ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah shall not shawab (turn back / repent), until he ishah (make) executed, and until he have qawam (rise up) the mazamawath (intents) of his lab (heart): in the acharayath (latter) yamayam (days) you shall bayan (between) it bayanah (perfectly).
I shalach (send) not these nabaayam (prophets), yet they rawatz (ran): I didn't dabar (word / matter) to them, yet they nabaa (prophesied).

But if they had imad (stood) in my council, then had they caused my im (nation / people) to shamai (hearken / hear) my dabar (word / matter), and had shawab (turn back / repent) them from their rai (evil) darak (way), and from the rai (evil) of their mailal (doings).
Am I a Alahayam at qarawab (hand), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, and not a Alahayam rachawaq (afar) off?

Can any sathar (hide) himself in masathar (secret) places so that I shall not raah (see) him? Naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah. Don't I malaa (fill) shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) and aratz (Earth/land)? Naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.
I have shamai (hearken / hear) what the nabaayam (prophets) have amar (spoke), who nabaa (prophesy) shaqar (lies) in my sham (name), amar (spoke), I have chalam (dream), I have chalam (dream).
How long yash (shall) this be in the lab (heart) of the nabaayam (prophets) who nabaa (prophesy) shaqar (lies), even the nabaayam (prophets) of the tharamah (deceit) of their own lab (heart)?

Who chashab (think) to cause my im (nation / people) to shakach (forget) my sham (name) by their chalawam (dreams) which they sapar (book) every ayash (man / husband) to his neighbor, as their ab (father) shakach (forgot) my sham (name) for Bail (Baal).

The nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) who has a chalawam (dream), let him sapar (book) a chalawam (dream); and he who has my dabar (word / matter), let him dabar (word / matter) my dabar (word / matter) faithfully. What is the thaban (straw) to the bar (wheat)? Naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.
Isn't my dabar (word / matter) kah (like) ash (fire)? Naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah; and like a patayash (hammer) that pawatz (breaks) the salai (rock) in pawatz (pieces)?
Therefore, behold, I am against the nabaayam (prophets), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, who ganab (steal) my dabar (word / matter) everyone from his neighbor.
Behold, I am against the nabayaam (prophets), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, who use their lashawan (tongue / language), and naam (declares prophetically), He naam (declares prophetically).

Behold, I am against those who nabaa (prophesy) shaqar (lying) chalamawath (dreams), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, and do sapar (book) them, and cause my im (nation / people) to thaih (err) by their shaqar (lies), and by their vain boasting: yet I didn't shalach (send) them, nor tzawah (commanded) them; neither yail (do) they profit this im (nation / people) at yail (all), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

When this im (nation / people), or the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), or a kahan (priest), shall shaal (ask) you, amar (spoke), What is the mashaa (burden) of Yahawah? Then you shall amar (spoke) them, What mashaa (burden)! I will natash (cast) you off, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

As for the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and the kahan (priest), and the im (nation / people), who shall amar (spoke), The mashaa (burden) of Yahawah, I will even paqad (visit) that ayash (man / husband) and his bayath (house).
You shall amar (spoke) everyone to his neighbor, and everyone to his ach (brother/kinsman), What has Yahawah inah (answer / respond)? And, What has Yahawah dabar (word / matter)?

You shall zakar (remember) the mashaa (burden) of Yahawah no more: for every ayash (man / husband) own dabar (word / matter) shall be his mashaa (burden); for you have perverted the dabaray (words) of the chay (life) Alahayam, of Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) our Alahayam.
You shall amar (spoke) to the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), What has Yahawah inah (answer / respond) you? And, What has Yahawah dabar (word / matter)?

But if you amar (spoke), The mashaa (burden) of Yahawah; therefore thus thaamaraw (says) Yahawah: Because you amar (spoke) this dabar (word / matter), The mashaa (burden) of Yahawah, and I have shalach (send) to you, amar (spoke), You shall not amar (spoke), The mashaa (burden) of Yahawah;
Therefore, behold, I will nashaa (lift) nashah (forget) you, and I will natash (cast) you off, and the iyar (city) that I nathan (give) to you and to your ab (father), away from my panayam (face):
And I will nathan (give) an iwalam (forever) charapah (reproach) on you, and a iwalam (forever) kalamawath (shame), which shall not be shakach (forgotten).

Yahawah showed me, and behold, shanayam (two) dawadaay (baskets) of thaanayam (figs) yaid (set) panayam (face) the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, achar (other) that Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) had galah (carried) away captive Yakanayah (Jeconiah) the ban (son) of Yahawayaqayam (Jehoiakim), malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and the sharay (princes) of Yahawadah (Judah), with the craftsmen and masagar (smiths), from Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and bawaa (come) brought them to Babal (Babylon).

Achad (one) dawad (basket) had very tawab (good / proper function) thaanayam (figs), like the thaanayam (figs) that are bakarah (first-ripe); and the other dawad (basket) had very rai (bad) thaanayam (figs), which could not be akal (eat), they were so rai (bad).

Then Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, What do you raah (see), Yaramayah (Jeremiah)? I amar (spoke), thaanayam (figs); the tawab (good / proper function) thaanayam (figs), very tawab (good / proper function); and the rai (bad), very rai (bad), that can't be akal (eat), they are so rai (bad).
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel): Like these tawab (good / proper function) thaanayam (figs), so will I nakar (regard) the galawath (captives) of Yahawadah (Judah), whom I have shalach (send) out of this maqawam (place) into the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), for tawab (good / proper function).

For I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) my iyan (eye) on them for tawab (good / proper function), and I will shawab (turn back / repent) them again to this aratz (Earth/land): and I will banah (build) them, and not haras (pull) them down; and I will natai (plant) them, and not nathash (pluck) them up.

I will nathan (give) them a lab (heart) to yadai (know) me, that I am Yahawah: and they shall be my im (nation / people), and I will be their Alahayam; for they shall shawab (turn back / repent) to me with their whole lab (heart).

As the rai (bad) thaanayam (figs), which can't be akal (eat), they are so rai (bad), surely thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, So will I nathan (give) up Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah) the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and his shar (prince / ruler), and the shaarayath (residue) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), who shaar (remain) in this aratz (Earth/land), and those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt),

I will even nathan (give) them up to be tossed back and forth among all the mamalakawath (kingdoms) of the aratz (Earth/land) for rai (evil); to be a charapah (reproach) and a mashal (proverb), a shanayanah (taunt) and a qalalah (curse), in all maqamawath (places) where I shall nadach (drive) them.

I will shalach (send) the charab (sword), the raib (famine), and the dabar (word / matter), among them, until they be thamam (consumed) from off the adamah (land) that I nathan (give) to them and to their ab (father).

The dabar (word / matter) that came to Yaramayah (Jeremiah) concerning all the im (nation / people) of Yahawadah (Judah), in the rabayaiy (fourth) shanah (year) of Yahawayaqayam (Jehoiakim) the ban (son) of Yaashayah (Josiah), malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) (the same was the raashanay (first) shanah (year) of Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon)),

Which Yaramayah (Jeremiah) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) dabar (word / matter) to all the im (nation / people) of Yahawadah (Judah), and to all the yashabay (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), amar (spoke):

From the thirteenth shanah (year) of Yaashayah (Josiah) the ban (son) of Amawan (Amon), malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), even to this yawam (day), these isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three) shanah (years), the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah has come to me, and I have dabar (word / matter) to you, shakam (rising) up early and dabar (word / matter); but you have not shamai (hearken / hear).

Yahawah has shalach (send) to you all his ibad (servant) the nabaayam (prophets), shakam (rising) up early and shalach (send) them (but you have not shamai (hearken / hear), nor natah (inclined) your azan (ear) to shamai (hearken / hear))

Amar (spoke), shawab (turn back / repent) now everyone from his rai (evil) darak (way), and from the rai (evil) of your mailal (doings), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the adamah (land) that Yahawah nathan (give) given to you and to your ab (father), from of iwalam (forever) and even forevermore;

And don't yalak (go) achar (other) other Alahayam to ibad (servant) them or shachah (worship) them, and don't provoke me to kais (anger) with the maishah (work) of your yad (hand); and I will raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil) you no harm.
Yet you have not shamai (hearken / hear) to me, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah; that you may provoke me to kais (anger) with the maishah (work) of your yad (hand) to your own rai (hurt).
Therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies): Because you have not shamai (hearken / hear) my dabar (word / matter),

Behold, I will shalach (send) and laqach (take / seize) all the mashapachawath (families) of the tzapawan (north), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, and I will send to Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), my ibad (servant), and will bawaa (come) them against this aratz (Earth/land), and against its yashab (inhabit/dwell), and against all these gawayam (nations) around; and I will utterly charam (destroy) them, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) them an shamah (astonishment), and a sharaqah (hissing), and iwalam (forever) desolations.

Moreover I will abad (destroy / perish) from them the qawal (sound / voice) of shashawan (mirth) and the qawal (sound / voice) of shamachah (gladness), the qawal (sound / voice) of the chathan (bridegroom) and the qawal (sound / voice) of the kalah (complete / finish), the qawal (sound / voice) of the millstones, and the awar (light) of the nayar (lamp).

This whole aratz (Earth/land) shall be a desolation, and an shamah (astonishment); and these gawayam (nations) shall ibad (servant) the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) shabaiyam (seventy) shanah (years).

It shall happen, when shabaiyam (seventy) shanah (years) are malaa (accomplished), that I will paqad (visit) the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), and that gaway (heathen / nation), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, for their iwan (guilt/iniquity), and the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans); and I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) it shamamah (desolate) iwalam (forever).

I will bawaa (come) on that aratz (Earth/land) all my dabar (word / matter) which I have dabar (word / matter) against it, even all that is kathab (write) in this sapar (book / scribed document), which Yaramayah (Jeremiah) has nabaa (prophesied) against all the gawayam (nations).

For many gawayam (nations) and gadawal (very great/important/mighty) malakayam (kings) shall ibad (servant) bondservants of them, even of them; and I will shalam (recompense) them according to their pail (deeds), and according to the maishah (work) of their yad (hand).

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), to me: laqach (take / seize) this kawas (cup) of the yayan (wine) of chamah (wrath) at my yad (hand), and cause all the gawayam (nations), to whom I shalach (send) you, to shaqah (drink) it.
They shall shathah (drinks), and reel back and forth, and be halal (praise), panayam (face) of the charab (sword) that I will shalach (send) among them.
