We have shamai (hearken / hear) of the gaawan (pride) of Mawaab (Moab). He is very gaah (proud); his gabah (loftiness), and his gaawan (pride), and his arrogance, and the rawam (will lift up) of his lab (heart).
I yadai (know) his ibarah (wrath), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, that it is nothing; his boastings ishah (make) worked nothing.
Therefore will I wail for Mawaab (Moab); yes, I will zaiq (cry) out for all Mawaab (Moab): for the anashay (men) of Qayaracharash (Kir Heres) shall they hagah (mourn).

With more than the bakay (weeping) of Yaizayar (Jazer) will I bakah (weep) for you, gapan (vine) of Shabam (Sibmah): your branches ibar (pass over/through) over the yam (sea/waters), they nagai (reached) even to the yam (sea/waters) of Yaizayar (Jazer): on your qayatz (summer) fruits and on your batzayar (vintage) the shadad (destroyer) is napal (fall / be cast down).

Gayal (gladness) and shamachah (joy) is asap (taken) away from the karamal (fruitful) field and from the aratz (Earth/land) of Mawaab (Moab); and I have caused yayan (wine) to shabath (shabath / rest) from the yaqab (wine) presses: none shall darak (tread) with hayadad (shouting); the hayadad (shouting) shall be no hayadad (shouting).

From the zaiq (cry) of Chashabawan (Heshbon) even to Alailaa (Elealeh), even to Yahatz (Jahaz) nathan (give) they uttered their qawal (sound / voice), from Tzair (Zoar) even to Charanayam (Horonaim), to Eglath Shelishiyah: for the may (waters) of Namarayam (Nimrim) also shall become mashamah (desolate).

Moreover I will shabath (shabath / rest) to cease in Mawaab (Moab), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, him who ilah (go up / offer) in the bamah (high) place, and him who qatar (burns) incense to his Alahayam.

Therefore my lab (heart) hamah (great uproar) for Mawaab (Moab) like chalalayam (pipes), and my lab (heart) hamah (great uproar) like chalalayam (pipes) for the anashay (men) of Qayaracharash (Kir Heres): therefore the yatharah (abundance) that he ishah (make) gotten is abad (destroy / perish).
For every raash (head) is qarachah (bald), and every zaqan (beard) garai (clipped): on all the yadayam (hands) are cuttings, and on the waist sackcloth.

On all the housetops of Mawaab (Moab) and in its rachab (streets) there is masapad (lamentation) every where; for I have shabar (broken) Mawaab (Moab) like a kalay (vessel) in which none chapatz (delights), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

How it is broken down! How they wail! How Mawaab (Moab) has panah (turn) the irap (neck) with shame! So shall Mawaab (Moab) become a shachawaq (laughter/joking matter) and a machathah (terror) to all who are around him.
For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: Behold, he shall daah (fly) as an nashar (eagle), and shall parash (spread) out his kanap (wings) against Mawaab (Moab).

Qarayawath (Kerioth) is lakad (taken), and the strongholds are seized, and the lab (heart) of the gabawar (mighty) men of Mawaab (Moab) at that yawam (day) shall be as the lab (heart) of a ayashah (woman / wife) in her tzarar (pangs).
Mawaab (Moab) shall be destroyed from being a im (nation / people), because he has gadal (magnified) himself against Yahawah.
Pachad (fear / dread), and the pachath (pit), and the pach (snare / trap), are on you, yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Mawaab (Moab), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

He who flees from the pachad (fear / dread) shall napal (fall / be cast down) into the pachath (pit); and he who ilah (go up / offer) up out of the pachath (pit) shall be lakad (taken) in the pach (snare / trap): for I will bawaa (come) on him, even on Mawaab (Moab), the shanah (year) of their paqadah (visitation), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

Those who nawas (fled) imad (stand) without kach (strength / mighty / power) under the tzal (shadow) of Chashabawan (Heshbon); for a ash (fire) is yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of Chashabawan (Heshbon), and a lahabah (flame) from the midst of Sayachawan (Sihon), and has akal (eat) the paah (corner) of Mawaab (Moab), and the qadaqad (crown) of the head of the tumultuous banay (ones).

Away (woe) to you, O Mawaab (Moab)! The im (nation / people) of Kamawash (Chemosh) is abad (destroy / perish); for your ban (son) are laqach (take / seize) shabay (away) captive, and your banath (daughter) into shabayah (captivity).

Yet will I shawab (turn back / repent) back the shabawath (captivity) of Mawaab (Moab) in the acharayath (latter) yamayam (days), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah. Hanah (here) far is the mashapat (judgment) of Mawaab (Moab).

Of the banay (children) of Ammon. Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: Has Yashar-Al (Israel) no banay (sons)? Has he no heir? Why then does Malcam yarash (possess) Gad (Gad), and his im (nation / people) yashab (inhabit/dwell) in its iyar (cities)?

Therefore, behold, the yamayam (days) bawaa (come), amar (spoke) Yahawah, that I will cause an tharawaih (alarm) of malachamah (war) to be shamai (hearken / hear) against Rabah (Rabbah) of the banay (children) of Ammon; and it shall become a shamamah (desolate) thal (heap), and her banath (daughter) shall be yatzath (burned) with ash (fire): then shall Yashar-Al (Israel) yarash (possess) those who yarash (possessed) him, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

Wail, Chashabawan (Heshbon), for Iy (Ai) is laid shadad (waste); tzaiq (cry), you banawath (daughters) of Rabah (Rabbah), clothe yourself in sackcloth: sapad (lament), and shawat (run) back and forth among the fences; for Malcam shall yalak (go) into gawalah (captivity), his kahan (priest) and his shar (prince / ruler) yachad (together).

Why do you glory in the imaqayam (valleys), your zawab (flow) imaq (valley), shawabab (backsliding) banath (daughter)? Who batach (trusted) in her awatzar (treasures), saying, "Who shall bawaa (come) to me?

Behold, I will bawaa (come) a pachad (fear / dread) on you, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), from all who are around you; and you shall be nadach (driven) out every ayash (man / husband) panayam (face) forth, and there shall be none to qabatz (gather) together the fugitives.
But afterward I will shawab (turn back / repent) back the shabawath (captivity) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

Of Adawam (Edom). Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies): Is chakamah (wisdom) no more in Thayaman (Teman)? Is itzah (counsel) abad (destroy / perish) from the bayan (between)? Is their chakamah (wisdom) vanished?

Nawas (flee), panah (turn) back, yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the haimayaqaw (depths), yashabay (inhabitants) of Dadan (Dedan); for I will bawaa (come) the ayad (calamity) of Ishaw (Esau) on him, the ith (time) that I shall paqad (visit) him.

If grape batzarayam (gatherers) bawaa (come) to you, would they not shaar (leave) some gleaning iwalalawath (grapes)? If thieves by layal (night), wouldn't they shachath (destroy) until they had day (enough)?

But I have made Ishaw (Esau) chashap (bare), I have galah (uncovered) his masathar (secret) places, and he shall not be yakal (able) to chabah (hide) himself: his zarai (seed) is shadad (destroyed), and his ach (brother/kinsman), and his neighbors; and he is no more.
Izab (leave) your yathawam (fatherless) children, I will chayah (preserve) them alive; and let your alamanah (widows) batach (trust) in me.

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: Behold, they to whom it didn't pertain to shathah (drinks) of the kawas (cup) shall shathah (drinks) shathah (drinks); and are you he who shall naqah (clean/innocent) go naqah (clean/innocent)? You shall not go naqah (clean/innocent), but you shall shathah (drinks) shathah (drinks).

For I have shabai (swear / take oath) by myself, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, that Batzarah (Bozrah) shall become an shamah (astonishment), a charapah (reproach), a charab (waste), and a qalalah (curse); and all its iyar (cities) shall be iwalam (forever) charabawath (wastes).

I have shamai (hearken / hear) shamawaih (news) from Yahawah, and an tzayar (ambassador) is shalach (send) among the gawayam (nations), saying, qabatz (gather) yourselves together, and bawaa (come) against her, and qawam (rise up) up to the malachamah (battle).
For, behold, I nathan (give) made you qatan (small / young / least) among the gawayam (nations), and bazah (despised) among adam (men).

As for your terror, the zadawan (pride) of your lab (heart) has nashaa (lift) you, O you who shakan (place) in the chagaway (clefts) of the salai (rock), who thapash (hold) the marawam (height) of the gabaih (hill): though you should make your qan (nest) as gabah (high) as the nashar (eagle), I will yarad (bring) you down from there, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.
Adawam (Edom) shall become an shamah (astonishment): everyone who passes by it shall be shamam (astonished), and shall sharaq (hiss) at all its makah (plagues).

As in the mahapakah (overthrow) of Sadam (Sodom) and Imarah (Gomorrah) and the neighbor cities of it, amar (spoke) Yahawah, no ayash (man / husband) shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) there, neither shall any ban (son) of adam (man) live therein.

Behold, he shall ilah (go up / offer) up like a aray (lion) from the gaawan (pride) of the Yaradan (Jordan) against the ayathan (strong) nawah (habitation): for I will ragai (suddenly) make them rawatz (run) away from it; and whoever is bachar (chosen), him will I paqad (visit) over it: for who is like me? And who will yaid (appoint) me a time? And who is the raih (shepherd) who will imad (stand) panayam (face) me?

Therefore shamai (hearken / hear) the itzah (counsel) of Yahawah, that he has yaitz (taken) against Adawam (Edom); and his machashabah (purposes), that he has chashab (purposed) against the yashabay (inhabitants) of Thayaman (Teman): Surely they shall drag them away, the tzaiyar (little) ones of the tzaan (flock); surely he shall make their nawah (habitation) shamam (desolate) over them.

The aratz (Earth/land) raish (trembles) at the qawal (sound / voice) of their napal (fall / be cast down); there is a tzaiqah (cry), the qawal (sound / voice) which is shamai (hearken / hear) in the sawap (red) yam (sea/waters).

Behold, he shall ilah (go up / offer) up and daah (fly) as the nashar (eagle), and parash (spread) out his kanap (wings) against Batzarah (Bozrah): and the lab (heart) of the gabawar (mighty) men of Adawam (Edom) at that yawam (day) shall be as the lab (heart) of a ayashah (woman / wife) in her tzarar (pangs).

Of Damashaq (Damascus). Chamath (Hamath) is bawash (confounded), and Arapad (Arpad); for they have shamai (hearken / hear) rai (evil) shamawaih (news), they are mawag (melted) away: there is daagah (sorrow) on the yam (sea/waters); it can't be shaqat (quiet).

Damashaq (Damascus) has grown rapah (feeble), she panah (turn) herself to nawas (flee), and trembling has chazaq (seized) on her: tzarah (anguish) and chabalayam (sorrows) achaz (have) taken hold of her, as of a yalad (birth / begot) in travail.
How is the iyar (city) of thahalah (praise) not forsaken, the qarayah (city / town) of my mashawash (joy)?

Therefore her bachawar (young) men shall napal (fall / be cast down) in her rachab (streets), and all the anashay (men) of malachamah (war) shall be brought to damam (silence) in that yawam (day), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies).
I will yatzath (kindle) a ash (fire) in the chawamah (wall) of Damashaq (Damascus), and it shall akal (eat) the aramanawath (palaces) of Banahadad (Ben Hadad).

Of Qadar (Kedar), and of the mamalakawath (kingdoms) of Chatzawar (Hazor), which Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) nakah (struck). Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: qawam (rise up), ilah (go up / offer) up to Qadar (Kedar), and shadad (destroy) the banay (children) of the qadam (east).

Their ahal (tents) and their tzaan (flocks) shall they nashaa (lift); they shall nashaa (lift) away for themselves their yarayaih (curtains), and all their kalay (vessels), and their gamal (camels); and they shall qaraa (called) to them, magawar (terror) on sabayab (surrounding) side!

Nawas (flee), wander maad (far) off, yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the haimayaqaw (depths), you yashabay (inhabitants) of Chatzawar (Hazor), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah; for Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) has taken itzah (counsel) against you, and has chashab (conceived) a machashabah (purpose) against you.

Qawam (rise up), ilah (go up / offer) up to a gaway (heathen / nation) that is at shalaw (ease), that yashab (inhabit/dwell) without batach (care), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah; that have neither dalathayam (gates) nor barayach (bars), that shakan (place) badad (alone).

Their gamal (camels) shall be a baz (booty), and the hamawan (multitude) of their livestock a shalal (spoil): and I will zarah (scatter) to all rawach (spirit / wind) those who have the paah (corners) of their beards cut off; and I will bawaa (come) their ayad (calamity) from every ibar (side) of them, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

Chatzawar (Hazor) shall be a maiwan (dwelling) place of jackals, a shamamah (desolation) iwalam (forever): no ayash (man / husband) shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) there, neither shall any ban (son) of adam (man) live therein.

The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah that came to Yaramayah (Jeremiah) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) concerning Iyalam (Elam), in the raashayath (beginning) of the malakawath (reign) of Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), amar (spoke),
Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies): Behold, I will shabar (break) the qashath (bow) of Iyalam (Elam), the raashayath (beginning) of their gabawarah (might).

On Iyalam (Elam) will I bawaa (come) the arabai (four) rawachawath (winds) from the arabai (four) quarters of the sky, and will zarah (scatter) them toward all those rawachawath (winds); and there shall be no gaway (heathen / nation) where the nadachay (outcasts) of Iyalam (Elam) shall not bawaa (come).

I will cause Iyalam (Elam) to be chathath (dismayed) panayam (face) their ayab (enemy), and panayam (face) those who baqash (seek) their napash (soul); and I will bawaa (come) rai (evil) on them, even my charawan (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah; and I will shalach (send) the charab (sword) achar (other) them, until I kalah (complete / finish) consumed them;

And I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) my kasaa (throne) in Iyalam (Elam), and will abad (destroy / perish) from there malak (king) and sharayam (princes), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.
But it shall happen in the acharayath (latter) yamayam (days), that I will shawab (turn back / repent) back the shabawath (captivity) of Iyalam (Elam), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

The dabar (word / matter) that Yahawah dabar (word / matter) concerning Babal (Babylon), concerning the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), by Yaramayah (Jeremiah) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy).

Nagad (declare) among the gawayam (nations) and shamai (hearken / hear), and nashaa (lift) up a nas (standard); shamai (hearken / hear), and don't kachad (conceal): amar (spoke), Babal (Babylon) is lakad (taken), Bal (Bel) is disappointed, Maradak (Merodach) is chathath (dismayed); her itzab (images) are disappointed, her galawal (idols) are chathath (dismayed).

For out of the tzapawan (north) there ilah (go up / offer) up a gaway (heathen / nation) against her, which shall shayath (put / appoint / make) her aratz (Earth/land) shamah (desolate), and none shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein: they are nawad (fled), they are halak (move), both adam (man) and animal.

In those yamayam (days), and in that ith (time), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall bawaa (come), they and the banay (children) of Yahawadah (Judah) yachad (together); they shall halak (move) on their yalak (way) bakah (weeping), and shall baqash (seek) Yahawah their Alahayam.

They shall inquire concerning Tzayawan (Zion) with their panayam (face) turned toward it, saying, bawaa (come), and lawah (join) yourselves to Yahawah in an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant) that shall not be shakach (forgotten).

My im (nation / people) abad (destroy / perish) been lost tzaan (sheep): their raih (shepherds) have thaih (caused) them to go astray; they have shawabab (turned) them away on the harayam (mountains); they have halak (move) from har (mountain) to gabaih (hill); they have shakach (forgotten) their rabatz (resting) place.

All who matzaa (found) them have akal (eat) them; and their tzar (oppressor / distressor) amar (spoke), We are not asham (guilty), because they have chataa (sinned) against Yahawah, the nawah (habitation) of tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), even Yahawah, the maqawah (gathering / collection) of their ab (father).

Nawad (flee) out of the thawak (midst) of Babal (Babylon), and yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), and be as the male ithawadayam (goats) panayam (face) the tzaan (flocks).

For, behold, I will ilah (go up / offer) up and ilah (go up / offer) to come up against Babal (Babylon) a qahal (company) of gadawal (very great/important/mighty) gawayam (nations) from the tzapawan (north) aratz (Earth/land); and they shall irak (set) themselves in array against her; from there she shall be lakad (taken): their chatz (arrows) shall be as of an expert gabawar (mighty) shakal (man); none shall shawab (turn back / repent) in rayaqam (vain).
Kashaday (Chaldea) shall be a shalal (prey): all who shalal (prey) on her shall be shabai (satisfied), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

Because you are shamach (glad), because you shamach (rejoice), O you who plunder my nachalah (heritage), because you are wanton as a igalah (heifer) that treads out the grain, and tzahal (neigh) as abayar (strong) horses;

Your am (mother) shall be maad (utterly) disappointed; she who yalad (birth / begot) you shall be chapar (confounded): behold, she shall be the least of the gawayam (nations), a madabar (wilderness), a dry tzayah (land), and a irabah (desert).

Because of the qatzap (wrath) of Yahawah she shall not be yashab (inhabit/dwell), but she shall be wholly shamamah (desolate): everyone who ibar (pass over/through) by Babal (Babylon) shall be shamam (astonished), and sharaq (hiss) at all her makah (plagues).

Irak (set) yourselves in array against Babal (Babylon) all around, all you who darak (bend) the qashath (bow); yadah (shoot) at her, chamal (spare) no chatz (arrows): for she has chataa (sinned) against Yahawah.

Rawai (shout) against her all around: she nathan (give) submitted herself; her bulwarks are napal (fall / be cast down), her chawamah (walls) are haras (thrown) down; for it is the naqamah (vengeance) of Yahawah: naqam (take) vengeance on her; as she ishah (make) done, ishah (make) to her.

Karath (cut) off the zarai (sower) from Babal (Babylon), and him who thapash (handles) the magal (sickle) in the ith (time) of qatzayar (harvest): for panayam (face) of the yanah (oppressing) charab (sword) they shall panah (turn) everyone to his im (nation / people), and they shall nawas (flee) everyone to his own aratz (Earth/land).

Yashar-Al (Israel) is a hunted shah (sheep); the arayawath (lions) have nadach (driven) him away: raashawan (first), the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria) akal (eat) him; and now at acharawan (last) Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) has itzam (broken) his bones.

Therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel): Behold, I will paqad (visit) the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) and his aratz (Earth/land), as I paqad (visit) punished the malak (king) of Ashawar (Assyria).

I will shawab (turn back / repent) Yashar-Al (Israel) again to his pasture, and he shall raih (feed) on Karamal (Carmel) and Bashan (Bashan), and his napash (soul) shall be shabai (satisfied) on the har (mountain) of Aparayam (Ephraim) and in Galaid (Gilead).

In those yamayam (days), and in that ith (time), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall be baqash (sought) for, and there shall be none; and the chataath (sins) of Yahawadah (Judah), and they shall not be matzaa (found): for I will salach (forgive/pardon/make clean) them whom I leave as a shaar (remnant).

Ilah (go up / offer) up against the aratz (Earth/land) of Marathayam (Merathaim), even against it, and against the yawashabay (inhabitants) of Paqawad (Pekod): kill and utterly charam (destroy) achar (other) them, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, and ishah (make) according to all that I have tzawah (commanded) you.
A qawal (sound / voice) of malachamah (battle) is in the aratz (Earth/land), and of gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shabar (destruction).
How is the patayash (hammer) of the whole aratz (Earth/land) gadai (cut) apart and shabar (broken)! How is Babal (Babylon) become a shamah (desolation) among the gawayam (nations)!

I have laid a yaqash (snare) for you, and you are also lakad (taken), Babal (Babylon), and you weren't yadai (aware): you are matzaa (found), and also thapash (caught), because you have garah (striven) against Yahawah.

Yahawah pathach (has) opened his awatzar (armory), and yatzaa (go out / come out) brought forth the kalay (weapons) of his zaim (indignation); for the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), has a malaakah (work) to do in the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans).

Bawaa (come) against her from the utmost qatz (border); pathach (open) her maabawas (storehouses); salal (cast) her up as iramayam (heaps), and charam (destroy) her utterly; let nothing of her be shaarayath (left).
Kill all her par (bulls); yarad (let) them go down to the tabach (slaughter): haway (Alas/Woe!) To them! For their yawam (day) bawaa (come) come, the ith (time) of their paqadah (visitation).

The qawal (sound / voice) of those who nawas (flee) and palayat (escape) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Babal (Babylon), to nagad (declare) in Tzayawan (Zion) the naqamah (vengeance) of Yahawah our Alahayam, the naqamah (vengeance) of his hayakal (temple).

Shamai (hearken / hear) together the rabayam (archers) against Babal (Babylon), all those who darak (bend) the qashath (bow); chanah (encamp) against her all around; let none of it palayatah (escape): shalam (recompense) her according to her pail (work); according to all that she ishah (make) done, ishah (make) to her; for she has been zawad (proud) against Yahawah, against the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Therefore her bachawar (young) men will napal (fall / be cast down) in her rachab (streets), and all her anashay (men) of malachamah (war) will be brought to damam (silence) in that yawam (day), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

Behold, I am against you, you zadawan (proud) one, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies); for your yawam (day) bawaa (come) come, the ith (time) that I will paqad (visit) you.

The zadawan (proud) one shall kashal (stumble / stagger) and napal (fall / be cast down), and none shall qawam (rise up) him up; and I will yatzath (kindle) a ash (fire) in his iyar (cities), and it shall akal (eat) all who are around him.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies): The banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) and the banay (children) of Yahawadah (Judah) are ishaq (oppressed) yachad (together); and all who shabah (took) them captive chazaq (hold) them fast; they maan (refuse) to shalach (send) them go.

Their gaal (redeemer) is chazaq (strong); Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) is his sham (name): he will rayab (thoroughly) rayab (plead) their rayab (cause), that he may give ragai (rest) to the aratz (Earth/land), and ragaz (disquiet) the yashabay (inhabitants) of Babal (Babylon).

A charab (sword) is on the Kashaday (Chaldeans), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, and on the yashabay (inhabitants) of Babal (Babylon), and on her shar (prince / ruler), and on her chakam (wise) men.
A charab (sword) is on the boasters, and they shall yaal (become) fools; a charab (sword) is on her gabawar (mighty) men, and they shall be chathath (dismayed).

A charab (sword) is on their sawas (horses), and on their rakab (chariots), and on all the mixed irab (evening) who are in the thawak (midst) of her; and they shall become as nashayam (women): a charab (sword) is on her awatzar (treasures), and they shall be bazaz (robbed).
A charab (drought) is on her mayam (Waters), and they shall be yabash (dry land) up; for it is a aratz (Earth/land) of engraved pasalayam (images), and they are halal (praise) over ayamayam (idols).

Therefore the tzayay (wild) animals of the desert with the wolves shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) there, and the ostriches shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein: and it shall be no more yashab (inhabit/dwell) natzach (forever); neither shall it be lived in from dawar (generation / age / period) to dawar (generation / age / period).

As when Alahayam mahapakah (overthrew) Sadam (Sodom) and Imarah (Gomorrah) and the neighbor cities of it, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, so shall no ayash (man / husband) yashab (inhabit/dwell) there, neither shall any ban (son) of adam (man) live therein.

Behold, a im (nation / people) bawaa (come) from the tzapawan (north); and a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) gaway (heathen / nation) and many malakayam (kings) shall be iwar (rouse / awaken) up from the uttermost yarakathay (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land).

They lay chazaq (hold) on qashath (bow) and kayadawan (spear); they are akazaray (cruel), and have no racham (show mercy / love); their qawal (sound / voice) hamah (great uproar) like the yam (sea/waters); and they rakab (ride) on sawasayam (horses), everyone irak (set) in array, as a ayash (man / husband) to the malachamah (battle), against you, banath (daughter) of Babal (Babylon).

The malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) has shamai (hearken / hear) the news of them, and his yad (hand) wax rapah (feeble): tzarah (anguish) has chazaq (taken) hold of him, chayal (pains) as of a yalad (birth / begot) in labor.

Behold, the enemy shall ilah (go up / offer) up like a aray (lion) from the gaawan (pride) of the Yaradan (Jordan) against the ayathan (strong) nawah (habitation): for I will ragai (suddenly) make them rawatz (run) away from it; and whoever is bachawar (chosen), him will I paqad (visit) over it: for who is like me? And who will yaid (appoint) me a time? And who is the raih (shepherd) who can imad (stand) panayam (face) me?

Therefore shamai (hearken / hear) the itzah (counsel) of Yahawah, that he has yaitz (taken) against Babal (Babylon); and his machashabah (purposes), that he has chashab (purposed) against the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans): Surely they shall drag them away, even the tzaiyar (little) ones of the tzaan (flock); surely he shall make their nawah (habitation) shamam (desolate) over them.
At the qawal (sound / voice) of the thapash (taking) of Babal (Babylon) the aratz (Earth/land) raish (trembles), and the zaiq (cry) is shamai (hearken / hear) among the gawayam (nations).
Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: Behold, I will iwar (rouse / awaken) up against Babal (Babylon), and against those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in Lebkamai, a shachath (destroying) rawach (spirit / wind).

I will shalach (send) to Babal (Babylon) strangers, who shall zarah (winnow) her; and they shall baqaq (empty) her aratz (Earth/land): for in the yawam (day) of rai (trouble) they shall be against her around.

Against him who darak (bends) let the darak (archer) darak (bend) his qashath (bow), and against him who ilah (go up / offer) himself up in his coat of mail: and don't chamal (spare) her bachawar (young) men; charam (utterly) destroy all her tzabaa (troop).
They shall napal (fall / be cast down) down chalal (slain) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), and thrust daqar (through) in her chawatz (streets).

For Yashar-Al (Israel) is not alaman (forsaken), nor Yahawadah (Judah), of his Alahayam, of Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies); though their aratz (Earth/land) is malaa (full) of asham (guilt) against the qadawash (holy) One of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Nawas (flee) out of the thawak (midst) of Babal (Babylon), and malat (save) every ayash (man / husband) his napash (soul); don't be damam (cut) off in her iwan (guilt/iniquity): for it is the ith (time) of Yahawah naqamah (vengeance); he will shalam (render) to her a gamawal (recompense).

Babal (Babylon) has been a zahab (gold) kawas (cup) in Yahawah yad (hand), who made all the aratz (Earth/land) shakar (drunken): the gawayam (nations) have shathah (drinks) of her yayan (wine); therefore the gawayam (nations) are halal (praise).

Babal (Babylon) is pathaawam (suddenly) napal (fall / be cast down) and shabar (destroyed): wail for her; laqach (take / seize) tzaray (balm) for her makaab (pain), if so be she may be rapaa (healed).

We would have rapaa (healed) Babal (Babylon), but she is not rapaa (healed): izab (forsake) her, and yalak (let) us go everyone into his own aratz (Earth/land); for her mashapat (judgment) reaches to shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and is nashaa (lift) up even to the shachaqayam (skies).
Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) brought forth our tzadaqah (righteousness): bawaa (come), and let us sapar (book) in Tzayawan (Zion) the maishah (work) of Yahawah our Alahayam.

Barar (make) sharp the chatzayam (arrows); hold firm the shalatayam (shields): Yahawah has iwar (rouse / awaken) up the rawach (spirit / wind) of the malakay (kings) of the Maday (Medes); because his purpose is against Babal (Babylon), to shachath (destroy) it: for it is the naqamah (vengeance) of Yahawah, the naqamah (vengeance) of his hayakal (temple).

Nashaa (lift) up a nas (standard) against the chawamath (walls) of Babal (Babylon), make the mashamar (watch) chazaq (strong), kawan (set) the watchmen, kawan (prepare) the ambushes; for Yahawah has both zamam (purposed) and ishah (make) that which he dabar (word / matter) concerning the yashabay (inhabitants) of Babal (Babylon).
You who shakan (place) on many mayam (Waters), abundant in awatzarath (treasures), your qatz (end) bawaa (come) come, the amah (measure) of your batzai (covetousness).

Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) has shabai (swear / take oath) by himself, saying, "Surely I will malaa (fill) you with adam (men), as with the canker worm; and they shall inah (answer / respond) up a hayadad (shout) against you.

He ishah (make) made the aratz (Earth/land) by his kach (strength / mighty / power), he has kawan (established) the thabal (world) by his chakamah (wisdom), and by his thabawan (understanding) has he natah (stretched) out the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens):

When he nathan (give) his qawal (sound / voice), there is a hamawan (tumult) of mayam (Waters) in the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and he causes the vapors to ilah (go up / offer) from the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the aratz (Earth/land); he ishah (make) baraq (lightning) for the matar (rain), and yatzaa (go out / come out) forth the rawach (spirit / wind) out of his awatzar (treasuries).

Every adam (man) has become bair (brutish) without daith (knowledge). Every tzarap (goldsmith) is disappointed by his pasal (image); for his molten nasak (image) is falsehood, and there is no rawach (spirit / wind) in them.
They are habal (vanity), a maishah (work) of delusion: in the ith (time) of their paqadah (visitation) they shall abad (destroy / perish).

The chalaq (portion) of Yaiqab (Jacob) is not like these; for he is the former of all things; and is the shabat (tribe) of his nachalah (inheritance): Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) is his sham (name).

You are my mapatz (battle) axe and kalay (weapons) of malachamah (war): and with you will I napatz (break) in pieces the gawayam (nations); and with you will I shachath (destroy) mamalakawath (kingdoms);
And with you will I napatz (break) in pieces the sawas (horse) and his rider;

And with you will I napatz (break) in pieces the chariot and him who rides therein; and with you will I napatz (break) in pieces ayash (man / husband) and ayashah (woman / wife); and with you will I napatz (break) in pieces the zaqan (old) nair (man) and the youth; and with you will I napatz (break) in pieces the bachawar (young) man and the bathawalah (virgin);

And with you will I napatz (break) in pieces the raih (shepherd) and his idar (flock); and with you will I napatz (break) in pieces the farmer and his tzamad (yoke); and with you will I napatz (break) in pieces pachawath (governors) and deputies.

I will shalam (render) to Babal (Babylon) and to all the yawashabay (inhabitants) of Kashaday (Chaldea) all their rai (evil) that they ishah (make) done in Tzayawan (Zion) in your iyan (eye), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

Behold, I am against you, mashachayath (destroying) har (mountain), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, which shachath (destroys) all the aratz (Earth/land); and I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on you, and galal (roll) you down from the salaiyam (rocks), and will nathan (give) you a burnt har (mountain).

They shall not laqach (take / seize) of you a aban (stone) for a panah (corner / cornerstone), nor a aban (stone) for mawasadawath (foundations); but you shall be shamamah (desolate) for iwalam (forever), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

Nashaa (lift) up a nas (standard) in the aratz (Earth/land), thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn) among the gawayam (nations), qadash (set apart / make holy) the gawayam (nations) against her, shamai (hearken / hear) together against her the mamalakawath (kingdoms) of Ararat (Ararat), Manay (Minni), and Ashakanaz (Ashkenaz): paqad (visit) a marshal against her; cause the sawas (horses) to ilah (go up / offer) up as the samar (rough) canker worm.

Qadash (set apart / make holy) against her the gawayam (nations), the malakay (kings) of the Maday (Medes), its pachah (governors), and all its deputies, and all the aratz (Earth/land) of their mamashalah (dominion).

The aratz (Earth/land) raish (trembles) and is in chawal (pain); for the machashabawath (purposes) of Yahawah against Babal (Babylon) do qawam (rise up), to shawam (place / establish / appoint) the aratz (Earth/land) of Babal (Babylon) a shamah (desolation), without yashab (inhabit/dwell).

The gabawar (mighty) men of Babal (Babylon) have forborne to lacham (fight), they yashab (inhabit/dwell) in their strongholds; their gabawarah (might) has nashath (failed); they are become as nashayam (women): her mashakan (dwelling) places are set on yatzath (fire); her barayach (bars) are shabar (broken).

Rawatz (one) runner will rawatz (run) to qaraah (meet) another, and one nagad (messenger) to qaraah (meet) another, to show the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) that his iyar (city) is lakad (taken) on every qatzah (end / extremity / border):
And the maibarawath (passages) are seized, and the reeds they have sharap (burned) with ash (fire), and the anashay (men) of malachamah (war) are frightened.

For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel): The banath (daughter) of Babal (Babylon) is like a garan (threshing) floor at the ith (time) when it is trodden; yet a mait (little) while, and the ith (time) of qatzayar (harvest) shall bawaa (come) for her.

Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) has akal (eat) me, he has hamam (crushed) me, he has yatzag (made) me an rayaq (empty) kalay (vessel), he has, like a thanayan (monster), balai (swallowed) me up, he malaa (has) filled his maw with my delicacies; he has dawach (cast) me out.

The chamas (violence) done to me and to my shaar (flesh) be on Babal (Babylon), shall the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Tzayawan (Zion) amar (spoke); and, My dam (blood) be on the yashabay (inhabitants) of Kashaday (Chaldea), shall Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) amar (spoke).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: Behold, I will rayab (plead) your rayab (cause), and naqam (take) vengeance for you; and I will charab (dry) up her yam (sea/waters), and make her maqawar (fountain) yabash (dry land).
Babal (Babylon) shall become galayam (heaps), a maiwan (dwelling) place for jackals, an shamah (astonishment), and a sharaqah (hissing), without yashab (inhabit/dwell).
They shall shaag (roar) yachad (together) like young kaparayam (lions); they shall growl as arayawath (lions)' cubs.

When they are cham (heated), I will shayath (put / appoint / make) their mashathah (feast), and I will shakar (make) them drunken, that they may ilaz (rejoice), and sleep a iwalam (forever) shanah (sleep), and not qawatz (wake), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.
I will yarad (bring) them down like karayam (lambs) to the tabach (slaughter), like ayalayam (rams) with male ithawadayam (goats).
How is Shashak (Sheshach) lakad (taken)! And the thahalah (praise) of the whole aratz (Earth/land) seized! How is Babal (Babylon) become a shamah (desolation) among the gawayam (nations)!
The yam (sea/waters) has ilah (go up / offer) up on Babal (Babylon); she is kasah (covered) with the hamawan (multitude) of its gal (waves).

Her iyar (cities) are become a shamah (desolation), a tzayah (dry) aratz (Earth/land), and a irabah (desert), a aratz (Earth/land) in which no ayash (man / husband) yashab (inhabit/dwell), neither does any ban (son) of adam (man) ibar (pass over/through) thereby.

I will execute paqad (visit) on Bal (Bel) in Babal (Babylon), and I will yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of his pah (mouth) that which he has balai (swallowed) up; and the gawayam (nations) shall not flow any more to him: yes, the chawamah (wall) of Babal (Babylon) shall napal (fall / be cast down).
My im (nation / people), go away from the thawak (midst) of her, and malat (save) yourselves every ayash (man / husband) from the charawan (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah.

Don't let your labab (heart) rakak (faint), neither yaraa (fear / be afraid) for the shamawaih (news) that shall be shamai (hearken / hear) in the aratz (Earth/land); for shamawaih (news) shall bawaa (come) one shanah (year), and achar (other) that in another shanah (year) shall come shamawaih (news), and chamas (violence) in the aratz (Earth/land), mashal (rule/have dominion) against mashal (rule/have dominion).

Therefore, behold, the yamayam (days) bawaa (come), that I will execute paqad (visit) on the engraved pasayalay (images) of Babal (Babylon); and her whole aratz (Earth/land) shall be bawash (confounded); and all her chalal (slain) shall napal (fall / be cast down) in the thawak (midst) of her.

Then the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) and the aratz (Earth/land), and all that is therein, shall ranan (sing) for joy over Babal (Babylon); for the shawadadayam (destroyers) shall bawaa (come) to her from the tzapawan (north), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

As Babal (Babylon) has caused the chalal (slain) of Yashar-Al (Israel) to napal (fall / be cast down), so at Babal (Babylon) shall napal (fall / be cast down) the chalal (slain) of all the aratz (Earth/land).

You who have palayat (escaped) the charab (sword), halak (move), don't imad (stand) still; zakar (remember) Yahawah from rachawaq (afar), and let Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) ilah (go up / offer) into your labab (mind).

We are bawash (confounded), because we have shamai (hearken / hear) charapah (reproach); kalamah (confusion) has kasah (covered) our panayam (face): for strangers bawaa (come) come into the maqadashay (sanctuaries) of Yahawah bayath (house).

Therefore, behold, the yamayam (days) bawaa (come), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, that I will execute paqad (visit) on her engraved pasayal (images); and through all her aratz (Earth/land) the chalal (wounded) shall anaq (groan).

Though Babal (Babylon) should ilah (go up / offer) up to the sky, and though she should batzar (fortify) the marawam (height) of her iz (strength / might / refuge), yet from me shall shadadayam (destroyers) bawaa (come) to her, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.
The qawal (sound / voice) of a zaiq (cry) from Babal (Babylon), and of gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shabar (destruction) from the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans)!

For Yahawah lays Babal (Babylon) shadad (waste), and abad (destroy / perish) out of her the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice); and their gal (waves) hamah (great uproar) like many mayam (Waters); the shaawan (noise) of their qawal (sound / voice) is nathan (give):

For the shadad (destroyer) bawaa (come) come on her, even on Babal (Babylon), and her gabawar (mighty) men are lakad (taken), their qashath (bows) are broken in pieces; for Yahawah is a Al of gamalawath (recompenses), he will shalam (surely) shalam (requite).

I will shakar (make) drunk her shar (prince / ruler) and her chakam (wise) men, her pachah (governors) and her deputies, and her gabawar (mighty) men; and they shall sleep a iwalam (forever) shanah (sleep), and not qawatz (wake) up, naam (declares prophetically) the malak (king), whose sham (name) is Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies): The rachab (broad) chamawath (walls) of Babal (Babylon) shall be irar (utterly) overthrown, and her gabah (high) shair (gates) shall be yatzath (burned) with ash (fire); and the imayam (peoples) shall yagai (labor) for rayaq (vanity), and the laamayam (nations) for the ash (fire); and they shall be yaip (weary).

The dabar (word / matter) which Yaramayah (Jeremiah) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) tzawah (commanded) Sharayah (Seraiah) the ban (son) of Narayah (Neriah), the ban (son) of Machasayah (Mahseiah), when he yalak (went) with Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah) the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) to Babal (Babylon) in the rabayaiy (fourth) shanah (year) of his malak (king). Now Sharayah (Seraiah) was chief quartermaster.

Yaramayah (Jeremiah) kathab (write) in a sapar (book / scribed document) all the rai (evil) that should bawaa (come) on Babal (Babylon), even all these dabarayam (words) that are kathab (write) concerning Babal (Babylon).
Yaramayah (Jeremiah) amar (spoke) to Sharayah (Seraiah), When you bawaa (come) to Babal (Babylon), then raah (see) that you qaraa (called) all these dabarayam (words),

And amar (spoke), Yahawah, you have dabar (word / matter) concerning this maqawam (place), to karath (cut) it off, that none shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein, neither adam (man) nor animal, but that it shall be shamamah (desolate) iwalam (forever).

It shall be, when you kalah (complete / finish) made an end of qaraa (called) this sapar (book / scribed document), that you shall qashar (bind) a aban (stone) to it, and shalak (cast) it into the thawak (midst) of the Parath (Euphrates):

And you shall amar (spoke), Thus shall Babal (Babylon) shaqai (sink), and shall not qawam (rise up) again panayam (face) of the rai (evil) that I will bawaa (come) on her; and they shall be yaip (weary). Thus far are the dabaray (words) of Yaramayah (Jeremiah).

Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah) was isharayam (twenty) - achad (one) shanah (years) ban (son) when he began to malak (king); and he malak (king) achad (one) shanah (years) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem): and his am (mother) sham (name) was Chamawatal (Hamutal) the banath (daughter) of Yaramayah (Jeremiah) of Labanah (Libnah).
He ishah (make) that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (eye) of Yahawah, according to all that Yahawayaqayam (Jehoiakim) ishah (make) done.

For il (over) the ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) of Yahawah it happened in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) and Yahawadah (Judah), until he had shalak (cast) them out from his panayam (face). Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah) marad (rebelled) against the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon).

It happened in the thashayaiy (ninth) shanah (year) of his malak (king), in the ishayaray (tenth) chadash (month), in the ishawar (tenth) day of the chadash (month), that Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) bawaa (come), he and all his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), against Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and chanah (encamped) against it; and they banah (build) dayaq (forts) against it sabayab (surrounding) about.
So the iyar (city) was matzawar (besieged) to the ishathay (eleven) shanah (year) of malak (king) Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah).

In the rabayaiy (fourth) chadash (month), in the thashai (nine) day of the chadash (month), the raib (famine) was severe in the iyar (city), so that there was no lacham (bread) for the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land).

Then a baqai (breach) was made in the iyar (city), and all the anashay (men) of malachamah (war) barach (fled), and yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the iyar (city) by layal (night) by the darak (way) of the shair (gate) between the two chamathayam (walls), which was by the malak (king) gan (garden); (now the Kashaday (Chaldeans) were against the iyar (city) all around;) and they yalak (went) toward the irabah (arabah).

But the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans) radap (pursued) achar (other) the malak (king), and overtook Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah) in the irabath (plains) of Yarayachaw (Jericho); and all his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) was pawatz (scattered) from him.

Then they thapash (took) the malak (king), and ilah (go up / offer) him up to the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) to Rabalah (Riblah) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Chamath (Hamath); and he dabar (word / matter) mashapat (judgment) on him.

The malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) shachat (killed) the banay (sons) of Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah) before his iyan (eye): he shachat (killed) also all the sharay (princes) of Yahawadah (Judah) in Rabalah (Riblah).

He iwar (put) out the iyanay (eyes) of Tzadaqayah (Zedekiah); and the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) asar (bound) him in nachashathayam (fetters), and bawaa (come) him to Babal (Babylon), and nathan (give) him in bayath (house) until the yawam (day) of his mawath (death).

Now in the chamayashay (fifth) chadash (month), in the ishawar (tenth) day of the chadash (month), which was the nineteenth shanah (year) of malak (king) Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar), malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), bawaa (come) Nabawazaraadan (Nebuzaradan) the rab (captain) of the tabach (guard), who stood before the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), into Yarawashalam (Jerusalem):

And he sharap (burned) the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the malak (king) bayath (house); and all the bathay (houses) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), even every gadawal (very great/important/mighty) bayath (house), sharap (burned) he with ash (fire).

All the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), who were with the rab (captain) of the tabach (guard), nathatz (broke) down all the chamawath (walls) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) all around.

Then Nabawazaraadan (Nebuzaradan) the rab (captain) of the tabach (guard) galah (carried) away captive of the poorest of the im (nation / people), and the yathar (residue) of the im (nation / people) who were shaar (left) in the iyar (city), and those who napal (fall / be cast down) away, who napal (fall / be cast down) to the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), and the yathar (residue) of the amawan (multitude).
But Nabawazaraadan (Nebuzaradan) the rab (captain) of the tabach (guard) shaar (left) of the poorest of the aratz (Earth/land) to be vineyard keepers and farmers.

The Kashaday (Chaldeans) shabar (broke) the imawaday (pillars) of nachashath (brass) that were in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the makanawath (bases) and the bronze yam (sea/waters) that were in the bayath (house) of Yahawah in pieces, and nashaa (lift) all the of their nachashath (brass) to Babal (Babylon).

They also laqach (take / seize) away the sarawath (pots), the yaiyam (shovels), the mazamarawath (snuffers), the basins, the kapawath (spoons), and all the kalay (vessels) of nachashath (brass) with which they sharath (ministered).

The rab (captain) of the tabach (guard) laqach (take / seize) laqach (take / seize) the cups, the machathah (fire) pans, the basins, the sayarawath (pots), the lampstands, the kapawath (spoons), and the manaqayawath (bowls); that which was of zahab (gold), in zahab (gold), and that which was of kasap (silver), in kasap (silver).

They took the shanayam (two) imawadayam (pillars), the achad (one) yam (sea/waters), and the shanayam (two) bronze baqar (morning) that were under the makanawath (bases), which malak (king) Shalamah (Solomon) ishah (make) made for the bayath (house) of Yahawah. The nachashath (brass) of all these kalayam (vessels) was without mashaqal (weight).

As for the imawadayam (pillars), the qawamah (height) of the achad (one) imawad (pillar) was eighteen amah (cubits); and a chawat (line) of shanayam (two) amah (cubits) encircled it; and its ibay (thickness) was arabai (four) atzabaiwath (fingers). It was nabab (hollow).

A capital of nachashath (brass) was on it; and the qawamah (height) of the achad (one) capital was chamash (five) amawath (cubits), with shabakah (network) and ramawanayam (pomegranates) on the capital all around, all of nachashath (brass): and the shanay (second) imawad (pillar) also had like these, and ramawanayam (pomegranates).
There were thashaiyam (ninety) - shash (six) ramanayam (pomegranates) on the rawach (spirit / wind); all the ramanayam (pomegranates) were one maah (hundred) on the shabakah (network) all around.

The rab (captain) of the tabach (guard) laqach (take / seize) Sharayah (Seraiah) the raash (head) kahan (priest), and Tzapanayah (Zephaniah) the mashanah (second) kahan (priest), and the shalawash (three) keepers of the sap (threshold):

And out of the iyar (city) he laqach (take / seize) an sarayas (officer) who paqayad (was) set over the achad (one) of malachamah (war); and shabai (seven) achad (one) of those who raah (see) the malak (king) panayam (face), who were matzaa (found) in the iyar (city); and the sapar (book) of the shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop), who tzabaa (troop) the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land); and shashayam (sixty) anashay (men) of the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land), who were matzaa (found) in the thawak (midst) of the iyar (city).
Nabawazaraadan (Nebuzaradan) the rab (captain) of the tabach (guard) laqach (take / seize) them, and yalak (brought) them to the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) to Rabalah (Riblah).

The malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) nakah (struck) them, and put them to mawath (death) at Rabalah (Riblah) in the adamah (land) of Chamath (Hamath). So Yahawadah (Judah) was galah (carried) away captive out of his aratz (Earth/land).

This is the im (nation / people) whom Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) galah (carried) away captive: in the shabai (seven) shanah (year) shalawash (three) alap (thousand) isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three) Yahawaday (Jews);

In the eighteenth shanah (year) of Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) he carried away captive from Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) napash (soul);

In the shalawash (three) and isharayam (twenty) shanah (year) of Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) Nabawazaraadan (Nebuzaradan) the rab (captain) of the tabach (guard) galah (carried) away captive of the Yahawaday (Jews) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - chamash (five) napash (soul): all the napash (soul) were arabai (four) alap (thousand) and shash (six) maah (hundred).

It happened in the shabai (seven) and shalawashayam (thirty) shanah (year) of the galawath (captivity) of Yahawayakayan (Jehoiachin) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), in the shanayam (two) chadash (month), in the chamash (five) and isharayam (twenty) day of the chadash (month), that awayalamaradak (evilmerodach) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), in the first shanah (year) of his malakawath (reign), nashaa (lift) up the raash (head) of Yahawayakayan (Jehoiachin) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and yatzaa (go out / come out) him forth out of bayath (house);

And he dabar (word / matter) tawab (good / proper function) to him, and nathan (give) his kasaa (throne) mail (top/above) the kasaa (throne) of the malakayam (kings) who were with him in Babal (Babylon),
And shanah (changed) his kalaa (prison) bagaday (garments). Jehoiachin akal (eat) lacham (bread) panayam (face) him continually all the yamay (days) of his chay (life):

And for his arachah (allowance), there was a thamayad (continual) arachah (allowance) nathan (give) him by the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), every yawam (day) a dabar (word / matter) until the yawam (day) of his mawath (death), all the yamay (days) of his chay (life).

How the iyar (city) yashab (inhabit/dwell) badad (solitary), that was rab (full) of im (nation / people)! She has become as a alamanah (widow), who was rab (great) among the gawayam (nations)! She who was a sharah (princess) among the madayanawath (provinces) has become mas (tributary)!

She bakah (weeps) bitterly in the layal (night), and her damaih (tears) are on her lachay (cheeks); among all her lovers she has none to nacham (turn away / repent) her: All her rai (neigbor/another person) have dealt bagad (treacherously) with her; they are become her ayabayam (enemies).

Yahawadah (Judah) is galah (gone) into captivity because of inay (affliction), and because of rab (great) servitude; she yashab (inhabit/dwell) among the gawayam (nations), she matzaa (finds) no manawach (rest): all her persecutors overtook her within the matzarayam (straits).

The darakay (ways) of Tzayawan (Zion) do abal (mourn), because none bawaa (come) to the solemn mawaid (Feast/Holy Day); all her shair (gates) are shamam (desolate), her kahan (priest) do anach (sigh): her bathawalah (virgins) are yagah (afflicted), and she herself is in bitterness.

Her tzar (oppressor / distressor) are become the raash (head), her ayab (enemy) shalah (prosper); for Yahawah has yagah (afflicted) her for the rab (multitude) of her pashai (transgressions): her young iwalal (children) are halak (move) into shabay (captivity) panayam (face) the tzar (oppressor / distressor).

From the banath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion) all her hadar (glory / majesty / splendor) is departed: her shar (prince / ruler) are become like ayalayam (harts) that matzaa (find) no maraih (pasture), they are yalak (gone) without kach (strength / mighty / power) panayam (face) the radap (pursuer).

Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) zakar (remember) in the yamay (days) of her inay (affliction) and of her marawad (miseries) all her machamad (pleasant) things that were from the yamay (days) of qadam (old): when her im (nation / people) napal (fall / be cast down) into the yad (hand) of the tzar (oppressor / distressor), and no one izar (helped) her, The tzarayam (adversaries) raah (see) her, they shachaq (mocked) at her desolations.

Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) has chataa (grievously) chataa (sinned); therefore she has become as an kabad (unclean) thing; all who honored her zawal (despise) her, because they raah (see) seen her irawah (nakedness): yes, she anach (sighs), and shawab (turn back / repent) backward.

Her tamaah (filthiness) was in her shawal (skirts); she didn't zakar (remember) her acharayath (latter) end; therefore is she yarad (come) down wonderfully; she has no comforter: raah (see), Yahawah, my inay (affliction); for the ayab (enemy) has gadal (magnified) himself.

The tzar (oppressor / distressor) has parash (spread) out his yad (hand) on all her machamad (pleasant) things: for she raah (see) seen that the gawayam (nations) are bawaa (come) into her maqadash (sanctuary), concerning whom you tzawah (commanded) that they should not bawaa (come) into your qahal (assembly).

All her im (nation / people) anach (sigh), they baqash (seek) lacham (bread); they nathan (give) given their machamad (pleasant) things for akal (food) to shawab (turn back / repent) the napash (soul): raah (see), Yahawah, and raah (see); for I am become abject.

Is it nothing to you, ibar (pass over/through) you who pass by? Nabat (look), and raah (see) if there is any makaab (sorrow) like my makaab (sorrow), which is brought on me, With which Yahawah has yagah (afflicted) me in the yawam (day) of his charawan (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).

From on marawam (high) has he shalach (send) ash (fire) into my itzam (bones), and it radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) against them; He has parash (spread) a rashath (net) for my ragal (feet / foot), he has shawab (turn back / repent) me achawar (back): He nathan (give) made me shamam (desolate) and dawah (faint) all the yawam (day).

The il (over) of my pashai (transgressions) is shaqad (bound) by his yad (hand); They are knit together, they have ilah (go up / offer) up on my tzawaar (neck); he has made my kach (strength / mighty / power) to kashal (stumble / stagger): The Adanay nathan (give) delivered me into their yaday (hands), against whom I am not yakal (able) to qawam (rise up).

The Adanay has set at nothing all my abayar (mighty) men in the qarab (among / near) of me; He has qaraa (called) a solemn mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) against me to shabar (crush) my bachawar (young) men: The Adanay has darak (trodden) as in a gath (winepress) the bathawalah (virgin) banath (daughter) of Yahawadah (Judah).

For these things I bakah (weep); my iyan (eye), my iyan (eye) yarad (runs) down with mayam (Waters); Because the comforter who should shawab (turn back / repent) my napash (soul) is rachaq (far) from me: My ban (son) are shamam (desolate), because the ayab (enemy) has gabar (prevailed).

Tzayawan (Zion) parash (spreads) forth her yad (hand); there is none to nacham (turn away / repent) her; Yahawah has tzawah (commanded) concerning Yaiqab (Jacob), that those who are around him should be his tzar (oppressor / distressor): Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) is among them as an nadah (unclean) thing.

Yahawah is tzadayaq (righteous); for I have marah (rebelled) against his commandment: Please shamai (hearken / hear) all you imayam (peoples), and raah (see) my makaab (sorrow): My bathawalah (virgins) and my bachawar (young) men are halak (move) into shabay (captivity).

I qaraa (called) for my lovers, but they ramah (deceived) me: My kahan (priest) and my zaqan (elders) gawai (gave) up the spirit in the iyar (city), While they baqash (sought) them akal (food) to shawab (turn back / repent) their napash (soul).

Raah (see), Yahawah; for I am in tzarar (distress); my maih (heart) is chamar (troubled); My lab (heart) is hapak (turned) qarab (among / near) me; for I have marah (grievously) marah (rebelled): chawatz (abroad) the charab (sword) shakal (bereaves), at bayath (house) there is as mawath (death).

They have shamai (hearken / hear) that I anach (sigh); there is none to nacham (turn away / repent) me; All my ayab (enemy) have shamai (hearken / hear) of my rai (trouble); they are shawash (glad) that you ishah (make) done it: You will bawaa (come) the yawam (day) that you have qaraa (called), and they shall be kamaw (like) me.

Let all their rai (wickedness) bawaa (come) panayam (face) you; ilal (do) to them, as you have ilal (done) to me for all my pashai (transgressions): For my anachah (sighs) are many, and my lab (heart) is daway (faint).

How has the Adanay iwab (covered) the banath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion) with a iwab (cloud) in his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting)! He has shalak (cast) down from shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) to the aratz (Earth/land) the thapaarah (beauty) of Yashar-Al (Israel), And hasn't zakar (remember) his hadam (footstool) in the yawam (day) of his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).

The Adanay has balai (swallowed) up all the naawath (habitations) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and chamal (has) not pitied: He has haras (thrown) down in his ibarah (wrath) the strongholds of the banath (daughter) of Yahawadah (Judah); He has nagai (brought) them down to the aratz (Earth/land); he has chalal (profaned) the mamalakah (kingdom) and its shar (prince / ruler).

He has gadai (cut) off in charay (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) all the qaran (horn) of Yashar-Al (Israel); He has shawab (turn back / repent) achawar (back) his right yamayan (right hand) from panayam (face) the ayab (enemy): He has bair (burned) up Yaiqab (Jacob) like a lahabah (flaming) ash (fire), which akal (eat) all around.

He has bent his qashath (bow) like an ayab (enemy), he has natzab (stood) with his right yamayan (right hand) as an tzar (oppressor / distressor), Has harag (kill) all that were machamad (pleasant) to the iyan (eye): In the ahal (tent) of the banath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion) he has shapak (poured) out his chamah (wrath) like ash (fire).

The Adanay has become as an ayab (enemy), he has balai (swallowed) up Yashar-Al (Israel); He has balai (swallowed) up all her aramawan (palaces), he has shachath (destroyed) his strongholds; He rabah (has) multiplied in the banath (daughter) of Yahawadah (Judah) thaanayah (mourning) and anayah (lamentation).

He has chamas (violently) taken away his shak (tabernacle), as if it were of a gan (garden); he has shachath (destroyed) his place of mawaid (Feast/Holy Day): Yahawah has caused solemn mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) and shabath (shabath / rest) to be shakach (forgotten) in Tzayawan (Zion), Has naatz (despised) in the zaim (indignation) of his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) the malak (king) and the kahan (priest).

The Adanay has zanach (cast) off his mazabach (altar), he has naar (abhorred) his maqadash (sanctuary); He has sagar (given) up into the yad (hand) of the ayab (enemy) the chawamath (walls) of her aramawan (palaces): They nathan (give) made a qawal (sound / voice) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, as in the yawam (day) of a solemn mawaid (Feast/Holy Day).

Yahawah has chashab (purposed) to shachath (destroy) the chawamah (wall) of the banath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion); He has natah (stretched) out the qaw (line), he has not shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand) from balai (destroying); He has made the chayal (rampart) and chawamah (wall) to abal (lament); they amal (languish) yachad (together).

Her shair (gates) are tabai (sunk) into the aratz (Earth/land); he abad (destroy / perish) destroyed and shabar (broken) her barayach (bars): Her malak (king) and her shar (prince / ruler) are among the gawayam (nations) where the thawarah (instruction) is not; Yes, her nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) matzaa (find) no chazawan (vision) from Yahawah.

The zaqanay (elders) of the banath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion) yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the aratz (Earth/land), they damam (keep) silence; They have ilah (go up / offer) up ipar (dust) on their raash (head); they have clothed themselves with sackcloth: The bathawalath (virgins) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) yarad (hang) down their raash (head) to the aratz (Earth/land).

My iyan (eye) kalah (complete / finish) fail with damaiwath (tears), my maih (heart) is chamar (troubled); My kabad (liver) is shapak (poured) on the aratz (Earth/land), because of the shabar (destruction) of the banath (daughter) of my im (nation / people), Because the young iwalal (children) and the infants itap (swoon) in the rachabawath (streets) of the qarayah (city / town).

They amar (spoke) their am (mother), Where is grain and yayan (wine)? When they itap (swoon) as the chalal (wounded) in the rachabawath (streets) of the iyar (city), When their napash (soul) is shapak (poured) out into their am (mother)' chayaq (bosom).

What shall I iwad (admonish/bear witness against) to you? Mah (what) shall I damah (liken) to you, banath (daughter) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem)? What shall I shawah (compare) to you, that I may nacham (turn away / repent) you, bathawalah (virgin) banath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion)? For your shabar (breach) is gadawal (very great/important/mighty) like the yam (sea/waters): who can rapaa (heal) you?

Your nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) have chazah (seen) for you shawaa (vanity) and thapal (foolish) visions; They have not galah (uncovered) your iwan (guilt/iniquity), to shawab (turn back / repent) back your shabawath (captivity), but have chazah (seen) for you shawaa (vanity) oracles and madawachayam (causes) of banishment.

Ibar (pass over/through) that pass by sapaq (clap) their kapayam (hands) at you. They sharaq (hiss) and nawai (wag) their raash (head) at the banath (daughter) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), saying, "Is this the iyar (city) that men amar (spoke) The kalayal (perfection) of yapay (beauty), The mashawash (joy) of the whole aratz (Earth/land)?

All your ayab (enemy) have patzah (opened) their pah (mouth) wide against you; They sharaq (hiss) and charaq (gnash) the shan (teeth); they amar (spoke), We have balai (swallowed) her up; ak (certainly) this is the yawam (day) that we qawah (gather/wait) for; we matzaa (have) found, we raah (see) seen it.

Yahawah ishah (make) done that which he zamam (purposed); he has batzai (fulfilled) his amarah (sayings) that he tzawah (commanded) in the yamay (days) of qadam (old); He has haras (thrown) down, and chamal (has) not pitied: He has caused the ayab (enemy) to shamach (rejoice) over you; he has rawam (will lift up) the qaran (horn) of your tzar (oppressor / distressor).

Their lab (heart) tzaiq (cried) to the Adanay: chawamah (wall) of the banath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion), let damaih (tears) yarad (run) down like a nachal (stream / river) yawamam (by day) and layal (night); nathan (give) yourself no respite; don't let the banath (daughter) of your iyan (eye) damam (cease).

Qawam (rise up), ranan (cry) out in the layal (night), at the raash (head) of the watches; shapak (pour) out your lab (heart) like mayam (Waters) nakach (before) the panayam (face) of the Adanay: nashaa (lift) up your kap (hands) toward him for the napash (soul) of your young iwalal (children), that itap (faint) for raib (hunger) at the raash (head) of every chawatz (street).

Raah (see), Yahawah, and raah (see) to whom you have ilal (done) thus! Shall the nashayam (women) akal (eat) their paray (fruit), the ilalay (children) that are dandled in the hands? Shall the kahan (priest) and the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) be harag (kill) in the maqadash (sanctuary) of the Adanay?

The youth and the zaqan (old) man shakab (lie) on the aratz (Earth/land) in the chawatzawath (streets); My bathawalah (virgins) and my bachawar (young) men are napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword): You have tabach (killed) them in the yawam (day) of your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting); you have tabach (slaughtered), and not chamal (pitied).

You have qaraa (called), as in the yawam (day) of a mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) assembly, my magawar (terrors) on sabayab (surrounding) side; There was none that palayat (escaped) or sharayad (remained) in the yawam (day) of Yahawah ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting): Those that I have dandled and rabah (brought) up has my ayab (enemy) kalah (complete / finish).
I am the gabar (man) that raah (see) seen inay (affliction) by the shabat (rod) of his ibarah (wrath).
He has nahag (led) me and yalak (caused) me to walk in chashak (darkness), and not in awar (light).
Surely against me he shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand) again and again all the yawam (day).
My bashar (flesh) and my iwar (skin) has he balah (made) old; he has shabar (broken) my itzam (bones).
He has banah (build) against me, and surrounded me with raash (head) and thalaah (travail).
He has yashab (inhabit/dwell) me to dwell in machashak (dark) places, as those that have been iwalam (forever) mawath (death).
He has walled me about, that I can't yatzaa (go out / come out) forth; he has made my nachashath (chain) kabad (heavy).
Yes, when I zaiq (cry), and zaiq (call) for help, he satham (shuts) out my thapalah (prayer).
He has walled up my darak (ways) with cut gazayath (stone); he has made my nathayab (paths) iwah (crooked).
He is to me as a dab (bear) lying in arab (wait), as a aray (lion) in masathar (secret) places.
He has sawar (turned) aside my darak (ways), and pashach (pulled) me in pieces; he has shawam (place / establish / appoint) me shamam (desolate).
He has bent his qashath (bow), and natzab (set) me as a mataraa (mark) for the chatz (arrow).
He has caused the shafts of his ashapah (quiver) to bawaa (come) into my kalayah (kidneys).
I am become a shachawaq (laughter/joking matter) to all my im (nation / people), and their nagayanah (song) all the yawam (day).
He shabai (has) filled me with marar (bitterness), he has sated me with lainah (wormwood).
He has also garas (broken) my shan (teeth) with chatzatz (gravel) stones; he has kapash (covered) me with ashes.
You have zanach (removed) my napash (soul) zanach (far) off from shalawam (peace / safety); I nashah (forgot) tawab (good / proper function).
I amar (spoke), My natzach (strength) is abad (destroy / perish), and my expectation from Yahawah.
Zakar (remember) my inay (affliction) and my marawad (misery), the lainah (wormwood) and the raash (head).
My napash (soul) still remembers them, and is shawach (bowed) down within me.
This I shawab (turn back / repent) to my lab (heart); therefore yachal (have) I hope.
It is because of Yahawah chasad (grace) kindnesses that we are not thamam (consumed), because his racham (show mercy / love) doesn't kalah (complete / finish).
They are chadash (new) every baqar (morning); rab (great) is your amawanah (faithfulness).
Yahawah is my chalaq (portion), amar (spoke) my napash (soul); therefore will I yachal (hope) in him.
Yahawah is tawab (good / proper function) to those who qawah (gather/wait) for him, to the napash (soul) that darash (seeks) him.
It is tawab (good / proper function) that a man yachayal (should) hope and dawamam (quietly) wait for the thashawaih (deliverance) of Yahawah.
It is tawab (good / proper function) for a gabar (man) that he nashaa (lift) the il (over) in his naiwar (youth).
Let him yashab (inhabit/dwell) badad (alone) and damam (keep) silence, because he has laid it on him.
Let him put his pah (mouth) in the ipar (dust), if so be there yash (may) be thaqawah (hope).
Nathan (give) him give his lachay (cheek) to him who nakah (strikes) him; let him be shabai (filled) full with charapah (reproach).
For the Adanay will not zanach (cast) off iwalam (forever).
For though he yagah (cause) grief, yet he will racham (show mercy / love) compassion according to the rab (multitude) of his chasad (grace) kindnesses.
For he does not inah (oppress / afflict) lab (heart), nor yagah (grieve) the banay (children) of ayash (man / husband).
To dakaa (crush) under ragal (feet / foot) all the asayaray (prisoners) of the aratz (Earth/land),
To natah (turn) aside the mashapat (right) of a gabar (man) before the panayam (face) of the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan),
To iwath (subvert) a adam (man) in his rayab (cause), the Adanay doesn't raah (see).
Who is he who amar (spoke), and it comes to pass, when the Adanay doesn't tzawah (command) it?
Doesn't rai (evil) and tawab (good / proper function) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the pah (mouth) of the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan)?
Why does a chay (life) adam (man) anan (complain), a gabar (man) for the punishment of his chataa (sins)?
Let us chapash (search) and chaqar (try) our darak (ways), and shawab (turn back / repent) again to Yahawah.
Let us nashaa (lift) up our labab (heart) with our kapayam (hands) to Al in the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens).
We have pashai (transgressed) and have marah (rebelled); you have not salach (forgive/pardon/make clean).
You have sakak (covered) with ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) and radap (pursued) us; you have harag (kill), you chamal (have) not pitied.
You have sakak (covered) yourself with a inan (cloud), so that no thapalah (prayer) can ibar (pass over/through) through.
You have shawam (place / establish / appoint) us an sachay (off-scouring) and maawas (refuse) in the qarab (among / near) of the imayam (peoples).
All our ayab (enemy) have patzah (opened) their pah (mouth) wide against us.
Pachad (fear / dread) and the pachath (pit) have come on us, devastation and shabar (destruction).
My iyan (eye) yarad (runs) down with palagay (streams) of mayam (Waters), for the shabar (destruction) of the banath (daughter) of my im (nation / people).
My iyan (eye) nagar (pours) down, and doesn't damah (cease), without any hapagah (intermission),
Until Yahawah shaqap (look) down, and raah (see) from shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens).
My iyan (eye) ilal (affects) my napash (soul), because of all the banawath (daughters) of my iyar (city).
They have tzawad (chased) me relentlessly like a tzapawar (bird), those who are my ayab (enemy) chanam (without) cause.
They have tzamath (cut) off my chay (life) in the bawar (dungeon), and have yadah (cast) a aban (stone) on me.
Mayam (Waters) tzawap (flowed) over my raash (head); I amar (spoke), I am gazar (cut) off.
I qaraa (called) on your sham (name), Yahawah, out of the lowest bawar (dungeon).
You shamai (hearken / hear) my qawal (sound / voice); don't ilam (hide) your azan (ear) at my rawachah (breathing), at my cry.
You qarab (come close) near in the yawam (day) that I qaraa (called) on you; you amar (spoke), Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid).
Adanay, you have rayab (pleaded) the rayabay (causes) of my napash (soul); you have gaal (redeemed) my chay (life).
Yahawah, you raah (see) seen my iwathah (wrong). Shapat (judge / judgement) my cause.
You raah (see) seen all their naqamah (vengeance) and all their machashabah (devices) against me.
You have shamai (hearken / hear) their charapah (reproach), Yahawah, and all their machashabah (devices) against me,
The shapathay (lips) of those that qawam (rise up) up against me, and their hagayawan (device) against me all the yawam (day).
You nabat (see) their sitting down, and their qayamah (rising) up; I am their song.
You will shawab (turn back / repent) to them a gamawal (recompense), Yahawah, according to the maishah (work) of their yad (hand).
You will nathan (give) them hardness of lab (heart), your thaalah (curse) to them.
You will radap (pursue) them in ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and shamad (destroy) them from under the shamay (heavens) of Yahawah.

How the zahab (gold) has imam (become) dim! The most katham (pure) gold has shanaa (hate)! The abanay (stones) of the qadash (set apart / make holy) are shapak (poured) out at the raash (head) of every chawatz (street).

The yaqar (precious) banay (sons) of Tzayawan (Zion), comparable to paz (fine) gold, How are they chashab (esteemed) as charash (earthen) nabalay (pitchers), the maishah (work) of the yaday (hands) of the yatzar (potter)!

Even the jackals chalatz (draw) out the shad (breast), they yanaq (nurse) their gawar (young) ones: The banath (daughter) of my im (nation / people) has become akazar (cruel), like the ostriches in the madabar (wilderness).

The lashawan (tongue / language) of the yanaq (nursing) child clings to the roof of his chak (mouth) for tzamaa (thirst): The young iwalalayam (children) shaal (ask) lacham (bread), and no man parash (breaks) it to them.
Those who akal (eat) maidan (delicately) are shamam (desolate) in the chawatzawath (streets): Those who were aman (believe / have faith) up in thawalai (scarlet) chabaq (embrace) dunghills.

For the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the banath (daughter) of my im (nation / people) is greater than the chataah (sin) of Sadam (Sodom), That was overthrown as in a ragai (in an instance), and no yadayam (hands) were laid on her.

Her nobles were zakak (purer) than shalag (snow), they were tzachach (whiter) than chalab (milk); They were more ruddy in itzam (body) than panayanayam (rubies), their gazarah (polishing) was as of sapayar (sapphire).

Their appearance is blacker than a shachawar (coal); they are not nakar (known) in the chawatzawath (streets): Their iwar (skin) clings to their itzam (bones); it is yabash (dry land), it has become like a itz (stick).

Those who are chalal (killed) with the charab (sword) are tawab (good / proper function) than those who are chalal (killed) with raib (hunger); For these zawab (flow) away, daqar (stricken) through, for want of the thanawabath (fruits) of the shadah (field).

The yaday (hands) of the rachamanay (pitiful) nashayam (women) have bashal (boiled) their own yalad (birth / begot); They were their food in the shabar (destruction) of the banath (daughter) of my im (nation / people).

Yahawah kalah (complete / finish) accomplished his chamah (wrath), he has shapak (poured) out his charawan (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting); He has yatzath (kindled) a ash (fire) in Tzayawan (Zion), which has akal (eat) its yasawad (foundations).

The malakay (kings) of the aratz (Earth/land) didn't aman (believe / have faith), neither all the yashabay (inhabitants) of the thabal (world), That the tzar (oppressor / distressor) and the ayab (enemy) would bawaa (come) into the shairay (gates) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

It is because of the chataath (sins) of her nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and the iwanawath (iniquities) of her kahan (priest), That have shapak (shed) the dam (blood) of the tzadayaq (righteous) in the qarab (among / near) of her.
They nawai (wander) as iwar (blind) men in the chawatzawath (streets), they are gaal (polluted) with dam (blood), So that men can't nagai (touch) their labawash (garments).

Sawar (depart)! They qaraa (called) to them, tamaa (unclean)! Sawar (depart), sawar (depart), don't nagai (touch)! When they nawatz (fled) away and nawai (wandered), men amar (spoke) among the gawayam (nations), They shall not live here any more.

The panayam (face) of Yahawah chalaq (has) scattered them; he will no more nabat (regard) them: They didn't nabat (respect) the panay (persons) of the kahanayam (priests), they didn't favor the zaqanayam (elders).

Our iyan (eye) still kalah (complete / finish), looking in habal (vain) for our izarah (help): In our tzapayah (watching) we have tzapah (watchman / keep watch) for a gaway (heathen / nation) that could not yashai (salvation).

They tzawad (hunt) our tzaid (steps), so that we can't yalak (go) in our rachab (streets): Our qatz (end) is qarab (come close), our yawam (day) are malaa (fulfilled); for our qatz (end) bawaa (come) come.
Our radap (pursuers) were swifter than the nasharay (eagles) of the sky: They dalaq (chased) us on the harayam (mountains), they arab (laid) wait for us in the madabar (wilderness).

The rawach (spirit / wind) of our ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), the mashayach (anointed one) of Yahawah, was lakad (taken) in their shachayath (pits); Of whom we amar (spoke), Under his tzal (shadow) we shall chayah (live) among the gawayam (nations).

Shawash (rejoice) and be shamach (glad), banath (daughter) of Adawam (Edom), that yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Iwatz (Uz): The kawas (cup) shall ibar (pass over/through) through to you also; you shall be shakar (drunken), and shall irah (make) yourself naked.

The punishment of your iwan (guilt/iniquity) is thamam (accomplished), banath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion); he will no more galah (carry) you away into captivity: He will paqad (visit) your iwan (guilt/iniquity), banath (daughter) of Adawam (Edom); he will galah (uncover) your chataah (sin).
