Zakar (remember), Yahawah, what raah (see) come on us: Look, and raah (see) our charapah (reproach).
Our nachalah (inheritance) is hapak (turned) to strangers, Our bayath (house) to nakarayam (aliens).
We are yathawamayam (orphans) and ayan (NO ONE); Our am (mother) are as alamanawath (widows).
We have shathah (drinks) our mayam (Waters) for kasap (money); Our itz (wood) is sold to us.
Our naradapanaw (pursuers) are on our tzawaar (necks): We are yagai (weary), and have no nawach (rest).
We nathan (give) given the yad (hand) to the Matzarayam (Egyptians), To the Ashawar (Assyrians), to be shabai (satisfied) with lacham (bread).
Our ab (father) chataa (sinned), and are no more; We have sabal (borne) their iwan (guilt/iniquity).
Ibadayam (servants) mashal (rule/have dominion) over us: There is none to paraq (deliver) us out of their yad (hand).
We bawaa (come) our lacham (bread) at the peril of our lives, panayam (face) of the charab (sword) of the madabar (wilderness).
Our iwar (skin) is kamar (black) like an thanawar (oven), panayam (face) of the burning heat of raib (famine).
They inah (oppress / afflict) the nashayam (women) in Tzayawan (Zion), The bathalath (virgins) in the iray (cities) of Yahawadah (Judah).
Sharayam (princes) were hanged up by their yad (hand): The panay (faces) of zaqanayam (elders) were not honored.
The bachawar (young) men bare the mill; The nairayam (children) kashal (stumble / stagger) under the itz (wood).
The zaqanayam (elders) have shabath (shabath / rest) from the shair (gate), The bachawar (young) men from their music.
The mashawash (joy) of our lab (heart) is shabath (shabath / rest); Our machawal (dance) is hapak (turned) into abal (mourning).
The itarah (crown) is napal (fall / be cast down) from our raash (head): away (woe) to us! For we have chataa (sinned).
For this our lab (heart) is dawah (faint); For these things our iyan (eye) are chashak (darkness);
For the har (mountain) of Tzayawan (Zion), which is shamam (desolate): The foxes halak (move) on it.
You, Yahawah, yashab (inhabit/dwell) iwalam (forever); Your kasaa (throne) is from dawar (generation / age / period) to dawar (generation / age / period).
Why do you shakach (forget) us natzach (forever), And izab (forsake) us so arak (length) yawam (day)?
Shawab (turn back / repent) us to yourself, Yahawah, and we shall be shawab (turn back / repent). Chadash (renew) our yawam (day) as of qadam (old).
But you have maas (utterly) maas (rejected) us; You are very qatzap (angry) against us.

Now it happened in the shalawashayam (thirty) shanah (year), in the rabayaiy (fourth) month, in the chamash (fifth) of the chadash (month), as I was thawak (midst) the gawalah (captives) by the nahar (river) Kabar (Chebar), that the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) were pathach (opened), and I raah (see) maraawath (visions) of Alahayam.
In the chamash (fifth) of the chadash (month), which was the chamayashay (fifth) shanah (year) of malak (king) Yawayakayan (Jehoiachin's) galawath (captivity),

The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came expressly to Yachazaqaal (Ezekiel) the kahan (priest), the ban (son) of Bawazay (Buzi), in the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans) by the nahar (river) Kabar (Chebar); and the yad (hand) of Yahawah was there on him.

I raah (see), and behold, a stormy rawach (spirit / wind) bawaa (come) out of the tzapawan (north), a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) inan (cloud), with flashing lightning, and a nagah (brightness) around it, and out of its thawak (midst) as it were glowing metal, out of the thawak (midst) of the ash (fire).
Out of its thawak (midst) came the damawath (likeness) of arabai (four) chay (life) creatures. This was their maraah (appearance): they had the damawath (likeness) of a adam (man).
Everyone had arabai (four) panayam (face), and achad (one) one of them had arabai (four) kanapayam (wings).

Their ragal (feet / foot) were yashar (upright) ragal (feet / foot); and the kap (sole) of their ragal (feet / foot) was like the kap (sole) of a igal (calf's) ragal (feet / foot); and they natzatz (sparkled) like qalal (burnished) nachashath (brass).
They had the yad (hand) of a adam (man) under their kanap (wings) on their arabai (four) rabai (fourth); and the arabai (four) of them had their panayam (face) and their kanap (wings) thus:
Their kanap (wings) were chabar (joined) ayashah (woman / wife) to achawath (another); they didn't sabab (turn) when they yalak (went); ayash (man / husband) one yalak (went) ibar (straight) forward.

As for the damawath (likeness) of their panay (faces), they had the panayam (face) of a adam (man); and the arabai (four) of them had the panayam (face) of a aray (lion) on the yamayan (right hand) side; and the arabai (four) of them had the panayam (face) of an shawar (ox) on the shamaawal (left hand) side; the arabai (four) of them also had the panayam (face) of an nashar (eagle).

Such were their panayam (face). Their kanap (wings) were spread out mail (top/above). Shanayam (two) wings of ayash (man / husband) ayash (man / husband) touched ayash (man / husband), and shanayam (two) kasah (covered) their gawayah (corpse).
Ayash (man / husband) one yalak (went) ibar (straight) forward: where the rawach (spirit / wind) was to yalak (go), they yalak (went); they didn't sabab (turn) when they yalak (went).

As for the damawath (likeness) of the chay (life) creatures, their maraah (appearance) was like bair (burning) gachalay (coals) of ash (fire), like the maraah (appearance) of torches: the fire halak (move) up and down among the chay (life) creatures; and the ash (fire) was nagah (bright), and out of the ash (fire) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth baraq (lightning).
The chay (life) creatures ratzaa (ran) and shawab (turn back / repent) as the maraah (appearance) of a bazaq (flash) of lightning.
Now as I raah (see) the chay (life) creatures, behold, achad (one) awapan (wheel) on the aratz (Earth/land) beside the chay (life) creatures, for each of the arabai (four) panayam (face) of it.

The maraah (appearance) of the awapanayam (wheels) and their maishah (work) was like a tharashayash (beryl): and the arabai (four) of them had achad (one) damawath (likeness); and their maraah (appearance) and their maishah (work) was as it were a awapan (wheel) thawak (midst) a awapan (wheel).
When they yalak (went), they yalak (went) in their arabai (four) directions: they didn't sabab (turn) when they yalak (went).
As for their rims, they were gabah (high) and yaraah (dreadful); and the arabai (four) of them had their rims malaa (full) of iyanayam (eyes) all around.

When the chay (life) creatures yalak (went), the awapanayam (wheels) yalak (went) beside them; and when the chay (life) creatures were nashaa (lift) up from the aratz (Earth/land), the awapanayam (wheels) were nashaa (lift) up.

Wherever the rawach (spirit / wind) was to yalak (go), they yalak (went); there was the rawach (spirit / wind) to yalak (go): and the awapanayam (wheels) were nashaa (lift) up imah (beside) them; for the rawach (spirit / wind) of the chay (life) creature was in the awapanayam (wheels).

When those yalak (went), these yalak (went); and when those imad (stood), these imad (stood); and when those were nashaa (lift) up from the aratz (Earth/land), the awapanayam (wheels) were nashaa (lift) up imah (beside) them: for the rawach (spirit / wind) of the chay (life) creature was in the awapanayam (wheels).

Over the raash (head) of the chay (life) creature there was the damawath (likeness) of an expanse, like the awesome qarach (crystal) to look on, natah (stretched) forth over their raashay (heads) mail (top/above).

Under the expanse were their kanap (wings) yashar (upright), the ayashah (woman / wife) toward the other: ayash (man / husband) one had shanayam (two) which kasah (covered) on hanah (Behold) side, and ayash (man / husband) one had shanayam (two) which kasah (covered) on that hanah (Behold), their gawayah (corpse).

When they yalak (went), I shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of their kanap (wings) like the qawal (sound / voice) of rab (great) mayam (Waters), like the qawal (sound / voice) of the Shaday, a qawal (sound / voice) of hamalah (tumult) like the qawal (sound / voice) of an machanah (army): when they imad (stood), they rapah (let) down their kanap (wings).
There was a qawal (sound / voice) above the expanse that was over their raash (head): when they imad (stood), they rapah (let) down their kanap (wings).

Mail (top/above) the expanse that was over their raash (head) was the damawath (likeness) of a kasaa (throne), as the maraah (appearance) of a sapayar (sapphire) aban (stone); and on the damawath (likeness) of the kasaa (throne) was a damawath (likeness) as the maraah (appearance) of a adam (man) on it mail (top/above).

I raah (see) as it were glowing metal, as the maraah (appearance) of ash (fire) bayath (house) it all around, from the maraah (appearance) of his waist and upward; and from the maraah (appearance) of his waist and matah (downward) I raah (see) as it were the maraah (appearance) of ash (fire), and there was nagah (brightness) around him.

As the maraah (appearance) of the rainbow that is in the inan (cloud) in the yawam (day) of gasham (rain), so was the maraah (appearance) of the nagah (brightness) all around. This was the maraah (appearance) of the damawath (likeness) of the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah. When I raah (see) it, I napal (fall / be cast down) on my panayam (face), and I shamai (hearken / hear) a qawal (sound / voice) of one that dabar (word / matter).
He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), imad (stand) on your ragal (feet / foot), and I will dabar (word / matter) with you.
The rawach (spirit / wind) bawaa (come) into me when he dabar (word / matter) to me, and imad (set) me on my ragal (feet / foot); and I shamai (hearken / hear) him who dabar (word / matter) to me.

He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), I shalach (send) you to the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), to a gaway (heathen / nation) of mawaradayam (rebels) who have marad (rebelled) against me. They and their ab (father) have pashai (transgressed) against me even to this very yawam (day).
The banayam (children) are qashah (rough / hard) and chazaq (stiff-hearted): I am shalach (send) you to them; and you shall amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah.

They, whether they will shamai (hearken / hear), or whether they will chadal (forbear), (for they are a rebellious bayath (house)), yet shall yadai (know) that there has been a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) thawak (midst) them.

You, ban (son) of adam (man), don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of them, neither be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of their dabar (word / matter), though sarabayam (briers) and salawanayam (thorns) are with you, and you do yashab (inhabit/dwell) among iqarabayam (scorpions): don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of their dabar (word / matter), nor be chathath (dismayed) at their panayam (face), though they are a rebellious bayath (house).
You shall dabar (word / matter) my dabar (word / matter) to them, whether they will shamai (hearken / hear), or whether they will chadal (forbear); for they are most rebellious.

But you, ban (son) of adam (man), shamai (hearken / hear) what I dabar (word / matter) you; don't be rebellious like that rebellious bayath (house): patzah (open) your pah (mouth), and akal (eat) that which I nathan (give) you.
When I raah (see), behold, a yad (hand) was shalach (send) forth to me; and, behold, a scroll of a sapar (book / scribed document) was therein;
He parash (spread) it panayam (face) me: and it was kathab (write) within and achawar (without); and there were kathab (write) therein qanayam (lamentations), and hagah (mourning), and hay (exist).
He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), akal (eat) that which you matzaa (find). Akal (eat) this scroll, and yalak (go), dabar (word / matter) to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel).
So I pathach (opened) my pah (mouth), and he caused me to akal (eat) the scroll.

He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), cause your batan (belly) to akal (eat), and malaa (fill) your maih (bowels) with this scroll that I nathan (give) you. Then I akal (eat) it; and it was as mathawaq (sweet) as dabash (honey) in my pah (mouth).
He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), yalak (go) to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and dabar (word / matter) my dabar (word / matter) to them.
For you are not shalach (send) to a im (nation / people) of a imaq (strange) shapah (speech) and of a kabad (hard) lashawan (tongue / language), but to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel);

Not to many imayam (peoples) of a imaq (strange) shapah (speech) and of a kabad (hard) lashawan (tongue / language), whose dabar (word / matter) you can not shamai (hearken / hear). Surely, if I shalach (send) you to them, they would shamai (hearken / hear) to you.

But the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) abah (be willing / desire) not shamai (hearken / hear) to you; for they abah (be willing / desire) not shamai (hearken / hear) to me: for all the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) are obstinate and qashah (rough / hard).
Behold, I nathan (give) made your panayam (face) hard imah (against) their panayam (face), and your matzach (forehead) hard imah (against) their matzach (foreheads).

As an shamayar (adamant) chazaq (harder) than tzar (flint) nathan (give) I made your matzach (forehead): don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid) of them, neither be chathath (dismayed) at their panayam (face), though they are a rebellious bayath (house).

Moreover he amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), all my dabar (word / matter) that I shall dabar (word / matter) to you laqach (take / seize) in your labab (heart), and shamai (hearken / hear) with your azan (ear).

Yalak (go) to them of the gawalah (captivity), to the banay (children) of your im (nation / people), and dabar (word / matter) to them, and amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah; whether they will shamai (hearken / hear), or whether they will chadal (forbear).

Then the rawach (spirit / wind) nashaa (lift) me up, and I shamai (hearken / hear) achar (other) me the qawal (sound / voice) of a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) raish (rushing), saying, barak (blessed) be the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah from his maqawam (place).

I heard the qawal (sound / voice) of the kanapay (wings) of the chay (life) creatures as they nashaq (touched) ayashah (woman / wife) achawath (another), and the qawal (sound / voice) of the awapanayam (wheels) imah (beside) them, even the qawal (sound / voice) of a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) raish (rushing).

So the rawach (spirit / wind) nashaa (lift) me up, and laqach (take / seize) me away; and I yalak (went) in bitterness, in the chamah (heat) of my rawach (spirit / wind); and the yad (hand) of Yahawah was chazaq (strong) on me.

Then I bawaa (come) to them of the gawalah (captivity) at Thalaabayab (Tel Aviv), that lived by the nahar (river) Kabar (Chebar), and to where they lived; and I yashab (inhabit/dwell) there overwhelmed thawak (midst) them shabai (seven) yamayam (days).
It happened at the qatzah (end / extremity / border) of shabai (seven) yamayam (days), that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), I nathan (give) made you a tzapah (watchman / keep watch) to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel): therefore shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) from my pah (mouth), and give them zahar (warn) from me.

When I amar (spoke) the rashai (wicked), You shall mawath (death) mawath (death); and you give him no zahar (warn), nor dabar (word / matter) to zahar (warn) the rashai (wicked) from his rashai (wicked) darak (way), to chayah (save) his life; the same rashai (wicked) mawath (death) shall die in his iwan (guilt/iniquity); but his dam (blood) will I baqash (require) at your yad (hand).

Yet if you zahar (warn) the rashai (wicked), and he doesn't shawab (turn back / repent) from his rashai (wickedness), nor from his rashai (wicked) darak (way), he shall mawath (death) in his iwan (guilt/iniquity); but you have natzal (delivered) your napash (soul).

Again, when a tzadayaq (righteous) man does shawab (turn back / repent) from his tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and ishah (make) iwal (iniquity), and I nathan (give) a makashawal (stumbling) block panayam (face) him, he shall mawath (death): because you have not given him zahar (warn), he shall mawath (death) in his chataah (sin), and his tzadaqah (righteousness) deeds which he ishah (make) done shall not be zakar (remember); but his dam (blood) will I baqash (require) at your yad (hand).

Nevertheless if you zahar (warn) the tzadayaq (righteous) man, that the tzadayaq (righteous) not chataa (sin), and he does not chataa (sin), he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live), because he took zahar (warn); and you have natzal (delivered) your napash (soul).
The yad (hand) of Yahawah was there on me; and he amar (spoke) to me, qawam (rise up), yatzaa (go out / come out) forth into the baqaih (plain), and I will there dabar (word / matter) with you.

Then I qawam (rise up), and yatzaa (go out / come out) forth into the baqaih (plain): and behold, the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah imad (stood) there, as the kabawad (glory) which I raah (see) by the nahar (river) Kabar (Chebar); and I napal (fall / be cast down) on my panayam (face).

Then the rawach (spirit / wind) bawaa (come) into me, and imad (set) me on my ragal (feet / foot); and he dabar (word / matter) with me, and amar (spoke) to me, bawaa (come), sagar (shut) yourself inside your bayath (house).

But you, ban (son) of adam (man), behold, they shall nathan (give) ibawathayam (bands) on you, and shall asar (bind) you with them, and you shall not yatzaa (go out / come out) out thawak (midst) them:

And I will make your lashawan (tongue / language) dabaq (stick) to the roof of your chak (mouth), that you shall be mute, and shall not be to them a reprover; for they are a rebellious bayath (house).

But when I dabar (word / matter) with you, I will pathach (open) your pah (mouth), and you shall amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: He who shamai (hearken / hear), shamai (hearken / hear) him hear; and he who chadal (forbears), chadal (let) him forbear: for they are a rebellious bayath (house).
You also, ban (son) of adam (man), laqach (take / seize) a labanah (tile), and nathan (give) it panayam (face) yourself, and portray on it a iyar (city), even Yarawashalam (Jerusalem):

And nathan (give) matzawar (siege) against it, and banah (build) dayaq (forts) against it, and shapak (cast) up a mound against it; nathan (give) machanawath (camps) also against it, and plant battering karayam (rams) against it all around.

Laqach (take / seize) for yourself an barazal (iron) machabath (pan), and nathan (give) it for a qayar (wall) of barazal (iron) between you and the iyar (city): and kawan (set) your panayam (face) toward it, and it shall be matzawar (besieged), and you shall tzawar (lay) siege against it. This shall be a awath (sign / mark / miracle) to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Moreover shakab (lie) on your shamaalay (left) tzad (side), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) on it; according to the masapar (number) of the yamayam (days) that you shall shakab (lie) on it, you shall nashaa (lift) their iwan (guilt/iniquity).

For I nathan (give) appointed the shanay (years) of their iwan (guilt/iniquity) to be to you a masapar (number) of yamayam (days), even shalawash (three) maah (hundred) thashaiyam (ninety) yamayam (days): so you shall nashaa (lift) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Again, when you kalah (complete / finish) accomplished these, you shall shakab (lie) on your yamayanay (right) tzad (side), and shall nashaa (lift) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah): arabaiyam (forty) yawam (day), each yawam (day) for a shanah (year), nathan (give) I appointed it to you.
You shall kawan (set) your panayam (face) toward the matzawar (siege) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), with your zarawai (arm) chashap (uncovered); and you shall nabaa (prophesy) against it.

Behold, I nathan (give) ibawathayam (bands) on you, and you shall not hapak (turn) you from one tzad (side) to the other, until you kalah (complete / finish) accomplished the yamay (days) of your matzawar (siege).

Laqach (take / seize) for yourself also chatah (wheat), and shairah (barley), and pawal (beans), and lentils, and dachan (millet), and spelt, and nathan (give) them in achad (one) kalay (vessel), and ishah (make) lacham (bread) of it; according to the masapar (number) of the yamayam (days) that you shall shakab (lie) on your tzad (side), even shalawash (three) maah (hundred) thashaiyam (ninety) yamayam (days), you shall akal (eat) of it.
Your maakal (food) which you shall akal (eat) shall be by mashaqawal (weight), isharayam (twenty) shaqal (shekels) a yawam (day): from ith (time) to ith (time) you shall akal (eat) it.
You shall shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters) by mashawarah (measure), the shashay (sixth) part of a hayan (hin): from ith (time) to ith (time) you shall shathah (drinks).
You shall akal (eat) it as shairah (barley) igah (cakes), and you shall iwag (bake) it in their iyan (eye) with galal (dung) that comes out of adam (man).
Yahawah amar (spoke), Even thus shall the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) akal (eat) their lacham (bread) tamaa (unclean), among the gawayam (nations) where I will nadach (drive) them.

Then I amar (spoke), ahah (ah) Adanay Yahawah! Behold, my napash (soul) has not been tamaa (polluted); for from my naiwar (youth) up even until now have I not akal (eat) of that which dies of nabalah (itself), or is tarapah (torn) of animals; neither bawaa (come) there pagawal (abominable) bashar (flesh) into my pah (mouth).
Then he amar (spoke) to me, raah (see), I nathan (give) given you baqar (morning) tzapawai (dung) for adam (man's) galal (dung), and you shall ishah (make) your lacham (bread) thereon.

Moreover he amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), behold, I will shabar (break) the matah (staff / rod / tribe) of lacham (bread) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem): and they shall akal (eat) lacham (bread) by mashaqal (weight), and with fearfulness; and they shall shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters) by mashawarah (measure), and in shamamawan (dismay):
That they may chasar (want) lacham (bread) and mayam (Waters), and be dismayed ayash (man / husband) with ach (brother/kinsman), and maqaq (pine) away in their iwan (guilt/iniquity).

You, ban (son) of adam (man), laqach (take / seize) a chad (sharp) charab (sword); You shall laqach (take / seize) it as a galabayam (barbers) thair (razor) to you, and shall ibar (pass over/through) it to pass on your raash (head) and on your zaqan (beard): then laqach (take / seize) maazanay (balances) to weigh, and chalaq (divide) the hair.

A shalayashay (third) part you shall bair (burn) in the awar (light) in the thawak (midst) of the iyar (city), when the yamay (days) of the matzawar (siege) are malaa (fulfilled); and you shall laqach (take / seize) a shalayashay (third) part, and nakah (strike) with the charab (sword) around it; and a shalayashay (third) part you shall zarah (scatter) to the rawach (spirit / wind), and I will rawaq (draw) out a charab (sword) achar (other) them.
You shall laqach (take / seize) of it a mait (few) in masapar (number), and tzawar (bind) them in your kanap (skirts).

Of these again you shall take, and shalak (cast) them into the thawak (midst) of the ash (fire), and sharap (burn) them in the ash (fire); from it shall a ash (fire) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth into all the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: This is Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) her in the thawak (midst) of the gawayam (nations), and aratzawath (countries) are around her.

She has marah (rebelled) against my mashapat (ordinances) in doing rashaih (wickedness) more than the gawayam (nations), and against my chaqah (statutes) more than the aratzawath (countries) that are around her; for they have maas (rejected) my mashapat (ordinances), and as for my chaqah (statutes), they have not halak (move) in them.

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you are turbulent more than the gawayam (nations) that are around you, and have not halak (move) in my chaqah (statutes), neither ishah (make) kept my mashapatay (ordinances), neither ishah (make) done after the mashapatay (ordinances) of the gawayam (nations) that are around you;

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I, even I, am against you; and I will ishah (make) mashapatayam (judgments) in the thawak (midst) of you in the iyan (eye) of the gawayam (nations).
I will ishah (make) in you that which I ishah (make) not done, and whereunto I will not ishah (make) any more the like, yain (because) of all your thawaibah (abominations).

Therefore the abawath (fathers) shall akal (eat) the banayam (sons) in the thawak (midst) of you, and the banayam (sons) shall akal (eat) their abawath (fathers); and I will ishah (make) shapatayam (judgments) on you; and the whole shaarayath (remnant) of you will I zarah (scatter) to all the rawach (spirit / wind).

Therefore, as I chay (life), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, surely, because you have tamaa (defiled) my maqadash (sanctuary) with all your shaqawatz (detestable) things, and with all your thawaibah (abominations), therefore will I also garai (diminish) you; neither shall my iyan (eye) chawas (spare), and I also will chamal (have) no pity.

A shalayashay (third) part of you shall mawath (death) with the dabar (word / matter), and with raib (famine) shall they be kalah (complete / finish) in the thawak (midst) of you; and a shalayashay (third) part shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword) around you; and a shalayashay (third) part I will zarah (scatter) to all the rawach (spirit / wind), and will rawaq (draw) out a charab (sword) achar (other) them.

Thus shall my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) be kalah (complete / finish), and I will cause my chamah (wrath) toward them to nawach (rest), and I shall be nacham (turn away / repent); and they shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) in my qanaah (zeal), when I kalah (complete / finish) accomplished my chamah (wrath) on them.
Moreover I will nathan (give) you a desolation and a charapah (reproach) among the gawayam (nations) that are around you, in the iyan (eye) of ibar (pass over/through) that pass by.

So it shall be a charapah (reproach) and a gadawapah (taunt), an mawasar (instruction) and an mashamah (astonishment), to the gawayam (nations) that are around you, when I shall ishah (make) shapatayam (judgments) on you in ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) and in chamah (wrath), and in chamah (wrathful) thakachawath (rebukes); (I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it;)

When I shall shalach (send) on them the rai (evil) chatzay (arrows) of raib (famine), that are for mashachayath (destruction), which I will shalach (send) to shachath (destroy) you: and I will yasap (increase) the raib (famine) on you, and will shabar (break) your matah (staff / rod / tribe) of lacham (bread);

And I will shalach (send) on you raib (famine) and rai (evil) animals, and they shall shakal (bereave) you; and dabar (word / matter) and dam (blood) shall ibar (pass over/through) through you; and I will bawaa (come) the charab (sword) on you: I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) toward the haray (mountains) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and nabaa (prophesy) to them,

And amar (spoke), You haray (mountains) of Yashar-Al (Israel), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of the Adanay Yahawah: Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah to the haray (mountains) and to the gabaiwath (hills), to the watercourses and to the gaayath (valleys): Behold, I, even I, will bawaa (come) a charab (sword) on you, and I will abad (destroy / perish) your bamah (high) places.

Your mazabach (altars) shall become shamam (desolate), and your incense mazabach (altars) shall be shabar (broken); and I will napal (fall / be cast down) down your chalal (slain) men panayam (face) your galawal (idols).

I will nathan (give) the pagar (dead) bodies of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) panayam (face) their galawal (idols); and I will zarah (scatter) your itzam (bones) around your mazabach (altars).

In all your mawashab (dwelling) places the irayam (cities) shall be charab (laid) waste, and the bamah (high) places shall be yasham (desolate); that your mazabach (altars) may be charab (laid) waste and asham (made) desolate, and your galawal (idols) may be shabar (broken) and shabath (shabath / rest), and your incense chaman (altars) may be gadai (cut) down, and your maishah (works) may be machah (abolished).
The chalal (slain) shall napal (fall / be cast down) in the thawak (midst) of you, and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Yet will I yathar (leave) a remnant, in that you shall have some that palayat (escape) the charab (sword) among the gawayam (nations), when you shall be zarah (scattered) through the aratzawath (countries).

Those of you that palayat (escape) shall zakar (remember) me among the gawayam (nations) where they shall be shabah (carried) captive, how that I have been shabar (broken) with their lewd lab (heart), which has sawar (departed) from me, and with their iyan (eye), which zanah (play) the prostitute achar (other) their galawal (idols): and they shall qawat (loathe) panayam (face) in their own sight for the raiwath (evils) which they ishah (make) committed in all their thawaibah (abominations).
They shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah: I have not dabar (word / matter) in chanam (vain) that I would ishah (make) this rai (evil) to them.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: nakah (strike) with your kap (hand), and raqai (stamp) with your ragal (feet / foot), and amar (spoke), ach (brother/kinsman)! Because of all the rai (evil) thawaibawath (abominations) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel); for they shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword), by the raib (famine), and by the dabar (word / matter).

He who is rachawaq (far) off shall mawath (death) of the dabar (word / matter); and he who is qarawab (near) shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword); and he who shaar (remains) and is natzar (besieged) shall mawath (death) by the raib (famine): thus will I kalah (complete / finish) my chamah (wrath) on them.

You shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when their chalal (slain) men shall be thawak (midst) their galawal (idols) around their mazabach (altars), on every rawam (will lift up) gabaih (hill), on all the raashay (tops) of the harayam (mountains), and under every rainan (green) itz (tree), and under every ibath (thick) alah (oak / terebinth), the maqawam (place) where they nathan (give) pleasant aroma to all their galawal (idols).

I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on them, and nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) shamamah (desolate) and waste, from the madabar (wilderness) toward Dabalah (Diblah), throughout all their habitations: and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Moreover the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

You, ban (son) of adam (man), thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah to the adamah (land) of Yashar-Al (Israel), An qatz (end): the qatz (end) bawaa (come) come on the arabai (four) kanapawath (corners) of the aratz (Earth/land).

Now is the qatz (end) on you, and I will shalach (send) my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) on you, and will shapat (judge / judgement) you according to your darak (ways); and I will nathan (give) on you all your thawaibah (abominations).

My iyan (eye) shall not chawas (spare) you, neither will I chamal (have) pity; but I will nathan (give) your darak (ways) on you, and your thawaibah (abominations) shall be in the thawak (midst) of you: and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: An rai (evil), an only rai (evil); behold, it bawaa (come).
An qatz (end) bawaa (come) come, the qatz (end) bawaa (come) come; it qawatz (awakes) bawaa (come) you; behold, it comes.

Your doom bawaa (come) come to you, yashab (inhabit/dwell) of the aratz (Earth/land): the ith (time) bawaa (come) come, the yawam (day) is qarawab (near), a day of mahawamah (tumult), and not of joyful shouting, on the harayam (mountains).

Now will I qarawab (shortly) shapak (pour) out my chamah (wrath) on you, and kalah (complete / finish) my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) against you, and will shapat (judge / judgement) you according to your darak (ways); and I will nathan (give) on you all your thawaibah (abominations).

My iyan (eye) shall not chawas (spare), neither will I chamal (have) pity: I will nathan (give) on you according to your darak (ways); and your thawaibah (abominations) shall be in the thawak (midst) of you; and you shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, do nakah (strike).
Behold, the yawam (day), behold, it bawaa (come): your doom is yatzaa (go out / come out) forth; the matah (staff / rod / tribe) has tzawatz (blossomed), zadawan (pride) has parach (budded).

Chamas (violence) has qawam (rise up) up into a matah (staff / rod / tribe) of rashai (wickedness). None of them shall remain, nor of their hamawan (multitude), nor of their wealth. There shall be nothing of value among them.

The ith (time) bawaa (come) come, the yawam (day) nagai (draws) near: don't let the qanah (buyer) shamach (rejoice), nor the seller abal (mourn); for charawan (wrath) is on all its hamawan (multitude).

For the seller shall not shawab (turn back / repent) to that which is mamakar (sold), although they be yet chay (life): for the chazawan (vision) is touching the whole hamawan (multitude) of it, none shall shawab (turn back / repent); neither shall any chazaq (strengthen) himself in the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of his chay (life).

They have thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the thaqawai (trumpet), and have kawan (made) all ready; but none halak (move) to the malachamah (battle); for my charawan (wrath) is on all its hamawan (multitude).

The charab (sword) is outside, and the dabar (word / matter) and the raib (famine) bayath (house): he who is in the shadah (field) shall mawath (death) with the charab (sword): and he who is in the iyar (city), raib (famine) and dabar (word / matter) shall akal (eat) him.

But those of those who palat (escape) shall palayat (escape), and shall be on the harayam (mountains) like yawanay (doves) of the gaayawath (valleys), all of them moaning, ayash (man / husband) one in his iwan (guilt/iniquity).
All yadayam (hands) shall be rapah (feeble), and all barakayam (knees) shall be yalak (weak) as mayam (Waters).

They shall also clothe themselves with sackcloth, and palatzawath (horror) shall kasah (cover) them; and bawashah (shame) shall be on all panayam (face), and qarachah (baldness) on all their raash (head).

They shall shalak (cast) their kasap (silver) in the chawatzawath (streets), and their zahab (gold) shall be as an nadah (unclean) thing; their kasap (silver) and their zahab (gold) shall not be yakal (able) to natzal (deliver) them in the yawam (day) of the ibarah (wrath) of Yahawah: they shall not shabai (satisfy) their napash (soul), neither malaa (fill) their maih (bowels); because it has been the makashawal (stumbling) block of their iwan (guilt/iniquity).

As for the beauty of his iday (ornament / adornment), he shawam (place / establish / appoint) it in gaawan (majesty); but they ishah (make) the tzalamay (images) of their thawaibah (abominations) and their shaqawatz (detestable) things therein: therefore nathan (give) I made it to them as an nadah (unclean) thing.
I will nathan (give) it into the yad (hand) of the strangers for a baz (prey), and to the rashai (wicked) of the aratz (Earth/land) for a shalal (spoil); and they shall chalal (profane) it.
My panayam (face) will I sabab (turn) also from them, and they shall chalal (profane) my tzapan (secret) place; and parayatzayam (robbers) shall bawaa (come) into it, and chalal (profane) it.
Ishah (make) the rathawaq (chain); for the aratz (Earth/land) is malaa (full) of bloody mashapat (crimes), and the iyar (city) is malaa (full) of chamas (violence).

Therefore I will bawaa (come) the rai (worst) of the gawayam (nations), and they shall yarash (possess) their bayath (house): I will also make the gaawan (pride) of the iz (strong) to shabath (shabath / rest); and their qadash (set apart / make holy) places shall be chalal (profaned).
Qapadah (destruction) bawaa (come); and they shall baqash (seek) shalawam (peace / safety), and there shall be none.

Hawah (calamity / destruction) shall bawaa (come) on hawah (calamity / destruction), and shamawaih (rumor) shall be on shamawaih (rumor); and they shall baqash (seek) a chazawan (vision) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy); but the thawarah (instruction) shall abad (destroy / perish) from the kahan (priest), and itzah (counsel) from the zaqanayam (elders).

The malak (king) shall abal (mourn), and the nashayaa (prince) shall be labash (clothed) with shamamah (desolation), and the yaday (hands) of the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land) shall be bahal (troubled): I will ishah (make) to them after their darak (way), and according to their own mashapat (judgments) will I shapat (judge / judgement) them; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

It happened in the shashay (sixth) shanah (year), in the shashay (sixth) month, in the chamash (fifth) day of the chadash (month), as I yashab (inhabit/dwell) in my bayath (house), and the zaqanay (elders) of Yahawadah (Judah) yashab (inhabit/dwell) panayam (face) me, that the yad (hand) of the Adanay Yahawah napal (fall / be cast down) there on me.

Then I raah (see), and behold, a damawath (likeness) as the maraah (appearance) of ash (fire); from the maraah (appearance) of his waist and matah (downward), ash (fire); and from his waist and upward, as the maraah (appearance) of zahar (brightness), as it were glowing metal.

He shalach (send) forth the thabanayath (form) of a yad (hand), and laqach (take / seize) me by a tzayatzath (lock) of my raash (head); and the rawach (spirit / wind) nashaa (lift) me up between aratz (Earth/land) and the sky, and bawaa (come) me in the maraawath (visions) of Alahayam to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), to the pathach (door) of the shair (gate) of the inner court that panah (turn) toward the tzapawan (north); where there was the mawashab (seat) of the samal (image) of qanaah (jealousy), which qanah (provokes) to jealousy.
Behold, the kabawad (glory) of the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel) was there, according to the maraah (appearance) that I raah (see) in the baqaih (plain).

Then he amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye) now the darak (way) toward the tzapawan (north). So I nashaa (lift) up my iyan (eye) the darak (way) toward the tzapawan (north), and see, northward of the shair (gate) of the mazabach (altar) this samal (image) of qanaah (jealousy) in the baah (entry).

He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), do you raah (see) what they ishah (make)? Even the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thawaibawath (abominations) that the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ishah (make) commit here, that I should rachaq (go) far off from my maqadash (sanctuary)? But you shall again raah (see) yet other gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thawaibawath (abominations).
He bawaa (come) me to the pathach (door) of the chatzar (court); and when I raah (see), behold, a chawar (hole) in the qayar (wall).
Then he amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), chathar (dig) now in the qayar (wall): and when I had chathar (dug) in the qayar (wall), behold, a pathach (door).
He amar (spoke) to me, bawaa (come) in, and raah (see) the rai (wicked) thawaibawath (abominations) that they ishah (make) here.

So I bawaa (come) in and raah (see); and see, every thabanayath (form) of ramash (creeping) things, and shaqatz (abominable) animals, and all the galawalay (idols) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), chaqah (portrayed) around on the qayar (wall).

There imad (stood) panayam (face) them shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (man / husband) of the zaqanay (elders) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel); and in their thawak (midst) imad (stood) Yaazanayah (Jaazaniah) the ban (son) of Shapan (Shaphan), every ayash (man / husband) with his maqatarath (censer) in his yad (hand); and the odor of the inan (cloud) of qatarath (incense) ilah (go up / offer) up.

Then he amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), raah (see) you seen what the zaqanay (elders) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) ishah (make) in the chashak (darkness), every ayash (man / husband) in his rooms of mashakayath (idol / carved image)? For they amar (spoke), Yahawah doesn't raah (see) us; Yahawah has forsaken the aratz (Earth/land).
He amar (spoke) also to me, You shall again raah (see) yet other gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thawaibawath (abominations) which they ishah (make).

Then he bawaa (come) me to the pathach (door) of the shair (gate) of Yahawah bayath (house) which was toward the tzapawan (north); and see, there yashab (inhabit/dwell) the nashayam (women) bakah (weeping) for Thamawaz (Tammuz).
Then he amar (spoke) to me, raah (see) you seen this, ban (son) of adam (man)? You shall again raah (see) yet greater thawaibawath (abominations) than these.

He bawaa (come) me into the inner chatzar (court) of Yahawah bayath (house); and see, at the pathach (door) of the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, between the awalam (porch) and the mazabach (altar), were about isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) ayash (man / husband), with their achawar (backs) toward the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, and their panayam (face) toward the qadam (east); and they were shachah (worshipping) the shamash (sun) toward the qadam (east).

Then he amar (spoke) to me, raah (see) you seen this, ban (son) of adam (man)? Is it a qalal (light) thing to the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) that they ishah (make) the thawaibawath (abominations) which they ishah (make) here? For they malaa (have) filled the aratz (Earth/land) with chamas (violence), and have shawab (turn back / repent) again to provoke me to kais (anger): and behold, they shalach (send) the zamawarah (branch) to their ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).

Therefore will I also ishah (make) in chamah (wrath); my iyan (eye) shall not chawas (spare), neither will I chamal (have) pity; and though they qaraa (called) in my azan (ear) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice), yet will I not shamai (hearken / hear) them.

Then he qaraa (called) in my azan (ear) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice), amar (spoke), Cause those who are in paqadah (charge) of the iyar (city) to qarab (come close) near, every ayash (man / husband) with his mashachath (destroying) kalay (weapon) in his yad (hand).

Behold, shash (six) anashayam (men) bawaa (come) from the darak (way) of the ilayawan (Ilayawan) shair (gate), which panah (turn) toward the tzapawan (north), every ayash (man / husband) with his mapatz (slaughter) kalay (weapon) in his yad (hand); and achad (one) ayash (man / husband) in their thawak (midst) labash (clothed) in bad (linen), with a sapar (book) qasath (inkhorn) by his mathan (side). They bawaa (come) in, and imad (stood) beside the bronze mazabach (altar).

The kabawad (glory) of the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel) was ilah (go up / offer) up from the karawab (cherub), whereupon it was, to the mapathan (threshold) of the bayath (house): and he qaraa (called) to the ayash (man / husband) labash (clothed) in bad (linen), who had the sapar (book) qasath (inkhorn) by his mathan (side).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, ibar (pass over/through) through the thawak (midst) of the iyar (city), thawak (midst) the midst of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and thawah (set) a thaw (mark) on the matzachawath (foreheads) of the ibar (pass over/through) that anach (sigh) and that anaq (cry) over all the thawaibawath (abominations) that are ishah (make) in its thawak (midst).

To the others he amar (spoke) in my azan (ear), ibar (pass over/through) through the iyar (city) achar (other) him, and nakah (strike): don't let your iyan (eye) chawas (spare), neither chamal (have) pity;

Harag (kill) mashachayath (utterly) the zaqan (old) man, the bachawar (young) man and the bathawalah (virgin), and little tap (children) and nashayam (women); but don't nagash (come) near any ayash (man / husband) on whom is the thaw (mark): and chalal (begin) at my maqadash (sanctuary). Then they chalal (began) at the zaqan (old) zaqanayam (men) that were panayam (face) the bayath (house).

He amar (spoke) to them, tamaa (defile) the bayath (house), and malaa (fill) the chatzarawath (courts) with the chalal (slain). Yatzaa (go out / come out) forth! They yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and nakah (struck) in the iyar (city).

It happened, while they were nakah (smiting), and I was shaar (left), that I napal (fall / be cast down) on my panayam (face), and zaiq (cried), and amar (spoke), ahah (ah) Adanay Yahawah! Will you shachath (destroy) all the shaarayath (residue) of Yashar-Al (Israel) in your shapak (pouring) out of your chamah (wrath) on Yarawashalam (Jerusalem)?

Then he amar (spoke) to me, The iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah) is maad (exceedingly) gadawal (very great/important/mighty), and the aratz (Earth/land) is malaa (full) of dam (blood), and the iyar (city) malaa (full) of perversion: for they amar (spoke), Yahawah has forsaken the aratz (Earth/land), and Yahawah doesn't raah (see).
As for me also, my iyan (eye) shall not chawas (spare), neither will I chamal (have) pity, but I will nathan (give) their darak (way) on their raash (head).

Behold, the ayash (man / husband) labawash (clothed) in bad (linen), who had the qasath (inkhorn) by his mathan (side), reported the dabar (word / matter), amar (spoke), I ishah (make) done as you have tzawah (commanded) me.

Then I raah (see), and see, in the expanse that was over the raash (head) of the karawab (cherubim) there raah (see) above them as it were a sapayar (sapphire) aban (stone), as the maraah (appearance) of the damawath (likeness) of a kasaa (throne).

He amar (spoke) to the ayash (man / husband) labash (clothed) in bad (linen), and amar (spoke), bawaa (come) in bayan (between) the whirling galagal (wheels), even under the karawab (cherub), and malaa (fill) both your chapan (hands) with gachalay (coals) of ash (fire) from bayan (between) the karawab (cherubim), and zaraq (scatter) them over the iyar (city). He bawaa (come) in as I watched.

Now the karawab (cherubim) imad (stood) on the yamayan (right hand) side of the bayath (house), when the ayash (man / husband) bawaa (come) in; and the inan (cloud) malaa (filled) the inner chatzar (court).

The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah rawam (will lift up) up from the karawab (cherub), and stood over the mapathan (threshold) of the bayath (house); and the bayath (house) was malaa (filled) with the inan (cloud), and the chatzar (court) was malaa (full) of the nagah (brightness) of Yahawah kabawad (glory).

The qawal (sound / voice) of the kanapay (wings) of the karawab (cherubim) was shamai (hearken / hear) even to the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court), as the qawal (sound / voice) of Al Shaday when he dabar (word / matter).

It came to pass, when he tzawah (commanded) the ayash (man / husband) labash (clothed) in bad (linen), amar (spoke), laqach (take / seize) ash (fire) from between the whirling galagal (wheels), from between the karawab (cherubim), that he bawaa (come) in, and imad (stood) beside a awapan (wheel).

The karawab (cherub) shalach (send) forth his yad (hand) from between the karawab (cherubim) to the ash (fire) that was between the karawab (cherubim), and nashaa (lift) of it, and nathan (give) it into the chapanay (hands) of him who was labash (clothed) in bad (linen), who laqach (take / seize) it and yatzaa (go out / come out) out.
There raah (see) in the karawab (cherubim) the thabanayath (form) of a adam (man's) yad (hand) under their kanap (wings).

I raah (see), and behold, arabai (four) awapanayam (wheels) beside the karawab (cherubim), achad (one) awapan (wheel) beside achad (one) karawab (cherub), and another awapan (wheel) beside another karawab (cherub); and the maraah (appearance) of the awapanayam (wheels) was like a tharashayash (beryl) aban (stone).
As for their maraah (appearance), the arabai (four) of them had achad (one) damawath (likeness), like a awapan (wheel) thawak (midst) a awapan (wheel).

When they yalak (went), they yalak (went) in their arabai (four) directions: they didn't sabab (turn) as they yalak (went), but to the maqawam (place) where the raash (head) panah (turn) they yalak (followed) it; they didn't sabab (turn) as they yalak (went).

Their whole bashar (flesh), and their gab (backs), and their yad (hand), and their kanap (wings), and the awapanayam (wheels), were malaa (full) of iyanayam (eyes) all around, even the awapanayam (wheels) that the arabai (four) of them had.
As for the awapanayam (wheels), they were qaraa (called) in my azan (ear), the whirling galagal (wheels).

Achad (one) one had arabai (four) panay (faces): the achad (one) panayam (face) was the panayam (face) of the karawab (cherub), and the shanay (second) panayam (face) was the panayam (face) of a adam (man), and the shalayashay (third) panayam (face) the face of a aray (lion), and the rabayaiy (fourth) the panayam (face) of an nashar (eagle).
The karawab (cherubim) ramam (mounted) up: this is the chay (life) creature that I raah (see) by the nahar (river) Kabar (Chebar).

When the karawab (cherubim) yalak (went), the awapanayam (wheels) yalak (went) beside them; and when the karawab (cherubim) nashaa (lift) up their kanap (wings) to rawam (will lift up) up from the aratz (Earth/land), the awapanayam (wheels) also didn't sabab (turn) from beside them.
When they imad (stood), these imad (stood); and when they rawam (will lift up) up, these ramam (mounted) up with them: for the rawach (spirit / wind) of the chay (life) creature was in them.
The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from over the mapathan (threshold) of the bayath (house), and imad (stood) over the karawab (cherubim).

The karawab (cherubim) nashaa (lift) up their kanap (wings), and ramam (mounted) up from the aratz (Earth/land) in my iyan (eye) when they yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and the awapanayam (wheels) imah (beside) them: and they imad (stood) at the pathach (door) of the qadamawanay (east) shair (gate) of Yahawah bayath (house); and the kabawad (glory) of the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel) was over them mail (top/above).
This is the chay (life) creature that I raah (see) under the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel) by the nahar (river) Kabar (Chebar); and I yadai (knew) that they were karawab (cherubim).

Achad (one) one had arabai (four) panayam (face), and achad (one) one arabai (four) kanapayam (wings); and the damawath (likeness) of the yaday (hands) of a adam (man) was under their kanapayam (wings).

As for the damawath (likeness) of their panayam (face), they were the panayam (face) which I raah (see) by the nahar (river) Kabar (Chebar), their maraah (appearances) and themselves; they yalak (went) ayash (man / husband) one ibar (straight) forward.

Moreover the rawach (spirit / wind) nashaa (lift) me up, and bawaa (come) me to the qadamawanay (east) shair (gate) of Yahawah bayath (house), which panah (turn) eastward: and see, at the pathach (door) of the shair (gate) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) ayash (man / husband); and I raah (see) in their thawak (midst) Yaazanayah (Jaazaniah) the ban (son) of Izawar (Azzur), and Palatayah (Pelatiah) the ban (son) of Banayah (Benaiah), sharay (princes) of the im (nation / people).
He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), these are the ban (son) who chashab (devise) awan (iniquity), and who yaitz (give) rai (wicked) itzah (counsel) in this iyar (city);
Who amar (spoke), The time is not qarawab (near) to banah (build) bathayam (houses): this is the sayar (caldron), and we are the meat.
Therefore nabaa (prophesy) against them, nabaa (prophesy), ban (son) of adam (man).

The rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah napal (fall / be cast down) on me, and he amar (spoke) to me, amar (spoke), Thus amaratham (says) Yahawah: Thus you have amar (spoke), bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel); for I yadai (know) the things that mailah (ascent/climbing up) into your rawach (spirit / wind).
You rabah (have) multiplied your chalal (slain) in this iyar (city), and you malaa (have) filled its chawatz (streets) with the chalal (slain).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Your chalal (slain) whom you have shawam (place / establish / appoint) in its thawak (midst), they are the meat, and this is the sayar (caldron); but you shall be yatzaa (go out / come out) out of its thawak (midst).
You have yaraa (fear / be afraid) the charab (sword); and I will bawaa (come) the charab (sword) on you, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
I will yatzaa (go out / come out) you forth out of its thawak (midst), and nathan (give) you into the yad (hand) of strangers, and will ishah (make) shapatayam (judgments) among you.

You shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword); I will shapat (judge / judgement) you in the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yashar-Al (Israel); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
This shall not be your sayar (caldron), neither shall you be the meat in its thawak (midst); I will shapat (judge / judgement) you in the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yashar-Al (Israel);

And you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah: for you have not halak (move) in my chaq (statute), neither ishah (make) you executed my mashapatay (ordinances), but ishah (make) done after the mashapatay (ordinances) of the gawayam (nations) that are around you.

It happened, when I nabaa (prophesied), that Palatayah (Pelatiah) the ban (son) of Banayah (Benaiah) mawath (death). Then napal (fall / be cast down) I down on my panayam (face), and zaiq (cried) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qawal (sound / voice), and amar (spoke), ahah (ah) Adanay Yahawah! Will you ishah (make) a kalah (complete / finish) end of the shaarayath (remnant) of Yashar-Al (Israel)?
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), your ach (brother/kinsman), even your ach (brother/kinsman), the ban (son) of your relatives, and all the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), all of them, to whom the yashabay (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) have amar (spoke), rachaq (go) far away from Yahawah. This aratz (Earth/land) nathan (give) been given to us for a mawarashah (possession).

Therefore amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Whereas I have rachaq (removed) them far off among the gawayam (nations), and whereas I have pawatz (scattered) them among the aratzawath (countries), yet will I be to them a maqadash (sanctuary) for a mait (little) while in the aratzawath (countries) where they bawaa (come) come.

Therefore amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will qabatz (gather) you from the imayam (peoples), and asap (assemble) you out of the aratzawath (countries) where you have been pawatz (scattered), and I will nathan (give) you the adamah (land) of Yashar-Al (Israel).
They shall bawaa (come) there, and they shall sawar (take) away all the shaqawatz (detestable) things of it and all its thawaibah (abominations) from there.

I will nathan (give) them achad (one) lab (heart), and I will nathan (give) a chadash (new) rawach (spirit / wind) qarab (among / near) you; and I will sawar (take) the aban (stone) lab (heart) out of their bashar (flesh), and will nathan (give) them a lab (heart) of bashar (flesh);
That they may yalak (walk) in my chaqah (statutes), and shamar (keep/guard) my mashapat (ordinances), and ishah (make) them: and they shall be my im (nation / people), and I will be their Alahayam.

But as for them whose lab (heart) halak (move) after the lab (heart) of their shaqawatz (detestable) things and their thawaibah (abominations), I will nathan (give) their darak (way) on their own raash (head), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

Then the karawab (cherubim) nashaa (lift) up their kanap (wings), and the awapanayam (wheels) were imah (beside) them; and the kabawad (glory) of the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel) was over them mail (top/above).
The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah ilah (go up / offer) up from the thawak (midst) of the iyar (city), and imad (stood) on the har (mountain) which is on the qadam (east) side of the iyar (city).

The rawach (spirit / wind) nashaa (lift) me up, and bawaa (come) me in the maraah (vision) by the rawach (spirit / wind) of Alahayam into Kashaday (Chaldea), to them of the gawalah (captivity). So the maraah (vision) that I raah (see) seen ilah (go up / offer) up from me.
Then I dabar (word / matter) to them of the gawalah (captivity) all the things that Yahawah raah (see) shown me.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah also came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), you yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the thawak (midst) of the rebellious bayath (house), who have iyanayam (eyes) to raah (see), and don't raah (see), who have azanayam (ears) to shamai (hearken / hear), and don't shamai (hearken / hear); for they are a rebellious bayath (house).

Therefore, you ban (son) of adam (man), ishah (make) your kalay (stuff) for moving, and move by yawamam (by day) in their iyan (eye); and you shall move from your maqawam (place) to achar (other) maqawam (place) in their iyan (eye): it may be they will raah (see), though they are a rebellious bayath (house).

You shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth your kalay (stuff) by yawamam (by day) in their iyan (eye), as kalay (stuff) for moving; and you shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth yourself at even in their iyan (eye), as when men mawatzaa (go) forth into exile.
Chathar (dig) through the qayar (wall) in their iyan (eye), and yatzaa (go out / come out) your stuff out that way.

In their iyan (eye) you shall nashaa (lift) it on your kathap (shoulder), and yatzaa (go out / come out) it forth in the ilatah (dark); you shall kasah (cover) your panayam (face), so that you don't raah (see) the aratz (Earth/land): for I nathan (give) set you for a mawapath (sign) to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

I ishah (make) so as I was tzawah (commanded): I yatzaa (go out / come out) forth my kalay (stuff) by yawamam (by day), as kalay (stuff) for gawalah (removing), and in the even I chathar (dug) through the qayar (wall) with my yad (hand); I yatzaa (go out / come out) it forth in the ilatah (dark), and nashaa (lift) it on my kathap (shoulder) in their iyan (eye).
In the baqar (morning) came the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), has not the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), the rebellious bayath (house), amar (spoke) to you, What are you ishah (make)?

Amar (spoke) to them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: This mashaa (burden) concerns the nashayaa (prince) in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and all the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) thawak (midst) whom they are.
Amar (spoke), I am your mawapath (sign): like as I ishah (make) done, so shall it be ishah (make) to them; they shall yalak (go) into exile, into shabay (captivity).

The nashayaa (prince) who is thawak (midst) them shall nashaa (lift) on his kathap (shoulder) in the ilatah (dark), and shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth: they shall chathar (dig) through the qayar (wall) to yatzaa (go out / come out) out thereby: he shall kasah (cover) his panayam (face), yain (because) he shall not raah (see) the aratz (Earth/land) with his iyan (eye).

My rashath (net) also will I parash (spread) on him, and he shall be thapash (taken) in my matzawad (snare); and I will bawaa (come) him to Babal (Babylon) to the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans); yet shall he not raah (see) it, though he shall mawath (death) there.
I will zarah (scatter) toward every rawach (spirit / wind) all who are around him to izar (help) him, and all his agap (bands); and I will rawaq (draw) out the charab (sword) achar (other) them.
They shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shall zarah (disperse) them among the gawayam (nations), and pawatz (scatter) them through the aratzawath (countries).

But I will yathar (leave) a masapar (few) anashay (men) of them from the charab (sword), from the raib (famine), and from the dabar (word / matter); that they may sapar (book) all their thawaibah (abominations) among the gawayam (nations) where they bawaa (come); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Moreover the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), akal (eat) your lacham (bread) with raish (quaking), and shathah (drinks) your mayam (Waters) with ragazah (trembling) and with fearfulness;

And amar (spoke) the im (nation / people) of the adamah (land), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah concerning the yawashabay (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and the aratz (Earth/land) of Yashar-Al (Israel): They shall akal (eat) their lacham (bread) with fearfulness, and shathah (drinks) their mayam (Waters) in shamamawan (dismay), that her aratz (Earth/land) may be yasham (desolate), and malaa (all) that is therein, because of the chamas (violence) of all those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein.
The irayam (cities) that are yashab (inhabit/dwell) shall be charab (laid) waste, and the aratz (Earth/land) shall be a shamamah (desolation); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), what is this mashal (proverb) that you have in the adamah (land) of Yashar-Al (Israel), amar (spoke), The yamayam (days) are prolonged, and every chazawan (vision) abad (destroy / perish)?

Amar (spoke) them therefore, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will make this mashal (proverb) to shabath (shabath / rest), and they shall no more use it as a mashal (speak in proverb/parable) in Yashar-Al (Israel); but dabar (word / matter) them, The yamayam (days) are at qarab (come close), and the fulfillment of every chazawan (vision).
For there shall be no more any shawaa (vanity) chazawan (vision) nor chalaq (flattering) maqasam (divination) thawak (midst) the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

For I am Yahawah; I will dabar (word / matter), and the dabar (word / matter) that I shall dabar (word / matter) shall be ishah (make); it shall be no more mashak (deferred): for in your yawam (day), rebellious bayath (house), will I dabar (word / matter) the dabar (word / matter), and will ishah (make) it, dabar (word / matter) the Adanay Yahawah.
Again the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), behold, they of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke), The chazawan (vision) that he chazah (sees) is for many yawam (day) to come, and he prophesies of ithayam (times) that are rachawaq (far) off.

Therefore amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: None of my dabar (word / matter) shall be mashak (deferred) any more, but the dabar (word / matter) which I shall dabar (word / matter) shall be ishah (make), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy) against the nabayaay (prophets) of Yashar-Al (Israel) who nabaa (prophesy), and amar (spoke) to those who nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) out of their own lab (heart), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah:
Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, haway (Alas/Woe!) To the foolish nabayaayam (prophets), who halak (move) their own rawach (spirit / wind), and raah (see) seen nothing!
Yashar-Al (Israel), your nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) have been like foxes in the charabah (waste) places.

You have not ilah (go up / offer) up into the paratzawath (gaps), neither built up the gadar (wall) for the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), to imad (stand) in the malachamah (battle) in the yawam (day) of Yahawah.

They have chazah (seen) falsehood and kazab (lying) qasam (divination), who naam (declares prophetically), Yahawah amarayam (says); but Yahawah has not shalach (send) them: and they yachal (have) made men to hope that the dabar (word / matter) would be qawam (rise up).

Haven't you chazah (seen) a shawaa (vanity) machazah (vision), and haven't you dabar (word / matter) a shawaa (vanity) maqasam (divination), in that you amar (spoke), Yahawah naam (declares prophetically); but I have not amar (spoke)?

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you have dabar (word / matter) falsehood, and chazah (seen) kazab (lies), therefore, behold, I am against you, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

My yad (hand) shall be against the nabayaayam (prophets) who chazah (see) shawaa (vanity) visions, and who qasam (divine) kazab (lies): they shall not be in the council of my im (nation / people), neither shall they be kathab (write) in the kathab (write) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), neither shall they bawaa (come) into the adamah (land) of Yashar-Al (Israel); and you shall yadai (know) that I am the Adanay Yahawah.

Because, even because they have taih (seduced) my im (nation / people), amar (spoke), shalawam (peace / safety); and there is no shalawam (peace / safety); and when one banah (build) up a chayatz (wall), hanah (Behold), they plaster it with whitewash:

Amar (spoke) those who plaster it with whitewash, that it shall napal (fall / be cast down): there shall be an shatap (overflowing) gasham (shower); and you, alagabayash (great) hailstones, shall napal (fall / be cast down); and a sair (stormy) rawach (spirit / wind) shall baqai (tear) it.
Behold, when the qayar (wall) napal (fall / be cast down) fallen, shall it not be amar (spoke) to you, Where is the plaster with which you have plastered it?

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will even baqai (tear) it with a sair (stormy) rawach (spirit / wind) in my chamah (wrath); and there shall be an shatap (overflowing) gasham (shower) in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and alagabayash (great) hailstones in chamah (wrath) to kalah (complete / finish) it.

So will I haras (break) down the qayar (wall) that you have plastered with whitewash, and nagai (bring) it down to the aratz (Earth/land), so that its yasawad (foundation) shall be galah (uncovered); and it shall napal (fall / be cast down), and you shall be kalah (complete / finish) in its thawak (midst): and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Thus will I kalah (complete / finish) my chamah (wrath) on the qayar (wall), and on those who have plastered it with whitewash; and I will amar (spoke) you, The qayar (wall) is no more, neither those who plastered it;

To wit, the nabayaay (prophets) of Yashar-Al (Israel) who nabaa (prophesy) concerning Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and who chazah (see) chazawan (vision) of shalawam (peace / safety) for her, and there is no shalawam (peace / safety), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

You, ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) against the banawath (daughters) of your im (nation / people), who nabaa (prophesy) out of their own lab (heart); and nabaa (prophesy) against them,

And amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: haway (Alas/Woe!) To the women who thapar (sew) kasathawath (pillows) on all elbows, and ishah (make) masapachawath (kerchiefs) for the raash (head) of persons of every qawamah (stature) to tzawad (hunt) napashawath (souls)! Will you tzawad (hunt) the napashawath (souls) of my im (nation / people), and chayah (save) napashawath (souls) chayah (alive) for yourselves?

You have chalal (profaned) me among my im (nation / people) for shailay (handfuls) of shairah (barley) and for pathawathay (pieces) of lacham (bread), to mawath (death) the napashawath (souls) who should not mawath (death), and to chayah (save) the napashawath (souls) chayah (alive) who should not chayah (live), by your kazab (lying) to my im (nation / people) who shamai (hearken / hear) to kazab (lies).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against your kasath (pillows), with which you there tzawad (hunt) the napashawath (souls) to parach (make) them fly, and I will qarai (tear) them from your zarawai (arms); and I will let the napashawath (souls) shalach (send), even the napashawath (souls) whom you tzawad (hunt) to parach (make) them fly.

Your masapachah (kerchiefs) also will I qarai (tear), and natzal (deliver) my im (nation / people) out of your yad (hand), and they shall be no more in your yad (hand) to be matzawad (hunted); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Because with shaqar (lies) you have kaah (grieved) the lab (heart) of the tzadayaq (righteous), whom I have not kaah (made) sad; and chazaq (strengthened) the yaday (hands) of the rai (wicked), that he should not shawab (turn back / repent) from his rashai (wicked) darak (way), and be chayah (saved) alive:

Therefore you shall no more chazah (see) shawaa (vanity) visions, nor practice qasam (divination). I will natzal (deliver) my im (nation / people) out of your yad (hand); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Then bawaa (come) ayash (man / husband) of the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel) to me, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) panayam (face) me.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), these ban (son) have ilah (go up / offer) their galawal (idols) into their lab (heart), and nathan (give) the makashawal (stumbling) block of their iwan (guilt/iniquity) nakach (before) their panayam (face): should I be darash (inquired) of at darash (all) by them?

Therefore dabar (word / matter) to them, and amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Every ayash (man / husband) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) who ilah (go up / offer) his galawal (idols) into his lab (heart), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the makashawal (stumbling) block of his iwan (guilt/iniquity) nakach (before) his panayam (face), and bawaa (come) to the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy); I Yahawah will inah (answer / respond) him therein according to the rab (multitude) of his galawal (idols);
That I may thapash (take) the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) in their own lab (heart), because they are all zawar (estranged) from me through their galawal (idols).

Therefore amar (spoke) the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: shawab (turn back / repent), and shawab (turn back / repent) yourselves from your galawal (idols); and shawab (turn back / repent) away your panayam (face) from all your thawaibah (abominations).

For everyone of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), or of the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) who live in Yashar-Al (Israel), who nazar (crown / consecrate) himself from me, and ilah (go up / offer) his galawal (idols) into his lab (heart), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) the makashawal (stumbling) block of his iwan (guilt/iniquity) nakach (before) his panayam (face), and bawaa (come) to the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) to darash (inquire) for himself of me; I Yahawah will inah (answer / respond) him by myself:

And I will nathan (give) my panayam (face) against that ayash (man / husband), and will shamam (make) him an astonishment, for a awath (sign / mark / miracle) and a mashal (proverb), and I will karath (cut) him off from the thawak (midst) of my im (nation / people); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

If the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) is pathah (deceived) and dabar (word / matter) a dabar (word / matter), I, Yahawah, have pathah (deceived) that nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on him, and will shamad (destroy) him from the thawak (midst) of my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel).
They shall nashaa (lift) their iwan (guilt/iniquity): the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) shall be even as the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of him who darash (seeks) him;

That the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) may thaih (go) no more astray from me, neither tamaa (defile) themselves any more with all their pashai (transgressions); but that they may be my im (nation / people), and I may be their Alahayam, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), when a aratz (Earth/land) chataa (sins) against me by committing a mail (top/above), and I natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on it, and shabar (break) the matah (staff / rod / tribe) of its lacham (bread), and shalach (send) raib (famine) on it, and karath (cut) off from it adam (man) and animal;

Though these shalawash (three) anashayam (men), Nach (Noah), Danayaal (Daniel), and Ayawab (Job), were in it, they should natzal (deliver) but their own napash (soul) by their tzadaqah (righteousness), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

If I cause rai (evil) animals to ibar (pass over/through) through the aratz (Earth/land), and they ravage it, and it be made shamamah (desolate), so that no ibar (pass over/through) may pass through panayam (face) of the animals;

Though these shalawash (three) anashayam (men) were in it, as I chay (life), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, they should natzal (deliver) neither banayam (sons) nor banawath (daughters); they only should be natzal (delivered), but the aratz (Earth/land) should be shamamah (desolate).

Or if I bawaa (come) a charab (sword) on that aratz (Earth/land), and amar (spoke), charab (sword), ibar (pass over/through) through the aratz (Earth/land); so that I karath (cut) off from it adam (man) and animal;

Though these shalawash (three) anashayam (men) were in it, as I chay (life), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, they should natzal (deliver) neither banayam (sons) nor banawath (daughters), but they only should be natzal (delivered) themselves.
Or if I shalach (send) a dabar (word / matter) into that aratz (Earth/land), and shapak (pour) out my chamah (wrath) on it in dam (blood), to karath (cut) off from it adam (man) and animal;

Though Nach (Noah), Danayaal (Daniel), and Ayawab (Job), were in it, as I chay (life), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, they should natzal (deliver) neither ban (son) am (mother) banath (daughter); they should but natzal (deliver) their own napash (soul) by their tzadaqah (righteousness).

For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: How much more when I shalach (send) my arabai (four) severe shapat (judge / judgement) on Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), the charab (sword), and the raib (famine), and the rai (evil) animals, and the dabar (word / matter), to karath (cut) off from it adam (man) and animal!

Yet, behold, therein shall be yathar (left) a palayatah (remnant) that shall be yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, both banayam (sons) and banawath (daughters): behold, they shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to you, and you shall raah (see) their darak (way) and their ilayalah (doings); and you shall be nacham (turn away / repent) concerning the rai (evil) that I bawaa (come) brought on Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), even concerning all that I bawaa (come) brought on it.

They shall nacham (turn away / repent) you, when you raah (see) their darak (way) and their ilayalah (doings); and you shall yadai (know) that I ishah (make) not done chanam (without) cause all that I ishah (make) done in it, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), what is the gapan (vine) itz (tree) more than any itz (tree), the vine-branch which is among the itzay (trees) of the yair (forest)?
Shall itz (wood) be laqach (take / seize) of it to ishah (make) any malaakah (work)? Or will men laqach (take / seize) a yathad (pin) of it to thalah (hang) any kalay (vessel) thereon?

Behold, it is nathan (give) into the ash (fire) for fuel; the ash (fire) has akal (eat) shanayam (two) its ends, and its thawak (midst) is charar (burned): is it tzalach (profitable) for any malaakah (work)?

Behold, when it was thamayam (complete / whole), it was ishah (make) for no malaakah (work): how much less, when the ash (fire) has akal (eat) it, and it is charar (burned), shall it yet be ishah (make) for any malaakah (work)!

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: As the gapan (vine) itz (tree) among the itz (trees) of the yair (forest), which I nathan (give) given to the ash (fire) for fuel, so will I nathan (give) the yashabay (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

I will nathan (give) my panayam (face) against them; they shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from the ash (fire), but the ash (fire) shall akal (eat) them; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shawam (place / establish / appoint) my panayam (face) against them.
I will nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) shamamah (desolate), because they have mail (top/above) a mail (top/above), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
Again the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), cause Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) to yadai (know) her thawaibah (abominations);

And amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem): Your makawarah (birth) and your birth is of the aratz (Earth/land) of the Kanainay (Canaanite); the Amaray (Amorite) was your ab (father), and your am (mother) was a Chathay (Hittite).

As for your birth, in the yawam (day) you were yalad (birth / begot) your shar (prince / ruler) was not karath (cut), neither were you rachatz (washed) in mayam (Waters) to cleanse you; you weren't malach (salted) at malach (all), nor chathal (swaddled) at chathal (all).

No iyan (eye) chawas (pitied) you, to ishah (make) any of these things to you, to chamal (have) compassion on you; but you were shalak (cast) out in the panayam (face) shadah (field), for that your napash (soul) was abhorred, in the yawam (day) that you were yalad (birth / begot).

When I ibar (pass over/through) by you, and raah (see) you wallowing in your dam (blood), I amar (spoke) to you, Though you are in your dam (blood), chayah (live); yes, I amar (spoke) to you, Though you are in your dam (blood), chayah (live).
