I nathan (give) you to rababah (multiply) as that which tzamach (grows) in the shadah (field), and you rabah (increased) and gadal (grew) great, and you bawaa (come) to iday (ornament / adornment) iday (ornament / adornment); your shadayam (breasts) were kawan (fashioned), and your shair (hair) was tzamach (grown); yet you were iyaram (naked) and bore.

Now when I ibar (pass over/through) by you, and raah (see) at you, behold, your ith (time) was the ith (time) of dawad (love); and I parash (spread) my kanap (skirt) over you, and kasah (covered) your irawah (nakedness): yes, I shabai (swear / take oath) to you, and bawaa (come) into a barayath (covenant) with you, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, and you became mine.
Then rachatz (washed) I you with mayam (Waters); yes, I thoroughly shatap (washed) away your dam (blood) from you, and I sawak (anointed) you with shaman (oil).
I labash (clothed) you also with embroidered raqamah (work), and shod you with sealskin, and I dressed you about with shash (six) linen, and kasah (covered) you with mashay (silk).
I idah (decked) you with iday (ornament / adornment), and I nathan (give) tzamayadayam (bracelets) on your yad (hand), and a rabayad (chain) on your garawan (neck).
I nathan (give) a ring on your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and igayalayam (earrings) in your azan (ear), and a thapaarah (beautiful) itarah (crown) on your raash (head).

Thus you were idah (decked) with zahab (gold) and kasap (silver); and your clothing was of shash (six) linen, and mashay (silk), and embroidered raqamah (work); you akal (eat) fine salath (flour), and dabash (honey), and shaman (oil); and you were maad (exceedingly) yapah (beautiful), and you tzalach (prospered) to malawakah (royal) estate.

Your sham (name) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth among the gawayam (nations) for your yapay (beauty); for it was kalayal (perfect), through my hadar (glory / majesty / splendor) which I had shawam (place / establish / appoint) on you, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

But you batach (trusted) in your yapay (beauty), and zanah (played) the prostitute because of your sham (name), and shapak (poured) out your prostitution on everyone who ibar (pass over/through) by; his it was.

You laqach (take / seize) of your bagad (garments), and made for yourselves bamah (high) places ishah (make) with various colors, and zanah (played) the prostitute on them: the like things shall not bawaa (come), neither shall it be so.

You also laqach (take / seize) your thapaarah (beautiful) kalay (jewels) of my zahab (gold) and of my kasap (silver), which I nathan (give) given you, and ishah (make) for yourself tzalamay (images) of zakar (remember), and zanah (played) the prostitute with them;
And you laqach (take / seize) your embroidered bagaday (garments), and kasah (covered) them, and nathan (give) my shaman (oil) and my qatarath (incense) panayam (face) them.

My lacham (bread) also which I nathan (give) you, fine salath (flour), and shaman (oil), and dabash (honey), with which I akal (eat) you, you even nathan (give) it panayam (face) them for a pleasant aroma; and thus it was, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

Moreover you have laqach (take / seize) your ban (son) and your banath (daughter), whom you have yalad (birth / begot) to me, and you have zabach (sacrificed) these to them to be akal (eat). Was your prostitution a mait (small) matter,
That you have shachat (slain) my ban (son), and nathan (give) them up, in ibar (pass over/through) them to pass through the fire to them?

In all your thawaibah (abominations) and your prostitution you have not zakar (remember) the yamay (days) of your naiwar (youth), when you were iyaram (naked) and bore, and were wallowing in your dam (blood).
It has happened achar (other) all your rai (wickedness), (away (woe), away (woe) to you! Naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah),
That you have banah (build) for yourselves a vaulted gab (place), and ishah (make) made yourselves a lofty ramah (place) in every rachab (street).

You have banah (build) your lofty ramah (place) at the raash (head) of every darak (way), and have made your yapay (beauty) a thaib (abomination), and have pashaq (opened) your ragal (feet / foot) to everyone who ibar (pass over/through) by, and rabah (multiplied) your prostitution.

You have also zanah (committed) sexual immorality with the banay (egyptians), your neighbors, gadal (great) of bashar (flesh); and rabah (have) multiplied your prostitution, to provoke me to kais (anger).

See therefore, I have natah (stretched) out my yad (hand) over you, and have garai (diminished) your ordinary food, and nathan (give) you to the napash (soul) of those who shanaa (hate) you, the banawath (daughters) of the Palashathay (Philistines), who are kalam (ashamed) of your zamah (lewd) darak (way).

You have zanah (played) the prostitute also with the banay (assyrians), balathay (without) you were insatiable; yes, you have zanah (played) the prostitute with them, and yet you weren't shabaih (seven).
You rabah (have) moreover multiplied your prostitution to the aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (merchants), to Kashaday (Chaldea); and yet you weren't shabai (satisfied) with zaath (this).
How amal (weak) is your labah (heart), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, since you ishah (make) all these things, the maishah (work) of a impudent prostitute;

In that you banah (build) your vaulted gab (place) at the raash (head) of every darak (way), and ishah (make) your lofty ramah (place) in every rachab (street), and have not been as a prostitute, in that you qalas (scorn) pay.
A ayashah (woman / wife) who naap (commits) adultery! Who laqach (take / seize) strangers instead of her ayash (man / husband)!

They nathan (give) nadah (gifts) to all prostitutes; but you nathan (give) your nadan (gifts) to all your lovers, and bribe them, that they may bawaa (come) to you on sabayab (surrounding) side for your prostitution.

You are different from other nashayam (women) in your prostitution, in that no one achar (other) you to zanah (play) the prostitute; and whereas you nathan (give) athanan (hire), and no athanan (hire) is nathan (give) to you, therefore you are different.
Therefore, prostitute, shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah:

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, Because your nachashath (filthiness) was shapak (poured) out, and your irawah (nakedness) galah (uncovered) through your prostitution with your lovers; and because of all the galawalay (idols) of your thawaibah (abominations), and for the dam (blood) of your ban (son), that you nathan (give) to them;

Therefore see, I will qabatz (gather) all your lovers, with whom you have irab (evening) pleasure, and all those who you have ahab (love), with all those who you have shanaa (hate); I will even qabatz (gather) them against you on sabayab (surrounding) side, and will galah (uncover) your irawah (nakedness) to them, that they may raah (see) all your irawah (nakedness).

I will shapat (judge / judgement) you, as naapawath (women) who break wedlock and shapak (shed) dam (blood) are mashapat (judged); and I will nathan (give) on you the dam (blood) of chamah (wrath) and qanaah (jealousy).

I will also nathan (give) you into their yad (hand), and they shall haras (throw) down your vaulted gab (place), and nathatz (break) down your lofty ramah (places); and they shall pashat (strip) you of your clothes, and laqach (take / seize) your thapaarah (beautiful) kalay (jewels); and they shall yanach (leave) you iyaram (naked) and bore.
They shall also ilah (go up / offer) up a qahal (company) against you, and they shall ragam (stone) you with aban (stone), and bathaq (thrust) you through with their charab (sword).

They shall sharap (burn) your bayath (house) with ash (fire), and ishah (make) shapatayam (judgments) on you in the iyan (eye) of many nashayam (women); and I will shabath (shabath / rest) you to cease from zanah (playing) the prostitute, and you shall also nathan (give) no athanan (hire) any more.
So will I cause my chamah (wrath) toward you to nawach (rest), and my qanaah (jealousy) shall sawar (depart) from you, and I will be shaqat (quiet), and will be no more kais (angry).

Because you have not zakar (remember) the yamay (days) of your naiwar (youth), but have ragaz (raged) against me in all these things; therefore, haa (behold), I also will nathan (give) your darak (way) on your raash (head), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah: and you shall not ishah (make) this lewdness with all your thawaibah (abominations).
Behold, everyone who uses mashal (speak in proverb/parable) shall use this mashal (speak in proverb/parable) amar (spoke) you, saying, "As is the am (mother), so is her banath (daughter).

You are the banath (daughter) of your am (mother), who loathes her ayash (man / husband) and her ban (son); and you are the achawath (sister) of your achawath (sisters), who loathed their ayash (man / husband) and their ban (son): your am (mother) was a Chathay (Hittite), and your ab (father) a Amaray (Amorite).

Your gadawal (very great/important/mighty) achawath (sister) is Shamarawan (Samaria), who yashab (inhabit/dwell) at your left shamaawal (left hand), she and her banath (daughter); and your younger achawath (sister), who yashab (inhabit/dwell) at your right yamayan (right hand), is Sadam (Sodom) and her banath (daughter).

Yet have you not halak (move) in their darak (ways), nor ishah (make) after their thawaibah (abominations); but, as if that were a very mait (little) thing, you were more shachath (corrupt) than they in all your darak (ways).

As I chay (life), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, Sadam (Sodom) your achawath (sister) ishah (make) not done, she nor her banath (daughter), as you ishah (make) done, you and your banath (daughter).

Behold, this was the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of your achawath (sister) Sadam (Sodom): gaawan (pride), fullness of lacham (bread), and prosperous ease was in her and in her banath (daughter); neither did she chazaq (strengthen) the yad (hand) of the inay (poor) and abayawan (needy).
They were gabah (haughty), and ishah (make) thawaibah (abomination) panayam (face) me: therefore I sawar (took) them away as I raah (see) good.

Neither has Shamarawan (Samaria) chataa (committed) chatzay (half) of your chataah (sin); but you rabah (have) multiplied your thawaibah (abominations) more than they, and have justified your achawath (sisters) by all your thawaibah (abominations) which you ishah (make) done.

You also, nashaa (lift) you your own kalamah (shame), in that you have given palal (judgment) for your achawath (sisters); through your chataah (sin) that you have thaib (committed) more abominable than they, they are more tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) that you: yes, be also bawash (confounded), and nashaa (lift) your kalamah (shame), in that you have justified your achawath (sisters).

I will shawab (turn back / repent) again their shabawath (captivity), the shabawath (captivity) of Sadam (Sodom) and her banath (daughter), and the shabawath (captivity) of Shamarawan (Samaria) and her banath (daughter), and the shabawath (captivity) of your shabawath (captives) in their thawak (midst);
That you may nashaa (lift) your own kalamah (shame), and may be kalam (ashamed) because of all that you ishah (make) done, in that you are a nacham (turn away / repent) to them.

Your achawath (sisters), Sadam (Sodom) and her banath (daughter), shall shawab (turn back / repent) to their qadamah (former) estate; and Shamarawan (Samaria) and her banath (daughter) shall shawab (turn back / repent) to their qadamah (former) estate; and you and your banath (daughter) shall shawab (turn back / repent) to your qadamah (former) estate.
For your achawath (sister) Sadam (Sodom) was not shamawaih (mentioned) by your pah (mouth) in the yawam (day) of your gaawan (pride),

Before your rai (wickedness) was galah (uncovered), as at the ith (time) of the charapah (reproach) of the banawath (daughters) of Aram (Syria), and of all who are around her, the banawath (daughters) of the Palashathay (Philistines), who do despite to you all around.
You have nashaa (lift) your lewdness and your thawaibah (abominations), naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.
For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will also ishah (make) with you as you ishah (make) done, who have bazah (despised) the alah (curse / oath) in parar (breaking) the barayath (covenant).
Nevertheless I will zakar (remember) my barayath (covenant) with you in the yamay (days) of your naiwar (youth), and I will qawam (rise up) to you a iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant).

Then you shall zakar (remember) your darak (ways), and be kalam (ashamed), when you shall laqach (take / seize) your achawath (sisters), your gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qatanawath (sisters) and your younger; and I will nathan (give) them to you for banawath (daughters), but not by your barayath (covenant).
I will qawam (rise up) my barayath (covenant) with you; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah;

That you may zakar (remember), and be bawash (confounded), and never pathachawan (open) your pah (mouth) any more, panayam (face) of your kalamah (shame), when I have kapar (forgiven) you all that you ishah (make) done, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), chawad (put) forth a chayadah (riddle), and mashal (speak in proverb/parable) a mashal (parable) to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel);

And amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: A gadawal (very great/important/mighty) nashar (eagle) with gadawal (very great/important/mighty) kanapayam (wings) and long feathers, malaa (full) of nawatzah (feathers), which had various colors, bawaa (come) to Labanawan (Lebanon), and laqach (take / seize) the tzamarath (top) of the araz (cedar):

He qatap (cropped) off the topmost of the yanayaqah (young) twigs of it, and bawaa (come) it to a aratz (Earth/land) of Kanain (traffic); he shawam (place / establish / appoint) it in a iyar (city) of rakalayam (merchants).

He laqach (take / seize) also of the zarai (seed) of the aratz (Earth/land), and planted it in a zarai (fruitful) shadah (soil); he laqach (take / seize) it beside many mayam (Waters); he shawam (place / establish / appoint) it as a tzapatzapah (willow) tree.

It tzamach (grew), and became a sarach (spreading) gapan (vine) of shapal (low) qawamah (stature), whose branches panah (turn) toward him, and its sharash (roots) were under him: so it became a gapan (vine), and ishah (make) forth branches, and shalach (send) forth paarawath (sprigs).

There was also another gadawal (very great/important/mighty) nashar (eagle) with gadawal (very great/important/mighty) kanapayam (wings) and many nawatzah (feathers): and behold, this gapan (vine) bent its sharash (roots) toward him, and shalach (send) forth its branches toward him, from the iragawath (beds) of its plantation, that he might shaqah (water) it.

It was shathal (planted) in a tawab (good / proper function) shadah (soil) by many mayam (Waters), that it might ishah (make) forth branches, and that it might nashaa (lift) paray (fruit), that it might be a adarath (goodly) gapan (vine).

Amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Shall it tzalach (prosper)? Shall he not nathaq (pull) up its sharash (roots), and qasas (cut) off its paray (fruit), that it may yabash (dry land); that all its fresh tzamach (springing) leaves may yabash (dry land)? And not by a strong zarawai (arm) or many im (nation / people) can it be nashaa (lift) from its sharash (roots).

Yes, behold, being shathal (planted), shall it tzalach (prosper)? Shall it not yabash (dry land) yabash (dry land), when the qadayam (east) rawach (spirit / wind) touches it? It shall yabash (dry land) in the iragath (beds) where it tzamach (grew).
Moreover the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Amar (spoke) now to the rebellious bayath (house), Don't you yadai (know) what these things mean? Amar (spoke) them, Behold, the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) bawaa (come) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and laqach (take / seize) its malak (king), and its shar (prince / ruler), and bawaa (come) them to him to Babal (Babylon):

And he laqach (take / seize) of the zarai (seed) malawakah (royal), and karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) with him; he also bawaa (come) him under an alah (curse / oath), and bawaa (come) away the ayal (mighty) of the aratz (Earth/land);
That the mamalakah (kingdom) might be shapal (base), that it might not nashaa (lift) itself up, but that by shamar (keep/guard) his barayath (covenant) it might imad (stand).

But he marad (rebelled) against him in shalach (send) his malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) into Matzarayam (Egypt), that they might nathan (give) him sawasayam (horses) and many im (nation / people). Shall he tzalach (prosper)? Shall he malat (escape) who ishah (make) such things? Shall he parar (break) the barayath (covenant), and yet malat (escape)?

As I chay (life), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, surely in the maqawam (place) where the malak (king) dwells who made him malak (king), whose alah (curse / oath) he bazah (despised), and whose barayath (covenant) he parar (broke), even with him in the thawak (midst) of Babal (Babylon) he shall mawath (death).

Neither shall Paraih (Pharaoh) with his gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) and rab (great) qahal (company) help him in the malachamah (war), when they shapak (cast) up mounds and banah (build) dayaq (forts), to karath (cut) off many napashawath (persons).

For he has bazah (despised) the alah (curse / oath) by parar (breaking) the barayath (covenant); and behold, he nathan (give) given his yad (hand), and yet ishah (make) done all these things; he shall not malat (escape).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: As I chay (life), surely my alah (curse / oath) that he has bazah (despised), and my barayath (covenant) that he has pawar (broken), I will even nathan (give) it on his own raash (head).

I will parash (spread) my rashath (net) on him, and he shall be thapash (taken) in my matzawad (snare), and I will bawaa (come) him to Babal (Babylon), and will enter into shapat (judge / judgement) with him there for his mail (top/above) that he has mail (top/above) against me.

All his mabarach (fugitives) in all his agap (bands) shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword), and those who shaar (remain) shall be parash (scattered) toward every rawach (spirit / wind): and you shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will also laqach (take / seize) of the rawam (will lift up) tzamarath (top) of the araz (cedar), and will nathan (give) it; I will qatap (crop) off from the topmost of its yawanaqath (young) twigs a rak (tender) one, and I will shathal (plant) it on a gabah (high) and lofty har (mountain):

In the har (mountain) of the marawam (height) of Yashar-Al (Israel) will I shathal (plant) it; and it shall nashaa (lift) forth inap (boughs), and ishah (make) paray (fruit), and be a adayar (goodly) araz (cedar): and under it shall shakan (place) all tzapawar (birds) of every kanap (wing); in the tzal (shade) of its branches shall they shakan (place).

All the itzay (trees) of the shadah (field) shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have shapal (brought) down the gabah (high) itz (tree), have gabah (exalted) the shapal (low) itz (tree), have yabash (dry land) up the lach (green) itz (tree), and have made the yabash (dry land) itz (tree) to parach (flourish); I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) and ishah (make) done it.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me again, amar (spoke),

What do you mean, that you use this mashal (proverb) concerning the adamah (land) of Yashar-Al (Israel), amar (spoke), The abawath (fathers) have akal (eat) basar (sour) grapes, and the banayam (childrens) shanay (teeth) are qahah (set) on edge?
As I chay (life), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, you shall not have occasion any more to use this mashal (proverb) in Yashar-Al (Israel).
Behold, all napashawath (souls) are mine; as the napash (soul) of the ab (father), so also the napash (soul) of the ban (son) is mine: the napash (soul) who chataa (sins), he shall mawath (death).
But if a ayash (man / husband) is tzadayaq (righteous), and ishah (make) that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (righteousness),

And has not akal (eat) on the harayam (mountains), neither has nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye) to the galawalay (idols) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), neither has tamaa (defiled) his neighbor's ayashah (woman / wife), neither has qarab (come close) near to a ayashah (woman / wife) in her impurity,

And has not wronged any, but has shawab (turn back / repent) to the chawab (debtor) his chabal (pledge), has gazal (taken) nothing by robbery, nathan (give) given his lacham (bread) to the raib (hungry), and has kasah (covered) the iyaram (naked) with a bagad (garment);

He who nathan (give) not given forth on interest, neither has laqach (take / seize) any tharabayath (increase), who has shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand) from iwal (iniquity), ishah (make) executed amath (truth) mashapat (justice) between ayash (man / husband) and ayash (man / husband),

Has halak (move) in my chaqah (statutes), and has shamar (keep/guard) my mashapat (ordinances), to ishah (make) truly; he is tzadayaq (righteous), he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
If he yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son) who is a parayatz (robber), a shedder of dam (blood), and who ishah (make) any achad (one) of these things,
And who ishah (make) not any of those duties, but even has akal (eat) on the harayam (mountains), and tamaa (defiled) his neighbor's ayashah (woman / wife),

Has wronged the inay (poor) and abayawan (needy), has gazal (taken) by robbery, has not shawab (turn back / repent) the chabal (pledge), and has nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye) to the galawalayam (idols), ishah (make) committed thawaibah (abomination),

Nathan (give) given forth on interest, and has laqach (take / seize) tharabayath (increase); shall he then chayay (life)? He shall not chayah (live): he ishah (make) done all these thawaibawath (abominations); he shall mawath (death) mawath (death); his dam (blood) shall be on him.
Now, behold, if he yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son), who raah (see) all his ab (father) chataath (sins), which he ishah (make) done, and raah (see), and ishah (make) not such like;

Who has not akal (eat) on the harayam (mountains), neither has nashaa (lift) up his iyan (eye) to the galawalay (idols) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), has not tamaa (defiled) his neighbor's ayashah (woman / wife),

Neither has wronged any, has not taken anything to chabal (pledge), neither has gazal (taken) by robbery, but nathan (give) given his lacham (bread) to the raib (hungry), and has kasah (covered) the iyaram (naked) with a bagad (garment);

Who has shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand) from the inay (poor), who has not laqach (take / seize) interest nor tharabayath (increase), ishah (make) executed my mashapat (ordinances), has halak (move) in my chaqah (statutes); he shall not mawath (death) for the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of his ab (father), he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live).

As for his ab (father), because he ishaq (cruelly) ishaq (oppressed), gazal (robbed) his ach (brother/kinsman), and ishah (make) that which is not tawab (good / proper function) thawak (midst) his im (nation / people), behold, he shall mawath (death) in his iwan (guilt/iniquity).

Yet you amar (spoke), Why doesn't the ban (son) nashaa (lift) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the ab (father)? When the ban (son) ishah (make) done that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (righteousness), and has shamar (keep/guard) all my chaqah (statutes), and ishah (make) done them, he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live).

The napash (soul) who chataa (sins), he shall mawath (death): the ban (son) shall not nashaa (lift) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the ab (father), neither shall the ab (father) nashaa (lift) the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the ban (son); the tzadaqah (righteousness) of the tzadayaq (righteous) shall be on him, and the rashaih (wickedness) of the rashai (wicked) shall be on him.

But if the rashai (wicked) shawab (turn back / repent) from all his chataah (sin) that he ishah (make) committed, and shamar (keep/guard) all my chaqah (statutes), and ishah (make) that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (righteousness), he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live), he shall not mawath (death).
None of his pashai (transgressions) that he ishah (make) committed shall be zakar (remember) against him: in his tzadaqah (righteousness) that he ishah (make) done he shall chayah (live).

Chapatz (have) I any chapatz (pleasure) in the mawath (death) of the rashai (wicked)? Naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah; and not rather that he should shawab (turn back / repent) from his darak (way), and chayah (live)?

But when the tzadayaq (righteous) shawab (turn back / repent) away from his tzadaqah (righteousness), and ishah (make) iwal (iniquity), and ishah (make) according to all the thawaibawath (abominations) that the rashai (wicked) ishah (make) does, shall he chayay (life)? None of his tzadaqah (righteousness) deeds that he ishah (make) done shall be zakar (remember): in his mail (top/above) that he has mail (top/above), and in his chataah (sin) that he has chataa (sinned), in them shall he mawath (death).

Yet you amar (spoke), The darak (way) of the Adanay is not thakan (equal). Shamai (hearken / hear) now, bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel): Is my darak (way) not thakan (equal)? Aren't your darak (ways) thakan (unequal)?

When the tzadayaq (righteous) man shawab (turn back / repent) away from his tzadaqah (righteousness), and ishah (make) iwal (iniquity), and mawath (death) therein; in his iwal (iniquity) that he ishah (make) done shall he mawath (death).

Again, when the rashai (wicked) man shawab (turn back / repent) away from his rashaih (wickedness) that he ishah (make) committed, and ishah (make) that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (righteousness), he shall chayah (save) his napash (soul) chayah (alive).
Because he raah (see), and shawab (turn back / repent) away from all his pashai (transgressions) that he ishah (make) committed, he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live), he shall not mawath (death).

Yet the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amaraw (says), "The darak (way) of the Adanay is not fair." Bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), aren't my darak (ways) fair? Aren't your darak (ways) unfair?

Therefore I will shapat (judge / judgement) you, bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), everyone according to his darak (ways), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah. Shawab (turn back / repent), and shawab (turn back / repent) yourselves from all your pashai (transgressions); so iwan (guilt/iniquity) shall not be your makashawal (ruin).

Shalak (cast) away from you all your pashai (transgressions), in which you have pashai (transgressed); and ishah (make) yourself a chadash (new) lab (heart) and a chadash (new) rawach (spirit / wind): for why will you mawath (death), bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel)?

For I chapatz (have) no pleasure in the mawath (death) of him who mawath (death), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah: therefore shawab (turn back / repent) yourselves, and chayah (live).
Moreover, nashaa (lift) up a qayanah (lamentation) for the nashayaay (princes) of Yashar-Al (Israel),
And amar (spoke), What was your am (mother)? A labayaa (lioness): she couched among arayawath (lions), in the thawak (midst) of the young kaparayam (lions) she rabah (nourished) her cubs.
She ilah (go up / offer) up achad (one) of her cubs: he became a young kapayar (lion), and he lamad (teach / instruct) to tarap (catch) the tarap (prey); he akal (eat) adam (men).

The gawayam (nations) also shamai (hearken / hear) of him; he was thapash (taken) in their shachath (pit); and they bawaa (come) him with chachayam (hooks) to the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

Now when she raah (see) that she yachal (had) waited, and her thaqawah (hope) was abad (destroy / perish), then she laqach (take / seize) another of her cubs, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) him a young kapayar (lion).
He halak (move) up and down thawak (midst) the arayawath (lions); he became a young kapayar (lion), and he lamad (teach / instruct) to tarap (catch) the tarap (prey); he akal (eat) adam (men).

He yadai (knew) their palaces, and charab (laid) waste their iyar (cities); and the aratz (Earth/land) was yasham (desolate), and its fullness, because of the qawal (sound / voice) of his shaagah (roaring).

Then the gawayam (nations) nathan (give) against him on sabayab (surrounding) side from the madayanawath (provinces); and they parash (spread) their rashath (net) over him; he was thapash (taken) in their shachath (pit).

They nathan (give) him in a cage with chachayam (hooks), and bawaa (come) him to the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon); they bawaa (come) him into strongholds, that his qawal (sound / voice) should no more be shamai (hearken / hear) on the haray (mountains) of Yashar-Al (Israel).
Your am (mother) was like a gapan (vine), in your dam (blood), shathal (planted) by the mayam (Waters): it was parah (fruitful) and inap (full) of branches by reason of many mayam (Waters).

It had iz (strength / might / refuge) matawath (rods) for the scepters of those who mashal (rule/have dominion) rule, and their qawamah (stature) was gabah (exalted) among the ibath (thick) boughs, and they were raah (see) in their gabah (height) with the rab (multitude) of their branches.

But it was nathash (plucked) up in fury, it was shalak (cast) down to the aratz (Earth/land), and the qadayam (east) rawach (spirit / wind) yabash (dry land) up its paray (fruit): its iz (strength / might / refuge) matah (staff / rod / tribe) were paraq (broken) off and yabash (dry land); the ash (fire) akal (eat) them.
Now it is shathal (planted) in the madabar (wilderness), in a tzayah (dry) and tzamaa (thirsty) aratz (Earth/land).

Ash (fire) is yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the matah (staff / rod / tribe) of its branches, it has akal (eat) its paray (fruit), so that there is in it no iz (strength / might / refuge) matah (staff / rod / tribe) to be a scepter to mashal (rule/have dominion). This is a qayanah (lamentation), and shall be for a qayanah (lamentation).

It happened in the shabayaiy (seventh) shanah (year), in the chamayashay (fifth) month, the ishawar (tenth) day of the chadash (month), that ayash (man / husband) of the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel) bawaa (come) to darash (inquire) of Yahawah, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) panayam (face) me.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), dabar (word / matter) to the zaqanay (elders) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Is it to darash (inquire) of me that you bawaa (come) come? As I chay (life), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, I will not be darash (inquired) of by you.
Will you shapat (judge / judgement) them, ban (son) of adam (man), will you shapat (judge / judgement) them? Yadai (cause) them to know the thawaibath (abominations) of their ab (father);

And amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: In the yawam (day) when I bachar (chose) Yashar-Al (Israel), and yad (hand) to the zarai (seed) of the bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and yadai (made) myself known to them in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), when I yad (hand) to them, amar (spoke), I am Yahawah your Alahayam;

In that yawam (day) I yad (hand) to them, to yatzaa (go out / come out) them forth out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) into a aratz (Earth/land) that I had thawar (searched) out for them, zawab (flow) with chalab (milk) and dabash (honey), which is the glory of all aratzawath (lands).

I amar (spoke) to them, shalak (cast) away every ayash (man / husband) the shaqawatzay (abominations) of his iyan (eye), and don't tamaa (defile) yourselves with the galawalay (idols) of Matzarayam (Egypt); I am Yahawah your Alahayam.

But they marah (rebelled) against me, and would not shamai (hearken / hear) to me; they ayash (man / husband) didn't shalak (throw) away the shaqawatzay (abominations) of their iyan (eye), neither did they izab (forsake) the galawalay (idols) of Matzarayam (Egypt). Then I amar (spoke) I would shapak (pour) out my chamah (wrath) on them, to kalah (complete / finish) my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) against them in the thawak (midst) of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

But I ishah (make) for my sham (name) sake, that it should not be chalal (profaned) in the iyan (eye) of the gawayam (nations), thawak (midst) which they were, in whose iyan (eye) I yadai (made) myself known to them, in yatzaa (go out / come out) them forth out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
So I yatzaa (go out / come out) them to go forth out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and bawaa (come) them into the madabar (wilderness).
I nathan (give) them my chaqah (statutes), and showed them my mashapat (ordinances), which if a adam (man) ishah (make), he shall chayay (life) in them.

Moreover also I nathan (give) them my shabath (shabath / rest), to be a awath (sign / mark / miracle) between me and them, that they might yadai (know) that I am Yahawah who qadash (set apart / make holy) them.

But the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) marah (rebelled) against me in the madabar (wilderness): they didn't halak (move) in my chaqah (statutes), and they maas (rejected) my mashapat (ordinances), which if a adam (man) ishah (make), he shall chayay (life) in them; and my shabath (shabath / rest) they maad (greatly) chalal (profaned). Then I amar (spoke) I would shapak (pour) out my chamah (wrath) on them in the madabar (wilderness), to kalah (complete / finish) them.
But I ishah (make) for my sham (name) sake, that it should not be chalal (profaned) in the iyan (eye) of the gawayam (nations), in whose iyan (eye) I yatzaa (go out / come out) them out.

Moreover also I yad (hand) to them in the madabar (wilderness), that I would not bawaa (come) them into the aratz (Earth/land) which I nathan (give) given them, zawab (flow) with chalab (milk) and dabash (honey), which is the glory of all aratzawath (lands);

Because they maas (rejected) my mashapat (ordinances), and didn't halak (move) in my chaqah (statutes), and chalal (profaned) my shabath (shabath / rest): for their lab (heart) halak (move) achar (other) their galawal (idols).
Nevertheless my iyan (eye) chawas (spared) them, and I didn't shachath (destroy) them, neither ishah (make) I make a kalah (complete / finish) end of them in the madabar (wilderness).

I amar (spoke) to their ban (son) in the madabar (wilderness), Don't yalak (walk) in the chawaqay (statutes) of your ab (father), neither shamar (keep/guard) their mashapat (ordinances), nor tamaa (defile) yourselves with their galawal (idols).
I am Yahawah your Alahayam: yalak (walk) in my chaqah (statutes), and shamar (keep/guard) my mashapat (ordinances), and ishah (make) them;
And make my shabath (shabath / rest) qadash (set apart / make holy); and they shall be a awath (sign / mark / miracle) between me and you, that you may yadai (know) that I am Yahawah your Alahayam.

But the banayam (children) marah (rebelled) against me; they didn't halak (move) in my chaqah (statutes), neither shamar (keep/guard) my mashapat (ordinances) to ishah (make) them, which if a adam (man) ishah (make), he shall chayay (life) in them; they chalal (profaned) my shabath (shabath / rest). Then I amar (spoke) I would shapak (pour) out my chamah (wrath) on them, to kalah (complete / finish) my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) against them in the madabar (wilderness).

Nevertheless I shawab (turn back / repent) my yad (hand), and ishah (make) for my sham (name) sake, that it should not be chalal (profaned) in the iyan (eye) of the gawayam (nations), in whose iyan (eye) I yatzaa (go out / come out) them forth.
Moreover I yad (hand) to them in the madabar (wilderness), that I would pawatz (scatter) them among the gawayam (nations), and zarah (disperse) them through the aratzawath (countries);

Because they ishah (make) not executed my mashapat (ordinances), but had maas (rejected) my chaqah (statutes), and had chalal (profaned) my shabath (shabath / rest), and their iyan (eye) were achar (other) their ab (father)' galawalay (idols).
Moreover also I nathan (give) them chaqayam (statutes) that were not tawab (good / proper function), and mashapatayam (ordinances) in which they should not chayah (live);

And I tamaa (polluted) them in their own mathanah (gifts), in that they ibar (pass over/through) to pass through the fire all that patar (opens) the racham (show mercy / love), that I might shamam (make) them desolate, to the end that they might yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Therefore, ban (son) of adam (man), dabar (word / matter) to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: In this moreover have your ab (father) gadap (blasphemed) me, in that they have mail (top/above) a mail (top/above) against me.

For when I bawaa (come) brought them into the aratz (Earth/land), which I yad (hand) to nathan (give) to them, then they raah (see) every rawam (will lift up) gabaih (hill), and every ibath (thick) itz (tree), and they zabach (offered) there their zabach (sacrifices), and there they presented the kais (provocation) of their zabach (offering); there also they shawam (place / establish / appoint) their pleasant aroma, and they nasak (poured) out there their drink nasak (offerings).
Then I amar (spoke) to them, What does the bamah (high) place where you bawaa (come) mean? So its sham (name) is qaraa (called) Bamah (Bamah) to this yawam (day).

Therefore amar (spoke) the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Do you tamaa (pollute) yourselves in the darak (way) of your ab (father)? And do you zanah (play) the prostitute achar (other) their shaqawatz (abominations)?

And when you offer your mathanah (gifts), when you make your ban (son) to ibar (pass over/through) through the ash (fire), do you tamaa (pollute) yourselves with all your galawal (idols) to this yawam (day)? And shall I be darash (inquired) of by you, bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel)? As I chay (life), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, I will not be darash (inquired) of by you;

And that which ilah (go up / offer) into your rawach (spirit / wind) shall not be at all, in that you amar (spoke), We will be as the gawayam (nations), as the mashapachawath (families) of the aratzawath (countries), to sharath (serve) itz (wood) and aban (stone).

As I chay (life), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, surely with a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and with an natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm), and with chamah (wrath) poured out, will I be malak (king) over you:

And I will yatzaa (go out / come out) you out from the imayam (peoples), and will qabatz (gather) you out of the aratzawath (countries) in which you are pawatz (scattered), with a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and with an natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm), and with chamah (wrath) shapak (poured) out;
And I will bawaa (come) you into the madabar (wilderness) of the imayam (peoples), and there will I enter into shapat (judge / judgement) with you panayam (face) to panayam (face).

Like as I entered into shapat (judge / judgement) with your ab (father) in the madabar (wilderness) of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), so will I enter into shapat (judge / judgement) with you, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
I will ibar (pass over/through) you to pass under the shabat (rod), and I will bawaa (come) you into the masarath (bond) of the barayath (covenant);

And I will barar (purge) out from among you the maradayam (rebels), and those who disobey against me; I will yatzaa (go out / come out) them forth out of the aratz (Earth/land) magawar (where) they live, but they shall not bawaa (come) into the adamah (land) of Yashar-Al (Israel): and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

As for you, bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: yalak (go), ibad (servant) everyone his galawal (idols), and achar (other) also, if you will not shamai (hearken / hear) to me; but my qadash (set apart / make holy) sham (name) you shall no more chalal (profane) with your mathanah (gifts), and with your galawal (idols).

For in my qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain), in the har (mountain) of the marawam (height) of Yashar-Al (Israel), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, there shall all the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), all of them, ibad (servant) me in the aratz (Earth/land): there will I ratzah (accept) them, and there will I darash (require) your tharawamah (offerings), and the raashayath (beginning) fruits of your mashaath (offerings), with all your qadash (set apart / make holy) things.

As a pleasant aroma will I ratzah (accept) you, when I yatzaa (go out / come out) you out from the imayam (peoples), and qabatz (gather) you out of the aratzawath (countries) in which you have been pawatz (scattered); and I will be qadash (set apart / make holy) in you in the sight of the gawayam (nations).

You shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shall bawaa (come) you into the adamah (land) of Yashar-Al (Israel), into the aratz (Earth/land) which I yad (hand) to nathan (give) to your ab (father).

There you shall zakar (remember) your darak (ways), and all your ilayalah (doings), in which you have tamaa (polluted) yourselves; and you shall qawat (loathe) yourselves in your own panayam (face) for all your rai (evils) that you ishah (make) committed.

You shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I ishah (make) dealt with you for my sham (name) sake, not according to your rai (evil) darak (ways), nor according to your shachath (corrupt) ilayalah (doings), you bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) darak (toward) the thayaman (south), and natap (drop) your word toward the darawam (south), and nabaa (prophesy) against the yair (forest) of the shadah (field) in the nagab (south);

And amar (spoke) the yair (forest) of the nagab (south), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah: Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, Behold, I will yatzath (kindle) a ash (fire) in you, and it shall akal (eat) every lach (green) itz (tree) in you, and every yabash (dry land) itz (tree): the lahabah (flaming) shalahabath (flame) shall not be kabah (quenched), and all panayam (face) from the nagab (south) to the tzapawan (north) shall be burnt thereby.
All bashar (flesh) shall raah (see) that I, Yahawah, have bair (kindled) it; it shall not be kabah (quenched).
Then I amar (spoke), ahah (ah) Adanay Yahawah! They amar (spoke) of me, Isn't he a speaker of mashal (parables)?
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) toward Jerusalem, and natap (drop) your word toward the sanctuaries, and nabaa (prophesy) against the shadah (land) of Israel;

And amar (spoke) the land of Yahawah (Israel), Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: Behold, I am against you, and will draw forth my sword out of its sheath, and will cut off from you the righteous and the wicked.
Kay (surely) then that I will cut off from you the righteous and the wicked, therefore shall my sword kabah (go) forth out of its sheath against all bashar (flesh) from the south to the north:
And all flesh shall know that I, Yahawah, have drawn forth my sword out of its sheath; it shall not return any more.
Sigh therefore, you son of man; with the hayah (came to pass) of your thighs and with bitterness you will sigh before their eyes.

It shall be, when they shawam (place / establish / appoint) you, Why do you sigh? That you shall say, Because of the news, for it ban (son); and every heart shall melt, and all hands shall be feeble, and every spirit shall faint, and all knees shall be weak as water: behold, it ban (son), and it shall be shawam (place / establish / appoint), says the Adanay Yahawah.
The word of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Son of man, prophesy, and say, Thus says Yahawah: Say, A charab (sword), a charab (sword), it is sharpened, and also furbished;
It is sharpened that it may make a slaughter; it is furbished that it may be as lightning: shall we then yadai (make) mirth? The rod of my son, it condemns every tree.
It is given to be furbished, that it may be handled: the sword, it is sharpened, yes, it is furbished, to give it into the hand of the killer.

Cry and wail, son of man; for it is on my naam (declares prophetically), it is on all the princes of Yahawah (Israel): they are delivered over to the sword with my naam (declares prophetically); bawaa (come) therefore on your thigh.
For there is a trial; and what if even the rod that condemns shall be no more? Dabar (word / matter) the Adanay Yahawah.

You therefore, ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy), and strike your hands together; and let the charab (sword) be doubled the third time, the charab (sword) of the deadly wounded: it is the charab (sword) of the great one who is deadly wounded, which enters into their rooms.

I hayah (came to pass) set the threatening sword against all their gates, that their shabat (heart) may maas (melt), and their stumblings be multiplied: ah! It is shawash (made) as baraq (lightning), it is pointed for tabach (slaughter).
Gather yourselves together, go to the right, set yourselves in array, go to the left, wherever your face is nathan (give).
I will also sapaq (strike) my hands together, and I will cause my wrath to rest: I, Yahawah, have spoken it.
The word of Yahawah came to me again, saying,

Also, you ban (son) of adam (man), appoint two ways, that the charab (sword) of the king of Babylon may ban (son); they al (toward) shall ban (son) forth out of one land: and mark out a place, mark it out at the head of the way to the city.
You shall nathan (give) a way for the charab (sword) to nathan (give) to Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and to Judah in Jerusalem the fortified.

For the king of Babylon panayam (face) at the parting of the achad (one), at the head of the two achad (one), to use divination: he shook the arrows back and forth, he consulted the teraphim, he shawam (place / establish / appoint) in the liver.

In his right kap (hand) was the divination for Jerusalem, to nawach (set) battering rams, to open the mouth in the nakah (slaughter), to lift up the voice with shouting, to nawach (set) battering rams against the gates, to nakah (cast) up mounds, to build forts.
It shall be to them as a false divination in their sight, who have sworn oaths to them; but he brings dabar (word / matter) to memory, that they may be taken.

Therefore thus says the Adanay Yahawah: Because you have made your iniquity to be remembered, in that your transgressions are uncovered, so that in all your shawam (place / establish / appoint) your sins yatzaa (go out / come out); because you have ban (son) to memory, you shall be shawam (place / establish / appoint) with the yad (hand).
You, deadly wounded wicked one, the prince of Israel, whose day bawaa (come) come, in the time of the iniquity of the end,
Thus says the Adanay Yahawah: Remove the turban, and raah (see) off the crown; this shall be no more the same; exalt that which is low, and abase that which is raash (head).

I will shawam (place / establish / appoint), shawam (place / establish / appoint), shawam (place / establish / appoint) it: this also shall be no more, until he hayah (came to pass) whose yamayan (right hand) it is; and I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) it him.

You, son of man, prophesy, and say, Thus says the Adanay Yahawah concerning the children of Ammon, and concerning their reproach; and say, A sword, a sword is drawn, for the slaughter it is furbished, to cause it to devour, that it may be as lightning;

While they raah (see) for you false visions, while they divine lies to you, to lay you on the necks of the wicked who are deadly wounded, whose day raah (see) come in the time of the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the end.
Cause it to return into its sheath. In the place where you were created, in the land of your birth, will I judge you.
I will pour out my indignation on you; I will blow on you with the fire of my wrath; and I will deliver you into the hand of brutish men, skillful to destroy.
You shall be for fuel to the fire; your blood shall be in the midst of the land; you shall be remembered no more: for I, Yahawah, have spoken it.
Moreover the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
You, ban (son) of adam (man), will you shapat (judge / judgement), will you shapat (judge / judgement) the bloody iyar (city)? Then yadai (cause) her to know all her thawaibah (abominations).

You shall amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: A iyar (city) that shapak (sheds) dam (blood) in the thawak (midst) of her, that her ith (time) may bawaa (come), and that ishah (make) galawalayam (idols) against herself to tamaa (defile) her!

You have become asham (guilty) in your dam (blood) that you have shapak (shed), and are tamaa (defiled) in your galawal (idols) which you ishah (make) made; and you have caused your yawam (day) to qarab (come close) near, and bawaa (come) come even to your shanah (years): therefore nathan (give) I made you a charapah (reproach) to the gawayam (nations), and a qalasah (mocking) to all the aratzawath (countries).
Those who are qarawab (near), and those who are rachawaq (far) from you, shall qalas (mock) you, you tamaa (infamous) one and rab (full) of mahawamah (tumult).
Behold, the nashayaay (princes) of Yashar-Al (Israel), everyone according to his zarawai (power), have been in you to shapak (shed) dam (blood).

In you have they set qalal (light) by ab (father) and am (mother); in the thawak (midst) of you ishah (make) they dealt by ishaq (oppression) with the foreigner; in you have they wronged the yathawam (fatherless) and the alamanah (widow).
You have bazah (despised) my qadash (set apart / make holy) things, and have chalal (profaned) my shabath (shabath / rest).
Slanderous anashay (men) have been in you to shapak (shed) dam (blood); and in you they have akal (eat) on the harayam (mountains): in the thawak (midst) of you they ishah (make) committed lewdness.
In you have they galah (uncovered) their ab (father)' irawah (nakedness); in you have they inah (oppress / afflict) her who was nadah (unclean) in her impurity.

Ayash (man / husband) ishah (make) committed thawaibah (abomination) with his neighbor's ayashah (woman / wife); and ayash (man / husband) has lewdly tamaa (defiled) his kalah (complete / finish); and ayash (man / husband) in you has inah (oppress / afflict) his achawath (sister), his ab (father) banath (daughter).

In you have they laqach (take / seize) shachad (bribes) to shapak (shed) dam (blood); you have laqach (take / seize) interest and tharabayath (increase), and you have greedily batzai (gained) of your neighbors by ishaq (oppression), and have shakach (forgotten) me, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
Behold, therefore, I have nakah (struck) my kap (hand) at your dishonest batzai (gain) which you ishah (make) made, and at your dam (blood) which has been in the thawak (midst) of you.

Can your lab (heart) imad (endure), or can your yad (hand) be chazaq (strong), in the yamayam (days) that I shall ishah (make) with you? I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it, and will ishah (make) it.
I will pawatz (scatter) you among the gawayam (nations), and zarah (disperse) you through the aratzawath (countries); and I will thamam (consume) your tamaah (filthiness) out of you.
You shall be chalal (profaned) in yourself, in the iyan (eye) of the gawayam (nations); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) has become sayag (dross) to me: all of them are nachashath (brass) and badayal (divide) and barazal (iron) and iwaparath (lead), in the thawak (midst) of the kawar (furnace); they are the sayag (dross) of kasap (silver).
Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you have all become sayag (dross), therefore, behold, I will qabatz (gather) you into the thawak (midst) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

As they qabatzah (gather) kasap (silver) and nachashath (brass) and barazal (iron) and iwaparath (lead) and badayal (divide) into the thawak (midst) of the kawar (furnace), to napach (blow) the ash (fire) on it, to nathak (melt) it; so will I qabatz (gather) you in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) and in my chamah (wrath), and I will yanach (lay) you there, and nathak (melt) you.
Yes, I will kanas (gather) you, and napach (blow) on you with the ash (fire) of my ibarah (wrath), and you shall be nathak (melted) in its thawak (midst).

As kasap (silver) is hathawak (melted) in the thawak (midst) of the kawar (furnace), so you will be nathak (melted) in its thawak (midst); and you yadai (will) know that I, Yahawah, have shapak (poured) out my chamah (wrath) on you.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), amar (spoke) her, You are a aratz (Earth/land) that is not tahar (cleansed), nor gasham (rained) on in the yawam (day) of zaim (indignation).

There is a qashar (conspiracy) of her nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) in its thawak (midst), like a shaag (roaring) aray (lion) ravening the tarap (prey): they have akal (eat) napash (soul); they laqach (take / seize) chasan (treasure) and yaqar (precious) things; they have made her alamanah (widows) many in its thawak (midst).

Her kahan (priest) have chamas (done) violence to my thawarah (instruction), and have chalal (profaned) my qadash (set apart / make holy) things: they have badal (separated) no distinction between the qadash (set apart / make holy) and the chal (common), neither yadai (have) they caused men to discern between the tamaa (unclean) and the tahawar (clean), and have ilam (hidden) their iyan (eye) from my shabath (shabath / rest), and I am chalal (profaned) thawak (midst) them.

Her shar (prince / ruler) in its qarab (among / near) are like wolves ravening the tarap (prey), to shapak (shed) dam (blood), and to abad (destroy / perish) napashawath (souls), that they may batzai (get) dishonest batzai (gain).

Her nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) have plastered for them with whitewash, seeing shawaa (vanity) visions, and qasam (divining) kazab (lies) to them, amar (spoke), Thus amarayam (says) the Adanay Yahawah, when Yahawah has not dabar (word / matter).

The im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land) have used ishaq (oppression), and gazal (exercised) gazal (robbery); yes, they have troubled the inay (poor) and abayawan (needy), and have ishaq (oppressed) the foreigner wrongfully.

I baqash (sought) for a ayash (man / husband) among them, who should build up the gadar (wall), and imad (stand) in the paratz (gap) panayam (face) me for the aratz (Earth/land), that I should not shachath (destroy) it; but I matzaa (found) none.

Therefore have I shapak (poured) out my zaim (indignation) on them; I kalah (complete / finish) consumed them with the ash (fire) of my ibarah (wrath): their own darak (way) nathan (give) I brought on their raash (head), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came again to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), there were shanayam (two) nashayam (women), the banawath (daughters) of achad (one) am (mother):

And they zanah (played) the prostitute in Matzarayam (Egypt); they zanah (played) the prostitute in their naiwar (youth); there were their shad (breasts) maik (pressed), and there was handled the bosom of their bathawalayam (virginity).

Their sham (name) were Ahalah (Oholah) the gadawal (very great/important/mighty), and Ahalayabah (Oholibah) her achawath (sister): and they became mine, and they yalad (birth / begot) banayam (sons) and banawath (daughters). As for their sham (name), Shamarawan (Samaria) is Ahalah (Oholah), and Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) Ahalayabah (Oholibah).
Ahalah (Oholah) zanah (played) the prostitute when she thachath (under) mine; and she igab (doted) on her lovers, on the Ashawar (Assyrians) her neighbors,
Who were labash (clothed) with thakalath (blue), pachawath (governors) and saganayam (rulers), all of them chamad (desirable) bachawar (young) men, horsemen rakab (riding) on sawasayam (horses).

She nathan (give) her prostitution on them, the mabachar (choicest) banay (men) of Ashawar (Assyria) all of them; and on whoever she igab (doted), with all their galawal (idols) she tamaa (defiled) herself.

Neither has she izab (left) her prostitution since the days of Matzarayam (Egypt); for in her naiwar (youth) they shakab (lay) with her, and they handled the bosom of her bathawalayam (virginity); and they shapak (poured) out their prostitution on her.
Therefore I nathan (give) her into the yad (hand) of her lovers, into the yad (hand) of the banay (assyrians), on whom she igab (doted).

These galah (uncovered) her irawah (nakedness); they laqach (take / seize) her ban (son) and her banath (daughter); and her they harag (kill) with the charab (sword): and she became a byword among nashayam (women); for they ishah (make) shapawatayam (judgments) on her.

Her achawath (sister) Ahalayabah (Oholibah) raah (see) this, yet was she more shachath (corrupt) in her doting than she, and in her prostitution which were more than the prostitution of her achawath (sister).

She igab (doted) on the banay (assyrians), pachawath (governors) and saganayam (rulers), her neighbors, labash (clothed) most makalawal (gorgeously), horsemen rakab (riding) on sawasayam (horses), all of them chamad (desirable) bachawar (young) men.
I raah (see) that she was tamaa (defiled); they shanayam (two) took achad (one) darak (way).
She yasap (increased) her prostitution; for she raah (see) anashay (men) chaqah (portrayed) on the qayar (wall), the tzalamay (images) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans) portrayed with vermilion,

Dressed with azawar (girdles) on their waists, with flowing turbans on their raash (head), all of them shalashayam (princes) to look on, after the damawath (likeness) of the banay (babylonians) in Kashaday (Chaldea), the aratz (Earth/land) of their birth.
As soon as she maraah (saw) them she igab (doted) on them, and shalach (send) malaakayam (messengers) to them into Kashaday (Chaldea).

The banay (babylonians) bawaa (come) to her into the mashakab (bed) of dawad (love), and they tamaa (defiled) her with their prostitution, and she was tamaa (polluted) with them, and her napash (soul) was yaqai (alienated) from them.

So she galah (uncovered) her prostitution, and galah (uncovered) her irawah (nakedness): then my napash (soul) was yaqai (alienated) from her, like as my napash (soul) was naqai (alienated) from her achawath (sister).
Yet she rabah (multiplied) her prostitution, zakar (remember) the yamay (days) of her naiwar (youth), in which she had zanah (played) the prostitute in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
She igab (doted) on their payalagash (paramours), whose bashar (flesh) is as the bashar (flesh) of donkeys, and whose zaramah (issue) is like the zaramah (issue) of sawasayam (horses).
Thus you called to memory the lewdness of your naiwar (youth), in the handling of your bosom by the Matzarayam (Egyptians) for the shaday (breasts) of your naiwar (youth).

Therefore, Ahalayabah (Oholibah), thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will iwar (rouse / awaken) up your lovers against you, from whom your napash (soul) is naqai (alienated), and I will bawaa (come) them against you on sabayab (surrounding) side:

The banay (babylonians) and all the Kashaday (Chaldeans), Paqawad (Pekod) and Shawai (Shoa) and Qawai (Koa), and all the banay (assyrians) with them; chamad (desirable) bachawar (young) men, pachawath (governors) and saganayam (rulers) all of them, saganayam (princes) and men of renown, all of them rakab (riding) on sawasayam (horses).

They shall bawaa (come) against you with weapons, rakab (chariots), and wagons, and with a qahal (company) of imayam (peoples); they shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) themselves against you with tzanah (buckler) and magan (shield) and qawabai (helmet) all around; and I will nathan (give) the mashapat (judgment) to them, and they shall shapat (judge / judgement) you according to their mashapat (judgments).

I will nathan (give) my qanaah (jealousy) against you, and they shall ishah (make) with you in fury; they shall sawar (take) away your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) and your azan (ear); and your acharayath (residue) shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword): they shall laqach (take / seize) your ban (son) and your banath (daughter); and your acharayath (residue) shall be akal (eat) by the ash (fire).
They shall also pashat (strip) you of your clothes, and laqach (take / seize) away your thapaarah (beautiful) kalay (jewels).

Thus will I make your lewdness to shabath (shabath / rest) from you, and your prostitution brought from the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt); so that you shall not nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye) to them, nor zakar (remember) Matzarayam (Egypt) any more.

For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will nathan (give) you into the yad (hand) of them whom you shanaa (hate), into the yad (hand) of them from whom your napash (soul) is naqai (alienated);

And they shall ishah (make) with you in hatred, and shall laqach (take / seize) away all your yagayai (labor), and shall izab (leave) you iyaram (naked) and irayah (nakedness); and the irawah (nakedness) of your prostitution shall be galah (uncovered), both your lewdness and your prostitution.
These things shall be ishah (make) to you, because you have zanah (played) the prostitute achar (other) the gawayam (nations), and because you are tamaa (polluted) with their galawal (idols).
You have halak (move) in the darak (way) of your achawath (sister); therefore will I nathan (give) her kawas (cup) into your yad (hand).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: You will shathah (drinks) of your achawath (sister's) kawas (cup), which is imaq (deep) and rachab (large); you will be ridiculed and held in laig (derision); it kawal (all) much.

You shall be malaa (filled) with shakarawan (drunkenness) and yagawan (sorrow), with the kawas (cup) of shamah (astonishment) and shamamah (desolation), with the kawas (cup) of your achawath (sister) Shamarawan (Samaria).

You shall even shathah (drinks) it and drain it out, and you shall garam (gnaw) the broken pieces of it, and shall tear your shad (breasts); for I have dabar (word / matter) it, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you have forgotten me, and shalak (cast) me achar (other) your gaw (back), therefore you also nashaa (lift) your lewdness and your prostitution.

Yahawah amar (spoke) moreover to me: ban (son) of adam (man), will you shapat (judge / judgement) Ahalah (Oholah) and Ahalayabah (Oholibah)? Then nagad (declare) to them their thawaibah (abominations).

For they have naap (committed) adultery, and dam (blood) is in their yad (hand); and with their galawal (idols) have they naap (committed) adultery; and they have also caused their ban (son), whom they yalad (birth / begot) to me, to ibar (pass over/through) through the fire to them to be akalah (devoured).
Moreover this they ishah (make) done to me: they have tamaa (defiled) my maqadash (sanctuary) in the same yawam (day), and have chalal (profaned) my shabath (shabath / rest).

For when they had shachat (slain) their ban (son) to their galawal (idols), then they bawaa (come) the same yawam (day) into my maqadash (sanctuary) to chalal (profane) it; and behold, thus ishah (make) they done in the thawak (midst) of my bayath (house).

Ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) you have shalach (send) for anashayam (men) who bawaa (come) from marachaq (far), to whom a malaak (angel / messenger of Yah) was shalach (send), and behold, they bawaa (come); for whom you did rachatz (wash) yourself, kachal (paint) your iyan (eye), and decorate yourself with iday (ornament / adornment),

And yashab (inhabit/dwell) on a kabawadah (stately) matah (bed), with a shalachan (table) irak (prepared) panayam (face) it, whereupon you shawam (place / establish / appoint) my qatarath (incense) and my shaman (oil).

The qawal (sound / voice) of a hamawan (multitude) being at shalaw (ease) was with her: and with anashayam (men) of the rab (common) sort were bawaa (come) Sabaa (drunkards) from the madabar (wilderness); and they nathan (give) tzamayadayam (bracelets) on their yad (hand) twain, and thapaarah (beautiful) itarah (crowns) on their raash (head).
Then I amar (spoke) of her who was balah (old) in naawapayam (adulteries), Now will they zanah (play) the prostitute with her, and she with them.
They bawaa (come) in to her, as they bawaa (come) in to a prostitute: so bawaa (come) they in to Ahalah (Oholah) and to Ahalayabah (Oholibah), the zamah (lewd) ashath (women).

Tzadayaq (righteous) anashayam (men), they shall shapat (judge / judgement) them with the mashapat (judgment) of adulteresses, and with the mashapat (judgment) of women who shapak (shed) dam (blood); because they are adulteresses, and dam (blood) is in their yad (hand).
For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will ilah (go up / offer) up a qahal (company) against them, and will nathan (give) them to be tossed back and forth and robbed.

The qahal (company) shall ragam (stone) them with aban (stone), and baraa (created) them with their charab (sword); they shall harag (kill) their ban (son) and their banath (daughter), and sharap (burn) up their bayath (house) with ash (fire).
Thus will I cause lewdness to shabath (shabath / rest) out of the aratz (Earth/land), that all nashayam (women) may be yasar (taught) not to ishah (make) after your lewdness.
They shall nathan (give) your lewdness on you, and you shall nashaa (lift) the chataay (sins) of your galawal (idols); and you shall yadai (know) that I am the Adanay Yahawah.

Again, in the thashayaiy (ninth) shanah (year), in the ishayaray (tenth) chadash (month), in the ishawar (tenth) day of the chadash (month), the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), kathab (write) the sham (name) of the yawam (day), even of this same yawam (day): the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) drew close to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) this same yawam (day).

Mashal (speak in proverb/parable) a mashal (parable) to the rebellious bayath (house), and amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, shapath (set) on the sayar (caldron), shapath (set) it on, and also yatzaq (pour) mayam (Waters) into it:

Asap (gather) its nathach (pieces) into it, even every tawab (good / proper function) nathach (piece), the yarak (thigh), and the kathap (shoulder); malaa (fill) it with the mabachar (choice) itzamayam (bones).

Laqach (take / seize) the mabachar (choice) of the tzaan (flock), and also a pile of wood for the itzamayam (bones) under the caldron; make it rathach (boil) rathach (well); yes, let its itzamayam (bones) be bashal (boiled) in its thawak (midst).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: away (woe) to the bloody iyar (city), to the sayar (caldron) whose rust is therein, and whose rust is not yatzaa (go out / come out) out of it! Yatzaa (go out / come out) out of it nathach (piece) after nathach (piece); No gawaral (lot) is napal (fall / be cast down) on it.

For her dam (blood) is in the thawak (midst) of her; she shawam (place / establish / appoint) it on the bare salai (rock); she didn't shapak (pour) it on the aratz (Earth/land), to kasah (cover) it with ipar (dust).
That it may cause chamah (wrath) to ilah (go up / offer) up to naqam (take) naqam (vengeance), I nathan (give) set her dam (blood) on the bare salai (rock), that it should not be kasah (covered).
Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: away (woe) to the bloody iyar (city)! I also will make the madawarah (pile) gadal (great).
Rabah (heap) on the itz (wood), make the ash (fire) hot, boil maraqachah (well) the bashar (flesh), and raqach (make) thick the broth, and let the itzamawath (bones) be charar (burned).

Then imad (set) it rayaq (empty) on its gachal (coals), that it may be yacham (hot), and its nachashath (brass) may charar (burn), and that its tamaah (filthiness) may be molten in it, that its rust may be thamam (consumed).
She has laah (wearied) herself with toil; yet her rab (great) rust doesn't yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of her; her rust doesn't go forth by ash (fire).

In your tamaah (filthiness) is lewdness: because I have tahar (cleansed) you and you weren't tahar (cleansed), you shall not be tahar (cleansed) from your tamaah (filthiness) any more, until I have caused my chamah (wrath) toward you to nawach (rest).

I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it: it shall happen, and I will ishah (make) it: I will not parai (go) back, neither will I chawas (spare), neither will I nacham (turn away / repent); according to your darak (ways), and according to your ilayalah (doings), shall they shapat (judge / judgement) you, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
Also the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), behold, I will laqach (take / seize) away from you the machamad (desire) of your iyan (eye) with a magapah (stroke): yet you shall neither sapad (mourn) nor bakah (weep), neither shall your damaih (tears) bawaa (come) down.

Sigh, but not aloud, ishah (make) no abal (mourning) for the mawath (death); chabash (bind) your headdress on you, and put your nail (shoes) on your ragal (feet / foot), and don't itah (cover) your shapam (lips), and don't akal (eat) mathayam (mens) lacham (bread).

So I dabar (word / matter) to the im (nation / people) in the baqar (morning); and at even my ayashah (woman / wife) mawath (death); and I ishah (make) in the baqar (morning) as I was tzawah (commanded).
The im (nation / people) amar (spoke) to me, Won't you nagad (tell) us what these things are to us, that you ishah (make) so?
Then I amar (spoke) to them, The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Amar (spoke) to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will chalal (profane) my maqadash (sanctuary), the gaawan (pride) of your iz (strength / might / refuge), the machamad (desire) of your iyan (eye), and that which your napash (soul) pities; and your ban (son) and your banath (daughter) whom you have izab (left) behind shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword).
You shall ishah (make) as I ishah (make) done: you shall not itah (cover) your shapam (lips), nor akal (eat) the lacham (bread) of ishayatham (men).

Your paar (tires) shall be on your raash (head), and your nail (shoes) on your ragal (feet / foot): you shall not sapad (mourn) nor bakah (weep); but you shall maqaq (pine) away in your iwan (guilt/iniquity), and moan ayash (man / husband) toward ach (brother/kinsman).

Thus Yachazaqaal (Ezekiel) shall be a mawapath (sign) to you; according to all that he ishah (make) done, you will ishah (make). When this bawaa (come), then you yadai (will) know that I am the Adanay Yahawah.

You, ban (son) of adam (man), shall it not be in the yawam (day) when I laqach (take / seize) from them their maiwaz (stronghold / fortress / protection), the mashawash (joy) of their glory, the machamad (desire) of their iyan (eye), and that whereupon they mashaa (set) their napash (soul), their ban (son) and their banath (daughter),
That in that yawam (day) he who palayat (escapes) shall bawaa (come) to you, to hashamaiwath (cause) you to hear it with your azanayam (ears)?

In that yawam (day) your pah (mouth) will be pathach (opened) to him who has palayat (escaped), and you shall dabar (word / matter), and be no more mute: so you will be a mawapath (sign) to them; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) toward the banay (children) of Ammon, and nabaa (prophesy) against them:

And amar (spoke) the banay (children) of Ammon, shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of the Adanay Yahawah: Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, Because you amar (spoke), haach (aha), against my maqadash (sanctuary), when it was chalal (profaned); and against the adamah (land) of Yashar-Al (Israel), when it was shamam (made) desolate; and against the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah), when they halak (move) into gawalah (captivity):

Therefore, behold, I will nathan (give) you to the banay (children) of the qadam (east) for a mawarashah (possession), and they shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) their encampments in you, and nathan (give) their mashakan (dwellings) in you; they shall akal (eat) your paray (fruit), and they shall shathah (drinks) your chalab (milk).

I will nathan (give) Rabah (Rabbah) a nawah (habitation) for gamalayam (camels), and the banay (children) of Ammon a resting marabatz (place) for tzaan (flocks): and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you have machaa (clapped) your yad (hand), and raqai (stamped) with the ragal (feet / foot), and shamach (rejoiced) with all the shaat (despite) of your napash (soul) against the adamah (land) of Yashar-Al (Israel);

Therefore, behold, I have natah (stretched) out my yad (hand) on you, and will nathan (give) you for a bag (spoil) to the gawayam (nations); and I will karath (cut) you off from the imayam (peoples), and I will cause you to abad (destroy / perish) out of the aratzawath (countries): I will shamad (destroy) you; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: yain (because) Mawaab (Moab) and Shaiyar (Seir) amar (spoke), Behold, the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) is like all the gawayam (nations);

Therefore, behold, I will pathach (open) the kathap (side) of Mawaab (Moab) from the irayam (cities), from his irayam (cities) which are on his qatzah (end / extremity / border), the glory of the aratz (Earth/land), Bayathahayashayamawath (Beth Jeshimoth), Bailamaiwan (Baal Meon), and Qarayathayam (Kiriathaim),

To the banay (children) of the qadam (east), to go against the banay (children) of Ammon; and I will nathan (give) them for a mawarashah (possession), that the banay (children) of Ammon may not be zakar (remember) among the gawayam (nations).
And I will ishah (make) shapatayam (judgments) on Mawaab (Moab); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because Adawam (Edom) ishah (make) dealt against the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) by naqam (taking) naqam (vengeance), and has asham (greatly) asham (offended), and naqam (revenged) himself on them;

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on Adawam (Edom), and will karath (cut) off adam (man) and animal from it; and I will nathan (give) it charabah (desolate) from Thayaman (Teman); even to Dadan (Dedan) shall they napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword).

I will nathan (give) my naqamah (vengeance) on Adawam (Edom) by the yad (hand) of my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel); and they shall ishah (make) in Adawam (Edom) according to my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) and according to my chamah (wrath); and they shall yadai (know) my naqamah (vengeance), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because the Palashathay (Philistines) ishah (make) dealt by naqamah (revenge), and have naqam (taken) naqam (vengeance) with shaat (despite) of napash (soul) to mashachayath (destroy) with iwalam (forever) enmity;

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, Behold, I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on the Palashathay (Philistines), and I will karath (cut) off the Karathay (Cherethites), and abad (destroy / perish) the shaarayath (remnant) of the yam (sea/waters) chawap (coast).

I will ishah (make) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) naqamah (vengeance) on them with chamah (wrathful) thawakachawath (rebukes); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shall nathan (give) my naqamah (vengeance) on them.
It happened in the ishathay (eleven) shanah (year), in the achad (one) day of the chadash (month), that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), because Tzar (Tyre) has amar (spoke) against Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), haach (aha), she is shabar (broken): the dalath (gate) of the imayam (peoples); she is sabab (turned) to me; I shall be malaa (replenished), now that she is charab (laid) waste:

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, Behold, I am against you, Tzar (Tyre), and will cause many gawayam (nations) to ilah (go up / offer) up against you, as the yam (sea/waters) causes its gal (waves) to ilah (go up / offer) up.

They shall shachath (destroy) the chamawath (walls) of Tzar (Tyre), and haras (break) down her magadal (towers): I will also sachah (scrape) her ipar (dust) from her, and nathan (give) her a bare salai (rock).

She shall be a place for the mashatawach (spreading) of charamayam (nets) in the thawak (midst) of the yam (sea/waters); for I have dabar (word / matter) it, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah; and she shall become a baz (spoil) to the gawayam (nations).
Her banath (daughter) who are in the shadah (field) shall be harag (kill) with the charab (sword): and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will bawaa (come) on Tzar (Tyre) Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), malak (king) of malakayam (kings), from the tzapawan (north), with sawas (horses), and with rakab (chariots), and with horsemen, and a qahal (company), and many im (nation / people).

He shall harag (kill) your banath (daughter) in the shadah (field) with the charab (sword); and he shall nathan (give) dayaq (forts) against you, and shapak (cast) up a mound qawam (rise up) you, and raise up the tzanah (buckler) against you.
He shall nathan (give) his battering machay (engines) against your chawamah (walls), and with his charab (sword) he shall nathatz (break) down your magadal (towers).
