By reason of the shapaih (abundance) of his sawas (horses) their abaq (dust) shall kasah (cover) you: your chawamah (walls) shall raish (shake) at the qawal (sound / voice) of the horsemen, and of the wagons, and of the rakab (chariots), when he shall bawaa (come) into your shair (gates), as mabawaay (men) enter into a iyar (city) in which is baqai (made) a breach.

With the parasawath (hoofs) of his sawas (horses) shall he ramas (tread) down all your chawatz (streets); he shall harag (kill) your im (nation / people) with the charab (sword); and the matzabawath (pillars) of your iz (strength / might / refuge) shall yarad (go) down to the aratz (Earth/land).

They shall shalal (make) a spoil of your riches, and make a bazaz (prey) of your rakalah (merchandise); and they shall haras (break) down your chawamah (walls), and nathatz (destroy) your chamadah (pleasant) bathay (houses); and they shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) your aban (stone) and your itz (timber) and your ipar (dust) in the thawak (midst) of the mayam (Waters).
I will cause the hamawan (noise) of your shayar (song) to shabath (shabath / rest); and the qawal (sound / voice) of your kanawar (harps) shall be no more shamai (hearken / hear).

I will nathan (give) you a bare salai (rock); you shall be a place for the mashatawach (spreading) of charamayam (nets); you shall be banah (build) no more: for I Yahawah have dabar (word / matter) it, naam (declares prophetically) the Adawan Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah to Tzar (Tyre): shall not the ayayam (islands) raish (shake) at the qawal (sound / voice) of your mapalath (fall), when the chalal (wounded) anaq (groan), when the harag (kill) is harag (kill) in the thawak (midst) of you?

Then all the nashayaay (princes) of the yam (sea/waters) shall yarad (come) down from their kasaa (thrones), and sawar (lay) aside their maiyal (robes), and pashat (strip) off their embroidered bagaday (garments): they shall labash (clothe) themselves with charadah (trembling); they shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the aratz (Earth/land), and shall charad (tremble) every ragai (in an instance), and be shamam (astonished) at you.

They shall nashaa (lift) up a qayanah (lamentation) over you, and amar (spoke) you, How you are abad (destroy / perish), who were yashab (inhabit/dwell) by seafaring yamayam (men), the halal (praise) iyar (city), who was chazaq (strong) in the yam (sea/waters), she and her yashab (inhabit/dwell), who nathan (give) their chathayath (terror) to be on all who lived there!
Now shall the ayan (islands) charad (tremble) in the yawam (day) of your mapalath (fall); yes, the ayan (islands) that are in the yam (sea/waters) shall be bahal (dismayed) at your departure.

For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: When I shall nathan (give) you a charab (desolate) iyar (city), like the irayam (cities) that are not yashab (inhabit/dwell); when I shall ilah (go up / offer) up the thahawam (depths) on you, and the rab (great) mayam (Waters) shall kasah (cover) you;

Then will I yarad (bring) you down with those who descend into the bawar (pit), to the im (nation / people) of iwalam (forever) time, and will make you to dwell in the lower thachathayawath (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land), in the places that are charabah (desolate) of iwalam (forever), with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit), that you be not yashab (inhabit/dwell); and I will nathan (give) glory in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life):

I will nathan (give) you a balahah (terror), and you shall no more have any being; though you are baqash (sought) for, yet you will iwalam (forever) be matzaa (found) again, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came again to me, amar (spoke),
You, ban (son) of adam (man), nashaa (lift) up a qayanah (lamentation) over Tzar (Tyre);

And amar (spoke) Tzar (Tyre), you who yashab (inhabit/dwell) at the mabawaah (entry) of the yam (sea/waters), who are the rakal (merchant) of the imayam (peoples) to many ayayam (islands), thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: You, Tzar (Tyre), have amar (spoke), I am kalayal (perfect) in yapay (beauty).
Your gabawal (border/boundary) are in the lab (heart) of the yamayam (seas); your banah (build) have kalal (perfected) your yapay (beauty).
They have banah (build) all your planks of barawash (fir) trees from Shanayar (Senir); they have laqach (take / seize) a araz (cedar) from Labanawan (Lebanon) to ishah (make) a tharan (mast) for you.

Of the alawanayam (oaks) of Bashan (Bashan) ishah (make) they made your mashawat (oars); they ishah (make) made your benches of shan (ivory) inlaid in Ashar (boxwood), from the ayay (islands) of Kathay (Kittim).

Of shash (six) linen with embroidered raqamah (work) from Matzarayam (Egypt) was your nas (sail), that it might be to you for a banner; thakalath (blue) and aragaman (purple) from the ayay (islands) of Alayashah (Elishah) was your awning.
The yashabay (inhabitants) of Tzayadawan (Sidon) and Arawad (Arvad) were your shatayam (rowers): your chakam (wise) men, Tzar (Tyre), were in you, they were your chabal (pilots).

The zaqan (old) men of Gabal (Gebal) and the chakam (wise) men of it were in you your repairers of anayah (ship) seams: all the ships of the yam (sea/waters) with their malach (mariners) were in you to deal in your mairab (merchandise).

Paras (Persia) and Lawad (Lud) and Pawat (Put) were in your chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), your chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) of malachamah (war): they hanged the magan (shield) and kawabai (helmet) in you; they nathan (give) forth your hadar (glory / majesty / splendor).

The banay (men) of Arawad (Arvad) with your chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) were on your chawamah (walls) all around, and Gamad (valorous) men were in your magadal (towers); they hanged their shalat (shields) on your chawamah (walls) all around; they have kalal (perfected) your yapay (beauty).

Tharashayash (Tarshish) was your sachar (merchant) by reason of the rab (multitude) of all kinds of riches; with kasap (silver), barazal (iron), badayal (divide), and iwaparath (lead), they nathan (give) for your izabawan (wares).

Yawan (Javan), Thawabal (Tubal), and Mashak (Meshech), they were your traffickers; they nathan (give) the napash (soul) of adam (men) and kalay (vessels) of nachashath (brass) for your mairab (merchandise).
They of the bayath (house) of Thawagaramah (Togarmah) nathan (give) for your wares with sawasayam (horses) and war horses and paradayam (mules).

The banay (men) of Dadan (Dedan) were your traffickers; many ayayam (islands) were the market of your yad (hand): they shawab (turn back / repent) you in exchange qaranawath (horns) of shan (ivory) and haban (ebony).

Aram (Syria) was your sachar (merchant) by reason of the rab (multitude) of your handiworks: they nathan (give) for your izabawan (wares) with napak (emeralds), aragaman (purple), and embroidered raqamah (work), and bawatz (fine) linen, and raamah (coral), and rubies.

Yahawadah (Judah), and the aratz (Earth/land) of Yashar-Al (Israel), they were your traffickers: they nathan (give) for your mairab (merchandise) chatah (wheat) of Manayath (Minnith), and confections, and dabash (honey), and shaman (oil), and tzaray (balm).

Damashaq (Damascus) was your sachar (merchant) for the rab (multitude) of your handiworks, by reason of the rab (multitude) of all kinds of riches, with the yayan (wine) of Chalabawan (Helbon), and tzachar (bright / glisten) tzamar (wool).
Wadan (Vedan) and Yawan (Javan) traded with yarn for your izabawan (wares): ishawath (bright) barazal (iron), qadah (cassia), and qanah (calamus), were among your mairab (merchandise).
Dadan (Dedan) was your trafficker in chapash (precious) bagaday (cloths) for riding.

Irab (Arabia), and all the nashayaay (princes) of Qadar (Kedar), they were the sacharay (merchants) of your yad (hand); in karayam (lambs), and ayalayam (rams), and ithawadayam (goats), in these were they your sacharay (merchants).

The traffickers of Shabaa (Sheba) and Raimah (Raamah), they were your traffickers; they nathan (give) for your izabawan (wares) with the raash (head) of all basham (spices), and with all yaqar (precious) aban (stone), and zahab (gold).
Charan (Haran) and Kanah (Canneh) and Idan (Eden), the traffickers of Shabaa (Sheba), Ashawar (Asshur) and Kalamad (Chilmad), were your traffickers.

These were your traffickers in choice wares, in wrappings of thakalath (blue) and embroidered raqamah (work), and in ganazay (chests) of barawam (rich) clothing, chabash (bound) with chabalayam (cords) and araz (made) of cedar, among your marakalath (merchandise).

The anayawath (ships) of Tharashayash (Tarshish) were your caravans for your mairab (merchandise): and you were malaa (replenished), and made very kabad (glorious) in the lab (heart) of the yamayam (seas).
Your shatayam (rowers) bawaa (come) brought you into rab (great) mayam (Waters): the qadayam (east) rawach (spirit / wind) has shabar (broken) you in the lab (heart) of the yamayam (seas).

Your riches, and your izabawan (wares), your mairab (merchandise), your malach (mariners), and your chabal (pilots), your repairers of ship seams, and the dealers in your mairab (merchandise), and all your machazayaqay (men) of malachamah (war), who are in you, with all your qahal (company) which is in the thawak (midst) of you, shall napal (fall / be cast down) into the lab (heart) of the yamayam (seas) in the yawam (day) of your mapalath (ruin).
At the qawal (sound / voice) of the zaiq (cry) of your chabal (pilots) the magarashawath (suburbs) shall raish (shake).

All who thapash (handled) the mashawat (oar), the malachayam (mariners), and all the chabalay (pilots) of the yam (sea/waters), shall yarad (come) down from their anayah (ships); they shall imad (stand) on the aratz (Earth/land),

And shall cause their qawal (sound / voice) to be shamai (hearken / hear) over you, and shall zaiq (cry) bitterly, and shall ilah (go up / offer) up ipar (dust) on their raash (head), they shall wallow themselves in the ashes:
And they shall make themselves qarach (bald) for you, and clothe them with sackcloth, and they shall bakah (weep) for you in bitterness of napash (soul) with mar (bitter) masapad (mourning).

In their nay (wailing) they shall nashaa (lift) up a qayanah (lamentation) for you, and qawan (lament) over you, saying, "Who is there like Tzar (Tyre), like her who is brought to silence in the thawak (midst) of the yam (sea/waters)?

When your izabawan (wares) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the yamayam (seas), you shabai (filled) many imayam (peoples); you enriched the malakay (kings) of the aratz (Earth/land) with the rab (multitude) of your riches and of your mairab (merchandise).

In the ith (time) that you were shabar (broken) by the yamayam (seas) in the maimaqay (depths) of the mayam (Waters), your mairab (merchandise) and all your qahal (company) napal (fall / be cast down) in your thawak (midst).

All the yashabay (inhabitants) of the ayayam (islands) are shamam (astonished) at you, and their malak (king) are shair (horribly) shair (dread / storm / horror); they are raim (troubled) in their panayam (face).
The sacharayam (merchants) among the imayam (peoples) sharaq (hiss) at you; you are become a balahah (terror), and you shall nevermore have any being.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came again to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), amar (spoke) the nagayad (prince) of Tzar (Tyre), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because your lab (heart) is gabah (lifted) up, and you have amar (spoke), I am a Al, I yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the mawashab (seat) of Alahayam, in the lab (heart) of the yamayam (seas); yet you are adam (man), and not Al, though you nathan (give) your lab (heart) as the lab (heart) of Alahayam—
Behold, you are wiser than Danayaal (Daniel); there is no satham (secret) that is satham (hidden) from you;
By your chakamah (wisdom) and by your thabawan (understanding) you ishah (make) gotten yourself riches, and ishah (make) gotten zahab (gold) and kasap (silver) into your awatzar (treasures);
By your rab (great) chakamah (wisdom) and by your rakalah (traffic) you rabah (have) increased your riches, and your labab (heart) is gabah (lifted) up because of your riches—
Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you nathan (give) set your lab (heart) as the labab (heart) of Alahayam,

Therefore, behold, I will bawaa (come) strangers on you, the irayatz (terrible) of the gawayam (nations); and they shall rawaq (draw) their charab (sword) against the yapay (beauty) of your chakamah (wisdom), and they shall chalal (defile) your yapaih (brightness).
They shall yarad (bring) you down to the shachath (pit); and you shall mawath (death) the mamawath (death) of those who are chalal (slain), in the lab (heart) of the yamayam (seas).
Will you yet amar (spoke) panayam (face) him who harag (kill) you, I am Alahayam? But you are adam (man), and not Al, in the yad (hand) of him who chalal (wounds) you.
You shall mawath (death) the mawath (death) of the iral (uncircumcised) by the yad (hand) of strangers: for I have dabar (word / matter) it, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
Moreover the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), nashaa (lift) up a qayanah (lamentation) over the malak (king) of Tzar (Tyre), and amar (spoke) him, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: You chatham (seal) up the thakanayath (sum), malaa (full) of chakamah (wisdom), and kalayal (perfect) in yapay (beauty).

You were in Idan (Eden), the gan (garden) of Alahayam; every yaqar (precious) aban (stone) adorned you: ruby, patadah (topaz), emerald, chrysolite, shaham (Onyx), yashapah (jasper), sapayar (sapphire), turquoise, and beryl. Zahab (gold) malaakah (work) of tambourines and of naqab (pipes) was in you. In the yawam (day) that you were baraa (created) they were kawan (prepared).

You were the mamashach (anointed) karawab (cherub) who sakak (covers): and I nathan (give) you, so that you were on the qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain) of Alahayam; you have halak (move) up and down in the thawak (midst) of the abanay (stones) of ash (fire).
You were thamayam (complete / whole) in your darak (ways) from the yawam (day) that you were baraa (created), until iwal (unrighteousness) was matzaa (found) in you.

By the rab (abundance) of your rakalah (traffic) they malaa (filled) the thawak (midst) of you with chamas (violence), and you have chataa (sinned): therefore I have cast you as chalal (profane) out of the har (mountain) of Alahayam; and I abad (destroy / perish) destroyed you, sakak (covering) karawab (cherub), from the thawak (midst) of the abanay (stones) of ash (fire).

Your lab (heart) was gabah (lifted) up because of your yapay (beauty); you have shachath (corrupted) your chakamah (wisdom) by reason of your yapaih (brightness): I have shalak (cast) you to the aratz (Earth/land); I nathan (give) laid you panayam (face) malakayam (kings), that they may raah (see) you.

By the rab (multitude) of your iwan (guilt/iniquity), in the iwal (unrighteousness) of your rakalah (traffic), you have chalal (profaned) your maqadash (sanctuaries); therefore yatzaa (go out / come out) I brought forth a ash (fire) from the thawak (midst) of you; it has akal (eat) you, and I nathan (give) turned you to ashes on the aratz (Earth/land) in the iyan (eye) of all those who raah (see) you.
All those who yadai (know) you among the imayam (peoples) shall be shamam (astonished) at you: you have become a balahah (terror), and you shall nevermore have any being.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) toward Tzayadawan (Sidon), and nabaa (prophesy) against it,

And amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against you, Tzayadawan (Sidon); and I will be kabad (glorified) in the thawak (midst) of you; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shall ishah (make) executed shapatayam (judgments) in her, and shall be qadash (set apart / make holy) in her.

For I will shalach (send) dabar (word / matter) into her, and dam (blood) into her chawatz (streets); and the chalal (wounded) shall napal (fall / be cast down) in the thawak (midst) of her, with the charab (sword) on her on sabayab (surrounding) side; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

There shall be no more a pricking salawan (brier) to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), nor a hurting qawatz (thorn) of any that are around them, that scorned them; and they shall yadai (know) that I am the Adanay Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: When I shall have qabatz (gathered) the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) from the imayam (peoples) among whom they are pawatz (scattered), and shall be qadash (set apart / make holy) in them in the iyan (eye) of the gawayam (nations), then shall they yashab (inhabit/dwell) in their own adamah (land) which I nathan (give) to my ibad (servant) Yaiqab (Jacob).

They shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely therein; yes, they shall banah (build) bathayam (houses), and natai (plant) karamayam (vineyards), and shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely, when I ishah (make) executed shapatayam (judgments) on all those who do them despite all around them; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah their Alahayam.
In the ishayaray (tenth) shanah (year), in the ishayaray (tenth) month, on the shanayam (two) day of the chadash (month), the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

"Ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) against Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and nabaa (prophesy) against him and against all Matzarayam (Egypt).

Dabar (word / matter) and amar (spoke), ‘Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: "Behold, I am against you, Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) thanayan (monster) that rabatz (lies) in the thawak (midst) of his yaar (rivers), that has amar (spoke), ‘My yaar (river) is my own, and I ishah (make) made it for myself.'

I will nathan (give) chachayayam (hooks) in your lachay (jaws), and I will make the dagah (fish) of your yaar (rivers) dabaq (stick) to your qashaqashath (scales); and I will ilah (go up / offer) you up out of the thawak (midst) of your yaar (rivers), with all the dagah (fish) of your yaar (rivers) which dabaq (stick) to your qashaqashath (scales).

I'll natash (cast) you forth into the madabar (wilderness), you and all the dagah (fish) of your yaar (rivers). You'll napal (fall / be cast down) on the panayam (face) shadah (field). You won't be asap (brought) together, nor qabatz (gathered). I nathan (give) given you for akalah (food) to the animals of the aratz (Earth/land) and to the iwap (flying) of the sky.
All the yashabay (inhabitants) of Matzarayam (Egypt) yadai (will) know that I am Yahawah, because they have been a mashainah (staff) of qanah (reed) to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

When they thapash (took) hold of you by your kap (hand), you ratzatz (broke), and baqai (tore) all their kathap (shoulders); and when they shain (leaned) on you, you shabar (broke), and paralyzed all of their thighs."
Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: "Behold, I will bawaa (come) a charab (sword) on you, and will karath (cut) off adam (man) and animal from you.

The aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) shall be a shamamah (desolation) and a charabah (waste); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah. Because he has amar (spoke), ‘The yaar (river) is mine, and I ishah (make) made it;'

Therefore, behold, I am against you, and against your yaar (rivers), and I will nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) an utter charabah (waste) and shamamah (desolation), from the Magadawal (tower) of Sawanah (Seveneh) even to the gabawal (border/boundary) of Kawash (Ethiopia).

No ragal (feet / foot) of adam (man) shall ibar (pass over/through) through it, nor ragal (feet / foot) of animal shall ibar (pass over/through) through it, neither shall it be yashab (inhabit/dwell) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years).

I will nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) a shamamah (desolation) in the thawak (midst) of the aratzawath (countries) that are shamam (desolate); and her irayam (cities) thawak (midst) the irayam (cities) that are charab (laid) waste shall be a shamamah (desolation) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years); and I will pawatz (scatter) the Matzarayam (Egyptians) among the gawayam (nations), and will zarah (disperse) them through the aratzawath (countries)."

For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: "At the qatz (end) of arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years) will I qabatz (gather) the Matzarayam (Egyptians) from the imayam (peoples) where they were pawatz (scattered);

And I will shawab (turn back / repent) back the shabawath (captivity) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and will cause them to shawab (turn back / repent) into the aratz (Earth/land) of Patharawas (Pathros), into the aratz (Earth/land) of their makawarah (birth); and they shall be there a shapal (base) mamalakah (kingdom).

It shall be the shapal (base) of the mamalakawath (kingdoms); neither shall it any more nashaa (lift) itself up above the gawayam (nations): and I will mait (diminish) them, that they shall no more radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) over the gawayam (nations).

It shall be no more the mabatach (confidence) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), zakar (remember) iwan (guilt/iniquity) to memory, when they panah (turn) to look achar (other) them: and they shall yadai (know) that I am the Adanay Yahawah."'"

It came to pass in the shabai (seven) and isharayam (twenty) shanah (year), in the raashawan (first) month, in the achad (one) day of the chadash (month), the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) ibad (servant) his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) to ibad (servant) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) ibadah (service) against Tzar (Tyre): every raash (head) was qarach (made) bald, and every kathap (shoulder) was worn; yet had he no shakar (wages), nor his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), from Tzar (Tyre), for the ibadah (service) that he had ibad (servant) against it.

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) to Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon); and he shall nashaa (lift) off her hamawan (multitude), and nashaa (lift) her shalal (spoil), and take her baz (prey); and it shall be the shakar (wages) for his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor).

I nathan (give) given him the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) as his recompense for which he ibad (servant), because they ishah (make) for me, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

In that yawam (day) will I tzamach (cause) a qaran (horn) to tzamach (bud) forth to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and I will nathan (give) you the pathachawan (opening) of the pah (mouth) in their thawak (midst); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came again to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy), and amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Wail, Alas for the yawam (day)!
For the yawam (day) is qarawab (near), even the yawam (day) of Yahawah is qarawab (near); it shall be a yawam (day) of inan (cloud), a ith (time) of the gawayam (nations).

A charab (sword) shall bawaa (come) on Matzarayam (Egypt), and anguish shall be in Kawash (Ethiopia), when the chalal (slain) shall napal (fall / be cast down) in Matzarayam (Egypt); and they shall laqach (take / seize) away her hamawan (multitude), and her yasawad (foundations) shall be haras (broken) down.

Kawash (Ethiopia), and Pawat (Put), and Lawad (Lud), and all the mixed banay (people), and Cub, and the banay (children) of the aratz (Earth/land) that is allied with them, shall napal (fall / be cast down) with them by the charab (sword).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: They also who samak (uphold) Matzarayam (Egypt) shall napal (fall / be cast down); and the gaawan (pride) of her iz (strength / might / refuge) shall yarad (come) down: from the Magadawal (tower) of Sawanah (Seveneh) shall they napal (fall / be cast down) in it by the charab (sword), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

They shall be shamam (desolate) in the thawak (midst) of the aratzawath (countries) that are shamam (desolate); and her irayam (cities) shall be in the thawak (midst) of the irayam (cities) that are charab (wasted).
They shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I nathan (give) set a ash (fire) in Matzarayam (Egypt), and all her helpers are shabar (destroyed).

In that yawam (day) shall malaakayam (messengers) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from panayam (face) me in tzayam (ships) to make the batach (careless) Kawash (Ethiopians) charad (afraid); and there shall be anguish on them, as in the yawam (day) of Matzarayam (Egypt); for, behold, it bawaa (come).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will also make the hamawan (multitude) of Matzarayam (Egypt) to shabath (shabath / rest), by the yad (hand) of Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon).

He and his im (nation / people) with him, the irayatz (terrible) of the gawayam (nations), shall be bawaa (come) in to shachath (destroy) the aratz (Earth/land); and they shall rawaq (draw) their charab (sword) against Matzarayam (Egypt), and malaa (fill) the aratz (Earth/land) with the chalal (slain).

I will nathan (give) the yaarayam (rivers) charabah (dry), and will makar (sell) the aratz (Earth/land) into the yad (hand) of rai (evil) men; and I will make the aratz (Earth/land) shamam (desolate), and malaa (all) that is therein, by the yad (hand) of strangers: I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will also abad (destroy / perish) the galawalayam (idols), and I will cause the alayalayam (images) to shabath (shabath / rest) from Nap (Memphis); and there shall be no more a nashayaa (prince) from the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt): and I will nathan (give) a yaraah (fear) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
I will make Patharawas (Pathros) shamam (desolate), and will nathan (give) a ash (fire) in Tzain (Zoan), and will ishah (make) shapatayam (judgments) on No.
I will shapak (pour) my chamah (wrath) on sayan (sin), the stronghold of Matzarayam (Egypt); and I will karath (cut) off the hamawan (multitude) of No.

I will nathan (give) a ash (fire) in Matzarayam (Egypt): sayan (sin) shall be in chawal (great) anguish, and No shall be baqai (broken) up; and Nap (Memphis) shall have tzaray (adversaries) in the yawamam (by day).
The bachawar (young) men of Awan (Aven) and of Payabasath (Pibeseth) shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword); and these cities shall yalak (go) into shabay (captivity).

At Thachapanachas (Tehaphnehes) also the yawam (day) shall withdraw itself, when I shall shabar (break) there the matawath (yokes) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and the gaawan (pride) of her iz (strength / might / refuge) shall shabath (shabath / rest) in her: as for her, a inan (cloud) shall kasah (cover) her, and her banath (daughter) shall yalak (go) into shabay (captivity).
Thus will I ishah (make) shapatayam (judgments) on Matzarayam (Egypt); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
It happened in the eleventh shanah (year), in the raashawan (first) month, in the shabai (seven) day of the chadash (month), that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), I have shabar (broken) the zarawai (arm) of Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt); and behold, it has not been chabash (bound) up, to apply rapaah (healing) medicines, to shawam (place / establish / appoint) a bandage to chabash (bind) it, that it be chazaq (strong) to thapash (hold) the charab (sword).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and will shabar (break) his zarawai (arms), the chazaq (strong) arm, and that which was shabar (broken); and I will cause the charab (sword) to napal (fall / be cast down) out of his yad (hand).
I will pawatz (scatter) the Matzarayam (Egyptians) among the gawayam (nations), and will zarah (disperse) them through the aratzawath (countries).

I will chazaq (strengthen) the zaraiwath (arms) of the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), and nathan (give) my charab (sword) in his yad (hand): but I will shabar (break) the zaraiwath (arms) of Paraih (Pharaoh), and he shall naaq (groan) panayam (face) him with the naaqawath (groanings) of a deadly chalal (wounded) man.

I will chazaq (hold) up the zaraiwath (arms) of the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon); and the zaraiwath (arms) of Paraih (Pharaoh) shall napal (fall / be cast down) down; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shall nathan (give) my charab (sword) into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon), and he shall natah (stretch) it out on the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).
I will pawatz (scatter) the Matzarayam (Egyptians) among the gawayam (nations), and zarah (disperse) them through the aratzawath (countries); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
It happened in the eleventh shanah (year), in the shalayashay (third) month, in the achad (one) day of the chadash (month), that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), amar (spoke) Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and to his hamawan (multitude): Whom are you damah (like) in your gadal (greatness)?

Behold, the Ashawar (Assyrian) was a araz (cedar) in Labanawan (Lebanon) with yapah (beautiful) branches, and with a forest-like Charash (shade), and of gabah (high) qawamah (stature); and its tzamarath (top) was among the ibath (thick) boughs.

The mayam (Waters) gadal (nourished) it, the thahawam (depths) rawam (will lift up) it to grow: its nahar (rivers) halak (move) all around its plantation; and it shalach (send) out its channels to all the itzay (trees) of the shadah (field).

Therefore its qawamah (stature) was gabah (exalted) above all the itzay (trees) of the shadah (field); and its saraipah (boughs) were rabah (multiplied), and its branches arak (became) long by reason of many mayam (Waters), when it shalach (send) them forth.

All the iwap (flying) of the sky qanan (made) their nests in its saipah (boughs); and under its branches all the animals of the shadah (field) yalad (birth / begot) forth their young; and all rab (great) gawayam (nations) lived under its tzal (shadow).
Thus was it yapah (beautiful) in its gadal (greatness), in the arak (length) of its branches; for its sharash (root) was by many mayam (Waters).

The arazayam (cedars) in the gan (garden) of Alahayam could not imam (hide) it; the barawash (fir) trees were not damah (like) its saipah (boughs), and the plane iramanayam (trees) were not as its branches; nor was any itz (tree) in the gan (garden) of Alahayam damah (like) it in its yapay (beauty).
I ishah (make) it yapah (beautiful) by the rab (multitude) of its branches, so that all the itzay (trees) of Idan (Eden), that were in the gan (garden) of Alahayam, qanaa (jealous) it.

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you are gabah (exalted) in qawamah (stature), and he nathan (give) set his tzamarath (top) among the ibath (thick) boughs, and his labab (heart) is rawam (will lift up) up in his gabah (height);
I will even nathan (give) him into the yad (hand) of the mighty one of the gawayam (nations); he shall ishah (make) ishah (make) with him; I have garash (driven) him out for his rashai (wickedness).

Strangers, the irayatz (terrible) of the gawayam (nations), have karath (cut) him off, and have natash (left) him: on the harayam (mountains) and in all the gaayawath (valleys) his branches are napal (fall / be cast down), and his paarah (boughs) are shabar (broken) by all the watercourses of the aratz (Earth/land); and all the imay (peoples) of the aratz (Earth/land) are yarad (gone) down from his tzal (shadow), and have natash (left) him.
On his mapalath (ruin) all the iwap (flying) of the sky shall shakan (place), and all the animals of the shadah (field) shall be on his branches;

To the end that none of all the itzay (trees) by the mayam (Waters) gabah (exalt) themselves in their qawamah (stature), neither nathan (give) their tzamarath (top) among the ibath (thick) boughs, nor that their ayal (mighty) ones imad (stand) up on their gabah (height), even all who shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters): for they are all nathan (give) to mawath (death), to the lower thachathay (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land), in the thawak (midst) of the banay (children) of adam (men), with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: In the yawam (day) when he yarad (went) down to shaawal (Sheol / afterlife) I caused a abal (mourning): I kasah (covered) the thahawam (depths) for him, and I manai (restrained) its nahar (rivers); and the rab (great) mayam (Waters) were kalaa (stayed); and I caused Labanawan (Lebanon) to qadar (mourn) for him, and all the itzay (trees) of the shadah (field) ilapah (fainted) for him.

I made the gawayam (nations) to raish (shake) at the qawal (sound / voice) of his mapalath (fall), when I yarad (cast) him down to shaawal (Sheol / afterlife) with those who descend into the bawar (pit); and all the itzay (trees) of Idan (Eden), the mabachar (choice) and tawab (good / proper function) of Labanawan (Lebanon), all that shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters), were nacham (turn away / repent) in the lower thachathay (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land).

They also yarad (went) down into shaawal (Sheol / afterlife) with him to those who are chalal (slain) by the charab (sword); yes, those who were his zarawai (arm), that lived under his tzal (shadow) in the thawak (midst) of the gawayam (nations).

To whom are you thus damah (like) in kabawad (glory) and in gadal (greatness) among the itzay (trees) of Idan (Eden)? Yet you will be yarad (brought) down with the itzay (trees) of Idan (Eden) to the lower thachathay (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land): you shall shakab (lie) in the thawak (midst) of the iral (uncircumcised), with those who are chalal (slain) by the charab (sword). This is Paraih (Pharaoh) and all his hamawan (multitude), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
It happened in the shanayam (two) shanah (year), in the twelfth chadash (month), in the achad (one) day of the chadash (month), that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), nashaa (lift) up a qayanah (lamentation) over Paraih (Pharaoh) malak (king) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and amar (spoke) him, You were damah (likened) to a young kapayar (lion) of the gawayam (nations): yet you are as a monster in the yamayam (seas); and you gayach (broke) out with your nahar (rivers), and dalach (troubled) the mayam (Waters) with your ragal (feet / foot), and rapash (fouled) their nahar (rivers).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I will parash (spread) out my rashath (net) on you with a qahal (company) of many imayam (peoples); and they shall ilah (go up / offer) you up in my charam (net).

I will natash (leave) you on the aratz (Earth/land), I will tawal (cast) you forth on the panayam (face) shadah (field), and will cause all the iwap (flying) of the sky to settle on you, and I will shabai (satisfy) the animals of the whole aratz (Earth/land) with you.
I will nathan (give) your bashar (flesh) on the harayam (mountains), and malaa (fill) the gaayawath (valleys) with your ramawath (height).
I will also shaqah (water) with your dam (blood) the aratz (Earth/land) in which you swim, even to the harayam (mountains); and the watercourses shall be malaa (full) of you.

When I shall extinguish you, I will kasah (cover) the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and make its kawakab (star) qadar (dark); I will kasah (cover) the shamash (sun) with a inan (cloud), and the yarach (moon) shall not awar (light) its awar (light).

All the maawar (Maawar / Luminary) awar (light) of the sky will I make qadar (dark) over you, and nathan (give) chashak (darkness) on your aratz (Earth/land), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

I will also trouble the lab (heart) of many imayam (peoples), when I shall bawaa (come) your shabar (destruction) among the gawayam (nations), into the aratzawath (countries) which you yadai (have) not known.

Yes, I will make many imayam (peoples) shamam (amazed) at you, and their malak (king) shall be shair (horribly) shair (dread / storm / horror) for you, when I shall iwap (flying) my charab (sword) panayam (face) them; and they shall charad (tremble) at every ragai (in an instance), every ayash (man / husband) for his own napash (soul), in the yawam (day) of your mapalath (fall).
For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: The charab (sword) of the malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) shall bawaa (come) on you.

By the charabawath (swords) of the gabawar (mighty) will I cause your hamawan (multitude) to napal (fall / be cast down); the irayatz (terrible) of the gawayam (nations) are they all: and they shall bring to nothing the gaawan (pride) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and all its hamawan (multitude) shall be destroyed.

I will abad (destroy / perish) also all its animals from beside many mayam (Waters); neither shall the ragal (feet / foot) of adam (man) dalach (trouble) them any more, nor the parasawath (hoofs) of animals dalach (trouble) them.
Then will I make their mayam (Waters) clear, and cause their nahar (rivers) to yalak (run) like shaman (oil), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

When I shall nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) shamamah (desolate) and waste, a aratz (Earth/land) shamam (destitute) of that of which it malaa (was) full, when I shall nakah (strike) all those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein, then shall they yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

This is the qayanah (lamentation) with which they shall qawan (lament); the banawath (daughters) of the gawayam (nations) shall qawan (lament) therewith; over Matzarayam (Egypt), and over all her hamawan (multitude), shall they qawan (lament) therewith, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
It happened also in the shanayam (two) shanah (year), in the fifteenth day of the chadash (month), that the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), nahah (wail) for the hamawan (multitude) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and yarad (cast) them down, even her, and the banawath (daughters) of the adayar (famous) gawayam (nations), to the lower thachathayawath (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land), with those who yarad (go) down into the bawar (pit).
Whom do you naim (pass) in beauty? Yarad (go) down, and be shakab (laid) with the iral (uncircumcised).

They shall napal (fall / be cast down) in the thawak (midst) of those who are chalal (slain) by the charab (sword): she is nathan (give) to the charab (sword); mashak (draw) her away and all her hamawan (multitudes).

The al (Alahayam) among the gabawar (mighty) shall dabar (word / matter) to him out of the thawak (midst) of shaawal (Sheol / afterlife) with those who izar (help) him: they are yarad (gone) down, they shakab (lie) still, even the iral (uncircumcised), chalal (slain) by the charab (sword).
Ashawar (Asshur) is there and all her qahal (company); her qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) are all around her; all of them chalal (slain), napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword);

Whose qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) are nathan (give) in the uttermost parts of the bawar (pit), and her qahal (company) is around her qabawarah (grave); all of them chalal (slain), napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword), who nathan (give) chathayath (terror) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life).

There is Iyalam (Elam) and all her hamawan (multitude) around her qabawarah (grave); all of them chalal (slain), napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword), who are yarad (gone) down iral (uncircumcised) into the lower thachathayawath (parts) of the aratz (Earth/land), who nathan (give) their chathayath (terror) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life), and have nashaa (lift) their kalamah (shame) with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit).

They nathan (give) set her a mashakab (bed) in the thawak (midst) of the chalal (slain) with all her hamawan (multitude); her qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) are around her; all of them iral (uncircumcised), chalal (slain) by the charab (sword); for their chathayath (terror) was nathan (give) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life), and they have nashaa (lift) their kalamah (shame) with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit): he is nathan (give) in the thawak (midst) of those who are chalal (slain).

There is Mashak (Meshech), Thawabal (Tubal), and all their hamawan (multitude); their qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher) are around them; all of them iral (uncircumcised), chalal (slain) by the charab (sword); for they nathan (give) their chathayath (terror) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life).

They shall not shakab (lie) with the gabawar (mighty) who are napal (fall / be cast down) of the iral (uncircumcised), who are yarad (gone) down to shaawal (Sheol / afterlife) with their kalay (weapons) of malachamah (war), and nathan (give) laid their charab (sword) under their raash (head), and their iwan (guilt/iniquity) are on their itzam (bones); for they were the chathayath (terror) of the gabawar (mighty) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life).
But you shall be shabar (broken) in the thawak (midst) of the iral (uncircumcised), and shall shakab (lie) with those who are chalal (slain) by the charab (sword).

There is Adawam (Edom), her malak (king) and all her nashayaa (princes), who in their gabawarah (might) are nathan (give) with those who are chalal (slain) by the charab (sword): they shall shakab (lie) with the iral (uncircumcised), and with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit).

There are the nasayakay (princes) of the tzapawan (north), all of them, and all the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), who are yarad (gone) down with the chalal (slain); in the chathayath (terror) which they caused by their gabawarah (might) they are bawash (put) to shame; and they shakab (lie) iral (uncircumcised) with those who are chalal (slain) by the charab (sword), and nashaa (lift) their kalamah (shame) with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit).

Paraih (Pharaoh) shall raah (see) them, and shall be nacham (turn away / repent) over all his hamawan (multitude), even Paraih (Pharaoh) and all his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), chalal (slain) by the charab (sword), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

For I nathan (give) put his chathayath (terror) in the aratz (Earth/land) of the chay (life); and he shall be shakab (laid) in the thawak (midst) of the iral (uncircumcised), with those who are chalal (slain) by the charab (sword), even Paraih (Pharaoh) and all his hamawan (multitude), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), dabar (word / matter) to the banay (children) of your im (nation / people), and amar (spoke) them, When I bawaa (come) the charab (sword) on a aratz (Earth/land), and the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land) laqach (take / seize) a ayash (man / husband) from among them, and nathan (give) him for their tzapah (watchman / keep watch);
If, when he raah (see) the charab (sword) bawaa (come) on the aratz (Earth/land), he thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn), and zahar (warn) the im (nation / people);

Then whoever shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn), and doesn't take zahar (warn), if the charab (sword) bawaa (come), and laqach (take / seize) him away, his dam (blood) shall be on his own raash (head).

He shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn), and didn't take zahar (warn); his dam (blood) shall be on him; whereas if he had taken zahar (warn), he would have malat (delivered) his napash (soul).

But if the tzapah (watchman / keep watch) raah (see) the charab (sword) bawaa (come), and doesn't thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn), and the im (nation / people) aren't zahar (warn), and the charab (sword) bawaa (come), and laqach (take / seize) any napash (soul) from among them; he is laqach (take / seize) away in his iwan (guilt/iniquity), but his dam (blood) will I darash (require) at the tzapah (watchman / keep watch) yad (hand).

So you, ban (son) of adam (man), I nathan (give) set you a tzapah (watchman / keep watch) to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel); therefore shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) at my pah (mouth), and give them zahar (warn) from me.

When I amar (spoke) the rashai (wicked), O rashai (wicked) mawath (death), you shall surely mawath (death), and you don't dabar (word / matter) to zahar (warn) the rashai (wicked) from his darak (way); that rashai (wicked) mawath (death) shall die in his iwan (guilt/iniquity), but his dam (blood) will I baqash (require) at your yad (hand).

Nevertheless, if you zahar (warn) the rashai (wicked) of his darak (way) to shawab (turn back / repent) from it, and he doesn't shawab (turn back / repent) from his darak (way); he shall mawath (death) in his iwan (guilt/iniquity), but you have natzal (delivered) your napash (soul).

You, ban (son) of adam (man), amar (spoke) the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel): Thus you amar (spoke), amar (spoke), Our pashai (transgressions) and our chataah (sin) are on us, and we maqaq (pine) away in them; how then can we chayah (live)?

Amar (spoke) them, As I chay (life), amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, I chapatz (have) no pleasure in the mawath (death) of the rashai (wicked); but that the rashai (wicked) shawab (turn back / repent) from his darak (way) and chayah (live): shawab (turn back / repent), shawab (turn back / repent) from your rai (evil) darak (ways); for why will you mawath (death), bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel)?

You, ban (son) of adam (man), amar (spoke) the banay (children) of your im (nation / people), The tzadaqah (righteousness) of the tzadayaq (righteous) shall not natzal (deliver) him in the yawam (day) of his disobedience; and as for the rashaih (wickedness) of the rashai (wicked), he shall not kashal (stumble / stagger) thereby in the yawam (day) that he shawab (turn back / repent) from his rashai (wickedness); neither shall he who is tzadayaq (righteous) be yakal (able) to chayah (live) thereby in the yawam (day) that he chataa (sins).

When I amar (spoke) the tzadayaq (righteous), that he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live); if he batach (trust) to his tzadaqah (righteousness), and ishah (make) iwal (iniquity), none of his tzadaqah (righteousness) deeds shall be zakar (remember); but in his iwal (iniquity) that he ishah (make) committed, therein shall he mawath (death).

Again, when I amar (spoke) to the rashai (wicked), You shall mawath (death) mawath (death); if he shawab (turn back / repent) from his chataah (sin), and ishah (make) that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (righteousness);

If the rashai (wicked) shawab (turn back / repent) the chabal (pledge), shalam (give) again that which he had taken by robbery, halak (move) in the chaqawath (statutes) of chay (life), ishah (make) no iwal (iniquity); he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live), he shall not mawath (death).

None of his chataah (sin) that he has chataa (committed) shall be zakar (remember) against him: he ishah (make) done that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (righteousness); he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live).
Yet the banay (children) of your im (nation / people) amar (spoke), The darak (way) of the Adanay is not thakan (equal): but as for them, their darak (way) is not thakan (equal).
When the tzadayaq (righteous) shawab (turn back / repent) from his tzadaqah (righteousness), and ishah (make) iwal (iniquity), he shall even mawath (death) therein.
When the rashai (wicked) shawab (turn back / repent) from his rashaih (wickedness), and ishah (make) that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (righteousness), he shall chayah (live) thereby.

Yet you amar (spoke), The darak (way) of the Adanay is not thakan (equal). Bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), I will shapat (judge / judgement) ayash (man / husband) one of you after his darak (ways).

It happened in the shanayam (two) shanah (year) of our galawath (captivity), in the ishayaray (tenth) month, in the chamash (fifth) day of the chadash (month), that one who had palayat (escaped) out of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) bawaa (come) to me, amar (spoke), The iyar (city) has been nakah (struck).

Now the yad (hand) of Yahawah had been on me in the irab (evening), panayam (face) he who was palayat (escaped) bawaa (come); and he pathach (had) opened my pah (mouth), until he bawaa (come) to me in the baqar (morning); and my pah (mouth) was pathach (opened), and I was no more mute.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), they who yashab (inhabit/dwell) those charabah (waste) places in the adamah (land) of Yashar-Al (Israel) amar (spoke), amar (spoke), Abaraham (Abraham) was achad (one), and he yarash (inherited) the aratz (Earth/land): but we are many; the aratz (Earth/land) is nathan (give) us for mawarashah (inheritance).

Therefore amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: You akal (eat) with the dam (blood), and nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eye) to your galawal (idols), and shapak (shed) dam (blood): and shall you yarash (possess) the aratz (Earth/land)?

You imad (stand) on your charab (sword), you ishah (make) thawaibah (abomination), and ayash (man / husband) one of you tamaatham (defiles) his neighbor's ayashah (woman / wife): and shall you yarash (possess) the aratz (Earth/land)?

You shall amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: As I chay (life), surely those who are in the charabah (waste) places shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword); and him who is in the panayam (face) shadah (field) will I nathan (give) to the animals to be akal (eat); and those who are in the strongholds and in the mairawath (caves) shall mawath (death) of the dabar (word / matter).

I will nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) a shamamah (desolation) and an astonishment; and the gaawan (pride) of her iz (strength / might / refuge) shall shabath (shabath / rest); and the haray (mountains) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall be shamam (desolate), so that none shall ibar (pass over/through) through.

Then shall they yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I nathan (give) made the aratz (Earth/land) a shamamah (desolation) and an astonishment, because of all their thawaibah (abominations) which they ishah (make) committed.

As for you, ban (son) of adam (man), the banay (children) of your im (nation / people) dabar (word / matter) of you by the qayarawath (walls) and in the pathachay (doors) of the bathayam (houses), and dabar (word / matter) chad (one) to another, everyone to his ach (brother/kinsman), amar (spoke), Please bawaa (come) and shamai (hearken / hear) what is the dabar (word / matter) that yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from Yahawah.

They bawaa (come) to you as the im (nation / people) mabawaa (come), and they yashab (inhabit/dwell) panayam (face) you as my im (nation / people), and they shamai (hearken / hear) your dabar (word / matter), but don't ishah (make) them; for with their pah (mouth) they show much igab (love), but their lab (heart) halak (move) achar (other) their batzai (gain).

Behold, you are to them as a very igab (lovely) shayar (song) of one who has a yapah (pleasant) qawal (sound / voice), and can tawab (good / proper function) well on an nagan (instrument); for they shamai (hearken / hear) your dabar (word / matter), but they don't ishah (make) them.
When this bawaa (come) to pass, (behold, it bawaa (come)), then shall they yadai (know) that a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) has been thawak (midst) them.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy) against the rawaiy (shepherds) of Yashar-Al (Israel), nabaa (prophesy), and amar (spoke) them, even to the rawaiy (shepherds), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: haway (Alas/Woe!) To the rawaiy (shepherds) of Yashar-Al (Israel) who raih (feed) themselves! Shouldn't the rawaiy (shepherds) raih (feed) the tzaan (sheep)?
You akal (eat) the chalab (fat), and you labash (clothe) yourself with the tzamar (wool), you zabach (kill) the fatlings; but you don't barayaa (feed) the tzaan (sheep).

You haven't chazaq (strengthened) the chalah (afflict), neither have you rapaa (healed) that which was chalah (afflict), neither have you chabash (bound) up that which was shabar (broken), neither have you shawab (turn back / repent) back that which was nadach (driven) away, neither have you baqash (sought) that which was abad (destroy / perish); but with chazaqah (force) and with rigor you radah (rule over / have dominion of / subdue) ruled over them.
They were pawatz (scattered), because there was no raih (shepherd); and they became akalah (food) to all the animals of the shadah (field), and were pawatz (scattered).

My tzaan (sheep) shagah (wandered) through all the harayam (mountains), and on every rawam (will lift up) gabaih (hill): yes, my tzaan (sheep) were pawatz (scattered) on all the surface of the aratz (Earth/land); and there was none who darash (searched) or baqash (sought).
Therefore, you raiyam (shepherds), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah:

As I chay (life), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, surely because my tzaan (sheep) became a baz (prey), and my tzaan (sheep) became akalah (food) to all the animals of the shadah (field), because there was no raih (shepherd), neither did my yaraiw (shepherds) darash (search) for my tzaan (sheep), but the yaraiw (shepherds) raih (fed) themselves, and didn't raih (feed) my tzaan (sheep);
Therefore, you raiyam (shepherds), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah:

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against the raiyam (shepherds); and I will darash (require) my tzaan (sheep) at their yad (hand), and shabath (shabath / rest) them to cease from raih (feeding) the tzaan (sheep); neither shall the raiyam (shepherds) raih (feed) themselves any more; and I will natzal (deliver) my tzaan (sheep) from their pah (mouth), that they may not be akalah (food) for them.
For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I myself, even I, will darash (search) for my tzaan (sheep), and will baqar (morning) them out.

As a raih (shepherd) baqarah (seeks) out his idar (flock) in the yawam (day) that he is thawak (midst) his tzaan (sheep) that are parash (scattered) abroad, so will I baqar (morning) out my tzaan (sheep); and I will natzal (deliver) them out of all maqawamath (places) where they have been pawatz (scattered) in the inan (cloud) and irapal (dark) yawam (day).

I will yatzaa (go out / come out) them out from the imayam (peoples), and qabatz (gather) them from the aratzawath (countries), and will bawaa (come) them into their own adamah (land); and I will raih (feed) them on the haray (mountains) of Yashar-Al (Israel), by the watercourses, and in all the mawashab (inhabited) places of the aratz (Earth/land).

I will raih (feed) them with tawab (good / proper function) maraih (pasture); and on the haray (mountains) of the marawam (height) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall their nawah (habitation) be: there shall they rabatz (lie) down in a tawab (good / proper function) nawah (habitation); and on shaman (fat) maraih (pasture) shall they raih (feed) on the haray (mountains) of Yashar-Al (Israel).
I myself will be the raih (shepherd) of my tzaan (sheep), and I will rabatz (cause) them to lie down, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

I will baqash (seek) that which was abad (destroy / perish), and will shawab (turn back / repent) back that which was nadach (driven) away, and will chabash (bind) up that which was shabar (broken), and will chazaq (strengthen) that which was chalah (afflict): but the shaman (fat) and the chazaq (strong) I will shamad (destroy); I will raih (feed) them in mashapat (justice).
As for you, O my tzaan (flock), thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I shapat (judge / judgement) between shah (sheep) and shah (sheep), the ayalayam (rams) and the male ithawadayam (goats).

Does it seem a mait (small) thing to you to have raih (fed) on the tawab (good / proper function) maraih (pasture), but you must ramas (tread) down with your ragal (feet / foot) the yathar (residue) of your maraih (pasture)? And to have shathah (drinks) of the clear mayam (Waters), but you must rapash (foul) the yathar (residue) with your ragal (feet / foot)?

As for my tzaan (sheep), they raih (eat) that which you have maramas (trodden) with your ragal (feet / foot), and they shathah (drinks) that which you marapash (have) fouled with your ragal (feet / foot).
Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah to them: Behold, I, even I, will shapat (judge / judgement) between the baray (fat) shah (sheep) and the razah (lean) shah (sheep).
Because you hadap (thrust) with tzad (side) and with kathap (shoulder), and nagach (push) all the chalah (afflict) with your qaran (horn), until you have pawatz (scattered) them chawatz (abroad);
Therefore will I yashai (salvation) my tzaan (flock), and they shall no more be a baz (prey); and I will shapat (judge / judgement) between shah (sheep) and shah (sheep).
I will qawam (rise up) up achad (one) raih (shepherd) over them, and he shall raih (feed) them, even my ibad (servant) Dawad (David); he shall raih (feed) them, and he shall be their raih (shepherd).
I, Yahawah, will be their Alahayam, and my ibad (servant) Dawad (David) nashayaa (prince) thawak (midst) them; I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it.

I will karath (cut) with them a barayath (covenant) of shalawam (peace / safety), and will cause rai (evil) animals to shabath (shabath / rest) out of the aratz (Earth/land); and they shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely in the madabar (wilderness), and sleep in the yairayam (woods).

I will nathan (give) them and the sabayabawath (places) around my gabaih (hill) a barakah (blessing); and I will cause the gasham (shower) to yarad (come) down in its ith (season); there shall be gashamay (showers) of barakah (blessing).

The itz (tree) of the shadah (field) shall nathan (give) its paray (fruit), and the aratz (Earth/land) shall nathan (give) its yabawal (increase), and they shall be batach (secure) in their adamah (land); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I have shabar (broken) the bars of their il (over), and have natzal (delivered) them out of the yad (hand) of those who ibad (servant) slaves of them.

They shall no more be a baz (prey) to the gawayam (nations), neither shall the animals of the aratz (Earth/land) akal (eat) them; but they shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely, and none shall make them charad (afraid).

I will qawam (rise up) up to them a plantation for sham (name), and they shall be no more asap (consumed) with raib (famine) in the aratz (Earth/land), neither nashaa (lift) the kalamah (shame) of the gawayam (nations) any more.

They shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, their Alahayam am with them, and that they, the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), are my im (nation / people), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
You my tzaan (sheep), the tzaan (sheep) of my maraiyath (pasture), are adam (men), and I am your Alahayam, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
Moreover the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),
Ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) against har (mountain) Shaiyar (Seir), and nabaa (prophesy) against it,

And amar (spoke) it, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against you, har (mountain) Shaiyar (Seir), and I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) against you, and I will nathan (give) you a shamamah (desolation) and an astonishment.
I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) your iyar (cities) charabah (waste), and you shall be shamamah (desolate); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Because you have had a iwalam (forever) enmity, and have given over the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) to the yad (hand) of the charab (sword) in the ith (time) of their ayad (calamity), in the ith (time) of the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of the qatz (end);

Therefore, as I chay (life), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, I will ishah (make) you for dam (blood), and dam (blood) shall radap (pursue) you: am (mother) you have not shanaa (hate) dam (blood), therefore dam (blood) shall radap (pursue) you.

Thus will I nathan (give) har (mountain) Shaiyar (Seir) an astonishment and a shamamah (desolation); and I will karath (cut) off from it him who passes through and him who shawab (turn back / repent).

I will malaa (fill) its har (mountain) with its chalal (slain): in your gabaih (hills) and in your gayaa (valleys) and in all your watercourses shall they napal (fall / be cast down) who are chalal (slain) with the charab (sword).
I will nathan (give) you a iwalam (forever) shamamah (desolation), and your iyar (cities) shall not be inhabited; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Because you have amar (spoke), These shanayam (two) gawayam (nations) and these shanayam (two) aratzawath (countries) shall be mine, and we will yarash (possess) it; whereas Yahawah was there:

Therefore, as I chay (life), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, I will ishah (make) according to your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and according to your qanaah (envy) which you ishah (make) shown out of your hatred against them; and I yadai (will) make myself known among them, when I shall shapat (judge / judgement) you.

You shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have shamai (hearken / hear) all your insults which you have amar (spoke) against the haray (mountains) of Yashar-Al (Israel), amar (spoke), They are shamam (laid) desolate, they nathan (give) been given us to akalah (devour).
You have gadal (magnified) yourselves against me with your pah (mouth), and have ithar (multiplied) your dabar (word / matter) against me: I have shamai (hearken / hear) it.
Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: When the whole aratz (Earth/land) shamach (rejoices), I will ishah (make) you shamamah (desolate).

As you shamachah (rejoiced) over the nachalah (inheritance) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), because it was shamam (desolate), so will I ishah (make) to you: you shall be shamamah (desolate), har (mountain) Shaiyar (Seir), and all Adawam (Edom), even all of it; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

You, ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy) to the haray (mountains) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and amar (spoke), You haray (mountains) of Yashar-Al (Israel), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah.
Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because the ayab (enemy) has amar (spoke) against you, haach (aha)! And, The iwalam (forever) bamah (high) places are ours in mawarashah (possession);

Therefore nabaa (prophesy), and amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Because, even because they have shamam (made) you desolate, and shaap (swallowed) you up on sabayab (surrounding) side, that you might be a mawarashah (possession) to the shaarayath (residue) of the gawayam (nations), and you are ilah (go up / offer) up in the shapah (lips) of lashawan (tongue / language), and the dabah (evil) report of the im (nation / people);

Therefore, you haray (mountains) of Yashar-Al (Israel), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of the Adanay Yahawah: Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah to the haray (mountains) and to the gabaiwath (hills), to the watercourses and to the gaayawath (valleys), to the charabah (desolate) charabawath (wastes) and to the irayam (cities) that are forsaken, which are become a baz (prey) and laig (derision) to the shaarayath (residue) of the gawayam (nations) that are all around;

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Surely in the ash (fire) of my qanaah (jealousy) have I dabar (word / matter) against the shaarayath (residue) of the gawayam (nations), and against all Adawam (Edom), that nathan (give) appointed my aratz (Earth/land) to themselves for a mawarashah (possession) with the shamachah (joy) of all their labab (heart), with shaat (despite) of labab (soul), to magarash (cast) it out for a baz (prey).

Therefore nabaa (prophesy) concerning the adamah (land) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and amar (spoke) the harayam (mountains) and to the gabaiwath (hills), to the watercourses and to the gaayawath (valleys), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I have dabar (word / matter) in my qanaah (jealousy) and in my chamah (wrath), because you have nashaa (lift) the kalamah (shame) of the gawayam (nations):
Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I have yad (hand), saying, "Surely the gawayam (nations) that are around you, they shall nashaa (lift) their kalamah (shame).

But you, haray (mountains) of Yashar-Al (Israel), you shall nathan (give) forth your branches, and nashaa (lift) your paray (fruit) to my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel); for they are at qarab (come close) to bawaa (come).
For, behold, I am for you, and I will panah (turn) into you, and you shall be ibad (servant) and zarai (sown);

And I will rabah (multiply) adam (men) on you, all the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), even all of it; and the irayam (cities) shall be yashab (inhabit/dwell), and the charabah (waste) places shall be banah (build);

And I will rabah (multiply) on you adam (man) and animal; and they shall rabah (increase) and be parah (fruitful); and I will yashab (inhabit/dwell) you to be inhabited after your qadamah (former) estate, and will tawab (good / proper function) better to you than at your raashah (beginnings): and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Yes, I will cause adam (men) to yalak (walk) on you, even my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel); and they shall yarash (possess) you, and you shall be their nachalah (inheritance), and you shall no more henceforth shakal (bereave) them of children.
Thus amarayam (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Because they amar (spoke) to you, You are a devourer of adam (men), and have been a bereaver of your gaway (heathen / nation);
Therefore you shall akal (eat) adam (men) no more, neither kashal (stumble / stagger) your gaway (heathen / nation) any more, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah;

Neither will I shamai (hearken / hear) you hear any more the kalamah (shame) of the gawayam (nations), neither shall you nashaa (lift) the charapah (reproach) of the imayam (peoples) any more, neither shall you cause your gaway (heathen / nation) to kashal (stumble / stagger) any more, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
Moreover the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), when the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) lived in their own adamah (land), they tamaa (defiled) it by their darak (way) and by their ilayalah (doings): their darak (way) panayam (face) me was as the tamaah (uncleanness) of a nadah (woman) in her impurity.

Therefore I shapak (poured) out my chamah (wrath) on them for the dam (blood) which they had shapak (poured) out on the aratz (Earth/land), and because they had tamaa (defiled) it with their galawal (idols);

And I pawatz (scattered) them among the gawayam (nations), and they were zarah (dispersed) through the aratzawath (countries): according to their darak (way) and according to their ilayalah (doings) I shapat (judge / judgement) them.

When they bawaa (come) to the gawayam (nations), where they bawaa (come), they chalal (profaned) my qadash (set apart / make holy) sham (name); in that men amar (spoke) of them, These are the im (nation / people) of Yahawah, and are yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of his aratz (Earth/land).

But I chamal (had) respect for my qadash (set apart / make holy) sham (name), which the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) had chalal (profaned) among the gawayam (nations), where they bawaa (come).

Therefore amar (spoke) the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: I don't ishah (make) this for your sake, bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), but for my qadash (set apart / make holy) sham (name), which you have chalal (profaned) among the gawayam (nations), where you bawaa (come).

I will qadash (set apart / make holy) my gadawal (very great/important/mighty) sham (name), which has been chalal (profaned) among the gawayam (nations), which you have chalal (profaned) in their thawak (midst); and the gawayam (nations) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, naam (declares prophetically) the Adawan Yahawah, when I shall be qadash (set apart / make holy) in you before their iyan (eye).
For I will laqach (take / seize) you from man (from) the gawayam (nations), and qabatz (gather) you out of all the aratzawath (countries), and will bawaa (come) you into your own adamah (land).
I will zaraq (sprinkle) tahawar (clean) mayam (Waters) on you, and you shall be tahar (clean): from all your tamaah (filthiness), and from all your galawal (idols), will I tahar (cleanse) you.

I will also nathan (give) you a chadash (new) lab (heart), and I will nathan (give) a chadash (new) rawach (spirit / wind) qarab (among / near) you; and I will sawar (take) away the aban (stone) lab (heart) out of your bashar (flesh), and I will nathan (give) you a lab (heart) of bashar (flesh).

I will nathan (give) my rawach (spirit / wind) qarab (among / near) you, and cause you to yalak (walk) in my chaq (statute), and you shall shamar (keep/guard) my mashapat (ordinances), and ishah (make) them.
You shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the aratz (Earth/land) that I nathan (give) to your ab (father); and you shall be my im (nation / people), and I will be your Alahayam.
I will yashai (salvation) you from all your tamaah (uncleanness): and I will qaraa (called) for the grain, and will rabah (multiply) it, and nathan (give) no raib (famine) on you.

I will rabah (multiply) the paray (fruit) of the itz (tree), and the thanawabah (increase) of the shadah (field), that you may laqach (take / seize) no more the charapah (reproach) of raib (famine) among the gawayam (nations).

Then you shall zakar (remember) your rai (evil) darak (ways), and your mailal (doings) that were not tawab (good / proper function); and you shall qawat (loathe) yourselves in your own panayam (face) for your iwan (guilt/iniquity) and for your thawaibah (abominations).

Nor for your sake ishah (make) I this, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, be it yadai (known) to you: be bawash (ashamed) and kalam (confounded) for your darak (ways), bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: In the yawam (day) that I tahar (cleanse) you from all your iwan (guilt/iniquity), I will cause the irayam (cities) to be yashab (inhabit/dwell), and the charabah (waste) places shall be banah (build).
The aratz (Earth/land) that was shamam (desolate) shall be ibad (servant), whereas it was a shamamah (desolation) in the iyan (eye) of ibar (pass over/through) who passed by.

They shall amar (spoke), halazaw (this) aratz (Earth/land) that was shamam (desolate) has become like the gan (garden) of Idan (Eden); and the charab (waste) and shamam (desolate) and haras (ruined) irayam (cities) are batzar (fortified) and yashab (inhabit/dwell).

Then the gawayam (nations) that are shaar (left) around you shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have banah (build) the haras (ruined) places, and natai (planted) that which was shamam (desolate): I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it, and I will ishah (make) it.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: For this, moreover, will I be darash (inquired) of by the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), to ishah (make) it for them: I will rabah (increase) them with adam (men) like a tzaan (flock).

As the tzaan (flock) for qadash (set apart / make holy), as the tzaan (flock) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) in her mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) feasts, so shall the charab (waste) irayam (cities) be malaa (filled) with tzaan (flocks) of adam (men); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

The yad (hand) of Yahawah was on me, and he yatzaa (go out / come out) me out in the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah, and nawach (set) me down in the thawak (midst) of the baqaih (valley); and it malaa (was) full of itzamawath (bones).
He ibar (pass over/through) me to pass by them all around: and behold, there were very many in the panayam (face) baqaih (valley); and behold, they were very yabash (dry land).
He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), can these itzamawath (bones) chayah (live)? I amar (spoke), Adanay Yahawah, you yadai (know).

Again he amar (spoke) to me, nabaa (prophesy) over these itzamawath (bones), and amar (spoke) them, you yabash (dry land) itzamawath (bones), shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah.
Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah to these itzamawath (bones): Behold, I will cause rawach (spirit / wind) to bawaa (come) into you, and you shall chayah (live).

I will nathan (give) gadayam (sinews) on you, and will ilah (go up / offer) up bashar (flesh) on you, and qaram (cover) you with iwar (skin), and nathan (give) rawach (spirit / wind) in you, and you shall chayah (live); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

So I nabaa (prophesied) as I was tzawah (commanded): and as I nabaa (prophesied), there was a qawal (sound / voice), and behold, an raish (earthquake); and the itzamawath (bones) qarab (come close) together, itzam (bone) to its itzam (bone).

I raah (see), and, behold, there were gadayam (sinews) on them, and bashar (flesh) ilah (go up / offer) up, and iwar (skin) qaram (covered) them mail (top/above); but there was no rawach (spirit / wind) in them.

Then he amar (spoke) to me, nabaa (prophesy) to the rawach (spirit / wind), nabaa (prophesy), ban (son) of adam (man), and amar (spoke) the rawach (spirit / wind), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: bawaa (come) from the arabai (four) rawachawath (winds), rawach (spirit / wind), and breathe on these harag (kill), that they may chayah (live).

So I nabaa (prophesied) as he tzawah (commanded) me, and the rawach (spirit / wind) bawaa (come) into them, and they chayah (lived), and imad (stood) up on their ragal (feet / foot), an maad (exceedingly) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor).

Then he amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), these itzamawath (bones) are the whole bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel): behold, they amar (spoke), Our itzamawath (bones) are yabash (dry land) up, and our thaqawah (hope) is abad (destroy / perish); we are clean gazar (cut) off.

Therefore nabaa (prophesy), and amar (spoke) them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will pathach (open) your qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher), and ilah (go up / offer) you to come up out of your qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher), my people; and I will bawaa (come) you into the adamah (land) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

You shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I pathach (have) opened your qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher), and ilah (go up / offer) you to come up out of your qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher), my im (nation / people).

I will nathan (give) my rawach (spirit / wind) in you, and you shall chayah (live), and I will yanach (place) you in your own adamah (land): and you shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have dabar (word / matter) it and ishah (make) it, naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came again to me, amar (spoke),

You, ban (son) of adam (man), laqach (take / seize) achad (one) itz (stick), and kathab (write) on it, For Yahawadah (Judah), and for the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) his chabar (companions): then laqach (take / seize) another itz (stick), and kathab (write) on it, For Yawasap (Joseph), the itz (stick) of Aparayam (Ephraim), and for all the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) his chabar (companions):
And qarab (come close) them for you achad (one) to another into achad (one) itz (stick), that they may become achad (one) in your yad (hand).
When the banay (children) of your im (nation / people) shall amar (spoke) to you, amar (spoke), Will you not show us what you mean by these?

Dabar (word / matter) them, Thus dabar (word / matter) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will laqach (take / seize) the itz (stick) of Yawasap (Joseph), which is in the yad (hand) of Aparayam (Ephraim), and the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel) his chabar (companions); and I will nathan (give) them with it, even with the itz (stick) of Yahawadah (Judah), and ishah (make) them achad (one) itz (stick), and they shall be achad (one) in my yad (hand).
The itzayam (sticks) whereon you kathab (write) shall be in your yad (hand) before their iyan (eye).

Dabar (word / matter) to them, Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will laqach (take / seize) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) from bayan (between) the gawayam (nations), where they are halak (move), and will qabatz (gather) them on sabayab (surrounding) side, and bawaa (come) them into their own adamah (land):

And I will ishah (make) them achad (one) gaway (heathen / nation) in the aratz (Earth/land), on the haray (mountains) of Yashar-Al (Israel); and achad (one) malak (king) shall be malak (king) to them iwad (more/again); and they shall be no more shanayam (two) gawayam (nations), neither shall they be chatzah (divided) into shanayam (two) mamalakawath (kingdoms) any more at all;

Neither shall they tamaa (defile) themselves any more with their galawal (idols), nor with their shaqawatz (detestable) things, nor with any of their pashai (transgressions); but I will yashai (salvation) them out of all their mawashab (dwelling) places, in which they have chataa (sinned), and will tahar (cleanse) them: so shall they be my im (nation / people), and I will be their Alahayam.

My ibad (servant) Dawad (David) shall be malak (king) over them; and they all shall have achad (one) raih (shepherd): they shall also yalak (walk) in my mashapat (ordinances), and shamar (keep/guard) my chaqah (statutes), and ishah (make) them.
