They shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the aratz (Earth/land) that I nathan (give) given to Yaiqab (Jacob) my ibad (servant), in which your ab (father) lived; and they shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein, they, and their banay (children), and their banay (childrens) banay (children), iwalam (forever): and Dawad (David) my ibad (servant) shall be their nashayaa (prince) for iwalam (forever).

Moreover I will karath (cut) a barayath (covenant) of shalawam (peace / safety) with them; it shall be an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant) with them; and I will nathan (give) them, and rabah (multiply) them, and will nathan (give) my maqadash (sanctuary) in their thawak (midst) forevermore.
My mashakan (tent) also shall be with them; and I will be their Alahayam, and they shall be my im (nation / people).
The gawayam (nations) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah who qadash (set apart / make holy) Yashar-Al (Israel), when my maqadash (sanctuary) shall be in their thawak (midst) forevermore.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to me, amar (spoke),

Ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) your panayam (face) toward Gawag (Gog), of the aratz (Earth/land) of Magawag (Magog), the nashayaa (prince) of Rosh, Mashak (Meshech), and Thawabal (Tubal), and nabaa (prophesy) against him,
And amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against you, Gawag (Gog), raash (head) of Rosh, Mashak (Meshech), and Thawabal (Tubal):

And I will shawab (turn back / repent) you around, and nathan (give) chachayam (hooks) into your lachay (jaws), and I will yatzaa (go out / come out) you forth, with all your chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), sawasayam (horses) and horsemen, all of them labash (clothed) in full armor, a rab (great) qahal (company) with tzanah (buckler) and magan (shield), all of them thapash (handling) charabawath (swords);
Paras (Persia), Kawash (Cush), and Pawat (Put) with them, all of them with magan (shield) and kawabai (helmet);
Gamar (Gomer), and all his hordes; the bayath (house) of Thawagaramah (Togarmah) in the uttermost yarakathay (parts) of the tzapawan (north), and all his hordes; even many imayam (peoples) with you.
Be kawan (prepared), yes, kawan (prepare) yourself, you, and all your qahal (companies) who are qahal (assembled) to you, and be a mashamar (guard) to them.

After many yamayam (days) you shall be paqad (visit): in the acharayath (latter) shanayam (years) you shall bawaa (come) into the aratz (Earth/land) that is shawab (turn back / repent) back from the charab (sword), that is qabatz (gathered) out of many imayam (peoples), on the haray (mountains) of Yashar-Al (Israel), which have been a thamayad (continual) charabah (waste); but it is yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the imayam (peoples), and they shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely, all of them.

You shall ilah (go up / offer), you shall bawaa (come) like a shawaa (vanity), you shall be like a inan (cloud) to kasah (cover) the aratz (Earth/land), you, and all your hordes, and many imayam (peoples) with you.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: It shall happen in that yawam (day), that things shall ilah (go up / offer) into your labab (mind), and you shall chashab (devise) an rai (evil) machashabah (device):

And you shall amar (spoke), I will ilah (go up / offer) up to the aratz (Earth/land) of parazah (unwalled) villages; I will bawaa (come) to those who are at shaqat (rest), who yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely, all of them yashab (inhabit/dwell) without chawamah (walls), and having neither barayach (bars) nor dalathayam (gates);

To take the shalal (spoil) and to bazaz (take) the baz (prey); to shawab (turn back / repent) your yad (hand) against the charabah (waste) places that are now yashab (inhabit/dwell), and against the im (nation / people) who are asap (gathered) out of the gawayam (nations), who ishah (make) gotten livestock and qanayan (goods), who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the tabawar (middle) of the aratz (Earth/land).

Shabaa (Sheba), and Dadan (Dedan), and the sacharay (merchants) of Tharashayash (Tarshish), with all the young kapayar (lions) of it, shall amar (spoke) you, bawaa (come) you come to take the shalal (spoil)? Have you qahal (assembled) your qahal (company) to bazaz (take) the baz (prey)? To nashaa (lift) away kasap (silver) and zahab (gold), to laqach (take / seize) away livestock and qanayan (goods), to take gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shalal (spoil)?

Therefore, ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy), and amar (spoke) Gawag (Gog), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: In that yawam (day) when my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel) yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely, shall you not yadai (know) it?

You shall bawaa (come) from your maqawam (place) out of the uttermost yarakathay (parts) of the tzapawan (north), you, and many imayam (peoples) with you, all of them rakab (riding) on sawasayam (horses), a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qahal (company) and a rab (mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor);

And you shall ilah (go up / offer) up against my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel), as a inan (cloud) to kasah (cover) the aratz (Earth/land): it shall happen in the acharayath (latter) yamayam (days), that I will bawaa (come) you against my aratz (Earth/land), that the gawayam (nations) may yadai (know) me, when I shall be qadash (set apart / make holy) in you, Gawag (Gog), before their iyan (eye).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Are you he of whom I dabar (word / matter) in qadamawanay (old) yawam (day) by my ibad (servant) the nabayaay (prophets) of Yashar-Al (Israel), who nabaa (prophesied) in those yamayam (days) for many shanayam (years) that I would bawaa (come) you against them?

It shall happen in that yawam (day), when Gawag (Gog) shall bawaa (come) against the adamah (land) of Yashar-Al (Israel), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, that my chamah (wrath) shall ilah (go up / offer) up into my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).

For in my qanaah (jealousy) and in the ash (fire) of my ibarah (wrath) have I dabar (word / matter), Surely in that yawam (day) there shall be a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) raish (shaking) in the adamah (land) of Yashar-Al (Israel);

So that the dag (fish) of the yam (sea/waters), and the iwap (flying) of the sky, and the animals of the shadah (field), and all ramash (creeping) things who ramash (creep) on the adamah (earth), and all the adam (men) who are on the surface of the adamah (earth), shall raish (shake) at my panayam (face), and the harayam (mountains) shall be haras (thrown) down, and the madaragah (steep) places shall napal (fall / be cast down), and every chawamah (wall) shall napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land).

I will qaraa (called) for a charab (sword) against him to all my har (mountain), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah: every ayash (man / husband) charab (sword) shall be against his ach (brother/kinsman).

With dabar (word / matter) and with dam (blood) will I enter into shapat (judge / judgement) with him; and I will matar (rain) on him, and on his hordes, and on the many imayam (peoples) who are with him, an shatap (overflowing) gasham (shower), and alagabayash (great) hailstones, ash (fire), and sulfur.

I will gadal (magnify) myself, and qadash (set apart / make holy) myself, and I yadai (will) make myself known in the iyanay (eyes) of many gawayam (nations); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

You, ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy) against Gawag (Gog), and amar (spoke), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against you, Gawag (Gog), raash (head) of Rosh, Mashak (Meshech), and Thawabal (Tubal):

And I will shawab (turn back / repent) you around, and will lead you on, and will ilah (go up / offer) you to come up from the uttermost yarakathay (parts) of the tzapawan (north); and I will bawaa (come) you on the haray (mountains) of Yashar-Al (Israel);

And I will nakah (strike) your qashath (bow) out of your shamaawal (left hand) yad (hand), and will cause your chatz (arrows) to napal (fall / be cast down) out of your yamayan (right hand) yad (hand).

You shall napal (fall / be cast down) on the haray (mountains) of Yashar-Al (Israel), you, and all your hordes, and the imayam (peoples) who are with you: I will nathan (give) you to the iyat (ravenous) tzapawar (birds) of every kanap (sort), and to the animals of the shadah (field) to be akalah (devoured).
You shall napal (fall / be cast down) on the panayam (face) shadah (field); for I have dabar (word / matter) it, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on Magawag (Magog), and on those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely in the ayayam (islands); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

My qadash (set apart / make holy) sham (name) yadai (will) I make known in the thawak (midst) of my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel); neither will I allow my qadash (set apart / make holy) sham (name) to be chalal (profaned) any more: and the gawayam (nations) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, the qadawash (holy) One in Yashar-Al (Israel).
Behold, it bawaa (come), and it shall be hayah (came to pass), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah; this is the yawam (day) about which I have dabar (word / matter).

Those who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in the iray (cities) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and shall make ash (fire) of the nashaq (weapons) and nashaq (burn) them, both the magan (shield) and the tzanah (bucklers), the qashath (bows) and the chatzayam (arrows), and the war clubs, and the ramach (spears), and they shall make ash (fire) of them shabai (seven) shanayam (years);

So that they shall nashaa (lift) no itz (wood) out of the shadah (field), neither chatab (cut) down any out of the yairayam (forests); for they shall make ash (fire) of the nashaq (weapons); and they shall plunder those who plundered them, and bazaz (rob) those who bazaz (robbed) them, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

It shall happen in that yawam (day), that I will nathan (give) to Gawag (Gog) a maqawam (place) for burial in Yashar-Al (Israel), the gayaa (valley) of those who ibar (pass over/through) through on the qadamah (east) of the yam (sea/waters); and it shall chasam (stop) those who ibar (pass over/through) through: and there shall they qabar (bury) Gawag (Gog) and all his hamawan (multitude); and they shall qaraa (called) it The gayaa (valley) of Hamawanagawag (Hamon Gog).
Shabai (seven) chadashayam (months) shall the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) be qabar (bury) them, that they may tahar (cleanse) the aratz (Earth/land).

Yes, all the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land) shall qabar (bury) them; and it shall be to them a sham (name) in the yawam (day) that I shall be kabad (glorified), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

They shall set apart anashay (men) of thamayad (continual) employment, who shall ibar (pass over/through) through the aratz (Earth/land), and, with those who ibar (pass over/through) through, those who qabar (bury) those who yathar (remain) on the surface of the aratz (Earth/land), to tahar (cleanse) it: qatzah (end / extremity / border) the end of shabai (seven) chadashayam (months) shall they chaqar (search).

Those who ibar (pass over/through) through the aratz (Earth/land) shall ibar (pass over/through) through; and when any raah (see) a adam (man's) itzam (bone), then shall he banah (build) up a tzayawan (visible marker/identifier/landmark) by it, until the undertakers have qabar (bury) it in the gayaa (valley) of Hamawanagawag (Hamon Gog).
Hamawanah (Hamonah) shall also be the sham (name) of a iyar (city). Thus shall they tahar (cleanse) the aratz (Earth/land).

You, ban (son) of adam (man), thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: amar (spoke) to the tzapawar (birds) of every kanap (sort), and to every animal of the shadah (field), qabatz (assemble) yourselves, and bawaa (come); asap (gather) yourselves on sabayab (surrounding) side to my zabach (sacrifice) that I do zabach (sacrifice) for you, even a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) zabach (sacrifice) on the haray (mountains) of Yashar-Al (Israel), that you may akal (eat) bashar (flesh) and shathah (drinks) dam (blood).

You shall akal (eat) the bashar (flesh) of the gabawar (mighty), and shathah (drinks) the dam (blood) of the nashayaay (princes) of the aratz (Earth/land), of ayalayam (rams), of karayam (lambs), and of ithawadayam (goats), of parayam (bulls), all of them fatlings of Bashan (Bashan).
You shall akal (eat) chalab (fat) until you be shabaih (seven), and shathah (drinks) dam (blood) until you are shakarawan (drunk), of my zabach (sacrifice) which I have zabach (sacrificed) for you.

You shall be shabai (filled) at my shalachan (table) with sawas (horses) and rakab (chariots), with gabawar (mighty) men, and with all ayash (man / husband) of malachamah (war), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

I will nathan (give) my kabawad (glory) among the gawayam (nations); and all the gawayam (nations) shall raah (see) my mashapat (judgment) that I ishah (make) executed, and my yad (hand) that I have shawam (place / establish / appoint) on them.
So the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah their Alahayam, from that yawam (day) and halaah (forward).

The gawayam (nations) shall yadai (know) that the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) galah (went) into captivity for their iwan (guilt/iniquity); because they mail (top/above) against me, and I sathar (hid) my panayam (face) from them: so I nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of their tzar (oppressor / distressor), and they napal (fall / be cast down) all of them by the charab (sword).
According to their tamaah (uncleanness) and according to their pashai (transgressions) ishah (make) I to them; and I sathar (hid) my panayam (face) from them.

Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: Now will I shawab (turn back / repent) back the shabawath (captivity) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and have racham (show mercy / love) on the whole bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel); and I will be qanaa (jealous) for my qadash (set apart / make holy) sham (name).

They shall nashaa (lift) their kalamah (shame), and all their trespasses by which they have mail (top/above) against me, when they shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) securely in their adamah (land), and none shall make them charad (afraid);

When I have shawab (turn back / repent) them back from the imayam (peoples), and qabatz (gathered) them out of their ayab (enemy)' aratzawath (lands), and am qadash (set apart / make holy) in them in the iyan (eye) of many gawayam (nations).

They shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah their Alahayam, in that I caused them to galah (go) into captivity among the gawayam (nations), and have kanas (gathered) them to their own adamah (land); and I will yathar (leave) none of them any more there;

Neither will I sathar (hide) my panayam (face) any more from them; for I have shapak (poured) out my rawach (spirit / wind) on the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

In the chamash (five) and isharayam (twenty) shanah (year) of our galawath (captivity), in the raash (head) of the shanah (year), in the ishawar (tenth) day of the chadash (month), in the fourteenth shanah (year) achar (other) that the iyar (city) was nakah (struck), in the same yawam (day), the yad (hand) of Yahawah was on me, and he bawaa (come) me there.

In the maraawath (visions) of Alahayam bawaa (come) he me into the aratz (Earth/land) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and nawach (set) me down on a very gabah (high) har (mountain), whereon was as it were the mabanah (frame) of a iyar (city) on the nagab (south).

He bawaa (come) me there; and, behold, there was a ayash (man / husband), whose maraah (appearance) was like the maraah (appearance) of nachashath (brass), with a pathayal (line) of pashathah (flax) in his yad (hand), and a madah (measuring) qanah (reed); and he imad (stood) in the shair (gate).

The ayash (man / husband) dabar (word / matter) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), raah (see) with your iyan (eye), and shamai (hearken / hear) with your azan (ear), and shawam (place / establish / appoint) your lab (heart) on all that I shall show you; for, to the intent that I may show them to you, you are bawaa (come) here: nagad (declare) all that you raah (see) to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Behold, a chawamah (wall) on the outside of the bayath (house) all around, and in the ayash (man / husband) yad (hand) a madah (measuring) qanah (reed) shash (six) amawath (cubits) long, of a amah (cubit) and a tapach (handbreadth) each: so he madad (measured) the thickness of the banayan (building), achad (one) qanah (reed); and the qawamah (height), achad (one) qanah (reed).

Then bawaa (come) he to the shair (gate) which panayam (face) darak (toward) the qadayam (east), and ilah (go up / offer) up its mailah (ascent/climbing up): and he madad (measured) the sap (threshold) of the shair (gate), achad (one) qanah (reed) rachab (broad); and the other sap (threshold), achad (one) qanah (reed) rachab (broad).

Every lodge was achad (one) qanah (reed) arak (length), and achad (one) qanah (reed) rachab (broad); and the space between the lodges was chamash (five) amawath (cubits); and the sap (threshold) of the shair (gate) by the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate) toward the house was one qanah (reed).
He madad (measured) also the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate) toward the house, one qanah (reed).

Then madad (measured) he the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate), shamanah (eight) amawath (cubits); and its ayal (posts), shanayam (two) amawath (cubits); and the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate) was toward the bayath (house).

The lodges of the shair (gate) darak (eastward) were shalawash (three) on pah (this) side, and shalawash (three) on that pah (side); they shalawash (three) were of achad (one) madah (measure): and the ayalam (posts) had achad (one) madah (measure) on this side and on that side.
He madad (measured) the rachab (breadth) of the pathach (opening) of the shair (gate), ishar (ten) amawath (cubits); and the arak (length) of the shair (gate), thirteen amawath (cubits);

And a gabawal (border/boundary) panayam (face) the lodges, achad (one) amah (cubit) on this side, and a gabawal (border/boundary), one amah (cubit) on that side; and the lodges, shash (six) amawath (cubits) on this side, and shash (six) amawath (cubits) on that side.

He madad (measured) the shair (gate) from the gag (roof) of the thaa (one) lodge to the gag (roof) of the other, a rachab (breadth) of isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amawath (cubits); pathach (door) against pathach (door).
He ishah (make) also ayalayam (posts), shashayam (sixty) amah (cubits); and the chatzar (court) reached to the ayalayam (posts), around the shair (gate).
From the panayam (face) of the shair (gate) at the yaathawan (entrance) to the panayam (face) of the inner awalam (porch) of the shair (gate) were chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits).

There were closed chalanawath (windows) to the lodges, and to their ayal (posts) panayamah (within) the shair (gate) all around, and likewise to the arches; and chalanawath (windows) were around inward; and on each ayal (post) were thamar (palm) trees.

Then bawaa (come) he me into the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court); and behold, there were rooms and a ratzapah (pavement), ishah (make) for the chatzar (court) all around: shalawashayam (thirty) rooms were on the ratzapah (pavement).
The ratzapah (pavement) was by the kathap (side) of the shairayam (gates), answerable to the arak (length) of the shairayam (gates), even the thachathawan (lower) ratzapah (pavement).

Then he madad (measured) the rachab (breadth) from the panayam (face) of the thachathawan (lower) shair (gate) to the panayam (face) of the inner chatzar (court) outside, one maah (hundred) amah (cubits), both on the qadayam (east) and on the tzapawan (north).
The shair (gate) of the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court) whose prospect is darak (toward) the tzapawan (north), he madad (measured) its arak (length) and its rachab (breadth).

The lodges of it were shalawash (three) on this side and shalawash (three) on that side; and its ayal (posts) and its arches were after the madah (measure) of the raashawan (first) shair (gate): its arak (length) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits), and the rachab (breadth) twenty - five amah (cubits).

The chalawan (windows) of it, and its arches, and the thamar (palm) trees of it, were after the madah (measure) of the shair (gate) whose prospect is darak (toward) the qadayam (east); and they ilah (go up / offer) up to it by shabai (seven) mailawath (steps); and its arches were panayam (face) them.

There was a shair (gate) to the inner chatzar (court) over against the other shair (gate), both on the tzapawan (north) and on the qadayam (east); and he madad (measured) from shair (gate) to shair (gate) one maah (hundred) amah (cubits).

He yalak (led) me darak (toward) the darawam (south); and behold, a shair (gate) darak (toward) the darawam (south): and he madad (measured) its ayal (posts) and its arches according to these madawath (measures).

There were chalawanayam (windows) in it and in its arches all around, like those chalawanayam (windows): the arak (length) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits), and the rachab (breadth) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amah (cubits).

There were shabai (seven) mailawath (steps) to ilah (go) up to it, and its arches were panayam (face) them; and it had thamar (palm) trees, achad (one) on this side, and another on that side, on its ayal (posts).

There was a shair (gate) to the inner chatzar (court) darak (toward) the darawam (south): and he madad (measured) from shair (gate) to shair (gate) darak (toward) the darawam (south) a maah (hundred) amawath (cubits).
Then he bawaa (come) me to the inner chatzar (court) by the darawam (south) shair (gate): and he madad (measured) the darawam (south) shair (gate) according to these madawath (measures);

And its lodges, and its ayal (posts), and its arches, according to these madawath (measures): and there were chalawanawath (windows) in it and in its arches all around; it was chamashayam (fifty) amawath (cubits) arak (length), and isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amawath (cubits) rachab (broad).
There were arches all around, isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amawath (cubits) arak (length), and chamash (five) amawath (cubits) rachab (broad).
The arches of it were toward the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court); and thamar (palm) trees were on its ayal (posts): and the mailah (ascent) to it had shamanah (eight) mailawath (steps).
He bawaa (come) me into the inner chatzar (court) darak (toward) the qadayam (east): and he madad (measured) the shair (gate) according to these madawath (measures);

And its lodges, and its ayal (posts), and its arches, according to these madawath (measures): and there were chalawanawath (windows) therein and in its arches all around; it was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits) arak (length), and isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amah (cubits) rachab (broad).

The arches of it were toward the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court); and thamar (palm) trees were on its ayal (posts), on this side, and on that side: and the mailah (ascent) to it had shamanah (eight) mailawath (steps).
He bawaa (come) me to the tzapawan (north) shair (gate): and he madad (measured) it according to these madawath (measures);

Its lodges, its ayal (posts), and its arches: and there were chalawanawath (windows) therein all around; the arak (length) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits), and the rachab (breadth) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amah (cubits).

The ayal (posts) of it were toward the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court); and thamar (palm) trees were on its ayal (posts), on this side, and on that side: and the mailah (ascent) to it had shamanah (eight) mailawath (steps).
A room with its pathach (door) was by the ayalayam (posts) at the shairayam (gates); there they dawach (washed) the burnt ilah (offering).

In the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate) were shanayam (two) shalachanawath (tables) on this side, and two shalachanawath (tables) on that side, to shachat (kill) thereon the burnt ilah (offering) and the chataah (sin) offering and the asham (trespass) offering.

On the one kathap (side) outside, as one ilah (go up / offer) up to the entry of the shair (gate) toward the tzapawan (north), were shanayam (two) shalachanawath (tables); and on the other kathap (side), which belonged to the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate), were shanayam (two) shalachanawath (tables).

Arabai (four) shalachanawath (tables) were on this side, and arabai (four) shalachanawath (tables) on that kathap (side), by the side of the shair (gate); shamanah (eight) shalachanawath (tables), whereupon they shachat (killed) the sacrifices.

There were arabai (four) shalachanawath (tables) for the burnt ilah (offering), of cut aban (stone), a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half) arak (length), and a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half) rachab (broad), and achad (one) amah (cubit) gabah (high); whereupon they yanach (laid) the kalayam (instruments) with which they shachat (killed) the burnt ilah (offering) and the zabach (sacrifice).
The shapathayam (hooks), a tapach (handbreadth) long, were kawan (fastened) bayath (house) all around: and on the shalachanawath (tables) was the bashar (flesh) of the qaraban (offering).

Outside of the inner shair (gate) were rooms for the singers in the inner chatzar (court), which was at the kathap (side) of the tzapawan (north) shair (gate); and their prospect was darak (toward) the darawam (south); achad (one) at the kathap (side) of the qadayam (east) shair (gate) having the prospect darak (toward) the tzapawan (north).
He dabar (word / matter) to me, zah (this / that / these) room, whose prospect is darak (toward) the darawam (south), is for the kahanayam (priests), the keepers of the duty of the bayath (house);

And the room whose prospect is darak (toward) the tzapawan (north) is for the kahanayam (priests), the keepers of the duty of the mazabach (altar): these are the banay (sons) of Tzadawaq (Zadok), who from among the banay (sons) of Laway (Levi) qarab (come) near to Yahawah to sharath (minister) to him.

He madad (measured) the chatzar (court), one maah (hundred) amah (cubits) arak (length), and a maah (hundred) amah (cubits) rachab (broad), rabai (fourth); and the mazabach (altar) panayam (face) before the bayath (house).

Then he bawaa (come) me to the awalam (porch) of the bayath (house), and madad (measured) each ayal (post) of the awalam (porch), chamash (five) amawath (cubits) on this side, and chamash (five) amawath (cubits) on that side: and the rachab (breadth) of the shair (gate) was shalawash (three) amawath (cubits) on this side, and shalawash (three) amawath (cubits) on that side.

The arak (length) of the awalam (porch) was isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits), and the rachab (breadth) ishathay (eleven) amah (cubits); even by the mailawath (steps) by which they ilah (go up / offer) up to it: and there were imadayam (pillars) by the ayalayam (posts), achad (one) on this side, and another on that side.

He bawaa (come) me to the hayakal (temple), and madad (measured) the ayalayam (posts), shash (six) amawath (cubits) rachab (broad) on the one pah (side), and shash (six) amawath (cubits) rachab (broad) on the other pah (side), which was the rachab (breadth) of the ahal (tent).

The rachab (breadth) of the pathach (entrance) was ishar (ten) amawath (cubits); and the kathapawath (sides) of the pathach (entrance) were chamash (five) amawath (cubits) on the one side, and chamash (five) amawath (cubits) on the other side: and he madad (measured) its arak (length), arabaiyam (forty) amawath (cubits), and the rachab (breadth), isharayam (twenty) amawath (cubits).

Then bawaa (come) he inward, and madad (measured) each ayal (post) of the pathach (entrance), shanayam (two) amawath (cubits); and the pathach (entrance), shash (six) amawath (cubits); and the rachab (breadth) of the pathach (entrance), shabai (seven) amawath (cubits).

He madad (measured) its arak (length), isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits), and the rachab (breadth), isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits), panayam (face) the hayakal (temple): and he amar (spoke) to me, This is the most qadash (set apart / make holy) place.

Then he madad (measured) the qayar (wall) of the bayath (house), shash (six) amawath (cubits); and the rachab (breadth) of every tzalai (side) room, arabai (four) amawath (cubits), all around the bayath (house) on sabayab (surrounding) side.

The tzalai (side) rooms were in shalawash (three) stories, tzalai (one) over another, and shalawashayam (thirty) in paim (order); and they bawaa (come) into the qayar (wall) which belonged to the bayath (house) for the tzalai (side) rooms all around, that they might achaz (have) hold therein, and not achaz (have) hold in the qayar (wall) of the bayath (house).

The tzalai (side) rooms were broader as they encompassed the mail (top/above) higher and higher; for the encompassing of the bayath (house) went higher and higher around the bayath (house): therefore the rachab (breadth) of the bayath (house) continued upward; and so one ilah (go up / offer) up from the thachathawan (lowest) room to the highest by the thayakawan (middle) room.

I raah (see) also that the bayath (house) had a raised base all around: the mayasadawath (foundations) of the tzalai (side) rooms were a malaa (full) qanah (reed) of shash (six) atzayal (great) amawath (cubits).

The rachab (thickness) of the qayar (wall), which was for the tzalai (side) rooms, on the outside, was chamash (five) amawath (cubits): and that which was yanach (left) was the bayath (house) of the tzalai (side) rooms that belonged to the bayath (house).
Between the rooms was a rachab (breadth) of isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) around the bayath (house) on sabayab (surrounding) side.

The pathach (doors) of the tzalai (side) rooms were toward the yanach (place) that was left, achad (one) pathach (door) darak (toward) the tzapawan (north), and another pathach (door) toward the darawam (south): and the rachab (breadth) of the maqawam (place) that was yanach (left) was chamash (five) amawath (cubits) all around.

The banayan (building) that panayam (face) before the gazarah (separate) place at the paah (side) darak (toward) the yam (sea/waters) was shabaiyam (seventy) amawath (cubits) rachab (broad); and the qayar (wall) of the banayan (building) was chamash (five) amawath (cubits) thick all around, and its arak (length) thashaiyam (ninety) amawath (cubits).

So he madad (measured) the bayath (house), one maah (hundred) amah (cubits) arak (length); and the gazarah (separate) place, and the banayah (building), with its qayar (walls), one maah (hundred) amah (cubits) arak (length);
Also the rachab (breadth) of the panayam (face) of the bayath (house), and of the gazarah (separate) place toward the qadayam (east), one maah (hundred) amah (cubits).

He madad (measured) the arak (length) of the banayan (building) panayam (face) the gazarah (separate) place which was at its achar (other), and its athawaq (galleries) on the one side and on the other side, one maah (hundred) amah (cubits); and the inner hayakal (temple), and the porches of the chatzar (court);

The sapayam (thresholds), and the closed chalawanayam (windows), and the athayaqayam (galleries) around on their shalawash (three) stories, over nagad (against) the sap (threshold), with itz (wood) ceilings all around, and from the aratz (Earth/land) up to the chalawanayam (windows), (now the chalawanayam (windows) were kasah (covered)),
To the space above the pathach (door), even to the inner bayath (house), and outside, and by all the qayar (wall) all around inside and outside, by madah (measure).

It was ishah (make) with karawab (cherubim) and thamar (palm) trees; and a thamar (palm) tree was between karawab (cherub) and karawab (cherub), and every karawab (cherub) had shanayam (two) panayam (face);

So that there was the panayam (face) of a adam (man) toward the thamar (palm) tree on the one side, and the panayam (face) of a young kapayar (lion) toward the thamar (palm) tree on the other side. Thus was it ishah (make) through all the bayath (house) all around:
From the aratz (Earth/land) to above the pathach (door) were karawab (cherubim) and thamar (palm) trees ishah (make): thus was the qayar (wall) of the hayakal (temple).

As for the hayakal (temple), the mazawazah (door) posts were rabai (fourth); and as for the panayam (face) of the qadash (set apart / make holy), the maraah (appearance) of it was as the maraah (appearance) of the temple.

The mazabach (altar) was of itz (wood), shalawash (three) amawath (cubits) gabah (high), and its arak (length) shanayam (two) amawath (cubits); and its maqatzawai (corners), and its arak (length), and its qayar (walls), were of itz (wood): and he dabar (word / matter) to me, This is the shalachan (table) that is panayam (face) Yahawah.
The hayakal (temple) and the qadash (set apart / make holy) had shanayam (two) dalathawath (doors).
The dalathawath (doors) had shanayam (two) leaves apiece, shanayam (two) mawasabah (turning) leaves: shanayam (two) leaves for the achad (one) dalath (door), and shanayam (two) leaves for the other.

There were ishah (make) on them, on the dalathawath (doors) of the hayakal (temple), karawab (cherubim) and thamar (palm) trees, like as were ishah (make) on the qayarawath (walls); and there was a threshold of itz (wood) on the panayam (face) of the awalam (porch) outside.

There were closed chalawanayam (windows) and thamar (palm) trees on the one kathap (side) and on the other side, on the sides of the awalam (porch): thus were the tzalai (side) rooms of the bayath (house), and the thresholds.

Then he yatzaa (go out / come out) me forth into the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court), the darak (way) toward the tzapawan (north): and he bawaa (come) me into the room that was over against the gazarah (separate) place, and which was over against the banayan (building) toward the tzapawan (north).
Panayam (face) the arak (length) of one maah (hundred) amawath (cubits) was the tzapawan (north) pathach (door), and the rachab (breadth) was chamashayam (fifty) amawath (cubits).

Over against the isharayam (twenty) cubits which belonged to the inner chatzar (court), and over against the ratzapah (pavement) which belonged to the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court), was athawaq (gallery) panayam (face) athawaq (gallery) in the shalayashay (third) story.

Panayam (face) the rooms was a mahalak (walk) of ishar (ten) amawath (cubits)' rachab (breadth) inward, a darak (way) of achad (one) amah (cubit); and their pathach (doors) were toward the tzapawan (north).
Now the ilayawan (Ilayawan) rooms were shorter; for the athayaqayam (galleries) took away from these, more than from the thachathawan (lower) and the thayakawan (middle), in the banayan (building).

For they were in shalash (three) stories, and they didn't have imawadayam (pillars) as the imawadayam (pillars) of the chatzarawath (courts): therefore the uppermost was atzal (straitened) more than the thachathawan (lowest) and the thayakawan (middle) from the aratz (Earth/land).
The gadar (wall) that was outside by the side of the rooms, toward the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court) panayam (face) the rooms, its arak (length) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits).

For the arak (length) of the rooms that were in the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits): and behold, panayam (face) the hayakal (temple) were one maah (hundred) amah (cubits).
From under these rooms was the mabawaa (entry) on the qadayam (east) side, as one bawaa (come) into them from the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court).

In the rachab (thickness) of the gadar (wall) of the chatzar (court) darak (toward) the qadayam (east), panayam (face) the gazarah (separate) place, and panayam (face) the banayan (building), there were rooms.

The darak (way) panayam (face) them was like the maraah (appearance) of the lashakah (way) of the rooms which were darak (toward) the tzapawan (north); according to their arak (length) so was their breadth: and all their exits were both according to their mashapat (fashions), and according to their pathach (doors).

According to the pathachay (doors) of the rooms that were darak (toward) the darawam (south) was a pathach (door) at the raash (head) of the darak (way), even the darak (way) hagayan (directly) panayam (face) the gadarah (wall) darak (toward) the qadayam (east), as one bawaa (come) into them.

Then he amar (spoke) to me, The tzapawan (north) rooms and the darawam (south) rooms, which are panayam (face) the gazarah (separate) place, they are the qadash (set apart / make holy) rooms, where the kahanayam (priests) who are qarawab (near) to Yahawah shall akal (eat) the most qadash (set apart / make holy) things: there shall they yanach (lay) the most qadash (set apart / make holy) things, and the meal manachah (offering), and the chataah (sin) offering, and the asham (trespass) offering; for the maqawam (place) is qadawash (holy).

When the kahanayam (priests) bawaa (come) in, then shall they not bawaa (come) out of the qadash (set apart / make holy) place into the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court), but there they shall yanach (lay) their bagadayam (garments) in which they sharath (minister); for they are qadash (set apart / make holy): and they shall labash (put) on other bagadayam (garments), and shall qarab (come close) to that which pertains to the im (nation / people).

Now when he kalah (complete / finish) made an end of madah (measuring) the inner bayath (house), he yatzaa (go out / come out) me forth by the darak (way) of the shair (gate) whose prospect is darak (toward) the qadayam (east), and madad (measured) it all around.

He madad (measured) on the qadayam (east) rawach (spirit / wind) with the madah (measuring) qanah (reed) chamash (five) amah (hundred) qanayam (reeds), with the madah (measuring) qanah (reed) all around.
He madad (measured) on the tzapawan (north) rawach (spirit / wind) chamash (five) maah (hundred) qanayam (reeds) with the madah (measuring) qanah (reed) all around.
He madad (measured) on the darawam (south) rawach (spirit / wind) chamash (five) maah (hundred) qanayam (reeds) with the madah (measuring) qanah (reed).
He sabab (turned) about to the yam (sea/waters) rawach (spirit / wind), and madad (measured) chamash (five) maah (hundred) qanayam (reeds) with the madah (measuring) qanah (reed).

He madad (measured) it on the arabai (four) rawachawath (sides): it had a chawamah (wall) around it, the arak (length) chamash (five) maah (hundred), and the rachab (breadth) chamash (five) maah (hundred), to badal (separated) a separation between that which was qadash (set apart / make holy) and that which was chal (common).
Afterward he yalak (brought) me to the shair (gate), even the shair (gate) that panah (turn) darak (toward) the qadayam (east).

Behold, the kabawad (glory) of the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel) bawaa (come) from the darak (way) of the qadayam (east): and his qawal (sound / voice) was like the qawal (sound / voice) of many mayam (Waters); and the aratz (Earth/land) shined with his kabawad (glory).

It was according to the maraah (appearance) of the maraah (vision) which I raah (see), even according to the maraah (vision) that I raah (see) when I bawaa (come) to shachath (destroy) the iyar (city); and the maraawath (visions) were like the maraah (vision) that I raah (see) by the nahar (river) Kabar (Chebar); and I napal (fall / be cast down) on my panayam (face).
The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) by the darak (way) of the shair (gate) whose prospect is darak (toward) the qadayam (east).
The rawach (spirit / wind) nashaa (lift) me up, and bawaa (come) me into the inner chatzar (court); and behold, the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah malaa (filled) the bayath (house).
I shamai (hearken / hear) one dabar (word / matter) to me out of the bayath (house); and a ayash (man / husband) imad (stood) by me.

He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), this is the maqawam (place) of my kasaa (throne), and the maqawam (place) of the kapawath (soles) of my ragal (feet / foot), where I will shakan (place) in the thawak (midst) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) iwalam (forever). The bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall no more tamaa (defile) my qadash (set apart / make holy) sham (name), neither they, nor their malak (king), by their prostitution, and by the pagar (dead) bodies of their malak (king) in their bamah (high) places;

In their nathan (give) of their sap (threshold) by my sap (threshold), and their doorpost beside my doorpost, and there was but the qayar (wall) between me and them; and they have tamaa (defiled) my qadash (set apart / make holy) sham (name) by their thawaibah (abominations) which they ishah (make) committed: therefore I nathan (give) consumed them in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting).
Now let them rachaq (put) away their prostitution, and the pagar (dead) bodies of their malak (king), rachaq (far) from me; and I will shakan (place) in their thawak (midst) iwalam (forever).

You, ban (son) of adam (man), show the bayath (house) to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), that they may be kalam (ashamed) of their iwan (guilt/iniquity); and let them madad (measure) the thakanayath (pattern).

If they be kalam (ashamed) of all that they ishah (make) done, yadai (make) known to them the tzawarah (form) of the bayath (house), and its thakawanah (fashion), and its exits, and its entrances, and all its tzawarah (forms), and all its chaqah (ordinances), and all its tzawarah (forms), and all its thawarah (instruction); and kathab (write) it in their iyan (eye); that they may shamar (keep/guard) the whole tzawarah (form) of it, and all its chaqah (ordinances), and ishah (make) them.

This is the thawarah (instruction) of the bayath (house): on the raash (head) of the har (mountain) the whole gabawal (border/boundary) around it shall be most qadash (set apart / make holy). Behold, this is the thawarah (instruction) of the bayath (house).

These are the madawath (measures) of the mazabach (altar) by amawath (cubits) (the amah (cubit) is a amah (cubit) and a tapach (handbreadth)): the chayaq (bottom) shall be a amah (cubit), and the tapach (breadth) a amah (cubit), and its gabawal (border/boundary) around its shapah (edge) a zarath (span); and this shall be the base of the mazabach (altar).

From the chayaq (bottom) on the aratz (Earth/land) to the thachathawan (lower) ledge shall be shanayam (two) amawath (cubits), and the rachab (breadth) achad (one) amah (cubit); and from the qatan (small / young / least) ledge to the greater ledge shall be arabai (four) amawath (cubits), and the rachab (breadth) a amah (cubit).
The upper araayal (alter hearth) shall be arabai (four) amawath (cubits); and from the araayal (alter hearth) hearth and upward there shall be arabai (four) qaranawath (horns).
The araayal (alter hearth) hearth shall be shanayam (two) cubits arak (length) by shanayam (two) rachab (broad), rabai (fourth) in the arabai (four) rabai (fourth) of it.

The ledge shall be fourteen cubits arak (length) by fourteen rachab (broad) in the arabai (four) rabai (fourth) of it; and the gabawal (border/boundary) sabayab (surrounding) it shall be chatzay (half) a amah (cubit); and its chayaq (bottom) shall be a amah (cubit) around; and its mailah (ascent/climbing up) shall panah (turn) toward the qadayam (east).

He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: These are the chaqawath (ordinances) of the mazabach (altar) in the yawam (day) when they shall ishah (make) it, to ilah (go up / offer) burnt ilah (offerings) thereon, and to zaraq (sprinkle) dam (blood) thereon.

You shall nathan (give) to the kahanayam (priests) the Lawayay (Levites) who are of the zarai (seed) of Tzadawaq (Zadok), who are qarawab (near) to me, to sharath (minister) to me, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, a ban (son) par (bull) for a chataah (sin) offering.

You shall laqach (take / seize) of its dam (blood), and nathan (give) it on the arabai (four) qaran (horn) of it, and on the arabai (four) panawath (corners) of the ledge, and on the gabawal (border/boundary) all around: thus you shall chataa (cleanse) it and make kapar (atonement) for it.
You shall also laqach (take / seize) the par (bull) of the chataah (sin) offering, and it shall be burnt in the mapaqad (appointed) place of the bayath (house), outside of the maqadash (sanctuary).

On the shanay (second) yawam (day) you shall qarab (come close) a male iz (goat) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish for a chataah (sin) offering; and they shall chataa (cleanse) the mazabach (altar), as they chataa (cleansed) it with the par (bull).

When you have finished chataa (cleansing) it, you shall qarab (come close) a ban (son) par (bull) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish, and a ayal (ram) out of the tzaan (flock) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish.

You shall qarab (come close) them near to Yahawah, and the kahanayam (priests) shall shalak (cast) malach (salt) on them, and they shall ilah (go up / offer) them up for a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah.

Shabai (seven) yamayam (days) you shall ishah (make) every yawam (day) a shaiyar (goat) for a chataah (sin) offering: they shall also ishah (make) a ban (son) par (bull), and a ayal (ram) out of the tzaan (flock), thamayam (complete / whole) blemish.
Shabai (seven) yamayam (days) shall they make kapar (atonement) for the mazabach (altar) and purify it; so shall they malaa (consecrate) it.

When they kalah (complete / finish) accomplished the yamayam (days), it shall be that on the shamayanay (eighth) yawam (day), and halaah (forward), the kahanayam (priests) shall ishah (make) your burnt ilah (offerings) on the mazabach (altar), and your shalam (peace) offerings; and I will ratzah (accept) you, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

Then he shawab (turn back / repent) me back by the darak (way) of the chayatzawan (outer) shair (gate) of the maqadash (sanctuary), which panah (turn) toward the qadayam (east); and it was sagar (shut).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, This shair (gate) shall be sagar (shut); it shall not be pathach (opened), neither shall any ayash (man / husband) bawaa (come) in by it; for Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yashar-Al (Israel), bawaa (come) entered in by it; therefore it shall be sagar (shut).

As for the nashayaa (prince), he shall yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein as nashayaa (prince) to akal (eat) lacham (bread) panayam (face) Yahawah; he shall bawaa (come) by the darak (way) of the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate), and shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out by the darak (way) of the same.

Then he bawaa (come) me by the darak (way) of the tzapawan (north) shair (gate) panayam (face) the bayath (house); and I raah (see), and behold, the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah malaa (filled) the bayath (house) of Yahawah: and I napal (fall / be cast down) on my panayam (face).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (place / establish / appoint) lab (heart), and raah (see) with your iyan (eye), and shamai (hearken / hear) with your azan (ear) all that I dabar (word / matter) you concerning all the chaqawath (ordinances) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and all its thawarah (instruction); and shawam (place / establish / appoint) lab (heart) the mabawaa (entrance) of the bayath (house), with every exit of the maqadash (sanctuary).

You shall amar (spoke) the rebellious, even to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: you bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), let it rab (suffice) you of all your thawaibah (abominations),

In that you bawaa (come) brought in foreigners, iral (uncircumcised) in lab (heart) and iral (uncircumcised) in bashar (flesh), to be in my maqadash (sanctuary), to chalal (profane) it, even my bayath (house), when you qarab (come close) my lacham (bread), the chalab (fat) and the dam (blood), and they have parar (broken) my barayath (covenant), to add to all your thawaibah (abominations).
You have not performed the duty of my qadash (set apart / make holy) things; but you have shawam (place / establish / appoint) performers of my duty in my maqadash (sanctuary) for yourselves.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah, No foreigner, iral (uncircumcised) in lab (heart) and iral (uncircumcised) in bashar (flesh), shall bawaa (come) into my maqadash (sanctuary), of any foreigners who are thawak (midst) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

But the Lawayay (Levites) who rachaq (went) far from me, when Yashar-Al (Israel) thaih (went) astray, who thaih (went) astray from me achar (other) their galawal (idols), they shall nashaa (lift) their iwan (guilt/iniquity).

Yet they shall be masharathayam (ministers) in my maqadash (sanctuary), having paqadah (oversight) at the shairay (gates) of the bayath (house), and sharath (ministering) in the bayath (house): they shall shachat (kill) the burnt ilah (offering) and the zabach (sacrifice) for the im (nation / people), and they shall imad (stand) panayam (face) them to sharath (minister) to them.

Because they sharath (ministered) to them panayam (face) their galawal (idols), and became a makashawal (stumbling) block of iwan (guilt/iniquity) to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel); therefore have I nashaa (lift) up my yad (hand) against them, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, and they shall nashaa (lift) their iwan (guilt/iniquity).

They shall not nagash (come) near to me, to execute the office of kahan (priest) to me, nor to nagash (come) near to any of my qadash (set apart / make holy) things, to the things that are most qadash (set apart / make holy); but they shall nashaa (lift) their kalamah (shame), and their thawaibah (abominations) which they ishah (make) committed.
Yet will I nathan (give) them performers of the duty of the bayath (house), for all its ibadah (service), and for all that shall be ishah (make) therein.

But the kahanayam (priests) the Lawayay (Levites), the banay (sons) of Tzadawaq (Zadok), who performed the duty of my maqadash (sanctuary) when the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) thaih (went) astray from me, they shall qarab (come close) near to me to sharath (minister) to me; and they shall imad (stand) panayam (face) me to qarab (come close) to me the chalab (fat) and the dam (blood), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah:
They shall bawaa (come) into my maqadash (sanctuary), and they shall qarab (come close) near to my shalachan (table), to sharath (minister) to me, and they shall shamar (keep/guard) my instruction.

It shall be that, when they bawaa (come) in at the shairay (gates) of the inner chatzar (court), they shall be labash (clothed) with pashathah (linen) bagaday (garments); and no tzamar (wool) shall ilah (go up / offer) on them, while they sharath (minister) in the shairay (gates) of the inner chatzar (court), and bayath (house).

They shall have pashathah (linen) paaray (tires) on their raash (head), and shall have pashathah (linen) breeches on their waists; they shall not clothe themselves with anything that causes yazai (sweat).

When they yatzaa (go out / come out) forth into the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court), even into the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court) to the im (nation / people), they shall pashat (put) off their bagadayam (garments) in which they sharath (minister), and yanach (lay) them in the qadash (set apart / make holy) rooms; and they shall labash (put) on other bagadayam (garments), that they not qadash (set apart / make holy) the im (nation / people) with their bagadayam (garments).
Neither shall they galach (shave) their raash (head), nor allow their parai (freegrowing locks) to shalach (send) long; they shall only cut off the hair of their raash (head).
Neither shall any of the kahan (priest) shathah (drinks) yayan (wine), when they bawaa (come) into the inner chatzar (court).

Neither shall they laqach (take / seize) for their wives a alamanah (widow), nor her who is garash (put) away; but they shall laqach (take / seize) bathawalath (virgins) of the zarai (seed) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), or a alamanah (widow) who is the widow of a kahan (priest).

They shall yarah (teach) my im (nation / people) the difference between the qadash (set apart / make holy) and the chal (common), and yadai (cause) them to discern between the tamaa (unclean) and the tahawar (clean).

In a rayab (controversy) they shall imad (stand) to shapat (judge / judgement); according to my shapat (judge / judgement) shall they shapat (judge / judgement) it: and they shall shamar (keep/guard) my thawarah (instruction) and my chaqah (statutes) in all my mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) feasts; and they shall make my shabath (shabath / rest) qadash (set apart / make holy).

They shall bawaa (come) in to no mawath (death) adam (person) to tamaa (defile) themselves; but for ab (father), or for am (mother), or for ban (son), or for banath (daughter), for ach (brother/kinsman), or for achawath (sister) who has had no ayash (man / husband), they may tamaa (defile) themselves.
Achar (other) he is taharah (cleansed), they shall sapar (book) to him shabai (seven) yamayam (days).

In the yawam (day) that he bawaa (come) into the qadash (set apart / make holy), into the inner chatzar (court), to sharath (minister) in the qadash (set apart / make holy), he shall qarab (come close) his chataah (sin) offering, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
They shall have an nachalah (inheritance): I am their nachalah (inheritance); and you shall nathan (give) them no achazah (possession) in Yashar-Al (Israel); I am their achazah (possession).
They shall akal (eat) the meal manachah (offering), and the chataah (sin) offering, and the asham (trespass) offering; and every charam (devoted) thing in Yashar-Al (Israel) shall be theirs.

The raashayath (beginning) of all the bakawar (first) fruits of every thing, and every tharawamah (offering) of everything, of all your tharawamah (offerings), shall be for the kahan (priest): you shall also nathan (give) to the kahanayam (priests) the raashayath (beginning) of your irayasah (dough), to cause a barakah (blessing) to nawach (rest) on your bayath (house).
The kahanayam (priests) shall not akal (eat) of anything that dies of nabalah (itself), or is tarapah (torn), whether it be iwap (flying) or animal.

Moreover, when you shall napal (fall / be cast down) by lot the aratz (Earth/land) for nachalah (inheritance), you shall rawam (will lift up) an tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah, a qadash (set apart / make holy) portion of the aratz (Earth/land); the arak (length) shall be the arak (length) of isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) reeds, and the rachab (breadth) shall be ishar (ten) alap (thousand): it shall be qadash (set apart / make holy) in all its gabawal (border/boundary) all around.

Of this there shall be for the qadash (set apart / make holy) place chamash (five) maah (hundred) in length by chamash (five) maah (hundred) in breadth, rabai (fourth) all around; and chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits) for its magarash (suburbs) all around.

Of this madah (measure) you shall madad (measure) a arak (length) of isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand), and a rachab (breadth) of ishar (ten) alap (thousand): and in it shall be the maqadash (sanctuary), which is most qadash (set apart / make holy).

It is a qadash (set apart / make holy) portion of the aratz (Earth/land); it shall be for the kahanayam (priests), the masharathay (ministers) of the maqadash (sanctuary), who qarab (come) near to sharath (minister) to Yahawah; and it shall be a maqawam (place) for their bathayam (houses), and a maqadash (holy) place for the maqadash (sanctuary).

Isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) in arak (length), and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) in rachab (breadth), shall be to the Lawayay (Levites), the masharathay (ministers) of the bayath (house), for a achazah (possession) to themselves, for isharayam (twenty) rooms.

You shall nathan (give) the achazah (possession) of the iyar (city) chamash (five) alap (thousand) rachab (broad), and isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) arak (length), side by side with the tharawamah (offering) of the qadash (set apart / make holy) portion: it shall be for the whole bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Whatever is for the nashayaa (prince) shall be on the one side and on the other side of the qadash (set apart / make holy) tharawamah (offering) and of the achazah (possession) of the iyar (city), in panayam (face) of the qadash (set apart / make holy) tharawamah (offering) and in panayam (face) of the achazah (possession) of the iyar (city), on the yam (sea/waters) paah (side) westward, and on the qadam (east) paah (side) eastward; and in arak (length) answerable to achad (one) of the chalaqayam (portions), from the yam (sea/waters) gabawal (border/boundary) to the qadayam (east) gabawal (border/boundary).

In the aratz (Earth/land) it shall be to him for a achazah (possession) in Yashar-Al (Israel): and my nashayaa (princes) shall no more yanah (oppress) my im (nation / people); but they shall nathan (give) the aratz (Earth/land) to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) according to their shabat (tribes).

Thus naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah: Let it rab (suffice) you, nashayaay (princes) of Yashar-Al (Israel): sawar (remove) chamas (violence) and shad (spoil), and ishah (make) mashapat (justice) and tzadaqah (righteousness); dispossessing my im (nation / people), amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah.
You shall have tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) maazanay (balances), and a tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) ayapah (ephah), and a tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) bath (bath / liquid measure).

The ayapah (ephah) and the bath (bath / liquid measure) shall be of achad (one) thakan (measure), that the bath (bath / liquid measure) may nashaa (lift) the maishar (tenth) part of a chamar (homer), and the ayapah (ephah) the ishayaray (tenth) part of a chamar (homer): its mathakanath (measure) shall be after the chamar (homer).

The shaqal (shekel) shall be isharayam (twenty) garah (gerahs). Isharayam (twenty) shaqalayam (shekels) plus isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) shaqalayam (shekels) plus chamash (fifteen) shaqalayam (shekels) shall be your mina.

This is the tharawamah (offering) that you shall rawam (will lift up): the shashay (sixth) part of an ayapah (ephah) from a chamar (homer) of chatah (wheat); and you shall give the shashah (sixth) part of an ayapah (ephah) from a chamar (homer) of shairah (barley);

And the chaq (statute) portion of shaman (oil), of the bath (bath / liquid measure) of shaman (oil), the maishar (tenth) part of a bath (bath / liquid measure) out of the kar (cor), which is ishar (ten) bathayam (baths), even a chamar (homer); (for ishar (ten) bathayam (baths) are a chamar (homer);)

And achad (one) shah (lamb) of the tzaan (flock), out of two maah (hundred), from the well-watered mashaqah (pastures) of Yashar-Al (Israel—for) a meal manachah (offering), and for a burnt ilah (offering), and for shalam (peace) offerings, to make kapar (atonement) for them, naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
All the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land) shall give to this tharawamah (offering) for the nashayaa (prince) in Yashar-Al (Israel).

It shall be the nashayaa (prince's) part to give the burnt iwalawath (offerings), and the meal manachah (offerings), and the drink nasak (offerings), in the chagayam (feasts), and on the new chadashayam (moons), and on the shabathawath (sabbaths), in all the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) feasts of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel): he shall ishah (make) the sin manachah (offering), and the meal ilah (offering), and the burnt ilah (offering), and the shalam (peace) offerings, to make kapar (atonement) for the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: In the raashawan (first) month, in the achad (one) day of the chadash (month), you shall laqach (take / seize) a ban (son) par (bull) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish; and you shall chataa (cleanse) the maqadash (sanctuary).

The kahan (priest) shall laqach (take / seize) of the dam (blood) of the chataah (sin) offering, and nathan (give) it on the mazawazah (door) posts of the bayath (house), and on the arabai (four) panawath (corners) of the ledge of the mazabach (altar), and on the mazawazah (posts) of the shair (gate) of the inner chatzar (court).

So you shall ishah (make) on the shabai (seven) day of the chadash (month) for everyone who shagah (errs), and for him who is pathay (simple): so you shall make kapar (atonement) for the bayath (house).

In the raashawan (first) month, in the fourteenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month), you shall have the pasach (passover), a chag (feast/festival) of shabawai (seven) yamayam (days); unleavened matzah (bread) shall be akal (eat).
On that yawam (day) shall the nashayaa (prince) ishah (make) for himself and for all the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land) a par (bull) for a chataah (sin) offering.

The shabai (seven) yamay (days) of the chag (feast/festival) he shall ishah (make) a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah, shabai (seven) parayam (bulls) and shabai (seven) ayalayam (rams) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish yawam (day) the shabai (seven) yamay (days); and a male shaiyar (goat) yawam (day) for a chataah (sin) offering.
He shall ishah (make) a meal manachah (offering), an ayapah (ephah) for a par (bull), and an ayapah (ephah) for a ayal (ram), and a hayan (hin) of shaman (oil) to an ayapah (ephah).

In the shabai (seven) month, in the fifteenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month), in the chag (feast/festival), shall he ishah (make) the like the shabayaiy (seventh) yamayam (days); according to the chataah (sin) offering, according to the burnt ilah (offering), and according to the meal manachah (offering), and according to the shaman (oil).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: The shair (gate) of the inner chatzar (court) that panah (turn) toward the qadayam (east) shall be sagar (shut) the shash (six) maishah (working) yamay (days); but on the shabath (shabath / rest) day it shall be pathach (opened), and on the yawam (day) of the new chadash (month) it shall be pathach (opened).

The nashayaa (prince) shall bawaa (come) by the darak (way) of the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate) outside, and shall imad (stand) by the mazawazah (post) of the shair (gate); and the kahanayam (priests) shall ishah (make) his burnt ilah (offering) and his shalam (peace) offerings, and he shall shachah (worship) at the mapathan (threshold) of the shair (gate): then he shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth; but the shair (gate) shall not be sagar (shut) until the irab (evening).

The im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land) shall shachah (worship) at the pathach (door) of that shair (gate) panayam (face) Yahawah on the shabathawath (sabbaths) and on the new chadashayam (moons).

The burnt ilah (offering) that the nashayaa (prince) shall qarab (come close) to Yahawah shall be on the shabath (shabath / rest) yawam (day) shash (six) kabashayam (lambs) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish and a ayal (ram) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish;

And the meal manachah (offering) shall be an ayapah (ephah) for the ayal (ram), and the meal manachah (offering) for the kabashayam (lambs) as he is yad (hand) to give, and a hayan (hin) of shaman (oil) to an ayapah (ephah).

On the yawam (day) of the new chadash (month) it shall be a ban (son) par (bull) thamayam (complete / whole) blemish, and shash (six) kabasham (lambs), and a ayal (ram); they shall be thamayam (complete / whole) blemish:

And he shall ishah (make) a meal manachah (offering), an ayapah (ephah) for the par (bull), and an ayapah (ephah) for the ayal (ram), and for the kabashayam (lambs) according as he is nashag (able), and a hayan (hin) of shaman (oil) to an ayapah (ephah).
When the nashayaa (prince) shall bawaa (come), he shall bawaa (come) in by the darak (way) of the awalam (porch) of the shair (gate), and he shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth by its darak (way).

But when the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land) shall bawaa (come) panayam (face) Yahawah in the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) feasts, he who bawaa (come) by the darak (way) of the tzapawan (north) shair (gate) to shachah (worship) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth by the darak (way) of the nagab (south) shair (gate); and he who bawaa (come) by the darak (way) of the nagab (south) shair (gate) shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth by the darak (way) of the tzapawan (north) shair (gate): he shall not shawab (turn back / repent) by the darak (way) of the shair (gate) by which he bawaa (come) in, but shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth straight nakach (before) him.
The nashayaa (prince), when they bawaa (come) in, shall bawaa (come) in with of them; and when they yatzaa (go out / come out) out, he shall yatzaa (go out / come out) out.

In the chagayam (feasts) and in the mawaidayam (solemnities) the meal manachah (offering) shall be an ayapah (ephah) for a par (bull), and an ayapah (ephah) for a ayal (ram), and for the kabashayam (lambs) as he is yad (hand) to give, and a hayan (hin) of shaman (oil) to an ayapah (ephah).

When the nashayaa (prince) shall ishah (make) a nadabah (voluntary / freewill offering) ilah (offering), a burnt ilah (offering) or shalam (peace) offerings as a freewill nadabah (voluntary / freewill offering) to Yahawah, one shall pathach (open) for him the shair (gate) that panah (turn) toward the qadayam (east); and he shall ishah (make) his burnt ilah (offering) and his shalam (peace) offerings, as he does on the shabath (shabath / rest) yawam (day): then he shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth; and achar (other) his yatzaa (go out / come out) forth one shall sagar (shut) the shair (gate).

You shall ishah (make) a kabash (lamb) a shanah (year) old thamayam (complete / whole) blemish for a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah yawam (day): baqar (morning) by baqar (morning) you shall ishah (make) it.

You shall ishah (make) a meal manachah (offering) with it baqar (morning) by baqar (morning), the shashay (sixth) part of an ayapah (ephah), and the shalayashay (third) part of a hayan (hin) of shaman (oil), to moisten the fine salath (flour); a meal manachah (offering) to Yahawah continually by a iwalam (forever) chaqah (ordinance).
Thus shall they ishah (make) the kabash (lamb), and the meal manachah (offering), and the shaman (oil), baqar (morning) by morning, for a thamayad (continual) burnt ilah (offering).

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: If the nashayaa (prince) nathan (give) a mathanah (gift) to any of his ban (son), it is his nachalah (inheritance), it shall belong to his ban (son); it is their achazah (possession) by nachalah (inheritance).

But if he nathan (give) of his nachalah (inheritance) a mathanah (gift) to achad (one) of his ibad (servant), it shall be his to the shanah (year) of darawar (liberty); then it shall shawab (turn back / repent) to the nashayaa (prince); but as for his nachalah (inheritance), it shall be for his ban (son).

Moreover the nashayaa (prince) shall not laqach (take / seize) of the im (nation / people) nachalah (inheritance), to thrust them out of their achazah (possession); he shall give nachal (inheritance) to his ban (son) out of his own achazah (possession), that my im (nation / people) not be pawatz (scattered) every ayash (man / husband) from his achazah (possession).

Then he bawaa (come) me through the mabawaa (entry), which was at the kathap (side) of the shair (gate), into the qadash (set apart / make holy) rooms for the kahanayam (priests), which panah (turn) toward the tzapawan (north): and behold, there was a maqawam (place) on the hinder yarakah (part) westward.

He amar (spoke) to me, This is the maqawam (place) where the kahanayam (priests) shall bashal (boil) the asham (trespass) offering and the chataah (sin) offering, and where they shall apah (bake) the meal manachah (offering); that they not yatzaa (go out / come out) them forth into the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court), to qadash (set apart / make holy) the im (nation / people).

Then he yatzaa (go out / come out) me forth into the chayatzawan (outer) chatzar (court), and ibar (pass over/through) me to pass by the arabai (four) maqatzawaiy (corners) of the chatzar (court); and behold, in every maqatzawai (corner) of the chatzar (court) there was a chatzar (court).

In the arabai (four) maqatzaiwath (corners) of the chatzar (court) there were chatzarawath (courts) enclosed, arabaiyam (forty) cubits arak (length) and shalawashayam (thirty) rachab (broad): these arabai (four) in the mahaqatzaiwath (corners) were of achad (one) madah (measure).
There was a wall around in them, around the arabai (four), and mabashalah (boiling) places were ishah (make) under the walls all around.

Then he amar (spoke) to me, These are the bashal (boiling) bayath (house), where the masharathay (ministers) of the bayath (house) shall bashal (boil) the zabach (sacrifice) of the im (nation / people).

He shawab (turn back / repent) me back to the pathach (door) of the bayath (house); and behold, mayam (Waters) yatzaa (go out / come out) out from under the mapathan (threshold) of the bayath (house) eastward; (for the panayam (face) of the bayath (house) was toward the qadayam (east);) and the mayam (Waters) yarad (came) down from under, from the yamanay (right) kathap (side) of the bayath (house), on the nagab (south) of the mazabach (altar).

Then he yatzaa (go out / come out) me out by the darak (way) of the shair (gate) northward, and led me round by the darak (way) outside to the outer shair (gate), by the darak (way) of the shair (gate) that panah (turn) toward the qadayam (east); and behold, there pakah (ran) out mayam (Waters) on the yamanay (right) kathap (side).

When the ayash (man / husband) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth eastward with the qaw (line) in his yad (hand), he madad (measured) one alap (thousand) amah (cubits), and he ibar (pass over/through) me to pass through the may (waters), may (waters) that were to the apasayam (ankles).

Again he madad (measured) one alap (thousand), and ibar (pass over/through) me to pass through the may (waters), may (waters) that were to the barakayam (knees). Again he madad (measured) one alap (thousand), and ibar (pass over/through) me to pass through the may (waters), mathanayam (waters) that were to the waist.

Afterward he madad (measured) one alap (thousand); and it was a nachal (stream / river) that I yakal (could) not ibar (pass over/through) through; for the may (waters) were gaah (risen), may (waters) to shachaw (swim) in, a nachal (stream / river) that could not be ibar (pass over/through) through.
He amar (spoke) to me, ban (son) of adam (man), raah (see) you seen this? Then he yalak (brought) me, and caused me to shawab (turn back / repent) to the shapah (bank) of the nachal (stream / river).
Now when I had shawab (turn back / repent), behold, on the shapah (bank) of the nachal (stream / river) were very many itz (trees) on the one side and on the other.

Then he amar (spoke) to me, These mayam (Waters) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth toward the eastern region, and shall bawaa (come) down into the irabah (arabah); and they shall go toward the yam (sea/waters); into the yam (sea/waters) shall the waters yatzaa (go out / come out) which were made to issue forth; and the mayam (Waters) shall be rapaa (healed).

It shall happen, that every living napash (soul) which swarms, in every place where the nachalayam (rivers) bawaa (come), shall chayah (live); and there shall be a very rab (great) multitude of dagah (fish); for these mayam (Waters) bawaa (come) come there, and the waters of the sea shall be rapaa (healed), and everything shall chayay (life) wherever the nachal (stream / river) baaw (comes).

It shall happen, that fishermen shall imad (stand) by it: from Iyan-Gaday (En Gedi) even to Iyanaigalayam (En Eglaim) shall be a place for the mashatawach (spreading) of charamayam (nets); their dagah (fish) shall be after their mayan (species), as the dagah (fish) of the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) yam (sea/waters), maad (exceeding) many.
But the miry places of it, and its marshes, shall not be rapaa (healed); they shall be nathan (give) up to malach (salt).

By the nachal (stream / river) on its shapah (bank), on this side and on that side, shall ilah (go up / offer) every itz (tree) for maakal (food), whose ilah (leaf) shall not nabal (wither), neither shall its paray (fruit) thamam (fail): it shall bakar (bring) forth new fruit every chadash (month), because its mayam (Waters) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the maqadash (sanctuary); and its paray (fruit) shall be for maakal (food), and its ilah (leaf) for healing.

Thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: gah (this) shall be the gabawal (border/boundary), by which you shall divide the aratz (Earth/land) for nachal (inheritance) according to the shanayam (two) shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel): Yawasap (Joseph) shall have two chabalayam (portions).

You shall nachal (inherit) it, ayash (man / husband) as well as ach (brother/kinsman); for I yad (hand) to nathan (give) it to your ab (father): and this aratz (Earth/land) shall napal (fall / be cast down) to you for nachalah (inheritance).

This shall be the gabawal (border/boundary) of the aratz (Earth/land): On the tzapawan (north) paah (side), from the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) yam (sea/waters), by the darak (way) of Chathalan (Hethlon), to the entrance of Tzadad (Zedad);

Chamath (Hamath), Barawathah (Berothah), Sabarayam (Sibraim), which is between the gabawal (border/boundary) of Damashaq (Damascus) and the gabawal (border/boundary) of Chamath (Hamath); Hazer Chatzarahathayakawan (Hatticon), which is by the gabawal (border/boundary) of Chawaran (Hauran).

The gabawal (border/boundary) from the yam (sea/waters), shall be Chatzar-Iyanawan (Hazar Enon) at the gabawal (border/boundary) of Damashaq (Damascus); and on the tzapawan (north) northward is the gabawal (border/boundary) of Chamath (Hamath). This is the tzapawan (north) paah (side).

The qadayam (east) paah (side), bayan (between) Chawaran (Hauran) and Damashaq (Damascus) and Galaid (Gilead), and the aratz (Earth/land) of Yashar-Al (Israel), shall be the Yaradan (Jordan); from the north gabawal (border/boundary) to the qadamawanay (east) yam (sea/waters) you shall madad (measure). This is the qadayam (east) paah (side).

The nagab (south) paah (side) southward shall be from Thamar (Tamar) as far as the may (waters) of Meriboth Qadash (Kadesh), to the nachal (stream / river) of Egypt, to the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) yam (sea/waters). This is the thayaman (south) paah (side) southward.

The yam (sea/waters) paah (side) shall be the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) yam (sea/waters), from the south gabawal (border/boundary) as far as over nakach (against) the entrance of Chamath (Hamath). This is the yam (sea/waters) paah (side).
So you shall chalaq (divide) this aratz (Earth/land) to you according to the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

It shall happen, that you shall napal (fall / be cast down) it by lot for an nachalah (inheritance) to you and to the garayam (aliens) who live thawak (midst) you, who shall yalad (birth / begot) banayam (children) thawak (midst) you; and they shall be to you as the native - azarach (born) among the banayam (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel); they shall napal (fall / be cast down) nachalah (inheritance) with you thawak (midst) the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

It shall happen, that in what shabat (tribe) the gar (sojourner / stranger / foreigner) lives, there you shall nathan (give) him his nachalah (inheritance), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

Now these are the shamawath (names) of the shabatayam (tribes): From the tzapawan (north) qatzah (end / extremity / border), yad (hand) the darak (way) of Chathalan (Hethlon) to the entrance of Chamath (Hamath), Chatzar-Iyanan (Hazar Enan) at the gabawal (border/boundary) of Damashaq (Damascus), northward yad (hand) Chamath (Hamath), (and they shall have their paah (sides) qadayam (east) and yam (sea/waters)), Dan (Dan), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Dan (Dan), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Ashar (Asher), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Ashar (Asher), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) even to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Napathalay (Naphtali), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Napathalay (Naphtali), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Manashah (Manasseh), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Manashah (Manasseh), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Aparayam (Ephraim), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Aparayam (Ephraim), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) even to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Raawaban (Reuben), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Raawaban (Reuben), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Yahawadah (Judah), achad (one) portion.

By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yahawadah (Judah), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), shall be the tharawamah (offering) which you shall rawam (will lift up), twenty - five alap (thousand) reeds in rachab (breadth), and in arak (length) as achad (one) of the chalaqayam (portions), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side): and the maqadash (sanctuary) shall be in its thawak (midst).

The tharawamah (offering) that you shall rawam (will lift up) to Yahawah shall be isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) reeds in arak (length), and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) in rachab (breadth).

For these, even for the kahanayam (priests), shall be the qadash (set apart / make holy) tharawamah (offering): toward the tzapawan (north) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) in length, and toward the yam (sea/waters) ishar (ten) alap (thousand) in rachab (breadth), and toward the qadayam (east) ishar (ten) alap (thousand) in rachab (breadth), and toward the nagab (south) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) in arak (length): and the maqadash (sanctuary) of Yahawah shall be in its thawak (midst).

It shall be for the kahanayam (priests) who are qadash (set apart / make holy) of the banay (sons) of Tzadawaq (Zadok), who have shamar (keep/guard) my instruction, who didn't thaih (go) astray when the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) thaih (went) astray, as the Lawayay (Levites) thaih (went) astray.
