It shall be to them an tharawamayah (offering) from the tharawamah (offering) of the aratz (Earth/land), a thing most qadash (set apart / make holy), by the gabawal (border/boundary) of the Lawayay (Levites).

Answerable to the gabawal (border/boundary) of the kahanayam (priests), the Lawayay (Levites) shall have isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) in arak (length), and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) in rachab (breadth): all the arak (length) shall be isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand), and the rachab (breadth) ishar (ten) alap (thousand).

They shall makar (sell) none of it, nor mawar (exchange) it, nor shall the raashayath (beginning) fruits of the aratz (Earth/land) be ibar (pass over/through); for it is qadash (set apart / make holy) to Yahawah.

The chamash (five) alap (thousand) that are yathar (left) in the rachab (breadth), in panayam (face) of the isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand), shall be for chal (common) use, for the iyar (city), for mawashab (dwelling) and for magarash (suburbs); and the iyar (city) shall be in its thawak (midst).

These shall be its madah (measures): the tzapawan (north) paah (side) arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred), and the nagab (south) paah (side) arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred), and on the qadayam (east) paah (side) arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred), and the yam (sea/waters) paah (side) arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred).

The iyar (city) shall have magarash (suburbs): toward the tzapawan (north) two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty), and toward the nagab (south) two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty), and toward the qadayam (east) two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty), and toward the yam (sea/waters) two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty).

The remainder in the arak (length), answerable to the qadash (set apart / make holy) tharawamah (offering), shall be ishar (ten) alap (thousand) eastward, and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) westward; and it shall be answerable to the qadash (set apart / make holy) tharawamah (offering); and its thabawaah (increase) shall be for lacham (food) to those who ibad (servant) in the iyar (city).
Those who ibad (servant) in the iyar (city), out of all the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel), shall cultivate it.

All the tharawamah (offering) shall be isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) by isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand): you shall rawam (will lift up) the qadash (set apart / make holy) tharawamah (offering) rabayaiy (foursquare), with the achazah (possession) of the iyar (city).

The yathar (residue) shall be for the nashayaa (prince), on the one side and on the other of the qadash (set apart / make holy) tharawamah (offering) and of the achazah (possession) of the iyar (city); in panayam (face) of the isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) of the tharawamah (offering) toward the qadayam (east) gabawal (border/boundary), and westward in panayam (face) of the isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) toward the yam (sea/waters) gabawal (border/boundary), answerable to the chalaqayam (portions), it shall be for the nashayaa (prince): and the qadash (set apart / make holy) tharawamah (offering) and the maqadash (sanctuary) of the bayath (house) shall be in its thawak (midst).

Moreover from the achazah (possession) of the Lawayay (Levites), and from the achazah (possession) of the iyar (city), being in the thawak (midst) of that which is the nashayaa (prince's), between the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yahawadah (Judah) and the gabawal (border/boundary) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), it shall be for the nashayaa (prince).
As for the yathar (rest) of the shabatayam (tribes): from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Banayamayan (Benjamin), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Shamaiwan (Simeon), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Shamaiwan (Simeon), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Yashashakar (Issachar), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Yashashakar (Issachar), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Zabawalawan (Zebulun), achad (one) portion.
By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Zabawalawan (Zebulun), from the qadayam (east) paah (side) to the yam (sea/waters) paah (side), Gad (Gad), achad (one) portion.

By the gabawal (border/boundary) of Gad (Gad), at the nagab (south) paah (side) southward, the gabawal (border/boundary) shall be even from Thamar (Tamar) to the may (waters) of Meribath Qadash (Kadesh), to the nachal (stream / river) of Egypt, to the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) yam (sea/waters).

This is the aratz (Earth/land) which you shall napal (fall / be cast down) by lot to the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel) for nachalah (inheritance), and these are their several machalaqath (portions), naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.
These are the exits of the iyar (city): On the tzapawan (north) paah (side) arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred) reeds by madah (measure);

And the shairay (gates) of the iyar (city) shall be after the shamawath (names) of the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel), shalawash (three) shairay (gates) northward: the shair (gate) of Raawaban (Reuben), achad (one); the shair (gate) of Yahawadah (Judah), achad (one); the shair (gate) of Laway (Levi), achad (one).

At the qadayam (east) paah (side) arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred) reeds, and shalawash (three) shairayam (gates): even the shair (gate) of Yawasap (Joseph), achad (one); the shair (gate) of Banayamayan (Benjamin), achad (one); the shair (gate) of Dan (Dan), achad (one).

At the nagab (south) paah (side) arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred) reeds by madah (measure), and shalawash (three) shairayam (gates): the shair (gate) of Shamaiwan (Simeon), achad (one); the shair (gate) of Yashashakar (Issachar), achad (one); the shair (gate) of Zabawalawan (Zebulun), achad (one).

At the yam (sea/waters) paah (side) arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred) reeds, with their shalawash (three) shair (gates): the shair (gate) of Gad (Gad), achad (one); the shair (gate) of Ashar (Asher), achad (one); the shair (gate) of Napathalay (Naphtali), achad (one).
It shall be eighteen alap (thousand) reeds around: and the sham (name) of the iyar (city) from that yawam (day) shall be, Yahawah is there.

In the shalawash (three) shanah (year) of the malakawath (reign) of Yahawayaqayam (Jehoiakim) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) bawaa (come) Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and tzawar (besieged) it.

The Adanay nathan (give) Yahawayaqayam (Jehoiakim) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) into his yad (hand), with qatzath (part) of the kalayam (vessels) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam; and he bawaa (come) them into the aratz (Earth/land) of Shanair (Shinar) to the bayath (house) of his Alahayam: and he bawaa (come) the kalayam (vessels) into the awatzar (treasure) bayath (house) of his Alahayam.

The malak (king) amar (spoke) to Ashapanaz (Ashpenaz) the rab (master) of his sarayas (eunuchs), that he should bawaa (come) in certain of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), even of the zarai (seed) malawakah (royal) and of the parathamayam (nobles);

Youths in whom was no maawam (blemish), but tawab (good / proper function) - favored, and shakal (skillful) in all chakamah (wisdom), and endowed with daith (knowledge), and bayan (between) madai (science), and such as had kach (strength / mighty / power) to imad (stand) in the malak (king) hayakal (palace); and that he should lamad (teach / instruct) them the sapar (book / scribed document) and the lashawan (tongue / language) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans).

The malak (king) manah (appointed) for them a yawam (day) dabar (word / matter) of the malak (king) dainties, and of the yayan (wine) which he mashathah (drank), and that they should be gadal (nourished) shalawash (three) shanayam (years); that at its qatzath (end) they should imad (stand) panayam (face) the malak (king).
Now among these were, of the banay (children) of Yahawadah (Judah), Danayaal (Daniel), Chananayah (Hananiah), Mayashaal (Mishael), and Izarayah (Azariah).

The shar (prince / ruler) of the sarayasayam (eunuchs) shawam (place / establish / appoint) shamawath (names) to them: to Danayaal (Daniel) he shawam (place / establish / appoint) the name of Balatashaatzar (Belteshazzar); and to Chananayah (Hananiah), of Shadarak (Shadrach); and to Mayashaal (Mishael), of Mayashak (Meshach); and to Izarayah (Azariah), of Ibadanagaw (Abednego).

But Danayaal (Daniel) shawam (place / establish / appoint) in his lab (heart) that he would not gaal (defile) himself with the malak (king) dainties, nor with the yayan (wine) which he mashathah (drank): therefore he baqash (requested) of the shar (prince / ruler) of the sarayasayam (eunuchs) that he might not gaal (defile) himself.
Now Alahayam nathan (give) Danayaal (Daniel) to find chasad (grace) and racham (show mercy / love) in the panayam (face) of the shar (prince / ruler) of the sarayasayam (eunuchs).

The shar (prince / ruler) of the sarayasayam (eunuchs) amar (spoke) to Danayaal (Daniel), I yaraa (fear) my Adawan the malak (king), who has manah (appointed) your maakal (food) and your mashathah (drink): for why should he raah (see) your panayam (face) worse raah (see) than the youths who are of your own age? So would you chawab (endanger) my raash (head) with the malak (king).

Then Danayaal (Daniel) amar (spoke) to the steward whom the shar (prince / ruler) of the sarayasayam (eunuchs) had manah (appointed) over Danayaal (Daniel), Chananayah (Hananiah), Mayashaal (Mishael), and Izarayah (Azariah):
Test your ibad (servant), I beg you, ishar (ten) yamayam (days); and nathan (give) them give us vegetables to akal (eat), and mayam (Waters) to shathah (drinks).

Then let our maraah (faces) be raah (see) on panayam (face) you, and the maraah (face) of the youths who akal (eat) of the malak (king) dainties; and as you raah (see), ishah (make) with your ibad (servant).
So he shamai (hearken / hear) to them in this dabar (word / matter), and nasah (proved) them ishar (ten) yamayam (days).
At the qatzath (end) of ishar (ten) yamayam (days) their maraah (faces) raah (see) fairer, and they were fatter in bashar (flesh), than all the youths who akal (eat) of the malak (king) dainties.
So the steward nashaa (lift) away their dainties, and the yayan (wine) that they should mashathah (drink), and nathan (give) them zarai (pulse).

Now as for these arabai (four) youths, Alahayam nathan (give) them madai (knowledge) and shakal (skill) in all sapar (book / scribed document) and chakamah (wisdom): and Danayaal (Daniel) had bayan (between) in all chazawan (vision) and chalamawath (dreams).

At the qatzath (end) of the yamayam (days) which the malak (king) had amar (spoke) for bawaa (come) them in, the shar (prince / ruler) of the sarayasayam (eunuchs) bawaa (come) them in panayam (face) Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar).

The malak (king) dabar (word / matter) with them; and among them all was matzaa (found) none like Danayaal (Daniel), Chananayah (Hananiah), Mayashaal (Mishael), and Izarayah (Azariah): therefore imad (stood) they panayam (face) the malak (king).

In every dabar (word / matter) of chakamah (wisdom) and bayanah (understanding), concerning which the malak (king) inquired of them, he matzaa (found) them ishar (ten) times better than all the charatamayam (magicians) and enchanters who were in all his malakawath (realm).
Danayaal (Daniel) continued even to the achad (one) shanah (year) of malak (king) Kawarash (Cyrus).

In the shanayam (two) shanah (year) of the malakawath (reign) of Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar), Nabawakadanaatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) chalam (dream) chalamawath (dreams); and his rawach (spirit / wind) was paim (troubled), and his shanah (sleep) went from him.

Then the malak (king) commanded to qaraa (called) the charatamayam (magicians), and the enchanters, and the makashapayam (sorcerers), and the Kashaday (Chaldeans), to nagad (tell) the malak (king) his chalawam (dreams). So they bawaa (come) in and imad (stood) panayam (face) the malak (king).
The malak (king) amar (spoke) to them, I have chalam (dream) a chalawam (dream), and my rawach (spirit / wind) is paim (troubled) to yadai (know) the chalawam (dream).

Then dabar (word / matter) the Kashaday (Chaldeans) to the malak (king) in the Aramayath (Syrian) language, O malak (king), chayaa (live) ilam (forever): amar (spoke) your ibad (servant) the dream, and we will show the pashar (interpretation).

The malak (king) inah (oppress / afflict) the Kashaday (Chaldeans), The thing is azad (gone) from me: if you don't yadai (make) known to me the dream and its pashar (interpretation), you shall be ibad (servant) in hadamayan (pieces), and your bayath (house) shall be shawam (place / establish / appoint) a nawalaw (dunghill).

But if you show the dream and its pashar (interpretation), you shall qabal (receive) of me mathanan (gifts) and nabazabah (rewards) and shagayaa (great) honor: therefore show me the dream and its pashar (interpretation).
They inah (oppress / afflict) the thanayanawath (second) time and amar (spoke), Let the malak (king) amar (spoke) his ibad (servant) the dream, and we will show the pashar (interpretation).
The malak (king) inah (oppress / afflict), I yadai (know) of a yatzayab (certainty) that you would zaban (gain) idan (Idan / Eden), qabal (because) you chazaa (see) the thing is azad (gone) from me.

But if you don't yadai (make) known to me the dream, there is but hawaa (which/who/that is) dath (law) for you; for you have zaman (prepared) kadab (lying) and shachath (corrupt) malah (words) to amar (spoke) qadam (before) me, id (until / as far as) the idan (Idan / Eden) be shanaa (hate): day (therefore) amar (spoke) me the dream, and I shall yadai (know) that you can show me its pashar (interpretation).

The Kashaday (Chaldeans) inah (oppress / afflict) qadam (before) the malak (king), and amar (spoke), There is not a anash (man) on the yabashath (earth) who yakal (can) show the malak (king) malah (matter), qabal (because) no malak (king), Adawan, or shalayat (ruler), has shaal (asked) such a thing of any charatam (magician), or enchanter, or Kashaday (Chaldean).

It is a yaqayar (rare) thing that the malak (king) shaal (requires), and there is no other who can show it qadam (before) the malak (king), lahan (except) the Alahayam, whose madawar (dwelling) is not with bashar (flesh).
For dan (this) kal (every) the malak (king) was banas (angry) and very qatzap (furious), and commanded to abad (destroy / perish) kal (every) the chakayam (wise) men of Babal (Babylon).
So the dath (decree) napaq (went) forth, and the chakayam (wise) men were to be qatal (slain); and they baia (sought) Danayaal (Daniel) and his chabar (companions) to be qatal (slain).

Then Danayaal (Daniel) thawab (returned) answer with itaa (counsel) and prudence to Arayawak (Arioch) the rab (captain) of the malak (king) tabach (guard), who was napaq (gone) forth to kill the chakayam (wise) men of Babal (Babylon);

He inah (oppress / afflict) Arayawak (Arioch) the malak (king) shalayat (captain), mah (why) is the dath (decree) so chatzap (urgent) from the malak (king)? Then Arayawak (Arioch) made the thing yadai (known) to Danayaal (Daniel).
Danayaal (Daniel) ilal (went) in, and baia (desired) of the malak (king) that he would appoint him a zaman (time), and he would show the malak (king) the pashar (interpretation).
Then Danayaal (Daniel) azal (went) to his bayath (house), and made the thing yadai (known) to Chananayah (Hananiah), Mayashaal (Mishael), and Izarayah (Azariah), his chabar (companions):

That they would baia (desire) rachamayan (mercies) of the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven) il (over) dan (this) raz (secret); that Danayaal (Daniel) and his chabar (companions) should not abad (destroy / perish) with the shaar (rest) of the chakayam (wise) men of Babal (Babylon).
Then was the raz (secret) galah (revealed) to Danayaal (Daniel) in a chazaw (vision) of the layalayaa (night). Then Danayaal (Daniel) barak (blessed) the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven).
Danayaal (Daniel) inah (oppress / afflict), barak (blessed) be the sham (name) of Alahayam id (until / as far as) and ilam (ever); for chakamah (wisdom) and gabawarah (might) are his.

He shanaa (hate) the idanay (times) and the zamanay (seasons); he idaa (removes) malakayan (kings), and qawam (rise up) up malakayan (kings); he yahab (gives) chakamah (wisdom) to the chakayam (wise), and manadai (knowledge) to those who have bayanah (understanding);
He galah (reveals) the imayaq (deep) and sathar (secret) things; he yadai (knows) mah (what) is in the chashawak (darkness), and the nahayar (light) sharaa (dwells) with him.

I yadaa (thank) you, and shabach (praise) you, you Alahayam of my ab (father), who have yahab (given) me chakamah (wisdom) and gabawarah (might), and have kain (now) yadai (made) known to me what we baia (desired) of you; for you have yadai (made) known to us the malak (king) malah (matter).

Qabal (therefore) Danayaal (Daniel) ilal (went) in to Arayawak (Arioch), whom the malak (king) had appointed to abad (destroy / perish) the chakayam (wise) men of Babal (Babylon); he azal (went) and amar (spoke) kan (for sure) to him: Don't abad (destroy / perish) the chakayam (wise) men of Babal (Babylon); ilal (bring) me in qadam (before) the malak (king), and I will show to the malak (king) the pashar (interpretation).

Then Arayawak (Arioch) ilal (brought) in Danayaal (Daniel) qadam (before) the malak (king) in bahal (haste), and amar (spoke) kan (for sure) to him, I have shakach (found) a gabar (man) of the banay (children) of the captivity of Yahawad (Judah), who will yadai (make) known to the malak (king) the pashar (interpretation).

The malak (king) inah (oppress / afflict) Danayaal (Daniel), whose sham (name) was Balatashaatzar (Belteshazzar), Are you kahal (able) to yadai (make) known to me the dream which I chazaa (have) seen, and its pashar (interpretation)?

Danayaal (Daniel) inah (oppress / afflict) qadam (before) the malak (king), and amar (spoke), The raz (secret) which the malak (king) has shaal (demanded) yakal (can) neither chakayam (wise) men, enchanters, charatamayan (magicians), nor gazarayan (soothsayers), show to the malak (king);

But there is a Alahayam in shamayan (heaven) who galah (reveals) razayan (secrets), and he has yadai (made) known to the malak (king) Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) mah (what) shall be in the acharayath (latter) yawamay (days). Your dream, and the chazaway (visions) of your raash (head) on your mashakab (bed), are these:

As for you, O malak (king), your raiyawan (thoughts) salaq (came) into your il (over) on your mashakab (bed), mah (what) should happen achar (other); and he who galah (reveals) razay (secrets) has yadai (made) known to you mah (what) shall happen.

But as for me, dan (this) raz (secret) is not galah (revealed) to me for any chakamah (wisdom) that I ayathay (have) more man (from) any chay (life), but to the intent that the pashar (interpretation) may be yadai (made) known to the malak (king), and that you may yadai (know) the raiyawanay (thoughts) of your labab (heart).

You, O malak (king), hawaa (which/who/that is), and alaw (behold), a great tzalam (likeness). Dakan (this) tzalam (likeness), which was rab (mighty), and whose zayaw (brightness) was yathayar (excellent), qawam (rise up) qabal (before) you; and its aspect was awesome.

As for this tzalam (likeness), its raash (head) was of tab (fine) dahab (gold), its chaday (breast) and its darai (arms) of kasap (silver), its maih (belly) and its yarakaa (thighs) of nachash (brass),
Its shaq (legs) of parazal (iron), its ragal (feet) man (from) of parazal (iron), and man (from) of chasap (clay).

You chazaa (saw) id (until / as far as) a aban (stone) was gazar (cut) out laa (NOT) yadayan (hands), which struck the tzalam (likeness) on its ragal (feet) that were of parazal (iron) and chasap (clay), and daqaq (broke) them in daqaq (pieces).

Then was the parazal (iron), the chasap (clay), the nachash (brass), the kasap (silver), and the dahab (gold), daqaq (broken) in pieces chad (together), and hawaa (which/who/that is) like the iwar (chaff) of the qayat (summer) threshing floors; and the rawach (spirit / wind) nashaa (lift) them nashaa (lift), so that no athar (place) was shakach (found) for them: and the aban (stone) that struck the tzalam (likeness) hawaa (which/who/that is) a rab (great) tawar (mountain), and malaa (filled) the kal (every) arai (earth).
Dan (this) is the dream; and we will amar (spoke) its pashar (interpretation) qadam (before) the malak (king).

You, O malak (king), are malak (king) of malakay (kings), to whom the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven) has yahab (given) the malakaw (kingdom), the chasan (power), and the thaqap (strength), and the glory;

And wherever the banay (children) of anash (men) dawar (dwell), the animals of the bar (field) and the birds of the sky has he yahab (given) into your yad (hand), and shalat (has) made you to rule over them kal (every): you are the raash (head) of dahab (gold).

Athar (after) you shall arise acharay (another) malakaw (kingdom) inferior to you; and acharay (another) thalayathay (third) malakaw (kingdom) of nachash (brass), which shall shalat (bear) rule over kal (every) the arai (earth).

The rabayaiy (fourth) malakaw (kingdom) shall be thaqayap (strong) as parazal (iron), because parazal (iron) daqaq (breaks) in pieces and chashal (subdues) kal (every) things; and as parazal (iron) that crushes kal (every) these, shall it daqaq (break) in pieces and raii (crush).

Whereas you chazaa (saw) the ragalay (feet) and atzabaith (toes), man (from) of pachar (potters)' chasap (clay), and man (from) of parazal (iron), it shall be a palag (divided) malakaw (kingdom); but there shall be in it of the natzabah (strength) of the parazal (iron), because you chazaa (saw) the parazal (iron) irab (evening) with tayan (miry) chasap (clay).

As the atzabaith (toes) of the ragalay (feet) were man (from) of parazal (iron), and man (from) of chasap (clay), so the malakaw (kingdom) shall be partly thaqayap (strong), and partly thabar (broken).

Whereas you chazaa (saw) the parazal (iron) irab (evening) with tayan (miry) chasap (clay), they shall hawaa (which/who/that is) themselves with the zarai (seed) of anash (men); but they shall not cling to dan (one) dan (another), even as parazal (iron) does not irab (evening) with chasap (clay).

In the yawam (day) of those malakay (kings) shall the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven) qawam (rise up) up a malakaw (kingdom) which shall ilam (never) be chabal (destroyed), nor shall its sovereignty be shabaq (left) to acharan (another) im (nation / people); but it shall daqaq (break) in pieces and sawap (consume) kal (every) these malakaw (kingdoms), and it shall qawam (rise up) ilam (forever).

Because you chazaa (saw) that a aban (stone) was gazar (cut) out of the tawar (mountain) laa (NOT) yadayan (hands), and that it daqaq (broke) in pieces the parazal (iron), the nachash (brass), the chasap (clay), the kasap (silver), and the dahab (gold); the rab (great) Alahayam has yadai (made) known to the malak (king) mah (what) shall happen achar (other): and the dream is yatzayab (certain), and its pashar (interpretation) aman (believe / have faith).

Then the malak (king) Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) napal (fall / be cast down) on his anap (face), and sagad (worshiped) Danayaal (Daniel), and commanded that they should nasak (offer) an manachah (offering) and nayachawach (sweet) odors to him.

The malak (king) inah (oppress / afflict) to Danayaal (Daniel), and amar (spoke), Of a qashawat (truth) your Alahayam is the Alahayam of Alahayam, and the Adawan of malakayan (kings), and a revealer of razayan (secrets), since you have been yakal (able) to galah (reveal) dan (this) raz (secret).

Then the malak (king) rabah (made) Danayaal (Daniel) rabarab (great), and yahab (gave) him many rabarab (great) mathanan (gifts), and made him to shalat (rule) over the kal (every) madayanah (province) of Babal (Babylon), and to be rab (chief) sagan (governor) over kal (every) the chakayam (wise) men of Babal (Babylon).

Danayaal (Daniel) baia (requested) of the malak (king), and he appointed Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego), over the ibayadah (affairs) of the madayanah (province) of Babal (Babylon): but Danayaal (Daniel) was in the tharai (gate) of the malak (king).

Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king) ibad (servant) an tzalam (likeness) of dahab (gold), whose rawam (will lift up) was shathayan (sixty) amah (cubits), and its pathay (breadth) shath (six) amah (cubits): he qawam (rise up) it up in the baqaia (plain) of Dawaraa (Dura), in the madayanah (province) of Babal (Babylon).

Then Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king) shalach (sent) to kanash (gather) together the satraps, the deputies, and the pachawath (governors), the adaragazaray (judges), the gadabaray (treasurers), the counselors, the thapathay (sheriffs), and kal (every) the shalatanay (rulers) of the madayanah (provinces), to athah (you (masc)) to the chanakaa (dedication) of the tzalam (likeness) which Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king) had qawam (rise up) up.

Then the satraps, the deputies, and the pachawath (governors), the adaragazaray (judges), the gadabaray (treasurers), the counselors, the thapathay (sheriffs), and kal (every) the shalatanay (rulers) of the madayanah (provinces), were kanash (gathered) together to the chanakaa (dedication) of the tzalam (likeness) that Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king) had qawam (rise up) up; and they qawam (rise up) qabal (before) the tzalam (likeness) that Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) had qawam (rise up) up.
Then the karawaz (herald) qaraa (called) chayal (aloud), To you it is commanded, imamay (peoples), amay (nations), and lashanay (languages),

That whenever you shamai (hear) the qal (sound) of the qaran (horn), masharawaqay (flute), zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and kal (every) zanay (kinds) of music, you napal (fall / be cast down) down and sagad (worship) the dahab (golden) tzalam (likeness) that Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king) has qawam (rise up) up;
And whoever doesn't napal (fall / be cast down) down and sagad (worship) shall the same shaih (hour) be ramah (cast) into the gaw (midst) of a yaqad (burning) nawar (fiery) athawan (furnace).

Qabal (therefore) at that zaman (time), when kal (every) the imamay (peoples) shamai (heard) the qal (sound) of the qaran (horn), masharawaqay (flute), zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and kal (every) zanay (kinds) of music, kal (every) the imamay (peoples), the amay (nations), and the lashanay (languages), napal (fall / be cast down) down and sagad (worshiped) the dahab (golden) tzalam (likeness) that Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king) had qawam (rise up) up.
Qabal (therefore) at that zaman (time) gabar (certain) Kashaday (Chaldeans) qarab (came) near, and brought accusation against the Yahawadaay (Jews).
They inah (oppress / afflict) Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king), O malak (king), chayaa (live) for ilam (ever).

You, O malak (king), have shawam (place / establish / appoint) a taim (decree), that kal (every) anash (man) that shall shamai (hear) the qal (sound) of the qaran (horn), masharawaqay (flute), zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and kal (every) zanay (kinds) of music, shall napal (fall / be cast down) down and sagad (worship) the dahab (golden) tzalam (likeness);
And whoever doesn't napal (fall / be cast down) down and sagad (worship) shall be ramah (cast) into the gaw (midst) of a yaqad (burning) nawar (fiery) athawan (furnace).

There are gabar (certain) Yahawadaay (Jews) whom you have appointed over the ibayadah (affairs) of the madayanah (province) of Babal (Babylon): Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego); these gabarayan (men), O malak (king), have not respected you. They don't palach (serve) your Alahayam, nor sagad (worship) the dahab (golden) tzalam (likeness) which you have qawam (rise up) up.

Then Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) in his ragaz (rage) and chamaa (fury) commanded to athah (you (masc)) Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego). Then they athah (you (masc)) these gabaray (men) qadam (before) the malak (king).

Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) inah (oppress / afflict) them, Is it on purpose, Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego), that you don't palach (serve) my Alahayam, nor sagad (worship) the dahab (golden) tzalam (likeness) which I have qawam (rise up) up?

Kain (now) if you are ithayad (ready) whenever you shamai (hear) the qal (sound) of the qaran (horn), masharawaqay (flute), zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and kal (every) zanay (kinds) of music to napal (fall / be cast down) down and sagad (worship) the tzalam (likeness) which I have ibad (servant), well: but if you don't sagad (worship), you shall be ramah (cast) the same shaih (hour) into the gaw (midst) of a yaqad (burning) nawar (fiery) athawan (furnace); and who is that Alahayam that shall shazab (deliver) you out of my yad (hand)?

Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego) inah (oppress / afflict) the malak (king), Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar), we have no chashach (need) to thawab (answer) you in dan (this) pathagam (matter).

If it be so, our Alahayam whom we palach (serve) is yakal (able) to shazab (deliver) us from the yaqad (burning) nawar (fiery) athawan (furnace); and he will shazab (deliver) us out of your yad (hand), O malak (king).

But if not, be it yadai (known) to you, O malak (king), that we ayathay (will) not palach (serve) your Alahayam, nor sagad (worship) the dahab (golden) tzalam (likeness) which you have qawam (rise up) up.

Then was Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) malaa (full) of chamaa (fury), and the tzalam (likeness) of his appearance was shanaa (hate) il (over) Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego): therefore he inah (oppress / afflict), and commanded that they should azaa (heat) the athawan (furnace) shabaih (seven) times more day (than) it was usually azaa (heated).

He commanded certain gabar (mighty) gabarayan (men) who were in his chayal (army) to kapath (bind) Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego), and to ramah (cast) them into the yaqad (burning) nawar (fiery) athawan (furnace).

Then these gabaray (men) were kapath (bound) in their pants, their tunics, and their mantles, and their other labawash (garments), and were ramah (cast) into the gaw (midst) of the yaqad (burning) nawar (fiery) athawan (furnace).

Therefore man (from) the malak (king) commandment was chatzap (urgent), and the athawan (furnace) yathayar (exceeding) azaa (hot), the shabayab (flame) of the nawar (fire) killed alak (those) gabaray (men) who nasaq (took) up Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego).

These thalath (three) gabaray (men), Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego), napal (fall / be cast down) down kapath (bound) into the gaw (midst) of the yaqad (burning) nawar (fiery) athawan (furnace).

Then Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the malak (king) was astonished, and qawam (rise up) up in bahal (haste): he inah (oppress / afflict) and amar (spoke) to his counselors, Didn't we ramah (cast) thalath (three) gabarayan (men) kapath (bound) into the gaw (midst) of the nawar (fire)? They inah (oppress / afflict) the malak (king), yatzayab (true), O malak (king).

He inah (oppress / afflict), Look, I chazaa (see) arabai (four) gabarayan (men) sharaa (loose), halak (move) in the gaw (midst) of the nawar (fire), and they are unharmed; and the aspect of the rabayaiy (fourth) is like a bar (son) of the Alahayam.

Then Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) qarab (came) near to the tharai (mouth) of the yaqad (burning) nawar (fiery) athawan (furnace): he inah (oppress / afflict) and amar (spoke), Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego), you ibad (servant) of the Most ilay (went up) Alahayam, napaq (come) forth, and athah (you (masc)) here. Then Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego) napaq (came) forth out of the gaw (midst) of the nawar (fire).

The satraps, the deputies, and the pachawath (governors), and the malak (king) counselors, being kanash (gathered) together, chazaa (saw) these gabaray (men), that the nawar (fire) had no shalat (power) on their gasham (bodies), nor was the shair (hair) of their raash (head) charak (singed), laa (NOT) were their pants shanaa (hate), nor had the rayach (smell) of nawar (fire) idaa (passed) on them.

Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) inah (oppress / afflict) and amar (spoke), barak (blessed) be the Alahayam of Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego), who has shalach (sent) his malaak (angel / messenger of Yah), and shazab (delivered) his ibad (servant) who rachatz (trusted) in him, and have shanaa (hate) the malak (king) malah (word), and have yahab (yielded) their gasham (bodies), that they might not palach (serve) nor sagad (worship) any Alahayam, lahan (except) their own Alahayam.

Therefore I shawam (place / establish / appoint) a taim (decree), that kal (every) im (nation / people), amah (nation), and lashan (language), which amar (spoke) anything evil il (over) the Alahayam of Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego), shall be ibad (servant) in hadamayan (pieces), and their bayath (house) shall be shawah (made) a nawalaw (dunghill); qabal (because) there is no other Alahayam who is able to natzal (deliver) dan (after) this sort.
Then the malak (king) tzalach (promoted) Shadarak (Shadrach), Mayashak (Meshach), and Ibadanagawaa (Abednego) in the madayanah (province) of Babal (Babylon).
Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) the king, to all the peoples, nations, and languages, who dwell in all the earth: Peace be multiplied to you.
It has seemed good to me to show the signs and wonders that the Ilayawan Alahayam has worked toward me.
How great are his signs! And how mighty are his wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his dominion is from generation to generation.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at rest in my house, and flourishing in my palace.
I saw a dream which made me afraid; and the thoughts on my bed and the visions of my head troubled me.
Therefore yadai (made) I a decree to bring in kal (every) the wise men of Babylon before me, that they might yadai (make) known to me the pashar (interpretation) of the dream.
Then hawaa (which/who/that is) in the magicians, the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers; and I told the dream before them; but they did not make known to me its interpretation.
But at the last Daniel came in before me, whose name was Belteshazzar, according to the name of my Alahayam, and in whom is the spirit of the holy Alahayam: and I told the dream before him, saying,

Belteshazzar, master of the magicians, because I know that the spirit of the holy Alahayam is in you, and no secret troubles you, tell me the visions of my dream that I talal (have) seen, and its interpretation.
Thus were the chazaway (visions) of my raash (head) on my mashakab (bed): I hawaa (which/who/that is), and alaw (behold), a tree in the midst of the earth; and its height was great.
The ayalan (tree) grew, and was strong, and its height reached to the sky, and its sight to the end of all the earth.

The shabaqaw (leaves) of it were beautiful, and its fruit much, and in it was food for all: the animals of the bar (field) had shadow under it, and the birds of the sky lived in its branches, and all flesh was fed from it.
I saw in the visions of my head on my bed, and behold, a watcher and a holy one came down from the sky.
He cried aloud, and said thus, Cut down the tree, and cut off its branches, shake off its leaves, and scatter its fruit: let the animals get away from under it, and the fowls from its branches.

Nevertheless leave the stump of its roots in the earth, even with a band of iron and brass, in the tender grass of the field; and let it be wet with the dew of the sky: and let his portion be with the animals in the grass of the earth:
Let his heart be changed from man's, and let an animal's heart be given to him; and let seven adayan (times) pass over him.

The sentence is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the holy ones; to the intent that the living may know that the Ilayawan rules in the kingdom of rabah (men), and gives it to whomever he will, and sets up over it the lowest of rabah (men).

This dream I, king Nebuchadnezzar, shakan (place) seen; and you, Belteshazzar, declare the interpretation, because kal (every) the wise men of my kingdom are not able to make known to me the interpretation; but you are able; for the spirit of the holy Alahayam is in you.

Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was stricken mute for a while, and his thoughts troubled him. The malak (king) answered, "Belteshazzar, don't let the dream, or the interpretation, trouble you. Belteshazzar answered, "My Adawan, the dream be to those who hate you, and its interpretation to your adversaries.
The ayalan (tree) that you chazaa (saw), which grew, and was strong, whose height reached to the sky, and its sight to all the arai (earth);
Whose leaves were beautiful, and its fruit much, and in it was food for all; under which the animals of the field lived, and on whose branches the birds of the sky had their habitation:
It is you, O king, that are grown and hawaa (which/who/that is) strong; for your greatness is grown, and reaches to the sky, and your dominion to the end of the earth.

Whereas the king saw a watcher and a holy one coming down from the sky, and amar (spoke), Cut down the ayalan (tree), and destroy it; nevertheless shabaq (leave) the iqar (stump) of its sharash (roots) in the earth, even with a band of iron and brass, in the tender grass of the field, and let it be wet with the dew of the sky: and let his portion be with the animals of the field, day (until) seven times pass over him;
This is the interpretation, O malak (king), and it is the decree of the Ilayawan, which has hawaa (which/who/that is) on my Adawan the malak (king):

That you shall be driven from men, and your dwelling shall be with the animals of the field, and you shall be made to eat grass as oxen, and shall be wet with the dew of the sky, and seven times shall pass over you; until you know that the Ilayawan rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he will.
Whereas they commanded to leave the stump of the roots of the tree; your malakaw (kingdom) shall be sure to you, after that you shall have known that the heavens do rule.

Day (therefore), O malak (king), let my counsel be acceptable to you, and break off your sins by righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor; if there may be a lengthening of your tranquility.
All this came on the malak (king) Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar).
At the end of twelve months he was walking in the royal palace of Babylon.
The king spoke and said, "Is not this rabah (great) Babylon, which I have built for the royal dwelling place, by the might of my power and for the glory of my majesty?
While the word was in the king's mouth, there fell a voice from the sky, saying, "O king Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar), to you it is spoken: The malakaw (kingdom) has departed from you:

And you shall be driven from men; and your dawar (dwelling) shall be with the animals of the field; you shall be ibad (servant) to eat grass as oxen; and seven times shall pass over you; day (until) you know that the Ilayawan rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he tzabaa (troop).

The same hour was the thing fulfilled on Nebuchadnezzar: and he was driven from men, and ate grass as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the sky, until his hair was grown like eagles' feathers, and his nails like birds' claws.

At the end of the days I, Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar), lifted up my eyes to shamayan (heaven), and my understanding returned to me, and I blessed the Ilayawan, and I shabach (praised) and honored him who lives forever; for his dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom from generation to generation.

Kal (every) the inhabitants of the arai (earth) are chashab (reputed) as laa (NOT); and he ibad (servant) according to his tzabaa (troop) in the chayal (army) of shamayan (heaven), and among the inhabitants of the arai (earth); and none ayathay (can) machaa (stay) his yad (hand), or ask him, mah (what) are you ibad (servant)?

At the same zaman (time) my manadai (understanding) thawab (returned) to me; and for the glory of my malakaw (kingdom), my hadar (majesty) and zayaw (brightness) thawab (returned) to me; and my counselors and my rabaraban (lords) baia (sought) to me; and I was thaqan (established) in my malakaw (kingdom), and yathayar (excellent) rabaw (greatness) was yasap (added) to me.

Kain (now) I, Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar), shabach (praise) and rawam (will lift up) and honor the malak (king) of shamayan (heaven); for kal (every) his maibad (works) are qashawat (truth), and his arach (ways) dayan (judge); and those who halak (move) in gawah (pride) he is yakal (able) to shapal (abase).

Balashaatzar (Belshazzar) the malak (king) ibad (servant) a rab (great) lacham (feast) to a alap (thousand) of his rabaraban (lords), and shathah (drinks) chamar (wine) qabal (before) the alap (thousand).

Balashaatzar (Belshazzar), while he tasted the chamar (wine), commanded to athah (you (masc)) the dahab (golden) and kasap (silver) maanay (vessels) which Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) his ab (father) had napaq (taken) out of the hayakal (temple) which was in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); that the malak (king) and his rabaraban (lords), his wives and his lachanah (concubines), might shathah (drinks) from them.

Then they athah (you (masc)) the dahab (golden) maanay (vessels) that were napaq (taken) out of the hayakal (temple) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam which was at Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); and the malak (king) and his rabaraban (lords), his wives and his lachanah (concubines), shathah (drinks) from them.
They shathah (drinks) chamar (wine), and shabach (praised) the Alahayam of dahab (gold), and of kasap (silver), of nachash (brass), of parazal (iron), of ai (wood), and of aban (stone).

In the same shaih (hour) napaq (came) forth the atzabain (fingers) of a anash (man's) yad (hand), and kathab (write) over qabal (against) the lampstand on the gayar (plaster) of the kathal (wall) of the malak (king) hayakal (palace): and the malak (king) chazaa (saw) the part of the yad (hand) that kathab (write).

Then the malak (king) zayaw (face) was shanaa (hate) in him, and his raiyawan (thoughts) bahal (troubled) him; and the qataray (joints) of his thighs were loosened, and his arakabah (knees) struck daa (one) against daa (another).

The malak (king) qaraa (called) chayal (aloud) to ilal (bring) in the enchanters, the Kashaday (Chaldeans), and the gazaray (soothsayers). The malak (king) inah (oppress / afflict) and amar (spoke) to the chakayam (wise) men of Babal (Babylon), Whoever shall qaraa (called) dan (this) kathab (write), and show me its pashar (interpretation), shall be labash (clothed) with aragawan (purple), and have a hamanayak (chain) of dahab (gold) il (over) his tzawaar (neck), and shall be the thalayathay (third) shalat (ruler) in the malakaw (kingdom).

Then ilal (came) in kal (every) the malak (king) chakayam (wise) men; but they kahal (could) not qaraa (called) the kathab (write), nor yadai (make) known to the malak (king) the pashar (interpretation).
Then was malak (king) Balashaatzar (Belshazzar) shagayaa (greatly) bahal (troubled), and his zayaw (face) was shanaa (hate) in him, and his rabaraban (lords) were perplexed.

Now the malakaa (queen) by qabal (reason) of the malay (words) of the malak (king) and his rabaraban (lords) ilal (came) into the mashathah (banquet) bayath (house): the malakaa (queen) inah (oppress / afflict) and amar (spoke), O malak (king), chayaa (live) ilam (forever); don't let your raiyawan (thoughts) bahal (trouble) you, nor let your zayaw (face) be shanaa (hate).

There is a gabar (man) in your malakaw (kingdom), in whom is the rawach (spirit / wind) of the qadayash (holy) Alahayam; and in the yawamay (days) of your ab (father) nahayar (light) and shakalathanaw (understanding) and chakamah (wisdom), like the chakamah (wisdom) of the Alahayam, were shakach (found) in him; and the malak (king) Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) your ab (father), the malak (king), I say, your ab (father), qawam (rise up) him rab (master) of the charatamayan (magicians), enchanters, Kashaday (Chaldeans), and gazarayan (soothsayers);

Qabal (because) an yathayar (excellent) rawach (spirit / wind), and manadai (knowledge), and shakalathanaw (understanding), pashar (interpreting) of dreams, and achawah (showing) of dark achayadan (sentences), and sharaa (dissolving) of qatarayan (doubts), were shakach (found) in the same Danayaal (Daniel), whom the malak (king) shawam (place / establish / appoint) Balatashaatzar (Belteshazzar). Kain (now) let Danayaal (Daniel) be qaraa (called), and he will show the pashar (interpretation).

Then was Danayaal (Daniel) ilal (brought) in qadam (before) the malak (king). The malak (king) inah (oppress / afflict) and amar (spoke) to Danayaal (Daniel), Are you that Danayaal (Daniel), who are of the banay (children) of the galawath (captivity) of Yahawad (Judah), whom the malak (king) my ab (father) athah (you (masc)) out of Yahawad (Judah)?

I have shamai (heard) of you, that the rawach (spirit / wind) of the Alahayam is in you, and that nahayar (light) and shakalathanaw (understanding) and yathayar (excellent) chakamah (wisdom) are shakach (found) in you.

Kain (now) the chakayam (wise) men, the enchanters, have been ilal (brought) in qadam (before) me, that they should qaraa (called) dan (this) kathab (write), and yadai (make) known to me its pashar (interpretation); but they kahal (could) not show the pashar (interpretation) of the thing.

But I have shamai (heard) of you, that you yakal (can) give pasharayan (interpretations), and sharaa (dissolve) qatarayan (doubts); kain (now) if you yakal (can) qaraa (called) the kathab (write), and yadai (make) known to me its pashar (interpretation), you shall be labash (clothed) with aragawan (purple), and have a hamanayak (chain) of dahab (gold) il (over) your tzawaar (neck), and shall be the thalath (third) shalat (ruler) in the malakaw (kingdom).

Then Danayaal (Daniel) inah (oppress / afflict) qadam (before) the malak (king), Let your mathanaa (gifts) be to yourself, and yahab (give) your nabazabah (rewards) to acharan (another); baram (nevertheless) I will qaraa (called) the kathab (write) to the malak (king), and yadai (make) known to him the pashar (interpretation).
You, malak (king), the Most ilay (went up) Alahayam yahab (gave) Nabawakadanatzar (Nebuchadnezzar) your ab (father) the malakaw (kingdom), and rabaw (greatness), and glory, and hadar (majesty):

And man (from) of the rabaw (greatness) that he yahab (gave) him, kal (every) the imamay (peoples), amay (nations), and lashanay (languages) hawaa (which/who/that is) and dachal (feared) man (from) him: whom he hawaa (which/who/that is) he killed, and whom he hawaa (which/who/that is) he hawaa (which/who/that is) alive; and whom he hawaa (which/who/that is) he raised up, and whom he hawaa (which/who/that is) he hawaa (which/who/that is) down.

But when his labab (heart) was rawam (will lift up) up, and his rawach (spirit / wind) was thaqap (hardened) so that he dealt proudly, he was nachath (deposed) from his malakaw (kingly) karasaa (throne), and they idaa (took) his glory from him:

And he was tarad (driven) from the banay (sons) of anash (men), and his labab (heart) was shawah (made) im (nation / people) the animals', and his madawar (dwelling) was with the irad (wild) donkeys; he was taim (fed) with grass like oxen, and his gasham (body) was tzabai (wet) with the tal (dew) of the sky; id (until / as far as) he yadai (knew) that the Most ilay (went up) Alahayam shalayat (rules) in the malakaw (kingdom) of anash (men), and that he qawam (rise up) up over it whomever he tzabaa (troop).
You, his bar (son), Balashaatzar (Belshazzar), have not shapal (humbled) your labab (heart), qabal (though) you yadai (knew) kal (every) dan (this),

But have rawam (will lift up) up yourself il (over) the Adawan of shamayan (heaven); and they have athah (you (masc)) the maanay (vessels) of his bayath (house) qadam (before) you, and you and your rabaraban (lords), your wives and your lachanah (concubines), have shathah (drinks) chamar (wine) from them; and you have shabach (praised) the Alahayam of kasap (silver) and dahab (gold), of nachash (brass), parazal (iron), ai (wood), and aban (stone), which don't chazaa (see), nor shamai (hear), nor yadai (know); and the Alahayam in whose yad (hand) your nashamaa (breath) is, and whose are kal (every) your arach (ways), you have not hadar (glorified).
Then was the part of the yad (hand) shalach (sent) from qadam (before) him, and dan (this) kathab (write) was inscribed.
Dan (this) is the kathab (write) that was inscribed: manaa (mene), manaa (mene), thaqal (tekel), paras (upharsin).
Dan (this) is the pashar (interpretation) of the thing: manaa (mene); Alahayam has manaa (numbered) your malakaw (kingdom), and brought it to an end;
Thaqal (tekel); you are thaqal (weighed) in the maazanay (balances), and are shakach (found) chasayar (wanting).
PERES; your malakaw (kingdom) is paras (divided), and yahab (given) to the Maday (Medes) and Paras (Persians).

Then commanded Balashaatzar (Belshazzar), and they labash (clothed) Danayaal (Daniel) with aragawan (purple), and put a hamanayak (chain) of dahab (gold) il (over) his tzawaar (neck), and karaz (made) proclamation il (over) him, that he should be the thalath (third) shalayat (ruler) in the malakaw (kingdom).
In that layalayaa (night) Balashaatzar (Belshazzar) the Kashaday (Chaldean) malak (king) was qatal (slain).
Darayawash (Darius) the Mede qabal (received) the malakaw (kingdom), being about shathayan (sixty) - tharayan (two) shanah (years) bar (old).
It pleased Darayawash (Darius) to set over the malakaw (kingdom) one hundred twenty satraps, who should be throughout the whole malakaw (kingdom);
And over them three presidents, of whom Daniel was one; that these satraps might hawaa (which/who/that is) account to them, and that the king should hawaa (which/who/that is) no damage.

Then this Danayaal (Daniel) was distinguished above the sarakayan (presidents) and the satraps, because an excellent spirit was in him; and the malak (king) thought to hawaa (which/who/that is) him over the whole realm.

Then the sarakay (presidents) and the satraps hawaa (which/who/that is) to find occasion against Danayaal (Daniel) as touching the malakaw (kingdom); but they could find no occasion nor fault, qabal (because) he was faithful, neither was there any error or fault found in him.
Then these men said, "We shall not shakach (find) any ilah (occasion) il (over) qabal (this) Danayaal (Daniel), except we shakach (find) it against him concerning the law of his Alahayam.
Then these presidents and satraps assembled together to the king, and amar (spoke) dan (thus) to him, King Darius, live forever.

All the sarakay (presidents) of the kingdom, the deputies and the satraps, the counselors and the governors, have consulted together to establish a malak (king) statute, and to make a strong decree, that whoever shall ask a petition of any Alahayam or man for thirty days, except of you, O malak (king), he shall be cast into the den of lions.
Day (now), O malak (king), qawam (rise up) the asar (decree), and sign the writing, that it not be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which doesn't alter.
Day (therefore) malak (king) Darius rasham (signed) the kathab (write) and the asar (decree).

When Daniel knew that the kathab (write) was rasham (signed), he went into his house (now his windows were open in his room toward Jerusalem) and he kneeled on his knees three dan (times) a day, and prayed, and gave thanks qabal (before) his Alahayam, as he did before.
Then these men assembled together, and found Danayaal (Daniel) yadai (making) petition and supplication qadam (before) his Alahayam.

Then they came near, and spoke qadam (before) the king concerning the king's decree: Haven't you signed an decree, that every gabar (man) who shall baia (make) petition to any Alahayam or gabar (man) within thirty days, except to you, O king, shall be cast into the den of lions? The king answered, "The thing is true, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which doesn't alter.

Then inah (oppress / afflict) they and amar (spoke) qadam (before) the malak (king), That Paras (Daniel), who is of the children of the captivity of Judah, doesn't respect you, O malak (king), nor the asar (decree) that you have rasham (signed), but baia (makes) his petition three adayan (times) a yawam (day).

Then the malak (king), when he heard these words, was very displeased, and shawam (place / establish / appoint) his heart on Danayaal (Daniel) to deliver him; and he labored day (until) the going down of the sun to rescue him.

Then these men assembled together to the malak (king), and said to the malak (king), Know, O malak (king), that it is a law of the Medes and Persians, that no decree nor statute which the malak (king) establishes may be changed.

Then the malak (king) commanded, and they brought Paras (Daniel), and cast him into the den of lions. Now the malak (king) amar (spoke) and amar (spoke) to Paras (Daniel), Your Alahayam whom you serve continually, he will deliver you.

A stone was athah (you (masc)), and laid on the mouth of the gab (den); and the malak (king) sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that nothing might be changed concerning Danayaal (Daniel).
Then the malak (king) went to his palace, and passed the night fasting; laa (NOT) were instruments of music athah (you (masc)) before him: and his sleep fled from him.
Then the malak (king) arose very early in the morning, and azal (went) in haste to the den of lions.

When he came near to the gab (den) to Daniel, he cried with a lamentable voice; the malak (king) spoke and said to Daniel, Daniel, servant of the living Alahayam, is your Alahayam, whom you serve continually, able to deliver you from the arayawath (lions)?
Then Danayaal (Daniel) amar (spoke) to the malak (king), O malak (king), live forever.
My Alahayam has sent his angel, and has shut the lions' mouths, and they have not hurt me; because as before him innocence was found in me; and also before you, O malak (king), have I done no hurt.

Then was the malak (king) exceeding glad, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no kind of harm was shakach (found) on him, because he had trusted in his Alahayam.

The malak (king) commanded, and they brought those men who had accused Danayaal (Daniel), and they cast them into the gab (den) of lions, them, their children, and their wives; and the lions mauled them, and broke kal (every) their bones in pieces, before they came to the bottom of the gab (den).
Then malak (king) Darius wrote to kal (every) the peoples, nations, and languages, who dwell in kal (every) the earth: Peace be multiplied to you.

I make a decree, that in all the dominion of my kingdom men tremble and fear before the Alahayam of Daniel; for he is the living Alahayam, and steadfast forever, His kingdom that which shall not be destroyed; and his dominion shall be even to the end.
He delivers and rescues, and he works signs and wonders in heaven and in earth, who has delivered Danayaal (Daniel) from the power of the lions.
So this Danayaal (Daniel) prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.

In the chad (first) shanah (year) of Balashaatzar (Belshazzar) malak (king) of Babal (Babylon) Danayaal (Daniel) chazaa (had) a dream and chazaway (visions) of his raash (head) on his mashakab (bed): then he kathab (write) the dream and amar (spoke) the raash (head) of the malayan (matters).

Danayaal (Daniel) inah (oppress / afflict) and amar (spoke), I chazaa (saw) in my chazaw (vision) by layalayaa (night), and, araw (behold), the arabai (four) rawachay (winds) of the sky broke forth on the rab (great) yam (sea).
Arabai (four) rabarab (great) animals salaq (came) up from the yam (sea), shanaa (hate) daa (one) from daa (another).

The qadamay (first) was like a arayah (lion), and had nashar (eagle's) gapayan (wings): I hawaa (which/who/that is) id (until / as far as) its gapayan (wings) were marat (plucked), and it was lifted up from the arai (earth), and qawam (rise up) to stand on two ragalayan (feet) as a anash (man); and a anash (man's) labab (heart) was yahab (given) to it.

Araw (behold), acharay (another) animal, a thanayan (second), damah (like) a dab (bear); and it was qawam (rise up) up on chad (one) shatar (side), and thalath (three) ilaiyan (ribs) were in its pam (mouth) bayan (between) its shanay (teeth): and they amar (spoke) kan (for sure) to it, Arise, akal (devour) much bashar (flesh).

Athar (after) dan (this) I hawaa (which/who/that is), and araw (behold), acharay (another), like a namar (leopard), which had on its gab (back) arabai (four) gapayan (wings) of a bird; the animal had also arabai (four) raashayan (heads); and shalatan (dominion) was yahab (given) to it.

Athar (after) dan (this) I hawaa (which/who/that is) in the layalayaa (night) chazaway (visions), and, araw (behold), a rabayaiy (fourth) animal, awesome and powerful, and thaqayap (strong) yathayar (exceedingly); and it had rabarab (great) parazal (iron) shanayan (teeth); it akal (devoured) and daqaq (broke) in pieces, and rapas (stamped) the shaar (residue) with its ragalay (feet): and it was shanaa (hate) from kal (every) the animals that were qadam (before) it; and it had ishar (ten) qaranayan (horns).

I hawaa (which/who/that is) the qaranay (horns), and alaw (behold), there salaq (came) up bayan (between) them acharay (another) qaran (horn), a zaiyar (little) one, qadam (before) which thalath (three) of the qadamay (first) qaranay (horns) were iqar (plucked) up by the roots: and alaw (behold), in daa (this) qaran (horn) were iyanayan (eyes) like the iyanayan (eyes) of a anash (man), and a pam (mouth) malal (speaking) rabarab (great) things.

I hawaa (which/who/that is) id (until / as far as) karasawan (thrones) were placed, and one who was ithayaq (ancient) of yawamayan (days) yathab (sat): his clothing was chawar (white) as thalag (snow), and the shair (hair) of his raash (head) like naqaa (pure) imar (wool); his karasaa (throne) was nawar (fiery) shabayabayan (flames), and its galagal (wheels) dalaq (burning) nawar (fire).

A nawar (fiery) nahar (stream) nagad (issued) and napaq (came) forth from qadam (before) him: alapayam (thousands) of alapayam (thousands) shamash (around/in attendance) to him, and rabaw (ten) thousand times rabaw (ten) thousand qawam (rise up) qadam (before) him: the dayan (judge) was yathab (set), and the saparayan (books) were pathach (opened).

I hawaa (which/who/that is) at that adayan (time) man (from) of the qal (voice) of the rabarab (great) malay (words) which the qaran (horn) malal (spoke); I hawaa (which/who/that is) even id (until / as far as) the animal was qatal (slain), and its gasham (body) abad (destroy / perish), and it was yahab (given) to be burned with ash (fire).
As for the shaar (rest) of the animals, their shalatan (dominion) was idaa (taken) away: yet their lives were yahab (prolonged) for a zaman (season) and a idan (Idan / Eden).

I hawaa (which/who/that is) in the layalayaa (night) chazaway (visions), and araw (behold), there athah (you (masc)) with the inanay (clouds) of the sky one like a bar (son) of anash (man), and he mataa (came) even to the ithayaq (ancient) of yawamay (days), and they brought him qarab (near) qadam (before) him.

There was yahab (given) him shalatan (dominion), and glory, and a malakaw (kingdom), that kal (every) the imamay (peoples), amay (nations), and lashanay (languages) should palach (serve) him: his shalatan (dominion) is an ilam (everlasting) shalatan (dominion), which shall not idaa (pass) away, and his malakaw (kingdom) that which shall not be chabal (destroyed).
As for me, Danayaal (Daniel), my rawach (spirit / wind) was karaa (grieved) in the gaw (midst) of my nadanah (body), and the chazaway (visions) of my raash (head) bahal (troubled) me.

I qarab (came) near to chad (one) of those who qawam (rise up) by, and baia (asked) him the yatzayab (truth) concerning kal (every) dan (this). So he amar (spoke) me, and yadai (made) me know the pashar (interpretation) of the things.
These rabarab (great) animals, which are arabai (four), are arabai (four) malakayan (kings), who shall arise out of the arai (earth).

But the qadayashay (saints) of the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan) shall qabal (receive) the malakaw (kingdom), and chasan (possess) the malakaw (kingdom) ilam (forever), even ilam (forever) and ilam (ever).

Then I desired to know the yatzab (truth) il (over) the rabayaiy (fourth) animal, which was shanaa (hate) from kal (every) of them, yathayar (exceedingly) dachal (terrible), whose shan (teeth) were of parazal (iron), and its tapar (nails) of nachash (brass); which akal (devoured), daqaq (broke) in pieces, and rapas (stamped) the shaar (residue) with its ragal (feet);

And concerning the ishar (ten) qaranay (horns) that were on its raash (head), and the other horn which salaq (came) up, and man (from) which thalath (three) napal (fall / be cast down), even that qaran (horn) that had iyanayan (eyes), and a pam (mouth) that malal (spoke) rabarab (great) things, whose chazaw (look) was more rab (stout) man (from) its fellows.
I hawaa (which/who/that is), and the same qaran (horn) ibad (servant) qarab (war) with the qadayashayan (saints), and yakal (prevailed) against them;

Id (until / as far as) the ithayaq (ancient) of yawam (day) athah (you (masc)), and dayan (judge) was yahab (given) to the qadayashay (saints) of the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan), and the zaman (time) mataa (came) that the qadayashay (saints) chasan (possessed) the malakaw (kingdom).

Kan (for sure) he amar (spoke), The rabayaiy (fourth) animal shall be a rabayaiy (fourth) malakaw (kingdom) on arai (earth), which shall be shanaa (hate) from kal (every) the malakawath (kingdoms), and shall akal (devour) the kal (every) arai (earth), and shall dawash (tread) it down, and daqaq (break) it in pieces.

As for the ishar (ten) qaranay (horns), out of this malakaw (kingdom) shall ishar (ten) malakayan (kings) arise: and acharan (another) shall arise achar (other) them; and he shall be shanaa (hate) from the former, and he shall shapal (put) down thalath (three) malakayan (kings).

He shall malal (speak) malayan (words) tzad (against) the Most ilay (went up), and shall balaa (wear) out the qadayashay (saints) of the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan); and he shall sabar (think) to shanaa (hate) the zamanayan (times) and the dath (law); and they shall be yahab (given) into his yad (hand) id (until / as far as) a idan (Idan / Eden) and idanayan (times) and half a idan (Idan / Eden).
But the dayan (judge) shall be yathab (set), and they shall idaa (take) away his shalatan (dominion), to shamad (consume) and to abad (destroy / perish) it to the sawap (end).

The malakaw (kingdom) and the shalatan (dominion), and the rabaw (greatness) of the malakawath (kingdoms) under the kal (every) sky, shall be yahab (given) to the im (nation / people) of the qadayashay (saints) of the Most ilayawan (Ilayawan): his malakaw (kingdom) is an ilam (everlasting) malakaw (kingdom), and kal (every) shalatanay (dominions) shall palach (serve) and shamai (obey) him.

Here is the sawap (end) of the malah (matter). As for me, Danayaal (Daniel), my thoughts much bahal (troubled) me, and my zayaw (face) was shanaa (hate) in me: but I natar (kept) the malah (matter) in my lab (heart).

In the shalawash (three) shanah (year) of the malakawath (reign) of malak (king) Balashaatzar (Belshazzar) a chazawan (vision) raah (see) to me, even to me, Danayaal (Daniel), achar (other) that which raah (see) to me at the thachalah (first).

I raah (see) in the chazawan (vision); now it was so, that when I raah (see), I was in the citadel of Shawashan (Susa), which is in the madayanah (province) of Iyalam (Elam); and I raah (see) in the chazawan (vision), and I was by the awabal (river) Awalay (Ulai).

Then I nashaa (lift) up my iyan (eye), and raah (see), and behold, there imad (stood) panayam (face) the awabal (river) a ayal (ram) which had two qaranayam (horns): and the two qaranayam (horns) were gabah (high); but achad (one) was gabah (higher) than the other, and the gabah (higher) ilah (go up / offer) up acharawan (last).

I raah (see) the ayal (ram) nagach (pushing) westward, and northward, and southward; and no animals could imad (stand) panayam (face) him, neither was there any who could natzal (deliver) out of his yad (hand); but he ishah (make) according to his ratzawan (will), and gadal (magnified) himself.

As I was bayan (between), behold, a male tzapayar (goat) bawaa (come) from the mairab (west) over the surface of the whole aratz (Earth/land), and didn't nagai (touch) the aratz (Earth/land): and the tzapayar (goat) had a chazawath (notable) qaran (horn) between his iyan (eye).

He bawaa (come) to the ayal (ram) that bail (had) the two qaranayam (horns), which I raah (see) imad (standing) panayam (face) the awabal (river), and rawatz (ran) on him in the fury of his kach (strength / mighty / power).

I raah (see) him nagai (come) close to the ayal (ram), and he was marar (moved) with anger against him, and nakah (struck) the ayal (ram), and shabar (broke) his shanayam (two) qaran (horn); and there was no kach (strength / mighty / power) in the ayal (ram) to imad (stand) panayam (face) him; but he shalak (cast) him down to the aratz (Earth/land), and ramas (trampled) on him; and there was none who could natzal (deliver) the ayal (ram) out of his yad (hand).

The male iz (goat) gadal (magnified) himself maad (exceedingly): and when he was itzam (strong), the gadal (great) qaran (horn) was shabar (broken); and instead of it there ilah (go up / offer) up arabai (four) notable horns toward the arabai (four) rawachawath (winds) of the sky.

Out of achad (one) of them yatzaa (go out / come out) forth a matzaiyarah (little) qaran (horn), which grew yathar (exceeding) gadal (great), toward the nagab (south), and toward the mazarach (east), and toward the tzabay (glorious) land.

It gadal (grew) great, even to the tzabaa (troop) of the sky; and some of the tzabaa (troop) and of the kawakabayam (stars) it napal (fall / be cast down) down to the aratz (Earth/land), and ramas (trampled) on them.

Yes, it gadal (magnified) itself, even to the shar (prince / ruler) of the tzabaa (troop); and it rawam (will lift up) away from him the thamayad (continual) burnt offering, and the makawan (place) of his maqadash (sanctuary) was shalak (cast) down.

The tzabaa (troop) was nathan (give) over to it together with the thamayad (continual) burnt pashai (offering) through disobedience; and it shalak (cast) down amath (truth) to the aratz (Earth/land), and it ishah (make) its pleasure and tzalach (prospered).

Then I shamai (hearken / hear) a qadawash (holy) one dabar (word / matter); and another holy one amar (spoke) to that palamawanay (certain) one who dabar (word / matter), How long shall be the chazawan (vision) concerning the thamayad (continual) burnt pashai (offering), and the disobedience that shamam (makes) desolate, to nathan (give) both the qadash (set apart / make holy) and the tzabaa (troop) to be trodden under maramas (foot)?
He amar (spoke) to me, To two alap (thousand) and shalawash (three) maah (hundred) irab (evening) and mornings; then shall the qadash (set apart / make holy) be tzadaq (righteous / just / fair).

It happened, when I, even I Danayaal (Daniel), raah (see) seen the chazawan (vision), that I baqash (sought) to understand it; and behold, there imad (stood) before me as the maraah (appearance) of a gabar (man).

I shamai (hearken / hear) a adam (man's) qawal (sound / voice) between the banks of the Awalay (Ulai), which qaraa (called), and amar (spoke), Gabarayaal (Gabriel), make halaz (this) bayan (between) to understand the maraah (vision).

So he bawaa (come) atzal (near) where I imad (stood); and when he bawaa (come), I was frightened, and napal (fall / be cast down) on my panayam (face): but he amar (spoke) to me, bayan (between), ban (son) of adam (man); for the chazawan (vision) belongs to the ith (time) of the qatz (end).
Now as he was dabar (word / matter) with me, I fell into a radam (deep) sleep with my panayam (face) toward the aratz (Earth/land); but he nagai (touched) me, and imad (set) me upright.
He amar (spoke), Behold, I yadai (will) make you know what shall be in the acharayath (latter) time of the zaim (indignation); for it belongs to the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) time of the qatz (end).
The ayal (ram) which you raah (see), that bail (had) the two qaranayam (horns), they are the malakay (kings) of Maday (Media) and Paras (Persia).

The shaiyar (rough) male tzapayar (goat) is the malak (king) of Yawan (Greece): and the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) qaran (horn) that is between his iyan (eye) is the raashawan (first) malak (king).

As for that which was shabar (broken), in the place where arabai (four) imad (stood) up, arabai (four) malakayawath (kingdoms) shall imad (stand) up out of the gaway (heathen / nation), but not with his kach (strength / mighty / power).

In the acharayath (latter) time of their malakawath (kingdom), when the transgressors thamam (have) come to the full, a malak (king) of iz (fierce) panayam (face), and bayan (between) chayadah (dark) sentences, shall imad (stand) up.

His kach (strength / mighty / power) shall be itzam (mighty), but not by his own kach (strength / mighty / power); and he shall shachath (destroy) wonderfully, and shall tzalach (prosper) and ishah (make) his pleasure; and he shall shachath (destroy) the itzawam (mighty) ones and the qadawash (holy) im (nation / people).

Through his shakal (policy) he shall cause maramah (craft) to tzalach (prosper) in his yad (hand); and he shall gadal (magnify) himself in his labab (heart), and in their security shall he shachath (destroy) many: he shall also imad (stand) up against the shar (prince / ruler) of sharayam (princes); but he shall be shabar (broken) apas (without) yad (hand).
The maraah (vision) of the irab (evening) and baqar (morning) which has been amar (spoke) is amath (truth): but seal up the chazawan (vision); for it belongs to many yamayam (days) to come.

I, Danayaal (Daniel), hayah (came to pass), and was chalah (afflict) certain yamayam (days); then I qawam (rise up) up, and ishah (make) the malak (king) malaakah (business): and I shamam (wondered) at the maraah (vision), but none bayan (between) it.

In the achad (one) shanah (year) of Darayawash (Darius) the ban (son) of Achashawarawash (Ahasuerus), of the zarai (seed) of the Maday (Medes), who was made malak (king) over the malakawath (realm) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans),

In the achad (one) shanah (year) of his malak (king) I, Danayaal (Daniel), bayan (between) by the saparayam (books) the masapar (number) of the shanayam (years) about which the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Yaramayah (Jeremiah) the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), for the malaa (accomplishing) of the desolations of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), even shabaiyam (seventy) shanayam (years).
I nathan (give) my panayam (face) to the Adanay Alahayam, to baqash (seek) by thapalah (prayer) and petitions, with tzawam (fasting) and sackcloth and ashes.

I palal (prayed) to Yahawah my Alahayam, and made yadah (confession), and amar (spoke), Oh, Adanay, the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and yaraa (fear / be afraid) Al, who shamaray (keeps) barayath (covenant) and loving chasad (grace) with those who ahab (love) him and shamar (keep/guard) his matzawah (commandments),

We have chataa (sinned), and have dealt iwah (perversely), and have rashai (done) wickedly, and have marad (rebelled), even sawar (turning) aside from your matzawah (precepts) and from your mashapat (ordinances);

Neither have we shamai (hearken / hear) to your ibad (servant) the nabayaayam (prophets), who dabar (word / matter) in your sham (name) to our malak (king), our shar (prince / ruler), and our ab (father), and to all the im (nation / people) of the aratz (Earth/land).

Adanay, tzadaqah (righteousness) belongs to you, but to us bashath (confusion) of panayam (face), as at this yawam (day); to the ayash (man / husband) of Yahawadah (Judah), and to the yawashabay (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), and to all Yashar-Al (Israel), who are qarawab (near), and who are rachawaq (far) off, through all the aratzawath (countries) where you have nadach (driven) them, because of their mail (top/above) that they have mail (top/above) against you.
Adanay, to us belongs bashath (confusion) of panayam (face), to our malak (king), to our shar (prince / ruler), and to our ab (father), because we have chataa (sinned) against you.
To the Adanay our Alahayam belong rachamayam (mercies) and salayachah (forgiveness); for we have marad (rebelled) against him;

Neither have we shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of Yahawah our Alahayam, to yalak (walk) in his thawarah (instruction), which he nathan (give) panayam (face) us by his ibad (servant) the nabayaayam (prophets).

Yes, all Yashar-Al (Israel) ibar (pass over/through) transgressed your thawarah (instruction), sawar (turning) aside, that they should not shamai (hearken / hear) your qawal (sound / voice): therefore the alah (curse / oath) and the shabawaih (oath) kathab (write) in the thawarah (instruction) of Mashah (Moses) the ibad (servant) of Alahayam has been nathak (poured) out on us; for we have chataa (sinned) against him.

He has qawam (rise up) his dabar (word / matter), which he dabar (word / matter) against us, and against our shapat (judge / judgement) who shapat (judge / judgement) us, by bawaa (come) on us a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) rai (evil); for under the whole sky, such ishah (make) not been done as ishah (make) been done to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

As it is kathab (write) in the thawarah (instruction) of Mashah (Moses), all this rai (evil) bawaa (come) come on us: yet have we not entreated the favor of Yahawah our Alahayam, that we should shawab (turn back / repent) from our iwan (guilt/iniquity), and shakal (have) discernment in your amath (truth).

Therefore has Yahawah shaqad (watched) over the rai (evil), and bawaa (come) it on us; for Yahawah our Alahayam is tzadayaq (righteous) in all his maishah (works) which he ishah (make), and we have not shamai (hearken / hear) his qawal (sound / voice).

Now, Adanay our Alahayam, who yatzaa (go out / come out) brought your im (nation / people) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) with a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and ishah (make) gotten yourself sham (name), as at this yawam (day); we have chataa (sinned), we have rashai (done) wickedly.

Adanay, according to all your tzadaqah (righteousness), let your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) and please let your chamah (wrath) be shawab (turn back / repent) away from your iyar (city) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), your qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain); because for our chataa (sins), and for the iwanawath (iniquities) of our ab (father), Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) and your im (nation / people) have become a charapah (reproach) to all who are around us.

Now therefore, our Alahayam, shamai (hearken / hear) to the thapalah (prayer) of your ibad (servant), and to his petitions, and cause your panayam (face) to awar (light) on your maqadash (sanctuary) that is shamam (desolate), for the Adanay sake.

My Alahayam, natah (turn) your azan (ear), and shamai (hearken / hear); paqach (open) your iyan (eye), and raah (see) our desolations, and the iyar (city) which is qaraa (called) by your sham (name): for we do not napal (fall / be cast down) our petitions panayam (face) you for our tzadaqah (righteousness), but for your rab (great) racham (show mercy / love)' sake.

Adanay, shamai (hearken / hear); Adanay, salach (forgive/pardon/make clean); Adanay, listen and ishah (make); don't achar (other), for your own sake, my Alahayam, because your iyar (city) and your im (nation / people) are qaraa (called) by your sham (name).

While I was dabar (word / matter), and palal (praying), and yadah (confessing) my chataah (sin) and the chataah (sin) of my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel), and napal (fall / be cast down) my thachanah (supplication) panayam (face) Yahawah my Alahayam for the qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain) of my Alahayam;

Yes, while I was dabar (word / matter) in thapalah (prayer), the ayash (man / husband) Gabarayaal (Gabriel), whom I raah (see) seen in the chazawan (vision) at the thachalah (beginning), being yaip (caused) to fly yaip (swiftly), nagai (touched) me about the ith (time) of the irab (evening) manachah (offering).
He bayan (between) me, and dabar (word / matter) with me, and amar (spoke), Danayaal (Daniel), I am now yatzaa (go out / come out) forth to give you shakal (wisdom) and bayanah (understanding).

At the thachalah (beginning) of your petitions the commandment yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, and I bawaa (come) come to nagad (tell) you; for you are greatly beloved: therefore bayan (between) the dabar (word / matter), and bayan (between) the maraah (vision).

Shabaiyam (seventy) shabaiyam (weeks) are decreed on your im (nation / people) and on your qadash (set apart / make holy) iyar (city), to kalaa (finish) disobedience, and to chatham (make) an end of chataawath (sins), and to kapar (make) reconciliation for iwan (guilt/iniquity), and to bawaa (come) in iwalam (forever) tzadaq (righteous / just / fair), and to chatham (seal) up chazawan (vision) and nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), and to mashach (anoint) the most qadash (set apart / make holy).

Yadai (know) therefore and discern, that from the mawatzaa (going) forth of the commandment to shawab (turn back / repent) and to banah (build) Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) to the mashayach (anointed one) One, the nagayad (prince), shall be shabai (seven) shabaiyam (weeks), and shashayam (sixty) - shanayam (two) shabaiyam (weeks): it shall be banah (build) again, with rachab (street) and moat, even in troubled ithayam (times).
