Achar (other) the shashayam (sixty) - shanayam (two) shabaiyam (weeks) the mashayach (anointed one) One shall be karath (cut) off, and shall have nothing: and the im (nation / people) of the nagayad (prince) who shall bawaa (come) shall shachath (destroy) the iyar (city) and the qadash (set apart / make holy); and its qatz (end) shall be with a shatap (flood), and even to the qatz (end) shall be malachamah (war); desolations are charatz (determined).

He shall make a firm barayath (covenant) with many for achad (one) shabawai (week): and in the chatzay (midst) of the shabawai (week) he shall cause the zabach (sacrifice) and the manachah (offering) to shabath (shabath / rest); and on the kanap (wing) of shaqawatzayam (abominations) shall come one who shamam (makes) desolate; and even to the kalah (complete / finish) end, and that charatz (determined), shall wrath be nathak (poured) out on the shamam (desolate).

In the shalawash (three) shanah (year) of Kawarash (Cyrus) malak (king) of Paras (Persia) a thing was galah (revealed) to Danayaal (Daniel), whose sham (name) was qaraa (called) Balatashaatzar (Belteshazzar); and the thing was amath (truth), even a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) tzabaa (troop): and he bayan (between) the thing, and had bayanah (understanding) of the maraah (vision).
In those yamayam (days) I, Danayaal (Daniel), was abal (mourning) shalawash (three) yawam (day) shabaiyam (weeks).

I akal (eat) no chamad (pleasant) lacham (bread), neither bawaa (come) bashar (flesh) nor yayan (wine) into my pah (mouth), neither did I sawak (anoint) myself at sawak (all), until shalawash (three) yawam (day) shabaiyam (weeks) were malaa (fulfilled).

In the arabai (four) and isharayam (twenty) yawam (day) of the raashawan (first) chadash (month), as I was by the yad (hand) of the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) nahar (river), which is Chadaqal (Hiddekel),
I nashaa (lift) up my iyan (eye), and raah (see), and behold, a ayash (man / husband) labash (clothed) in bad (linen), whose thighs were adorned with katham (pure) gold of Awapaz (Uphaz):

His gawayah (corpse) also was like the tharashayash (beryl), and his panayam (face) as the maraah (appearance) of baraq (lightning), and his iyan (eye) as ash (fire) torches, and his zarawai (arms) and his maragalah (feet) like qalal (burnished) nachashath (brass), and the qawal (sound / voice) of his dabar (word / matter) like the qawal (sound / voice) of a hamawan (multitude).

I, Danayaal (Daniel), alone raah (see) the maraah (vision); for the anashayam (men) who were with me didn't raah (see) the maraah (vision); but a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) charadah (quaking) napal (fall / be cast down) on them, and they barach (fled) to chabaa (hide) themselves.

So I was shaar (left) alone, and raah (see) this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) maraah (vision), and there shaar (remained) no kach (strength / mighty / power) in me; for my hawad (comeliness) was hapak (turned) in me into mashachayath (corruption), and I itzar (retained) no kach (strength / mighty / power).

Yet shamai (hearken / hear) I the qawal (sound / voice) of his dabar (word / matter); and when I shamai (hearken / hear) the qawal (sound / voice) of his dabar (word / matter), then was I fallen into a radam (deep) sleep on my panayam (face), with my panayam (face) toward the aratz (Earth/land).
Behold, a yad (hand) nagai (touched) me, which nawai (set) me on my barak (blessed) and on the kapawath (palms) of my yad (hand).

He amar (spoke) to me, Danayaal (Daniel), you ayash (man / husband) greatly beloved, bayan (between) the dabarayam (words) that I dabar (word / matter) to you, and imad (stand) upright; for am I now shalach (send) to you. When he had dabar (word / matter) this dabar (word / matter) to me, I imad (stood) raid (trembling).

Then he amar (spoke) to me, Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), Danayaal (Daniel); for from the raashawan (first) yawam (day) that you nathan (give) your lab (heart) to bayan (between), and to inah (oppress / afflict) yourself panayam (face) your Alahayam, your dabar (word / matter) were shamai (hearken / hear): and I bawaa (come) come for your dabar (word / matter)' sake.

But the shar (prince / ruler) of the malakawath (kingdom) of Paras (Persia) withstood me isharayam (twenty) - achad (one) yawam (day); but, behold, Mayakaal (Michael), achad (one) of the chief sharayam (princes), bawaa (come) to izar (help) me: and I yathar (remained) there with the malakay (kings) of Paras (Persia).

Now I bawaa (come) come to bayan (between) you understand what shall qarah (happen) to your im (nation / people) in the acharayath (latter) yamayam (days); for the chazawan (vision) is yet for many yamayam (days):
And when he had dabar (word / matter) to me according to these dabarayam (words), I nathan (give) my panayam (face) toward the aratz (Earth/land), and was mute.

Behold, one in the damawath (likeness) of the banay (sons) of adam (men) nagai (touched) my shapah (lips): then I pathach (opened) my pah (mouth), and dabar (word / matter) and amar (spoke) to him who imad (stood) before me, my Adawan, by reason of the maraah (vision) my tzayar (sorrows) are hapak (turned) on me, and I itzar (retain) no kach (strength / mighty / power).

For hayak (how) yakal (can) the ibad (servant) of this my Adawan dabar (word / matter) with this my Adawan? For as for me, immediately there imad (remained) no kach (strength / mighty / power) in me, neither was there nashamah (breathing thing) shaar (left) in me.
Then there nagai (touched) me again one like the maraah (appearance) of a adam (man), and he chazaq (strengthened) me.

He amar (spoke), "Greatly beloved ayash (man / husband), don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid): shalawam (peace / safety) be to you, be chazaq (strong), yes, be chazaq (strong)." When he dabar (word / matter) to me, I was chazaq (strengthened), and amar (spoke), "Let my Adawan dabar (word / matter); for you have chazaq (strengthened) me."

Then he amar (spoke), "Do you yadai (know) why I bawaa (come) come to you? Now I will shawab (turn back / repent) to lacham (fight) with the shar (prince / ruler) of Paras (Persia). When I yatzaa (go out / come out) forth, behold, the shar (prince / ruler) of Yawan (Greece) shall bawaa (come).

But I will nagad (tell) you that which is inscribed in the kathab (write) of amath (truth): and there is none who chazaq (holds) with me against these, but Mayakaal (Michael) your shar (prince / ruler)."
"As for me, in the achad (one) shanah (year) of Darayawash (Darius) the maday (mede), I imad (stood) up to chazaq (confirm) and maiwaz (stronghold / fortress / protection) him.

Now will I show you the amath (truth). Behold, there shall imad (stand) up yet shalawash (three) malakayam (kings) in Paras (Persia); and the rabayaiy (fourth) shall be ishar (wealth / riches) richer than they all: and when he has grown chazaqah (strong) through his riches, he shall iwar (rouse / awaken) up all against the malakawath (realm) of Yawan (Greece).
A gabawar (mighty) malak (king) shall imad (stand) up, who shall mashal (rule/have dominion) with rab (great) mamashal (authority), and ishah (make) according to his ratzawan (will).

When he shall imad (stand) up, his malakawath (kingdom) shall be shabar (broken), and shall be chatzah (divided) toward the arabai (four) rawachawath (winds) of the sky, but not to his acharayath (posterity), nor according to his mashal (dominion) with which he mashal (rule/have dominion); for his malakawath (kingdom) shall be nathash (plucked) up, even for others besides these.

The malak (king) of the nagab (south) shall be chazaq (strong), and one of his shar (prince / ruler); and he shall be chazaq (strong) above him, and mashal (rule/have dominion) dominion; his mamashalah (dominion) shall be a rab (great) mamashal (authority).

At the qatz (end) of shanayam (years) they shall chabar (join) themselves together; and the banath (daughter) of the malak (king) of the nagab (south) shall bawaa (come) to the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north) to ishah (make) an mayashar (agreement): but she shall not itzar (retain) the kach (strength / mighty / power) of her zarawai (arm); neither shall he imad (stand), nor his zarawai (arm); but she shall be nathan (give) up, and those who bawaa (come) her, and he who became the yalad (birth / begot) of her, and he who chazaq (strengthened) her in those ithayam (times).

But out of a shoot from her sharash (roots) shall one imad (stand) up in his kan (for sure), who shall bawaa (come) to the chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), and shall bawaa (come) into the maiwaz (stronghold / fortress / protection) of the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north), and shall ishah (make) against them, and shall chazaq (prevail).

Also their Alahayam, with their molten nasayak (images), and with their chamadah (goodly) kalay (vessels) of kasap (silver) and of zahab (gold), shall he bawaa (come) shabay (captive) into Matzarayam (Egypt); and he shall refrain some shanayam (years) from the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north).
He shall bawaa (come) into the malakawath (realm) of the malak (king) of the nagab (south), but he shall shawab (turn back / repent) into his own adamah (land).

His ban (son) shall war, and shall asap (assemble) a hamawan (multitude) of rab (great) chayalayam (forces), which shall bawaa (come) on, and shatap (overflow), and ibar (pass over/through) through; and they shall shawab (turn back / repent) and war, even to his maiwaz (stronghold / fortress / protection).

The malak (king) of the nagab (south) shall be marar (moved) with anger, and shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth and lacham (fight) with him, even with the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north); and he shall imad (set) forth a rab (great) hamawan (multitude), and the hamawan (multitude) shall be nathan (give) into his yad (hand).

The hamawan (multitude) shall be rawam (will lift up) up, and his labab (heart) shall be rawam (will lift up); and he shall napal (fall / be cast down) down rabaawath (tens) of thousands, but he shall not izaz (prevail).

The malak (king) of the tzapawan (north) shall shawab (turn back / repent), and shall imad (set) forth a hamawan (multitude) greater than the raashawan (former); and he shall bawaa (come) on at the qatz (end) of the ithayam (times), even of shanayam (years), with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) and with much rakawash (wealth / property / goods / possessions).

In those ithayam (times) there shall many imad (stand) up against the malak (king) of the nagab (south): also the banay (children) of the violent among your im (nation / people) shall nashaa (lift) themselves up to imad (establish) the chazawan (vision); but they shall kashal (stumble / stagger).

So the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north) shall bawaa (come), and shapak (cast) up a mound, and lakad (take) a well-fortified iyar (city): and the forces of the nagab (south) shall not imad (stand), neither his mabachar (chosen) im (nation / people), neither shall there be any kach (strength / mighty / power) to imad (stand).

But he who bawaa (come) against him shall ishah (make) according to his ratzawan (own) will, and none shall imad (stand) panayam (face) him; and he shall imad (stand) in the tzabay (glorious) aratz (Earth/land), and in his yad (hand) shall be destruction.

He shall shawam (place / establish / appoint) his panayam (face) to bawaa (come) with the thaqap (strength) of his whole malakawath (kingdom), and with him equitable conditions; and he shall ishah (make) them: and he shall nathan (give) him the banath (daughter) of nashayam (women), to shachath (corrupt) her; but she shall not imad (stand), neither be for him.

After this shall he shawab (turn back / repent) his panayam (face) to the ayayam (islands), and shall lakad (take) many: but a qatzayan (prince) shall cause the charapah (reproach) offered by him to shabath (shabath / rest); yes, moreover, he shall cause his charapah (reproach) to shawab (turn back / repent) on him.

Then he shall shawab (turn back / repent) his panayam (face) toward the fortresses of his own aratz (Earth/land); but he shall kashal (stumble / stagger) and napal (fall / be cast down), and shall not be matzaa (found).

Then shall imad (stand) up in his kan (for sure) ibar (pass over/through) who shall cause a nagash (tax) collector to pass through the malakawath (kingdom) to maintain its glory; but within achad (one) yamayam (days) he shall be shabar (destroyed), neither in ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), nor in malachamah (battle).

In his kan (for sure) shall imad (stand) up a bazah (contemptible) person, to whom they nathan (give) not given the honor of the malakawath (kingdom): but he shall bawaa (come) in time of security, and shall obtain the malakawath (kingdom) by chalaqalaqawath (flatteries).
The overwhelming forces shall be shatap (overwhelmed) from panayam (face) him, and shall be shabar (broken); yes, also the nagayad (prince) of the barayath (covenant).
After the treaty made with him he shall ishah (make) deceitfully; for he shall ilah (go up / offer) up, and shall become itzam (strong), with a mait (small) gaway (heathen / nation).

In time of security shall he bawaa (come) even on the fattest mashamanay (places) of the madayanah (province); and he shall ishah (make) that which his abawath (fathers) ishah (make) not done, nor his abawath (fathers)' abawath (fathers); he shall bazar (scatter) among them bazah (prey), and shalal (spoil), and rakawash (wealth / property / goods / possessions): yes, he shall chashab (devise) his machashabah (devices) against the strongholds, even for a ith (time).

He shall iwar (rouse / awaken) up his kach (strength / mighty / power) and his labab (courage) against the malak (king) of the nagab (south) with a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor); and the malak (king) of the nagab (south) shall war in malachamah (battle) with an maad (exceeding) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and itzawam (mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor); but he shall not imad (stand); for they shall chashab (devise) machashabawath (devices) against him.

Yes, they who akal (eat) of his dainties shall shabar (destroy) him, and his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) shall shatap (overflow); and many shall napal (fall / be cast down) down chalal (slain).

As for shanayam (two) these malakayam (kings), their labab (hearts) shall be to marai (do) mischief, and they shall dabar (word / matter) kazab (lies) at achad (one) shalachan (table): but it shall not tzalach (prosper); for yet the qatz (end) shall be at the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) appointed.

Then shall he shawab (turn back / repent) into his aratz (Earth/land) with gadawal (very great/important/mighty) rakawash (wealth / property / goods / possessions); and his labab (heart) shall be against the qadash (set apart / make holy) barayath (covenant); and he shall ishah (make) his pleasure, and shawab (turn back / repent) to his own aratz (Earth/land).

At the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) appointed he shall shawab (turn back / repent), and bawaa (come) into the nagab (south); but it shall not be in the acharawan (latter) raashawan (time) as it was in the former.

For tzayayam (ships) of Kathay (Kittim) shall bawaa (come) against him; therefore he shall be kaah (grieved), and shall shawab (turn back / repent), and have zaim (indignation) against the qadash (set apart / make holy) barayath (covenant), and shall ishah (make) his pleasure: he shall even shawab (turn back / repent), and bayan (between) regard to those who izab (forsake) the qadash (set apart / make holy) barayath (covenant).

Forces shall imad (stand) on his part, and they shall chalal (profane) the maqadash (sanctuary), even the maiwaz (stronghold / fortress / protection), and shall sawar (take) away the thamayad (continual) burnt nathan (give), and they shall set up the shaqawatz (abomination) that shamam (makes) desolate.

Such as rashai (do) wickedly against the barayath (covenant) shall he pervert by chalaqawath (flatteries); but the im (nation / people) who yadai (know) their Alahayam shall be chazaq (strong), and ishah (make) exploits.

Those who are shakal (wise) among the im (nation / people) shall bayan (between) many; yet they shall kashal (stumble / stagger) by the charab (sword) and by lahabah (flame), by shabay (captivity) and by bazah (spoil), many yamayam (days).
Now when they shall kashal (stumble / stagger), they shall be izar (helped) with a mait (little) izar (help); but many shall lawah (join) themselves to them with chalaqalaqawath (flatteries).

Some of those who are shakal (wise) shall kashal (stumble / stagger), to tzarap (refine) them, and to barar (purify), and to laban (make) them white, even to the ith (time) of the qatz (end); because it is yet for the mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) appointed.

The malak (king) shall ishah (make) according to his ratzawan (will); and he shall rawam (will lift up) himself, and gadal (magnify) himself above every Al, and shall dabar (word / matter) palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) things against the Al of Al; and he shall tzalach (prosper) until the zaim (indignation) be kalah (complete / finish); for that which is charatz (determined) shall be ishah (make).
Neither shall he bayan (between) the Alahayam of his ab (father), nor the chamadah (desire) of nashayam (women), nor bayan (between) any Alawah; for he shall gadal (magnify) himself above all.

But in his kan (for sure) shall he honor the Alawah of fortresses; and a Alawah whom his ab (father) didn't yadai (know) shall he honor with zahab (gold), and kasap (silver), and with yaqar (precious) aban (stone), and chamad (pleasant) things.

He shall ishah (make) with the strongest fortresses by the help of a foreign Alawah: whoever nakar (acknowledges) him he will rabah (increase) with kabawad (glory); and he shall mashal (rule/have dominion) them to rule over many, and shall chalaq (divide) the adamah (land) for a machayar (price).

At the ith (time) of the qatz (end) shall the malak (king) of the nagab (south) contend with him; and the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north) shall shair (dread / storm / horror) against him like a whirlwind, with rakab (chariots), and with horsemen, and with many anayawath (ships); and he shall bawaa (come) into the aratzawath (countries), and shall shatap (overflow) and ibar (pass over/through) through.

He shall bawaa (come) also into the tzabay (glorious) aratz (Earth/land), and many countries shall be kashal (stumble / stagger); but these shall be malat (delivered) out of his yad (hand): Adawam (Edom), and Mawaab (Moab), and the raashayath (beginning) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon).
He shall shalach (send) forth his yad (hand) also on the aratzawath (countries); and the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt) shall not palayatah (escape).

But he shall have mashal (rule/have dominion) over the makamanay (treasures) of zahab (gold) and of kasap (silver), and over all the chamad (precious) things of Matzarayam (Egypt); and the labayam (libyans) and the Kawashay (Ethiopians) shall be at his matzaid (steps).

But shamaiwath (news) out of the mazarach (east) and out of the tzapawan (north) shall bahal (trouble) him; and he shall yatzaa (go out / come out) forth with gadawal (very great/important/mighty) fury to shamad (destroy) and charam (utterly) to sweep away many.

He shall natai (plant) the ahalay (tents) of his apadan (palace) between the yam (sea/waters) and the tzabay (glorious) qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain); yet he shall bawaa (come) to his qatz (end), and none shall izar (help) him.

"At that ith (time) shall Mayakaal (Michael) imad (stand) up, the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shar (prince / ruler) who imad (stands) for the banay (children) of your im (nation / people); and there shall be a ith (time) of tzarah (trouble), such as never was since there was a gaway (heathen / nation) even to that same ith (time): and at that ith (time) your im (nation / people) shall be malat (delivered), everyone who shall be matzaa (found) kathab (write) in the sapar (book / scribed document).
Many of those who sleep in the ipar (dust) of the adamah (earth) shall qawatz (awake), some to iwalam (forever) chay (life), and some to charapah (shame) and iwalam (forever) daraawan (contempt).

Those who are shakal (wise) shall zahar (warn) as the zahar (brightness) of the expanse; and those who rab (turn) many to tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) as the kawakabayam (stars) id (until / as far as) and iwalam (forever).

But you, Danayaal (Daniel), satham (shut) up the dabarayam (words), and chatham (seal) the sapar (book / scribed document), even to the ith (time) of the qatz (end): many shall shawat (run) back and forth, and daith (knowledge) shall be rabah (increased)."

Then I, Danayaal (Daniel), raah (see), and behold, shanayam (two) others imad (stood), achad (one) on the yaar (river) shapah (bank) on hanah (here) side, and the other on the yaar (river) shapah (bank) on that side.

One amar (spoke) to the ayash (man / husband) labash (clothed) in bad (linen), who was mail (top/above) the mayamay (waters) of the yaar (river), How long shall it be to the qatz (end) of these palaawath (wonders)?

I shamai (hearken / hear) the ayash (man / husband) labash (clothed) in bad (linen), who was mail (top/above) the mayamay (waters) of the yaar (river), when he rawam (will lift up) up his right yamayan (right hand) and his left shamaawal (left hand) to shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and shabai (swear / take oath) by him who chay (life) iwalam (forever) that it shall be for a mawaid (Feast/Holy Day), mawaidayam (times), and a chatzay (half); and when they kalah (complete / finish) made an end of napatz (breaking) in pieces the yad (hand) of the qadash (set apart / make holy) im (nation / people), all these things shall be kalah (complete / finish).
I shamai (hearken / hear), but I didn't bayan (between): then I amar (spoke), my Adawan, what shall be the issue of these things?
He amar (spoke), Go your yalak (way), Danayaal (Daniel); for the dabarayam (words) are satham (shut) up and chatham (sealed) until the ith (time) of the qatz (end).

Many shall barar (purify) themselves, and laban (make) themselves white, and be tzarap (refined); but the rashai (wicked) shall rashai (do) wickedly; and none of the rashai (wicked) shall bayan (between); but those who are shakal (wise) shall bayan (between).

From the ith (time) that the thamayad (continual) burnt offering shall be sawar (taken) away, and the shaqawatz (abomination) that shamam (makes) desolate nathan (give) up, there shall be one alap (thousand) two maah (hundred) thashaiyam (ninety) yamayam (days).
Ashar (who/that) is he who chakah (waits), and nagai (comes) to the one alap (thousand) shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - chamash (five) yamayam (days).
But go you your yalak (way) until the qatz (end); for you shall nawach (rest), and shall imad (stand) in your gawaral (lot), at the qatz (end) of the yamayan (days).

The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah that came to Hawashai (Hosea) the ban (son) of Baaray (Beeri), in the yamay (days) of Izayah (Uzziah), Yawatham (Jotham), Achaz (Ahaz), and Chazaqayah (Hezekiah), malakay (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah), and in the yamay (days) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Yawaash (Joash), malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

When Yahawah amar (spoke) at thachalah (first) by Hawashai (Hosea), Yahawah amar (spoke) to Hawashai (Hosea), "yalak (go), laqach (take / seize) for yourself a ayashah (woman / wife) of prostitution and yaladay (children) of unfaithfulness; for the aratz (Earth/land) zanah (commits) great adultery, forsaking Yahawah."
So he yalak (went) and laqach (take / seize) Gamar (Gomer) the banath (daughter) of Dabalayam (Diblaim); and she harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) him a ban (son).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to him, "qaraa (called) his sham (name) Yazaraial (Jezreel); for yet a mait (little) while, and I will paqad (visit) the dam (blood) of Yazaraial (Jezreel) on the bayath (house) of Yahawaa (Jehu), and will cause the mamalakawath (kingdom) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) to shabath (shabath / rest).
It will happen in that yawam (day) that I will shabar (break) the qashath (bow) of Yashar-Al (Israel) in the imaq (valley) of Yazaraial (Jezreel)."

She harah (conceived) again, and yalad (birth / begot) a banath (daughter). Then he amar (spoke) to him, "qaraa (called) her sham (name) laarachamah (lo-ruhamah); for I will no longer have racham (show mercy / love) on the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), that I should in any way nashaa (lift) them.

But I will have racham (show mercy / love) on the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah), and will yashai (salvation) them by Yahawah their Alahayam, and will not yashai (salvation) them by qashath (bow), charab (sword), malachamah (battle), sawasayam (horses), or horsemen."
Now when she had weaned laarachamah (lo-ruhamah), she harah (conceived), and yalad (birth / begot) a ban (son).
He amar (spoke), "qaraa (called) his sham (name) laaimay (lo-ammi); for you are not my im (nation / people), and I will not be yours.

Yet the masapar (number) of the ban (son) of Yashar-Al (Israel) will be as the chawal (sand) of the yam (sea/waters), which can't be madad (measured) nor sapar (book); and it will come to pass that, in the maqawam (place) where it was amar (spoke) to them, ‘You are not my im (nation / people),' they will be amar (spoke) ‘ban (son) of the chay (life) Al.'

The ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah) and the ban (son) of Yashar-Al (Israel) will be qabatz (gathered) yachad (together), and they will shawam (place / establish / appoint) themselves achad (one) raash (head), and will ilah (go up / offer) up from the aratz (Earth/land); for gadawal (very great/important/mighty) will be the yawam (day) of Yazaraial (Jezreel).
"Amar (spoke) to your brothers, ‘My im (nation / people)!' And to your sisters, ‘My loved one!'

Contend with your mother! Contend, for she is not my wife, neither am I her husband; and let her shawam (place / establish / appoint) away her prostitution from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts;
Lest I strip her naked, and make her bare as in the day that she was born, and make her like a wilderness, and set her like a dry land, and kill her with thirst.
Indeed, on her children I will have no mercy; for they are children of unfaithfulness;

For their mother has played the prostitute. She who conceived them has done shamefully; for she said, ‘I will go after my lovers, who shawam (place / establish / appoint) me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink.'
Therefore, behold, I will hedge up your zanawan (way) with thorns, and I will build a wall against her, that she can't racham (show mercy / love) her zanawan (way).

She will yalak (follow) after her lovers, but she won't overtake them; and she will seek them, but won't find them. Then she will amar (spoke), ‘I will yalak (go) and return to my first husband; for then was it better with me than kay (surely).'
For she did not know that I gave her the grain, the new wine, and the oil, and multiplied to her silver and gold, which they used for Baal.

Therefore I will nashag (take) shawab (turn back / repent) my grain in its raashawan (time), and my new wine in its season, and will pluck away my wool and my flax which should have covered her nakedness.
Now I will uncover her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and no one will nathan (give) her out of my hand.
I will also cause all her celebrations to shawab (turn back / repent): her mawaid (Feast/Holy Day), her new moons, her Sabbaths, and all her solemn mawaid (Feast/Holy Day).
I will lay waste her vines and her fig trees, about which she has said, ‘These are my wages that my lovers have given me; and I will make them a forest,' and the animals of the field shall eat them.
I will visit on her the days of the Baals, to which she burned incense, when she decked herself with her earrings and her jewels, and went after her lovers, and forgot me," says Yahawah.
"Therefore, behold, I will allure her, and shamam (bring) her into the wilderness, and amar (spoke) tenderly to her.

I will paqad (visit) her vineyards from there, and the valley of Achor for a door of hope; and she will respond there, as in the yamay (days) of her youth, and as in the yawam (day) when she yalak (came) up out of the land of Egypt.
It will be in that day," dabar (word / matter) Yahawah, "that you will call me ‘my husband,' and no longer call me ‘my master.'
For I will nathan (give) away the names of the Baals out of her mouth, and they will no longer be ilah (go up / offer) by name.

In that yawam (day) I will make a covenant for them with the animals of the field, and with the birds of the sky, and with the creeping things of the ground. I will hayah (came to pass) the bow, the sword, and the battle out of the land, and will make them lie down safely.
I will betroth you to me forever. Yes, I will betroth you to me in righteousness, in justice, in loving kindness, and in compassion.
I will even betroth you to me in faithfulness; and you shall know Yahawah.
It will happen in that day, I will respond," says Yahawah, "I will respond to the heavens, and they will respond to the earth;
And the earth will respond to the grain, and the new wine, and the oil; and they will respond to Jezreel.

I will sow her to me in the aratz (Earth/land); and I will have naam (declares prophetically) on her who had not obtained naam (declares prophetically); and I will tell those who were not my naam (declares prophetically), ‘You are my naam (declares prophetically);' and they will inah (answer / respond), ‘My Alahayam!'"

Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, "yalak (go) again, ahab (love) a ayashah (woman / wife) ahab (love) by rai (neigbor/another person), and an naap (adulteress), even as Yahawah ahabah (loves) the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), though they panah (turn) to other Alahayam, and ahab (love) cakes of raisins."
So I bought her for myself for fifteen pieces of kasap (silver) and a chamar (homer) and a lathak (half) of shairah (barley).

I amar (spoke) to her, "You shall stay with me many yamayam (days). You shall not zanah (play) the prostitute, and you shall not be with any other ayash (man / husband). I will also be so toward you."

For the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall live many yamayam (days) without malak (king), and without shar (prince / ruler), and without zabach (sacrifice), and without sacred matzabah (stone), and without apawad (ephod) or tharapayam (idols).

Afterward the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) shall shawab (turn back / repent), and baqash (seek) Yahawah their Alahayam, and Dawad (David) their malak (king), and shall come with trembling to Yahawah and to his tawab (good / proper function) in the acharayath (last) yamayam (days).

Shamai (hearken / hear) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, you banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel); for Yahawah has a charge against the yawashabay (inhabitants) of the aratz (Earth/land): "Indeed there is no amath (truth), nor goodness, nor daith (knowledge) of Alahayam in the aratz (Earth/land).
There is alah (swear / adjure), kachash (lying), ratzach (murder), ganab (stealing), and naap (committing) adultery; they paratz (break) boundaries, and bloodshed causes bloodshed.

Therefore the aratz (Earth/land) will abal (mourn), and everyone who yashab (inhabit/dwell) therein will waste away. All chay (life) things in her, even the animals of the shadah (field) and the iwap (flying) of the sky; yes, the dag (fish) of the yam (sea/waters) also asap (die).
"Yet let no ayash (man / husband) bring a charge, neither let any yakach (man) accuse; For your im (nation / people) are like those who bring charges against a kahan (priest).

You will kashal (stumble / stagger) in the yawam (day), and the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) will also kashal (stumble / stagger) with you in the layal (night); and I will damah (destroy) your am (mother).

My im (nation / people) are damah (destroyed) for lack of daith (knowledge). Because you have maas (rejected) daith (knowledge), I will also maas (reject) you, that you may be no kahan (priest) to me. Because you have shakach (forgotten) your Alahayam thawarah (instruction), I will also shakach (forget) your ban (son).
As they were multiplied, so they chataa (sinned) against me. I will mawar (change) their kabawad (glory) into qalawan (shame).
They akal (eat) on the chataah (sin) of my im (nation / people), and nashaa (lift) their napash (soul) on their iwan (guilt/iniquity).
It will be, like im (nation / people), like kahan (priest); and I will paqad (visit) them for their darak (ways), and will repay them for their deeds.
They will akal (eat), and not shabai (have) enough. They will zanah (play) the prostitute, and will not paratz (increase); because they have abandoned giving to Yahawah.
Prostitution, yayan (wine), and new thayarawash (wine) laqach (take / seize) away lab (heart).

My im (nation / people) shaal (consult) with their wooden idol, and answer to a stick of wood. Indeed the rawach (spirit / wind) of prostitution has led them thaih (astray), and they have been unfaithful to their Alahayam.

They zabach (sacrifice) on the raashay (tops) of the harayam (mountains), and qatar (burn) incense on the gabaiwath (hills), under alawan (oaks) and labanah (poplars) and terebinths, because its tzal (shade) is tawab (good / proper function). Therefore your banath (daughter) zanah (play) the prostitute, and your kalah (complete / finish) naap (commit) adultery.

I will not paqad (visit) your banath (daughter) when they zanah (play) the prostitute, nor your kalah (complete / finish) when they naap (commit) adultery; because the men consort with prostitutes, and they zabach (sacrifice) with the shrine prostitutes; so the im (nation / people) without bayan (between) will come to ruin.

"Though you, Yashar-Al (Israel), zanah (play) the prostitute, yet don't let Yahawadah (Judah) asham (offend); and don't bawaa (come) to Galagal (Gilgal), neither ilah (go up / offer) up to Bayathaawan (Beth Aven), nor shabai (swear / take oath), ‘As Yahawah chay (life).'
For Yashar-Al (Israel) has behaved extremely stubbornly, like a sarar (stubborn) parah (heifer). Then how will Yahawah raih (feed) them like a kabash (lamb) in a meadow.
Aparayam (Ephraim) is chabar (joined) to itzabayam (idols). Leave him yanach (alone)!
Their sabaa (drink) has become sawar (sour). They zanah (play) the prostitute zanah (continually). Her magan (shield) dearly ahab (love) their shameful qalawan (way).
The rawach (spirit / wind) has wrapped her up in its kanap (wings); and they shall be disappointed because of their zabach (sacrifices).

"Shamai (hearken / hear) to this, you kahanayam (priests)! Listen, bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and azan (ear) ear, bayath (house) of the malak (king)! For the mashapat (judgment) is against you; for you have been a pach (snare / trap) at Matzapah (Mizpah), and a rashath (net) parash (spread) on Thabawar (Tabor).
The rebels are imaq (deep) in shachat (slaughter); but I mawasar (discipline) all of them.
I yadai (know) Aparayam (Ephraim), and Yashar-Al (Israel) is not kachad (hidden) from me; for now, Aparayam (Ephraim), you have zanah (played) the prostitute. Yashar-Al (Israel) is tamaa (defiled).
Their deeds won't allow them to shawab (turn back / repent) to their Alahayam; for the rawach (spirit / wind) of prostitution is qarab (among / near) them, and they don't yadai (know) Yahawah.

The gaawan (pride) of Yashar-Al (Israel) inah (answer / respond) to his panayam (face). Therefore Yashar-Al (Israel) and Aparayam (Ephraim) will kashal (stumble / stagger) in their iwan (guilt/iniquity). Yahawadah (Judah) also will kashal (stumble / stagger) with them.
They will yalak (go) with their tzaan (flocks) and with their baqar (morning) to baqash (seek) Yahawah; but they won't matzaa (find) him. He has chalatz (withdrawn) himself from them.
They are bagad (unfaithful) to Yahawah; for they have yalad (birth / begot) illegitimate banayam (children). Now the new chadash (month) will akal (eat) them with their fields.

"Thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn) in Gabaih (Gibeah), and the chatzatzarah (trumpet) in Ramah (Ramah)! Rawai (sound) a battle cry at Bayathaawan (Beth Aven), achar (other) you, Banayamayan (Benjamin)!

Aparayam (Ephraim) will become a shamah (desolation) in the yawam (day) of thawakachah (rebuke). Among the shabatay (tribes) of Yashar-Al (Israel), I yadai (have) made known that which will aman (believe / have faith) be.
The sharay (princes) of Yahawadah (Judah) are like those who nasag (remove) a gabawal (border/boundary). I will shapak (pour) out my ibarah (wrath) on them like mayam (Waters).
Aparayam (Ephraim) is ishaq (oppressed), he is ratzatz (crushed) in mashapat (judgment); Because he is intent in his pursuit of idols.
Therefore I am to Aparayam (Ephraim) like a ish (made), and to the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) like raqab (rottenness).

"When Aparayam (Ephraim) raah (see) his chalay (sickness), and Yahawadah (Judah) his mazawar (wound), Then Aparayam (Ephraim) yalak (went) to Ashawar (Assyria), and shalach (send) to malak (king) Yarab (Jareb): but he is not yakal (able) to rapaa (heal) you, neither will he gahah (cure) you of your mazawar (wound).

For I will be to Aparayam (Ephraim) like a shachal (lion), and like a young kapayar (lion) to the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah). I myself will tarap (tear) in pieces and yalak (go) away. I will nashaa (lift) off, and there will be no one to natzal (deliver).

I will yalak (go) and shawab (turn back / repent) to my maqawam (place), until they acknowledge their offense, and baqash (seek) my panayam (face). In their tzar (oppressor / distressor) they will shachar (seek) me earnestly."
"Yalak (come), and let us shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah; for he has tarap (torn) us to pieces, and he will rapaa (heal) us; he has injured us, and he will chabash (bind) up our wounds.
After yawam (day) days he will chayah (revive) us. On the shalayashay (third) yawam (day) he will qawam (rise up) us up, and we will chayah (live) panayam (face) him.

Yadai (let) us acknowledge Yahawah. Let us press on to yadai (know) Yahawah. As surely as the sun rises, Yahawah will appear. He will bawaa (come) to us like the rain, like the spring rain that waters the aratz (Earth/land)."

"Aparayam (Ephraim), what shall I ishah (make) to you? Yahawadah (Judah), what shall I ishah (make) to you? For your chasad (grace) is like a baqar (morning) inan (cloud), and like the tal (dew) that disappears shakam (early).

Therefore I have chatzab (cut) them to pieces with the nabayaayam (prophets); I harag (kill) them with the amaray (words) of my pah (mouth). Your mashapat (judgments) are like a flash of awar (light).
For I chapatz (desire) chasad (grace), and not zabach (sacrifice); and the daith (knowledge) of Alahayam more than burnt ilawath (offerings).
But they, like Adam, ibar (pass over/through) broken the barayath (covenant). They were bagad (unfaithful) to me, there.
Galaid (Gilead) is a qarayah (city / town) of those who pail (work) awan (iniquity); it is stained with dam (blood).

As gangs of robbers chakah (wait) to ambush a ayash (man / husband), so the chabar (company) of kahanayam (priests) ratzach (murder) in the darak (way) toward Shechem, ishah (make) shameful zamah (crimes).
In the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) I raah (see) seen a shairawarah (horrible) thing. There is prostitution in Aparayam (Ephraim). Yashar-Al (Israel) is tamaa (defiled).
"Also, Yahawadah (Judah), there is a qatzayar (harvest) shayath (put / appoint / make) for you, when I shawab (turn back / repent) the fortunes of my im (nation / people).

When I would rapaa (heal) Yashar-Al (Israel), then the iwan (guilt/iniquity) of Aparayam (Ephraim) is galah (uncovered), also the rai (wickedness) of Shamarawan (Samaria); for they pail (commit) falsehood, and the ganab (thief) bawaa (come) in, and the gang of robbers ravages outside.
They don't amar (spoke) in their labab (hearts) that I zakar (remember) all their rai (wickedness). Now their own deeds have engulfed them. They are before my panayam (face).
They make the malak (king) shamach (glad) with their rai (wickedness), and the sharayam (princes) with their kachash (lies).

They are all manaapayam (adulterers). They are bair (burning) like an thanawar (oven) that the baker stops iwar (rouse / awaken), from the lawash (kneading) of the batzaq (dough), until it is chamatz (leavened).
On the yawam (day) of our malak (king), the sharayam (princes) chalah (afflict) themselves sick with the chamah (heat) of yayan (wine). He joined his yad (hand) with mockers.

For they have prepared their lab (heart) like an thanawar (oven), while they lie in arab (wait). Their baker sleeps all the layal (night). In the baqar (morning) it bair (burns) as a lahabah (flaming) ash (fire).

They are all chamam (hot) as an thanawar (oven), and akal (eat) their shapat (judge / judgement). All their malak (king) napal (fall / be cast down) fallen. There is no one among them who qaraa (called) to me.
Aparayam (Ephraim), he mixes himself among the imayam (nations). Aparayam (Ephraim) is a pancake not hapak (turned) over.

Strangers have akal (eat) his kach (strength / mighty / power), and he doesn't realize it. Indeed, shayabah (old age / white hair - due to age) hairs are here and there on him, and he doesn't realize it.
The gaawan (pride) of Yashar-Al (Israel) inah (answer / respond) to his panayam (face); yet they haven't shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah their Alahayam, nor baqash (sought) him, for all this.
"Aparayam (Ephraim) is like an easily pathah (deceived) yawanah (dove), without lab (heart). They qaraa (called) to Matzarayam (Egypt). They halak (move) to Ashawar (Assyria).

When they yalak (go), I will parash (spread) my rashath (net) on them. I will yarad (bring) them down like the iwap (flying) of the sky. I will yasar (chastise) them, as their idah (congregation) has shamai (heard).

Away (woe) to them! For they have nadad (wandered) from me. Shad (destruction) to them! For they have trespassed against me. Though I would padah (redeem) them, yet they have dabar (word / matter) kazabayam (lies) against me.

They haven't zaiq (cried) to me with their lab (heart), but they yalal (howl) on their mashakab (beds). They gawar (assemble) themselves for grain and new thayarawash (wine). They sawar (turn) away from me.
Though I have yasar (taught) and chazaq (strengthened) their zarawai (arms), yet they plot rai (evil) against me.

They shawab (turn back / repent), but not to the Most il (over). They are like a faulty qashath (bow). Their shar (prince / ruler) will napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword) for the zaim (rage) of their lashawan (tongue / language). Zaw (this) will be their laig (derision) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

"Put the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn) to your lips! Something like an nashar (eagle) is over Yahawah bayath (house), because they ibar (pass over/through) broken my barayath (covenant), and pashai (rebelled) against my thawarah (instruction).
They zaiq (cry) to me, ‘My Alahayam, we Israel yadai (acknowledge) you!'
Yashar-Al (Israel) has zanach (cast) off that which is tawab (good / proper function). The ayab (enemy) will radap (pursue) him.

They have set up hamalayakaw (kings), but not by me. They have made hashayaraw (princes), and I didn't approve. Of their kasap (silver) and their zahab (gold) they ishah (make) made themselves itzabayam (idols), that they may be karath (cut) off.
Let Shamarawan (Samaria) throw out his igal (calf) idol! My ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) charah (hot with anger) against them! How long will it be until they are capable of purity?
For this is even from Yashar-Al (Israel)! The charash (workman) ishah (make) it, and it is no Alahayam; indeed, the igal (calf) of Shamarawan (Samaria) shall be shabab (broken) in pieces.

For they zarai (sow) the rawach (spirit / wind), and they will qatzar (reap) the sawapah (whirlwind). He has no standing grain. The stalk will ishah (make) no qamach (head). If it ishah (make) yield, strangers will balai (swallow) it up.
Yashar-Al (Israel) is balai (swallowed) up. Now they are among the gawayam (nations) like a worthless thing.
For they have ilah (go up / offer) up to Ashawar (Assyria), like a paraa (wild) donkey wandering badad (alone). Aparayam (Ephraim) has thanah (hired) ahabayam (lovers) for himself.
But although they sold themselves among the gawayam (nations), I will now qabatz (gather) them; and they begin to waste mashaa (away) because of the oppression of the malak (king) of mighty ones.
Because Aparayam (Ephraim) rabah (has) multiplied mazabachath (altars) for chataa (sinning), they became for him mazabachath (altars) for chataa (sinning).
I kathab (write) for him the many things of my thawarah (instruction); but they were chashab (regarded) as a zawar (strange) thing.

As for the yazabachaw (sacrifices) of my habahab (offerings), they zabach (sacrifice) bashar (flesh) and akal (eat) it; But Yahawah doesn't ratzah (accept) them. Now he will zakar (remember) their iwan (guilt/iniquity), and paqad (visit) their chataah (sin). They will shawab (turn back / repent) to Matzarayam (Egypt).

For Yashar-Al (Israel) has shakach (forgotten) his Maker and banah (build) hayakalawath (palaces); and Yahawadah (Judah) rabah (has) multiplied batzar (fortified) irayam (cities); but I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on his irayam (cities), and it will akal (eat) its fortresses."

Don't shamach (rejoice), Yashar-Al (Israel), to jubilation like the imayam (nations); for you were unfaithful to your Alahayam. You ahab (love) the wages of a prostitute at every grain garan (threshing) floor.
The garan (threshing) floor and the yaqab (winepress) won't raih (feed) them, and the new thayarawash (wine) will kachash (fail) her.

They won't yashab (inhabit/dwell) in Yahawah aratz (Earth/land); but Aparayam (Ephraim) will shawab (turn back / repent) to Matzarayam (Egypt), and they will akal (eat) tamaa (unclean) food in Ashawar (Assyria).

They won't nasak (pour) out yayan (wine) offerings to Yahawah, neither will they be pleasing to him. Their zabach (sacrifices) will be to them like the lacham (bread) of awanayam (mourners); akal (eat) who eat of it will be tamaa (polluted); for their lacham (bread) napash (soul) be for their appetite. It will not bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
What will you ishah (make) in the yawam (day) of mawaid (Feast/Holy Day) assembly, and in the yawam (day) of the chag (feast/festival) of Yahawah?

For, behold, they have halak (move) away from shad (destruction). Matzarayam (Egypt) will qabatz (gather) them up. Map (Memphis) will qabar (bury) them. Qamawash (nettles) will yarash (possess) their machamad (pleasant) things of kasap (silver). Chawach (thorns) will be in their ahal (tents).

The yamay (days) of paqadah (visitation) bawaa (come) come. The yamay (days) of reckoning bawaa (come) come. Yashar-Al (Israel) yadai (will) consider the nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) to be a awayal (fool), and the ayash (man / husband) who is inspired to be insane, because of the rab (abundance) of your iwan (guilt/iniquity), and because your hostility is rab (great).

A nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) watches over Aparayam (Ephraim) with my Alahayam. A yaqawash (fowler's) pach (snare / trap) is on all of his darak (paths), and hostility in the bayath (house) of his Alahayam.

They imaq (have) deeply shachath (corrupted) themselves, as in the yamay (days) of Gabaih (Gibeah). He will zakar (remember) their iwan (guilt/iniquity). He will paqad (visit) them for their chataah (sin).

I matzaa (found) Yashar-Al (Israel) like inabayam (grapes) in the madabar (wilderness). I raah (see) your ab (father) as the bakawarah (first) ripe in the thaan (fig) tree at its raashayath (beginning) season; but they bawaa (come) to Bailapaiwar (Baal) Peor, and nazar (crown / consecrate) themselves to the shameful thing, and became abominable ahab (love) that which they loved.
As for Aparayam (Ephraim), their kabawad (glory) will iwap (flying) away like a iwap (flying). There will be no yalad (birth / begot), none with child, and no harawan (conception).
Though they gadal (bring) up their ban (son), yet I will shakal (bereave) them, so that not a adam (man) shall be left. Indeed, away (woe) also to them when I sawar (depart) from them!
I raah (see) seen Aparayam (Ephraim), like Tzar (Tyre), shathal (planted) in a nawah (habitation) place; but Aparayam (Ephraim) will yatzaa (go out / come out) out his ban (son) to the harag (kill).
Nathan (give) them—Yahweh what will you nathan (give)? Nathan (give) them a shakal (miscarrying) racham (womb) and tzamaq (dry) shadayam (breasts).

"All their rai (wickedness) is in Galagal (Gilgal); for there I shanaa (hate) them. Because of the rai (wickedness) of their deeds I will garash (drive) them out of my bayath (house)! I will ahabah (love) them no more. All their shar (prince / ruler) are rebels.

Aparayam (Ephraim) is nakah (struck). Their sharash (root) has yabash (dry land) up. They will ishah (make) no paray (fruit). Even though they yalad (birth / begot) forth, yet I will mawath (death) the machamad (beloved) ones of their batan (womb)."
My Alahayam will maas (cast) them away, because they did not shamai (hearken / hear) to him; and they will be wanderers among the gawayam (nations).

Yashar-Al (Israel) is a luxuriant gapan (vine) that puts shawah (forth) his paray (fruit). According to the rab (abundance) of his paray (fruit) he rabah (has) multiplied his mazabachawath (altars). As their aratz (Earth/land) has prospered, they have adorned their sacred matzabawath (stones).
Their lab (heart) is chalaq (divided). Now they will be asham (found) guilty. He will demolish their mazabach (altars). He will shadad (destroy) their sacred matzabah (stones).
Surely now they will amar (spoke), "We have no malak (king); for we don't yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah; and the malak (king), what can he ishah (make) for us?"

They make dabarayam (promises), alah (swear / adjure) shawaa (vanity) in karath (cut) barayath (covenant). Therefore mashapat (judgment) parach (springs) up like poisonous weeds in the thalamay (furrows) of the shadah (field).

The shakan (place) of Shamarawan (Samaria) will be in terror for the calves of Bayathaawan (Beth Aven); for its im (nation / people) will abal (mourn) over it, Along with its kamar (priests) who gayal (rejoiced) over it, for its kabawad (glory), because it has departed from it.

It also will be yabal (carried) to Ashawar (Assyria) for a manachah (present) to a great malak (king). Aparayam (Ephraim) will laqach (take / seize) bashanah (shame), and Yashar-Al (Israel) will be bawash (ashamed) of his own itzah (counsel).
Shamarawan (Samaria) and her malak (king) float away, like a twig on the mayam (Waters).

The bamah (high) places also of Aven, the chataah (sin) of Yashar-Al (Israel), will be destroyed. The qawatz (thorn) and the daradar (thistle) will ilah (go up / offer) up on their mazabach (altars). They will amar (spoke) the harayam (mountains), "kasah (cover) us!" And the gabaiwath (hills), "napal (fall / be cast down) on us!"

"Yashar-Al (Israel), you have chataa (sinned) from the yamay (days) of Gabaih (Gibeah). There they imad (remained). The malachamah (battle) against the banay (children) of ilawah (iniquity) doesn't nashag (overtake) them in Gabaih (Gibeah).
When it is my awah (desire), I will yasar (chastise) them; and the imayam (nations) will be asap (gathered) against them, when they are asar (bound) to their shanayam (two) iyan (eye).

Aparayam (Ephraim) is a trained igalah (heifer) that ahab (love) to dawash (thresh); so I will ibar (pass over/through) a yoke on her beautiful tzawaar (neck). I will rakab (set) a rider on Aparayam (Ephraim). Yahawadah (Judah) will charash (plow). Yaiqab (Jacob) will shadad (break) his clods.

Zarai (sow) to yourselves in tzadaqah (righteousness), qatzar (reap) according to chasad (grace). Nayar (break) up your fallow nayar (ground); for it is ith (time) to darash (seek) Yahawah, until he bawaa (come) and rains tzadaq (righteous / just / fair) on you.

You have charash (plowed) rashai (wickedness). You have qatzar (reaped) iwal (iniquity). You have akal (eat) the paray (fruit) of kachash (lies), for you batach (trusted) in your darak (way), in the rab (multitude) of your gabawar (mighty) men.

Therefore a battle roar will qawam (rise up) among your im (nation / people), and all your fortresses will be shadad (destroyed), as Shalaman (Shalman) destroyed Bayathaarabaal (Beth Arbel) in the yawam (day) of malachamah (battle). The am (mother) was ratash (dashed) in pieces with her banayam (children).
So Bayath-Al (Bethel) will ishah (make) to you panayam (face) of your rai (great) rai (wickedness). At daybreak the malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel) will be damah (destroyed).
"When Yashar-Al (Israel) was a nair (child), then I ahab (love) him, and qaraa (called) my ban (son) out of Matzarayam (Egypt).
They qaraa (called) to them, so they halak (move) from them. They zabach (sacrificed) to the Bail (Baals), and qatar (burned) incense to engraved pasalayam (images).
Yet I tharagal (taught) Aparayam (Ephraim) to walk. I laqach (take / seize) them by his zarawai (arms); but they didn't yadai (know) that I rapaa (healed) them.

I mashak (drew) them with chabalay (cords) of a adam (man), with ties of ahabah (love); and I was to them like those who rawam (will lift up) up the il (over) on their necks; and I bent down to him and I akal (eat) him.

"They won't shawab (turn back / repent) into the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt); but the Ashawar (Assyrian) will be their malak (king), because they maan (refused) to shawab (turn back / repent).
The charab (sword) will chawal (fall) on their iyar (cities), and will kalah (complete / finish) the bad (bars) of their gates, and will put an end to their plans.
My im (nation / people) are determined to mashawabah (turn) from me. Though they qaraa (called) to the Most il (over), he certainly won't rawam (will lift up) them.

"How can I nathan (give) you up, Aparayam (Ephraim)? How can I magan (hand) you over, Yashar-Al (Israel)? How can I nathan (give) you like Adamah (Admah)? How can I nathan (give) you like Tzabaayam (Zeboiim)? My lab (heart) is hapak (turned) within me, my compassion is aroused.

I will not ishah (make) the charawan (fierceness) of my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting). I will not shawab (turn back / repent) to shachath (destroy) Aparayam (Ephraim): for I am Al, and not ayash (man / husband); the qadawash (holy) One in the qarab (among / near) of you; and I will not bawaa (come) in iyar (wrath).
They will yalak (walk) achar (other) Yahawah, who will shaag (roar) like a aray (lion); for he will shaag (roar), and the banayam (children) will come charad (trembling) from the yam (sea/waters).

They will come charad (trembling) like a tzapawar (bird) out of Matzarayam (Egypt), and like a yawanah (dove) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Ashawar (Assyria); and I will yashab (inhabit/dwell) them in their bayath (house)," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

Aparayam (Ephraim) surrounds me with falsehood, and the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) with maramah (deceit). Yahawadah (Judah) still strays from Al, and is unfaithful to the qadawash (holy) One.
Aparayam (Ephraim) feeds on wind, and chases the east wind. He continually multiplies kachash (lies) and desolation. They sabab (make) a covenant with Assyria, and oil is sabab (carried) into Egypt.
Yahawah also has a controversy with Judah, and will punish Jacob according to his ways; according to his deeds he will repay him.
In the womb he took his brother by the heel; and in his manhood he contended with Alahayam.
Indeed, he struggled with the alahayam (God), and prevailed; he wept, and made supplication to him. He found him at Bethel, and there he spoke with us,
Even Yahawah, the Alahayam of Armies; Yahawah is his dabar (word / matter) of renown!
Therefore turn to your Alahayam. Keep kindness and justice, and wait continually for your Alahayam.
A merchant has dishonest scales in his hand. He chasad (grace) to defraud.
Ephraim said, "Surely I have become rich, I have found myself wealth. In all my wealth they won't find in me any iniquity that is sin."
"But I am Yahawah your Alahayam from the land of Egypt. I will yet again ishar (make) you dwell in tents, as in the days of the solemn feast.
I have also spoken to the ahalayam (prophets), and I have multiplied visions; and by the ministry of the ahalayam (prophets) I have used parables.
If Gilead is wicked, surely they are worthless. In Gilgal they sacrifice bulls. Indeed, their altars are like rabah (heaps) in the furrows of the field.
Jacob fled into the shadah (country) of Aram, and Israel served to get a wife, and for a wife he tended flocks and herds.
By a prophet Yahawah ibad (servant) Yashar-Al (Israel) up out of Egypt, and by a prophet he was shamar (keep/guard).
Ephraim has bitterly provoked anger. Therefore his blood will be left on him, and his Adawan will repay his contempt.
When Aparayam (Ephraim) dabar (word / matter), there was rathath (trembling). He nashaa (lift) himself in Yashar-Al (Israel), but when he became asham (guilty) in Bail (Baal), he mawath (death).

Now they chataa (sin) more and more, and ishah (make) made themselves masakah (molten) images of their kasap (silver), even itzabayam (idols) according to their own thabawan (understanding), all of them the maishah (work) of the craftsmen. They amar (spoke) of them, ‘They offer human zabach (sacrifice) and nashaq (kiss) the calves.'

Therefore they will be like the baqar (morning) mist, and like the tal (dew) that passes halak (move) shakam (early), like the matz (chaff) that is sair (driven) with the whirlwind out of the garan (threshing) floor, and like the ishan (smoke) out of the arabah (chimney).
"Yet I am Yahawah your Alahayam from the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt); and you shall yadai (acknowledge) no Alahayam but me, and balathay (without) me there is no savior.
I yadai (knew) you in the madabar (wilderness), in the aratz (Earth/land) of thalaawabah (great) drought.
According to their maraiyath (pasture), so were they shabai (filled); they were shabai (filled), and their lab (heart) was rawam (will lift up). Therefore they have shakach (forgotten) me.
Therefore I am like a shachal (lion) to them. Like a namar (leopard), I will lurk by the darak (path).

I will pagash (meet) them like a dab (bear) that is shakawal (bereaved) of her cubs, and will qarai (tear) the covering of their lab (heart). There I will akal (eat) them like a labayaa (lioness). The shadah (wild) animal will baqai (tear) them.
You are shachath (destroyed), Yashar-Al (Israel), because you are against me, against your izar (help).

Apaw (where) is your malak (king) now, that he may yashai (salvation) you in all your iyar (cities)? And your shapat (judge / judgement), of whom you amar (spoke), ‘nathan (give) me a malak (king) and sharayam (princes)?'
I nathan (give) given you a malak (king) in my ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and have laqach (take / seize) him away in my ibarah (wrath).
The iwan (guilt/iniquity) of Aparayam (Ephraim) is stored up. His chataah (sin) is stored up.
The chabalay (sorrows) of a travailing yalad (birth / begot) will bawaa (come) on him. He is an unwise ban (son); for when it is ith (time), he doesn't come to the opening of the womb.

I will padah (ransom) them from the yad (hand) of shaawal (Sheol / afterlife). I will gaal (redeem) them from mawath (death)! Mawath (death), where are your dabar (word / matter)? Shaawal (Sheol / afterlife), where is your qatab (destruction)? "Compassion ahay (will) be sathar (hidden) from my iyan (eye).

Though he is paraa (fruitful) among his achayam (brothers), an east qadayam (wind) will bawaa (come), the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah ilah (go up / offer) up from the madabar (wilderness); and his maqawar (spring) will bawash (become) dry, and his maiyan (fountain) will be charab (dried) up. He will plunder the storehouse of awatzar (treasure).

Shamarawan (Samaria) will bear her asham (guilt); for she has marah (rebelled) against her Alahayam. They will napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword). Their iwalal (infants) will be ratash (dashed) in pieces, and their pregnant women will be baqai (ripped) open."
Israel, return to Yahawah your Alahayam; for you have napal (fall / be cast down) because of your sin.

Shawab (turn back / repent) words with you, and shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah. Tell him, "Forgive all our iwan (guilt/iniquity), and accept that which is good: so we offer our lips like bulls.
Assyria can't save us. We won't ride on horses; neither will we amar (spoke) any more to the dabar (word / matter) of our hands, ‘Our Alahayam!' For in you the fatherless finds mercy."
"I will heal their waywardness. I will racham (show mercy / love) them freely; for my anger is turned away from him.
I will be like the dew to Israel. He will blossom like the lily, and send down his roots like Lebanon.
His branches will parach (spread), and his beauty will be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like Labanawan (Lebanon).
Men will live in his shade. They will revive like the grain, and blossom like the vine. Their fragrance will be like the wine of Labanawan (Lebanon).
Ephraim, what have I to do any more with idols? I shawab (turn back / repent), and will take care of him. I am like a green fir tree; from me your fruit is found."
Who is wise, that he may understand these things? Who is prudent, that he may know them? For the ways of Yahawah are right, and the righteous walk in them; But the rebellious stumble in them.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah that came to Yawaal (Joel), the ban (son) of Pathawaal (Pethuel).

Shamai (hearken / hear) this, you zaqanayam (elders), And listen, all you yawashabay (inhabitants) of the aratz (Earth/land). Has this ever happened in your yamay (days), or in the yamay (days) of your ab (father)?
Sapar (book) your ban (son) about it, and have your ban (son) tell their ban (son), and their ban (son), achar (other) dawar (generation / age / period).

What the swarming locust has yathar (left), the great arabah (locust) has akal (eat). What the great arabah (locust) has yathar (left), the grasshopper has akal (eat). What the grasshopper has yathar (left), the chasayal (caterpillar) has akal (eat).
Qawatz (wake) up, you drunkards, and bakah (weep)! Wail, all you drinkers of yayan (wine), because of the sweet isayas (wine); for it is karath (cut) off from your pah (mouth).

For a gaway (heathen / nation) has ilah (go up / offer) up on my aratz (Earth/land), itzawam (strong), and without masapar (number). His shanay (teeth) are the shanay (teeth) of a aray (lion), and he has the fangs of a labayaa (lioness).

He has shawam (place / establish / appoint) my gapan (vine) shamah (waste), and stripped my thaan (fig) tree. He has stripped its bark, and shalak (thrown) it away. Its branches are laban (made) white.
Mourn like a bathawalah (virgin) dressed in sackcloth for the bail (husband) of her naiwar (youth)!
The meal manachah (offering) and the drink nasak (offering) are karath (cut) off from Yahawah bayath (house). The kahanayam (priests), Yahawah masharathay (ministers), abal (mourn).

The shadah (field) is laid shadad (waste). The adamah (land) abal (mourns), for the grain is shadad (destroyed), The new thayarawash (wine) has yabash (dry land) up, and the yatzahar (fresh oil) languishes.

Be bawash (confounded), you farmers! Wail, you vineyard keepers; for the chatah (wheat) and for the shairah (barley); for the qatzayar (harvest) of the shadah (field) abad (destroy / perish) perished.

The gapan (vine) has yabash (dry land) up, and the thaan (fig) tree withered; the ramawan (pomegranate) tree, the palm tree also, and the thapawach (apple) tree, even all of the itzay (trees) of the shadah (field) are yabash (dry land); for shashawan (joy) has yabash (dry land) away from the banay (sons) of adam (men).

Chagar (put) on sackcloth and sapad (mourn), you kahanayam (priests)! Wail, you masharathay (ministers) of the mazabach (altar). Bawaa (come), lie all lawan (night) in sackcloth, you masharathay (ministers) of my Alahayam, for the meal manachah (offering) and the drink nasak (offering) are withheld from your Alahayam bayath (house).

Qadash (set apart / make holy) a tzawam (fast). Qaraa (called) a solemn itzarah (assembly). Asap (gather) the zaqanayam (elders), and all the yashabay (inhabitants) of the aratz (Earth/land), to the bayath (house) of Yahawah, your Alahayam, and zaiq (cry) to Yahawah.
Ahah (alas) for the yawam (day)! For the yawam (day) of Yahawah is at qarawab (hand), and it will bawaa (come) as shad (destruction) from the Shaday.
Isn't the akal (food) karath (cut) off before our iyan (eye); shamachah (joy) and gayal (gladness) from the bayath (house) of our Alahayam?
The paradawath (seeds) rot under their magarapah (clods). The granaries are shamam (laid) desolate. The barns are haras (broken) down, for the grain has yabash (dry land).
How the animals anach (groan)! The idaray (herds) of livestock are perplexed, because they have no maraih (pasture). Yes, the idaray (flocks) of tzaan (sheep) are asham (made) desolate.

Yahawah, I qaraa (called) to you, For the ash (fire) has akal (eat) the naawath (pastures) of the madabar (wilderness), and the lahabah (flame) has lahat (burned) all the itzay (trees) of the shadah (field).

Yes, the animals of the shadah (field) irag (pant) to you, for the mayam (Waters) apayaqay (brooks) have yabash (dry land) up, And the ash (fire) has akal (eat) the naawath (pastures) of the madabar (wilderness).

Thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn) in Tzayawan (Zion), and rawai (sound) an alarm in my qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain)! Let all the yashabay (inhabitants) of the aratz (Earth/land) ragaz (tremble), for the yawam (day) of Yahawah bawaa (come), for it is close at qarawab (hand):

A yawam (day) of chashak (darkness) and apalah (gloominess), a yawam (day) of inan (cloud) and irapal (thick) darkness. As the dawn parash (spreading) on the harayam (mountains), a rab (great) and itzawam (strong) im (nation / people); there has iwalam (forever) been the like, neither will there be any more achar (other) them, even to the shanay (years) of many dawar (generation / age / period).

A ash (fire) akal (eat) panayam (face) them, and achar (other) them, a lahabah (flame) lahat (burns). The aratz (Earth/land) is as the gan (garden) of Idan (Eden) panayam (face) them, and achar (other) them, a shamamah (desolate) madabar (wilderness). Yes, and no one has palayatah (escaped) them.
Their maraah (appearance) is as the maraah (appearance) of sawasayam (horses), and as horsemen, so do they rawatz (run).

Like the qawal (sound / voice) of marakabawath (chariots) on the raashay (tops) of the harayam (mountains) do they raqad (leap), like the qawal (sound / voice) of a lahab (flame) of ash (fire) that akal (eat) the qash (stubble), as a itzawam (strong) im (nation / people) set in malachamah (battle) irak (array).
At their panayam (face) the imayam (peoples) are in anguish. All panayam (face) have grown pale.

They rawatz (run) like gabawar (mighty) men. They ilah (go up / offer) the chawamah (wall) like malachamah (warriors). They ayash (man / husband) yalak (march) in his line, and they don't swerve off course.
Neither does ayash (man / husband) jostle ach (brother/kinsman); they yalak (march) everyone in his masalah (path), and they burst through the defenses, and don't break ranks.
They rush on the iyar (city). They rawatz (run) on the chawamah (wall). They ilah (go up / offer) up into the bathayam (houses). They bawaa (come) in at the chalawanayam (windows) like thieves.

The aratz (Earth/land) ragaz (quakes) panayam (face) them. The shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) raish (tremble). The shamash (sun) and the yarach (moon) are qadar (darkened), and the kawakabayam (stars) asap (withdraw) their nagah (shining).

Yahawah thunders his qawal (sound / voice) panayam (face) his chayal (army); for his forces are very rab (great); for he is itzawam (strong) who obeys his command; for the yawam (day) of Yahawah is gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and very awesome, and who kawal (all) endure it?

"Yet even now," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, "shawab (turn back / repent) to me with all your labab (heart), and with tzawam (fasting), and with bakay (weeping), and with masapad (mourning)."

Qarai (tear) your labab (heart), and not your bagad (garments), and shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah, your Alahayam; for he is chanawan (gracious) and rachawam (merciful), arak (slow) to ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and abundant in loving chasad (grace), and relents from sending rai (calamity).

Who yadai (knows)? He may shawab (turn back / repent) and relent, and shaar (leave) a barakah (blessing) achar (other) him, even a meal manachah (offering) and a drink nasak (offering) to Yahawah, your Alahayam.
Thaqai (blow / sound alarm) the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn) in Tzayawan (Zion)! Qadash (set apart / make holy) a tzawam (fast). Qaraa (called) a solemn itzarah (assembly).

Asap (gather) the im (nation / people). Qadash (set apart / make holy) the qahal (assembly). Qabatz (assemble) the zaqanayam (elders). Asap (gather) the iwalalayam (children), and those who yanaq (nurse) from shadayam (breasts). Let the chathan (bridegroom) yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from his room, and the kalah (complete / finish) out of her room.

Let the kahanayam (priests), the masharathay (ministers) of Yahawah, bakah (weep) between the awalam (porch) and the mazabach (altar), and let them amar (spoke), "chawas (spare) your imayam (people), Yahawah, and don't nathan (give) your nachalah (heritage) to charapah (reproach), that the gawayam (nations) should mashal (rule/have dominion) over them. Why should they amar (spoke) among the imayam (peoples), ‘Where is their Alahayam?'"
Then Yahawah was qanaa (jealous) for his aratz (Earth/land), And chamal (had) pity on his im (nation / people).

Yahawah inah (answer / respond) his im (nation / people), "Behold, I will shalach (send) you grain, new thayarawash (wine), and yatzahar (fresh oil), and you will be shabai (satisfied) with them; and I will no more nathan (give) you a charapah (reproach) among the gawayam (nations).

But I will remove the tzapawanay (northern) army rachaq (far) away from you, and will nadach (drive) it into a tzayah (barren) and shamamah (desolate) aratz (Earth/land), its panayam (face) into the eastern yam (sea/waters), and its back into the western yam (sea/waters); and its stench will ilah (go up / offer) up, and its bad smell will ilah (go up / offer)." Ishah (make) he has done gadal (great) things.
Adamah (land), don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid). Be gayal (glad) and shamach (rejoice), for Yahawah ishah (make) done gadal (great) things.

Don't be yaraa (fear / be afraid), you animals of the shadah (field); for the naawath (pastures) of the madabar (wilderness) dashaa (spring) up, for the itz (tree) nashaa (lift) its paray (fruit). The thaan (fig) tree and the gapan (vine) nathan (give) their chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor).

"Be gayal (glad) then, you banay (children) of Tzayawan (Zion), and shamach (rejoice) in Yahawah, your Alahayam; for he nathan (give) you the former mawarah (rain) in just measure, and he causes the gasham (rain) to yarad (come) down for you, the former mawarah (rain) and the malaqawash (latter) rain, as raashawan (before).
The garan (threshing) floors will be malaa (full) of bar (wheat), and the vats will shawaq (overflow) with new thayarawash (wine) and yatzahar (fresh oil).

I will shalam (restore) to you the shanayam (years) that the swarming arabah (locust) has akal (eat), the great locust, the grasshopper, and the caterpillar, my gadawal (very great/important/mighty) chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), which I shalach (send) among you.

You will have akal (eat) to akal (eat), and be shabai (satisfied), and will halal (praise) the sham (name) of Yahawah, your Alahayam, who ishah (make) dealt wondrously with you; and my im (nation / people) will iwalam (forever) again be disappointed.

You yadai (will) know that I am in the qarab (among / near) of Yashar-Al (Israel), and that I am Yahawah, your Alahayam, and there is no one else; and my im (nation / people) will iwalam (forever) again be disappointed.

"It will happen afterward, that I will shapak (pour) out my rawach (spirit / wind) on all bashar (flesh); and your ban (son) and your banath (daughter) will nabaa (prophesy). Your zaqan (old) men will dream chalawam (dreams). Your bachawar (young) men will raah (see) chazayawan (visions).
And also on the ibad (servant) and on the handmaids in those yawam (day), I will shapak (pour) out my rawach (spirit / wind).
I will show mawapath (wonders) in the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) and in the aratz (Earth/land): dam (blood), ash (fire), and thayamarah (pillars) of ishan (smoke).

The shamash (sun) will be hapak (turned) into chashak (darkness), and the yarach (moon) into dam (blood), panayam (face) the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) and yaraa (fear / be afraid) yawam (day) of Yahawah bawaa (come).

It will happen that whoever will qaraa (called) on the sham (name) of Yahawah shall be malat (saved); for in har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion) and in Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) there will be those who palayatah (escape), as Yahawah has amar (spoke), and among the sharayad (remnant), those whom Yahawah qaraa (called).
"For, behold, in those hayah (came to pass), and in that il (over), when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,

I will gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat; and I will execute judgment on them there for my people, and for my heritage, Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations. They il (over) divided my land,
And have nathan (give) lots for my people, and nathan (give) given a boy for a prostitute, and sold a girl for wine, that they may drink.
"Yes, and what are you to me, Tyre, and Sidon, and all the regions of Philistia? Will you repay me? And if you repay me, I will swiftly and speedily return your repayment on your own head.
Because you have taken my silver and my gold, and hayah (came to pass) carried my finest treasures into your temples,

And have makar (sold) the ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah) and the ban (son) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) to the sons of the Yawanay (Greeks), that you may rachaq (remove) them far from their gabawal (border/boundary).
Behold, I will iwar (rouse / awaken) them up out of the maqawam (place) where you have makar (sold) them, and will shawab (turn back / repent) your repayment on your own raash (head);

And I will makar (sell) your ban (son) and your banath (daughter) into the yad (hand) of the ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah), and they will makar (sell) them to the men of Sheba, to a faraway gaway (heathen / nation), for Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) it."

Qaraa (called) this among the gaway (heathen / nation): "qadash (set apart / make holy) for malachamah (war)! Iwar (rouse / awaken) up the gabawar (mighty) men. Let all the malachamah (warriors) nagash (draw) near. Let them ilah (go up / offer) up.
Kathath (beat) your ath (entirety) into charab (sword), and your mazamarah (pruning) hooks into ramach (spears). Let the chalash (weak) amar (spoke), ‘I am gabawar (strong).'
Hurry and bawaa (come), all you surrounding gaway (heathen / nation), and gather yourselves qabatz (together)." Cause your gabawar (mighty) ones to nachath (come) down there, Yahawah.

"Let the gaway (heathen / nation) arouse themselves, and ilah (go up / offer) up to the imaq (valley) of Yahawashapat (Jehoshaphat); for there will I yashab (inhabit/dwell) to shapat (judge / judgement) all the surrounding gaway (heathen / nation).

Shalach (send) in the magal (sickle); for the qatzayar (harvest) is ripe. Bawaa (come), tread, for the gath (winepress) is malaa (full), the vats shawaq (overflow), for their rai (wickedness) is rab (great)."
Hamawan (multitudes), hamawan (multitudes) in the imaq (valley) of charawatz (decision)! For the yawam (day) of Yahawah is qarawab (near), in the imaq (valley) of charawatz (decision).
The shamash (sun) and the yarach (moon) are qadar (darkened), and the kawakab (star) asap (withdraw) their nagah (shining).

Yahawah will shaag (roar) from Tzayawan (Zion), and qawal (sound / voice) from Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); and the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens) and the aratz (Earth/land) will raish (shake); but Yahawah will be a machasah (refuge) to his im (nation / people), and a stronghold to the ban (son) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

"So you yadai (will) know that I am Yahawah, your Alahayam, shakan (place) in Tzayawan (Zion), my qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain). Then Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) will be qadash (set apart / make holy), and no strangers will ibar (pass over/through) through her any more.

It will happen in that yawam (day), that the har (mountain) will natap (drop) down sweet isayas (wine), the gabaih (hills) will yalak (flow) with chalab (milk), all the apayaq (brooks) of Yahawadah (Judah) will yalak (flow) with mayam (Waters), and a maiyan (fountain) will yatzaa (go out / come out) forth from the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and will shaqah (water) the nachal (stream / river) of Shatayam (Shittim).

Matzarayam (Egypt) will be a shamamah (desolation), and Adawam (Edom) will be a shamamah (desolate) madabar (wilderness), for the chamas (violence) done to the ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah), because they have shapak (shed) naqay (innocent) dam (blood) in their aratz (Earth/land).
But Yahawadah (Judah) will be yashab (inhabit/dwell) iwalam (forever), and Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) from dawar (generation / age / period) to dawar (generation / age / period).
I will naqah (clean/innocent) their dam (blood), that I have not naqah (clean/innocent): for Yahawah shakan (place) in Tzayawan (Zion)."

The dabaray (words) of Imawas (Amos), who was among the herdsmen of Thaqawai (Tekoa), which he chazah (saw) concerning Yashar-Al (Israel) in the yamay (days) of Izayah (Uzziah) malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and in the yamay (days) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) the ban (son) of Yawaash (Joash) malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), two shanathayam (years) panayam (face) the raish (earthquake).

He amar (spoke): "Yahawah will shaag (roar) from Tzayawan (Zion), and nathan (give) his qawal (sound / voice) from Yarawashalam (Jerusalem); and the naawath (pastures) of the raiyam (shepherds) will abal (mourn), and the raash (head) of Karamal (Carmel) will yabash (dry land)."

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: "For shalawash (three) pashaiy (transgressions) of Damashaq (Damascus), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they have dawash (threshed) Galaid (Gilead) with charawatz (threshing) instruments of barazal (iron);
