But I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) into the bayath (house) of Chazaal (Hazael), and it will akal (eat) the aramanawath (palaces) of Banahadad (Ben Hadad).

I will shabar (break) the barayach (bar) of Damashaq (Damascus), and karath (cut) off the yashab (inhabit/dwell) from the baqaih (valley) of Awan (Aven), and him who thamak (holds) the scepter from the bayath (house) of Eden; and the im (nation / people) of Aram (Syria) shall galah (go) into captivity to Qayar (Kir)," amar (spoke) Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: "For shalawash (three) pashaiy (transgressions) of Izah (Gaza), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they galah (carried) away captive the shalam (full / whole / complete) community, to sagar (deliver) them up to Adawam (Edom);
But I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on the chawamah (wall) of Izah (Gaza), and it will akal (eat) its aramawan (palaces).

I will karath (cut) off the yashab (inhabit/dwell) from Ashadawad (Ashdod), and him who thamak (holds) the scepter from Ashaqalawan (Ashkelon); and I will shawab (turn back / repent) my yad (hand) against Iqarawan (Ekron); and the shaarayath (remnant) of the Palashathay (Philistines) will abad (destroy / perish)," amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: "For shalawash (three) pashaiy (transgressions) of Tzar (Tyre), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they sagar (delivered) up the shalam (full / whole / complete) community to Adawam (Edom), and didn't zakar (remember) the ach (brother/kinsman) barayath (covenant);
But I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on the chawamah (wall) of Tzar (Tyre), and it will akal (eat) its aramawan (palaces)."

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: "For shalawash (three) pashaiy (transgressions) of Adawam (Edom), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because he radap (pursued) his ach (brother/kinsman) with the charab (sword), and shachath (cast) off all racham (show mercy / love), and his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) raged continually, and he shamar (keep/guard) his ibarah (wrath) natzach (forever);
But I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on Thayaman (Teman), and it will akal (eat) the aramanawath (palaces) of Batzarah (Bozrah)."

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: "For shalawash (three) pashaiy (transgressions) of the banay (children) of Imawan (Ammon), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they have baqai (ripped) open the pregnant women of Galaid (Gilead), that they may enlarge their gabawal (border/boundary).

But I will yatzath (kindle) a ash (fire) in the chawamah (wall) of Rabah (Rabbah), and it will akal (eat) its aramawan (palaces), with tharawaih (shouting) in the yawam (day) of malachamah (battle), with a sair (storm) in the yawam (day) of the sawapah (whirlwind);
And their malak (king) will halak (move) into gawalah (captivity), he and his shar (prince / ruler) yachad (together)," amar (spoke) Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: "For shalawash (three) pashaiy (transgressions) of Mawaab (Moab), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because he sharap (burned) the itzamawath (bones) of the malak (king) of Adawam (Edom) into shayad (lime);

But I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on Mawaab (Moab), and it will akal (eat) the aramanawath (palaces) of Qarayawath (Kerioth); and Mawaab (Moab) will mawath (death) with shaawan (tumult), with tharawaih (shouting), and with the qawal (sound / voice) of the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn);
And I will karath (cut) off the shapat (judge / judgement) from their qarab (among / near), and will harag (kill) all its shar (prince / ruler) with him," amar (spoke) Yahawah.

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: "For shalawash (three) pashaiy (transgressions) of Yahawadah (Judah), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they have maas (rejected) Yahawah thawarah (instruction), and have not shamar (keep/guard) his chaq (statute), and their kazab (lies) have led them thaih (astray), achar (other) which their ab (father) halak (move);
But I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on Yahawadah (Judah), and it will akal (eat) the aramanawath (palaces) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem)."

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: "For shalawash (three) pashaiy (transgressions) of Yashar-Al (Israel), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they have makar (sold) the tzadayaq (righteous) for kasap (silver), and the abayawan (needy) for a pair of nailayam (shoes);

They trample on the ipar (dust) of the aratz (Earth/land) on the raash (head) of the dal (poor), and deny darak (justice) to the oppressed; and a ayash (man / husband) and his ab (father) use the same nairah (maiden), to chalal (profane) my qadash (set apart / make holy) sham (name);

And they natah (lay) themselves down beside every mazabach (altar) on clothes taken in chabal (pledge); and in the bayath (house) of their Alahayam they shathah (drinks) the yayan (wine) of those who have been fined.

Yet I destroyed the Amaray (Amorite) panayam (face) them, whose gabah (height) was like the gabah (height) of the arazayam (cedars), and he was chasan (strong) as the alawanayam (oaks); yet I destroyed his paray (fruit) from mail (top/above), and his sharash (roots) from beneath.

Also I ilah (go up / offer) you up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and yalak (led) you arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years) in the madabar (wilderness), to yarash (possess) the aratz (Earth/land) of the Amaray (Amorite).

I qawam (rise up) up some of your banay (sons) for nabayaayam (prophets), and some of your bachawar (young) men for Nazirites. Isn't this true, you banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel)?" Naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.
"But you gave the Nazirites yayan (wine) to shaqah (drink), and tzawah (commanded) the nabayaayam (prophets), amar (spoke), ‘Don't nabaa (prophesy)!'
Behold, I will iwaq (crush) you in your place, as a igalah (cart) crushes that is full of grain.

Manawas (flight) will abad (destroy / perish) from the qal (swift); and the chazaq (strong) won't amatz (strengthen) his kach (strength / mighty / power); neither shall the gabawar (mighty) malat (deliver) himself;

Neither shall he imad (stand) who thapash (handles) the qashath (bow); and he who is qal (swift) of ragal (feet / foot) won't malat (escape); neither shall he who rakab (rides) the sawas (horse) malat (deliver) himself;
And he who is amayatz (courageous) among the gabawar (mighty) will nawas (flee) away irawam (naked) on that yawam (day)," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

Shamai (hearken / hear) this dabar (word / matter) that Yahawah has dabar (word / matter) against you, banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), against the whole mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) which I ilah (go up / offer) up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), amar (spoke):
"You only yadai (have) I chosen of all the mashapachawath (families) of the adamah (earth). Therefore I will paqad (visit) you for all of your iwan (guilt/iniquity)."
Do shanayam (two) yalak (walk) yachad (together), unless they have yaid (agreed)?
Will a aray (lion) shaag (roar) in the thicket, when he has no tarap (prey)? Does a young kapayar (lion) nathan (give) out of his maiwanah (den), if he has lakad (caught) balathay (without)?

Can a tzapawar (bird) napal (fall / be cast down) in a mawaqash (trap) on the aratz (Earth/land), where no pach (snare / trap) is set for him? Does a pach (snare / trap) ilah (go up / offer) up from the adamah (ground), when there is nothing to lakad (catch)?

Does the shawapar (Shofar / Ram's horn) alarm sound in a iyar (city), without the im (nation / people) being charad (afraid)? Does rai (evil) happen to a iyar (city), and Yahawah hasn't ishah (make) it?
Surely the Adanay Yahawah will ishah (make) nothing, unless he galah (reveals) his sawad (secret) to his ibad (servant) the nabayaayam (prophets).
The aray (lion) has shaag (roared). Who will not yaraa (fear / be afraid)? The Adanay Yahawah has dabar (word / matter). Who can but nabaa (prophesy)?

Shamai (hearken / hear) in the aramanawath (palaces) at Ashadawad (Ashdod), and in the aramanawath (palaces) in the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and amar (spoke), "asap (assemble) yourselves on the haray (mountains) of Shamarawan (Samaria), and raah (see) what unrest is in her, and what ishawaq (oppression) is thawak (midst) them."
"Indeed they don't yadai (know) to ishah (make) nakachah (right)," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, "Who hoard plunder and loot in their aramawan (palaces)."
Therefore thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: "An tzar (oppressor / distressor) will overrun the aratz (Earth/land); and he will pull down your strongholds, and your fortresses will be plundered."

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: "As the raih (shepherd) yanatzalaw (rescues) out of the pah (mouth) of the aray (lion) shanayam (two) karaiyam (legs), or a badal (separated) of an azan (ear), so shall the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel) be natzal (rescued) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in Shamarawan (Samaria) on the paah (corner) of a couch, and on the Damashaq (silken) cushions of a matah (bed)."

"Shamai (hearken / hear), and iwad (admonish/bear witness against) against the bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob)," naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies).

"For in the yawam (day) that I paqad (visit) the pashaiy (transgressions) of Yashar-Al (Israel) on him, I will also paqad (visit) the mazabachawath (altars) of Bayath-Al (Bethel); and the qaranawath (horns) of the mazabach (altar) will be gadai (cut) off, and napal (fall / be cast down) to the aratz (Earth/land).

I will nakah (strike) the charap (winter) bayath (house) with the qayatz (summer) bayath (house); and the bathay (houses) of shan (ivory) will abad (destroy / perish), and the rab (great) bathay (houses) will sawap (have) an end," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

Shamai (hearken / hear) to this dabar (word / matter), you parawath (cows) of Bashan (Bashan), who are on the har (mountain) of Shamarawan (Samaria), who ishaq (oppress) the dal (poor), who ratzatz (crush) the abayawan (needy), who amar (spoke) their adawan (master / lord), "bawaa (come) us nashathah (drinks)!"

The Adanay Yahawah has shabai (swear / take oath) by his qadash (set apart / make holy) that behold, "The yamayam (days) shall bawaa (come) on you that they will nashaa (lift) you away with tzanawath (hooks), and the acharayath (last) of you with fish tzanawath (hooks).
You will yatzaa (go out / come out) out at the breaks in the wall, everyone straight before her; and you will shalak (cast) yourselves into Haramawan (Harmon)," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

"Bawaa (come) to Bayath-Al (Bethel), and pashai (sin); to Galagal (Gilgal), and pashai (sin) more. Bawaa (come) your zabach (sacrifices) every baqar (morning), your maishar (tithes) every shalawash (three) yamayam (days),

Qatar (offer) a qatar (sacrifice) of thanksgiving of that which is chamatz (leavened), and qaraa (called) free will nadabawath (offerings) and brag about them: for kan (for sure) pleases you, you banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel)," naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah.

"I also nathan (give) given you naqayawan (cleanness) of shanayam (teeth) in all your iyar (cities), and lack of lacham (bread) in every town; yet you haven't shawab (turn back / repent) to me," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

"I also have withheld the gasham (rain) from you, when there were yet shalawash (three) chadashayam (months) to the qatzayar (harvest); and I caused it to matar (rain) on achad (one) iyar (city), and caused it not to matar (rain) on another iyar (city). Achad (one) chalaqah (place) was matar (rained) on, and the chalaqah (piece) where it didn't matar (rain) yabash (dry land).

So shanayam (two) or shalawash (three) irayam (cities) nawai (staggered) to achad (one) iyar (city) to shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters), and were not shabai (satisfied): yet you haven't shawab (turn back / repent) to me," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

"I nakah (struck) you with blight and mildew many times in your ganah (gardens) and your karam (vineyards); and your thaan (fig) trees and your zayath (olive) trees have the swarming locust akal (eat): yet you haven't shawab (turn back / repent) to me," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

"I shalach (send) dabar (word / matter) among you like I did Matzarayam (Egypt). I have harag (kill) your bachawar (young) men with the charab (sword), and have carried shabay (away) your sawas (horses); and I filled your ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) with the stench of your machanah (camp), yet you haven't shawab (turn back / repent) to me," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

"I have overthrown some of you, as when Alahayam mahapakah (overthrew) Sadam (Sodom) and Imarah (Gomorrah), and you were like a burning stick natzal (plucked) out of the sharapah (fire); yet you haven't shawab (turn back / repent) to me," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

"Therefore thus will I ishah (make) to you, Yashar-Al (Israel); iqab (award / effect after the cause) I will ishah (make) this to you, kawan (prepare) to qaraah (meet) your Alahayam, Yashar-Al (Israel).

For, behold, he who yatzar (forms) the harayam (mountains), and baraa (created) the rawach (spirit / wind), and nagad (declares) to adam (man) what is his shach (thought); who ishah (make) the shachar (morning) iyapah (darkness), and darak (treads) on the bamah (high) places of the aratz (Earth/land): Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies), is his sham (name)."
Shamai (hearken / hear) to this dabar (word / matter) which I nashaa (lift) up for a qayanah (lamentation) over you, O bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel).

"The bathawalah (virgin) of Yashar-Al (Israel) napal (fall / be cast down) fallen; She shall qawam (rise up) no more. She is natash (cast) down on her adamah (land); there is no one to qawam (rise up) her up."

For thus amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah: "The iyar (city) that yatzaa (go out / come out) forth a alap (thousand) shall have a maah (hundred) shaar (left), and that which yatzaa (go out / come out) forth one maah (hundred) shall have ishar (ten) shaar (left) to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel)."
For thus amar (spoke) Yahawah to the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel): "darash (seek) me, and you will chayah (live);

But don't darash (seek) Bayath-Al (Bethel), nor bawaa (come) into Galagal (Gilgal), and don't ibar (pass over/through) to Baar-Shabai (Beersheba): for Galagal (Gilgal) shall galah (surely) galah (go) into captivity, and Bayath-Al (Bethel) shall come to nothing.

Darash (seek) Yahawah, and you will chayah (live); lest he tzalach (break) out like ash (fire) in the bayath (house) of Yawasap (Joseph), and it akal (eat), and there be no one to kabah (quench) it in Bayath-Al (Bethel).
You who hapak (turn) mashapat (justice) to lainah (wormwood), and yanach (cast) down tzadaqah (righteousness) to the aratz (Earth/land):

Seek him who ishah (make) the kayamah (pleiades) and kasayal (orion), and hapak (turns) the shadow of tzalamawath (death) into the baqar (morning), and makes the yawam (day) chashak (darkness) with layal (night); who qaraa (called) for the may (waters) of the yam (sea/waters), and shapak (pours) them out on the surface of the aratz (Earth/land), Yahawah is his sham (name),
Who brings sudden shad (destruction) on the iz (strong), so that shad (destruction) bawaa (come) on the mabatzar (fortress).
They shanaa (hate) him who yakach (reproves) in the shair (gate), and they thaib (abhor) him who dabar (word / matter) blamelessly.

Yain (forasmuch) therefore as you trample on the dal (poor), and laqach (take / seize) taxes from him of bar (wheat): You have banah (build) bathay (houses) of cut gazayath (stone), but you will not yashab (inhabit/dwell) in them. You have natai (planted) chamad (pleasant) karamay (vineyards), but you shall not shathah (drinks) their yayan (wine).

For I yadai (know) how many your offenses, and how itzawam (great) are your chataah (sin)— you who tzarar (afflict) the tzadayaq (righteous), who laqach (take / seize) a kapar (bribe), and who natah (turn) aside the abayawan (needy) in the courts.
Therefore a shakal (prudent) person damam (keeps) silent in such a ith (time), for it is an rai (evil) ith (time).
Darash (seek) tawab (good / proper function), and not rai (evil), that you may chayah (live); and so Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies), will be with you, as you amar (spoke).

Shanaa (hate) rai (evil), ahab (love) tawab (good / proper function), and yatzag (establish) mashapat (justice) in the courts. It may be that Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies), will be gracious to the shaarayath (remnant) of Yawasap (Joseph)."

Therefore thus yaamaraw (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies), the Adanay: "masapad (wailing) will be in all the rachab (broad) ways; and they will amar (spoke) in all the chawatzawath (streets), ‘haw (alas)! Haw (alas)!' And they will qaraa (called) the farmer to abal (mourning), and those who are skillful in nahay (lamentation) to masapad (wailing).
In all karamayam (vineyards) there will be masapad (wailing); for I will ibar (pass over/through) qarab (among / near) the midst of you," amar (spoke) Yahawah.
"Haway (Alas/Woe!) To you who awah (desire) the yawam (day) of Yahawah! Mah (why) do you long for the yawam (day) of Yahawah? It is chashak (darkness), and not awar (light).

As if a ayash (man / husband) nawas (fled) from a aray (lion), and a dab (bear) pagai (met) him; Or he bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) and samak (leaned) his yad (hand) on the qayar (wall), and a snake bit him.
Won't the yawam (day) of Yahawah be chashak (darkness), and not awar (light)? Even very apal (dark), and no nagah (brightness) in it?
I shanaa (hate), I maas (despise) your chag (feast/festival), and I can't stand your solemn itzarah (assemblies).

Yes, though you ilah (go up / offer) me your burnt ilawath (offerings) and meal manachah (offerings), I will not ratzah (accept) them; neither will I nabat (regard) the shalam (peace) offerings of your marayaa (fat) animals.
Sawar (take) away from me the hamawan (noise) of your shayar (song)! I will not shamai (hearken / hear) to the music of your harps.
But let mashapat (justice) galal (roll) on like mayam (Waters), and tzadaqah (righteousness) like a ayathan (mighty) nachal (stream / river).
"Did you nagash (bring) to me zabachayam (sacrifices) and manachah (offerings) in the madabar (wilderness) arabaiyam (forty) shanah (years), bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel)?
You also nashaa (lift) the sakawath (tent) of your king and the Kayawan (shrine) of your tzalam (likeness), the kawakab (star) of your Alahayam, which you ishah (make) for yourselves.
Therefore will I cause you to galah (go) into captivity halaah (beyond) Damashaq (Damascus)," amar (spoke) Yahawah, whose sham (name) is the Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies).

Haway (Alas/Woe!) To those who are at shaanan (ease) in Tzayawan (Zion), and to those who are batach (secure) on the har (mountain) of Shamarawan (Samaria), the notable men of the raashayath (beginning) of the gawayam (nations), to whom the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) bawaa (come)!

Ibar (pass over/through) to Kalanah (Calneh), and raah (see); and from there yalak (go) to Hamath the rab (great); then yarad (go) down to gath (gath) of the Palashathay (Philistines). Are they tawab (good / proper function) than these mamalakawath (kingdoms)? Or is their gabawal (border/boundary) greater than your gabawal (border/boundary)?
Those who nadah (put) far away the rai (evil) yawam (day), and cause the shabath (shabath / rest) of chamas (violence) to nagash (come) near;

Who shakab (lie) on matawath (beds) of shan (ivory), and sarach (stretch) themselves on their couches, and akal (eat) the karayam (lambs) out of the tzaan (flock), and the calves out of the thawak (midst) of the marabaq (stall);
Who strum on the strings of a harp; who chashab (invent) for themselves kalay (instruments) of music, like Dawad (David);

Who shathah (drinks) yayan (wine) in mazaraqay (bowls), and mashach (anoint) themselves with the best shamanayam (oils); but they are not chalah (afflict) for the shabar (affliction) of Yawasap (Joseph).
Therefore they will now galah (go) captive with the raash (head) who galah (go) captive; and the feasting and lounging will end.

"The Adanay Yahawah has shabai (swear / take oath) by himself," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies): "I thaab (abhor) the gaawan (pride) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and detest his fortresses. Therefore I will sagar (deliver) up the iyar (city) with malaa (all) that is in it.
It will happen, if there yathar (remain) ishar (ten) anashayam (men) in achad (one) bayath (house), that they shall mawath (death).

"When a dawad (man's) relative nashaa (lift) him, even he who sarap (burns) him, to yatzaa (go out / come out) bodies out of the bayath (house), and asks him who is in the innermost yarakathay (parts) of the bayath (house), ‘Is there yet any with you?' And he amar (spoke), ‘No;' then he will amar (spoke), ‘Hush! Indeed we must not zakar (remember) the sham (name) of Yahawah.'
"For, behold, Yahawah tzawah (commands), and the gadawal (very great/important/mighty) bayath (house) will be smashed to pieces, and the qatan (small / young / least) bayath (house) into bits.

Do sawasayam (horses) rawatz (run) on the rocky crags? Does one charash (plow) there with oxen? But you have hapak (turned) mashapat (justice) into raash (head), and the paray (fruit) of tzadaqah (righteousness) into bitterness;
You who shamach (rejoice) in a thing of nothing, who amar (spoke), ‘Haven't we laqach (take / seize) for ourselves qaran (horn) by our own chazaq (strength)?'

For, behold, I will qawam (rise up) up against you a gaway (heathen / nation), bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel)," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaawath (armies); "and they will lachatz (afflict) you from the entrance of Chamath (Hamath) to the nachal (stream / river) of the irabah (arabah)."

Thus the Adanay Yahawah showed me: and behold, he yatzar (formed) locusts in the thachalah (beginning) of the ilah (go up / offer) up of the laqash (latter) growth; and behold, it was the laqash (latter) growth achar (other) the malak (king) harvest.

It happened that, when they kalah (complete / finish) an end of akal (eat) the ishab (grass) of the aratz (Earth/land), then I amar (spoke), "Adanay Yahawah, salach (forgive/pardon/make clean), I beg you! How could Yaiqab (Jacob) qawam (rise up)? For he is qatan (small / young / least)."
Yahawah relented concerning this. "It shall not be," amar (spoke) Yahawah.

Thus the Adanay Yahawah showed me and behold, the Adanay Yahawah qaraa (called) for rayab (judgment) by ash (fire); and it dried up the rab (great) thahawam (depths), and would have akal (eat) the chalaq (land).
Then I amar (spoke), "Adanay Yahawah, stop, I beg you! How could Yaiqab (Jacob) qawam (rise up)? For he is qatan (small / young / least)."
Yahawah relented concerning this. "This also shall not be," amar (spoke) the Adanay Yahawah.
Thus he showed me and behold, the Adanay natzab (stood) beside a chawamah (wall) made by a anak (plumb) line, with a anak (plumb) line in his yad (hand).

Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, "Imawas (Amos), what do you raah (see)?" I amar (spoke), "A anak (plumb) line." Then the Adanay amar (spoke), "Behold, I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) a anak (plumb) line in the qarab (among / near) of my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel). I will not again ibar (pass over/through) by them any more.

The bamah (high) places of Yashachaq (Isaac) will be shamam (desolate), the maqadashay (sanctuaries) of Yashar-Al (Israel) will be charab (laid) waste; and I will qawam (rise up) against the bayath (house) of Yarabaim (Jeroboam) with the charab (sword)."

Then Amatzayah (Amaziah) the kahan (priest) of Bayath-Al (Bethel) shalach (send) to Yarabaim (Jeroboam) malak (king) of Yashar-Al (Israel), amar (spoke), "Imawas (Amos) has qashar (conspired) against you in the qarab (among / near) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel). The aratz (Earth/land) is not yakal (able) to kawal (all) all his dabar (word / matter).
For Imawas (Amos) amar (spoke), ‘Yarabaim (Jeroboam) will mawath (death) by the charab (sword), and Yashar-Al (Israel) shall galah (surely) be galah (led) away captive out of his adamah (land).'"

Amatzayah (Amaziah) also amar (spoke) to Imawas (Amos), "You chazah (seer), yalak (go), barach (flee) away into the aratz (Earth/land) of Yahawadah (Judah), and there akal (eat) lacham (bread), and nabaa (prophesy) there:
But don't nabaa (prophesy) again any more at Bayath-Al (Bethel); for it is the malak (king) maqadash (sanctuary), and it is a mamalakah (royal) bayath (house)!"

Then Imawas (Amos) inah (answer / respond) Amatzayah (Amaziah), "I was no nabayaa (prophet/prophecy), neither was I a nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) ban (son); but I was a herdsman, and a farmer of shaqamah (sycamore) figs;
And Yahawah laqach (take / seize) me from achar (other) the tzaan (flock), and Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, ‘yalak (go), nabaa (prophesy) to my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel).'

Now therefore shamai (hearken / hear) to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah: ‘You amar (spoke), Don't nabaa (prophesy) against Yashar-Al (Israel), and don't preach against the bayath (house) of Yashachaq (Isaac).'

Therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: ‘Your ayashah (woman / wife) shall be a prostitute in the iyar (city), and your ban (son) and your banath (daughter) shall napal (fall / be cast down) by the charab (sword), and your adamah (land) shall be chalaq (divided) by chabal (line); and you yourself shall mawath (death) in a adamah (land) that is tamaa (unclean), and Yashar-Al (Israel) shall galah (surely) be galah (led) away captive out of his adamah (land).'"
Thus the Adanay Yahawah showed me: behold, a kalawab (basket) of qayatz (summer) fruit.

He amar (spoke), "Imawas (Amos), what do you raah (see)?" I amar (spoke), "A kalawab (basket) of qayatz (summer) fruit." Then Yahawah amar (spoke) to me, "The qatz (end) bawaa (come) come on my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel). I will not again ibar (pass over/through) by them any more.

The shayarawath (songs) of the hayakal (temple) will be wailings in that yawam (day)," naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah. "The pagar (dead) bodies will be many. In every maqawam (place) they will shalak (throw) them out with hasah (silence).
Shamai (hearken / hear) this, you who shaap (desire) to swallow up the abayawan (needy), and shabath (shabath / rest) the abayawan (poor) of the aratz (Earth/land) to shabath (shabath / rest),

Amar (spoke), ‘When will the new chadash (month) be ibar (pass over/through), that we may shabar (sell) grain? And the shabath (shabath / rest), that we may market bar (wheat), making the ayapah (ephah) qatan (small / young / least), and the shaqal (shekel) large, and iwath (dealing) falsely with maazanay (balances) of maramah (deceit);
That we may qanah (buy) the dal (poor) for kasap (silver), and the abayawan (needy) for a pair of nailayam (shoes), and shabar (sell) the sweepings with the bar (wheat)?'"
Yahawah has shabai (swear / take oath) by the gaawan (pride) of Yaiqab (Jacob), "Surely I will never shakach (forget) any of their maishah (works).

Won't the aratz (Earth/land) ragaz (tremble) for this, and everyone abal (mourn) who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in it? Yes, it will ilah (go up / offer) up wholly like the yaar (river); and it will be stirred up and sink again, like the yaar (river) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

It will happen in that yawam (day)," naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, "that I will cause the shamash (sun) to bawaa (come) down at tzahar (noon), and I will chashak (darkness) the aratz (Earth/land) in the awar (light) yawam (day).

I will hapak (turn) your chag (feast/festival) into abal (mourning), and all your shayar (song) into qayanah (lamentation); and I will ilah (go up / offer) you wear sackcloth on all your bodies, and qarachah (baldness) on every raash (head). I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) it like the abal (mourning) for an only son, and its acharayath (end) like a mar (bitter) yawam (day).

Behold, the yamayam (days) bawaa (come)," naam (declares prophetically) the Adanay Yahawah, "that I will shalach (send) a raib (famine) in the aratz (Earth/land), not a raib (famine) of lacham (bread), nor a tzamaa (thirst) for mayam (Waters), but of shamai (hearken / hear) the dabaray (words) of Yahawah.

They will nawai (wander) from yam (sea/waters) to yam (sea/waters), and from the tzapawan (north) even to the mazarach (east); they will shawat (run) back and forth to baqash (seek) the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah, and will not matzaa (find) it.
In that yawam (day) the yapah (beautiful) bathawalath (virgins) and the bachawar (young) men will ilap (faint) for tzamaa (thirst).

Those who shabai (swear / take oath) by the ashamah (sin) of Shamarawan (Samaria), and amar (spoke), ‘As your Alahayam, Dan (Dan), chay (life);' and, ‘As the darak (way) of Baar-Shabai (Beersheba) chay (life);' they will napal (fall / be cast down), and never qawam (rise up) up again."

I raah (see) the Adanay natzab (standing) beside the mazabach (altar), and he amar (spoke), "nakah (strike) the tops of the pillars, that the sapayam (thresholds) may raish (shake); and break them in pieces on the raash (head) of all of them; and I will harag (kill) the acharayath (last) of them with the charab (sword): there shall not one of them nawas (flee) nawas (away), and there shall not one of them palayat (escape).

Though they chathar (dig) into shaawal (Sheol / afterlife), there my yad (hand) will laqach (take / seize) them; and though they ilah (go up / offer) up to shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), there I will yarad (bring) them down.

Though they chabaa (hide) themselves in the raash (head) of Karamal (Carmel), I will chapash (search) and laqach (take / seize) them out there; and though they be sathar (hidden) from my iyan (eye) in the qaraqai (bottom) of the yam (sea/waters), there I will tzawah (command) the nachash (serpent), and it will nashak (bite) them.

Though they yalak (go) into shabay (captivity) panayam (face) their ayab (enemy), there I will tzawah (command) the charab (sword), and it will harag (kill) them. I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) my iyan (eye) on them for rai (evil), and not for tawab (good / proper function).

For the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies), is he who touches the aratz (Earth/land) and it mawag (melts), and all who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in it will abal (mourn); and it will ilah (go up / offer) up wholly like the yaar (river), and will shaqai (sink) again, like the yaar (river) of Matzarayam (Egypt).

It is he who banah (build) his rooms in the shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), and has founded his vault on the aratz (Earth/land); he who qaraa (called) for the may (waters) of the yam (sea/waters), and shapak (pours) them out on the surface of the aratz (Earth/land); Yahawah is his sham (name).

Are you not like the banay (children) of the Kawashay (Ethiopians) to me, banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel)?" Naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah. "Haven't I ilah (go up / offer) up Yashar-Al (Israel) out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and the Palashathay (Philistines) from Kapathar (Caphtor), and the Aram (Syrians) from Qayar (Kir)?

Behold, the iyanay (eyes) of the Adanay Yahawah are on the sinful mamalakah (kingdom), and I will shamad (destroy) it from off the surface of the adamah (earth); except that I will not shamad (utterly) shamad (destroy) the bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob)," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

"For, behold, I will tzawah (command), and I will nawai (sift) the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel) among all the gawayam (nations), as grain is nawai (sifted) in a kabarah (sieve), yet not the tzarawar (least) kernel will napal (fall / be cast down) on the aratz (Earth/land).
All the chataay (sinners) of my im (nation / people) will mawath (death) by the charab (sword), who amar (spoke), ‘rai (evil) won't nagash (overtake) nor qadam (meet) us.'

In that yawam (day) I will qawam (rise up) up the sakah (tent) of Dawad (David) who is napal (fall / be cast down), and gadar (close) up its breaches, and I will qawam (rise up) up its harayasah (ruins), and I will banah (build) it as in the yamay (days) of iwalam (forever);

That they may yarash (possess) the shaarayath (remnant) of Adawam (Edom), and all the gawayam (nations) who are qaraa (called) by my sham (name)," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah who ishah (make) this.

"Behold, the yamayam (days) bawaa (come)," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, "that the plowman shall nagash (overtake) the qatzar (reaper), and the one darak (treading) inabayam (grapes) him who mashak (sows) zarai (seed); and sweet isayas (wine) will drip from the gabaiwath (mountains), and flow from the gabaiwath (hills).

I will bring my im (nation / people) Yashar-Al (Israel) shawab (turn back / repent) from shabawath (captivity), and they will rebuild the ruined irayam (cities), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) them; and they will natai (plant) karamayam (vineyards), and shathah (drinks) yayan (wine) from them. They shall also ishah (make) ganawath (gardens), and akal (eat) their paray (fruit).
I will natai (plant) them on their adamah (land), and they will no more be nathash (plucked) up out of their adamah (land) which I nathan (give) given them," amar (spoke) Yahawah your Alahayam.

The chazawan (vision) of Ibadayah (Obadiah). This is what the Adanay Yahawah amar (spoke) about Adawam (Edom). We have shamai (hearken / hear) shamawaih (news) from Yahawah, and an tzayar (ambassador) is shalach (send) among the gawayam (nations), saying, "qawam (rise up), and let's qawam (rise up) up against her in malachamah (battle).
Behold, I nathan (give) made you qatan (small / young / least) among the gawayam (nations). You are maad (greatly) bazah (despised).

The zadawan (pride) of your lab (heart) has nashaa (lift) you, you who shakan (place) in the chagaway (clefts) of the salai (rock), whose shakan (place) is marawam (high), who amar (spoke) in his lab (heart), ‘Who will yarad (bring) me down to the aratz (Earth/land)?'

Though you gabah (mount) on high as the nashar (eagle), and though your qan (nest) is shawam (place / establish / appoint) among the kawakabayam (stars), I will yarad (bring) you down from there," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah.

"If thieves bawaa (come) to you, if shawadaday (robbers) by layal (night)— oh, what disaster awaits you— wouldn't they only ganab (steal) until they had day (enough)? If grape pickers bawaa (come) to you, wouldn't they shaar (leave) some gleaning ilalawath (grapes)?
How Ishaw (Esau) will be ransacked! How his matzapan (hidden) treasures are sought out!

All the anashay (men) of your alliance have shalach (send) you on your way, even to the gabawal (border/boundary). The anashay (men) who were at shalawam (peace / safety) with you have nashaa (lift) you, and yakal (prevailed) against you. Friends who eat your lacham (bread) shawam (place / establish / appoint) a snare under you. There is no thabawan (understanding) in him."

"Won't I in that yawam (day)," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, "abad (destroy / perish) the chakam (wise) men out of Adawam (Edom), and thabawan (understanding) out of the har (mountain) of Ishaw (Esau)?
Your gabawar (mighty) men, Thayaman (Teman), will be chathath (dismayed), to the end that everyone may be karath (cut) off from the har (mountain) of Ishaw (Esau) by qatal (slaughter).
For the chamas (violence) done to your ach (brother/kinsman) Yaiqab (Jacob), bawashah (shame) will kasah (cover) you, and you will be karath (cut) off iwalam (forever).

In the yawam (day) that you imad (stood) on the other side, in the yawam (day) that strangers shabah (carried) away his chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor), and nakarayam (foreigners) bawaa (come) into his shair (gates), and yadad (cast) gawaral (lots) for Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), even you were like achad (one) of them.

But don't raah (see) down on your ach (brother/kinsman) in the yawam (day) of his disaster, and don't shamach (rejoice) over the banay (children) of Yahawadah (Judah) in the yawam (day) of their abad (destroy / perish). Don't pah (speak) gadal (proudly) in the yawam (day) of tzarah (distress).

Don't bawaa (come) into the shair (gate) of my im (nation / people) in the yawam (day) of their ayad (calamity). Don't raah (see) down on their rai (affliction) in the yawam (day) of their ayad (calamity), neither seize their wealth on the yawam (day) of their ayad (calamity).
Don't imad (stand) in the crossroads to karath (cut) off those of his who palayat (escape). Don't sagar (deliver) up those of his who sharayad (remain) in the yawam (day) of tzarah (distress).

For the yawam (day) of Yahawah is qarawab (near) all the gawayam (nations)! As you ishah (make) done, it will be ishah (make) to you. Your deeds will shawab (turn back / repent) upon your own raash (head).

For as you have shathah (drinks) on my qadash (set apart / make holy) har (mountain), so will all the gawayam (nations) shathah (drinks) continually. Yes, they will shathah (drinks), lawai (swallow) down, and will be as laa (NOT) they had not been.

But in har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion), there will be those who palayatah (escape), and it will be qadash (set apart / make holy). The bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob) will yarash (possess) their mawarash (possessions).

The bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob) will be a ash (fire), the bayath (house) of Yawasap (Joseph) a lahabah (flame), and the bayath (house) of Ishaw (Esau) for qash (stubble). They will dalaq (burn) among them, and akal (eat) them. There will not be any sharayad (remaining) to the bayath (house) of Ishaw (Esau)." Indeed, Yahawah has dabar (word / matter).

Those of the nagab (south) will yarash (possess) the har (mountain) of Ishaw (Esau), and those of the lowland, the Palashathay (Philistines). They will yarash (possess) the shadah (field) of Aparayam (Ephraim), and the shadah (field) of Shamarawan (Samaria). Banayamayan (Benjamin) will possess Galaid (Gilead).

The galawath (captives) of this chayal (army) of the banay (children) of Yashar-Al (Israel), who are among the Kanainay (Canaanites), will possess even to Tzarapath (Zarephath); and the galawath (captives) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem), who are in Saparad (Sepharad), will yarash (possess) the iray (cities) of the Negev.
Saviors will ilah (go up / offer) up on har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion) to shapat (judge / judgement) the har (mountain) of Ishaw (Esau), and the malawakah (kingdom) will be Yahawah.
Now the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Yawanah (Jonah) the ban (son) of Amathay (Amittai), amar (spoke),

"Qawam (rise up), yalak (go) to Nayanawah (Nineveh), that gadawal (very great/important/mighty) iyar (city), and qaraa (called) against it, for their rai (wickedness) has ilah (go up / offer) up panayam (face) me."

But Yawanah (Jonah) qawam (rise up) up to barach (flee) to Tharashayash (Tarshish) from the panayam (face) of Yahawah. He yarad (went) down to Yapaw (Joppa), and matzaa (found) a anayah (ship) bawaa (come) to Tharashayash (Tarshish); so he nathan (give) its fare, and yarad (went) down into it, to bawaa (come) with them to Tharashayash (Tarshish) from the panayam (face) of Yahawah.

But Yahawah tawal (sent) out a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) rawach (spirit / wind) on the yam (sea/waters), and there was a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) sair (storm) on the yam (sea/waters), so that the anayah (ship) was likely to shabar (break) up.

Then the malachayam (mariners) were yaraa (fear / be afraid), and every ayash (man / husband) zaiq (cried) to his Alahayam. They threw the cargo that was in the anayah (ship) into the yam (sea/waters) to lighten the ship. But Yawanah (Jonah) had yarad (gone) down into the innermost yarakathay (parts) of the sapayanah (ship), and he was shakab (laying) down, and was radam (fast) asleep.

So the rab (shipmaster) qarab (come close) to him, and amar (spoke) to him, "What do you mean, sleeper? Qawam (rise up), qaraa (called) on your Alahayam! Maybe your Alahayam will notice us, so that we won't abad (destroy / perish)."

They all amar (spoke) to ayash (man / husband) other, "yalak (come), napal (fall / be cast down) us cast gawaralawath (lots), that we may yadai (know) who is responsible for this rai (evil) that is on us." So they napal (fall / be cast down) gawaralawath (lots), and the gawaral (lot) napal (fall / be cast down) on Yawanah (Jonah).

Then they asked him, "nagad (tell) us, please, for whose cause this rai (evil) is on us. What is your malaakah (occupation)? Ayan (NO ONE) do you bawaa (come) from? What is your aratz (Earth/land)? Of what im (nation / people) are you?"

He amar (spoke) to them, "I am a ibaray (hebrew), and I yaraa (fear) Yahawah, the Alahayam of shamayam (Shamayam / Heavens), who ishah (make) made the yam (sea/waters) and the dry yabashah (dry land)."

Then were the anashayam (men) gadawal (very great/important/mighty) yaraa (fear / be afraid), and amar (spoke) to him, "What is this that you ishah (make) done?" For the anashayam (men) yadai (knew) that he was fleeing from the panayam (face) of Yahawah, because he had nagad (told) them.
Then they amar (spoke) to him, "What shall we ishah (make) to you, that the yam (sea/waters) may be shathaq (calm) to us?" For the yam (sea/waters) halak (move) more and more stormy.

He amar (spoke) to them, "nashaa (lift) me up, and throw me into the yam (sea/waters). Then the yam (sea/waters) will be shathaq (calm) for you; for I yadai (know) that because of me this gadawal (very great/important/mighty) sair (storm) is on you."

Nevertheless the anashayam (men) chathar (rowed) hard to shawab (turn back / repent) them back to the yabashah (dry land); but they yakal (could) not, for the yam (sea/waters) halak (move) more and more stormy against them.

Therefore they qaraa (called) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "We beg you, Yahawah, we beg you, don't let us die for this ayash (man / husband) napash (soul), and don't nathan (give) on us naqay (innocent) dam (blood); for you, Yahawah, ishah (make) done as it chapatz (pleased) you."
So they nashaa (lift) up Yawanah (Jonah), and threw him into the yam (sea/waters); and the yam (sea/waters) imad (ceased) its zaip (raging).
Then the anashayam (men) yaraa (fear / be afraid) Yahawah gadawal (very great/important/mighty); and they zabach (offered) a zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah, and made nadarayam (vows).

Yahawah manah (prepared) a gadawal (very great/important/mighty) dag (fish) to balai (swallow) up Yawanah (Jonah), and he was in the maih (belly) of the dag (fish) shalawash (three) yawam (day) and shalawash (three) layal (nights).
Then Yawanah (Jonah) prayed to Yahawah, his Alahayam, out of the dag (fish's) maih (belly).
He said, "I called because of my affliction to Yahawah. He answered me. Out of the maih (belly) of Sheol I cried. You heard my voice.
For you threw me into the depths, in the heart of the seas. The flood was all around me. All your waves and your billows passed over me.
I said, ‘I have been banished from your sight; yet I will look again toward your holy temple.'
The waters surrounded me, even to the soul. The deep was around me. The weeds were wrapped around my head.
I sabab (went) down to the bottoms of the mountains. The earth barred me in forever: yet have you sabab (brought) up my napash (soul) from the pit, Yahawah my Alahayam.
"When my soul fainted within me, I remembered Yahawah. My prayer yarad (came) in to you, into your holy temple.
Those who regard lying vanities forsake their own mercy.
But I will sacrifice to you with the voice of thanksgiving. I will pay that which I have vowed. Salvation belongs to Yahawah."
Yahawah spoke to the fish, and it vomited out on the dry land.
The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah came to Yawanah (Jonah) the shanay (second) time, amar (spoke),
"Qawam (rise up), yalak (go) to Nayanawah (Nineveh), that gadawal (very great/important/mighty) iyar (city), and qaraa (called) to it the message that I dabar (word / matter) you."

So Yawanah (Jonah) qawam (rise up), and yalak (went) to Nayanawah (Nineveh), according to the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah. Now Nayanawah (Nineveh) was an exceedingly gadawal (very great/important/mighty) iyar (city), shalawash (three) yamayam (days)' mahalak (journey) across.

He chalal (began) to bawaa (come) into the iyar (city) a yawam (day) mahalak (journey), and he qaraa (called) out, and amar (spoke), "In arabaiyam (forty) yawam (day), Nayanawah (Nineveh) will be overthrown!"

The anashay (people) of Nayanawah (Nineveh) aman (believe / have faith) Alahayam; and they qaraa (called) a tzawam (fast), and labash (put) on sackcloth, from their greatest even to their qatan (small / young / least).

The news nagai (reached) the malak (king) of Nayanawah (Nineveh), and he qawam (rise up) from his kasaa (throne), and ibar (pass over/through) off his royal adarath (robe), kasah (covered) himself with sackcloth, and yashab (inhabit/dwell) in ashes.

He made a proclamation and amar (spoke) through Nayanawah (Nineveh) by the taim (decree) of the malak (king) and his gadawal (very great/important/mighty), amar (spoke), "Let neither adam (man) nor animal, baqar (morning) nor tzaan (flock), taim (taste) anything; let them not raih (feed), nor shathah (drinks) mayam (Waters);

But let them be kasah (covered) with sackcloth, both adam (man) and animal, and let them qaraa (called) chazaqah (mightily) to Alahayam. Yes, let them shawab (turn back / repent) everyone from his rai (evil) darak (way), and from the chamas (violence) that is in his kap (hands).

Who yadai (knows) whether Alahayam will not shawab (turn back / repent) and relent, and shawab (turn back / repent) shawab (turn back / repent) from his charawan (fierce) ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), so that we might not abad (destroy / perish)?"

Alahayam raah (see) their maishah (works), that they shawab (turn back / repent) from their rai (evil) darak (way). Alahayam relented of the disaster which he dabar (word / matter) he would ishah (make) to them, and he didn't ishah (make) it.
But it displeased Yawanah (Jonah) gadawal (very great/important/mighty), and he was charah (hot with anger).

He palal (prayed) to Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "Please, Yahawah, wasn't this dabar (word / matter) I said when I was still in my own adamah (country)? Therefore I hurried to flee to Tharashayash (Tarshish), for I yadai (knew) that you are a chanawan (gracious) Al, and rachawam (merciful), arak (slow) to ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and abundant in loving chasad (grace), and you relent of doing rai (harm).
Therefore now, Yahawah, laqach (take / seize), I beg you, my napash (soul) from me; for it is tawab (good / proper function) for me to mawath (death) than to chay (life)."
Yahawah amar (spoke), "Is it right for you to be charah (hot with anger)?"

Then Yawanah (Jonah) yatzaa (go out / come out) out of the iyar (city), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) on the qadam (east) side of the iyar (city), and there ishah (make) himself a sakah (booth), and yashab (inhabit/dwell) under it in the tzal (shade), until he might raah (see) what would become of the iyar (city).

Yahawah Alahayam manah (prepared) a vine, and ilah (go up / offer) it to come up over Yawanah (Jonah), that it might be a tzal (shade) over his raash (head), to natzal (deliver) him from his discomfort. So he was gadawal (very great/important/mighty) shamach (glad) because of the vine.
But Alahayam manah (prepared) a thawalai (worm) at dawn the next macharath (day), and it chewed on the vine, so that it yabash (dry land).

It happened, when the shamash (sun) arose, that Alahayam manah (prepared) a sultry qadayam (east) rawach (spirit / wind); and the shamash (sun) nakah (beat) on Yawanah (Jonah's) raash (head), so that he ilap (fainted), and shaal (requested) for himself that he might mawath (death), and amar (spoke), "It is tawab (good / proper function) for me to mawath (death) than to chay (life)."
Alahayam amar (spoke) to Yawanah (Jonah), "Is it right for you to be charah (hot with anger) about the vine?" He amar (spoke), "I am right to be charah (hot with anger), even to mawath (death)."
Yahawah amar (spoke), "You have been concerned for the vine, for which you have not labored, neither gadal (made) it grow; which ban (son) up in a night, and abad (destroy / perish) in a ban (son).

Shouldn't I be concerned for Nayanawah (Nineveh), that gadawal (very great/important/mighty) iyar (city), in which are more than one hundred shanayam (two) rabaw (thousand) adam (persons) who can't yadai (discern) between their right yamayan (right hand) and their left shamaawal (left hand); and also much livestock?"

The dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah that came to Mayakah (Micah) the Morashtite in the yamay (days) of Yawatham (Jotham), Achaz (Ahaz), and Chazaqayah (Hezekiah), malakay (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah), which he chazah (saw) concerning Shamarawan (Samaria) and Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

Shamai (hearken / hear), you imayam (peoples), all of you. Listen, O aratz (Earth/land), and malaa (all) that is therein: and let the Adanay Yahawah be id (until / as far as) against you, the Adanay from his qadash (set apart / make holy) hayakal (temple).
For, behold, Yahawah yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of his maqawam (place), and will yarad (come) down and darak (tread) on the bamah (high) places of the aratz (Earth/land).

The harayam (mountains) masas (melt) under him, and the imaqayam (valleys) split apart, like dawanag (wax) panayam (face) the ash (fire), like mayam (Waters) that are nagar (poured) down a mawarad (steep) place.

"All this is for the disobedience of Yaiqab (Jacob), and for the chataawath (sins) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel). What is the disobedience of Yaiqab (Jacob)? Isn't it Shamarawan (Samaria)? And what are the bamah (high) places of Yahawadah (Judah)? Aren't they Yarawashalam (Jerusalem)?

Therefore I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) Shamarawan (Samaria) like a rubble iy (heap) of the shadah (field), like places for planting karam (vineyards); and I will nagar (pour) down its aban (stone) into the gayaa (valley), and I will galah (uncover) its yasawad (foundations).

All her idols will be kathath (beaten) to pieces, and all her temple gifts will be sharap (burned) with ash (fire), and all her itzab (images) I will shamamah (destroy); for of the athanan (hire) of a prostitute has she qabatz (gathered) them, and to the athanan (hire) of a prostitute shall they shawab (turn back / repent)."
For this I will sapad (lament) and wail; I will yalak (go) shawalal (stripped) and irawam (naked); I will howl like the jackals, and moan like the banawath (daughters) of owls.
For her makah (wounds) are anash (incurable); for it bawaa (come) come even to Yahawadah (Judah). It reaches to the shair (gate) of my im (nation / people), even to Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).
Don't nagad (tell) it in gath (gath). Don't bakah (weep) at bakah (all). At Beth Ophrah I have palash (rolled) myself in the ipar (dust).

Ibar (pass over/through) on, yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Shapayar (Shaphir), in nakedness and bashath (shame). The yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Tzaanan (Zaanan) won't yatzaa (go out / come out) out. The sapad (wailing) of bayathahaatzal (beth) Ezel will laqach (take / seize) from you his protection.

For the yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Marawath (Maroth) chawal (waits) anxiously for tawab (good / proper function), because rai (evil) has yarad (come) down from Yahawah to the shair (gate) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

Harness the marakabah (chariot) to the rakash (swift) steed, yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Lakayash (Lachish). She was the raashayath (beginning) of chataah (sin) to the banath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion); For the pashaiy (transgressions) of Yashar-Al (Israel) were matzaa (found) in you.

Therefore you will nathan (give) a parting shalawach (gift) to Mawarashathagath (Moresheth Gath). The bathay (houses) of Akazayab (Achzib) will be a deceitful thing to the malakay (kings) of Yashar-Al (Israel).
I will yet bawaa (come) to you, yashab (inhabit/dwell) of Maraashah (Mareshah). He who is the kabawad (glory) of Yashar-Al (Israel) will bawaa (come) to Idalam (Adullam).

Shave your heads, and gazaz (cut) off your hair for the banay (children) of your thainawag (delight). Enlarge your qarachah (baldness) like the vulture; for they have galah (gone) into captivity from you!

Haway (Alas/Woe!) To those who chashab (devise) awan (iniquity) and pail (work) rai (evil) on their mashakab (beds)! When the baqar (morning) is awar (light), they practice it, because it is in the al (Alahayam) of their yad (hand).

They chamad (covet) shadawath (fields), and seize them; and bathayam (houses), and nashaa (lift) them away: and they ishaq (oppress) a gabar (man) and his bayath (house), even a ayash (man / husband) and his nachalah (heritage).

Therefore thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: "Behold, I am planning against these mashapachah (tribe / clan / family) a disaster, from which you will not mawash (remove) your tzawaar (necks), neither will you yalak (walk) rawamah (haughtily); for it is an rai (evil) ith (time).

In that yawam (day) they will nashaa (lift) up a mashal (parable) against you, and nahah (lament) with a nahayah (doleful) nahay (lamentation), amar (spoke), ‘We are shadad (utterly) ruined! My im (nation / people) chalaq (possession) is divided up. Indeed he mawash (takes) it from me and assigns our shadah (fields) to traitors!'"
Therefore you will have no shalak (one) who divides the chabal (land) by gawaral (lot) in the qahal (assembly) of Yahawah.
"Don't natap (prophesy)!" They natap (prophesy). "Don't natap (prophesy) about these things. Disgrace won't overtake us."

Shall it be amar (spoke), O bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob): "Is the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah angry? Are these his mailal (doings)? Don't my dabar (word / matter) do yatab (good) to him who halak (move) blamelessly?"

But lately my im (nation / people) have qawam (rise up) up as an ayab (enemy). You pashat (strip) the adar (robe) and clothing from those who ibar (pass over/through) by without a batach (care), shawab (turn back / repent) from malachamah (battle).

You drive the nashay (women) of my im (nation / people) out from their thainawag (pleasant) bayath (house); from their young iwalal (children) you laqach (take / seize) away my hadar (glory / majesty / splendor) iwalam (forever).
Qawam (rise up), and depart! For this is not your manawachah (resting) place, because of uncleanness that chabal (destroys), even with a maratz (grievous) chabal (destruction).

If a ayash (man / husband) halak (move) in a rawach (spirit / wind) of falsehood kazab (lies): "I will natap (prophesy) to you of yayan (wine) and of shakar (strong) drink;" he would be the natap (prophet) of this im (nation / people).

I will asap (surely) asap (assemble), Yaiqab (Jacob), all of you; I will qabatz (surely) qabatz (gather) the shaarayath (remnant) of Yashar-Al (Israel); I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) them yachad (together) as the tzaan (sheep) of batzarah (bozrah), as a idar (flock) in the thawak (midst) of their pasture; they will swarm with adam (people).

He who paratzaw (breaks) open the way ilah (go up / offer) up panayam (face) them. They paratz (break) ibar (pass over/through) the shair (gate), and yatzaa (go out / come out) out. And their malak (king) passes on panayam (face) them, with Yahawah at their raash (head).

I amar (spoke), "Please shamai (hearken / hear), you raashay (heads) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and qatzayanay (rulers) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel): Isn't it for you to yadai (know) mashapat (justice)?
You who shanaa (hate) the tawab (good / proper function), and ahab (love) the rai (evil); who gazal (tear) off their iwar (skin), and their shaar (flesh) from off their itzam (bones);

Who also akal (eat) the shaar (flesh) of my im (nation / people), and pashat (flay) their iwar (skin) from off them, and patzach (break) their itzam (bones), and parash (chop) them in pieces, as for the sayar (pot), and as bashar (flesh) thawak (midst) the qalachath (caldron).

Then they will zaiq (cry) to Yahawah, but he will not inah (answer / respond) them. Yes, he will sathar (hide) his panayam (face) from them at that ith (time), because they made their deeds raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil)."

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah concerning the nabayaayam (prophets) who lead my im (nation / people) thaih (astray); for those who feed their shan (teeth), they qaraa (called), "shalawam (peace / safety)!" And whoever doesn't provide for their pah (mouths), they qadash (set apart / make holy) malachamah (war) against him:

"Therefore layal (night) is over you, with no chazawan (vision), and it is chashak (darkness) to you, that you may not qasam (divine); and the shamash (sun) will bawaa (come) down on the nabayaayam (prophets), and the yawam (day) will be qadar (black) over them.
The chazayam (seers) shall be disappointed, and the diviners chapar (confounded). Yes, they shall all itah (cover) their shapam (lips); for there is no mainah (answer) from Alahayam."

But as for me, I am malaa (full) of kach (strength / mighty / power) by the rawach (spirit / wind) of Yahawah, and of mashapat (judgment), and of gabawarah (might), to nagad (declare) to Yaiqab (Jacob) his disobedience, and to Yashar-Al (Israel) his chataah (sin).

Please shamai (hearken / hear) to this, you raashay (heads) of the bayath (house) of Yaiqab (Jacob), and qatzayanay (rulers) of the bayath (house) of Yashar-Al (Israel), who thaib (abhor) mashapat (justice), and iqash (pervert) all yashar (upright).
They banah (build) up Tzayawan (Zion) with dam (blood), and Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) with iwal (iniquity).

Her leaders shapat (judge / judgement) for shachad (bribes), and her kahan (priest) yarah (teach) for a machayar (price), and her nabayaa (prophet/prophecy) of it tell fortunes for kasap (money): yet they shain (lean) on Yahawah, and amar (spoke), "Isn't Yahawah in the qarab (among / near) of us? No disaster will bawaa (come) on us."

Therefore Tzayawan (Zion) for your sake will be charash (plowed) like a shadah (field), and Yarawashalam (Jerusalem) will become iyayan (heaps) of rubble, and the har (mountain) of the bayath (house) like the bamah (high) places of a yair (forest).

But in the acharayath (latter) yamayam (days), it will happen that the har (mountain) of Yahawah bayath (house) will be kawan (established) on the raash (head) of the harayam (mountains), and it will be nashaa (lift) above the gabaiwath (hills); and imayam (peoples) will stream to it.

Many gawayam (nations) will halak (move) and amar (spoke), "yalak (come), and let us ilah (go up / offer) up to the har (mountain) of Yahawah, and to the bayath (house) of the Alahayam of Yaiqab (Jacob); and he will yarah (teach) us of his darak (ways), and we will yalak (walk) in his arach (paths)." For out of Tzayawan (Zion) will yatzaa (go out / come out) forth the thawarah (instruction), and the dabar (word / matter) of Yahawah from Yarawashalam (Jerusalem);

And he will shapat (judge / judgement) between many imayam (peoples), and will decide concerning itzawam (strong) gawayam (nations) rachawaq (afar) off. They will kathath (beat) their charab (sword) into athayam (plowshares), and their chanayath (spears) into mazamarah (pruning) hooks. Gaway (heathen / nation) will not nashaa (lift) up charab (sword) against gaway (heathen / nation), neither will they lamad (teach / instruct) malachamah (war) any more.

But they will yashab (inhabit/dwell) every ayash (man / husband) under his gapan (vine) and under his thaan (fig) tree; and no one will make them charad (afraid): For the pah (mouth) of Yahawah of tzabaawath (armies) has dabar (word / matter).
Indeed all the imayam (nations) may yalak (walk) in the sham (name) of their Alahayam; but we will yalak (walk) in the sham (name) of Yahawah our Alahayam iwalam (forever) and id (until / as far as).

"In that yawam (day)," naam (declares prophetically) Yahawah, "I will asap (assemble) that which is lame, and I will qabatz (gather) that which is nadach (driven) away, and that which I have raii (wicked / dysfunctional / evil);

And I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) that which was lame a shaarayath (remnant), and that which was halaa (cast) far off a itzawam (strong) gaway (heathen / nation): and Yahawah will malak (king) over them on har (mountain) Tzayawan (Zion) from then on, even iwalam (forever)."

You, magadal (tower) of the idar (flock), the hill of the banath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion), to you it will athah (you (masc)), yes, the raashawan (former) mamashalah (dominion) will bawaa (come), the mamalakah (kingdom) of the banath (daughter) of Yarawashalam (Jerusalem).

Now why do you rawai (cry) out rai (aloud)? Is there no malak (king) in you? Has your yaitz (counselor) abad (destroy / perish), that chayal (pains) have chazaq (taken) hold of you as of a yalad (birth / begot) in travail?

Be in chawal (pain), and gayach (labor) to bring forth, banath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion), like a yalad (birth / begot) in travail; for now you will yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the qarayah (city / town), and will shakan (place) in the shadah (field), and will come even to Babal (Babylon). There you will be natzal (rescued). There Yahawah will gaal (redeem) you from the kap (hand) of your ayab (enemy).
Now many gawayam (nations) have asap (assembled) amar (spoke) you, that say, "Let her be chanap (defiled), and let our iyan (eye) gloat over Tzayawan (Zion)."

But they don't yadai (know) the machashabawath (thoughts) of Yahawah, neither do they bayan (between) his itzah (counsel); for he has qabatz (gathered) them like the sheaves to the garan (threshing) floor.

Qawam (rise up) and dawash (thresh), banath (daughter) of Tzayawan (Zion); for I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) your qaran (horn) barazal (iron), and I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) your parasah (hoofs) nachawashah (brass); and you will daqaq (beat) in pieces many imayam (peoples): and I will charam (devote) their batzai (gain) to Yahawah, and their chayal (wealth / substance / capability / valor) to the Adawan of the whole aratz (Earth/land).
Now you shall gather yourself in troops, daughter of troops. He has yatzaa (go out / come out) siege against us. They will strike the judge of Yashar-Al (Israel) with a rod on the cheek.

But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, being small among the clans of Judah, out of you one will nathan (give) forth to me that is to be ruler in Yashar-Al (Israel); whose yashawabaw (goings) forth are from of ban (son), from everlasting.
Therefore he will abandon them until the ithah (now / present moment) that she who is in labor gives birth. Then the rest of his brothers will yashab (inhabit/dwell) to the children of Israel.

He shall qawam (rise up), and shall raih (shepherd) in the strength of Yahawah, in the majesty of the name of Yahawah his Alahayam: and they will live, for then he will be shalawam (peace / safety) to the ends of the aratz (Earth/land).

He will be our peace when Ashawar (Assyria) bawaa (come) our aratz (Earth/land), and when he marches through our fortresses, then we will raise against him seven raiw (shepherds), and eight leaders of men.
They will rule the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in its gates. He will deliver us from the Ban (Assyrian), when he invades our land, and when he marches within our border.

The shaarayath (remnant) of Yaiqab (Jacob) will be in the qarab (among / near) of many imayam (peoples), like dew from Yahawah, like showers on the grass, that don't wait for rab (man), nor wait for the sons of imayam (men).

The remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the animals of the forest, like a young lion among the flocks of sheep; who, if he rawam (will lift up) through, treads down and tears in pieces, and there is no one to deliver.
Let your hand be lifted up above your adversaries, and let all of your enemies be karath (cut) off.
"It will happen in that day," says Yahawah, "That I will karath (cut) off your horses out of the midst of you, and will karath (cut) your chariots.
I will karath (cut) off the cities of your land, and will tear down all your strongholds.
I will karath (cut) witchcraft from your yad (hand); and you shall have no soothsayers.
I will cut off your engraved images and your pillars out of your qarab (among / near); and you shall no more worship the work of your hands.
I will uproot your Asherim out of your midst; and I will destroy your cities.
I will ishah (make) naqam (vengeance) in ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and chamah (wrath) on the gaway (heathen / nation) that didn't shamai (hearken / hear)."

Shamai (hearken / hear) now to what Yahawah amar (spoke): "qawam (rise up), rayab (plead) your case before the harayam (mountains), and let the gabaiwath (hills) shamai (hearken / hear) what you have to say.

Shamai (hearken / hear), you harayam (mountains), Yahawah rayab (controversy), and you enduring masaday (foundations) of the aratz (Earth/land); for Yahawah has a rayab (controversy) with his im (nation / people), and he will contend with Yashar-Al (Israel).
My im (nation / people), what ishah (make) I done to you? How have I burdened you? Inah (answer / respond) me!

For I ilah (go up / offer) you up out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), and padah (redeemed) you out of the bayath (house) of ibad (servant). I shalach (send) panayam (face) you Mashah (Moses), Aharawan (Aaron), and Marayam (Miriam).

My im (nation / people), zakar (remember) now what Balaq (Balak) malak (king) of Mawaab (Moab) yaitz (devised), and what Balaim (Balaam) the ban (son) of Baiwar (Beor) inah (answer / respond) him from Shatayam (Shittim) to Galagal (Gilgal), that you may yadai (know) the tzadaqah (righteousness) acts of Yahawah."
How shall I qadam (come) before Yahawah, and kapap (bow) myself before the exalted Alahayam? Shall I qadam (come) before him with burnt iwalawath (offerings), with calves a shanah (year) ban (son)?

Will Yahawah be ratzah (pleased) with alapay (thousands) of ayalayam (rams)? With rababawath (tens) of thousands of nachalay (rivers) of shaman (oil)? Shall I nathan (give) my bakawar (firstborn) for my disobedience? The paray (fruit) of my batan (body) for the chataah (sin) of my napash (soul)?

He has shown you, O adam (man), what is tawab (good / proper function). What does Yahawah darash (require) of you, but to act justly, to ahabah (love) chasad (grace), and to yalak (walk) tzanai (humbly) with your Alahayam?

Yahawah qawal (sound / voice) qaraa (called) to the iyar (city), and thawashayah (wisdom) yaraa (fear / be afraid) your sham (name): "shamai (hearken / hear) to the matah (staff / rod / tribe), and he who yaid (appointed) it.
Are there yet atzarawath (treasures) of rashai (wickedness) in the bayath (house) of the rashai (wicked), and a short ayapah (ephah) that is accursed?
Shall I be zakah (pure) with dishonest scales, and with a kayas (bag) of deceitful abanay (weights)?

Her ishayar (rich) men are malaa (full) of chamas (violence), her yashab (inhabit/dwell) dabar (word / matter) shaqar (lies), and their lashawan (tongue / language) is deceitful in their pah (speech).
Therefore I also have struck you with a grievous nakah (wound). I have shamam (made) you desolate because of your chataah (sin).

You shall akal (eat), but not be shabai (satisfied). Your humiliation will be in your qarab (among / near). You will store up, but not palat (save); and that which you palat (save) I will nathan (give) up to the charab (sword).

You will zarai (sow), but won't qatzar (reap). You will darak (tread) the zayath (olive), but won't sawak (anoint) yourself with shaman (oil); and thayarawash (crush) grapes, but won't shathah (drinks) the thayarawash (wine).

For the chaqawath (statutes) of Imaray (Omri) are shamar (keep/guard), and all the maishah (works) of the bayath (house) of Achaab (Ahab). You yalak (walk) in their mawaitzah (counsels), that I may nathan (give) you a ruin, and her yashab (inhabit/dwell) a sharaqah (hissing); And you will nashaa (lift) the charapah (reproach) of my im (nation / people)."

Misery is mine! Indeed, I am like asap (one) who gathers the qayatz (summer) fruits, as gleanings of the vineyard: There is no ashakawal (cluster) of grapes to akal (eat). My napash (soul) awah (desires) to eat the early fig.

The chasayad (godly) man abad (destroy / perish) perished out of the aratz (Earth/land), and there is no one yashar (upright) among adam (men). They all lie in arab (wait) for dam (blood); every ayash (man / husband) yatzawadaw (hunts) his ach (brother/kinsman) with a charam (net).

Their kapayam (hands) are on that which is rai (evil) to yatab (do) it diligently. The shar (prince / ruler) and shapat (judge / judgement) shaal (ask) for a bribe; and the powerful dabar (word / matter) dictates the hawah (calamity / destruction) napash (soul) of his ibath (soul). Thus they conspire together.

The tawab (good / proper function) of them is like a chadaq (brier). The most yashar (upright) is worse than a masawakah (thorn) hedge. The yawam (day) of your watchmen, even your paqadah (visitation), bawaa (come) come; now is the time of their mabawakah (confusion).

Don't aman (believe / have faith) in a neighbor. Don't batach (put) confidence in a rai (neigbor/another person). With the shakab (woman) lying in your embrace, be careful of the pathachay (words) of your pah (mouth)!

For the ban (son) dishonors the ab (father), the banath (daughter) qawam (rise up) up against her am (mother), the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a anashay (mans) ayabay (enemies) are the ban (son) of his own bayath (house).
But as for me, I will tzapah (watchman / keep watch) to Yahawah. I will yachal (wait) for the Alahayam of my yashai (salvation). My Alahayam will shamai (hearken / hear) me.

Don't shamach (rejoice) against me, my ayab (enemy). When I napal (fall / be cast down), I will qawam (rise up). When I yashab (inhabit/dwell) in chashak (darkness), Yahawah will be a awar (light) to me.

I will nashaa (lift) the zaip (indignation) of Yahawah, because I have chataa (sinned) against him, until he rayab (pleads) my case, and ishah (make) mashapat (judgment) for me. He will yatzaa (go out / come out) me forth to the awar (light). I will raah (see) his tzadaqah (righteousness).

Then my ayab (enemy) will raah (see) it, and bawashah (shame) will kasah (cover) her who amar (spoke) to me, where is Yahawah your Alahayam? Then my enemy will raah (see) me and will cover her shame. Now she will be maramas (trodden) down like the tayat (mire) of the chawatzawath (streets).
A yawam (day) to banah (build) your gadar (walls)— In that yawam (day), he will extend your boundary.

In that yawam (day) they will bawaa (come) to you from Ashawar (Assyria) and the iray (cities) of Matzawar (Egypt), and from Matzawar (Egypt) even to the nahar (river), and from yam (sea/waters) to yam (sea/waters), and har (mountain) to har (mountain).
Yet the aratz (Earth/land) will be shamamah (desolate) because of those who live in it, for the paray (fruit) of their mailal (doings).

Raih (shepherd) your im (nation / people) with your shabat (staff), the tzaan (flock) of your nachalah (heritage), who live by themselves in a yair (forest), in the thawak (midst) of Karamal (fertile) pasture land, let them raih (feed); in Bashan (Bashan) and Galaid (Gilead), as in the yamay (days) of iwalam (forever).
"As in the yamay (days) of your yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of the aratz (Earth/land) of Matzarayam (Egypt), I will show them palaa (be wonderful / extraordinary / marvelous) things."

The gawayam (nations) will raah (see) and be bawash (ashamed) of all their gabawarah (might). They will shawam (place / establish / appoint) their yad (hand) on their pah (mouth). Their azan (ear) will be charash (deaf).

They will lachak (lick) the ipar (dust) like a nachash (serpent). Like crawling things of the aratz (Earth/land) they shall come ragaz (trembling) out of their dens. They will come with yaraa (fear / be afraid) to Yahawah our Alahayam, and will be yaraa (fear / be afraid) because of you.

Who is a Al like you, who nashaa (lift) iwan (guilt/iniquity), and passes over the disobedience of the shaarayath (remnant) of his nachalah (heritage)? He doesn't chazaq (retain) his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting) id (until / as far as), because he chapatz (delights) in loving chasad (grace).

He will again racham (show mercy / love) compassion on us. He will tread our iwan (guilt/iniquity) under foot; and you will shalak (cast) all their chataah (sin) into the matzalawath (depths) of the yam (sea/waters).
You will nathan (give) amath (truth) to Yaiqab (Jacob), and chasad (grace) to Abaraham (Abraham), as you have shabai (swear / take oath) to our ab (father) from the yamay (days) of qadam (old).
An oracle about Nayanawah (Nineveh). The sapar (book / scribed document) of the chazawan (vision) of Nachawam (Nahum) the alaqashay (elkoshite).

Yahawah is a qanawaa (jealous) Al and naqam (avenges). Yahawah naqam (avenges) and is full of bail (wrath). Yahawah naqam (takes) vengeance on his tzar (oppressor / distressor), and he maintains wrath against his ayab (enemy).

Yahawah is arak (slow) to ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting), and gadawal (very great/important/mighty) in kach (strength / mighty / power), and will by no naqah (clean/innocent) leave the guilty naqah (clean/innocent). Yahawah has his darak (way) in the sawapah (whirlwind) and in the shairah (storm), and the inan (cloud) are the abaq (dust) of his ragal (feet / foot).

He gair (rebukes) the yam (sea/waters), and charab (makes) it dry, and yabash (dry land) up all the naharawath (rivers). Bashan (Bashan) languishes, and Karamal (Carmel); and the parach (flower) of Labanawan (Lebanon) languishes.

The harayam (mountains) raish (quake) before him, and the gabaiwath (hills) mawag (melt) away. The aratz (Earth/land) trembles at his panayam (face), yes, the thabal (world), and all who yashab (inhabit/dwell) in it.

Who can imad (stand) panayam (face) his zaim (indignation)? Who can qawam (rise up) the charawan (fierceness) of his ap (nostril / picture: bull snorting)? His chamah (wrath) is nathak (poured) out like ash (fire), and the tzarayam (rocks) are nathatz (broken) apart by him.
Yahawah is tawab (good / proper function), a stronghold in the yawam (day) of tzarah (trouble); and he yadai (knows) those who take chasah (refuge) in him.
But with an overflowing shatap (flood), he will ishah (make) a kalah (complete / finish) end of her maqawam (place), and will radap (pursue) his ayab (enemy) into chashak (darkness).
What do you plot against Yahawah? He will ishah (make) a kalah (complete / finish) end. Tzarah (affliction) won't qawam (rise up) up the paim (second) time.
For entangled like sayarayam (thorns), and drunken as with their sabaa (drink), they are akal (eat) utterly like yabash (dry land) qash (stubble).
There is one yatzaa (go out / come out) forth out of you, who chashab (devises) rai (evil) against Yahawah, who yaitz (counsels) balayail (wickedness).

Thus amar (spoke) Yahawah: "Though they be in shalam (full / whole / complete) strength, and likewise many, even so they will be gazaz (cut) down, and he shall ibar (pass over/through) away. Though I have inah (oppress / afflict) you, I will inah (oppress / afflict) you no more.
Now will I shabar (break) his mawat (yoke) from off you, and will nathaq (burst) your mawasar (bonds) apart."

Yahawah has tzawah (commanded) concerning you: "No more descendants will bear your sham (name). Out of the bayath (house) of your Alahayam, will I karath (cut) off the engraved pasal (image) and the masakah (molten) image. I will shawam (place / establish / appoint) your qabar (grave / tomb / sepulcher), for you are qalal (vile)."

Behold, on the har (mountain) the ragal (feet / foot) of him who brings bashar (good) news, who publishes shalawam (peace / safety)! Chagag (keep) your chag (feast/festival), Yahawadah (Judah)! Shalam (perform) your nadar (vow), for the balayail (wicked) yasap (one) will no more ibar (pass over/through) through you. He is karath (cut) cut off.
He who dashes in pieces has yasap (come) up il (over) you. Chagag (keep) the fortress! Watch the ibar (pass over/through)! Strengthen your waist! Fortify your power mightily!
For Yahawah ilah (go up / offer) the excellency of Jacob, as the excellency of Israel; for the destroyers have destroyed them, and ruined their vine branches.
The shield of his mighty men is shawab (turn back / repent) red. The valiant men are in scarlet. The chariots flash with steel in the day of his preparation, and the pine spears are brandished.
The rakab (chariots) rage in the streets. They rush back and forth in the broad ways. Their appearance is like torches. They run like the lightnings.
He summons his picked troops. They stumble on their way. They dash to its wall, and the protective shield is put in place.
The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace is dissolved.
It is decreed: she is uncovered, she is carried away; and her handmaids moan as with the voice of doves, beating on their breasts.
But Nineveh has been from of old like a pool of water, yet they flee away. "Stop! Stop!" They cry, but no one looks back.
Take the spoil of silver. Take the spoil of gold, for there is no yawam (day) of the store, the glory of all goodly furniture.
She is empty, void, and waste. The heart melts, the knees knock together, their bodies and faces have grown pale.
Where is the den of the lions, and the feeding place of the young lions, where the lion and the lioness walked, the lion's cubs, and no one made them afraid?
The aray (lion) tore in pieces enough for his cubs, and strangled for his lionesses, and filled his caves with the kill, and his maiwan (dens) with prey.

"Behold, I am against you," says Yahawah of Armies, "and I will burn her chariots in the smoke, and the sword will devour your young aray (lions); and I will cut off your tarap (prey) from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will no longer be heard."
Haway (Alas/Woe!) To the bloody iyar (city)! It is all full of kachash (lies) and paraq (robbery). The tarap (prey) doesn't depart.
The qawal (sound / voice) of the shawat (whip), the qawal (sound / voice) of the raish (rattling) of awapan (wheels), prancing sawas (horses), and bounding marakabah (chariots),

The parash (horseman) ilah (go up / offer), and the flashing charab (sword), the baraq (glittering) chanayath (spear), and a rab (multitude) of chalal (slain), and a kabad (great) heap of pagar (corpses), and there is no qatzah (end / extremity / border) of the pagar (bodies).
